payload.name: Sanish Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with full services through Labor Day. After Labor Day, the marina store closes and all comfort stations except Elbowoods are shut down. Campground water is discontinued October 4. Reservations available at reservendparks.com up to 95 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Sanish Campground offers lakeside camping at Lake Sakakawea State Park with electric/water hookups, accessible cabins, and access to the North Country National Scenic Trail on North Dakota's third-largest reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Sanish Campground is one of several camping loops within Lake Sakakawea State Park, situated on the south shore of the third-largest man-made reservoir in the United States. The campground features modern sites with 30/50 amp electric and water hookups, plus two ADA-accessible seasonal camping cabins. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, a dump station, and fire rings with picnic tables at each site. A full-service marina with convenience store, boat rentals, and deep-water boat ramps are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Sanish Campground is part of Lake Sakakawea State Park, located on the south shore of the massive 368,000-acre Lake Sakakawea. The campground is named after the town of Sanish, one of three communities inundated when Garrison Dam created the reservoir in the 1950s. The park serves as the western terminus of the 4,800-mile North Country National Scenic Trail, and the Shoreline Trail traverses the park along the water's edge, showcasing unique scoria formations, petrified trees, and exposed coal veins.

The park offers 140 modern campsites with electric and water hookups across multiple loops including Sanish, Elbowoods, and Van Hook, plus 43 primitive sites and 10 group sites. Sanish Campground hosts two seasonal camping cabins that are ADA-accessible, air-conditioned, and equipped with refrigerators, sleeping up to five guests. Each campsite includes a fire ring and picnic table, with flush toilet comfort stations and showers available throughout the camping season.

Recreation opportunities abound with a full-service marina featuring a convenience store, gas dock, pump-out service, and boat storage. Two boat ramps provide deep-water access to prime walleye, northern pike, and salmon fishing. The park also features a swim beach, multiple picnic shelters, playgrounds, sand volleyball courts, horseshoe pits, and rental equipment including pontoon boats and kayaks.

location.directions: From Pick City, the park is located at 720 Park Ave. From New Town, head west on ND-23 for approximately 2.6 miles.

payload.name: Twin Lakes State Park Cabins And Lodge
payload.status_description: The cabins and lodge are open year-round. During peak season (Memorial Day through Labor Day), a 6-night minimum stay is required, reduced to 4 nights three months prior and 2 nights in the final month before arrival. Off-season requires a 2-night minimum. Check-in is at 4 p.m. and check-out is at 10 a.m.
payload.short_description: Year-round cabin and lodge rentals at Twin Lakes State Park near Farmville, Virginia, featuring climate-controlled accommodations overlooking Prince Edward and Goodwin Lakes.
payload.medium_description: Twin Lakes State Park offers 11 climate-controlled cabins and the 16-person Bowen Lodge, ranging from 2-bedroom cottages to a 6-bedroom waterfront lodge. All cabins feature full kitchens, bathrooms, and fireplaces. The park sits on 548 acres with two lakes offering swimming, fishing, and boating. Linens are not provided. No Wi-Fi is available.
payload.long_description:
Twin Lakes State Park Cabins and Lodge provides year-round overnight accommodations in the heart of Virginia's Piedmont region, approximately one hour southwest of Richmond. The park features 11 climate-controlled cabins sleeping 4-8 guests and the Bowen Lodge accommodating up to 16 people. Cabin types include 2-bedroom and 3-bedroom options, with several offering waterfront views of Prince Edward Lake. All units feature full kitchens, indoor bathrooms, and fireplaces (wood-burning or gas).

The park encompasses 548 acres surrounding two lakes: the 36-acre Prince Edward Lake and 15-acre Goodwin Lake. Guests can enjoy swimming at the designated beach area on Goodwin Lake, fishing for largemouth bass and catfish (Virginia license required), and boating with electric motors. Six miles of hiking trails wind through the park, connecting to an additional 8-mile multi-use trail in the adjacent Prince Edward-Gallion State Forest.

Cabin 2 and the Bowen Lodge are ADA-accessible. Pets are permitted with a $20 per night fee. Guests must bring their own linens, towels, and toiletries. The park has no Wi-Fi, TV, or telephone service in the cabins. A concession stand operates during summer months, and boat rentals are available seasonally.

location.directions: From Richmond, take US-360 West toward Burkeville. Turn south on VA-307, then west on VA-629 to the park entrance at 788 Twin Lakes Road, Green Bay, VA 23942.

address.full: 595 Cedar Crest Rd, Green Bay, VA 23942

links.title: Twin Lakes State Park Official Page

payload.name: Remote Campsites
payload.status_description: Remote campsites are open from April 1 through November 1, weather permitting. Reservations required via reservemn.usedirect.com up to 120 days in advance. Vehicle permit required ($7 daily or $35 annual).
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry campsites at Scenic State Park accessible by backpacking or canoe/boat. Two backpack sites on Pine Lake and five water-access sites on Coon and Sandwick Lakes amid towering virgin pines.
payload.medium_description: Scenic State Park offers seven remote campsites in Minnesota's Northwoods: two backpack-in sites along Pine Lake (1.5-mile hike on flat trails) and five canoe/boat-in sites on pristine Coon and Sandwick Lakes. These primitive sites sit among some of the last stands of virgin pine in Minnesota, providing a true wilderness experience with basic amenities including tent pads, fire rings, and pit toilets. Reservations required through the Minnesota State Parks system.
payload.long_description:
Scenic State Park's remote campsites offer backcountry camping amid towering virgin red and white pines, some of the last remaining old-growth stands in Minnesota. The park features two types of remote camping: backpack-in sites along small Pine Lake, requiring an easy 1.5-mile hike on flat trails, and five canoe or boat-in sites scattered along the shores of crystal-clear Coon and Sandwick Lakes.

These primitive sites provide a true wilderness experience with basic amenities typical of Minnesota State Parks backcountry camping. Each site includes a tent pad, fire ring, and access to primitive pit toilet facilities. Some sites feature picnic tables and fire grates. The canoe-in sites surrounded by red pine on the lakeshore are particularly popular for their cathedral-like pine canopy and excellent fishing access.

The remote campsites operate seasonally from April 1 through November 1, weather permitting. Reservations are required and can be made up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota State Parks reservation system online or by phone. Campers should be prepared to pack in all supplies including drinking water, as no potable water is available at the backcountry sites.

location.directions: From Bigfork, travel north on County Road 7 approximately 7 miles to the park entrance. For backpack sites, access via trail from parking area near Pine Lake. For canoe/boat-in sites, launch from park boat access on Coon Lake.

payload.name: Old Shady Rest Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Sites are available through Recreation.gov with some first-come, first-served availability. One vehicle is included per reservation; additional vehicles cost $10 per night. Bear boxes are mandatory for all food storage.
payload.short_description: Popular 47-site campground in a Jeffrey pine forest at 7,800 feet, within walking distance of Mammoth Lakes. Ideal for tents and small to medium RVs.
payload.medium_description: Old Shady Rest Campground sits in a shady grove of Jeffrey pines at 7,800 feet elevation, just minutes from the town of Mammoth Lakes in Inyo National Forest. The 47 sites accommodate tents and small to medium RVs, with flush toilets, potable water from hand pumps, picnic tables, fire rings, and bear boxes at each site. A dump station is available but there are no hookups. The campground provides easy access to hiking, mountain biking, fishing, and the shops and restaurants of Mammoth Lakes.
payload.long_description:
Old Shady Rest Campground offers 47 campsites beneath a mature Jeffrey pine canopy in the eastern Sierra Nevada Mountains. At 7,800 feet elevation, the campground provides a cool forested retreat within walking distance of the full-service town of Mammoth Lakes. Sites include picnic tables, fire rings, and bear-proof food storage lockers. Flush toilets and potable water from hand pumps are available throughout the campground, along with a dump station for RV users.

The Mammoth Lakes area is renowned for its exceptional trout fishing in nearby creeks and lakes, challenging trails for hikers and mountain bikers, and world-class skiing in winter. A paved walking and biking trail connects the campground to two nearby campgrounds, a town park with a playing field and skate park, and downtown Mammoth Lakes. Day trips to Yosemite National Park, Mono Basin, and Devils Postpile National Monument are easily accessible.

The campground is an active bear area, and all food and scented items must be stored in the provided bear boxes (48" x 30" x 36"). Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Showers are not available on-site but can be found nearby in town.

location.directions: Take US Highway 395 to State Route 203. Proceed west on 203 for 2.8 miles to Old Sawmill Road. Turn right, go 0.5 mile. The campground entrance is on the left.

address.full: 30 Old Shady Rest Cg Rd, Mammoth Lakes, CA 93546

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **EXTRA VEHICLE FEES: One vehicle is included in your reservation. Any additional vehicles will be charged $10.00 per vehicle, per night and will be collected by the camp host.**

payload.name: Flint Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed, likely due to early season conditions. While officially designated as open year-round, mountain campgrounds in this area often have delayed openings in spring due to snow and frozen ground. No advance reservations are accepted; sites are first-come, first-served with on-site payment via cash, check, or QR code scan through the Recreation.gov mobile app.
payload.short_description: Streamside first-come, first-served campground with 10 sites along Flint Creek, 8 miles south of Philipsburg and 4 miles north of Georgetown Lake in the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Flint Creek Campground offers 10 first-come, first-served sites nestled among mixed conifers along the banks of Flint Creek in southwest Montana. Located just minutes from Georgetown Lake, the campground provides excellent trout fishing access, vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings. Bear-resistant food storage lockers are provided due to prevalent bear activity. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Flint Creek Campground sits at the base of the Anaconda Range in Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, eight miles south of Philipsburg and four miles north of Georgetown Lake. The 10 campsites are shaded by mixed conifers and positioned along Flint Creek, offering streamside access for trout fishing and occasional moose sightings. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with a double-vault ADA-accessible restroom centrally located.

The campground operates first-come, first-served only with no advance reservations. Campers should bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available on site. The area falls under a food storage order due to grizzly and black bear activity; bear-resistant storage lockers are provided. Pack out all trash as there is no garbage service.

Georgetown Lake is a 10-minute drive south and offers fishing, boating, and day-use areas. The Pintler Ranger District provides access to numerous trails leading into the Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness, which spans nearly 250 square miles along the Continental Divide.

location.directions: From Philipsburg, travel south on Highway 1 for approximately 7.8 miles. Turn left onto Power House Road into the campground.

payload.name: Maurice K Goddard State Park
payload.status_description: Maurice K. Goddard State Park is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping. Pavilions are available for reservation. The marina operates May 1 through October 31.
payload.short_description: Day-use state park on 1,680-acre Lake Wilhelm featuring marina, boat launches, fishing piers, hiking trails, and reservable picnic pavilions. No overnight camping available.
payload.medium_description: Maurice K. Goddard State Park is a 2,856-acre day-use park centered on the 1,680-acre Lake Wilhelm in northwestern Pennsylvania. Popular with anglers and boaters, the park features a 241-slip marina, seven boat launches, fishing piers, hiking trails, and picnic areas with reservable pavilions. While the park does not offer overnight camping, nearby private campgrounds provide that option.
payload.long_description:
Maurice K. Goddard State Park encompasses 2,856 acres in Mercer County, Pennsylvania, with the 1,680-acre Lake Wilhelm as its centerpiece. The lake is a prime destination for fishing (largemouth bass, walleye, muskie, panfish) and boating, with motors limited to 20 hp. The park operates a 241-slip marina and 48-space dry land mooring area from May 1 through October 31, plus seven boat launches around the lake.

Day-use facilities include four reservable pavilions accommodating 40-96 guests, picnic areas with tables and charcoal grills, restrooms, and a boat rental concession offering pontoons, rowboats, kayaks, and canoes. The park features over 20 miles of hiking and biking trails, ADA-accessible fishing piers, and hunting opportunities in season.

This is a day-use park only. Maurice K. Goddard State Park does not have tent sites, RV sites, cabins, or other overnight camping facilities. Campers seeking overnight accommodations should look to nearby private campgrounds.

location.directions: From I-79, take Exit 130 (Sandy Lake/Stoneboro). Head west on PA-358 toward Sandy Lake. Turn left onto Lake Wilhelm Road and continue to the park entrance at 684 Lake Wilhelm Road, Sandy Lake, PA 16145.

address.full: 684 Lake Wilhelm Rd, Sandy Lake, PA 16145

payload.name: Hirz Bay
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served. Potable water may not be available. Bears are active in the area; use provided bear lockers for all food storage.
payload.short_description: Hillside campground overlooking the McCloud Arm of Shasta Lake with flush toilets, fire rings, and nearby boat ramp access.
payload.medium_description: Hirz Bay Campground sits among manzanita and oak trees on a hilltop overlooking the McCloud Arm of Shasta Lake at 1,067 feet elevation. The 46-site campground offers flush toilets, paved parking spurs, fire rings, picnic tables, and bear-proof food lockers at each site. A boat ramp is about 1 mile away, and the 2-mile Hirz Bay Trail departs from the campground.
payload.long_description:
Hirz Bay Campground is perched on a scenic hilltop among manzanita and oak trees, offering views of the McCloud Arm of Shasta Lake within the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The campground provides 46 sites with paved parking spurs, picnic tables, fire rings, and bear-proof food lockers. Flush toilets and a pay phone are available on site.

The location is ideal for water recreation, with the Hirz Bay boat ramp about 1 mile away. Shasta Lake offers excellent fishing for trout, catfish, Chinook salmon, crappie, bluegill, bass, and white sturgeon. Power boating, water skiing, and swimming are popular activities. Hikers can access the 2-mile Hirz Bay Trail directly from the campground.

Nearby attractions include the Hirz Mountain Lookout at 3,500 feet with panoramic views of Mt. Shasta and Mt. Lassen, and the Lake Shasta Caverns on the McCloud Arm. Campers should be aware of active bears in the area and store all food in the provided bear lockers. Poison oak is abundant.

location.directions: From Redding, CA, take I-5 to the Gilman Road exit. From the north, take the Salt Creek exit to Gilman Road. Follow Gilman Road east for 11 miles to the entrance of Hirz Bay.

payload.name: W.p. Franklin South Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for day use from sunrise to sunset. No overnight camping is allowed. Two group shelters are available for reservation, currently limited to 25 people maximum. The courtesy dock at the boat ramp is closed for repairs.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on the Caloosahatchee River with reservable group shelters, boat ramp, and picnic facilities. No overnight camping allowed.
payload.medium_description: W.P. Franklin South Recreation Area is a day-use facility operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on the south bank of the Caloosahatchee River, adjacent to the W.P. Franklin Lock and Dam. The area features a boat ramp, visitor center, playground, volleyball and horseshoe courts, and two reservable group picnic shelters. No overnight camping is permitted.
payload.long_description:
W.P. Franklin South Recreation Area is a day-use facility operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, located on the south bank of the Caloosahatchee River adjacent to the W.P. Franklin Lock and Dam. Situated about 10 miles east of Fort Myers, the area provides access to the 152-mile Okeechobee Waterway connecting the Atlantic Ocean to the Gulf of Mexico.

The recreation area features a boat ramp for river access (though the courtesy dock is currently closed for repairs), flush toilets, drinking water, a visitor center with exhibits, playground, and volleyball and horseshoe courts. Two group picnic shelters with water, electricity, charcoal grills, and picnic tables are available for reservation, currently limited to 25 people maximum.

This is strictly a day-use facility with no overnight camping permitted. The area opens at sunrise and closes at sunset daily. For overnight camping, the nearby W.P. Franklin North campground on the opposite bank offers RV and tent sites.

location.directions: From Interstate 75, take Exit 141 (Palm Beach Blvd.) east for 7 miles to Old Olga Road. Turn left on Old Olga Road and proceed 0.3 miles to Franklin Lock Road. Turn right on Franklin Lock Road into the recreation area.

address.full: 1710 S Franklin Lock Rd, Alva, FL 33920

payload.name: Dry Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is accessible year-round with no fee. Vault toilets are available June through early September only. Outside the primary season, there are no facilities. No potable water at any time; bring your own.
payload.short_description: A free, primitive 3-site campground in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest near Malad City, Idaho, with vault toilets, fire rings, and tables but no water or trash service.
payload.medium_description: Dry Canyon Campground is a small, free first-come, first-served campground tucked into a quiet hollow southeast of Malad City, Idaho. The three single-family sites each have a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available during the June through early September season, but there is no potable water and all trash must be packed out.
payload.long_description:
Dry Canyon Campground sits at approximately 6,000 feet elevation in the Bear River Range within the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. This small campground offers three single-family sites, each equipped with a picnic table and campfire ring. The setting features sparse trees and open terrain with limited shade, providing a peaceful and secluded retreat.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees required. Vault toilets are available from June through early September. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Trash service is not provided; pack-in, pack-out rules apply. The area offers opportunities for fishing, hunting, and hiking in the surrounding forest. Small trailers are welcome, though the dirt roads and parking areas may limit access for larger RVs.

location.directions: From Weston, ID head west on ID-36 for 4.7 miles. Take a slight right onto Dry Canyon Road and go 1.1 miles. Campground is located at the end of the road.

payload.name: Robie Creek Park Group Shelter
payload.status_description: This is a day-use only facility, not an overnight campground. The park is open sunrise to sunset. The group shelter is reservable via Recreation.gov; check-in is 9:00 AM and check-out is 9:00 PM same day. Parking is first-come, first-served with recommended arrival before 11:00 AM on busy days.
payload.short_description: Reservable day-use group shelter at Lucky Peak Lake with covered picnic area, grills, vault toilets, and access to swimming beach and boat launch.
payload.medium_description: Robie Creek Park Group Shelter is a day-use only facility at Lucky Peak Lake managed by the US Army Corps of Engineers. The covered group shelter accommodates up to 50 people with 10 picnic tables, high-top serving counters, two large grills, and a hot coal bin. The park also features six individual shade shelters with tables and grills, three vault toilets, a playground, and access to a buoyed swimming area and nearby boat launch.
payload.long_description:
Robie Creek Park Group Shelter is a secluded day-use facility at the confluence of Mores Creek and Robie Creek on the edge of the Boise National Forest. The site is part of the Lucky Peak Lake recreation area managed by the US Army Corps of Engineers, located about 12 miles from Boise via Highway 21.

The reservable group shelter is non-electric and accommodates up to 50 people with parking for 10 vehicles. Amenities include 10 picnic tables, high-top serving counters, two large grills, and a hot coal bin. The surrounding park has six individual shade shelters each with a table and stand-up grill, three vault toilets, and a playground.

Recreation opportunities include swimming at the buoyed beach area and boating at the adjacent Robie Creek Launch Area. The setting features basalt canyons, ponderosa pines, and granite outcrops. Note there is no cellular service at this location; an emergency phone is available at the park entrance.

location.directions: From the intersection of Warm Springs Road and Highway 21 in Boise, turn north onto Highway 21 towards Idaho City. Continue 9.2 miles, passing Lucky Peak Dam and the Forest Service Nursery. Cross the Mores Creek High Bridge and continue another 2.3 miles. Near mile marker 21, as the road descends into Mores Creek canyon and the speed limit drops from 55 to 45 MPH, make a hairpin left turn onto Robie Creek Road. Continue past Mores Creek Park and Robie Creek Launch Area to reach the gravel parking area at Robie Creek Park.

photos.name: Robie Creek Group Shelter High Tables
Robie Creek Group Shelter Tables and High Tables
Robie Creek Park Group Use Shelter.

payload.name: Las Huertas Picnic Site
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 15 through October 15. This is a day-use picnic site only; overnight camping is not permitted.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC-built day-use picnic area on the east slope of the Sandia Mountains along year-round Las Huertas Creek. No overnight camping permitted.
payload.medium_description: Las Huertas Picnic Site is a day-use recreation area built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, situated at 7,600 feet elevation on the east side of the Sandia Mountains. Las Huertas Creek, the only year-round stream in the range, meanders through the site. Dispersed picnic tables and grills are tucked among aspen and fir trees, and a group pavilion accommodates up to 50 people. Overnight camping is not allowed.
payload.long_description:
Las Huertas Picnic Site occupies a scenic stretch along Las Huertas Creek at the northeast end of the Sandia Ranger District in Cibola National Forest. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps between 1933 and 1941, the site preserves historic architecture including a group pavilion designed in the original CCC style. At 7,600 feet elevation, the area is shaded by aspen and fir trees, with the sound of the creek audible throughout.

The site offers dispersed picnic areas on a first-come, first-served basis, each with tables and grills suitable for small family groups. The reservable group pavilion can host up to 50 people under a covered shelter with multiple tables and grills. Accessible vault toilets and bear-proof trash receptacles are provided. No potable water is available; bring your own supply.

This is a day-use area only. Overnight camping is prohibited. Nearby attractions include Sandia Man Cave to the north and the town of Placitas for restaurants and services.

location.directions: From Albuquerque, drive north on I-25 to Exit 242 (Bernalillo/State Hwy 165). Stay right as you exit the ramp and proceed east on State Road 165 through Placitas. The road curves south into the Sandia Mountain range. Las Huertas Picnic Site will be on your right. Display an amenity/parking pass or pay $5 day-use fee.

links.title: USFS Cibola NF - Las Huertas Picnic Site

photos.name: Picnic tables going up the hill.
Stream and Bridge in Las Huertas Picnic Site
Reservation site with pavilion at Las Huertas

payload.name: Spillway Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from late May through late September. First-come, first-served only; no reservations accepted. No fees required.
payload.short_description: Small free 3-site primitive campground on Anderson Ranch Reservoir with vault toilet, no water, and excellent fishing access.
payload.medium_description: Spillway Campground is a compact, free first-come-first-served campground with 3 sites along Anderson Ranch Reservoir in the Boise National Forest. The reservoir offers excellent fishing for smallmouth bass and kokanee, plus boating and waterskiing. Basic amenities include a vault toilet, picnic tables, and fire rings, but there is no potable water.
payload.long_description:
Spillway Campground sits at the edge of Anderson Ranch Reservoir, just a stone's throw from the dam in Idaho's Boise National Forest. This compact, free campground has just 3 first-come-first-served sites, making it a quiet spot for anglers and boaters who want to stay close to the water without crowds or fees.

The reservoir is a popular summer destination known for excellent fishing. Target smallmouth bass and kokanee in the reservoir, or try fly fishing for trout in the waters just below the dam. Boating, waterskiing, and personal watercraft are all popular activities. Rafting access is available at Reclamation Village, located just south of the campground.

Amenities are basic: vault toilet, picnic tables, and fire rings. There is no potable water, so bring your own supply. No hookups are available, making this best suited for tent campers or self-contained RVs.

location.directions: From Mountain Home, Idaho, travel northeast 21 miles on State Highway 20 to the Forest Service Road 134 turnoff. Take FR 134 north approximately 6 miles to Anderson Ranch Dam. Spillway Campground is adjacent to the dam.

address.full: 18001-20699 NE South Fork Rd, Mountain Home, ID 83647

payload.name: Franz Jevne Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping through late October. Reservations available via reservemn.usedirect.com up to 120 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Minnesota's smallest state park offers 21 rustic riverside campsites along the Rainy River, with opportunities for fishing walleye, northern pike, and sturgeon on the Canadian border.
payload.medium_description: Franz Jevne State Park campground sits on the scenic Rainy River at the Minnesota-Ontario border, offering 18 drive-in and 3 walk-in rustic campsites. Two sites have electric hookups. The peaceful campground features vault toilets, hand-pump water, fire rings, and picnic tables with distinctive Adirondack-style shelters. A boat launch provides river access for fishing and paddling.
payload.long_description:
Franz Jevne State Park is Minnesota's smallest state park, a secluded 118-acre preserve along the Rainy River that forms the international boundary between the United States and Canada. The campground offers 21 rustic sites tucked into riverside forest, including 18 drive-in sites and 3 walk-in sites. Two of the drive-in sites feature electric hookups for those wanting a bit more convenience.

The campground provides basic but functional amenities including vault toilets, hand-pump potable water, fire rings, and picnic tables. Many sites feature distinctive Adirondack-style picnic table shelters that offer some protection from the elements. The park's boat launch provides direct access to the Rainy River, where anglers pursue walleye, northern pike, smallmouth bass, and lake sturgeon. About 2.5 miles of hiking trails wind through the riverside forest, offering excellent opportunities for birdwatching and wildlife viewing.

This is a true get-away-from-it-all destination with no cell service and minimal development, ideal for campers seeking solitude and natural beauty in far northern Minnesota.

location.directions: Located on State Highway 11 in Birchdale, Minnesota, approximately 30 miles west of International Falls and 40 miles east of Baudette.

links.title: Franz Jevne State Park - MN DNR

payload.name: Hemlock Butte Ski Cabin
payload.status_description: The cabin is open for reservations through Recreation.gov. Over-snow access via the Hemlock Butte Trail is typically available late December through March. Oregon State Sno-Park permit required for parking at Three Lakes Sno-Park from November 1 through April 30. Current fire danger is low with no restrictions.
payload.short_description: A backcountry ski cabin in Umpqua National Forest near Mount Bailey, accessible via a 4-mile ski or snowshoe trip on the Hemlock Butte Trail. Sleeps 8 with a wood stove and vault toilet.
payload.medium_description: Hemlock Butte Ski Cabin is a three-room A-frame cabin built by the Edelweiss Ski Club in 1990, located at the base of Mount Bailey in Umpqua National Forest. The cabin sleeps up to 8 guests and is accessed via a challenging 4-mile backcountry ski or snowshoe journey from Three Lakes Sno-Park. Amenities are minimal: a wood stove for heat and melting snow, a vault toilet, and possibly firewood. Guests must bring all supplies including sleeping gear, cookware, and drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Hemlock Butte Ski Cabin is a rustic three-room A-frame structure built by the Edelweiss Ski Club in 1990, situated at the base of Mount Bailey in Oregon's Umpqua National Forest. This backcountry cabin offers access to some of the Pacific Northwest's best skiing terrain, with Mount Bailey averaging 600 inches of snow annually and featuring 6,000 acres of skiable terrain. The cabin accommodates up to 8 people and may be shared between multiple reservation groups.

Access requires a 4-mile ski, snowshoe, or snowmobile trip from Three Lakes Sno-Park via the Hemlock Butte Trail. The trail offers views of Mount Thielsen, Mount Bailey, and Crater Lake on clear days. An Oregon State Sno-Park permit is required for parking at the trailhead from November through April.

The cabin provides only basic amenities: a wood stove for heating and melting snow, a single cooking pot, and an indoor vault toilet. Firewood may be available but is not guaranteed mid-season. Guests must pack in all supplies including sleeping bags and pads, cookware, lanterns, food, and garbage bags. All trash must be packed out. Pets are prohibited.

location.directions: From Roseburg, travel east on OR-138 / Diamond Lake Boulevard for approximately 84 miles. Turn right onto Highway 230; Three Lakes Sno-Park is approximately 2.5 miles down the road on the right. From the Sno-Park, access the cabin via the 4-mile Hemlock Butte Trail by ski, snowshoe, or snowmobile.

payload.name: Headlands Beach State Park Campground
payload.status_description: This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. The park is open year-round. Ohio state parks do not charge entrance fees.
payload.short_description: Headlands Beach State Park is Ohio's largest natural sand beach, offering day-use facilities for swimming, sunbathing, and picnicking on Lake Erie. No overnight camping is available.
payload.medium_description: Headlands Beach State Park features Ohio's largest natural sand beach at 35 acres within a 120-acre park along Lake Erie. This day-use facility offers swimming, sunbathing, beach glass hunting, fishing from the breakwall, and picnicking with a seasonal concessionaire. The adjacent Headlands Dunes State Nature Preserve and Mentor Marsh provide hiking and birding opportunities. No overnight camping is available at this park.
payload.long_description:
Headlands Beach State Park, located in Mentor and Painesville Township in Lake County, Ohio, boasts the state's largest natural sand beach. The mile-long beach attracts approximately two million visitors annually for swimming, sunbathing, and beach glass hunting along Lake Erie. The park opened to the public in 1953 and has been recognized by CNN as one of the top 20 beaches in the United States.

The park provides day-use facilities including change booths, restrooms, picnic tables, grills, and a seasonal concession area. A breakwall at the east end of the beach offers fishing opportunities for bass, perch, walleye, salmon, and carp. Adjacent to the park is Headlands Dunes State Nature Preserve, one of the finest remaining Lake Erie beach and dune communities, and the 644-acre Mentor Marsh State Nature Preserve with hiking trails and exceptional birding (over 200 species).

This is a day-use only park with no overnight camping facilities. Campers seeking overnight accommodations should consider nearby Punderson State Park, which offers a campground, cabins, and lodge approximately 30 minutes away.

location.directions: From Cleveland, take I-90 east to State Route 44 north. Follow SR 44 north to State Route 283 (Heisley Road). Turn left and follow to Headlands Road. Turn right and proceed to the park entrance at 9601 Headlands Road, Mentor, Ohio 44060.

payload.name: Grizzly Creek Primitive
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground is experiencing a temporary water outage; bring all water you need for your visit. Operating season runs mid-to-late May through late September. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC-era primitive campground beneath oak and Ponderosa pine on Grizzly Creek, just 2 miles from Mount Rushmore along scenic Iron Mountain Road.
payload.medium_description: Grizzly Creek Primitive lies beneath a canopy of oak and Ponderosa pine on the banks of Grizzly Creek in Black Hills National Forest. This campground has retained much of its original Civilian Conservation Corps character, including a historic pavilion available for camper use. Located along Iron Mountain Road between Mount Rushmore and Custer State Park, the campground offers 19 sites with vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings. Towing vehicles are prohibited due to tight turns; maximum vehicle length is 24 feet.
payload.long_description:
Grizzly Creek Primitive occupies a shaded stretch of oak and Ponderosa pine forest along Grizzly Creek in Black Hills National Forest. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the campground retains its historic character, including a stone pavilion still available for camper use. The 19 sites are mostly tent-only, though one standard nonelectric site can accommodate vehicles up to 24 feet.

The campground sits on the scenic Iron Mountain Road, famous for its CCC-built pigtail bridges and tunnels framing views of Mount Rushmore. The memorial is just 2 miles away. Nearby destinations include Custer State Park, Crazy Horse Monument, Wind Cave National Park, and Jewel Cave. From the campground, visitors can access the Centennial Trail and portions of the Black Elk Wilderness and Norbeck Wildlife Preserve for primitive hiking.

Due to tight, sharp turns on the access road, towing is prohibited. This includes trailers, fifth-wheels, motorhomes towing vehicles, and pop-up campers. Generators are permitted from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. only. A $2 per pet per night fee applies.

location.directions: From Keystone, South Dakota, take Route 16A west 1.9 miles to campground on the right.

links.title: Black Hills NF - Grizzly Bear Campground

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Our facility is experiencing a temporary water outage. Please bring all the water you’ll need for your visit, including drinking water.

payload.name: Macedonia Brook State Park
payload.status_description: Closed for the season until May 22, 2026. The campground operates through October 12, 2026, with weekends-only camping after Labor Day. Reservations are required through Reserve America with no walk-ins accepted.
payload.short_description: Rustic 51-site campground in Connecticut's Northwest Hills offering stream fishing, 10+ miles of hiking trails, and scenic Catskill and Taconic mountain views. No running water or showers.
payload.medium_description: Macedonia Brook State Park offers a rustic camping experience across 51 wooded, meadow, and brook-side sites in a 2,300-acre natural setting. The campground provides basic amenities including pit toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site, but no running water, showers, or hookups. Excellent hiking trails wind through varied terrain with scenic vistas of the Catskill and Taconic mountains.
payload.long_description:
Macedonia Brook State Park in Kent, Connecticut provides a true back-to-basics camping experience for those seeking to disconnect from modern conveniences. The 51 campsites are spread across wooded areas, open meadows, and brook-side locations within the park's 2,300 acres. Sites accommodate tents and RVs up to 35 feet, though all camping here is primitive with no electrical hookups, running water, or showers available.

The park's extensive trail network spans more than 10 miles of varied terrain, offering hikers challenging climbs and rewarding views of the Catskill and Taconic mountain ranges. Stream fishing opportunities abound, and the area features historic sites from the region's iron industry era. Note that cell phone service is extremely limited to nonexistent throughout the campground.

Reservations are required with no walk-ins permitted. A two-night minimum stay applies, and bookings must be made at least 48 hours in advance through Reserve America. Both pets and alcohol are prohibited within the campground, though leashed pets are allowed on trails and in picnic areas.

location.directions: Located at 159 Macedonia Brook Road, Kent, CT 06757. From Route 341 in Kent, head north on Macedonia Brook Road approximately 2 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Cedar Hill State Park
payload.status_description: Open daily from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Reservations strongly recommended, especially for weekends and holidays. Invasive Argentine ants have been detected at some campsites; they do not sting but campers should prepare accordingly. Some dirt trails may be closed due to weather or maintenance. Firewood transportation is restricted due to emerald ash borer quarantine in Dallas County.
payload.short_description: Cedar Hill State Park offers 350 developed campsites on Joe Pool Lake's shore, featuring water and electric hookups at all sites, hot showers, and access to hiking, biking, fishing, and swimming just 20 minutes from downtown Dallas.
payload.medium_description: Cedar Hill State Park sits on Joe Pool Lake in the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, offering 350 developed campsites across four camping areas: Eagle Ford, Lakeview, Shady Ridge, and Coyote Crossing. All sites include water and electricity, with 147 sites offering full hookups including sewer. The park features restrooms with hot showers, fire rings and picnic tables at each site, and several ADA-accessible options. Beyond camping, visitors can explore the DORBA Trail system spanning 1,200 acres, swim at the beach area, fish, or launch boats on Joe Pool Lake.
payload.long_description:
Cedar Hill State Park provides an accessible camping destination within the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex, located on the shores of Joe Pool Lake. The park offers 350 developed campsites divided among four distinct camping areas: Eagle Ford, Lakeview, Shady Ridge, Coyote Crossing, and Hog Wallow. All developed sites include water and electric hookups with both 30 and 50 amp service available. For RVers seeking full amenities, 147 sites also provide sewer connections. Each developed campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring, with restroom facilities featuring hot showers located nearby. Sites #111, 112, 124, and 140 are wheelchair accessible.

Beyond the developed camping areas, the park offers 30 primitive hike-in campsites at $10 per night for those seeking a more rustic experience. Note that campfires are prohibited in the primitive camping area, and facilities are limited to chemical toilets. Firewood transportation is restricted due to an emerald ash borer quarantine affecting Dallas County.

The park serves as a hub for outdoor recreation with the DORBA Trail system crisscrossing 1,200 acres, open to both hikers and mountain bikers. Joe Pool Lake provides opportunities for swimming, fishing, and boating. The Penn Farm Agricultural History Center within the park offers a glimpse into North Texas farming heritage. Due to its proximity to Dallas, the park recommends reservations for camping and day use, especially on weekends and holidays.

location.directions: From Dallas, take I-20 West to FM 1382 (Belt Line Road) exit. Head south on FM 1382 for approximately 4 miles. The park entrance is at 1570 West FM 1382, Cedar Hill, TX 75104.

address.full: 7000 Farm To Market Rd 1382, Dallas, TX 75249

links.title: Cedar Hill State Park Official Page

payload.name: Monte Cristo Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. May temporarily close due to weather or road conditions during winter months. First-come, first-served only; no advance reservations. Fire restrictions may apply during high fire danger periods. Quiet hours 10 PM to 6 AM.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground at 3,600 ft elevation on the backside of the San Gabriel Mountains with vault toilets, potable water, and fire rings. RVs up to 30 ft.
payload.medium_description: Monte Cristo Campground sits at 3,600 feet elevation on the high-desert backside of the San Gabriel Mountains within the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument. The campground offers 19 spacious sites including two double sites, all with picnic tables and fire rings. Potable water is available from a hand pump, and vault toilets are provided. It operates year-round on a first-come, first-served basis at $12-20 per night.
payload.long_description:
Monte Cristo Campground is located on the quieter, high-desert side of the San Gabriel Mountains at 3,600 feet elevation, offering expansive views that feel almost endless. As one of Angeles National Forest's lesser-used campgrounds, it provides a more secluded camping experience compared to the heavily trafficked sites closer to Los Angeles. The 19 large, spacious sites are well-suited for groups, with sites #6 and #7 serving as double sites.

The campground recently underwent a complete renovation, with all sites rebuilt to include picnic tables and fire rings. Potable drinking water is available from a hand pump, and vault toilets are provided. RVs up to 30 feet can be accommodated, though no hookups are available. Bears frequent the area, so all food and scented items must be properly stored.

Nearby attractions include Granite Mountain for hiking and the postcard-worthy Switzer Falls. The campground can be reached from Pasadena via the Angeles Crest Highway or from the Antelope Valley via the Angeles Forest Highway. Cell phone coverage is poor or nonexistent.

location.directions: From Interstate 210 in Pasadena, exit the Angeles Crest Highway (Highway 2) and drive north for 9 miles. Turn left onto the Angeles Forest Highway (County Road N3) and drive about 9 miles to the campground. May also be reached from Sunland via Big Tujunga Canyon Road turning left at Angeles Forest Highway, or from Palmdale via Angeles Forest Highway.

payload.name: Pine Glen
payload.status_description: The campground opens for the 2026 season around May 22. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov. Fire restrictions may be imposed during dry conditions. This is an active bear area; bear boxes are provided and required for all food and scented items.
payload.short_description: Group campground in a Jeffrey pine forest near Mammoth Lakes, offering 9 reservable group sites for 15-30 people with flush toilets and bear lockers.
payload.medium_description: Pine Glen is a group campground tucked within a mature Jeffrey pine forest at 7,800 feet elevation, located at the end of New Shady Rest Campground. Within walking distance of downtown Mammoth Lakes, it offers nine group sites accommodating 15-30 people each, with flush toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables, fire rings, and bear-proof storage lockers.
payload.long_description:
Pine Glen Group Campground sits beneath a shady canopy of Jeffrey pines at 7,800 feet in Inyo National Forest, just minutes from the full-service town of Mammoth Lakes. Nine group sites loop around the back of New Shady Rest Campground, each designed to accommodate large families or groups of 15 to 30 people. A paved walking and biking trail connects the campground to Shady Rest Town Park and downtown Mammoth Lakes.

The facility provides flush toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables, campfire rings, and trash service. Each site includes a bear-proof locker (48"x30"x36"), and all food and scented items must be stored inside. This is an active bear area. Firewood is available for purchase on-site. Showers and a dump station are located within a few miles but not at the campground.

The Eastern Sierra offers exceptional trout fishing at nearby creeks and lakes, plus hiking, mountain biking, and OHV trails. Day trips to Devils Postpile National Monument, Mono Basin, and Yosemite National Park are all accessible from camp.

location.directions: From US Highway 395, take State Route 203 west for 2.8 miles to Old Sawmill Road. Turn right, go 0.1 mile, then turn right into the campground. Proceed to the rear of New Shady Rest Campground near site #127 to reach the Pine Glen entrance.

address.full: 301 Pine Glen Cg Rd, Mammoth Lakes, CA 93546

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **EXTRA VEHICLE FEES: One vehicle is included in your reservation. Any additional vehicles will be charged $10.00 per vehicle, per night and will be collected by the camp host.**

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: IMPORTANT: For Group Sites, you must read the NEED-TO-KNOW section for the site description info.

payload.name: Shanty Pond Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground operates October 15 through April 15 and reopens in fall 2026. First-come, first-served only; no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Primitive seasonal campground in Ocala National Forest popular with equestrians and hunters, featuring vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Shanty Pond Campground is a primitive seasonal campground located in the longleaf pine ecosystem of Ocala National Forest, south of Salt Springs off SR 19. Open October 15 through April 15, this first-come, first-served site is a favorite among equestrians accessing the Ocala horse trail system and hunters during designated seasons. The campground offers basic facilities including vault toilets and bear-safe trash receptacles, but campers must bring their own drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Shanty Pond Campground provides a rustic camping experience in the heart of Ocala National Forest's longleaf pine ecosystem. Located south of Salt Springs off State Road 19, this primitive campground operates seasonally from October 15 through April 15, coinciding with cooler weather and hunting seasons in Florida.

The campground is particularly popular with equestrians who use it as a base for exploring the extensive horse trail network in the Ocala National Forest, including the Ocala One Hundred Mile Horse Trail. Hunters also frequent the area during designated seasons. Sites accommodate tents and camping trailers, though there are no hookups or developed amenities beyond vault toilets and trash receptacles.

Campers should come prepared for a primitive experience. There is no potable water on site, so visitors must bring an adequate supply. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations available through recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Salt Springs, travel south on State Road 19. Turn west onto Forest Road 33 and follow signs to Shanty Pond Recreation Area.

payload.name: Palisades Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. First-come, first-served only; no reservations available through Recreation.gov. 14-day stay limit enforced.
payload.short_description: Scenic BLM campground on the Upper Madison River with 10 primitive sites, vault toilets, and a nearby boat launch, located 25 miles south of Ennis, Montana.
payload.medium_description: Palisades Campground is a BLM-managed recreation area on the banks of the Upper Madison River in southwestern Montana. The 80-acre site offers 10 primitive campsites with picnic tables and fire rings, two accessible vault toilets, and access to excellent trout fishing. A separate day-use area with a paved boat launch is located nearby.
payload.long_description:
Palisades Campground sits along the Upper Madison River at 5,500 feet elevation, approximately 25 miles south of Ennis in Madison County. The campground provides 10 primitive campsites spread across 80 acres of riverside terrain, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Two accessible vault toilets serve the campground, and a host site provides seasonal oversight.

The location is popular with anglers targeting the Madison River's renowned trout fishery. A separate day-use area adjacent to the campground features a paved boat launch capable of accommodating standard trailers with 2WD vehicles. The campground operates on a pack-in, pack-out trash policy.

Palisades is one of six BLM campgrounds along the Madison River corridor managed by the Dillon Field Office. Modern off-grid payment kiosks installed in 2026 accept credit cards in addition to cash and checks.

location.directions: From Ennis, drive approximately 26 miles south on US Highway 287. Turn west and continue about 1 mile to the campground.

payload.name: Citrus Tract Primitive Camp Zone Loop D
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No potable water or restrooms available. Campers should contact WSF Dispatch at 352-797-4100 before each trip to check for prescribed burns. During drought conditions, check the Burn Ban Public Dashboard before camping. Wear blaze orange during hunting seasons.
payload.short_description: Remote hike-in primitive camping zone on the Citrus Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest, accessible via the Citrus Hiking Trail 4-8 miles from the trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Citrus Tract Primitive Camp Zone Loop D is a backcountry camping zone within Withlacoochee State Forest's Citrus Tract, approximately 5 miles southwest of Inverness, Florida. This hike-in, hike-out primitive area is accessible via the Mutual Mine or Tillis Hill trailheads and sits 4-8 miles from the parking area along the Citrus Hiking Trail. The camp zone is marked by yellow bands on trees and offers a true wilderness experience with no developed amenities.
payload.long_description:
Citrus Tract Primitive Camp Zone Loop D offers backcountry camping in one of Florida's most scenic hiking areas. Located on the Citrus Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest, this primitive zone showcases rolling sandhill forests and rocky limestone karst terrain. The area is delineated by yellow-colored bands on trees and requires a 4-8 mile hike from either the Mutual Mine or Tillis Hill trailheads.

This is a true primitive camping experience with no developed facilities. Some areas may have fire rings or picnic tables, but campers should be prepared to pack in all water and supplies and pack out all trash. The zone falls within a Wildlife Management Area, so hunters and campers should wear 500 square inches of blaze orange during hunting seasons.

Recreational activities in the area include hiking, bird watching, wildlife viewing, stargazing, wildflower viewing, and nature study. Campers should contact WSF Dispatch at 352-797-4100 before each trip to verify if prescribed burning will be taking place in the area.

location.directions: From I-75, take Exit 329 to SR 44 west toward Inverness. At US 41, continue west to C-581 (Pleasant Grove Road), then south approximately 6 miles to FR 16. Access via Mutual Mine or Tillis Hill trailheads. The camp zone is 4-8 miles from the parking area.

payload.name: French Pete Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 7 through September 7. No potable water available for the entire 2026 season; campers must bring their own water supply. Sites are primarily first-come, first-served with some available via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Shaded forest campground at the confluence of French Pete Creek and the South Fork of the McKenzie River in Willamette National Forest, offering access to the Three Sisters Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: French Pete Campground sits at 1,800 feet elevation where French Pete Creek meets the South Fork of the McKenzie River. The 17 sites are heavily shaded by Douglas fir and vine maple, providing relief from summer heat. The French Pete Creek Trail across the road offers direct access to the Three Sisters Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
French Pete Campground occupies a scenic location at the confluence of French Pete Creek and the South Fork of the McKenzie River in Oregon's Willamette National Forest. At 1,800 feet elevation, the campground is heavily wooded with Douglas fir and vine maple, creating a cool, shaded retreat during summer months. The 17 campsites provide access to both waterways for fishing, though McKenzie River trout fishing is catch-and-release only.

The French Pete Creek Trail (#3311) begins directly across the road, providing access into the Three Sisters Wilderness. Nearby attractions include Terwilliger (Cougar) Hot Springs, Cougar Reservoir, and Hidden Lake. The area offers opportunities for hiking, boating, swimming, and scenic drives along the Aufderheide National Scenic Byway.

The campground offers vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and garbage service. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive nights per 60-day period, and chainsaw use is prohibited.

location.directions: From Blue River, OR, travel 4 miles east on Highway 126 to Aufderheide Drive (Forest Service Road 19). Continue south on Aufderheide Drive, turning right at the Y and climbing to the top of Cougar Reservoir. Continue south on Aufderheide Drive 8 miles to French Pete Campground.

links.title: USFS Willamette NF - French Pete Campground

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: No Water for the 2026 Season!

payload.name: Ditch Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Currently experiencing a temporary water outage; bring all water needed for your visit. Peak season fee is $22/night, off-season is free. Stage 1 fire restrictions in effect in South Dakota: campfires allowed only in established fire grates at designated sites.
payload.short_description: Quiet first-come-first-served campground with 13 sites along Ditch Creek in Black Hills National Forest, about 5 miles south of Deerfield Reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Ditch Creek Campground is a peaceful 13-site campground situated in an open area with scattered spruce trees along Ditch Creek. Located approximately 5 miles south of Deerfield Reservoir, the campground was reconstructed in 2022 to accommodate modern RVs and improve accessibility. Sites are first-come-first-served with a 14-day stay limit. The Ditch Creek OHV Trailhead is directly across the road.
payload.long_description:
Ditch Creek Campground offers a quiet camping experience adjacent to Ditch Creek in the Black Hills National Forest. The campground features 13 sites in an open setting with spruce trees along the creek banks. In June 2022, the sites were completely reconstructed to accommodate modern-sized RVs, provide accessibility, reduce resource damage, and improve fire safety.

The campground operates year-round on a first-come-first-served basis with no reservations available. Peak season camping costs $22 per night, while off-season camping is free. Interagency Senior and Access passes provide a 50% discount on the campsite fee. The stay limit is 14 days.

The Ditch Creek OHV Trailhead is located directly across the road, making this an ideal base for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts. The campground is approximately 5 miles south of Deerfield Reservoir, accessible via Deerfield Road from Hill City.

location.directions: From Hill City, travel west on Deerfield Road for 11 miles, then turn left onto Ditch Creek Road and follow for 4.5 miles. The campground will be on the right.

links.title: USFS Black Hills - Ditch Creek Campground

payload.name: Lake Mineral Wells State Park And Trailway
payload.status_description: The campground is open. No burn ban is currently in effect. An Emerald Ash Borer quarantine restricts firewood transport; buy firewood locally where you burn it. The park operates daily 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and frequently reaches capacity, so advance reservations are recommended.
payload.short_description: Texas state park near Mineral Wells with over 100 campsites ranging from primitive hike-in spots to full-hookup RV sites, plus equestrian camping, a swim beach, and 20+ miles of multi-use trails.
payload.medium_description: Lake Mineral Wells State Park offers diverse camping experiences just 45 minutes west of Fort Worth. Choose from 47 sites with 50-amp electric hookups, 30 sites with 30-amp service, 11 water-only sites, 20 equestrian campsites, or primitive hike-in camping. The park features a swim beach, lighted fishing pier, park store with canoe and kayak rentals, and over 20 miles of trails including the popular Trailway connecting to downtown Mineral Wells.
payload.long_description:
Lake Mineral Wells State Park sits in the rolling Cross Timbers region near what was once a famous health resort town. The park wraps around a 646-acre lake offering swimming, fishing from a lighted pier, and boat rentals. Multiple camping areas accommodate different styles: Live Oak has 50-amp sites for larger RVs, Plateau offers 30-amp electric sites on higher ground, Post Oak provides water-only tent camping, and Cross Timbers caters to equestrians with 20 horse-friendly sites. Primitive backcountry camping is available 1.7 miles from the trailhead for those seeking solitude.

The 20-mile Trailway is a highlight, with a paved 2-mile section through downtown Mineral Wells and 18 miles of crushed limestone surface open to hikers, bikers, and equestrians. All four trailheads have paved parking and accessible restrooms. The park store sells firewood and rents canoes, kayaks, and paddleboards.

Note that an Emerald Ash Borer quarantine is in effect; firewood must be purchased locally and cannot be transported into the park. The park operates daily from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and reaches capacity frequently, so reservations are strongly recommended.

location.directions: Located at 100 Park Road 71, Mineral Wells, TX 76067, approximately 45 minutes west of Fort Worth.

links.title: TPWD Lake Mineral Wells State Park

payload.name: Glacier View
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May through September. All sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Payment accepted via cash, check, or Recreation.gov Scan and Pay.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on the south shore of Lake Wenatchee with walk-in sites, a boat launch, and access to paddling and hiking in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Glacier View Campground sits at 1,900 feet elevation on the south shore of Lake Wenatchee, offering 23 sites including 16 walk-in lakeshore sites. The campground provides vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. A small boat launch accommodates kayaks, canoes, and small watercraft. Sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.long_description:
Glacier View Campground occupies a scenic position on the south shore of Lake Wenatchee within the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The campground features 23 sites total, with 16 walk-in sites positioned directly on the lakeshore for prime water access. At 1,900 feet elevation, the area offers cool summer camping with direct access to the lake for paddling, swimming, and fishing.

Amenities include vault toilets and potable water available from a hand pump. Each campsite is equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. A small boat launch on-site accommodates kayaks, canoes, paddleboards, and other small watercraft. Day use with boat launching is available for a separate fee. The campground enforces a 15-foot maximum trailer length, limiting it to tent camping and small trailers.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Payment can be made on-site using cash, check, or the Recreation.gov mobile app's Scan and Pay feature. Cell service is limited, so downloading the app before arrival is recommended.

location.directions: From Leavenworth, travel southwest on US-2 West for 15.1 miles to Coles Corner. Turn right onto WA-207 North and go 3.6 miles. Turn left onto Cedar Brae Road and go 0.3 mile. Turn left to stay on Cedar Brae Road/South Shore Road for 4.8 miles to the end of the road and the campground.

payload.name: Route 66 State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: These are day-use picnic shelters only, not overnight camping. Shelters are open for reservation year-round at $70 per day. Restrooms and water are available seasonally from April 1 through October 31. Park gates close one-half hour after sunset.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelters at Route 66 State Park along the historic highway corridor near Eureka, Missouri. Not an overnight camping facility.
payload.medium_description: Route 66 State Park offers two reservable day-use picnic shelters, Forest and Dogwood, each accommodating up to 100 people. Located along the historic Route 66 corridor near Eureka, the shelters include electricity with restrooms and water nearby. These are day-use facilities only; no overnight camping is available at this park.
payload.long_description:
Route 66 State Park Shelters are day-use picnic facilities, not overnight campgrounds. The park, located on the site of former Times Beach along the historic Route 66 corridor, offers two reservable shelters: Forest and Dogwood. Each shelter accommodates up to 100 people and includes electricity, with restrooms and water available nearby from April 1 through October 31.

The 424-acre park features hiking and cycling trails, a boat ramp on the Meramec River, and a visitor center housed in the historic 1935 Bridgehead Inn with Route 66 exhibits. Both shelters are ADA accessible and can be reserved for $70 per day through the Missouri State Parks reservation system.

Note that this is strictly a day-use facility. The park gates close one-half hour after sunset daily. For overnight camping in the area, visitors should consider nearby Robertsville State Park or private campgrounds along the Route 66 corridor.

location.directions: Route 66 State Park is located approximately 1 mile east of Eureka, Missouri. From eastbound Interstate 44, take exit 265 to access the park. The visitor center is accessible from either direction at exit 266.

links.title: Route 66 State Park - Missouri State Parks

payload.name: Massacre Rocks State Park
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. The Upper Loop and cabins typically remain available year-round. Reservations can be made online at getoutside.idaho.gov or by calling 1-888-922-6743.
payload.short_description: Historic state park campground along the Snake River featuring 42 electric sites, modern amenities, disc golf, and Oregon Trail history in southeast Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Massacre Rocks State Park offers 42 serviced campsites and 4 cabins along the Snake River in southeast Idaho. The park features flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, and electric hookups. Named for its dramatic volcanic rock formations, the park preserves Oregon Trail wagon ruts and offers hiking trails, world-class disc golf, and excellent bird watching opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Massacre Rocks State Park sits on the banks of the Snake River where dramatic volcanic rock formations once funneled Oregon Trail emigrants through a narrow passage. The 42-site campground features electric hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, and a dump station. Four heated and air-conditioned cabins sleep up to five guests each with outdoor fire pits and grills. The park has one ADA-accessible campsite and one ADA cabin.

Beyond camping, the park offers miles of hiking trails through sagebrush steppe habitat rich with bird species, access to historic Oregon Trail wagon ruts, and one of Idaho's most challenging disc golf courses. A visitor center and museum provide interpretive exhibits about the area's geology and pioneer history. Firewood is available for purchase on-site.

The park operates year-round with the Upper Loop and cabins available during winter months. Day-use hours are 7 AM to 10 PM. Pets are welcome on a 6-foot leash throughout the park.

location.directions: Located 10 miles west of American Falls on Interstate 86. Use street address 3592 N. Park Lane, American Falls, ID 83211 for GPS navigation.

address.full: American Falls, ID, 83211, USA Massacre Rocks State Park, American Falls, ID 83211

payload.name: Elks Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through late October. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect across Coconino National Forest as of May 21, 2026; campfires are permitted within the designated fire ring. The facility has a locked gate with combination provided in the Recreation.gov confirmation email.
payload.short_description: Large group campground in Coconino National Forest accommodating up to 300 people among ponderosa pines and juniper at 6,500 feet elevation, featuring a pavilion, fire ring, and recreational amenities.
payload.medium_description: Elks Group Campground sits among ponderosa pines and juniper on the Mogollon Rim at 6,500 feet elevation. Built and donated by the Winslow Elks Lodge, this fenced 6-acre facility can host groups of up to 300 people with a large pavilion, metal fire ring, horseshoe court, volleyball net poles, and swing set. Vault toilets and potable water from a 500-gallon tank are provided; groups over 50 must supply additional portable toilets.
payload.long_description:
Elks Group Campground occupies a transition zone where ponderosa pines fade into pinyon-juniper woodlands on the Mogollon Rim Ranger District. Originally constructed and donated by the Winslow Elks Lodge, the facility spans 6 fenced acres at 6,496 feet and can accommodate groups ranging from 10 to 300 people with parking for up to 50 vehicles.

The campground includes a large pavilion, metal fire ring, picnic tables, grills, horseshoe pit, volleyball net poles, small swing set, and flagpole. Vault toilets and a 500-gallon water buffalo provide basic services. Groups exceeding 50 people must bring additional portable toilets. RVs and trailers up to 45 feet are permitted, though no hookups exist.

Nearby recreational opportunities include C.C. Cragin Reservoir and Knoll Lake for fishing and water activities, plus the Arizona National Scenic Trail, General Crook National Recreation Trail, and Cabin Loop Trail System for hiking, biking, and horseback riding. The community of Happy Jack offers convenience stores, restaurants, and fuel.

location.directions: From Flagstaff, drive 55 miles south on Lake Mary Road (FH 3) to AZ 87 at Clints Well. Turn left onto AZ 87 and drive approximately 20 miles to milepost 309.9. Turn left on FR 9717H and drive about one quarter mile to the campground. From Winslow, drive south on AZ 87 for approximately 32 miles, then turn right on FR 9717H. Do not use Apple Maps; Google Maps will navigate to the correct location.

payload.name: Windy Point Group
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 20, 2026 and operates through early October. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov up to 12 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Group campground on Dillon Reservoir at 9,000 ft elevation in White River National Forest, with two reservable sites accommodating up to 100 people each.
payload.medium_description: Windy Point Group Campground sits at 9,000 feet on the shores of Dillon Reservoir in Summit County, Colorado. The campground features two group sites: a Forest Loop standard area and a Lake Loop with a 2,600 square foot covered pavilion. Both sites accommodate up to 100 people and offer views of the Tenmile Range and Gore Range. Due to pine beetle mitigation, there is little to no shade remaining.
payload.long_description:
Windy Point Group Campground is located on Dillon Reservoir in the heart of Summit County between Keystone and Breckenridge on Swan Mountain Road. At 9,000 feet elevation in the White River National Forest, the campground offers dramatic views of the Gore Range, Tenmile Range, and the reservoir itself.

The facility consists of two distinct group sites. The Forest Loop is a standard group area with fire rings, grills, and gathering tables on a grassy overlook. The Lake Loop features a 2,600 square foot covered pavilion on a concrete pad with multiple serving tables, tall gathering tables, and large grills. Both sites accommodate tents, trailers, and RVs up to 45 feet on hardened gravel surfaces and can host groups of up to 100 people.

Dillon Reservoir offers fishing for rainbow, brown, and cutthroat trout, along with motorized and non-motorized boating. Water contact activities including swimming, water skiing, and scuba diving are prohibited. Nearby attractions include over 7 miles of paved Summit County trails and proximity to Arapahoe Basin, Keystone, Breckenridge, and Copper Mountain ski resorts.

location.directions: From I-70, take the Silverthorne exit 205. Travel east on Highway 6 approximately 4 miles to Swan Mountain Road. Proceed 2 miles to Swan Mountain Recreation Area. Take dirt road to campground.

Just a short hike from Windy Point Campground

payload.name: Jane's Reservoir Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally, typically mid-May through late October depending on weather. First-come, first-served; no reservations or fees. No potable water available; bring your own. Pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground on the shores of Jane's Reservoir in northern Modoc National Forest, offering solitude, fishing, and boating access about 30 miles north of Alturas.
payload.medium_description: Jane's Reservoir Campground is a free, primitive campground situated along the southeastern edge of Jane's Reservoir in the Devil's Garden Ranger District of Modoc National Forest. The remote location, accessible via Crowder Flat Road, offers light usage and true solitude. A dirt boat ramp provides lake access just north of the campground entrance. No potable water or garbage service is provided.
payload.long_description:
Jane's Reservoir Campground sits along the southeastern shore of its namesake reservoir in the remote Devil's Garden Ranger District of Modoc National Forest. Located approximately 30 miles north of Alturas via Crowder Flat Road, the campground is known for its solitude and natural beauty. The reservoir supports fishing, and a dirt boat ramp north of the campground entrance provides easy lake access.

This is a primitive, no-fee campground with minimal facilities. Two vault toilets serve the area, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Garbage service is not provided; visitors must pack out all trash including fish guts. Each site has a picnic table. The campground operates seasonally, typically from mid-May through late October depending on weather conditions.

The area is suitable for those seeking a quiet, undeveloped camping experience. Dogs are permitted on leash. The 14-day stay limit applies. Light usage levels mean campsites are generally available on a first-come, first-served basis without reservations.

location.directions: From Alturas, travel west on Highway 299 for 3 miles. Turn north on Crowder Flat Road (County Road 73) and travel approximately 29 miles to the Jane's Reservoir turnoff on the left.

payload.name: Medeiros Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations. Park hours are 6:00 a.m. to sunset daily.
payload.short_description: Primitive first-come, first-served campground along the southern shoreline of O'Neill Forebay, offering basic amenities and fishing access at San Luis Reservoir State Recreation Area.
payload.medium_description: Medeiros Campground is a primitive camping area situated along the southern shoreline of O'Neill Forebay at San Luis Reservoir State Recreation Area. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with limited sites featuring fire rings, shade ramadas, and picnic tables. Drinking water is available at three locations, and chemical toilets are provided. Campers at Medeiros have the unique privilege of fishing after sunset.
payload.long_description:
Medeiros Campground offers a primitive camping experience on the southern shoreline of O'Neill Forebay, part of the larger San Luis Reservoir State Recreation Area in California's Central Valley. This first-come, first-served campground provides basic amenities including a limited number of fire rings, shade ramadas, and picnic tables distributed among the sites. Drinking water is available at three locations throughout the campground, and chemical toilets serve campers' needs.

The campground provides direct access to O'Neill Forebay, where boating, fishing, and windsurfing are popular activities. Medeiros campers enjoy the exclusive benefit of being able to fish after sunset, unlike day visitors. A boat ramp is located nearby for water access. The area is known for being very windy, with conditions that can change suddenly, so campers should be prepared.

Three accessible campsites are available with accessible restrooms. Dogs are allowed in the campground but must remain on a leash and under immediate control at all times. The park is open from 6:00 a.m. to sunset daily.

location.directions: On Highway 152, 7 miles west of I-5, or 33 miles east of Highway 101 from Gilroy. Park headquarters located at 31426 Gonzaga Road, Gustine, CA 95322.

links.title: San Luis Reservoir SRA Main Page

payload.name: Two Rivers
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservation required for all sites through Recreation.gov. Full amenities including flush toilets, showers, potable water, and camp store operate April 15 through October 15. Winter camping available October 16 through April 14 with vault toilet only and reduced fees. 14-day stay limit per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Developed campground at the confluence of the Current and Jacks Fork rivers in Ozark National Scenic Riverways, offering excellent river access for canoeing, swimming, and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Two Rivers Campground sits where the Jacks Fork meets the Current River, providing direct access to over 130 miles of spring-fed waterways. The 22-site campground offers standard sites, walk-in tent sites, and cluster sites for groups. Modern restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers operate from mid-April through mid-October, with a vault toilet available year-round. All sites require reservations through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Two Rivers Campground occupies a prime location at the confluence of two of Missouri's most scenic spring-fed rivers: the Current and Jacks Fork. Part of Ozark National Scenic Riverways, America's first national park protecting a wild river system, the campground provides immediate access to crystal-clear waters ideal for canoeing, kayaking, tubing, swimming, and fishing.

The campground offers 22 sites divided among standard family sites (accommodating two tents or one RV and one tent), walk-in tent-only sites, and two cluster sites for larger groups of up to 20 people with six tents maximum. Each site includes a fire ring, grill, and picnic table. Flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and a seasonal camp store operate from April 15 through October 15. A vault toilet near the boat launch remains available year-round. No hookups are available.

Nearby attractions include the historic Alley Mill at Alley Spring and Round Spring Cave, both offering ranger-led tours during summer months. Multiple hiking and horseback trails traverse the surrounding Ozark forest, including segments of the Ozark Trail.

location.directions: From Eminence, take Highway 106 East to V Highway. Turn left on Highway V, which ends at the Two Rivers Campground and river access.

photos.name: The confluence of the Current and Jacks Fork rivers, now known as Two Rivers, was historically called the Junction.
Tree lined banks of the Two Rivers in late summer.
