alerts.title: Round Spring - September Paving Work
alerts.content: Paving work will be done in the Round Spring area throughout the month of September. Currently, the parking area at the pavilion is closed. Closure of the electric sites (E1-E6) in the campground will begin Monday, 9/8.

alerts.title: Peavine Road Closed
alerts.content: Peavine Road near Big Spring will be closed for paving beginning 7/28 at noon and will remain closed for several weeks. Please use Highway 103 to reach all destinations in the Big Spring area.

alerts.title: Campground Closures
alerts.content: The following campgrounds are closed pending repairs: Pulltite (sites 1-13) and Dee Murray. Day use areas remain open for visitors.

alerts.title: Pulltite Campground Partial Closure
alerts.content: Sites 1-13 remain closed. All other sites are open. Sites are available by reservation only - book online at https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234357

alerts.title: Reservations Required for Developed Campgrounds
alerts.content: As of January 1, 2025, ALL developed campsites will be available through reservation ONLY. These include Pulltite, Round Spring, Alley Spring, Big Spring, Two Rivers, and Akers. Reservations must be made through recreation.gov (online or by calling).

alerts.title: River Ferry at Akers (on State Highway K) CLOSED until further notice
alerts.content: The Akers Ferry on State Highway K will not be in service until further notice.

alerts.title: Scan & Pay Required for Backcountry Campgrounds
alerts.content: Starting April 15, 2025, "backcountry" campgrounds will only accept payment through Scan & Pay, on the recreation.gov mobile app. While the app works offline, visitors should download the app and set up their account beforehand. Cell service is limited.

payload.name: Big Oaks
payload.status_description: This is a day-use area only; no overnight camping is allowed. The area is open year-round. The picnic shelter is available for reservation from April 1 through September 30.
payload.short_description: Big Oaks is a day-use recreation area on Hartwell Lake featuring a boat ramp, picnic shelter, comfort station, playground, and access to a 2.75-mile paved trail atop Hartwell Dam.
payload.medium_description: Big Oaks Recreation Area is a 12-acre day-use facility on Hartwell Lake managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. No overnight camping is allowed. The site offers a reservable picnic shelter, 26 picnic sites, a two-lane boat ramp with courtesy dock, comfort station, playground, and access to a paved walking and biking trail along Hartwell Dam's Georgia embankment.
payload.long_description:
Big Oaks Recreation Area is a popular 12-acre day-use facility located on Hartwell Lake near Hartwell, Georgia, operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The gently sloping site features good grass cover and scattered pine and hardwood trees. No overnight camping is permitted at this location.

The area provides a large reservable picnic shelter with water and electric service, 26 individual picnic sites, a two-lane boat ramp with a courtesy dock, a comfort station, and a playground. Boat launching costs $7 per vehicle. The shelter is available for reservation from April 1 through September 30.

Big Oaks serves as the access point to a 2.75-mile paved walking and bicycling trail located atop the Georgia earthen embankment of Hartwell Dam. The site hosts numerous large special events annually, including the Hartwell Dam Run and Pre-Fourth Fireworks celebration.

location.directions: From Hartwell, GA, take Highway 29 North towards Anderson, SC for about 5 miles. Big Oaks is located on the left next to the Hartwell Visitor Center and Manager's Office. Address: 5823 Dam Road, Hartwell, GA 30643.

photos.name: Big Oaks Shelter.  Shelter reservation includes use of the two large and one small shelter.
A photo of facility BIG OAKS with Boat Ramp, Picnic Table

payload.name: Twin Eagle
payload.status_description: Open seasonally mid-May to mid-October, weather dependent. No reservations; all sites are first-come, first-served. Maximum 14 consecutive night stay. No potable water or trash service available.
payload.short_description: Remote 9-site first-come, first-served campground at 8,600 ft in Pike National Forest, offering vault toilets, fire rings, and tables with access to Lost Creek Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Twin Eagles Campground sits at 8,600 feet elevation in Pike National Forest, 14 miles north of Lake George via County Road 77. The small campground has nine sites, some walk-in/hike-in, and provides direct access to Lost Creek Wilderness via the Brookside-McCurdy Trail. Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings. No water or trash service; campers must pack out all garbage and bring drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Twin Eagles Campground is a quiet, primitive campground located at 8,600 feet in the Pike National Forest near Tarryall Reservoir. The campground features nine campsites, some of which are walk-in or hike-in, making it ideal for tenters and those seeking a more secluded experience. Maximum trailer length is 22 feet. The campground is strictly first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted.

Facilities are basic: vault toilets, picnic tables at each site, and fire rings. There is no potable water available, and campers must pack out all trash. Bears are common in the area, so proper food storage is essential. Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

The campground provides access to the Lost Creek Wilderness via the Twin Eagles Trailhead, which connects to the Brookside-McCurdy Trail. This makes it a popular basecamp for hikers exploring the wilderness area. The surrounding landscape features granite domes, forested slopes, and the characteristic terrain of Colorado's Front Range.

location.directions: From Lake George, travel west on Highway 24 and turn right on County Road 77 toward Tarryall Reservoir. Travel about 14 miles north on County Road 77; the campground will be on your right.

payload.name: Jewell Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 3 through October 31. Sites are $15 per night. Senior/Access Pass holders receive 50% discount.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on 193-acre Jewell Lake in Huron National Forest offering fishing, boating, and swimming with vault toilets and hand-pump water.
payload.medium_description: Jewell Lake Campground is situated on the east shore of the scenic 193-acre Jewell Lake in Michigan's Huron National Forest. The campground provides access to excellent fishing and boating opportunities, with both motorized and non-motorized watercraft permitted. Facilities include vault toilets and potable water from a hand pump. A snowmobile trail runs through the area during winter months.
payload.long_description:
Jewell Lake Campground occupies a prime location on the eastern shore of Jewell Lake, a 193-acre lake in Michigan's Huron National Forest within Alcona County. The lake supports a variety of fish species and permits both motorized and non-motorized boating, making it a destination for anglers and paddlers alike. Swimming is also available.

The developed campground features vault toilets and potable drinking water available from a hand pump. Sites are $15 per night, with Interagency Senior/Access Pass holders receiving a 50% discount. The campground operates seasonally from early May through the end of October.

During winter months, a snowmobile trail passes through the recreation area, extending the site's usefulness beyond the camping season for winter recreation enthusiasts.

location.directions: From Harrisville, travel west on M-72 for 14.5 miles. Turn right and travel north on Sanborn Rd for 2 miles. Turn left and travel west on FR 4601 for 0.5 miles.

payload.name: Keyhole State Park Pronghorn Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservation season runs May 15 through September 15 via Reserve.Wyoming.gov. First-come, first-served outside this window. Restrooms and drinking water systems close October 1 through April 30, though the grounds remain open year-round weather permitting.
payload.short_description: Pronghorn Campground offers 36 shaded campsites nestled among pine trees at Keyhole State Park on the western edge of the Black Hills, featuring fire rings, picnic tables, and access to the 14,720-acre reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Pronghorn Campground at Keyhole State Park provides 36 campsites set among pine trees overlooking Keyhole Reservoir. Sites include fire rings, picnic tables, and water hydrants throughout. The campground features a universally accessible playground and two ADA-compliant sites with cement pads. No hookups are available at Pronghorn; those seeking electric and water hookups should book at Tatanka Campground instead.
payload.long_description:
Pronghorn Campground sits within Keyhole State Park on the western edge of Wyoming's Black Hills, between Sundance and Moorcroft at 4,100 feet elevation. The campground offers 36 sites nestled among pine trees, with most being back-in configurations and a few pull-throughs available. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with water hydrants and restrooms spaced throughout. Two sites feature cement pads for universal accessibility, and a large accessible playground is available for children.

Keyhole Reservoir provides 14,720 acres of water recreation with excellent fishing for walleye, catfish, smallmouth bass, and northern pike. The park serves as a haven for resident and migrating bird species. Park-wide amenities include a dump station at the main entrance, coin-operated showers at the shower house near Tatanka Campground, and seasonal boat docks and fish cleaning stations. Note that Pronghorn Campground does not have electric or water hookups; campers requiring hookups should reserve sites at Tatanka Campground.

location.directions: From I-90, take exit 165. The park entrance is located between Sundance and Moorcroft. Address: 22 Marina Rd, Moorcroft, WY 82721.

payload.name: Jack Pine State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservations available through the Michigan DNR reservation system at midnrreservations.com. Sites book quickly for summer and holiday weekends.
payload.short_description: Rustic 10-site hike-in campground nestled among dunes and jack pines at Ludington State Park, offering secluded tent camping just steps from Lake Michigan.
payload.medium_description: Jack Pine is a primitive walk-in campground within Ludington State Park featuring 10 secluded tent sites accessible via a 1-mile hike or bike ride from the designated parking area behind park headquarters. Sites are tucked among dunes and jack pines with Lake Michigan shoreline steps away. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table, with vault toilets and a hand pump for water nearby. Firewood delivery to sites is available in the evenings.
payload.long_description:
Jack Pine Campground offers a backcountry-style experience without venturing deep into the wilderness. Located within Ludington State Park in Mason County, Michigan, this rustic 10-site walk-in campground requires a roughly 1-mile hike or bike ride from the parking area behind park headquarters. The trail follows the same sand-and-gravel path leading to Big Sable Point Lighthouse, making it an excellent staging point for lighthouse visits.

Sites are scattered among jack pine trees and dune ridges, providing natural privacy and shade while keeping Lake Michigan's shoreline just a short walk away. The campground operates on a pack-in/pack-out mentality with minimal infrastructure: vault toilets, a hand pump for potable water, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site. No electricity is available. Showers can be accessed at the nearby Pines modern campground during its operating season.

This campground works well as an introductory backpacking destination for families with children given the manageable 1-mile distance. Reservations are available through the Michigan DNR system six months in advance and fill quickly for summer weekends.

location.directions: From Ludington, head north on M-116 for approximately 8 miles to Ludington State Park entrance. Jack Pine campers park in the designated area behind park headquarters, then hike approximately 1 mile north on the lighthouse trail to reach the campground.

payload.name: Spring Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates seasonally beginning March 1. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own water supply.
payload.short_description: Primitive riverside campground with 5 developed sites on the Wild and Scenic Salmon River in Idaho's Salmon-Challis National Forest, offering fishing, rafting access, and backcountry exploration.
payload.medium_description: Spring Creek Campground sits along the Wild and Scenic Salmon River, upstream from its confluence with the Wild and Scenic Middle Fork. The campground offers 5 developed campsites plus numerous undeveloped sites, making it a popular base for anglers targeting cutthroat and rainbow trout, steelhead, and whitefish. A boat ramp provides put-in access for a 10-mile Class III rafting run to Cove Creek.
payload.long_description:
Spring Creek Campground is a rustic riverside campground located on the Wild and Scenic Salmon River in Idaho's Salmon-Challis National Forest. Positioned upstream from the confluence with the Wild and Scenic Middle Fork, the area offers exceptional scenery and direct river access. The campground features 5 developed campsites along with numerous undeveloped sites for those seeking a more dispersed experience.

The surrounding area is webbed with dirt roads, jeep trails, and single-track trails, making it easy to explore the rugged backcountry. Fishing opportunities abound in the Salmon River, with cutthroat and rainbow trout, steelhead, and whitefish all present. The campground also serves as a put-in point for a popular 10-mile rafting section featuring Class III rapids, with take-out at Cove Creek downstream.

Facilities are basic, with vault toilets available but no potable water on site. Campers should come prepared with their own water supply. The campground is accessed via Forest Road 030, approximately 18 miles west of North Fork.

location.directions: From North Fork, go 18 miles west on Forest Road 030 (Salmon River Road).

address.full: 1410 Salmon River Rd, North Fork, ID 83466

payload.name: Borrego Mesa
payload.status_description: The campground is open. The vault toilet is currently not in service. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through September 30, 2026, permitting fires only in designated fire rings. No potable water is available.
payload.short_description: A primitive, lightly-used equestrian campground near the Pecos Wilderness with horse corrals at each site, ideal for overnight stays before backcountry trips.
payload.medium_description: Borrego Mesa Campground is a primitive, lightly-used site in Santa Fe National Forest, primarily serving equestrians and backpackers heading into the Pecos Wilderness. Each site features a picnic table, fire pit, and small corral suitable for one or two horses. Adjacent to the Rio Medio Trailhead, it offers easy access to the north half of the Pecos Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Borrego Mesa Campground sits on the edge of the Pecos Wilderness in Santa Fe National Forest, offering a quiet, primitive camping experience. The campground is designed with equestrians in mind, featuring small corrals at each site that can accommodate one or two horses. Picnic tables and fire pits are provided at every site.

The campground is adjacent to the Rio Medio Trailhead, one of the major access points to the northern Pecos Wilderness. It sees light use and serves primarily as an overnight staging area for horsepacking and backpacking trips, though locals also use it for day picnicking. The setting is rustic and undeveloped compared to most Forest Service campgrounds.

No potable water is available, and the vault toilet is currently not in service. Campers should come fully self-sufficient with water and sanitation supplies. There is ample space for trailers and RVs, but no hookups or dump station are provided.

location.directions: Twenty miles east of Española, NM. Take State Road 503 out of Pojoaque through Nambe and Cundiyo. Just past the turnoff to Santa Cruz Lake, turn right onto Forest Road 306. After nine miles, turn right onto Forest Road 435 into the campground.

payload.name: REDBUD - BELL SMITH SPRINGS
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates March 15 through December 15 annually. Sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Payment is cash or check only.
payload.short_description: Primitive forest campground at Bell Smith Springs Recreation Area in Shawnee National Forest, featuring scenic canyons, sandstone cliffs, and eight miles of interconnected hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Redbud Campground sits within Bell Smith Springs Recreation Area, one of the most beautiful areas in Shawnee National Forest. The surrounding landscape features clear rocky streams, scenic canyons, high sandstone cliffs, and unique rock formations including Devil's Backbone, Boulder Falls, and a natural rock bridge. The campground offers a primitive camping experience with vault toilets and potable water, ideal for hikers exploring the eight miles of interconnected trails.
payload.long_description:
Redbud Campground is located within Bell Smith Springs Recreation Area in southern Illinois's Shawnee National Forest. This area is renowned for its striking geological features: clear, rocky streams wind through scenic canyons bordered by towering sandstone cliffs and lush vegetation unique to Illinois. The eight-mile trail system connects hikers to remarkable formations such as Devil's Backbone, Boulder Falls, and a natural rock bridge.

The campground operates seasonally from March 15 through December 15, offering a primitive camping experience at $10 per night. Sites accommodate up to 8 people and 2 vehicles, with payment accepted by cash or check only. Amenities include vault toilets and potable water. Campers must pack out their trash. Pets are welcome but must be kept on leash, and glass containers are prohibited outside the campground area.

Bell Smith Springs is managed by the Hidden Springs Ranger District. The recreation area's trail system remains open year-round, though camping in the designated Natural Area is prohibited. This campground is best suited for tent campers and those with smaller vehicles seeking an immersive experience in one of Illinois's most scenic natural areas.

location.directions: From Harrisburg, take Highway 145 south 11 miles to Burden Falls Road, turn right, go 5 miles to Ozark Road, turn south (left), go to Bell Smith Springs Road, turn southwest (right) and proceed 2 miles to Bell Smith Springs.

links.title: Bell Smith Springs Recreation Area - USFS

payload.name: Horseshoe Point
payload.status_description: Open seasonally May 1 through September 30. Park gates are closed 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. No alcohol permitted.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on Philpott Lake in Virginia's Blue Ridge foothills with electric/water hookup sites and primitive camping, plus beach access and boat ramp.
payload.medium_description: Horseshoe Point Campground sits on the shores of Philpott Lake in Franklin County, Virginia, offering 49 campsites including 15 with electric and water hookups and 34 primitive sites. The campground features flush toilets, hot showers, drinking water, and a dump station. A swimming beach, boat ramp, dock, picnic shelter, and playground round out the amenities. The lake provides excellent fishing for bass, walleye, bluegill, crappie, and catfish.
payload.long_description:
Horseshoe Point Campground is nestled on the shores of Philpott Lake in the rugged foothills of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. Located in a rural and sparsely populated part of Franklin County near the small community of Henry, this US Army Corps of Engineers facility provides a peaceful retreat with 49 campsites. Fifteen sites offer electric (50 amp) and water hookups, while 34 primitive sites cater to those seeking a more rustic experience.

Philpott Lake covers 2,900 acres with 100 miles of shoreline. The lake's steep, rocky banks meet beautiful mixed forests of oak, maple, hickory, pine, and cedar. Wildlife is abundant: deer, turkeys, squirrels, raccoons, and a variety of songbirds and waterfowl are commonly seen. The clear water and natural shoreline make it ideal for boating, swimming, and fishing for largemouth and smallmouth bass, walleye, bluegill, crappie, and catfish.

The campground includes a swimming beach, boat ramp, dock, picnic shelter, and playground. Many miles of hiking and biking trails surround the lake. The adjacent Fairystone State Park and Fairystone Farms Wildlife Management Area add over 5,300 acres of public recreational lands to explore.

location.directions: From HWY 220, turn onto Henry Road (SR-605) and go 8 miles. Turn left onto Horseshoe Point Road and follow signs to the park.

photos.name: Campsite with picnic table, and lantern post.
Campsite parking spur with steps to camping area.
Horseshoe Point beach and swim area.

payload.name: Beauty Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open late May through mid-September. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. 14-day stay limit per 30-day period. Bears frequent the area; approved food storage containers required.
payload.short_description: Peaceful creekside campground a half mile from Lake Coeur d'Alene with vault toilets, drinking water, and direct access to the Caribou Ridge National Recreation Trail.
payload.medium_description: Beauty Creek Campground sits in a narrow valley along Beauty Creek in Idaho's Panhandle National Forests. The 18-site campground offers vault toilets, drinking water from a hand pump, and paved parking aprons. The trailhead for the 5-mile Caribou Ridge National Recreation Trail starts at the campground, featuring overlooks of Lake Coeur d'Alene.
payload.long_description:
Beauty Creek Campground is located a half mile from Lake Coeur d'Alene along the peaceful Beauty Creek in northern Idaho. At an elevation of 2,100 feet, it sits in a sparsely wooded valley surrounded by heavily wooded hillsides in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests, between the Cascade Mountains to the west and the Bitterroot Mountains to the east.

The campground offers 18 single sites and one 35-person group site with vault toilets, drinking water from a hand pump, and paved parking aprons. The trailhead for the Caribou Ridge National Recreation Trail starts right at the campground. This 5-mile trail features a moderate climb with two outstanding overlooks of Lake Coeur d'Alene. Additional trails include the 1.8-mile Beauty Creek Overlook and the 4.9-mile Mt. Coeur d'Alene Viewpoint.

Lake Coeur d'Alene offers excellent boating, fishing, and canoeing. The nearest boat ramp is at Mineral Ridge, less than a mile from the campground. Anglers can pursue northern pike, chinook salmon, and bass in the area. Note that bears frequent this area and approved food storage containers are required.

location.directions: From Coeur d'Alene, go east on I-90 to exit 22, then turn south on ID-97. Drive 2.5 miles to Forest Road 438 and turn left. Go one mile and look for signs.

address.full: 9313 E Fs Rd 1575, Coeur D Alene, ID 83814

links.title: USFS Idaho Panhandle NF - Beauty Creek

photos.name: Seasonally dry Beauty Creek with standing stones.

payload.name: Himes Peak Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens late June and closes in early fall, depending on snow conditions. No reservations; all sites are first-come, first-served. Water availability is variable; bring your own supply.
payload.short_description: Remote 11-site Forest Service campground at 9,000 ft elevation near Trappers Lake, offering direct access to Big Fish Trail and the Flat Tops Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Himes Peak Campground is a small, primitive Forest Service campground with 11 sites located 46 miles east of Meeker in the White River National Forest. The campground provides direct access to Big Fish Trail #1819 and serves as a gateway to the Flat Tops Wilderness. Fishing is available at nearby Rainbow Lake and Big Fish Lake, and elk hunting is productive in season.
payload.long_description:
Himes Peak Campground sits at approximately 9,000 feet elevation in the Blanco Ranger District of the White River National Forest, about 6 miles north of Trappers Lake. This small, first-come, first-served campground offers 11 sites in a remote high-country setting surrounded by spruce-fir forest.

The campground serves as a trailhead for Big Fish Trail #1819, providing direct access to the Flat Tops Wilderness for day hikes or extended backcountry trips. Rainbow Lake and Big Fish Lake are nearby and offer good fishing for native cutthroat trout. The area is known for productive elk hunting in season.

Facilities are primitive: vault toilets are available but potable water is not reliable. Campers should bring their own water supply. The campground operates seasonally, typically opening in late June after snowmelt and closing in early fall. Due to the remote location and single-lane forest roads, this campground is best suited for tents and smaller camping vehicles.

location.directions: From Meeker, travel east on Colorado Highway 13 for 1 mile, then turn right (east) on Rio Blanco County Road 8 and continue for 39 miles. Turn south on Trappers Lake Road (Forest Road 205) and continue 6 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Wolf Ford Horse Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates seasonally from March 23 through November 15. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov; walk-up reservations are not available. Access is gated with a combination code provided upon reservation. Yellow Gap Road (FSR 1206) is subject to weather-related closures; all reservations are refunded if the road is administratively closed.
payload.short_description: Equestrian-only horse camp in Pisgah National Forest offering 11-12 sites with vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and access to over 100 miles of multi-use trails near Brevard, NC.
payload.medium_description: Wolf Ford Horse Camp is a reservation-only equestrian campground in the Pisgah Ranger District of Pisgah National Forest, located 3.2 miles down Yellow Gap Road (FSR 1206). The campground features 11-12 non-electric sites designed specifically for horse camping, with vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, hitching racks, and lantern posts. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. The site provides direct access to over 100 miles of equestrian trails in the South Mills River area.
payload.long_description:
Wolf Ford Horse Camp is a reservation-only equestrian campground nestled in the Pisgah Ranger District of Pisgah National Forest, approximately 3.2 miles down Yellow Gap Road (gravel Forest Service Road 1206) near Brevard, North Carolina. The campground is specifically designed for horse camping and offers 11-12 non-electric sites, each equipped with fire rings, picnic tables, hitching racks, and lantern posts. A vault toilet is available on-site, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring adequate supplies.

The campground serves as an excellent launching point for exploring over 100 miles of equestrian trails in the South Mills River area, along with numerous Forest Service roads suitable for riding. The surrounding landscape features the confluence of several creeks and the South Fork of the Mills River, with abundant wildlife including various bird species and black bears. Large shade trees including maples, oaks, poplars, birches, and pines provide cover throughout the camp.

Nearby attractions include the Cradle of Forestry (America's first forestry school), the Blue Ridge Parkway, Pisgah Inn, the NC Wildlife Education Center and Fish Hatchery, DuPont State Forest, and the town of Brevard. This is bear country, so all food, cookware, and trash must be secured in vehicles when unattended. Campers are required to clean up after their horses, including manure and hay. A dumpster is available 4 miles away at Pink Beds Picnic Area.

location.directions: From the intersection of US-280/US-64 West, turn onto US-276 North. Go 11.7 miles, then turn right onto Yellow Gap Road (Forest Service Road 1206), an unpaved gravel road. Go 3.3 miles, then turn right onto South Mills River Road (Forest Service Road 475). Wolf Ford Horse Camp is immediately on your left.

address.full: 59 Wolf Ford Horse Camp Rd, Pisgah Forest, NC 28768

payload.name: Park Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May through September. Sites are available through Recreation.gov reservations and first-come, first-served. Check-in is 2:00 p.m. and check-out is 12:00 p.m. Fire restrictions may be imposed during dry conditions.
payload.short_description: A small 12-site primitive campground along Park Creek in the Baker Lake basin, offering easy access to hiking, fishing, and old-growth forest exploration in Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Park Creek Campground sits along the banks of Park Creek in the stunning Baker Lake basin. The campground offers 12 sites (11 standard and 1 tent-only) in an old-growth forested setting. Sites include picnic tables, campfire rings with grills, and vault toilets. No potable water is available; the closest water source is at Swift Creek Campground nearby. Both reservations and first-come, first-served availability are offered.
payload.long_description:
Park Creek Campground is nestled along the banks of Park Creek in the spectacular Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. The campground's old-growth forest setting provides a serene atmosphere with towering Douglas fir and cedar trees creating a canopy overhead. Baker Lake is close by, offering excellent fishing and boating opportunities, while numerous hiking trails and climbing routes are within a short driving distance.

The campground features 12 sites total: 11 standard nonelectric sites accommodating both tent and RV camping, plus one tent-only site. Each site is equipped with a picnic table and campfire ring with grill. Vault toilets are provided, but this is a no-water facility. Campers must bring their own drinking water or obtain it from nearby Swift Creek Campground.

Nearby attractions include the Shadow of the Sentinels Trail, a barrier-free interpretive trail winding through a 500-year-old ancient forest, and the Baker Lake Trail, an easy family hike along the eastern shoreline. The area also serves as a basecamp for snowshoeing in winter months and provides access to the Mt. Baker National Recreation Area, Mt. Baker Wilderness, and North Cascades National Park.

location.directions: From Seattle, go north on I-5 to Burlington. Take Exit 230 onto State Highway 20. Pass the Mt. Baker Ranger District Office in Sedro-Woolley and follow State Route 20 east for 16 miles to milepost 82. Turn left (north) on Baker Lake Highway (Forest Service Road 11). Continue for approximately 18 miles to the sign for Park Creek Campground Road (Forest Service Road 1144). Turn left and travel less than 1/4 mile to access the campground.

payload.name: Sunrise Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens June 12 and operates through October 4. Reservations available via Recreation.gov with a minimum 5-day advance booking. Weekend stays require 2-night minimum; holiday weekends require 3 nights.
payload.short_description: Forested campground at 7,800 feet near Bear Lake Summit, offering 26 sites including two yurts, with vault toilets and drinking water in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Sunrise Campground sits at 7,800 feet elevation on Bear Lake Summit, just 6 miles west of Garden City and Bear Lake, Utah. The campground features 24 standard tent/RV sites and 2 yurts set among mixed conifers and aspens. Amenities include vault toilets, potable water, paved roads and spurs, with fire rings and picnic tables at each site. The nearby Limber Pine Trail leads to a 500-year-old limber pine.
payload.long_description:
Sunrise Campground occupies a scenic forested setting at 7,800 feet on Bear Lake Summit in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. Located 6 miles west of Garden City and Bear Lake, Utah, the campground sits in a mixed-growth conifer and aspen forest that provides partial shade and privacy between sites. Summer wildflowers are abundant throughout the area.

The campground offers 24 standard nonelectric sites and 2 yurts, all accessible via paved roads and parking spurs. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Vault toilets and potable drinking water are provided. Visitors should arrive with RV water tanks filled, as hooking up to spigots is prohibited.

Bear Lake, known for its striking turquoise color, is just 6 miles away and offers boating, water skiing, jet skiing, swimming, and scuba diving. The family-friendly Limber Pine Trail begins less than half a mile from camp and leads to a 500-year-old limber pine. Bear Lake Summit, one mile away, features picnic tables, interpretive displays, and panoramic views.

location.directions: From Garden City, UT, at the intersection of State Route 30 and US Route 89, take Route 89 south for 6.3 miles to the campground sign. Turn left at the sign into the campground. Alternatively from Logan, take Highway 89 east for 31 miles, then turn south onto FR102 and follow for 0.6 miles.

payload.name: Summersville Lake Shelters
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter facility, not an overnight campground. The four group shelters are available for reservation through Recreation.gov. Overnight camping is not available here; use nearby Battle Run Campground instead.
payload.short_description: Day-use group picnic shelters on the shores of West Virginia's largest lake, offering flush toilets and drinking water. No overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Summersville Lake Shelters consists of four large group picnic shelters available for day-use reservation near Summersville, West Virginia. Located on the shores of the state's largest lake, the shelters are ideal for parties and family gatherings. Overnight camping is not available here; campers should use nearby Battle Run Campground instead.
payload.long_description:
Summersville Lake Shelters is a day-use facility featuring four large group picnic shelters situated on the shores of Summersville Lake, West Virginia's largest lake at 2,700 acres. The shelters are located in two areas: three at Damsite Picnic Area (PS1, PS2, PS3) and one at Battle Run Recreation Area (PS4). All shelters are non-electric and designed for group gatherings, parties, and family functions.

The facility offers flush toilets and drinking water. Pets and livestock are not permitted. Vehicles cannot be driven directly to the shelters, and firewood must be purchased locally. No confetti is allowed.

This is not an overnight camping facility. Visitors seeking camping should reserve sites at the nearby Battle Run Campground, also managed through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Summersville, West Virginia, take Highway 19 south for 5 miles to the campground.

address.full: 2886 Summersville Lake Rd, Mount Nebo, WV 26679

payload.name: Middle Mountain Cabins
payload.status_description: Open April through November. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Check-in at 2:00 PM, check-out at 12:00 PM. Access code for the gated entrance and cabin locks provided by Greenbrier Ranger District after booking.
payload.short_description: Historic cabin complex in Monongahela National Forest with three rustic cabins, hand pump water, vault toilet, and fireplaces. Rented as a single unit for up to 10 guests near Laurel Fork South Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Middle Mountain Cabins offer a secluded retreat at 3,750 feet elevation on a grassy clearing surrounded by red spruce and yellow birch near the Laurel Fork South Wilderness. The complex includes a main cabin with kitchen facilities and two 1939-era sleeping cabins that once served as Forest Service bunk houses. While there is no electricity, the cabins feature fireplaces with supplied firewood, an outside hand pump for drinking water, and a vault toilet. A campfire ring, grill, and picnic table are available outside.
payload.long_description:
Middle Mountain Cabins occupy 3.5 acres in a small grassy opening near Camp Five Run in the Greenbrier Ranger District of Monongahela National Forest. At 3,750 feet elevation, the site is surrounded by red spruce and yellow birch and sits adjacent to the 11,839-acre Laurel Fork South Wilderness. The complex is rented as a single unit and consists of a main cabin plus two historic sleeping cabins built in 1939 that originally served as bunk houses for Forest Service employees.

The main cabin features a gas stove, kitchen cabinets, cooking utensils, a table with six chairs, two lounge chairs, one full-size bed, and a fireplace. Each sleeping cabin contains two sets of bunk beds and a fireplace. There is no electricity or running water inside; an outside hand pump provides drinking water and a vault toilet serves the site. Firewood is supplied but not guaranteed. Visitors must bring their own bedding, lanterns, flashlights, matches, and food.

Recreation opportunities include fishing on the Cheat, Glady Fork, Shavers Fork, and the Greenbrier River forks. The High Falls of Cheat Trail #345 offers a 2.9-mile hike to waterfalls, while the West Fork Rail Trail #312 follows an old railroad grade along the West Fork of the Greenbrier River. The Allegheny Trail #701 passes through the area spanning multiple ranger districts.

location.directions: From Elkins or Harman, drive east on State Route 33. Turn south (right) on Forest Route 14 at Wymer (14.6 miles east of Elkins). Continue south for 18.2 miles to the entrance road marked by a sign. From the south, turn onto FR 14 five miles east of Bartow and follow FR 14 north for 12 miles to the gated entrance. A gravel parking area accommodates up to 4 vehicles.

links.title: USFS Monongahela NF - Middle Mountain Cabins

payload.name: Arapaho Bay
payload.status_description: The campground is open. The Moraine and Roaring Fork loops are experiencing a temporary water outage; campers in these loops must bring all water needed and receive a 25% fee discount. Sites 1-7 remain open during winter with no fees or amenities; restrooms are locked and campers must be self-contained.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on Arapaho Bay at Lake Granby, offering 84 sites across three loops at 8,300 feet elevation with access to boating, fishing, and the Continental Divide Trail.
payload.medium_description: Arapaho Bay Campground sits on the eastern tip of Lake Granby in the Arapaho National Recreation Area at 8,300 feet elevation. The campground features 84 sites across three loops (Big Rock, Mora, Roaring Fork), each equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and tent pad. Vault toilets and drinking water are provided. Due to mountain pine beetle hazard tree removal, the campground offers little shade. Popular activities include boating, fishing for kokanee salmon and trout, and hiking trails including the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail.
payload.long_description:
Arapaho Bay Campground occupies a prime lakefront location on Arapaho Bay at the eastern end of Lake Granby, within the Arapaho National Recreation Area southeast of Grand Lake. At 8,300 feet elevation, the campground provides access to excellent recreational opportunities including boating, sailing, swimming, and fishing for kokanee salmon, rainbow, brown, mackinaw, and cutthroat trout.

The campground offers 84 single and double-family sites distributed across three loops: Big Rock, Mora, and Roaring Fork. Each site includes a picnic table, campfire ring, and tent pad. Vault toilets and drinking water from hand pumps are available. Due to extensive hazard tree removal following mountain pine beetle infestation, shade is limited throughout the campground. Afternoon thunderstorms are common during summer months.

Numerous trails are accessible from the campground, including the Roaring Fork Trail, Monarch Lake Trail, Cascade Creek Trail, and the East Shore Trail, which is part of the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail. Rocky Mountain National Park's west entrance lies just north of Grand Lake, offering additional hiking, wildlife viewing, and scenic driving opportunities.

location.directions: From the intersection of US Highways 40 and 34 in Granby, head north on Highway 34 for about 5 miles to County Road 6. Go east for 9 miles to the campground.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: The Moraine and Roaring Fork Loops are experiencing a temporary water outage. Please bring all the water you’ll need for your visit, including drinking water. Reservation holders will receive a 25% use fee discount while the water is off.

payload.name: LOOKOUT HILL
payload.status_description: No official information found for this campground on USFS or Recreation.gov. The site is located within Pike National Forest in the South Park Ranger District, but no current status, fees, or amenities could be confirmed from official sources.
payload.short_description: A remote campground located in Pike National Forest within Park County, Colorado, in the South Park Ranger District area.
payload.medium_description: Lookout Hill is a scenic high point within Prospect Park, Brooklyn, NY, featuring a wildflower meadow and restored woodlands, but has no evidence suggesting it is an official campground with camping amenities.
payload.long_description: There is no clear evidence that Lookout Hill within Prospect Park, Brooklyn, NY is a campground. The area is described as one of the park's highest points and features a wildflower meadow and woodlands under restoration, but there are no references to camping amenities or overnight stays. Prospect Park is a large urban park famous for its natural beauty and public recreation areas, and while it is managed by the Prospect Park Alliance, its main uses include hiking, picnicking, and outdoor events rather than camping. Visitors can enjoy restored woodlands and scenic overlooks, but should not expect traditional campground facilities here. If looking for nearby campgrounds, consider locations outside New York City where overnight camping is permitted as Prospect Park and Lookout Hill do not offer camping.

location.directions: Lookout Hill is located within Prospect Park in Brooklyn, New York. The hill can be accessed from inconspicuous pathways originating from the southeastern end of the park, between the lower lake and the Nethermead.

payload.name: Lake Shetek State Park Camper Cabins
payload.status_description: The camper cabins are open for the season. Reservations can be made online at reservemn.usedirect.com or by phone at 866-857-2757. Reservations open 120 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Four rustic camper cabins at Lake Shetek State Park in southwest Minnesota, featuring heated wood interiors, bunk beds, and lakeside views within an old-growth oak canopy.
payload.medium_description: Lake Shetek State Park offers four heated camper cabins in the Oak Woods Campground, each a cozy 12x16 foot one-room structure with wood interiors, bunk beds sleeping up to six, and a screened porch. Cabins include electricity, an outdoor picnic table, and fire ring. No indoor plumbing; seasonal restrooms, showers, and drinking water are nearby. Located in southwest Minnesota's prairie region, the park features a sandy swimming beach, fishing on Lake Shetek, and access to the Casey Jones State Trail.
payload.long_description:
Lake Shetek State Park, situated in Murray County in southwest Minnesota, is the largest lake in the region and offers four rustic camper cabins for overnight stays. These 12x16 foot one-room wooden cabins are nestled in the Oak Woods Campground under a canopy of old-growth oaks overlooking the lake. Each cabin features wood interiors with bunk beds and mattresses sleeping up to six guests, a table with benches, electricity, heat, and a screened porch. An outdoor picnic table and fire ring with cooking grate are provided at each cabin site.

Cabins do not have indoor plumbing or cooking facilities beyond crockpots and coffeepots. Seasonal restrooms with flush toilets, showers, and drinking water are located nearby in the campground. Pets are not permitted in the camper cabins. Accessible cabins are available with a maximum capacity of five guests.

The park encompasses over 1,100 acres of restored prairie, wetlands, and oak savanna along the shores of 3,500-acre Lake Shetek. Activities include fishing for walleye, northern pike, and panfish, swimming at the sandy beach with its historic bathhouse, and boating with rentals available. The six-mile Casey Jones State Trail connects the park to the town of Currie.

location.directions: From Currie, take County Road 37 north for 1 mile to State Park Road. Turn east and follow signs to the park entrance at 163 State Park Road, Currie, MN 56123.

payload.name: Lake Hill
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season and opens May 22, 2026. The season typically runs through September. Reservations available via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at 8,400 feet in the Manti-La Sal National Forest near Ephraim, Utah, offering fishing, canoeing, and access to the Arapeen OHV Trail System.
payload.medium_description: Lake Hill Campground sits alongside Lake Hill Reservoir in Ephraim Canyon, about 5 miles east of Ephraim, Utah. At 8,400 feet elevation, the campground features single-family and group sites beneath a mixed forest of spruce, fir, and aspen. Rainbow trout fishing and canoeing on the small reservoir are popular activities, and nearby trails offer hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Lake Hill Campground is nestled next to Lake Hill Reservoir at 8,400 feet in the Manti-La Sal National Forest, just 5 miles east of Ephraim, Utah via Forest Highway 8. The campground offers both single-family sites and two group sites, with Group Site #1 accommodating up to 30 people and Group Site #2 handling up to 75 people. A mixed forest of spruce, fir, and aspen provides partial shade throughout the campground, with summer wildflowers abundant.

The small man-made reservoir is popular for canoeing and rainbow trout fishing. Beyond the water, Ephraim Canyon serves as a gateway to the Arapeen OHV Trail System with over 350 miles of routes. Jimmies Fork Trail and the Great Basin Experimental Trail nearby offer opportunities for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. The self-guided Great Basin Experimental Range Auto Tour provides historical context on one of North America's oldest range research sites.

This is a pack-it-out facility with vault toilets. Roads and parking spurs are dirt. No livestock permitted.

location.directions: From Ephraim, turn east on 400 South, then right on 300 East. 300 East becomes State Route 29. Continue approximately 5 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Kennedy Meadows Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations. Snow is often present November through March, which may limit access. Campfire restrictions may apply during fire season.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive campground on the Pacific Crest Trail near the South Fork of the Kern River, offering 37 first-come, first-served sites at 6,100 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Kennedy Meadows Campground is a free, no-reservation campground located on the Pacific Crest Trail near the South Fork of the Kern River. The 37 sites are surrounded by the South Sierra and Golden Trout wildernesses, with some sites shaded by juniper and pinion pine. This primitive campground has vault toilets but no potable water, trash service, or hookups. Campers must pack out all garbage and bring their own water.
payload.long_description:
Kennedy Meadows Campground sits at 6,100 feet elevation on the Pacific Crest Trail, serving as a popular resupply point for PCT thru-hikers and a gateway to the surrounding South Sierra and Golden Trout wildernesses. The 37 sites are scattered among juniper and pinion pine, offering a remote high-desert camping experience near the South Fork of the Kern River.

This is a primitive, no-fee campground operating on a first-come, first-served basis year-round. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water, trash service, or hookups. Campers must pack out all garbage and bring adequate water supplies. Some sites have fire pits, though campfire restrictions may apply during fire season.

The area is extremely remote with no cell phone service. Maximum vehicle length is 30 feet, and the maximum stay is 14 days. Dogs are allowed but must be leashed. Snow is often present from November through March, and winter access may be limited.

location.directions: From US 395, north of Ridgecrest, CA, exit near Pearsonville and travel west on Nine Mile Canyon Road (paved) to Kennedy Meadows.

payload.name: Beartown State Forest
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Reservations required through ReserveAmerica. Same-day bookings accepted until 2 p.m.; no walk-in camping. Season typically runs from mid-May through late October.
payload.short_description: Intimate 12-site campground in the Berkshires with direct access to Benedict Pond, featuring flush toilets and updated facilities after a four-year renovation.
payload.medium_description: Beartown State Forest offers 12 well-spaced campsites in a 12,000-acre forest in the Berkshires. The campground provides direct access to Benedict Pond for swimming and fishing. Recently renovated with flush toilets, running water, and updated amenities at each site including fire rings, picnic tables, and food storage lockers. Reservations required through ReserveAmerica.
payload.long_description:
Beartown State Forest campground is a small, intimate camping destination nestled within 12,000 acres of forest in the southern Berkshires near Great Barrington. The campground features 12 well-maintained sites, several of which are positioned directly along the shore of Benedict Pond, offering campers immediate access to swimming and fishing.

After a four-year upgrade project, the campground now features two bathrooms with flush toilets and running water, multiple water spigots throughout the site, and updated amenities. Each campsite comes equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and food storage locker. The surrounding forest offers excellent hiking on the Appalachian Trail and other trails, as well as cross-country skiing and snowmobiling in winter.

This is a primitive campground with no hookups, dump station, or showers. RVs are limited to 25 feet. Camping is by reservation only through ReserveAmerica; same-day reservations are accepted until 2 p.m. but walk-in camping is not permitted.

location.directions: From East or West/MassPike (I-90): Take Exit 10 in Lee. Follow MA Rte. 102 west for 4.7 miles to Stockbridge. Turn left and follow U.S. Rte. 7 south for 6.1 miles to Great Barrington. Turn left and follow MA Rte. 23 east for 5.3 miles to Monterey. Turn left onto Blue Hill Road then follow the brown lead-in signs; 0.5 miles to park headquarters on left, or 2.2 miles to park entrance on right (Benedict Pond Rd.).

address.full: 281 Blue Hill Rd, Great Barrington, MA 01230

payload.name: San Onofre Sb San Mateo Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia. Park hours are 6 AM to 10 PM daily.
payload.short_description: Coastal campground at San Onofre State Beach with 157 sites, RV hookups, and a 1.5-mile trail to world-famous Trestles Beach surfing spot.
payload.medium_description: San Mateo Campground sits one mile inland from the coast within San Onofre State Beach, offering 157 campsites ranging from primitive tent sites to full RV hookup sites with electric and water. The campground features flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, and drinking water. A 1.5-mile nature trail connects directly to Trestles Beach, one of the world's premier surfing destinations. The campground operates year-round with reservations available through ReserveCalifornia.
payload.long_description:
San Mateo Campground is the primary overnight camping area at San Onofre State Beach, located about one mile inland from Interstate 5 at the Cristianitos Road exit. The campground offers 157 sites spread across several loops: sites 1-67 are RV hookup sites with electric and water connections, sites 68-100 are standard campsites, and sites 101-157 are tent-only primitive sites. A group camping area accommodates larger parties.

The campground provides solid amenities including flush toilets, hot indoor showers, potable water, and an RV dump station. Every site includes a fire pit and picnic table. Mature trees throughout the campground provide shade and privacy between sites. The maximum vehicle length is 36 feet.

The signature attraction is the 1.5-mile Nature Trail connecting the campground to Trestles Beach, home to legendary surf breaks like Lower Trestles, Upper Trestles, and Church. The beach was selected to host surfing events for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Beyond surfing, the 3.5 miles of sandy beaches offer swimming, fishing, and wildlife watching. The campground operates year-round with hours from 6 AM to 10 PM.

location.directions: From Interstate 5, take the Cristianitos Road exit. The campground is located at 830 Cristianitos Road, San Clemente, approximately one mile inland from the freeway.

payload.name: Dalles Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from early May through late September. First-come, first-served with no reservations. Peak season fees ($15/night) apply April through September; no fee during non-peak season.
payload.short_description: A first-come, first-served campground in Lolo National Forest's Rock Creek drainage, set in a mixed conifer forest above a renowned blue-ribbon trout stream.
payload.medium_description: Dalles Campground sits above Rock Creek in a mixed conifer forest within Montana's Lolo National Forest. The area is prized for its blue-ribbon trout fishing and rugged canyon scenery. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no reservations, and fees apply only during peak season. Access requires navigating a narrow, rough road unsuitable for large RVs or trailers.
payload.long_description:
Dalles Campground occupies a scenic position above Rock Creek in the Lolo National Forest's Rock Creek drainage. The setting is a mixed conifer forest typical of western Montana's mountain valleys, with the creek below offering some of the state's best trout fishing. Rock Creek is designated a blue-ribbon trout stream, drawing anglers from across the region.

The campground provides basic amenities including flush toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. Sites include picnic tables. This is a primitive camping experience with no hookups, showers, or dump stations. Pets are permitted but must be kept on a 6-foot leash; pack and saddle stock are not allowed.

Access is via Rock Creek Road, a narrow and rough route that makes the campground unsuitable for trailers, motorhomes, and tow vehicles. The tradeoff for the challenging access is a quieter, more secluded camping experience in quality trout water habitat.

location.directions: From Missoula, drive 20 miles east on Interstate 90 to Rock Creek exit #126. Turn onto Rock Creek Road and travel 14.5 miles south on Rock Creek Road #102. Note: Trailers, motorhomes, and tow vehicles are not recommended due to the narrow and rough road.

payload.name: Big Pine River Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Boat-in access only. All campers must bring a portable toilet system. A Flaming Gorge NRA Recreational Use Pass is required in addition to the campsite fee.
payload.short_description: Remote boat-in river camp on the Green River in Flaming Gorge NRA, featuring a single site with fire ring and table accessible only by water from Spillway or Little Hole boat ramps.
payload.medium_description: Big Pine I River Camp is a primitive boat-in campsite on the north bank of the Green River, 10.5 miles below Flaming Gorge Dam. The single site accommodates up to 8 people and includes a picnic table, fire ring with benches, and two tent pads. There is no potable water or trash service; campers must pack out all garbage and bring a portable toilet system. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov, and a Flaming Gorge NRA Recreational Use Pass is required.
payload.long_description:
Big Pine I River Camp offers a secluded riverside camping experience on the Green River below Flaming Gorge Dam in northeastern Utah. The site sits on the north bank amid pinyon pine, juniper, and ponderosa pine, with river bottom vegetation providing natural shade. Access is exclusively by non-motorized watercraft, launching from either Spillway Boat Ramp (10.5 miles upstream) or Little Hole Boat Ramp (3.3 miles downstream).

The single campsite accommodates up to 8 people and includes one picnic table, one fire ring with two benches, and two tent pads. A privacy screen is provided for portable toilet use, which is mandatory for all campers. No potable water is available, and there are no garbage facilities, so pack-in/pack-out rules apply. The area is popular for fly fishing and float trips on the Green River's trophy trout waters.

Standard overnight fees are $13 per night, with reduced winter rates of $5 per night from October 1 through March 31. A Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area Recreational Use Pass is also required. Reservations can be made through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Vernal, UT, take US Highway 191 north 45 miles. Cross Flaming Gorge Dam and turn right to access Spillway Boat Ramp for the upper launch. For Little Hole, cross the dam and continue to Dutch John, then turn right onto Little Hole Road (Forest Road 075) and drive about 6 miles. Big Pine I is located 10.5 miles below Spillway or 3.3 miles below Little Hole on river left.

links.title: USFS Big Pine I River Camp

payload.name: Mohican Cabins
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Cottages are heated and available in all seasons. Reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance through ReserveOhio. Two-night minimum stay required.
payload.short_description: Riverfront cottages at Mohican State Park in Ohio's Mohican Memorial State Forest, offering fully equipped two-bedroom accommodations with gas fireplaces and screened porches year-round.
payload.medium_description: Mohican State Park offers 25 newly-renovated cottages along the Clear Fork of the Mohican River in a wooded setting. Each cottage sleeps six guests and comes fully furnished with two bedrooms, a kitchen with appliances, bathroom with shower, living room with sofa bed, TV/DVD, gas fireplace, and a screened-in porch with picnic table. Linens, cooking utensils, and blankets are provided. Four cottages are pet-friendly.
payload.long_description:
Mohican Cabins at Mohican State Park consist of 25 riverfront cottages situated in a wooded area along the Clear Fork of the Mohican River in north-central Ohio. Each cottage accommodates up to six guests with two bedrooms and a sofa bed in the living room. The fully furnished units include a kitchen with stove, refrigerator, microwave, toaster, and coffee maker, plus a bathroom with shower. The living area features a gas fireplace and TV/DVD player, and each cottage has a screened-in porch with a picnic table.

The cottages are heated for year-round use and come equipped with bed linens, towels, blankets, and cooking utensils. Four of the 25 cottages are designated as pet-friendly. Reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance through ReserveOhio.

Mohican State Park encompasses over 1,100 acres adjacent to the 4,700-acre Mohican-Memorial State Forest, providing extensive opportunities for hiking on more than 50 miles of multi-use trails. The Clear Fork Gorge, a designated State Scenic River, offers dramatic scenery with 300-foot cliffs and old-growth hemlock forest. Activities include fishing, canoeing, and exploring the covered bridge and waterfalls within the park.

location.directions: From State Route 3, head west of Loudonville, Ohio. The park entrance is accessible from State Route 3. Follow signs to the campground and cottage area along the river.

payload.name: Orland Buttes
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Due to ongoing sanitation infrastructure issues, flush toilets and showers are not available. Portable restrooms and handwashing stations are in place. Potable water and dump station remain operational. The campground operates April 1 through the second Monday in September. Entrance gates close at 10 PM. Quiet hours 10 PM to 6 AM.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at Black Butte Lake with 35 sites, disc golf, and boat ramp access in Northern California's Sacramento Valley.
payload.medium_description: Orland Buttes Recreation Area sits on the shores of Black Butte Lake, a US Army Corps of Engineers reservoir in Glenn County. The campground offers 35 individual sites and one group site accommodating up to 50 people. Facilities include an 18-hole disc golf course, boat ramp complex, dump station, and water filling station. The lake is popular for warm-water fishing including crappie, catfish, and bass.
payload.long_description:
Orland Buttes Recreation Area occupies a prime location at Black Butte Lake, situated at the northern end of the Sacramento Valley about 100 miles north of Sacramento and 30 miles south of Red Bluff. The lake was formed in 1963 with the completion of Black Butte Dam on Stony Creek, creating a 4,460-acre reservoir surrounded by black basalt buttes and blue oak woodland along 40 miles of shoreline.

The campground features 35 individual campsites with paved driveways and back-in access, plus a group site that accommodates up to 50 people with pull-through access. Recreation options include wakeboarding, sailing, swimming, and warm-water fishing for crappie, channel catfish, and largemouth and smallmouth bass. An 18-hole disc golf course is located within the campground, and the Paul Thomas Trail provides hiking opportunities.

Direct lake access from the campground is limited due to steep terrain, but a boat ramp complex serves watercraft. Horseback riders can access trails at nearby Grizzly Flat and Burris Creek, while Buckhorn Recreation Area offers 13 miles of fitness trails for hiking, running, and biking.

location.directions: From Interstate 5, take the Black Butte Lake exit at Orland, CA. Travel west on County Road 200/Newville Road for 6 miles. Turn left on County Road 206 and drive 4 miles to the campground.

photos.name: A photo of facility ORLAND BUTTES
A photo of facility ORLAND BUTTES

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Orland Buttes Campground – Limited Restroom Facilities  Due to ongoing sanitation infrastructure issues, **flushing toilets and showers will not be available.** Portable restrooms and handwashing stations will be in place to support public health and safety. These facilities will be located near existing restroom areas.  Potable water and dump stations will remain available for visitor use.  We appreciate the public’s patience and apologize for any inconvenience.  For more information, please contact the Project Office at (530) 865-4781.

payload.name: Don Carter State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The designated swimming area is currently not accessible due to low water level conditions, but the beach area is open to the public. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.
payload.short_description: Georgia's only state park on Lake Lanier, offering RV and tent camping with full hookups, primitive sites, lakeside cottages, a sand beach, and boat access.
payload.medium_description: Don Carter State Park is Georgia's only state park located on Lake Lanier, northeast of Gainesville. The 1,318-acre park features 44 developed campsites with electric hookups (15/20/30/50 amp), water, and sewer options, plus 16 primitive tent and hammock sites. Amenities include a sand beach with bathhouse, boat ramps and docks, a fish cleaning station, comfort stations with hot showers and flush toilets, a dump station, and a gift shop. A multi-use paved trail winds through the hardwood forest for hiking and biking.
payload.long_description:
Don Carter State Park sits on the northern shores of Lake Lanier in Hall County, Georgia, making it the only state park with direct access to the popular 38,000-acre reservoir. The park offers a full-service campground with 44 developed sites featuring electric hookups ranging from 15 to 50 amps, plus water and sewer connections. An additional 16 primitive campsites cater to tent and hammock campers seeking a simpler experience without the long hike typically required for backcountry camping.

The park's lakeside location provides excellent recreation opportunities including two boat ramps, courtesy docks, and seasonal kayak, paddleboard, and aquacycle rentals. A sand beach with bathhouse offers swimming when water levels permit. The park also features a fish cleaning station, playground, outdoor fitness equipment, and a multi-use paved trail through mature hardwood forest. Comfort stations provide hot showers and flush toilets, and a gift shop sells firewood, ice, and supplies.

Two-bedroom cottages perched on wooded hillsides near the lake provide an alternative to camping. The park operates year-round with reservations available up to 14 months in advance through ReserveAmerica. A daily ParkPass is required for all vehicles, though overnight guests pay only once per stay.

location.directions: Located at 5000 North Browning Bridge Road, Gainesville, GA 30506, northeast of Gainesville on the north side of Lake Lanier.

address.full: 5218 N Browning Bridge Rd, Gainesville, GA 30506

links.title: Don Carter State Park Official Site

payload.name: Rainy Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come-first-served with no fees. No potable water available; bring your own.
payload.short_description: Free, first-come-first-served 6-site campground on Rainy Lake in Montana's Clearwater Chain of Lakes with walk-in tent sites and one accessible small trailer site.
payload.medium_description: Rainy Lake Campground is a small, free campground offering six sites on Rainy Lake, part of the Clearwater Chain of Lakes north of Seeley Lake. Five sites are walk-in tent-only while site 1 accommodates small trailers and is designed as an accessible site. The lake offers fishing, canoeing, and kayaking opportunities with hiking nearby.
payload.long_description:
Rainy Lake Campground is a quiet, primitive campground tucked along Rainy Lake in Montana's Lolo National Forest. Part of the scenic Clearwater Chain of Lakes, this small campground offers six first-come-first-served sites with no fees required. Sites 2 through 6 are walk-in tent sites, while site 1 is designed as an accessible site that can accommodate smaller trailers.

The campground provides basic amenities including vault toilets and picnic tables, though campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on site. Vehicles must remain on designated roads. Rainy Lake offers fishing opportunities for species like rainbow trout and provides calm waters suitable for canoeing and kayaking. Hiking trails are also accessible in the surrounding area.

Pets are welcome but must be kept on a 6-foot leash at all times. The campground operates year-round with 24-hour access, making it a solid option for those seeking a peaceful lakeside experience without reservation hassles or camping fees.

location.directions: From the town of Seeley Lake, Montana, head north on MT-83 N toward Thelma for 12.2 miles. Turn left onto Rainy Lake Campground Road (Forest Road 4357).

payload.name: Plaskett Meadows Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Fees of $10/night apply Memorial Day through Labor Day; off-season camping is free. First-come, first-served with scan-and-pay through recreation.gov or cash/check. 14-day stay limit within any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Remote high-elevation campground in Mendocino National Forest with two small trout fishing lakes, vault toilets, and drinking water in a mixed pine and fir forest setting.
payload.medium_description: Plaskett Meadows Campground sits at approximately 6,000 feet elevation in a mixed pine and fir forest in western Glenn County. The campground features two small lakes (3-4 acres each) stocked with trout where non-motorized boating is permitted. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings, with vault toilets and drinking water available. The campground operates first-come, first-served with payment via scan-and-pay through recreation.gov or cash/check.
payload.long_description:
Plaskett Meadows Campground is a secluded, high-elevation destination in the Mendocino National Forest, located 36 miles northwest of Elk Creek on Forest Highway 7. The campground rests in a scenic area of mixed pine and fir trees at roughly 6,000 feet elevation, offering a cool retreat during summer months.

The primary draw is the pair of small trout fishing lakes adjacent to the campground, each spanning three to four acres. Non-motorized boats are permitted, making it ideal for float tubes, canoes, and kayaks. Swimming is not recommended due to water conditions. The surrounding forest provides opportunities for hiking and wildlife viewing.

The campground was extensively restored and reopened in June 2025 following damage from the 2020 August Complex fire and subsequent winter storms. New fire rings, barriers, and signage were installed during the restoration. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings, with vault toilets and drinking water available throughout. The campground operates first-come, first-served; fees are $10 per night during the summer season (Memorial Day through Labor Day) with free camping during the off-season.

location.directions: Located 36 miles northwest of Elk Creek and 15 miles east of Eel River Station on Forest Highway 7.

payload.name: Mountain View Snow Shelter
payload.status_description: Closed for overnight use. The shelter is open for overnight stays from November 15 through April 30 only. No reservations; first-come, first-served with a 3-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Backcountry winter snow shelter in Willamette National Forest accessible via ski or snowshoe from Maxwell Sno-Park, offering views of Mount Washington and Three Finger Jack.
payload.medium_description: Mountain View Snow Shelter is a rustic backcountry shelter in the Willamette National Forest, accessible via cross-country ski or snowshoe trails from Maxwell Sno-Park. The shelter features a wood stove with firewood provided and can accommodate up to 15 overnight guests on a first-come, first-served basis. Open November 15 through April 30 for overnight use, visitors enjoy panoramic views of Mount Washington, North Sister, and Three Finger Jack on clear days.
payload.long_description:
Mountain View Snow Shelter is a rustic backcountry warming shelter located in the Willamette National Forest, accessible from Maxwell Sno-Park via cross-country ski or snowshoe trails. The shelter provides a welcome refuge for winter recreationists exploring the area's extensive trail network, which includes routes to Birthday Lakes, Pothole Meadows, Fuji Mountain, and Island Lakes. On clear days, visitors are rewarded with spectacular views of Mount Washington, North Sister, and Three Finger Jack.

The shelter features a wood stove with firewood provided, a sleeping loft, and a wood picnic table on a gravel floor. No potable water or restroom facilities are available, and visitors must pack out all garbage and human waste. Candles are prohibited; bring your own lights. The shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted, and all users must share the space. Maximum overnight capacity is 15 persons with a 3-night stay limit.

Overnight visitors should park at Maxwell Sno-Park rather than Big Meadows, as vehicles at Big Meadows risk being temporarily plowed in during heavy snowfall. A valid Oregon Sno-Park permit is required for parking during the winter season.

location.directions: From Santiam Junction on Highway 22, travel 3.5 miles west to Maxwell Sno-Park. The shelter is accessed via ski or snowshoe trails from the sno-park. Overnight visitors should use Maxwell Sno-Park parking rather than Big Meadows to avoid being plowed in during heavy snowfall.

payload.name: Horseshoe Bend
payload.status_description: Open for reservations via Recreation.gov. Check-in is 4:00 PM; check-out is 1:00 PM (changed from 3:00 PM for reservations starting April 1, 2026). Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights per 30-day period. Commercial delivery and setup of rental campers or watercraft is prohibited.
payload.short_description: Horseshoe Bend Campground sits along the shores of Beaver Lake in the Ozark Mountains of Northwest Arkansas, offering 188 spacious campsites with electric hookups, flush toilets, and abundant water recreation.
payload.medium_description: Horseshoe Bend Campground is a US Army Corps of Engineers facility on Beaver Lake with 188 electric campsites ranging from tent sites to large pull-through sites accommodating RVs up to 53 feet. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, dump station, swimming beach, hiking trails, boat launch ramps, and a marina. Sites feature fire rings and concrete picnic tables on level crushed rock pads surrounded by mature shade trees.
payload.long_description:
Horseshoe Bend Campground occupies a scenic peninsula along Beaver Lake in the Ozark Mountains near Rogers, Arkansas. As the largest Corps of Engineers campground on the lake, it offers 188 campsites with electric hookups (including 50-amp service) plus 3 group picnic pavilions. The campground features a mix of back-in and pull-through sites on paved surfaces, with many accommodating large RVs and trailers up to 53 feet. Sites are well-shaded with mature hardwoods and include concrete picnic tables and fire rings on level crushed rock pads.

Beaver Lake spans over 28,000 surface acres and offers excellent fishing for largemouth and smallmouth bass, crappie, bream, white bass, stripers, and catfish. The campground provides two boat launch ramps and an on-site marina for water access. A swimming beach, hiking trails, and wildlife viewing opportunities round out the recreation options. Below the dam, the cold waters of the upper White River support rainbow and German brown trout.

The surrounding Ozark landscape features towering limestone bluffs, natural caves, and diverse hardwood and evergreen forests. Hunters can access nearby public lands for deer, rabbit, and squirrel in season. The campground sits approximately 8 miles east of Rogers off Highway 94.

location.directions: From Rogers, Arkansas, take Highway 94 East/New Hope Road for approximately 8 miles, and follow into Horseshoe Bend Park.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Engaging in commercial business on US Army Corps of Engineers recreation areas is prohibited. This includes the delivery and setup of rental campers, rental boats or any other type of water craft.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: To improve the camping experience for our guests at all Beaver Lake campgrounds, the Check-Out time for campsite reservations will be adjusted from 3:00pm to 1:00pm on the day that reservation ends. This change will apply to all reservations beginning on or after April 1st, 2026, regardless of when the reservation was originally booked. Check-In time will remain 4:00pm on the day incoming reservations start.  The additional time before incoming reservation holders may check in will allow Park Attendants, Cleaners, and Park Ranger staff to ensure that outgoing guests have not only vacated their sites, but that the facilities are fully operational, clean, and prepared to welcome incoming guests.  As always, should you wish to make, modify, or cancel a reservation, you may do so from your [Recreation.gov][1] account or by calling 1-877-444-6777.  We look forward to seeing you at Beaver Lake this recreation season!  [1]: http://Recreation.gov

payload.name: Beaver View Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (Highway 150) is currently closed from Kamas, Utah to Evanston, Wyoming due to snow. The campground typically operates seasonally from late May/early June through fall, depending on road and weather conditions. Reservations available through Recreation.gov; some first-come-first-served sites available.
payload.short_description: High-elevation riverside campground at 8,960 ft along the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway, featuring 17 sites among pine and aspen with access to High Uintas Wilderness trails.
payload.medium_description: Beaver View Campground sits alongside the Hayden Fork River at 8,960 feet elevation, about 34 miles south of Evanston, Wyoming on the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway. The campground features 17 single sites nestled among pine and aspen trees with beaver ponds nearby. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. Vault toilets are provided but there is no potable water. Pack-it-in/pack-it-out for trash.
payload.long_description:
Beaver View Campground occupies a scenic riverside setting at 8,960 feet elevation in the Uinta Mountains, approximately 34 miles south of Evanston, Wyoming along the Mirror Lake Scenic Byway (State Route 150). The campground sits alongside the Hayden Fork River with numerous small beaver ponds scattered throughout the area. A thin forest of pine and aspen provides limited shade, while summer wildflowers and grasses dot the landscape.

The campground offers 17 single campsites and one group day-use picnic area. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water on site, so campers must bring all water needed. Trash service is pack-it-in/pack-it-out. Dogs are allowed with a maximum of two per site, kept on a leash not exceeding six feet.

Recreation opportunities abound with nearby fishing in the river and alpine lakes, hiking, backpacking, and mountain biking. Access to High Uintas Wilderness trails is available from several points along the byway. The campground has a 14-day stay limit and enforces quiet hours from 10 PM to 7 AM.

location.directions: From Evanston, WY, take State Route 150 (Mirror Lake Scenic Byway) south 34.1 miles to the campground sign. Turn left into the campground.

payload.name: Pelton Creek
