payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. Handpump water is typically available July through September, suggesting a late June or early July opening. For 2026, the campground operates as first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Primitive Forest Service campground at the edge of Platte River Wilderness with 14 sites along Pelton Creek, offering trailhead access to Douglas Creek and Platte Ridge Trails.
payload.medium_description: Pelton Creek Campground sits at the eastern edge of the Platte River Wilderness in Medicine Bow National Forest. The 14-site single-loop campground runs parallel to Pelton Creek among Lodgepole pines, with some sites overlooking the creek and a meadow. Trailheads for Douglas Creek Trail and Platte Ridge Trail provide direct wilderness access from the north end of the campground.
payload.long_description:
Pelton Creek Campground lies at the convergence of Douglas Creek and Pelton Creek, just outside the Platte River Wilderness in Wyoming's Medicine Bow National Forest. Although the Mullen Fire burned through the area in 2020, the campground was spared and retains tall pine trees providing shade. The 14 sites are arranged in a single loop with one side running parallel to Pelton Creek. Some sites overlook the creek and a meadow, though the grass understory and close spacing provide minimal privacy.

The campground serves as a gateway to the Platte River Wilderness, with trailheads for the Douglas Creek Trail and Platte Ridge Trail departing from the north end. Douglas Creek Trail follows the creek for 9.5 miles through an open canyon, and hikers can complete a loop by connecting to the Platte River Trail. Fishing opportunities abound in Douglas Creek and the nearby North Platte River, which offers blue-ribbon trout fishing. A stock unloading facility is located near the campground, though stock are not permitted within the campground itself.

Facilities include vault toilets, a water handpump near site 1, picnic tables, and fire grates at each site. Four sites accommodate longer vehicles or trailers as pull-through configurations. Campers must pack out all trash. The 14-day stay limit is enforced.

location.directions: From Laramie, take WY 230 west for 40.6 miles to National Forest Recreation Area sign on Forest Route 898. Turn right onto FR 898 and go 8.7 miles to campground.

photos.name: The Platte Ridge Trailhead is located inside Pelton Creek Campground

payload.name: Big Lake Premium Camper Cabins
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from April 15 through October 31. Reservations require a two-night minimum on weekends and three-night minimum on holiday weekends. Full payment due at reservation. Check-in is 3 p.m., check-out is 11 a.m.
payload.short_description: Lakefront premium camper cabins at Big Lake State Park featuring full kitchens, private bathrooms with showers, air conditioning, and scenic covered decks overlooking Missouri's largest oxbow lake.
payload.medium_description: Big Lake State Park offers eight premium camper cabins with direct views of Missouri's largest remaining oxbow lake. Each cabin sleeps up to four adults and two children with a queen bed, full futon, and lofted sleeping area. Cabins include full kitchens with stove, refrigerator, and microwave, plus private bathrooms with showers. Outdoor amenities include a covered deck, picnic table, grill, and fire ring.
payload.long_description:
Located in northwest Missouri's Holt County, Big Lake State Park's premium camper cabins provide comfortable lakefront lodging on the shores of the state's largest remaining oxbow lake. The eight log cabins accommodate up to four adults and two children, featuring a queen-size bed, full-size futon, and a carpeted loft for sleeping bags.

Each cabin comes fully equipped with climate control, a complete kitchen including four-burner electric stove, oven, refrigerator, microwave, coffee maker, and toaster, plus cooking utensils and dining sets. Private bathrooms with showers eliminate the need for shared facilities. Outside, guests enjoy a covered deck with lake views, picnic table, barbecue grill, outdoor fire ring, and lantern post.

Cabins 4 and 5 are ADA accessible. Dogs are permitted in cabins 5 and 6 for an additional fee. Guests must bring their own linens, towels, and toiletries. There are no televisions, phones, or Wi-Fi in the cabins.

location.directions: Big Lake State Park is located at 204 Lake Shore Drive in Craig, Missouri. From Mound City, travel 11 miles southwest on Route 111 to reach the park.

payload.name: Joes Valley Reservoir
payload.status_description: Closed for construction and upgrades from April 13, 2026 through June 10, 2026. The campground will reopen after renovations are complete. Reservations available via Recreation.gov once the closure ends.
payload.short_description: High-elevation reservoir campground in the Manti-La Sal National Forest offering 51 accessible campsites with vault toilets, drinking water, and a boat ramp for fishing and water sports.
payload.medium_description: Joes Valley Reservoir Campground sits at 7,000 feet in a scenic mountain valley on the Wasatch Plateau in central Utah. The campground features 51 single and double-family campsites, all ADA accessible, with paved roads and parking spurs. Vault toilets and drinking water are provided. A boat ramp offers direct access to the reservoir, which is stocked with cutthroat trout, rainbow trout, tiger muskie, and trophy splake.
payload.long_description:
Joes Valley Reservoir Campground is located in a high mountain valley adjacent to its namesake reservoir at approximately 7,000 feet elevation in the Manti-La Sal National Forest. The surrounding landscape features juniper, pinyon pine, and sagebrush, with aspens and pines dotting the hillsides. Several sites offer views of the reservoir, and some are shaded. All 51 campsites are accessible, with paved roads and parking spurs throughout.

The reservoir provides excellent fishing opportunities for cutthroat trout, rainbow trout, tiger muskie, and trophy splake. A boat ramp within the campground allows easy access for boating, water skiing, and canoeing. The area also offers horseback riding (outside the campground), bouldering, hiking, and mountain biking.

The expansive Arapeen Off-Highway Vehicle Trail System can be accessed just west of the reservoir via the Reeder Trailhead, offering more than 350 miles of designated trails suitable for all skill levels. Nearby attractions include renowned bouldering in Straight and Cottonwood Canyons, mountain fisheries at Grassy Lake, Pete's Hole, and Potters Ponds, as well as the Orange Olsen Guard Station cabin rentals.

location.directions: From Orangeville, Utah, head northwest on State Route 29 for approximately 14 miles until you reach Joes Valley Reservoir. Continue following SR-29 around the reservoir for about 5 more miles to the west side, past the Pavilion. Turn southeast on Forest Road 0170 for 0.14 miles, then head east on Forest Road 0167 into the campground.

photos.name: A photo of facility JOES VALLEY RESERVOIR with No Amenities Shown

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Joes Valley Campground will be undergoing construction from April 13, 2026 through June 10, 2026. This project will disrupt access and the availability of amenities and services. The campground will be closed to all visitors during this time. Please be sure to schedule a reservation once it opens.

payload.name: Upper Salt Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. This site is no longer operational and has been decommissioned by the Forest Service.
payload.short_description: Upper Salt Creek Campground is a permanently closed former campground in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest near Shasta Lake.
payload.medium_description: Upper Salt Creek Campground, located in the Shasta Unit of the Whiskeytown-Shasta-Trinity National Recreation Area within Shasta-Trinity National Forest, is permanently closed and no longer operates as a camping facility. No amenities or services are available at this site.
payload.long_description:
Upper Salt Creek Campground was once a camping area in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, situated near Shasta Lake in northern California. The campground has been permanently closed and decommissioned by the Forest Service.

As of now, no facilities, water, or restrooms are available at this location. Visitors looking for camping in the Salt Creek area should consider nearby alternatives such as the Salt Creek Dispersed Area or Lower Salt Creek Shoreline Area, both of which offer shoreline camping along Shasta Lake.

location.directions: This campground is closed. No directions are provided, as the site is no longer in operation.

payload.name: Madison Campground
payload.status_description: Open May 1 through October 18, 2026. Reservations required through Yellowstone National Park Lodges. The dump station may be unavailable early and late season due to freezing conditions.
payload.short_description: Large, popular campground at 6,800 feet elevation where the Gibbon and Firehole rivers form the Madison River, 14 miles from West Yellowstone and 16 miles from Old Faithful.
payload.medium_description: Madison Campground sits at the confluence of the Gibbon and Firehole rivers in Yellowstone's western region. The 278-site campground operates seasonally with flush toilets, potable water, dump station, and a small camp store. All sites include picnic tables and fire rings. No hookups or showers are available. Reservations are required through Yellowstone National Park Lodges.
payload.long_description:
Madison Campground occupies a scenic location at 6,800 feet elevation where the Gibbon and Firehole rivers converge to form the Madison River. The campground sits 14 miles east of the West Yellowstone entrance and 16 miles north of Old Faithful, making it well-positioned for exploring the park's western attractions including the Madison Information Station and nearby geyser basins.

The campground offers 278 individual sites and 3 group sites in a partially wooded setting. Facilities include 14 restroom buildings with flush toilets and cold running water, dishwashing stations, an RV dump station, shared bear-proof food storage boxes, and a small mercantile store selling camping supplies and snacks. All individual sites have a picnic table and fire grate. No hookups or shower facilities are available on-site.

Wildlife viewing opportunities abound, with bison frequenting the surrounding meadows in early summer and elk bugling audible during September and October. The campground accommodates both tent and RV camping, with some sites suitable for vehicles up to 40 feet, though larger sites are limited and may not be level.

location.directions: Located on the Grand Loop Road near the West Entrance junction. From the West Entrance at West Yellowstone, drive 14 miles east. From Old Faithful, drive 16 miles north.

address.full: 157 Madison Junction Rd, Yellowstone National Park, WY 82190

links.title: Yellowstone National Park Lodges - Madison Campground

photos.name: Even on a rainy day, there are many things to do at Madison, including having a meal under a canopy.
Tent sites at the Madison Campground
Even on a rainy day at Madison Campground there are many things to do nearby including the Madison Information Station.
Madison Campground is set in a partially woody area.

payload.name: Fort Morris State Historic Site
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The historic site operates daily 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. with museum staff available Friday through Sunday. Self-guided tours available Monday through Thursday with $5 vehicle fee at collection box. Campers should note the site may flood during extreme high tides.
payload.short_description: Revolutionary War-era historic site on Georgia's coast with a primitive Pioneer Campsite offering group tent camping with an Adirondack shelter and shared fire ring amid 66 coastal acres.
payload.medium_description: Fort Morris State Historic Site preserves a Revolutionary War fortification on Georgia's coastal marshes near the historic port town of Sunbury. The site offers a single Pioneer Campsite designed for group tent camping, accommodating up to 35 people. The campsite includes one Adirondack shelter, a common fire ring, and three benches. No water or electricity is available. The site may become soggy during extreme high tides. Visitors can explore the earthwork fort, museum, and nature trails, with excellent birding opportunities along the marsh.
payload.long_description:
Fort Morris State Historic Site sits on 66 acres of coastal Georgia marshland in Liberty County, preserving the earthwork fortifications where American forces twice defended against British attacks during the Revolutionary War. The site commemorates the colonial port of Sunbury, once a thriving rival to Savannah that has since vanished.

The Pioneer Campsite offers a back-to-basics group camping experience for up to 35 people. The tent-only site features one Adirondack shelter, a shared fire ring, and three benches in a common area. There is no potable water or electricity at the campsite, so campers must bring all supplies. The site sits near tidal marshes and may become soggy during extreme high tides.

Beyond camping, visitors can tour the earthwork fort, browse exhibits in the museum (staffed Friday through Sunday), and walk the nature trail. The park loans binoculars and field guides for birding, with species including painted buntings, wood storks, pileated woodpeckers, and great egrets frequenting the marsh habitat.

location.directions: Located at 2559 Fort Morris Road, Midway, GA 31320. GPS coordinates: N 31.767894, W -81.281233.

payload.name: Wish Poosh Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens Memorial Day weekend through mid-September. Drinking water system and flush toilets are out of order; portable toilets are provided and campers must bring their own water.
payload.short_description: Scenic lakeside campground on Cle Elum Lake in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, offering 34 sites for tents and RVs with access to hiking, fishing, and the Pacific Crest Trail.
payload.medium_description: Wish Poosh Campground sits on the southeastern shore of Cle Elum Lake at 2,250 feet elevation within the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The campground offers 34 sites in a mixed conifer forest setting, suitable for both tent and RV camping. Nearby Speelyi Beach provides swimming and kayaking opportunities, while hiking trails and the Pacific Crest Trail are accessible within a few miles.
payload.long_description:
Wish Poosh Campground occupies a forested setting on the southeastern shore of Cle Elum Lake in Washington's Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. At 2,250 feet elevation, the campground provides 34 sites spread through a mixed conifer forest, accommodating both tent campers and RVs. The location serves as a base for exploring the surrounding mountains and lake.

Recreational opportunities include hiking, fishing, swimming, horseback riding, and mountain biking during summer and early fall. The Pacific Crest Trail is accessible nearby, and Speelyi Beach offers a sandy swimming area surrounded by conifers. Anglers should note that lake water levels drop through summer as water is drawn for irrigation, typically closing the boat ramp by early July.

The campground operates on a mixed reservation and first-come, first-served basis through Recreation.gov. Sites include picnic tables and campfire rings with grills. Note that the drinking water system and flush toilets are currently out of order; portable toilets are provided and campers must bring their own water.

location.directions: From Cle Elum, travel 10 miles northwest on Highway 903. The campground entrance is on the left.

address.full: 14991   14991 Salmon La Sac Rd, Ronald, WA 98940

payload.name: The Cottage At Sailors Haven
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from mid-May through Columbus Day weekend in October. Reservations require a 6-night minimum stay during peak season; shorter stays may be accommodated off-peak on a case-by-case basis by emailing fiis_information@nps.gov.
payload.short_description: A secluded one-bedroom cottage at Fire Island National Seashore, steps from the beach and the rare Sunken Forest. Requires ferry access and a 6-night minimum stay.
payload.medium_description: The Cottage at Sailors Haven offers a unique Fire Island experience in a single-bedroom, single-bathroom cottage that sleeps up to 4 guests. Located within Fire Island National Seashore, the cottage features a fully equipped kitchen, outdoor deck with grill and shower, and is just a short walk from a lifeguarded beach, the globally rare Sunken Forest, and the historic community of Cherry Grove. Accessible only by ferry from Sayville or Cherry Grove.
payload.long_description:
The Cottage at Sailors Haven provides a secluded getaway within Fire Island National Seashore, offering one of the few overnight lodging options managed by the National Park Service on Fire Island. This small cottage includes one bedroom with a queen-sized bed, a living area with a full-sized sofabed, a fully equipped kitchen with microwave, oven, range, coffeemaker, blender, toaster, and all necessary cookware, plus an outdoor deck featuring a grill and shower.

Guests can walk to the lifeguarded Atlantic Ocean beach, explore the Sunken Forest via boardwalk trails, go clamming in the Great South Bay, or enjoy ranger-led programs. The nearby LoveFINS concessions at Sailors Haven Marina offer food, beverages, and a general store. The historic town of Cherry Grove is approximately a 3/4 mile walk west via boardwalks, providing restaurants, shops, and nightlife.

Access is by ferry only from Sayville, Long Island (41 River Road) or from Cherry Grove. Guests must provide their own bed sheets and towels. Pillows and light blankets are included. No pets, smoking, or open fires are permitted. A $250 refundable security deposit is required.

location.directions: Take the ferry from Sayville, Long Island to Sailors Haven. The Sayville Ferry Terminal is at 41 River Road, Sayville, NY 11782. From the ferry dock, follow the main walk south toward the public restroom, then head east on the concrete trail and follow the boardwalk to the fenced cottage. Ferry access is also available from Cherry Grove, approximately 3/4 mile east. By train: Take the LIRR to Sayville Station, then shuttle or taxi to the ferry terminal.

photos.name: View from the southeast corner of the Sailors Haven Cottage, looking at the sliding glass doors and deck.
The bedroom at the Sailors Haven Cottage
A South facing view of the Sailors Haven Cottage as you approach from the boardwalk.
A view of the eat-in kitchen from the Sailors Haven Cottage.
A view of the eat-in kitchen from the living area.

payload.name: Chicot State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours are 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday, Saturday, and holidays. Water playground operates Tuesday through Sunday 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., closed Mondays.
payload.short_description: The park covers over 6,400 acres of rolling hills and water in South Central Louisiana.
payload.medium_description: Chicot State Park features 198 improved campsites with water and electric hookups spread across three landings on Lake Chicot. The South Landing serves as the main hub with cabins, a water playground, boat launch, fishing pier, and boat rentals. The park's 22-mile Lake Chicot Loop Trail, the longest in the Louisiana State Parks system, encircles the lake with backcountry campsites along the way. The Louisiana State Arboretum within the park showcases a mature beech-magnolia forest and nature trails.
payload.long_description: The park covers over 6,400 acres of rolling hills and water in South Central Louisiana. The cool, clear waters of Lake Chicot have yielded record freshwater catches of largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill and red-ear sunfish. Fishermen will enjoy the convenient boathouse, three boat launches and boat rental facilities. An extensive hiking/backpacking trail completely encircles Lake Chicot and includes several primitive campsites along the way. The hiking trails allow visitors to experience and enjoy the park's natural landscape, its bottomland hardwood forest and the lake itself. For visitors who enjoy a quicker pace, much of the trail is geared toward mountain bikers, and all cyclists are welcome to ride the roadways throughout the park. The South Landing includes cabins, a group camp, picnic areas and playground, a water playground, a boat launch, a fishing pier and a dock with rental boats. A scenic road links the South Landing with the North Landing. The North Landing features campsites, a boat launch, a dock, a 400 ft. fishing pier and a primitive group-camping area. Lodges also are located in this area. The East Landing is accessible from LA 106. It is less developed than the other two areas. It includes a boat launch, a dock, a meeting room and a barbeque pavilion, which makes this area ideal for day visitors. The Louisiana State Arboretum, located within Chicot State Park, is home to a magnificent mature beech-magnolia forest and features an outdoor classroom and several miles of nature trails with labeled plant life native to Louisiana.

location.directions: The park is located at 3469 Chicot Park Road, Ville Platte, LA 70586 in South Central Louisiana.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: St. Johns Rock Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for winter. The campground typically operates seasonally, with availability resuming in early January.
payload.short_description: An eight-site ORV-focused campground in Savage River State Forest near Finzel, offering direct trail access for off-road vehicle enthusiasts in the mountains of western Maryland.
payload.medium_description: St. Johns Rock Campground is a small, specialized facility in Savage River State Forest that caters to off-road vehicle enthusiasts. The eight campsites provide direct access to the St. Johns Rock ORV Trail system, with some sites accommodating pop-up campers, trailers, or RVs while others are tent-only. Located in the mountainous terrain of Garrett County near Interstate 68.
payload.long_description:
St. Johns Rock Campground opened in 2017 as part of Maryland's effort to expand off-road vehicle recreation opportunities on state forest lands. Located in Savage River State Forest near the town of Finzel in Garrett County, this specialized campground features eight sites designed specifically for ORV enthusiasts seeking direct trail access.

The campground serves as a base camp for riders exploring the St. Johns Rock ORV Trail system, which features crushed gravel surfaces with light elevation changes and rock crawl obstacles. The sites vary in configuration, with some able to accommodate pop-up campers, trailers, or RVs, while others are designated for tent camping only. A large parking area provides space for vehicles and trailers.

Situated in the mountainous western region of Maryland just south of Interstate 68, the campground offers a rustic experience in the dense forests characteristic of this area. The facility includes vault toilet facilities and is part of Maryland's growing network of public land recreation areas managed by the Department of Natural Resources.

location.directions: Located in Savage River State Forest south of Interstate 68. Take the Finzel exit off I-68 near the Allegany and Garrett County line.

address.full: 96 Old Beall School Rd, Frostburg, MD 21532

payload.name: Troy Meadow Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through November. Potable water is currently unavailable; campers must bring their own water supply. No trash collection; pack it out. Campfires may be prohibited depending on current fire danger level.
payload.short_description: High-elevation OHV-friendly campground at 7,800 feet in Sequoia National Forest with 73 first-come, first-served sites, vault toilets, bear boxes, and access to off-highway vehicle trails.
payload.medium_description: Troy Meadow Campground sits at 7,800 feet elevation in Sequoia National Forest, offering 73 campsites on a first-come, first-served basis. The campground connects directly to OHV trails and features paved parking spurs, bear boxes, picnic tables, and vault toilets. Fish Creek runs along the rear of the campground providing stream fishing opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Troy Meadow Campground is a high-elevation destination at 7,800 feet in the Kern River Ranger District of Sequoia National Forest. The campground offers 73 sites accommodating tents and RVs with no posted trailer length limit, making it popular with both tent campers and larger rigs. Paved parking spurs, picnic tables, and bear boxes are provided at sites, with vault toilets available throughout.

The campground connects directly to OHV trails, making it a hub for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts exploring the surrounding forest. Fish Creek runs along the rear of the campground, offering stream fishing opportunities. The area provides classic high-elevation forest camping with relatively heavy usage during peak season.

Access is via paved roads either 53 miles northeast of Kernville via Mountain 99 and Sherman Pass Road (22S05), or 34 miles west of Highway 395 via Nine Mile Canyon Road (J41). All camping is first-come, first-served at $17 per night. Campers must pack out all trash as there is no trash collection service.

location.directions: 53 miles northeast of Kernville via Mountain 99 and Sherman Pass Road (22S05), or 34 miles west of Highway 395 via Nine Mile Canyon Road (J41). Paved roads throughout.

payload.name: Pataha Cg
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May through fall. No reservations required; first-come, first-served. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water supply. Camping limited to 14 days within any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground in the Umatilla National Forest offering fishing access to stocked Pataha Creek and hunting opportunities in the Blue Mountains.
payload.medium_description: Pataha Campground is a small, free primitive campground in the Umatilla National Forest near Pomeroy, Washington. The campground sits along Pataha Creek, which is stocked with fish each spring, making it a popular spot for anglers. Fish weirs have been installed to aid fish passage through a culvert. The site also provides access to hunting in the surrounding Blue Mountains.
payload.long_description:
Pataha Campground is a quiet, primitive campground located in the Umatilla National Forest in southeastern Washington's Blue Mountains. The campground sits along Pataha Creek, which receives annual fish stocking each spring. Fish weirs have been installed to assist fish passage through a culvert in the creek, making this a worthwhile destination for anglers seeking trout.

The campground offers basic facilities with a single vault toilet but no potable water, so campers should plan to bring their own water supply. There is no fee to camp here, making it an accessible option for budget-conscious visitors. The surrounding area provides opportunities for hunting and exploring the scenic Blue Mountains landscape.

Access is via Forest Service Road 42 and Pataha Spur Road, approximately 35 minutes southeast of Pomeroy. The campground sees light use, offering a peaceful setting for those seeking solitude in the forest.

location.directions: From Pomeroy, Washington (35 minutes): Take 15th Street south to Highway 128 and continue for 13.2 miles. Continue onto Forest Service Road 42 (Iron Springs Road) for 2.5 miles. The road turns slightly right and becomes Ruchert Road; continue 0.2 miles. Turn right onto Pataha Spur Road and arrive at the campground in 1.2 miles.

payload.name: Winnie Dam Campground - Usace
payload.status_description: The campground is open and accepting reservations. Operating season runs from early May through mid-October. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: USACE campground on the Mississippi River near Lake Winnibigoshish with 22 electric sites, showers, and excellent walleye fishing in northern Minnesota.
payload.medium_description: Winnie Dam Campground is a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers facility located walking distance from the Mississippi River near Lake Winnibigoshish. All 22 sites feature 30/50 AMP electric hookups with water. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, a dump station, boat ramp, and playground. The 67,000-acre Lake Winnie offers premier fishing for walleye, perch, and musky.
payload.long_description:
Winnie Dam Campground is a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers facility situated at the outlet of Lake Winnibigoshish on the Mississippi River, approximately 14 miles northwest of Deer River, Minnesota. The campground offers 22 sites, all equipped with 30/50 AMP electric hookups and water. Facilities include flush toilets, showers (code required from host), drinking water, a dump station, picnic shelter, and playground.

The surrounding area features a forest of mixed hardwoods and towering red pines, home to wildlife including nesting bald eagles, porcupines, black bears, and chipmunks. Wild blackberries, raspberries, and blueberries grow seasonally on the forest floor. A boat ramp provides access to the Mississippi River near the picnic shelter, with the closest Lake Winnie boat access located 1 mile northeast down Plug Hat Road.

Lake Winnibigoshish spans 67,000 acres and is one of Minnesota's premier fisheries, offering excellent opportunities for walleye, perch, and musky. The lake remains mostly undeveloped and is surrounded primarily by public land, particularly the Chippewa National Forest.

location.directions: From Deer River, Minnesota, take Highway 2 west for one mile. Turn right on Highway 46 and go 12 miles. Turn left on Itasca County 9 and continue 2 miles, then turn left at signs and follow to the campground.

payload.name: Cowan Lake Cabins
payload.status_description: The cabins are currently open and accepting reservations. Cabins are available year-round. Book through ReserveOhio.com or call (866) 644-6727.
payload.short_description: Fully equipped cabins nestled in a wooded setting at Cowan Lake State Park, featuring two bedrooms, full kitchens, and easy access to lake activities and nature trails.
payload.medium_description: Cowan Lake State Park offers 21 fully equipped cabins in a peaceful, wooded setting near the Nature Center. Each cabin includes two private bedrooms, a full kitchen with dishes and cookware, bathroom with shower, heating and air conditioning, and all linens. Outside, each cabin has a charcoal grill and picnic table. Two cabins are ADA-accessible, some offer partial lake views, and select cabins feature gas fireplaces. Three cabins are designated pet-friendly.
payload.long_description:
Cowan Lake State Park's cabin area provides a comfortable retreat for families and couples seeking the outdoors without sacrificing modern conveniences. The 21 cabins are tucked into a scenic wooded setting just a short walk from the Nature Center, offering privacy while remaining close to park amenities including swimming, fishing, sailing, kayaking, archery, disc golf, and hiking trails.

Cabins come in three tiers: 11 standard cabins sleeping four people, 9 preferred cabins sleeping six with some featuring gas fireplaces, and 2 ADA-accessible cabins sleeping five. All cabins are fully furnished with two private bedrooms, a complete kitchen with dishes, cookware, and small appliances, a bathroom with shower, heating and air conditioning, and TV. Bed, bath, and kitchen linens are provided. Each cabin has parking, a charcoal grill, and a picnic table. A seasonal commissary stocks camping essentials and rental gear.

Three standard cabins are pet-friendly, allowing guests to bring their dogs. The park sits on 700-acre Cowan Lake, known for its clear water and sailing opportunities. Reservations are made through ReserveOhio.com or by calling the reservation center.

location.directions: The cabins are located at Cowan Lake State Park, 1750 Osborn Road, Wilmington, Ohio 45177.

payload.name: Hay Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours daily. First-come, first-served, no reservations. No potable water available. Mandatory food storage required due to bear activity.
payload.short_description: Primitive 7-site campground in the Little Belt Mountains with fishing access to the South Fork of the Judith River and nearby ATV trails.
payload.medium_description: Hay Canyon Campground offers 7 sites in a quiet setting within the Little Belt Mountains. The campground provides access to fishing on the South Fork of the Judith River and scenic ATV trails. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water. Mandatory bear-resistant food storage is required.
payload.long_description:
Hay Canyon Campground is a small, lightly-used campground tucked into the Little Belt Mountains of the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest. The 7 sites sit near the South Fork of the Judith River, providing convenient access for anglers targeting trout. ATV and motorbike enthusiasts will find scenic trails in the surrounding area.

This is a primitive campground with vault toilets but no potable water. Campers must bring their own drinking water. The area sees bear activity, and mandatory food storage in approved containers is required. All food must be removed from the area after eating.

Access is via 17 miles of gravel road from Utica. The maximum recommended trailer length is 30 feet. Stays are limited to 16 days. The campground operates first-come, first-served at $10 per night.

location.directions: At Hobson on US Highway 87, turn into town and follow Montana Highway 239 to Utica. At Utica, turn left onto a county gravel road. Travel 17 miles southwest to campground.

payload.name: Lion Creek Outfitter
payload.status_description: Operating season and current status unknown. Similar outfitter camps in Flathead National Forest typically operate on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees. Contact the Swan Lake Ranger District at (406) 837-7500 for current conditions.
payload.short_description: Primitive horse camp in Flathead National Forest used by outfitters accessing the Bob Marshall Wilderness via Lion Creek drainage.
payload.medium_description: Lion Creek Outfitter is a primitive horse camp in the Flathead National Forest near the Bob Marshall Wilderness. The site serves as a staging area for stock users and outfitters accessing the Lion-Palisade Trail #25, which follows Lion Creek drainage for 13 miles and climbs 3,400 feet to Lion Creek Pass.
payload.long_description:
Lion Creek Outfitter is a primitive horse camp located in the Flathead National Forest in Lake County, Montana. The site serves outfitters and stock users accessing the backcountry via the Lion-Palisade Trail #25, which follows the Lion Creek drainage into the Bob Marshall Wilderness Complex.

The trail climbs approximately 3,400 feet over 7.3 miles to Lion Creek Pass, with the full trail extending 13 miles. The area is heavily used by permitted outfitters running pack trips into the Bob Marshall Wilderness. Stock users should bring weed-free certified hay as required on all Forest Service lands in Region One.

This is a primitive backcountry staging area with minimal developed facilities. Campers should be self-sufficient with water, feed for stock, and all supplies needed for wilderness travel.

location.directions: From Kalispell, Montana, take Highway 83 south for approximately 50 miles to Condon. Turn east onto Lion Creek Road (Forest Service Road 561) and continue for about 6 miles to reach the campground.

links.title: Flathead NF Horse Riding and Camping

payload.name: Umapine Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May through September. The campground is not maintained during the off-season. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own water supply. First-come, first-served with $10/night fee paid at the self-service pay station.
payload.short_description: Rustic OHV-focused campground in ponderosa pine forest, serving as the staging area for 140+ miles of Winom-Frazier trails in Wallowa-Whitman National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Umapine Campground is a rustic 8-site campground nestled between Cuuyem and Umapine Creeks in a ponderosa pine forest west of Vey Meadows. It serves as the primary staging area for the Winom-Frazier OHV trail system, offering off-road enthusiasts access to more than 140 miles of challenging trails. The campground features 5 single sites and 3 group sites with a large adjacent parking lot ideal for loading and unloading OHV equipment.
payload.long_description:
Umapine Campground sits in the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, positioned between Cuuyem and Umapine Creeks amid ponderosa pines. This rustic facility caters primarily to off-highway vehicle enthusiasts, functioning as the central staging area for the Winom-Frazier OHV trail network with access to over 140 miles of trails ranging from beginner-friendly to technically challenging.

The campground offers 8 sites total: 5 single-family sites and 3 group sites, one of which is a pull-through configuration accommodating larger rigs. A large parking lot adjacent to the campground provides convenient loading and unloading space for OHV equipment. Each site includes a picnic table, and vault toilets are available on-site.

This is a primitive, self-service campground with no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Payment of $10 per night for single sites is handled at the on-site pay station. The campground operates seasonally from May through September and is not maintained during the off-season.

location.directions: From La Grande, Oregon: Travel north on Interstate 84 for about 8 miles to Exit 252 toward Ukiah/Hilgard on Highway 244. Travel west on Highway 244 towards Ukiah for 23 miles to Forest Road 5160. Turn left on Forest Road 5160 and go 8 miles to the campground and OHV trailhead entrance on the right side of the road.

payload.name: Echo Bay Rv Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations are made directly through the concessionaire, not Recreation.gov. The Echo Bay boat launch is currently closed due to low water levels; Callville Bay launch is the nearest alternative. High fire danger restrictions are in effect parkwide but campfires remain permitted within developed campground fire rings.
payload.short_description: Full-hookup RV park on Lake Mead's north shore with 55 paved sites, marina access, and proximity to Valley of Fire State Park.
payload.medium_description: Echo Bay RV Village is a concessioner-operated RV park on the Overton Arm of Lake Mead, offering 55 full-hookup sites with 30/50 amp electric, water, and sewer. The park includes showers, laundry, a small camp store, and free WiFi. A boat launch and marina are adjacent. The secluded location provides access to Valley of Fire State Park and the submerged ruins of historic St. Thomas.
payload.long_description:
Echo Bay RV Village sits on the northwestern shore of Lake Mead along the Overton Arm, accessible via Northshore Road from either Las Vegas or Overton. The 55-site RV park is operated by Lake Mead Mohave Adventures as an authorized NPS concessioner. All sites are paved back-in spaces with full hookups including 30 or 50 amp electric, water, and sewer connections. Amenities include modern restrooms with showers, laundry facilities, free WiFi, trash service, and a small convenience store in the office complex.

The park caters exclusively to RVs with no tent camping permitted. Most sites include a picnic table and fire ring. Pets are welcome with a two-pet maximum per site on leash. Nearby attractions include the free boat launch at Echo Bay Marina, Valley of Fire State Park, and the ruins of St. Thomas visible when lake levels drop.

Reservations are made directly through the concessionaire rather than Recreation.gov. The adjacent Echo Bay Campground is a separate NPS-managed facility with tent/RV sites but no hookups.

location.directions: From Las Vegas, take I-15 north to exit 75 for Valley of Fire/Lake Mead. Turn right onto Northshore Road (NV-167) and continue approximately 50 miles east to Echo Bay Road. Turn right and follow signs to Echo Bay RV Village. From Overton, take NV-169 south to Northshore Road, then west to Echo Bay Road.

links.title: Echo Bay RV Park (Lake Mead) Official Website

alerts.title: Willow Beach Area Temporarily Closed from Storm Damage - Temple Bar Rd 1 lane open at mile marker 22
alerts.content: Saturday morning's storm caused flooding that damaged roads and made them impassable. Staff are fixing the roads and restoring access as quickly as possible. South Cove open. Pearce Ferry has reopened. Temple Bar Rd one lane now open.

alerts.title: Hemenway Harbor Boat Ramp Extension Starting June 2 - Reduced Launch Lane Capacity - Expect Delays
alerts.content: Boaters who want to launch at Hemenway Harbor this summer will experience delays at the ramp on busy days. The nearby PWC launch is open to boats during the project. Callville Bay, Echo Bay, Temple Bar, and South Cove launches are open on Lake Mead.

alerts.title: Government Wash closure to vehicle access and overnight camping
alerts.content: Government Wash Road and 8.0 Mile Road will be blocked, and motor vehicle access and overnight camping in the area will be prohibited. Hiking, biking, and shoreline access by boat for recreation within 100 feet of the shoreline will remain available.

alerts.title: Goldstrike Canyon, Arizona Hot Springs, White Rock Canyon, and Liberty Bell Arch Seasonal Closure
alerts.content: The annual seasonal trail closures are in effect due to hazardous heat. Temperatures can exceed 120 degrees in the canyons. Goldstrike and Arizona hot springs remain open but must be accessed by boat on Lake Mohave. These trails will reopen in early fall.

alerts.title: Fire Restrictions - HIGH FIRE DANGER
alerts.content: Currently prohibited: 1) fires/campfires outside of developed rec. site (e.g. campground) 2) Campfires in areas posted “no campfires” or near marinas and launch ramps 3) Smoking outside of an enclosed vehicle; discarding cigarettes outside of ashtray

alerts.title: Harmful Algae Blooms Spotted on the Shoreline of Lake Mohave
alerts.content: Avoid swimming where bright green algae is floating on the water. Keep pets away from the water. For more information and photos click the ‘more’ link.

payload.name: Van Damme Sp Group Camping Area
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Spring through fall reservations are strongly recommended and available up to six months in advance through ReserveCalifornia. A temporary single-lane bridge provides access to east-side campsites; large trailers may have difficulty navigating the 10-foot-wide crossing.
payload.short_description: Group camping site at Van Damme State Park on the Mendocino Coast, offering a secluded forest setting with access to Fern Canyon trails and a protected cove beach.
payload.medium_description: Van Damme State Park's group camping area accommodates larger parties in a second-growth redwood and fir forest setting along the Mendocino Coast. The single group site provides access to the park's signature attractions including Fern Canyon, the Pygmy Forest, and a sheltered beach cove at the mouth of Little River. Reservations are handled through ReserveCalifornia.
payload.long_description:
Van Damme State Park's group camping area is located three miles south of the village of Mendocino on Highway 1. The park's campground sits in a lush canyon setting among second-growth coastal redwoods, Douglas fir, and a fern-lined understory along Little River. The single group site shares the campground's infrastructure including restrooms with showers, potable water, and an RV dump station.

The park is best known for Fern Canyon Trail, a 2.5-mile path following Little River through dense fern groves, and the Pygmy Forest, where acidic soils and hardpan create a stunted forest of mature yet miniature cypress and pine trees accessible via boardwalk. The day-use beach area at the river mouth offers tide pooling, kayak access, and diving opportunities in the adjacent Van Damme State Marine Conservation Area.

A temporary single-lane bridge (10 feet wide, 53 feet long) currently provides access to east-side campsites. Groups with large trailers should inspect the bridge before crossing and may need to park in the beach lot. Firewood must be purchased on-site; gathering dead wood is prohibited.

location.directions: From Mendocino, drive three miles south on Highway 1. The park entrance is on the left (east) side of the highway.

links.title: Van Damme State Park Official Page

payload.name: Pine Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 8. Operates early May through Labor Day. Single sites are $30/night; senior and access pass holders receive 50% off camping fees.
payload.short_description: Lakeside Forest Service campground on Pine Lake with swimming beach, vault toilets, and hand-pump water in Manistee National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Pine Lake Campground sits on the shore of 156-acre Pine Lake in Michigan's Manistee National Forest. The federally-owned west shore features wetlands where bald eagles nest, while the gravel-bottomed beach offers shallow wading ideal for families. A small campground with vault toilets and hand-pump drinking water, it provides rustic lakeside camping with swimming and boating access.
payload.long_description:
Pine Lake Campground occupies a scenic spot on the shores of Pine Lake, a 156-acre glacially-carved lake in Michigan's Manistee National Forest. The campground sits along the federally-protected western shore, where swampy wetlands provide habitat for bald eagles that have nested in the area for years. The eastern shore is lined with private cabins visible through the pine and hardwood forest.

The day-use area features a gravel-bottomed beach that stays shallow far out into the lake, making it excellent for swimming. A boat launch provides access for anglers and paddlers. Facilities are rustic: vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. The campground operates seasonally from early May through Labor Day.

Sites are spread through a wooded setting that provides semi-privacy. The campground is reached via a dirt road that terminates at the lake, offering a secluded feel despite being only about 20 miles east of Manistee.

location.directions: From Manistee, travel east on M-55 for 17 miles. Turn right and travel south on Bosschem Rd./CR-F669 for 1 mile. Turn right and travel west on Pine Lake Rd. for 3 miles. Road terminates at the site.

payload.name: Lake Cleveland Campground - West Side
payload.status_description: Closed for the season due to snow. The campground typically opens in early to mid-July once late-season snowdrifts clear from the access road and campground. The season runs through September.
payload.short_description: High-alpine first-come, first-served campground at 8,300 feet elevation on the west shore of Lake Cleveland in Idaho's Sawtooth National Forest, offering 9 sites with vault toilets and no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Lake Cleveland Campground - West Side sits at 8,300 feet in a scenic alpine basin below Mt. Harrison in the Sawtooth National Forest. The 9 first-come, first-served campsites offer proximity to the lake for fishing, swimming, and non-motorized boating. Vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but campers must bring their own drinking water. The steep, winding access road and tight turnaround make this loop unsuitable for trailers.
payload.long_description:
Located in a stunning alpine setting at 8,300 feet elevation, Lake Cleveland Campground - West Side occupies the western shore of its namesake lake in a basin beneath 9,240-foot Mt. Harrison. The campground sits near timberline surrounded by alpine wildflower meadows, with expansive views north across the Snake River Plain and south into Utah and Nevada.

The West Side loop offers 9 campsites available strictly on a first-come, first-served basis. Each site includes a picnic table, and vault toilets serve the area. There is no potable water; campers must bring their own supply. The steep terrain and very tight turnaround make this loop unsuitable for trailers and large RVs. Payment of $10 per night can be made on-site via the Recreation.gov mobile app's Scan and Pay feature, though campers should download the app before arrival due to limited cellular service.

Fishing, swimming, and non-motorized boating are popular activities on the lake. A 14-day camping limit per 28-day period applies. Motorized boats and horses are prohibited.

location.directions: From Interstate 84, take exit 216 and follow State Highway 77 south approximately 18 miles through Declo and Albion to Howell Canyon Road. Turn west at the Pomerelle Ski Area sign and drive up Howell Canyon Road another 7 miles. The road is steep and winding.

links.title: USFS Lake Cleveland Campground - West Side

payload.name: San Angelo State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The water/electric campgrounds will close September 1, 2026 through January 1, 2027 for a construction project. South Shore Gatehouse hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. daily. North Shore gate is locked; campers obtain the code at South Shore check-in.
payload.short_description: Texas state park on O.C. Fisher Reservoir offering diverse camping from full-hookup RV sites to primitive and equestrian camping, with trails, wildlife viewing, and water access.
payload.medium_description: San Angelo State Park sits along the shores of O.C. Fisher Reservoir in west-central Texas, offering over 7,000 acres of rolling mesquite grasslands, rocky outcrops, and shoreline. The park features multiple camping areas including full-hookup RV sites with 30/50 amp electric and water, primitive drive-up sites, and equestrian camping. Campers can enjoy over 50 miles of multi-use trails, fishing, wildlife watching including the official state longhorn herd, and birding opportunities.
payload.long_description:
San Angelo State Park encompasses over 7,000 acres surrounding O.C. Fisher Reservoir in Tom Green County, Texas. The landscape features rolling mesquite grasslands, rocky outcrops, and extensive shoreline access. The park is home to the Official Texas State Longhorn Herd as well as a small bison herd, offering reliable wildlife viewing opportunities directly from park roads.

Camping options span multiple areas across the park's north and south shores. The Red Arroyo camping area on the South Shore is closest to town and offers 40 sites with 30/50 amp electric and water hookups, each featuring a picnic table, fire ring, outdoor grill, and shade shelter. The Bald Eagle area provides 11 similar electric/water sites where horses are permitted when the North Concho area is full. The North Concho Equestrian area has 10 sites with pens for horses. Primitive drive-up camping is available at 33 sites scattered across Bald Eagle, Isabel Harte, and Red Arroyo areas.

The park offers over 50 miles of multi-use trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. Fishing and boating are available when water levels permit. Restrooms with showers serve the developed camping areas, and a dump station is on site for RV waste disposal.

location.directions: From San Angelo, take US 67 south toward Mertzon. Turn left onto FM 2288. The park entrance is approximately 5 miles on the right at 362 S. FM 2288, San Angelo, TX 76901.

links.title: San Angelo State Park Main Page

payload.name: Buescher State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. The park often reaches capacity, especially on weekends; reservations are highly recommended. Friday/Saturday reservations require both nights, and holiday weekends (MLK Day, Presidents Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Columbus Day) require a 3-night minimum.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC-built state park near Smithville offering wooded campsites with water and electric hookups, a 30-acre lake for fishing and paddling, and scenic hiking trails through the Lost Pines region.
payload.medium_description: Buescher State Park occupies 1,017 acres of rolling hills covered in the distinctive Lost Pines ecosystem near Smithville, Texas. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, the park features 32 electric/water campsites, 20 water-only sites, and 5 primitive walk-in sites surrounding a scenic 30-acre lake. Campers can fish, paddle, hike, or bike between Buescher and neighboring Bastrop State Park via a 13-mile connecting trail.
payload.long_description:
Buescher State Park preserves a striking section of the Lost Pines, an isolated stand of loblolly pines separated from the main East Texas pine belt by roughly 100 miles of post oak savanna. The 1,017-acre park sits in Bastrop County near the small town of Smithville and showcases classic CCC-era stonework throughout its facilities, including a group hall, pavilion, and several screened shelters.

Camping options range from developed electric/water sites in the Cozy Circle and Oak Haven loops to tent-focused water-only sites in the Lakeview area and primitive walk-in sites for those seeking a quieter experience. Every site includes a fire ring with grill and picnic table. Restrooms with showers serve all camping areas. A park store stocks gifts and basic supplies.

The 30-acre lake anchors the park's recreation, supporting fishing for bass, catfish, and sunfish as well as non-motorized boating. A 13-mile trail connects Buescher to Bastrop State Park through rolling piney woods, popular with hikers and mountain bikers. Wildlife viewing is excellent, with white-tailed deer, armadillos, and diverse birdlife frequenting the area.

location.directions: From Austin, take TX-71 east toward Bastrop. Continue through Bastrop and turn right onto TX-21 east toward Smithville. After approximately 2 miles, turn right onto FM 153/Park Road 1. Follow Park Road 1 for about 1 mile to the park entrance.

payload.name: Bittersweet Wild Lakes Campgrounds
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Operating dates are April 30 through November 1. Reservations required via wisconsin.goingtocamp.com.
payload.short_description: Five primitive paddle-in campsites spread across four remote wilderness lakes in northern Wisconsin's Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest.
payload.medium_description: The Bittersweet Wild Lakes Area offers five secluded paddle-in campsites on Prong Lake, Smith Lake, Oberlin Lake, and Bittersweet Lake. This 2,553-acre wilderness area is accessible only by canoe or kayak, with no motors permitted on any of the lakes. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and nearby open-air toilet.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest northeast of Minocqua, the Bittersweet Wild Lakes Area provides one of Wisconsin's most remote camping experiences. The five designated primitive campsites are spread across four wilderness lakes: Sunken Rowboat on Prong Lake, Loon Song on Smith Lake, Sunset Point on Oberlin Lake, and Big Rock and Trapper's Cabin on Bittersweet Lake.

Access is exclusively by paddle; no motors of any kind are permitted on these lakes. The road to the boat launch parking lot is rough, and a four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended. Each campsite accommodates up to six people and includes a tent clearing, picnic table, and fire ring, with an open-air pit toilet located nearby. There is no potable water, so campers must pack in all drinking water.

Reservations are required during the main season (late April through early November) and can be made through wisconsin.goingtocamp.com up to 11 months in advance. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.

location.directions: Located northeast of Minocqua, north of Highway 70, east of Arbor Vitae, Wisconsin. The road to the boat launch parking lot is rough; a four-wheel-drive vehicle is recommended.

links.title: WI DNR NHAL State Forest Camping

payload.name: Sand Pond Campground And Pavilion Pine Log State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica.
payload.short_description: Primitive-style campground with 20 RV/tent sites featuring electric and water hookups, showers, dump station, and fishing pier in Florida's first state forest, about 14 miles north of Panama City Beach.
payload.medium_description: Sand Pond Campground offers 20 back-in RV/tent sites with 30/50-amp electric and water hookups in Pine Log State Forest, Florida's oldest state forest acquired in 1936. The campground features a bathhouse with showers, dump station, fishing pier, and pavilion. Sites include fire rings and picnic tables, with equipment lengths accommodating up to 42 feet depending on the site.
payload.long_description:
Sand Pond Campground is located in Pine Log State Forest, Florida's first state forest, acquired in 1936 and named for Pine Log Creek which runs through its approximately 7,000 acres. The forest comprises diverse natural communities including sandhills, flatwoods, cypress ponds, and titi swamps that support a variety of indigenous wildlife and plant species.

The campground offers 20 back-in RV/tent sites with 30/50-amp electric and water hookups. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with maximum equipment lengths varying from 23 to 42 feet depending on the specific site. A bathhouse with restrooms and showers serves campers, and a dump station is available for RV waste disposal.

Recreational opportunities abound, including fishing from the on-site pier, hiking, mountain biking, canoeing, swimming, and wildlife observation. The campground is located approximately 14 miles north of Panama City Beach, making it a convenient base for exploring both the forest and the Gulf Coast.

location.directions: Located at 5583-A Longleaf Road, Ebro, FL 32437, approximately 14 miles north of Panama City Beach.

payload.name: Birch Grove
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 2 through October 31. Sites are available first-come, first-served with some sites reservable through Recreation.gov. Firewood must originate within 25 miles or be certified heat-treated to prevent invasive pest spread.
payload.short_description: Rustic lakeside campground on East and West Twin Lakes in the Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest, featuring 16 sites with fire rings and picnic tables, vault toilets, and drinking water.
payload.medium_description: Birch Grove Campground is a quiet, rustic campground located between 22-acre East Twin Lake and 16-acre West Twin Lake, just 8 miles west of Washburn. The campground offers 16 sites including two double sites, each with a fire ring and picnic table. Amenities include drinking water and vault toilets. Sites can accommodate RVs up to 35 feet. Fishing opportunities include bass, panfish, and northern pike, and both lakes have boat access for non-motorized watercraft.
payload.long_description:
Birch Grove Campground sits in a scenic woodland setting between East Twin Lake (22 acres) and West Twin Lake (16 acres) in the Washburn District of Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest. The campground provides a peaceful retreat for tent and RV campers seeking a quiet northwoods experience with easy lake access.

The facility includes 16 campsites with defined parking spurs, fire rings, and picnic tables. Some sites include tent pads, and RVs up to 35 feet can be accommodated. Two sites have been converted to double sites with extra capacity. Amenities are basic but adequate: potable drinking water and vault toilets are provided. There are no hookups, showers, or dump station.

Both lakes offer small boat launches suitable for canoes, kayaks, and other non-motorized watercraft. Fishing is popular for bass, panfish, and northern pike. Swimming access points are available along the lakeshore. In late summer, berry picking in the nearby Moquah Barrens is a popular activity. ATVs and UTVs are prohibited in the recreation area.

location.directions: From Washburn: South 1 mile on Hwy 13, west 8 miles on Wannebo Rd, north 2 miles on FR 252, east 1 mile on FR 435.

payload.name: Lake Creek Campground - Entiat River
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Nine sites are reservable through Recreation.gov; nine are first-come, first-served. The access road is narrow with very limited passing areas.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground with 18 sites along the Entiat River in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, offering access to hiking, mountain biking, and OHV trails at 2,200 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Lake Creek Campground sits along the Entiat River at 2,200 feet elevation in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The 18-site campground provides vault toilets, potable water from hand pumps, garbage service, and fire rings and picnic tables at each site. Nine sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while nine are first-come, first-served. Multiple trails for hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking, and dirt biking begin adjacent to the campground.
payload.long_description:
Lake Creek Campground occupies a scenic stretch along the Entiat River in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, about 27 miles up the Entiat River Road from Highway 97A. At 2,200 feet elevation, the open forest setting provides ample sunshine and views of the river as it cascades down the valley toward the Columbia. The campground supports deer, bears, coyotes, and spawning salmon and steelhead.

The 18 campsites are split evenly between reservable (via Recreation.gov) and first-come, first-served. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Two vault toilets and two hand-pump wells with potable water serve the campground, along with garbage service. No hookups, showers, or dump stations are available. Maximum trailer length is 25 feet, and the access road is narrow with limited passing areas.

Three trails depart directly from the campground for hiking, mountain biking, dirt biking, and horseback riding. The Silver Falls National Recreation Trail is a short drive upriver and offers a 1.5-mile loop to spectacular waterfalls. The Entiat River Trailhead, approximately 12 miles further, provides access to the Glacier Peak Wilderness for backpackers and horse riders.

location.directions: From Wenatchee, WA, travel north on US-97A for 14.4 miles to Entiat. Just after the bridge, turn left onto Entiat River Road (County Road #19) and travel 27.4 miles to Lake Creek Campground on the left. County Road #19 becomes Forest Road 51 at mile 27. From Chelan, WA, travel south on US-97A for 19.3 miles to Entiat, turn right just before the bridge onto Entiat River Road, and continue 27.4 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Hidden Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens May 31 and operates through October 14. Water is shut off after September 30. No trash services; pack it in, pack it out.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground nestled in old growth cedar groves along the North Fork of the Clearwater River in northwest Idaho, offering 13 sites with fishing and hiking access.
payload.medium_description: Hidden Creek Campground sits at 3,400 feet elevation in groves of ancient cedar trees along the scenic North Fork of the Clearwater River. The campground offers 13 individual sites and one group tent pad, with vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. Popular activities include river fishing for trout and access to nearby hiking trails.
payload.long_description:
Hidden Creek Campground is a small Forest Service campground tucked into old growth cedar forest along the North Fork of the Clearwater River in northwest Idaho. At 3,400 feet elevation, the site offers 13 individual campsites and one group tent camping pad, making it a favorite for visitors seeking an intimate setting surrounded by towering cedars and the sounds of the river.

The campground provides basic amenities including vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. Trash services are not available, so campers must pack out all garbage. Water is shut off after September 30 each year. The North Fork of the Clearwater River offers excellent fishing opportunities for trout, and several hiking trails are accessible from the area.

Reaching Hidden Creek requires a drive on forest roads. From Superior, Montana, head southeast on Diamond Road toward River Street for 5.5 miles, then continue onto Forest Road 250 and drive southwest approximately 37 miles to the campground. The remote access contributes to the campground's peaceful character.

location.directions: From Superior, MT head southeast on Diamond Rd toward River St for 5.5 miles. Continue onto Forest Rd 250 and drive southwest for approximately 37 miles to campground.

payload.name: Rainy Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Most campgrounds in this area typically open late May to early June depending on snow conditions.
payload.short_description: Small primitive Forest Service campground along Rainy Creek, 10 miles from Lake Wenatchee in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Rainy Creek Campground is a quiet, lightly-used Forest Service campground at 2,100 feet elevation providing access to Rainy Creek. Located off the Little Wenatchee River Road on Forest Road 6701, this primitive campground offers vault toilets but no potable water. The maximum trailer length is 30 feet.
payload.long_description:
Rainy Creek Campground is a small, primitive campground in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, situated about 10 miles from Lake Wenatchee at 2,100 feet elevation. Managed by the Wenatchee River Ranger District, this lightly-used campground provides a peaceful base for exploring the Little Wenatchee River drainage and surrounding forest lands.

The campground offers basic facilities including vault toilets, but campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available on site. Trailers up to 30 feet can be accommodated. The remote location off Forest Road 6701 (Rainy Creek Road) provides a quiet setting away from more crowded recreation areas near Lake Wenatchee.

location.directions: From Leavenworth, travel west on Highway 2 for 15.1 miles to Coles Corner. Turn right onto Highway 207 N and travel 10.5 miles. Continue onto Little Wenatchee River Road for 6.1 miles. Turn left on Forest Road 6701 (Rainy Creek Road) and go about 1 mile to the campground on the right.

address.full: 682 Labyrinth Mountain Fs 6701st Rd, Leavenworth, WA 98826

payload.name: Battle Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the 2026 season due to hazardous trees. Typically operates mid-May through September when open.
payload.short_description: A 50-site developed campground on Highway 36 near Lassen Volcanic National Park at 4,800 feet elevation, offering vault toilets, potable water, fire rings, and tables.
payload.medium_description: Battle Creek Campground is a developed Forest Service campground with 50 sites nestled along Highway 36, approximately 2 miles west of Mineral, CA. At 4,800 feet elevation, it provides convenient access to Lassen Volcanic National Park's hiking trails. Sites include fire rings and picnic tables, with vault toilets and potable water available. No hookups or dump station.
payload.long_description:
Battle Creek Campground is a developed campground in Lassen National Forest with 50 designated sites, located on Highway 36 approximately 2 miles west of Mineral, CA and 38 miles east of Red Bluff, CA. At 4,800 feet elevation, the campground offers a forested mountain setting with each site featuring a fire ring and picnic table.

The campground is positioned as a gateway to Lassen Volcanic National Park, which offers diverse hiking trails and geothermal features. Amenities include vault toilets and potable drinking water from faucets. There are no RV hookups, showers, or dump station facilities. Maximum occupancy is 8 people and 2 vehicles per site.

Quiet hours are enforced from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Dogs are permitted but must remain leashed at all times. Fireworks are prohibited. Payment of $18 per night is required upon arrival and before each subsequent night.

location.directions: From Red Bluff, travel east on Highway 36 for approximately 40 miles. The campground is located 2 miles west of Mineral, CA.

payload.name: Schoolhouse Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Operating dates are April 15 through October 15. Reservations available through Recreation.gov; some sites may be first-come, first-served. Bear-proof food storage containers required.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at Bullards Bar Reservoir with 56 shaded sites, flush toilets, potable water, and excellent access to boating, fishing, and swimming in Tahoe National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Schoolhouse Campground sits at 2,000 feet elevation near Bullards Bar Reservoir in Tahoe National Forest. The campground offers 56 sites (44 single, 12 double) beneath conifer and hardwood forest canopy, with flush toilets, treated potable water, and convenient access to Dark Day Boat Ramp (0.5 miles) and Cottage Creek Boat Ramp (3 miles). The reservoir provides year-round fishing for warm and cold water species, along with boating, water skiing, and swimming opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Schoolhouse Campground occupies a forested hillside along Marysville Road near the shores of Bullards Bar Reservoir in Tahoe National Forest. At 2,000 feet elevation, the 56-site campground (44 single sites, 12 double sites) sits under a mixed canopy of conifers and hardwoods that provides ample shade throughout the camping season. The campground features flush toilets, one vault toilet, and treated potable water.

Bullards Bar Reservoir stretches over 16 miles with more than 60 miles of shoreline at maximum capacity. The reservoir supports year-round fishing for both warm and cold water species, and serves as a popular destination for motorized and non-motorized boating, water skiing, and swimming. Steep shoreline slopes limit beach access, but boaters can find swimming spots throughout the reservoir.

The campground provides direct access to several non-motorized trails including the 0.7-mile Schoolhouse Trail, 1-mile 7 Ball Trail, 3.8-mile 8 Ball Trail, and 1.6-mile Rebel Ridge Trail. Dark Day Boat Ramp is approximately half a mile away, with Cottage Creek Boat Ramp about 3 miles distant. Supplies are available at the marina and in nearby Camptonville, North San Juan, and Dobbins.

location.directions: From Nevada City, travel approximately 20 miles on Highway 49 to Marysville Road, turn left onto Marysville Road and continue approximately 4 miles to Schoolhouse Campground. From Camptonville, drive south on Highway 49 to Marysville Road, turn right, and continue 4 miles.

photos.name: Aerial view of Bullards Bar Reservoir

payload.name: Upper Buck Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May 15 through October 15. First-come, first-served with no reservations. No fee. No potable water available. Pack-out all trash.
payload.short_description: Rustic free campground with five secluded sites along Buck Creek in the Fremont-Winema National Forest, 30 minutes southwest of Silver Lake, Oregon.
payload.medium_description: Upper Buck Creek Campground offers rustic seclusion at 5,000 feet elevation in the Fremont-Winema National Forest. Five primitive campsites with fire rings and picnic tables sit among ponderosa and lodgepole pines, aspens, and willows adjacent to open meadows and marshland. No fees, no potable water, and pack-out trash policy. Vault toilet on site.
payload.long_description:
Upper Buck Creek Campground is a quiet, primitive forest camp located 30 minutes southwest of Silver Lake, Oregon in the Fremont-Winema National Forest. At approximately 5,000 feet elevation, the campground features five sites nestled among ponderosa pines, lodgepole pines, aspens, and willows, with open meadows and marshland nearby.

This is a free, first-come first-served campground with minimal amenities suited for those seeking solitude. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. A vault toilet is available, but there is no potable water and no trash service, so campers must bring their own water and pack out all garbage. Vehicles must remain at least 200 feet from the creek's edge.

Recreational opportunities include fishing in Buck Creek, wildlife viewing, and plant observation. The campground operates from mid-May through mid-October, with reduced services during the extended season.

location.directions: From Silver Lake, take Highway 31 north for about 1 mile, then turn left on County Road 4-10 (Bear Flat Road). Continue for 11.5 miles. Turn left on Forest Road 2804 and travel 3.4 miles. The campground will be on your left down an unnamed spur and is visible from FR 2804.

payload.name: Chemin-A-Haut State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Swimming pool operates Memorial Day through Labor Day, Thursday through Sunday only.
payload.short_description: Situated on a high bluff overlooking Bayou Bartholomew, this 503-acre site takes its name from the French word meaning "high road".
payload.medium_description: Chemin-A-Haut State Park offers 26 premium campsites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer) on a wooded bluff above Bayou Bartholomew. The campground features a modern bathhouse with showers and coin-operated laundry, a dump station, and access to the park's swimming pool, hiking trails along the bayou, an 8-mile equestrian trail, and kayak rentals on Big Slough Lake.
payload.long_description: Situated on a high bluff overlooking Bayou Bartholomew, this 503-acre site takes its name from the French word meaning "high road". This park offers great fishing, beautiful scenery for Horseback riding and kayaking, a seasonal swimming pool, full hook-up RV Camping, and overnight cabins. There is currently no wi-fi in the campground and deluxe cabins.

location.directions: From Bastrop, take US-425 north approximately 10 miles. The park entrance is on the west side of the highway.

payload.name: Hickey Gap Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees required. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water supply.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground along Mill Creek trout stream in the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, offering year-round first-come, first-served camping near the Cohutta Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Hickey Gap Campground sits alongside Mill Creek, a scenic trout stream, in the Conasauga Ranger District of the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest. This free, primitive campground offers a quiet basecamp for fishing, hiking, and mountain biking in the surrounding Cohutta Wilderness area. Sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted.
payload.long_description:
Hickey Gap Campground is a rustic camping area nestled along the banks of Mill Creek, a clear mountain trout stream in northwest Georgia's Cohutta Wildlife Management Area. The campground takes its name from the Hickey family who once lived in this remote corner of Murray County, just east of the community of Crandall.

This primitive Forest Service campground provides a genuine backcountry experience with minimal development. Campers should come prepared to be self-sufficient as there is no potable water available on site. Each site features a tent pad where tents must be placed, and standard campground amenities typical of developed USFS campgrounds in this forest.

The location makes an excellent basecamp for exploring the surrounding Cohutta Wilderness and WMA. Mill Creek offers stream fishing opportunities, while nearby trails provide access to hiking and mountain biking. The campground enforces quiet hours from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. and prohibits alcohol. Sites are limited to two vehicles each, and the narrow forest road makes it unsuitable for large RVs or trailers over 24 feet.

location.directions: From Chatsworth, GA: Travel north on Highway 411 for 6 miles, turn right on Grassy Street, continue to T intersection, turn right 100 feet, then turn left onto Mill Creek Road (Forest Service Road 630). Continue approximately 6.5 miles and turn right at the campground portal sign.

payload.name: Horseglades Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed. Primary season with full maintenance services runs June 15 through September 15. Reduced services are available September 16 through June 14.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground on the OC&E Trail in Fremont-Winema National Forest, offering access to 100 miles of rail-trail for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding.
payload.medium_description: Horseglade Campground is a free dispersed camping area on the historic Oregon California and Eastern (OC&E) Trail in Fremont-Winema National Forest. Located 40 minutes northwest of Bly, Oregon, it serves as a trailhead for the 100-mile rail-trail system extending from Klamath Falls to Sycan Marsh. The site has a vault toilet, picnic table, campfire ring, and parking with trailer turnaround, but no potable water.
payload.long_description:
Horseglade Campground sits on the Woods Line Spur of the OC&E Trail, a 100-mile multi-use trail built on the historic railbed of the Oregon California and Eastern Railroad. The trail network extends from downtown Klamath Falls east to Bly and north into the scenic Sycan Marsh. From the campground, trail users can head south along Five Mile Creek or travel north toward the Merritt Creek Trestle.

This primitive dispersed camping area provides basic amenities including a vault toilet, picnic table, campfire ring, and a parking area with trailer turnaround capability. There is no potable water, so campers must bring an adequate supply. The campground is free to use and does not require reservations.

The trail is open to hikers, horseback riders, and mountain bikers, making this an ideal basecamp for exploring the high desert landscape of south-central Oregon. Wildlife viewing and fishing opportunities are available in the surrounding area.

location.directions: From the Bly Ranger District Office, take Highway 140 West approximately 3 miles to County Road 1257. Turn right and go approximately 12 miles to Forest Service Road 27. Turn left, go approximately 1.3 miles to the Horseglade campground entrance on the right.

payload.name: Holiday
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open. Gates are locked from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. Check-in is guaranteed after 4 p.m. and checkout is 3 p.m. Credit/debit card payments only. Four-vehicle limit per site.
