payload.short_description: Waterfront campground on the western shore of West Point Lake with 112 sites including electric hookups, flush toilets, showers, and direct lake access for boating and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Holiday Campground sits on a forested peninsula overlooking the 25,900-acre West Point Lake on the Georgia-Alabama border. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers facility offers 112 campsites ranging from primitive tent sites to 50-amp electric sites with water hookups, plus two group camping areas. Amenities include two bathhouses with flush toilets and hot showers, a dump station, laundry facilities, playground, and basketball and tennis courts. The lake provides excellent fishing for bass, catfish, crappie, and bream, with 34 boat ramps around the shoreline.
payload.long_description:
Holiday Campground occupies a scenic peninsula on the western shore of West Point Lake, a 25,900-acre reservoir formed by damming the Chattahoochee River along the Georgia-Alabama state line. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the campground offers 112 individual sites and two group camping areas beneath a canopy of mixed forest that displays outstanding fall foliage. Site options include primitive tent-only spots, standard non-electric sites, and electric sites with either 30-amp or 50-amp service plus water hookups.

Two bathhouses provide flush toilets and hot showers, and a dump station serves RV campers. Additional facilities include laundry rooms, a playground, basketball and tennis courts, and a swimming area. The Lakeside Trail passes nearby for hiking and mountain biking. West Point Lake ranks among the top bass fishing destinations in the Southeast, with crappie, catfish, and bream also abundant. Bank fishing is available at nearby public piers, and 34 boat ramps around the lake provide easy water access.

Gates are locked from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. Check-in is guaranteed after 4 p.m. and checkout is 3 p.m. A four-vehicle limit applies per site, and only credit or debit card payments are accepted on-site. Reservations are handled through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From LaGrange, Georgia, take State Highway 109 west for 7 miles. After crossing the First Lake Bridge, continue another mile and turn left onto Thompson Road. At the next intersection, bear left and follow signs to the park.

payload.name: Max V. Shaul State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Reservations accepted up to 9 months in advance via ReserveAmerica. Walk-in registration available for campsites. Maximum stay is 14 continuous nights. Quiet hours 10 PM to 7 AM.
payload.short_description: A small, quiet 30-site wooded campground in the Schoharie Valley offering tent and trailer camping, showers, hiking trails, and fishing access to Schoharie Creek.
payload.medium_description: Max V. Shaul State Park is a peaceful 30-site wooded campground nestled in the Schoharie Valley at the base of Toepath Mountain. The park features shaded campsites with fire pits and picnic tables, modern restrooms with showers, a playground, hiking trails, and easy access to fishing at Schoharie Creek. This small park is ideal for campers seeking a quiet retreat with basic amenities.
payload.long_description:
Max V. Shaul State Park offers a tranquil camping experience in the scenic Schoharie Valley, approximately 6 miles south of Middleburgh along Route 30. The campground features 30 wooded tent and trailer sites, each equipped with a fire pit and picnic table. Modern restroom facilities with showers are available, making it suitable for families and those who appreciate basic comforts while camping.

The park sits at the base of Toepath Mountain and provides access to hiking trails, a playground, and ball fields for volleyball, basketball, and softball. Anglers can walk through the ball fields to reach Schoharie Creek for fishing. A group campsite accommodating up to 35 people is available by reservation, and a pavilion can be rented for day-use events.

This is a primitive campground with no hookups or dump station, so RV campers should plan accordingly. The quiet atmosphere and wooded setting make it a good choice for tent campers and those with self-contained trailers seeking a low-key getaway in upstate New York.

location.directions: Located on Route 30 approximately 6 miles south of Middleburgh in Schoharie County. The park is in the hamlet of Fultonham.

payload.name: Graham Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates May through September with 15 sites available through Recreation.gov and 10 sites first-come, first-served. The old boat ramp is permanently closed; lake access is by foot only for registered campers.
payload.short_description: Scenic lakeside campground above Vallecito Reservoir in San Juan National Forest with 25 sites, potable water, and access to excellent fishing and hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Graham Creek Campground sits above Vallecito Lake at 7,900 feet in southwestern Colorado's San Juan National Forest. The 25-site campground offers a mix of reservable and first-come, first-served sites with potable water, composting toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables. Scattered ponderosa pines provide partial shade while hillside sites offer lake views. Popular activities include fishing for trout and kokanee salmon, boating, and hiking on nearby North Canyon and East Creek trails.
payload.long_description:
Graham Creek Campground is situated on the east side of Vallecito Reservoir in the San Juan National Forest, offering 25 campsites split between 15 reservable and 10 first-come, first-served. The hillside sites sit about 100 yards from the high-water line at 7,900 feet elevation, with scattered ponderosa pines providing partial shade and thick understory vegetation ensuring privacy between sites. Willow thickets separate the camping area from the lakeshore, with short trails providing foot access to the water.

Vallecito Lake is a premier fishing destination for German brown, cutthroat, and rainbow trout, kokanee salmon, and northern pike. The lake also supports boating, water skiing, and canoeing, with boat rentals available at nearby resorts. Trailered boats must use the boat ramp on the west side of the lake after a Colorado Parks and Wildlife inspection, as the old boat ramp at the campground is permanently closed.

North Canyon Trail begins directly across from the campground, leading through ponderosa pine and aspen forests with a shorter spur to a scenic lake overlook. East Creek Trail starts a quarter-mile up Forest Road 852 and accesses a lightly used drainage popular with fly fishermen pursuing brook trout. Both trails accommodate horseback riders, though horses are not permitted in the campground itself.

location.directions: From Bayfield, travel 14 miles north on County Road 501. Turn right on County Road 501A at the fire station, travel over the dam and continue just over 3 miles to the campground on the east side of Vallecito Reservoir. From Durango, travel 17 miles on Florida Road (County Road 240), turn left onto County Road 501 for 4 miles, then slight right onto Forest Road 603 for about 2.2 miles to the campground entrance.

payload.name: George J. Hatfield State Recreation Area Group Campground
payload.status_description: The group campground is currently open and accepting reservations through ReserveCalifornia. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance of arrival date.
payload.short_description: Scenic group campground on the Merced River in California's San Joaquin Valley, featuring a large barbecue pit, picnic facilities, and river access for fishing and kayaking.
payload.medium_description: George J. Hatfield State Recreation Area Group Campground sits along the Merced River in California's Central Valley, offering a dedicated group camping area for parties of 9-50 people. The group site features a large barbecue pit, sinks with running water, serving areas, picnic tables, and benches. The park provides over a mile of river frontage with opportunities for fishing, kayaking, wading, and nature study.
payload.long_description:
Located on the banks of the Merced River about 20 miles south of Modesto, George J. Hatfield State Recreation Area Group Campground provides a dedicated space for group camping in California's San Joaquin Valley. The park was established in 1953 when former California Lieutenant Governor and State Senator George J. Hatfield donated the land. The group campground accommodates 9-50 people and includes a large barbecue pit, sinks with running water, serving areas, picnic tables, and benches.

The park offers more than a mile of river frontage, making it ideal for fishing, kayaking, river wading, and nature study. All camping is tent-only, with campers parking in a general lot and walking to their sites. Facilities include flush toilets, drinking water, and coin-operated showers. Dogs are allowed in the campground on leashes 6 feet or shorter but are prohibited on trails and beaches.

Reservations are made through ReserveCalifornia and can be booked up to six months in advance. The group site is priced at $150 per night. Day use hours are 8 a.m. to sunset.

location.directions: From Interstate 5, take the Newman exit into Newman and continue east on County Road J-18 for five miles. The park entrance is just past the San Joaquin River bridge.

links.title: California State Parks - George J. Hatfield SRA

payload.name: Lost Johnny Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season and opens May 21, 2026. Operating season runs mid-May through September. All 5 sites are reservable through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Small 5-site campground on Hungry Horse Reservoir in the Flathead National Forest, offering vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables with stunning Rocky Mountain views near Glacier National Park.
payload.medium_description: Lost Johnny Campground is a small, reservable campground on the west shore of Hungry Horse Reservoir in Montana's Flathead National Forest. Situated at 3,600 feet elevation in the Rocky Mountains, the campground features 5 tent and RV sites, each with a picnic table and fire ring with grill. Vault toilets and bear-resistant food containers are provided, but there is no potable water on site. The campground is approximately 18 miles southwest of Glacier National Park's West Glacier entrance.
payload.long_description:
Lost Johnny Campground sits along the west shore of Hungry Horse Reservoir, a 27,750-acre body of water backed by the 10th highest dam in the United States. Located high in the Rocky Mountains west of the Continental Divide, the campground offers spectacular views and direct access to water-based recreation including fishing for cutthroat trout, swimming, and boating.

The campground has 5 sites, all reservable through Recreation.gov. Each site includes a picnic table and campfire ring with grill. Vault toilets and bear-resistant food containers are provided. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own supply. Garbage services are available at nearby Lost Johnny Point. A concrete boat ramp can be accessed at Lost Johnny Point Campground to the northeast or Doris Point Boat Launch to the northwest.

Home to lynx, grizzly bear, and bull trout, this area provides a true wilderness experience. A food storage order is in effect requiring proper storage of all food, garbage, and attractants. The maximum trailer length is 22 feet, making this campground best suited for tents and smaller trailers. The 16-day consecutive stay limit allows extended visits to explore the surrounding forest and nearby Glacier National Park.

location.directions: Turn off U.S. Highway 2 at milepost 144 and follow the West Side Hungry Horse Reservoir Road (Forest Road 895) across the Hungry Horse Dam. The campground is 6.5 miles south of the dam. The road is paved to the site.

links.title: USFS Flathead NF - Lost Johnny Campground

photos.name: The view looking west from Lost Johnny campground

payload.name: Wallace State Park Shelter
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter, not an overnight camping facility. The shelter is available for reservation at $40/day or on a first-come, first-served basis. Reservations can be made online 30 days to 12 months in advance, or by contacting the park at 816-632-3745 for dates within 30 days.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter overlooking Lake Allaman at Wallace State Park, accommodating up to 50 people with covered seating, grill, and electricity.
payload.medium_description: The Open Shelter at Wallace State Park is a day-use picnic facility overlooking the park's six-acre Lake Allaman. The shelter accommodates up to 50 people and features eight picnic tables, a group grill, two electrical outlets, and a nearby water fountain. A vault toilet is located about 100 feet away. The shelter can be reserved for $40/day or used on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved.
payload.long_description:
The Open Shelter at Wallace State Park is a day-use picnic facility designed for group gatherings, family reunions, and picnics. Located overlooking the scenic six-acre Lake Allaman, the 30.5' x 20.4' covered structure can accommodate up to 50 people and provides a shaded setting for outdoor meals and events.

The shelter is equipped with eight picnic tables, a group grill for cooking, two electrical outlets, and has a water fountain nearby. A vault toilet is located approximately 100 feet away, and additional recreational amenities include a horseshoe pit (100 feet) and playground (300 feet) within easy walking distance.

This is a day-use facility only and is not intended for overnight camping. Wallace State Park offers separate campgrounds with basic, electric, and walk-in tent sites for those seeking overnight accommodations. The park is located seven miles south of Cameron in Clinton County, less than an hour from Kansas City.

location.directions: Located at 10621 NE Highway 121, Cameron, MO 64429, seven miles south of Cameron in Clinton County.

payload.name: Coleman Lake Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Operating dates are March 15 through December 8. First-come, first-served; no advance reservations. Check-in at 2:00 p.m., check-out at 12:00 p.m. An Occupancy and Use Forest Order is currently in effect.
payload.short_description: A renovated 39-site campground with electric and water hookups, nestled in the Talladega Mountains with a 21-acre lake, bathhouses, and Pinhoti Trail access.
payload.medium_description: Coleman Lake Recreation Area offers 39 campsites with water and electrical hookups in Alabama's Talladega National Forest. The renovated facility features flush toilet bathhouses, a 21-acre lake for fishing and swimming, and direct access to the Pinhoti Trail. Seven sites and two comfort stations are fully ADA accessible. Most sites accommodate RVs up to 35 feet.
payload.long_description:
Coleman Lake Recreation Area is a well-appointed campground in the Shoal Creek District of Talladega National Forest. The recently renovated facility provides 39 campsites, all equipped with water and electrical hookups, serving both tent campers and RV users. Two modern bathhouses with flush toilets offer convenience, and potable water is available throughout the campground.

The centerpiece is a 21-acre lake supporting fishing, swimming, and non-motorized boating. The campground also serves as an access point for the Pinhoti Trail, making it a solid base for hikers exploring the Talladega Mountains. A 29-unit picnic area and a reservable shelter accommodate day visitors.

Accessibility is a priority here, with seven campsites and two comfort stations designed for visitors with disabilities. Most sites handle RVs up to 35 feet. The campground operates first-come, first-served from mid-March through early December.

location.directions: Travel Highway 78 east from Heflin approximately 8 miles. Turn onto County Road 61 and travel 8.7 miles. Turn onto Forest Service Road 500 and travel 2 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Beaver Lake State Park Equipment Rental
payload.status_description: This is a day-use equipment rental service (kayaks), not a campground. No overnight camping is available at this specific facility. For camping, see Beaver Lake State Park Campground.
payload.short_description: Kayak rental service at Beaver Lake State Park in North Dakota, offering half-day and full-day rentals with paddles and life vests included.
payload.medium_description: This is a kayak rental facility at Beaver Lake State Park, not a campground. Equipment can be reserved online at reservendparks.com or rented on a first-come, first-served basis. Rentals include paddles and life vests.
payload.long_description:
Beaver Lake State Park Equipment Rental is a kayak rental service located within Beaver Lake State Park near Wishek, North Dakota. This is not an overnight camping facility. Kayaks are available for rent at $32 per half day or $50 per full day, with paddles and life vests included.

The equipment rental service operates seasonally and allows visitors to explore the 100-acre lake. Reservations can be made online through reservendparks.com or by calling the park directly. First-come, first-served rentals are also available.

For overnight camping at Beaver Lake State Park, visitors should look for the separate campground listings which include 25 modern campsites with electric and water hookups, 5 primitive sites, and 3 seasonal cabins.

location.directions: Located at Beaver Lake State Park, 3850 70th St. SE, Wishek, ND 58495.

payload.name: Lake Of The Ozarks State Park Yurt Lodging
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required with full payment at booking. Self-check-in via provided code. Modern restroom and showerhouse available April 1 through October 31; vault toilets and water available year-round near the check station.
payload.short_description: Yurt lodging at Missouri's largest state park offers a unique glamping experience with climate-controlled circular structures, fire rings, and access to showers within walking distance.
payload.medium_description: Lake of the Ozarks State Park Yurt Lodging provides a comfortable alternative to tent camping in Missouri's largest state park. Each yurt sits on a wooden platform with locking doors, three large windows, and a dome skylight. Inside, guests find a futon, bunk bed, dorm-size refrigerator, microwave, air conditioning, and heat. Outside each unit is a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. A modern restroom and showerhouse are within walking distance during the main season, with vault toilets and water available year-round.
payload.long_description:
Lake of the Ozarks State Park Yurt Lodging offers a distinctive glamping experience in Missouri's largest state park. The yurts are circular structures with fabric covers over sturdy wooden frames, situated on elevated wooden platforms with decking and locking doors. Each unit features three large windows and a dome skylight that provides natural light and a view of the stars. Inside, guests will find a futon and bunk bed (sleeping up to five people, maximum six occupants), a dorm-size refrigerator, microwave, coffee table, air conditioner, and heater for year-round comfort.

Located in campground sections 1 and 2, the yurts provide a semi-primitive experience without running water inside the units. A modern restroom and showerhouse is within walking distance and operates from April 1 through October 31. During the off-season, vault toilets and water are available near the campground check station. Outside each yurt, guests have a picnic table, fire ring for campfires, and a barbecue grill.

Guests must bring their own linens, sleeping bags, lanterns, cooking utensils, and water containers. Open-flame cooking is prohibited inside the yurts, but non-flame devices like griddles and Crock-Pots are permitted. Yurts A and B are ADA accessible and participate in the Cabins for Canines program, allowing up to two dogs with additional fees. Reservations are made by phone with full payment due at booking, and self-check-in is available via a provided code.

location.directions: The park is located at 403 Highway 134, Brumley, MO 65017. Yurt lodging is situated in campground sections 1 and 2.

links.title: Lake of the Ozarks State Park Main Page

payload.name: Karick Lake North Youth Group Camp Blackwater River State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required and can be made up to 11 months in advance through floridastateforests.reserveamerica.com. Drought conditions and burn bans may affect camping; check the Florida Forest Service Burn Ban Public Dashboard before booking.
payload.short_description: Youth group campsite on 65-acre Karick Lake in Blackwater River State Forest, featuring primitive tent camping with nearby restrooms, showers, and lake access for fishing and paddling.
payload.medium_description: Karick Lake North Youth Group Camp is an exclusive youth group camping area in Florida's largest state forest. The primitive group site accommodates up to 25 people and includes fire rings, potable water, and access to restrooms with showers at the adjacent Karick Lake North Campground. Groups can enjoy the 65-acre lake for fishing and paddling with electric motors, plus the 4-mile Karick Lake Loop Trail.
payload.long_description:
Karick Lake North Youth Group Camp provides organized youth groups a dedicated camping experience in the heart of Blackwater River State Forest, located about an hour northeast of Pensacola. The single group site accommodates up to 25 people in a primitive tent camping setting, with potable water available on-site and fire rings for evening campfires. Restrooms with showers are accessible at the nearby Karick Lake North Campground.

The campsite sits alongside the 65-acre Karick Lake, offering excellent opportunities for fishing, canoeing, and kayaking. A boat launch ramp and fishing dock provide easy water access. Electric boat motors only are permitted, and swimming is prohibited. The area is a designated non-hunting zone, though visitors are encouraged to wear fluorescent orange from Thanksgiving through mid-February during hunting season.

Bird watching, wildlife viewing, photography, and nature study are popular activities, with the 4-mile Karick Lake Loop Trail accessible from the recreation area. Youth groups must have adult chaperones, and reservations are required at least two days in advance through the Florida State Forests reservation system.

location.directions: From I-10 Exit 56, take Highway 85 north to Highway 90 in Crestview, head west toward Milligan, turn right onto Highway 4/189 north for 7.7 miles to North Karick Lake sign.

address.full: 7170 Karick Lake Rd N, Baker, FL 32531

payload.name: Columbia Hills State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Horsethief Lake campground operates April through October; closed November through March. Reservations available through washington.goingtocamp.com. Level 1 burn ban currently in effect.
payload.short_description: Columbia Hills Historical State Park offers 18 campsites at Horsethief Lake with partial hookups, showers, and stunning Columbia River Gorge views.
payload.medium_description: Columbia Hills Historical State Park Campground at Horsethief Lake features 18 campsites along the Columbia River Gorge. The campground offers standard sites, partial hookup sites with water and electric, walk-in tent sites, and primitive hiker/biker sites. Amenities include restrooms, showers, drinking water, fire pits, picnic tables, and a dump station. The park is known for Native American petroglyphs, wildflower-covered hills, and access to miles of hiking, biking, and equestrian trails.
payload.long_description:
Columbia Hills Historical State Park Campground is located at the Horsethief Lake area along the scenic Columbia River Gorge in Klickitat County, Washington. The campground provides 18 sites including 4 standard campsites, 8 partial hookup sites with water and electric, 4 standard walk-in tent sites, and 2 primitive hiker/biker sites. Full amenities include restrooms with showers, potable water, fire pits at each site, picnic tables, and a trailer dump station.

The park showcases acres of shrub-steppe landscape with high-desert panoramas and river shoreline. The area is renowned for its Native American rock art, including the famous She Who Watches (Tsagaglalal) petroglyph, accessible via guided tours. North of State Route 14, the Crawford Oaks and Dalles Mountain Ranch trailheads provide access to miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding with views of Mount Hood, Mount Jefferson, and the Columbia River Gorge.

Springtime visitors are rewarded with spectacular wildflower displays, particularly arrow-leaf balsam root and lupine that blanket the hillsides. The Horsethief Lake area also offers fishing, swimming, and a boat launch for water recreation on the Columbia River.

location.directions: From State Route 14 along the Columbia River, the park entrance is located approximately 2 miles east of Dallesport at 8514 Lewis & Clark Hwy, Lyle, WA 98635.

payload.name: Horseneck Beach State Reservation
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. The campground operates from the first week of May through Columbus Day. Reservations available through the Massachusetts DCR camping system.
payload.short_description: Oceanfront campground with 100 sites behind the sand dunes at Horseneck Beach, offering electric hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, and direct access to a two-mile cobblestone beach on Buzzards Bay.
payload.medium_description: Horseneck Beach State Reservation campground features 100 fully paved back-in campsites tucked behind coastal dunes in Westport, Massachusetts. Sites 1-68 offer electric hookups. Amenities include a comfort station with flush toilets and hot showers, a dump station, playground, basketball and volleyball courts, dishwashing station, and a boat ramp. Each site has a paved parking spur, picnic table, fire ring, and grill. The campground provides access to a scenic two-mile cobblestone beach on Buzzards Bay, though dogs are prohibited on the beach from April 1 through September 15.
payload.long_description:
Horseneck Beach State Reservation is a 600-acre coastal park at the southern tip of Westport, Massachusetts, where the Westport River meets Buzzards Bay. The campground sits just behind the dunes, placing campers within easy walking distance of a beautiful two-mile beach known for its unique cobblestone shoreline.

The campground offers 100 fully asphalted back-in campsites with sites 1-68 featuring electric hookups. Every site includes a paved parking spur, picnic table, fire ring, and grill. A modern comfort station provides flush toilets and hot showers. Additional amenities include a dump station, drinking water, playground, basketball and volleyball courts, a dishwashing station, and a boat ramp for accessing Buzzards Bay.

Nine ADA-accessible campsites are available with paved surfaces and accessible paths. Pets are permitted at the campground with proof of rabies vaccination and must remain leashed, though dogs are not allowed on the beach during peak season (April 1 through September 15). The flat, coastal terrain can accommodate RVs up to 42 feet, though all sites are back-in only. Reservations are made through the Massachusetts DCR camping system.

location.directions: From I-195, take Exit 16 to Route 88 South. Follow Route 88 South for 11 miles to its end. Continue following signs for Horseneck Beach. The campground entrance is located beyond the main beach parking lot on the right.

payload.name: Roaring River State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: Open for day-use reservations. Shelters operate 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. April through October and 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. November through March. These are day-use facilities only with no overnight camping. Reserve online 30 days to 12 months in advance or call the park for dates within 30 days.
payload.short_description: Two reservable picnic shelters at Roaring River State Park in Missouri's Ozarks, featuring historic CCC architecture, grills, electricity, and nearby restrooms.
payload.medium_description: Roaring River State Park offers two day-use picnic shelters available for reservation. The River Shelter accommodates up to 75 guests and is ADA accessible, while the historic CCC Shelter holds up to 50 guests. Both include outdoor grills, picnic tables, electrical outlets, and nearby restroom facilities. Shelters can be reserved for $60/day or used free on a first-come, first-served basis when not reserved.
payload.long_description:
Located in Barry County in Missouri's Ozark Mountains, Roaring River State Park Shelters provide covered gathering spaces for groups visiting this popular trout fishing destination. The CCC Shelter, a historic Civilian Conservation Corps structure built with wood and brick, features six picnic tables, two fireplaces, and electricity within its 22' x 45' footprint. The larger River Shelter accommodates up to 75 guests and offers wheelchair accessibility.

These are day-use facilities only, not overnight camping. Operating hours are 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. from April through October and 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. from November through March. The shelters sit within a park known for year-round rainbow trout fishing, seven hiking trails, and a nature center. A playground is approximately 200 yards from the CCC Shelter, with river access about 250 yards away.

location.directions: Located at 12716 Farm Road 2239, Cassville, MO 65625. The park is in Barry County in southwest Missouri, approximately 7 miles south of Cassville via Highway 112.

links.title: Roaring River State Park Main Page

payload.name: Pine Bluff Individual Backpacking Sites
payload.status_description: Open year-round with required backcountry permits obtained through Recreation.gov. Vault toilets, food storage lockers, and non-potable water are available seasonally. No potable water; campers must filter or boil water from Lake Superior or nearby streams.
payload.short_description: Primitive backcountry campsites on a sandy bluff above Lake Superior along the North Country Trail in Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, accessible only by hiking.
payload.medium_description: Pine Bluff offers five individual backcountry campsites situated on a sandy, fern-covered bluff with scattered pine trees overlooking Lake Superior. Located along the North Country Trail within the Beaver Basin Wilderness, these hike-in sites provide direct beach access via a trail at the campground entrance. Backcountry permits are required year-round.
payload.long_description:
Pine Bluff Individual Backpacking Sites occupy a scenic sandy bluff above Lake Superior within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore's Beaver Basin Wilderness. The five designated sites rest in an open, fern-covered area dotted with pine trees, offering both forest shelter and proximity to the lakeshore. A trail from the campground entrance leads down the bluff to the beach and Lake Superior access.

These primitive backcountry sites are accessible only by hiking along the North Country Trail. Each site accommodates 1-6 people with a maximum of 3 tents or hammocks. Campers must set up within 15 feet of their assigned numbered post. Seasonal amenities include vault toilets, non-potable water sources (requiring filtration or boiling), and bear-proof food storage lockers. One designated fire ring is available at the campground area for campfires using only dead and down wood.

A backcountry camping permit is required year-round for all overnight stays. Permits must be obtained through Recreation.gov before arrival. Camping is limited to 3 consecutive nights per site and 14 total nights per calendar year within the lakeshore. Pets are prohibited at all backcountry campgrounds.

location.directions: Access Pine Bluff by hiking the North Country Trail from either Twelvemile Beach Campground to the east or Little Beaver Lake Campground to the west. The sites are located on a sandy bluff just off the trail above Lake Superior within the Beaver Basin Wilderness.

alerts.title: Munising Falls Trail Closed Until Further Notice
alerts.content:
The Munising Falls Trail within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore is closed until further notice.

Approximately 75-feet of the paved trail was washed out April 28th from recent heavy rainfall and seasonal snow melt.

payload.name: Fairview-Riverside State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours are 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, extended to 8 p.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, and holidays. Reservations available through gooutdoorslouisiana.com or by calling 1-833-609-0686.
payload.short_description: Scenic Louisiana state park campground on the Tchefuncte River with 101 sites beneath ancient oak trees, offering water and electric hookups, flush restrooms with showers, and access to fishing and boating.
payload.medium_description: Fairview-Riverside State Park sits on the banks of the Tchefuncte River near Madisonville, Louisiana, beneath a canopy of massive live oak trees. The campground offers 101 sites including premium, improved, and unimproved options with water and electric hookups available. Amenities include bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, a dump station, laundry facilities, playground, boat launch, and nature trails. The park also features the historic 1880s Otis House Museum.
payload.long_description:
Fairview-Riverside State Park occupies a beautiful stretch along the Tchefuncte River in St. Tammany Parish, Louisiana. The campground is shaded by towering live oak trees draped in Spanish moss, creating a quintessential Louisiana bayou atmosphere. With 101 campsites divided among premium, improved, and unimproved loops, the park accommodates everything from tent campers to large RVs up to 55 feet.

The improved and premium sites feature water and electric hookups, while unimproved sites offer a more primitive experience. All campers have access to modern bathhouses with flush toilets, hot showers, and laundry facilities. Two dump stations serve RV campers. Throughout the park you'll find picnic tables, fire rings, and two playgrounds for families.

The Tchefuncte River provides excellent fishing opportunities for bass, bluegill, white perch, bream, and where it meets Lake Pontchartrain, channel catfish, speckled trout, and redfish. A boat launch provides river access, and a waterfront boardwalk extends through the swamp. The quarter-mile nature trail is ADA accessible. History enthusiasts can tour the Otis House Museum, an 1880s sawmill owner's home on the property.

location.directions: Located in Madisonville, Louisiana on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The park is accessible from Interstate 12 via Louisiana Highway 22 or Highway 21.

payload.name: Watermelon Pond Primitive Campsites Goethe State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required via ReserveAmerica. Peak season runs October 1 through May 31. Current drought conditions have prompted burn bans in numerous Florida counties; verify fire restrictions before arrival.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent camping at Watermelon Pond Trailhead in Goethe State Forest, offering 3 tent sites with fire rings and picnic tables near multi-use trails in Alachua County.
payload.medium_description: Watermelon Pond Primitive Campsites is a small, rustic camping area within Goethe State Forest's Watermelon Pond tract. The campground features 3 tent-only sites (max 6 people each) and a group pavilion, all equipped with fire rings and picnic tables. No potable water or electricity is available. A restroom is located at the adjacent trailhead parking area. The site serves as a basecamp for hiking, horseback riding, birding, and wildlife photography on the surrounding multi-use trails.
payload.long_description:
Watermelon Pond Primitive Campsites occupies a separate tract of Goethe State Forest in Alachua County, north of the main forest body near Newberry. This small primitive camping area is co-located with the Watermelon Pond Trailhead, providing direct access to miles of multi-use trails suitable for hiking, horseback riding, and mountain biking. The forest landscape includes pine flatwoods and wetland areas that attract diverse birdlife and wildlife.

The campground offers 3 tent-only sites, each accommodating up to 6 people, plus a pavilion for larger groups (up to 35). Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. Facilities are minimal: a restroom is available at the trailhead parking area, but there is no potable water, showers, or electricity. Campers must bring all water supplies. Reservations are required through ReserveAmerica and can be made up to 11 months in advance.

The area operates year-round with peak season from October through May. Note that pets are only permitted at the pavilion, not at the individual tent sites. Current drought conditions in Florida have prompted burn bans in numerous counties, so campers should verify fire restrictions before arrival.

location.directions: From downtown Newberry, head west on State Road 26 for 1 mile to County Road 337. Turn left (south) on CR 337 and follow it for 6.3 miles. The trailhead entrance is on your left (east side of the road) at a State Forest recreation area sign. Turn in at the sign and follow the road for 0.2 miles to reach the campsites on your left.

payload.name: Rock Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opens May 15, 2026 on a first-come, first-served basis. The typical season runs through mid-October, with the campground transitioning to FCFS in early October. Potable water is turned on in May depending on weather conditions and shut off by September 30 to prevent freeze damage.
payload.short_description: Forested campground on the western shore of Crane Prairie Reservoir offering excellent fishing for rainbow trout, largemouth bass, and wildlife viewing including osprey and bald eagles.
payload.medium_description: Rock Creek Campground sits along the western shore of Crane Prairie Reservoir in Oregon's Deschutes National Forest. The 32-site campground features large, well-spaced sites with many positioned directly on the lakeshore. A boat ramp and fish cleaning stations are available within the campground, providing direct access to the reservoir's excellent fishing for rainbow trout, mountain whitefish, brook trout, and largemouth bass.
payload.long_description:
Rock Creek Campground occupies a scenic stretch of the western shore of Crane Prairie Reservoir along the Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway, approximately 50 miles southwest of Bend. The campground features 32 sites spread across 5 loops, with almost all sites being large and well-isolated from neighboring campers. Many sites sit directly on the reservoir shoreline, offering prime access for anglers and boaters.

Crane Prairie Reservoir is renowned for its fishing opportunities, with Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife managing healthy populations of rainbow trout, mountain whitefish, brook trout, and largemouth bass. The campground includes a boat launch and fish cleaning stations. Beyond fishing, the area provides exceptional wildlife viewing. Sandhill cranes, bald eagles, and osprey frequent the reservoir, while the surrounding forest hosts black-backed woodpeckers, Williamson's sapsuckers, and mountain chickadees. On summer mornings and evenings, visitors may spot Rocky Mountain elk grazing in lakeside meadows.

Nearby Osprey Point offers an interpretive area where visitors can observe osprey nesting platforms erected after natural snags toppled from age. The Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway climbs 66 miles through the Cascade Range, weaving past snow-capped peaks and alpine lakes.

location.directions: From Bend, travel approximately 50 miles southwest on Cascade Lakes Highway (Highway 46). The campground is on the left-hand side of the highway.

payload.name: Walk In The Water Campground Lake Wales Ridge State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All sites require advance reservation through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica. No potable water available; campers must bring their own drinking water. Check current burn ban status before lighting campfires during drought conditions.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground in Lake Wales Ridge State Forest featuring 8 reservable sites with fire rings and picnic tables. No water or hookups; bring your own drinking water.
payload.medium_description: Walk In The Water Campground offers 8 primitive campsites within Lake Wales Ridge State Forest, a biodiversity hotspot in central Florida. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings, with port-a-potties and a dumpster on site. The campground provides access to hiking trails including the Big Bay Trail and Scrub Jay Loop, as well as equestrian trails. RV sites accommodate vehicles up to 15 feet. No potable water or hookups are available.
payload.long_description:
Walk In The Water Campground is a primitive camping area nestled within the 26,713-acre Lake Wales Ridge State Forest in Polk County, Florida. This unique forest is recognized as a global hotspot for rare and endangered species, featuring scrub and sandhill ecosystems with one of the highest concentrations of imperiled plants in the United States. The campground offers 8 reservable sites: sites 1-3 and 5 are tent-only, while sites 4 and 6-8 accommodate both RVs and tents with 15-foot back-in parking.

Each site features a picnic table and fire ring. Facilities include two port-a-potties and a dumpster for trash disposal. There is no potable water, electricity, or hookups available, so campers must bring their own drinking water. Recreational opportunities include hiking on the Big Bay Trail and Scrub Jay Loop Trail, fishing, hunting, bicycling, horseback riding on designated equestrian trails, and wildlife viewing.

Pets are permitted on leashes up to 10 feet in length. All sites are ADA-accessible. Quiet hours are from 10 PM to 7 AM. There is a 14-night maximum stay, after which campers must leave for a minimum of 3 nights before booking again. Bears and raccoons frequent the area, so proper food storage is essential. During hunting seasons, visitors should wear day-glo orange for visibility.

location.directions: Located at 6110 Walk-in-the-Water Road, Lake Wales, FL 33898, approximately 44 miles southeast of Lakeland.

address.full: 5550 Walk In The Water Rd, Frostproof, FL 33843

links.title: Lake Wales Ridge State Forest - Florida Forest Service

payload.name: Lower Chatanika State Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Both Olnes Pond and Whitefish campgrounds are currently closed for the season. Seasonal services including potable water, restrooms, and refuse disposal are not operational during closure. Opening dates are weather-dependent and have not been announced.
payload.short_description: Scenic Alaska Interior campground featuring Olnes Pond and Whitefish campgrounds along the Elliott Highway, offering fishing, boating access to the Chatanika River, and a 16-acre rainbow trout stocked pond.
payload.medium_description: Lower Chatanika State Recreation Area encompasses 400 acres at mile 10.5-11 of the Elliott Highway near Fairbanks. The recreation area contains two campgrounds: Olnes Pond with 15 sites surrounding a 16-acre pond stocked with Rainbow Trout and Arctic Grayling, and Whitefish Campground with 25 sites providing boat launch access to the Chatanika River and Minto Flats. Both campgrounds operate first-come, first-served at $20 per night.
payload.long_description:
Lower Chatanika State Recreation Area sits in Alaska's Interior about 30 minutes north of Fairbanks along the Elliott Highway. The 400-acre recreation area features two distinct camping areas: Olnes Pond Campground at mile 10.5 with 15 campsites surrounding a peaceful 16-acre pond stocked with Rainbow Trout and Arctic Grayling, and Whitefish Campground at mile 11 with 25 sites providing boat launch access to the Chatanika River.

The Whitefish boat launches are popular with hunters accessing Minto Flats via the Chatanika River. Both campgrounds offer potable water, toilets, picnic sites, and refuse disposal during the operating season. A reservable picnic shelter is available at each location, and Olnes Pond also has a public-use cabin available for reservation.

Recreational opportunities abound year-round including camping, fishing, picnicking, hiking, berry picking, boating, ATV and snowmachine use, ice fishing, dog sledding, night sky viewing, and cross-country skiing. The maximum camping stay is 15 days. Winter maintenance is not provided at Whitefish Campground.

location.directions: From Fairbanks, take the Steese Highway north which becomes the Elliott Highway. Olnes Pond Campground is at mile 10.5 and Whitefish Campground is at mile 11. From George Parks Highway, take Robert Mitchell Expressway to Steese Highway and continue to Elliott Highway.

payload.name: Bloxham Pavilion Lake Talquin State Forest
payload.status_description: This is a day-use facility only. No overnight camping is permitted. The pavilion is available for reservation year-round for daytime gatherings, cookouts, and fishing access.
payload.short_description: Bloxham Pavilion is a day-use only facility on a high bluff overlooking Lake Talquin, featuring a picnic pavilion, boat ramp, and restrooms. No overnight camping is permitted.
payload.medium_description: Bloxham Pavilion at Lake Talquin State Forest is a day-use only facility located on a scenic high bluff on the southwest side of Lake Talquin. The site includes a picnic pavilion with a large grill, a small boat ramp and dock, restrooms, and water. This is an ideal location for afternoon cookouts and fishing, but overnight camping is not allowed.
payload.long_description:
Bloxham Pavilion at Lake Talquin State Forest is a reservable day-use facility situated on a scenic high bluff overlooking the southwest side of Lake Talquin, approximately 20 minutes west of Tallahassee. The facility is designed for group gatherings and outdoor recreation, featuring a covered picnic pavilion with a large grill, picnic tables, restrooms, and potable water. A small boat ramp and dock provide access to Lake Talquin for fishing and boating.

This is strictly a day-use facility with no overnight camping permitted. The maximum capacity is 300 people, and groups exceeding 150 attendees are required to arrange and pay for portable toilets. There is no electricity at the facility. Reservations require picking up keys at the Lake Talquin State Forest office at 865 Geddie Road in Tallahassee, and the gate must be locked upon departure.

location.directions: From Tallahassee, head west approximately 20 minutes. The Lake Talquin State Forest office is located at 865 Geddie Road, Tallahassee, FL, where keys must be picked up for the facility.

payload.name: Hell Hole Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from approximately June through October, with official dates of May 15 through November 1 depending on snow conditions. There is no potable water available; campers must bring their own drinking water.
payload.short_description: Remote walk-in tent campground with 10 sites near Hell Hole Reservoir in Eldorado National Forest, offering vault toilets and fire rings but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Hell Hole Campground is a rustic walk-in tent campground with 10 sites located near Hell Hole Reservoir in the Georgetown Ranger District of Eldorado National Forest. The campground features vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables but has no potable water available. Trailers are not recommended due to limited parking space.
payload.long_description:
Hell Hole Campground sits in the scenic Hell Hole Upper Country area of Eldorado National Forest, providing access to Hell Hole Reservoir and the surrounding backcountry. This walk-in tent campground offers 10 primitive sites equipped with fire rings and picnic tables. The campground has vault toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own drinking water or a water filter.

The campground is reached via a 22-mile drive east of Georgetown on Wentworth Springs Road, then 29 miles northeast on Forest Highway 2 (Eleven Pines Road). Due to limited parking space, trailers are not recommended. The reduced fee of $10 per night reflects the lack of water services. This is a first-come, first-served campground with no reservations available.

location.directions: 22 miles east of Georgetown on Wentworth Springs Road, then 29 miles northeast on Forest Highway 2 (Eleven Pines Road) to just before Hell Hole Reservoir.

payload.name: Lums Pond State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round with sites available for reservations. Construction for a new 14-cabin complex is underway through March 2027, with activity occurring 7am-4pm Monday through Friday. Expect vehicle traffic and noise in the campground area during construction hours.
payload.short_description: Delaware's largest freshwater pond offers year-round camping with 68 full-hookup RV sites, tent sites, and yurts in a recently renovated campground recognized as the best RV park in the state.
payload.medium_description: Lums Pond State Park campground surrounds Delaware's largest freshwater pond. The recently renovated campground features 68 full-hookup sites with electric, water, and sewer, plus 10 tent-only sites and yurts. Amenities include modern bathhouses with showers, dump station, camp store, and an on-site dog park. The park offers extensive recreation including hiking, mountain biking, fishing, kayaking, and a zip line adventure course.
payload.long_description:
Lums Pond State Park campground sits along the shores of Delaware's largest freshwater pond, created in the early 1800s as a feeder pond for the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal. The campground underwent a $5.6 million renovation that upgraded all sites with full hookups and modern amenities, earning recognition from Reader's Digest as the best RV park in Delaware.

The campground offers 68 full-hookup sites with 30- or 50-amp electric, water, and sewer connections suitable for RVs up to 50 feet. Ten tent-only sites provide a more primitive experience, while yurts offer unique accommodations with bunk beds, a futon, and outdoor deck seating. Each campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring. Modern bathhouses with individual shower rooms and ADA-accessible facilities are located throughout the campground.

Beyond camping, the park offers outstanding recreation on the 200-acre pond including fishing, kayaking, and stand-up paddleboarding. The trail system provides miles of hiking and mountain biking, while Go Ape! zip line and treetop adventure course delivers aerial thrills. An off-leash dog park welcomes four-legged family members.

location.directions: From I-95, take Exit 1A toward DE-896 South. Continue on DE-896 South for approximately 2 miles, then turn left onto Howell School Road. The park entrance will be on your right at 1068 Howell School Road, Bear, DE 19701.

payload.name: Gull Lake Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season May 1 through October 15. Showers and potable water available May 14 through October 15. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Main playground closed for construction; alternative playgrounds available near the picnic shelter and swimming beach. North park entrance closed; use south entrance only. Only certified firewood permitted.
payload.short_description: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers campground on Gull Lake with 39 wooded electric sites, showers, swimming beach, and boat access on Minnesota's famous Gull Chain of Lakes.
payload.medium_description: Gull Lake Recreation Area is a well-maintained Army Corps of Engineers campground at the outlet of Gull Lake, the largest lake in the 10-lake Gull Chain. The 39 wooded sites offer 30/50-amp electric service, picnic tables, and fire rings. Facilities include flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, swimming beach, boat ramp, and hiking trails connecting to the Paul Bunyan State Trail. Popular for walleye, northern pike, and bass fishing.
payload.long_description:
Gull Lake Recreation Area sits on the Gull River at the outlet of Minnesota's famous Gull Lake, carved by glaciers retreating from Canada. As part of the Mississippi Headwaters Project operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this 39-site campground provides a quality camping experience with well-spaced wooded sites, each equipped with 30 or 50-amp electric hookups, picnic tables, and fire rings. A centrally located showerhouse with flush toilets serves the campground, with potable water and a dump station near the entrance.

Recreational opportunities abound. Anglers target the lake's abundant walleye, northern pike, bass, and panfish populations. The swimming beach, two canoe launches, and boat ramp provide water access, while a paved shoreline fishing platform and fish cleaning station serve anglers. A self-guided interpretive trail winds through undeveloped forest, and the City of East Gull Lake's paved multi-use trail connects to the 100-mile Paul Bunyan State Trail.

The area lies minutes from Brainerd, Baxter, and Nisswa, offering 520 holes of golf, amusement parks, a zoo, and shopping. Watchable wildlife includes bald eagles, white-tailed deer, river otters, songbirds, and loons.

location.directions: From the intersection of MN 210 and MN 371 in Baxter, drive north 5.8 miles. Turn left on County Road 125 (Gull Lake Dam Road). Follow the signs approximately 3 miles. Turn left into the campground at the playground.

address.full: 1293 Gull Lake Dam Rd, Brainerd, MN 56401

links.title: City of East Gull Lake Info

photos.name: Sunset view over Gull Lake from the hiking trail
Catch of the day at the upper fishing pier
Swimming beach and picnic area use during a holiday weekend

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Our main playground near the campground is closed for construction. A new playground is coming soon! In the meantime, you may find our other playgrounds across the dam near the picnic shelter and by the swimming beach.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Only firewood certified, or approved by a state or federal natural resource agency is permitted. Certified firewood is available for purchase in the campground. Any unauthorized firewood in the campground may be removed and destroyed by Corps of Engineers staff.

payload.name: Granite Creek
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. The campground typically opens mid-May and operates through September 30. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. Reservations available via Recreation.gov up to 180 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Small creekside campground in Chugach National Forest at Turnagain Pass with 19 sites, vault toilets, and excellent fishing and hiking access along the Seward Highway.
payload.medium_description: Granite Creek Campground is a 19-site loop campground set in the Kenai Mountains at Turnagain Pass, about 64 miles south of Anchorage on the Seward Highway. Sites are nestled among spruce trees near the confluence of Granite Creek and Six-Mile Creek, with most sites positioned right beside the glacier-fed creek. The campground offers vault toilets, a hand pump, dumpster, fire rings, picnic tables, and bear boxes at each site.
payload.long_description:
Granite Creek Campground sits at the confluence of Granite Creek and Six-Mile Creek in the Chugach National Forest, surrounded by the towering peaks of the Kenai Mountains. The 19-site loop campground is positioned among spruce trees with most sites offering creekside locations and mountain views. Bears frequent the area, so bear boxes are provided at each site for food storage.

Recreation opportunities abound from this location. Dolly Varden fishing is available directly in Granite Creek, while nearby Six-Mile Creek offers Class V whitewater for experienced rafters and kayakers. The Johnson Pass North Trailhead, located about a mile east, provides access to a well-maintained 23-mile trail with breathtaking vistas suitable for hiking or mountain biking. A paved bike path along the Seward Highway extends five miles south to the Hope Highway.

Wildlife viewing is excellent, with moose, black and brown bears, mountain goats, marmots, and snowshoe hares commonly spotted. The area is also known for raspberries and wildflowers during summer months.

location.directions: Located at mile 62.6 of the Seward Highway, 64.4 miles south of Anchorage and 62.6 miles north of Seward. The campground is about 1 mile past the Johnson Pass North Trailhead.

payload.name: Texas Springs Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for seasonal closure. The campground typically reopens October 15 at noon and operates through mid-April. First-come, first-served only; pay fees at the automated pay station using credit/debit card.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground in the hills above Furnace Creek in Death Valley, offering great views and shade trees. Open seasonally from mid-October through mid-April.
payload.medium_description: Texas Springs Campground sits in the hills above Furnace Creek in Death Valley National Park, providing 106 first-come, first-served sites with scenic views and some tree cover. Each site includes a fire grate and picnic table. The campground operates seasonally from mid-October through mid-April to avoid the extreme summer heat. Facilities include flush toilets, potable water, and a dump station when open. No generators are allowed.
payload.long_description:
Texas Springs Campground occupies a hillside location above the historic Furnace Creek area in Death Valley National Park. The elevated position provides sweeping desert views and scattered trees that offer welcome shade during cooler months. All 106 sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations available.

Each campsite features a fire grate and picnic table on a gravel pad accessed by paved roadways. The campground has two comfort stations with flush toilets, and potable water is available from spigots when the campground is operational. A dump station serves RV campers. No hookups are provided at any sites.

The campground enforces a strict no-generator policy to preserve the desert quiet. Quiet hours run from 10 PM to 7 AM. Pets are permitted but must be leashed and attended at all times. Maximum stay is 30 consecutive days. Fires are allowed only in the provided NPS fire grates; no wood gathering is permitted within the park.

location.directions: Located off CA-190 in Furnace Creek. From the Furnace Creek Visitor Center, turn right on CA-190 and drive past Furnace Creek Ranch. Just beyond the Ranch on the left is the campground access road.

photos.name: The spring which gives the campground its name is a short walk away.
Historic restrooms at the Texas Spring campground.

payload.name: Wood-tikchik State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Permits ($350) required for camping at Nishlik, Slate, Upnuk, and Chikuminuk Lakes, and for Tikchik River floats. Reservations available through Reserve America up to 7 months in advance. Access by floatplane, boat, or foot only.
payload.short_description: Remote fly-in wilderness camping in America's largest state park, spanning 1.6 million acres of pristine lakes and rivers in southwest Alaska.
payload.medium_description: Wood-Tikchik State Park is the largest state park in the nation at nearly 1.6 million acres. Accessible only by floatplane, boat, or foot, this remote wilderness offers primitive camping along twelve interconnected lakes and connecting rivers. Camping permits ($350) are required for specific lake areas and the Tikchik River float.
payload.long_description:
Wood-Tikchik State Park encompasses nearly 1.6 million acres of roadless wilderness in southwest Alaska, north of Dillingham. The park features two separate lake systems connected by the Wood River, offering world-class fishing for rainbow trout, arctic char, grayling, and all five species of Pacific salmon. Access is exclusively by floatplane, boat, or foot, with air charter services available from Dillingham.

Camping is primitive throughout the park with a strong emphasis on low-impact practices. The Agulukpak River Campground, located on the south side of Lake Beverly, offers one of the few developed facilities with picnic tables and an outhouse, though stays are limited to three nights. Elsewhere, campers can stay up to 10 consecutive days at any undeveloped location before relocating at least one mile.

Permits ($350) are required for camping at Nishlik, Slate, Upnuk, or Chikuminuk Lakes, floating the Tikchik River, and for groups over 20 people. Reservations are available through Reserve America up to seven months in advance. The park operates on pack-it-in, pack-it-out principles with no potable water, trash service, or developed facilities outside the Agulukpak Campground.

location.directions: Accessible only by floatplane, boat, or foot. Most visitors fly from Dillingham via air charter. Lake Aleknagik State Recreation Site provides boat launch access ($10 fee) to the lower lake system.

payload.name: Cross Ranch State Park Primitive Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations available 95 days in advance. Water access in the primitive loop remains active through winter. The dump station water shuts off October 1 annually.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground along the Missouri River in central North Dakota offering 22 walk-in tent sites with vault toilets and year-round water access.
payload.medium_description: Cross Ranch State Park Primitive Campground offers 22 primitive campsites along the west bank of the Missouri River. Sites feature nearby vault toilets and year-round water access in the primitive loop. Showers are available at the Visitor Center. The campground operates year-round with reservations available 95 days in advance through reservendparks.com.
payload.long_description:
Cross Ranch State Park Primitive Campground sits on the west bank of the Missouri River, offering a true backcountry camping experience in central North Dakota. The 22 primitive sites are walk-in tent camping spots ideal for those seeking a more rustic outdoor experience. Two group primitive sites are also available for larger parties at the same nightly rate per unit.

The primitive loop maintains water access year-round, and vault toilets are located near the campsites. Campers can access shower facilities at the Visitor Center throughout the year. The park encompasses diverse habitats including mixed-grass prairie and Missouri River bottomland forest, providing excellent opportunities for wildlife viewing, hiking, and experiencing the natural beauty of the Northern Great Plains.

The park transitions to limited services in fall through spring, with the dump station water shutting off October 1. However, the main campground and primitive loop water remain active through winter. Check-in is at 4:00 PM and check-out at 3:00 PM.

location.directions: From Bismarck, take ND-200A west to ND-200, then head north toward Center. The park is located on the west side of the Missouri River, approximately 9 miles south of Washburn off River Road. Address: 1403 River Rd, Center, ND 58530.

links.title: Cross Ranch State Park Official Page

payload.name: Aiken'S Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served. No reservations, no fees. 14-day stay limit. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground along the Klamath River in Six Rivers National Forest with fire rings and picnic tables at each site. No water, toilets, or services.
payload.medium_description: Aikens Creek West is a small, primitive campground in the Orleans Ranger District of Six Rivers National Forest, located along the scenic Klamath River corridor. The campground offers 10 first-come, first-served sites with fire rings and picnic tables. There are no facilities: no toilets, no potable water, and no trash service. Campers must be fully self-sufficient and pack out all garbage.
payload.long_description:
Aikens Creek West Campground sits along the Klamath River in the Orleans Ranger District of Six Rivers National Forest. This primitive, dispersed-style campground provides access to the river for fishing and water activities, with the nearby Aikens Creek Trail offering additional river access.

The campground has approximately 10 sites that accommodate trailers up to 35 feet. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, but that's the extent of the amenities. There are no toilets, no potable water, and no garbage service. Campers must bring all their own water and pack out all trash.

The campground is free and operates year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. A 14-day stay limit applies. Pets are permitted on leash. Dates may vary due to wet weather conditions affecting road access.

location.directions: Located in the Orleans Ranger District of Six Rivers National Forest along the Klamath River corridor near Orleans, California.

payload.name: San Onofre Sb Bluff Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations through ReserveCalifornia. Entrance gate locks nightly from 10 PM to 6 AM during camping season.
payload.short_description: Cliffside coastal campground at San Onofre State Beach with 175 sites atop sandstone bluffs and direct beach access via rugged trails.
payload.medium_description: San Onofre Bluffs Campground sits atop dramatic sandstone bluffs overlooking 3.5 miles of undeveloped beachfront south of San Clemente. Six rugged dirt trails lead from the bluff-top campsites down to the beach below, popular with swimmers and surfers. All sites include fire pits and picnic tables, with chemical toilets, cold outdoor showers, and an RV dump station on-site.
payload.long_description:
San Onofre Bluffs Campground occupies a stunning stretch of Southern California coastline three miles south of San Clemente along the old Pacific Coast Highway. The 175-site campground sits atop sandstone bluffs with panoramic ocean views, and six rugged trails provide access to 3.5 miles of undeveloped beach below. Established in 1971 under Governor Ronald Reagan, this remains one of the most scenic coastal camping destinations in Orange County.

The campground accommodates tents, RVs, and trailers up to 36 feet. Every site comes equipped with a fire pit and picnic table. Facilities include chemical toilets, cold outdoor showers, and an RV dump station, though no hookups are available. Fifteen sites are designated as ADA accessible, including 13 tent sites and 2 RV/trailer sites, with generally accessible parking and restrooms throughout.

Dogs are welcome on leash throughout the campground but are prohibited on the beach and inside buildings. The entrance gate locks nightly from 10 PM to 6 AM during camping season. A beach wheelchair is available during peak season (June 1 through September 15) by reservation through the lifeguard tower.

location.directions: From Interstate 5, take the Basilone Road exit approximately 3 miles south of San Clemente. The campground entrance is off Old Pacific Coast Highway.

links.title: San Onofre State Beach - CA State Parks

payload.name: Whitefish Lake Rustic Campground
payload.status_description: Open May 8 through October 1, 2026. First come, first served with no reservations. Active emergency road closures on Forest Road 166 (Cross River Road) due to spring washouts may affect access routes.
payload.short_description: Free 3-site rustic campground on Whitefish Lake serving as the trailhead for the Timber-Frear Canoe Route, with 11 backcountry campsites scattered across 5 interconnected lakes outside the BWCAW.
payload.medium_description: Whitefish Lake Rustic Campground offers a free, primitive camping experience on the Superior National Forest. The three drive-in sites feature vault toilets, fire rings, and tent pads, but no potable water or trash service. The campground doubles as the launch point for the Timber-Frear Canoe Route, connecting nine lakes via portages for an excellent paddling adventure outside the Boundary Waters. OHV riders can also access Grant-In-Aid trails directly from the campground.
payload.long_description:
Whitefish Lake Rustic Campground is a small, no-fee campground tucked into the Superior National Forest in Lake County, Minnesota. With only three drive-in sites, it provides a quiet base for paddlers, anglers, and OHV enthusiasts. The campground sits at the trailhead of the Timber-Frear Canoe Route, which connects Whitefish Lake to four other lakes via portages, with 11 backcountry campsites distributed along the route. This area offers a wilderness paddling experience similar to the Boundary Waters but without the permit requirements.

Facilities are minimal: each site has a fire ring and tent pad, and a vault toilet serves the campground. There is no potable water, so bring your own or treat lake water. Trash service is not provided; all garbage, including fish remains, must be packed out. Boat access is carry-down only with no trailer launch available.

Two of the three sites can accommodate vehicles over 21 feet, though the forest roads leading in may challenge larger rigs. Dogs are welcome but must be leashed (6-foot max), kept in a tent or vehicle at night, and their waste packed out. Sites are first come, first served with a maximum of nine people per site.

location.directions: From MN 61 northeast of Schroeder: Between Schroeder and the entrance to Temperance River State Park, turn inland on FR 343 (Temperance River Rd.). Drive 4 miles to a T intersection with FR 166 (The "600" Road). Turn left, drive 1 mile to FR 346. Turn right on FR 346. Drive 5.5 miles to FR 170 (The Grade). Turn left on FR 170. Drive 2 miles to FR 348 (Whitefish Lake Access). Turn right on FR 348. Drive 4.5 miles to Whitefish Lake Rustic Campground.

payload.name: Hidden Springs Camp
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens Memorial Day weekend and operates through late September. Reservations are available through ReserveCalifornia. Some sites available first-come, first-served for single-night stays.
payload.short_description: Secluded tent campground in old-growth redwoods along Avenue of the Giants with 154 forested hillside sites, flush toilets, and hot showers.
payload.medium_description: Hidden Springs Campground sits on a forested hillside along the Avenue of the Giants, approximately 5 miles south of the Humboldt Redwoods Visitor Center and just south of Myers Flat. The 154-site campground offers a quieter alternative to nearby Burlington, with each site equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and bear box. Flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers are available, along with potable water.
payload.long_description:
Hidden Springs Campground occupies a shaded hillside in the heart of Humboldt Redwoods State Park, surrounded by towering coast redwoods and mixed forest. The campground's 154 sites provide a more secluded camping experience compared to the park's other developed campgrounds, with good spacing between sites and dense vegetation offering privacy. Each site comes equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and bear-resistant food locker.

The campground provides modern amenities including flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers. Potable water is available throughout. A seasonal kiosk operates during peak season from 11am to 5pm. The South Fork of the Eel River is accessible nearby via a trail across the Avenue of the Giants, leading to a popular swimming hole at Eagle Point.

Hidden Springs operates seasonally, typically from Memorial Day weekend through September. Site-specific reservations are available through ReserveCalifornia, with some sites offered on a first-come, first-served basis for single-night stays. The campground has no RV hookups or dump station, and the forested hillside terrain is best suited for tents and smaller RVs or trailers.

location.directions: From US-101, take the Avenue of the Giants exit near Myers Flat. Head north on Avenue of the Giants approximately 1 mile. The campground entrance is on the east side of the road, about 5 miles south of the Humboldt Redwoods Visitor Center.

address.full: 638 Bridge Creek Rd, Myers Flat, CA 95554

links.title: Accessible Features at Humboldt Redwoods SP

payload.name: Polk Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round, weather permitting. Reservations via Recreation.gov with a 3-day minimum stay required. Check-in and check-out at noon.
payload.short_description: Three-bedroom Forest Service cabin on Prince of Wales Island in Tongass National Forest, accessible by vehicle, boat, or floatplane with excellent salmon fishing and wildlife viewing at nearby Dog Salmon Creek.
payload.medium_description: Polk Camp is a former Forest Service administrative cabin converted to a recreation rental on Polk Inlet, Prince of Wales Island. The three-bedroom cabin sleeps six with a full kitchen featuring a propane stove and oven. Guests must bring their own drinking water as none is available on-site. The cabin offers access to outstanding fishing at Dog Salmon Creek and prime wildlife viewing, including bears at Dog Salmon Fish Pass in August.
payload.long_description:
Polk Camp is a three-bedroom rental cabin nestled in young Sitka spruce and western hemlock on Polk Inlet, Prince of Wales Island in Alaska's Tongass National Forest. Originally used as remote housing for Forest Service timber staff, the cabin now serves as a recreation rental accessible by vehicle, boat, or floatplane. The facility features a large kitchen with a full-size propane stove and oven, ample counter and cupboard space, a gathering room, and a deck overlooking the inlet.

The cabin's three bedrooms each contain two moveable beds, accommodating up to six guests. An outhouse provides restroom facilities. Potable water is not available, so guests must bring their own supply along with sleeping bags, dishes, and cleaning supplies. Firewood may be available but is not guaranteed.

Dog Salmon Creek flows into the inlet just south of the cabin, offering excellent runs of coho, chum, sockeye, and pink salmon, as well as cutthroat trout, rainbow trout, and Dolly Varden. The Dog Salmon Fish Pass is a popular bear viewing site in August. The surrounding estuary hosts abundant wildlife including sandhill cranes, eagles, wolves, black bears, and Sitka black-tailed deer. A network of ATV trails provides additional exploration opportunities.

location.directions: From Craig, take the Craig/Klawock-Hollis Highway toward Hollis. Turn right on Hydaburg Road (State Route 913) and travel 8 miles. Turn left onto Forest Road 21 (Polk Inlet and Twelvemile Road). Follow FR 21 for 14 miles, then turn left toward Polk Inlet. The cabin parking area is about 1.5 miles ahead on the left. Access is through a locked gate at the end of the road.

photos.name: The kitchen in Polk Camp Cabin; running water (except winter) and stove.
NE view of Polk Camp Cabin
Aerial View of the area around Polk Camp Cabin on Polk Inlet.
South Side of Polk Camp Cabin

payload.name: Santos Trailhead And Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Entrance station hours are 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive days with a 7-day break required before returning. Reservations available through Florida State Parks/ReserveAmerica up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Mountain biker's paradise with 23 electric/water hookup sites adjacent to 80+ miles of internationally recognized single-track trails in Marion County, Florida.
payload.medium_description: Santos Trailhead and Campground sits on the Marjorie Harris Carr Cross Florida Greenway in Marion County, offering 23 campsites with electric and water hookups. The campground serves as a base camp for the internationally recognized Santos trail system, an IMBA Bronze Ride Center featuring over 80 miles of diverse single-track mountain bike trails. Amenities include a bathhouse with showers, dump station, fire rings, and picnic pavilions.
payload.long_description:
Santos Trailhead and Campground is a Florida State Parks facility located on the Marjorie Harris Carr Cross Florida Greenway between Ocala and Belleview. The 23-site campground provides electric and water hookups suitable for RVs up to 42 feet, trailers, and tent campers. Each site includes a picnic table, and fire rings or barbecue grills are permitted. A modern bathhouse with flush toilets and showers serves the campground, along with a dump station and trash receptacles throughout.

The adjacent Santos Trailhead is internationally recognized as a Bronze Ride Center by the International Mountain Bike Association, featuring over 80 miles of diverse single-track mountain bike trails developed and maintained through partnership with the Ocala Mountain Bike Association. The trailhead offers air pumps, tools, bike wash stations, and ADA-accessible paved trails.

The campground operates year-round with reservations available through ReserveAmerica. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive days with a 7-day break required before returning. Horses are permitted with a negative Coggins test. Quiet hours are 10:00 PM to 6:00 AM with checkout at 1:00 PM.

location.directions: From US-441 between Ocala and Belleview, turn west onto SE 80th Street. The trailhead and campground entrance is on the left, across from the Marion County Sheriff's Santos Station.

links.title: Florida State Parks - Hours and Fees
Ocala Mountain Bike Association - Santos Campground

payload.name: East Boulder Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round depending on weather conditions. First-come, first-served with no reservations. A food storage order is in effect on the Yellowstone Ranger District through December 1, 2026 to prevent bear encounters.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground alongside the East Boulder River in Custer Gallatin National Forest with 2 first-come, first-served sites, vault toilet, and no fees.
payload.medium_description: East Boulder Campground is a quiet 2-site primitive campground situated along the East Boulder River in the Yellowstone Ranger District of Custer Gallatin National Forest. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees. Facilities are minimal with only a vault toilet available. There is no potable water or trash service, so campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. RVs are not permitted at this location.
payload.long_description:
East Boulder Campground offers a peaceful backcountry camping experience along the banks of the East Boulder River in Montana's Custer Gallatin National Forest. This small campground features just two sites, providing a secluded setting ideal for campers seeking solitude away from more developed recreation areas. The campground is free to use and operates entirely on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations.
