Facilities are intentionally primitive, consisting only of a vault toilet. There is no potable water, so campers must bring an adequate supply. Trash service is not provided, requiring visitors to pack out all waste. RVs and trailers are not permitted due to access constraints. Popular activities include day hiking in the surrounding forest and fishing in the East Boulder River.

The campground is accessed by traveling 19 miles south of Big Timber on US 298, then 6 miles east on East Boulder Road (County Road 205). While officially open year-round, access may be limited during winter months depending on weather and road conditions.

location.directions: 19 miles south of Big Timber on US 298, then 6 miles east on East Boulder Road (County Road 205).

address.full: 878 E Boulder Rd, Mc Leod, MT 59052

payload.name: Comer's Rock Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-April through late October. First-come, first-served only with no advance reservations. Campers must bring their own drinking water. Bear safety food storage requirements in effect.
payload.short_description: Primitive mountaintop campground at 3,800 feet on Iron Mountain in the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area, featuring a historic CCC-built picnic shelter and access to Dry Run Wilderness trails.
payload.medium_description: Comer's Rock Recreation Area sits atop Iron Mountain at 3,800 feet in the heart of the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. This primitive first-come, first-served campground offers vault toilets and a historic log picnic shelter with stone fireplace built by the Civilian Conservation Corps. Nearby attractions include 360-degree views from Comers Rock Overlook, hiking into Dry Run Wilderness, and fishing at Hale Lake less than 2 miles away.
payload.long_description:
Perched at 3,800 feet on Iron Mountain, Comer's Rock Recreation Area provides a rustic camping experience in Virginia's Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. The primitive campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis and features vault toilets, though campers must bring their own drinking water. A highlight of the area is the historic log picnic shelter with its large stone fireplace, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps during the 1930s.

The location offers excellent access to backcountry adventures. Dry Run Wilderness is within walking distance, providing opportunities for long-distance hiking. Comers Rock Overlook and the former fire tower site deliver panoramic 360-degree views of the surrounding valleys. For those seeking water recreation, Hale Lake lies less than 2 miles away with fishing, hiking, and canoeing opportunities.

The campground is accessed via a 4-mile gravel Forest Service road, making it best suited for tent camping and smaller vehicles. Bear safety food storage requirements are in effect, and cell service is very limited throughout the area.

location.directions: From I-81 at Wytheville, take exit 67, 70, or 73 onto US 11 (Main Street). On the west end of town US 11 turns off, and Main Street becomes VA 21 south. Follow VA 21 south for 17 miles, then turn right onto gravel Forest Service Road 57 and follow it west for 4 miles to the campground.

address.full: R3703 Hales Lake Rd, Elk Creek, VA 24326

payload.name: Cookson Lake Campsites
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Operating dates are May 15 through Columbus Day. Reservations required via Recreation.gov at least 24 hours in advance; walk-ins are not permitted. Maximum 14-day stay. Campsites cannot be left unattended for more than 24 hours.
payload.short_description: Primitive lakeside camping on the shores of 35-acre Cookson Lake in Michigan's Hiawatha National Forest, featuring five reservable sites with boat ramp access.
payload.medium_description: Cookson Lake Campsites offers five primitive tent and RV sites on the south shore of a 35-acre lake in the Hiawatha National Forest. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. A pit toilet is available but there is no potable water. A public boat ramp adjacent to Site 2 provides access to fishing for largemouth bass, northern pike, bluegill, and bullhead. The open-field setting offers little privacy between sites.
payload.long_description:
Cookson Lake Campsites is a small primitive campground on the south shore of Cookson Lake, a scenic 35-acre lake with two small islands in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Managed by the Munising Ranger District of Hiawatha National Forest, the five campsites occupy a large open field surrounded by mixed aspens and northern hardwoods. Site 1 accommodates up to 8 people while Sites 2-5 each hold up to 16 people. The open layout means minimal privacy between sites.

Amenities are basic: each site has a picnic table and fire ring, and one pit toilet serves the area. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Pack-in, pack-out rules apply for trash. A public boat ramp next to Site 2 provides access to the lake's fishery of largemouth bass, northern pike, bluegill, and bullhead. Only dead and down firewood may be collected; outside firewood is prohibited.

The campground sits near the Indian Wild and Scenic River and the Big Island Lake Wilderness Area. Supplies including groceries, ice, and gasoline are available 5 miles east on County Road 437 in the Steuben area.

location.directions: From Munising, Michigan: Drive east on M-28 towards Wetmore. Turn right (south) on Forest Highway 13 at Wetmore and drive 11.9 miles to FR 2258. Turn left (southeast) and drive about 2.5 miles to FR 2257 (just before the bridge over the Indian River). Turn left (northeast) on FR 2257 and drive 1.8 miles to the campground access road.

links.title: USFS Hiawatha NF - Cookson Lake Campsites

payload.name: Wildcat Mountain State Park Horse Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The horse campground operates May 1 through November 14 annually. All 24 sites are reservable.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground in Wisconsin's Driftless Area with 24 sites adjacent to 15 miles of horse trails through wooded hills and valleys.
payload.medium_description: Wildcat Mountain State Park Horse Campground offers 24 reservable equestrian sites northeast of the park office off Taylor Valley Road. The campground provides direct access to 15 miles of horse trails winding through the scenic hills and valleys of the Driftless Area, with elevation changes of 200-250 feet on gradual ascents. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and tether pole, with shared corrals, hitching posts, loading ramps, and a large parking lot available.
payload.long_description:
Located in Vernon County within the unglaciated Driftless Area of southwestern Wisconsin, Wildcat Mountain State Park Horse Campground serves equestrians seeking access to some of the state's most scenic riding terrain. The 24-site campground sits northeast of the park office off Taylor Valley Road and connects directly to the park's 15-mile trail system, which includes multiple loops ranging from the 1.7-mile Red Loop to longer circuits like the 3-mile Purple Loop with three ridge overlooks.

The campground features vault toilets, potable water, and equestrian-specific facilities including corrals, hitching posts, tether poles at each site, parking pads, and loading ramps. Campers must bring their own tethering ropes. A state trail pass is required for riders 16 and older. The trails wind through forested hills and valleys with gradual climbs reaching 200-250 feet, and riders should avoid wet conditions to minimize erosion.

No horse rentals are available at the park, though experienced riders can rent horses in nearby Ontario. The park is open 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, with campground check-in at 3 p.m. and check-out at 1 p.m. Reservations are available through the Wisconsin State Park reservation system.

location.directions: From Ontario, Wisconsin, head east on State Highway 33 for approximately 2 miles. The entrance to Wildcat Mountain State Park will be on your right. Follow the park's internal signage to reach the Horse Campground, located northeast of the park office off Taylor Valley Road.

address.full: E13784 Taylor Valley Rd, Ontario, WI 54651

payload.name: KINGFISHER ISLAND
payload.status_description: Open for camping from May through September. First-come, first-served only. Boat access required. Recreation Fee Pass required at Forest Service boat launch parking areas.
payload.short_description: Remote boat-in campground on Kingfisher Island in Flaming Gorge Reservoir with 8 tent sites, vault toilets, and stunning views of the surrounding landscape.
payload.medium_description: Kingfisher Island is a boat-in only campground nestled in the southwest arm of Flaming Gorge Reservoir, offering 8 private tent sites on the island's east shore. Each site has its own dock tie-off spot, with vault restrooms available including a floating restroom on the dock. Campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available. The campground is 3 miles from Sheep Creek Boat Ramp, 7 miles from Lucerne Valley or Antelope Flat, and 17.5 miles from Flaming Gorge Dam.
payload.long_description:
Kingfisher Island offers a unique and serene camping experience with 8 boat-in only tent sites on its picturesque east shore in the southwest arm of Flaming Gorge Reservoir. The campground features new docks that provide easy access to the island, with each campsite having its own individual dock tie-off spot. Vault restrooms are available on the island, including a floating restroom on the dock. Campers must bring all their own drinking water as potable water is not available.

The island provides an excellent base for exploring Flaming Gorge Reservoir, which is home to mackinaw (lake trout), Utah chub, rainbow trout, channel catfish, and smallmouth bass. The Green River below the dam is one of the best trout streams in the country and is also popular among rafters and kayakers. Over 220 miles of trails are available throughout the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area.

Weather conditions on the reservoir can change rapidly with potential thunderstorms, so boaters should monitor conditions carefully. A Recreation Fee Pass is required at all Forest Service boat launch parking areas, including Sheep Creek Bay and Lucerne Boat Launch where campers typically park.

location.directions: Accessible by boat only. Launch from Sheep Creek Boat Ramp (3 miles to island), Lucerne Valley (7 miles), Antelope Flat (7 miles), or Flaming Gorge Dam (17.5 miles). Park at Lucerne Boat Launch or Sheep Creek Bay Boat Launch.

payload.name: Jimmie Davis State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open daily. Gate hours 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Entrance station staffed 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, extended to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorslouisiana.com or by phone.
payload.short_description: Jimmie Davis State Park, located 45 minutes southwest of Monroe provides 68 paved campsites, 17 deluxe cabins that were renovated in 2021, 2 lodges, 4 group camp dorms with conference center, a picnic area, 2 boat launches and boat docks, 3 covered pavilions, a swimming beach with splash pad and playground, fishing pier and cleaning stations.
payload.medium_description: Jimmie Davis State Park sits on a peninsula jutting into Caney Lake in north-central Louisiana. The 68-site campground features paved pads with water and electric hookups, picnic tables, and fire rings or grills at each site. Premium sites add sewer connections. Facilities include a comfort station with restrooms, showers, and laundromat, plus a dump station. The park offers two boat launches, a fishing pier, splash pad, swimming beach, and playground.
payload.long_description: Jimmie Davis State Park, located 45 minutes southwest of Monroe provides 68 paved campsites, 17 deluxe cabins that were renovated in 2021, 2 lodges, 4 group camp dorms with conference center, a picnic area, 2 boat launches and boat docks, 3 covered pavilions, a swimming beach with splash pad and playground, fishing pier and cleaning stations. The two-bedroom deluxe cabins sleep up to 8 people with 1 queen size bed, 1 queen size sleeper sofa and 2 sets of bunk beds, bathroom, kitchen with utensils and cookware, living room and screened in porch. Two four-bedroom lodges that sleeps up to 14 people with 2 queen size beds, 1 sleeper sofa, and 4 bunks each, kitchen with utensils and cookware, a large living room with wood-burning fireplace, satellite television and screened in porch. The Group Camp consist of four separate dorms with 8 individual rooms per dorm with a total sleep capacity of 124 people, a dining hall that includes a full commercial kitchen and basic cookware. The Park has 68 improved concrete campsites and pads, picnic tables, fire rings or grills are provided. A comfort station is provided for campers and includes restrooms, showers, and laundromat. Three covered pavilions with tables and grill, running water and electric.

payload.name: Saddleback Butte Sp Group Site
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required through ReserveCalifornia. The campground operates 24 hours daily.
payload.short_description: Group campsite in the high Mojave Desert at Saddleback Butte State Park, accommodating 9-30 people among native Joshua tree woodlands.
payload.medium_description: The Joshua Group Camp at Saddleback Butte State Park offers group camping for 9-30 people with up to 12 vehicles in the Antelope Valley. The site provides access to flush restrooms and potable water throughout the campground, with no showers available. Reservations are required through ReserveCalifornia.
payload.long_description:
Located 17 miles east of Lancaster in the Antelope Valley, the Joshua Group Camp at Saddleback Butte State Park provides group camping in a preserved high desert environment featuring native Joshua tree woodlands. The group site accommodates 9-30 people and up to 12 vehicles, making it suitable for organized groups, scouts, or large family gatherings.

The campground operates year-round and offers potable water faucets and full restrooms with flush toilets and sinks throughout the facility. An accessible group campsite is available. Dogs are permitted in the campground on a 6-foot leash but are not allowed on park trails. The park also features an RV dump station available for $10 (credit card only).

Saddleback Butte rises to 3,651 feet and offers hiking opportunities including the 2.4-mile summit trail with panoramic views of the Mojave Desert, San Gabriel Mountains, and Tehachapi Range. The park preserves plants and animals once common throughout this high desert region.

location.directions: From Lancaster, travel 17 miles east on Avenue J to 170th Street East. The park entrance is on 170th Street East between East Avenue J and K.

payload.name: Tucker Hollow Park
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. The boat ramp underwent construction in April 2026 but the campground operates normally.
payload.short_description: Small lakeside campground with 28 electric sites on Bull Shoals Lake in the Arkansas Ozarks, featuring a swimming beach, playground, marina access, and modern restroom facilities.
payload.medium_description: Tucker Hollow Park is a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers campground situated on the upper reaches of Bull Shoals Lake near Lead Hill, Arkansas. The park offers 28 campsites with 50-amp electric hookups, flush restrooms with showers, a swimming beach, playground, dump station, and boat ramp. The marina provides convenient lake access for fishing, jet skiing, and canoeing on this 71,000-acre Ozark reservoir.
payload.long_description:
Tucker Hollow Park is a compact, family-friendly campground managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on the northern reaches of Bull Shoals Lake. Built in 1951 for flood control, Bull Shoals spans 71,000 acres and extends 80 miles through the Arkansas Ozarks. The campground offers 28 sites split between two loops, all equipped with 50-amp electric service.

Facilities include flush restrooms with showers in the A loop area, a bathhouse near the marina in the B loop, drinking water, and a dump station. The swimming beach and playground make this a good choice for families. An on-site boat ramp and marina provide direct lake access for fishing, water skiing, and paddling.

Nearby Bull Shoals-White River State Park offers hiking on the Big Bluff Trail with views of the White River below the dam, and the Lakeside Trail along the shoreline. In-season hunting is permitted in surrounding areas.

location.directions: From Lead Hill, AR, travel SR 14 northwest 7 miles to SR 281. Turn north on SR 281 and continue 3 miles, following signs into the campground.

payload.name: Three Prong Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping, first-come first-served with no reservations. No fees. No potable water available. Access roads at this elevation may be impassable in winter and are not plowed.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at 5,800 feet in Mendocino National Forest, set among fir and pine trees along a large meadow with vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Three Prong Campground is a free, first-come first-served primitive campground located at 5,800 feet elevation in Mendocino National Forest. The campground sits among fir and pine trees along the edge of a large meadow, offering a quiet backcountry setting. Vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but campers must bring their own drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Three Prong Campground offers a remote camping experience in the higher elevations of Mendocino National Forest. At 5,800 feet, the campground is nestled among fir and pine trees along the edge of a large meadow, providing a peaceful setting away from developed areas. The free, first-come first-served campground requires no reservations and has no fees.

Facilities are basic, with vault toilets and picnic tables at each site. There is no potable water on-site, so campers must bring an adequate supply. The campground is located 25 miles west of Paskenta via Forest Roads M-2, 24N01, and 24N13. Due to the high elevation, access roads may be impassable during winter months and are not plowed.

Quiet hours are enforced from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. A 14-day camping stay limit applies within any 30-day period, with no more than 28 cumulative days in any 12-month period.

location.directions: From Paskenta, take Road M-2 to Road 24N01, then turn right on Road 24N13 to the campground. Located 25 miles west of Paskenta and 60 miles west of Red Bluff.

payload.name: Paradise Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. No reservations accepted. No potable water available; bring your own or treat from Mann Creek. The Weiser Ranger District office is temporarily closed, but the campground remains accessible.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed camping with three primitive sites along Mann Creek in the Hitt Mountains of Payette National Forest, ideal for mountain biking exploration.
payload.medium_description: Paradise Campground offers three dispersed primitive campsites along the edge of Mann Creek in the Weiser Ranger District. This free, first-come first-served area provides vault toilets and picnic tables but no potable water. The surrounding Hitt Mountains feature miles of backcountry roads and trails, making it a prime destination for mountain biking.
payload.long_description:
Paradise Campground is a small dispersed camping area with three primitive sites situated along Mann Creek in the Payette National Forest. Located in the scenic Hitt Mountains of western Idaho near Weiser, this free campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations.

The sites include basic amenities: vault toilets and picnic tables at each site. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own or filter/treat water from nearby sources. The campground is free with no fees required.

The area is particularly well-suited for mountain biking, with backcountry roads and trails covering miles of the Hitt Mountains. Dogs are permitted throughout the campground and on trails, though the Forest Service recommends keeping them leashed.

location.directions: From Weiser, go 12.5 miles north on Highway 95, then 10 miles north on County Road and Forest Road 009.

payload.name: Firefighters Campground
payload.status_description: Open May through September. Water availability may be limited due to supply conditions; campers should bring adequate drinking water. First-come, first-served with partial availability via Recreation.gov. Check-in at 2 PM, check-out by 11 AM.
payload.short_description: Memorial campground honoring firefighters lost in the 1977 Cart Creek Fire, located 3 miles from Flaming Gorge Reservoir with 94 sites, flush toilets, and access to world-class fishing.
payload.medium_description: Firefighters Campground sits on a pine-covered hillside at 6,900 feet within the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area. The campground memorializes three firefighters who died in the 1977 Cart Creek Fire. Sites feature picnic tables and fire rings on paved spurs, with flush toilets, drinking water, and a dump station available. Bear Canyon Trail begins across the road, offering an easy 3-mile hike to views of Red Canyon.
payload.long_description:
Firefighters Campground is a developed Forest Service campground in the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area on the Ashley National Forest. Situated at 6,900 feet on a gentle slope shaded by ponderosa pines and juniper, the campground serves as a memorial to three firefighters who lost their lives battling the 1977 Cart Creek Fire. The reservoir is just 3 miles away and offers world-class fishing for lake, brown, and rainbow trout.

The campground has approximately 94 standard nonelectric sites spread across two loops, six of which are ADA accessible. Each site includes a picnic table and campfire ring, with some sites also having grills. Facilities include flush toilets, drinking water, and a dump station. Roads and parking spurs are paved. Firewood is available for purchase from the camp host. Showers are not on-site but are available 2.5 miles away at Deer Run Campground with proof of registration.

Bear Canyon Trail starts directly across the road from the campground, providing an easy 3-mile round-trip hike with views of Red Canyon and Flaming Gorge. Flaming Gorge Dam offers guided tours of the hydroelectric plant and visitor center. The Green River below the dam provides rafting opportunities through unique geology and past Native American rock art.

location.directions: From Vernal, Utah, take U.S. 191 north about 41 miles. From Manila, Utah, take Highway 44 for 28 miles, turn left on U.S. 191 and travel approximately 3 miles north. From Rock Springs, Wyoming, take I-80 west toward Green River about 6 miles to the junction with U.S. 191/Flaming Gorge Road, then take U.S. 191 south for about 71 miles, passing through Dutch John.

address.full: 1017 E Flaming Gorge Meadows Rd, Dutch John, UT 84023

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Due to current water supply conditions, water availability throughout the summer may be uncertain because of potential water shortages. Plan on bringing enough water for your stay.

payload.name: Quaddick Picnic Shelter
payload.status_description: The picnic shelter opens for the 2026 season on May 23. Peak season runs May 23 through September 7, with walk-in availability September 8 through November 1. Restrooms are closed for the 2026 season; portable toilets are available. This is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter at Quaddick State Park on Quaddick Lake in Thompson, Connecticut. Reservable pavilion accommodating up to 50 people with lake access and sandy beaches.
payload.medium_description: Quaddick Picnic Shelter is a reservable day-use pavilion located within Quaddick State Park in northeastern Connecticut. The open-air shelter accommodates up to 50 guests and provides access to the 408-acre Quaddick Lake, sandy beaches, grills, and picnic tables. This is a day-use facility only; no overnight camping is permitted at this shelter.
payload.long_description:
Quaddick Picnic Shelter is a day-use pavilion situated within Quaddick State Park, a recreation area centered on the 408-acre Quaddick Lake in Thompson, Connecticut. The site was once Thompson's town farm and served as a fishing area for the Nipmuck Indians before becoming a state park in 1951. The shelter accommodates up to 50 people and is available for reservation through Reserve America.

The park offers swimming at sandy beaches, boating with a boat launch, fishing, hiking, and picnicking. Grills and picnic tables are available at the shelter. Note that this is strictly a day-use facility; overnight camping is not permitted at the picnic shelter. The park does have a separate youth group camping area, but it is currently closed until further notice.

Alcohol is permanently prohibited, and amplified music, bounce houses, and similar play equipment are not allowed. Pets are permitted on leash (7 feet max) in picnic areas but not in swimming areas. Out-of-state vehicles require a day pass ($10 weekdays, $15 weekends/holidays) from April through October.

location.directions: Located at 811 Quaddick Town Farm Road, Thompson, CT 06277. The park is in northeastern Connecticut near the Rhode Island border.

address.full: 818 Quaddick Town Farm Rd, Thompson, CT 06277

links.title: CT State Parks - Quaddick State Park

payload.name: Kelly Forks Campground
payload.status_description: Opens for the 2026 season on May 24 and operates through October 14. Access from Superior, Montana via Hoodoo Pass is typically impassable until early July due to snow. First-come, first-served; no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Streamside campground at the confluence of Kelly Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River in northwest Idaho, offering Blue Ribbon catch-and-release cutthroat trout fishing and access to Flat Mountain trails.
payload.medium_description: Kelly Forks Campground sits at the confluence of Kelly Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River at 2,680 feet elevation. The 14-site campground features a group area, campground host, and direct trail access to Flat Mountain. Known for Blue Ribbon cutthroat trout fishing (catch and release only), the heavily wooded site also offers swimming, horseback riding trails, and abundant wildlife viewing opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Tucked away in a heavily wooded, streamside setting in northwest Idaho, Kelly Forks Campground occupies a scenic location at the confluence of Kelly Creek and the North Fork Clearwater River. The campground offers 14 individual sites plus a group area, with a campground host on duty during the operating season. At 2,680 feet elevation, the site provides a cool retreat with swimming access and a hiking trail leading directly up to Flat Mountain.

Kelly Forks is particularly renowned among anglers for its Blue Ribbon cutthroat trout stream, though all fishing is catch and release only. Horseback riding trails in the vicinity and abundant wildlife make this a well-rounded destination for outdoor enthusiasts. The remote location requires significant travel on gravel forest roads, with the Montana approach via Hoodoo Pass typically impassable from November through early July due to snow.

location.directions: From Pierce, Idaho: Drive through town and turn left on French Mountain Road (FSR 250). Continue 48 miles on FSR 250 to the campground, located just past the Kelly Forks Work Center. From Superior, Montana: Travel west on FSR 250/Trout Creek Road, crossing Hoodoo Pass at the Idaho-Montana state line. Continue south approximately 29 miles to the campground. Note: Hoodoo Pass (6,000 ft) is typically impassable from November until early July due to snow.

payload.name: Camino Cove Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically operates June through October. No fees and no reservations required.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground on the northwest shore of Union Valley Reservoir in Eldorado National Forest with vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Camino Cove Campground is a free, first-come, first-served primitive campground situated on the northwest shore of Union Valley Reservoir at 4,875 feet elevation in the Eldorado National Forest. The campground offers vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables but has no potable water. Campers should bring their own drinking water and be prepared to store food properly in bear boxes.
payload.long_description:
Camino Cove Campground is a rustic, no-fee campground perched at 4,875 feet elevation on the scenic northwest shore of Union Valley Reservoir in California's Eldorado National Forest. The campground provides a quiet base for fishing, boating, and exploring the Crystal Basin Recreation Area. Basic amenities include vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables, though campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on-site.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Bear activity is common in the area, so all food, toiletries, and garbage must be stored in the provided bear boxes. Campfires are permitted in the fire rings when fire restrictions are not in effect. The access road is unpaved and reaches the campground via Ice House Road, Peavine Ridge Road, and Bryant Springs Road, passing the West Point boat ramp before arriving at Camino Cove.

location.directions: From Highway 50, go 7 miles north on Ice House Road. Turn left on Peavine Ridge Road and go 3 miles west to Bryant Springs Road. Turn right and go 5 miles north past West Point boat ramp. Continue 1.5 miles east to the campground turn-off on the right. Total distance is approximately 17 miles from Highway 50.

payload.name: Mill Flat Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates from June through October, with exact opening and closing dates varying by year based on conditions. No reservations are required; all sites are first-come, first-served. No potable water is available.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 7 sites in an open canyon setting in the Sawtooth National Forest, offering vault toilets and access to trout fishing and mountain trails.
payload.medium_description: Mill Flat Campground is a no-fee, first-come first-served campground with 7 sites located in an open canyon setting within the Sawtooth National Forest. The campground offers vault toilets but no potable water. Suited for both tent and trailer camping, visitors can fish for trout in the nearby stream and explore an extensive trail system through the mountain canyons.
payload.long_description:
Mill Flat Campground is a developed, no-fee campground managed by the Minidoka Ranger District in the Sawtooth National Forest. The campground features 7 individual sites in an open canyon setting, with gravel parking spurs for vehicles. It accommodates both tent and trailer camping, though facilities are primitive with vault toilets and no potable water available.

The surrounding area offers recreational opportunities including trout fishing in the adjacent stream and access to an extensive trail system winding through the mountain canyons. Horses are not permitted within the campground itself. Campers are limited to 2 vehicles per site and must observe the 14-day stay limit within any 28-day period, after which they must leave National Forest lands in the Minidoka Ranger District for at least 14 days.

location.directions: From I-84, take exit 228 and go east on Yale Road 85 miles, then 16 miles east on Haigler Canyon Road.

payload.name: Devils Fork
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All sites require reservations through Recreation.gov. An attendant is on duty during peak season.
payload.short_description: Family campground on Greers Ferry Lake in the Arkansas Ozarks with 55 electric sites, showers, and swimming beach access.
payload.medium_description: Devils Fork is a US Army Corps of Engineers campground on Greers Ferry Lake in north-central Arkansas. The 55-site campground offers electric hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, drinking water, and a dump station. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring with grill, and lantern post. The park features a swimming beach, boat ramp, and playground.
payload.long_description:
Devils Fork campground occupies a prime location on Greers Ferry Lake in the Ozark Mountains of north-central Arkansas. Operated by the US Army Corps of Engineers, this well-maintained facility provides 55 campsites spread across four loops, all equipped with electric hookups. Each site features a concrete pad, picnic table, fire ring with grill, and lantern post.

Campground amenities include both flush and vault toilets, hot showers, potable water, and a dump station for RV waste. A swimming beach provides lake access, and a boat ramp makes launching easy for anglers and boaters. A playground keeps kids entertained.

Greers Ferry Lake spans over 30,000 acres, offering outstanding opportunities for boating, water skiing, swimming, scuba diving, and fishing. The surrounding area features three National Recreation Trails and a multi-purpose fitness trail. Dense forests of red cedar, oak, and sweet gum provide shade in summer and vibrant colors in fall.

location.directions: From Greers Ferry, AR, take SR-16 north for 1/4 mile and follow signs to the campground.

payload.name: Paris Landing State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 12 months in advance through reserve.tnstateparks.com with a non-refundable $5 reservation fee. Check-in at 4:00 PM, check-out at 12:00 PM. Only certified heat-treated firewood is permitted.
payload.short_description: Year-round campground on Kentucky Lake offering 45 electric/water hookup sites and 18 primitive sites with bathhouses, dump station, and beach access.
payload.medium_description: Paris Landing State Park Campground sits on the western shore of Kentucky Lake, Tennessee's largest body of water. The campground features 45 sites with water and 30/50-amp electric hookups plus 18 primitive tent sites in a hardwood forest setting. Facilities include two bathhouses with hot showers, a laundry room, dump station, and a seasonal camp store. The park offers swimming beach access, a marina, golf course, and extensive hiking trails.
payload.long_description:
Paris Landing State Park Campground occupies a prime location on the western shore of Kentucky Lake, formed by the damming of the Tennessee River. The 841-acre park provides direct access to 160,000 acres of water, making it a popular destination for fishing, boating, and swimming. The campground offers 45 sites equipped with water and either 30-amp or 50-amp electric service, while 18 primitive sites provide a more rustic experience in a shaded hardwood forest.

Campers have access to two bathhouses with restrooms and hot showers, though one may close seasonally. A laundry room and dump station operate year-round. The camp store, located adjacent to the laundry facility, is open May through October and stocks snacks and camping supplies. The park also features a swimming beach, full-service marina, 18-hole championship golf course, and multiple hiking trails.

Sites accommodate RVs up to 38 feet. Only one pull-through site exists; the remainder are back-in sites approximately 30x30 feet. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive days, extending to 28 days from December through February. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 PM to 6 AM.

location.directions: Located 18 miles east of Paris, TN on US Highway 79, or 45 miles west of Clarksville, TN on US Highway 79.

address.full: 200 1 Paris Landing Campground Dr, Buchanan, TN 38222

payload.name: Springfield
payload.status_description: Open and accepting reservations through Recreation.gov. Entrance gate opens 7 a.m. and locks 10 p.m. daily. Maximum stay is 14 days within any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Popular lakefront campground on Hartwell Lake with 79 full-hookup sites, swimming beach, boat ramp, and showers in a forested setting.
payload.medium_description: Springfield Campground is one of Hartwell Lake's most popular camping destinations, featuring 79 sites with water and 50-amp electric hookups spread across 60 acres of Virginia pine and mixed hardwoods. The campground offers direct lake access with a boat ramp, courtesy dock, and designated swimming beach, plus six comfort stations with showers, a dump station, and three playgrounds.
payload.long_description:
Springfield Campground sits on 60 acres along the shores of Hartwell Lake, a 56,000-acre reservoir on the Georgia-South Carolina border. The campground features 79 sites with gravel pads, water hookups, and 50-amp electric service. Sites range from pull-through to back-in configurations, with many offering waterfront views. The mature Virginia pine and hardwood forest provides shade throughout.

Facilities include six comfort stations (several with hot showers), a dump station, boat ramp with courtesy dock, designated swimming beach between sites 26-27, and three playgrounds. The lake is known for excellent fishing including largemouth bass, striped bass, crappie, and catfish. Boating, swimming, and water skiing are popular activities.

The campground is located near Clemson, South Carolina, providing convenient access to restaurants, groceries, and Clemson University. Reservations are handled through Recreation.gov. The entrance gate locks at 10 p.m. and reopens at 7 a.m., with no vehicle movement permitted during overnight hours.

location.directions: From Interstate 85 in South Carolina, take exit 11 onto Highway 187 south. Turn on Providence Church Road and follow signs to the park at 1915 Providence Church Road, Anderson, SC 29625.
