payload.name: Boykin Springs Camping
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations accepted for campsites. Payment can be made on-site via QR code using the Recreation.gov mobile app or by cash/check. Day use hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground on a 9-acre spring-fed lake in Angelina National Forest, featuring flush toilets, hot showers, and hiking access to the Sawmill Trail.
payload.medium_description: Boykin Springs Recreation Area sits on a scenic 9-acre spring-fed lake in Angelina National Forest near the Louisiana border. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1938, this first-come, first-served campground offers standard sites with picnic tables, fire rings, and lantern posts. A bathhouse provides flush toilets and hot showers, and potable water is available throughout. The area serves as the trailhead for the Sawmill Hiking Trail.
payload.long_description:
Boykin Springs Recreation Area occupies a picturesque setting around a 9-acre spring-fed lake in Angelina National Forest, east Texas. Originally constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1938, the area retains historic character while offering modern amenities including a bathhouse with flush toilets and hot showers. Potable drinking water is available from faucets throughout the campground, though individual sites lack hookups.

The campground provides standard nonelectric sites equipped with picnic tables, fire rings, and lantern posts. Nine sites can accommodate RVs up to 24 feet in length. Activities include fishing in the lake, swimming, and hiking the Sawmill Trail which begins at the recreation area. A picnic shelter accommodating up to 74 people is available by reservation for day-use gatherings.

Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Pets are permitted but must be leashed (6 feet maximum) or otherwise physically restrained, and are prohibited in swimming areas except for service animals.

location.directions: From Zavalla, travel east on Highway 63 for 10.5 miles; turn right (south) on Forest Service Road 313 for 2.5 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Lake Havasu Cabin Loop
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The park operates 24 hours daily. Reservations can be made up to 365 days in advance through azstateparks.com/reserve or by calling 1-877-MY-PARKS. Two-night minimum on weekends April 1 through October 31; three-night minimum on holidays. Maximum stay is 14 nights per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Beachside camping cabins at Lake Havasu State Park featuring A/C, heating, and stunning river views with nearby shower facilities and beach access.
payload.medium_description: Lake Havasu Cabin Loop offers 13 climate-controlled cabins along the shores of Lake Havasu. Each cabin includes a queen bed, bunk beds, electricity, and outdoor amenities including a fire ring, BBQ grill, and picnic table. Family-style showers are a short walk away, and registered guests have beach access and use of the dump station.
payload.long_description:
Lake Havasu Cabin Loop sits within Lake Havasu State Park on the Arizona shoreline of the Colorado River. The 13 two-to-three room cabins offer climate control with both heating and air conditioning, making them comfortable year-round. Each cabin is furnished with a queen bed, two sets of bunk beds, table and chairs, ceiling fan, and electricity. Maximum occupancy is six people total with no more than four adults.

Outdoor amenities at each cabin include an individual fire ring, barbecue grill, and picnic table. Family-style shower facilities and modern ADA-accessible restrooms are within walking distance. The park features a visitor center with a camp store, three boat ramps, canoe and kayak rentals, and the 1.75-mile Mohave Sunset Trail. A dump station is available for registered campers at no additional charge.

Guests must bring their own linens and bedding. Pets are not permitted in the cabins except for service animals. Tent camping is prohibited in the cabin loop. Check-in is at 3:00 p.m. and check-out at 10:00 a.m. A two-night minimum applies on weekends from April through October, with a three-night minimum on holidays.

location.directions: Located at 699 London Bridge Road, Lake Havasu City, AZ 86403. The park is on the Arizona side of Lake Havasu, accessible from State Route 95.

address.full: 565 Sea Queen Dr, Lake Havasu City, AZ 86403

payload.name: New Canyon
payload.status_description: Open April through November. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through August 31, 2026, but campfires are permitted in agency-built fire rings. No potable water; campers should bring their own. Pack-out trash policy in effect.
payload.short_description: Rustic campground in the Manzano Mountains of Cibola National Forest with vault toilets and access to the Crest Trail.
payload.medium_description: New Canyon Campground is a primitive camping area in the Manzano Mountains west of Manzano, New Mexico. The campground offers vault toilets and picnic tables but no potable water. It provides direct access to the Crest Trail and other hiking opportunities in the Manzano Mountain Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
New Canyon Campground sits in the Manzano Mountains within the Cibola National Forest, managed by the Mountainair Ranger District. The campground offers a rustic experience at approximately 7,800 feet elevation, with vault toilets and picnic tables at each site. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own supply.

The campground provides direct access to the Crest Trail and serves as a gateway to the Manzano Mountain Wilderness. The area features pine forests, diverse wildlife including deer, and opportunities for hiking and exploring the surrounding backcountry. Sites accommodate vehicles up to 22 feet in length.

New Canyon operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. The primitive setting means reduced services; campers should be prepared to pack out all trash and may encounter closed or unserviced restrooms depending on seasonal staffing.

location.directions: Located west of the community of Manzano in Torrance County, New Mexico.

payload.name: Ohanapecosh Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the entire 2026 season due to a major rehabilitation project that will upgrade the campground's 185 campsites, nine bathrooms, wastewater collection system, electrical and water systems, and accessibility features. The campground is anticipated to reopen for the 2027 camping season.
payload.short_description: Ohanapecosh Group Campground offers two tent-only group sites for up to 25 people each, nestled in old-growth forest along the Ohanapecosh River in Mount Rainier National Park's southeast corner.
payload.medium_description: Ohanapecosh Group Campground features two reservable group sites, each accommodating up to 25 people with tent-only camping. Located at 1,914 feet elevation along the Ohanapecosh River, the campground is surrounded by old-growth Douglas fir forest and provides access to popular trails including Silver Falls. Amenities include drinking water, flush toilets, and picnic tables. No RVs are permitted at the group sites.
payload.long_description:
Ohanapecosh Group Campground is situated on the southeast side of Mount Rainier National Park, surrounded by towering old-growth forest and crossed by the exceptionally clear, snow-fed Ohanapecosh River. The name is thought to derive from a Taidnapam Indian word meaning "standing on the edge." The campground provides two group sites, each limited to 25 people and five parking spaces, with tent-only camping.

The location offers convenient access to both the Paradise and Sunrise areas of the park. Popular nearby trails include the Grove of the Patriarchs, which winds through ancient forest stands, and several routes leading to Silver Falls. The Ohanapecosh Visitor Center and amphitheater are located nearby for ranger programs and interpretive activities.

Amenities at the group campground include drinking water, flush toilets, and picnic tables. Fire rings are not provided at the group sites, and gathering firewood is prohibited. Food must be stored properly due to bear activity in the area. Pets are allowed but must be leashed (6 feet maximum) or caged at all times and cannot be left unattended.

location.directions: Located on State Route 123, four miles north of State Route 12, near Packwood, WA.

photos.name: Ohanapecosh River, Mt Rainier National Park

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: We now expect the Ohanapecosh Campground rehabilitation project to continue into the spring and early summer of 2026. We will reopen the campground as soon after the completion of the project as possible, but we cannot predict an exact opening date. Information on how to secure a campsite for summer 2026, will be posted to the Mount Rainier National Park website at [Campgrounds - Mount Rainier National Park (U.S. National Park Service) ][1]prior to the 2026 camping season*.*  [1]: https://www.nps.gov/mora/planyourvisit/campgrounds.htm

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Ohanapecosh Campground Closure in Summer 2026. **The **Ohanapecosh Campground rehabilitation project** will provide significant upgrades to the popular campground located in the southeast corner of the park. This effort will rehabilitate the campground’s 185 campsites and nine bathrooms, replace the aging wastewater collection system, upgrade electrical and water systems, and support improvements to campground accessibility. The Ohanapecosh Campground is anticipated to reopen for the 2027 camping season. More information is available on the [**Park Construction FAQs**][1] page  [1]: https://www.nps.gov/mora/planyourvisit/park-construction-faqs.htm

payload.name: Gill Point
payload.status_description: Gill Point is a day-use recreation area with a reservable group shelter, not a traditional campground with individual overnight sites. The facility operates daily 8:00 a.m. to 8:30 p.m. with a $5-7 entry fee. The group shelter (capacity 24) can be reserved through Recreation.gov; shelter must be occupied by 2:00 p.m. on reservation day.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on J. Strom Thurmond Lake with a reservable group shelter, boat ramp, beach, and flush toilets.
payload.medium_description: Gill Point Recreation Area is a wooded day-use facility on the northern shore of J. Strom Thurmond Lake in Lincoln County, Georgia. The area features a group picnic shelter accommodating up to 24 people, flush toilets, drinking water, a boat ramp with courtesy dock, and a swimming beach. This is not a traditional campground with individual campsites.
payload.long_description:
Gill Point Recreation Area sits on the northern end of J. Strom Thurmond Lake, a 70,000-acre U.S. Army Corps of Engineers reservoir straddling the Georgia-South Carolina border. The area is accessible via Georgia State Highway 79, approximately 12 miles north of Lincolnton.

The facility centers on a reservable group shelter that can accommodate up to 24 people for picnics and gatherings. Supporting amenities include flush toilets, drinking water, a boat ramp with courtesy dock, and a designated swimming beach. The mixed pine and hardwood forest provides shade along the shoreline.

The lake offers fishing for largemouth bass, crappie, bream, catfish, and striped bass. Boating, water skiing, and swimming are popular activities. Wildlife including bald eagles, wild turkeys, and whitetail deer frequent the area. The historic town of Petersburg lies submerged beneath the lake, and Elberton, the Granite Capital of the World, is 20 miles northwest.

location.directions: From Lincolnton, Georgia, travel approximately 12 miles north on SR-79.

payload.name: Heyburn Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. No gate attendant at Heyburn Park Gate Shack this season; pass sales and cash sales are not available at the gate. Purchase USACE Annual or ATB passes at the Heyburn or Keystone Lake Office, or buy digital passes online. Credit cards only at Heyburn Lake Office. Gates locked 10 PM to 6 AM. Camping limited to 14 days per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: USACE campground on Heyburn Lake with 46 electric sites, restrooms, showers, swim beach, and boat ramp near Kellyville, Oklahoma.
payload.medium_description: Heyburn Park is a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers campground on Heyburn Lake featuring 46 campsites with water and electric hookups. The park offers two restroom/shower facilities, a large swim beach, two-lane boat ramp, playground, and group shelters. Popular activities include boating, water skiing, fishing for crappie, bass, and catfish.
payload.long_description:
Heyburn Park is a well-equipped USACE campground situated on the shores of Heyburn Lake in Creek County, Oklahoma. The campground offers 46 campsites with water and electric hookups, with some sites featuring 50-amp service. Site sizes vary considerably, with some accommodating RVs up to 90 feet while others are better suited for smaller rigs up to 35 feet. The park includes both back-in and pull-through sites on gravel driveways.

Facilities include two restroom and shower buildings, a large swim beach with picnic tables, a two-lane boat ramp with courtesy dock, playground, and two group shelters. Metal fire rings are provided at campsites. The swim beach and associated facilities are designated alcohol-free and pet-free zones, though pets are permitted elsewhere in the campground on leash.

The campground lies in a scenic setting of grasslands and sandstone hills covered with oak, hickory, ash, elm, and cottonwood. In spring, flowering wild plum and redbud add color to the landscape. Heyburn Public Hunting Area covers over 6,000 acres nearby, offering hunting for squirrel, rabbit, quail, waterfowl, and wild turkey during season.

location.directions: From Bristow, go 9 miles east and turn left onto 257th West Ave. Follow the paved road about 3 miles to the campground. From Sapulpa, take State Highway 66 west to Kellyville, turn west onto 151st South Ave and go about 3.5 miles to the 4-way intersection at S. 257th W. Ave. Turn right and stay on the paved road for about 2 miles to the park.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **No Gate Attendant for Heyburn Park Gate Shack 2026 Season**: Pass Sales and Cash Sales will **NOT** be available this season. Please visit the Heyburn or Keystone Lake Office to purchase USACE Annual or ATB passes. Digital Passes can be purchased online. Only Credit Cards are being accepted at the Heyburn Lake Office. Please note, staffing is limited for Heyburn Lake Office. Please reach out to the Heyburn Lake Office at 918-247-6391 or the Keystone Lake Office at 918-865-2621 for questions.

payload.name: Apache Maid Cabin
payload.status_description: Open for the season May through September. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Check-in is 2:00 PM, checkout is 11:00 AM. During fire restrictions (Stage 1 or 2), outdoor campfires are prohibited but propane devices remain allowed.
payload.short_description: Historic 1909 rental cabin at the base of Apache Maid Mountain in Coconino National Forest, sleeping up to 6 guests with propane heat, solar lighting, and rustic charm near Sedona.
payload.medium_description: Apache Maid Cabin is a 520 square-foot historic cabin originally built in 1909 as a ranch house, later serving as a Forest Service ranger station. Located at 6,382 feet elevation at the eastern base of Apache Maid Mountain, the cabin features one bedroom with bunk beds, a living room with futon, and a kitchen with propane stove. Solar lighting provides limited illumination; there are no electrical outlets. An outdoor vault toilet is located 50 yards from the cabin. Guests must bring their own potable water, bedding, and food.
payload.long_description:
Apache Maid Cabin offers a unique overnight experience in a piece of Arizona history. Built in 1909 by Charles Babbitt as a cattle ranch house, the cabin later served as a U.S. Forest Service ranger station before being restored and opened for public rental. The 520 square-foot structure sits at 6,382 feet in the shade of ponderosa pines, just south of the Mogollon Rim.

The cabin accommodates up to 6 overnight guests with a bedroom containing a bunk bed (double on bottom, twin on top) and a rollaway bed, plus a futon couch in the living room. The kitchen includes a propane stove with dishes and cookware but no refrigerator. Propane heating keeps the cabin comfortable, while solar-powered overhead lights provide limited illumination with no electrical outlets available. An outdoor vault toilet is located approximately 50 yards from the cabin.

Guests must bring all potable water for drinking, cooking, and cleaning, as well as bedding, towels, food, flashlights, and an axe for the outdoor fire pit. A propane grill and picnic tables are available outside. The cabin is accessible by passenger car in good weather, though high-clearance vehicles are recommended and 4WD is required during inclement conditions. Stoneman Lake, Beaver Creek, and Sedona's red rock country are all within an hour's drive.

location.directions: From Phoenix, travel north on I-17 to exit 306 (Stoneman Lake Road/FR 213). Go east on Stoneman Lake Road approximately 6.5 miles to the junction with FR 229. Turn right onto FR 229 and go 4.5 miles to FR 230. Veer right, continuing on FR 229 approximately a quarter-mile to the intersection with FR 620 (Apache Maid Lookout). The cabin gate is at this intersection on the left. Access is through a locked gate; combination codes are provided in the reservation confirmation. High-clearance vehicle recommended; 4WD required in inclement weather.

payload.name: OJO REDONDO
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates from May 15 through October 15, weather and road conditions permitting. No potable water or trash services; campers must bring water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground in the Zuni Mountains at 8,900 feet elevation, featuring vault toilets and fire rings amid ponderosa pine, Douglas fir, and aspen forest near Mt. Sedgwick.
payload.medium_description: Ojo Redondo is a free, primitive campground in the Zuni Mountains of Cibola National Forest, located southwest of Mt. Sedgwick. Situated at 8,900 feet elevation among ponderosa pine, Douglas fir, and aspen trees, the campground offers a scenic meadow setting. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill. Vault toilets are available, but campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Ojo Redondo Campground is a free, primitive camping destination in the Zuni Mountains of Cibola National Forest, positioned southwest of Mt. Sedgwick, the highest peak in the range. At 8,900 feet elevation, the campground sits among ponderosa pine, Douglas fir, and aspen trees with a scenic meadow adjacent to the camping area.

The campground offers dispersed-style camping with basic amenities. Each site is equipped with a picnic table and fire ring with grill for cooking. Vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water or trash service, so campers must bring adequate water and pack out all refuse.

Access requires travel on forest roads that can be affected by weather conditions. The campground serves as a base for hiking and mountain biking in the Zuni Mountains. The high elevation provides cool summer temperatures but can see early season snow.

location.directions: Take Exit 53 at Thoreau and drive south on NM State Highway 612 past Bluewater Lake. The road becomes FR178 at the Forest boundary. Continue south on FR178 for 8 miles to the junction with FR480. Turn east (left) and drive two miles to the campground entrance on the right.

payload.name: Big Island Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Showers and the White Fox comfort station are available mid-May through mid-October. Reservations accepted 120 days in advance through Reserve Minnesota. Some sites operate first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground on a 116-acre island within Myre-Big Island State Park, offering 35 shaded sites with flush toilets, showers, and trail access near Albert Lea Lake.
payload.medium_description: Big Island Campground sits on a maple and basswood-covered island within Myre-Big Island State Park near Albert Lea. The 35 densely wooded sites provide shade and privacy, with 17 offering electric hookups. A nearby building houses flush toilets and seasonal showers. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground connects to paved accessible trails and sits near Albert Lea Lake.
payload.long_description:
Big Island Campground occupies the forested 116-acre Big Island within Myre-Big Island State Park in southern Minnesota. The 35 campsites are set among mature maple and basswood trees, providing shade and a sense of seclusion despite the campground's moderate density. Seventeen sites offer 30-amp electric hookups. Standard amenities include a picnic table and fire ring with grill at each site, potable water, and a nearby comfort station with flush toilets and hot showers available seasonally from mid-May through mid-October.

The park preserves diverse habitats including oak savanna, prairie, and wetlands along 8 miles of Albert Lea Lake shoreline. Birders visit during migration for waterfowl and grassland species. The paved, ADA-accessible Blazing Star State Trail connects the campground to Albert Lea, while park trails loop through wet lowlands and grasslands. Canoe and kayak rentals are available.

A dump station serves RV campers. The campground accommodates trailers and RVs up to 60 feet, though some individual sites may be challenging for larger rigs due to tight maneuvering. An accessible cabin sleeping five is also available. The park is 3 miles southeast of Albert Lea, about 90 minutes south of Minneapolis via I-35.

location.directions: From I-35 exit 11, head east 1/3 mile, then turn south on Highway 38 and follow signs to the park entrance. Address: 19499 780th Ave, Albert Lea, MN 56007.

links.title: Myre-Big Island State Park Virtual Tour

payload.name: Bennett Spring State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round at Campground 1. Campgrounds 4 and 5 open February 25 through October 31. Campgrounds 2 and 3 open April 15 through October 31. Water at individual campsites is available April 15 through October 15. Reservations available up to 12 months in advance via iCampMO.
payload.short_description: Popular Missouri state park campground offering five campgrounds with basic to full-hookup sites, showers, and year-round camping near a renowned trout fishing spring.
payload.medium_description: Bennett Spring State Park features five campgrounds nestled in wooded Ozark hills, ranging from basic tent sites to full-hookup RV sites with 50-amp electric, water, and sewer. Campground 1 operates year-round with heated showers and a dump station, while campgrounds 2-5 are seasonal. The park is famous for its spring-fed trout stream stocked daily with rainbow trout.
payload.long_description:
Bennett Spring State Park Campground is one of Missouri's most beloved camping destinations, centered around a spring that releases over 100 million gallons of crystal-clear water daily. The park offers five distinct campgrounds with a total mix of basic, electric, and full-hookup sewer/electric/water sites, including 50-amp service for larger RVs. Campground hosts are on-site to assist visitors throughout the season.

Campground 1 operates year-round and provides the most amenities including accessible sites, showers, restrooms, a dump station, and a wood lot. Campgrounds 2-5 are seasonal, opening between late February and mid-April and closing by the end of October. Note that significant uphill travel is required to reach campgrounds 2, 3, 4, and 5. The park features a nature center, hiking trails, dining at the lodge, a camp store, and world-class trout fishing in the spring branch.

Reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance through the Missouri State Parks reservation system online or by phone. Walk-up sites are available on a first-come, first-served basis when unreserved. Camping is limited to 15 days within any 30-consecutive-day period.

location.directions: Located at 26250 Highway 64A, Lebanon, MO 65536. From Lebanon, take Highway 64 west approximately 12 miles to the park entrance.

address.full: 89 Bennett Spring State Park 12th Rd, Lebanon, MO 65536

links.title: Bennett Spring Camping - Missouri State Parks
Bennett Spring State Park - Missouri State Parks

payload.name: Darien Lakes State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season from May 16 through October 11. Reservations available up to 9 months in advance with a 2-night minimum stay and 14-night maximum consecutive stay. Boat rentals are no longer available; swimming is subject to lifeguard availability and water quality testing.
payload.short_description: Darien Lakes State Park offers 154 campsites amid wooded terrain surrounding a scenic 12-acre lake in western New York, with electric hookups, heated shower facilities, and access to hiking, fishing, and disc golf.
payload.medium_description: Darien Lakes State Park campground features 154 sites spread across hilly, wooded terrain with ravines and streams surrounding 12-acre Harlow Lake. The campground offers 141 sites with electric hookups (15/20/30/50 amp) and 13 primitive sites. Heated comfort stations with hot showers, a dump station, and water fill stations are available throughout. Activities include fishing, swimming at the beach (seasonal lifeguards), hiking, disc golf, basketball, and horseback riding on designated bridle paths.
payload.long_description:
Darien Lakes State Park campground sits on over 1,800 acres of rolling terrain in Genesee County, featuring mixed woodlands, scenic ravines, and the centerpiece 12-acre Harlow Lake. The 154 campsites accommodate both tent campers and RV users, with 141 sites offering electric hookups at 15, 20, 30, or 50 amps and 13 primitive sites for those seeking a more rustic experience. Sites can accommodate RVs and trailers up to 45 feet, though all driveways are back-in style.

The campground provides heated comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers, a dump station for RV waste disposal, and water fill stations. Each site includes a picnic table and post grill. Pets are welcome on all sites with a maximum of two per site, kept on leashes no longer than six feet, and must have current rabies vaccination.

Recreation options abound with a swimming beach staffed by seasonal lifeguards, fishing opportunities at Harlow Lake, an extensive trail system for hiking and horseback riding, disc golf course, basketball courts, and playground. Winter visitors can enjoy cross-country skiing and snowmobiling on designated trails.

location.directions: From the NYS Thruway (I-90), take Exit 48A (Pembroke Exit). Follow Route 77 (Allegany Road) south approximately 6 miles to the park entrance at 10475 Harlow Road, Darien Center, NY 14040.

payload.name: Falls Lake State Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Holly Point Campground is open and accepting reservations. Rolling View, Shinleaf, and B.W. Wells campgrounds are currently closed for construction. All permanent bathrooms are temporarily closed with portable toilets available throughout the park. Day-use areas at Beaverdam and Rolling View remain open.
payload.short_description: Falls Lake State Recreation Area offers over 300 campsites with electric and water hookups on a 12,000-acre reservoir near Raleigh, featuring swimming beaches, boat ramps, and miles of hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Falls Lake State Recreation Area spans seven access areas along a 12,000-acre reservoir in Wake and Durham counties. The park offers more than 300 campsites ranging from primitive backpacking sites to full-hookup RV spots. Holly Point and Rolling View campgrounds feature water and electric hookups, centrally located bathhouses, and camper-only boat ramps. Each campsite includes a picnic table, outdoor grill, and lantern hook.
payload.long_description:
Falls Lake State Recreation Area is a premier recreation destination located approximately 15 miles east of downtown Durham, North Carolina. The park encompasses seven access areas along a 12,000-acre reservoir managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. With over 300 campsites spread across multiple campgrounds, Falls Lake accommodates everything from primitive backpacking at Shinleaf to full-hookup RV camping at Holly Point and Rolling View.

Holly Point Campground offers 158 sites with 89 featuring water and 50/30-amp electric hookups, while Rolling View provides 115 sites with 80 hookup-equipped spots. Both campgrounds include dump stations, bathhouses with showers, and camper-only boat ramps. Every campsite is equipped with a picnic table, outdoor grill, and lantern hook on the tent pad.

Beyond camping, Falls Lake provides 25 miles of hiking trails, 14 miles of mountain biking trails, swimming beaches, fishing, and boating access. The park serves as a critical water supply reservoir while offering year-round outdoor recreation opportunities for the Raleigh-Durham metropolitan area.

location.directions: Located in Wake and Durham counties, approximately 15 miles east of downtown Durham and 18 miles north of Raleigh. Access via NC Highway 98.

payload.name: Grays Peak Group Cg
payload.status_description: Closed. Opening day has been delayed to May 28, 2026, due to a road closure. The campground operates seasonally from late May through early October.
payload.short_description: Remote group campground in San Bernardino National Forest at 7,132 feet elevation, accommodating up to 40 people with a fire ring, grills, and picnic tables in a mixed conifer setting.
payload.medium_description: Grays Peak Group Campground is a secluded group site in the San Bernardino National Forest near Big Bear Lake at 7,132 feet elevation. The campground accommodates up to 40 people and 8 vehicles, featuring picnic tables, a barbecue grill, and a group fire ring surrounded by mixed conifer forest. Nearby trails lead to Grays Peak and Butler Peak Fire Lookout. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Grays Peak Group Campground sits at 7,132 feet elevation in the San Bernardino National Forest, approximately 45 miles from San Bernardino. The single group site is nestled in a mixed conifer forest with a grassy understory, providing a peaceful retreat for organized groups of up to 40 people.

The campground offers basic amenities including picnic tables, a barbecue grill, and a communal fire ring. Vault toilets are available. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is provided on site. Gravel parking spurs accommodate up to 8 vehicles, with no additional vehicles permitted.

Nearby recreation includes the Grays Peak hiking trails (1W05 and 1W06) and the historic Butler Peak Fire Lookout. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov and open on a 12-month rolling basis.

location.directions: From San Bernardino, take I-10 to Running Springs, then CA-18 to Big Bear Lake Dam. Continue on CA-38 to Fawnskin, then turn onto Rim of the World Drive (3N14) for 1.2 miles. Turn onto Forest Road 2N13 to reach the campground.

address.full: 39046 N Shore Dr, Big Bear City, CA 92314

payload.name: Summit  Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. Summit typically opens late spring and closes early fall, with exact dates varying by snow conditions. Contact the Rocky Mountain Ranger District to confirm opening status. Sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.short_description: A high-elevation 17-site campground on Montana's Front Range with trail access to the Continental Divide Trail and Bob Marshall Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Summit Campground offers 17 first-come, first-served sites at high elevation in the Rocky Mountain Front Range. A 3-mile spur trail connects the campground to the Continental Divide Scenic Trail and the Bob Marshall Wilderness. Adjacent Memorial Square features a miniature Washington Monument commemorating Theodore Roosevelt and the Blackfeet tribe. Mandatory bear-resistant food storage is required.
payload.long_description:
Summit Campground sits high in the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains within the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest. The 17-site campground provides a gateway to serious backcountry travel, with a 3-mile spur trail connecting directly to the Continental Divide Scenic Trail and into the Bob Marshall Wilderness.

The campground offers basic amenities including vault toilets and potable water from a hand pump. Bears frequent the area, and mandatory food storage in approved bear-resistant containers is required. All food must be removed from the eating area after meals.

Adjacent to the campground, Memorial Square features a miniature Washington Monument commemorating Theodore Roosevelt and the Blackfeet tribe. The campground experiences heavy use during its operating season and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations available.

location.directions: From East Glacier, go 11 miles west on US 2.

payload.name: Loop Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 8. Sites are available first-come-first-served or via Recreation.gov reservations. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own. 7-day stay limit enforced.
payload.short_description: Remote forest campground at 7,400 feet in the Stansbury Range with vault toilets, no water, and trailhead access to Deseret Peak Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Loop Campground sits at 7,400 feet in South Willow Canyon, surrounded by oak, maple, and juniper trees with Willow Creek running alongside. The campground serves as a primary access point for the Deseret Peak Wilderness via the Stansbury Front Trail and Medina Flat Trail. Sites include picnic tables and vault toilets, but no potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Loop Campground is nestled in the Stansbury Range of the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest, approximately 4.5 miles up a gravel road from the forest boundary in South Willow Canyon. At 7,400 feet elevation, the campground offers partial shade from oak, maple, and juniper trees, with Willow Creek providing a scenic backdrop.

The campground features 12 single sites and 1 double site, each with picnic tables. Vault restrooms are available, but there is no potable water so campers must pack in their own supply. This is bear country, and proper food storage is mandatory.

The multi-use Stansbury Front Trail and Medina Flat Trail begin across from the campground entrance, offering direct access to the rugged Deseret Peak Wilderness. Willow Creek provides rainbow and brown trout fishing opportunities. The access road is gravel and not recommended for trailer use due to steep, narrow sections with potholes.

location.directions: From Grantsville, Utah, head southwest into South Willow Canyon. The campground is located 4.5 miles up the canyon from the National Forest boundary on a gravel road. The road is steep and narrow with potholes; not recommended for trailers.

payload.name: Cedar Grove Campground
payload.status_description: Open and operating year-round. Reservations required via Recreation.gov or the Recreation.gov mobile app using Scan & Pay. Cell service is limited; download the app and set up your account before arriving. No potable water available.
payload.short_description: A riverside backcountry campground along the Current River in northwest Ozark National Scenic Riverways, offering primitive camping near swimming, floating, and the historic Susie Nichols Cabin.
payload.medium_description: Cedar Grove Campground sits in the northwest corner of Ozark National Scenic Riverways along the Current River. This backcountry campground offers 6 primitive sites with picnic tables, fire rings, lantern posts, and vault toilets. Popular for river recreation in summer and mild-weather camping in fall and winter, it provides access to swimming, floating, blue ribbon fishing upstream, and a hiking trail to the historic Susie Nichols Cabin.
payload.long_description:
Cedar Grove Campground is a backcountry campground in the Upper Current District of Ozark National Scenic Riverways. Located about 10 minutes from Jadwin, Missouri, the campground sits along the Current River in a scenic area popular for swimming, floating, and fishing. A nearby hiking trail connects to the historic Susie Nichols Cabin.

The campground offers 6 primitive, non-electric sites suitable for tents or small RVs/trailers. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. Vault toilet restrooms are available but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Access requires a short stretch of gravel road (less than 1,000 feet) off NPS Road 154.

Cedar Grove sees year-round visitation. Summer brings crowds seeking the cool river to beat the heat, while the southern exposure keeps campers comfortable during the milder fall and winter months. The area offers excellent blue ribbon trout fishing upstream on the Current River.

location.directions: From Jadwin, Missouri, drive west on State Highway ZZ for approximately 5.3 miles. After 2.3 miles, the road becomes County Road 651. Just before the large concrete river crossing, turn right onto NPS Road 154. This gravel road leads through the campground. Less than 1,000 feet of gravel road driving required.

alerts.title: Round Spring - September Paving Work
alerts.content: Paving work will be done in the Round Spring area throughout the month of September. Currently, the parking area at the pavilion is closed. Closure of the electric sites (E1-E6) in the campground will begin Monday, 9/8.

alerts.title: Peavine Road Closed
alerts.content: Peavine Road near Big Spring will be closed for paving beginning 7/28 at noon and will remain closed for several weeks. Please use Highway 103 to reach all destinations in the Big Spring area.

alerts.title: Campground Closures
alerts.content: The following campgrounds are closed pending repairs: Pulltite (sites 1-13) and Dee Murray. Day use areas remain open for visitors.

alerts.title: Pulltite Campground Partial Closure
alerts.content: Sites 1-13 remain closed. All other sites are open. Sites are available by reservation only - book online at https://www.recreation.gov/camping/campgrounds/234357

alerts.title: Reservations Required for Developed Campgrounds
alerts.content: As of January 1, 2025, ALL developed campsites will be available through reservation ONLY. These include Pulltite, Round Spring, Alley Spring, Big Spring, Two Rivers, and Akers. Reservations must be made through recreation.gov (online or by calling).

alerts.title: River Ferry at Akers (on State Highway K) CLOSED until further notice
alerts.content: The Akers Ferry on State Highway K will not be in service until further notice.

alerts.title: Scan & Pay Required for Backcountry Campgrounds
alerts.content: Starting April 15, 2025, "backcountry" campgrounds will only accept payment through Scan & Pay, on the recreation.gov mobile app. While the app works offline, visitors should download the app and set up their account beforehand. Cell service is limited.

payload.name: Pines Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens in June and closes mid to late October, both dates weather dependent. Due to high elevation (9,200 feet), snow is possible even in summer months. There is no potable water on site. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Remote 11-site campground at 9,200 feet along the South Fork of the Michigan River in Routt National Forest, offering fishing, OHV access, and wilderness trails near Gould, Colorado.
payload.medium_description: Pines Campground is a small, primitive campground with 11 sites located 25 miles southeast of Walden in the Gould area. Situated at 9,200 feet along the scenic South Fork of the Michigan River, the campground offers vault toilets, fire grates, and picnic tables at each site. Due to beetle kill, sites have little to no shade. Campers must bring their own water. Dogs allowed on leash.
payload.long_description:
Pines Campground sits at 9,200 feet in Routt National Forest, adjacent to the South Fork of the Michigan River. Built in 1964, this small 11-site campground is located at the base of Owl Mountain with easy access to OHV roads and wilderness trails. The campground provides a quiet basecamp for fishing the mountain stream, backpacking, and off-highway vehicle riding.

Each site includes a fire grate and picnic table, with two vault toilets serving the campground. Due to extensive beetle kill in the area, campsites offer very little to no shade. There is no potable water on site; campers must bring their own supply. The nearest dump station is 35 miles away in Walden. Maximum trailer length is 20 feet.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis and accepts exact cash or check only. Cell phone reception is limited, with T-Mobile and AT&T providing the best coverage. Maximum of two vehicles allowed per site.

location.directions: From Walden, head east on Highway 14 for 22 miles to Gould. Take County Road 21 (Forest Road 740) south 4 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Mesa
payload.status_description: Open mid-March through December, weather dependent. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through September 30, 2026; campfires are permitted only in the provided fire rings. All sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.short_description: A scenic first-come, first-served campground on a mesa above Lake Roberts in Gila National Forest, featuring juniper and pinon trees with lake views and excellent birding.
payload.medium_description: Mesa Campground sits at 6,150 feet elevation on a juniper and pinon-covered mesa overlooking Lake Roberts. The campground offers sites with lake views, heated flush-toilet restrooms, potable water, and 12 sites with electric and water hookups. All sites are first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit.
payload.long_description:
Mesa Campground occupies a scenic mesa above Lake Roberts in Gila National Forest's Wilderness Ranger District. At 6,150 feet elevation, the campground is shaded by juniper and pinon pine trees, with several sites positioned along the bluff offering views of the lake below. The location makes it an excellent base for birding, as migrating birds frequent the campground while waterfowl gather on the lake.

The campground features heated restrooms with flush toilets, potable water, picnic tables at each site, fire rings, and garbage service. Twelve sites include water and electric hookups. Two ADA-accessible sites are available. All sites operate first-come, first-served with a 14-day maximum stay.

Located approximately 25 miles north of Silver City via NM 35, Mesa Campground provides convenient access to Lake Roberts and the surrounding Gila wilderness. Pets are welcome but must be leashed, and horses or pack animals are not permitted in the campground.

location.directions: From Silver City, take US 180 east approximately 9 miles to NM 152 east. Continue on NM 152 for about 15 miles, then turn north on NM 35 and continue approximately 25 miles to Lake Roberts and the campground.

payload.name: Kneff Lake Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates May 1 through September 30. The 2026 season opens May 15 following a delayed start likely related to April flooding assessments across Huron-Manistee National Forests. All 27 sites are first-come, first-served with some sites also reservable through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: A 27-site campground on a 20-acre stocked trout lake in the Huron-Manistee National Forests near Grayling, Michigan, with vault toilets, hand-pump water, and an accessible swimming beach.
payload.medium_description: Kneff Lake Campground sits in a mixed oak and pine forest surrounding a 20-acre lake stocked with rainbow trout each spring. The 27 non-electric sites feature picnic tables, fire rings, and lantern posts. The embedded day use area offers an accessible beach with swimming and non-motorized boating. Vault toilets and hand-pump drinking water are provided.
payload.long_description:
Kneff Lake Campground is located on the western edge of the Mio Ranger District in the Huron-Manistee National Forests, a short drive east of Grayling. The 27 campsites ring a scenic 20-acre lake shared among federal, state, and private ownership. Sites 1-18 have crushed stone parking pads while sites 19-27 feature asphalt pads. Site 9 is designated tent-only. Each site includes a picnic table, campfire ring, and lantern post.

The campground provides vault toilets and potable water from hand-pump wells. Trash collection is available. The embedded day use area features an ADA-accessible ramp to the beach and swimming area, along with picnic tables and grills. Kneff Lake is designated as a trout lake and stocked with rainbow trout in spring; anglers also catch perch. Maximum lake depth is 40 feet. Non-motorized boats such as canoes and kayaks can be carried in.

The surrounding forest is predominantly oak and pine. A campground host is on-site during the operating season. Standard developed-area rules apply, including quiet hours and prohibitions on fireworks and ORVs within the campground.

location.directions: From Grayling: Travel east on M-72 for 6.5 miles. Turn right and travel south on Stephan Bridge Rd. for 1 mile. Turn left and travel east on FR 4003 for about 1 mile.
