payload.name: Wannagan Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Limited services after Labor Day through Memorial Day: potable water is turned off during winter months. Firewood use and possession restrictions currently in effect. First-come, first-served with a 14-day consecutive stay limit.
payload.short_description: Remote USFS campground in the North Dakota Badlands with 10 rustic sites and direct trailhead access to the Maah Daah Hey and Buffalo Gap trails.
payload.medium_description: Wannagan Campground offers 10 spacious first-come, first-served sites in the remote North Dakota Badlands. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. Amenities include an ADA-accessible vault toilet and seasonal potable water via hand pump. Direct trailhead access to both the Maah Daah Hey and Buffalo Gap trails makes it popular with hikers and equestrians.
payload.long_description:
Wannagan Campground is a remote, year-round camping destination nestled in the North Dakota Badlands within the Dakota Prairie Grasslands. The campground features 10 large, open campsites suitable for tents, trailers, and RVs. Six sites are single-unit back-in spurs, while four sites are pull-through configurations. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Hitching rails are available for equestrians.

Amenities include an ADA-accessible vault toilet (seasonally accessible spring through fall) and potable drinking water from a hand pump. The water system operates from spring through fall and is turned off during winter months. There are no hookups, showers, or dump stations. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a 14-day consecutive stay limit.

Wannagan serves as an excellent meeting point for the north end of the Buffalo Gap Trail and provides direct access to the Maah Daah Hey Trail. The nearby switchbacks on the Maah Daah Hey offer sweeping vistas of the surrounding badlands and large buttes. E-bikes, motorcycles, ATVs, UTVs, and snowmobiles are prohibited on the trails.

location.directions: From the Sentinel Butte exit on I-94, go east three miles, then 14 miles northeast on road #726 to the campground.

payload.name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 365 days. Park gates open 8 a.m. until sunset daily. Reservations available via Florida State Parks website or by calling 800-326-3521.
payload.short_description: Camp at America's first undersea park in Key Largo, offering 47 full-hookup sites near coral reefs, snorkeling, and glass-bottom boat tours in the Florida Keys.
payload.medium_description: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park Campground offers 47 sites with water and electric hookups in Key Largo at Mile Marker 102.5. The campground features flush restrooms with hot showers, a dump station, coin-operated laundry, and ADA-accessible facilities. Sites accommodate RVs up to 62 feet and include picnic tables and grills. The park is famous for its underwater attractions, including the submerged Christ of the Abyss statue, coral reef snorkeling, glass-bottom boat tours, and kayak trails through mangrove swamps.
payload.long_description:
John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park Campground sits at the gateway to the Florida Keys in Key Largo, making it an ideal base for exploring the only living coral reef in the continental United States. The 47-site campground accommodates both tent and RV campers with water and 30/50/110-volt electric hookups at each site. A central restroom building provides flush toilets and hot showers that meet ADA requirements, and three paved campsites offer accessible paths to the facilities.

The park's main draw is its underwater world. Visitors can view vibrant coral formations and marine life aboard glass-bottom boat tours, or get closer through snorkeling and scuba diving excursions offered by the park concessionaire. The iconic Christ of the Abyss statue rests 25 feet underwater at Key Largo Dry Rocks reef. Back on land, kayak and canoe trails wind through mangrove habitat, short nature trails traverse tropical hardwood hammocks, and a swimming beach provides easy water access.

The Blue Heron Cafe inside the park serves food and drinks, while dive shops offer equipment rentals, sundries, and souvenirs. A community campfire circle at the Point provides a gathering spot for campers. Reservations fill quickly, especially during the dry season from December through April when conditions are optimal for reef activities.

location.directions: From Miami, take Florida's Turnpike south to US 1. Continue on US 1 to Key Largo. The park entrance is on the left (ocean side) at Mile Marker 102.5.

payload.name: Doe Lake Group Site
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. Stage 1 fire restrictions in effect for Ocala National Forest; campfires permitted in Forest Service-provided rings. Check-in at 3:00 PM, check-out at 11:00 AM. Maximum stay 14 consecutive days per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Historic 1930s CCC group campsite overlooking Doe Lake in Ocala National Forest, accommodating up to 250 guests with a restored dining hall and group kitchen.
payload.medium_description: Doe Lake Group Site centers around a restored 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps dining hall perched on a grassy hill overlooking Doe Lake. The site accommodates up to 250 people and is popular with equestrian groups, weddings, and large gatherings. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and hitching posts. Guests have exclusive access to canoeing, low-powered boating, and fishing on the lake.
payload.long_description:
Doe Lake Group Site is a reservation-only group campground in the Ocala National Forest, built around a beautifully restored 1930s Civilian Conservation Corps dining hall. The historic lodge features a large group kitchen and sits atop a grassy hill with views of clear Doe Lake below. The site can accommodate up to 250 people and is a favorite among equestrian groups, though it also hosts weddings, reunions, and other large social gatherings.

Tent camping is the primary accommodation, with RVs and horse trailers permitted in designated areas without hookups. The campground provides flush toilets, an accessible bathhouse with showers, drinking water, picnic tables, and hitching posts for horses. Guests with reservations have exclusive access to the lake for canoeing, kayaking, low-powered boating, and fishing.

The Ocala National Forest spans 383,000 acres and is the southernmost national forest east of the Mississippi. The camping area rests beneath a shady grove of oaks and pines, offering a scenic natural setting for group activities. Bands and DJs are permitted, but overnight sleeping in the dining hall is prohibited.

location.directions: From I-75 west of Ocala, take SR 40 east for 11 miles to Forest Corners. Turn right on CR 314-A and continue about 9 miles through the Moss Bluff blinker. Make the next major right at an old country store. Drive 3.6 miles passing Sunnyhill Restoration Area entrances on the left, then turn left on FR 14 (Cross Road/Big Scrub Road). Continue 0.9 mile, bear right, then turn right into the recreation area.

payload.name: Pioneer Camp
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Day-use reservations are required Friday through Sunday and on holidays from May 15 through September 27, 2026. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia up to six months in advance during peak season (mid-May through Labor Day). First-come, first-served from Labor Day until mid-May.
payload.short_description: Forested campground in McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park featuring tent sites and rustic cabins, located within walking distance of the spectacular 129-foot Burney Falls waterfall.
payload.medium_description: Pioneer Camp is a developed campground within McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park in Shasta County, California. The campground offers a mix of tent sites and rustic cabins nestled in a forested setting, with flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, a camp store, and a dump station available. The famous 129-foot Burney Falls waterfall is a short 5-10 minute walk from camp via accessible trails.
payload.long_description:
Pioneer Camp sits within McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial State Park, home to the stunning 129-foot Burney Falls that Theodore Roosevelt once called the eighth wonder of the world. The campground features a mix of tent sites and 22 rustic one- and two-bedroom cabins. Each campsite includes a paved parking spur, picnic table, fire ring with grill, and a food storage locker. The cabins are heated by propane but have no electricity or running water.

The campground offers modern conveniences including flush toilets, hot water showers, potable water, trash collection, and a dump station for RVs. A camp store is available within walking distance of all sites. The Pioneer Cemetery Trail begins near campsite #75, following a historic wagon trail to an old cemetery. Vehicles over 32 feet cannot be accommodated in the park.

The park is located six miles north of Highway 299 on Highway 89 near Burney. Dogs are allowed in the campgrounds but not on trails or day-use areas. Weekend and holiday visitors from mid-May through late September must make day-use reservations in addition to camping reservations.

location.directions: From Redding, take Highway 299 east approximately 55 miles to Highway 89. Turn left (north) on Highway 89 and drive 6 miles to the park entrance on the left.

payload.name: Porcupine Springs
payload.status_description: Open seasonally, typically June through September depending on conditions. Individual sites are first-come, first-served; group sites require reservations through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Forest campground at 6,950 feet in southern Idaho's Rock Creek drainage, offering hiking, equestrian trails, and fishing access with vault toilets and potable water.
payload.medium_description: Porcupine Springs Campground sits at 6,950 feet along Rock Creek Road in the Sawtooth National Forest. The developed campground features 12 individual sites across four loops plus 3 group sites accommodating up to 100 people. Amenities include vault toilets, potable water faucets, picnic tables, and campfire rings. Little Fork Trailhead provides direct access to an extensive multi-use trail system for hiking, biking, and horseback riding. Rock Creek offers fishing opportunities nearby.
payload.long_description:
Porcupine Springs Campground occupies a scenic forest setting of pine and aspen trees in southern Idaho's Sawtooth National Forest. At 6,950 feet elevation along Rock Creek Road, the campground provides a base for exploring the area's extensive trail network. Loop A contains 4 single and 2 double sites, Loop B has 3 single and 3 double sites plus a horseman area, Loop C offers 3 single and 3 double sites, and Loop D features 18 family units with water faucets and accessible restrooms. Three group sites can accommodate 50 to 100 people each.

The campground is suitable for both tent and trailer camping. Little Fork Trailhead (#163) begins at the campground, providing access to Porcupine Springs, Ross Falls, Rim View, Pike Mountain, and Third Fork trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. An accessible Stock Transfer Station serves equestrian users. Rock Creek runs nearby for fishing.

Individual sites are available first-come, first-served with fee envelopes at the entrance. Group sites and select individual sites can be reserved through Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is 14 days per 28-day period, with a limit of 2 vehicles per site.

location.directions: From Twin Falls, travel east 8 miles on ID 50 and US 30, then south 30 miles on Rock Creek Road (County Road G3/Forest Road 515). From Hansen, travel south on County Road G3 for approximately 31 miles as the road becomes Forest Road 515 then Forest Road 500.

photos.name: This location features a horse corral.
Large recreation area for LOOP reservations. This site is perfect for large family reunions!

payload.name: Deer Flat Group Site
payload.status_description: The campground was closed for the entire 2025 season and reopens May 22, 2026. Reservations are handled through Recreation.gov. Check-in is 1:00 PM at the gated site with the campground host; check-out is 11:00 AM. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Large group campsite in old-growth Douglas fir and sugar pine forest adjacent to the Wild and Scenic North Umpqua River, accommodating up to 70 people.
payload.medium_description: Deer Flat Group Site is a reservable group camping area located within Horseshoe Bend Campground on the scenic North Umpqua River in Umpqua National Forest. The site sits beneath towering old-growth Douglas fir and sugar pine trees, offering full shade and a secluded setting for family reunions or large group gatherings. The paved site accommodates up to 70 people and 25 vehicles, with flush toilets, potable water, picnic tables, campfire rings, and grills provided.
payload.long_description:
Deer Flat Group Site occupies a shaded bench of old-growth Douglas fir, sugar pine, and deciduous trees near the banks of the North Umpqua River, a federally designated Wild and Scenic River renowned for salmon and steelhead fishing as well as challenging whitewater. The single reservable group site can host up to 70 people with parking for 25 vehicles (maximum 35 feet each). Roads and spurs are paved with back-in access.

The site is equipped with multiple picnic tables, campfire rings, grills, flush toilets, and potable water. The adjacent Horseshoe Bend Campground provides access to a boat launch, and the 79-mile North Umpqua Trail passes nearby, offering hiking and mountain biking opportunities. The Illahee Flat Trail descends from Horseshoe Bend to connect with the Jessie Wright Segment of the North Umpqua Trail.

Crater Lake National Park and the Rogue-Umpqua National Scenic Byway are within easy driving distance for day trips.

location.directions: From Roseburg, Oregon, travel east on OR-138 (Diamond Lake Boulevard) for approximately 48 miles. Turn right onto Forest Road 4750 near Milepost 48, then turn right again onto Forest Road 4750-001. The Deer Flat Group Site is to the right at the first road junction inside the campground.

photos.name: Deer Flat Group Site in Horseshoe Bend Campground

payload.name: Payne Lake Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served. Check-in at 2:00 PM, check-out at noon. Quiet hours 10:00 PM to 6:00 AM.
payload.short_description: Payne Lake Recreation Area offers 26 campsites along a scenic 110-acre lake in Alabama's Talladega National Forest, featuring flush restrooms, showers, swimming beach, and boat ramp.
payload.medium_description: Payne Lake Recreation Area is a year-round campground in the Oakmulgee Ranger District of Talladega National Forest. The 26 developed sites line the shores of a 110-acre lake and include both primitive tent sites on the east side and modern RV-friendly sites with water and electric hookups on the west side. Amenities include two bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, a swimming beach, boat ramp (electric motors only), and dump station.
payload.long_description:
Payne Lake Recreation Area sits on the western edge of Talladega National Forest in Alabama's Oakmulgee Ranger District. The campground wraps around a peaceful 110-acre lake, providing campers with waterfront sites and easy access to fishing, swimming, and boating. The area is divided into two camping zones: the Eastside Camping Area with 8 primitive sites for those seeking solitude, and the Westside Camping Area with 18 more developed sites that can accommodate RVs and tents.

All 18 westside sites have water hookups, and 7 of those also include electrical hookups. Every site comes equipped with a picnic table, fire circle, and tent or trailer pad. Two bathhouses with flush toilets and showers serve the campground, along with a dump station near the entrance. A swimming beach provides lake access, and a boat ramp allows watercraft with electric motors (gasoline motors must be tilted up).

Payne Lake is open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Check-in is at 2:00 PM and check-out is at noon, with quiet hours from 10:00 PM to 6:00 AM. The base camping fee is $18 per night, with additional charges of $12 for water and electric hookups or $5 for water-only hookups. Cash or check payment is required.

location.directions: From Brent, AL take State Hwy 5 South for approximately 5.7 miles, turn right onto State Hwy 25 South and travel for approximately 16 miles, turn sharp right onto County Road 71 for approximately 0.7 of a mile. Campground will be straight ahead.

payload.name: Pennyrile Forest State Resort Park
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season through October 31, 2026. Equestrian sites operate year-round. Burn bans may apply; contact park for current fire restrictions. Water availability is not guaranteed during months with freezing temperatures. Firewood importation from outside Kentucky is prohibited.
payload.short_description: Wooded Kentucky state park campground with 63 sites ranging from primitive tent spots to full-hookup RV pads, plus equestrian camping with direct access to 40+ miles of horse trails.
payload.medium_description: Pennyrile Forest State Resort Park offers 63 campsites in a forested setting near a 56-acre lake. Site types include primitive non-electric tent sites, standard electric, full-service RV sites with water/electric/sewer, and 8 pull-through equestrian sites with horse hitching posts. A central service building provides showers, restrooms, and laundry. The park features an 18-hole golf course, hiking trails, boat rentals, tennis and basketball courts, and a lodge with dining.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the rolling hills of western Kentucky near Dawson Springs, Pennyrile Forest State Resort Park campground sits at the edge of dense forest, deliberately positioned out of view from other park facilities for a secluded camping experience. The 63-site campground accommodates diverse camping styles: 20 primitive non-electric sites for tent campers, 10 standard electric sites, 25 full-service sites with electric/water/sewer hookups, and 8 pull-through equestrian sites designed for horse owners with hitching posts for up to four horses and direct trail access.

The adjacent Pennyrile State Forest provides over 40 miles of horse trails, with a 1.25-mile connector trail leading directly from the equestrian campground. Beyond camping, the park centers around a 56-acre lake offering fishing, pedal boat, and rowboat rentals. An 18-hole golf course, hiking trails, tennis and basketball courts, and a lodge with a 200-seat dining room round out the amenities. Equipment lengths up to 62 feet can be accommodated depending on site selection.

location.directions: Located 20 miles northwest of Hopkinsville at 20781 Pennyrile Lodge Road, Dawson Springs, KY 42408.

payload.name: Kershaw Ryan State Park Group Day Use Campground
payload.status_description: This is a day-use facility only, not an overnight campground. Open daily from 8am to sunset. Reservations available through Reserve Nevada. For overnight camping at Kershaw-Ryan State Park, see the separate 16-unit campground.
payload.short_description: Group day-use pavilion at Kershaw-Ryan State Park in Nevada's colorful Rainbow Canyon, featuring covered shelters with tables and grills for group gatherings.
payload.medium_description: Kershaw-Ryan State Park's Group Day Use area provides a reservable group pavilion nestled in a scenic canyon with towering 700-foot walls near Caliente, Nevada. The facility includes covered shelters with picnic tables and grills, with access to park restrooms and coin-operated showers. This is a day-use facility only, not an overnight campground.
payload.long_description:
Kershaw-Ryan State Park offers two group day-use areas set within Rainbow Canyon, where towering sandstone walls rise up to 700 feet. The park's natural springs nurture wild grapevines, white oaks, and fruit trees, creating a lush oasis in the high desert. Group pavilions provide covered shelters with picnic tables and grills for gatherings, with access to park restrooms featuring coin-operated showers.

This Group Day Use facility is for daytime activities only and does not permit overnight camping. The park is located two miles south of Caliente on Nevada State Route 317, with 14 miles of hiking and mountain biking trails nearby. A seasonal spring-fed wading pool adds to the park's family-friendly appeal.

For overnight stays, the park operates a separate 16-site campground with hookups and four first-come-first-served tent sites, which is a different facility from this group day-use area.

location.directions: Located two miles south of Caliente on Nevada State Route 317.

address.full: 5818 Kershaw Ryan Sp Rd, Caliente, NV 89008

links.title: Nevada State Parks Group Use Fees

payload.name: Lowell State Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Open for day use. This is not a campground; no overnight camping is available. Day-use parking requires a $10 fee or annual pass.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on the north shore of Dexter Lake featuring a swim beach, marina with boat launch, picnic shelter, and playground. No overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Lowell State Recreation Site is a day-use park on the north shore of Dexter Lake, about 20 minutes southeast of Eugene/Springfield. The park features a reservable picnic shelter, large swim beach with lawn area, playground, basketball court, flush restrooms, and a full-service marina with moorage slips, courtesy dock, and 4-lane boat launch ramp. Popular activities include sailing, water skiing, fishing, paddling, and wildlife viewing. No overnight camping is available.
payload.long_description:
Lowell State Recreation Site sits on the north shore of Dexter Lake adjacent to the city of Lowell in Lane County. This day-use facility offers a variety of recreational opportunities centered around lake access and family-friendly amenities. The park features a reservable picnic shelter overlooking the lake, a wooded picnic area with tables, a large swim beach backed by expansive lawn, a playground, and a basketball court.

The marina provides moorage slips ranging from 8 to 11 feet wide, a courtesy dock, and a 4-lane boat launch ramp supporting sailing, water skiing, fishing, paddling, rowing, and drag boat racing. Bald eagles are frequently spotted around the lake. Flush restrooms and a life jacket loaner station are available.

This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. Day-use parking costs $10 per vehicle or an annual pass. The picnic shelter is reservable from April 1 through October 31; outside that window or when unreserved, it operates first-come, first-served.

location.directions: From Eugene, take OR-58 east toward Oakridge. After approximately 12 miles, take the Lowell/Dexter exit and follow signs to the city of Lowell. The park is located on the north shore of Dexter Lake.

payload.name: Gigantea Campground
payload.status_description: Closed by forest order through July 27, 2026 for recreation site repairs (Forest Order No. 05-15-00-26-01). Normal operating season is May through October, first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Primitive first-come, first-served campground in the Sierra National Forest, located half a mile from the McKinley Grove of Giant Sequoias. No water or trash services.
payload.medium_description: Gigantea Campground offers rustic camping near the McKinley Grove of Giant Sequoias in Sierra National Forest. The area features a mix of slopes and flat terrain shaded by cedar, fir, and sugar pine trees. Each site includes a picnic table and grill. This is a pack-in, pack-out facility with vault toilets but no potable water or trash service. First-come, first-served only.
payload.long_description:
Gigantea Campground provides a rustic camping experience just half a mile from the McKinley Grove of Giant Sequoias in the Sierra National Forest. The campground sits at approximately 6,400 feet elevation amid cedar, fir, and sugar pine trees that provide excellent shade throughout the camping area. The terrain includes both slopes and flat areas suitable for different camping preferences.

This is a primitive, first-come, first-served campground with no reservations accepted. Each site is equipped with a picnic table and grill. Vault toilets are available, but campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. Access to the campground is via paved road with the final stretch on dirt roads through the campground itself.

The maximum vehicle length is 35 feet, making it unsuitable for larger RVs. Stays are limited to 14 days, with a maximum of 6 people per site. Pay showers and limited supplies are available in Dinkey Creek, approximately 15 minutes away. The campground typically operates from May through October.

location.directions: Take Hwy 168 east from Clovis towards Prather. Continue through Prather to Shaver Lake. Just before reaching Shaver Lake, turn right on Dinkey Creek Road. Travel 11.7 miles east to the intersection of Dinkey Creek Road and McKinley Grove Road. Turn right and travel 7 miles north on McKinley Grove Road to the campground.

payload.name: Hatchet Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Isle Royale operates April 16 through October 31 annually. Individual sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Groups of 7 or more must reserve group sites in advance ($25 per permit). A 2-night consecutive stay limit applies June 1 through Labor Day. Free overnight permit required, obtained upon arrival.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry campground on Hatchet Lake in the center of Isle Royale, accessible only by foot via the Hatchet Lake Trail.
payload.medium_description: Hatchet Lake Campground is a primitive backcountry site located on Hatchet Lake near the center of Isle Royale National Park. Accessible only by foot via the Hatchet Lake Trail, this campground offers 8 tent sites (5 first-come, first-served and 3 reservable group sites). Amenities include seasonal composting toilets, non-potable water, and food storage lockers. A 2-night stay limit applies from June 1 through Labor Day.
payload.long_description:
Hatchet Lake Campground sits on the shores of Hatchet Lake in the interior of Isle Royale, one of America's most remote national parks. The campground is reached via the Hatchet Lake Trail, which connects the Minong Ridge Trail to the Greenstone Ridge Trail. This location makes it a strategic overnight stop for backpackers traversing the island's main ridgeline routes.

The campground features 8 tent sites: 5 individual sites available first-come, first-served, and 3 group sites that require advance reservation for parties of 7 or more. Seasonal composting toilets and food storage lockers are provided. Water is available but non-potable and must be treated before drinking. The terrain is uneven and rough throughout, with no accessible facilities.

As with all Isle Royale backcountry campgrounds, campers must use self-contained stoves only as open fires are prohibited. All trash must be packed out. Pets are not allowed anywhere in the park. A free overnight permit is required for all campers and must be obtained upon arrival at Rock Harbor or Windigo.

location.directions: Hatchet Lake Campground is accessible only by foot. From Todd Harbor, take the Hatchet Lake Trail (2.3 miles) which connects the Minong Ridge Trail to the Greenstone Ridge Trail. The campground is located near the center of the island. Ferry service to Isle Royale departs from Houghton or Copper Harbor, MI, or Grand Portage, MN.

photos.name: Hatchet Lake is a major campground stop along the Greenstone Ridge Trail.
Hatchet Lake Campground is a popular stop for backpackers along the Greenstone Ridge Trail.

payload.name: Black Canyon Of The Gunnison South Rim Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is partially open with limited capacity due to the 2025 South Rim Fire. Only 25 non-electric sites in Loop A are available for the 2026 season (May 18 through September 30). Loops B and C remain closed for rehabilitation with no set reopening date. Reservations required via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: South Rim Campground perches at 8,400 feet on the rim of Black Canyon of the Gunnison, surrounded by scrub oak forests with dramatic canyon views. Reservations required via Recreation.gov.
payload.medium_description: South Rim Campground sits at 8,400 feet elevation on the rim of Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park. The 88-site campground offers vault toilets, seasonal potable water, bear boxes, and an evening ranger program amphitheater. Loop B provides electric hookups for RVs up to 55 feet, while Loops A and C accommodate smaller rigs up to 23 feet. Reservations are required year-round via Recreation.gov, though winter camping operates first-come, first-served.
payload.long_description:
South Rim Campground occupies a stunning perch at 8,400 feet elevation on the South Rim of Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park. The campground is surrounded by scrub oak forests atop ancient hard rock, with deer, grouse, bears, and bobcats frequenting the area. Sites are fairly close together, partially shaded by tall shrubs, with bear-proof food storage lockers at each site.

The campground has three loops: Loop A and C offer standard non-electric sites at $20/night, while Loop B provides 20 and 30 amp electric hookups at $34/night. Loop B accommodates RVs and trailers up to 55 feet combined length, though most sites average 30 feet. Loops A and C fit vehicles up to 23 feet combined. Vault toilets are available year-round, but potable water is only available mid-May through mid-October. There are no showers, dump station, or water hookups.

Summer visitors can attend evening educational programs at the campground amphitheater. Winter activities include snowshoeing on Rim Rock Trail and cross-country skiing on South Rim Drive when the road is closed to vehicles.

location.directions: From Montrose, take US Highway 50 east for 6 miles, then turn left onto Highway 347 and follow it for 6 miles into the park. About 0.3 mile past the entrance station, turn right onto the South Rim Campground road.

photos.name: Water spigot available in South Rim Loop B
Recycling and trash disposal options available in South Rim Campground
A campsite at South Rim Campground showing the firepit and picnic table.
South Rim Campground standard non-electric site
Park visitors admire the view of Black Canyon of the Gunnison's high cliff walls at Gunnison Point.
Sunlit Black Canyon of the Gunnison cliff face as seen from the South Rim
One of South Rim Campground's electric sites
Signs seen at water spigots within the South Rim Campground

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Due to wildfire damage, there is no set date to reopen Loops B & C at the South Rim Campground in 2026. Please visit the park website's [Current Conditions][1] page for more information and rehabilitation status updates.  [1]: https://www.nps.gov/blca/planyourvisit/conditions.htm

payload.name: Dimond O
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season, operating May through September. Potable water levels are currently low; bring extra water for cooking, cleaning, and drinking. Some sites are first-come, first-served while others are reservable via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Forest campground on the Middle Fork Tuolumne River, closest to Yosemite's Big Oak Flat entrance and Hetch Hetchy. Offers river access for swimming, wading, and trout fishing.
payload.medium_description: Dimond O Campground sits among mixed conifers adjacent to the Middle Fork Tuolumne River in Stanislaus National Forest. The campground serves as the closest camping option to Yosemite's Big Oak Flat entrance and Hetch Hetchy Reservoir. Sites feature picnic tables, bear boxes, and fire pits with grills. The river provides swimming holes and rainbow trout fishing, while nearby Carlon Falls Trail offers an easy hike.
payload.long_description:
Dimond O Campground occupies a scenic mixed conifer forest along the Middle Fork Tuolumne River in Stanislaus National Forest. Its location makes it the closest campground to Yosemite National Park's Big Oak Flat entrance and Hetch Hetchy Reservoir, providing convenient access to the park's northwest features without the crowds of valley-side camping.

The Middle Fork Tuolumne River runs directly through the area, offering warm-weather swimming, wading, and fly fishing for rainbow trout. Ponderosa pine and cedar trees provide shade throughout the campground. Several sites sit along the riverfront.

Nearby recreation includes the Carlon Falls Trail at Carlon Day Use Area and the extensive trail network accessible from Hetch Hetchy. The campground serves as a solid basecamp for exploring both Stanislaus National Forest and the northern reaches of Yosemite.

location.directions: From the Groveland Ranger District Office, head east 15 miles on Highway 120, then turn left on Evergreen Road and travel 4 miles. The campground is on the left.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Limited Water Available**: Please be aware that we are seeing a low levels of potable water in the campground. We do apologize for the inconvenience but there is a possibility you may not have water at the time of your reservation. Please use the water for your necessities and Bring Extra Water Incase of outage. Bring water for things Like Cooking, Cleaning, drinking, etc. Thank you so much for your patience.

payload.name: South Jetty Sand Camping
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations required via Recreation.gov. Sites must be occupied within the first 24 hours of arrival time or the reservation is released. An OHV riding curfew is in effect from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Alcohol is prohibited. Watch for seasonal flooding.
payload.short_description: Primitive sand camping for OHV enthusiasts on the Oregon Dunes, accessible only by 4x4 vehicles. Sites are dispersed on the dunes with no amenities; pack in everything including water and portable toilets.
payload.medium_description: South Jetty Sand Camping offers primitive dispersed camping directly on the sand dunes within Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area. This is an OHV-focused area located just south of Florence, Oregon, requiring 4x4 vehicle access over soft sand. Sites have no developed amenities whatsoever. Campers must bring their own water, portable toilets, fire pans, and pack out all trash. Standard sites accommodate up to 20 people and 5 vehicles; group sites hold up to 40 people and 10 vehicles.
payload.long_description:
South Jetty Sand Camping is a primitive camping area within the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area, specifically designed for off-road vehicle enthusiasts. Located less than two miles south of Florence, Oregon, the camping area sits directly on the sand dunes with access via the Goosepasture Staging Area off South Jetty Road. This is true dispersed camping with no developed infrastructure. Sites are accessible only by 4x4 vehicles capable of navigating soft sand.

The Oregon Dunes contain the largest expanse of coastal sand dunes in North America, with wind-sculpted formations towering up to 500 feet above sea level. From the nearby South Jetty Day-Use Area, visitors can access miles of open beach for hiking and wildlife viewing, separate from the motorized riding areas. Designated OHV routes and open riding areas extend south of South Jetty Road.

Campers must be fully self-sufficient. There is no potable water, no toilets (portable facilities required), no fire rings (fire pans required), no picnic tables, and no trash service. Oregon OHV permits are required for riding. An OHV curfew is in effect from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., and an alcohol prohibition applies. The 14-day stay limit is enforced per 30 rolling days across the entire forest.

location.directions: From Florence, Oregon, travel south on Highway 101 for 1 mile to South Jetty Road. Turn right and proceed 1.5 miles to the Goosepasture Staging Area on the left. 4x4 vehicle required for sand access to campsites.

links.title: Siuslaw NF South Jetty Sand Camping

photos.name: A portion of the North Riding Area OHV Map

payload.name: Buttgenbach Campground At Croom Motorcycle Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through Reserve America up to 11 months in advance. All campers must purchase an annual OHV pass and arrive before 5 PM on the first day for unit inspection and gate code. Drought conditions may affect camping; check current burn ban status.
payload.short_description: An OHV-focused campground in Withlacoochee State Forest with 50 electric/water sites, bathhouses with showers, and direct access to 2,600 acres of ATV and dirt bike trails.
payload.medium_description: Buttgenbach Campground sits at the heart of the 2,600-acre Croom Motorcycle Area inside Withlacoochee State Forest. All 50 sites include electric (30/50 amp) and water hookups, and the facility features two bathhouses with showers and flush restrooms, a dump station, fire rings, and an ATV/dirt bike wash station. An annual OHV pass is required for all campers, and campers must arrive before 5 PM on their first day to receive the gate code.
payload.long_description:
Buttgenbach Campground at Croom Motorcycle Area is purpose-built for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts, offering direct access to one of Florida's premier OHV riding facilities. The campground is located within Withlacoochee State Forest in Hernando County, roughly 20 minutes northeast of Brooksville. All 50 campsites accommodate RVs or tents and include both electric hookups (30 and 50 amp service) and potable water connections.

Facilities include two modern bathhouses with flush restrooms and hot showers, an RV dump station, fire rings, grills, and a dedicated ATV/dirt bike wash station. A pavilion is available for rent. The campground is open year-round, and overnight campers can ride the trails from sunrise to sunset. Reservations are available through Reserve America up to 11 months in advance.

All campers must purchase an annual OHV pass before camping and must arrive before 5 PM on their first day for unit inspection and to receive the gate access code. Pets and alcohol are prohibited on the state-managed property. Cell service is unreliable and no WiFi is available.

location.directions: From Brooksville, head northeast on US-41. Turn east on Croom Road and continue to La Rose Road. The campground is at 6420 La Rose Rd, Brooksville, FL 34602.

payload.name: Lake Easton State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Utility sites 1-45 are open first-come-first-serve. Standard campground is closed through May 14, 2026. Reservations for the full season open on washington.goingtocamp.com. The campground typically closes November 1 through May 1, with off-season camping permitted in day-use and boat launch parking areas.
payload.short_description: Lake Easton State Park offers full-hookup and standard campsites on the shores of Lake Easton, located along I-90 between Seattle and Ellensburg in the Cascade foothills.
payload.medium_description: Lake Easton State Park campground sits at the edge of a reservoir formed by the Yakima River, offering both full-hookup utility sites and standard tent/RV sites. The park features four accessible restroom/shower buildings, a dump station, boat launch, swimming beach, and playground. Sites can accommodate RVs up to 60 feet. Note that highway noise from I-90 can be noticeable.
payload.long_description:
Lake Easton State Park campground provides a convenient mountain getaway along the I-90 corridor between Seattle and Ellensburg. The campground features utility sites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer) as well as standard non-hookup sites suitable for tents and RVs. Four accessible restroom buildings with showers serve the campground, and a dump station is available for RV waste disposal. Sites include fire pits and picnic tables.

The park sits along the shores of Lake Easton, a reservoir on the Yakima River, offering a boat launch, dock, and swimming beach. Additional amenities include a playground, basketball court, horseshoe pits, and an amphitheater. The surrounding area provides access to hiking, fishing, and winter activities at the adjacent Lake Easton Sno-Park.

Due to the campground's proximity to Interstate 90, highway noise is audible throughout the park. Light sleepers may want to bring earplugs. The campground operates seasonally from May through October, with limited winter camping available in the day-use and boat launch parking areas during the closure period.

location.directions: From Seattle, take I-90 east approximately 70 miles to Exit 70 (Lake Easton State Park). Turn right at the end of the off-ramp and follow signs to the park entrance.

links.title: Lake Easton State Park Official Page

payload.name: Clarkco State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The campground reopened March 19, 2026 following extensive renovations with all 43 RV sites, bathhouses, and amenities fully operational. Reservations available through reserve.mdwfp.com.
payload.short_description: Clarkco State Park offers 43 full-hookup RV sites and 6 renovated cabins on 815 acres near Quitman, Mississippi, featuring a 65-acre lake, disc golf, nature trails, and a splash pad.
payload.medium_description: Clarkco State Park, located about 15 miles south of Meridian near the Mississippi-Alabama state line, reopened in March 2026 after extensive renovations. The campground features 43 RV sites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer) on long concrete pads, each with a picnic table and grill. Amenities include three bathhouses (two with hot showers and laundry), a dump station, camp store with kayak rentals, playground, splash pad, and the Twin Pines 18-hole disc golf course.
payload.long_description:
Clarkco State Park encompasses 815 acres of gently rolling woodlands in Clarke County, Mississippi, about 15 miles south of Meridian. Originally developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1938, the park underwent comprehensive renovations from 2023-2026 and celebrated its grand reopening on March 19, 2026. The centerpiece is 65-acre Ivy Lake, which offers freshwater fishing and a boat launch.

The campground features 43 updated RV sites, each with full hookups including water, electricity, and sewer service. Sites have long concrete pads with picnic tables and grills. Three bathhouses serve the camping area, with two offering hot showers and laundry facilities. A central dump station is available for RV waste disposal. The park also has six fully renovated cabins with modern appliances, flatscreen TVs, walk-in showers, and outdoor porches with fire pits and grills.

Recreational offerings include 14 miles of nature and mountain biking trails, tennis and pickleball courts, a playground, splash pad, and the Twin Pines disc golf course. The park has a camp store with retail goods and kayak rentals. Day-use facilities include 60 picnic sites around Ivy Lake and three reservable pavilions.

location.directions: From Interstate 20 eastbound, take exit 153 onto Highway 145 for 3 miles, merge onto Highway 45 South for 18 miles, then turn left onto Highway 145 South for a quarter mile to the park entrance.

payload.name: Horse Heaven Group
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground operates Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend. Reservations required through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Tent-only group campground in the Laguna Mountains accommodating up to 100 people, located one hour east of San Diego at 5,600 feet elevation in Cleveland National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Horse Heaven Group Campground offers three group sites (Lupine, Buttercup, and Hollyhock) for tent camping in the pine forests of the Laguna Mountains. Despite its name, the campground has no equestrian facilities. The sites accommodate groups of 40 to 100 people and provide access to hiking trails including a segment of the Pacific Crest Trail. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Horse Heaven Group Campground is a tent-only group facility nestled in the pines at 5,600 feet elevation within the Laguna Mountains of Cleveland National Forest. Located about 50 miles east of San Diego, it provides a mountain escape with cool summer temperatures for groups ranging from 40 to 100 people across three separate sites: Lupine, Buttercup, and Hollyhock.

Despite the name, the campground has no equestrian sites or horse facilities. The area is known for excellent hiking opportunities, including access to a segment of the 2,650-mile Pacific Crest Trail and the Big Laguna Trail System. Mountain biking and wildlife viewing are also popular activities. The campground is managed by Westrek Services and operates seasonally from Memorial Day through Labor Day weekend.

This is an overnight camping facility only with no day use permitted. Vault toilets are available but potable water is not available at this site. Pets are allowed and campfires are permitted in designated areas, though fire restrictions may be imposed during hot, dry conditions.

location.directions: From San Diego, take I-8 east to the Sunrise Highway exit. Continue approximately 14 miles on Sunrise Highway until you see the Horse Heaven Group Campground sign, then turn onto the campground entrance road.

address.full: 11413 San Diego County Rd S 1, Mount Laguna, CA 91948

links.title: USFS Cleveland NF - Horse Heaven Group

payload.name: Timber Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed. Opens at 1 p.m. on Thursday, May 21, 2026. The campground will close early this season at noon on August 10, 2026, for a sewer system rehabilitation project and will remain closed through the end of the 2026 summer season. Expected to reopen for the 2027 season.
payload.short_description: Timber Creek Campground is the only campground on the west side of Rocky Mountain National Park, offering 98 reservable sites at 8,900 ft elevation along Trail Ridge Road, 8 miles north of Grand Lake.
payload.medium_description: Timber Creek is Rocky Mountain National Park's sole west-side campground, situated at 8,900 feet elevation along the Colorado River corridor. The 98-site campground accommodates tents and RVs up to 30 feet combined length. Sites include fire rings, picnic tables, and access to food storage lockers. Seasonal flush toilets, potable water, and a dump station are available. Forest recovery from pine beetle and wildfire has reduced shade but created open views and wildflower meadows.
payload.long_description:
Timber Creek Campground occupies a scenic location on the west slope of Rocky Mountain National Park, 8 miles north of the Grand Lake entrance at 8,900 feet elevation. As the only campground on the park's west side, it provides access to Trail Ridge Road, the Colorado River Trail, Coyote Valley Trail, and the historic Holzwarth site. The campground sits in a recovering forest landscape shaped by mountain pine beetle infestation and wildfire, resulting in minimal shade but expansive meadow views and wildflower displays.

The campground has 98 sites available by reservation only through Recreation.gov. Sites accommodate tents and RVs with a strict 30-foot combined vehicle length limit. Each site includes a fire ring with grate and picnic table. Seasonal amenities include flush toilets, potable water, a dump station, dish sinks, and food storage lockers for bear-country food storage compliance. Four ADA-accessible sites are available. The campground enforces an 8-person limit per site, with parking limited to 2 vehicles per site.

The town of Grand Lake lies 10 miles south, offering dining, supplies, and services. Check-in begins at 1 p.m. and checkout is noon. A 7-night maximum stay applies across all park campgrounds during summer. Campground reservations include a timed entry permit for park access (excluding Bear Lake Road corridor, which requires a separate permit).

location.directions: From Grand Lake: Drive north on US Highway 34 and enter the park via the Grand Lake Entrance. Continue 8 miles on Trail Ridge Road; the campground is on the left. From Estes Park: Enter via Beaver Meadows or Fall River Entrance and follow Trail Ridge Road west approximately 35 miles, crossing the Continental Divide. The campground entrance is on the right.

photos.name: Examples of Sites at Timber Creek.
A Tent Pitched at Timber Creek Campground

This is a map of Timber Creek Campground, divided into four loops (A-D) with numbered campsites. It shows key facilities like restrooms, water stations, food storage lockers, firewood sales, and an amphitheater. Accessible sites and a ranger station are also marked. The campground is near the Colorado River, with nearby trails leading to the Holzwarth Ranch Historic Site. Trail Ridge Road (Hwy 34) provides access, and the map is oriented with north at the top.
A Tent Pitched at Timber Creek Campground
Beautiful Timber Creek Flows Near the Campground

payload.name: Pigeon Point Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Individual sites are first-come-first-served; the group site requires reservations via Recreation.gov. No potable water available. During winter months, facilities have limited maintenance and trash pick-up.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground on the Wild and Scenic Trinity River at the start of the Class III Pigeon Point rafting run, with pull-through sites for boat trailers.
payload.medium_description: Pigeon Point Campground sits above the Wild and Scenic Trinity River at 1,100 feet elevation, marking the put-in for the popular Pigeon Point to Big Flat Class III rafting run. The campground offers both individual first-come-first-served sites and a reservable group site with a picnic pavilion. Pull-through parking accommodates boat trailers. No potable water is available; campers must filter from nearby sources or bring their own.
payload.long_description:
Pigeon Point Campground occupies a scenic spot above the Wild and Scenic Trinity River, approximately 15 miles west of Weaverville on Highway 299. At 1,100 feet elevation, the campground serves as a popular base for river recreation, sitting at the put-in for the Pigeon Point to Big Flat rafting section featuring Class III rapids. The Trinity River offers fishing, swimming, floating, kayaking, and boating, though hand-carry boat access only is available at this location.

The campground has individual sites available first-come-first-served for $12/night, plus a group site that accommodates up to 50 people and 10 vehicles for $75/night (reservations required via Recreation.gov). Pull-through parking is available for boat trailers. Amenities include vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings. There is no potable water; campers must filter or treat water from nearby sources or bring their own supply.

The Trinity River is subject to periodic flow changes from releases at Lewiston Dam. Current flow conditions can be obtained by calling (530) 246-7594. The Pigeon Point to Big Flat stretch is considered too dangerous for tubers and family canoeists; several commercial outfitters operate guided trips under Forest Service permits.

location.directions: From the Big Bar Ranger Station, travel east on Highway 299 for 8 miles. The campground is on the south side of Highway 299. From Weaverville, travel west on Highway 299 for approximately 15 miles.

payload.name: Lonesome Beaver Campground
payload.status_description: Open first-come, first-served with no reservations. Access via Sawmill Basin Road can be challenging; high-clearance vehicle recommended. Road conditions and accessibility vary seasonally based on weather and snowpack at this 8,000+ foot elevation.
payload.short_description: Remote 5-site BLM campground at 8,000 feet in Sawmill Basin, offering fire rings, picnic tables, potable water, and accessible restrooms in Utah's Henry Mountains region.
payload.medium_description: Lonesome Beaver Campground is a secluded 5-site BLM campground nestled in the middle of Sawmill Basin at over 8,000 feet elevation. Despite challenging road access, the setting rewards those who make the journey with picnic tables, fire rings, grills, potable water, and accessible restrooms. The campground operates on a pay-what-you-feel basis with no reservations required.
payload.long_description:
Lonesome Beaver Campground lies in the heart of Sawmill Basin within Utah's Henry Mountains region, sitting at an elevation exceeding 8,000 feet. This small, primitive BLM campground offers just five sites, making it an ideal destination for campers seeking solitude away from crowded developed campgrounds. The setting in the Mount Ellen-Blue Hills Wilderness Study Area provides access to remote desert landscapes and high-elevation terrain.

Each site is equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, grill, and bench. The campground provides potable water and accessible restrooms. The fee structure is unique: there is no minimum fee, and campers pay what they feel their experience is worth, payable on-site. No reservations are accepted; all sites are first-come, first-served.

Access requires traveling 23 miles south of Hanksville on Sawmill Basin Road, which can be challenging due to road conditions. High-clearance vehicles are recommended, and road accessibility varies seasonally depending on weather and snowpack at this elevation.

location.directions: From Hanksville, turn onto 100 West at the Post Office and travel 23 miles south on Sawmill Basin Road. Road conditions can be challenging; high-clearance vehicle recommended.

payload.name: Mount Magazine State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with restrooms open year-round. Reservations available online at reserve.arkansasstateparks.com or by phone. Check-in and check-out are both at 3:00 p.m. Campsites limited to 14 rental nights within a 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Campground atop Arkansas' highest point (2,753 ft) featuring 18 full-hookup sites with a barrier-free bathhouse, offering year-round access to sweeping Ozark Mountain views.
payload.medium_description: Mount Magazine State Park Campground sits atop the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 feet elevation. The campground offers 18 campsites with full hookups including water, electric (30/50 amp), and sewer connections. Amenities include a barrier-free bathhouse with hot showers and flush toilets, plus an RV dump station. Sites accommodate RVs up to 60 feet. The park provides access to hiking trails, rock climbing, hang gliding launch sites, and scenic overlooks of the surrounding Ozark-St. Francis National Forests.
payload.long_description:
Mount Magazine State Park Campground occupies a dramatic ridgetop setting on Arkansas' highest peak at 2,753 feet. The 18 campsites feature full hookups with water, electric, and sewer connections. Two Class AAA sites offer 50-amp electric service while 16 Class AA sites provide 30-amp service. The campground can accommodate RVs up to 60 feet in length, making it suitable for larger rigs despite the mountain access road.

The barrier-free bathhouse includes hot showers and flush toilets, remaining open year-round along with the campground itself. An RV dump station serves campers needing to empty holding tanks. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring per Arkansas State Parks standards. Pets are welcome but must remain on leash at all times.

Beyond the campground, the park offers extensive recreation including multiple hiking trails, world-class hang gliding from Signal Hill, technical rock climbing routes on sandstone bluffs, and mountain biking. The visitor center provides interpretive programs highlighting the unique natural diversity of the mountaintop ecosystem. The Lodge at Mount Magazine with its Skycrest Restaurant offers dining and additional lodging options nearby.

location.directions: Located at 16878 AR-309, Paris, AR 72855. From Paris, take Highway 309 South approximately 17 miles to the park entrance on the mountain summit.

payload.name: Erickson Springs
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. The campground typically operates from late spring to early fall, weather dependent. First-come, first-served only; no advance reservations. Payment via QR code using the Recreation.gov mobile app may be available on-site.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground in a cool, shaded spruce and fir forest near Anthracite Creek, with access to Dark Canyon Trail and the Raggeds Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Erickson Springs Campground sits in a dense spruce and fir forest near Anthracite Creek at approximately 6,800 feet elevation. The heavy tree cover keeps it cooler than surrounding areas. Each of the 18 primitive sites includes a tent pad, picnic table, and combination fire ring/grill. Vault toilets and trash service are provided, but there is no potable water. The Dark Canyon Trailhead is just past the campground, offering access to the Raggeds Wilderness Area.
payload.long_description:
Erickson Springs Campground offers a secluded camping experience in the Gunnison National Forest, tucked into a dense spruce and fir forest along Anthracite Creek. The heavy canopy creates a cool, shaded environment that provides relief from summer heat. The campground has 18 first-come, first-served primitive sites, each equipped with a tent pad, picnic table, and combination fire ring/grill. Vault toilets and trash collection are available, but campers must bring their own drinking water.

The location serves as a gateway to excellent backcountry recreation. The Dark Canyon Trailhead sits just beyond the campground, providing hiking and equestrian access into the Raggeds Wilderness Area. A separate parking area accommodates horse trailers. OHV enthusiasts can ride Forest Road 795 (Munsey Creek Road) north from the campground to the Raggeds Trailhead. OHV use within the campground itself is prohibited.

A separate picnic area with two tables and a restroom is located before the campground entrance. Sites can accommodate tents and smaller camping trailers up to 35 feet, though the narrow forest roads and tight sites make this campground better suited for smaller rigs.

location.directions: From Paonia, travel northeast on Highway 133 for approximately 15 miles to County Road 12 (Kebler Pass Road). Turn onto CR 12 and continue east for approximately 6 miles to the Erickson Springs Campground Road, just after crossing the bridge.

payload.name: FOREST LAKE DISPERSED AREA
payload.status_description: The area is typically accessible from June through October, with access roads closed by snow from mid-October through late May. Current fire danger is low with no active fire restrictions. Dispersed camping is limited to 14 days in any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: High-elevation dispersed camping area near Forest Lake in American Fork Canyon, accessible via rugged 4WD roads through aspen and spruce forests in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Forest Lake Dispersed Area offers primitive backcountry camping in the Pleasant Grove Ranger District of the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The area sits in a mid-elevation setting surrounded by aspen, spruce, and fir forests with mountain views. Access requires a high-clearance 4WD vehicle or ATV via Schaffer Fork Road, including a ford of the American Fork River. Forest Lake itself is a shallow holding basin for snowmelt with no fish.
payload.long_description:
Forest Lake Dispersed Area provides a true backcountry camping experience in Utah County within the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. Located in the Pleasant Grove Ranger District above American Fork Canyon, the area offers dispersed camping opportunities near Forest Lake, a scenic alpine destination surrounded by aspen groves and mountain meadows.

Access is challenging and requires high-clearance 4WD or ATV. From I-15 Alpine Exit 284, travel east on Highway 92 approximately 7 miles to the mouth of American Fork Canyon, continue on the Alpine Scenic Loop to the North Fork junction, turn left onto Highway 144 to Tibble Fork Reservoir, then proceed northeast on a dirt road for approximately 4.6 miles past the reservoir. Forest Lake is reached via Schaffer Fork, which begins just before Dutchman Flat. The route requires fording the American Fork River.

As dispersed camping, there are no developed amenities. Campers must be fully self-sufficient, bringing all water and packing out all trash. The area is popular with OHV users and connects to Ridge Trail #157.

location.directions: From I-15, take Alpine Exit 284 and travel east on Highway 92 for approximately 7 miles to American Fork Canyon. Continue on the Alpine Scenic Loop to the North Fork junction, turn left onto Highway 144 to Tibble Fork Reservoir. Continue northeast on a dirt road 4.6 miles past the reservoir to Shaffer Fork, which begins just before Dutchman Flat. High-clearance 4WD or ATV required. River ford required.

payload.name: Belfair State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available online at washington.goingtocamp.com or by phone at (888) 226-7688. Tree Loop is open for reservations May 15 through September 15 and has an 18-foot vehicle length limit.
payload.short_description: Washington state park campground on Hood Canal featuring full hookup, standard, and primitive sites with showers, potable water, and saltwater beach access.
payload.medium_description: Belfair State Park offers year-round camping on the shores of Hood Canal in Mason County. The campground provides a mix of full hookup, partial utility, standard, and primitive sites, along with restrooms with showers, potable water, a dump station, and ADA-accessible facilities. The park features saltwater swimming, a tidal marsh nature trail, and is part of the Cascadia Marine Trail.
payload.long_description:
Belfair State Park sits at the southern tip of Hood Canal, offering 65 acres of saltwater shoreline and wetland habitat. The campground provides diverse site options ranging from primitive tent sites to full-hookup RV sites with electric, water, and sewer connections. Standard amenities include flush restrooms with hot showers, potable water throughout, picnic tables and fire pits at each site, and firewood for sale. The Tree Loop area accommodates smaller rigs with an 18-foot vehicle length limit and is open seasonally from mid-May through mid-September.

The park is known for its unique tidal marsh and Big Mission Creek, which support a rich ecosystem. Recreational opportunities include saltwater swimming and wading at the beach, shellfish harvesting in season, and hiking the wetland nature trail. Horseshoe pits and volleyball courts are available. A marine trail campsite serves paddlers and sailors traveling the Cascadia Marine Trail on a first-come, first-served basis.

Four rental cabins provide roofed accommodation options, with one cabin allowing pets. The park operates year-round with reservations available through Washington State Parks. Leashed dogs are welcome in the campground, and ADA-accessible sites, restrooms, and trails are available throughout the park.

location.directions: From Belfair, head west on State Route 300. The park entrance is approximately 3 miles from downtown Belfair on the left side.

payload.name: Fort Stevenson State Park Equipment Rental
payload.status_description: This is an equipment rental service, not a campground. The facility operates seasonally with the marina store open daily Memorial Day through Labor Day. Boat rentals require phone reservations.
payload.short_description: Equipment rental service at Fort Stevenson State Park offering boats, kayaks, paddleboards, fat tire bikes, and winter gear for exploring Lake Sakakawea and park trails.
payload.medium_description: Fort Stevenson State Park Equipment Rental provides recreational equipment for visitors to explore Lake Sakakawea and the park's 10 miles of trails. Rentals include motorized fishing boats, pontoon boats, kayaks, canoes, stand-up paddleboards, paddleboats, aqua pads, fat tire bikes, cross-country skis, snowshoes, and kicksleds. This is an equipment rental facility, not an overnight camping area.
payload.long_description:
Fort Stevenson State Park Equipment Rental is a recreational equipment rental service located at Fort Stevenson State Park on the north shore of Lake Sakakawea, three miles south of Garrison, North Dakota. The facility offers the widest variety of rental equipment among North Dakota state parks, providing visitors with everything needed to explore the lake and surrounding trails.

Water equipment includes 16-foot and 17-foot motorized fishing boats ($150-175/day), 20-22 foot pontoon boats seating 10 ($400-450/day), kayaks and canoes ($32/half-day or $50/full day), stand-up paddleboards ($8/hour or $50/day), paddleboats ($8/hour or $50/day), and aqua pads ($20/hour or $80/day). All water rentals include life jackets and paddles where applicable.

Land-based rentals include fat tire bikes with helmets ($8/hour or $50/day) for exploring the park's nearly 10 miles of trails. Winter equipment includes cross-country skis, snowshoes, and kicksleds (each $15/day). This is an equipment rental service only and does not provide overnight camping. Visitors seeking campgrounds should book separately at Fort Stevenson State Park's campground facilities.

location.directions: Located at Fort Stevenson State Park, 3 miles south of Garrison, North Dakota on Lake Sakakawea. Park address: 1252A 41st Avenue NW, Garrison, ND 58540.

payload.name: South Abutment Pavilion
payload.status_description: Open for day use and group camping reservations. Arkabutla Lake is experiencing substantially lower water levels for an extended period while long-term repairs to Arkabutla Dam are completed. This affects boating access and water-based activities. Most day use and campground facilities remain open.
payload.short_description: Day-use pavilion area at Arkabutla Lake with two group electric campsites, overlooking the dam and lake in northwest Mississippi.
payload.medium_description: South Abutment Pavilion is primarily a day-use area at Arkabutla Lake featuring two reservable pavilions, restrooms, a playground, and picnic facilities on a bluff overlooking the dam. The site also offers two group campsites with electric hookups for overnight stays. Located about 30 minutes south of Memphis.
payload.long_description:
South Abutment Pavilion sits along Arkabutla Lake and Dam in the hills of northwest Mississippi. The facility is primarily designed for day use, featuring two pavilions, restrooms, a playground, and ample parking. Positioned on a bluff overlooking the dam structure and lake, the area provides scenic views and includes numerous picnic tables and grills throughout.

While the main purpose is day use, the facility also offers two group campsites (South Abutment 821 and 734) classified as Group Standard Electric sites, allowing overnight camping with electric hookups. The Coldwater River dam project offers some of the best sailing east of the Mississippi River, though current dam repairs have resulted in substantially lower water levels affecting boating access.

Arkabutla Lake is situated about 30 minutes south of Memphis. For those seeking more extensive camping options, three Class A campgrounds nearby support RVs and tent camping with full hookups, plus three primitive campgrounds for tent camping only.

location.directions: South Abutment Day Use is located on top of the hill between the South Abutment Campgrounds and the west side of Arkabutla Dam. Address: 3905 Arkabutla Dam Rd, Coldwater, MS 38618.

photos.name: Pavilion is close to playgrounds and has many picnic tables and grills in the area.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Arkabutla Lake will be experiencing substantially lower water levels for an extended period of time. Long-term repairs to Arkbabutla Dam must be completed before water levels can return to normal. This affects boating access and water-based activities on the lake. Many boat ramps are currently closed with Hwy. 51 Landing being the only open ramp. Most day use and campground facilities remain open for public use. For more information, please contact the Arkabutla Lake Field Office at 662-562-6261 or 662-292-1992. For a full list of all affected areas and facilities as well as to get information on what's going on at Arkabutla Lake, please visit our project page at [https://www.mvk.usace.army.mil/Missions/Programs-and-Project-Management/Project-Management/Projects/Arkabutla-Project-Page/][1]  [1]: https://www.mvk.usace.army.mil/Missions/Programs-and-Project-Management/Project-Management/Projects/Arkabutla-Project-Page/

payload.name: Glacial Lakes State Park Oak Ridge Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservations available online at reservemn.usedirect.com up to 120 days in advance. Seasonal showers may have limited availability outside peak summer months.
payload.short_description: Rustic 18-site campground atop a glacial esker in Pope County, offering shaded sites among oak trees with vault toilets and potable water near Signalness Lake.
payload.medium_description: Oak Ridge Campground provides a quieter, more primitive camping experience at Glacial Lakes State Park, situated atop a scenic esker ridge surrounded by oak trees. The 18 non-electric sites offer vault toilets and potable water, with shower access available at the Lower Campground 0.3 miles away. A fishing dock on Signalness Lake is just 0.2 miles from camp.
payload.long_description:
Oak Ridge Campground at Glacial Lakes State Park offers a rustic retreat set apart from the main day-use area. Perched atop an esker, a winding ridge formed by glacial meltwater streams, the campground provides 18 shaded campsites nestled among mature oak trees. This setting delivers more privacy and solitude compared to the Lower Campground.

The campground provides vault toilets and potable water via communal spigots. While there are no electric hookups or showers on-site, campers can access the shower building at the Lower Campground approximately 0.3 miles away. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill.

Glacial Lakes State Park sits within Minnesota's prairie-lake country, featuring rolling hills, native prairie remnants, and several lakes. A fishing dock on Signalness Lake is located just 0.2 miles from Oak Ridge Campground. The park offers hiking, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing across its glacially sculpted landscape.

location.directions: From Starbuck, Minnesota, head south on MN-29 for approximately 5 miles. Turn right onto County Road 41, then follow signs to Glacial Lakes State Park. Oak Ridge Campground is located on the esker ridge away from the main day-use area.

links.title: Glacial Lakes State Park Virtual Tour

payload.name: Horse Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Expected to reopen May 21, 2026. The campground typically operates from mid to late May through Labor Day. First-come, first-served only; no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: A nine-site first-come, first-served campground on Horse Creek in Shoshone National Forest, offering fishing access, vault toilets, and hand-pump drinking water about 12 miles north of Dubois.
payload.medium_description: Horse Creek Campground provides nine campsites along Horse Creek in the Shoshone National Forest. Each site includes RV parking, tent pads, a bear box, fire ring, and picnic table. Amenities include vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, and garbage collection. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no advance reservations and a maximum spur length of 32 feet.
payload.long_description:
Horse Creek Campground is a small, scenic facility located along Horse Creek in Wyoming's Shoshone National Forest, approximately 12 miles north of Dubois via Forest Road 285. The campground offers nine sites, each equipped with RV parking, tent pads, bear boxes for food storage, fire rings with grills, and picnic tables.

Amenities include vault toilets and potable drinking water available from a hand pump. Garbage collection is provided during the operating season. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Sites cost $20 per night, payable by cash or check only. Interagency Senior/Access pass holders receive a 50% discount on the site they occupy.

The area offers excellent fishing opportunities in Horse Creek and nearby streams. Food storage is mandatory per the Shoshone National Forest Food Storage Order. The campground has a 16-day stay limit and accommodates RVs and trailers up to 32 feet. The facility is not accessible for those with mobility impairments.

location.directions: From Dubois, take Forest Road 285 north 12 miles.

payload.name: Highway 7 Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for day-use recreation. The group pavilion is reservable through Recreation.gov at $50 per day. This is a day-use facility; overnight camping is not available. For overnight camping at DeGray Lake, use nearby USACE campgrounds such as Arlie Moore, Caddo Drive, or Edgewood.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on DeGray Lake featuring two swim beaches, a reservable group pavilion, playground, and picnic facilities on a wooded peninsula.
payload.medium_description: Highway 7 Recreation Area is a scenic day-use facility on a tree-covered peninsula along DeGray Lake, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The area offers two swim beaches, a playground, two restrooms, numerous picnic sites, and a reservable group pavilion with electricity that accommodates up to 50 people. Known for its resident black squirrel population, it's one of the most popular swimming destinations in the region.
payload.long_description:
Highway 7 Recreation Area is a day-use facility situated on a narrow, wooded peninsula adjacent to State Highway 7 along DeGray Lake in Clark County, Arkansas. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this scenic area provides two beach areas where visitors can swim and cool off during warm months, along with playground equipment for families.

The facility features a reservable group use pavilion located at the end of the peninsula, equipped with electricity, tables, and grills, accommodating up to 50 people. Two restrooms serve the area, and numerous picnic sites are scattered throughout the tree-covered grounds. The area is notably home to many black squirrels.

DeGray Lake encompasses 13,500 water acres with 207 miles of shoreline and hosts professional fishing tournaments and triathlons. The nearby DeGray Lake State Resort Park on the northern shores offers additional amenities including kayaking tours, golf, tennis courts, and horseback riding trails. Note that alcohol is prohibited at Highway 7 Recreation Area.

location.directions: From Interstate 30, take exit 78. Merge onto State Highway 7 north for 4 miles. Turn left into Highway 7 Recreation Area and proceed to the end of the road.

Pavilion with electricity, tables, grills, and scenic views.
One of two swim beaches located at Hwy 7 Recreation Area.

payload.name: Fir Group
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground typically operates from late May through late September. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Reservable group campground near Hume Lake in Sequoia National Forest, accommodating up to 100 people at 6,400 feet elevation amid towering pines.
payload.medium_description: Fir Group Campground is a group-only site in the Giant Sequoia National Monument, located 14 miles southeast of Grant Grove via Generals Highway. The campground sits at 6,400 feet elevation and can accommodate up to 100 guests with parking for 35 vehicles. Amenities include vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables, a group fire pit, and bear-proof food storage lockers. Nearby Hume Lake offers swimming, non-motorized boating, and fishing.
payload.long_description:
Fir Group Campground provides a single reservable group site nestled in the pine forests of the Sequoia National Forest's Hume Lake Ranger District. Situated at 6,400 feet elevation within the Giant Sequoia National Monument, the campground offers a secluded setting for gatherings of up to 100 people. The site includes back-in parking for 35 vehicles, vault toilets, potable drinking water, picnic tables, food storage lockers, and a central group fire pit.

The surrounding area provides excellent recreation opportunities. Several hiking trails pass nearby, and streams in the area offer trout fishing. Hume Lake, approximately 18 miles away, features swimming beaches, non-motorized boating, and additional hiking. The campground's location along the Generals Highway provides convenient access to both Kings Canyon and Sequoia National Parks.

The campground is operated by Rocky Mountain Recreation Company under a Forest Service concessionaire permit. Campfire permits are required for fires, and outside firewood is prohibited to prevent the spread of invasive insects. Fire restrictions may be enforced during hot, dry weather conditions.

location.directions: From Fresno, go east on Highway 180 towards Kings Canyon National Park. Take a right on the Generals Highway and travel approximately 10 miles south to the campground entrance on the left.
