payload.name: Viking Lake State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. The campground operates April 1 through October 31 and is 100% reservable. Water systems, shower buildings, and the dump station are operational. Closed November 1 through March 31.
payload.short_description: Viking Lake State Park offers a scenic lakeside campground in southwestern Iowa with 117 sites ranging from primitive tent camping to full-hookup RV sites, modern restrooms, showers, and direct lake access.
payload.medium_description: Viking Lake State Park in Montgomery County features a shady, lakeside campground with 117 reservable sites including tent-only, electric, full hookup, and buddy sites. Modern shower buildings, flush restrooms, and a dump station serve campers. The park surrounds a 136-acre lake with four boat ramps, six accessible fishing jetties, a sandy swimming beach, and a 5.5-mile multi-use trail circling the water.
payload.long_description:
Viking Lake State Park sits in the rolling hills of southwestern Iowa, centered on a 136-acre impoundment built in 1958. The campground occupies a wooded stretch of lakeshore with 117 sites: 61 standard electric (20/30/50 amp), 22 full-hookup (electric, water, sewer), 23 tent-only, 6 buddy sites for groups, and a youth group area. Modern shower buildings and flush restrooms serve the campground, and a sanitary dump station is available. Sites accommodate RVs up to 60 feet, with both back-in and pull-through configurations.

The park offers excellent water access via four boat ramps (no-wake speeds for all motors) and six universally accessible fishing jetties. A sandy beach on the west shore provides swimming, and the 5.5-mile multi-use trail encircles the lake for hiking, biking, and wildlife viewing. Three reservable picnic shelters, including one with an enclosed kitchenette, accommodate day-use gatherings.

The campground operates April 1 through October 31, with reservations required for all sites. Water systems and shower buildings typically open mid-April and close mid-October depending on weather. Reservations can be made up to three months in advance through the Iowa State Parks ReserveAmerica system.

location.directions: From Stanton, Iowa, travel 4 miles east on Highway 34, then 1 mile south on Viking Lake Road to the park entrance at 2780 Viking Lake Road, Stanton, IA 51573.

links.title: Iowa DNR Viking Lake State Park

payload.name: Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds
payload.status_description: Open year-round with free permit required. Permits must be requested at least 10 days in advance through the park; no same-day permits issued. Winter campsites are not maintained and snow travel requires snowshoes or skis. Current alert: flooding at Poplar Creek Crossing on the Grand Portage Trail due to beaver activity.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry campsites at the historic Pigeon River terminus of Grand Portage National Monument, accessible only by an 8.5-mile hike or paddling the Pigeon River from the Boundary Waters.
payload.medium_description: Fort Charlotte offers two primitive backcountry campsites at the Canada-U.S. border end of Grand Portage National Monument. Reaching these sites requires either hiking the 8.5-mile Grand Portage Trail or paddling down the Pigeon River from South Fowl Lake. Free permits are required and must be requested at least 10 days in advance through the park.
payload.long_description:
Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds are the only overnight camping option within Grand Portage National Monument, located where the historic Grand Portage fur trade route meets the Pigeon River at the U.S.-Canada border. The two campsites occupy ground steeped in history, near the reconstructed North West Company fort where voyageurs once portaged goods around the impassable High Falls.

Access requires commitment: hikers face an 8.5-mile trek along the Grand Portage Trail from Lake Superior, while paddlers can approach via the Pigeon River from South Fowl Lake in the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness. Both routes traverse rugged terrain with significant elevation changes. Each site accommodates up to nine people on tent platforms with picnic tables. Vault toilets are provided, but water from the river and trail sources is not potable. Campfires are permitted only in designated fire rings using dead, fallen wood. All trash must be packed out.

location.directions: Fort Charlotte is reached by hiking 8.5 miles on the Grand Portage Trail from the historic depot at Grand Portage Bay on Lake Superior, or by paddling down the Pigeon River from South Fowl Lake. An alternative trail entry point exists where Old Highway 61 intersects the portage via County Road 17.

links.title: Fort Charlotte Backcountry Campgrounds Official Website

photos.name: Serenity pervades the Pigeon River at Fort Charlotte.
Campsites have tent platforms, tables and shade trees.
Colorful and informative panels welcome visitors.
Panels welcome and inform visitors about Fort Charlotte.

payload.name: Shannon Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through mid-September. Currently open with a mix of first-come-first-served and reservable sites. Check-in is 2:00 p.m. and check-out is 12:00 p.m. 14-day stay limit applies.
payload.short_description: Scenic lakeside campground on Baker Lake in Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest with vault toilets, potable water, and a small boat launch.
payload.medium_description: Shannon Creek Campground sits on a forested slope leading down to the western shore of Baker Lake in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. The campground offers 18-19 campsites with picnic tables and fire rings, vault toilets, and potable water from a hand pump. A small gravel boat ramp provides lake access, though it is not suitable for larger boats. Views across the lake look toward the Noisy Creek drainage and the Noisy-Diobsud Wilderness Area.
payload.long_description:
Shannon Creek Campground is nestled along the western shore of Baker Lake in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest on the west side of the Cascades. The area showcases glacier-covered peaks, broad mountain meadows, and old-growth forests. On clear days, visitors can see Mt. Baker rising to 10,781 feet with its perpetually snow-capped summit.

The campground includes approximately 19 tent/trailer campsites spread across the forested hillside leading down to the lakeshore. Sites are equipped with picnic tables and fire rings, with vault toilets and potable water available. A small gravel boat ramp provides lake access for campers, though it is not suitable for larger boats. During Sockeye fishing season, boat launch access is limited to Shannon Creek campers only.

Baker Lake is a popular destination for boating, water skiing, canoeing, fishing, and swimming. The nearby Baker Lake and Baker River Trails offer family-friendly hikes through majestic old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar trees. The Baker River Trail leads to North Cascades National Park, while higher elevation trails access the Mt. Baker National Recreation Area and Mt. Baker Wilderness.

location.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to Burlington and Exit 230 onto State Highway 20. Continue past the Mt. Baker Ranger District Office in Sedro-Woolley and follow SR 20 east for 16 miles to milepost 82. Turn left (north) on Baker Lake Highway (Forest Service Road 11) and continue for 23.3 miles to Shannon Creek Campground on the right.

links.title: USFS Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF - Shannon Creek

payload.name: Caney Creek
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations accepted. No potable water or trash service available; campers must bring water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Primitive lakeside campground on Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Angelina National Forest with 26 first-come, first-served tent sites, vault toilets, and boat ramp access.
payload.medium_description: Caney Creek Recreation Area offers 26 primitive tent camping sites along the 114,000-acre Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Angelina National Forest. Each site includes a tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Vault toilets are located at the boat ramp parking lot, but there is no potable water or trash service. Campers should bring drinking water and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Caney Creek Recreation Area is a primitive lakeside campground situated on the shores of Sam Rayburn Reservoir within Angelina National Forest in East Texas. The 114,000-acre reservoir provides excellent opportunities for fishing and boating, with a boat ramp on site for water access. The campground features 26 designated tent camping sites, each equipped with a tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post.

This is a true primitive camping experience. There is no potable water available, so campers must bring their own supply. The campground operates on a pack-it-in, pack-it-out basis with no trash service provided. Two vault toilets are located at the boat ramp parking lot. Camping is first-come, first-served only; no advance reservations are accepted. Payment of $6 per night can be made via cash, check, or the Recreation.gov Scan and Pay mobile app.

Pets are welcome but must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet or otherwise under physical control. They are prohibited in swimming areas except for service animals. The campground is located about 6 miles east of Zavalla via Highway 63, then 6 miles on FM 2743, and 1 mile on Forest Service Road 336.

location.directions: From Zavalla, travel 6 miles east on Highway 63; turn left on FM 2743 for 6 miles; then left (northeast) on Forest Service Road 336 for 1 mile.

payload.name: Lake Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates from early June through early to mid-September. Sites are first-come, first-served at $15 per night, cash or check only. Food storage in bear boxes is required from March 1 through December 1.
payload.short_description: Small, primitive 6-site campground along Lake Creek on the Chief Joseph Scenic Highway in Shoshone National Forest, offering fishing and wildlife viewing at 6,400 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Lake Creek Campground is a quiet 6-site primitive campground nestled along Lake Creek in Wyoming's Shoshone National Forest. Located off the scenic Chief Joseph Highway at 6,400 feet elevation, the campground offers vault toilets, picnic tables, and bear boxes but no potable water. Maximum spur length is 22 feet. Sites are first-come, first-served at $15 per night with a 16-day stay limit.
payload.long_description:
Lake Creek Campground is a small, secluded campground containing six sites along Lake Creek in the Shoshone National Forest. Situated at 6,400 feet elevation off the Chief Joseph Scenic Highway (State Highway 296), the campground provides a base for exploring the Absaroka Range and the surrounding wilderness.

The campground offers basic amenities including vault toilets, picnic tables, and bear boxes for food storage. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own supply. The maximum spur length is 22 feet, making it suitable for tents, truck campers, and small trailers but not larger RVs. Food storage in the provided bear boxes is required due to active bear populations in the area.

Recreational opportunities include fishing in Lake Creek, wildlife viewing, scenic drives along the Chief Joseph Highway, and access to day hikes and backpacking routes in the surrounding forest. The 16-day stay limit allows for extended visits. Payment is cash or check only, and Interagency Senior/Access passes receive a 50% discount on the single site fee.

location.directions: From Cody, take State Highway 120 north for 16 miles. Turn left onto State Highway 296 (Chief Joseph Scenic Highway) and proceed approximately 46 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Coffee Mill
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations. Day use fee is $2 per vehicle; overnight camping is $10 per night. Payment accepted via Recreation.gov Scan and Pay, cash, or check.
payload.short_description: A 13-site first-come, first-served campground on the north shore of 750-acre Coffee Mill Lake in Caddo National Grassland, offering fishing, boating, and a scenic lakeside setting.
payload.medium_description: Coffee Mill Campground sits on the north shore of Coffee Mill Lake within Caddo National Grassland in northeast Texas. The 13-site campground offers vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables, and direct boat access to the 750-acre lake. A fishing pier provides easy shore access. Sites are first-come, first-served at $10 per night year-round.
payload.long_description:
Coffee Mill Campground is located on the north shore of the 750-acre Coffee Mill Lake within the Caddo National Grassland, about 12 miles north of Honey Grove, Texas. The recreation area was originally completed in 1968, with significant improvements added by volunteers in the early 1990s. The lake itself dates back to the 1930s and remains a popular destination for fishing and non-motorized boating.

The campground features 13 campsites, each with a picnic table. Vault toilets and potable water are available on-site. A fishing pier and boat ramp provide access to the lake, making this a solid choice for anglers. Quiet hours are enforced between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM.

All sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Campers can pay the $10 nightly fee using the Recreation.gov Scan and Pay feature via the mobile app, or with cash or check. Day use is $2 per vehicle. Pets are allowed but must be leashed (6 feet maximum) or otherwise under physical control.

location.directions: From Honey Grove, Texas, follow FM 100 north 12 miles to FM 409. Turn left and go west 5 miles to camp entrance on the left.

address.full: 4707 Farm To Market Rd 409, Honey Grove, TX 75446

links.title: USFS Coffee Mill Lake Recreation Area

payload.name: Simax Group Camp
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. It opens May 22, 2026 and operates through late September. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. Potable water is activated in May and shut off by September 30.
payload.short_description: Fully accessible group campground on the northeast shore of Crescent Lake in Deschutes National Forest, offering four group sites and a pavilion with water activities and stunning alpine scenery.
payload.medium_description: Simax Group Camp sits on the northeast end of Crescent Lake in central Oregon's Deschutes National Forest. Designed as a fully accessible campground, it features four group sites accommodating up to 40 people each, plus a 50-person pavilion. The brilliant blue-green lake offers water skiing, sailing, swimming, and fishing for kokanee salmon and trout. Paved roads, spurs, and an accessible trail system make this an excellent choice for groups with varied mobility needs.
payload.long_description:
Simax Group Campground occupies a prime position on the northeast shore of Crescent Lake, a naturally glaciated alpine lake known for its exceptional blue-green water and sandy beaches. The campground sits within a forest of towering lodgepole pine, mountain hemlock, fir, and spruce trees typical of the central Oregon Cascades.

The campground was designed from the ground up for full accessibility, featuring paved roads and spurs, designated tent pads at each site, and an accessible trail system. Four group sites (A, B, C, and D) each accommodate up to 40 people, while a large pavilion handles groups up to 50. Site A is better suited to tent camping, with 8 designated tent pads and limited RV parking.

Recreation centers on Crescent Lake, where visitors enjoy water skiing, sailing, windsurfing, and swimming. Anglers target kokanee salmon, mackinaw, rainbow and brown trout, and mountain whitefish. The Fawn Lake Trail departs nearby, offering a 4.7-mile hike through mixed conifer forest to views of Redtop and Lakeview Mountains. A resort on Crescent Lake provides lodging, a general store, and equipment rentals.

location.directions: From Crescent, OR: Travel 12.2 miles west on County Road 61/Crescent Cut-off Road, then 3.5 miles north on Highway 58, then 2.2 miles west on Forest Road 60, then 1 mile south on Forest Road 6005.

payload.name: Elkhead Reservoir State Park
payload.status_description: Open for camping May 1 through November 30. No current closures or alerts. Check-in is 1 p.m., check-out is noon. Maximum stay is 14 days within a 28-day period.
payload.short_description: Elkhead Reservoir State Park offers 46 campsites with shade shelters and electric hookups along a 900-acre reservoir in northwest Colorado's Yampa Valley, open May through November.
payload.medium_description: Elkhead Reservoir State Park sits at 6,400 feet elevation near Craig in northwest Colorado, featuring a 900-acre reservoir surrounded by high desert terrain. The park's two campgrounds provide 46 sites with gravel pads, picnic tables, shade shelters, and fire pits. Electric hookups are available at select sites. Boating, swimming, fishing, and 10.5 miles of hiking trails round out the recreation options.
payload.long_description:
Elkhead Reservoir State Park occupies 2,100 acres in Moffat County, centered on a 900-acre reservoir that serves as an oasis in the high desert of the Yampa Valley. The park lies about 11 miles northeast of Craig and offers warm-water fishing for bass, bluegill, and crappie, plus boating, swimming, and jet skiing when the boat ramp opens in mid-May.

Two campgrounds provide 46 sites, including six that are ADA accessible. Each site features a hardened gravel pad, picnic table, shade shelter, and fire pit. Some sites offer electric hookups. The park has vault restrooms but no potable water or dump station on site; the nearest dump station is 12 miles west at Yampa River State Park. Reservations are made through cpwshop.com up to six months in advance.

Beyond camping, 10.5 miles of trails wind through sagebrush and juniper terrain with views of the reservoir and surrounding mesas. Leashed pets are welcome on trails and in campgrounds. The park gates are open daily from 5 a.m. to 10 p.m.

location.directions: From Craig, travel east on Highway 40 for approximately 7 miles to Moffat County Road 29. Turn left and continue north 4 miles, then turn right on MCR 28 to enter the park.

payload.name: Lemolo #2 Forebay Forest Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the season. This is a free, first-come, first-served campground with no reservations. No potable water or garbage services available. Maximum 14-day stay.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive forest camp in a grove of old-growth trees along Lemolo #2 Forebay with boat ramp access to Lemolo Lake in the Umpqua National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Lemolo #2 Forebay Forest Camp is a quiet, secluded free campground nestled in a grove of large old-growth trees along the Lemolo #2 Forebay. The site features a boat ramp providing access to Lemolo Lake. This first-come, first-served campground offers vault toilets but no potable water or garbage services.
payload.long_description:
Lemolo #2 Forebay Forest Camp sits in a peaceful grove of large old-growth trees along the Lemolo #2 Forebay in the Umpqua National Forest. This free, primitive campground offers pond-side campsites and includes a boat ramp that provides access to Lemolo Lake, making it a solid choice for anglers and paddlers seeking a quieter alternative to the busier developed campgrounds around Diamond Lake.

The campground is first-come, first-served with no fees required. Amenities are minimal: vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water and no garbage services, so campers must bring their own water supply and pack out all trash. The maximum vehicle length is 25 feet. Nearby attractions include Toketee Falls, Umpqua Hot Springs, and Watson Falls.

location.directions: From Glide, OR, take Highway 138E eastbound toward Diamond Lake for 41 miles. Turn left on NF-34 and continue for 5 miles. Turn left on NF-3402 and continue until reaching Lemolo #2 Forebay Forest Camp on the left.

payload.name: Clear Creek Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Operates May through mid-October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Fire restrictions may apply; contact Cuba Ranger District for current conditions.
payload.short_description: A secluded group campground in Santa Fe National Forest near Cuba, NM, featuring a 40-foot shelter with picnic tables and vault toilet for groups up to 35 people.
payload.medium_description: Clear Creek Group Campground offers a dedicated group site in Santa Fe National Forest, about 11 miles east of Cuba. The site accommodates up to 35 people with a large 40-foot diameter shelter, picnic tables, vault toilet, and stand-up grill. Located in the last loop of Clear Creek Campground alongside the creek, it provides cool shade among ponderosa pines and Engelmann spruce in the Jemez Mountains.
payload.long_description:
Clear Creek Group Campground sits in the cool, pine-covered Jemez Mountains of Santa Fe National Forest, less than two hours from Albuquerque. The single group site can host up to 35 people and includes a 40-foot diameter shelter with picnic tables, a stand-up grill, vault toilet, and parking for up to 5 vehicles plus one bus or RV. The campground allows 3 tent pads and 2 RV/trailer camping units.

The surrounding area offers excellent recreation opportunities. Local streams and San Gregorio Reservoir provide fishing, while the nearby San Pedro Parks Wilderness features scenic day hikes with minimal elevation gain, ideal for both beginner and experienced backpackers. Three main trailheads (San Gregorio, Palomas, and Los Pinos) are within driving distance.

Wildlife in the area includes black bears, mule deer, elk, and numerous bird species. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 PM to 7 AM, and no ATV/UTV/ORV use is permitted in the campground.

location.directions: From Cuba, New Mexico, travel 11 miles east on New Mexico State Highway 126. The campground is approximately 1.5 hours from Albuquerque.

photos.name: A parking area with a group shelter and vault toilet in a forest.
A metal ramada provides shade for picnic tables in a coniferous forest.

payload.name: Clear Springs Campground
payload.status_description: Open May 15 through October 15 with full services. Remains accessible October 16 through May 14 with reduced services. No reservations; first-come, first-served. 14-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground along Dairy Creek in the Fremont-Winema National Forest, popular with hunters and anglers seeking rainbow trout.
payload.medium_description: Clear Springs Campground is a small, free primitive site at 5,400 feet elevation along Dairy Creek in Oregon's Fremont-Winema National Forest. The campground offers dispersed camping spaces with minimal developed facilities including one shared picnic table, fire ring, and vault toilet. Potable water is available, but campers must pack out all trash. The area is popular with hunters during fall season and anglers targeting rainbow trout in Dairy Creek.
payload.long_description:
Clear Springs Campground sits at approximately 5,400 feet elevation along Dairy Creek in the Paisley Ranger District of Oregon's Fremont-Winema National Forest, about an hour southwest of Paisley. This primitive free campground offers a mix of dispersed camping spaces with minimal developed infrastructure, making it ideal for those seeking a backcountry experience without venturing far from road access.

The campground provides basic amenities including potable water from faucets, one vault toilet, a shared picnic table, and a fire ring. There is no garbage service, so campers must pack out all trash. The 14-day stay limit applies forest-wide.

The site sees its heaviest use during hunting season, as the surrounding forest provides good habitat for game. Anglers can pursue rainbow trout in Dairy Creek, which runs directly alongside the campground. Access requires navigating forest roads from Paisley, Lakeview, or Bly, with the final approach via Forest Road 2800-047.

location.directions: From Paisley, head west on Mill Street which becomes Forest Road 33. Continue 20 miles, staying left. At the T-intersection with Forest Road 28, stay left and continue 2 miles. Just before crossing Dairy Creek, turn right on Forest Road 2800-047 and go 4 miles to the pull-off marked Clear Springs. From Lakeview, take Highway 140 west 3 miles, turn right on County Road 2-16 for 5 miles, then left on County Road 2-16A which becomes Forest Road 28. Follow FR 28 for 19 miles, turn left on Forest Road 2800-047 after crossing Dairy Creek, and go 4 miles.

payload.name: QUEMADO LAKE - EL CASO CG #3
payload.status_description: The campground is open. A harmful algal bloom advisory remains in effect for Quemado Lake itself, making the water unsafe for drinking, swimming, wading, or pet contact. Non-contact boating is permitted. No potable water is available at the campground.
payload.short_description: Primitive, free campground near Quemado Lake in Gila National Forest, nestled among ponderosa pines and cottonwoods at 7,700 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: El Caso Campground #3 is part of the El Caso I-IV complex at Quemado Lake Recreation Area in Gila National Forest. This partially developed campground sits in a valley alongside an intermittent stream, surrounded by ponderosa pine and cottonwood trees. Popular with hunters, groups, and horse campers seeking a primitive experience, the campground offers vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables but no potable water or hookups.
payload.long_description:
El Caso Campground #3 is one of four primitive campgrounds comprising the El Caso I-IV complex at Quemado Lake Recreation Area in New Mexico's Gila National Forest. Located at 7,700 feet elevation, the campgrounds occupy a shaded valley stretching along an intermittent stream, with ponderosa pine and cottonwood providing natural canopy. The area is within hiking distance of 130-acre Quemado Lake.

This partially developed campground caters to those seeking a more rustic experience. While vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings are provided, campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash. No fees are charged, and sites operate first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit. The campground is popular with hunters, organized groups, and horse campers due to its spacious layout and proximity to trails.

location.directions: From Quemado, NM, drive south on Highway 32 for approximately 14 miles to the Quemado Lake/Highway 103 junction. Turn east on Highway 103 and continue about 4 miles, then follow Forest Road 13 to the campground.

payload.name: Rillway Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations via Recreation.gov. Entry via combination lock provided in confirmation email. Check-in 2:00 PM, check-out 11:00 AM.
payload.short_description: Historic 1920s Forest Service rental cabin in Deep Creek Canyon, 14 miles east of Townsend, Montana. Sleeps 6 with rustic furnishings but no electricity or running water.
payload.medium_description: Rillway Cabin is a charming 1920s-era cabin tucked against a moss-covered canyon wall with Deep Creek flowing through the backyard. Located along Highway 12 in Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest, it offers year-round vehicle access and sleeps up to 6 guests on three bunk beds. The cabin includes a fireplace insert, propane cook stove, propane lanterns, table and chairs, cookware, and cleaning supplies. Guests must bring drinking water, sleeping bags, food, and small propane cylinders. A vault toilet outhouse is on site.
payload.long_description:
Rillway Cabin traces its history to Dr. A.C. Kelly, a Townsend physician who obtained a Forest Service permit for the site in 1918. Built between 1918 and 1922, the cabin was later sold to Nellie Hale Averill and her son-in-law Floyd L. Hollaway, giving rise to the name "Rillway" as a combination of the two family names.

The cabin sits in scenic Deep Creek Canyon with the creek splashing through the backyard. It offers the easiest access of any cabin on the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest, being accessible by vehicle year-round. Three bunk beds with mattresses accommodate up to 6 guests. Amenities include a fireplace insert, propane lanterns, propane cook stove, table and chairs, cookware, utensils, cleaning supplies, axe, and shovel. Firewood availability varies and is not guaranteed June through August.

Guests must bring sufficient drinking water, sleeping bags, warm clothing, food, flashlight, toilet paper, garbage bags, and one or two small propane cylinders for the lanterns and stove. All garbage and food must be packed out. Entry is via combination lock provided in the reservation confirmation email.

location.directions: From the 4-way stop in Townsend, turn east on Highway 12. Follow the road 14 miles and watch for the Rillway Cabin sign along the right side of the highway at the 14-mile marker. Only right turns are allowed when departing due to sight distance concerns. A turnaround is available approximately 1 mile east if you need to travel west.

links.title: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF Rillway Cabin

payload.name: Curtis Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through September 15. As of early May 2026, the campground has not yet opened for the season. All sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Wooded 12-site campground above the National Elk Refuge offering stunning views of the Tetons, located just 8 miles from downtown Jackson, Wyoming.
payload.medium_description: Curtis Canyon Campground is a first-come, first-served forest campground in the Bridger-Teton National Forest, perched above the National Elk Refuge with panoramic views of the Teton Range. The 12 wooded sites accommodate tents and RVs up to 24 feet, each equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and bear-proof food storage box. At just 8 miles from Jackson, it offers convenient access to hiking and horseback riding while maintaining a secluded mountain atmosphere.
payload.long_description:
Curtis Canyon Campground sits in a forested setting above the National Elk Refuge, offering campers quick access to sweeping views of both the refuge and the iconic Teton mountain range. Located approximately 8 miles and 16 minutes from downtown Jackson, Wyoming, this Bridger-Teton National Forest campground provides a balance of accessibility and backcountry feel.

The campground features 12 individual sites spread through the woods, each with a picnic table, fire ring, and bear-proof food storage container. Vault toilets are provided, and drinking water is available from a hand pump when operational. A dumpster on-site handles trash disposal. All sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations accepted.

The area serves as a launching point for hiking and horseback riding opportunities just minutes from camp. The nearby Curtis Canyon Overlook Interpretive Site offers an easily accessible viewpoint. A two-vehicle maximum applies per site, with a $7 additional vehicle fee on top of the $20 nightly rate.

location.directions: From Jackson, head east on US-189/West Broadway Avenue for approximately 1 mile. At the end of West Broadway, turn left onto North Elk Refuge Road and continue for about 3 miles. Make the first left onto National Elk Refuge Road 2240. After 1 mile, take the first right and continue 3 miles to the campground entrance on the right. Total distance: 8 miles, approximately 16 minutes.

address.full: 2 Curtis Canyon Fs Campground, Jackson, WY 83001

payload.name: Warren Fork Trailhead Campground
payload.status_description: This is a trailhead with limited roadside parking, not a developed campground. No overnight camping facilities are available at the trailhead itself. Overnight use in the adjacent Hoover Wilderness requires a wilderness permit. Highway 120 (Tioga Pass Road) is subject to seasonal closure due to snow.
payload.short_description: Warren Fork Trailhead provides access to the Hoover Wilderness near Tioga Pass. This is a trailhead with limited roadside parking, not a developed campground.
payload.medium_description: Warren Fork Trailhead is a small roadside pullout providing access to the Warren Fork Trail in the Hoover Wilderness, located about a mile east of Ellery Lake on Highway 120 (Tioga Pass Road). This is not a developed campground but rather a trailhead with limited parking. Overnight camping in the wilderness area requires a wilderness permit year-round.
payload.long_description:
Warren Fork Trailhead serves as the starting point for the Warren Fork Trail, a 1.5-mile path following Warren Fork Creek through a canyon between Tioga Peak and Lee Vining Peak to a high meadow in the Hoover Wilderness. The trailhead is located at approximately 9,500 feet elevation along Highway 120, about a mile east of Ellery Lake outlet.

This is not a developed campground. The site consists only of limited roadside parking pulled off the edge of the pavement with no camping facilities, toilets, water, or other amenities. Overnight use in the adjacent Hoover Wilderness requires a wilderness permit year-round (day use does not require a permit). Campers seeking developed facilities should consider nearby Ellery Lake Campground or other established campgrounds along Highway 120.

Water from creeks, lakes, and springs in the area should be treated before drinking. The trailhead and Highway 120 are subject to seasonal closures due to snow, typically from November through late May or early June depending on conditions.

location.directions: From Highway 395, take Highway 120 (Tioga Pass Road) west toward Yosemite. The trailhead is approximately one mile east of Ellery Lake outlet, with limited roadside parking off the edge of the pavement.

payload.name: Damsite - Fall River Lake
payload.status_description: Open April 1 through October 31. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Corps of Engineers campground below Fall River Lake spillway in the Kansas Flint Hills, offering 13 sites with electric/water hookups, vault toilets, and access to lake recreation.
payload.medium_description: Damsite Campground sits below the Fall River Lake spillway in the Flint Hills of Greenwood County, Kansas. The 13-site campground is split between Damsite West and Damsite East, connected by a river bridge with limited clearance. Sites range from water-only to 50-amp electric hookups, with vault toilets, drinking water, fire rings, picnic tables, and a playground. The lake offers boating, swimming, water skiing, and fishing for white bass, crappie, bluegill, and channel catfish.
payload.long_description:
Damsite Campground occupies a scenic location directly below the Fall River Lake dam and spillway, where Fall River flows through the rolling Flint Hills prairie of southeastern Kansas. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Tulsa District, the campground provides 13 reservable sites across two loops: Damsite West and Damsite East. The loops are separated by a river bridge with limited clearance and weight restrictions, so larger RVs and trailers should use the appropriate entrance to avoid the bridge crossing.

Site amenities vary: two premium sites offer 50-amp electric with water hookups, six sites have 30-amp electric with water, and five sites provide water hookups only. All sites include fire rings and picnic tables. Campground facilities include vault toilets, potable drinking water, and a playground. The lake itself spans 15 miles up the Fall River valley, offering boating, swimming, water skiing, and quality fishing for white bass, bluegill, crappie, green sunfish, and channel catfish.

Birdwatchers and wildlife enthusiasts can explore the adjacent 8,000-acre public wildlife area, home to prairie chickens, wild turkeys, white-tailed deer, waterfowl, and quail. Fall River State Park is nearby for additional hiking and canoeing opportunities along the river.

location.directions: From US HWY 400, turn left (north) at mile marker 344 (Z 50 Rd) 0.09 miles, turn right (east) 2.4 miles, turn right (south) at entrance to park.

payload.name: Cape Perpetua
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season, operating March through September. Reservations available through Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served. The Cape Perpetua Visitor Center is temporarily closed for remodel through May 2026, though the parking lot, restrooms, and trails remain accessible.
payload.short_description: Coastal campground in Siuslaw National Forest nestled along Cape Creek, offering easy access to 23 miles of trails, old-growth forests, tidepools, and stunning Pacific Ocean overlooks.
payload.medium_description: Cape Perpetua Campground sits along the banks of Cape Creek within the Cape Perpetua Scenic Area on Oregon's central coast. Surrounded by towering Sitka spruce, Douglas fir, and alder trees, the campground offers 39 sites with flush toilets and drinking water. Trails lead directly from camp to the Giant Spruce, coastal tidepools, and the St. Perpetua viewpoint, one of the best vantage points on the Oregon Coast.
payload.long_description:
Cape Perpetua Campground occupies a prime location in the Cape Perpetua Scenic Area, positioned between the dense forests of Siuslaw National Forest and the rugged Oregon coastline. The 39 campsites are arranged along Cape Creek under a canopy of old-growth Sitka spruce, Douglas fir, and alder. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with flush toilets and hand-pump drinking water available throughout the campground.

A 23-mile trail network begins at the campground, offering routes through ancient forest to dramatic coastal features. Popular destinations include the Giant Spruce, one of the largest trees on the Oregon Coast, and the St. Perpetua viewpoint at 803 feet elevation. The Cape Perpetua Visitor Center is a short hike from camp and features interpretive exhibits and an outdoor viewing deck with panoramic ocean views.

The campground operates seasonally from March through September. Sites are reservable through Recreation.gov, with some available first-come, first-served. The location provides convenient access to tidepools, whale watching, and Highway 101 exploration along this scenic stretch of coastline.

location.directions: Located on Highway 101, 22 miles north of Florence, Oregon and 3 miles south of Yachats, Oregon. Turn east off Highway 101 into the Cape Perpetua Scenic Area, then take a right at the split following signs to Cape Perpetua Campground.

payload.name: Van Deriet Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally, typically late June through early October depending on snow conditions. No fees or reservations required. Mandatory bear-resistant food storage is in effect forest-wide. No vehicle access; fly-in only.
payload.short_description: A primitive 6-site backcountry campground accessible only by small aircraft, located at an airstrip 30 miles west of Augusta on the Rocky Mountain Front.
payload.medium_description: Van Deriet Campground is a unique fly-in campground situated at a backcountry airstrip in Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest. With 6 primitive sites, vault toilets, and a hand pump for drinking water, this free campground serves pilots exploring Montana's Rocky Mountain Front and the gateway to the Bob Marshall Wilderness. No vehicle access exists; the site is maintained in partnership with the Montana Aeronautics Division.
payload.long_description:
Van Deriet Campground, also known as Vanderiet Memorial Pilots Campground, offers a rare backcountry camping experience exclusively for pilots who can fly into the adjacent airstrip. Located 30 miles west of Augusta amid the Rocky Mountain Front, this primitive 6-site campground provides vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. The campground honors Ray Van De Riet, a local cattle rancher instrumental in developing camping facilities at Montana's backcountry airstrips.

The site sits near the edge of the Bob Marshall Wilderness Complex, offering access to some of Montana's most pristine backcountry. Bears frequent the area, and mandatory food storage in approved containers is required. Campers must store food out of sight and remove all food from the area after eating. Light usage makes this an uncrowded destination for adventurous aviators seeking solitude on the Rocky Mountain Front.

location.directions: No vehicle access. Fly into the adjacent backcountry airstrip approximately 30 miles west of Augusta along the Benchmark Road corridor. The campground is located at the south end of the airstrip.

links.title: Rocky Mountain Ranger District Augusta Info Station

payload.name: Sweetwater Guard Station Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping, first-come first-served with no fee. No winter road maintenance; access is typically snowmobile-only from late fall through spring depending on conditions. A 14-day stay limit applies.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at the base of Wyoming's Wind River Mountains with 11 sites featuring fire rings and bear-proof trash receptacles. First-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.medium_description: Sweetwater Guard Station Campground offers 11 primitive sites (3 walk-in and 8 pull-in) at the historic site of the first Fire Guard Station in Wyoming's Wind River Mountains. Located next to the Sweetwater River with the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail on the opposite bank, the campground provides fire rings, picnic tables at drive-up sites, one accessible pit toilet, and bear-proof trash receptacles. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Sweetwater Guard Station Campground sits at the base of the Wind River Mountains in western Wyoming, roughly 69 miles from Lander and 73 miles from Rock Springs. The campground occupies the historic site of the first Fire Guard Station in the area and features 11 sites: 3 walk-in tent sites and 8 pull-in sites including one group site. The Sweetwater River flows alongside the campground, with the Continental Divide National Scenic Trail accessible on the opposite bank.

All drive-up sites include picnic tables with wheelchair-accessible gaps in seating and fire rings with grill attachments. The walk-in sites lack improved paths and picnic tables. A single accessible pit vault toilet serves the campground centrally, and bear-proof trash receptacles are provided throughout. There is no potable water, hookups, or cell phone reception. Tree coverage offers natural shade in lieu of picnic shelters.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees and no reservations. A 14-day stay limit applies. The access road is an improved dirt road well-maintained during summer months. No winter road maintenance is provided, making the site typically accessible only by snowmobile during winter.

location.directions: From State Highway 28, turn north onto County Road 5-13/Continental Divide Road. Continue for 15 miles and turn east onto BLM Road 4105/Sweetwater Gap Ranch Road for 6 miles. Staying left, travel down BLM Road 4112 for 2.3 miles to the campground loop road.

payload.name: Pipi Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Potential opening date is May 22, 2026. Season runs May through October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov up to 6 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Riverside camping in Eldorado National Forest with 51 sites across three loops, offering fishing and swimming on the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River at 4,100 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Pipi Campground (pronounced "pie pie") provides tent and RV camping along the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River in California's Eldorado National Forest. At 4,100 feet elevation, the campground features 51 sites spread across three loops shaded by cedar and fir trees. Rainbow trout are regularly stocked in the river, and a paved walkway provides wheelchair-accessible fishing access.
payload.long_description:
Pipi Campground sits at 4,100 feet elevation in the Eldorado National Forest, offering 51 campsites across three loops along the Middle Fork of the Cosumnes River. The area is shaded by a dense mixture of conifers including cedar and fir trees, typical of the central Sierra Nevada. The campground accommodates both tent and RV camping, with single, double, and triple sites available.

Rainbow trout are regularly stocked in the river, making it a popular fishing destination. A paved river walkway meanders along the water for just under a mile, providing wheelchair-accessible fishing from designated piers. Swimming opportunities are available along the river, and a day-use picnic area with 8 sites sits near the campground.

Historically, the native Miwok people camped in this region during summertime. Today the campground operates seasonally from May through October. Bear activity is common in the area, and all food, toiletries, and garbage must be stored in the provided bear boxes. Campfire restrictions may apply seasonally depending on fire conditions.

location.directions: From Jackson, head east on Highway 88 for 26 miles to Omo Ranch Road. Turn left (north) on Omo Ranch Road and follow for 0.8 miles to North South Road. Turn right on North South Road and continue for about 6 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Susquehanna State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open for the season, operating from the first weekend in May through the last weekend in October. Reservations are highly recommended for weekend camping.
payload.short_description: Susquehanna State Park in Maryland offers camping, hiking, fishing, and historical sites along the Susquehanna River.
payload.medium_description: Susquehanna State Park in Havre de Grace, Maryland, offers a variety of outdoor activities, including camping, hiking, fishing, and boating, set against a backdrop of rich history and scenic river views.
payload.long_description:
Susquehanna State Park, located along the Susquehanna River in Havre de Grace, Maryland, offers a diverse range of recreational activities amidst a rich historical backdrop. The park encompasses over 2,700 acres of dense forests, rocky terrains, and riverfront landscapes, making it a haven for outdoor enthusiasts.

The campground features 69 sites, six of which are equipped with electric hookups, and six mini-cabins available for rent. Each campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground operates from the first weekend in May through the last weekend in October. Comfort stations with hot showers are available in each loop, and a camp store provides essentials like firewood and ice.

Outdoor activities abound, with over 15 miles of trails suitable for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. The Susquehanna River offers excellent fishing opportunities, with species such as pike, perch, and bass. Boating enthusiasts can access the river via the Lapidum Boat Ramp. The park also features the Rock Run Historic Area, which includes a working gristmill, the Carter-Archer Mansion, and remnants of the Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal.

For picnicking, the Deer Creek Picnic Area provides shaded tables, grills, two picnic shelters, and a modern restroom. Large open fields nearby are ideal for family games. The pavilions are available for rent from March through October and are perfect for gatherings like family reunions or company picnics.

location.directions: From I-95, take Exit 89 for MD-155 toward Havre de Grace. Head north on MD-155 for approximately 2.8 miles, then turn right onto MD-161. Continue for 1.5 miles, then turn right onto Wilkinson Road. The park entrance is about 0.8 miles ahead.

address.full: 729 Craigs Corner Rd, Havre De Grace, MD 21078

payload.name: Rifle River Grousehaven Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Reservations available through MiDNRReservations.com or by calling 800-447-2757. Some dates transition to first-come-first-served when the reservation window closes.
payload.short_description: Modern lakeside campground in Rifle River Recreation Area with 75-80 electric sites, showers, and a swim beach on Grousehaven Lake.
payload.medium_description: Grousehaven Campground sits on the shores of Grousehaven Lake within Michigan's 4,449-acre Rifle River State Recreation Area. This modern campground offers wooded electric sites spread across two loops, with flush restrooms, hot showers, a dump station, and a designated swim beach with accessible beach mats.
payload.long_description:
Grousehaven Modern Campground occupies a prime location directly on Grousehaven Lake in the Rifle River State Recreation Area. The campground features approximately 75-80 electric sites arranged in two loops: the Upper Loop overlooks the lake from higher ground, while the Lower Loop sits at lake level. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and 20/30-amp electric hookup on a gravel pad.

The recreation area spans 4,449 acres of forested hills, wetlands, and over 10 no-wake lakes and ponds connected by 14 miles of multiuse trails. Grousehaven Lake itself is paddle-only, making it ideal for kayaking and paddleboarding without motorized boat traffic. The campground's swim beach includes accessible beach mats to the water's edge and a beach wheelchair available for guests.

Beyond camping, the area offers a 3-D archery range open April through October, an observation tower, a swinging bridge across the Rifle River, and excellent fishing opportunities throughout the park's lakes and streams.

location.directions: From I-75, take exit 202 onto M-33 North. Continue approximately 15 miles to Rose City Road (F-28). Turn right (east) onto Rose City Road and continue about 5 miles to the park entrance at 2550 E. Rose City Road, Lupton, MI 48635.

links.title: Rifle River Recreation Area - Michigan Tourism

payload.name: Box Elder Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates April 24 through October 4. Reservations available through Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served. Bear country rules apply with mandatory food/trash storage. 7-day stay limit in effect.
payload.short_description: Forest Service campground near Mantua Reservoir with flush toilets, potable water, and shaded sites along Box Elder Creek, 5 miles from Brigham City, Utah.
payload.medium_description: Box Elder Campground sits in a wooded mountain valley near Mantua Reservoir in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The 29 single sites and 4 group sites are shaded by dense bottomland hardwoods, with Box Elder Creek flowing through. Flush toilets and potable water are provided. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served.
payload.long_description:
Box Elder Campground is located in a scenic mountain valley adjacent to the town of Mantua and about one mile from Mantua Reservoir. Managed by the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest with operations by Utah Recreation Company, the campground offers 29 single-family sites and 4 group sites. A dense forest of bottomland hardwoods provides full shade at most sites, and Box Elder Creek flows gently through the grounds.

Facilities include flush restrooms and potable water. Sites accommodate tents, RVs, and trailers up to 40 feet on gravel driveways with back-in access. The campground operates seasonally from late April through early October, with reservations through Recreation.gov. Some sites remain first-come, first-served.

Mantua Reservoir is just one mile away, offering fishing, boating, canoeing, and swimming. Horseback riding and hiking on local trails are also popular activities. The Bear River Migratory Bird Refuge, with nearly 80,000 acres of marsh and wetlands, is nearby and features a 12-mile auto tour route for wildlife viewing.

location.directions: From Highway 89/91, travel 4.5 miles east of Brigham City, Utah. Look for highway signing at the town of Mantua.

address.full: 237 S Willard Peak Rd, Mantua, UT 84324

payload.name: Clark Memorial Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-May through mid-fall. First-come, first-served with no reservations. No potable water available; bring your own supply.
payload.short_description: Free, first-come-first-served campground along the Thompson River in Lolo National Forest, offering fishing access and vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Clark Memorial Campground is a free, primitive campground situated in an open, sunny canyon bottom along the Thompson River. The site offers vault toilets and picnic tables, but campers must bring their own drinking water. Fishing opportunities are available in the Thompson River, and the campground is accessible via a 5-mile drive north of MT 200 on Thompson River Road.
payload.long_description:
Clark Memorial Campground is a free, primitive camping area located in the Plains/Thompson Falls area of Lolo National Forest in Sanders County, Montana. Situated at approximately 2,500 feet elevation in an open, sunny canyon bottom along the Thompson River, the campground provides a peaceful setting with a nearby forest and excellent fishing opportunities.

The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through mid-fall and is managed on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required or accepted. Facilities are basic: vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but there is no potable water on site, so campers must bring their own supply. Horse and pack animals are not permitted at this location.

Access is straightforward, located 5 miles north of Montana Highway 200 on Thompson River Road. The campground is free of charge, making it an attractive option for anglers and campers seeking a quiet riverside spot in western Montana.

location.directions: 5 miles north of MT 200 on the Thompson River Road.

payload.name: Lake Michigan At St. Ignace
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. Opens May 15, 2026 and operates through September 15 on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations required.
payload.short_description: Beachfront campground nestled between 20-30 foot sand dunes along Lake Michigan in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, offering excellent body-surfing waves and access to the North Country National Scenic Trail.
payload.medium_description: Lake Michigan Campground at St. Ignace sits between towering sand dunes and Lake Michigan's sandy beaches in Hiawatha National Forest. The 33 non-electric sites are steps away from excellent body-surfing waves and provide access to both the Sand Dunes Cross-Country Ski Trail and the North Country National Scenic Trail. Anglers often visit nearby Brevort Lake for walleye, pike, bass, perch, and crappie.
payload.long_description:
Lake Michigan Campground at St. Ignace offers a unique Upper Peninsula camping experience where 20-30 foot sand dunes separate you from miles of sandy Lake Michigan beaches. The commonly high winds create excellent body-surfing conditions, while the dunes provide a natural backdrop to the 33 campsites. Shorebirds like the Spotted Sandpiper are frequently spotted running along the beach throughout the day.

The campground provides access to the Sand Dunes Cross-Country Ski Trail and connects to the North Country National Scenic Trail, which winds through valleys, hilltops, prairies, and forests. While Lake Michigan offers fishing opportunities, nearby Brevort Lake (5 miles away) is the preferred spot for walleye, pike, bass, perch, and crappie. St. Ignace lies about 18 miles east along US-2.

All sites are standard non-electric with picnic tables and campfire rings with grills. Vault toilets and drinking water are available on-site. There is no dump station at this campground, but one is available at Brevort Lake Campground. Firewood from outside the local area is prohibited to prevent the spread of invasive species.

location.directions: From Mackinac Bridge, take US-2 approximately 18 miles west to the campground entrance. Address: W 3853 US-2, Moran, MI 49760.

payload.name: Willow Beach Rv Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Recent storm damage has affected the broader Willow Beach area; check current road conditions before traveling. Temple Bar Road has one lane open at mile marker 22. Fire restrictions are in effect prohibiting fires outside developed recreation sites. Harmful algae blooms have been spotted on Lake Mohave shorelines.
payload.short_description: Full-service RV park and tent campground on the Colorado River in Black Canyon, offering 28 hookup RV sites and 9 tent sites with scenic views, 30 minutes from Boulder City.
payload.medium_description: Willow Beach RV Park is a concessionaire-operated campground within Lake Mead National Recreation Area, situated along the Colorado River in Black Canyon. The facility offers 28 full-hookup RV sites with water, sewer, and electric connections, plus 9 tent camping sites. All sites include fire rings and picnic tables, with 24-hour access to showers and laundry facilities. An on-site store, grill, boat rentals, and fish cleaning station serve visitors.
payload.long_description:
Willow Beach RV Park occupies a prime location on the Colorado River below Hoover Dam, within Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The campground sits in Black Canyon, offering striking views of the river corridor and surrounding desert mountains. It serves as a popular launch point for kayaking, fishing, and motorized boating on Lake Mohave.

The facility features 28 full-service RV sites equipped with water, sewer, and 30/50-amp electric hookups. Each RV site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Nine tent camping sites accommodate up to 2 tents and 6 people per site, with fire rings, picnic tables, and access to potable water. All campers have 24-hour access to shower and laundry facilities.

On-site amenities include the Willow Beach Grill for dining with river views, a marina store selling snacks, drinks, and charcoal, and boat rentals including pontoons, kayaks, and canoes. A fish cleaning station serves anglers, and the adjacent U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Willow Beach Fish Hatchery offers tours. Boulder City is 30 minutes away and Las Vegas approximately 45 minutes.

location.directions: From Boulder City, take US-93 south toward Kingman. Turn right onto Willow Beach Road and follow it approximately 4 miles down into Black Canyon to the harbor and campground.

address.full: 25858 Willow Beach Rd, White Hills, AZ 86445

links.title: Willow Beach RV Park Official Website

alerts.title: Willow Beach Area Temporarily Closed from Storm Damage - Temple Bar Rd 1 lane open at mile marker 22
alerts.content: Saturday morning's storm caused flooding that damaged roads and made them impassable. Staff are fixing the roads and restoring access as quickly as possible. South Cove open. Pearce Ferry has reopened. Temple Bar Rd one lane now open.

alerts.title: Hemenway Harbor Boat Ramp Extension Starting June 2 - Reduced Launch Lane Capacity - Expect Delays
alerts.content: Boaters who want to launch at Hemenway Harbor this summer will experience delays at the ramp on busy days. The nearby PWC launch is open to boats during the project. Callville Bay, Echo Bay, Temple Bar, and South Cove launches are open on Lake Mead.

alerts.title: Government Wash closure to vehicle access and overnight camping
alerts.content: Government Wash Road and 8.0 Mile Road will be blocked, and motor vehicle access and overnight camping in the area will be prohibited. Hiking, biking, and shoreline access by boat for recreation within 100 feet of the shoreline will remain available.

alerts.title: Goldstrike Canyon, Arizona Hot Springs, White Rock Canyon, and Liberty Bell Arch Seasonal Closure
alerts.content: The annual seasonal trail closures are in effect due to hazardous heat. Temperatures can exceed 120 degrees in the canyons. Goldstrike and Arizona hot springs remain open but must be accessed by boat on Lake Mohave. These trails will reopen in early fall.

alerts.title: Fire Restrictions - HIGH FIRE DANGER
alerts.content: Currently prohibited: 1) fires/campfires outside of developed rec. site (e.g. campground) 2) Campfires in areas posted “no campfires” or near marinas and launch ramps 3) Smoking outside of an enclosed vehicle; discarding cigarettes outside of ashtray

alerts.title: Harmful Algae Blooms Spotted on the Shoreline of Lake Mohave
alerts.content: Avoid swimming where bright green algae is floating on the water. Keep pets away from the water. For more information and photos click the ‘more’ link.

payload.name: Andrew's Cove Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from March 15 through December 15. Reservation only via Recreation.gov; no first-come, first-served sites available. Potable water is not available due to well system decommissioning. Campers must bring their own drinking water.
payload.short_description: Quiet 10-site USFS campground along Andrews Creek, 15 minutes north of Helen, GA with hiking trail access to the Appalachian Trail.
payload.medium_description: Andrew's Cove Campground offers 10 peaceful campsites nestled along Andrews Creek in the Chattahoochee National Forest. The 1.9-mile Andrews Cove Trail begins at the campground and connects to the Appalachian Trail, while nearby streams provide fishing opportunities. Located just 15 minutes from the alpine village of Helen, Georgia, campers can enjoy mountain solitude with easy access to area attractions including Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, and the Raven Cliffs Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Andrew's Cove Campground is a small, forested retreat in the Chattahoochee National Forest offering 10 campsites along Andrews Creek. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. Site 9 is a double site accommodating up to 16 people and 4 vehicles, while standard sites allow 8 people and 2 vehicles maximum. A toilet facility is located adjacent to site 3.

The campground serves as a basecamp for hikers, with the 1.9-mile Andrews Cove Trail starting between sites 6 and 7. This moderately challenging trail follows a mountain stream and connects to the Appalachian Trail, making it ideal for day hikes or longer backpacking trips. Fishing is available in the creek with a valid Georgia license.

The alpine-themed town of Helen is approximately 6 miles south on Highway 75, offering restaurants, shopping, tubing, rafting, and zip-lining on the Chattahoochee River. Nearby attractions include Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, and three wilderness areas for those seeking additional solitude.

location.directions: From Helen, GA, drive north on Highway 75 for approximately 6 miles and turn right into the campground. From Hiawassee, drive south on Highway 75 for about 20 minutes; the entrance is a left turn on a sharp right curve. Physical address: 15000 Hwy 75 North, Helen, Georgia.

photos.name: Site #5 is the first site on the right when you go up the hill
Campsite 9 is a double site with two parking areas and double the tables, pads, and camping next to the creek together
Site #2 is a step down from the parking area to enjoy your visit
Welcome to Andrews Cove Recreation Area

payload.name: Pete Ott Camp
payload.status_description: This is a primitive dispersed camping area with no developed facilities. Access roads are typically snow-covered into late spring or early summer. The area is generally accessible July through September. Campers must be self-sufficient.
payload.short_description: Primitive backcountry camping area near Pete Ott Lake in the remote Clearwater County region of Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Pete Ott Camp is an undeveloped camping area in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of north-central Idaho. Located in the rugged backcountry near Pete Ott Lake and Pete Ott Creek, this primitive site offers dispersed camping opportunities for those seeking solitude in the Clearwater mountains.
payload.long_description:
Pete Ott Camp is situated in the backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. This primitive camping area lies in the remote mountain terrain near Pete Ott Lake, a small alpine lake accessible via the Flat Mountain Trail system. The area is characterized by dense forest cover and rugged ridgelines typical of the Clearwater region.

As a dispersed camping area rather than a developed campground, Pete Ott Camp has no established amenities such as toilets, potable water, or designated sites. Campers must be fully self-sufficient, bringing all water and supplies and packing out all trash. Access requires high-clearance vehicles due to rough forest roads, and the area is typically accessible from July through September depending on snow conditions.

The Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests allows dispersed camping throughout most of the forest with a 14-day stay limit. Campers should follow Leave No Trace principles and check current fire restrictions before visiting.

location.directions: From Orofino, Idaho, take Highway 12 to Greer, then Highway 11 to Pierce. Before entering Pierce, turn right onto Road 250 (French Mountain Road) and follow it to the Bungalow Ranger Station. Continue on Road 250 along the North Fork River, then turn onto Road 711 at Cold Springs Creek. Follow Road 711 to Road 5295, then switchback onto Road 5297, which leads to the Flat Mountain Trailhead.

payload.name: Punderson Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season. Water and sewer hookups are not available during winter months beginning October 31. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance via reserveohio.com.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground at Punderson State Park in northeastern Ohio featuring 190 campsites with options from primitive to full hookup, flush toilets, showers, and direct lake access for boating and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Punderson State Park Campground offers 190 sites across three designated camping areas in Geauga County's glacial lake region. Options range from 15 non-electric tent sites to 155 electric sites (20-amp) and 20 full-hookup sites with 30/50-amp electric, water, and sewer. Modern amenities include heated showerhouses, flush toilets, and a dump station. The camp office provides kayak and canoe rentals, with a launch nearby. The surrounding 996-acre park features Ohio's largest natural lake, swimming beach, fishing, an 18-hole golf course, and miles of hiking trails through mature beech-maple forest.
payload.long_description:
Located in Newbury Township about 45 minutes east of Cleveland, Punderson State Park Campground sits within one of Ohio's finest glacial lake landscapes. The 741-acre natural lake, the state's largest, anchors a park known for its dense beech-maple forests and year-round recreational opportunities.

The campground is divided into three areas with paved roads, offering 15 non-electric sites suited for tent campers, 155 electric sites with 20-amp service, and 20 full-service sites featuring 30/50-amp electric plus water and sewer hookups. Three group sites accommodate up to 25 people each. Every site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Centrally located showerhouses provide flush toilets and hot showers. A dump station serves RV campers, and the camp office loans games and rents kayaks and canoes.

Beyond camping, the park offers swimming at a sandy beach, fishing for bass, bluegill, and crappie, and an extensive trail network for hiking and mountain biking. The championship 18-hole golf course and historic Punderson Manor Lodge round out the amenities. Winter brings cross-country skiing and ice fishing when conditions permit.

location.directions: From I-271, take exit for US-322 East (Mayfield Road). Continue east on US-322 approximately 14 miles through Chardon. Turn left (north) onto State Route 87. The park entrance is about 1 mile ahead on the right at 11755 Kinsman Road.

payload.name: Williamson Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates from June through October. Campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River with 13 sites in a shaded pine and fir forest, adjacent to Eagle Cap Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Williamson Campground sits along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River in a shaded canyon of pine and fir trees. The campground offers 13 sites (8 tent/trailer, 5 tent-only) located below the campground road, with several sites directly adjacent to the river. Popular with summer and fall campers as a base for exploring the Lostine River Canyon and nearby Eagle Cap Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Williamson Campground is one of the larger developed campgrounds in the Lostine River Canyon, located within the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest. The campground is situated along the Wild and Scenic Lostine River under a canopy of pine and fir trees, providing welcome shade during summer months. With 13 total sites, including 8 that accommodate tents or trailers and 5 designated tent-only sites, the campground offers variety in camping experiences.

All sites are positioned below the campground road, and some of the most sought-after sites sit directly beside the river. Each campsite includes a picnic table, fire ring, and parking space. Vault toilets are available, but campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is provided on-site. The campground serves as an excellent basecamp for fishing the Lostine River and exploring the adjacent Eagle Cap Wilderness, which requires a free self-issued permit for entry.

The setting draws moderate use throughout the season, with riverside sites filling up quickly on weekends and holidays. Quiet hours are enforced from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.

location.directions: From Enterprise, Oregon travel west on Highway 82 for 10 miles to Lostine. In Lostine turn left at Lostine River Road and go 7 miles. The Lostine River Road turns into Forest Road 8210 at the Forest Boundary. Continue 4 miles on Forest Road 8210. Campground entrance is on the right side of the road.

payload.name: Sugarloaf Ridge Sp Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations via ReserveCalifornia from March 15 through October 31. First-come, first-served camping from November 1 through March 14. No current alerts or closures.
payload.short_description: Family campground in Sonoma County wine country with 47 sites around a meadow bordered by Sonoma Creek, offering flush toilets, hot showers, and 25 miles of hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Sugarloaf Ridge State Park Campground sits at 1,200 feet elevation in the Mayacamas Mountains, about an hour north of San Francisco. The 47 family campsites surround a large meadow bordered by year-round Sonoma Creek, with oak woodland and chaparral providing shade. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring with grill, and parking spur. The campground offers flush toilets, hot-water coin-operated showers, potable water, and trash service. No hookups or dump station.
payload.long_description:
Sugarloaf Ridge State Park Campground offers a quiet escape in the heart of Sonoma County wine country, located 7 miles east of Santa Rosa off Highway 12 at the end of Adobe Canyon Road. The campground sits at 1,200 feet elevation in the Mayacamas Mountains, with 47 family sites arranged around a scenic meadow bordered by year-round Sonoma Creek. Sites feature a parking spur, picnic table, and fire ring with grill, set among oak woodland and chaparral.

The park provides 25 miles of trails for hiking and horseback riding, including a self-guided nature trail along Sonoma Creek. The Robert Ferguson Observatory offers public viewing programs. Campground facilities include flush toilets, hot-water showers (coin-operated), potable drinking water, and trash collection. There are no hookups or dump station, but water spigots are available to fill RV tanks.

Three ADA-accessible campsites (#6, #7, #12) are available with accessible restrooms and showers. Dogs are permitted in the campground but prohibited on trails and backcountry areas; they must be leashed at all times and kept in a tent or vehicle at night. Maximum trailer length is 27 feet; maximum motorhome length is 30 feet.

location.directions: From Santa Rosa, take Highway 12 east toward Sonoma. Turn left onto Adobe Canyon Road in Kenwood and follow it to the park entrance at the end of the road.

payload.name: John Day River Basin Developed Campgrounds
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served only. Fire closure in effect May 13 through October 15, 2026. No campfires, propane campfires, charcoal grills, or wood pellet burning devices permitted. Liquid fuel metal cookstoves and shielded lanterns are allowed. No potable water available; campers must bring their own. Pack out all trash. No cell phone service at any campground.
payload.short_description: Four primitive BLM campgrounds along the John Day River in Central Oregon, offering first-come, first-served riverside camping near the Wild and Scenic River corridor.
payload.medium_description: The John Day River Basin Developed Campgrounds consist of four primitive BLM campgrounds in Central Oregon: Service Creek and Muleshoe along the main John Day River, and Lone Pine and Big Bend along the North Fork. All 21 sites are first-come, first-served with vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables, but no potable water or hookups. The campgrounds serve as popular staging areas for multi-day rafting trips on the Wild and Scenic John Day River.
payload.long_description:
The Bureau of Land Management's Central Oregon Field Office manages four separate fee campgrounds within the John Day River Basin: Service Creek (4 walk-in sites), Muleshoe (8 sites), Lone Pine (5 sites), and Big Bend (4 sites). Service Creek and Muleshoe are located near the town of Service Creek along State Route 207 and the main John Day River, while Lone Pine and Big Bend sit along the North Fork of the John Day River and State Route 402 between Kimberly and Monument.

At approximately 2,000 feet elevation, this high-desert landscape features sage, juniper, and occasional ponderosa pines, with dramatic canyon walls and exposed geological formations. The region is rural and quiet except during spring boating season and fall hunting. Weather is highly variable, especially in spring and fall, while mid-summer tends to be very hot. The river offers cooling relief in summer months. Dark night skies make for excellent stargazing.

The campgrounds are well-positioned for exploring the Journey Through Time Scenic Byway and visiting John Day Fossil Beds National Monument. Service Creek and Muleshoe serve as primary launch points for rafting the Wild and Scenic section of the John Day River. Year-round permits are required to boat between Service Creek and Tumwater Falls.

location.directions: Service Creek Campground: From Prineville, take US 26 east 46.5 miles to OR 207 N, turn left and drive 23.5 miles. Muleshoe Campground: Continue past Service Creek, turn right at stop sign onto OR 207 N, drive 1.9 miles. Lone Pine Campground: From Prineville, take US 26 east 77.7 miles, turn left onto OR-19 N for 18.4 miles, then right onto OR-402 E for 1.8 miles. Big Bend Campground: Same as Lone Pine but continue on OR-402 E for 3 miles total.
