payload.name: Cow Creek Campground And Picnic Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis, weather dependent. No fees. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 5 sites in Custer Gallatin National Forest, about 25 miles south of Ashland, Montana. First-come, first-served with accessible facilities.
payload.medium_description: Cow Creek Campground is a small, free primitive campground on the Ashland Ranger District of Custer Gallatin National Forest. The campground offers 5 campsites and 1 picnic area on a first-come, first-served basis with a 10-day stay limit. Facilities include accessible toilets and tables, but campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. Pond and lake fishing opportunities are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Cow Creek Campground and Picnic Area is a quiet, primitive campground tucked into the Ashland Ranger District of Custer Gallatin National Forest in southeastern Montana. With just 5 campsites and a single picnic area, it offers a secluded experience for campers seeking solitude in the Powder River country. The campground is free to use and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a maximum 10-day stay limit.

Facilities are basic but functional, with accessible toilets and picnic tables available. Campers should come prepared as there is no potable water on site and no trash pickup service. Firewood is also not provided. The area offers opportunities for picnicking and pond/lake fishing.

The campground is located approximately 25 miles south of Ashland, Montana, accessed via Otter Creek Road and Cow Creek Road. During summer weekends and holidays, the small campground can fill up quickly, so arriving in the early afternoon is recommended to secure a site.

location.directions: From Ashland, go 4 miles east on US 212. Turn right on Otter Creek Road (County Road 485) and travel 20 miles south. Turn right on Cow Creek Road (Forest Road 4095) and travel 5 miles to campground on left.

links.title: Cow Creek Campground And Picnic Area

payload.name: South Fork Campground
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to extensive flood and landslide damage from winter storms. The access road is impassable to vehicles. Road repairs were planned but no reopening date has been announced.
payload.short_description: A small, primitive campground in a remote foothills area along the South Fork of the Kaweah River in Sequoia National Park. Currently closed indefinitely due to flood and landslide damage.
payload.medium_description: South Fork Campground is a primitive, first-come first-served campground located at 3,600 feet elevation in the remote foothills of Sequoia National Park, along the South Fork of the Kaweah River. The campground provides vault toilets and bear-proof food storage lockers but has no potable water. Trailers and RVs are not permitted due to the rough dirt access road. The campground and access road sustained extensive damage from winter storm flooding and landslides and remain closed indefinitely.
payload.long_description:
South Fork Campground sits at 3,600 feet elevation in a remote, quiet section of Sequoia National Park's foothills, along the South Fork of the Kaweah River. This primitive campground offers a secluded experience away from the main park highways and popular giant sequoia groves. The area features hot, dry summers and cool, rainy winters with occasional snow.

The campground is tent-only with no hookups or dump stations. Each site includes a bear-proof food storage locker. Vault toilets are available year-round, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. When fire restrictions are not in effect, campfires are permitted in fire rings. Pets are allowed but must remain leashed at all times and are prohibited on trails.

The campground and its access road were heavily damaged by floods and landslides from winter storms. The dirt portion of South Fork Road is currently impassable to vehicles. A repair project was planned, but no reopening date has been confirmed.

location.directions: Take Highway 198 to the town of Three Rivers. Five miles before the main Sequoia park entrance, turn onto South Fork Road and travel east for 12.3 miles. The paved road ends shortly before the campground, with a rough dirt road continuing to the campsites and Ladybug Trailhead. Note: The dirt road is currently impassable due to storm damage.

address.full: 48997 S Fork Dr, Three Rivers, CA 93271

payload.name: Nichols Lake South Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season and reopens May 9, 2026. Operating season runs early May through mid-October. Some sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while others are first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on the south shore of 160-acre Nichols Lake in Manistee National Forest, offering 29 paved sites with swimming beach, accessible fishing pier, and North Country Trail access.
payload.medium_description: Nichols Lake South Campground sits on the southern shore of 160-acre Nichols Lake in Michigan's Huron-Manistee National Forests. The 29-site campground features paved spurs, flush toilets, showers, and potable water. A swimming beach with buoyed areas, accessible fishing pier, and paved boat launch provide direct lake access. The North Country National Scenic Trail passes through near the boat ramp.
payload.long_description:
Nichols Lake South Campground occupies a prime position on the southern shore of 160-acre Nichols Lake within the Huron-Manistee National Forests in Newaygo County, Michigan. The campground offers 29 family sites on paved spurs, each equipped with a fire pit and picnic table. Facilities include flush toilets, showers, and potable drinking water.

The lake itself provides excellent fishing opportunities for bass, bluegill, pumpkinseed, black crappie, and northern pike, accessible from shore, an accessible fishing pier, or by boat via the paved launch. A designated swimming beach with buoyed swim areas is available, though no lifeguards are on duty. Ice fishing draws visitors during winter months.

The North Country National Scenic Trail passes through the recreation area near the boat ramp, connecting hikers to one of America's premier long-distance trails. A day use area on the north side of the lake accommodates visitors not camping overnight. The nearest towns of Woodland, Bitely, and Brohman are approximately two miles south.

location.directions: From White Cloud, travel north on M-37 for 13 miles. Turn left and travel west on 11 Mile Road for 4.25 miles. The campground entrance is on the right. From Baldwin, take M-37 south for 13.5 miles to 11 Mile Road, turn right, and go west approximately 4.5 miles to the entrance.

payload.name: Paxson Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day. The campground is currently open and operating on a first-come, first-served basis. Opening and closing dates are weather-dependent and may vary year to year.
payload.short_description: Scenic BLM campground on Paxson Lake at MP 175 Richardson Highway, serving as the launch point for floating the Gulkana Wild and Scenic River. First-come, first-served sites with vault toilets and potable water.
payload.medium_description: Paxson Lake Campground is a 50-site BLM campground located at Mile 175 of the Richardson Highway on the shores of Paxson Lake. The campground features 40 drive-in sites and 10 walk-in tent sites, all available first-come, first-served. Amenities include vault toilets, potable water from hand pumps, fire rings, picnic tables, bear-proof food lockers, and a paved boat launch that serves as the put-in for the Gulkana Wild and Scenic River.
payload.long_description:
Paxson Lake Campground sits along the Richardson Highway at Mile 175, offering direct access to Paxson Lake in the heart of Alaska's Copper River region. The campground provides 50 sites split between two loops, including 10 walk-in tent sites and two ADA-accessible sites with raised tent pads. All sites include fire rings with grill attachments, picnic tables, and access to bear-proof food lockers.

The facility serves as the primary put-in for floating the main branch of the Gulkana Wild and Scenic River, featuring a large paved boat launch with parking for 70 vehicles including trailers. A boardwalk connects the first loop to the lakeshore and boat mooring area. Six double-vault toilets are distributed throughout the campground, three of which are universally accessible.

Potable water is available from hand pump wells. An RV dump station is on-site. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Activities include boating, fishing, canoeing, whitewater rafting, birding, and berry picking in the surrounding area.

location.directions: Located at Mile 175 of the Richardson Highway, approximately 10 miles south of the junction with the Denali Highway near the community of Paxson.

photos.name: Biker on Paxson Lake Entrance Rd

payload.name: Watchman Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All sites require reservations via Recreation.gov up to 6 months in advance for standard sites or 12 months for group sites. Check-in after 12:00 pm, check-out by 11:00 am. Quiet hours 10:00 pm to 8:00 am. Generators prohibited. Toxic cyanobacteria advisory in effect for the adjacent Virgin River.
payload.short_description: Year-round campground at Zion's south entrance near the visitor center, offering tent and RV sites with electric hookups, direct trail access, and shuttle service to Zion Canyon.
payload.medium_description: Watchman Campground sits at the base of the Watchman peak near Zion National Park's south entrance, a short walk from the visitor center and Springdale. The 184-site campground offers electric and non-electric options for tents and RVs up to 40 feet, plus group sites and walk-to tent sites with pergola shade. Three trails leave directly from camp: the Watchman Trail, Archeology Trail, and the paved Pa'rus Trail along the Virgin River.
payload.long_description:
Watchman Campground occupies the mouth of Zion Canyon beside the Virgin River, surrounded by red and orange sandstone cliffs that catch sunrise and sunset light. The campground's 184 sites span several loops: A and B loops provide 30-amp electric hookups suitable for RVs or tents; C and D loops are non-electric with a 19-foot vehicle limit; E-loop holds group tent sites for 7 to 40 people; and F-loop offers walk-to tent sites under pergola shade structures. All sites include a picnic table, fire ring, and parking.

The campground serves as a base for exploring Zion Canyon via the mandatory shuttle system, which stops at the nearby visitor center from approximately March through November. Hikers can walk directly to three trailheads: the moderate Watchman Trail ascending the peak behind camp, the short Archeology Trail, and the paved Pa'rus Trail, which is the only trail in the park allowing dogs and bicycles.

Facilities include flush toilets, potable water, a dump station, and trash collection. No showers or laundry exist on site, but both are available in Springdale. Generators are prohibited. Campers should be aware that April and May bring tent caterpillar infestations, and July and August see elevated ant activity following monsoons. Toxic cyanobacteria in the Virgin River means campers should not submerge their heads or drink river water.

location.directions: From the South Entrance of Zion National Park, take the first right after the entrance station toward the Visitor Center. After passing the Visitor Center, enter Watchman Campground and stop at the kiosk for site directions. From Interstate 15, take Exit 16 (from south) or Exit 27 (from north) to State Route 9 east through Springdale to the South Entrance.

payload.name: Hidden Valley Picnic
payload.status_description: The site opens May 22, 2026 for the season. Operates Memorial Day through September, weather dependent. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Gate code provided in confirmation email. High elevation site; contact Laramie Ranger District at +1 (307) 745-2300 for current fire or road closure information before arrival.
payload.short_description: Large group picnic site in Medicine Bow National Forest that accommodates overnight camping for up to 300 guests, with vault toilet, tables, grills, and fire rings at 8,600 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Hidden Valley Group Picnic Site is a spacious open area in the Pole Mountain region of Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, designed for large gatherings of up to 300 people. The site features a vault toilet, picnic tables, grills, and fire rings. It can be used for day-use events like reunions, weddings, and outdoor sporting activities, or as an overnight group campground. Located at 8,636 feet elevation east of Laramie, Wyoming.
payload.long_description:
Hidden Valley Group Picnic Site offers a large open space surrounded by scenic lodgepole pine and aspen forests in the Pole Mountain Area of Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest. The site accommodates groups of up to 300 people and 50 vehicles, making it well-suited for family reunions, weddings, youth group outings, and large outdoor sporting events like volleyball and kickball.

The facility provides basic amenities including one vault toilet, picnic tables, grills, and fire rings (USFS-approved metal rings only). Hand pump water may be available from May through September depending on weather and maintenance conditions, but campers should be prepared to bring their own water. There are no electric, water, or sewer hookups.

The site operates seasonally from Memorial Day through September, weather dependent. Check-in is after 2:00 p.m. and check-out is at 1:00 p.m. A gate code is provided in the reservation confirmation email and must be used for access. Maximum stay is 14 days. Due to the high elevation of 8,636 feet, visitors arriving from lower elevations should use caution and acclimate gradually.

location.directions: From Laramie, Wyoming, take I-80 east to exit 323 at Happy Jack Road. Turn left onto Happy Jack Road and follow it past the Summit Visitor Center. Take Forest Road 705 for about one mile southeast to the picnic area.

links.title: USFS Hidden Valley Group Picnic Site

payload.name: Big Arm Unit - Flathead Lake State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Water and showers are operational mid-May through mid-September. Bear-resistant food storage required; all food must be stored in closed, hard-sided containers or vehicles when not in immediate use.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Flathead Lake's Big Arm Bay with 41 sites, yurts, beach access, and stunning views of the Swan and Mission mountain ranges.
payload.medium_description: Big Arm Unit at Flathead Lake State Park offers 41 campsites nestled under mature ponderosa pine and juniper trees along the shoreline of Big Arm Bay. The park features a long pebble beach popular with swimmers and sunbathers, flush and vault toilets, seasonal showers, a boat launch, and serves as a jumping-off point for Wild Horse Island. Sites range from $4-$34 per night with yurt rentals also available.
payload.long_description:
Big Arm Unit is one of six units comprising Flathead Lake State Park, located on the western shore of Montana's largest natural freshwater lake. The campground sits along Big Arm Bay with many of its 41 sites positioned directly on the shoreline, offering views of the Swan and Mission mountain ranges. Mature stands of ponderosa pine and juniper provide shade and a classic Montana camping atmosphere.

The park's long pebble beach draws swimmers and sunbathers during summer months, while the boat launch makes Big Arm a popular departure point for visiting Wild Horse Island, a 2,163-acre island home to bighorn sheep, deer, and wild horses. Three yurts provide an alternative to tent or RV camping. Amenities include flush and vault toilets, a seasonal shower house, potable water, fire pits, bear-resistant food storage lockers, and firewood for sale.

The campground operates from April through October, with full water and shower services available mid-May through mid-September. One wheelchair-accessible site is available. The maximum RV/trailer length is 40 feet. Reservations can be made through Reserve America or by calling 1-855-922-6768.

location.directions: Located 15 miles north of Polson on U.S. Highway 93. Turn west onto Big Arm State Park Road.

links.title: Montana FWP Big Arm State Park

payload.name: Jumbo Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens around May 21, 2026, weather permitting. Operating season runs late spring to early fall. Mix of first-come-first-served and reservable sites via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: High-elevation campground at 9,800 feet nestled between Jumbo and Sunset Lakes on Colorado's Grand Mesa, offering electric hookups, lakeside views, and excellent fishing access.
payload.medium_description: Jumbo Campground sits at 9,800 feet on the northern slope of Grand Mesa, positioned between Jumbo and Sunset Lakes along the Grand Mesa National Scenic and Historic Byway. The 26-site campground features 21 electric hookup sites and 5 non-electric sites among mature spruce and aspen trees. Most sites offer lake views and easy walking access to the water. Vault toilets, potable water, and trash service are provided.
payload.long_description:
Jumbo Campground occupies a scenic location at 9,800 feet elevation on Colorado's Grand Mesa, tucked between Jumbo and Sunset Lakes in the Mesa Lakes area. The campground provides 26 sites spread through a forest of mature spruce and aspen trees, with 21 sites featuring electric hookups and 5 remaining primitive. The hilly terrain creates natural privacy between closely spaced sites, and most offer views of the surrounding lakes.

The Mesa Lakes area is home to over 300 lakes, making this an ideal base for fishing and paddling. Jumbo and Sunset Lakes allow non-motorized watercraft, and anglers target brown, brook, and rainbow trout. The West Bench Trail No. 501 provides hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding opportunities through the surrounding landscape.

The nearby Mesa Lakes Ranger Station, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1941, offers visitor information. Lodges in the area provide dining options. Mosquitoes are abundant throughout summer; bring repellent. The Grand Mesa Visitor Center at Island Lake features interpretive exhibits and a native wildflower garden with over 50 species.

location.directions: From Mesa, Colorado, travel south on State Route 65 for approximately 13 miles to the campground sign. Turn right into the campground.

photos.name: Grand Mesa Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forest
Grand Mesa Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forest

payload.name: Winstanley Island Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round for reservations via Recreation.gov. Peak season runs May 1 through September 30 at $75/night; non-peak season October 1 through April 30 at $65/night. Same-day reservations are permitted. Visitors must bring their own drinking water, firewood, sleeping bags, cooking gear, and garbage bags.
payload.short_description: Remote USFS rental cabin on Winstanley Island in Misty Fiords National Monument Wilderness, accessible only by float plane, boat, or kayak. Sleeps 6 with wood stove heat and outhouse.
payload.medium_description: Winstanley Island Cabin is a rustic 12x14 ft USFS rental cabin located 30 air miles east of Ketchikan on Shoalwater Pass within the Misty Fiords National Monument Wilderness. The primitive cabin sleeps up to 6 on bunk beds, with a wood stove for heat, cooking counter, and nearby outhouse. Accessible only by float plane, boat, or kayak; helicopter access is prohibited in this designated Wilderness area.
payload.long_description:
Winstanley Island Cabin offers a remote wilderness experience on the east side of Behm Canal between Rudyerd and Smeaton Bays within the Misty Fiords National Monument Wilderness. Built in 2010, this rustic 12x14 ft pan-abode style cabin accommodates up to 6 guests with 2 single bunks and 2 double bunks. Amenities include a wood stove with splitting maul, table with benches, cooking counter, food storage, and a nearby outhouse. A mooring buoy is provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

The surrounding area features rugged mountain peaks and spruce, hemlock, and cedar forest. Wildlife viewing opportunities abound, with mountain goats, bears, moose, and bald eagles in the area. The waters host Dall's porpoise, orcas, humpback whales, sea otters, and harbor seals. Saltwater fishing is possible near the cabin.

Numerous scenic attractions are accessible by boat or kayak, including Walker Cove, Chickamin River, Smeaton Bay, New Eddystone Rock, and the Behm Canal. Rudyerd Bay makes a good day trip for experienced sea kayakers. Several hiking trails to freshwater streams, lakes, and hunting areas are reachable by boat, including Winstanley Lake, Checats, Ella, Manzanita, and Nooya Lake trails.

location.directions: Located on saltwater approximately 30 air miles east of Ketchikan on the east side of Behm Canal between Rudyerd and Smeaton Bays. Accessible by float plane or boat only. A mooring buoy is provided. Refer to USGS map Ketchikan B-3 and consult local tide tables before departing. Helicopter access is prohibited in this designated Wilderness area.

payload.name: West Shore Unit - Flathead Lake State Park
payload.status_description: Open for camping through November 1, 2026. Potable water is available May through September only. Bear country protocols in effect requiring all food and attractants secured in bear-resistant containers day and night.
payload.short_description: Quiet lakeside camping on Flathead Lake's west shore, featuring 33 sites nestled in mature fir, pine, and larch forest with views of the Swan and Mission mountain ranges.
payload.medium_description: West Shore is the most secluded unit of Flathead Lake State Park, set on 129 forested acres of glacially carved dolomite outcrops. The campground offers 33 sites including tent-only and electric hookup options, a deep-water boat launch, and 2.5 miles of hiking trails. The mature conifer forest and rocky shoreline provide excellent swimming, fishing, and scenic views of the surrounding mountains.
payload.long_description:
West Shore Unit sits along the western edge of Flathead Lake, the largest natural freshwater lake west of the Mississippi. The 129-acre park features glacially carved dolomite rock formations rising from the lakeshore, creating natural overlooks with panoramic views of the Swan and Mission mountain ranges. A mature forest of fir, pine, and larch shelters the campground, making it the quietest of Flathead Lake's six units.

The campground has 33 sites spread across the forested terrain, including 7 tent-only sites and one ADA-accessible site. Many sites offer electric hookups at various amperages, and some include water and sewer connections. Bear-resistant storage lockers are provided at each site. The deep-water boat launch remains ice-free throughout winter, offering year-round access for watercraft. A concessionaire operates kayak, paddleboard, and pedal boat rentals from mid-June through Labor Day.

Hiking trails wind through 2.5 miles of the park, and the extensive rocky shoreline is ideal for swimming and picnicking. Potable water is available seasonally from May through September. The park operates with a camp host on-site during the camping season.

location.directions: Located 6 miles south of Lakeside on U.S. Highway 93 along the west shore of Flathead Lake. Address: 17768 MT Hwy 93, Lakeside, MT 59922.

payload.name: El Capitan Sb Hike/bike Campsite
payload.status_description: Currently closed due to the El Capitán State Beach Entrance Improvement Project. The previously anticipated March 2026 reopening has been delayed; no revised date has been announced. When operations resume, camping will initially operate first-come, first-served before reservations are reactivated.
payload.short_description: Primitive hike and bike campsite at El Capitán State Beach offering coastal bluff camping for non-motorized travelers along California's Gaviota Coast.
payload.medium_description: El Capitán State Beach Hike & Bike Campsite provides budget-friendly overnight camping for cyclists and hikers traveling without motor vehicles. The site features shared fire pits, picnic tables, food lockers, and a bike rack, with access to the park's restrooms and outdoor showers. Located on coastal bluffs overlooking the Pacific Ocean and Channel Islands.
payload.long_description:
El Capitán State Beach Hike & Bike Campsite serves non-motorized travelers exploring California's scenic Gaviota Coast. The primitive camping area offers shared amenities including fire pits, picnic tables, food storage lockers, and a bike rack. Campers have access to the park's flush restrooms and outdoor showers.

The campsite enforces a two-night consecutive stay limit and a maximum of five nights per calendar year. Check-in is at 2:00 PM with checkout at noon. Quiet hours run from 10 PM to 6 AM. Dogs are permitted on a 6-foot leash but cannot be left unattended and are prohibited on the beach.

The surrounding park features a bluff-top bike trail with ocean views, the 0.6-mile Nature Trail through riparian habitat, and access to 2,500 acres of backcountry via the Bill Wallace Trail. Beach wheelchairs are available at no charge.

location.directions: From Santa Barbara, take US-101 north approximately 17 miles to the El Capitán State Beach exit. Note: Vehicle access is currently closed due to construction; only pedestrian access is available.

address.full: 2 El Capitan Beach Rd, Goleta, CA 93117

links.title: El Capitán State Beach Main Page

payload.name: Lewis & Clark State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Reservations available May 16 through September 15 via washington.goingtocamp.com. First-come, first-served camping only May 1-15 and September 16-30. Campground closed October 1 through April 30. Fires currently allowed in all designated fire pits and grills.
payload.short_description: A 616-acre Washington State Park campground set in magnificent old-growth forest, offering primitive and standard campsites plus equestrian camping with 8 miles of multiuse trails.
payload.medium_description: Lewis and Clark State Park preserves one of the last remaining stands of old-growth forest in the Puget Sound lowlands. The campground offers primitive and standard sites nestled among towering Douglas fir, western red cedar, and big-leaf maple. Equestrian campers have access to 5 primitive horse sites and 8 miles of trails. The park also features group camping, reservable shelters, and the Lewis & Clark Lodge for larger gatherings.
payload.long_description:
Lewis and Clark State Park protects 616 acres of rare old-growth forest in Lewis County, Washington, offering campers a chance to experience towering Douglas fir, western red cedar, and grand fir trees that have stood for centuries. The campground provides primitive and standard sites with picnic tables and fire pits, along with modern restrooms and showers. Five primitive equestrian campsites are available first-come, first-served, with access to 8 miles of multiuse trails shared by hikers and horseback riders.

The park offers additional group facilities including a group camp accommodating up to 50 visitors with fresh water, stove, picnic tables, and vault toilets. The Lewis & Clark Lodge provides indoor group lodging with a full kitchen, 22 twin beds, and a wood stove. Two kitchen shelters are available for day-use gatherings. Beyond camping, visitors can explore hiking and biking trails winding through the ancient forest, use the horseshoe pits, or simply enjoy the cathedral-like atmosphere created by the massive old-growth trees.

location.directions: From I-5, take Exit 63 (Toledo/Jackson Highway). Head east on Jackson Highway (US-12) for approximately 3 miles. The park entrance is on the right at 4583 Jackson Highway, Winlock, WA 98596.

links.title: WA State Parks - Lewis and Clark

payload.name: Camp Ten Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season due to snow. High elevation typically limits access until June. Culvert repairs on FR 4220 began May 4, 2026. Fire recovery work continues in the area from the 2020 Lionshead Fire.
payload.short_description: Remote lakeside campground in the Olallie Lake Scenic Area offering non-motorized boating, fishing, and access to numerous trails including the Pacific Crest Trail.
payload.medium_description: Camp Ten is a primitive first-come, first-served campground on the shores of Olallie Lake at nearly 5,000 feet elevation in Mt. Hood National Forest. The remote location offers non-motorized boating, fishing, and access to trails throughout the Olallie Lake Scenic Area, including the Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail heading south into Mount Jefferson Wilderness. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own.
payload.long_description:
Camp Ten Campground sits on the south shore of Olallie Lake within the scenic Olallie Lake Scenic Area of Mt. Hood National Forest. At nearly 5,000 feet elevation, this remote campground provides a true backcountry camping experience with vault toilets but no potable water. The lake is perfect for non-motorized boating and fishing, with numerous trails winding through the lake-dotted landscape.

The Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail passes through the area, heading south into the Mount Jefferson Wilderness. Olallie Lake Trail #731 connects Camp Ten to Paul Dennis Campground on the north shore. The high elevation means the campground is typically only accessible from June through early fall, with snow limiting access earlier in the season.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Due to the narrow, winding access roads and remote location, vehicles are limited to 16 feet maximum length. Nearby Olallie Lake Resort provides limited supplies during the summer season.

location.directions: From Estacada, OR: Go 27 miles southeast on OR 224, 19 miles east on Forest Road 46, 8 miles southeast on FR 4690, and 6 miles south on FR 4220. Alternatively from Portland: Take Hwy 26 to Forest Road 42 (Timothy Lake/Skyline Rd turnoff), continue 18 miles on FR 42, then turn left onto FR 4220 and continue to Olallie Lake area.

payload.name: Beaver Creek Equestrian Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Reservations required through ReserveOhio.com. Peak season rates apply April 1 through October 31; off-season rates November 1 through March 31. Closed December 1 through March 31 for winter.
payload.short_description: Primitive equestrian camp with 59 sites offering horse tie-ups and fire rings, providing direct access to 23 miles of bridle trails through the Little Beaver Creek gorge in Ohio's Appalachian foothills.
payload.medium_description: Beaver Creek Equestrian Camp offers primitive camping for horse and rider on Sprucevale Road in Columbiana County, Ohio. The 59 sites include high lines for tying horses and fire rings with grills. Campers access 23 miles of bridle trails winding through 2,722 acres of forested wilderness along Little Beaver Creek, a state and national wild and scenic river. Vault latrines are provided but potable water is limited; campers should bring their own water supply.
payload.long_description:
Beaver Creek Equestrian Camp sits in the sandstone hills of Ohio's Appalachian foothills within Beaver Creek State Park. The primitive campground caters specifically to horseback riders, with 59 sites featuring high lines for securing horses and fire rings with grills for cooking. The camp provides direct access to 23 miles of bridle trails that wind through 2,722 acres of diverse terrain including forests, bottomlands, and ridges along the Little Beaver Creek gorge.

The trail system follows the Little Beaver Creek, designated both a state and national wild and scenic river. Riders encounter historic remnants of the Sandy and Beaver Canal, including lock structures and lock keepers' houses dating to the 1830s-1840s. Trail difficulty varies from gentle slopes with groomed surfaces to challenging terrain with steeper grades and water crossings.

Facilities are primitive in nature. Vault latrines and a shelter house serve the camp, but there are no showers, electric hookups, or RV water connections. Well water may be available on a limited basis to fill small containers up to 5 gallons, but campers should plan to bring their own potable water. The camp accommodates larger rigs with adequate space to park and turn around horse trailers.

location.directions: Located on Sprucevale Road in East Liverpool, Ohio. Address: 12816 Sprucevale Rd, East Liverpool, OH 43920. The camp is within Beaver Creek State Park in Columbiana County.

links.title: Beaver Creek State Park - Ohio DNR

payload.name: Ridge Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Sites 37-47 close November through March. Water and showers available April 1 through October 31. Reservations accepted April 1 through October 31 via Missouri State Parks (877-422-6766 or online). Walk-up registration available for unreserved sites. Camping limited to 15 days within any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Ridge Campground at Lake Wappapello State Park offers 55 campsites on a scenic ridge overlooking the lake, with electric hookups, modern restrooms, and access to swimming, fishing, and hiking in the Missouri Ozarks.
payload.medium_description: Ridge Campground sits atop a forested ridge overlooking Lake Wappapello in southeast Missouri's Ozark foothills. The campground provides 55 sites ranging from basic to 50-amp electric, with modern amenities including hot showers, flush toilets, laundry facilities, and a dump station. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Three ADA-accessible electric sites are available. The park offers swimming at a sandy beach, fishing for crappie and catfish, hiking trails, and boat access to the 8,400-acre reservoir.
payload.long_description:
Ridge Campground occupies a prominent ridge within Lake Wappapello State Park, offering campers elevated views of the 8,400-acre reservoir below. Located in Wayne County in Missouri's Ozark foothills, the campground provides 55 sites spread across two loops. Most sites feature electric hookups with both 30-amp and 50-amp service available, while a handful of basic sites accommodate tent campers preferring a more primitive experience. Water hydrants are distributed throughout the campground, and each site comes equipped with a picnic table and fire ring.

The campground's showerhouse provides hot showers, flush toilets, and laundry facilities, all available during the on-season from April 1 through October 31. A centrally located vault toilet in the second loop and a dump station round out the facilities. Three ADA-accessible electric sites (10, 11, and 29) feature extended-end tables, accessible water hydrants, and access to a fully accessible showerhouse with roll-in showers and front-transfer toilets.

Lake Wappapello offers excellent fishing for crappie, bluegill, bass, and catfish, plus a sandy swimming beach and boat ramp. The park includes hiking and mountain biking trails through oak-hickory forest. Four rustic camper cabins within the campground provide an alternative for those wanting a roof overhead. Reservations are available April through October via the Missouri State Parks reservation system, while walk-up registration handles unreserved sites.

location.directions: From Poplar Bluff, travel north on US Highway 67 approximately 20 miles. Turn right onto MO Highway 172 and continue approximately 6-9 miles to the park entrance. Highway 172 ends at the park.

payload.name: Barlow Crossing Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 22, 2026 and operates through September 7, 2026. First-come, first-served only; no reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Primitive first-come, first-served campground along Historic Barlow Road near Barlow Creek in Mount Hood National Forest, featuring vault toilets and no potable water at 3,100 ft elevation.
payload.medium_description: Barlow Crossing Campground sits along the Historic Barlow Road near Barlow Creek in the Mount Hood National Forest. This primitive, first-come, first-served campground offers a quiet forest setting at 3,100 feet elevation. Facilities include vault toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Sites cost $16 per night for single sites and $32 for double sites, with 50% discounts for Interagency Access or Senior Pass holders.
payload.long_description:
Barlow Crossing Campground offers a rustic camping experience along the Historic Barlow Road, the first road over the Cascade Range used by Oregon Trail pioneers. Located near Barlow Creek in the Mount Hood National Forest at 3,100 feet elevation, the campground provides a peaceful retreat in a forested setting.

This primitive campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Facilities are limited to vault toilets; there is no potable water available, so campers must bring an adequate supply. Access is via Forest Roads 43 and 3530.

The campground is managed by Alaska Recreational Management under a concessionaire agreement with the Forest Service. Single sites are $16 per night and double sites are $32 per night. Holders of the Interagency Access Pass or Senior Pass receive a 50% discount on camping fees. Payment is accepted in cash or check only.

location.directions: Access via Forest Roads 43 and 3530 from the Barlow Ranger District area.

payload.name: Malabar Farm State Park Day Use Area
payload.status_description: This is a day-use shelter house facility, not an overnight campground. The shelter is available for group reservations during park hours. For overnight camping, see the separate Malabar Farm Campground listing.
payload.short_description: Day-use shelter house at Malabar Farm State Park available for group gatherings and events, with restrooms and picnic facilities nearby.
payload.medium_description: The Malabar Farm Day Use Shelter House is a covered picnic pavilion available for group rentals at Malabar Farm State Park in Richland County, Ohio. This is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping. The shelter can accommodate groups for meetings, reunions, and gatherings during park hours.
payload.long_description:
The Malabar Farm State Park Day Use Area is a shelter house facility designed for group gatherings, not overnight camping. Located within the historic Malabar Farm State Park in Lucas, Ohio, the shelter house offers a covered pavilion for picnics, meetings, family reunions, and other group events.

This day-use facility requires advance reservations through ReserveOhio. Nearby amenities include restrooms and drinking water. The surrounding park offers 12 miles of hiking and equestrian trails, farm tours of the historic Louis Bromfield estate, fishing in farm ponds, and tours of the iconic 32-room Big House.

Note: For overnight camping at Malabar Farm State Park, visitors should look for the separate Malabar Farm Campground, which offers 15 primitive equestrian-friendly sites.

location.directions: Located at 4050 Bromfield Road, Lucas, OH 44843. The park is in Richland County near Mansfield and Ashland.

links.title: Malabar Farm State Park Official Site

payload.name: Station Creek Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Typically opens mid-May and closes September 15 annually. Reservations required through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Group campground in Snake River Canyon with two reservable sites accommodating up to 40 people each, offering vault toilets, drinking water, and access to world-class whitewater rafting.
payload.medium_description: Station Creek Group Campground is located along the Wild and Scenic Snake River in Bridger-Teton National Forest, 27 miles southwest of Jackson, Wyoming at 5,800 feet elevation. The campground offers two group sites nestled in a lodgepole pine forest, each equipped with picnic and serving tables, fire pits, grills, and food storage lockers. It serves as an excellent base camp for rafting and fly-fishing on the Snake River.
payload.long_description:
Station Creek Group Campground sits in Snake River Canyon within Bridger-Teton National Forest, about 27 miles southwest of Jackson, Wyoming. At 5,800 feet elevation, the campground is surrounded by lodgepole pines that provide partial shade throughout. The Wild and Scenic Snake River runs adjacent to the campground, accessible across the road and down an embankment.

The campground features two group sites, each accommodating up to 40 people (standard capacity 30). Sites include picnic and serving tables, large fire pits, grills, and bear-proof food storage lockers. Vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump are provided. Firewood is available for purchase on-site.

Fly-fishing for cutthroat, rainbow, and brown trout is popular on the Snake River, as is whitewater rafting and kayaking. A boat ramp is nearby. Grand Teton National Park lies approximately 40 miles north, while Jackson offers full services 27 miles away.

location.directions: From Jackson, travel south on US-189/89/26 for about 13 miles to Hoback Junction. At the roundabout, take the first exit onto US-26 East/US-89 South and continue along Snake River Canyon for 13 miles. Station Creek Group Campground is on the left, across the highway from the general Station Creek Campground.

payload.name: Adams Lake State Park Shelter
payload.status_description: The shelter is open and reservable. Reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance and must be booked at least 3 days before arrival. Book online at reserveohio.com or by calling 866-644-6727.
payload.short_description: A reservable picnic shelter house at Adams Lake State Park in Ohio, set beside a 47-acre lake offering fishing and paddling in the state's Bluegrass region.
payload.medium_description: Adams Lake State Park Shelter is a day-use picnic shelter located within the compact 95-acre Adams Lake State Park in Adams County, Ohio. The shelter sits near picnic areas and overlooks the 47-acre lake, which supports fishing for largemouth bass, bluegill, channel catfish, and carp. The park also features a paved walking path circling the lake and the adjacent Adams Lake Prairie State Nature Preserve, home to rare prairie remnants.
payload.long_description:
Adams Lake State Park Shelter is a reservable day-use picnic facility located approximately half a mile from the park entrance within Adams Lake State Park. The shelter is situated in one of Ohio's smaller state parks, which encompasses 49 acres of land surrounding a 47-acre lake in the state's Bluegrass region near the Ohio River.

The park offers a peaceful setting for fishing and paddling, with largemouth bass, bluegill, channel catfish, carp, and bullhead available in the lake. Only non-powered craft and electric motors are permitted, making it ideal for kayaks, canoes, and small boats. A paved blacktop path encircles the lake, providing easy walking access to views of the water, wildlife, and distinctive lily pads.

Adjacent to the park lies Adams Lake Prairie State Nature Preserve, one of the last remaining pockets of prairie habitat in Ohio. Visitors must stay on established trails due to the botanical sensitivity of the area. The preserve is home to rare plant species and Allegheny mound ants.

location.directions: Located 1 mile north of West Union on State Route 41. The shelter is approximately half a mile from the park entrance on the right side.

payload.name: Nevada Creek Cabin
payload.status_description: The cabin is currently closed for the season. The Nevada Creek Road is not plowed or maintained during winter months, and access can be difficult or impossible through early spring depending on snowpack. Reservations are made through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Historic one-room log cabin in the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest along Nevada Creek, offering access to the Continental Divide Trail and remote backcountry experience.
payload.medium_description: Nevada Creek Cabin is a rustic one-room log cabin at 5,400 ft elevation in a lodgepole pine forest along the upper reaches of Nevada Creek. The cabin features a wood stove, propane stove with lights, bunk bed and full bed, vault toilet, and hand pump well for potable water. Trails lead directly from the cabin to the Continental Divide, with excellent opportunities for hiking, horseback riding, fishing, hunting, and huckleberry picking in a protected roadless area.
payload.long_description:
This historic one-room log cabin sits on National Forest lands along the upper reaches of Nevada Creek, between Avon and Helmville, Montana. At 5,400 feet elevation in a thick lodgepole pine forest, the cabin provides access to a largely intact ecosystem in the northern Rocky Mountains. The entire surrounding area to the north, east, and south is protected as an Inventoried Roadless Area, offering excellent solitude and exploration opportunities.

The cabin sleeps 2-4 guests with one bunk bed and one full-size bed. Amenities include a wood stove for heat, propane stove and lights for cooking and illumination, and basic kitchen supplies including dishes, pots, pans, and utensils. A vault toilet is located nearby, and potable water is available from a hand pump well. Guests must bring their own bedding or sleeping bags, as only mattresses are provided.

Hikers and horse riders can connect to the Continental Divide Trail via Nevada Creek Trail #466, about 5 miles of gentle terrain from the cabin. Other nearby trails include the Prickly-Nevada Trail, Helmville-Gould Trail, and Washington Gulch. All trails in the area are non-motorized. Nevada Creek offers small pools for cooling off in summer, and the huckleberry picking can be excellent. Elk and deer are common, making this an ideal base for hunting trips.

location.directions: From Highway 141 between Avon and Helmville, turn east onto Nevada Creek Road (FR #296), which is well signed with Forest Access signs. Stay on FR #296 for approximately 7 miles, passing through private land for the first several miles. The cabin turnoff is marked with a large sign. Use the combination lock code provided with your reservation to unlock the gate and drive the final few hundred yards to the cabin. FR #296 is a dirt road with occasional washboards and potholes; high clearance vehicles are recommended but not required.

links.title: Helena-Lewis and Clark NF - Nevada Creek Cabin

photos.name: old cook stove next to back door
Counter tops, cabinets and a propane stove

payload.name: First Landing State Park Shelters And Yurts
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Yurts are available from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December. Weekend reservations require both Friday and Saturday nights; one-night stays are allowed Sunday through Thursday.
payload.short_description: Four yurts tucked in the dunes along the Chesapeake Bay at Virginia's most-visited state park, offering a unique blend of tent camping and cabin comfort without electricity or running water.
payload.medium_description: First Landing State Park features four yurts situated in the dunes overlooking the Chesapeake Bay. Each yurt includes a queen bed with a twin trundle, indoor seating, a large wooden deck with Adirondack chairs, two picnic tables, a pedestal grill, and a fire ring. Guests use the nearby campground bathhouse for showers and restrooms. Yurts have no electricity, plumbing, or climate control. Pets are not permitted except service animals.
payload.long_description:
First Landing State Park's yurts provide an excellent middle ground between tent camping and cabin lodging. The four yurts sit in the coastal dunes along the Chesapeake Bay, offering proximity to both beach access and the park's 19 miles of trails through cypress swamps and maritime forest. Each yurt sleeps three (queen bed plus twin trundle) with a maximum occupancy of four, and includes indoor furnishings like a sofa, chair, coffee table, and dining table for four.

Outdoor amenities include a spacious wooden deck with four Adirondack chairs, two picnic tables, a pedestal grill, and a fire ring with cooking grate. Guests should bring their own linens or sleeping bags, as well as lanterns or flashlights since the yurts have no electricity. The campground bathhouse with hot showers and flush toilets is a short walk away. Two vehicles are permitted per yurt; additional vehicles pay the daily parking fee.

The yurt season runs from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December. Weekend stays require booking both Friday and Saturday nights, while one-night stays are allowed Sunday through Thursday. Reservations are made through Reserve Virginia Parks (reservevaparks.com) or by calling 1-800-933-PARK.

location.directions: From I-64, take exit 282 onto US-13 North toward Northampton Boulevard. Continue to Shore Drive (US-60) and turn right. The park entrance is approximately 4.5 miles ahead on the right.

address.full: 2476 Tranquil Woods Trl, Virginia Beach, VA 23451

links.title: First Landing State Park Official Page
Virginia State Parks Cabin & Yurt Fees

payload.name: Wilson Island State Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through October 15. The campground operates from April 15 through October 15 annually. All 44 sites are 100% reservable through the Iowa State Parks reservation system. Seasonal hunting occurs throughout the recreation area.
payload.short_description: A secluded 544-acre campground along the Missouri River in western Iowa with 44 sites featuring electric hookups, modern restrooms, showers, and boat access.
payload.medium_description: Wilson Island State Recreation Area offers a quiet retreat among cottonwood stands along the Missouri River. The campground features 31 electric sites with 50-amp service and 10 non-electric sites, all accommodating RVs up to 70 feet. Modern amenities include flush toilets, showers, a dump station, and boat launch facilities. The park operates seasonally from mid-April through mid-October and requires advance reservations.
payload.long_description:
Wilson Island State Recreation Area spans 544 acres of cottonwood forest along the Missouri River in Pottawattamie County, providing one of western Iowa's most secluded camping experiences. The campground sits on what was historically an island in the river, now connected to the mainland, and offers easy access to fishing and boating on the Missouri.

The modern campground contains 44 sites total: 31 electric sites with 50-amp service, 10 non-electric sites, and 3 youth group areas. All sites are back-in configuration and can accommodate RVs up to 70 feet in length. Facilities include modern restrooms with flush toilets and showers, a dump station, water hydrants, playground, picnic shelters, and a boat launch ramp with dock.

The recreation area provides excellent fishing opportunities on the Missouri River (Iowa or Nebraska license required) and seasonal hunting. Hiking trails wind through the cottonwood stands, and the park's relatively remote location makes it ideal for those seeking a peaceful camping experience away from crowds.

location.directions: Located at 32801 Campground Lane, Missouri Valley, IA 51555. The park is situated along the Missouri River in western Iowa.

payload.name: Tie Hack
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically opens mid-May through mid-September, weather dependent. Most Bighorn National Forest campgrounds open by Memorial Day weekend. The campground is gated during seasonal closures.
payload.short_description: Forested campground near Tie Hack Reservoir in Bighorn National Forest, offering fishing, canoeing, and access to Cloud Peak Wilderness trails at 7,900 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Tie Hack Campground sits in a dense lodgepole pine forest near Tie Hack Reservoir, 15 miles west of Buffalo, Wyoming on the Cloud Peak Skyway. The reservoir supports rainbow, cutthroat, brown, and brook trout fishing with electric motors only. The Circle Park Trailhead, 3 miles away, provides access to alpine lakes and 12,000-foot peaks in the Cloud Peak Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Tie Hack Campground is located on the east side of the Cloud Peak Skyway in the Bighorn National Forest, near the shore of Tie Hack Reservoir at 7,900 feet elevation. The campground features 19 standard nonelectric sites nestled in a dense lodgepole pine forest with rock outcroppings. Each site includes a picnic table and campfire ring with grill. Accessible vault toilets and drinking water are available, along with trash collection.

Tie Hack Reservoir offers excellent fishing for rainbow, cutthroat, brown, and brook trout, with electric motors only permitted. A short trail connects the campground to the lake. The Circle Park Trailhead, located 3 miles from camp, accesses numerous alpine lakes and two 12,000-foot peaks within the Cloud Peak Wilderness. Scenic off-road driving, hiking, and mountain biking are available on nearby Elgin Park, Pole Creek, and Crazy Woman Canyon Roads.

South Fork Lodge is nearby, offering dining, lodging, guided horseback riding, a fishing pond, and a small store with fishing and camping supplies. The campground is managed by Rustic Freedom/Gallatin Canyon Campgrounds and reservations are available through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Buffalo, Wyoming, take US Highway 16 west for approximately 13 miles. Turn left onto Forest Road 21 (Tie Hack Reservoir Road) and continue 0.5 miles to the campground.

links.title: USFS Bighorn NF - Tie Hack Campground

payload.name: Sylvania Wilderness Backcountry Camping
payload.status_description: Open year-round. First-come, first-served camping through May 14. Reservations required May 15 through September 30 via Recreation.gov. During the reservation season, 37 sites are bookable up to 6 months in advance and 13 sites open 2 weeks in advance. A wilderness permit is required for all users during the reservation season.
payload.short_description: Primitive paddle-in and hike-in backcountry camping at 50 designated sites within 18,327 acres of old-growth forest and pristine lakes in Michigan's Upper Peninsula.
payload.medium_description: The Sylvania Wilderness offers 50 designated backcountry campsites scattered across pristine lakes and old-growth forest. All sites are accessible by canoe, kayak, or hiking trail. Each site includes a fire ring and wilderness latrine. Reservations are required May 15 through September 30 via Recreation.gov; the rest of the year is first-come, first-served. Motorized vehicles and bicycles are prohibited within the wilderness.
payload.long_description:
The Sylvania Wilderness encompasses 18,327 acres of primitive lands within the Ottawa National Forest, containing one of the largest remaining tracts of old-growth forest in the Midwest. The wilderness includes 34 named lakes, many featuring sandy beaches and surrounded by record-size red and white pines. The area provides habitat for bald eagles, loons, osprey, and rare orchids.

Camping is limited to 50 designated backcountry sites, each equipped with a metal fire ring and wilderness latrine. Sites are accessible only by paddle or on foot; no motorized or mechanized vehicles are permitted. A maximum of six people per campsite is strictly enforced. Potable water is available at the entrance station and boat landings.

Recreation opportunities include canoeing and kayaking on undeveloped lakes, hiking through ancient forest, and fishing under special regulations. Electric trolling motors up to 48 pounds thrust are allowed only on Crooked Lake. Visitors must pack out all trash, and no metal, glass, or foam containers are permitted within the wilderness.

location.directions: From Watersmeet, travel approximately 4 miles west on US-2 to County Road 535, then drive south on CR 535 approximately 4 miles to the Sylvania Recreation Area entrance station.

payload.name: Crooked River Group Camp Withlacoochee State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica. This site is restricted to organized youth groups only.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent-only group camp in Withlacoochee State Forest's Silver Lake Recreation Complex, designed exclusively for organized youth groups such as scouts and church groups.
payload.medium_description: Crooked River Group Camp is a single tent-only site within the Silver Lake Recreation Complex of Withlacoochee State Forest near Brooksville, Florida. Reserved exclusively for organized youth groups such as Boy Scouts, Girl Scouts, Cub Scouts, and church groups, the site accommodates up to 30 campers. Located on the shores of Silver Lake, part of the Withlacoochee River system, campers have access to fishing, canoeing, kayaking, hiking trails including the Withlacoochee State Trail, and a boat ramp.
payload.long_description:
Crooked River Group Camp sits within the Croom Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest, approximately 5 miles from I-75 near Brooksville in Hernando County. This single tent-only group site is part of the Silver Lake Recreation Complex and is reserved exclusively for organized youth groups including Boy Scouts, Girl Scouts, Cub Scouts, and church groups. The site accommodates up to 30 people and features a fire ring with grate and grill, picnic tables, and access to a bathhouse with restrooms.

The campground is positioned on the shore of Silver Lake, which connects to the Withlacoochee River system, offering excellent opportunities for canoeing, kayaking, and fishing. A boat ramp provides water access. Hiking and biking trails are nearby, including connections to the Withlacoochee State Trail. The natural vegetative screening between sites provides privacy in this classic Florida flatwoods setting.

This is a primitive camping experience with no electric, water, or sewer hookups available at the site. Campers should come prepared for tent camping conditions. Leashed pets are allowed with proof of rabies vaccination. Quiet hours are 10:00 PM to 8:00 AM, and fires are only permitted in designated fire rings.

location.directions: From I-75, take exit 301 toward Brooksville. The campground is located approximately 5 miles from the interstate at 15003 Broad Street, Brooksville, FL 34601. Follow signs to Silver Lake Recreation Complex within the Croom Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest.

payload.name: Eldridge Guard Station
payload.status_description: Open year-round and reservable via Recreation.gov. Summer vehicle access typically begins in May when snow melts; drive 6.5 miles on Taylor Fork Road/FSR 134 from Highway 191. Winter access requires a 2-mile ski, snowshoe, or snowmobile trek from Albino Lake Trailhead. Maximum 7-night stay per group.
payload.short_description: A primitive year-round log cabin rental in the Custer Gallatin National Forest offering access to hiking, biking, skiing, and snowmobiling trails between the Madison and Gallatin Mountain Ranges.
payload.medium_description: Eldridge Guard Station is a rustic, uninsulated log cabin at 7,030 feet elevation, situated at the edge of a meadow with Taylor Creek nearby. The cabin sleeps 6 with a maximum group size of 8 and features a wood stove for heat, propane stove and refrigerator for cooking, and a vault toilet. Guests must bring their own drinking water, bedding, and firewood from June through September.
payload.long_description:
Eldridge Guard Station is a primitive log structure nestled between the Madison and Gallatin Mountain Ranges in the Custer Gallatin National Forest. The cabin sits at the edge of a meadow at 7,030 feet elevation with Taylor Creek flowing nearby. This year-round rental offers access to extensive trail systems for hiking, mountain biking, and motorized vehicles under 50 inches in summer, with snowmobiling, cross-country skiing, and snowshoeing available in winter.

The cabin sleeps 6 with a maximum overnight group size of 8. Basic amenities include a wood stove for heating, propane gas stove and small refrigerator for cooking, two cots, two full-size futons with mattresses, a table and chairs, and minimal cookware. An outhouse is located behind the cabin. Note that this is an uninsulated, high-ceiling structure that can be very cold in winter even with the wood stove burning.

Guests must bring their own drinking water, flashlight, bedding, matches, toilet paper, trash bags, and dish soap. Firewood is provided from October 1 through May 31; guests must gather their own from June 1 through September 30. A corral is available for stock animals. The area is high-population grizzly bear habitat, so carry bear spray and store food securely from March through December.

location.directions: From West Yellowstone, Montana, proceed north on Highway 191 for approximately 33.5 miles. Turn left on Taylor Fork Road/Forest Service Road 134 and proceed for approximately 6.5 miles. The cabin will be on the left side of the road. Winter access requires parking at Albino Lake Trailhead (4 miles up FSR 134) and skiing, snowshoeing, or snowmobiling the remaining 2 miles to the cabin.

address.full: 4995 Taylor Fork Rd, Gallatin Gateway, MT 59730

payload.name: Beaver Creek Group Camp
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to extensive erosion. No reopening date has been announced.
payload.short_description: Group campground along the Stillaguamish River with views of Big Four Mountain, located on the Mountain Loop Scenic Byway in Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Beaver Creek Group Camp is a single-site group campground situated along the Stillaguamish River in Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. The fairly flat site is surrounded by old-growth cedar, fir, and hemlock forest and offers spectacular views of Big Four Mountain. Located about 13 miles east of the Verlot Public Service Center on the Mountain Loop Scenic Byway, the campground provides access to nearby trails including the Big Four Ice Caves Trail and Gold Basin Mill Pond interpretive trail.
payload.long_description:
Beaver Creek Group Camp is a popular group campground nestled along the Stillaguamish River in the Cascade region of Washington's Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. The site offers a spectacular view of Big Four Mountain and is surrounded by stands of old-growth forest featuring towering cedar, fir, and hemlock trees. The fairly flat terrain and proximity to bubbling Beaver Creek make it an ideal location for small group or family camping excursions.

Located about 13 miles east of the Verlot Public Service Center on the Mountain Loop Scenic Byway, the campground serves as a basecamp for hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing. Nearby attractions include the Big Four Ice Caves Trail, which ends with views of ice fields and the 6,153-foot north face of Big Four Mountain, and the Gold Basin Mill Pond interpretive trail featuring historic mill relics and a floating viewpoint. On clear days, the snow-capped summit of Mt. Baker is visible in the distance.

The diverse forest habitat supports a variety of wildlife including black bears, and the area sustains rarer species such as lynx, moose, and wolverine. Winter visitors can enjoy skiing and snowshoeing in the surrounding terrain.

location.directions: From Seattle, take I-5 north to exit 194 in Everett. Take Highway 2 north at Highway 204 toward Lake Stevens. Turn north on Highway 9, then east on Highway 92 to Granite Falls. Continue about 23 miles on the Mountain Loop Scenic Byway. From the Verlot Public Service Center, travel east on the Mountain Loop Scenic Byway for 13 miles. The campground is on the south side of the road near the river.

address.full: 52000 Blk Mountain Loop Hwy, Granite Falls, WA 98252

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Due to extensive erosion, Beaver Creek Group Campground will be closed to reservations indefinitely. **

payload.name: Aspenglen Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the winter season. Opens at 1 p.m. on Thursday, May 21, 2026 and closes at noon on Monday, September 28, 2026. All sites are reservation-only during summer season via Recreation.gov. 7-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Aspenglen Campground offers 52 forested campsites near Rocky Mountain National Park's Fall River Entrance, with flush toilets, potable water, and easy access to Trail Ridge Road.
payload.medium_description: Aspenglen Campground sits at approximately 8,200 feet elevation on the east side of Rocky Mountain National Park, near the Fall River Entrance. The campground features 52 sites nestled among Douglas fir, lodgepole pine, and ponderosa pine along the Fall River. Sites include drive-to family sites for tents and RVs up to 30 feet, plus several walk-to tent-only sites. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring with grate, and tent pad. Flush toilets and potable water are available during the summer season.
payload.long_description:
Aspenglen Campground occupies a scenic location on the east side of Rocky Mountain National Park, just 0.2 miles west of the Fall River Entrance Station. The campground sits at roughly 8,200 feet elevation in a pleasant mix of Douglas fir, lodgepole pine, ponderosa pine, and occasional Engelmann spruce, providing a balance of sun and shade. The rushing Fall River borders the campground, creating a peaceful backdrop.

The 52 campsites include standard nonelectric sites for both tents and RVs, as well as more secluded walk-to tent-only sites. Each site is equipped with a picnic table, fire ring with grate, and tent pad. Paved roads and parking spurs make for easy navigation. Flush toilets and drinking water are provided during the summer season. Food storage lockers are available throughout the campground due to active wildlife including bears, elk, deer, raccoons, and skunks.

The campground offers excellent access to Rocky Mountain National Park's attractions, including Trail Ridge Road and Old Fall River Road. The town of Estes Park is a short drive away, offering dining, shopping, and additional recreation. Generators are permitted only in Loop C between 7:30-10:00 a.m. and 4:00-8:30 p.m. There is no dump station at Aspenglen; RV sewage must be emptied at Moraine Park Campground.

location.directions: From Estes Park, drive west on US Highway 34. Enter Rocky Mountain National Park at the Fall River Entrance. The turn for Aspenglen Campground is approximately 0.2 miles past the entrance station on the left side of the road.

payload.name: Raleigh Ryan Ramp Picnic Shelter
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter only with no overnight camping. The facility is open year-round. Shelter reservations are available through Recreation.gov and are refundable up to seven days before the reservation date.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter on Aliceville Lake along the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway, featuring water, electricity, and picnic tables with a boat ramp for tournaments and group gatherings.
payload.medium_description: Raleigh Ryan Ramp Picnic Shelter is a day-use facility on Aliceville Lake along the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway. The shelter offers water, electricity, and picnic tables, and is located adjacent to a boat ramp, making it ideal for fishing tournaments and group events. The site provides views of the main waterway channel where barges and recreational boats pass by.
payload.long_description:
Raleigh Ryan Ramp Picnic Shelter is a day-use facility situated on Aliceville Lake along the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway near Pickensville, Alabama. The facility features one rentable shelter equipped with water, electricity, and picnic tables. A boat ramp is located on-site, making it a popular choice for fishing tournaments and boating events.

The shelter overlooks the main channel of the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway, offering views of passing barges, yachts, and recreational boats. The area is known for wildlife viewing, with fish jumping in the water and migratory birds overhead. This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping accommodations.

location.directions: Raleigh Ryan Ramp is located near Pickensville Campground on Aliceville Lake along the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway. From Pickensville, head west on Highway 86, then turn left onto Lock and Dam Road. Follow the signs to the Raleigh Ryan Ramp area.

photos.name: Raleigh Ryan Shelter has a wonderful view of the Tennessee Tombigbee Waterway where you can view barges and recreational boats.
Raleigh Ryan Shelter has a wonderful view of the Tennessee Tombigbee Waterway where you can view barges and recreational boats.

payload.name: Big Bar Camping Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations required. No fees. No potable water available; bring your own or filter from natural sources.
payload.short_description: A primitive dispersed camping area along the Snake River in Hells Canyon, offering riverside camping with vault toilet access and proximity to Allison Creek Trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Big Bar Camping Area is a large dispersed camping site situated along the Snake River in Hells Canyon within Payette National Forest. The area accommodates both tent campers and RVs but has minimal infrastructure. A single vault toilet and informational sign mark the entrance. No potable water is available; campers must filter or treat water from nearby sources. Allison Creek Trailhead (#514) is located directly across Hells Canyon Road.
payload.long_description:
Big Bar Camping Area offers primitive dispersed camping along the scenic Snake River in Hells Canyon, one of the deepest river gorges in North America. Located within Payette National Forest in Adams County, Idaho, this camping area provides a rugged, undeveloped experience for self-sufficient campers seeking solitude and river access.

The area has no formal camping units or designated parking spots. Both tent campers and RVs can find space, though the lack of developed sites means campers choose their own spots. The only amenities are a single vault toilet (outhouse) and an informational sign at the pull-in area. No potable water is provided; campers must bring their own supply or treat water from nearby sources.

Recreation opportunities include day hiking, scenery viewing, and motorized boating on the Snake River. Allison Creek Trailhead, providing access to Allison Creek Trail #514, is located directly across Hells Canyon Road from the camping area.

location.directions: From Cambridge, take Highway 71 approximately 26 miles to the Snake River. Continue on Highway 71 another 30 miles to the entrance of the camping area.

payload.name: Fort Clinch State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park gates open 8 a.m. to sunset daily. Primitive group camping is currently unavailable. Construction of a new dump station at the River campground may cause intermittent noise.
payload.short_description: Oceanfront and riverfront camping at a historic Civil War fort on Amelia Island, with 69 sites across two scenic campgrounds offering full hookups and beach access.
payload.medium_description: Fort Clinch State Park offers 69 campsites divided between two distinct campgrounds on Amelia Island. The Amelia River Campground features 42 shaded sites under Spanish moss-draped oaks with river views, while the Atlantic Beach Campground provides 21 RV and 6 tent-only sites steps from the ocean amid white sand dunes. Both campgrounds include full hookups, heated bathrooms with showers, dump stations, and laundry facilities.
payload.long_description:
Fort Clinch State Park Campground sits at the northeastern tip of Amelia Island, combining coastal camping with access to one of the best-preserved 19th-century forts in the country. The park's two campgrounds offer distinctly different experiences: the Amelia River Campground on the north end provides 42 sites shaded by ancient live oaks draped in Spanish moss, with views of the St. Marys River and Cumberland Island beyond. The Atlantic Beach Campground places 27 sites among snow-white dunes just steps from the Atlantic Ocean.

Every site includes a fire ring, picnic table, and access to potable water within 100 feet. Electric hookups (30 and 50 amp), water, and sewer connections are available for RV sites. Both campgrounds feature modern heated bathrooms with hot showers, dump stations, and laundry machines. The Amelia River restroom building is air-conditioned during warmer months. Several ADA-accessible sites are available in each campground.

Beyond the campground, the park offers 6 miles of trails through maritime hammock and coastal scrub, miles of undeveloped beach, excellent fishing from the jetties, and daily programs at the historic fort where costumed interpreters recreate garrison life.

location.directions: From I-95, take exit 373 and head east on A1A toward Amelia Island. Continue approximately 15 miles through Fernandina Beach. The park entrance is at 2601 Atlantic Ave., Fernandina Beach, FL 32034, at the north end of Amelia Island.

payload.name: Back Country Camping - Pope Bay
payload.status_description: Open for first-come, first-served permits at the Maryland Ranger Station. No advance reservations. Closed during firearm hunting seasons (dates typically in October through early January). No potable water; campers must pack in water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Remote bayside backcountry campsite at Assateague Island National Seashore, accessible by hiking or paddling, with a fire ring, picnic table, and chemical toilet for up to 25 people.
payload.medium_description: Pope Bay is a primitive backcountry campsite on the bay side of Assateague Island National Seashore in Maryland. The forested site accommodates up to 25 people and features a fire ring, picnic table, and chemical toilet. Permits are issued first-come, first-served only at the Maryland Ranger Station; no advance reservations are accepted. All campers must hike or paddle in, as motorized transport of campers or equipment is prohibited.
payload.long_description:
Pope Bay offers a secluded backcountry camping experience on the bayside of Assateague Island National Seashore. Located in a forested area with limited shade, this primitive site is reached by hiking or paddling and provides a fire ring, picnic table, and chemical toilet. The site can accommodate groups of up to 25 people.

Permits cost $10 per person for ages 16 and older, plus the standard $25 vehicle entrance fee. Permits must be obtained in person at the Maryland District Ranger Station on a first-come, first-served basis; no advance reservations are accepted. All members of your party must be present before the permit will be issued. Campers must depart at least 4 hours before sunset.

Pets are prohibited at all backcountry sites. Glass bottles are not allowed, and all trash must be packed out. Fires are permitted only in the designated fire ring, using dead and down wood collected on site or firewood purchased locally (no out-of-state firewood). The site closes during firearm hunting seasons, typically in October, November, December, and January.

location.directions: Obtain your permit at the Maryland District Ranger Station at 6633 Bayberry Drive, Berlin, MD 21811. GPS systems may provide inaccurate directions; follow official NPS signage. Access to the campsite is by hiking or paddling only.
