payload.name: Fremont Bay Group Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. The group shelter requires advance reservation.
payload.short_description: A small group camping area on the west side of Boysen Reservoir with lake access, part of Loop 1 which includes several camping areas with limited facilities and a boat ramp.
payload.medium_description: Fremont Bay Group Camp is part of Loop 1 on the west side of Boysen Reservoir, a collection of small camping areas including South Muddy, Fremont Bay, Libby Point, and Sandy Hills Loop. The area features close lake access, a reservable group shelter, some picnic shelters, a few shade trees, a sandy beach, and a boat launching area. The campground is located within the Wind River Indian Reservation in scenic central Wyoming.
payload.long_description:
Fremont Bay Group Camp is located within Loop 1 on the western shore of Boysen Reservoir at Boysen State Park. This loop encompasses several small camping areas including South Muddy, Fremont Bay, Libby Point, and Sandy Hills Loop, offering approximately 20 campsites total with limited but functional facilities. The area provides direct access to the reservoir's western shoreline, making it ideal for groups interested in water-based recreation.

The campground features a reservable group shelter suitable for gatherings, along with picnic shelters scattered throughout the area. While shade trees are limited, the site offers a sandy beach and boat launching area for easy water access. The setting is characteristic of the high desert landscape of central Wyoming, positioned at the southern end of the Owl Creek Mountains and the beginning of the Wind River Canyon.

Boysen State Park surrounds the 19,560-acre Boysen Reservoir, created by a dam completed in 1951. The park is situated on the edge of the Wind River Indian Reservation, offering 76 miles of shoreline and diverse recreational opportunities. The Wind River, which flows north through the area, provides a unique geographical feature in this scenic and geologically interesting region of Wyoming.

location.directions: Fremont Bay Campground is located within Boysen State Park, approximately 12 miles northwest of Shoshoni, Wyoming, off US Highway 20. Follow the park signs to reach the campground.

address.full: 386 W Shoreline Loop 1st Dr, Shoshoni, WY 82649

payload.name: Holliday Lake State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: These are day-use picnic shelters only, not overnight camping facilities. Available for rental from 8 a.m. to dusk. Reserve by calling 800-933-7275; when not reserved, available first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelters at Holliday Lake State Park in Virginia's Appomattox-Buckingham State Forest, available for group gatherings with tables, grills, and nearby restrooms.
payload.medium_description: Holliday Lake State Park offers two day-use picnic shelters available for rent. Shelter 1 is a historic log structure near the lakeshore accommodating 25 people. Shelter 2 is ADA-accessible with a wooden ramp and accommodates 36 people, located across from the swimming beach. Both feature picnic tables, large pedestal grills, electrical outlets, and access to nearby restrooms. Shelters are available from 8 a.m. to dusk and can be reserved by calling the Virginia State Parks Customer Service Center.
payload.long_description:
Holliday Lake State Park features two day-use picnic shelters ideal for family reunions, group outings, and special events. These are not overnight camping facilities but rather covered picnic areas available for rental from 8 a.m. to dusk.

Shelter 1 is a historic log structure situated adjacent to the lake's edge near the restroom, accommodating up to 25 people. Shelter 2 is positioned across from the swimming beach and can accommodate 36 people. Shelter 2 is fully ADA-accessible with a wooden ramp and accessible picnic table.

Both shelters include large pedestal grills, picnic tables, and electrical outlets. Restrooms are located nearby. Reservations are made through the Virginia State Parks Customer Service Center at 800-933-7275. When not reserved, shelters are available to park guests on a first-come, first-served basis. Parking fees are not included in shelter rentals.

location.directions: Access via State Route 24 between Appomattox and U.S. 60 and from Routes 626, 640 and 692. The park is approximately 12 miles from Appomattox Court House National Historical Park. Park address is 2759 State Park Road, Appomattox, VA 24522. Visitors driving west via Routes 60 and 636 may want to avoid Routes 614 and 640, which have gravel, and proceed west to Route 24.

payload.name: Dixie Meadow Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with no fee. Access may be limited due to snow during winter months. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water supply and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed campsite at 5,500 feet elevation in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests with a vault toilet and pack-out trash policy.
payload.medium_description: Dixie Meadow Campground is a free dispersed camping area located in the Highway 14 Corridor of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests near Elk City, Idaho. The site sits at 5,500 feet elevation and offers a vault toilet but no potable water or trash services. Campers must pack out all garbage.
payload.long_description:
Dixie Meadow Campground is a primitive dispersed camping area situated at 5,500 feet elevation in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of central Idaho. Located approximately 5 miles past the town of Dixie along Red River-Dixie Road #222, this free campsite provides a basic vault toilet as its only developed amenity.

The campground operates on a pack-it-in, pack-it-out basis with no garbage services or potable water available. Campers should come fully prepared with their own water supply and plan to haul out all trash. The site is open year-round, though access can be limited or impossible during winter months due to snow accumulation on the forest roads.

location.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south on Red River-Dixie Road #222 and continue past the Red River Ranger Station (now closed) and past Dixie Town approximately 5 miles.

payload.name: Steel Creek Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens late May through early September. Reservations available via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Large group campground in Caribou-Targhee National Forest accommodating up to 200 people, set among willow and pine trees along Steel Creek with mountain views.
payload.medium_description: Steel Creek Group Campground offers a single large group site capable of hosting up to 200 people in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. The campground sits at 6,675 feet elevation among willow and pine trees adjacent to Steel Creek, providing picturesque mountain views and access to hiking, fishing, mountain biking, and ATV riding.
payload.long_description:
Steel Creek Group Campground is located 35 miles northeast of Dubois, Idaho, in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest's Dubois Ranger District. The campground features one large accessible group site nestled among willow and pine trees along a small stream, offering picturesque views of the surrounding mountains.

The site accommodates up to 200 people with tiered pricing based on group size. Amenities include vault toilets, potable drinking water from faucets, picnic and serving tables, a grill, and a campfire circle. A common parking area sits adjacent to the dining space. Bear-resistant garbage containers and food lockers are provided for proper food storage.

Popular activities in the area include hiking, fishing, mountain biking, and ATV riding, though no OHVs are allowed beyond the parking area and pack or saddle stock are prohibited in the campground. The access road is gravel. Basic services including phone, gas, and groceries are available in Dubois, Idaho.

location.directions: From Dubois, Idaho: Travel north on I-15 to the Stoddard Creek Exit (Exit 184). Go east on West Camas-Miners Creek Road (FR 006) for approximately 14 miles to Steel Creek Road (FR 478), turn right and continue 0.75 miles to the campground entrance.

payload.name: Finger Lakes Trail Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Shelter use limited to two consecutive nights. Camping prohibited in pastures May 15 through October 31. No potable water; pack in all drinking water.
payload.short_description: Primitive Adirondack-style lean-to shelter on the Finger Lakes Trail in New York's only National Forest, available first-come, first-served with no fees.
payload.medium_description: The Finger Lakes Trail Shelter is a three-sided Adirondack-style lean-to located along the Finger Lakes Trail (part of the North Country Trail) in Finger Lakes National Forest. This hike-in shelter offers primitive backcountry camping on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees. There is no potable water; campers must bring their own. A composting toilet is available nearby.
payload.long_description:
The Finger Lakes Trail Shelter is a rustic three-sided Adirondack-style lean-to situated along the Finger Lakes Trail, which is also part of the North Country National Scenic Trail. Located in Finger Lakes National Forest between Cayuga and Seneca Lakes in the Southern Tier of New York, this is a true backcountry camping experience in New York's only National Forest.

The shelter is accessible only by foot and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservation system or fees. Campers should be prepared for primitive conditions: there is no potable water available, so all drinking water must be packed in. A composting toilet serves the area. As this is shared backcountry infrastructure, you may need to share the shelter with other hikers.

Use of the shelter is limited to two consecutive nights. General Finger Lakes National Forest rules apply: camping is prohibited in pastures from May 15 through October 31, and dispersed camping elsewhere must be at least 50 feet from trails, roads, and water sources. Maximum stay in the forest is 14 days within any 30-day period.

location.directions: The Finger Lakes Trail Shelter is located directly along the Finger Lakes Trail, near Burdett in the Finger Lakes region of New York. Access the shelter by hiking along the FLT main trail or via nearby trailheads at major road crossings such as NY-14 or NY-414 near Watkins Glen State Park. Look for trail signage pointing towards the lean-to, which is a typical Adirondack-style structure situated for backpackers and through-hikers.

payload.name: Cold Spring
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates from late May through October 1, weather dependent. Currently closed due to seasonal conditions. No potable water is available. Camping within Taylor Canyon is restricted to developed campgrounds only per forest order GMUG-2022-09.
payload.short_description: Rustic 6-site first-come, first-served campground in Taylor Canyon along the Taylor River, offering gold-medal fishing access near the Fossil Ridge Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Cold Spring Campground is a small, rustic first-come, first-served campground located in Taylor Canyon along the Taylor River in Gunnison National Forest. The 6-site campground provides access to gold-medal fishing in the Taylor River and sits at the northern boundary of the Fossil Ridge Wilderness. The landscape features aspen and spruce trees with light usage levels.
payload.long_description:
Cold Spring Campground is a primitive, first-come, first-served campground situated in Taylor Canyon along the Taylor River within the Grand Mesa, Uncompahgre and Gunnison National Forests. With only 6 campsites, this rustic destination offers a quiet camping experience surrounded by aspen and spruce forests.

The campground provides excellent access to gold-medal fishing in the Taylor River, which also supports rafting and kayaking. Located at the northern boundary of the Fossil Ridge Wilderness, the area offers opportunities for hiking, backpacking, and horseback riding in pristine natural settings. Campers should note that no potable water is available on site.

Camping in Taylor Canyon is restricted to developed Forest Service campgrounds only. Open fires are prohibited within 100 feet of the Taylor River per forest order GMUG-2022-09, which remains in effect through May 31, 2027. OHV use is not authorized within the campground.

location.directions: From Gunnison, travel northeast on County Road 724 (Taylor River Road) for 15 miles.

payload.name: Richloam Tract Primitive Camp Zone North
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No potable water or restrooms in the camping zone. Campers must be self-sufficient and prepared for a four-mile hike to reach camp.
payload.short_description: Remote primitive hike-in camping zone within Withlacoochee State Forest's Richloam Tract, offering backcountry solitude approximately four miles from the trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Richloam Tract Primitive Camp Zone North is a designated backcountry camping area within Withlacoochee State Forest, located about 20 miles east of Brooksville. This hike-in only zone sits approximately four miles from the Richloam Fire Tower trailhead parking area. The zone is marked by yellow tree bands and offers a true primitive experience with no developed amenities, though some scattered areas may have fire rings or picnic tables.
payload.long_description:
Richloam Tract Primitive Camp Zone North offers backcountry camping in the heart of Withlacoochee State Forest, one of Florida's largest state forests spanning over 160,000 acres across five counties. The North zone is one of three primitive camping zones in the Richloam Tract, each delineated by yellow-colored bands on trees. Reaching camp requires a four-mile hike from the trailhead parking area at the Richloam Fire Tower.

This is true primitive camping with no developed facilities in the camping zone itself. There are no restrooms and no potable water at camp; the nearest water source is back at the Richloam Fire Tower. Some scattered locations within the zone may have fire rings, picnic tables, or grills, but these are not guaranteed at every spot. Campers should be fully self-sufficient and prepared for backcountry conditions.

The surrounding Richloam Wildlife Management Area offers excellent opportunities for hiking, bird watching, wildlife viewing, stargazing, and nature photography. Before your trip, contact WSF Dispatch at 352-797-4100 to check for scheduled prescribed burns. During hunting season, wearing bright-colored clothing is strongly recommended.

location.directions: From Interstate 75, take Exit 301 and turn right (south) onto Clay Sink Road. Continue to the trailhead parking area at the Richloam Fire Tower. The camping zone is approximately four miles from the parking area via hiking trails.

payload.name: Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge Cabins
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations via Recreation.gov at $45 per night. Blue Fox Bay Cabin is undergoing renovations through summer 2026; the ramp to/from the cabin will be under construction during this time. Accessible by floatplane only; Blue Fox Bay, Uganik Island, and Viekoda Bay are also boat-accessible.
payload.short_description: Remote public use cabins in Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge, accessible only by floatplane or boat. Ten rustic cabins with heating stoves and pit toilets scattered across Alaska's Kodiak Archipelago.
payload.medium_description: Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge maintains 10 rustic public use cabins spread across 1.9 million acres of wilderness on the Kodiak Archipelago, 252 miles southwest of Anchorage. Each cabin sleeps 4-8 people and includes bunk beds without mattresses, an oil or wood heating stove, table and chairs, exterior storage cache for supplies or game meat, and a pit toilet. No roads or trails exist in the refuge; all cabins require floatplane access, though Blue Fox Bay, Uganik Island, and Viekoda Bay cabins are also reachable by boat.
payload.long_description:
Kodiak National Wildlife Refuge Cabins offer a rare opportunity to stay within one of Alaska's most iconic wilderness areas, home to approximately 3,000 Kodiak brown bears and over 400 breeding pairs of bald eagles. The refuge covers 1.9 million acres on Kodiak, Uganik, Ban, and Afognak Islands, encompassing diverse habitats from misty fiords and glacial valleys to tundra, alpine meadows, and Sitka spruce forests. Popular activities include wildlife viewing, fishing for all five species of Pacific salmon on world-class rivers like Uganik, Karluk, and Ayakulik, and hunting elk, Sitka black-tailed deer, mountain goats, and brown bears.

All 10 cabins are primitive and require complete self-sufficiency. Each has bunk beds without mattresses, a Nordic-brand heating stove burning kerosene, #1 heating oil, or automotive diesel, a table with chairs, and an exterior cache for supplies or game storage. Pit toilets are provided. Visitors must bring all fuel for heaters, cooking equipment, lighting, food, water, and toiletries. There is no electricity, running water, or trash service. All garbage, unused food, and fuel cans must be packed out.

The refuge has a maritime climate with cool, wet, and windy conditions prevailing year-round. Hypothermia is possible in any season without proper waterproof gear, and weather delays for floatplane travel are common. Refuge staff cannot arrange transportation but can provide a list of permitted charter operators.

location.directions: No roads or maintained trails exist in the refuge. All cabins are accessible by floatplane. Blue Fox Bay, Uganik Island, and Viekoda Bay cabins are also accessible by boat. Refuge staff cannot arrange transportation but can provide a list of charter operators permitted to transport visitors into the refuge.

photos.name: View of Red peak over trees from boardwalk of Blue Fox Bay public use cabin

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Update: Blue Fox Bay Cabin is undergoing renovations for the remainder of 2025 through summer 2026. During this time, the ramp to/from the cabin will be under construction.

payload.name: Thompsons Lake Campground At Thacher State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Loop A operates May 1 through October 11. Loop B operates May 22 through September 6. Reservations available up to 9 months in advance via ReserveAmerica. Swimming availability depends on lifeguard coverage and water quality conditions.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground with 140 sites on Thompson's Lake in the Helderberg Mountains, featuring a sandy beach, boat rentals, and access to over 25 miles of trails at Thacher State Park.
payload.medium_description: Thompson's Lake Campground offers 140 wooded sites nestled in the Helderberg Mountains, just 18 miles southwest of Albany. The campground features a sandy swimming beach, kayak and canoe rentals, a nature center, and hiking access to over 25 miles of trails at adjacent Thacher State Park. Sites accommodate tents and smaller RVs up to 40 feet, though no electric hookups are available.
payload.long_description:
Thompson's Lake Campground sits at the base of the Helderberg Escarpment within Thacher State Park, offering a classic Northeastern camping experience surrounded by mixed hardwood and conifer forests, limestone outcroppings, and open fields. The campground's 140 wooded sites are split between two loops: Loop A operates from early May through mid-October, while Loop B runs from late May through early September. Each site can accommodate up to six people with a maximum of two vehicles.

The centerpiece of the campground is Thompson's Lake itself, which features a sandy beach with lifeguard-staffed swimming areas during the summer season. Boat rentals including kayaks, canoes, and stand-up paddleboards are available, and fishing is permitted year-round including winter ice fishing. The Emma Treadwell Thacher Nature Center is located adjacent to the campground and offers exhibits, interpretive programs, and educational displays.

Recreational facilities include volleyball courts, horseshoe pits, a playing field, basketball court, and playgrounds. The campground provides convenient access to over 25 miles of hiking and cross-country skiing trails at Thacher State Park, including dramatic views from the Helderberg Escarpment overlooks.

location.directions: Located 18 miles southwest of Albany via Route 157. The campground address is 68 Thompson's Lake Rd, East Berne, NY 12059.

links.title: NY State Parks - Thompson's Lake Campground
NY State Parks - Thacher State Park

payload.name: Kentucky Horse Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. During winter season (November through March), only loops B and D are operational. Water at individual campsites is not available from mid-November through mid-March due to freezing conditions. Pool is closed for the season.
payload.short_description: Large equine-themed campground at Kentucky Horse Park with 260 sites featuring electric and water hookups, modern bathhouses, camp store, and free WiFi in the heart of Kentucky's Bluegrass region.
payload.medium_description: Kentucky Horse Park Campground offers 260 spacious paved sites with 20/30/50 amp electric and water hookups on over 1,200 acres of Kentucky's Bluegrass country. The campground features two modern bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, two dump stations, laundry facilities, a camp store, free WiFi, and a seasonal junior Olympic-sized pool. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. The park is home to the International Museum of the Horse and offers horseback riding, horse shows, and numerous recreational amenities.
payload.long_description:
Kentucky Horse Park Campground is a premier equine-themed destination located in Lexington, Kentucky, approximately 9 miles from downtown. Situated on over 1,200 acres of Kentucky's famous Bluegrass country, the campground provides 260 spacious paved campsites with 55-foot back-in pads. All standard electric sites feature water and 20, 30, or 50 amp electric service, fire rings, and picnic tables. Pull-through sites are available for an additional fee.

The campground offers extensive amenities including two modern bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, two dump stations near the front entrance, two laundry facilities, and a well-stocked camp store with groceries, ice, firewood, RV supplies, and souvenirs. Free WiFi is available throughout the campground via the KHP Campground network. A seasonal junior Olympic-sized swimming pool, tennis courts, volleyball and basketball courts, playgrounds, horseshoe pits, and a dog park provide ample recreation opportunities.

As part of Kentucky Horse Park, campers enjoy access to world-class equine attractions including the International Museum of the Horse, daily horse shows, and horseback riding trails. A shuttle service operates during summer months to transport guests around the park. The campground operates year-round, though sites B77-B130 and D207-D260 (loops B and D) are the only sites available during winter season. Water at individual sites is turned off from mid-November through mid-March due to freezing temperatures.

location.directions: From I-75, take Exit 120 (Iron Works Pike). The park is located at 4089 Iron Works Pike, approximately 3 miles south of Georgetown and 9 miles north of downtown Lexington.

payload.name: Indian Scotty Group Site
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Potable water is not available; campers must bring their own drinking water. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Fire restrictions may be in effect.
payload.short_description: Group campsite on the Wild and Scenic Scott River in Klamath National Forest, accommodating up to 50 people with swimming, fishing, and access to Marble Mountain Wilderness trailheads.
payload.medium_description: Indian Scotty Group Site is a reservation-only group campground located along the Wild and Scenic Scott River in Klamath National Forest. Set in a forest of cedar, Douglas fir, and Ponderosa pine at 2,400 feet elevation, the site accommodates up to 50 people and is suited for RVs up to 30 feet. Visitors enjoy riverfront access for swimming, tubing, and fishing, with several Marble Mountain Wilderness trailheads nearby including Boulder, Kelsey, and Lovers Camp.
payload.long_description:
Indian Scotty Group Site sits in an open grassy area surrounded by cedar, Douglas fir, and Ponderosa pine trees along the Wild and Scenic Scott River in California's Klamath National Forest. At 2,400 feet elevation, the single group site can accommodate up to 50 people with a campfire circle and grill provided. The site is particularly suited for RVs up to 30 feet due to its configuration, with a 200-foot gravel driveway.

During summer when river flows are low, campers enjoy swimming, tubing, and fishing in the Scott River. In spring, higher flows create Class IV-V whitewater runs through the Scott River canyon. Several Marble Mountain Wilderness trailheads are easily accessed from the campground, including Boulder, Kelsey, and Lovers Camp.

Vault toilets are available but potable water is not currently provided. Campers must bring their own drinking water. This is bear country and all food must be stored in approved containers. Firewood should be purchased locally rather than transported to prevent spread of invasive species.

location.directions: Take I-5 to Yreka, CA. Take the south Yreka exit for Highway 3 to Fort Jones for 18 miles. Turn right (west) on Scott River Road, between the Forest Service Office and grocery store, and go approximately 14 miles. At the Indian Scotty Campground sign, turn left (south) on the 44N45 Road and cross the Scott River. Go approximately 300 feet and turn right on the 44N53 Road toward the campground. Go past the campground entrance and next campground loop to the group site entrance.

address.full: 14434 Scott River Rd, Fort Jones, CA 96032

links.title: USFS Klamath NF - Indian Scotty Campground

payload.name: Lynx Campground
payload.status_description: Open April 1 through October 31. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. The Lynx Lake boat launch is temporarily unavailable due to low water levels. A seasonal bald eagle nesting closure affects portions of the Lynx Lake area through June 30.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground in Prescott National Forest at 5,600 feet elevation, offering 35 sites along Lynx Lake's west shoreline with vault and flush toilets, potable water, and easy access to hiking, fishing, and boating.
payload.medium_description: Lynx Campground sits within the popular Lynx Lake Recreation Area, roughly 7 miles southeast of Prescott, Arizona. The 35-site campground features asphalt driveways in pull-through, back-in, and parallel configurations with picnic tables and fire rings at each site. Potable water, vault and flush toilets, and trash service are available. The 55-acre lake just steps away offers trout fishing and boating with motors up to 10 HP.
payload.long_description:
Lynx Campground occupies a prime location in the Lynx Lake Recreation Area at 5,600 feet elevation within a ponderosa pine ecosystem mixed with alligator juniper and oak. The campground borders the west shore of the 55-acre Lynx Lake, one of central Arizona's most popular recreation spots drawing over 90,000 visitors annually.

All 35 single sites and 4 double sites include picnic tables, steel fire rings, and either established tent pads or adequate tent space. Driveways are asphalt-surfaced in pull-through, back-in, or parallel configurations. The campground provides 8 water faucets, 4 vault toilets, 2 flush toilets, and 6 dumpsters. No hookups or dump station are available; filling RV water tanks is not permitted.

Recreation options abound. Lynx Lake permits boating with motors 10 HP or less, plus paddle and sail-powered craft. Multiple trail systems accommodate hikers, mountain bikers, and equestrians. Wildlife viewing includes potential sightings of bald eagles, osprey, great blue herons, deer, and various other species. Recreational gold panning is allowed without motorized equipment.

location.directions: From Highway 69, turn south on Walker Road (by Costco, approximately 5 miles east of Prescott). Continue south on Walker Road for about 3 miles. The campground entrance is on the left side of Walker Road.

address.street1: E United States Forest Service Road 622
address.full: 4305 E United States Forest Service Road 622, Prescott, AZ 86303

photos.name: Camp site on a raised platform with stairs, some tripping hazards
Uncovered camp site in the afternoon shade along a paved road.
Camp site with covered picnic benches.
Uncovered camp site with fire pit in the afternoon shade.

payload.name: Bowman Bay Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates from approximately April through late September. Water systems are shut off by mid-November. Note: the Bowman Bay pier and trailered boat launch are closed indefinitely due to unsafe conditions, but kayaks and paddleboards still have access.
payload.short_description: Small 19-site campground at Deception Pass State Park with beach access on Bowman Bay, featuring mostly standard tent sites with one partial-hookup site, restrooms with showers, and proximity to the CCC Interpretive Center.
payload.medium_description: Bowman Bay Campground offers an intimate camping experience at Deception Pass State Park with just 19 sites located close to the beach. The campground features 18 standard sites and one partial-hookup site with electric and water. Facilities include restrooms with coin-operated showers. The adjacent Bowman Bay day-use area provides access to tidepools, the historic CCC Interpretive Center, and kayak rentals, though the pier and trailered boat launch are currently closed indefinitely.
payload.long_description:
Bowman Bay Campground is a smaller, more secluded camping area within Deception Pass State Park, Washington's most-visited state park. With only 19 sites situated near the beach, it offers a quieter alternative to the larger Cranberry Lake campground. The campground consists of 18 standard sites and one partial-hookup site featuring electric and water connections. All campers have access to restrooms equipped with coin-operated showers.

The Bowman Bay area is rich in history and natural beauty. The nearby CCC Interpretive Center, housed in a 1930s bathhouse built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, tells the story of the CCC's work across Washington during the Great Depression and is free to visit April through September. The bay itself offers excellent tidepooling, kayaking, and crabbing opportunities. Kayak rentals are available seasonally at the bay.

Due to the narrow access roads and limited maneuvering space, vehicles and trailers over 25 feet are restricted from the Bowman Bay area. The campground operates seasonally from approximately April through late September, with the upper parking lot and restroom closing October 1 through March 31 and water systems shut down by mid-November. Reservations are available through the Washington State Parks reservation system online or by calling 1-888-CAMPOUT.

location.directions: From I-5, take exit 230 and head west on Highway 20 toward Anacortes. Continue on Highway 20 for approximately 12 miles, crossing the Deception Pass Bridge. After the bridge, watch for signs to Bowman Bay and turn right. Follow the narrow road to the campground. Vehicles and trailers over 25 feet are restricted due to limited maneuverability.

links.title: Deception Pass State Park Official Page

payload.name: Flumet Flat Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. The gate is locked; the combination is provided in the confirmation. No potable water available on site.
payload.short_description: A reservable group campground in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest with a large meadow ideal for reunions, scout groups, and group events near Applegate River.
payload.medium_description: Flumet Flat Group Campground is a reservation-only group site in southwest Oregon's Siskiyou Mountains Ranger District. The campground features a large meadow with individual spurs for tents and trailers, picnic tables, campfire rings, vault toilet, and garbage collection. It accommodates up to 50 people and 20 vehicles. Swimming and fishing on the Applegate River are within walking distance, and the Gin Lin National Recreation Trail is just south of the campground.
payload.long_description:
Flumet Flat Group Campground sits in a large meadow along the Applegate River corridor in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest. The site is designed for group events such as family reunions, church camps, school field trips, and scouting activities. The entire campground must be reserved as a single unit and features individual spurs for tents and trailers on a paved surface, along with picnic tables and Forest Service-approved campfire rings.

The campground has a vault toilet and garbage collection but no potable water or electricity. Campers must bring all drinking water. The gate is locked; a combination is provided in the reservation confirmation. Nearby recreation includes swimming and fishing on the Applegate River, and the Gin Lin National Recreation Trail offers a 3/4-mile self-guided loop exploring 19th century mining history. The area is known for spring wildflowers but also rattlesnakes, ticks, and poison oak.

Applegate Lake lies north of the campground and offers boating, swimming, and year-round fishing. The Red Buttes Wilderness is accessible to the south. The Mule Mountain Trail provides long-distance hiking through the Oregon Siskiyous with views of Applegate Valley.

location.directions: From Jacksonville, OR, travel west on Highway 238 for 8 miles to Ruch, OR. Turn left onto Upper Applegate Road and travel 9.6 miles to Palmer Creek Road. Turn right onto Palmer Creek Road and travel 0.5 mile to the campground entrance on the right.

payload.name: Gates Of Lodore Campground
payload.status_description: Open and operating first-come, first-served. Drinking water is available. Pack out all trash. Access may be difficult in winter due to snow and road conditions.
payload.short_description: Remote first-come, first-served campground on the Green River at the entrance to Lodore Canyon in Dinosaur National Monument, popular with rafters launching multi-day river trips.
payload.medium_description: Gates of Lodore Campground sits at the boat ramp where the Green River enters the dramatic Lodore Canyon. This remote 19-site campground, 106 miles from the Canyon Visitor Center, is a staging area for rafters and a base for exploring the wild northern reaches of Dinosaur National Monument. Sites have tables and fire pits or grills, with vault toilets and seasonal drinking water. No reservations; pay via Scan & Pay on arrival.
payload.long_description:
Gates of Lodore Campground occupies a striking location on the Green River at the head of Lodore Canyon, where the river cuts into steep-walled mountains. The campground primarily serves as a staging point for rafters launching multi-day trips through the canyon, though it also attracts visitors seeking solitude in one of the monument's most remote corners. A short trail provides views of the river entering the gates.

The 19 sites are all pull-throughs on level ground, suitable for tents and RVs up to about 25 feet (some sites accommodate larger rigs). Amenities include picnic tables at every site, fire pits or grills, vault toilets year-round, and potable water during summer months. There are no showers, hookups, or dump stations anywhere in Dinosaur National Monument. Food storage is required due to black bears in the area.

The drive to Gates of Lodore is long (137 miles from the Quarry Visitor Center), and winter access may be limited by snow and road conditions. The isolation is part of the appeal, offering quiet camping beneath cottonwoods near the river with minimal development.

location.directions: From Maybell, Colorado, follow US Highway 40 west for 0.4 mile. Turn right onto CO 318 and follow it west for 46.2 miles. Turn left onto Moffat County Road 34N and continue 1.7 miles. Turn right onto Moffat County Road 34 and drive 4.5 miles to the ranger station and campground.

payload.name: Cagle
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required at least 48 hours in advance via Recreation.gov. No current alerts or closures.
payload.short_description: Cagle Recreation Area offers 47 full-hookup RV sites along Lake Conroe in Sam Houston National Forest, just one hour north of Houston with boating, fishing, and access to the Lone Star Hiking Trail.
payload.medium_description: Cagle Recreation Area is a developed campground nestled among the pines of Sam Houston National Forest along the shoreline of Lake Conroe. All 47 sites feature full hookups (water, electric, sewer), fire rings, and tent pads. The area provides flush toilets and hot showers, a boat ramp with large parking area, and a picnic area overlooking the lake. Reservations are required at least 48 hours in advance through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Cagle Recreation Area sits on the west fork of the San Jacinto River where it forms Lake Conroe, offering one of the best-equipped campgrounds in Sam Houston National Forest. The campground features two loops with 47 full-service RV sites, each with water, electric, and sewer hookups along with fire rings, tent pads, and lantern posts. Both loops have flush toilets, sinks, and hot showers.

The recreation area serves as an excellent base for exploring the surrounding forest and lake. A developed boat ramp provides access to Lake Conroe for fishing and water sports (swimming is not allowed). The campground connects to 85 miles of OHV, equestrian, and mountain bike trails, plus 129 miles of hiking on the Lone Star Hiking Trail. A picnic area overlooking the lake is available for day use.

Alcohol is prohibited throughout the campground. Pets are permitted but must be leashed (6 feet or less) or crated at all times. Each site is limited to one camping unit plus one vehicle, with a maximum of two tents and eight people per site.

location.directions: From I-45 northbound, take exit #102 at FM-1375 near New Waverly. From I-45 southbound, take exit #103. Head west on FM-1375 approximately 5 miles to the recreation area.

payload.name: Colonel Denning State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground opened April 4 and operates through the day after rifle deer season in mid-December. Reservations available online through Pennsylvania State Parks or by calling 888-PA-PARKS.
payload.short_description: A 49-site wooded campground nestled in Doubling Gap valley with access to the 96,000-acre Tuscarora State Forest and a 3.5-acre lake for fishing and swimming.
payload.medium_description: Colonel Denning State Park offers 49 tent and trailer sites in a forested setting within Cumberland County's Blue Mountain region. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring, with restrooms offering warm showers and a dump station. The park surrounds a 3.5-acre lake and serves as a gateway to the expansive Tuscarora State Forest, providing excellent hiking including access to the Tuscarora Trail.
payload.long_description:
Situated in Doubling Gap, where Blue Mountain curves back on itself in a distinctive S-turn, Colonel Denning State Park provides a secluded camping experience in north-central Cumberland County. The 273-acre park centers around a 3.5-acre lake offering fishing, swimming, and non-powered boating, while the surrounding 96,000-acre Tuscarora State Forest opens up extensive backcountry exploration.

The 49-site campground accommodates tents and trailers, with each site equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Modern restroom facilities with warm showers serve the camping area, along with a sanitary dump station. Firewood and ice are available for purchase from the campground host. A separate group tenting area accommodates up to 20 people with five tent pads, lantern holders, and a large communal fire ring.

Hiking is a major draw, with trails ranging from easy lakeside walks to challenging routes connecting to the Tuscarora Trail. Flat Rock Trail leads to panoramic views of the Cumberland Valley. The park operates seasonally from early April through mid-December, aligning with Pennsylvania's trout and deer hunting seasons.

location.directions: Located 8 miles north of Newville and 9 miles south of Landisburg along PA Route 233. The park address is 1599 Doubling Gap Road, Newville, PA 17241.

links.title: Colonel Denning State Park - Stay Overnight
Colonel Denning State Park Main Page

payload.name: Silver Bell Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season and opens May 22, 2026. Sites 2-4 and 8-14 are first-come, first-served only. The welcome station on Maroon Creek Road is staffed 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily for check-in and availability inquiries. A vehicle pass is required in addition to the camping fee. 5-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: Scenic campground on Maroon Creek near Aspen at 8,460 feet, with 14 sites featuring vault toilets, fire rings, and bear boxes. No potable water; access to Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Silver Bell Campground sits on the banks of Maroon Creek in the Maroon Bells Scenic Area, surrounded by aspen groves and subalpine forests at 8,460 feet elevation. The 14-site campground offers vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and bear boxes, but no potable water or hookups. Sites 1, 5-7 are reservable through Recreation.gov; the remaining sites are first-come, first-served with a 5-day stay limit. Expect warm summer days, cool evenings, and frequent afternoon thunderstorms.
payload.long_description:
Silver Bell Campground is tucked into aspen groves and subalpine forest along Maroon Creek, just 5.5 miles from Aspen via Maroon Creek Road. At 8,460 feet, the campground provides a base for exploring the iconic Maroon Bells-Snowmass Wilderness, one of Colorado's original 1964 wilderness designations. The area showcases metamorphic sedimentary mudstone peaks, alpine wildflower meadows, and habitat for bighorn sheep, pika, and ptarmigan.

The campground has 14 sites including tent-only and walk-in options. Standard sites accommodate RVs and trailers. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring, and access to bear boxes for food storage. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water, so bring your own supply. Sites 1, 5-7 can be reserved via Recreation.gov; sites 2-4 and 8-14 are first-come, first-served only. During peak summer and fall, the campground typically fills before noon.

Access depends on Independence Pass (Highway 82), which typically opens Memorial Day weekend and closes mid-October due to snow. A vehicle pass is required in addition to the camping fee. The West Maroon Trail from nearby Maroon Lake offers challenging backcountry access, while Maroon Creek Trail provides a gentler day-hiking option with views of the Maroon Bells and Pyramid Peak.

location.directions: From Aspen: Take Highway 82 West 1 mile to the roundabout, then take Maroon Creek Road 4.7 miles to the Maroon Bells Welcome Station. Continue past the Welcome Station 0.5 mile; Silver Bell Campground is on the left. Total distance approximately 5 miles from Highway 82.

links.title: USFS White River NF - Silver Bell Campground

payload.name: Pocahontas Cabins And Lodge
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance. During peak season (Memorial Day through Labor Day), a six-night minimum stay is required. Check-in at 4 p.m., check-out at 10 a.m. Burn ban in effect February 15 through April 30 restricts open fires from midnight to 4 p.m.
payload.short_description: Four three-bedroom cabins and one six-bedroom lodge at Pocahontas State Park near Richmond, offering year-round waterfront accommodations with full kitchens and climate control.
payload.medium_description: Pocahontas Cabins and Lodge provides comfortable year-round accommodations within Virginia's largest state park, just 20 miles from Richmond. The four three-bedroom cabins sleep up to 8 guests each, while the six-bedroom lodge accommodates up to 16. All units feature full kitchens, central heating and air conditioning, gas fireplaces, and scenic water views from partially covered decks. Guests must bring their own linens.
payload.long_description:
Located within Pocahontas State Park, Virginia's largest state park at over 8,000 acres, these cabins and lodge offer a comfortable retreat near Swift Creek Lake. The four three-bedroom cabins each accommodate up to 8 guests across three bedrooms and two bathrooms, featuring queen beds, twin beds, and bunk beds. The six-bedroom lodge sleeps up to 16 guests with three bathrooms, including one universally accessible.

All accommodations include fully equipped kitchens with electric range, refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher, and complete cookware and dishes. Living areas feature gas fireplaces, ceiling fans, and comfortable seating. Each unit has a partially covered deck with rocking chairs overlooking the water, plus an outdoor picnic table, fire ring, and charcoal grill. The lodge uniquely includes a washer and dryer.

Guests have access to the park's extensive trail system, mountain biking, fishing, and the seasonal aquatic center. Note that there is no WiFi, TV, or phone service in the cabins. Linens are not provided; guests must bring sheets, towels, and blankets. Pillows are supplied.

location.directions: Located at 10301 State Park Road, Chesterfield, VA 23832. From I-95, take exit 61 and follow Route 10 west approximately 4 miles. Turn right onto Beach Road, then follow signs to the park entrance.

address.full: 9276 E State Park Rd, Chesterfield, VA 23832

payload.name: Interrorem Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Closed every Thursday for cleaning. No potable water is currently available; guests must bring their own water supply. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is 7 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Historic 1907 ranger cabin in Olympic National Forest's Duckabush Recreation Area, offering year-round rustic lodging beneath magnificent Big Leaf Maple trees with access to hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing.
payload.medium_description: Interrorem Cabin is a historic peeled-log cabin built in 1907 as the first administrative site in Olympic National Forest. Ranger Emery J. Finch constructed it for his bride Mabel, and today it offers year-round rustic lodging for up to four guests. The cabin features propane heating, cooking, and lighting, plus a fire ring and picnic table outside. Located in the Duckabush Recreation Area with nearby access to the Duckabush River, The Brothers Wilderness, and Olympic National Park.
payload.long_description:
Interrorem Cabin holds the distinction of being the first administrative site in Olympic National Forest, built in 1907 by Ranger Emery J. Finch for his new bride Mabel. This 24x20-foot square peeled-log building with its pyramidal cedar shake roof and open front porch sits on a grassy clearing beneath magnificent stands of Big Leaf Maple trees in the Duckabush Recreation Area.

The cabin accommodates up to four guests with a futon in the living room and twin bunk beds in the bedroom. Propane is furnished for the heater, cook range, and lights. Guests must bring sleeping bags, pillows, towels, dish soap, cleaning supplies, matches, toilet paper, and garbage bags. A vault toilet is located outside, along with a fire ring and picnic table.

A nature trail behind the cabin features interpretive signs and historic photos describing the lives of Emery and Mabel Finch. The Ranger Hole Trail, built by Finch himself, leads to his favorite fishing spot on the Duckabush River. The cabin provides easy access to The Brothers Wilderness, Olympic National Park, Hood Canal, and nearby Murhut Falls.

location.directions: From Quilcene, WA take Highway 101 South for 15 miles to the Duckabush Recreation Area, turn west onto Duckabush River Road (Forest Road #2510). Follow the road for 4 miles to the end of the pavement. Interrorem Cabin is on the left side of the road.

payload.name: Mix Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Seasonal campground typically operating Memorial Day through Labor Day. Reports indicate a potential multi-year closure due to Spruce Beetle infestation affecting the area. Contact Conejos Peak Ranger District at (719) 274-8971 to confirm current status before visiting.
payload.short_description: High-elevation campground at 10,000 feet near Mix Lake and Platoro Reservoir in the Rio Grande National Forest, offering 22 sites with access to the South San Juan Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Mix Lake Campground sits at 10,000 feet in the Conejos River drainage, one mile west of Platoro. The 22-site campground provides convenient access to Mix Lake, Platoro Reservoir, Lily Pond, Kerr Lake, and the Conejos River for fishing. Trail access includes Lake Fork Trail 716 and Sawmill Gulch Trail leading into the South San Juan Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Mix Lake Campground is a high-elevation Forest Service campground located at 10,000 feet in the Rio Grande National Forest. Situated one mile west of the historic mining town of Platoro in the Conejos River drainage, the campground offers 22 sites with picnic tables and fire rings, vault toilets, potable water, and trash service.

The area is a gateway to excellent fishing opportunities at Mix Lake (25 surface acres stocked with Brown, Rainbow, and Brook trout), Platoro Reservoir, Conejos River, Lily Pond, and Kerr Lake. Hiking access includes Lake Fork Trail 716 and Sawmill Gulch Trail, both providing entry into the South San Juan Wilderness. The Mix Lake overlook adjacent to the campground offers scenic vistas of Platoro Reservoir and the surrounding mountains.

The campground accommodates RVs and trailers up to 40 feet. Fires are permitted only in metal fire rings and must be completely extinguished before leaving. Dogs are allowed on leashes up to 6 feet. Horses and pack animals are not permitted in the campground. Private land exists in the surrounding area; obtain permission before entering.

location.directions: From Monte Vista: Take Highway 17 south 12 miles, then Twelve Mile Road west 12 miles to the forest boundary where it becomes Alamosa-Conejos River Road #250. Follow #250 for 17 miles over Stunner Pass to Mix Lake. From Antonito: Take Highway 17 west 23 miles to Road #250 at Elk Creek, then follow #250 for 23 miles up the Conejos River to Mix Lake.

payload.name: Elk Summit Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens in July once snow melts and Forest Road 360 becomes passable. It closes in late autumn when snow returns. Currently still closed for the season. First-come, first-served; no reservations.
payload.short_description: Remote 15-site campground at 5,756 ft elevation near the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, with stock facilities and access to Hoodoo Lake and backcountry trails.
payload.medium_description: Elk Summit Campground offers 15 primitive campsites at the edge of the 1.34 million-acre Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness. Located 24 miles south of Highway 12 via Forest Road 360, this remote destination features stock facilities in Loops A and B, vault toilets, and access to Hoodoo Lake just a short walk away. No potable water is available, though stock water is provided. Pack-it-in, pack-it-out policy for trash. No cell service.
payload.long_description:
Elk Summit Campground is a remote, no-fee destination perched at 5,756 feet in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, serving as a gateway to some of Idaho's wildest backcountry. The campground sits a short distance from the 1.34 million-acre Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness, offering access to remote alpine lakes, rugged mountain peaks, and extensive trail systems for hikers and equestrians alike.

The campground provides 15 campsites across three loops. Loops A and B accommodate stock animals with hitching rails and water for horses, while Loop C near Hoodoo Lake is walk-in only with no stock permitted. Hoodoo Lake, a scenic mountain lake popular for fishing and wildlife viewing, is just a short stroll from camp. Facilities are primitive: vault toilets are available but there is no potable water, no garbage service, and no hookups. Campers must bring all drinking water and pack out all trash.

This is rugged wild country with no cell phone service, accessed via 24 miles of mountain roads that are not plowed in winter. The setting rewards those willing to make the journey with stunning scenery, solitude, and proximity to genuine wilderness.

location.directions: From Lolo, MT head west on Hwy 12 for 44 miles and turn left onto Elk Summit Rd 360. In 5.4 miles, turn right onto Forest Rd 360 and continue 14 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Battle Ground State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Standard and partial hookup sites are reservable; primitive sites are available. Park hours are 6:30 a.m. to dusk during summer (April 1 through September 30) and 8:00 a.m. to dusk in winter. Some facilities may have reduced services during winter months.
payload.short_description: A 280-acre state park campground nestled around a volcanic crater lake in Clark County, offering standard, partial hookup, and primitive tent sites plus cabins, with swimming, fishing, and trails through old-growth Douglas fir.
payload.medium_description: Battle Ground Lake State Park offers camping along a scenic 28-acre spring-fed lake formed in an ancient volcanic crater. The campground features standard sites, partial hookup sites for RVs up to 35 feet, and primitive walk-in tent sites requiring up to a half-mile hike. Amenities include restrooms with showers, drinking water, a dump station, and a camp store selling supplies and hot food. The lake permits non-motorized boats and electric motors, with a boat ramp on site.
payload.long_description:
Battle Ground Lake State Park sits in the forested foothills of the Cascade Range, centered on a pristine 28-acre lake filling an ancient volcanic crater. The 280-acre park provides a range of camping options: standard campsites, partial hookup sites with water and electric for RVs and trailers up to 35 feet, primitive walk-in sites that require hiking up to half a mile from parking, and primitive equestrian campsites with corrals. Four cabins are also available for those preferring roofed accommodations.

The campground offers modern amenities including restrooms with flush toilets and showers, potable water, a dump station, and recycling services. A camp store operates seasonally, offering camping supplies, fishing gear, hot food, and snacks. The park's kitchen shelter with electricity can be reserved for group gatherings.

Battle Ground Lake is open to swimming, fishing, and non-motorized boating with electric motors permitted. Over 10 miles of trails wind through towering Douglas fir forest, suitable for hiking and horseback riding. The park operates year-round with limited services in winter, and reservations can be made through the Washington State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: From I-5, take exit 11 for NE 179th Street. Head east on NE 179th Street, which becomes NE 244th Street. Continue east approximately 8 miles to Battle Ground. Turn north on Heisson Road and follow signs to the park entrance.

payload.name: St. Joe State Park Equestrian Campground 2
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems operational April 1 through October 31. Gate access requires code from reservation confirmation. Two-night minimum on weekends. Camping limited to 15 days within any 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground at St. Joe State Park offering electric and basic sites with hitching posts, vault toilets, and access to 28 miles of equestrian trails in the Missouri Ozarks.
payload.medium_description: Campground 2 at St. Joe State Park is an equestrian-focused campground offering both basic and electric sites with 20 and 30-amp service. Each site includes a hitching post for horses, parking pad, picnic table, and grill. While primarily designed for equestrian campers, sites are also available to non-horse campers. Vault toilets and frost-free water hydrants are on-site, with showers and a dump station accessible at nearby Campground 1.
payload.long_description:
St. Joe State Park's Equestrian Campground (Campground 2) provides a dedicated camping area for horse enthusiasts and non-ORV campers looking to explore the park's extensive trail system. The campground offers both basic and electric campsites with 20 and 30-amp electrical service. Each site features a hitching post, parking pad, picnic table, grill, and lantern post. Vault toilets and frost-free water hydrants are located within the campground.

The park encompasses over 8,200 acres of former lead mining land that has been reclaimed into a diverse recreational area. Equestrian campers have access to 28 miles of dedicated horse trails winding through Ozark hills and forests. Non-equestrian campers are welcome to reserve sites here as an alternative to the ORV-focused Campground 1. Showers and the dump station are located at Campground 1 but are accessible to all registered campers.

Access to Campground 2 requires a gate code provided with your reservation confirmation. The campground operates year-round, though water systems are seasonal from April 1 through October 31. A two-night minimum stay applies on weekends, and camping is limited to 15 days within any 30-consecutive-day period.

location.directions: From Park Hills, take Highway 32 east approximately 4 miles. Turn south on Pimville Road and follow signs to St. Joe State Park. The park entrance is at 2800 Pimville Road.

address.full: 203 St Joe Park Rd H, Park Hills, MO 63601

links.title: St. Joe State Park Main Page

payload.name: Cherry Creek
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Occasionally closed in winter due to heavy ice buildup. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through September 30, 2026; campfires are permitted only in designated fire rings.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at 6,800 feet elevation along the scenic Trail of the Mountain Spirits Byway, 14 miles from Silver City in dense mixed conifer forest.
payload.medium_description: Cherry Creek Campground offers a quiet, no-fee camping experience in the Gila National Forest at 6,800 feet. Located along NM Highway 15, one of the most scenic stretches of the Trail of the Mountain Spirits Scenic Byway, the campground sits in dense mixed conifer forest. Sites have picnic tables and vault toilets are available, but campers must bring their own water and firewood.
payload.long_description:
Cherry Creek Campground is a small, primitive campground tucked into dense mixed conifer forest at 6,800 feet elevation in the Silver City Ranger District of the Gila National Forest. The campground is located approximately 14 miles from Silver City along the east side of NM Highway 15, placing it on one of the most scenic stretches of the Trail of the Mountain Spirits Scenic Byway.

The campground offers 12 sites with picnic tables and vault toilet facilities. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Firewood is not provided; bring your own or use charcoal or propane for cooking. A small seasonal stream runs through the campground, though it may only be a trickle depending on recent precipitation.

Camping is free and first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit. The campground is generally open year-round but may close temporarily during winter when heavy ice buildup creates safety hazards. The site is not recommended for RVs over 17 feet due to access limitations. OHVs, ATVs, hunting, shooting, and stock animals are prohibited within the campground.

location.directions: From Silver City, travel north on NM Highway 15 approximately 14 miles. The campground is located on the east side of the highway.

payload.name: Tumbleweeds
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Currently first-come-first-served through May 14, 2026. Starting May 15, all sites transition to reservation-only through September 30. Water systems are typically shut off October 1 for winter and restored in spring.
payload.short_description: Primitive and electric campsites overlooking Granite Springs Reservoir in Wyoming's Curt Gowdy State Park, with access to fishing, mountain biking, and hiking in the Laramie Range foothills.
payload.medium_description: Tumbleweeds is one of several campgrounds at Curt Gowdy State Park, situated between Cheyenne and Laramie at roughly 7,000 feet elevation. The campground offers both primitive sites and sites with water and electric hookups, with some sites positioned near Granite Springs Reservoir. The park features over 35 miles of IMBA-certified mountain biking trails, excellent trout and kokanee salmon fishing, and opportunities for boating and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Tumbleweeds Campground sits within Curt Gowdy State Park in southeastern Wyoming, a scenic recreation area straddling the Laramie Range foothills roughly 24 miles west of Cheyenne and 24 miles east of Laramie via State Route 210 (Happy Jack Road). The campground includes sites 17-31 with water and electric hookups, while some sites near the reservoir offer more primitive camping experiences.

Granite Springs Reservoir provides quality fishing for rainbow trout and kokanee salmon, along with boating and waterskiing. Crystal Reservoir offers a quieter alternative with a 15-horsepower motor limit. The park's trail system includes over 35 miles of IMBA-certified mountain biking routes, hiking trails, and an archery range. Aspen Grove campground nearby offers a free public horse corral for equestrian campers.

The park's Visitor Center provides flush toilets and showers. Note that Curt Gowdy State Park does not have a dump station; the nearest options are the Southeast Wyoming Welcome Center in Cheyenne (free, 24 hours) or Wyoming Territorial Prison near Laramie ($10, May through October).

location.directions: From Cheyenne, drive 24 miles west on State Route 210 (Happy Jack Road) to County Road 106. From Laramie, drive 24 miles east on Happy Jack Road.

links.title: Curt Gowdy State Park - Wyoming State Parks

payload.name: Kaner Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Twenty-five sites become reservable via Recreation.gov starting Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend. After mid-September, all 49 sites revert to first-come, first-served. Maximum stay is 14 nights.
payload.short_description: A 49-site campground near the Little Naches River in Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, popular with OHV riders, hunters, and anglers. Features an RV loop with pull-through parking, vault toilets, and potable water.
payload.medium_description: Kaner Flat Campground sits along the Little Naches River in a ponderosa pine forest, offering 49 paved sites including single and double units. The campground features an RV loop with long pull-through parking, vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, and an on-site Forest Service host. Popular as a base camp for OHV riding, hunting, and fishing, with numerous trails for dirt bikes, jeeps, hiking, and horseback riding nearby.
payload.long_description:
Kaner Flat Campground is located in the Little Naches drainage of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, surrounded by ponderosa pine forest near the Little Naches River. The campground offers 49 paved sites including single units and six double sites that accommodate up to 16 people. An RV loop provides long pull-through parking, though trailers are limited to 30 feet maximum.

Amenities include vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables, and campfire rings at each site. An on-site Forest Service host is present during the season. The campground is ADA accessible with wheelchair-accessible facilities.

This is a popular base camp for OHV enthusiasts, with a plethora of trails for dirt bikes and jeeps within 10 miles. Hunters and anglers frequent the area for deer, black bear, and native fish in the Little Naches River. Nearby Boulder Cave National Recreation Trail offers an accessible walk along the river with interpretive signs explaining local geology, plants, and fire history.

location.directions: From Naches, WA travel west on Highway 12 for 4.4 miles. Continue straight onto Highway 410 W for 24.2 miles. Turn right on Little Naches Road / Forest Road 19 and follow for 2.5 miles to the campground entrance on the right.

photos.name: Access to the Little Naches River

payload.name: Silver Fir Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 15, 2026 with first-come-first-served sites. Reservations available through Recreation.gov starting May 18. Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
payload.short_description: Forest Service campground along the North Fork Nooksack River offering 18 sites with vault toilets and drinking water, near Mt. Baker Wilderness trailheads.
payload.medium_description: Silver Fir Campground is situated in a shaded forest of silver fir, western red cedar, and western hemlock along the North Fork Nooksack River. The campground offers 18 individual sites and a historic CCC-built day-use picnic shelter. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring with grill. A sunny gravel bar between the campground and river provides river access. Trails accessed from nearby Hannegan Pass Road lead into the Mt. Baker Wilderness and North Cascades National Park.
payload.long_description:
Silver Fir Campground occupies a forested setting along the North Fork Nooksack River in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest. The campground sits beneath a canopy of silver fir, western red cedar, and western hemlock, with a sunny gravel bar providing access to the river. Sites range from tent-only configurations to standard nonelectric sites that can accommodate RVs up to 53 feet on select sites.

The location serves as an excellent base for exploring the Mt. Baker Wilderness and North Cascades National Park. Hannegan Pass Road, less than a mile from the campground, provides access to trails leading into alpine terrain with views of Mt. Baker's glaciated summit. The campground also features a historic Civilian Conservation Corps-built picnic shelter available for day-use groups up to 25 people.

Facilities include vault toilets, drinking water from faucets, and garbage service. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill. No hookups are available. The nearest supplies, groceries, and firewood are available in Glacier, approximately 20 minutes west. In winter, the area operates as a non-motorized Sno-Park.

location.directions: From Glacier, travel 14 miles east on Mt. Baker Highway (SR 542). The campground is on the west side of the highway after crossing the North Fork Nooksack River near milepost 46. From Seattle, take I-5 north to Bellingham, exit 255 onto Sunset Drive/Mt. Baker Highway SR 542, and continue past Glacier approximately 14 miles.

payload.name: Copan Point
payload.status_description: Copan Point is a day-use area only with no overnight camping. The reservable group shelter is currently open for daytime use. For overnight camping at Copan Lake, use Washington Cove or Post Oak Park campgrounds instead.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on Copan Lake in Oklahoma's Green Country with a reservable group shelter, boat ramp, swimming beach, and fishing dock.
payload.medium_description: Copan Point is a day-use area on the banks of Copan Lake offering a reservable group picnic shelter that accommodates up to 45 people. Facilities include flush and pit toilets, drinking water, picnic sites with tables, grills, and fire pits, a boat ramp with courtesy dock, a fishing dock, and a swimming beach with volleyball court. Overnight camping is not permitted here; campers should look to Washington Cove or Post Oak Park on the same lake.
payload.long_description:
Copan Point is a day-use recreation area located on the banks of Copan Lake in Oklahoma's Green Country, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The area features one reservable group picnic shelter that can accommodate up to 45 people, making it suitable for family reunions, group outings, and other gatherings. Amenities include flush and pit toilets, drinking water, and multiple picnic sites equipped with utility tables, grills, and fire pits.

The area provides excellent lake access with a boat ramp and courtesy dock for launching watercraft, plus a separate fishing dock for anglers. A swimming beach with a volleyball court rounds out the recreational offerings. The 4,850-acre lake sits on the Little Caney River and is home to largemouth bass, white crappie, channel and flathead catfish, and various sunfish species.

Note that Copan Point is strictly a day-use facility with no overnight camping. Visitors seeking overnight accommodations at Copan Lake should consider Washington Cove (101 sites with electric hookups) or Post Oak Park (19 sites with electric hookups), both located on the same lake.

location.directions: From HWY 75, travel 2 miles west on HWY 10 and 1 mile north on County Road 3970, then turn left on W 850 Road and go 1 mile to the park.

payload.name: Balsam Mountain Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through mid-October. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. The campground closes annually from mid-October through late May. Maximum 14 consecutive night stay limit.
payload.short_description: Remote, high-elevation campground in Great Smoky Mountains National Park offering 42 sites with flush toilets and drinking water, accessed via Heintooga Ridge Road.
payload.medium_description: Balsam Mountain Campground sits at 5,310 feet elevation in a secluded corner of Great Smoky Mountains National Park. The 42-site campground offers flush toilets and drinking water but no hookups or showers. Access requires navigating the narrow Heintooga Ridge Road, limiting vehicles to 24 feet maximum length. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Balsam Mountain Campground occupies one of the most remote and peaceful sections of Great Smoky Mountains National Park, perched at 5,310 feet elevation on the North Carolina side. The high altitude keeps summer temperatures mild, with daytime highs rarely exceeding 70°F. The 42 campsites include both standard nonelectric sites (accommodating tents, RVs, or trailers up to 24 feet) and tent-only walk-in sites.

The campground provides flush toilets, drinking water, and food storage lockers at each site due to high bear activity in the area. There are no hookups, showers, or dump station. A short nature trail begins near site 43, and the Flat Creek Trail offers an easy hike through hardwood forest. More ambitious hikers can tackle the 14-mile Hemphill Bald and Rough Fork loop for outstanding views and old-growth trees.

The Balsam Mountain and Straight Fork Roads provide access to some of the park's best backcountry trout fishing. Wildlife viewing is excellent, with elk commonly spotted in spring and fall. The 14-mile Heintooga Round Bottom Road offers scenic auto touring but prohibits vehicles over 25 feet.

location.directions: From the North: Take I-40 Exit 20 at Maggie Valley and travel US-19 toward Cherokee. Access the Blue Ridge Parkway at Soco Gap and continue south to mile 458.2, turning right onto Heintooga Ridge Road. Enter the park at Black Camp Gap and continue 9 miles to the campground. From the South: Follow US-441/US-23 North, merge onto US-74 West/US-441 North at Dillsboro, then take exit 74 onto US-441 through Cherokee into the park. Access the Blue Ridge Parkway traveling north to mile 458.2, turn left onto Heintooga Ridge Road, and continue 9 miles to the campground.
