payload.name: Olive Ridge
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season. Sites 1-24, 38, 41, 42, and 46 are first-come-first-served. Sites 26-40, 42, and 44-56 are reservable through Recreation.gov. Fire restrictions may be in effect due to high fire danger in the Boulder and Canyon Lakes Districts.
payload.short_description: Olive Ridge Campground offers 56 wooded sites near Rocky Mountain National Park's Wild Basin area at 8,350 feet elevation in Roosevelt National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Olive Ridge Campground sits at 8,350 feet in a peaceful forest of ponderosa pine and aspen near the southeastern corner of Rocky Mountain National Park. The 56-site campground accommodates tents, trailers, and RVs, with a mix of first-come-first-served and reservable sites. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with vault toilets and trash service provided. No water, hookups, or showers are available. The campground provides quick access to Wild Basin trailheads including Finch Lake and Sandbeach Lake.
payload.long_description:
Olive Ridge Campground is located within Roosevelt National Forest at 8,350 feet elevation, positioned near the southeastern corner of Rocky Mountain National Park. The campground features 56 sites spread through a heavily wooded setting of ponderosa pine and aspen trees, with interior roads of gravel and dirt. Twenty-six sites accommodate RVs and trailers while thirty are better suited for tent camping. Sites with tent pads include bear lockers for food storage.

Each campsite has a picnic table and fire ring or grill. Vault toilets and trash services are provided, but there is no potable water, electricity, hookups, dump station, or showers. Campers should bring adequate water supplies. A maximum of eight people are allowed per standard site, with oversized sites 26 and 39 accommodating up to ten people at an additional fee.

The campground provides easy access to Wild Basin trails including Finch Lake and Sandbeach Lake. Rocky Mountain National Park's main entrance at Estes Park is 14 miles north. The area sees heavy use on weekends, with the campground typically filling by Friday morning. Afternoon thunderstorms are common during summer months.

location.directions: Located on the west side of Colorado Highway 7 between Allenspark and Meeker Park at mile-marker 14. Approximately 6 miles north of the intersection of Highways 7 and 72 (21 miles west-northwest of Lyons), 15 miles south of Estes Park, and 29 miles north of Nederland.

payload.name: Cape Blanco State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through oregonstateparks.reserveamerica.com up to six months in advance. Group camp is currently closed. Firewood must be locally harvested or certified heat-treated due to Emerald Ash Borer restrictions.
payload.short_description: Oregon's westernmost campground, perched on forested bluffs overlooking the Pacific Ocean near a historic 19th-century lighthouse.
payload.medium_description: Cape Blanco State Park campground occupies a forested bluff at Oregon's westernmost point, offering 58 sheltered campsites with water and electric hookups. The park features flush restrooms with hot showers, a historic lighthouse, and over eight miles of trails leading to beaches, ocean viewpoints, and fishing spots along the Sixes River.
payload.long_description:
Cape Blanco State Park sits at Oregon's westernmost tip, where dramatic coastal bluffs drop to the Pacific Ocean. The campground provides 52 electrical sites with water hookups and 4 full-hookup sites, all nestled in a sheltered forest setting that blocks coastal winds. A modern bathhouse offers flush toilets and hot showers. The park also features standard cabins (two pet-friendly), a hiker/biker camp, and an 8-site horse camp with corrals.

Beyond camping, the park preserves the 1870 Cape Blanco Lighthouse (Oregon's oldest standing lighthouse) and the Hughes House, an 1898 Victorian home built by an Irish settler. Over eight miles of hiking trails traverse the headlands to secluded beaches, ocean overlooks, and fishing access along the Sixes River. Equestrians have seven miles of dedicated trails plus a 150-acre open riding area.

The campground operates year-round with reservations available through Oregon State Parks. Some sites accommodate RVs up to 68 feet, though all are back-in only. Surface water may pool in certain sites after heavy rain. The group camp is currently closed.

location.directions: From Port Orford, drive north on US Highway 101 for 4 miles. Turn west onto Cape Blanco Road and continue 5 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Wekiwa Springs State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open following completion of the 2025 waterline infrastructure project. Reservations required through Florida State Parks reservation system and can be made 1 day to 11 months in advance. Park gates open 8 a.m. to sundown year-round; campers arriving after sunset should call the park before 5 p.m. that day for the gate combination.
payload.short_description: A popular Central Florida campground featuring 60 wooded sites with water and electric hookups, set among rolling sandhills with longleaf pines just 10 miles from Orlando.
payload.medium_description: Wekiwa Springs State Park Campground offers 60 spacious wooded campsites on rolling sandhills covered with longleaf pines and native specialty plants. Each site features water and electric hookups, a fire ring with grill, and a picnic table. The campground provides two accessible restroom buildings with showers, a dump station, and accommodates RVs up to 50 feet. The park's crystal-clear spring and spring run offer swimming, paddling, and wildlife viewing opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Located just 10 miles from Orlando, Wekiwa Springs State Park Campground provides an accessible natural retreat in Central Florida. The 60 wooded campsites are nestled among rolling sandhills featuring longleaf pine flatwoods and scrub habitat, home to deer, black bears, and numerous bird species. Each site comes equipped with water and electric hookups, a fire ring with grill grate, and a picnic table, with some sites also offering sewer connections.

The campground facilities include two accessible restroom buildings with hot showers located within the camping loops, plus a dump station for RV waste disposal. Sites can accommodate recreational vehicles up to 50 feet in length, making it suitable for larger rigs. Pets are welcome in the campground on a 6-foot leash.

Beyond camping, the park offers a first-magnitude spring with year-round 72-degree water perfect for swimming, as well as the Wekiva River for paddling adventures. Thirteen miles of multi-use trails wind through the park's diverse ecosystems. Primitive backcountry camping is also available at Otter Camp and Big Buck Camp along Rock Springs Run, accessible only by canoe or kayak.

location.directions: From Interstate 4, take Exit 94 and head west on Wekiva Springs Road for approximately 4 miles. Turn right into the park entrance at 1800 Wekiwa Circle, Apopka, FL 32712. From Highway 429 in the west, take Lester Road east to Welch Road, then follow signs to the park.

payload.name: Daingerfield State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gates open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Morris County is under an emerald ash borer quarantine; moving firewood into or out of the park is restricted. Reservations recommended.
payload.short_description: Forested East Texas state park featuring an 80-acre spring-fed lake, rustic CCC-era cabins, and diverse camping from tent-only sites to full-hookup RV sites.
payload.medium_description: Daingerfield State Park offers a quiet escape in the pine and hardwood forests of East Texas, centered around an 80-acre spring-fed lake built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s. The park provides tent camping in the Cedar Ridge area with fire rings and grills, plus full-hookup RV sites in the Big Pine area. Fishing, paddling, and hiking the 2.5-mile Rustling Leaves Nature Trail are popular activities.
payload.long_description:
Daingerfield State Park sits in the rolling Piney Woods of northeast Texas, preserving 551 acres of mixed pine and hardwood forest surrounding an 80-acre spring-fed lake. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps during the Great Depression, the park retains its rustic character through historic stone and timber structures including rental cabins and the Bass Lodge.

The campground offers 58 sites across three loops. Cedar Ridge provides 18 tent-only sites with water spigots, fire rings, grills, and tent pads. The Big Pine area has 40 RV sites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer), including 10 pull-through sites. All sites have picnic tables and access to nearby restrooms with showers.

The lake supports fishing for bass, catfish, and crappie, with a fishing pier and boat ramp available. Paddleboats, canoes, and kayaks can be rented at the park store. Fall foliage draws visitors in October and November when sweetgums and maples turn brilliant colors.

location.directions: From Daingerfield, take TX-49 east for approximately 3 miles. Turn south on Park Road 17 and continue to the park entrance.

payload.name: Valley Of Fires Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served. Visitor center operates 9 AM to 11 AM and 1 PM to 3 PM daily, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
payload.short_description: BLM campground perched on the edge of a 5,000-year-old lava flow in New Mexico's Tularosa Basin, offering RV hookup sites, tent camping, flush toilets, showers, and an accessible nature trail through the Malpais.
payload.medium_description: Valley of Fires Recreation Area sits immediately adjacent to one of the youngest lava flows in the continental United States. The 44-mile Malpais flow filled the Tularosa Basin approximately 5,000 years ago and now supports a surprising diversity of Chihuahuan Desert wildlife. The campground offers 25 sites including 13 with water and 30/50-amp electric hookups, a central shower house with flush toilets, an RV dump station, and a 3/4-mile paved nature trail winding through the volcanic landscape.
payload.long_description:
Valley of Fires Recreation Area is a Bureau of Land Management site located four miles west of Carrizozo, New Mexico, on US Highway 380. The campground sits at the edge of the Malpais Lava Flow, which erupted from Little Black Peak roughly 5,000 years ago and spread 44 miles into the Tularosa Basin. At four to six miles wide and up to 160 feet thick, this 125-square-mile basalt expanse is considered one of the youngest lava flows in the lower 48 states.

The recreation area offers 25 campsites: 13 full-service RV sites with water and 30/50-amp electric hookups, several primitive RV sites, and dedicated tent camping. Every site includes a picnic shelter, table, trash can, and barbecue grill; most have fire rings. A central shower house provides flush toilets and showers, with accessible vault toilets and water spigots distributed throughout. An RV dump station operates from 7 AM to 7 PM.

The nearly one-mile paved Malpais Nature Trail is fully accessible and offers an up-close look at the lava surface and the plants and animals that have colonized it. A newer Kipuka Trail (over one mile each way) leads through an "island" of soil and vegetation surrounded by lava. Wildlife includes mule deer, barbary sheep, roadrunners, great horned owls, golden eagles, and various lizards and bats. The visitor center operates limited hours and is closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

location.directions: Travel four miles west of Carrizozo, New Mexico on US Highway 380. Valley of Fires Recreation Area is on the left (south side of the highway).

payload.name: Chinquapin Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for reservations via Recreation.gov. The gate is locked; a combination is provided with reservation confirmation. No cell phone service on site. Check-in at 2:00 p.m., check-out at 12:00 p.m. Quiet hours 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC camp site turned group campground in Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, accommodating up to 75 people with a large meadow, creek access, and proximity to Oregon Caves National Monument.
payload.medium_description: Chinquapin Group Campground sits at the former Camp Oregon Caves CCC camp site, where over 200 men worked during the Great Depression. The large meadow is ideal for reunions, church camps, school field trips, and scouting events. Water, picnic tables, and fire rings are available at three locations throughout the campground, with a vault toilet at the parking area. Swimming areas in Grayback Creek and the Grayback Interpretive Trail are within walking distance.
payload.long_description:
Chinquapin Group Campground occupies the historic site of the Camp Oregon Caves Civilian Conservation Corps camp, which operated from 1933 to 1941 and housed over 200 men working on projects in Siskiyou National Forest and Oregon Caves National Monument. The adjacent Grayback Ranger Station, built by CCC crews around 1936, remains as a tangible link to this history. A large Port-Orford cedar near the parking area was dedicated in 2011 as Oregon's 56th State Heritage Tree.

The campground's expansive meadow makes it well-suited for group events. Water, picnic tables, and fire rings are distributed across three areas, and a vault toilet is located at the back of the parking area. There is no electricity. Trash must be packed out or disposed of at nearby Grayback Campground across the road.

Grayback Creek runs adjacent to the property, offering swimming holes and access to the Grayback Interpretive Trail. Oregon Caves National Monument is a 10-mile drive east on Highway 46, featuring one of the few marble caves in the world.

location.directions: From Cave Junction, take Highway 46 east toward Oregon Caves National Monument for approximately 10.5 miles. Just past Grayback Campground on the left, look for Cedar Guard Station. Chinquapin Group Campground is behind Cedar Guard Station, accessed through the gate immediately to the right (east) of the station.

payload.name: Many Pines Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally late May through October. First-come, first-served only; no reservations. Camping fees begin May 22, 2026. Water systems may not be operational until late May; bring water early in the season. 16-day stay limit. Food storage order in effect March 1 through December 1.
payload.short_description: A 23-site first-come, first-served campground along Belt Creek in the Little Belt Mountains, offering fishing, proximity to Memorial Falls, and space for large RVs up to 51 feet.
payload.medium_description: Many Pines Campground sits in a stand of lodgepole pine directly off US Highway 89 in the Little Belt Mountains. The 23 campsites stretch along Belt Creek, which offers trout fishing with mandatory catch-and-release for cutthroat. Each site includes a fire ring or grill and picnic table. The campground is the most RV-friendly option on the Highway 89 corridor, accommodating trailers up to 51 feet. Memorial Falls trailhead lies about a mile north.
payload.long_description:
Many Pines Campground is located in a lodgepole pine forest directly off US Highway 89 in the Little Belt Mountains of the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest. The 23 campsites are situated along Belt Creek, which provides fishing opportunities for trout with mandatory catch-and-release rules for cutthroat. The campground is considered the most convenient option for campers with large RVs traveling the Highway 89 corridor, with a maximum trailer length of 51 feet.

Each campsite is equipped with a fire ring or grill and a picnic table. Vault toilets are available, including at least one ADA-accessible facility. Potable water from a hand pump is provided during the warmer months. Approximately one mile north lies the Memorial Falls trailhead, a popular day hike destination.

A food storage order is in effect from March 1 through December 1 to prevent human-bear conflicts. Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days at one location. Leashed dogs are welcome, but horses are not permitted in the campground. Motorized OHVs must stay on the campground road.

location.directions: From Great Falls, drive 58 miles south on US Highway 89.

payload.name: Kartchner Caverns Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park gate closes at 10 p.m. nightly. The Bat Cave Cafe is currently closed until further notice. Interstate 10 construction may impact travel times to the park.
payload.short_description: Arizona state park campground with 60 electric/water hookup sites, modern showers, and dump station, located 9 miles south of Benson near the famous Kartchner Caverns.
payload.medium_description: Kartchner Caverns State Park campground offers 60 campsites with electric and water hookups, fire rings, and picnic tables at every site. The campground includes 12 pull-through sites accommodating RVs up to 60 feet, 3 ADA-accessible sites, and modern restroom/shower facilities. All sites are $50 per night and include access to the dump station. The campground sits in the Whetstone Mountain foothills with excellent views.
payload.long_description:
Kartchner Caverns State Park campground provides 60 well-appointed campsites in the Whetstone Mountain foothills of southeastern Arizona. The campground features 43 standard back-in sites (up to 35 feet), 12 pull-through sites (up to 60 feet), and 3 ADA-accessible sites with paved pads and wheelchair-accessible tables. Every site includes electric hookups (30-amp on back-in sites, 50-amp on pull-throughs), water via hose bib, a fire ring, and a picnic table.

Modern restroom and shower facilities are located within the campground loop, with showers included in the camping fee. A dual-lane dump station with 110-foot lanes is available to registered campers. The park gate closes at 10 p.m. nightly, with check-in at 2 p.m. and checkout at noon. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.

The campground is located 9 miles south of Benson on Highway 90. Pets are welcome in outdoor areas on leash but are prohibited in buildings and cave tours. The Discovery Center offers a gift shop, and while the Bat Cave Cafe is currently closed, the park's main attraction remains the spectacular cave tours.

location.directions: Located 9 miles south of Benson on Highway 90. From Interstate 10, take Exit 302 and head south on AZ-90. The park address is 2980 S Hwy 90, Benson, AZ 85602.

payload.name: Fifield
payload.status_description: Fifield is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. Shelters are available first-come, first-served free of charge when unreserved, or can be reserved through Recreation.gov. Shelter occupancy permitted until dusk.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area at Lake Red Rock with four reservable picnic shelters, fire rings, outdoor grills, and access to the Volksweg bike trail. No overnight camping allowed.
payload.medium_description: Fifield is a day-use recreation area on Lake Red Rock, Iowa's largest lake, located 10 miles from Pella. The area features four reservable picnic shelters with 20-amp electrical outlets, fire rings, and outdoor grills. A playground and modern restrooms are available. Shelter occupancy is permitted until dusk only; no overnight camping is allowed.
payload.long_description:
Fifield Recreation Area is situated on the shores of Lake Red Rock, a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers project on the Des Moines River and Iowa's largest lake. The area provides day-use facilities including four reservable picnic shelters, each equipped with 20-amp electrical outlets, fire rings, and outdoor grills. Modern flush restrooms and a playground are available on site.

The recreation area offers access to the Volksweg Trail, a 15-mile paved bike path stretching west from Pella to the Des Moines River. Lake Red Rock provides excellent boating, water skiing, swimming, and fishing opportunities. Anglers can expect crappie, walleye, largemouth and striped bass, channel and flathead catfish, northern pike, and bluegill.

Note: Fifield is a day-use facility only. Shelter occupancy is permitted until dusk and no overnight camping is allowed. Golf carts, UTVs, and ATVs are prohibited. For overnight camping at Lake Red Rock, visitors should explore other campgrounds in the project area such as Elk Rock, Whitebreast, or Roberts Creek.

location.directions: From Pella, Iowa, follow County Road G28 west for 6 miles, then follow signs to Fifield. Address: 1672 Hwy G28, Pella, Iowa 50219.

payload.name: Cold Spring Indian Campging Area
payload.status_description: This is a tribal-only camping area and is not open to the general public. The site is reserved for Native American tribal members.
payload.short_description: A tribal-only camping area in Gifford Pinchot National Forest reserved for Native American use, not open to the general public.
payload.medium_description: Cold Spring Indian Camping Area is a primitive camping area in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest near the Indian Heaven Wilderness. This site is reserved exclusively for tribal members and is not open to public camping. The area is traditionally used by Native American tribes during the huckleberry harvest season.
payload.long_description:
Cold Spring Indian Camping Area is located in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest in Skamania County, Washington, near the Indian Heaven Wilderness at approximately 3,900 feet elevation. This is a tribal-only camping area that is not open to the general public.

The site is part of the historically significant huckleberry harvesting grounds used by multiple tribes including the Yakama Nation, Klickitat, Wishram, and other Columbia River tribes for centuries. A 1932 Handshake Agreement between the U.S. Forest Service and tribal representatives reserved certain areas in this region for exclusive tribal use during the traditional summer huckleberry harvest.

Public campers should seek alternative campgrounds in the area such as Cultus Creek Campground or other established Forest Service campgrounds that are open to general recreation.

location.directions: From Trout Lake, take Mt. Adams Road north to the intersection with Forest Road 23. Stay right and continue about one mile to the left turn onto Forest Road 80, signed South Climb. Follow Forest Road 80 to its end at the intersection with Forest Road 8040 and 8031. Turn right onto Forest Road 8040 and continue north past Morrison Creek Campground to the trailhead area. Road is steep and narrow with sharp switchbacks; not suitable for RVs or trailers.

links.title: Gifford Pinchot NF Tribal Huckleberry Harvest

payload.name: Bear Paw Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping from May through October. All sites require advance reservations through the Minnesota DNR reservation system. Showers and full restroom facilities are seasonally available during the camping season.
payload.short_description: Historic 79-site campground on the shores of Lake Itasca in Minnesota's oldest state park, featuring electric sites, modern facilities, and proximity to the Mississippi River headwaters.
payload.medium_description: Bear Paw Campground sits within Itasca State Park, Minnesota's oldest state park established in 1891. The campground offers 79 sites including the scenic Lakeview Loop on Lake Itasca's shores. Sites feature fire rings with cooking grates and picnic tables, with electric hookups available. Modern amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, and a dump station. Wireless internet is available throughout the campground area.
payload.long_description:
Bear Paw Campground is one of two main campgrounds in Itasca State Park, offering 79 campsites in a classic northwoods setting near the headwaters of the Mississippi River. The campground includes the popular Lakeview Loop positioned along Lake Itasca's shores, providing scenic water views and easy access to the park's extensive trail system and historic sites.

The campground features a mix of electric and non-electric sites accommodating tents, trailers, and RVs up to 60 feet. Each site includes a fire ring with cooking grate and picnic table. Modern facilities include restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers, as well as an on-site dump station. Wireless internet access is available throughout the Bear Paw area, and ADA-accessible sites are available.

Itasca State Park encompasses over 32,000 acres with more than 100 lakes, old-growth pine forests, and 49 miles of hiking trails. The park is famous as the source of the Mississippi River, where visitors can walk across the mighty river at its humble beginning.

location.directions: From Park Rapids, head north on US-71 for approximately 20 miles, then follow signs to Itasca State Park. Bear Paw Campground is located within the park.

address.full: 28299 N Shore Ln, Park Rapids, MN 56470

payload.name: Slumgullion Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens Memorial Day weekend and closes in late September, weather dependent. Sites are first-come-first-served with no advance reservations. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own supply.
payload.short_description: High-elevation USFS campground near Lake City with 21 first-come-first-served sites, vault toilets, and access to motorized trails, fishing streams, and wilderness areas.
payload.medium_description: Slumgullion Campground sits at over 11,300 feet elevation southeast of Lake City in the Gunnison National Forest. This lightly-used campground offers 21 first-come-first-served sites with vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables. No potable water is available. The location provides access to motorized trails, fishing streams, hiking and biking trails, wilderness areas, scenic drives, and four-wheel-drive roads. Lake City's historic museums and art galleries are a short drive away.
payload.long_description:
Slumgullion Campground is a quiet, high-elevation retreat in the Gunnison National Forest, located just off Colorado Highway 149 southeast of Lake City. At over 11,300 feet, the campground offers cool summer temperatures and access to the diverse recreation opportunities of the San Juan Mountains. The 21 sites are first-come-first-served with no reservations accepted.

The campground features vault toilets, fire rings with cooking grates, and picnic tables at each site. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on-site. Trash bags can be purchased for $2 each. The surrounding area offers motorized trails, fishing streams, hiking and biking trails, and access to nearby wilderness areas.

From the campground, visitors can easily explore scenic drives including the Silver Thread Scenic Byway and rugged four-wheel-drive roads. Lake San Cristobal, Colorado's second-largest natural lake formed by the famous Slumgullion Earthflow, is nearby. The historic mining town of Lake City offers museums, galleries, and services.

location.directions: Take Colorado State Highway 149 to Forest Road 788. Turn left onto Forest Road 788 and drive 0.25 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Hammock Day Use Area Pavilion At Cma Withlacoochee State Forest
payload.status_description: This is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping. The pavilion operates from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. seven days a week. Reservations are required through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica.
payload.short_description: A 30x40 foot day-use pavilion for group gatherings at the Croom Motorcycle Area in Withlacoochee State Forest. Day-use only; no overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Hammock Day Use Area Pavilion is a group day-use facility within the Croom Motorcycle Area of Withlacoochee State Forest. The 30x40 foot pavilion accommodates up to 60 people and includes picnic tables, grills, restrooms, water, and electric service. This is a day-use facility only and does not offer overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Hammock Day Use Area Pavilion is a reservable group facility located within the Croom Motorcycle Area (CMA) of Withlacoochee State Forest in Hernando County, Florida. The covered pavilion measures 30 by 40 feet and can accommodate groups of 1 to 60 people for day-use activities such as picnics, gatherings, and events.

The pavilion is equipped with eight 8-foot picnic tables, a double grill, and a single grill. Restrooms, potable water, and electric service are available on site. Parking is provided on a sand/gravel surface. The facility does not have lighting.

This is strictly a day-use facility operating from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. seven days a week. Overnight camping is not permitted. Reservations are required for all groups and pavilion use. Pets and alcohol are prohibited. A day-use fee of $2 per person applies to anyone age 6 and older without an Annual or Single Day Motor Permit.

location.directions: Located at 6420 LaRose Road, Brooksville, FL 34602, within the Croom Motorcycle Area of Withlacoochee State Forest.

links.title: Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica - Facility Details

payload.name: Island Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-April through November. Sites are first-come, first-served at $10 per night with payment collected on-site. No advance reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Primitive first-come, first-served campground in Monongahela National Forest adjacent to Long Run and the East Fork of the Greenbrier River, popular with anglers and hikers.
payload.medium_description: Island Campground is a primitive fishing and hiking campground in the Greenbrier Ranger District of Monongahela National Forest, located about 5 miles northeast of Bartow, West Virginia. The campground sits adjacent to Long Run and the East Fork of the Greenbrier River, making it a favorite among anglers. Nearby trails include the challenging 8-mile East Fork Trail and the shorter 1.8-mile Smoke Camp Trail.
payload.long_description:
Island Campground is a rustic, primitive campground in the Greenbrier Ranger District of Monongahela National Forest, situated approximately 5 miles northeast of Bartow, West Virginia. The campground's location adjacent to Long Run and the East Fork of the Greenbrier River makes it particularly appealing to fishermen seeking native trout waters.

Hikers have access to nearby trails including the East Fork Trail #365, an 8-mile route with challenging terrain, and the more accessible Smoke Camp Trail #324, a 1.8-mile day hike option. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations.

As a primitive site, the campground has no restrooms or potable water. Campers should come fully prepared with their own water supply and plan to pack out all waste.

location.directions: From Bartow, WV, take US Route 250S for approximately 3 miles. Take a left on Route 28. Campground is on the left after approximately 3 more miles.

payload.name: Seymour Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground opens in June and operates through September. No reservations required; all sites are first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 17 sites near the Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness in Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, offering vault toilets and fishing access along Seymour Creek.
payload.medium_description: Seymour Creek Campground is a rustic 17-site campground in the Wise River Ranger District of Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, situated at 6,700 feet elevation. The first-come, first-served campground features ADA-accessible vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings, with fishing access along the adjacent creek. No potable water or garbage service is available, and the maximum recommended trailer length is 18 feet.
payload.long_description:
Seymour Creek Campground sits at 6,700 feet in the Wise River Ranger District of Montana's Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, providing a base camp for exploring the nearby Anaconda-Pintler Wilderness. The 17-site campground offers a quiet, primitive camping experience along Seymour Creek with good fishing opportunities in the surrounding streams.

The campground provides basic amenities including two ADA-accessible vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings. Some sites have bear boxes for food storage. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Garbage services are not provided; pack out everything you pack in. Cell phone coverage is not available in the area.

Access is via Forest Service Road 934, which limits RV and trailer length to 18 feet maximum. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fee required. The setting offers solitude and access to backcountry trails, fishing, and wildlife viewing in the surrounding national forest.

location.directions: Travel 11 miles west from Wise River on Highway 43. Take State Highway 569 north for 4 miles, then Forest Service Road 934 northwest for 8 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Hatchechubbee Creek Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The group shelter with electric hookup is reservable through Recreation.gov starting at $35/night. Day-use access requires a pass. The location is unstaffed.
payload.short_description: Day-use park with reservable group shelter on Walter F. George Lake, offering flush toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, and boat ramp access.
payload.medium_description: Hatchechubbee Creek Park is a U.S. Army Corps of Engineers facility on the shores of Walter F. George Lake (Lake Eufaula) on the Alabama-Georgia border. The park features a reservable group shelter with electric hookup, flush toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, and a boat ramp. It primarily serves as a day-use area with group shelter reservations available through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Hatchechubbee Creek Park sits on the shores of Walter F. George Lake, also known as Lake Eufaula, which stretches 85 miles along the Chattahoochee River. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this unstaffed facility offers a group shelter with electric hookup that can be reserved for overnight stays or events.

The park provides basic amenities including flush toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, and a public boat ramp for lake access. The surrounding area features dense stands of mixed hardwood forests and abundant wildlife including waterfowl, deer, eagles, hawks, and bobcats.

Walter F. George Lake offers excellent fishing opportunities for largemouth bass, white bass, hybrids, crappie, channel catfish, and bream along its 640 miles of shoreline. The historic towns of Eufaula, Alabama and Cuthbert, Georgia are nearby, featuring antebellum mansions and sites on the National Register of Historic Places.

location.directions: From Eufaula, Alabama, follow US 431 north. Turn right on State Route 165 and continue for 12 miles, then follow signs into the day use area.

links.title: Walter F. George Lake Recreation.gov Gateway

payload.name: Scenic Cabin
payload.status_description: The cabin is open for the 2026 season, operating May 1 through October 31. Reservations are made through the Minnesota State Parks reservation system up to 120 days in advance.
payload.short_description: A 1930s CCC-built cabin near the lodge and beach on Coon-Sandwick Lake at Scenic State Park, surrounded by virgin pines in Minnesota's Northwoods.
payload.medium_description: This historic cabin at Scenic State Park was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s and sits near the lodge and swimming beach on Coon-Sandwick Lake. It sleeps up to four in a double-over-double bunk bed, with a kitchenette featuring a hot plate and mini-fridge, plus a fireplace with electrical insert. No private bathroom; guests use nearby campground facilities with flush toilets and hot showers.
payload.long_description:
Scenic Cabin is a piece of Depression-era history tucked into one of Minnesota's most pristine state parks. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, the cabin sits near the historic lodge on Coon-Sandwick Lake, surrounded by towering virgin white and red pines that give the park its name.

The cabin accommodates four guests in a single bedroom with a double-over-double bunk bed. Amenities include a small kitchenette with a hot plate and mini-refrigerator, plus a fireplace with an electrical insert for ambiance. There's no private bathroom, but flush toilets and hot showers are a short walk away in the campground. Outside, guests have access to a picnic area and fire pit.

Scenic State Park offers excellent paddling on its clear lakes, a sandy swimming beach, 14 miles of hiking trails, and rental boats available at the park office. In winter, the park grooms cross-country ski and snowmobile trails. The park lies just off the Edge of the Wilderness Scenic Byway near Bigfork.

location.directions: From Bigfork, take County Highway 7 (Scenic Highway 7) north approximately 7 miles to the park entrance at 56956 Scenic Highway 7, Bigfork, MN 56628.

payload.name: Big Cottonwood Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from April through October, weather permitting. All sites are first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit. No reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Free primitive BLM campground on the East Fork of the Jarbidge River, half a mile north of Murphy Hot Springs in remote southwest Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Big Cottonwood Campground is a free, first-come first-served BLM campground with 4 sites located on the East Fork of the Jarbidge River, approximately half a mile north of Murphy Hot Springs. The campground offers basic amenities including picnic tables, grills, and vault toilets, but no potable water. The remote location provides opportunities for fishing, wildlife viewing, and photography.
payload.long_description:
Big Cottonwood Campground is a small, primitive Bureau of Land Management campground situated along the East Fork of the Jarbidge River in remote Owyhee County, Idaho. Located about half a mile north of Murphy Hot Springs, this free campground offers 4 sites with basic amenities including picnic tables, grills, and vault toilets. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on site.

The campground sits at approximately 5,125 feet elevation and is accessible by two-wheel drive vehicles via the paved Jarbidge Road (Three Creek Highway) from Rogerson or via the Bruneau-Three Creek Road. The remote setting provides excellent opportunities for fishing in the Jarbidge River, wildlife viewing, and photography. No cell service is available in this area.

The campground operates seasonally from April through October, weather permitting. All sites are first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit. The maximum vehicle length is 30 feet, making it suitable for smaller RVs and trailers but not large rigs.

location.directions: Travel to Murphy Hot Springs via the Bruneau-Three Creek Road or the Jarbidge Road (Three Creek Highway). The Jarbidge Road has an asphalt surface and originates from U.S. 93 at Rogerson, Idaho. From Rogerson to Murphy Hot Springs is 49 miles. The campground is half a mile north of Murphy Hot Springs.

payload.name: Maud Williamson State Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Day-use only; no overnight camping is permitted. The park is open and the covered picnic shelter is available for group reservations. Within the Yamhill County permanent quarantine zone for ash tree materials; do not transport firewood from outside the immediate area.
payload.short_description: Day-use only park in Oregon's Willamette Valley with a reservable picnic shelter, restrooms, volleyball courts, and horseshoe pits beneath towering Douglas fir trees.
payload.medium_description: Maud Williamson State Recreation Site is a 24-acre day-use park in the Willamette Valley near Salem. The property features second-growth Douglas fir, hemlock, and cedar trees, with abundant trilliums blooming in early spring. A covered picnic shelter accommodating up to 25 people is available for group reservations. Facilities include restrooms, picnic tables, volleyball courts, and horseshoe pits. The historic Charles S. Williamson House (1890, Queen Anne style) remains on the property but is closed to visitors.
payload.long_description:
Maud Williamson State Recreation Site is a peaceful 24-acre day-use park set on the flat edge of cultivated Willamette Valley farmland. The property was bequeathed by educator Maud Williamson around 1933 to honor her mother, Ruby T. Williamson. The land features a canopy of second-growth Douglas fir, hemlock, and cedar trees, creating a serene retreat from the surrounding agricultural landscape.

The park offers a covered picnic shelter that can accommodate groups of up to 25 people and is available by reservation. Day-use amenities include restrooms, picnic tables, volleyball courts, and horseshoe pits. Admission is free, though shelter reservations require a fee. The historic Charles S. Williamson House, built in 1890 in Queen Anne architectural style, stands on the property but is not open to visitors.

Spring visitors are treated to abundant wildflower displays, particularly trilliums blooming throughout the forest floor. The park falls within Yamhill County's permanent quarantine zone for ash, olive, and white fringe tree materials, so visitors should not transport firewood from outside the immediate area.

location.directions: Maud Williamson State Recreation Site is located on the west side of the Salem-Dayton Highway (OR-221) at the junction with Hopewell Road in Yamhill County, Oregon. The park entrance is across from Wheatland Road, which leads to the Wheatland Ferry.

payload.name: Crags Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open late May through September, weather and conditions permitting. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov. Fire danger is currently low. Bears are active in the area; all food must be stored in bear-resistant containers.
payload.short_description: Group campground near Twin Lakes at 7,000 feet elevation in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, accommodating up to 45 people with views of Sawtooth Ridge.
payload.medium_description: Crags Group Campground is a group camping site near Twin Lakes in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, about 10 miles from Bridgeport, California. Situated at 7,000 feet elevation with views of the rugged Sawtooth Ridge, the site accommodates up to 45 people and features a campfire circle, picnic and serving tables, grills, food storage lockers, and ample parking. Flush toilets, potable water, and trash collection are provided.
payload.long_description:
Crags Group Campground is a reservable group camping site within Crags Campground, located near Twin Lakes in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. The site sits at approximately 7,000 feet elevation with striking views of the craggy peaks of Sawtooth Ridge, which tops out at over 10,500 feet. The group area can accommodate up to 45 people and includes a central campfire circle, multiple picnic and serving tables, grills, food storage lockers, and ample parking on paved surfaces.

The campground is about 10 miles from Bridgeport via Twin Lakes Road and offers easy access to Upper and Lower Twin Lakes. The lakes provide opportunities for boating, canoeing, and fishing for Kokanee salmon, rainbow trout, and brown trout. Hiking and horseback riding trails in the area lead toward the Hoover Wilderness and Yosemite backcountry.

Facilities include flush toilets and potable drinking water. Black bears frequent the area, so all food must be stored in the provided bear-resistant lockers. Dogs are permitted but must remain leashed. Nearby amenities in Bridgeport include restaurants, showers, and laundry facilities.

location.directions: From Highway 395 south in Bridgeport, turn left and travel approximately 11 miles on Twin Lakes Road. Turn left on South Twin Road and travel about 1/2 mile. Turn left at the Crags Campground sign.

payload.name: Jazz Creek Camp
payload.status_description: Campground status is currently unknown. Many Forest Service campgrounds in this region are inaccessible during winter due to snow.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground along Jazz Creek in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in north-central Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Jazz Creek Camp is a primitive campground located along Jazz Creek within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. The site sits at approximately 2,750 feet elevation in the forested mountains of north-central Idaho.
payload.long_description:
Jazz Creek Camp is a primitive campground situated along Jazz Creek in the remote backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. The site is located in Clearwater County, Idaho, within the vast 4-million-acre forest system that spans north-central Idaho.

This undeveloped campground offers a rustic camping experience in the mountainous terrain typical of the region. The surrounding Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests provide opportunities for fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing in one of the largest remaining wild areas in the lower 48 states.

location.directions: Jazz Creek Camp is located along County Road 250 in Idaho. From Pierce, Idaho, head northeast on Idaho 11, then turn onto County Road 250. The campground is situated at GPS coordinates 46.601758, -115.53044.

payload.name: Hocking Hills Old Mans Cave Shelter
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. Rock shelters at Hocking Hills book 6+ months in advance due to limited availability and high demand. Maximum stay is 7 days.
payload.short_description: Primitive rock shelter camping experience at iconic Old Man's Cave in Hocking Hills State Park, offering a unique overnight stay in a natural recess cave formation.
payload.medium_description: The Old Man's Cave Shelter provides a bucket-list camping experience in one of Ohio's most famous geological formations. This primitive rock shelter offers overnight accommodations in a natural recess cave carved by erosion, complete with a built-in fireplace for campfires. The shelter is located near the park's most popular hiking trails connecting Old Man's Cave, Cedar Falls, and Ash Cave. Pets are welcome and reservations book quickly due to extremely limited availability.
payload.long_description:
The Old Man's Cave Shelter at Hocking Hills State Park offers a rare opportunity to camp overnight in one of Ohio's most iconic natural formations. Named after hermit Richard Rowe who lived in the cave in the 19th century, Old Man's Cave is a dramatic recess cave carved from Blackhand sandstone by centuries of water erosion. The shelter provides primitive accommodations with a built-in fireplace but no electrical hookups or running water.

This unique camping experience places you at the heart of Hocking Hills' trail system. The six-mile Grandma Gatewood Trail begins here and connects to Cedar Falls and Ash Cave, making the shelter an ideal base for multi-day exploration. The gorge features dramatic waterfalls, towering hemlock trees, and stunning rock formations.

Due to the one-of-a-kind nature of this accommodation, reservations typically book 6+ months in advance through ReserveOhio. The shelter allows pets and enforces a 7-day maximum stay. Basic pit toilet facilities are available nearby, but campers should come prepared for primitive conditions with their own water supply.

location.directions: Located at Old Man's Cave in Hocking Hills State Park off State Route 664 in Hocking County. The park visitor center is at the Old Man's Cave parking lot.

links.title: Hocking Hills State Park - Ohio DNR

payload.name: Reyes Peak Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season from May through December. Four sites are reservable via Recreation.gov; two sites are first-come, first-served. No potable water available. Campfires are normally permitted in designated fire rings but may be prohibited during high fire danger periods.
payload.short_description: High-elevation campground at 7,000 feet in Los Padres National Forest with panoramic views of the Cuyama Badlands and Pacific Ocean. Six tent-only sites along a forested ridge above the Sespe Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Reyes Peak Campground sits at 7,000 feet elevation along a ridgeline in Los Padres National Forest, offering spectacular views of the Cuyama Badlands to the north and the Pacific Ocean and Channel Islands to the south. The campground has six tent-only sites amid Jeffrey pines, sugar pines, white fir, and ponderosa pines. Several trails depart from the campground, including the Reyes Peak Trail into the Sespe Wilderness and the short Raspberry Spring Trail through the pines.
payload.long_description:
Perched at 7,000 feet on the Pine Mountain ridge, Reyes Peak Campground provides a high-elevation escape with dual vistas: the rugged Cuyama Badlands to the north and the Pacific Ocean with Channel Islands visible to the south on clear days. The six tent-only campsites are scattered along the ridgeline beneath a canopy of Jeffrey pines, sugar pines, white fir, and ponderosa pines. Wildflowers including lupine, scarlet bugler, and false lupine bloom abundantly in spring and early summer.

The campground serves as a trailhead for several routes. The Reyes Peak Trail (23W04) leads 5.8 miles eastward into the Sespe Wilderness to connect with the Gene Marshall-Piedra Blanca National Recreation Trail. Chorro Grande Trail begins at the gate past the last campsite, while the half-mile Raspberry Spring Trail offers a gentle walk through the pines. Red-tailed hawks and California condors soar overhead, and deer, bear, and coyote inhabit the surrounding forest.

Facilities are basic: each site has a picnic table, fire ring, and barbecue grill, with one vault toilet near the first few sites. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Four sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while two remain first-come, first-served.

location.directions: Follow Highway 33 to the turnoff at Pine Mountain Summit (6N06) at mile marker 42.50. Turn right and follow the partially paved road for 5.7 miles to the campground. Total distance from Ojai is approximately 39 miles.

links.title: Los Padres NF - Reyes Peak Campground

payload.name: Millpond Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from March 1 through October 31. Reservations available online through the operator's website or by phone. RV and boat storage available year-round.
payload.short_description: Family-friendly campground with 72 RV and tent sites in the Eastern Sierra foothills, featuring electric and water hookups, hot showers, and access to a recreation area with a fishing pond.
payload.medium_description: Millpond Campground sits at the base of the Eastern Sierra, 6 miles north of Bishop along a cool-running creek. Operated by Brown's Campgrounds, it offers 72 sites with electric and water hookups, hot showers, flush toilets, and coin-op laundry. The adjacent Millpond Recreation Area provides a swimming and fishing pond, disc golf, archery, tennis courts, and playgrounds.
payload.long_description:
Millpond Campground occupies a scenic spot on the Owens Valley floor between the Eastern Sierra and the White Mountains. A small creek runs through the center of the campground, and sites are spread across grassy stretches beneath tree canopy. The 72 RV and tent sites offer electric and water hookups, with hot showers, flush toilets, handicapped-accessible facilities, and coin-op laundry on site.

The campground is adjacent to Inyo County's Millpond Recreation Area, which includes a pond for swimming and fishing (no motorized boats), disc golf, archery, softball fields, tennis courts, horseshoe pits, hiking and mountain bike trails, and a playground. A concession stand operates within the recreation area. RV and boat storage is available year-round even when camping is closed.

Operated by Brown's Campgrounds under contract with Inyo County, the campground accepts reservations online or by phone. The setting offers easy access to Bishop's services while providing a quieter alternative to campgrounds closer to town.

location.directions: From Highway 395, approximately 6 miles north of Bishop, turn south on Ed Powers Road, then west on Sawmill Road to the park entrance. The campground is at 230 Sawmill Road.

payload.name: Independence Lakes Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically opens in July and operates through October, depending on snow conditions. Access roads and trails in the area may retain snow at higher elevations through early summer.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at the trailhead to Independence Lakes in Sawtooth National Forest, with 5 sites, vault toilets, and accessible facilities. No water or trash services.
payload.medium_description: Independence Lakes Campground is a free, first-come, first-served campground in the Sawtooth National Forest near Burley, Idaho. The small campground serves as the trailhead for Independence Lakes Trail, a 3.1-mile hike to an alpine cirque basin with four lakes. The five sites have picnic tables and grills, with vault toilets available. No drinking water or trash service is provided. Sites are ADA accessible and livestock facilities are available for pack animals, though horses are prohibited within the campground itself.
payload.long_description:
Independence Lakes Campground is a rustic, no-fee campground located in the Minidoka Ranger District of the Sawtooth National Forest in southern Idaho. The campground provides access to Independence Lakes Trail, which climbs 3.1 miles through varied terrain to reach the first of four lakes nestled in an alpine cirque basin. The first mile of trail is rocky, but the remainder features a reasonable grade with switchbacks. Only non-motorized travel is permitted on the trail.

The campground offers five single campsites with picnic tables and grills, plus vault toilets. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Trash service is not provided, so pack out what you pack in. Sites are ADA accessible. Livestock facilities are available for those arriving with pack animals, though horses are prohibited within the campground area itself.

Fishing opportunities include trout in the alpine lakes, accessible by wade, shore, float tube, or non-motorized boat. The area supports fly, spin, and bait fishing. Camping is limited to 14 consecutive days within any 28-day period, with a maximum of 2 vehicles per site.

location.directions: From Oakley, Idaho, take Basin Road east into the mountains for approximately one hour. A high-clearance vehicle is recommended due to rough road conditions. The campground is located near the trailhead for Independence Lakes Trail #35.

payload.name: Evergreen Campground
payload.status_description: Open mid-May through mid-September, dependent on snow levels. Five of 12 sites are reservable through Recreation.gov; the remaining seven are first-come, first-served. Check-in is 2:00 PM, check-out is 11:00 AM. Pack-it-out trash policy. Be prepared to pay with cash or check.
payload.short_description: Scenic forest campground along the Weiser River in Payette National Forest, featuring 12 sites with vault toilets, drinking water, and access to the Weiser River Trail.
payload.medium_description: Evergreen Campground is nestled in a lush Douglas fir and spruce forest along the Weiser River, just off Highway 95 between Council and New Meadows. The 12 campsites include picnic tables, paved site pads, and grills. Fishing for rainbow trout and access to the Weiser River Trail for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding are highlights.
payload.long_description:
Evergreen Campground sits at approximately 4,000 feet elevation in a dense Douglas fir and spruce forest along the Weiser River in Payette National Forest. Despite its proximity to Highway 95, the large trees and dense vegetation provide seclusion and privacy. The river flows between the campsites and the highway, offering excellent rainbow trout fishing.

The campground has 12 sites with paved parking spurs, picnic tables, and grills. Vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump are provided. Five sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while the remaining seven are first-come, first-served. Access roads are gravel but well-maintained.

The popular Weiser River Trail is accessible directly from the campground for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. The campground is often used as a stopover between Council and New Meadows but offers enough amenities and recreation for a longer stay.

location.directions: From Council, Idaho, follow Highway 95 north approximately 14 miles to the campground on the east side of the highway. From New Meadows, travel 12 miles southwest on Highway 95. Access into the site is paved; internal roads are gravel with paved site pads.

payload.name: Potawatomi State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: The group campground is closed through June 2026 due to a major infrastructure construction project. All campsites in the park are unavailable in the reservation system from January 1 through June 2026. Visitors can use the "Notify Me" feature on the reservation website for availability updates when sites reopen.
payload.short_description: Group camping in Door County's Potawatomi State Park, with four sites accommodating up to 30 people each along the shore of Sturgeon Bay.
payload.medium_description: Potawatomi State Park Group Campground offers four group sites within the Daisy Field campground area, each accommodating up to 30 people. Two sites are designed for trailers and motor homes while the other two serve tent campers. The park features 1,200 acres of rolling terrain, limestone cliffs, and Sturgeon Bay shoreline in southern Door County.
payload.long_description:
Potawatomi State Park Group Campground is located within the Daisy Field campground complex in Door County, Wisconsin. The facility offers four group sites, each capable of hosting up to 30 people. Two of these sites accommodate trailers and motor homes, while the other two are designated for tent camping only. The group area provides access to showers and a sanitary dump station during the operating season.

The park spans 1,200 acres of gently rolling upland terrain bordered by steep slopes and rugged limestone cliffs along Sturgeon Bay. Named after the Potawatomi tribe, whose name means "keeper of the fire," the park offers extensive recreational opportunities including hiking trails that connect to the Ice Age National Scenic Trail.

Reservations are made through Wisconsin's state park reservation system. Group sites include picnic tables and fire rings. The park is open year-round from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m., though camping facilities operate seasonally.

location.directions: Located in southern Door County on the shore of Sturgeon Bay. GPS coordinates: 44.8518, -87.4250.

address.full: 3732 S Norway Rd, Sturgeon Bay, WI 54235

payload.name: Lonesomehurst Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates from mid-May through late September, weather dependent. Some sites are first-come-first-served while others are reservable via Recreation.gov. Bears frequent the area; all food must be stored in approved bear-resistant containers.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Hebgen Lake in Custer Gallatin National Forest, offering vault toilets, potable water, and boat ramp access just 20 minutes from West Yellowstone and Yellowstone National Park.
payload.medium_description: Lonesomehurst Campground sits on the shores of Hebgen Lake at 6,240 feet elevation, surrounded by lodgepole pines. The campground features 26 single-family sites, including four with electric hookups for RVs. A boat ramp provides direct lake access for fishing Montana's premier stillwater trout fishery. Located 20 minutes from West Yellowstone, it serves as a convenient base for exploring Yellowstone National Park.
payload.long_description:
Lonesomehurst Campground occupies a scenic stretch of the South Fork Arm of Hebgen Lake within the Custer Gallatin National Forest. The 21-square-mile lake, fed by the Madison River, supports healthy populations of brown, cutthroat, and rainbow trout, making it one of Montana's top stillwater fishing destinations. A boat ramp and dock within the campground provide direct access for anglers and boaters.

The campground offers 26 sites nestled among lodgepole pines, with four RV-compatible sites featuring electric hookups. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with vault toilets and potable water available throughout. Firewood can be purchased from the campground host. Wildlife viewing opportunities abound, with frequent sightings of bison, moose, deer, and various waterfowl including Sandhill cranes, ospreys, and bald eagles.

Bears are active in the area, and all food must be stored in approved bear-resistant containers. The surrounding landscape offers extensive hiking, biking, and OHV trails. West Yellowstone provides dining, shopping, and the Grizzly and Wolf Discovery Center, while Yellowstone National Park's west entrance is a short drive away.

location.directions: From West Yellowstone, travel west on Highway 20 for 8 miles, then continue 4 miles north on Denny Creek Road (Hebgen Lake Road).

address.full: 135 Lonesomehurst South Rd, West Yellowstone, MT 59758

payload.name: East Branch Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opens for the 2026 season on May 18. Operating season runs mid-May through mid-September. All reservations must be made through Recreation.gov. Overhead clearance is 13'4" for RVs.
payload.short_description: Army Corps campground on East Branch Lake in Elk County featuring electric sites, cabins, flush restrooms with showers, and excellent fishing for bass, walleye, musky, and trout.
payload.medium_description: East Branch Campground sits on East Branch Lake in northeastern Elk County, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The campground offers 31 sites including electric RV sites, tent-only sites, and four cabins. Amenities include flush restrooms with showers, a dump station, potable water, and trash service. The lake is known for exceptional water clarity and quality fishing for smallmouth and largemouth bass, lake trout, musky, walleye, and panfish. The outflow area below the dam is managed as a delayed harvest trout fishing area and is popular with kayakers and canoers.
payload.long_description:
East Branch Campground is located at East Branch Lake in northeastern Elk County, Pennsylvania, managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Pittsburgh District. The campground features 31 sites: 23 RV sites (21 with 30-amp electric hookups, 2 non-electric), 4 electric cabins with bedding provided, and 3 tent-only sites. All campsites and cabins include fire rings, picnic tables, and lantern hangers. The single camping loop has a restroom facility with flush toilets and showers.

East Branch Lake is renowned for its exceptional water clarity, with visibility up to 12 feet. The fishery supports smallmouth and largemouth bass, lake trout, musky, walleye, and various panfish. The outflow area below the dam maintains year-round cool to cold water temperatures and is managed as a delayed harvest trout fishing area, making it a popular destination for anglers as well as kayakers and canoers.

Nearby attractions include Elk State Park, Bendigo State Park, and the Allegheny National Forest. The cities of St. Marys and Kane offer restaurants, microbreweries, wineries, and shopping. An overlook and picnic area located across from the campground provides a tranquil spot to enjoy lake views.

location.directions: From I-80 Southeast: Take exit 111, travel PA 153 North to Penfield for 8 miles. Take PA 255 North to St. Marys for 19 miles. Continue on PA 255 North, make a sharp left onto South Michael Street. Turn right onto N St. Marys Street for 2.5 miles. Turn left onto Windfall Road for 1 mile. Take a slight left onto Flower Valley Road/Glenn Hazel Road for 8 miles. Turn right onto East Branch Dam Road for approximately 1 mile. From I-80 Southwest: Take exit 97, travel US 219 North for 44 miles to Johnsonburg. Continue onto East Center Street for 0.5 miles. Turn right onto Cobb Street, continue onto Bendigo Rd for 5 miles. Turn left onto Flower Valley/Glen Hazel Rd (SR 1001) for 1.7 miles. Turn right onto East Branch Dam Road for 0.8 miles; campground is on your left. From points north: Take US 219 South to Wilcox. Turn left onto Flower Valley Rd/Glen Hazel Rd at the flashing signal in Wilcox, continue for 6 miles. Turn left onto East Branch Dam Road for 0.8 miles; campground is on your left.

address.full: 753 E Branch Dam Rd, Wilcox, PA 15870

links.title: East Branch Clarion River Lake Gateway
