payload.name: Fontainebleau State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gates open at 7 a.m. and close at 9 p.m. daily. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, and holidays. Reservations available online at gooutdoorslouisiana.com or by calling 1-833-609-0686.
payload.short_description: Located on the banks of the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, Fontainebleau State Park offers a unique experience and with an amazing view of the sunset.
payload.medium_description: Fontainebleau State Park offers 96 full-hookup campsites and 37 primitive sites on the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain. The campground features modern bathhouses with hot showers, dump station, free laundry facilities, and WiFi. Sites include grills and picnic tables. The park provides access to swimming beaches, hiking trails including a 4.8-mile trail, an all-inclusive playground, and water activities.
payload.long_description: Located on the banks of the north shore of Lake Pontchartrain, Fontainebleau State Park offers a unique experience and with an amazing view of the sunset. Located just a short drive from both New Orleans and Baton Rouge, Fontainebleau offers a variety of amenities such as a sandy beach, splash pad, marsh board walk, and ample parking. Additionally, the beach is a short distance away from our nature trails, which spotlight Louisiana’s untamed beauty and feature numerous magnificent oak trees. Fontainebleau offers a remarkable outdoor experience, whether it be a day on the lake or an overnight stay in a cabin, there is something for everyone. Fontainebleau State Park is the perfect place to spend time with family and friends surrounded by Louisiana’s natural beauty. You may now reserve a boat slip at nearby JSBB Marina during your stay by navigating to www.jsbbmarina.net!

location.directions: From I-12, take Exit 59 (Louisiana Highway 59) south toward Mandeville. Continue approximately 3 miles to US Highway 190. Turn east on US 190 and travel about 3 miles to Louisiana Highway 1089. Turn left onto Highway 1089 and continue to the park entrance at 62883 Hwy. 1089, Mandeville, LA 70448.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Salmon La Sac
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens around late May for camping. Approximately 40 sites are reservable through Recreation.gov; the remaining sites are first-come-first-served. The campground operates through mid-September.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground in Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest with 69 sites for tents and RVs, offering hiking access to Waptus River Trail and the Pacific Crest Trail at 2,400 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Salmon La Sac Campground sits between the Cle Elum and Cooper Rivers in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest at 2,400 feet elevation. The campground offers 69 sites for tent and RV camping, with vault toilets, potable water from hand pumps, picnic tables, and fire rings at each site. Popular activities include hiking the nearby Waptus River Trail, fishing for rainbow and cutthroat trout, swimming, and mountain biking.
payload.long_description:
Salmon La Sac Campground is a popular destination in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, situated at 2,400 feet elevation where the Cle Elum and Cooper Rivers meet. The campground has 69 sites accommodating both tents and RVs, with approximately 40 sites reservable through Recreation.gov and the remainder available first-come-first-served. Sites feature paved driveways, picnic tables, and campfire rings with grills. Some pull-through sites can accommodate vehicles up to 44 feet.

The area is a prime location for outdoor recreation. The Waptus River Trail begins within walking distance of the campground, offering a 3-mile hike to Hour Creek or a longer 9-mile trek to Waptus Lake with views of Summit Chief Mountain. The Pacific Crest Trail is also accessible nearby. Anglers will find rainbow trout, cutthroat trout, and kokanee salmon in the rivers. Swimming, horseback riding, and mountain biking are popular summer activities.

The campground operates from late May through mid-September, with exact dates depending on snow conditions. Facilities include vault toilets, potable water from hand pumps, and trash collection. There are no hookups, showers, or dump stations. Bears are active in the area, so proper food storage is required. Pets are permitted but must be kept leashed at all times.

location.directions: From Seattle, take I-90 east for approximately 80 miles. Take exit 80 toward Salmon La Sac and turn left on Bullfrog Road. Continue to the second traffic circle and take the second exit onto WA-903 north. Continue onto Salmon La Sac Road for approximately 19 miles. The campground is on the left, just past Cayuse Campground. Address: 30160 Salmon La Sac Road, Ronald, WA 98940.

address.full: 20   20 Cle Elum River Cabins Rd, Ronald, WA 98940

payload.name: Whitewater Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season mid-May through mid-October. Reservations required. Wisconsin vehicle admission sticker required.
payload.short_description: Primitive 63-site campground on Whitewater Lake in Kettle Moraine State Forest Southern Unit, featuring vault toilets, dump station, and beach access with Ice Age Trail connections.
payload.medium_description: Whitewater Lake Campground offers 63 primitive campsites in a scenic setting within Kettle Moraine State Forest's Southern Unit. The campground features vault toilets, a sanitary dump station, and recycling/garbage facilities. Fire rings and picnic tables are provided at sites. Reservations are required, and a Wisconsin vehicle admission sticker is needed. Beach access and boat launches are nearby at Whitewater Lake and Rice Lake.
payload.long_description:
Whitewater Lake Campground is a primitive facility nestled within the Southern Unit of Kettle Moraine State Forest in Walworth County, Wisconsin. The campground features 63 campsites suitable for tent and trailer camping, set among the glacially sculpted terrain that defines the Kettle Moraine region. The Whitewater Lake segment of the Ice Age National Scenic Trail runs through this area, offering excellent hiking opportunities.

Amenities include vault toilets, a sanitary dump station, and recycling/garbage collection. Fire rings and picnic tables are standard at campsites. There are no showers on-site; the nearest shower facilities are approximately 20 miles north at Pinewoods, Ottawa Lake, or Horserider's campgrounds. Accessible campsites are available with paved paths to restrooms and the beach, plus electrical hookups.

Whitewater Lake beach and boat launch are a short drive from the campground, as is Rice Lake with its playground and boat launch. A Wisconsin state park vehicle admission sticker is required for all vehicles in addition to camping fees. Reservations are required and can be made online at wisconsin.goingtocamp.com or by calling 1-888-947-2757.

location.directions: Located off Kettle Moraine Drive near Whitewater, Wisconsin. Address: W7908 Kettle Moraine Dr, Whitewater, WI 53119.

links.title: Wisconsin DNR Kettle Moraine Southern Unit Camping
Wisconsin DNR Kettle Moraine Southern Unit

payload.name: Fort Churchill State Historic Park Group Use Areas
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. Group use area requires advance reservation through Reserve Nevada. No RVs permitted in the group area.
payload.short_description: Group camping and day-use area at Fort Churchill State Historic Park with covered pavilion, vault toilets, fire ring, and charcoal grill. Accommodates up to 60 people by reservation only.
payload.medium_description: Fort Churchill State Historic Park Group Use Areas offer a designated space for groups of up to 60 people, available for day use or overnight camping. The area includes a covered pavilion with picnic tables, a sink and food preparation countertop, a large charcoal grill, a fire ring with amphitheater-style seating, garbage service, and two vault toilets. No electricity or water is available, and RVs are not permitted. Reservations are required through Reserve Nevada.
payload.long_description:
Fort Churchill State Historic Park Group Use Areas provide a reservation-only facility for groups of up to 60 people within this historic Nevada state park along the Carson River. The site features a covered pavilion equipped with picnic tables, a sink with food preparation countertop, and a large charcoal grill. An amphitheater-style fire ring offers a gathering space for evening programs or campfires. Two vault toilets serve the area, and garbage cans are provided.

The group area is primitive with no electricity or potable water available, so campers must bring their own water supply. RVs and trailers are not permitted in the group use area. The park itself preserves the adobe ruins of a Civil War-era military outpost established in 1860 to protect settlers and Pony Express riders. Trails connect the campground to the historic fort ruins and the Carson River.

Reservations must be made in advance through Reserve Nevada (reservenevada.com). The group use reservation fee is $25, with additional entrance fees ($5 Nevada residents, $10 non-residents) and camping fees ($15-$20) per vehicle for overnight stays.

location.directions: Located 8 miles south of the Highway 95A/Highway 50 intersection on Highway 95A at 10000 Highway 95A, Silver Springs, NV 89429.

links.title: Nevada State Parks Group Use Fees

payload.name: Clyde Holliday State Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations available up to six months in advance. Water hookups at campsites are turned off from late October through March due to freezing temperatures, though water remains available at the dump station. A $10 per-use dump station fee is in effect as of March 30, 2026.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground along the John Day River offering 31 electrical sites with water, flush toilets, hot showers, and easy access to Strawberry Mountain Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Clyde Holliday State Recreation Site is a shaded riverside campground along the John Day River near John Day, Oregon. The park offers 31 electrical sites with water hookups, one pull-through site, and a hiker/biker camp. Amenities include hot showers, flush toilets, an RV dump station, firewood and ice sales, horseshoe pits, and an outdoor amphitheater with summer interpretive programs. A nature trail leads to a wildlife viewing pond. The campground serves as a base camp for exploring Strawberry Mountain Wilderness and nearby historical sites including the Kam Wah Chung State Heritage Site.
payload.long_description:
Clyde Holliday State Recreation Site sits along the sparkling John Day River, providing a shaded oasis in the high desert of eastern Oregon. The campground features 31 electrical sites with water hookups, including one pull-through site, plus a primitive hiker/biker camp. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. Modern amenities include hot showers and flush toilets available year-round, an RV dump station, and firewood and ice available for purchase.

The park offers a nature trail leading to a wildlife viewing pond, horseshoe pits, and an outdoor amphitheater hosting interpretive programs during summer months. Mosquitoes can be particularly active from May through July. From late October through March, water hookups at individual campsites are turned off due to weather, though water remains available at the dump station.

The campground serves as an excellent base camp for exploring the Strawberry Mountain Wilderness and the region's historical attractions. Nearby, the Kam Wah Chung State Heritage Site preserves an 1866-67 trading post and Chinese herbal apothecary with a fascinating collection of artifacts from Oregon's gold mining era.

location.directions: Located 7 miles west of John Day on U.S. Highway 26 in Grant County, Oregon.

payload.name: Cottonwood Campground - Slrd
payload.status_description: Closed for the early season. Opens around May 9 for first-come, first-served camping. No potable water available. Seasonal vault toilets. 7-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground in South Willow Canyon at 6,080 feet in the Stansbury Range, with vault toilets and access to the Deseret Peak Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Cottonwood Campground sits in the remote South Willow Canyon of the Stansbury Range at 6,080 feet elevation. This primitive campground offers just three sites along Willow Creek, serving as a basecamp for the Stansbury Front Trail and Medina Flat Trail into the Deseret Peak Wilderness. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Cottonwood Campground is a small, primitive campground located 0.7 miles up South Willow Canyon from the forest boundary in the Stansbury Range. At 6,080 feet elevation, the canyon is forested with oak, maple, and juniper trees providing partial shade. Willow Creek flows through the site, offering rainbow and brown trout fishing opportunities.

The campground serves as a gateway to the Deseret Peak Wilderness. The multi-use Stansbury Front Trail and Medina Flat Trail begin across the road from the entrance, providing access to the rugged backcountry. The campground has a 7-day stay limit and operates on a pack-it-in, pack-it-out basis. Campers must bring their own water as no potable water is available on site.

location.directions: From Grantsville, head south on Mormon Trail Road. Turn right onto South Willow Road/South Willow Canyon. The campground is located 0.7 miles up South Willow Canyon from the forest boundary on a gravel road.

payload.name: Spring Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the winter season. The campground typically opens mid-May and operates through late October. The water system was out of order as of September 2025; campers should bring their own water until repairs are confirmed.
payload.short_description: Creekside campground in the Hitt Mountains of western Idaho's Payette National Forest, offering fishing, hiking, and shade beneath tall ponderosa pines at 4,750 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Spring Creek Campground sits along peaceful Spring Creek in the Hitt Mountains of western Idaho. The 12-site campground provides vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, picnic tables, and fire rings beneath tall ponderosa pine and fir trees at 4,750 feet elevation. Five sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while seven are first-come, first-served. Nearby attractions include the Sturgill Peak Trail to a historic 1934 fire lookout and Mann Creek Reservoir for boating and fishing.
payload.long_description:
Spring Creek Campground is a peaceful Forest Service campground located along Spring Creek in the Hitt Mountains of the Payette National Forest. At 4,750 feet elevation, tall ponderosa pine and fir trees provide welcome shade during hot summer days. The campground offers 12 single-family sites and one group picnic area that accommodates up to 100 guests.

Five campsites are reservable through Recreation.gov while seven operate on a first-come, first-served basis. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground has accessible vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump during the operating season. This is a pack-it-in, pack-it-out facility, so bring garbage bags.

Several miles of hiking, biking, and OHV trails crisscross the surrounding area. The Sturgill Peak Trail climbs to a 7,289-foot summit with an active fire lookout built in 1934, offering views of the Hitt Range and Wallowa Mountains. Mann Creek Reservoir is about 15 miles away for boating and fishing.

location.directions: From Weiser, Idaho, travel north on Highway 95 for approximately 12 miles, then turn onto Upper Mann Creek Road/Forest Road 009 and travel another 15-18 miles to the campground. Forest Road 009 is an improved gravel road suitable for passenger cars.

links.title: USFS Payette NF - Spring Creek Campground

photos.name: Campsites 3 and 5 in Spring Creek Campground.
Campsite 4 in Spring Creek Campground surrounded by Ponderosa Pine trees.
Sleeping Springs interpretive trail begins in the Spring Creek Campground.

payload.name: H.R. Bluegill Loop
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Hardin Ridge opened April 4, 2026 and operates through mid-to-late October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Bluegill Loop is a family-friendly campground loop within Hardin Ridge Recreation Area on Monroe Lake, featuring electric sites, a small fishing pond, playground, and modern shower facilities.
payload.medium_description: Bluegill Loop is one of six campground loops at Hardin Ridge Recreation Area in Hoosier National Forest, situated on the shores of Monroe Lake. This loop offers approximately 34 sites with most featuring electric hookups, plus a small fishing pond perfect for families and a playground. Modern amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, and centralized water. Generators are not permitted in this loop.
payload.long_description:
Bluegill Loop is part of the 1,200-acre Hardin Ridge Recreation Area on Monroe Reservoir in southern Indiana's Hoosier National Forest. This campground loop provides a family-oriented camping experience with a small on-site fishing pond stocked with panfish and a playground. Most sites include electric hookups, and all have a picnic table, fire ring with grill, lantern hook, and designated tent space on paved, level parking spurs.

The greater Hardin Ridge complex offers extensive recreation including a three-lane boat launch, 300-foot swimming beach, over 12 miles of hiking trails, and two lakeside rental cabins. Modern comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers serve the campground, along with centralized potable water spigots and an RV dump station. Pets are welcome on leash throughout the campground.

Reservations are available through Recreation.gov and are recommended for peak summer weekends. The campground operates seasonally from early April through mid-to-late October. Note that generators are prohibited in Bluegill Loop; campers requiring generator use should reserve sites in the adjacent Eads Loop.

location.directions: From Bloomington, Indiana, head south on State Road 446. Continue approximately 14 miles to Hardin Ridge Road. Turn right and follow signs to Hardin Ridge Recreation Area. Bluegill Loop is located within the campground complex at 6464 Hardin Ridge Road, Heltonville, IN 47436.

payload.name: Williams River Rua Sites D4
payload.status_description: Open mid-March through end of November. Free, first-come first-served with no reservations. Vault toilets close during winter months. Maximum stay is 14 days.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive dispersed campsite along Williams River Road in Monongahela National Forest, popular with anglers seeking riverside camping in West Virginia's highlands.
payload.medium_description: Williams River RUA Sites D4 is one of 30 designated dispersed campsites scattered along Williams River Road (Forest Roads 86 and 216) in Monongahela National Forest. These rustic sites offer primitive camping near the river, making them especially popular with anglers. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post, with vault toilets spaced along the corridor.
payload.long_description:
Williams River RUA Sites D4 is part of a unique dispersed camping system within Monongahela National Forest, where 30 individually numbered primitive campsites are distributed along the scenic Williams River corridor. The sites stretch from the Three Forks area upstream toward the river's headwaters, with many positioned close to the water's edge.

This is free, first-come first-served camping with no reservations accepted. Each site provides basic amenities including a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. Vault toilets are strategically placed along the road near sites 5, 8, 11, and 20, with self-service bulletin boards. There is no potable water available, so campers must bring their own supply.

The Williams River is renowned for its trout fishing, making these campsites particularly popular with anglers. The surrounding area offers access to day hiking, backpacking, and the Tea Creek Wildlife Management Area. Site regulations limit occupancy to one motorhome or travel trailer, no more than two vehicles, and a maximum of eight people per site.

location.directions: From Cowen, WV, follow State Route 46 to Forest Road 86 (Williams River Road). The first campsites begin approximately 10 miles upstream from Cowen.

links.title: Williams River Sites - USFS Monongahela NF

payload.name: Tom Merrill Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservation only through Recreation.gov; no fee booth on site. Check-in 3:00 PM, check-out 1:00 PM. Quiet hours 10 PM to 6 AM.
payload.short_description: Year-round Class A campground downstream of Bayou Bodcau Dam with full hookups, flush toilets, showers, and access to creek fishing and wildlife management areas.
payload.medium_description: Tom Merrill Recreation Area is a quiet 20-site campground along Bodcau Creek in northwest Louisiana, operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. All sites feature electric (20/30/50 amp) and water hookups, picnic tables, fire pits, and grills. The campground offers a showerhouse with flush toilets, dump station, playground, disc golf course, and game cleaning station. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Tom Merrill Recreation Area sits downstream of Bayou Bodcau Dam along Bodcau Creek near Haughton, Louisiana. This Class A campground provides 20 sites, including 19 standard electric sites and one group shelter. Each site includes electric hookups (20/30/50 amp), water hookups, a picnic table, fire pit, grill, and lantern hanger. Sites are positioned within walking distance of the water, with a mix of shaded forest and open locations.

The campground features a showerhouse with flush toilets, a dump station, playground, outdoor exercise equipment, disc golf course, bike trails, and a game cleaning station. Bayou Bodcau is a 33,500-acre wildlife management area popular during hunting season for deer and other game. The area includes moss-laden cypress swamps, mixed deciduous and pine forests, and Ivan Lake for fishing and boating.

Downtown Bossier City and Shreveport are 30-45 minutes away. The campground enforces quiet hours from 10 PM to 6 AM and allows one RV plus up to three tents per site. Maximum stay is 14 days per 30-day period.

location.directions: From Interstate 20, take exit 33 and head north on State Route 157. Drive 9 miles and turn right on Bodcau Dam Road. Drive 3 miles and destination will be on the left.

payload.name: Nooya Lake Shelter Site Lookout/cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come-first-served basis. No fee or advance reservation required. Visitors must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free backcountry 3-sided shelter on the edge of Nooya Lake within Misty Fjords National Monument Wilderness, accessible only by floatplane or boat.
payload.medium_description: The Nooya Lake Shelter is a rustic 3-sided Adirondack-style structure situated on the shore of Nooya Lake in the heart of Misty Fjords National Monument Wilderness. This free, first-come-first-served shelter offers stunning wilderness views and excellent opportunities for wildlife observation. Access is exclusively by floatplane or boat via Rudyerd Bay off Behm Canal.
payload.long_description:
The Nooya Lake Shelter is a rustic 3-sided Adirondack-style structure located on the edge of Nooya Lake within the spectacular Misty Fjords National Monument Wilderness in southeast Alaska's Tongass National Forest. The shelter sits in the north arm of Rudyerd Bay, which opens off the east shore of Behm Canal, offering visitors dramatic views of the surrounding wilderness landscape.

This primitive shelter is available year-round on a first-come-first-served basis at no charge. Facilities include two pit toilets, but visitors must bring all their own drinking water as no potable water is available on site. The area requires Leave No Trace practices including packing out all trash, leftover food, and toilet paper.

The location is notable for being in the flightseeing path of floatplanes serving Misty Fjords, resulting in heavy daytime air traffic from May through August. Visitors should be prepared for remote wilderness conditions and extreme weather, as the shelter can only be accessed by floatplane or boat.

location.directions: Located in the north arm of Rudyerd Bay, which opens off the east shore of Behm Canal in Misty Fjords National Monument. Access is by floatplane or boat only. Coordinates: 55.62448°N, 130.72309°W.

payload.name: Lake Bruin State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park gates open 6am to 10pm daily. Entrance station hours are 8am to 5pm Sunday through Thursday, and 8am to 8pm Friday, Saturday, and holidays.
payload.short_description: There are over 3,000 acres of water surface on Lake Bruin, and the visitors to Lake Bruin State Park have access to every acre for incomparable freshwater fishing, superb water sports and fine outdoor living.
payload.medium_description: Lake Bruin State Park sits on a 3,000-acre oxbow lake in Tensas Parish, offering 48 improved campsites with water and electric hookups, fire rings, and picnic tables. The park features three fishing piers, a boat launch, water playground, and accessible bathhouses with showers. Premium sites include pull-through options accommodating large RVs up to 84 feet.
payload.long_description: There are over 3,000 acres of water surface on Lake Bruin, and the visitors to Lake Bruin State Park have access to every acre for incomparable freshwater fishing, superb water sports and fine outdoor living. The 53-acre site was originally established in 1928 as a fish hatchery. Three large fishing piers, a year-round boat launch, and a boat shed for docking make things convenient for the casual or serious fisherman. Rental boats are available. Largemouth bass fishing is popular all year round, but the best months are April, May, June, September and October. Crappie (white perch) are taken around the piers and mats in the early spring. Bluegill fishing is best in the shallower waters at both ends of the lake. Water sports and pleasure boating are also popular activities at Lake Bruin. A water playground offers a great way to cool off during warm spring and summer months, with a bathhouse located nearby. Lake Bruin's day use area offers picnic tables and barbeque grills situated near the lake and adjacent to two of the fishing piers, restrooms and playground areas. A covered pavilion allows park visitors to enjoy their meals whatever the weather. Most facilities are wheelchair accessible.

location.directions: From St. Joseph, Louisiana, take Highway 605 south to State Park Road. The park is located at 201 State Park Road, St. Joseph, LA 71366.

address.full: 243 State Park Rd, Saint Joseph, LA 71366

links.title: Lake Bruin State Park Official Page

payload.name: Colorado Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically opens Memorial Day weekend (late May) through Labor Day. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; some sites are first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Family-friendly campground at 7,800 feet in Pike National Forest near Manitou Lake, offering 80 sites with vault toilets, potable water, and access to fishing, hiking, and the Centennial Bike Trail.
payload.medium_description: Colorado Campground is a popular family destination in the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains, situated at 7,800 feet in a ponderosa pine forest near the 5-acre Manitou Lake. The campground features 80 non-electric sites with picnic tables, fire grates, vault toilets, and potable water. A short trail leads to Manitou Lake for trout fishing and canoeing, while the paved Centennial Bike Trail connects to South Meadows Campground and the Manitou Lake Picnic Area.
payload.long_description:
Colorado Campground sits at 7,800 feet elevation in a ponderosa pine forest within Pike National Forest, approximately 6 miles north of Woodland Park and 25 miles northwest of Colorado Springs. The campground's 80 sites accommodate tents and RVs up to 30 feet, with paved roads and gravel parking spurs. Each site includes a picnic table and fire grate, and the campground provides vault toilets, potable water, and trash collection. An amphitheater hosts campfire programs on weekend evenings.

The nearby 5-acre Manitou Lake offers excellent trout fishing and canoeing opportunities, accessible via a short trail from the campground. The paved, accessible Centennial Bike Trail connects Colorado Campground to the Manitou Lake Picnic Area and South Meadows Campground, popular with hikers, cyclists, and rollerbladers. OHV enthusiasts can access the Rainbow Falls and North Divide trail systems nearby.

The town of Woodland Park provides gas, groceries, dining, and shopping just 6 miles south. Colorado Springs offers additional services and attractions including Garden of the Gods, while Pikes Peak can be reached via highway from Manitou Springs about 20 miles away.

location.directions: From Colorado Springs, travel west on Highway 24 for approximately 18 miles to Woodland Park. Turn north on Highway 67 and travel about 7 miles to Colorado Campground on the right side of the road.

payload.name: MARIAN
payload.status_description: Seasonally open May through December. Currently listed as closed due to seasonal closure. Access is via steep, narrow dirt road requiring high-clearance vehicle.
payload.short_description: A free primitive campground at 6,590 feet in Los Padres National Forest, shaded by Jeffrey pines and oaks, serving as a trailhead for McPhearson Peak and Aliso trails.
payload.medium_description: Marian Campground sits along a ridgeline in the Mt. Pinos area of Los Padres National Forest at 6,590 feet elevation. This primitive, no-fee campground is shaded by Jeffrey pines and oak trees and serves as a popular fall hunting camp. The McPhearson Peak Trail and Aliso Trail begin here, providing access to the San Rafael Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Marian Campground occupies a scenic ridgeline position at 6,590 feet elevation in the Mt. Pinos Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. The campground is shaded by a mix of Jeffrey pines and oak trees, offering a cool retreat during warmer months. It serves as a trailhead for the McPhearson Peak Trail and the Aliso Park Trail (27W02), which extends 4.76 miles into the San Rafael Wilderness in Santa Barbara County.

This is a primitive, free campground with no reservations required. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table, but there are no restrooms or potable water, so campers must be fully self-sufficient. The campground is particularly popular with hunters during fall season. A 14-day stay limit applies.

Access requires navigating Forest Service road 9N27, a steep and narrow dirt road where high-clearance vehicles are strongly recommended. The campground is not suitable for RVs or trailers due to road conditions.

location.directions: Located off Mil Potrero Highway, approximately three miles west of Pine Mountain Club. Take Forest Service road 9N27 north for 1.5 miles. Steep, narrow dirt road; high-clearance vehicle recommended.

payload.name: Meadow Ridge
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 20, 2026 on a first-come, first-served basis. The campground operates mid-May through mid-September, weather dependent. Reservations available via Recreation.gov; walk-up sites also available.
payload.short_description: Scenic 19-site campground on a ridge above Rampart Reservoir in Pike National Forest, offering excellent trout fishing, mountain biking, and hiking at 9,200 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Meadow Ridge Campground sits at 9,200 feet in the Front Range of the Rocky Mountains, overlooking Rampart Reservoir about 10 miles from Woodland Park, Colorado. The 19-site campground is surrounded by ponderosa pine, spruce, Douglas fir, and aspen, with grass meadows throughout. Rainbow and mackinaw trout fishing in the reservoir draws anglers, while the 14-mile Rampart Reservoir Trail offers hiking and mountain biking.
payload.long_description:
Located on a ridge above Rampart Reservoir in Pike National Forest, Meadow Ridge Campground provides a scenic mountain camping experience at 9,200 feet elevation. The campground is about 10 miles from Woodland Park and sits due north of Pikes Peak, America's easternmost 14,000-foot peak. The surrounding terrain features ponderosa pine forest mixed with spruce, Douglas fir, aspen, and open grass meadows.

The 19 campsites include parking spurs at least 30 feet long, picnic tables, and fire grates. Two vault toilets and potable water are available, along with trash collection and firewood sales. Sites 12 and 13 are developed for wheelchair accessibility, while most other sites have steps to the table and fire ring areas. This is a standard non-electric campground with no hookups, showers, or dump station.

Rampart Reservoir is renowned for rainbow and mackinaw trout fishing. The Rampart Reservoir Trail extends 14 miles around the lake and is open to mountain biking. Nearby attractions include the U.S. Air Force Academy and the town of Green Mountain Falls.

location.directions: From Colorado Springs, travel west on Highway 24 for about 18 miles to Woodland Park. Turn north on Baldwin Street (which becomes Rampart Range Road). Go about 2 miles to Loy Creek Road, turn right, then turn right on Forest Road 300 (Rampart Range Road). Follow signs. Rampart Reservoir entrance is about 4 miles further on the left.

payload.name: Monument Park
payload.status_description: Status uncertain. Forest Road 226 was closed in 2023 due to severe damage from the 2022 Black Fire and monsoon flooding. Road repairs were underway but current access to the cabin is unconfirmed. The cabin is not currently listed on Recreation.gov. Restroom facilities are closed. Contact Black Range Ranger District at 575-894-6677 for current conditions.
payload.short_description: Historic Forest Service cabin in the Black Range of Gila National Forest, accessed via Forest Road 226 near Chloride, New Mexico.
payload.medium_description: Monument Park Cabin is a historic USFS cabin situated in the remote Black Range area of Gila National Forest in Sierra County. The cabin lies along Forest Road 226 (Chloride Canyon Road), which provides access to the Aldo Leopold Wilderness and Continental Divide Trail corridor.
payload.long_description:
Monument Park Cabin is a historic rental cabin managed by the Gila National Forest's Black Range Ranger District. Located at Monument Park along Forest Road 226, the cabin sits in a remote and rugged section of the Black Range, which forms the eastern boundary of the Gila National Forest in Sierra County, New Mexico.

The cabin provides a base for exploring the surrounding Aldo Leopold Wilderness and accessing the Continental Divide Trail. The Black Range features elevations ranging from 4,200 feet to over 10,000 feet along the Continental Divide, with dramatic terrain shaped by volcanic activity and erosion.

Note: This is a single historic cabin, not a multi-site campground. Forest Road 226 (Chloride Canyon Road) sustained major damage from the 2022 Black Fire and subsequent monsoon flooding, with deep washouts at creek crossings. Check with the Black Range Ranger District for current road and cabin availability before planning a visit.

location.directions: From Chloride, NM, travel west on Forest Road 226 (Chloride Canyon Road) approximately 10 miles to Monument Park. The road follows Chloride Creek with numerous creek crossings. High-clearance vehicle recommended. Verify road conditions before travel as this route was severely damaged by flooding.

links.title: Gila NF Black Range Ranger District

payload.name: Lake Bistineau State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gates open daily at 8 a.m. and close at 10 p.m. Entrance station hours are Sunday through Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Friday through Saturday and holiday eves 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Reservations can be made through ReserveLaStateParks.com or by calling 1-833-609-0686, with bookings available 48 hours to 13 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Situated on the western shore of Lake Bistineau, this park offers a satisfying blend of beautiful vistas and outstanding recreational facilities.
payload.medium_description: Lake Bistineau State Park offers 61 improved campsites with water and electric hookups on the western shore of Lake Bistineau, about 40 minutes southeast of Shreveport. The park features restrooms, showers, a dump station, swimming pool, boat ramps, and disc golf. Popular activities include fishing, boating, and riding the 6.5-mile equestrian trail through pine and hardwood forests.
payload.long_description: Situated on the western shore of Lake Bistineau, this park offers a satisfying blend of beautiful vistas and outstanding recreational facilities. Memorable for its upland mixed hardwood forest, and its enchanting stands of cypress and tupelo trees, the park offers a boat launch, hiking and biking trails, playgrounds, camping, cabins and excellent fishing! Beginning in January with the "yo- yo" season and lasting through the spring, summer, and early fall, the dedicated fisherman can draw such freshwater catches as black crappie, largemouth bass, yellow bass, catfish, bluegill, and red-ear sunfish from the lake's waters. Lake Bistineau dates back over 200 years. It began in 1800 when several thousand acres of land were flooded due to a gigantic log jam in the Red River. Gradually, however, as the area was dredged, the lake began to drain. Then in 1935, a permanent dam was built across Loggy Bayou, creating the present-day Lake Bistineau. The dam has since been enlarged, giving the reservoir a surface area of 26.9 square miles, with an average depth of seven feet and a maximum depth of 25 feet. Located in the park are cabins, campsites, and a group camp. Picnicking along the lake is tremendously popular at numerous sites equipped with tables, grills, and nearby restrooms. Several picnic pavilions are also available for larger groups. The park's trail system encompasses nearly 10 miles of woodland trails with a section devoted to horseback riding for those who bring their own horses and an 11-mile canoe trail, for visitors who want to see the park's beauty from the water. The park also contains an 18 hole disc golf course that will challenge every player.

location.directions: From Shreveport, head southeast on I-20 to Exit 47. Take LA-157 south through Doyline. Turn left onto State Park Road and follow signs to the park entrance at 103 State Park Road, Doyline, LA 71023.

payload.name: Tahquamenon Falls Rivermouth Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Modern facilities including showers, flush toilets, and dump station operate mid-May through mid-October. Reservations available through the Michigan DNR reservation system.
payload.short_description: Modern riverside campground with 72 electric sites near Michigan's largest waterfall, offering flush toilets, hot showers, and direct access to the Tahquamenon River for paddling and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Rivermouth Modern Campground sits along the Tahquamenon River in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, about five miles south of Paradise. The 72 electric sites (20/30/50 amp) are wooded and spacious, many accommodating larger RVs up to 40 feet. Modern amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, and a camp store. The campground provides direct river access with kayak rentals available on-site, making it an ideal base for paddlers exploring the waterway or hikers visiting the famous Upper and Lower Falls.
payload.long_description:
Rivermouth Modern Campground occupies a scenic stretch along the Tahquamenon River within the nearly 50,000-acre Tahquamenon Falls State Park. The 72 electric sites sit beneath mature pines and hardwoods, with many offering river views or easy access to the water. Sites feature 20/30/50 amp electrical service, picnic tables, and fire rings. The campground accommodates RVs and trailers up to 40 feet at most sites, with some pull-through options available.

Modern facilities include a restroom building with flush toilets and hot showers, a sanitation station, potable water spigots, and a camp store. An accessible paved boat launch near the campground provides easy entry to the river for kayaking, canoeing, and fishing. Kayak rentals are available on-site for those without their own watercraft.

The campground serves as a convenient base for exploring Tahquamenon Falls State Park, home to Michigan's largest waterfall. The Upper Falls drops nearly 50 feet and spans 200 feet across, while the Lower Falls offers a series of smaller cascades. Over 35 miles of trails wind through the park for hiking and mountain biking, and the river itself provides excellent paddling opportunities through pristine Upper Peninsula wilderness.

location.directions: From Paradise, head west on M-123 for approximately 5 miles. The campground entrance is on the south side of the highway at 41382 W M-123.

address.full: 32189 W South River Rd, Paradise, MI 49768

links.title: Tahquamenon Falls State Park - Michigan DNR

payload.name: Little Crater Lake
payload.status_description: The campground opens for the 2026 season on May 22. Season runs through late September. Some sites are first-come, first-served early in the season, with reservations available through Recreation.gov starting late May.
payload.short_description: Small, scenic campground near crystal-clear Little Crater Lake in Mt. Hood National Forest, with access to the Pacific Crest Trail and Timothy Lake.
payload.medium_description: Little Crater Lake Campground is nestled in an evergreen forest at 3,300 feet elevation in Mt. Hood National Forest. The campground offers about 15 single-family sites, each with a picnic table and fire ring. A short trail leads to Little Crater Lake, a geologically unique spring-fed pond with stunning turquoise water. Timothy Lake and the Pacific Crest Trail are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Little Crater Lake Campground is one of the most scenic spots in Mt. Hood National Forest. Set in a quiet evergreen forest at 3,300 feet elevation, the campground provides comfortable tent and small RV camping with about 15 single-family sites. Each site includes a picnic table and campfire ring with grill. Accessible vault toilets and a hand-pump water spigot near the entrance serve the facility.

The campground's namesake, Little Crater Lake, is a geologic oddity thought to have formed when artesian water forced its way through soft volcanic rock. The small, spring-fed pond features crystal-clear turquoise water that remains cold year-round. A short viewing trail begins in the campground and connects to the Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail. Swimming is strictly prohibited to protect the lake's sensitive ecological features.

Timothy Lake, a 1,400-acre reservoir popular for boating and fishing, is nearby. Anglers will find Kokanee salmon and stocked trout. The surrounding meadows offer excellent huckleberry picking in season and good wildlife viewing opportunities.

location.directions: From Sandy, travel southeast on Highway 26 past Government Camp and Frog Lake to Forest Road 42. Follow Road 42 south approximately 4 miles to Forest Road 58. Turn right and travel northwest about 2 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Joplin
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates seasonally with reservations available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on a scenic peninsula at Lake Ouachita with electric hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, swim beach, and boat ramp in the Ouachita Mountains of Arkansas.
payload.medium_description: Joplin Campground occupies a slender peninsula on Lake Ouachita, Arkansas's largest lake wholly within state borders. All 59 campsites have electric hookups with water faucets available in each loop. Facilities include flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, fish cleaning station, swim beach, and boat ramp. The terrain is uneven and sites are small, making this campground unsuitable for large RVs or trailers with slide-outs.
payload.long_description:
Joplin Campground sits on a narrow peninsula extending into Lake Ouachita, offering campers scenic views of the water and surrounding Ouachita Mountains. The lake spans over 40,000 acres and is prized as one of the clearest in the nation, making it ideal for scuba diving, swimming, and fishing. World-class striper fishing is available, and wildlife watchers may spot bobcats or even rare freshwater jellyfish.

All 59 campsites feature electric hookups with water faucets located in each loop. The campground provides flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, and fish cleaning station. Each site includes a concrete picnic table and ground grill. A boat ramp and swim beach provide direct lake access.

Due to the natural terrain, campsite pads vary significantly in size and levelness. Sites 35-63 have particularly uneven ground. The campground is not recommended for large RVs, trailers, or units with slide-outs. The narrow peninsula setting trades flat terrain for exceptional waterfront access.

location.directions: From Hot Springs, Arkansas: Take US 270 west for 23.5 miles to Mountain Harbor Road. Turn right and follow the access road 3 miles north to the campground.

address.full: 28 N Basin Dr, Mount Ida, AR 71957

payload.name: Unity Lake State Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Open for camping April 14 through October 31. Reservations available up to 6 months in advance. Note: Due to low water levels, boat docks have been removed from the lake as of July 2025 with no estimated restoration date.
payload.short_description: A quiet lakeside campground in Oregon's high desert offering 35 electric sites with water hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, and excellent fishing on Unity Reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Unity Lake State Recreation Site sits along the 926-acre Unity Reservoir in eastern Oregon's high desert, about 40 miles southwest of Baker City. The campground features 35 electrical campsites with water hookups, two reservable cabins, and a hiker/biker camp. Amenities include hot showers, flush toilets, an ADA-accessible dump station, and a boat ramp. Popular activities include fishing for rainbow trout, smallmouth bass, and crappie, as well as exploring nearby wilderness areas and historical sites like the Oregon Trail Interpretive Center.
payload.long_description:
Unity Lake State Recreation Site is a green oasis in Oregon's high desert, located on the shores of Unity Reservoir approximately 5 miles north of the small town of Unity off U.S. Highway 26. The 926-acre reservoir with 10 miles of shoreline provides excellent opportunities for boating, fishing, and water sports. Anglers target rainbow trout, smallmouth bass, and black crappie in these waters.

The campground offers 35 electrical sites with water hookups spread across a shaded lawn area, plus two reservable cabins (one pet-friendly) and a hiker/biker camp. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring. Facilities include hot showers, flush toilets, and an ADA-accessible dump station. Firewood and ice are available for purchase on-site.

The area serves as an ideal base camp for exploring three nearby wilderness areas and historical attractions including the National Historic Oregon Trail Interpretive Center and Sumpter Valley Dredge. The campground operates seasonally from mid-April through the end of October, with reservations available up to 6 months in advance through Oregon State Parks.

location.directions: Located 5 miles north of Unity, Oregon off U.S. Highway 26. The park is approximately 40 miles southwest of Baker City.

payload.name: Palmetto Island State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours are 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station staffed 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Reservations available at reservations.gooutdoorslouisiana.com.
payload.short_description: Located on the Vermilion River, Palmetto Island State Park offers a real south Louisiana outdoors experience.
payload.medium_description: Palmetto Island State Park sits along the Vermilion River in south Louisiana's Vermilion Parish. The campground features 95 premium campsites with water, electric, and sewer hookups, plus backcountry walk-in sites and a primitive group camping area. A bathhouse serves campers, and a boat launch provides river access for fishing and boating while interior lagoons offer paddling through native cypress swamp habitat.
payload.long_description: Located on the Vermilion River, Palmetto Island State Park offers a real south Louisiana outdoors experience. A boat launch provides access to the river for fishing and boating, while the interior lagoons allow canoers and kayakers an up-close look at the native plant and animal life.

links.title: Palmetto Island State Park Official Page

payload.name: Takhlakh Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for winter. The campground operates mid-July through mid-September. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. An active closure affects Adams Fork Bridge on Forest Road 5601.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at 4,400 feet in Gifford Pinchot National Forest with iconic views of Mt. Adams. Offers vault toilets, no potable water, and access to Takhlakh Loop Trail.
payload.medium_description: Takhlakh Lake Campground sits at 4,400 feet elevation on the shores of its namesake lake, offering stunning views of Mt. Adams reflected in the water. The campground features 54 back-in sites with varying spur lengths and 10 walk-in tent sites. Popular with hikers exploring the northern Mt. Adams area, the 1.1-mile Takhlakh Loop Trail encircles the lake directly from camp. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own supply. The lake is open to non-motorized boating and offers rainbow trout fishing.
payload.long_description:
Takhlakh Lake Campground occupies a prime location in the Cowlitz Valley Ranger District of Gifford Pinchot National Forest, sitting at 4,400 feet elevation on the shore of Takhlakh Lake. The campground is renowned for its postcard views of Mt. Adams towering above the lake, with Mt. Rainier and Mt. St. Helens also visible from various vantage points. The setting is well-shaded and attracts hikers exploring the northern trails of the Mt. Adams Wilderness.

The campground offers 54 back-in sites with unpaved parking spurs ranging from 15 to 40 feet, plus 10 walk-in tent sites closer to the water. Sites include picnic tables and vault toilets are available. There is no potable water, so campers must bring adequate drinking water. The maximum vehicle length is 22 feet, making this unsuitable for larger RVs. Campfires are not permitted.

The 1.1-mile Takhlakh Loop Trail starts from the campground and circles the lake on flat terrain accessible to all skill levels. The Takh Takh Meadows Trail connects to an old lava flow with excellent views. The lake supports non-motorized boating and fishing for rainbow trout. Mosquitoes can be numerous in early season.

location.directions: From I-5, take exit 68 and head east on US Highway 12 to Randle, Washington. Turn south onto State Highway 131 and travel 1 mile, stay left at the Y and continue southeast on Forest Road 23 for 30 miles to Forest Road 2329. Turn left onto Forest Road 2329 and follow it through the junction with Forest Road 5601. Proceed on Forest Road 2329 for 0.75 mile to the campground. The last 7 miles of Forest Road 23 are gravel.

links.title: USFS Gifford Pinchot NF Takhlakh Lake

payload.name: Obsidian Flat
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Typically opens around June 15, depending on snow conditions, through September 30. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Group campground near Mammoth Lakes in the eastern Sierra Nevada Mountains at 7,800 feet elevation, accommodating up to 50 people in a pine forest setting near Deadman Creek.
payload.medium_description: Obsidian Flat Group Campground offers a secluded group camping experience in the Inyo National Forest near Mammoth Lakes, California. The single group site accommodates up to 50 people with space for five RVs up to 40 feet or 15 vehicles. The primitive site features vault toilets, a picnic table, fire ring, and bear-proof food lockers, but no potable water. Access is through a security gate with a combination provided in your reservation confirmation.
payload.long_description:
Obsidian Flat Group Campground is a secluded group site in the Inyo National Forest, named after a nearby obsidian lava flow. Situated at 7,800 feet in a pine forest near Mammoth Lakes, California, the campground offers mountain views and a peaceful setting adjacent to Deadman Creek. The single large group site can accommodate up to 50 people with space for five RVs up to 40 feet in length or 15 vehicles total.

The site is fairly primitive, equipped with a vault toilet, picnic table, campfire ring, and bear-proof locker for food storage. No potable water is available, so campers must bring their own supply. Strict food storage rules apply due to bear activity in the area. Access is controlled by a security gate; the combination is provided in your reservation confirmation letter.

The area provides excellent opportunities for fishing in Deadman Creek, hiking trails including access to the Ansel Adams Wilderness, mountain biking, and off-road vehicle riding. Yosemite National Park makes a great day trip from the campground.

location.directions: From U.S. Highway 395 and State Highway 203 (Mammoth Lakes Junction), travel 8.2 miles north on 395. Turn west onto Deadman Road and follow for 3.2 miles to Upper Deadman Campground. Turn toward the Group Campground turnoff onto FS Road 2S05F. Continue one mile to the campground on the right.

payload.name: Lincoln State Park
payload.status_description: Open for camping with reservations available late April through late October. Modern comfort stations remain open through November 30. Lake Lincoln is closed and drained for dam repairs but camping continues. Blue-green algae is present year-round in park waters.
payload.short_description: Historic Indiana state park campground near Abraham Lincoln's boyhood home, offering 269 sites with electric, non-electric, and primitive camping options among rolling hills and thick forest.
payload.medium_description: Lincoln State Park preserves the land where Abraham Lincoln spent his formative years from ages 7 to 21. The campground offers 269 sites across three campground areas: Lake Lincoln Electric (150 sites), a non-electric campground (88 sites), and primitive camping (31 sites). Modern facilities include restrooms with showers, a dump station, and potable water. The park features 10 miles of hiking trails and two scenic lakes. Reservations are available through camp.IN.gov with sites available from late April through late October.
payload.long_description:
Lincoln State Park sits on nearly 1,800 acres in Spencer County, Indiana, where young Abraham Lincoln lived from 1816 to 1830. The park encompasses the land where the future president learned to farm, split rails, and develop the character that would shape American history. His mother, Nancy Hanks Lincoln, is buried nearby at the Lincoln Boyhood National Memorial.

The campground provides 269 total sites spread across multiple loops. Lake Lincoln Electric Campground offers 150 electric sites with modern restroom and shower facilities. The non-electric campground has 88 sites with a family restroom available to all campers. Primitive camping includes 31 sites for a more rustic experience. A dump station serves RV campers. The park also offers Blue Heron Family Cabins and Pine Hills Group Cottages for those seeking more amenities.

Beyond camping, visitors can explore 10 miles of hiking trails, fish in Lake Lincoln and Lake Sarah Lincoln, and visit the Colonel Jones Home interpretive center. The Little Pigeon Primitive Baptist Church, where the Lincoln family worshiped, remains on park grounds. The Noah Gordon Gristmill site and various historical markers provide additional insight into pioneer life in southern Indiana.

location.directions: From I-64, take Exit 57 south on US-231 toward Dale. Continue approximately 4 miles south, then turn east on IN-162. Follow IN-162 for about 3 miles to the park entrance on the left.

address.full: 15466 N County Rd 300 E, Lincoln City, IN 47552

payload.name: East Fork Turkey Ridge Shelter
payload.status_description: Turkey Ridge Shelter is a day-use picnic shelter, not an overnight camping facility. The shelter is open year-round for reservations through reserveohio.com. Restroom access is seasonal.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter at East Fork State Park near Cincinnati, featuring a large fire ring, charcoal grills, and picnic tables with 100-person capacity.
payload.medium_description: Turkey Ridge Shelter is a reservable day-use picnic shelter located within East Fork State Park in Clermont County, Ohio, approximately 25 miles southeast of Cincinnati. The shelter accommodates up to 100 people and includes a large 6-foot campfire ring, two permanent charcoal grills, and picnic tables. Seasonal restroom access and dumpster service are available nearby, though there is no potable water at the shelter.
payload.long_description:
Turkey Ridge Shelter is a group picnic shelter situated within East Fork State Park, one of Ohio's largest state parks at 7,480 acres. The park surrounds William Harsha Lake, offering access to swimming beaches, boat ramps, and extensive trail systems for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding.

The shelter is designed for group gatherings with a 100-person capacity. Amenities include a large 6-foot campfire ring, two permanent charcoal grills, and multiple picnic tables. Restroom facilities are available seasonally nearby, and trash dumpsters are provided. The shelter does not have potable water, so groups should bring their own drinking water.

East Fork State Park also offers a 416-site campground for overnight stays, as well as backcountry camping along the Backpack Trail and Steven Newman Worldwalker Perimeter Trail. The backcountry areas feature Adirondack-style shelters at camping areas 1 and 2, with fire rings at each site.

location.directions: From Cincinnati, take I-275 to State Route 125 East. Follow SR-125 for approximately 15 miles to East Fork State Park.

payload.name: Summit Lake State Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for camping through November 15, 2026. Approximately 75% of electric sites are reservable through Nebraska Game and Parks; remaining sites are first-come, first-served. A valid Nebraska park entry permit is required.
payload.short_description: A 190-acre lake in northeastern Nebraska offering 76 campsites with electric hookups, tent sites, shower house, and excellent fishing for bass, bluegill, catfish, crappie, and walleye.
payload.medium_description: Summit Lake State Recreation Area encompasses a 190-acre lake surrounded by 345 acres of land near Tekamah, Nebraska. The campground offers 43 electric sites with 20/30/50-amp service and 33 primitive tent sites. Amenities include a coin-operated shower house, vault toilets, drinking water, dump station, and accessible fishing dock. The no-wake lake supports kayaking and canoeing, with 4 miles of hiking trails and equestrian trails available.
payload.long_description:
Summit Lake State Recreation Area sits three miles west of Tekamah in northeastern Nebraska's Burt County. The 190-acre lake, surrounded by 345 acres of parkland, provides a quieter alternative to larger state recreation areas. The campground features 43 Electric Plus sites with 20, 30, and 50-amp connections and 33 basic tent sites scattered throughout the property.

The lake maintains a 5 mph no-wake speed limit, making it ideal for kayaking, canoeing, and fishing from the 13 jetties or accessible fishing dock. Anglers target bass, bluegill, catfish, crappie, and walleye. Beyond fishing, the park offers 4 miles of hiking trails, equestrian trails requiring superintendent approval for overnight horse camping, a swimming beach, archery range, playground, and horseshoe pits.

Camping facilities include a coin-operated shower house, vault toilets, drinking water hydrants, and an RV dump station. Approximately 75% of electric sites accept reservations through Nebraska Game and Parks up to 180 days in advance; remaining sites operate first-come, first-served with fees paid at the Iron Ranger station.

location.directions: Located 3 miles west of Tekamah, Nebraska on County Road G. Address: 2787 County Road G, Tekamah, NE 68061.

links.title: Summit Lake SRA - Nebraska Game and Parks

payload.name: Gooseberry Admin Site Cabins
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens mid-June 2026, with reservations available starting June 12. The facility operates mid-June through early September annually.
payload.short_description: Historic Forest Service cabins from 1907-1960, now available for group rentals. Three bunk cabins sleep 50, with a full kitchen, recreation hall, and bathhouse with flush toilets and hot showers.
payload.medium_description: Gooseberry Admin Site Cabins is a historic group rental facility in Fishlake National Forest at 8,000 feet elevation. Originally the Forest Service summer headquarters from 1907 to 1960, it now hosts family reunions, scout groups, church camps, and youth events. The site includes three bunk cabins with 50 single beds, a recreation hall with fireplace, a full kitchen with propane appliances, and a bathhouse with flush toilets and hot showers. Dense aspen stands surround the site, providing shade and spectacular fall color.
payload.long_description:
Gooseberry Admin Site Cabins is a historic group rental facility located 18 miles from Salina, Utah in the Fishlake National Forest. These structures served as Forest Service summer headquarters from 1907 to 1960 and are now preserved for group use. The site sits at approximately 8,000 feet elevation in the Gooseberry drainage, surrounded by dense aspen forests.

The facility includes three bunk cabins with 50 single beds and mattresses (one cabin has propane heating), a large recreation hall with fireplace, tables and chairs, and a fully equipped kitchen with propane cooking range, oven, three refrigerators, sinks with hot water, and outdoor grills. A bathhouse provides flush toilets, sinks, and hot showers. A small amphitheater with a fire circle is available for evening gatherings.

Guests must bring their own linens, bedding, dishes, utensils, and cookware. A propane generator provides limited electricity during evening and morning hours. Popular activities in the area include fishing, hiking, biking, horseback riding, and wildlife watching. The Great Western Trail runs nearby with two easily accessible trailheads.

location.directions: From Salina, Utah, take I-70 east approximately 7 miles to Exit 63 (Gooseberry Road). Turn south on County Road 640 and continue for 10 miles. The site is on the right side of the road, just beyond Gooseberry Campground.
