payload.name: Fort Ransom State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Full services including water, showers, and dump station are available through September 30. On October 1, comfort stations and modern campground water shut off for the winter limited service season. Year-round primitive camping remains available. Reservations accepted 95 days in advance via reservendparks.com.
payload.short_description: Scenic state park campground in the wooded Sheyenne River Valley with modern and primitive sites, horse camping facilities, and access to the North Country National Scenic Trail.
payload.medium_description: Fort Ransom State Park Campground sits in the scenic Sheyenne River Valley amid heavily wooded terrain. The park offers diverse camping options including modern sites with electricity, primitive sites, and dedicated horse camping with corral access. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, and a dump station. The Sheyenne River provides opportunities for canoeing, fishing, and bird watching, while a segment of the North Country National Scenic Trail passes through the park.
payload.long_description:
Named after an 1860s military fort, Fort Ransom State Park occupies a prime location in the heavily wooded Sheyenne River Valley in southeastern North Dakota. The campground offers 24 modern horse campsites with electricity and corral access, 9 primitive horse campsites, 16 standard campsites with electricity and water hydrant access, 10 primitive campsites, plus group camping options for both modern and primitive configurations.

The park features flush toilets, showers, and a sewage dump station near the visitor center. A playground and designated off-leash dog area are available. The Sheyenne River flows through the area, providing excellent opportunities for canoeing, fishing, and wildlife observation.

During summer months, horseback riding and camping are the primary activities, while winter brings cross-country skiing. A segment of the North Country National Scenic Trail traverses the park, connecting to an extensive trail network. The park operates year-round, though limited services apply from October through spring when water systems and comfort stations are shut down.

location.directions: From Interstate 94, take Exit 288 south on ND Highway 1 for approximately 40 miles to the town of Fort Ransom, then follow signs to Fort Ransom State Park.

links.title: Fort Ransom State Park Official Page
ND Parks Limited Service Season Info

payload.name: Quemado Lake - El Caso Cg
payload.status_description: Open and free to use year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect as of March 23, 2026. A harmful algae bloom advisory remains active for Quemado Lake itself, prohibiting swimming, wading, and fish consumption, though camping is unaffected. Winter visitors should vacate ahead of approaching storms to avoid being snowed in.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at Quemado Lake in Gila National Forest, offering shaded sites among ponderosa pine and cottonwood at 7,700 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: El Caso I-IV is a partially developed campground on the east end of Quemado Lake in the Gila National Forest. The shaded sites are nestled in a valley alongside an intermittent stream, surrounded by ponderosa pine and cottonwood trees. Popular with hunters, groups, and horse campers seeking a more primitive experience within hiking distance of the lake.
payload.long_description:
El Caso I-IV Campground sits at 7,700 feet elevation on the east side of 130-acre Quemado Lake in New Mexico's Gila National Forest. The partially developed campground occupies a shaded valley alongside an intermittent stream, with sites scattered beneath ponderosa pine and cottonwood trees. It offers a quieter, more primitive alternative to the nearby Juniper Campground.

The campground is popular with hunters during season, group campers, and horse campers (though no equestrian facilities are provided). Hiking trails connect to the lake, including the Largo Trail #14 which departs near the campground. This is a pack-it-in/pack-it-out area with no potable water, so visitors must bring their own water supply and remove all trash.

The site is generally open year-round and free of charge, though winter visitors should be prepared to leave ahead of storms to avoid being snowed in. ATVs are prohibited, and all pets must be kept on leash. A 14-day stay limit applies throughout Gila National Forest.

location.directions: From Quemado, NM, head south on NM Highway 32 for approximately 14 miles to the Quemado Lake / NM Highway 103 sign. Turn east on Highway 103 and continue 4 miles to Forest Road 13. Continue past Quemado Lake; the campground is approximately 0.25 miles east of Piñon Campground.

payload.name: Sun Lakes Dry Falls Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Level 2 burn ban in effect as of May 22, 2026: wood fires restricted to fire pits in designated areas only. Reservations available April 15 through September 15 via washington.goingtocamp.com. Sites 1-31 close November 1; water at those sites may be turned off after October 1.
payload.short_description: Large state park campground at the base of Dry Falls with 137 sites, full hookups available, and access to multiple lakes in the dramatic coulees of central Washington.
payload.medium_description: Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park offers 137 campsites at the foot of the ancient Dry Falls cataract, including 96 standard sites and 41 full-hookup sites accommodating RVs up to 65 feet. The park provides access to Park Lake and Deep Lake for swimming, fishing, and boating, with 15 miles of trails winding through sage-covered coulees and along dramatic basalt cliffs.
payload.long_description:
Sun Lakes-Dry Falls State Park sits in the heart of Washington's Channeled Scablands, a landscape carved by the catastrophic Missoula Floods at the end of the last Ice Age. The park encompasses 3,774 acres at the base of Dry Falls, once one of the largest waterfalls in geologic history, now a 400-foot cliff overlooking a chain of lakes that fill the ancient plunge pool.

The campground offers 96 standard campsites and 41 full-hookup sites spread along Park Lake's shoreline. Sites accommodate RVs and trailers up to 65 feet, though availability at maximum length is limited. All sites include fire rings, and the park provides restrooms, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. A group camp accommodates up to 75 people for tent camping.

Recreation options include swimming, fishing, and boating on Park Lake and nearby Deep Lake, plus 15 miles of hiking trails with panoramic views of the coulees. The park also features a nine-hole golf course and miniature golf. The Dry Falls Visitor Center overlooks the ancient waterfall and interprets the region's dramatic geologic history.

location.directions: From Coulee City, head south on State Route 17 for approximately 4 miles. Turn left onto Park Lake Road NE and continue to the park entrance.

address.full: 34875 Park Lake Rd NE, Coulee City, WA 99115

payload.name: Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-May through October 31, weather dependent. First-come, first-served only; no reservations available. Cash or check payment required on-site.
payload.short_description: Primitive equestrian-friendly campground on Big Smoky Creek in Sawtooth National Forest, offering 10 sites with horse corrals, stock facilities, and trailhead access to Skillern Hot Springs.
payload.medium_description: Canyon Campground is a rustic first-come, first-served campground on Big Smoky Creek featuring 7 single sites and 3 group sites. The campground caters to equestrians with horse corrals, stock water, and a loading ramp. Big Smoky Trail #072 departs from the north end, leading to Skillern Hot Springs and connecting to a network of backcountry trails open to hikers, horses, and motorcycles.
payload.long_description:
Canyon Campground, also known as Canyon Transfer Camp, sits along Big Smoky Creek in the Fairfield Ranger District of Sawtooth National Forest. The campground serves as both a traditional camping destination and an equestrian staging area, with 7 single sites and 3 group sites arranged in a loop. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with vault toilets and potable water from a hand pump available centrally.

The campground is particularly well-suited for horse camping, featuring corrals with feeders, stock water, and a handicap-accessible loading ramp for stock. Horses must be kept in the designated corral area northwest of the campground and are not permitted in individual campsites.

Big Smoky Trail #072 begins at the north end of the campground and leads to Skillern Hot Springs. The main trail is open to non-motorized travel and motorcycles, though several branch trails are restricted to non-motorized use only. A Motor Vehicle Use Map from the Fairfield Ranger Station is recommended for navigation.

location.directions: From Fairfield, go north 18 miles on Forest Road #094, turn left onto Forest Road #227 for 5.5 miles, then turn north onto Forest Road #085 for 2 miles.

payload.name: Fairy Stone State Park Cabins And Lodge
payload.status_description: Cabins and lodge are open year-round and accepting reservations. Between Memorial Day weekend and Labor Day, a six-night minimum stay applies, reduced to four nights three months out and two nights in the final month before arrival. Two-night minimum applies the rest of the year.
payload.short_description: Rustic cabins and a 16-person lodge at Fairy Stone State Park in Virginia's Blue Ridge foothills, featuring historic CCC-era log cabins with lake views, full kitchens, and wood-burning fireplaces.
payload.medium_description: Fairy Stone State Park offers 25 cabins and a 16-guest lodge on the shores of Fairy Stone Lake in Patrick County, Virginia. Accommodations range from efficiency cabins to two-bedroom waterfront units, including nine historic CCC-era log cabins built in the 1930s. All cabins are climate-controlled with full kitchens, bathrooms with showers, wood-burning fireplaces, and outdoor fire rings with picnic tables. The Fairy Stone Lodge sleeps 16 with five bedrooms and three bathrooms, including universally accessible features.
payload.long_description:
Fairy Stone State Park's cabin and lodge complex sits along the 168-acre Fairy Stone Lake in Virginia's Blue Ridge foothills. The park offers 25 cabins in several configurations: efficiency cabins, one-bedroom waterfront cabins, and two-bedroom cabins with some offering lake views. Cabins 1-9 are historic Civilian Conservation Corps log structures from the 1930s, while cabins 10-25 are wood-framed with screened porches.

All cabins are climate-controlled with heat and air conditioning, and feature full kitchens with refrigerator, stove, microwave, coffeemaker, and cookware. Each cabin has one bathroom with shower, a wood-burning fireplace with one bundle of wood included, and outdoor amenities including a picnic table, pedestal grill, and fire ring. Guests must bring their own linens including sheets, blankets, towels, and kitchen towels.

The Fairy Stone Lodge accommodates up to 16 guests in five bedrooms with three bathrooms. The lodge includes universally accessible features with a ramp entrance, accessible bedroom, kitchen, and bathroom with roll-in shower. Four yurts and a 14-person bunkhouse are also available seasonally from March through December. Pets are permitted in cabins and the lodge on a leash with a nightly pet fee.

location.directions: From Stuart, VA, take US-58 west approximately 10 miles. Turn right onto Route 57 (Fairy Stone Lake Drive) and follow signs to the park entrance at 967 Fairystone Lake Drive, Stuart, VA 24171.

links.title: Fairy Stone State Park Official Page

payload.name: Ribbonwood Equestrian Cg
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to staffing and budget constraints. The campground was closed in 2025 as part of San Jacinto District closures affecting low-use facilities, and remains closed.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground in San Bernardino National Forest with 8 pull-through sites, horse corrals, and views of Palm Desert and the Salton Sea. Currently closed due to staffing constraints.
payload.medium_description: Ribbonwood Equestrian Campground offers 8 spacious pull-through sites designed for equestrian campers in a high desert environment of chaparral, pinyon pine, and yucca at 4,000 feet elevation. Each site includes two 10x10 horse corrals, a hitching rack, picnic table, fire ring, and potable water hookup. The campground features flush toilets, hot showers, and access to the 5.3-mile Sawmill Trail and Cactus Spring Trail.
payload.long_description:
Located approximately 16 miles southeast of Palm Desert in the Santa Rosa and San Jacinto Mountains National Monument, Ribbonwood Equestrian Campground is a dedicated horse camp at roughly 4,000 feet elevation. The campground sits in a high desert landscape characterized by chaparral brush, cactus, pinyon pine, and yucca, with views overlooking Palm Desert and the Salton Sea.

The facility features 8 pull-through campsites built for equestrian use, each equipped with two 10x10 horse corrals, a hitching rack, picnic table, fire ring, and potable water hookup. Campground amenities include accessible flush toilets and hot showers. Roads and spurs are gravel and may not be level.

Recreation opportunities include the 5.3-mile Sawmill Trail, which begins within the campground and gains 2,220 feet of elevation along an old road, and the Cactus Spring Trail near the parking area. Both trails offer scenic views and diverse botanical species. When operational, reservations are required through Recreation.gov with no first-come, first-served availability.

location.directions: From Palm Desert, take Palms to Pines Highway (Highway 74) south for approximately 16 miles to the community of Pinyon. Turn left onto Transfer Station Road (watch for signs). The entrance is on the right.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: A bear or multiple bears have been spotted in the area. Please be aware at all times, and visit our agency website for bear safety tips and more information.

payload.name: Caledon State Park Hunts Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for primitive camping. Advance reservations required. Check-in is 4 p.m., check-out is 1 p.m. The park closes briefly in November and early December for resource management projects.
payload.short_description: Primitive paddle-in and hike-in campground on the Potomac River at Caledon State Park with six tent sites featuring fire rings and picnic tables.
payload.medium_description: Caledon State Park's Hunts Campground offers six primitive tent camping sites accessible only by a 3.5-mile hike or bike ride, or by paddling in via kayak or canoe. Each site features a sand-filled pad with a fire ring, lantern post, and picnic table. There is no potable water and campers must pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Hunts Campground at Caledon State Park provides a true backcountry camping experience along the Potomac River in Virginia's Northern Neck. The six primitive tent sites are intentionally remote, requiring either a 3.5-mile hike or bike ride from the overnight parking area near the visitor center, or a paddle-in approach via kayak, canoe, or other non-motorized watercraft landing at Jones Pond.

Each campsite is a framed, sand-filled pad equipped with a fire ring, lantern post, and picnic table. A portable toilet serves the campground, but there is no potable water, electricity, or showers. Campers must pack in all water and supplies and pack out all trash. The maximum capacity is six people per site.

The park is known for its bald eagle habitat along the Potomac River and offers hiking trails through mature forest. Overnight guests must remain in the campground from dusk until 8 a.m. The campground operates year-round with required advance reservations.

location.directions: From I-95, take exit 133 (Fredericksburg) and head east on Route 3. Continue approximately 20 miles to King George. Turn left onto Route 218 North (Caledon Road) and continue about 4 miles to the park entrance at 11617 Caledon Rd., King George, VA 22485. The campground requires a 3.5-mile hike/bike from overnight parking or paddle-in access via the Potomac River.

payload.name: Fallen Leaf Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens May 22, 2026. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Sites typically fill quickly.
payload.short_description: Popular 206-site campground on Fallen Leaf Lake's north shore near South Lake Tahoe, featuring tent sites, RV sites, and yurts with flush toilets, showers, and a camp store.
payload.medium_description: Fallen Leaf Campground sits on the north shore of Fallen Leaf Lake, adjacent to Taylor Creek and less than a mile from Lake Tahoe's south shore. The 206-site campground includes standard tent and RV sites plus six yurts, all with bear boxes, fire rings, pedestal grills, and picnic tables. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated showers, drinking water, and a camp store. The campground provides access to the Moraine Trail and serves as a basecamp for Desolation Wilderness via nearby Glen Alpine and Mt. Tallac trailheads.
payload.long_description:
Fallen Leaf Campground occupies a prime location on the north shore of Fallen Leaf Lake, with Taylor Creek bordering the campground and Lake Tahoe's south shore less than a mile away. The 206 sites are nestled among towering pine, cedar, fir, and aspen trees, with some sites adjacent to wildflower meadows. While campsites don't offer direct lake views, Fallen Leaf Lake is a short walk away, where the forested shoreline and surrounding peaks including Cathedral Peak and Mount Tallac reflect in crystal-clear waters.

The campground features 200 standard tent and RV sites plus six yurts. Each site includes a bear-proof food storage locker, fire ring with pedestal grill, picnic table, and paved parking apron. Yurts accommodate five to six people with futons, bunk beds, electric light, and space heater. Campground facilities include flush toilets, coin-operated showers, and water spigots throughout.

Recreation options abound. Both lakes offer boating, fishing, swimming, and waterskiing. The 1-mile Moraine Trail starts at the campground, and the Taylor Creek Visitor Center across Highway 89 features interpretive programs and the Stream Profile Chamber. Desolation Wilderness backpacking access is available via Glen Alpine and Mt. Tallac trailheads. The Pope-Baldwin bike path parallels Highway 89, connecting to Pope and Baldwin swim beaches and the Tallac Historic Site.

location.directions: From South Lake Tahoe, take Highway 89 North from the junction of Highway 50 and 89. In 3 miles, turn left on Fallen Leaf Road. The campground entrance is about half a mile on the right.

address.full: 2109 Fallen Leaf Rd, South Lake Tahoe, CA 96150

payload.name: Tram Road Equestrian Campground Tiger Bay State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations are required and can be made up to 11 months in advance through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica. A gate combination is provided in the confirmation email for campground access.
payload.short_description: Primitive equestrian campground with 4 sites in Tiger Bay State Forest near Ormond Beach, featuring horse corrals, fire rings, and access to miles of equestrian trails.
payload.medium_description: Tram Road Equestrian Campground is a small primitive facility in Tiger Bay State Forest designed for horseback riders. Each of the four campsites includes a horse corral, picnic table, fire ring, and grill. The campground features a central round training pen and the Foster Pavilion. No electricity or potable water is available, with only a pitcher pump providing non-potable water for horses. A gate combination is required for entry.
payload.long_description:
Tram Road Equestrian Campground sits within the 27,330-acre Tiger Bay State Forest in Volusia County, approximately 10 minutes west of Ormond Beach. This primitive equestrian facility offers four campsites, each equipped with a small horse corral, picnic table, fire ring, and grill. The campground provides a central round training pen for horse work and the Foster Pavilion for group gatherings (requires separate reservation).

The area is truly primitive with no electricity or water hookups. A pitcher pump supplies non-potable water suitable for horses but not for drinking. A single portable toilet serves the campground. Two of the four sites are pull-through, accommodating rigs up to 30 feet. Access requires a gate combination provided in the reservation confirmation email.

Horseback riders can explore miles of multi-use trails through pine flatwoods and wetland habitats. The forest also supports hiking, bicycling, hunting (in season), wildlife viewing, and photography. Bear activity occurs in the area, so proper food storage is required.

location.directions: From Exit 268 on I-95, travel west on State Road 40 for 5.6 miles. Turn left on Rima Ridge Road and travel 2.1 miles to Tram Road. Turn left and travel east 0.1 mile to Tram Road Equestrian Area entrance on the left.

address.full: 2200 Rima Ridge Rd, Ormond Beach, FL 32174

payload.name: Rattin Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 22, 2026 (weather permitting). The opening was delayed due to the East Side Fire but the facility is now cleared. The south bridge is out; use the northside entrance only. 16-day maximum stay limit applies to all Beartooth Ranger District campgrounds.
payload.short_description: Small creekside campground along Rock Creek near the Beartooth Highway, 7 miles south of Red Lodge, Montana, with vault toilets and potable water.
payload.medium_description: Rattin Campground offers 6 intimate sites on the banks of the Main Fork of Rock Creek in the Custer Gallatin National Forest. The campground provides vault toilets, drinking water from a hand pump, and bear-resistant trash storage. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings with grills. Access to the Beartooth Highway makes this an excellent base for fishing, hiking nearby wilderness trails, and scenic drives toward Yellowstone's northeast entrance.
payload.long_description:
Rattin Campground sits in the shadow of the Beartooth Range along the Main Fork of Rock Creek, approximately 7 miles south of Red Lodge, Montana. The campground features 6 sites, with 3 standard nonelectric sites (1, 2, 3) that can accommodate small trailers up to 20 feet, and 3 tent-only sites (5, 6, 7). A forest of aspen and pine surrounds the area, which is home to grizzly bears, deer, and elk.

Amenities include accessible vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables, campfire rings with grills, and a bear-resistant dumpster. Firewood is available for purchase. A campground host is present during the season. Note that trailers are prohibited past Site #3 due to no turnaround, and the south bridge is currently out.

The campground serves as a gateway to excellent recreation: rainbow trout fishing in Rock Creek, nearby trails including Mount Maurice, Corral Creek, Bear Track, and the Parkside National Recreation Trail. The Beartooth Wilderness is accessible via Hellroaring and Lake Fork Trailheads. Yellowstone National Park's Northeast Entrance is 60 miles away via the scenic Beartooth Highway.

location.directions: From Red Lodge, MT: Drive south on US Highway 212 for approximately 6.7 miles. Turn left onto East Side Road (Forest Road 379, formerly Eastside Road). Proceed 0.3 miles to the campground on your left. Alternatively, turn onto East Side Road at 3.7 miles south of Red Lodge and drive 3.1 miles to reach the campground on your right. Note: The south bridge is out.

address.full: 19 Rattin Campground Rd, Red Lodge, MT 59068

payload.name: North Clear Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opens May 22, 2026 for the season and operates through Labor Day weekend. All sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations. 14-day camping limit.
payload.short_description: Remote 21-site campground along North Clear Creek in Rio Grande National Forest, offering solitude at 9,900 feet with vault toilets, potable water, and excellent fishing access.
payload.medium_description: North Clear Creek Campground sits hidden from Forest Road 510 at 9,900 feet elevation, 24.5 miles west of Creede. All 21 sites are first-come, first-served with parking spurs, picnic tables, and fire rings. A hand pump provides potable water. The campground offers direct access to North Clear Creek for fishing and is well-suited for those seeking quiet, primitive camping away from busy roads. A campground host is present during the operating season.
payload.long_description:
North Clear Creek Campground is a secluded retreat in the Rio Grande National Forest, completely hidden from Forest Road 510 at 9,900 feet elevation. The 21 sites are scattered among small openings and shaded areas of aspen, spruce, and fir. Each site includes a parking spur (maximum 40 feet, though not all sites accommodate this length), picnic table, and fire ring. Two vault toilets serve the campground, and potable water is available from a hand pump well.

The campground sits adjacent to North Clear Creek, providing excellent stream fishing opportunities. Wildlife viewing is a highlight, with moose sightings possible in the area. Fall visitors can photograph striking aspen colors throughout the surrounding landscape. A campground host is stationed on-site during the operating season.

This is a primitive camping experience with no hookups, showers, or dump station. Trash service is provided Memorial Day through Labor Day via centrally located cans. Bear-country food storage requirements apply. The 14-day camping limit keeps sites turning over for those seeking extended solitude in the high country.

location.directions: From Creede, Colorado, travel west on Colorado Highway 149 for 22.4 miles to Forest Road 510. Take FR 510 north for 2.1 miles to the campground entrance.

payload.name: Davidson Lake Shelter Lookout/cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations or fees. Davidson Lake is typically ice-free from early May through mid-November. The shelter is primitive with no potable water or restrooms; visitors must bring drinking water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Historic 1935 CCC-built three-sided Adirondack shelter on Davidson Lake along the cross Admiralty Island canoe route, accessible by float plane or canoe.
payload.medium_description: Davidson Lake Shelter is a 12' x 10' three-sided Adirondack-style shelter with a gravel floor, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1935 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Located on the western end of Davidson Lake in the Kootznoowoo Wilderness on Admiralty Island, the shelter sits along the 32-mile cross-Admiralty canoe route and is accessible only by float plane or canoe from Juneau or Angoon.
payload.long_description:
Davidson Lake Shelter is a historic backcountry shelter built in 1935 by the Civilian Conservation Corps as part of a series of 15 Adirondack-style shelters along the cross Admiralty Island canoe route. The 12' x 10' three-sided structure features peeled log construction with wooden shake roof and walls, and a gravel floor. Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1995, the shelter provides basic overnight accommodations in the remote Kootznoowoo Wilderness.

The shelter sits at the western end of Davidson Lake in the central region of Admiralty Island, surrounded by temperate rainforest, muskeg meadows, and pristine waterways. Access is exclusively by float plane (approximately 40 minutes from Juneau) or by canoe via the cross-Admiralty route from Mitchell Bay or Angoon. The lake is typically ice-free from early May through mid-November.

Trails connect the shelter to Salt Lake (2.78 miles), Freshwater Lake, Mitchell Bay, and Thayer Lake, offering opportunities for extended backcountry travel through varied ecosystems. Admiralty Island is known as Kootznoowoo ("Fortress of the Bears") and has one of the highest brown bear densities in North America, so proper food storage and bear awareness are essential.

location.directions: Located on the western end of Davidson Lake in the central region of Admiralty Island. Accessible only by float plane from Juneau (approximately 40 minutes) or by canoe along the cross Admiralty canoe route from Mitchell Bay or Angoon.

payload.name: Tailrace Park
payload.status_description: Open for day-use. The picnic shelter is available for reservation through Recreation.gov. Overnight camping is not permitted at this facility.
payload.short_description: Day-use park below John H. Kerr Dam with a reservable picnic shelter, kayak launch, fishing pier, and boat ramp along the Roanoke River. No overnight camping permitted.
payload.medium_description: Tailrace Park is a semi-wooded day-use area located directly below John H. Kerr Dam in Mecklenburg County, Virginia. The park offers a reservable picnic shelter accommodating up to 250 people, a handicap-accessible kayak launch for Roanoke River access, a fishing pier popular for bald eagle viewing, and a boat ramp. Flush toilets are available during peak season. No overnight camping, hunting, or alcoholic beverages are permitted.
payload.long_description:
Tailrace Park sits at the base of John H. Kerr Dam, where the tailrace waters flow into the Roanoke River. This semi-wooded day-use area managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers provides excellent access to fishing and wildlife viewing. The park is particularly notable for bald eagle sightings, especially during winter months when over a dozen eagles may be observed from the small pier.

The park features a large picnic shelter available for reservation through Recreation.gov, suitable for birthday parties, reunions, and group gatherings of up to 250 people with parking for 50 vehicles. A handicap-accessible kayak launch provides paddlers direct access to the Roanoke River, and a boat ramp serves motorized watercraft. Flush toilets are available during peak season.

Important: This is a day-use facility only. Overnight camping is prohibited. The park is free to visit and open daily, though the picnic shelter requires advance reservation for exclusive use.

location.directions: Located at 5458 Buggs Island Road, Boydton, Virginia 23917. The park is approximately 17 miles south of South Hill, Virginia.

payload.name: Backcountry Camping In Lassen's Wilderness
payload.status_description: Open year-round for backcountry camping. Wilderness permit required via Recreation.gov; no quotas or daily limits. Bear-resistant containers mandatory April 16 through November 30. Some trails within the 2021 Dixie Fire footprint have ongoing hazards; areas marked CLOSED are off-limits.
payload.short_description: Dispersed backcountry camping in Lassen Volcanic National Park's 75,000-acre wilderness. No designated sites or amenities; wilderness permit required via Recreation.gov.
payload.medium_description: Lassen Volcanic's wilderness offers year-round dispersed backcountry camping across over 75,000 acres of designated wilderness. There are no designated campsites, no amenities, and no quotas. Access the backcountry from Warner Valley, Butte Lake, Juniper Lake, or Summit Lake trailheads. A wilderness permit is required for all overnight stays and must be obtained online through Recreation.gov up to 90 days in advance.
payload.long_description:
Lassen Volcanic National Park's wilderness encompasses over 75,000 acres of volcanic terrain, alpine lakes, and subalpine meadows available for dispersed backcountry camping. Unlike established campgrounds, there are no designated campsites, tent pads, picnic tables, or facilities of any kind. Campers must be fully self-sufficient and practice Leave No Trace principles, including packing out all trash and toilet paper.

A wilderness permit is required for all overnight stays and must be obtained exclusively through Recreation.gov up to 90 days before your trip. There are no quotas or limits on daily permits. Bear-resistant food containers are mandatory from April 16 through November 30; hanging food is prohibited. Fires are not allowed anywhere in the backcountry; only liquid or gas fuel stoves are permitted. Camping is prohibited within 100 feet of water, 1/4 mile of hydrothermal areas, and 1/2 mile of developed areas.

The backcountry is typically accessed from four primary trailheads: Warner Valley, Butte Lake, Juniper Lake, and Summit Lake. Trails may be snow-covered into July, and weather can change rapidly. Some trails within the 2021 Dixie Fire footprint remain affected; check current conditions and be prepared for burned area hazards.

location.directions: Access Lassen's backcountry from four primary trailheads: Warner Valley, Butte Lake, Juniper Lake, and Summit Lake. Park headquarters is at 38050 Highway 36 East, Mineral, CA 96063. Wilderness permits must be obtained online via Recreation.gov before arrival; no in-person permits are issued.

payload.name: Hornsilver Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open seasonally, typically mid-May through fall depending on conditions. A food storage order is in effect due to bear activity. Fires are prohibited within a quarter mile outside the campground boundary but allowed in designated sites. No potable water available.
payload.short_description: Small, quiet forest campground off Highway 24 near Minturn with vault toilet, fishing access to Homestake Creek, and trailheads nearby in White River National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Hornsilver Campground sits at roughly 9,500 feet in the Eagle-Holy Cross Ranger District, directly off Highway 24 about 10 miles south of Minturn. The campground offers easy access to Homestake Creek fishing across the highway and multiple trailheads off Homestake Road (FSR 703) about a mile south. This is a primitive campground with vault toilet facilities, no potable water, and light usage levels.
payload.long_description:
Hornsilver Campground is a small, lightly-used Forest Service campground in White River National Forest, located directly off Highway 24 approximately 10 miles south of Minturn, Colorado. The campground sits across the highway from Homestake Creek, providing convenient access for anglers. Several trailheads are accessible via Homestake Road (FSR 703), located about one mile south of the campground.

This is a primitive campground offering basic amenities including a vault toilet but no potable water. Campers should bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash. Parking spurs accommodate vehicles up to 30 feet in length, making it suitable for smaller RVs and trailers but not large rigs.

A food storage order is in effect requiring all food and refuse to be stored in hard-sided vehicles, approved bear-resistant containers, or suspended at least 10 feet off the ground and 4 feet from any tree or pole. The campground has a 10-consecutive-day stay limit.

location.directions: From Minturn, Colorado, head south on Highway 24 for approximately 10 miles. The campground is located directly off the highway on the east side, across from Homestake Creek.

payload.name: Buck Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground underwent renovations from October 2025 through early summer 2026. Current availability shows all sites fully reserved through at least late May. Reservations required via ReserveOhio.
payload.short_description: Ohio state park campground on a 2,120-acre reservoir with 101 campsites, electric hookups, flush toilets, showers, and a dump station near Springfield.
payload.medium_description: Buck Creek State Park Campground sits along a 2,120-acre reservoir in Clark County, Ohio. The modern campground offers 101 sites, most with 30-amp electric service, along with flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, and laundry facilities. The park provides excellent fishing, boating, and beach access for campers.
payload.long_description:
Buck Creek State Park Campground is located within a diverse 1,896-acre park centered around a 2,120-acre reservoir near Springfield, Ohio. The modern campground offers 101 campsites, with 89 featuring 30-amp electric service and the remainder as primitive sites. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Campground facilities include flush restrooms with hot showers, a dump station, laundry room, water spigots, and trash service throughout.

The park's recreational opportunities focus on the lake, with fishing for largemouth bass, crappie, and catfish, plus boating and a marina with fuel and bait. Campers have access to a designated beach area, walking and biking paths, and basketball courts. The campground sits in a separate area from the park's 23 cabins, which offer an alternative lodging option.

Pets are permitted at designated campsites and must be leashed at all times. Reservations are required and can be made through ReserveOhio or by calling the reservation line. Ohio state parks do not charge entrance fees.

location.directions: From I-70, take Exit 62 (State Route 41) north. Follow SR 41 north to Buck Creek Lane and turn right into the park. The campground is located at 1976 Buck Creek Lane, Springfield, OH 45502.

links.title: Ohio DNR Buck Creek State Park

payload.name: Lapine State Park
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Open flame ban in effect May 11 through September 30, 2026, prohibiting campfires, charcoal, and candles. South loop and cabins open year-round; north loop closes October 1, middle loop closes October 15. Water hookups at campsites disabled October 15 through April 30.
payload.short_description: La Pine State Park offers full-hookup RV camping and cozy cabins in a subalpine forest along the Upper Deschutes River, with 14 miles of trails and year-round access to the south loop.
payload.medium_description: La Pine State Park sits along the trout-filled Upper Deschutes River in Oregon's high desert subalpine forest. The campground features 82 full-hookup sites, 47 electric/water sites, and 10 cabins ranging from rustic to deluxe. Amenities include hot showers, flush toilets, a dump station, and a fenced off-leash dog area. The south loop and cabins remain open year-round, while the north and middle loops close seasonally in October.
payload.long_description:
La Pine State Park occupies a scenic stretch of the Upper Deschutes River in Oregon's high desert subalpine forest. The quiet, shaded campground connects to 14 miles of multi-use trails that follow both sides of the river and link key park landmarks. The park offers 82 full-hookup RV sites, 47 electric/water sites, 7 tent sites, and 10 cabins (5 rustic and 5 deluxe). Pull-through sites accommodate rigs up to 95 feet.

Amenities include hot showers, flush toilets, a dump station ($10 fee), and firewood for purchase. A fenced off-leash pet exercise area is a short walk from the campground. Several deluxe cabins and one rustic cabin are ADA accessible. The South Loop Campers Clubhouse is open first-come, first-served from 8 AM to 9 PM.

The south loop and all cabins remain open year-round, making this a viable winter camping destination. The north loop closes October 1 and the middle loop closes October 15. Water hookups at campsites are disabled from October 15 through April 30, though water remains available at restrooms and deluxe cabins.

location.directions: From Bend, Oregon, drive south on Highway 97 for 22 miles. Turn onto State Recreation Road and continue for 5.5 miles to reach the campground.

links.title: Reserve America - La Pine Campground Details

payload.name: Mammoth Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required via Recreation.gov from mid-April through mid-October. First-come, first-served from mid-October through early April with payment via Scan and Pay in the Recreation.gov app. Camping limited to 14 consecutive days from July 1 through Labor Day, and 30 days the rest of the year.
payload.short_description: Yellowstone's only year-round campground, located at Mammoth Hot Springs with 82 sites, flush toilets, potable water, and excellent wildlife viewing opportunities.
payload.medium_description: Mammoth Campground sits at 6,200 feet elevation near Mammoth Hot Springs, just five miles from Yellowstone's North Entrance. The 82-site campground offers flush toilets year-round, potable water, dump station access, and food storage lockers. Scattered juniper and Douglas fir trees provide shade in summer. Elk, bison, pronghorn, and mule deer frequently pass through the area.
payload.long_description:
Mammoth Campground is uniquely positioned as Yellowstone's only campground open year-round, making it a valuable option for winter visitors and shoulder-season travelers. Located in a high sagebrush steppe at 6,200 feet elevation, the campground provides easy access to the Mammoth Hot Springs terraces, historic Fort Yellowstone, and excellent wildlife viewing throughout the seasons.

The 82 standard nonelectric sites accommodate tents and RVs, with some sites fitting combined vehicle lengths up to 75 feet during peak season, though winter limits drop to 30 feet total. Pull-through and back-in sites are available, with limited width for slide-outs and potentially unlevel surfaces. Five ADA-accessible campsites serve visitors with mobility needs.

Amenities include flush toilets (year-round, though limited in winter), potable water spigots, dump station, trash and recycling collection, food storage lockers, and seasonal firewood sales. No showers are available on-site, though accessible shower facilities can be found in nearby Gardiner, Montana. Wood and charcoal fires are permitted in fire grates unless fire restrictions are in effect.

location.directions: Located in the Mammoth Hot Springs area in the northern section of Yellowstone National Park, five miles south of the North Entrance near Gardiner, Montana.

address.full: 412 Lower Mamouth, Yellowstone National Park, WY 82190

payload.name: Bay Campground - South Manitou Island
payload.status_description: Bay Campground is closed for the entire 2026 season due to a major dock relocation and infrastructure repair project. The ferry service is not operating to the island. South Manitou Island dock and village are expected to reopen in 2027. Access in 2026 is limited to private boats anchoring offshore, with only Popple and Weather Station campgrounds available.
payload.short_description: Remote island campground on South Manitou Island in Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, accessible only by boat. Features 25 individual tent sites and 3 group sites near the dock and beach.
payload.medium_description: Bay Campground is the closest campground to the dock on South Manitou Island, less than a mile walk with easy beach access. This tent-only campground offers 25 individual first-come, first-served sites and 3 reservable group sites for parties of 9-20 people. Sites are well-secluded with shared community fire rings and vault toilets. Campers must bring water filtration equipment as there is no purified drinking water, and must pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Bay Campground sits on South Manitou Island within Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, a remote wilderness destination accessible only by a 1.5-hour ferry ride from Leland, Michigan, or by private boat. As the closest campground to the island dock, Bay offers convenient access while maintaining a backcountry character. The campground features 25 individual tent sites available first-come, first-served and 3 group sites that accommodate 9-20 people with a maximum of 10 tents per site.

The island experience is primitive by design. Vault toilets are available year-round, but there is no potable water at the campground itself. Campers must bring water filtration equipment or haul water from the village area when services are operational. Several shared community fire rings are provided for campfires, and campers may collect dead and down wood on the island. Transporting firewood to the island is prohibited due to emerald ash borer quarantine regulations.

All gear must be backpacked from the ferry dock. Food must be stored in hard containers or suspended to prevent wildlife access. Camping is limited to 14 calendar days per campground from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day. The island has no stores, food service, or medical facilities, and emergency response times can range from hours to days.

location.directions: From Traverse City, take M-22 north to Suttons Bay, then west on M-204 toward Leland. At the junction of M-22 and M-204, turn north to Leland. The Manitou Island Transit ferry departs from Fishtown Dock in Leland for the 1.5-hour trip to South Manitou Island. The campground is less than one mile from the island dock.

alerts.title: North Manitou Island village and dock are closed for the 2025 season
alerts.content: The North Manitou Island village and dock are closed for the 2025 season due to construction of a new dock. The island remains open for camping via access by private boat and CUA holders.

alerts.title: Ironman Triathlon: Sunday, September 14, 2025
alerts.content: Road closures on SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 14. The race takes place on M-22 and will have a significant impact on local traffic. M-22 will be closed between Esch Road and Frankfort until 2 pm. Lake Michigan Road will not be accessible during the race.

payload.name: Mccubbins Gulch Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 15 through September 30. The OHV trail system closes December 1 through March 31 to protect winter range for deer and elk, and may close temporarily during fire season.
payload.short_description: Rustic OHV campground in Mount Hood National Forest with shady creekside sites, vault toilets, and direct access to 72 miles of ATV and motorcycle trails.
payload.medium_description: McCubbins Gulch Campground is a rustic, no-frills campground within the McCubbins Gulch OHV riding area on the eastern edge of Mount Hood National Forest. Many of the shady sites sit adjacent to a creek. The campground caters primarily to off-highway vehicle enthusiasts riding Class 1 (quads) and Class 3 (single-track) trails. Amenities are limited to vault toilets and picnic tables; there is no potable water and campers must pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
McCubbins Gulch Campground is a rustic, primitive campground located within the McCubbins Gulch OHV riding area on the eastern slopes of Mount Hood National Forest, near the boundary with Warm Springs Tribal Lands. The campground offers shady sites, many positioned alongside a small creek, providing a base camp for OHV riders exploring approximately 72 miles of designated trails open to Class 1 (quads) and Class 3 (single-track motorcycles). Full-size 4x4s and side-by-sides over 50 inches wide are not permitted on the trail system.

Facilities are minimal: vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but there is no potable water, trash service, or hookups. Campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all garbage. The 25-foot vehicle length limit makes this campground unsuitable for large RVs. Expect to hear and see OHV activity throughout your stay.

The campground is operated by concessionaire Alaska Recreational Management. Note that the adjacent Warm Springs Reservation is private tribal land; do not trespass. Oregon OHV permits and safety education cards are required for trail use.

location.directions: From Maupin, OR, drive about 23 miles west on County Road 216, then 2 miles northeast on Forest Road 2110.

links.title: USFS McCubbins Gulch Campground & Day Use

payload.name: Aquarius Campground And Purple Beach Group Site
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. Opens May 24, 2026 and operates through October 14. Potable water typically becomes unavailable after September 30. All sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground with 9 developed sites and 2 group sites on the North Fork Clearwater River, offering swimming, fishing, tubing, and access to Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Aquarius Campground sits at 1,700 feet elevation on the banks of the North Fork Clearwater River in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. The campground features 9 individual sites and 2 group sites (Purple Beach), with picnic tables and seasonal potable water. Popular activities include swimming, fly fishing, tubing, and whitewater rafting during May and June when water levels are high.
payload.long_description:
Aquarius Campground occupies a scenic riverside location along the North Fork of the Clearwater River in north-central Idaho. The developed campground offers 9 individual campsites and 2 group sites known as Purple Beach, all situated at approximately 1,700 feet elevation. Each site includes a picnic table, and potable water is available during the operating season until late September.

The North Fork Clearwater corridor provides exceptional water-based recreation. Swimming, fly fishing, tubing, and whitewater rafting are popular activities, with rafting conditions best during May and June when snowmelt raises water levels. Anglers will find quality fishing opportunities throughout the corridor.

Hiking trails near the campground access the Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area and lead to Black Mountain summit, one of the few remaining places in Idaho where mountain goats can still be observed. Hunters and families alike find this campground a quiet basecamp for exploring the surrounding backcountry.

location.directions: Access via Forest Road 247 from Headquarters or Forest Road 250 from near Pierce, Idaho.

links.title: Aquarius Campground and Purple Beach Group Site

payload.name: Petoskey Dunes Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. The park recently reopened after completing major sewer system upgrades and infrastructure improvements. Reservations are available through MiDNRReservations.com.
payload.short_description: Modern campground on Little Traverse Bay with 80 electric sites, flush toilets, showers, and beach access along a mile of Lake Michigan shoreline.
payload.medium_description: Petoskey-Dunes Campground occupies the north end of Petoskey State Park on Little Traverse Bay. The 80 modern sites are smaller and better suited for tent camping and compact RVs, each equipped with electric hookups, a fire ring, and picnic table. Flush toilets, showers, and potable water are available in the campground, with a dump station near the park entrance. The campground provides direct access to a mile of sandy Lake Michigan beach and the Old Baldy Trail.
payload.long_description:
Petoskey-Dunes Campground is the northernmost of two campgrounds within Petoskey State Park, located on the shores of Little Traverse Bay three miles northeast of downtown Petoskey. The 80 modern sites are intentionally smaller and more intimate, designed primarily for tent camping, vans, and compact trailers rather than large RVs. Each site includes 20- or 30-amp electric service, a fire ring, and a picnic table. The campground building contains flush toilets and four shower stalls, with potable water available throughout.

The park features a mile of sandy beach along Lake Michigan, accessible via a short walk from the north end of the Dunes loop. The Old Baldy Trail offers a half-mile loop with scenic views of Little Traverse Bay and the surrounding dunes. A seasonal concession at the beach house offers food, ice cream, and equipment rentals including kayaks, paddleboards, and bikes from Memorial Day through Labor Day.

Petoskey State Park recently completed major infrastructure improvements connecting the sanitation facilities to the city sewer system. Reservations are handled through MiDNRReservations.com. The nearby Little Traverse Wheelway provides 26 miles of paved trail for biking and walking between Charlevoix and Harbor Springs.

location.directions: From Petoskey, take US-31 north to M-119. Turn left on M-119 and continue approximately 1.5 miles. The park entrance is on the left at 2475 M-119 Highway.

payload.name: Mont Alto State Park
payload.status_description: The park is open year-round for day-use activities, sunrise to sunset. No overnight camping is available at this location. The reservable pavilion is available for group events. For overnight camping, nearby Caledonia State Park or Michaux State Forest offer camping facilities.
payload.short_description: Historic 24-acre day-use park in Franklin County featuring a unique pavilion, picnicking, playground, and trout fishing along Antietam Creek. No overnight camping available.
payload.medium_description: Mont Alto State Park is Pennsylvania's oldest state park still in the system, designated in 1902. This small 24-acre day-use park in southeastern Franklin County offers a historic pavilion for group events, picnic facilities, a playground, hiking trails, and trout fishing on Antietam Creek. There is no overnight camping at this location; nearby Caledonia State Park and Michaux State Forest offer camping options.
payload.long_description:
Established in 1902, Mont Alto State Park holds the distinction of being the oldest park still in Pennsylvania's state park system. This compact 24-acre park sits in southeastern Franklin County near the town of Mont Alto, surrounded by the Michaux State Forest. The park's centerpiece is a unique historic pavilion available for group rentals and events.

The park provides day-use facilities including picnic areas, a playground, restrooms with pit toilets, and hiking trails. Antietam Creek runs through the park offering trout fishing opportunities. Winter activities include access to snowmobiling trails in the adjacent state forest.

Mont Alto State Park does not offer overnight camping. Campers seeking nearby accommodations should consider Caledonia State Park approximately 6 miles north, which has tent and RV sites with modern amenities, or the Michaux State Forest which offers primitive and motorized camping options.

location.directions: Located on PA Route 233 in Mont Alto, Franklin County, Pennsylvania. The park is approximately 6 miles south of Caledonia State Park.

address.full: 35 Rocky Mountain Rd S, Mont Alto, PA 17237

links.title: PA DCNR Mont Alto State Park

payload.name: Capitol Reef Np Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open mid-April through mid-October. Closed every Tuesday and Wednesday for maintenance. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. No first-come, first-served availability.
payload.short_description: Group campsite at Capitol Reef's Fruita area with flush toilets, potable water, fire pit, covered pavilions, and space for up to 40 people. Reservations required.
payload.medium_description: Capitol Reef's Group Campsite sits near Loop C of Fruita Campground in the historic Fruita district, offering a semi-shaded grassy setting at the base of striking red rock cliffs. The site accommodates up to 40 people with two covered pavilions, designated tent pads, flush toilets, potable water, a fire pit, and an above-ground grill. Vehicles longer than 27 feet cannot turn around.
payload.long_description:
Capitol Reef's Group Campsite provides a semi-shaded, grassy retreat in the park's historic Fruita district, surrounded by towering red rock cliffs and historic orchards along the Fremont River at approximately 5,500 feet elevation. The site is designed for organized groups of up to 40 people and 10 vehicles, with two covered pavilions for gatherings, designated tent pads, restrooms with flush toilets, potable water faucets, a utility sink, a fire pit, and an above-ground grill.

The location offers easy walking access to Fruita Campground's amenities, the amphitheater, picnic areas, and trailheads for hikes like Capitol Gorge and Goosenecks. The nearby Gifford Homestead store and museum showcases Mormon pioneer history, and the surrounding orchards allow fruit picking when in season. Generator use is restricted to 8-10am and 6-8pm.

Reservations are required through Recreation.gov on a 12-month rolling basis. The site is limited to vehicles 27 feet or shorter, as longer vehicles cannot turn around. Trucks with trailers count as two vehicles toward the 10-vehicle maximum.

location.directions: From Interstate 70 westbound, take Utah Highway 24 west at exit 149 toward Hanksville, continuing 80 miles to the park Visitor Center. The Group Campsite is approximately one mile south of the Visitor Center near Loop C of Fruita Campground.

address.full: 719 S Fruita Farm Rd, Torrey, UT 84775

photos.name: Turn off from Scenic Drive southbound to access Group Area.
Entrance to Group Area from Scenic Drive.
Turn off to access Group Area
Dirt road leading to Group Campsite
The Group Site includes two covered pavilions, designated tent pads, restrooms, grills, fire pits, and an outside sink.
Orchards are the primary remnant of the town of Fruita, as well as a few buildings like the Pendleton Barn.
View of Group Site from one side.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Reef Ride Bike Days 2026- On September 19 and 26, 2026 from sunrise to mid-afternoon the Scenic Drive will be closed to vehicles for this special event. Vehicles will still have access to the Fruita area, including the campground and Gifford House.

payload.name: Ozena
payload.status_description: This campground has been closed indefinitely for many years. It is not listed among active campgrounds on Recreation.gov or current USFS Mt. Pinos Ranger District campground guides. The official USFS campground page redirects to a general recreation page.
payload.short_description: A small primitive campground in Los Padres National Forest on Lockwood Valley Road, historically popular as a hunting camp with trailhead access to the San Rafael Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Ozena Campground is a primitive site located at approximately 3,000 feet elevation on Lockwood Valley Road in Los Padres National Forest. The campground historically served as a popular hunting camp and provides access to hiking trails including the McPhearson Peak Trail and Aliso Trail, which leads to the San Rafael Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Ozena Campground is situated in the Ozena Valley area of Los Padres National Forest, near the Ozena Fire Station just off State Highway 33. The campground sits at approximately 3,000 feet elevation on Lockwood Valley Road and historically offered around 10 primitive campsites shaded by oak trees.

The site has traditionally served as a base for hunters in the fall season and provides trailhead access to the surrounding backcountry. The McPhearson Peak Trail and Aliso Trail begin at or near this location, with the Aliso Park Trail leading approximately 4.76 miles to the San Rafael Wilderness in Santa Barbara County.

The campground offered basic amenities typical of primitive Forest Service sites, including vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables. The entrance road is sandy, requiring appropriate vehicle precautions.

location.directions: From Highway 33, turn east onto Lockwood Valley Road (9N03). The campground is located a short distance east of Highway 33, near the Ozena Fire Station.

payload.name: Timothy Lake- Oak Fork Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for winter. Opens May 22, 2026 for the season, operating through the second full weekend of September. Reservations available through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Timothy Lake in Mt. Hood National Forest offering 36 sites, cabins, and hike-to camping with excellent fishing and boating access.
payload.medium_description: Oak Fork Campground sits on the southeastern shore of Timothy Lake at 3,400 feet elevation in Mt. Hood National Forest. The campground features 36 single-family campsites, six rustic cabins, and eight hike-to tent sites. Each site includes a picnic table and fire grill, with vault toilets and potable water from hand pumps available throughout. Timothy Lake offers kokanee salmon and trout fishing, boating, and a 12-mile loop trail around the lake for hiking, biking, and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Oak Fork Campground occupies a prime spot on the southeastern shore of Timothy Lake, a 1,400-acre reservoir nestled at 3,400 feet in the shadow of Mt. Hood. The surrounding old-growth forest provides a scenic backdrop for camping, with 36 standard single-family sites, six rustic cabins, and eight walk-in tent sites for those seeking a quieter experience. Each campsite is equipped with a picnic table and fire grill, and the campground has accessible vault toilets and drinking water from hand pumps.

Timothy Lake is the main attraction, offering excellent fishing for kokanee salmon, rainbow trout, and brook trout. A 10 mph speed limit keeps motorized boat traffic manageable, making it popular for kayaking, canoeing, and sailing. A large lakeshore parking area serves boaters. The Timothy Lake Trail loops 12 miles around the lake on relatively flat terrain, open to hikers, mountain bikers, and equestrians.

The campground is operated by PGE Parks and Recreation and accepts reservations through Recreation.gov. Day use hours run from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Generators are permitted from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. only. Pets are allowed on leash at tent and RV sites but restricted at most cabin sites. The 32-foot vehicle limit and lack of hookups make this campground better suited for tent campers and smaller RV rigs.

location.directions: From Sandy, OR, travel east on Highway 26 for approximately 40 miles to Skyline Road (Road 42). Turn right on Skyline Road and travel south 9 miles. Turn right on Forest Road 57 for 1 mile, then turn right at the Oak Fork Campground entrance sign.

payload.name: Hurricane River Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground opens May 15, 2026 and operates through October 15. All sites require advance reservations via Recreation.gov; there is no drop-in camping.
payload.short_description: Rustic campground on the Lake Superior shoreline at Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore, split into upper and lower loops with vault toilets, potable water, and trailhead access to the Au Sable Light Station.
payload.medium_description: Hurricane River Campground sits 12 miles west of Grand Marais within Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore. The 21-site campground is divided into two loops: the lower loop (11 sites) provides trailhead access to the Au Sable Light Station, while the upper loop (10 sites) offers a more secluded wooded setting. All sites are rustic with no hookups, but include fire rings, picnic tables, vault toilets, and seasonal potable water.
payload.long_description:
Hurricane River Campground is located along County Road H-58, approximately 12 miles west of Grand Marais in Michigan's Upper Peninsula. The campground is divided into two distinct sections: Hurricane River Upper with 10 sites tucked into deciduous forest, and Hurricane River Lower with 11 sites near the river mouth. Each loop includes one wheelchair-accessible campsite, and sites 4-7 are designated generator-free zones.

The lower campground serves as the trailhead for the Au Sable Light Station, a 3-mile round-trip hike along Lake Superior offering views of Jacobsville sandstone formations and historic shipwreck remains. The campground provides vault toilets, seasonal well water, fire rings with grill grates, and picnic tables at each site. There are no electric, water, or sewer hookups.

Due to limited turning radius and parking space lengths, single vehicles should not exceed 36 feet and vehicle/trailer combinations should not exceed 42 feet. Quiet hours run 8 PM to 8 AM (including generators), checkout is 11 AM, and camping is limited to 14 days per calendar year within the park. All food and scented items must be stored in hard-sided vehicles due to bear activity.

location.directions: From Grand Marais, drive 12 miles west on County Road H-58. The campground entrance is off H-58 with separate access roads for the upper and lower loops.

payload.name: Limekiln Lake
payload.status_description: Open May 15 through September 7, 2026. Reservations available through ReserveAmerica up to 9 months in advance. Some campsites may be closed for restoration work.
payload.short_description: Scenic Adirondack campground on Limekiln Lake with 271 sites, a sandy swimming beach, flush toilets, hot showers, boat launch, and canoe rentals.
payload.medium_description: Limekiln Lake Campground sits on a 463-acre lake in the Adirondack Park near Inlet, NY. The campground offers 271 tent and trailer sites with flush toilets, hot showers, and a dump station. The guarded sand beach, boat launch, and canoe/kayak rentals make this a popular destination for water recreation. Black bears are active in the area and food lockers are provided at sites.
payload.long_description:
Limekiln Lake Campground is a well-established DEC facility located in the heart of the Adirondack Park in Hamilton County, New York. The 271 campsites are spread along the shores of 463-acre Limekiln Lake, offering both tent camping and trailer accommodations with equipment length limits varying by site from 15 to 40 feet. The campground features modern amenities including flush toilets, hot showers, a bathhouse, potable water spigots, and a trailer dump station.

The lake itself is a major draw, with a sandy swimming beach, small boat launch, and canoe/kayak rentals available on-site. Motorboats are permitted. Fishing is popular with yellow perch, bullhead, bluegill, and splake present in the lake. The Old Dam Nature Trail offers a 1.6-mile loop hike, and the campground provides access to the Moose River Plains Wild Forest for more extensive backcountry exploration.

Black bears are active throughout the area and food lockers (bear boxes) are provided at campsites. Firewood and ice are sold at the campground. A picnic area with tables, fireplaces, and a pavilion is available for day use. There are no electrical hookups, WiFi, or camp store.

location.directions: From New York State Thruway (I-90), take Exit 31 at Utica. Head north on Route 12 to Alder Creek, then take Route 28 through Old Forge and Inlet. Just outside of Inlet, turn right on Limekiln Lake Road, then continue 1.5 miles and turn right at the campground sign.

payload.name: Toohey Lake Rustic Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally May 8 through October 1. First-come, first-served with no reservations. No fees. Campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free rustic lakeside campground in Superior National Forest with seven sites, boat launch, and OHV trail access near Tofte, Minnesota.
payload.medium_description: Toohey Lake Rustic Campground offers seven primitive sites on the shores of Toohey Lake in Superior National Forest. The campground features a boat launch, dock, and trailer parking, making it popular with anglers. OHV riders can access trails directly from the campground. No fees, no reservations, and no potable water.
payload.long_description:
Toohey Lake Rustic Campground is a free, seven-site primitive campground located in the Superior National Forest near Tofte, Minnesota. Situated on an easily accessible gravel road (Forest Road 170, "The Grade") that follows an old railroad grade, the campground provides a quiet lakeside experience with a boat launch, dock, and trailer parking for anglers and paddlers.

The campground offers OHV ride-in and ride-out opportunities, making it a convenient base for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts exploring the area. Sites are pull-in style with fire rings and vault toilets, though campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all garbage, including fish remains. Three of the seven sites are longer than 21 feet and may accommodate smaller RVs, though the campground is not specifically designed for RV camping.

Pets are welcome on a leash no longer than six feet. Due to the remote location, campers should come prepared with all supplies and practice Leave No Trace principles. The road is not plowed during winter months.

location.directions: From MN 61 in Tofte: Take County Road 2 (Sawbill Trail) 15 miles north to FR 170 (The Grade). Turn left on FR 170 and drive 5 miles to Toohey Lake. The campground is directly off FR 170 on the right.

payload.name: Millerton Lake North Shore Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Check-in at 2:00 PM, checkout at noon. Reservations via ReserveCalifornia.com or (800) 444-7275. A small section of Blue Oak Trail is currently closed due to storm erosion.
payload.short_description: Group camping at Millerton Lake with two sites (up to 75 people) featuring pit toilets, shared flush toilets and showers, fire rings, and free dump station access on the North Shore.
payload.medium_description: Millerton Lake North Shore Group Campground offers two group camping options in Madera County, about 20 miles northeast of Fresno. The large group site accommodates up to 75 people and 25 vehicles, while the small site holds 40 people and 15 vehicles. Both sites share flush toilets and showers, with on-site pit toilets, fire rings, potable water, and a free dump station at the entrance.
payload.long_description:
Millerton Lake North Shore Group Campground provides dedicated group camping facilities on the Madera County side of the lake, ideal for family reunions, scout troops, or large gatherings. The campground offers two distinct sites: a large group site accommodating up to 75 people with 25 vehicles, and a smaller site for up to 40 people with 15 vehicles. Both sites feature on-site pit toilets with access to shared flush toilets and coin-operated showers between the two group areas.

The campground sits within Millerton Lake State Recreation Area, a popular destination for boating, fishing, and water sports on the 4,900-acre reservoir formed by Friant Dam on the San Joaquin River. The North Shore area includes hiking and multi-use trails, a boat launch facility, and horse camp. Group campers have access to fire rings for campfires, a free dump station, and potable water refill station at the campground entrance.

Reservations are handled through ReserveCalifornia.com or by phone. Check-in is at 2:00 PM and checkout is at noon. During off-season months (October through March), walk-ins may check with the camp host for availability. Summer season visitors will find a park aide at the kiosk to assist with reservations.

location.directions: From Fresno, head 20 miles northeast via Highway 41 and Highway 145 to the North Shore entrance. For GPS navigation, use Plus code 2894+FPP Friant, California.

payload.name: Cascade Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally May through October. First-come, first-served only; no advance reservations. No potable water available on site.
payload.short_description: A quiet 14-site campground in a mixed conifer forest along Highway 108 in Stanislaus National Forest, offering vault toilets and fire rings at each site but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Cascade Creek Campground is a first-come, first-served campground with 14 sites nestled in a mixed conifer forest along Highway 108, about 11 miles east of Pinecrest. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground has vault toilets but no potable water. Dirt roads and parking pads accommodate vehicles, though campers should bring all drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Cascade Creek Campground occupies a peaceful setting in a mixed conifer forest within Stanislaus National Forest. Located on Highway 108 approximately 11 miles from the Summit Ranger Station and east of Pinecrest, the campground offers 14 individual sites along dirt-surfaced roads with dirt parking pads.

Each campsite features a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water on site. Campers must bring their own drinking water. An RV dump station is located 0.25 miles west on Highway 108, and water fill is available at the nearby Strawberry Store.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Check-in is at 2:00 p.m. and check-out is at noon. Quiet hours are enforced from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. Sites are limited to 6 people and a maximum 14-day stay applies. Horses and pack animals are not permitted.

location.directions: 11 miles east of Pinecrest on Highway 108.

payload.name: Washington Monument State Park Youth Group Campground
payload.status_description: The youth group campsites at Washington Monument State Park are closed from April 1 to October 31, 2025, due to reduced services. Day-use areas remain open for visitors.
payload.short_description: Washington Monument State Park in Maryland offers historical landmarks, hiking trails, and scenic views, including the first monument dedicated to President George Washington.
payload.medium_description: Washington Monument State Park, near Middletown, Maryland, features the first monument dedicated to President George Washington and offers access to the Appalachian Trail, a museum, and scenic views.
payload.long_description: Washington Monument State Park, located near Middletown, Maryland, is home to the first monument dedicated to President George Washington. The park offers a rich blend of history and natural beauty, with the Appalachian Trail passing through its grounds. Visitors can explore the 40-foot-tall stone tower, originally built in 1827, and enjoy panoramic views of the surrounding countryside. The park also features a museum showcasing the area's cultural and natural history, providing insights into its significance during the Civil War. While the youth group campsites are closed for the 2025 season, the park remains a popular destination for day-use activities, including picnicking, hiking, and bird watching. The park's proximity to the Appalachian Trail makes it a favored spot for hikers seeking to experience a segment of this iconic trail. Additionally, the park's playground and open spaces offer recreational opportunities for visitors of all ages.

location.directions: From I-70, take Exit 49 for US-40 Alt toward Middletown. Follow US-40 Alt west for approximately 7 miles. The park entrance is on the right, marked by signs for Washington Monument State Park.

payload.name: Target Tree Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the 2026 season, operating May through September. Both reservable and first-come, first-served sites are available. Quiet hours 10pm to 6am. Check-in at 2pm, check-out at noon. Limited to 14 consecutive nights per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: A 28-site campground in the San Juan National Forest near Mancos, featuring historic Ute target trees, an accessible interpretive trail, and easy day-trip access to Mesa Verde National Park.
payload.medium_description: Target Tree Campground sits at 7,643 feet on a south-facing hillside overlooking Thompson Park, between Durango and Mancos off Highway 160. Named for the Ute practice of using Ponderosa pines for target practice and harvesting sap, the campground offers 28 sites including 17 barrier-free accessible sites and three sites with corrals for horse camping. Amenities include potable water, composting vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire grates. The campground serves as an excellent base for exploring Mesa Verde National Park, the Anasazi Heritage Center, and Canyon of the Ancients.
payload.long_description:
Target Tree Campground, also known by its Ute name "IVIKUKUCH," is located 7 miles east of Mancos on a south-facing hillside in the San Juan National Forest at 7,643 feet elevation. The campground takes its name from the historic practice of the Ute Indians, who used Ponderosa pines in the area for target practice and harvested sap and bark as food supplements. A short, accessible interpretive trail allows visitors to view one of these historic scarred trees.

The campground features 28 sites spread beneath Ponderosa pine and Gambel oak forest, with 17 barrier-free accessible sites and three sites with corrals for overnight horse camping. Most sites are shady but can get hot on sunny days, cooling significantly at night. Pull-through sites are available, though most large sites require mechanical leveling for RVs. The maximum RV length is 45 feet.

Amenities include potable water, three accessible composting vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire grates. There are no electrical hookups, dump station, showers, or firewood sales. The campground is known for excellent birding opportunities. Its location makes it ideal for day trips to Mesa Verde National Park, the Anasazi Heritage Center in Dolores, Canyon of the Ancients, and Hovenweep National Monument.

location.directions: From Mancos, take US Highway 160 east for 7 miles. The campground is on the north (left) side of the highway. Turn left at the campground sign and follow the gravel road 0.3 miles to the campground. From Durango, take US Highway 160 west for 20 miles to the campground sign.

links.title: USFS San Juan NF - Target Tree Campground

payload.name: Gates-group Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed for the season. Gates Group typically operates June through September. There is a water system disruption; campers should bring their own water or fill up at nearby French Meadows Campground when the season opens.
payload.short_description: Group campground on the east shore of French Meadows Reservoir in Tahoe National Forest, featuring three reservable group sites near the Granite Chief Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Gates Group Campground sits at approximately 5,200 feet elevation on the east shore of French Meadows Reservoir in Tahoe National Forest. The campground offers three group sites along the North Fork American River: two 25-person sites and one 75-person site. Each site features fire rings, grills, picnic tables, and vault toilets. High-clearance or 4WD vehicles are recommended for access.
payload.long_description:
Gates Group Campground is a reservable group camping area located on the east shore of French Meadows Reservoir within Tahoe National Forest. Situated in a coniferous forest at roughly 5,200 feet elevation, the campground offers proximity to the Granite Chief Wilderness and access to the North Fork American River.

The campground has three group sites: two sites that accommodate up to 25 people with 8 vehicles, and one larger site for up to 75 people with 25 vehicles. All sites can accommodate RVs or tents and feature cooking grills, campfire rings with benches, serving and eating tables, and ample tent space. Vault toilets and piped water are provided.

This is an extremely remote location with no services available nearby. High-clearance or four-wheel-drive vehicles are strongly recommended for navigating the access roads. Campers should arrive with a full tank of gas and be prepared for primitive conditions. Firewood is sold at the campground.
