location.directions: From Foresthill, drive 36 miles east on Mosquito Ridge Road (Forest Road 96). The campground is on the east shore of French Meadows Reservoir.

payload.name: North Tongue
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically opens Memorial Day weekend and operates through Labor Day, weather dependent. The campground is gated during seasonal closures.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground at 8,400 feet in the Bighorn Mountains, located near Burgess Junction where the Medicine Wheel Passage and Bighorn Scenic Byways meet.
payload.medium_description: North Tongue Campground sits on the banks of the North Fork Tongue River at 8,400 feet elevation in the Bighorn Mountains. The 12-site campground offers an excellent base for fishing the river, hiking trails accessing Cloud Peak Wilderness, and exploring the scenic byways. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill, with vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, and trash collection provided.
payload.long_description:
North Tongue Campground is nestled along the North Fork Tongue River and Big Willow Creek in the Bighorn Mountains of Wyoming, where craggy granite peaks rise over 13,000 feet. Located about a mile north of Burgess Junction at 8,400 feet elevation, the campground sits in a lodgepole pine forest interspersed with Engelmann spruce and Douglas fir, providing excellent wildlife habitat.

The 12 standard nonelectric sites each feature a picnic table and campfire ring with grill. The campground provides vault toilets, drinking water from a hand pump, and trash collection. It's particularly popular with anglers fishing the North Fork Tongue River. Nearby Sibley Lake offers non-motorized boating and an accessible fishing dock.

The area offers diverse recreation including OHV trails, scenic jeep roads, and hiking trails ranging from creek-side strolls to mountain peak treks, many accessing Cloud Peak Wilderness. Shell Falls Visitor Center is 22 miles southwest, and the Medicine Wheel National Historic Landmark is 25 miles away.

location.directions: From Dayton, WY, take Highway 14 west for about 27 miles to the junction of Highway 14A. Continue 0.4 miles onto Highway 14A, then turn right onto Forest Road 15 for about 1.1 miles. The campground is on the left.

payload.name: Driftwood Campground - Deschutes
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Tentative opening is June 12, 2026, through September 27, 2026. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. A 14-day consecutive stay limit applies.
payload.short_description: Lakeside tent camping at 6,550 ft elevation on Three Creeks Lake in the Deschutes National Forest, with access to the Tam McArthur Trail and stunning views of the Three Sisters volcanic peaks.
payload.medium_description: Driftwood Campground sits on the shores of Three Creeks Lake, a 28-acre alpine gem nestled in a glacial cirque below Tam McArthur Rim. The campground offers 18 tent-only sites with vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables, but no potable water. Located at the trailhead for the Tam McArthur Trail, campers enjoy easy access to panoramic views of the Three Sisters and excellent shore or non-motorized boat fishing on the lake.
payload.long_description:
Driftwood Campground is the first of four camping facilities around Three Creeks Lake, positioned at an elevation of 6,550 feet in Oregon's Deschutes National Forest. The campground provides direct lakeside access to a scenic alpine lake surrounded by old-growth forest, set within a glacial cirque beneath the dramatic Tam McArthur Rim. The 28-acre lake offers excellent fishing from shore, by wading, or from non-motorized boats launched from a primitive boat ramp on the east shore.

The 18 tent-only sites each include a picnic table and fire ring with grill, served by vault toilets. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own supply. The limited parking spur sizes make this campground unsuitable for RVs or trailers. Driftwood sits at the trailhead for the Tam McArthur Trail, a moderately easy hike offering spectacular views of the Three Sisters: Faith (North), Hope (Middle), and Charity (South), Oregon's third-, fourth-, and fifth-highest peaks.

The campground typically operates from mid-June through late September, with reservations available through Recreation.gov. The nearby town of Sisters provides additional amenities, while the surrounding area offers access to the Sisters Wilderness, Cascade Lakes Scenic Byway, and numerous other recreational opportunities.

location.directions: From Sisters, OR: Travel about 16 miles south on Forest Road 16 (Elm Street in Sisters).

payload.name: Two Mile Prairie Tract Bearhead Hammock Equestrian Primitive Campsites Withlacoochee State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through ReserveAmerica. Prescribed burning may occur; check with WSF Dispatch at (352) 797-4100 before your outing.
payload.short_description: Primitive equestrian campground in Withlacoochee State Forest's Two Mile Prairie Tract with covered horse stalls, vault toilets, and access to 10.5 miles of equestrian trails.
payload.medium_description: Bearhead Hammock is a small primitive equestrian campground in the Two Mile Prairie Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest, Citrus County. Each of the three well-spaced sites features a covered equestrian stall, fire ring, picnic table, and access to 10.5 miles of horse trails. The campground has vault toilets and a hand pump for non-potable water only.
payload.long_description:
Located approximately 10 miles north of Inverness in Citrus County, Florida, Bearhead Hammock Equestrian Primitive Campsites offers a rustic camping experience for horse enthusiasts. The campground sits within the Two Mile Prairie Tract of Withlacoochee State Forest, Florida's third-largest state forest. With only three sites spread a comfortable distance apart, campers enjoy privacy and a peaceful atmosphere.

Each site accommodates up to 8 people and includes a covered equestrian stall, fire ring, picnic table, and space for trailers up to 60 feet. The campground provides vault toilets and a hand pump with non-potable water; campers must bring their own drinking water. There are no electric hookups or bathhouse facilities, making this a true primitive camping experience.

The main draw is access to 10.5 miles of dedicated equestrian trails winding through pine flatwoods and hardwood hammocks. Beyond horseback riding, the area offers hiking, bird watching, wildlife viewing, stargazing, and wildflower viewing opportunities. Note that prescribed burns occur periodically; contact WSF Dispatch at (352) 797-4100 before your outing to check burning schedules.

location.directions: From I-75 Exit 350: Take SR-200 South approximately 3.4 miles, continue as SR-200 SW for about 13.1 miles, then turn right on N Lecanto Highway (C-491) and continue approximately 2.4 miles to reach Bearhead Hammock.

links.title: Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica - Campground Details
Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica - Facility Details

payload.name: Cottonwood Creek Trailhead/campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations accepted. No fee.
payload.short_description: Primitive BLM campground with 5 sites near Bighorn Lake, offering access to the scenic Cottonwood Creek Trail for hiking and horseback riding.
payload.medium_description: Cottonwood Creek Trailhead/Campground is a small, no-fee BLM campground with five primitive campsites near the mouth of Cottonwood Canyon. The campground serves as the trailhead for the 4.5-mile Cottonwood Creek Trail and includes equestrian facilities with four horse corrals and a watering trough. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table, with a toilet facility and food storage boxes available.
payload.long_description:
Cottonwood Creek Trailhead/Campground is a primitive Bureau of Land Management campground located near the eastern shore of Bighorn Lake in Big Horn County, Wyoming. The campground features five campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table, along with a toilet facility, interpretive kiosk, and food storage boxes for bear-safe food storage.

The campground doubles as the trailhead for the Cottonwood Creek Trail, a highly scenic 4.5-mile route winding through BLM, Bighorn National Forest, and State of Wyoming lands. The trail is suitable for hiking and horseback riding, with experienced riders in mind. Equestrian campers will appreciate the four horse corrals and horse watering trough on-site.

Cottonwood Canyon features dramatic vertical cliffs, with elevation ranging from 4,800 feet at the canyon mouth to 7,200 feet at the rim. Wildlife viewing and photography opportunities abound in this rugged landscape adjacent to the Bighorn Canyon National Recreation Area.

location.directions: From Lovell, take Highway 14A east for approximately 10 miles. Immediately after the causeway on the east side of Bighorn Lake, turn left onto John Blue Canyon Road (BLM Road 1122). Take the first road on the right and travel roughly 5 miles to the campground and trailhead.

payload.name: Tate's Hell State Forest High Bluff Primitive Campsites
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through FloridaStateForests.ReserveAmerica.com. Sites have no water, electricity, or restrooms. Check the Florida Burn Ban Dashboard before camping, as drought conditions may restrict campfires.
payload.short_description: Primitive campsites in Tate's Hell State Forest offering secluded tent and RV camping with fire rings and picnic tables across three separate locations in the Florida panhandle.
payload.medium_description: High Bluff Primitive Campsites consist of seven dispersed sites spread across three locations (Dry Bridge, Rake Creek, and Pidcock Road) within Tate's Hell State Forest. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grill but has no water, electricity, or restrooms. The forest offers 35 miles of rivers and creeks for paddling, fishing, and wildlife viewing.
payload.long_description:
Located in the heart of Tate's Hell State Forest in Franklin County, High Bluff Primitive Campsites offer a true backcountry camping experience across three separate locations: Dry Bridge, Rake Creek, and Pidcock Road. Each site accommodates up to 8 people and includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grill, but campers must be fully self-sufficient as there is no water, electricity, or restroom facilities.

Tate's Hell State Forest encompasses over 200,000 acres of flatwoods, swamps, and tidal marshes along Florida's Forgotten Coast. The forest offers excellent opportunities for canoeing, kayaking, fishing, hiking, bird watching, and wildlife photography, with 35 miles of rivers, streams, and creeks to explore. A valid Florida fishing license is required for fishing. The primitive sites are located 18-22 miles west of Carrabelle, accessible via forest roads off SR 65.

location.directions: From SR 65 near Carrabelle: For Pidcock Road site, take North Road 1.75 miles to Dry Bridge Road, then 1.2 miles to Pidcock Road, and continue 1.3 miles to the site. For Rake Creek, take North Road 1 mile then campsite road 0.35 miles. For Dry Bridge, take North Road 0.5 miles to Tucker Road, then 0.67 miles to Dry Bridge Road, and continue 1.3 miles to the site.

payload.name: Aspen Grove Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 15. The campground operates May 15 through September 30, with reservable sites available through Labor Day and walk-in first-come, first-served access only from Labor Day through season end. Fire restrictions may be imposed based on conditions.
payload.short_description: Tent-only campground on the south shore of Eagle Lake in Lassen National Forest, featuring flush toilets, potable water, and direct access to a designated swim beach at 5,100 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Aspen Grove Campground offers 28 tent-only sites nestled in a mature conifer forest with aspens lining the lakeshore at Eagle Lake, California's third-largest natural lake. The campground features flush toilets, potable water, fire rings with grills, and picnic tables at each site. It sits adjacent to the Gallatin Beach swim area and connects to four other campgrounds via a 5.2-mile paved hiking and biking trail.
payload.long_description:
Aspen Grove Campground sits at 5,100 feet elevation in the Eagle Lake Recreation Area of Lassen National Forest, where the Sierra Nevada meets the Cascade Range. The 28 tent-only sites are set among pines and firs, with a strip of aspens separating the camp from Eagle Lake's shoreline. Sites 1-10 are first-come, first-served walk-in sites, while sites 11-28 are reservable through Recreation.gov.

Eagle Lake spans 22,000 acres and is famous for the Eagle Lake Rainbow Trout, a California Heritage Trout species. The lake accommodates swimming, kayaking, waterskiing, and motorboating with no two-cycle engine restrictions. The campground is immediately adjacent to the designated swim area at Gallatin Beach Day Use Area.

A 5.2-mile paved trail connects all five Eagle Lake campgrounds, three day-use areas, and the marina. The marina, about a 10-minute walk from camp, offers a store with gas, propane, supplies, showers, and laundry facilities. Firewood is available for purchase at the campground.

location.directions: From Susanville, California, take Highway 36 west for 2 miles to County Road A-1. Turn north and continue 14 miles to the Eagle Lake Recreation Area. Turn right on Gallatin Road, the first highway you will come to in the lake basin, and follow the signs towards the marina and Aspen Campground.

photos.name: The aspen grove at Aspen Grove Campground, Eagle Lake
Aerial view of the tent camping only grounds

payload.name: Medicine Lake Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Closed for the season and spring project work including hazard tree removal. Traditionally opens late June or July 1 through October. From July 15-21, 2026, the Annual Pit River Tribal Gathering will close all Medicine and Hogue Loop sites; few remaining sites can accommodate large RVs during that period.
payload.short_description: High-elevation lakeside campground in the Medicine Lake Highlands of Modoc National Forest, offering boating, fishing, swimming, and hiking at 6,770 feet.
payload.medium_description: Medicine Lake Recreation Area comprises five campgrounds with 86 total campsites nestled along Medicine Lake in northeastern California's volcanic highlands. The area features vault toilets, water hydrants, and garbage service at most loops. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and barbecue grill. The adjacent day-use area provides a concrete boat ramp, dock, and designated swimming beach. Trails for hiking and mountain biking originate from the recreation area, including the route up Little Mt Hoffman.
payload.long_description:
Medicine Lake Recreation Area sits at 6,770 feet elevation in the Medicine Lake Highlands of Modoc National Forest. The five campgrounds (Medicine, A.H. Hogue, Hemlock, Headquarters, and Schonchin Springs) together offer 86 campsites spread through mature lodgepole pine forest along the lakeshore. Only 15 sites in Medicine and A.H. Hogue loops accept advance reservations through Recreation.gov; the remaining 71 sites are first-come, first-served.

The lake supports trout fishing, motorized boating from a concrete ramp with dock, and swimming at the designated beach adjacent to the picnic area. Hiking and mountain biking trails begin in the recreation area, with the route up Little Mt Hoffman being the longest. The area lies adjacent to the Medicine Lake Lava Flow, accessible via a short hike, and the Glass Mountain and Burnt Lava Flow Geologic Areas are within a 15-minute drive. Lava Beds National Monument, with its extensive lava tube cave system, is about 30 minutes away.

Facilities include vault toilets, water hydrants, and garbage dumpsters at all campgrounds except Schonchin Springs, which has no water or trash service. Each campsite has a picnic table, fire ring, and barbecue grill. Cell reception is limited throughout the area. Site spacing varies from tight, rugged spots to areas more suitable for RVs, though few sites can accommodate large rigs.

location.directions: From McCloud, go east on US Highway 89 for 16 miles to Forest Service Road 15 (Harris Spring Road). Turn left and drive 4.4 miles to Forest Service Road 49 (Medicine Lake Road). Follow signs 27.5 miles to Medicine Lake. From Tulelake, take US Highway 139 south for 21 miles to Forest Service Road 97. Turn right and drive 24 miles, then turn right on Road 49. Drive 2 more miles and turn left into the Medicine Lake Recreation Area entrance.

links.title: Modoc NF Medicine Lake Recreation Area

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **ATTN: The Annual Pit River Tribal Gathering** will occur from July 15th to July 21st; during this timeframe all sites in the Medicine and Hogue Loops will be closed to the public, of the remaining loops in the Medicine Lake Recreation Area, few can accommodate large RVs.

payload.name: East Harbor State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From November 1 through April 1, only electric sites B1-B64 are available. The camp store operates seasonally from April through October. Yurts are available May through mid-October. Reservations required via reserveohio.com or by calling (866) 644-6727.
payload.short_description: Ohio's largest state park campground on Lake Erie with 570+ sites offering full hookups, electric, and primitive options, plus flush toilets, showers, WiFi, and a seasonal camp store.
payload.medium_description: East Harbor State Park Campground is the largest in the Ohio State Park system, located on the shores of Lake Erie near Marblehead. The campground offers over 570 sites including full hookup, electric, non-electric, and ADA-accessible options. Facilities include flush toilets, hot showers, a dump station, fish cleaning station, and a seasonal camp store. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring. The park provides access to a family-friendly Lake Erie swimming beach, marina, boat launch, and 11 miles of multi-use trails.
payload.long_description:
East Harbor State Park Campground sits on 1,831 acres along Lake Erie's southern shore in Ottawa County, Ohio. As the largest campground in the Ohio State Park system, it offers a wide variety of camping options including 23 full hookup sites, over 350 electric sites, and nearly 200 primitive sites. Two Sherman Cabins (one ADA-accessible) and an ADA-accessible yurt are also available. Each campsite comes equipped with a picnic table and fire ring.

The campground features modern amenities including flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and a dump station. Free WiFi is available for registered campers. A seasonal camp store operates from April through October, selling firewood, ice, camping supplies, and ice cream. The facility also includes a boat launch ramp and fish cleaning building for campers.

Recreational opportunities abound with a family-friendly swimming beach on Lake Erie just a short drive or bike ride away. The park offers swimming, boating, fishing, 11 miles of multi-use trails, picnicking, hunting, and disc golf. The marina provides seasonal and day-use dock rentals, fuel, supplies, and a restaurant.

location.directions: Located off Highway 269, approximately 6 miles from Lakeside-Marblehead, Ohio. From the west or north, take Highway 53 to Highway 269. From the south, take Highway 163 to Highway 269. The campground address is 1169 North Buck Road, Lakeside-Marblehead, OH 43440.

address.full: 1169 N Buck Rd, Lakeside Marblehead, OH 43440

payload.name: Sandy Beach Campground
payload.status_description: Open and operating first-come-first-served. Reservable camping begins May 15. Water hookups are available April 15 through October 15; electric hookups are available year-round. Water systems and dump station winterize October 1.
payload.short_description: Sandy Beach Campground offers 32 electric and water hookup sites on the west side of Guernsey State Park, Wyoming, along the scenic Guernsey Reservoir shoreline.
payload.medium_description: Sandy Beach Campground sits on the west side of Guernsey State Park along Guernsey Reservoir. The campground offers 32 utility sites with electric and water hookups, comfort stations, picnic tables, and fire rings. Electric service is available year-round while water service runs April 15 through October 15. The central shower facility near park headquarters operates seasonally with coin-operated showers.
payload.long_description:
Sandy Beach Campground is one of the utility campgrounds at Guernsey State Park, a historic park surrounding Guernsey Reservoir in southeastern Wyoming. The campground features 32 sites equipped with electric and water hookups, making it suitable for RV and trailer camping. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with comfort stations serving the campground area.

Guernsey State Park has long attracted visitors for boating, water skiing, and swimming, with miles of shoreline providing access for water-based recreation. The park also features historic CCC-era structures, a museum, and hiking trails. A coin-operated shower facility is located near park headquarters, and a dump station is available at the park's south entrance.

Electric service remains available year-round, though water service to the campgrounds operates only from April 15 through October 15. All water systems and the dump station close and winterize on October 1. Reservable camping operates May 1 through September 30, with reservations available up to four months in advance through reserve.wyoming.gov or by phone.

location.directions: Located on the west side of Guernsey State Park. The park address is 2187 Lake Side Drive, Guernsey, WY 82214.

payload.name: Windsor State Forest
payload.status_description: Closed to camping until further notice. DCR recommends nearby DAR State Forest as an alternative for camping in western Massachusetts.
payload.short_description: Rustic state forest campground in the northern Berkshires near Windsor Jambs, a scenic 80-foot granite gorge with waterfalls. Currently closed until further notice.
payload.medium_description: Windsor State Forest offers 24 primitive campsites in the northern Berkshires of western Massachusetts. The campground provides a rustic camping experience near Windsor Jambs, a spectacular 80-foot-deep granite gorge featuring rapids and waterfalls. The forest also includes a swimming area with a sandy beach. Currently closed to camping until further notice.
payload.long_description:
Windsor State Forest is located in the northern Berkshires of western Massachusetts, offering a rustic camping experience amidst scenic New England woodlands. The highlight of this state forest is Windsor Jambs, a spectacular 80-foot-deep granite gorge carved by Jambs Brook, featuring stunning rapids and waterfalls that draw hikers and photographers throughout the warmer months.

When operational, the campground features 24 primitive, unserviced tent sites without hookups or modern conveniences. The forest also includes a day-use area with a swimming hole and sandy beach along Windsor Jambs Brook. Picnic facilities and comfort stations are available throughout the park.

The campground is currently closed to camping until further notice. DCR recommends nearby DAR State Forest as an alternative, which offers 50 campsites on a ridge between Highland Lake and scenic wetlands where moose, bear, and beaver are common visitors.

location.directions: From the east via I-90: Take Exit 4 to I-91 north in West Springfield. Take I-91 to Route 9 west. Follow Route 9 to Route 116 in the village of Savoy. From Savoy center, travel 0.5 miles east and turn south onto River Road. Follow River Road for 2.9 miles to the day-use area entrance on the right or campground on the left.

payload.name: Gregory Creek Group Campground
payload.status_description: Opens May 10 for the 2026 season. Operating season runs through September 12. Season dates are subject to change for bald eagle habitat protection per Forest Order 14-58-40. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Call (530) 275-8113 one week before arrival for entry gate code. Check-in 3:00 PM, check-out 12:00 PM. No amplified sound permitted.
payload.short_description: Group campground on Shasta Lake's Upper Sacramento Arm with flush toilets, drinking water, and fire rings. Accommodates up to 100 people and 20 vehicles. Reservations via Recreation.gov.
payload.medium_description: Gregory Creek Group Campground is a single-loop group site on the Upper Sacramento River Arm of Shasta Lake in Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The campground sits in a moderately to thickly wooded setting of oak and pine trees providing 80%+ shade cover. It accommodates up to 100 people and 20 vehicles with trailers up to 24 feet. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring, with flush toilets and drinking water on site. A boat ramp at nearby Antlers provides lake access for fishing, swimming, and watersports.
payload.long_description:
Gregory Creek Group Campground is located adjacent to Gregory Beach along the Upper Sacramento River Arm of Shasta Lake, 15 miles northeast of I-5 in Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The single-loop campground is moderately to thickly wooded with a mix of oak and pine trees that provide plenty of shade during hot summers. The understory consists of manzanita, blackberries, poison oak, tree fern, wild grape, and native grasses.

The group site accommodates up to 100 people and 20 vehicles. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring, and tent pad with paved parking spurs. Flush toilets and drinking water are provided. When lake levels are high, the bank is moderately sloped for water access; as levels drop, steep drop-offs are exposed near Gregory Beach.

A public boat ramp at Antlers is nearby for launching. Lake activities include fishing for trout, catfish, Chinook salmon, crappie, bluegill, sturgeon, and bass, along with swimming, motorized and non-motorized boating, and water skiing. Lake Shasta Caverns tours and the town of Lakehead with restaurants and shopping are also nearby.

location.directions: From I-5, take exit 698 Salt Creek/Gilman Road. Turn left at end of off ramp and follow Salt Creek Road (also known as Gregory Creek Road) for 4 miles. Located adjacent to Gregory Beach dispersed area along the Upper Sacramento River Arm of Shasta Lake, 15 miles northeast of I-5 on Gilman Road.

photos.name: Gregory Creek Sign in the Fall

payload.name: Selkirk
payload.status_description: Opens May 15, 2026 for the season. Operates mid-May through mid-October, weather dependent, closing when roads become snowed in. First-come-first-served only with no advance reservations. Bear closure order in effect requiring bear-resistant food storage.
payload.short_description: Remote high-elevation campground at 10,500 feet in Pike National Forest near Como, Colorado. 15 first-come-first-served sites with vault toilets, fire rings, and tables but no water or trash service.
payload.medium_description: Selkirk Campground sits at 10,500 feet elevation eight miles north of Como in Pike National Forest. The 15 primitive campsites are first-come-first-served only with a maximum trailer length of 25 feet. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and pedestal grill. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water or trash service. Pack out all trash and bring your own water.
payload.long_description:
Selkirk Campground is a remote, high-elevation campground nestled in Pike National Forest at 10,500 feet, approximately eight miles north of the historic mining town of Como, Colorado. The campground offers 15 primitive sites accessible via unpaved forest roads, making it suitable for those seeking a quieter mountain camping experience away from developed facilities.

Each campsite features a picnic table, fire ring, and pedestal grill for cooking. Vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water or trash service, so campers must bring adequate water supplies and pack out all garbage. The maximum trailer length is 25 feet, and sites accommodate up to eight people with a limit of two vehicles or one RV included in the camping fee.

Bears are common in the area and a bear closure order requires all attractants be stored in bear-resistant containers, bear bags, or hard-sided vehicles. Dogs must remain on leash at all times. Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., and the maximum consecutive stay is 14 nights.

location.directions: From Fairplay, travel north on US Highway 285 to Como. Turn left onto County Road 33 and continue to County Road 50. Turn right onto Forest System Road 33 and follow for about 4 miles, then turn left onto Road 33.3A and travel 3/4 mile to the campground.

payload.name: Millerton Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open with restrictions. The campground is accepting reservations for all loops. Meadows Loop and Group Camps operate year-round; Fort Miller, Mono, Rocky Point, Dumna Strands, and Valley Oak loops are open April through September. A section of the Blue Oak Trail is closed due to storm-related erosion. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia.com.
payload.short_description: Millerton Lake State Recreation Area offers tent and RV camping along the 47-mile shoreline of Millerton Lake, featuring full hookup sites, primitive tent camping, group camps, and boat-in camping in California's Sierra Nevada foothills.
payload.medium_description: Millerton Lake State Recreation Area provides diverse camping options along its scenic reservoir shoreline east of Fresno. The campground features six loops ranging from full-hookup RV sites at Meadows Loop to primitive tent camping at Dumna Strands and Valley Oak. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated showers, potable water, and a free RV dump station. The park serves as a hub for boating, swimming, fishing, and hiking with 47 miles of lake shoreline to explore.
payload.long_description:
Millerton Lake State Recreation Area sits in the Sierra Nevada foothills east of Fresno, impounding the San Joaquin River to create a 47-mile shoreline popular with boaters, anglers, and swimmers. The campground spans six distinct loops on the North Shore, each offering a different camping experience. Meadows Loop operates year-round and provides full hookup sites alongside standard sites with access to flush restrooms and coin-operated showers. Fort Miller, Mono, and Rocky Point loops open seasonally from April through September and offer standard sites without hookups but with modern restroom facilities.

For more primitive camping, Dumna Strands and Valley Oak loops provide tent-only sites with chemical toilets. The park also features two group camps accommodating up to 75 and 40 people respectively, plus a horse camp with stalls and RV parking. Temperance Flat offers boat-in camping for up to 25 vessels when water levels permit. Each standard campsite includes a fire ring, and campers should bring their own firewood as none is sold on-site.

The surrounding recreation area provides extensive day-use facilities including multiple picnic areas, swimming beaches, and boat launches. The park features hiking trails including the Blue Oak Trail, portions of which are currently closed due to storm-related erosion. Fishing opportunities include bass, catfish, and trout depending on season. The historic courthouse facility offers educational exhibits about the area's past.

location.directions: From Fresno, take State Route 41 north to State Route 145. Turn east on SR-145 and continue approximately 6 miles to the park entrance at 5290 Millerton Road, Friant.

payload.name: Colorado River Primitive Camping Between Glen Canyon Dam And Lees Ferry
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations. A free Lees Ferry Backcountry River Permit is required, available at the self-serve kiosk at Lees Ferry. Camping limited to 14 consecutive days. Note: The river near Kayak Beach (mile -15.1) is closed annually March 15 through September 1 for osprey breeding season.
payload.short_description: Five primitive boat-in camping beaches along the Colorado River between Glen Canyon Dam and Lees Ferry, accessible only by small watercraft with vault toilets and fire pits at each site.
payload.medium_description: Five designated primitive camping beaches along the 15-mile stretch of the Colorado River between Glen Canyon Dam and Lees Ferry in Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. Sites are accessible only by small boat, located above the river with short walks from the water. Each site has vault toilets and fire pits. First-come, first-served with no fees beyond park entrance and vessel use fees. A free Lees Ferry Backcountry River Permit is required.
payload.long_description:
Along the fifteen-mile stretch of the Colorado River between Glen Canyon Dam and Lees Ferry, five primitive beach camping areas are designated for overnight use. These remote sites can only be reached by small watercraft launched from the Lees Ferry boat ramp, making them ideal for kayakers, rafters, and small motorboat users seeking solitude on the river. Each campsite is marked with signs and sits above the river, requiring a short uphill walk from the beach.

The sites provide basic amenities including vault toilets and fire pits, but campers must be self-sufficient. There is no potable water, so bring all drinking water needed for your trip. Fires are permitted only in provided fireplaces or portable fire pans; ground fires and wood collection are prohibited. All trash must be packed out, though free litter bags are available at the ranger station and dumpsters at the launch ramps.

A free Lees Ferry Backcountry River Permit is required for all watercraft using this section of river, available 24/7 at the self-serve kiosk in the Lees Ferry launch ramp parking lot. Do not boat below the cable downstream from Lees Ferry due to dangerous rapids requiring a separate Grand Canyon National Park permit.

location.directions: Lees Ferry is 42 miles from Page via Hwy 89 south and Hwy 89A west. From the North Rim of the Grand Canyon, it is 85 miles via Hwy 89A and Hwy 67. The Lees Ferry Junction and Park Entrance is in Marble Canyon, just west of Navajo Bridge Interpretive Center. A paved road leads 5 miles to the ferry area. Use the public launch ramp to access the river, then motor or paddle to one of the five marked camping sites.

links.title: Colorado River Primitive Camping Between Glen Canyon Dam and Lees Ferry Official Website

photos.name: Ferry Swale is one of five designated camping sites upriver of Lees Ferry
Ferry Swale is an easy landmark to help find the camp site
The view is pretty nice when you motor or paddle up to one of the designated camping sites

payload.name: Porcupine Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via Recreation.gov up to six months in advance. Maximum 5-night stay. Summer access requires high-clearance 4WD vehicle. Winter access requires skiing, snowshoeing, or snowmobiling 2-3 miles from the end of the maintained road. Check-in 2:00 PM, check-out noon.
payload.short_description: Historic 1914 Forest Service cabin in the Crazy Mountains foothills at 6,400 feet, offering year-round rustic lodging with views of Shields Valley and the Bridger Mountains.
payload.medium_description: Porcupine Cabin is a historic 1914 rental cabin in the Custer Gallatin National Forest, remodeled by the CCC in 1934. The rustic cabin sleeps up to 8 on bunk beds with mattresses, features a wood heating stove and propane lantern, and includes a vault toilet. No potable water or electricity. Summer access requires high-clearance 4WD; winter access requires skiing, snowshoeing, or snowmobiling 2-3 miles from the maintained road.
payload.long_description:
Porcupine Cabin sits in the foothills of the Crazy Mountains at 6,400 feet elevation, overlooking the grasslands of Shields Valley with views of the Bridger Mountains and the northern Crazy Mountain peaks. Built in 1914 after a previous structure burned, the cabin was remodeled by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934 and historically served as temporary housing for Forest Service rangers patrolling for timber poachers, watching for fires, and monitoring livestock.

The cabin accommodates up to 8 guests on bunk beds with mattresses. Amenities include a wood heating stove, propane lantern, table and chairs, screened front porch, and an outdoor campfire ring with benches. A vault toilet outhouse is located behind the cabin. Guests must bring their own drinking water, bedding, cooking gear, food, toilet paper, and flashlights. Firewood is provided in winter; summer guests must bring or gather their own.

The nearby trailhead provides access to hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian trails heading east into the Crazy Mountains. Winter visitors can cross-country ski or snowshoe the same trails. Wildlife in the area includes deer, moose, bears, elk, bald eagles, and various mountain bird species.

location.directions: From Livingston, Montana, travel north on Highway 89 to Wilsall. Just north of Wilsall, turn northeast onto Shields River Road. Continue 8 miles to Porcupine Road, turn east (right) and drive another 8 miles to the cabin. High-clearance 4WD recommended. In winter, the last 2-3 miles are not plowed.

photos.name: Views to the southwest of Porcupine
Field of flowers at Porcupine Cabin

payload.name: Wickiup Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Operates May 1 through October 31. All sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations. No potable water available; campers must bring their own. Pack out all trash. 14-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: Primitive 6-site campground along Canyon Creek in Malheur National Forest, offering shaded streamside camping, fishing, and access to hiking and wildlife viewing.
payload.medium_description: Wickiup Campground sits tucked among trees next to Canyon Creek on Forest Road 15, about 17 miles south of John Day. The shaded, streamside setting provides a peaceful base for fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing. All six sites are first-come, first-served with vault toilets but no potable water. Pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Wickiup Campground occupies a quiet spot along Canyon Creek in the Blue Mountain Ranger District of Malheur National Forest. The six standard nonelectric sites are nestled among trees, offering welcome shade during summer months and the soothing sound of the creek flowing past. Stream fishing is popular here, and the campground serves as a convenient starting point for hiking and wildlife viewing.

This is a primitive campground with vault toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. There is no trash service; pack it in, pack it out. Sites accommodate tents, RVs, trailers, and fifth wheels up to 50 feet with back-in gravel driveways. The area sees no cell phone coverage, though Verizon works in nearby Canyon City.

During winter, the campground entry serves as a popular staging area for snowmobile riders. Horses are prohibited within the campground perimeter except for loading and unloading, and must not be pastured on Wickiup Creek or the riparian area.

location.directions: From John Day, OR, travel south on US Highway 395 approximately 10 miles to the junction with County Road 65. Follow County Road 65 approximately 7 miles; the campground will be on the right.

payload.name: Deep Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Check-in at 1:00 PM, checkout at noon. Office may operate intermittently November through April. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive days.
payload.short_description: Primitive streamside campground in Great Smoky Mountains National Park with 92 sites near waterfalls and tubing opportunities on Deep Creek, 3 miles from Bryson City, NC.
payload.medium_description: Deep Creek Campground offers 92 primitive sites along one of the most popular creeks in Great Smoky Mountains National Park. Each site includes a grill, picnic table, and fire ring. Flush toilets and potable water are available, but there are no showers or hookups. The campground is ideal for creek access with fishing, wading, and tubing. Two waterfalls are accessible via an easy 1.6-mile hike from the trailhead.
payload.long_description:
Located near Bryson City on the North Carolina side of Great Smoky Mountains National Park, Deep Creek Campground provides 92 individual campsites in a forested setting alongside Deep Creek. The campground operates year-round and requires advance reservations through Recreation.gov. Sites accommodate tents and RVs without hookups, with site dimensions varying throughout the campground.

Deep Creek is renowned for water recreation. The creek runs along the campground edge, offering easy access for fishing, wading, and tubing during warmer months. Brook and rainbow trout inhabit the stream. The campground serves as a base for hiking to Tom Branch Falls and Indian Creek Falls via an easy 1.6-mile loop trail.

The area experiences high bear activity, averaging 339 negative bear-human encounters annually. All food and scented items must be stored properly. Only USDA-certified heat-treated firewood is permitted. Pets must remain leashed at 6 feet maximum and are not allowed on park trails. Generator use is restricted to 8 AM-8 PM, with quiet hours from 10 PM to 6 AM.

location.directions: From downtown Bryson City, NC, follow signs to Deep Creek. The campground is approximately 3 miles from town at 1912 East Deep Creek Road.

photos.name: River Tubes are considered “vessels” by the NPS and the State of NC, therefore children 13 and under are required to wear PFD’s.  Over age 13, PFDs are highly recommended.  Close-toed shoes and helmets are strongly recommended.

payload.name: Lodi Point Marine State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round, dawn to dusk. This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. Marina and transient slips available April 1 through October 23.
payload.short_description: Day-use boat launch and picnic site on Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes region. No overnight camping available.
payload.medium_description: Lodi Point Marine State Park is a modest day-use facility on Seneca Lake offering boat launching, a marina with seasonal and transient slips, a playground, grills, and one reservable pavilion. The park serves boaters, picnickers, and anglers but does not provide overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Lodi Point Marine State Park is a compact day-use facility situated on the eastern shore of Seneca Lake in New York's Finger Lakes region. The park primarily serves as a boat launch and picnic area with modest accommodations for boaters, anglers, and day visitors.

Facilities include multiple boat launches, a marina offering both seasonal slips (April 1 through October 23) and transient docking, a playground, charcoal grills, and one pavilion available for day-use reservation accommodating up to 20 people. The park has restroom facilities and parking. There are no showers, dump station, or hookups.

This is strictly a day-use facility. No overnight camping is available at Lodi Point. The park is open year-round from dawn to dusk, with vehicle entry fees collected on weekends and holidays from late May through early September.

location.directions: Located on Lower Lake Road in Lodi, NY 14860, on the eastern shore of Seneca Lake.

payload.name: Dumont Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. No advance reservations. Payment is cashless via the Recreation.gov Scan & Pay app only. No potable water; campers must bring their own. Pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Secluded 3-site primitive campground at the confluence of Dumont Creek and the South Umpqua River, featuring a trail to a rocky beach perfect for wading.
payload.medium_description: Dumont Creek Campground offers a tranquil escape in Umpqua National Forest with just three campsites near the confluence of Dumont Creek and the South Umpqua River. A short trail leads to a small, rocky beach ideal for wading. This primitive campground has vault toilets and fire rings but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supplies and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Tucked away in the Umpqua National Forest, Dumont Creek Campground provides an intimate camping experience with only three sites near where Dumont Creek meets the South Umpqua River. The small size virtually guarantees solitude, and a short trail from camp leads to a rocky beach on a calm stretch of river perfect for wading and cooling off on summer days.

This is a primitive, first-come first-served campground. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring, and vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water on site. Campers must bring all drinking water and pack out all trash. The campground is open year-round and uses a Scan & Pay system via the Recreation.gov app; cash and checks are no longer accepted. OHV/ATV use is prohibited, and cell coverage is nonexistent.

location.directions: From Canyonville, OR, turn off Southeast Main Street onto Southeast 3rd Street / OR-227. Continue on OR-227 for approximately 23 miles until reaching the town of Tiller, OR. Turn left onto County Road 46 (South Umpqua Road 28) and continue for approximately 12 miles. The campground is on the right side of the road.

payload.name: Crystal Lake Legion State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Open April 1 through December 1 (snow conditions permitting). Reservations required and can be made same-day or up to 11 months in advance via wisconsin.goingtocamp.com or 1-888-947-2757. Maximum 14-night stay. Pets allowed in campground but prohibited on the shoreline.
payload.short_description: Scenic modern campground on Crystal Lake in Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest featuring 101 wooded sites, flush toilets, showers, and a swimming beach.
payload.medium_description: Crystal Lake Campground offers 101 reservable sites (401-501) in the heart of Wisconsin's largest state forest. The modern campground features flush toilets with showers, vault toilets, hand-pumped drinking water, a dump station, and a swimming beach. Walk-to tent sites and double campsites are available. The entire shoreline is a designated beach with no pets or motorized boats allowed on the lake.
payload.long_description:
Crystal Lake Campground is the most popular facility in the 232,000-acre Northern Highland-American Legion State Forest, located in Vilas County near Woodruff. The campground offers 101 wooded sites numbered 401-501, including walk-to tent-only sites (415-418, 421-423) and double campsites (439-440, 484-485, 497-498, 499-500) that accommodate up to 12 people.

Facilities include five vault toilet buildings, one flush toilet building with showers, three hand pumps for drinking water, a sanitary dump station, and trash/recycling dumpsters. A small craft boat landing provides lake access, and a large marked swimming beach with picnic area is nearby. The campground connects to paved bike trails and a nature center with hard-surfaced nature trail.

Crystal Lake's entire shoreline is designated as a beach, so pets are not allowed anywhere along the water. Motorized boats are prohibited on the lake, making it ideal for paddling and swimming. Sites 463 and 438 are ADA-accessible. Firewood is available for purchase at the campground.

location.directions: From the intersection of Highways 51 and 47 in Woodruff, travel Highway 51 north 6.2 miles to Highway M. Turn right on Highway M and drive 2.7 miles to Highway N. Turn right on Highway N and travel 2 miles; the Crystal Lake Visitor Station entrance is on the left.

payload.name: Swanson Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for hazard tree removal. Normal operating season is May through September.
payload.short_description: Shaded pine campground near Shaver Lake in Sierra National Forest with vault toilets, fire rings, and tables at each site. No potable water available.
payload.medium_description: Swanson Campground sits beneath dense pine trees just 3 miles from Shaver Lake in Sierra National Forest. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. A vault toilet is provided but campers must bring their own water. The nearby town of Shaver Lake offers restaurants, gas, and supplies. Maximum vehicle length is 25 feet.
payload.long_description:
Swanson Campground offers a quiet, shaded retreat in the pine forests of Sierra National Forest, located approximately 3 miles from the recreational hub of Shaver Lake. The campground provides basic amenities typical of national forest sites: vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings with grills at each campsite. A campground host is present during the operating season.

Potable water is not available, so campers must bring an adequate supply. The nearby town of Shaver Lake provides convenient access to restaurants, fuel, groceries, and fishing supplies. Popular activities in the area include fishing, boating, swimming, and hiking at Shaver Lake.

Access is via paved and dirt roads off Dinkey Creek Road. The campground enforces a 25-foot maximum vehicle length, 14-day stay limit, and 6-person maximum per site. Single sites are $32 per night and double sites are $61 per night.

location.directions: Take Highway 168 east from Clovis toward Shaver Lake. Before reaching the town, turn right onto Dinkey Creek Road. Travel 3 miles east to Swanson Campground.

address.full: 46429 Dinkey Creek Rd, Shaver Lake, CA 93664

payload.name: Grass Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water and shower facilities operate May through October only. Reservations required for all sites via Reserve Minnesota (reservemn.usedirect.com) and can be made up to 120 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground within Maplewood State Park offering 71 drive-in sites with optional electric hookups, flush toilets, showers, and direct access to Grass Lake and 27 miles of hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Grass Lake Campground occupies the eastern shore of Grass Lake within Maplewood State Park, one of Minnesota's largest state parks at 9,250 acres. The campground consists of three loops: Main Loop with 50-amp electric hookups, and Knoll and Hollow loops without electricity. All sites include a fire ring with grill and picnic table. An accessible shower building serves the campground, and a dump station is available for RVs.
payload.long_description:
Grass Lake Campground serves as the primary camping area within Maplewood State Park, situated on the eastern edge of Grass Lake in Otter Tail County. The campground features 71 drive-in sites spread across three distinct loops. The Main Loop offers 32 sites with 50-amp electrical hookups, while the Knoll and Hollow loops provide non-electric camping. Two ADA-accessible campsites and an accessible shower building accommodate campers with mobility needs.

Maplewood State Park encompasses 9,250 acres of rolling hills and hardwood forests dotted with eight major lakes and numerous smaller ponds. Grass Lake itself is popular among panfish anglers. Twenty-seven miles of hiking trails wind through the park, with several connecting directly to the campground. The park's namesake maples produce spectacular fall foliage, making autumn a particularly scenic time to visit.

All campsites include a fire ring with cooking grill and a picnic table. The campground provides flush toilets, drinking water, hot-water showers (fee-based), trash collection, and an RV dump station. Sites can accommodate RVs and trailers up to 50 feet in length. The campground operates year-round, though water and shower facilities are only available from May through October.

location.directions: From Pelican Rapids, drive east on MN Highway 108 for approximately 8 miles. Turn left onto Park Entrance Road and follow signs to the campground.

address.full: 38384 Beers Lake Rd, Pelican Rapids, MN 56572

payload.name: Sherando Lake Group Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates from early April through late October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Potable water is available April 1 through October 31.
payload.short_description: Tent-only group campground in the Blue Ridge Mountains at Sherando Lake Recreation Area, ideal for scouts, church groups, and family gatherings with up to 75 campers across five sites.
payload.medium_description: Sherando Lake Group Camp offers five tent-only group sites in George Washington National Forest, each accommodating up to 15 people. Sites include picnic tables, grills, serving tables, and lantern posts. A bathhouse with flush toilets and showers serves the upper loop, with a vault toilet at the lower end. Drinking water is available at each site. The campground sits near the 7-acre upper lake with access to hiking trails leading to the Blue Ridge Parkway.
payload.long_description:
Sherando Lake Group Camp is located at the upper end of the Sherando Lake Recreation Area in Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains, often called the jewel of the Blue Ridge. The campground features five distinct tent-only sites arranged around a loop road, with a large grassy common area in the center suitable for group activities and stargazing. Each site is fenced and equipped with picnic tables, a charcoal grill, serving table, and lantern posts.

The recreation area offers a 25-acre lower lake with a sandy swimming beach, accessible ramp to the water, and bathhouse with changing facilities. The 7-acre upper lake near the group camp provides fishing-only access with stocked trout during spring and fall seasons. Hiking options range from easy lakeside walks on the Cliff Trail to challenging day hikes up the Blue Loop Trail to Bald Mountain.

RVs, pop-ups, and camper vans are not permitted in the group camping area. Food must be secured in a locked vehicle due to bear activity. Cell coverage is unreliable throughout the area.

location.directions: From I-64, take Exit 96 just east of Stuarts Draft. Go south on State Route 624, which becomes State Route 664 at Lyndhurst. Continue south on State Route 664 approximately 8 miles to the entrance for Sherando Lake Recreation Area on the right. The gatehouse is approximately 0.5 miles ahead. Continue through the recreation area to the group camping area at the end of the road.

photos.name: Group Camp Sites G5, G4, and G3.
Group camp sites G1 and G2.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Tent camping only in Group Camping.** RVs, Pop - Ups and Camper Vans are not authorized to camp in Group Camping.

payload.name: WHITE PINES GROUP CAMPGROUND
payload.status_description: Open year-round for tent camping. Potable water is currently unavailable; campers must bring their own water supply. Reservations required through Recreation.gov. Note: dispersed camping within 1000 feet of roads is prohibited on the Pisgah Ranger District until September 1, 2026, but this established campground remains open.
payload.short_description: Walk-in tent-only group campground in Pisgah National Forest accommodating up to 25 people, featuring vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables along Avery Creek.
payload.medium_description: White Pines Group Campground is a walk-in tent-only facility on the Pisgah Ranger District of Pisgah National Forest in Western North Carolina. The single group site can accommodate up to 25 campers, making it ideal for scout troops, family reunions, and organized groups. Located at approximately 2,600 feet elevation along Avery Creek, the site offers access to hiking, fishing, and swimming in one of the most scenic areas of the southern Appalachians.
payload.long_description:
White Pines Group Campground is a primitive walk-in tent camping facility situated in the lush hardwood forests of the Pisgah Ranger District in Pisgah National Forest. The campground features one group site that can accommodate up to 25 people, with parking provided in a separate lot. All equipment must be walked into the campsite.

The site is equipped with vault toilets, picnic tables, lantern posts, and campfire rings with grills. Drinking water is currently unavailable, so campers must bring an adequate supply. Visitors are responsible for packing out all trash. The campground sits at approximately 2,600 feet elevation adjacent to Avery Creek, with the Davidson River nearby offering excellent trout fishing opportunities.

Reservations are handled through Recreation.gov and managed by Naventure. The area provides access to numerous recreation opportunities including day hiking, swimming, mountain biking, and fishing in one of North Carolina's most scenic mountain regions.

location.directions: From Brevard, take US 276 east approximately 1.75 miles, then turn right onto Forest Road 477 and continue 0.75 miles. Parking is on the right; walk across the bridge to the campground entrance.

address.full: 5119 N Mills River Rd, Mills River, NC 28759

links.title: Recreation.gov White Pine South Group Camp

payload.name: Timothy Lake- The Cove Day Use Area
payload.status_description: This is a day-use area only with no overnight camping. Currently closed for the season; opens May 22, 2026. Operating hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic and swim area on Timothy Lake in Mount Hood National Forest. No overnight camping permitted.
payload.medium_description: The Cove Day Use Area is a scenic shoreline picnic spot on Timothy Lake in Mount Hood National Forest. The site offers swimming, fishing, and serves as a trailhead for nearby hiking trails. No overnight camping is allowed; the area operates from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily during the open season.
payload.long_description:
The Cove Day Use Area sits along the western shore of Timothy Lake in Oregon's Mount Hood National Forest. This popular day-use site offers picnicking beneath towering conifers, swimming in clear mountain waters, and shore fishing for trout and kokanee salmon. The area also serves as a base for exploring nearby hiking and biking trails, including access to the Timothy Lake Trail system.

This is strictly a day-use facility with no overnight camping permitted. Visitors will find vault toilets and picnic tables, but no potable water is available. There is no boat ramp at The Cove; watercraft access is available at nearby Pine Point Day Use Area. The site is operated by Portland General Electric in partnership with the US Forest Service.

location.directions: From Sandy, OR, travel east on US 26 for approximately 40 miles to Skyline Road (Forest Road 42). Turn right and travel south 9 miles. Turn right on Forest Road 57 and travel west 2 miles to The Cove Day Use Area entrance.

links.title: USFS Cove Day Use Area Page

payload.name: Boundary Creek Yurt
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The yurt operates during winter months only when snow conditions allow ski or snowshoe access. Reservations for the upcoming winter season open the last Monday of October through the Evanston Recreation Center.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry ski-in yurt at 9,550 feet in the High Uintas, 6.5 miles from the Lily Lake trailhead. Wood stove, bunks for 4-6, and white gas cooking stove provided.
payload.medium_description: Boundary Creek Yurt is the most remote of the five BRORA yurts in the High Uintas, located 2 miles beyond Ridge Yurt at 9,550 feet elevation. The 16-foot yurt features bunks sleeping 4-6 people, a wood-burning stove with firewood provided, and a white gas cooking stove. Access requires a 6.5-mile ski or snowshoe approach with 1,164 feet of elevation gain. This is a true backcountry experience requiring winter travel skills, proper equipment, and avalanche awareness.
payload.long_description:
Boundary Creek Yurt sits at 9,550 feet in the High Uintas of Utah, offering experienced backcountry skiers and snowshoers access to open slopes ascending to nearly 11,000 feet. As the final and most remote yurt in the Bear River Outdoor Recreation Alliance system, it requires a 6.5-mile approach from the Lily Lake Touring Area near Evanston, Wyoming. The unmarked trail beyond Ridge Yurt is marked only with blue diamonds and is not groomed, often requiring trail-breaking after fresh snow.

The 16-foot yurt accommodates 4-6 people on bunks and includes a wood-burning stove with a supply of firewood for heating, plus a white gas cooking stove for meal preparation. Unlike the lower yurts in the system, Boundary Creek has no propane. This is a carry-in, carry-out facility with no potable water; guests must filter stream water or melt snow.

BRORA operates this yurt in cooperation with the USFS and Boy Scouts of America. Reservations require a $20 BRORA membership and are made through the Evanston Recreation Center. Winter reservations open the last Monday of October. Due to the advanced skills and conditioning required for access, this yurt is recommended only for experienced backcountry travelers with avalanche awareness training.

location.directions: From Evanston, Wyoming, take WY-150 South toward the Lily Lake XC Touring Area. Park at the Lily Lake trailhead. Ski or snowshoe approximately 6.5 miles, passing Lily Lake Yurt, East Fork Yurt, and Ridge Yurt. The trail beyond Ridge Yurt is not groomed and marked with blue diamonds. Boundary Creek Yurt is 2 miles past Ridge Yurt.

payload.name: Massasoit State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from April 30 through October 11. Reservations required via ReserveAmerica; no walk-in camping. Same-day reservations accepted until 2:00 PM.
payload.short_description: Family campground in southeastern Massachusetts offering 84 wooded sites near six ponds, with electric hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, and swimming beach access.
payload.medium_description: Massasoit State Park campground sits within 1,200 forested acres featuring six lakes and ponds in East Taunton, Massachusetts. The 84 campsites include 50 with electric hookups and tent-only options in a generator-free area. Each site has a picnic table, charcoal pedestal grill, and fire ring. Comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers serve all loops. Activities include swimming at the park beach, kayaking, fishing, mountain biking, and hiking.
payload.long_description:
Massasoit State Park campground occupies a scenic section of the 1,200-acre park in southeastern Massachusetts, surrounded by mixed hardwood and pine forest with six ponds and lakes. The campground offers 84 sites across multiple loops: 50 sites with 20/30/50-amp electric hookups, tent-only sites, and a generator-free quiet area. Every site includes a picnic table, charcoal pedestal grill, and fire ring. Comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers are within 300 yards of all sites, and a dump station is available for RVs.

The park provides excellent recreational opportunities including swimming at the main beach (with beach wheelchairs available), kayaking, canoeing, fishing, mountain biking on wooded trails, and hiking. The kettle ponds are remnants of glacial activity and offer calm waters ideal for paddling. The campground draws families and outdoor enthusiasts looking for an accessible state park experience within easy reach of Boston and Cape Cod.

Reservations are required and can be made through the Massachusetts DCR ReserveAmerica system up to four months in advance. Walk-in camping is not permitted. Check-in runs from 1:00 PM to 8:00 PM, checkout by 11:00 AM, with quiet hours from 10:00 PM to 7:00 AM. Pets are allowed with current rabies certificates, limited to four per site.

location.directions: From Boston, take Route 24 South to Exit 14B (Route 44 West). Follow Route 44 West for approximately 3 miles, then turn left onto Middleboro Avenue. The park entrance is on the right.

payload.name: Bicentennial Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required via Recreation.gov up to six months in advance. Maximum stay is three nights per season per camper. No water available on-site.
payload.short_description: Walk-in tent campground in Marin Headlands with three sites nestled in a cypress grove, offering views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco, just minutes from the city.
payload.medium_description: Bicentennial Campground offers a unique camping experience in the Marin Headlands, tucked within a secluded cypress grove with stunning views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco. This small, walk-in tent campground has just three sites, each accommodating up to three people. Located about 200 yards down a moderately steep trail from the parking area, the campground provides picnic tables, barbecue grills, and food lockers at each site. No water is available on-site, and wood fires are prohibited.
payload.long_description:
Bicentennial Campground is the most accessible of the campgrounds in Golden Gate National Recreation Area, located approximately 100 yards from the parking area near Battery Wallace in the Marin Headlands. The campground sits in a secluded cypress tree grove and offers remarkable views of the Golden Gate Bridge and the San Francisco skyline, making it an ideal choice for campers seeking a wilderness experience close to the city.

The campground has three tent-only sites, each accommodating a maximum of three guests. Every site is equipped with a picnic table, barbecue grill, and food storage locker. A portable restroom is located on-site, with a vault toilet available 0.5 miles away at Bicentennial Picnic Area. There is no potable water at the campground, so campers must bring all water needed for drinking, cooking, and cleaning.

Nearby attractions include Point Bonita Lighthouse and the historic Nike Missile Site, both within walking distance. Rodeo Beach is about 1.5 miles away, and the Marin Headlands offers numerous hiking trails with scenic coastal views. The campground is accessible via a 200-yard walk down a moderately steep, packed dirt trail from the parking area.

location.directions: Upon entering the Marin Headlands via the Baker-Barry Tunnel, drive until you reach Field Road. Turn left onto Field Road, drive less than 0.5 miles uphill and make the first left turn you can, followed by a right. Signs for Bicentennial Campground will be visible. Either parallel park on the road or in the small dirt pull-out. The campground is 200 yards down a moderately steep trail from the parking area.

photos.name: Golden Gate Bridge from Bicentennial Campground
Entrance to Bicentennial Campground from Conzelman Road

payload.name: Summit Guard Station Bunkhouse
payload.status_description: Open for reservations May 15 through November 14. Automobile access typically available June 1 through November 1. Winter access requires skis, snowshoes, or snowmobile from Meacham Divide/Mt. Emily Sno-Park (approximately 11.3 miles). Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Historic 1938 CCC-built bunkhouse on a ridge in Oregon's Blue Mountains with exceptional views, propane amenities, and vault toilet. Sleeps 4.
payload.medium_description: Summit Guard Station Bunkhouse is a rustic 1938 Civilian Conservation Corps cabin perched on a high ridge in Umatilla National Forest. The single-room bunkhouse features four beds with mattresses, propane heating, lights, and cooking stove. No water or electricity; visitors must bring their own supplies. A vault toilet is located nearby, and tent camping is permitted in the yard.
payload.long_description:
Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1938, Summit Guard Station Bunkhouse sits on a high ridge overlooking Meacham Canyon in Umatilla National Forest, offering spectacular views of the Blue Mountains including Wilbur Mountain, Spring Mountain, and Sugarloaf Mountain. The site was originally the Summit Ranger Station in 1908, when the land was part of the historic Wenaha National Forest.

The rustic bunkhouse contains a single multi-use room for cooking, sleeping, and relaxing. It's furnished with a table, four chairs, and four bed frames with mattresses (two full and two twin). Propane lights, a propane heater, and a propane range are provided. There is no water or electricity on site, so visitors must bring ample drinking water and supplies. A vault toilet is located a short distance from the cabin, and tent camping is allowed in the yard.

The area is exceptional for bird and wildlife watching, with species including kinglets, sparrows, chickadees, and hummingbirds. Wildflowers such as larkspur, lupine, and orchids bloom in season. The nearby Whitman Route Overlook offers views of Meacham Canyon and the Hell Hole Roadless Area.

location.directions: From Pendleton, OR: Take I-84 east for 34 miles to Exit 243 (Mt. Emily Exit). Turn left at the stop sign, cross the freeway overpass, and proceed to where the pavement ends at Forest Service Road 31. Travel FSR 31 for 12.2 miles to the junction with FSR 3113. Turn left onto FSR 3113 and travel 0.8 miles to the access road to Summit Guard Station. Turn left and follow the road to the right. From Weston, OR: Travel 28 miles east on Highway 204. Turn right onto FSR 31 and go 9.4 miles to Ruckel Junction. Continue on FSR 31 for 17 miles to FSR 3113, turn right, and travel 0.8 miles to the access road.

payload.name: Crystal & Twin Lakes
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservations required May 15 through September 30 via reserve.wyoming.gov. Water systems are operational. No current fire restrictions. Water is shut off annually October 1; visitor center flush toilets and showers remain available year-round.
payload.short_description: Lakeside camping at Curt Gowdy State Park with access to Crystal Reservoir fishing for trout and kokanee salmon. Electric sites available at select campsites.
payload.medium_description: Crystal & Twin Lakes campground sits within Curt Gowdy State Park in the Laramie Mountains foothills. Sites surround Crystal Reservoir, the park's smallest lake, offering shoreline fishing for brown trout, rainbow trout, and kokanee salmon. Boating is permitted with a 15 HP motor limit. Some sites feature electric hookups, and all include a fire ring with grill and picnic table. Flush toilets and showers are available at the visitor center.
payload.long_description:
Crystal & Twin Lakes is one of several camping areas within Curt Gowdy State Park, a 3,395-acre recreation area straddling the Laramie Mountains between Cheyenne and Laramie, Wyoming. The campground clusters around Crystal Reservoir, the smallest of the park's three reservoirs, at elevations between 6,450 and 7,500 feet. The landscape features low-lying meadows, rolling hills, and massive granite formations.

Crystal Reservoir provides excellent shoreline fishing for brown trout, rainbow trout, and kokanee salmon. Small watercraft including kayaks and canoes are welcome, with a 15 HP motor limit. The park has earned recognition for its IMBA-certified mountain bike trail system and offers extensive hiking opportunities.

Sites include fire rings with grills and picnic tables. Select sites (168-171) offer electric hookups. Flush toilets and showers are located at the visitor center, which operates 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily. The park does not have a dump station; the nearest options are the Southeast Wyoming Welcome Center in Cheyenne (free, 24 hours) and Wyoming Territorial Prison near Laramie ($10, seasonal).

location.directions: From Cheyenne, drive 24 miles west on Happy Jack Road (Highway 210). From Laramie, drive 24 miles east on Highway 210. The park entrance is at 1264 Granite Springs Rd.

payload.name: Big Creek Baldy. Lookout Rental
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The lookout typically opens mid-June through late September, road conditions permitting. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is 5 consecutive nights with a required 7-day break before rebooking.
payload.short_description: Historic 52-foot fire lookout tower at 5,780 feet in the Purcell Range with panoramic views of Lake Koocanusa and the Yaak River valley. Sleeps 4 with propane heating and cooking.
payload.medium_description: Big Creek Baldy Lookout is a historic fire observation tower perched at 5,780 feet in the Kootenai National Forest. The 225-square-foot cabin atop the 52-foot tower sleeps four and comes equipped with propane lights, a two-burner cooktop, heater, table, and chairs. A vault toilet is located at the base. No potable water or electricity is available. High-clearance vehicles are required for the final mile of rough road. Cell service is available from the tower.
payload.long_description:
Big Creek Baldy Lookout sits atop its namesake mountain in the Purcell Range of the Rocky Mountains within the Kootenai National Forest. This historic fire lookout has served as an observation point for spotting forest fires for over 60 years and now offers visitors a unique overnight rental experience with sweeping panoramic views of densely forested peaks, Lake Koocanusa, and the Yaak River valley.

The 225-square-foot cabin crowns a 52-foot tower encircled by a catwalk. It sleeps four on one double bed and one twin bed, both with mattresses. The lookout is furnished with propane lights, a two-burner propane cooktop, heater, fire extinguisher, table, chairs, cleaning supplies, and some cooking utensils. Propane is provided. An outdoor campfire ring is available though firewood is not supplied.

Guests must bring all water for drinking, cooking, and washing, as no potable water is available on-site. A vault toilet outhouse is located near the tower base. Access requires a high-clearance vehicle as the final mile of road is fairly rough. The surrounding Libby area offers more than 400 miles of summer trails, and the tower provides exceptional stargazing on clear nights. Bear-resistant food storage is required.

location.directions: From Libby, travel 1 mile north on Highway 37 to Pipe Creek Road. Turn left and follow for 19 miles, then turn right onto East Fork Pipe Creek Road/Big Creek Baldy Road 336. Proceed about three-quarters of a mile and turn right onto Big Creek Baldy Mountain Road 309. Follow this road for 5 miles to the lookout. High-clearance vehicle recommended; the last mile is fairly rough.

links.title: USFS Kootenai NF - Big Creek Baldy Lookout

photos.name: Big Creek Baldy-cooking burners and wash tubs

payload.name: Wood River Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally May through September. The back loop closes September 16; front loop closes September 30. No campground host after September 15. First-come, first-served only. No potable water available; bring your own water supply.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground on the Big Wood River in the Sawtooth National Recreation Area with 30 first-come, first-served sites, flush toilets, and easy access to fishing, tubing, and the Harriman Trail.
payload.medium_description: Wood River Campground sits at 6,400 feet along the Big Wood River, just 10 miles north of Ketchum in the Sawtooth National Recreation Area. The 30 single campsites (including one double site) are available first-come, first-served and accommodate both tents and RVs. Visitors enjoy fishing and tubing in the river, plus access to the 20-mile Harriman Trail for hiking and biking.
payload.long_description:
Wood River Campground occupies a heavily forested setting on the banks of the Big Wood River at 6,400 feet elevation within the Sawtooth National Recreation Area. Located 10 miles north of Ketchum on Highway 75, the campground offers 30 single campsites including one double site, all available on a first-come, first-served basis. Both tent campers and RVs are welcome.

The campground provides flush toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. An amphitheater with electricity and wooden benches sits a short walk from the sites, hosting ranger programs and group events. The Big Wood River running through the campground offers excellent fishing and tubing opportunities.

Nearby, the 20-mile Harriman Trail provides hiking and biking access, with spur trails leading to deep canyons, alpine lakes, and high-country fishing. The Wood River Group Overnight Area within the campground can accommodate up to 150 people and is reservable through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Ketchum, drive north 10 miles on Highway 75 past the Sawtooth National Recreation Area Headquarters. The campground is the second campground on the south side of the highway.

address.full: 13429 State Hwy 75 Scn, Sun Valley, ID 83353

payload.name: Governors Landing Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served only. County-wide burn ban currently in effect until July 8, 2026, prohibiting all fires including charcoal. Only the provided fire grills may be used when no burn ban is active. Standard sites are $10 per night ($5 with Interagency Senior/Access Pass), payable at a self-pay fee station accepting credit/debit cards only.
payload.short_description: Year-round NPS campground at Amistad National Recreation Area with potable water, vault toilets, covered picnic tables, and access to popular swimming areas on Lake Amistad.
payload.medium_description: Governors Landing Campground is the only campground at Amistad National Recreation Area with potable water available. The 15-site first-come, first-served campground operates year-round and rarely fills except on holiday weekends. Each site has a covered picnic table and fire grill. The campground accommodates tents and RVs up to 28 feet and offers access to some of the most popular swimming areas in the park.
payload.long_description:
Governors Landing Campground sits within Amistad National Recreation Area near Del Rio, Texas, offering direct access to Lake Amistad's popular swimming areas. The campground features 15 first-come, first-served sites suitable for tents and RVs up to 28 feet in length. It is the only campground in the park with potable water available at shared spigots, making it a more convenient option than the primitive campgrounds elsewhere in the recreation area.

Each campsite includes a covered picnic table and fire grill, with vault toilets available year-round. There are no hookups, but an RV dump station with potable water is located near the Diablo East boat ramp for campers with receipts proving park camping. The campground has paved roads and gravel surfaces in individual sites.

Site capacity is limited to eight persons and one recreational vehicle per site, with a maximum stay of 14 consecutive nights and 60 nights per calendar year. Quiet hours are 10pm to 6am, and checkout is 11am. Picnicking at vacant sites is allowed from 7am to 3pm; occupying sites outside these hours requires payment of camping fees.

location.directions: From Amistad National Recreation Area Visitor Center, turn right (west) onto Highway 90 and drive 1.9 miles. Turn left onto Spur 349 and travel 0.2 miles. Turn right and follow directional signs.

address.full: 1190 United States Highway 90 Access Rd, Del Rio, TX 78840

photos.name: Arial view of Governors Landing Campground

alerts.title: County-wide Burn Ban in Effect until July 8
