alerts.content: In keeping with the county-wide burn ban enacted on January 15 and extended on April 9, fires--including charcoal fires--are not permitted within Amistad National Recreation Area. To read the Val Verde County Commissioners Court Order, click "More".

alerts.title: Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and Walkway Access Are Closed
alerts.content: The Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and walkway access are closed because of the presence of excessive docking material, unsafe walkway and dock, and unstable, loose ground. The area will reopen once these hazards have been corrected.

alerts.title: Only Left Side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon Boat Ramps Are Open - Rest Are Closed
alerts.content: Due to low water levels, only the left side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon boat ramps are open. Please use caution with Spur 406 and Spur 454 launches, as the water may be too shallow to launch most boats. To see a list of open ramps, click on "more."

alerts.title: Help Prevent Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Infestation
alerts.content: A number of lakes are infested with an array of aquatic invasive species that damage natural ecosystems and waterways. Boaters are advised to Clean, Drain, and Dry all boats and equipment every time they leave the water.

alerts.title: Visitor Center Will Be Open But Cannot Process Transactions on 8/14
alerts.content: On August 14, Amistad Visitor Center will provide orientation and information but cannot sell passes or permits or exchange annual lake use pass receipts. Camping permits and lake use passes may be purchased at fee machines or at Pay.gov.

payload.name: Paonia State Park
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates May 1 through September 30. Reservations are required through cpwshop.com or by phone. No potable water is available on site.
payload.short_description: Scenic alpine campground at 6,500 feet elevation beside Paonia Reservoir, offering 20 sites with vault toilets and fire rings beneath the Ragged Mountains in western Colorado.
payload.medium_description: Paonia State Park sits at 6,500 feet beneath the Ragged Mountains, featuring a 334-acre reservoir and 20 campsites. Seven sites at Anthracite Campground offer electric hookups while the remainder are basic tent sites. The park provides vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site, but no potable water is available. Reservations are required through Colorado Parks and Wildlife.
payload.long_description:
Paonia State Park is a 1,857-acre alpine recreation area nestled at 6,500 feet elevation in the West Elk Mountains near Crawford, Colorado. The park centers on Paonia Reservoir, a 334-surface-acre impoundment popular for fishing and boating when water levels permit. The surrounding landscape offers views of the Ragged Mountains and serves as a gateway to Gunnison National Forest.

The park features 20 campsites split between basic tent sites and seven electric hookup sites at Anthracite Campground, accessible via County Road 12 (Kebler Pass Road). Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The campground operates seasonally from May 1 through September 30.

Beyond camping, visitors enjoy wildlife viewing, photography, and access to nearby hiking. The reservoir supports warm-water fishing species. Water levels can fluctuate significantly, occasionally affecting boat launch access. The park is approximately 16 miles northeast of the town of Paonia via State Highway 133.

location.directions: From Paonia, head northeast on State Highway 133 for approximately 16 miles. Anthracite Campground is accessible via County Road 12 (Kebler Pass Road). From Glenwood Springs, take CO-82 south to Carbondale, then CO-133 southwest for approximately 46 miles.

links.title: Paonia State Park - Colorado Parks & Wildlife

payload.name: Big Creek State Park
payload.status_description: Big Creek State Park is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. Picnic shelters and cabanas are reservable May 1 through September 30 and available walk-in during spring and fall shoulder seasons. The park is open year-round for day-use activities.
payload.short_description: Big Creek State Park offers day-use facilities including picnic shelters, beach cabanas, swimming beach, and boating on a 883-acre lake near Des Moines. No overnight camping is available.
payload.medium_description: Big Creek State Park is a popular day-use recreation area in Polk County, Iowa, centered around an 883-acre lake. The park features 22 picnic shelters and beach cabanas available for reservation, a swimming beach, boat ramps, marina with rentals, disc golf course, large playground, and access to the 27-mile paved Neil Smith Trail. While excellent for day trips, the park does not offer overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Big Creek State Park, located just north of Des Moines near Polk City, is one of Iowa's most visited day-use recreation areas. The park surrounds Big Creek Lake, an 883-acre impoundment popular for fishing, boating, and swimming. Anglers target largemouth bass, crappie, bluegill, and channel catfish, while the marina offers kayak, paddleboard, and pontoon rentals.

The park features extensive day-use amenities including 22 picnic shelters and cabanas scattered around the lakeshore, a sandy swimming beach with modern restrooms, multiple boat ramps, a disc golf course, volleyball courts, and a large wooden playground. The 27-mile paved Neil Smith Trail passes through the park, connecting to Des Moines via the Saylorville Lake area.

Importantly, Big Creek State Park does not have camping facilities. Visitors seeking overnight accommodations should look to nearby Saylorville Lake, which has several federal campgrounds approximately four miles away.

location.directions: From Des Moines, take I-80 west to exit 124 (Ankeny/Polk City). Head north on NW Polk City Drive approximately 8 miles to Polk City, then follow signs to Big Creek State Park. The main entrance is at 8794 NW 125th Ave, Polk City, IA 50226.

links.title: Iowa DNR - Big Creek State Park

payload.name: Cossatot Reefs
payload.status_description: Open and accepting reservations via Recreation.gov. The area has the possibility of flooding throughout the year; water level changes below the dam are signaled by horn.
payload.short_description: Shaded lakeside campground on Gillham Lake in southwest Arkansas with electric hookups, hot showers, and flush toilets managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers.
payload.medium_description: Cossatot Reefs Campground sits along the banks of Gillham Lake, a 1,370-acre reservoir fed by the Cossatot River, designated a National Wild and Scenic River. The campground offers 31 shaded sites with water and electric hookups (50-amp), plus hot showers and flush toilets. A boat ramp provides direct lake access for fishing and boating.
payload.long_description:
Cossatot Reefs Campground is located on the lush, wooded banks of Gillham Lake in Howard County, Arkansas. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the campground features 31 shaded campsites with water and 50-amp electric hookups, plus a group shelter. Hot showers, drinking water, and flush toilets provide comfortable amenities. Sites accommodate tents, RVs, trailers, fifth wheels, and camper vans, with some sites handling vehicles up to 67 feet.

Gillham Lake spans 1,370 surface acres with 36 miles of shoreline, created by damming the Cossatot River. A boat ramp at the campground provides easy lake access for fishing and boating. Anglers can target smallmouth, largemouth, and spotted bass, crappie, channel and flathead catfish, and various sunfish. Canoeists can paddle from below the dam to US Highway 71 South, roughly 16 miles.

A short nature trail winds through a wooded section of the campground, displaying colorful redbud and dogwood blossoms in spring. The area is subject to potential flooding throughout the year, with water level warnings signaled by horn below the dam.

location.directions: From De Queen, Arkansas, head north on US-59/US-71. Continue for nearly 10 miles and turn right at Gillham EZ-Mart. Turn right on Tower Road, go 1.3 miles, turn left onto Gillham Lake Road, go 4.3 miles, turn right and follow signs into the campground.

address.full: 242 Cossatot Reef Park Rd, Gillham, AR 71841

payload.name: Ross Prairie Primitive Backpacking Campsite
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required through Florida State Forests Reserve America system. The forest allows hunting seasonally; wear blaze orange during hunting seasons. Burn bans may restrict campfires during drought conditions.
payload.short_description: Hike-in primitive backpacking campsite in Ross Prairie State Forest along the Holly Hammock Hiking Trail, offering a secluded tent camping experience in central Florida.
payload.medium_description: Ross Prairie Primitive Backpacking Campsite is a single tent-only site located in Ross Prairie State Forest, accessible only by backpacking from the trailhead parking area. The site accommodates up to 8 people and features a fire ring and picnic table but no potable water, restrooms, or electricity. Situated along the Holly Hammock Hiking Trail, this primitive campsite offers opportunities for hiking, bird watching, wildlife photography, and nature study in a quiet forest setting.
payload.long_description:
Ross Prairie Primitive Backpacking Campsite provides a true backcountry experience in Marion County, approximately 15 minutes southwest of Ocala. Campers park at the limerock parking lot near the State Forest/Wildlife Management Area sign off SR 200 and backpack in to the designated campsite along the Holly Hammock Hiking Trail. This single site accommodates up to 8 people and is equipped with a fire ring and picnic table.

The surrounding Ross Prairie State Forest offers over 5,600 acres of pine flatwoods, sandhills, and wetlands with trails for hiking and horseback riding. Wildlife viewing and bird watching are popular activities, with opportunities to see gopher tortoises, white-tailed deer, and various bird species. Hunters also use the forest seasonally, so visitors should check hunting dates and wear blaze orange during hunting seasons.

This is a pack-it-in, pack-it-out experience with no potable water, restrooms, or trash facilities on site. Campers must be fully self-sufficient and prepared for primitive conditions. During drought periods, burn bans may restrict campfire use.

location.directions: From Ocala, head west on SR 200 for 10.5 miles. Parking is directly off SR 200 at the trailhead. Park in the limerock parking area by the State Forest/Wildlife Management Area sign and backpack in to the campsite.

payload.name: Hurricane Creek Horse & Primitive Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates March 15 through December 31 and closes January 1 through March 14. First-come, first-served only; no reservations.
payload.short_description: Primitive horse camp in Nantahala National Forest with horse stalls, vault toilet, and fire rings. First-come, first-served at $6/night.
payload.medium_description: Hurricane Creek Horse & Primitive Camp is a rustic camping area in the Standing Indian Basin of the Nantahala National Forest. Designed primarily for equestrians, the camp features horse stalls and provides access to an extensive network of trails for horseback riding and hiking. The site offers basic amenities including a vault toilet and fire rings, but campers must bring their own water.
payload.long_description:
Hurricane Creek Horse & Primitive Camp sits in the scenic Standing Indian Basin within Nantahala National Forest, about 9 miles west of Franklin, North Carolina. This primitive campground caters primarily to equestrians, offering horse stalls and direct access to a network of trails suitable for horseback riding and hiking. The Hurricane Creek Loop Trail and other routes in the area provide opportunities for multi-day backcountry exploration.

Facilities are minimal but functional: a vault toilet serves the camp, and fire rings are provided for campfires. There is no potable water on site, so campers must bring their own supply. Horses are restricted to the designated horse camp area and approved trails only. The access road is gravel, and camping within 50 feet of any water source is prohibited.

location.directions: From Franklin, take US 64W for 9 miles, turn left on old US 64 and follow signs to Standing Indian Campground. Continue south on FS Rd 67 past Standing Indian Campground for 2 miles. Gravel road.

links.title: USFS Hurricane Creek Horse & Primitive Campground

payload.name: Peaks Of Otter Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opens for the 2026 season on May 22. Operating season runs through late October, weather permitting. Reservations available up to six months in advance via Recreation.gov; 79 of 139 sites are first-come-first-served only.
payload.short_description: Seasonal campground at milepost 85.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway, nestled between mountain peaks with 139 tent and RV sites, flush toilets, potable water, and access to Abbott Lake.
payload.medium_description: Peaks of Otter Campground sits at the base of Sharp Top and Flat Top mountains along Virginia's Blue Ridge Parkway. The 139-site campground offers both reservable and first-come-first-served sites across three loops, with flush toilets, potable water, dump station, and a fire ring and picnic table at each site. Abbott Lake and multiple hiking trails are within walking distance, along with the Peaks of Otter Lodge and Sharp Top Country Store.
payload.long_description:
Peaks of Otter Campground occupies a scenic location at milepost 85.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway, where Sharp Top and Flat Top mountains dominate the Virginia skyline. The campground features 139 sites spread across three loops (A, B, and T), with 60 sites available for advance reservation through Recreation.gov and 79 sites held for first-come-first-served campers. Both tent and RV camping are accommodated, though no electric, water, or sewer hookups are available.

Facilities include comfort stations with flush toilets, potable water spigots, and a dump station. Every site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill. Bears frequent the area, so food storage lockers are provided and campers must maintain clean camps. Only USDA or state-certified heat-treated firewood is permitted; collecting dead and down wood from nearby areas is allowed.

The 24-acre Abbott Lake sits nearby, stocked with smallmouth bass and bluegill. Hiking options range from the flat lakeside trail to demanding summit climbs. The historic Peaks of Otter Lodge with restaurant and the Sharp Top Country Store are within walking distance, offering meals, camping supplies, firewood, and ice.

location.directions: From Roanoke, Virginia, take the Blue Ridge Parkway north for 26 miles to Milepost 86. From Bedford, Virginia, follow Route 43 to Blue Ridge Parkway; the campground is on the left before reaching the Parkway.

payload.name: Clints Well
payload.status_description: Open year-round but not plowed in winter. First-come, first-served only. Fees of $8 per night apply during spring and summer months beginning March 27. Check for current fire restrictions before visiting. 14-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: A first-come, first-served campground tucked among tall old-growth ponderosa pines at 6,868 feet elevation in Coconino National Forest, 55 miles southeast of Flagstaff near the Mogollon Rim.
payload.medium_description: Clints Well Campground sits among tall old-growth ponderosa pines at 6,868 feet elevation along Forest Highway 3 (Lake Mary Road). This rustic first-come, first-served campground offers vault toilets and picnic tables but no potable water. The nearby Clints Well community provides access to a gas station, country store, and restaurant. The scenic Mogollon Rim and several fishing lakes are within easy driving distance.
payload.long_description:
Clints Well Campground is a rustic Forest Service campground located 55 miles southeast of Flagstaff on Forest Highway 3 (Lake Mary Road), just north of the Clints Well intersection. At an elevation of 6,868 feet, the campsites are nestled in a stand of tall old-growth ponderosa pines set back from the highway.

This is a primitive campground with vault toilets and picnic tables at sites, but no potable water is available. Campers must pack out all trash as there is no trash service. Fire rings are provided but may be subject to seasonal fire restrictions. Pets are allowed but must remain leashed; horses and pack animals are prohibited.

The campground is open year-round but is not plowed during winter, so access may be limited by snow. A small community at the crossroads provides convenient access to a gas station with a country store and a restaurant. The scenic Mogollon Rim, with its dramatic two-thousand-foot escarpment marking the southern edge of the Colorado Plateau, is a short drive away, as are several forest lakes known for excellent fishing.

location.directions: From Flagstaff, travel 55 miles southeast on Forest Highway 3 (Lake Mary Road) to the Clints Well intersection. The campground is located just north of the intersection.

payload.name: Patapsco Valley Hilton Vally State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The Hilton Area Campground is currently open for the season, operating from April 1 to October 30. Reservations are recommended and can be made up to one year in advance. Camp hosts are available on-site to assist campers during their stay.
payload.short_description: The Hilton Area Campground in Patapsco Valley State Park offers tent-only sites and camper cabins with access to trails and family-friendly amenities.
payload.medium_description: The Hilton Area Campground in Patapsco Valley State Park offers 12 tent-only sites and six camper cabins amidst lush woodlands. Amenities include restroom facilities, a playground, a nature center, and access to hiking and biking trails. The campground operates seasonally from April 1 to October 30.
payload.long_description:
The Hilton Area Campground, located within Patapsco Valley State Park in Catonsville, Maryland, offers a serene camping experience amidst lush woodlands. This campground features 12 tent-only sites and six single-room camper cabins. The tent sites are primitive, lacking electricity, while the cabins are equipped with a full-size bed, a set of bunk beds, baseboard heating, electric outlets, and a single overhead light. Restroom facilities with flush toilets and showers are available nearby.

The Hilton Area is renowned for its family-friendly amenities, including a recycled tire playground and a nature center that offers educational programs. Campers have access to a network of trails, such as the Sawmill Branch Trail, which features unique stream crossings and connects to other trails leading to the Patapsco River. These trails are suitable for hiking and mountain biking, providing opportunities to explore the park's diverse landscapes.

While pets are permitted in the day-use area of the Hilton Area, they are prohibited within the campground itself. Campers are advised to plan accordingly and ensure their pets are cared for outside the camping premises. The campground operates from April 1 to October 30, offering a seasonal retreat for nature enthusiasts.

Reservations are recommended and can be made up to one year in advance. Camp hosts are available on-site to assist with information, emergencies, and guidance on campground rules and regulations. Their presence enhances the camping experience by providing support and ensuring a safe environment for all visitors.

location.directions: From I-695 (Baltimore Beltway), take Exit 13 for Frederick Road west. Follow for two miles and turn left on South Rolling Road. At the first intersection, bear right onto Hilton Avenue. Continue 1.5 miles and turn right into the park.

payload.name: Poplar Grove Youth Group Tent Campground
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. Closed during winter due to seasonal road closures on Manahan Road. During December through February, parking is at Camp Round Meadow. No potable water available on site; campers must bring their own water supply.
payload.short_description: Primitive group tent camping for organized youth groups in Catoctin Mountain Park. Three sites with vault toilets, fire circles, and a shared pavilion in Maryland's rolling hills.
payload.medium_description: Poplar Grove Youth Group Tent Campground offers primitive tent camping exclusively for organized youth groups with at least 50% of members under age 18. Located in the western portion of Catoctin Mountain Park on Manahan Road, the campground features three tree-sheltered sites surrounded by hardwood forest. Each site accommodates up to 25 people with picnic tables, grills, and fire circles. Groups share vault toilets and a covered pavilion.
payload.long_description:
Poplar Grove Youth Group Tent Campground provides year-round primitive tent camping for sanctioned youth organizations in the rolling hills of Thurmont, Maryland. The campground sits just steps from the Catoctin National Recreation Trail, offering groups easy access to hiking and nature exploration. Three flat, tree-sheltered sites are nestled within a hardwood deciduous forest, each accommodating up to 25 people.

Each site includes picnic tables, grills, and a fire circle. Groups share centrally located vault toilets and a covered pavilion. Firewood is provided or campers may collect dead and downed wood; bringing outside firewood is prohibited. Water is not available on site as of 2025, so groups must bring all water for drinking, cooking, and cleaning. Pets, alcohol, and fireworks are prohibited.

Reservations are required through Recreation.gov and may be booked up to 6 months in advance with a minimum 2-day advance booking. Check-in is at 1:00 PM and check-out at 11:00 AM. Adult supervision is required at all times, and at least 50% of group members must be under 18 and currently enrolled in the organization.

location.directions: From Route 15, exit at Catoctin Mountain Park/Route 77. Travel approximately 6 miles west, passing the Visitor Center and Park Central Road. Turn right onto Foxville-Deerfield Road. At the fork, bear right onto Manahan Road (gravel). Poplar Grove is about 1 mile ahead. From the west, take MD 64 to MD 77 East, drive about 4 miles, turn left onto Foxville-Deerfield Road, bear right onto Manahan Road at the fork, and continue about 1.7 miles.

alerts.title: Camp Greentop
alerts.content: Due to ongoing construction to improve the visitor and group experience Camp Greentop is currently closed for renovation and rehabilitation. We anticipate an opening of late summer. For updates or inquiries please email, CATO_CampManager@nps.gov.

alerts.title: Visitor Center Early Closure

alerts.title: Temporary Trail Closure - Wolf Rock & Thurmont Vista
alerts.content: On March 2, 2023, portion of Wolf Rock and Thurmont Vista trails will be closed to pedestrians from 8:00 a.m. through 2:00 p.m. for resource management. Thank you for your understanding.

alerts.content: Chestnut Picnic Area will be inaccessible through Friday, June 27, due to utility work being completed. Owens Creek Picnic Area is open for picnicking.

alerts.title: Catoctin Mountain Park announces upcoming closures on Foxville Deerfield and Park Central roads
alerts.content: Beginning Monday, August 4 through the end of October, portions of Foxville Deerfield and Park Central roads will be under construction. At times access will be limited or restricted. Click "More" for updated status and closure information.

payload.name: Cranesnest Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is temporarily closed for construction. Road surfaces, pull-offs, and campsite entrances are being resurfaced. The reservation window will reopen and the camping season will be extended once work is complete. Alternative camping is available at Pound River Campground and Lower Twin Campground.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at John W. Flannagan Dam and Reservoir in Virginia's Cumberland Mountains, offering electric hookups, bath houses, and boat launch access.
payload.medium_description: Cranesnest Campground sits along the shores of John W. Flannagan Reservoir in the rolling Cumberland Mountains of southwest Virginia. The campground offers approximately 30 sites including RV electric, tent electric, and non-electric options. Amenities include bath houses, a dump station, playgrounds, boat launch ramps, and picnic shelters with grills and horseshoe pits.
payload.long_description:
Cranesnest Campground is located within the John W. Flannagan Dam and Reservoir recreation area in Dickenson County, Virginia. The reservoir, created by a dam completed in 1964, covers 1,145 acres with nearly 40 miles of shoreline maintained at approximately 1,400 feet elevation. The campground offers sites with 50-amp electric hookups as well as non-electric options for both RVs and tent campers.

Facilities include bath houses, a dump station, trash service, playgrounds, and boat launch ramps with no launch fee. Picnic shelters equipped with grills and horseshoe pits are available for group gatherings. The reservoir is known for excellent fishing with bass, walleye, and trout in its deep, clean coves. Breaks Interstate Park is nearby, offering additional lodging, dining, a museum, rafting, rock climbing, and other outdoor activities.

location.directions: From Clintwood, VA main street turn left onto Rt. 83. Travel 2.6 miles and turn left onto Cranesnest Campground Rd. Travel 2.8 miles to the campground.

address.full: 2689 Cranesnest River Campground Rd, Clintwood, VA 24228

links.title: Corps Lakes Gateway - John W. Flannagan

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Due to planned construction at Cranesnest Campground, we regret to inform our customers that we will be temporarily closing the campground to allow the re-surfacing of roadways, pull-offs, and campsite entrances to be completed. Once the work is complete, we will re-open the reservation window to allow customers to make reservations. We will also extend the camping season to allow additional time to camp due to the closure. Thank you for your understanding and **we *apologize *for any inconvenience. **Alternatively, you may choose to make a reservation at Pound River Campground and/or Lower Twin Campground.

payload.name: Kingston Campground
payload.status_description: Open mid-May through late October, weather and conditions permitting. No fees or reservations required; all sites are first-come, first-served. No potable water available.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground in the Toiyabe Range at 7,100 feet elevation, offering vault toilets, fire rings, and access to the Toiyabe Crest National Recreation Trail and nearby Groves Lake.
payload.medium_description: Kingston Campground is a free, first-come first-served primitive campground nestled along Kingston Creek in the Toiyabe Range within the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. At 7,100 feet elevation, it provides access to the northern trailhead for the Toiyabe Crest National Recreation Trail and nearby Groves Lake. The campground features vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings at each site, though campers must bring their own water. A stock loading ramp is available for horses and pack animals.
payload.long_description:
Kingston Campground sits at 7,100 feet elevation along Kingston Creek in the Toiyabe Range, offering a remote high-desert camping experience in central Nevada. The campground serves as the northernmost entry point to the Toiyabe Crest National Recreation Trail and provides easy access to Groves Lake, a small county-owned lake popular for fishing.

This primitive campground offers basic amenities including vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings with grates at each site. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own supply. A stock loading ramp accommodates horses and pack animals for backcountry trips. Dogs are allowed but must remain on leash, and certified weed-free hay is required for stock animals.

The surrounding area offers diverse recreation including lake and stream fishing, mountain and road biking, backpacking, day hiking, non-motorized boating, and OHV road riding. The remote canyon setting along the eastern slopes of the Toiyabe Range provides a quiet escape from more crowded campgrounds.

location.directions: From Austin, follow US 50 East to State Route 376 South for 16 miles to the turnoff-campground sign. The campground is five miles west of the State Route 376 turnoff.

payload.name: Cape Lookout State Park
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open and accepting reservations. Scheduled to close June 1, 2026 for GO Bond-funded improvements including foredune reinforcement, utility upgrades in C and D loops, and new restroom/shower facility construction. Expected to reopen after summer 2026.
payload.short_description: Scenic Oregon Coast campground on a sand spit between Netarts Bay and the Pacific Ocean, offering tent sites, RV hookups, yurts, and deluxe cabins with beach access and hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Cape Lookout State Park campground sits on a scenic sand spit between Netarts Bay and the Pacific Ocean along Oregon's Three Capes Scenic Route. The park offers 38 full-hookup RV sites, 170 tent sites with nearby water, 13 yurts, 6 deluxe cabins, plus group camping and hiker/biker options. Amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, and an RV dump station.
payload.long_description:
Cape Lookout State Park is one of Oregon's most popular coastal campgrounds, located on a dramatic sand spit separating Netarts Bay from the Pacific Ocean. The park features over 200 campsites across multiple loops: 38 full-hookup RV sites, 170 tent sites with water nearby, one electrical site, 13 yurts (6 pet-friendly), and 6 deluxe cabins (3 pet-friendly). Group tent camping and hiker/biker camping are also available.

The campground provides full amenities including flush toilets, hot showers for registered campers, an RV dump station, and firewood sales in C Loop. Two campsites and one cabin accommodate visitors with disabilities, and two yurts feature ADA-compliant ramps. Dogs are welcome on a 6-foot leash, with off-leash beach access permitted north of the campground.

Beyond camping, the park offers excellent hiking including the Cape Lookout Trail with its dramatic ocean views, beachcombing along miles of sandy shoreline, and access to the scenic Three Capes Route. The park accepts reservations up to 6 months in advance.

location.directions: From Tillamook, head west on Third Street, which becomes Netarts Highway (Highway 131). Continue approximately 10 miles through Netarts to the park entrance on the left.

links.title: Cape Lookout State Park - Oregon State Parks
Cape Lookout GO Bond Project Details

payload.name: Lake Keomah State Park
payload.status_description: Open for camping April 1 through October 31. Currently in peak season with reservations required for all sites. The lake is undergoing restoration with completion expected by spring 2026; camping and all campground amenities remain operational during the project.
payload.short_description: Lake Keomah State Park offers 49 campsites with electric and non-electric options near an 84-acre lake in southern Iowa, featuring modern restrooms, showers, and a dump station.
payload.medium_description: Lake Keomah State Park near Oskaloosa features 49 campsites including 37 electric sites with 20/30/50-amp hookups, 7 non-electric sites, and 2 buddy sites. The campground provides modern restrooms, showers, a dump station, and water hydrants throughout. A three-mile trail circles the lake, and amenities include an accessible fishing pier, swimming beach, and two boat launches.
payload.long_description:
Lake Keomah State Park encompasses 366 acres of wooded terrain surrounding an 84-acre lake in Mahaska County, approximately six miles east of Oskaloosa. The campground offers 49 sites ranging from primitive non-electric to full 50-amp electric hookups, all available through the online reservation system. Modern restrooms with showers, a dump station, and water hydrants serve the camping area.

Recreational opportunities include fishing for bluegill, crappie, largemouth bass, and channel catfish from the accessible fishing pier or two boat ramps (electric trolling motors only). A three-mile walking trail winds around the lake and through the historic village of Keomah, passing through diverse wildlife habitats where visitors may spot great blue herons, bullfrogs, and quail. An unsupervised swimming beach, playground, and picnic shelters round out the facilities.

The park also offers a day-use lodge and group camping area available for larger gatherings such as weddings and reunions. The lodge is ADA accessible and can be reserved separately from individual campsites.

location.directions: From Oskaloosa, travel 6 miles east on Highway 92 to Keomah Lane.

links.title: Lake Keomah State Park - Iowa DNR

payload.name: Moose Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Operating dates are May 1 through October 31. First-come, first-served with no reservations. A 5-day stay limit is in effect from May 1 through Labor Day. Food storage requirements are in effect forest-wide.
payload.short_description: Rustic 10-site campground along the Greys River in Bridger-Teton National Forest, offering potable water, vault toilets, and access to Pearson Creek Trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Moose Flat Campground sits along the scenic Greys River, 22 miles from the north end of Greys River Road in Bridger-Teton National Forest. This first-come, first-served campground offers 10 sites that accommodate trailers up to 30 feet, potable water via hand pump, and vault toilets. The adjacent Pearson Creek Trailhead provides backcountry access, though it begins with a river ford.
payload.long_description:
Moose Flat Campground is a quiet, lightly-used campground situated along the Greys River in the Bridger-Teton National Forest. Located 22 miles from the north end of Greys River Road, the campground offers 10 sites suitable for tents and trailers up to 30 feet. Amenities include potable water from a hand pump and vault toilets. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted.

The Pearson Creek Trailhead lies adjacent to the campground, providing access to backcountry trails, though hikers should be prepared for a river ford at the start. The Greys River corridor is known for excellent fishing, wildlife viewing, and dispersed recreation opportunities. From Alpine, Wyoming, the drive takes approximately 38 minutes via Forest Service Road 10138.

During the operating season, a 5-day stay limit applies from May 1 through Labor Day. After the seasonal closure in late October, the gate remains open for off-season use at no charge, though water is shut off, restrooms are locked, and trash service is discontinued.

location.directions: From Alpine, Wyoming, head east on Greys River Road (Forest Service Road 10138) for approximately 8 miles. Bear right at the junction, staying on FS-10138, and follow it southeast for an additional 14 miles. Turn right into the entrance of Moose Flat Campground. Total distance approximately 23 miles, 38 minutes from Alpine.

payload.name: Gray Falls Campground
payload.status_description: This is a day-use only area. No overnight camping is permitted. The site provides daytime access for picnicking, hiking, and river recreation along the Wild and Scenic Trinity River.
payload.short_description: Gray Falls is a day-use area in Six Rivers National Forest along the Wild and Scenic Trinity River, offering river access and hiking but no overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Gray Falls is a day-use area located in Six Rivers National Forest along the Wild and Scenic Trinity River, approximately 12 miles east of Willow Creek and 2 miles west of Burnt Ranch. The site provides river access via the Grays Falls Trail, picnic facilities, and a vault toilet. Despite being listed as a campground by some third-party websites, official Forest Service documentation confirms this is a day-use only location with no overnight camping permitted.
payload.long_description:
Gray Falls is a day-use recreation site managed by Six Rivers National Forest, situated along the designated Wild and Scenic Trinity River corridor in Trinity County, California. The site is located approximately 12 miles east of Willow Creek and 2 miles west of Burnt Ranch off Highway 299.

The primary attraction is the Grays Falls Trail (#6E30), a moderate 1-mile round-trip hike with approximately 300 feet of elevation change featuring stairs. The trail descends to the Trinity River, providing access for fishing, rafting put-in/take-out, and general river recreation. The day-use area includes picnic tables and a toilet facility.

Important clarification: Despite being listed as a campground with 33 sites by various third-party camping websites, official U.S. Forest Service documentation explicitly identifies Gray Falls as a day-use only area. No overnight camping is permitted at this location. Campers seeking overnight accommodations in this area should consider nearby developed campgrounds such as Burnt Ranch Campground or other Six Rivers National Forest camping facilities.

location.directions: From Willow Creek, travel east on Highway 299 approximately 12 miles. The Gray Falls Day Use Area is located 2 miles west of Burnt Ranch.

links.title: Six Rivers NF Grays Falls Trail

payload.name: Don Robinson State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park grounds accessible 7 a.m. to half-hour after sunset. The special-use camping area requires advance reservations by phone and is gated with combination access. No water available on-site.
payload.short_description: Group camping area in Don Robinson State Park featuring tent platforms, a centralized fire ring, and vault toilet amid Missouri's sandstone canyons and shelter caves.
payload.medium_description: Don Robinson State Park's special-use camping area offers primitive group camping for up to 30 people. The gated area includes four tent platforms, six picnic tables, seven lantern posts, and a centralized fire ring. A vault toilet is provided but no water is available. Priority is given to nonprofit organizations and youth groups. Reservations are made by phone and include a gate combination for access.
payload.long_description:
Located in Jefferson County near Cedar Hill, Don Robinson State Park's special-use camping area provides a primitive group camping experience in Missouri's scenic sandstone landscape. The park sits in the upper watershed of LaBarque Creek and features dramatic geological formations including sandstone box canyons, natural shelter caves, towering cliffs, and both upland and bottomland forests.

The special-use camping area accommodates groups of up to 30 people with a maximum of 12 vehicles. Facilities include four tent platforms, six picnic tables, seven lantern posts, and one centralized fire ring. A vault toilet is on-site, but campers must bring their own water as none is available. The area is gated with a combination lock; groups receive the code upon reservation.

Priority scheduling is given to nonprofit organizations and youth groups. Reservations must be made by calling the park directly. Standard Missouri State Parks group camp regulations apply, including no pets allowed (service animals welcome), fires only in designated areas with facility manager approval, and a 100% smoke-free policy throughout the facility.

location.directions: Located at 9275 Byrnesville Road, Cedar Hill, MO 63016, not far from St. Louis.

address.full: 5000 Don Robinson Rd, Cedar Hill, MO 63016

payload.name: Crow Wing State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: The group campground typically operates from mid-May through October. Reservations can be made up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota DNR reservation system online at reservemn.usedirect.com or by calling 866-857-2757. Vehicle permit required ($7 daily or $35 annual).
payload.short_description: Rustic group campground at the historic confluence of the Mississippi and Crow Wing rivers, accommodating up to 75 people with tent lawn and RV parking area.
payload.medium_description: Crow Wing State Park Group Campground offers a rustic camping experience at the historically significant confluence of the Mississippi and Crow Wing rivers. The site can accommodate up to 75 people with ample space for more than a dozen tents on the grassy lawn or six to eight campers or RVs in the designated parking area. The spacious setting is ideal for family reunions, Scout troops, and other organized groups seeking proximity to 18 miles of hiking trails and river access.
payload.long_description:
Crow Wing State Park Group Campground sits within a 3,119-acre state park at the confluence of the Mississippi and Crow Wing rivers, a site of significant historical importance where oxcart trade routes between Winnipeg and Saint Paul thrived for over two decades. The group camp provides a rustic setting alongside the Mississippi River, with a grassy lawn accommodating more than a dozen tents and a parking area suitable for six to eight RVs or campers.

The campground serves as a base for exploring diverse landscapes representing three of Minnesota's major ecological regions: prairie, pine forest, and hardwood forest. Campers have access to 18 miles of hiking trails, 6.5 miles of paved bike trail connecting to the 115-mile Paul Bunyan State Trail, and calm waters ideal for novice paddlers. Canoe and kayak rentals are available at the park. The group camp features primitive amenities including vault toilets, water access, picnic tables, and fire rings with grills.

location.directions: From Brainerd, travel south on Highway 371. Turn west onto County Road 27, then follow signs to Crow Wing State Park. The park entrance is at 3124 State Park Road, Brainerd, MN 56401.

links.title: Crow Wing State Park Virtual Tour
Crow Wing State Park - Explore Minnesota

payload.name: Mt Cabot Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round, free, first-come, first-served. No reservations accepted. Accessible only via a 4.6-mile hike; no vehicle access. No potable water or official restroom facilities available.
payload.short_description: Historic backcountry fire warden cabin in the White Mountain National Forest, accessible via a 4.6-mile hike on the Kilkenny Ridge Trail near Mt. Cabot summit.
payload.medium_description: Mt Cabot Cabin is a rustic backcountry shelter originally built for a fire warden who staffed the now-defunct fire tower on Mt. Cabot's summit. Located about 0.3 miles from the 4,170-foot peak, this free first-come, first-served cabin provides basic overnight shelter for hikers traversing the Kilkenny Ridge Trail. The cabin features bunk platforms, a table, and insulated walls, sleeping approximately 4-8 people.
payload.long_description:
Mt Cabot Cabin is a historic fire warden cabin nestled on the Kilkenny Ridge Trail in the northern reaches of New Hampshire's White Mountain National Forest. Originally constructed to house the fire warden who manned the summit lookout tower, the cabin now serves as a free backcountry shelter for hikers on a first-come, first-served basis. The cabin sits approximately 0.3 miles from Mt. Cabot's 4,170-foot summit.

The two-room cabin features a kitchen/eating area with a table and a bunk room with wooden sleeping platforms accommodating 4-8 people. The structure has insulated walls and windows, providing reasonable protection from the elements. Maintained by a local Boy Scout troop, the cabin offers a unique overnight experience for those willing to make the trek.

Reaching the cabin requires a 4.6-mile hike from the Bunnell Notch trailhead. Hikers should come fully prepared as there is no potable water on site and restroom facilities are not officially provided. The nearby former fire tower site offers panoramic views of the Mahoosuc Range to the east and the Kilkenny Range to the north.

location.directions: Access via Bunnell Notch Trail. The trailhead is located off York Pond Road near Berlin, NH. The hike to the cabin is approximately 4.6 miles.

address.full: 4042 L / O Vankyke Etal, Berlin, NH 03570

payload.name: Fort Ridgely State Park Farm House
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May 1 through late October. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance through Reserve Minnesota. No pets and no smoking permitted.
payload.short_description: Historic farmhouse sleeping six adjacent to the equestrian campground at Fort Ridgely State Park, offering rustic lodging with outdoor cooking facilities and access to the Fair Ridge Trail.
payload.medium_description: The Fort Ridgely State Park Farm House is a three-room rental unit sleeping up to six guests in three double beds. Located near the equestrian campground, it offers heating, air conditioning, and a small refrigerator, but no indoor cooking or plumbing. A fire ring, pedestal grill, and picnic table provide outdoor cooking options. A primitive toilet sits nearby, showers are available at the equestrian campground, and potable water is accessible via an outside spigot.
payload.long_description:
The Farm House at Fort Ridgely State Park provides a unique rustic lodging experience in Minnesota's Renville County. This historic structure sleeps six people in one bedroom containing three double beds, two of which are bunked. The unit features modern comforts including heating, air conditioning, and a dorm-sized refrigerator, though indoor cooking is prohibited. Guests receive a combination lock code via email for self-check-in and must bring their own bedding and linens.

Outdoor amenities include a picnic table, pedestal grill, and fire ring with grill for all cooking needs. The farmhouse has no indoor plumbing; a primitive toilet is located nearby, showers are available at the adjacent equestrian campground, and potable water comes from an outdoor spigot. Parking accommodates up to three vehicles.

The property sits near the Fair Ridge Trail, offering convenient equestrian and hiking access. Fort Ridgely State Park itself preserves the historic fort site from the Dakota War of 1862 and features additional amenities including a CCC-built picnic shelter, amphitheater, and trout-stocked creek.

location.directions: From Fairfax, Minnesota, head south on Highway 4 for approximately 7 miles. Turn right onto County Road 30 and continue for about 1 mile to reach Fort Ridgely State Park. The Farmhouse is located near the equestrian campground within the park.

links.title: Fort Ridgely State Park Virtual Tour

payload.name: Mississippi River State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Visitor Center hours are daily 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Swimming at Storm Creek Lake is available Memorial Day through Labor Day without lifeguard supervision. Primitive campgrounds (Lone Pine and Maple Flats) are accessible by dirt roads only.
payload.short_description: Arkansas state park campground offering sites at Bear Creek Lake and Storm Creek Lake with full hookups, primitive camping, and distinctive shipping container-style camper cabins.
payload.medium_description: Mississippi River State Park features multiple camping areas where the Mississippi River, Crowley's Ridge, and the Arkansas Delta converge. Beech Point and Storm Creek Lake campgrounds offer full-hookup sites with bathhouses and free Wi-Fi, while Lone Pine provides primitive camping. Five unique camper cabins designed to resemble Mississippi River shipping containers are available at Storm Creek Lake.
payload.long_description:
Mississippi River State Park provides quality access to the St. Francis National Forest and endless adventures where the Mississippi River, Crowley's Ridge, and the Arkansas Delta meet. The park spans hardwood forests to the sandy shores of the Mississippi River, featuring three lakes, the All American Great River Road, and Crowley's Ridge Parkway (both National Scenic Byways), four hiking trails, and two recreational areas.

Camping options include Beech Point Campground at Bear Creek Lake (sites 1-14 with full hookups, sites 15T-17T tent-only), Storm Creek Lake Campground (sites 32-45 with full hookups, sites 38-40 bike-in tent sites), Lone Pine Campground (sites 18-31 primitive), and Maple Flats Group Campground (primitive group area). Five distinctive camper cabins at Storm Creek Lake sleep up to four people and include queen beds, bunk beds, heating/AC, screened porches, outdoor grills, and fire pits. The developed campgrounds feature modern bathhouses with hot showers and free Wi-Fi.

Recreation includes a swim beach at Storm Creek Lake (Memorial Day through Labor Day, no lifeguard), kayak/paddleboard/boat rentals, accessible fishing piers at both lakes, and hiking trails. The visitor center is open daily 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

location.directions: From Marianna, take State Highway 44 east for approximately 3 miles to reach the park entrance.

payload.name: South Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season. Forest Road 4440 has several washouts and is not recommended for trailers or low clearance vehicles. All vehicles should proceed with caution at their own risk. First-come first-served only with on-site Scan and Pay available via the Recreation.gov app.
payload.short_description: Primitive 4-site campground at the confluence of South Creek and Twisp River, providing trailhead access to the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: South Creek Campground is a small, peaceful first-come first-served campground at 3,100 feet elevation in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. Located 22 miles west of Twisp near the confluence of South Creek and the Twisp River, it serves as a base camp for hikers accessing the Twisp River Trail 440, South Creek Trail 401, and Scatter Creek Trail 427 into the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
South Creek Campground offers a quiet, primitive camping experience at 3,100 feet elevation in the Methow Valley region of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. With only four campsites, this small campground sits near the confluence of South Creek and the Twisp River, surrounded by forested terrain that provides access to some of the best hiking in the Lake Chelan-Sawtooth Wilderness.

The campground serves as an excellent staging area for backcountry exploration. From here, hikers can access the Twisp River Trail 440 as well as the South Creek Trail 401 and nearby Scatter Creek Trail 427, both of which lead into the wilderness. The area also offers opportunities for bicycling, scenic drives, horseback riding, and stream fishing.

Facilities are basic: vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but there is no potable water and no trash service. Campers must filter or treat water from nearby sources and pack out all trash following Leave No Trace principles. Each site accommodates a maximum of 2 vehicles and either 2 tents or 1 RV with 1 tent. The access road (Forest Road 4440) has several washouts and is not recommended for trailers or low clearance vehicles.

location.directions: From Twisp, drive west on paved Twisp River Road (County Road 9114) for 12 miles until it becomes paved Forest Service Road 44. Continue straight on FS Road 44 for 5 miles until the road turns to gravel and becomes Forest Service Road 4440. Continue straight on FS Road 4440 for an additional 4 miles to South Creek Campground (22 miles total from Twisp).

payload.name: Cowan Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. Sites are reservable up to six months in advance via reserveohio.com or by calling (866) 644-6727. Check-in is 3:00 PM, check-out is 1:00 PM. Maximum stay is 14 nights within a 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Family campground at Cowan Lake State Park featuring 254 sites with electric hookups, showers, dump station, camp store, and beach access on a scenic 700-acre lake in southwestern Ohio.
payload.medium_description: Cowan Lake State Park Campground offers 254 sites ranging from primitive non-electric to full hookup sites in a wooded setting beside a 700-acre lake. Facilities include two shower houses with flush toilets, laundry, dump station, and a well-stocked camp store with snacks, bait, and seasonal kayak rentals. The campground sits within walking distance of the camper beach, nature center, and boat ramp.
payload.long_description:
Cowan Lake State Park Campground is set within the 1,775-acre park in Clinton County, Ohio, surrounding a scenic 700-acre lake with wooded shoreline and peaceful inlets. The campground offers 254 sites including 237 electric sites, 17 primitive non-electric sites, and four ADA-accessible sites. Full hookup sites with electric and sewer are also available.

Amenities include two shower houses with flush toilets, laundry facilities, and a dump station. Potable water is available at the check-in station and Shower House 1. The camp store offers camping supplies, bait, snacks, hand-dipped ice cream, a grill, and seasonal bike and kayak rentals. Each site is equipped with a fire ring, and campfires are permitted only within fire rings.

Recreation options abound with swimming at the camper beach, fishing, sailing, and kayaking on the lake which permits boats up to 10 horsepower. The park also features hiking trails through mature woodlands, archery, and disc golf.

location.directions: Located at 1750 Osborn Road, Wilmington, OH 45177, approximately 50 miles east of Cincinnati. GPS coordinates: N 39° 23' 0.26", W 83° 54' 0.05".

payload.name: Lake Claiborne State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. The day-use area and swimming beach are temporarily closed for renovations including a new boat dock, picnic pavilions, and sand volleyball court. Park gates open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Reservations available through ReserveLaStateParks.com or by calling 833-609-0686.
payload.short_description: Welcome to beautiful Lake Claiborne State Park.
payload.medium_description: Lake Claiborne State Park sits on 617 wooded acres along a 6,400-acre clear-water reservoir in the rolling hills of north Louisiana. The campground offers 87 sites ranging from premium pull-through spots with water and electric hookups to primitive sites, all within easy access of excellent bass, crappie, and catfish fishing. A comfort station with showers and laundry facilities serves the campground, and the park features highly rated disc golf courses and a swimming beach.
payload.long_description: Welcome to beautiful Lake Claiborne State Park. Enjoy our 10 cabins, 87 campsites and many outdoor activities or just visit us to relax in unsurpassed natural beauty. For fishermen, our freshwater lake is lavishly stocked with bass, bluegill, catfish, crappie and bream. The whole family will love swimming at our sandy beach. Did we mention that we have the #1 and #2 rated disc golf courses in the whole state? Come one, come all and visit " your" Lake Claiborne State Park!

location.directions: From Homer, take LA-146 southeast for approximately 10 miles. The park entrance is on the left at 225 State Park Road.

links.title: Lake Claiborne State Park Official Page
Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Gwynn Tank
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come-first-served, no fee. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect on Gila National Forest through September 30, 2026. No potable water available. 14-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive campground in a ponderosa meadow adjacent to Gwynn Tank pond in the Gila National Forest, offering year-round first-come-first-served camping.
payload.medium_description: Gwynn Tank Campground is a flat, primitive site set in an open ponderosa meadow adjacent to its namesake pond, which is historically stocked for recreational fishing. The campground offers vault toilets and picnic tables but no potable water. Access is via Forest Road 141 from Reserve, a road that was once paved but now has many potholes.
payload.long_description:
Gwynn Tank Campground sits in the Reserve Ranger District of the Gila National Forest at the edge of a ponderosa pine meadow. The campground takes its name from the adjacent Gwynn Tank pond, which New Mexico Game and Fish has historically stocked for recreational fishing. The flat terrain and open setting make it a straightforward spot for tent camping or small RVs.

Facilities are primitive but functional: each site has a picnic table, and a vault toilet serves the campground. No potable water is available, so campers must bring their own supply. There is no fee, and sites are first-come-first-served with a 14-day stay limit.

The campground enforces several restrictions: OHVs and ATVs are prohibited within the campground, and saddle, pack, and draft animals are not allowed. Pets are welcome but must remain leashed. Each site is limited to two vehicles.

location.directions: From Reserve, drive south on State Highway 435 for 5 miles to Forest Road 141. Continue on FR 141 for 27.8 miles to the campground on the north side of the road. Note: FR 141 was once paved but now has many potholes; a resurfacing project is expected in 2026.

payload.name: Scenic Lake Of The Isles Group Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the camping season from April 1 through November 1. Reservations are required and can be made up to 120 days in advance online or by phone. A non-refundable reservation fee applies in addition to the nightly rate.
payload.short_description: Primitive group campsite for up to 60 people on the southern shore of Lake of the Isles at Scenic State Park, surrounded by virgin pine forests in northern Minnesota.
payload.medium_description: Scenic Lake of the Isles Group Camp is a primitive group camping area within Scenic State Park, accommodating up to 60 people. Located on the southern shore of Lake of the Isles, the site features picnic tables, fire rings with grills, hand pump water, and primitive toilets. A fishing pier sits at the group camp with a nearby carry-in boat launch for canoes and kayaks.
payload.long_description:
Scenic Lake of the Isles Group Camp provides a wilderness camping experience for scout troops, church groups, families, and organized gatherings within one of Minnesota's most treasured state parks. Established in 1921, Scenic State Park protects nearly 4,000 acres of virgin red and white pine forests surrounding several pristine lakes including Sandwick Lake, Coon Lake, and Lake of the Isles.

The group camp sits on the southern shore of Lake of the Isles, offering seclusion from the park's main campground areas while still providing access to the extensive trail system and multiple lakes. A fishing pier is located directly at the group camp, and a small carry-in boat launch nearby accommodates canoes and kayaks for exploring the lake.

As a primitive group camp, the site includes picnic tables, fire rings with grills for cooking, hand pump water access, and vault toilets. Modern restroom and shower facilities are not available at the group camp. Reservations are required and can be made up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota state park reservation system.

location.directions: From Bigfork, Minnesota, head east on County Road 7 for approximately 7 miles to reach Scenic State Park.

payload.name: Markham Springs
payload.status_description: Open for camping May 1 through October 1, 2026. Some sites reservable via Recreation.gov up to 6 months in advance; others are first-come, first-served. Low water levels in the pond; use caution near edges.
payload.short_description: Scenic riverside campground on the Black River in Mark Twain National Forest with electric and primitive sites, hot showers, and access to hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Markham Springs Campground sits along the Black River in a historic recreation area within Missouri's Mark Twain National Forest. The campground offers both electric RV sites and primitive tent camping loops in a wooded setting, with hot showers, vault toilets, and potable water. Fishing, kayaking, and hiking the Eagle Bluff and Bubble Springs trails are popular activities.
payload.long_description:
Markham Springs Campground is located in the scenic Markham Springs Recreation Area along the Black River in southwestern Missouri's Mark Twain National Forest. The area's history dates to 1901 when M. J. Markham operated a lumber mill on the property through the 1930s. The historic Fuchs House, a five-bedroom concrete and native stone home, remains on the property and is available for rental.

The campground features 32 sites across four loops: one electric loop with RV hookups, concrete vault toilets, water, and hot showers, plus three primitive loops in wooded settings along the river. Each site includes a picnic table, campfire ring with grill, and lantern post. The Black River offers excellent fishing for bass, sunfish, walleye, and catfish, with a boat ramp providing access for motorized and non-motorized watercraft.

Several hiking trails are accessible from the campground, including the 1.5-mile Eagle Bluff Trail loop along the river. The nearby town of Williamsville (3 miles) has a general store and fuel station.

location.directions: From Poplar Bluff, take Highway 67 north for 14 miles, then drive west on Highway 49 for 9 miles (about 3 miles past the town of Williamsville). Take the first right after crossing the Black River to enter Markham Springs Recreation Area.

photos.name: Showers and Restroom at Markham Springs

payload.name: Big Lake
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season, operating May through October. Both reservable and first-come, first-served sites are available. Fire bans are common during summer months. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights per 60-day period.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Big Lake at Santiam Pass with 49 sites, vault toilets, drinking water, and boat ramp. Views of Mt. Washington and access to Patjens Lakes Trail.
payload.medium_description: Big Lake Campground sits on the western shore of Big Lake at the top of Santiam Pass in the Willamette National Forest. Surrounded by alpine fir, hemlock, and lodgepole pine, the 49-site campground offers views of Mt. Washington and direct lake access via a boat launch. Water skiing, sailing, and swimming are popular activities. The nearby Patjens Lakes Trail provides hiking into Mt. Washington Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Big Lake Campground occupies the western shore of Big Lake at an elevation near Santiam Pass in Oregon's Willamette National Forest. The 49 single-unit campsites are spread across two original loops (sites 1-20, some with lake frontage) and an expansion section (sites 21-49) with larger parking spurs. The expansion sites feature stairs down to the table, fire ring, and tent pad below the parking area. Trailers up to 35 feet can be accommodated depending on site selection.

The campground is a hub for both motorized and non-motorized recreation. Big Lake is popular for water skiing, sailing, and swimming. The adjacent Santiam Pass Motorized Recreation Area draws OHV users, though OHV operation within the campground itself is prohibited except for entering and exiting. Patjens Lakes Trail departs from the area and loops through Mt. Washington Wilderness, passing scenic alpine lakes.

Amenities include filtered drinking water drawn from the lake, vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site. A boat launch and day-use picnic area sit mid-campground. Sites are a mix of reservable and first-come, first-served. Cellular service is limited or nonexistent.

location.directions: From McKenzie Bridge, OR, travel east on Highway 126 for 29.5 miles to Santiam Pass. Turn south on Big Lake Road (Forest Road 2690). Follow Big Lake Road for 3 miles to the campground on the north side of Big Lake.

links.title: USFS Willamette NF - Big Lake Campground

payload.name: Dexter
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. The campground typically operates from late May through September, weather dependent. First-come, first-served only with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground on the northern shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir in San Isabel National Forest, offering tent and RV sites at 9,300 feet elevation with vault toilets, fire rings, and no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Dexter Campground sits on the northern shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir in San Isabel National Forest, approximately 20 miles south of Leadville. The campground offers 11 tent-only sites and 8 large RV sites on a first-come, first-served basis. Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings, but no potable water is available. Firewood can be purchased at the host site.
payload.long_description:
Dexter Campground is a scenic first-come, first-served campground located on the northern shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir at 9,300 feet elevation. Adjacent to the Dexter Point Boating Site, the campground provides direct access to fishing, boating, and the stunning views of Colorado's highest peaks.

The campground features 11 tent-only sites and 8 large RV sites. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring all water needed for drinking, cooking, and fire extinguishing. Firewood is sold at the host site for $10 per bundle.

Sites cost $26 per night, which includes two vehicles. A third vehicle costs an additional $11 per night. Maximum occupancy is 8 people per site. Check-in is at 2 p.m., check-out at 11 a.m., and quiet hours are enforced from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Dogs are allowed but must remain leashed at all times.

location.directions: From Leadville, travel approximately 20 miles south on Highway 82 to the Twin Lakes area. The campground is located on the northern shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir, adjacent to Dexter Point Boating Site.

payload.name: Lake D'Arbonne State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park gates open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday, Saturday, and holidays. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorslouisiana.com or by phone at 833-609-0686.
payload.short_description: Piney forests, rolling hills, five fishing piers and a beautiful lake draw visitors to this quiet, majestic park.
payload.medium_description: Set on the shores of a 15,250-acre recreational lake in north-central Louisiana, Lake D'Arbonne State Park provides 65 improved campsites equipped with water and electricity. The camping area is tucked into rolling piney forests with comfort stations offering restrooms, hot showers, and laundry facilities nearby. The park features five fishing piers, a boat launch, hiking trails up to four miles, an 18-basket disc golf course, lighted tennis courts, and a seasonal swimming pool.
payload.long_description: Piney forests, rolling hills, five fishing piers and a beautiful lake draw visitors to this quiet, majestic park. Designed to keep the focus on nature, park facilities blend with the natural landscape to enhance the outdoor experience of this 655-acre park. Park sits on a 15,250-acre recreational lake. Seasonal swimming pool available for guest to enjoy during summer.

location.directions: Located at 3628 Evergreen Road, Farmerville, LA 71241. The park is in Union Parish in north-central Louisiana, accessible via LA Highway 33.

links.title: Lake D'Arbonne State Park Official Page

payload.name: Crooked Meadows Campground
payload.status_description: Closed in winter due to snow and road conditions. Typically opens in late spring when roads become accessible, usually sometime in May or June depending on snowpack. No reservations; first-come, first-served only.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground at 8,800 feet in Inyo National Forest near Mono Lake, offering pit toilets and picnic tables in a remote high-desert setting.
payload.medium_description: Crooked Meadows is a free, first-come, first-served primitive campground located at 8,800 feet elevation in the Glass Mountain area of Inyo National Forest. Accessed via dirt roads off Highway 120 East near Lee Vining, the campground provides basic facilities including pit toilets and picnic tables. Campers must bring their own water as none is available on site.
payload.long_description:
Crooked Meadows Campground sits at 8,800 feet elevation several miles south of Mono Lake in a geologically fascinating area of Inyo National Forest. The campground offers a remote, primitive camping experience in the Glass Mountain region, far from the crowds of more developed campgrounds.

Access is via a series of dirt roads: from Highway 120 East (east of Highway 395), take Pilot Springs Road to Taylor Canyon Road, then Forest Service Road 1S17 to the campground. The road conditions are rough enough that airing down tires may be advisable for some vehicles. This is not suitable for large RVs or trailers.

As a primitive campground, facilities are minimal. Pit toilets and picnic tables are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring all water needed for their stay. The campground is free and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations available.

location.directions: From Highway 120 East (east of Highway 395 near Lee Vining), take Pilot Springs Road south. Follow to Taylor Canyon Road, then take Forest Service Road 1S17 to the campground. Roads are unpaved and may be rough.

payload.name: Sandy Beach Camp
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates May 1 through September 30. All 58 sites are reservable through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Sandy Beach Campground sits on the northern shores of Coralville Lake, offering 58 sites with full hookups, electric, and walk-to tent options amid hardwood forest.
payload.medium_description: Sandy Beach Campground is an Army Corps of Engineers facility on the northern shores of Coralville Lake in eastern Iowa. The 58-site campground offers full hookup sites, standard electric sites with 20/30 amp service, and primitive walk-to tent sites. Modern restroom and shower facilities, a dump station, potable water, and a playground are available. The adjacent day use area provides boat ramp access, picnic shelters, and lake swimming.
payload.long_description:
Sandy Beach Campground occupies a prime location on the northern shores of Coralville Lake, nestled among heavily wooded mixed hardwood forest. Managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the campground provides 58 sites ranging from full hookup RV sites with water and electric to standard electric sites (20/30 amp) and primitive walk-to tent sites for those seeking a more rustic experience.

The campground features modern flush restrooms with shower facilities, a dump station, and potable water. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Sites accommodate RVs up to 44-48 feet depending on location. The adjacent Sandy Beach Day Use Area offers a boat ramp, fish cleaning station, large group picnic shelter, sand volleyball, and direct lake access for swimming.

Coralville Lake supports excellent fishing for largemouth and smallmouth bass, crappie, walleye, and catfish. The surrounding area features mountain bike and hiking trails, hunting opportunities, and the unique Devonian Fossil Gorge below the dam where visitors can explore a 375-million-year-old sea floor.

location.directions: From Interstate 380 at Shueyville, take Exit 10 east on 120th St NW for 1.2 miles. Turn right onto NE Curtis Bridge Rd and travel south 1.1 miles. Turn left onto Sandy Beach Rd NE and continue east 1.9 miles to the campground entrance on the right.

address.full: 3405 Sandy Beach Rd NE, Solon, IA 52333

payload.name: Clearwater #2 Forebay Forest Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served with no fees. No potable water available. Campers must pack out all trash. Maximum 14-day stay limit applies.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 5 pond-side sites near Toketee Falls and Umpqua Hot Springs in Umpqua National Forest. First-come, first-served with vault toilets and no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Clearwater #2 Forebay Forest Camp offers 5 quiet, secluded campsites around a forebay pond in the Umpqua National Forest. This free, first-come, first-served campground provides a peaceful setting for stargazing and serves as a base for visiting nearby attractions including Toketee Falls, Umpqua Hot Springs, and Watson Falls. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water or trash service.
payload.long_description:
Clearwater #2 Forebay Forest Camp is a small, primitive campground featuring 5 sites situated around a scenic forebay pond in Oregon's Umpqua National Forest. The campground offers a quiet, secluded atmosphere ideal for those seeking solitude and a night under the stars away from more developed recreation areas.

The campground operates on a free, first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Vault toilets are provided, but campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available on site. Water from nearby sources can be treated or filtered. There is no trash service, so all campers must pack out their garbage.

Nearby recreation attractions make this an excellent basecamp, including the spectacular Toketee Falls, relaxing Umpqua Hot Springs (day-use only), and the impressive Watson Falls. The maximum vehicle length is 25 feet, making this campground unsuitable for large RVs. Dogs are allowed but must be leashed during the day and confined to vehicles or tents at night.

location.directions: From Glide, OR, take Highway 138E eastbound toward Diamond Lake for 44 miles. Turn left onto NF-4776 and continue for 0.2 miles. Turn right onto NF-300 and continue for 0.1 miles. Turn left onto NF-252 and continue for 1.5 miles until reaching Clearwater #2 Forebay Forest Camp.

payload.name: Turtle River North Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with full services through early October. Water and dump station shut off October 4; comfort station closes November 1 for winter. Reservations available 95 days in advance via reservendparks.com.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground in the Turtle River valley offering electric and water hookups, showers, and pull-through sites 22 miles west of Grand Forks.
payload.medium_description: Turtle River North Campground sits in a scenic, wooded valley along the meandering Turtle River, part of a park built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s. The campground features modern sites with electric and water hookups, pull-through capability, flush toilets, showers, and a dump station. Over 13 miles of trails wind through forested hills and along the river.
payload.long_description:
Turtle River North Campground occupies the northern section of Turtle River State Park's modern camping area, set within a beautiful wooded valley carved by the Turtle River in Grand Forks County. The park's infrastructure dates to the 1930s when the Civilian Conservation Corps developed the area, and that legacy remains visible in the mature tree canopy and stonework throughout the grounds.

The North Campground offers modern sites equipped with water and 50-amp electric hookups. Nearly all sites are pull-through configurations shaded by large trees. A central dump station is located near the campground entrance. Facilities include a comfort station with flush toilets and showers. Fire rings and picnic tables are provided at sites.

Beyond camping, the park features over 13 miles of trails for hiking and mountain biking in summer, and cross-country skiing and sledding in winter. A visitor center provides orientation and interpretive materials. Primitive tent camping areas (Riverside, Cottonwood Crest, and Trapper's Rest) are available elsewhere in the park for those seeking more seclusion.

location.directions: From Grand Forks, drive 22 miles west on US Highway 2 to the park entrance near Arvilla. The park address is 3084 Park Avenue, Arvilla, ND 58214.

links.title: ND Parks - Turtle River State Park
ND Tourism - Turtle River State Park

payload.name: Sherando Lake Recreation Area Family Camping
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates early April through late October. All sites require advance reservation via Recreation.gov. Check-in is 1 PM and check-out is 11 AM. Entrance gate closed 10 PM to 6 AM daily. Firewood and ice are not available at the park. Cell service is unreliable; gate entry code provided in reservation confirmation.
payload.short_description: Family campground nestled between two lakes in Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains, featuring 66 reservable sites with flush toilets, showers, electric hookups in select loops, and beach access to a 25-acre spring-fed lake.
payload.medium_description: Sherando Lake Recreation Area Family Campground sits at 1,800 feet elevation between Upper and Lower Sherando Lake in the George Washington National Forest. The campground offers 66 sites across three loops: White Oak (Loop A) for tents and small units under 20 feet, and River Bend (Loop B) and Meadow (Loop C) with electric hookups for larger RVs up to 38 feet. Each site includes a picnic table, lantern post, and fire ring with grill. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, potable water, and a dump station. The 25-acre Lower Lake features a sandy swimming beach with bathhouse facilities.
payload.long_description:
Known locally as the jewel of the Blue Ridge Mountains, Sherando Lake Recreation Area Family Campground provides a complete outdoor experience in Virginia's George Washington National Forest. The campground occupies a scenic location between the 7-acre Upper Lake and 25-acre Lower Lake at approximately 1,800 feet elevation along Torry Ridge.

The facility features 66 campsites distributed across three distinct loops. White Oak Loop (Loop A) contains 35 non-electric sites suited for tents and camping units under 20 feet. River Bend Loop (Loop B) has 13 sites and Meadow Loop (Loop C) has 18 sites, both offering electric hookups with 50-amp service for larger RVs and trailers up to 38 feet. All sites include a picnic table, serving table, lantern post, and fire ring with grill. Food storage lockers are provided and their use is mandatory.

The Lower Lake swimming area features a sand beach with accessible ramp, bathhouse with changing rooms and showers, and designated swim zone. Both lakes are stocked with trout during spring and fall seasons. Hiking trails range from easy lakeside walks on the Lakeside and Cliff Trails to challenging day hikes on the White Rock Trail connecting to the Blue Ridge Parkway. Boats with gasoline motors are prohibited; only electric trolling motors, canoes, and kayaks are permitted.
