location.directions: From I-64, take Exit 96 just east of Stuarts Draft. Go south on State Route 624, which becomes State Route 664 at Lyndhurst. Continue south on State Route 664 approximately 8 miles to the entrance on the right. The gatehouse is approximately 0.5 miles ahead.

photos.name: Ramp to access lower lake swimming.
Lower lake swimming beach in early morning.
Lower Sherando Lake in the early morning.
Loop A, site A-11 Campground Host.
A photo of facility SHERANDO LAKE RECREATION AREA FAMILY CAMPING with Waterfront
Loop A bathhouse near site A-11.

payload.name: Suwannee River Wilderness Trail Woods Ferry Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for replacement of the access platform and boardwalk. The closure began February 17, 2026. No reopening date has been announced. Reservations are made through Florida State Parks.
payload.short_description: Primitive river camp on the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail accessible only by water, featuring screened sleeping platforms, tent sites, and hot showers at no cost.
payload.medium_description: Woods Ferry River Camp is the first river camp on the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail, located approximately 10 miles downstream from White Springs. This water-access-only facility offers five screened sleeping platforms with ceiling fans and electrical outlets, primitive tent camping sites, flush restrooms, and hot showers. Reservations are required but camping is free.
payload.long_description:
Woods Ferry River Camp serves as the gateway camp for paddlers embarking on the Suwannee River Wilderness Trail, situated at river mile 158 approximately 10 miles downstream from White Springs. The 4.79-acre facility is accessible exclusively by water, making it an ideal first-night destination for multi-day canoe and kayak expeditions down one of Florida's most scenic blackwater rivers.

The camp features five screened sleeping platforms, each accommodating up to eight people and equipped with a ceiling fan, electrical outlet, hammock hooks for three hammocks, and a small table with seating. Every platform includes an outdoor water spigot, dedicated fire ring, and picnic table. Beyond the platforms, primitive tent camping sites are available for those preferring traditional camping.

Facilities include flush restrooms with hot showers, grills, and a covered picnic pavilion. The camp operates year-round with no overnight fees, though reservations are required through Florida State Parks. Since no vehicle access exists, paddlers should coordinate with local outfitters if gear shuttling is needed.

location.directions: Woods Ferry River Camp is accessible only by water. The most common launch point is White Springs, approximately 10 miles upstream. Paddlers put in at the boat ramp in White Springs and travel downstream to reach the camp at river mile 158.

links.title: Suwannee River Water Management District - Woods Ferry

payload.name: Riley Horse Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Some sites are first-come, first-served while others are reservable through Recreation.gov. No potable water is available. Seasonal fire restrictions may be imposed.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground in Mount Hood National Forest with horse corrals, trail access to Cast Creek and Zigzag Mountain trails, and vault toilets along Lost Creek near the Sandy Wild and Scenic River.
payload.medium_description: Riley Horse Campground is a 14-site equestrian facility in the Old Maid Flat area of Mount Hood National Forest at 2,100 feet elevation. Sites include horse corrals or hitching posts, picnic tables, and fire rings with grills. The campground provides direct access to horseback riding trails including the 5.3-mile Cast Creek Trail connecting to Zigzag Mountain Trail. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Riley Horse Campground is an equestrian-focused facility located northwest of Mount Hood in Oregon's Mount Hood National Forest. Situated at approximately 2,100 feet elevation in the Old Maid Flat geologic area, the campground sits alongside Lost Creek near the Sandy Wild and Scenic River. While designed for equestrians, the 14 campsites may be used by other visitors as well.

Each site features horse corrals or cross-rail hitching posts, picnic tables, and campfire rings with grills. The campground has vault toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Average spur length is 35 feet. Campers are responsible for cleaning up after their horses.

Several trails are accessible directly from the campground. The 5.3-mile Cast Creek Trail leads to the Zigzag Mountain Trail, and combined with the 4.9-mile Horseshoe Ridge Trail, riders can complete a nearly 14-mile loop. The 3-mile Sandy River Trail follows the river. Fishing for trout, salmon, and whitefish is available in Lost Creek and the nearby Sandy River. The trailhead for Ramona Falls, one of Mount Hood's most popular hikes, is a short drive away.

location.directions: From Sandy, OR, follow US Highway 26 for 18 miles to Zigzag. Turn north (left) onto Lolo Pass Road (Road 18). Travel 4.5 miles, then turn right on Road 1825 and continue for approximately half a mile. Bear right, staying on Road 1825, cross the Sandy River bridge, and continue for another half mile to Road 1825-382. Turn right, cross the Lost Creek bridge, and the campground is immediately on the right.

payload.name: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, and holidays. Reservations can be made online or by phone up to 13 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Jewel of the Atchalaya Basin - Located deep in the heart of the Atchalaya Basin Swamp, recreational park that features: 18 rentable furnished cabins, 50 - Rv campsites with tent pads, Conference Center, Boat launch, rental pavilions, primitive campsites, and canoe -in campsites.
payload.medium_description: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park sits on 6,000 acres in the heart of the Atchafalaya Basin, providing campers access to one of America's largest river swamps. The campground offers premium waterfront sites with lake views, improved sites with hookups, and backcountry/canoe camping for those seeking solitude in the bayou wilderness. Flat-bottom boats, kayaks, and canoes are available for rent at the visitor center.
payload.long_description: Jewel of the Atchalaya Basin - Located deep in the heart of the Atchalaya Basin Swamp, recreational park that features: 18 rentable furnished cabins, 50 - Rv campsites with tent pads, Conference Center, Boat launch, rental pavilions, primitive campsites, and canoe -in campsites. The perfect place for a quiet relaxing stay, family picnic, bike ride, wetting a hook or just a quiet afternoon enjoying the wildlife and scenery at one of Louisiana's hidden treasures that has something for everyone.

location.directions: From New Iberia, take LA-31 north to Loreauville. Continue north on LA-86 through Loreauville, then turn west on Levee Road. Follow signs to the park entrance.

links.title: Lake Fausse Pointe State Park Official Page
Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Union Creek Campground - Rogue River
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open on a first-come, first-served basis. Sites 64-87 have a narrow access road with tight curves and large trees that may be difficult for some vehicles. Bears frequent the area; keep a clean camp and store food in closed containers.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC-built campground in old-growth forest where Union Creek meets the Rogue River, 18 miles west of Crater Lake National Park.
payload.medium_description: Union Creek Campground sits within the Union Creek Historic District amid towering old-growth forest where Union Creek flows through the campground to meet the Rogue River. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934, this heavily-used campground offers 73 campsites with vault toilets and potable water. Union Creek Resort is within walking distance for supplies and meals. The Upper Rogue River Trail and Rogue Gorge Trail System provide immediate hiking access, with Crater Lake National Park just 18 miles east.
payload.long_description:
Union Creek Campground occupies a scenic stretch of old-growth forest in the Union Creek Historic District, where its namesake creek intersects the Rogue River. Constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934, the campground retains a classic national forest character with well-spaced sites tucked among large trees. The Upper Rogue River here is fed by snowmelt and springs from the Cascade Range, including Mount Mazama's slopes.

The campground offers 73 individual sites, most standard nonelectric, plus 3 full-hookup RV sites located near the day-use parking area along an ATV trail. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. Thirteen vault toilets and drinking water spigots are distributed throughout. A campground host sells firewood and gray water sumps are available. Union Creek Resort is within walking distance, providing a convenience store, restaurant, and ice cream shop.

The entire length of the Upper Rogue River is paralleled by the hiker-only Upper Rogue River Trail, easily accessed for short segments. The Rogue Gorge Trail System connects Rogue Gorge Day Use through the campground to Natural Bridge Day Use Area. Nearby attractions include Rogue Gorge, Natural Bridge (where the river runs underground through a lava tube), Diamond Lake Resort, and Crater Lake National Park.

location.directions: From Medford, take OR-62 (Crater Lake Highway) approximately 56 miles toward Crater Lake National Park. The campground is on the left (west) through the Union Creek Wayside parking area. From Klamath Falls, travel north on US 97 to OR-62, then west about 15 miles past Crater Lake National Park to Farewell Bend at the intersection of OR-62 and OR-230; Union Creek is about 1 mile south on OR-62.

payload.name: Raccoon Lake
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 6 months in advance through Indiana State Parks reservation system. Blue-green algae advisory in effect for the lake; do not drink lake water and shower after swimming. Only approved firewood is permitted.
payload.short_description: Raccoon Lake State Recreation Area offers over 300 campsites on Cecil M. Harden Lake in Parke County, Indiana, featuring electric and non-electric options, a swimming beach, boat ramps, and miles of hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Raccoon Lake State Recreation Area, centered on the 2,060-acre Cecil M. Harden Lake, provides over 300 campsites including electric, non-electric, and primitive options. The park features a swimming beach, five boat launch ramps, a camp store, modern restroom and shower facilities, and 8 miles of hiking trails through hardwood forests and prairie restorations. The nearby Historic Mansfield Roller Mill adds cultural interest with tours and demonstrations.
payload.long_description:
Raccoon Lake State Recreation Area encompasses Cecil M. Harden Lake, a 2,060-acre reservoir created by damming Big Raccoon Creek in Parke County. Located 50 miles west of Indianapolis and 35 miles northeast of Terre Haute, the park offers 327 campsites spread across multiple campgrounds including 240 electric sites with 30-amp hookups, 39 non-electric sites, and 35 primitive sites. Facilities include modern bath houses with showers, dump stations, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site.

The recreation area provides extensive water-based activities with five boat launch ramps, a marina with boat rentals including jon boats and jet skis, and a swimming beach with a beach house featuring showers and a concession stand. Anglers will find a fish cleaning station and bait shop on site. Beyond the water, visitors can explore 8 miles of hiking trails ranging from easy to rugged, featuring views of rocky cliffs, second-growth forests, and prairie restorations.

Additional amenities include a camp store selling firewood and supplies, an amphitheater, playground, basketball and volleyball courts, horseshoe pits, and an archery range. The Historic Mansfield Roller Mill, a working 1880s grist mill, offers tours and demonstrations nearby. The park also provides 330 acres of hardwood forest and open field for seasonal hunting.

location.directions: From Indianapolis, travel west on US-36 approximately 50 miles to Rockville. The park entrance is on US-36 in Parke County. From Terre Haute, travel northeast on US-36 approximately 35 miles.

links.title: Indiana DNR - Cecil M. Harden Lake

payload.name: Stonelick State Park Grant Family Shelter
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter, not a campground. Overnight camping is not permitted at this facility. The shelter is available for reservation year-round for group picnics and gatherings. The park is open daily from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
payload.short_description: Reservable picnic shelter near the beach at Stonelick State Park in southwestern Ohio, featuring covered space with tables, grills, and electricity for group gatherings.
payload.medium_description: The Grant Family Shelter is a day-use picnic shelter located near the swimming beach at Stonelick State Park in Pleasant Plain, Ohio. This covered facility accommodates up to 60 people and includes picnic tables, grills, and electrical hookups, making it suitable for family reunions, celebrations, and group picnics.
payload.long_description:
The Grant Family Shelter is a reservable day-use picnic shelter situated near the beach at Stonelick State Park, a 1,058-acre park tucked into the rolling highlands of southwestern Ohio about 24 miles east of Cincinnati. The shelter offers covered space with picnic tables, grills, and electrical hookups, accommodating groups of up to 60 people.

This facility is designed for day-use activities such as family celebrations, reunions, and company picnics. It is not a campground and does not permit overnight camping. For overnight stays, Stonelick State Park operates a separate campground with over 100 electric sites, a camper cabin, showers, flush toilets, and a dump station.

The park surrounding the shelter offers a 200-acre lake with a 500-foot swimming beach, boat launches for electric motors, kayak and paddleboard rentals, fishing opportunities, and over 5 miles of hiking trails. The park is open daily from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.

location.directions: From Cincinnati, take State Route 727 east. The Grant Family Shelter is located near the beach entrance at 2895 Lake Drive, Pleasant Plain, Ohio.

links.title: Ohio DNR Stonelick Lake Fishing Area

payload.name: Long Point State Park - Finger Lakes
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The cottage reopens Saturday, May 16, 2026 through Sunday, October 11, 2026. Reservations require a 7-night minimum (Saturday to Saturday) from Memorial Day through Labor Day, and a 2-night minimum during shoulder season.
payload.short_description: A lakeside cottage rental on Cayuga Lake's east shore, featuring a private boat dock, fire ring, and access to 4.5 miles of hiking trails in New York's Finger Lakes wine country.
payload.medium_description: Long Point State Park offers a single full-service cottage on a scenic V-shaped peninsula extending into Cayuga Lake. The cottage sleeps four and includes a private boat dock, fire ring, and picnic area. The park features a 4-lane boat launch, swimming beach with lifeguards, playground, and 4.5 miles of hiking trails with views of spectacular sunsets over the lake.
payload.long_description:
Situated on a V-shaped spit of land extending into Cayuga Lake, Long Point State Park provides a unique lakeside retreat in the heart of New York's Finger Lakes wine region. The park's sole accommodation is a full-service cottage sleeping four guests, featuring a bedroom with double bed, living room with sleeper sofa, full bathroom, kitchen with gas stove and refrigerator, wood stove, and air conditioning. Outside, guests enjoy a private boat dock, fire ring, grill, and picnic table on a small lawn.

The park itself offers a 4-lane boat launch popular with anglers and boaters, a swimming beach with seasonal lifeguards, a modern playground, and 4.5 miles of hiking trails. Located just south of the village of Aurora and near numerous Finger Lakes wineries, the park is known for its spectacular sunset views across Cayuga Lake. Cross-country skiing and snowshoeing are permitted on trails during winter months.

location.directions: Located at 2063 Lake Rd., Aurora, NY 13026 on the east side of Cayuga Lake, just south of the village of Aurora.

links.title: NY State Parks - Long Point Finger Lakes

payload.name: Carolina Beach State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The park is closed only on Christmas Day. Reservations are available through ReserveAmerica.
payload.short_description: Coastal campground near Wilmington featuring 79 sites in a wooded setting by Snow's Cut, with full hookup options, camper cabins, and access to the famous Venus flytrap habitat.
payload.medium_description: Carolina Beach State Park offers 79 wooded campsites along the Cape Fear River and Snow's Cut, including 10 sites with full hookups and 6 camper cabins. The campground features flush restrooms with hot showers, picnic tables and fire rings at every site, and long driveways that accommodate large RVs. The park protects one of the few places in the world where Venus flytraps grow naturally.
payload.long_description:
Carolina Beach State Park sits along the Cape Fear River and Snow's Cut near Wilmington, offering 79 campsites in a shaded coastal forest. The campground includes 69 sites without hookups and 10 sites with full hookups (water, electric, and sewer), plus six camper cabins that sleep up to six people with heating and air conditioning. Every site has a picnic table and fire ring or grill, and long driveways can accommodate RVs of all sizes.

A centrally located bathhouse provides flush toilets and hot showers, with potable water spigots distributed throughout the campground. Trash and recycling bins are available, and firewood is sold on site. Three ADA-accessible campsites and one accessible cabin are available for campers with mobility needs.

The park is notable for protecting one of the few remaining habitats where Venus flytraps grow wild. Hiking trails wind through diverse ecosystems including longleaf pine savanna and pocosin wetlands. A marina provides boat access to the river and Intracoastal Waterway, making this an excellent base for both terrestrial and water-based recreation.

location.directions: From I-40 East, take NC 132 through Wilmington, continue on US 421, cross Snow's Cut Bridge over the Intracoastal Waterway, turn right at the second stoplight onto Dow Road, and follow park signs. Address: 1010 State Park Road, Carolina Beach, NC 28428.

address.full: 1010 State Park Rd, Carolina Beach, NC 28428

payload.name: Clear Creek Ohv Riding Area Blackwater River State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round but camping is only permitted Friday and Saturday nights. Drought conditions may trigger burn bans affecting camping availability. All campers must have an OHV riding pass to reserve a campsite.
payload.short_description: Primitive OHV campground in Blackwater River State Forest with 4 electric/water hookup sites, open Friday and Saturday nights only for registered off-highway vehicle riders.
payload.medium_description: Clear Creek OHV Riding Area offers 4 primitive campsites with electric (30/50 amp) and water hookups in an open grass field within Blackwater River State Forest. Camping is restricted to Friday and Saturday nights, and all campers must possess an OHV annual pass or day-use riding pass. The facility provides access to over 52 miles of challenging off-highway vehicle trails through the forest.
payload.long_description:
Clear Creek OHV Riding Area at Blackwater River State Forest is a dedicated campground for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts located north of Milton, Florida. The facility features 4 primitive campsites with 30/50 amp electric and water hookups, situated in an open grass field without shade. Each site accommodates up to 8 people and 50-foot equipment length. A large picnic shelter with 4 tables and ceiling fans provides a communal gathering space, and restrooms are available on-site.

Camping is only permitted on Friday and Saturday nights, and all campers must possess either an annual OHV riding pass or a day-use riding pass to reserve a site. The riding area provides access to more than 52 miles of challenging OHV trails through the forest. DOT-approved helmets are required for all riders, and children under 16 must also wear eye protection and over-ankle boots. This is an alcohol-free facility, and pets are not permitted.

The surrounding Blackwater River State Forest offers additional recreational opportunities including hiking trails, fishing lakes, and canoe/kayak trips through pristine forest lands.

location.directions: From Milton, head north on Highway 191, turn left on Eastgate Road, right on Whiting Field Circle, then left on Redbird Trail. Drive north until the facility appears on your right. Enter at the first gate when you see an open grass field.

payload.name: The Ledge Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. Individual sites are $20/night (cash or check only), 14-night stay limit per 30 days. Seasonal fire restrictions may apply during high fire danger periods.
payload.short_description: Primitive BLM campground in a scenic red rock valley along Kane Creek Road near Moab, popular with ATV, UTV, and 4WD enthusiasts seeking desert canyon camping.
payload.medium_description: The Ledge Campground offers 105 first-come, first-served sites spread across five separate camping areas in a striking red rock valley southwest of Moab. Popular with off-road vehicle enthusiasts, the campground provides access to world-class OHV and mountain bike trails including Amasa Back, Pritchett Canyon, and Captain Ahab. Best visited in spring and fall due to intense summer heat and limited shade.
payload.long_description:
The Ledge Campground encompasses five distinct camping areas (Ledges A through E) with 105 individual sites nestled in a dramatic red rock canyon along Kane Creek Road, approximately 8.5 miles from Moab. The scenic desert valley setting draws ATV, UTV, and 4WD users who come for the exceptional network of nearby trails, including Amasa Back, Hymasa, Hunter Canyon Rim, Pritchett Canyon, Jackson, and Captain Ahab.

This is a primitive campground with vault toilets but no potable water or hookups. Sites operate on a first-come, first-served basis at $20 per night, payable by cash or check at the campground. Each site accommodates up to 10 people and two vehicles, with a 14-night stay limit per 30-day period. A reservable group site accommodating 15-30 people is available separately through Recreation.gov.

The access road is paved for the first 4 miles from Moab before becoming gravel with two shallow wash crossings and one short, steep switchback. Spring and fall are the ideal seasons; summer brings extreme heat with minimal shade.

location.directions: From central Moab (Center St. and Main St.), head south to Kane Creek Road between Burger King and McDonald's. Turn right (west) on Kane Creek Road and continue straight at the stop sign. The road is paved for 4 miles, then becomes gravel with two shallow wash crossings and one short, steep switchback. The campground is approximately 8.5 miles from Highway 191.

payload.name: Forestville Mystery Cave State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open mid-May through October. Reservations required via reservemn.usedirect.com or by calling 866-857-2757. Reservations can be made up to 120 days in advance with a non-refundable $8 online or $10 phone reservation fee.
payload.short_description: Two primitive group campsites at Forestville/Mystery Cave State Park offering tent camping with fire rings, picnic tables, and a shared roofed shelter in southeastern Minnesota's bluff country.
payload.medium_description: Forestville/Mystery Cave State Park's Group Campground features two primitive sites, Riverview and Sumac Hill, each accommodating up to 50 people. Both sites have picnic tables, fire rings with grills, and share a roofed shelter. Vault toilets and water access are nearby. The park spans 3,583 acres with guided cave tours, historic Forestville village, spring-fed trout streams, and 20 miles of hiking trails.
payload.long_description:
Located in Minnesota's bluff country in Fillmore County, Forestville/Mystery Cave State Park's Group Campground offers two secluded primitive campsites tucked among the trees. Riverview and Sumac Hill each accommodate up to 50 people, making them ideal for scout troops, family reunions, or outdoor clubs. Each site includes picnic tables and a fire ring with grill, and both sites share access to a roofed shelter for group gatherings.

The group camps are primitive in nature with vault toilets nearby and access to water, but no modern restroom facilities or showers. The main park campground has shower and restroom facilities as well as a dump station, though these are separate from the group camping area.

Forestville/Mystery Cave is one of southern Minnesota's largest state parks at 3,583 acres. Beyond camping, visitors can explore Mystery Cave on guided tours, visit the restored 1899 village of Historic Forestville, fish three spring-fed trout streams, or hike 20 miles of trails through hardwood forests and prairies. The park also offers equestrian camping and horseback riding trails.

location.directions: From Spring Valley or Preston on State Highway 16, go four miles south on Fillmore County Highway 5, then two miles east on Fillmore County Highway 118 to the park entrance.

payload.name: South Fork State Recreation Area Tomera Cove
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through ReserveNevada.com from 3 days to 11 months in advance. Camping limited to 14 consecutive nights per 30-day period. Quiet hours 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.
payload.short_description: Group camping area on the shore of South Fork Reservoir in northeastern Nevada, offering basic amenities with 2 picnic tables and a fire ring for group gatherings.
payload.medium_description: Tomera Cove is a group use camping area at South Fork State Recreation Area, located on the 1,650-acre South Fork Reservoir near Elko, Nevada. Named after the historic Tomera Ranch that once occupied this land, the cove provides a basic group camping setup with 2 picnic tables and 1 fire ring. Campers have access to flush restrooms with showers and an RV dump station at the main park facilities. The area is open year-round and reservable through ReserveNevada.com.
payload.long_description:
Tomera Cove is a group use camping area within South Fork State Recreation Area, situated on the scenic 1,650-acre South Fork Reservoir in northeastern Nevada. The site takes its name from the historic Tomera Ranch, which was established in the area during the 1860s settlement period and later sold to the State of Nevada in the early 1980s. The cove offers a basic but functional group camping setup with 2 picnic tables and 1 fire ring, ideal for groups seeking a lakeside camping experience.

The broader South Fork State Recreation Area provides additional amenities that Tomera Cove campers can access. Flush restrooms with free showers are available at the East Campground, and an RV dump station is located near the main north park entrance, open year-round. The reservoir offers excellent fishing opportunities including trout, bass, and catfish, with a designated trophy fishery section along the South Fork Humboldt River featuring catch-and-release regulations.

The park remains open year-round, with camping limited to 14 consecutive nights per 30-day period. Campfires are permitted only in designated fire rings. Pets are welcome but must remain on a leash no longer than 6 feet. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. The area also offers opportunities for wildlife viewing, with mule deer, beavers, badgers, and various waterfowl commonly spotted around the reservoir.

location.directions: From Elko, head south on State Route 228 for approximately 16 miles to reach South Fork State Recreation Area. The park entrance is off the main north access road. Contact the ranger station for specific directions to Tomera Cove within the park.

links.title: South Fork State Recreation Area - Nevada State Parks

payload.name: Deer Tower
payload.status_description: Deer Tower is a day-use horse trailhead, not an overnight campground. No fees, no restrooms, and no water are available at this site.
payload.short_description: Deer Tower is a horse trailhead in the Ozark National Forest, not an overnight campground. It serves as a rustic pull-off access point for 17 miles of equestrian trails through the rugged Ozark Mountains.
payload.medium_description: Deer Tower Trailhead is a rustic pull-off in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest designed for horse riders seeking access to 17 miles of trails through the rugged Ozark Mountains. This is a day-use trailhead, not an overnight campground. The site has no restrooms, no water, and no fees. The trail system consists of three smaller loop trails.
payload.long_description:
Deer Tower Trailhead is a primitive access point in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest in Newton County, Arkansas, designed primarily for equestrian users. It provides a rustic starting point for exploring 17 miles of trails through the scenic and rugged Ozark Mountains. The trail system is composed of three interconnected loop trails that offer horse riders a challenging backcountry experience.

This is a day-use trailhead, not an overnight campground. The USFS indicates there are no restrooms, no potable water, and no developed facilities at this location. Horse riders looking for overnight accommodations should seek out nearby developed campgrounds in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest that offer equestrian facilities.

location.directions: From Jasper, take Arkansas 7 south for 15 miles, then turn right (west) on Arkansas 16 and go 1 mile. Turn right (northwest) on FS 1206 (paved) and go approximately 1 mile.

payload.name: Grapevine
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to flood damage from the 2022 Black Fire burn scar. Monsoon flooding washed away portions of the campground. The Forest Service is evaluating options including reducing the footprint or converting to day-use. No reopening date announced.
payload.short_description: A free primitive campground on the banks of the Gila River near Gila Cliff Dwellings. Currently closed indefinitely due to flood damage from the 2022 Black Fire.
payload.medium_description: Grapevine Campground sits where the East, West, and Middle Forks of the Gila River converge, with beautiful cliffs as a backdrop. Named after an old grapevine still visible today, this free primitive campground offered sandy grounds with both marked sites and dispersed camping options. The campground has been closed since July 2022 after post-Black Fire monsoon flooding swept away portions of the facility.
payload.long_description:
Grapevine Campground is located in the heart of the Gila wilderness, approximately 40 miles north of Silver City along New Mexico Highway 15. The campground occupies a scenic spot where the three forks of the Gila River come together, offering campers a riverside experience with dramatic cliff formations as a backdrop. Before its closure, the campground was known for its shaded sites right next to the river and its proximity to Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument.

The campground was severely damaged in July 2022 when monsoon storms sent floods of water, rock, soil, and debris rushing down the East Fork from the Black Fire burn scar, washing away portions of the campground that held campsites. The Forest Service has received $16.5 million in Black Fire recovery funding, with approximately $3 million earmarked for recreational facility repairs including campgrounds.

Options under consideration include reducing the campground's footprint to retain sites outside the floodplain or converting the site to day-use only while enlarging nearby campgrounds to compensate for lost camping opportunities. No reopening timeline has been announced.

location.directions: Located 40 miles north of Silver City on the east side of New Mexico Highway 15 between mile markers 37 and 38. Long vehicles should use caution due to the steep downgrade road into the campground.

links.title: NPS - Camping Near Gila Cliff Dwellings

payload.name: Airport Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Typically opens in early June and remains open through October. No fees or reservations required.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground in Eldorado National Forest at 5,300 ft elevation, popular as a staging area for the Rubicon 4WD Trail and OHV recreation.
payload.medium_description: Airport Flat Campground is a free, first-come-first-served primitive campground in the Crystal Basin area of Eldorado National Forest. At 5,300 feet elevation, it serves as a popular staging area for OHV enthusiasts accessing the Rubicon 4WD Trail. Sites are arranged in pods and include vault toilets, picnic tables, fire rings, bear boxes, and trash service, but no potable water.
payload.long_description:
Airport Flat Campground sits at 5,300 feet elevation in the Crystal Basin area of Eldorado National Forest. The campground is a favorite staging area for off-highway vehicle recreationists, providing direct access to the legendary Rubicon 4WD Trail and a network of OHV-accessible forest roads. Sites are arranged into pods that can accommodate groups of 15 to 25 people.

This is a primitive, no-fee campground operating on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, fire rings with grills, bear boxes for food storage, and trash disposal. There is no potable water on-site; nearby river water must be boiled or filtered before drinking. A dump station is available at the Loon Lake boat ramp.

Campers are limited to a 14-day stay per district per year. Check-in is at 2:00 PM and check-out at 1:00 PM. Single sites are limited to 2 vehicles and 6 people. Pets are allowed but must be kept on a leash at all times. All OHVs require spark arrestors, proper safety helmets, and Green Sticker registration.

location.directions: 23 miles east of Placerville on Highway 50, then 24 miles north on Ice House Road (Forest Road 3), and 3 miles north on Forest Road 33.

address.full: 1 Gerle Creek Tract, Pollock Pines, CA 95726

payload.name: Mohican Group Camps & Shelters
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Group camp sites accommodate up to 25 people each at $45 per night. Reservations available through reserveohio.com. Day-use shelters can be reserved up to 1 year in advance with a 3-day cutoff.
payload.short_description: Primitive group camping facilities at Mohican State Park offering four rustic group sites and day-use shelters, ideal for organized groups seeking a wilderness experience near the scenic Clear Fork Gorge.
payload.medium_description: Mohican Group Camps & Shelters provides primitive group camping in Mohican Memorial State Forest adjacent to Mohican State Park. Four group camp sites accommodate up to 25 people each around a central communal firepit. Facilities are rustic with portable toilets, well water, and no electricity, making this ideal for scout troops, church groups, and other organizations seeking a back-to-basics outdoor experience. Day-use shelters are also available for reservation.
payload.long_description:
Located within the 4,525-acre Mohican Memorial State Forest surrounding Mohican State Park, the Group Camps & Shelters provide a primitive camping experience for organized groups. The four group campsites are arranged around a large central communal firepit, with each site also featuring its own individual fire ring and picnic tables. Amenities are intentionally minimal: three portable toilets, a well water spigot, and dumpsters serve all sites.

This rustic setting is separate from the main family campground and offers a more secluded experience near the striking Clear Fork Gorge and its hemlock forests. The area provides access to over 32 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding. Nearby attractions include Malabar Farm State Park, Pleasant Hill Lake, and Charles Mill Lake.

Day-use shelters are also available for group gatherings and can be reserved through the Ohio State Parks reservation system. The group facilities are designed for nonprofits, scout troops, church groups, and other organizations seeking an affordable outdoor experience without the amenities of developed campgrounds.

location.directions: From State Route 3 in Loudonville, head south. The group camps are located at 3054 County Highway 939, Perrysville, OH 44864, within Mohican Memorial State Forest adjacent to Mohican State Park.

payload.name: Rush Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for seasonal winter closure. Opens the week prior to Memorial Day Weekend (around May 18-22) through October 31. First-come, first-served; no reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Primitive 8-site campground along Rush Creek, 8 miles north of Weaverville in Shasta-Trinity National Forest. First-come, first-served with vault toilets, fire rings, and no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Rush Creek Campground is a small, rustic campground nestled along Rush Creek among Douglas fir, oak, and maple trees. Located 8 miles north of Weaverville off Highway 3, the campground offers 8 well-separated single sites providing good privacy. All sites include fire rings with grills and picnic tables. The campground has vault toilets but no potable water. Sites accommodate shorter vehicles with an average back-in length around 16 feet. First-come, first-served only.
payload.long_description:
Rush Creek Campground is a primitive Forest Service campground situated along the banks of Rush Creek in Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The campground stretches through a forest of Douglas fir, oak, and maple, with the sound of the creek audible throughout. Most of the 8 campsites are well-separated, offering good privacy for campers seeking a quiet, natural setting.

All sites feature fire rings with grills and picnic tables, with some sites also having a Klamath stove. Vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The campground road and spurs are unpaved and accommodate smaller vehicles, with an average back-in length of about 16 feet. Fishing for brook trout is available in Rush Creek.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. It is managed by Vista (formerly Shasta Recreation Company) as a concessionaire for the Forest Service. Dogs are allowed on a leash of 6 feet or shorter. Horse and pack animals are not permitted.

location.directions: From Weaverville, take Highway 3 north for about 8 miles. Turn left at the Rush Creek Campground sign and drive 1/2 mile.

payload.name: Cedar Pass Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from late March through mid-October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Check-in at 1:00 p.m., check-out at 11:00 a.m. Kiosk staffed 8:00 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. 14-night stay limit applies during summer. Quiet hours 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
payload.short_description: Seasonal campground in Badlands National Park with 96 sites offering spectacular views of badlands formations. Features flush toilets, coin-operated showers, dump station, and electric hookup sites.
payload.medium_description: Cedar Pass Campground is the primary developed campground in Badlands National Park, featuring 96 level sites surrounded by prairie grasslands and iconic badlands buttes. Located near the Ben Reifel Visitor Center and Cedar Pass Lodge, the campground offers tent sites, non-electric RV sites, and electric RV sites. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, potable water, and a dump station. Ranger-led evening programs and night sky viewing are held at the adjacent amphitheater from Memorial Day through Labor Day.
payload.long_description:
Cedar Pass Campground serves as the main base camp for exploring Badlands National Park, offering 96 level sites with expansive views of the park's dramatic geologic formations. The campground sits amid the vast open prairie, with badlands buttes of sandstone, siltstone, and volcanic ash providing a stunning backdrop for sunrises, sunsets, and exceptional night sky viewing due to minimal light pollution.

The campground accommodates both tent campers and RVs, with site types including tent-only, RV non-electric, and RV electric. All sites include a shaded picnic table. Facilities include flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers during the summer season, with vault toilets available year-round. Potable water is available on-site, and a complimentary dump station is located in the group loop area. Two wheelchair-accessible campsites and one accessible group site are available.

Campfires are prohibited throughout Badlands National Park to protect the prairie grassland ecosystem; however, small portable propane grills are permitted for cooking. The Cedar Pass Amphitheater, within walking distance of the campground, hosts nightly ranger programs from Memorial Day through Labor Day featuring educational talks and guided night sky viewing with telescopes.

location.directions: From Rapid City: Travel east on I-90 to exit 110, turn south onto Hwy 240 (Badlands Loop Road), enter at the Pinnacles entrance, travel 30 miles, then turn right on Hwy 377. Campground is on the left. Alternatively, take I-90 to exit 131, turn south on Hwy 240, enter at the Northeast entrance, travel 8 miles to Cedar Pass Lodge, and make a slight left onto Hwy 377. From Sioux Falls: Travel west on I-90 to exit 131, turn south onto Hwy 240, enter at Northeast entrance, travel 8 miles.

payload.name: Woodland Cg
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates April through November. Some sites are reservable via Recreation.gov; others are first-come, first-served. No potable water on site.
payload.short_description: Small 6-site forest campground off Highway 204 in the Umatilla National Forest, offering easy access to hiking trails in the North Fork Umatilla Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Woodland Campground is a small, quiet campground located just off Highway 204 in the Umatilla National Forest. With only 6 standard nonelectric sites, it offers both shady and sunny options that are easily accessible for quick overnight stops or longer stays. The campground provides convenient access to numerous hiking trails, including those in the North Fork Umatilla Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Woodland Campground is a modest 6-site campground tucked just off Highway 204 in Oregon's Umatilla National Forest. Managed by the Walla Walla Ranger District, this low-key spot sits at an elevation that provides relief from summer heat while remaining accessible for most of the camping season. Sites feature picnic tables and fire pits, though campers should note there is no potable water available.

The campground serves as a convenient base for exploring the Blue Mountains and the North Fork Umatilla Wilderness. Highway 204 makes access straightforward whether approaching from Weston (23 miles east) or Elgin (18 miles northwest). The light usage levels mean solitude is easy to find, making it ideal for those seeking a peaceful forest experience without crowds.

Some sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while others remain first-come, first-served. The campground's simple amenities and affordable $8 per night fee make it well-suited for tent campers and those with smaller rigs looking for a no-frills forest camping experience.

location.directions: From Weston, Oregon: Travel approximately 23 miles east on Highway 204. Woodland Campground is located just off Highway 204 on your left. From Elgin, Oregon: Travel approximately 18 miles northwest on Highway 204. Woodland Campground is on your right.

payload.name: Horseshoe Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December. Currently open and accepting reservations.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground at James River State Park with pull-through sites, electric/water hookups, 20 covered horse stalls, and a full-service bathhouse in Virginia's Blue Ridge foothills.
payload.medium_description: Horseshoe Campground at James River State Park is a dedicated equestrian facility featuring 9 pull-through sites with electric and water hookups (20/30/50 amp) that can accommodate horse trailers up to 40 feet. The campground includes 20 covered horse stalls, 5 tent pads, a full-service bathhouse with hot showers including wheelchair-accessible facilities, and a free dump station for overnight guests. Each site has a fire ring grill, picnic table, and lantern hanger.
payload.long_description:
Horseshoe Campground is the equestrian camping area at James River State Park, nestled in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains in Buckingham County, Virginia. The park features rolling grasslands, quiet forests, and beautiful views along 3 miles of James River shoreline. Equestrian campers will find 9 generously sized pull-through sites designed to allow two trailers to share a common area between them, with each site accommodating trailers up to 40 feet.

The campground provides 20 covered horse stalls for boarding your horses, along with 5 tent pads for additional camping flexibility. A current negative Coggins report is required by state law for all horses. Pine shavings for horse bedding are available for purchase, though bedding is not provided. Each campsite includes a fire ring grill, picnic table, and lantern hanger.

Amenities include a full-service bathhouse with hot showers (4 unisex showers plus 1 wheelchair-accessible), electric pedestals with 20, 30, and 50-amp outlets at each site, and a free dump station for overnight guests. Firewood is available for a small fee. The park offers access to extensive equestrian trails, and overnight guests enjoy free use of the boat launch for river access.

location.directions: From U.S. 60 West, turn right onto Route 605 (Riverside Dr.) at the James River Bridge. Travel 7 miles, then turn left onto Route 606. The park is located at 104 Green Hill Drive, Gladstone, VA 24553.

payload.name: Poplar Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally, typically late May through September depending on snow conditions. Road 4440 (Twisp River Road) is currently open but has several washouts not recommended for trailers or low clearance vehicles. First-come, first-served only; 14-day maximum stay.
payload.short_description: A forested campground on the Twisp River at 2,900 ft elevation with vault toilets, potable water, and access to Twisp River Trail #440.
payload.medium_description: Poplar Flat Campground is a peaceful, forested site along the Twisp River in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, 21 miles northwest of Twisp. The campground features vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables, a group shelter, and direct access to Twisp River Trail #440 for hiking and mountain biking. Sites are first-come, first-served at $20/night.
payload.long_description:
Poplar Flat Campground sits at 2,900 feet elevation in a pretty forested setting along the banks of the Twisp River in the Methow Valley. The campground provides a quiet base for exploring the area, with direct access to Twisp River Trail #440 for hiking, mountain biking, and day hikes. River and stream fishing opportunities are available nearby.

Facilities include vault toilets, potable water from a hand pump, picnic tables at each site, and a group picnic shelter that can accommodate up to 12 people. A community kitchen area is also available. Sites accommodate 2 tents or 1 RV plus 1 tent, with a maximum of 2 vehicles per site.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Payment is $20/night for a single site, with an additional $10/night for a second vehicle. On-site payment is available via the Recreation.gov mobile app's Scan and Pay feature where cell connectivity permits. Interagency Senior/Access pass holders receive a 50% discount on single sites.

location.directions: From Twisp, turn west off State Highway 20 onto Twisp River Road (County Road #9114). Drive 12 miles as the road becomes Forest Road #44. Continue 5 miles as the paved road turns to gravel and becomes Forest Road #4440. Drive 4 more miles to Poplar Flat Campground. Total distance is 21 miles northwest of Twisp.

payload.name: Beacon Rock State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season, which runs April 15 through October 15. Reservations available through washington.goingtocamp.com. Some sites are first-come, first-served. Note: South side of Beacon Rock is closed for rock climbing through July 15, 2026 due to peregrine falcon nesting; the hiking trail remains open.
payload.short_description: Scenic campground in the Columbia River Gorge with forested tent sites and full-hookup RV sites, offering hiking, rock climbing, and equestrian access.
payload.medium_description: Beacon Rock State Park Campground sits within a 4,458-acre park in the heart of the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area. The campground features a historic Upper Campground built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1935, the Woodard Creek Campground with both standard and full-hookup RV sites, an equestrian camp, and a group camp. Over 26 miles of trails provide access to hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Beacon Rock State Park Campground is located in Skamania County, Washington, within the Columbia River Gorge National Scenic Area. The park encompasses 4,458 acres and offers multiple camping areas to suit different needs. The Upper Campground, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1935, provides a forested setting with standard campsites. Woodard Creek Campground offers 2 standard sites and 5 full-hookup RV sites accommodating vehicles up to 40 feet.

The park is renowned for Beacon Rock itself, an 848-foot volcanic plug that offers some of the best traditional rock climbing routes in the Pacific Northwest. A trail with 52 switchbacks leads to the summit for non-climbers. Over 26 miles of roads and trails are open to hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian use, with two primitive sites available for horse campers.

Facilities include restrooms with showers, drinking water, trash service, fire pits at sites, and picnic tables. The group camp features a kitchen shelter with power and a picnic shelter. Reservations are available through washington.goingtocamp.com from mid-April through mid-October, with some sites available first-come, first-served.

location.directions: Located on State Route 14, approximately 35 miles east of Vancouver, Washington, in the Columbia River Gorge. The park entrance is on the north side of the highway.

links.title: Beacon Rock State Park - WA State Parks

payload.name: Rocky Fork State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. Reservations are required and can be made up to 6 months in advance through reserveohio.com.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at Rocky Fork Lake in Highland County, Ohio, offering 190 sites with electric and full hookup options, modern amenities, and direct lake access.
payload.medium_description: Rocky Fork State Park Campground sits on the northwest shore of Rocky Fork Lake, a 2,080-acre reservoir in Highland County. The 190-site campground is divided into upper and lower areas, with the lower section offering more open terrain and lake views while the upper area is more wooded. Sites range from primitive to full hookup, with amenities including flush toilets, showers, laundry, dump station, and camp store. Campers enjoy beach access, mini-golf, disc golf, and direct boating from the campground.
payload.long_description:
Rocky Fork State Park Campground occupies a prime location on the northwest corner of Rocky Fork Lake, a 2,080-acre reservoir with 31 miles of shoreline in Highland County, Ohio. The campground features 190 sites spread across upper and lower camping areas. The lower area provides more open terrain with lake views, while the upper area offers more wooded, shaded sites. Site options include 31 primitive sites, 96 electric hookup sites, and 44 full hookup sites, accommodating everything from tent campers to large RVs.

Modern amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, laundry facilities, a dump station, and a camp store. Free WiFi is available at the camp office for registered campers. Recreation options within the campground include a miniature golf course, disc golf course, basketball courts, and corn hole. Campers also have access to a dedicated beach area and boat launch with tie-ups.

The surrounding park offers unlimited horsepower boating, multiple boat ramps, fishing piers, and public beaches. The landscape includes wetlands, mixed hardwood forests, and the scenic Rocky Fork Gorge. The marina provides boat rentals and supplies during the season.

location.directions: From Hillsboro, take US-50 east approximately 6 miles. Turn left onto North Shore Drive and follow to the campground at 9800 North Shore Drive.

links.title: Ohio DNR Rocky Fork Campground Map
Ohio DNR Rocky Fork Park Map

payload.name: North Toledo Bend State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. Park gates are open 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. The entrance station operates 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Reservations are made through the Go Outdoors Louisiana system.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Toledo Bend Reservoir offering 63 RV campsites with water and electric hookups, flush restrooms, hot showers, and direct access to one of the South's premier fishing lakes.
payload.medium_description: North Toledo Bend State Park campground sits on the shores of Toledo Bend Reservoir, one of the largest man-made lakes in the United States. The 63-site campground features both premium waterfront sites and improved sites a short walk from the shoreline, all with water and electric hookups, picnic tables, and fire rings. Facilities include flush restrooms, hot showers, a dump station, laundry, and a full-size swimming pool.
payload.long_description:
North Toledo Bend State Park occupies over 900 acres along the western shore of Toledo Bend Reservoir, a 185,000-acre impoundment straddling the Louisiana-Texas border that consistently ranks among the top bass fishing lakes in the country. The campground offers 63 sites split between Loop A (27 sites) and Loop B (36 sites), with premium sites commanding direct lake views and improved sites positioned a short walk from the water. All sites include water and electric hookups, a picnic table, and a fire ring; sewer hookups are not available, but a dump station serves the campground.

Facilities cater to extended stays with flush restrooms, bathhouses with hot showers, and an on-site laundry. The park's day-use area includes an Olympic-size swimming pool open seasonally, two pavilions with electrical lighting and grills, and a meeting room accommodating 60 people. The double-lane boat ramp, large parking lot, and fish cleaning station make it easy to spend full days on the water chasing largemouth bass, crappie, and catfish.

Beyond fishing, the park features two 18-hole disc golf courses and trails for hiking. Ten deluxe cabins sleeping up to six are available for those preferring more comfort, and a group camp with five dormitories can accommodate up to 150 guests. The park welcomes pets in outdoor areas when leashed.

location.directions: From Zwolle, head west on LA-3229 for approximately 9 miles to North Toledo Park Road. Turn right and follow the road to the park entrance at 2907 North Toledo Park Road, Zwolle, LA 71486.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks - North Toledo Bend

payload.name: Robinson Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. High-elevation campgrounds in this area typically open late May to June depending on snow conditions. First-come, first-served when open; no reservations.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive high-elevation campground at 6,800 feet with family and equestrian sites on the Western States Trail in Tahoe National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Robinson Flat Campground is a remote, free campground at the end of Foresthill Divide Road, offering 7 family sites and 7 equestrian sites at 6,800 feet elevation. Located near a meadow and stream on the Western States Trail, this primitive campground has vault toilets and requires campers to pack out all trash. The narrow, winding access road makes trailers inadvisable.
payload.long_description:
Robinson Flat Campground sits at 6,800 feet elevation in the Tahoe National Forest, marking the terminus of the scenic Foresthill Divide Road driving tour. This remote, no-fee campground offers 14 sites split evenly between family camping and equestrian use, positioned near a beautiful meadow and stream under a canopy of pines and firs.

The campground serves as a staging area for the Western States Trail, popular with both hikers and equestrians. Facilities are minimal: vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water or trash service. A hand pump well exists nearby but water should be treated. Campers must pack out everything they bring in.

Access requires driving 27 miles northeast of Foresthill on a road that becomes narrow, winding, and unpaved near the end. Trailers are not recommended due to road conditions. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no reservation system. OHV use is restricted to 2-wheeled vehicles only, with motorized vehicles prohibited in adjacent wilderness areas.

location.directions: From I-80, take the Foresthill exit and drive on Foresthill Road for 15 miles to the Forest Service Ranger Station just before Foresthill. Continue on Foresthill Road for 27 miles until the pavement ends at Robinson Flat. The final stretch is narrow and winding.

payload.name: River Island Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours daily. Park improvements are in process with possible construction noise on weekdays. Weekend stays April through September require a 2-night minimum; holiday weekends require 3 nights. Reservations available at azstateparks.com or by calling (877) MY-PARKS.
payload.short_description: Colorado River campground in Parker, AZ with 37 hookup sites, pull-throughs up to 65 feet, sandy beach, boat launch, and year-round desert water recreation.
payload.medium_description: River Island State Park offers 37 electric/water hookup campsites along the Colorado River near Parker, Arizona. The campground features 8 beachfront sites and 29 standard RV sites including 19 pull-throughs accommodating rigs up to 65 feet. Amenities include flush restrooms with showers, a dump station, fire rings, and a three-lane boat launch providing direct river access for boating, fishing, and jet skiing.
payload.long_description:
River Island State Park sits on the banks of the Colorado River in the Sonoran Desert near Parker, Arizona. The 37-site campground caters to both tent campers and RVers, with 8 grass beachfront sites overlooking the river (20-amp/water, max 24 feet) and 29 larger sites with 20/30/50-amp service and water hookups. Nineteen of the standard sites are pull-throughs accommodating RVs up to 65 feet deep, while 10 are back-ins.

The park provides solid amenities for its location: two ADA-accessible restroom/shower buildings, a dump station near the ranger station, fire rings and picnic tables at each site, and a covered ramada. A three-lane boat launch offers direct access to the Colorado River, making this a hub for boating, jet skiing, waterskiing, and fishing. A sandy beach and cove provide swimming areas.

Beyond water activities, the park has a hiking trail and connects to off-highway vehicle routes for desert exploration. River Island Market sits a quarter mile outside the park entrance for groceries, fuel, and supplies. The mild winter climate draws snowbirds, while summer brings peak water recreation season.

location.directions: 5200 N. Highway 95, Parker, AZ 85344. The park is located on Highway 95 approximately 15 miles north of Parker.

payload.name: San Pedro Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Standard sites are first-come, first-served; the group site requires a Recreation.gov reservation 3-180 days in advance. County-wide burn ban in effect until July 8, 2026: all fires including charcoal are prohibited. No potable water available. 14-night consecutive stay limit, 60-night annual limit.
payload.short_description: Year-round primitive campground on Lake Amistad with 41 sites, vault toilets, covered tables, and BBQ grills. Best suited for large RVs among Amistad's campgrounds.
payload.medium_description: San Pedro Campground sits within Amistad National Recreation Area on the U.S.-Mexico border near Del Rio, Texas. The campground offers 34 standard sites, 8 walk-in tent sites, and one reservable group site accommodating up to 75 people. Each site has a covered picnic table and BBQ grill. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water or hookups. The campground is accessed via a 1.25-mile graded gravel road and is well-suited for large RVs.
payload.long_description:
San Pedro Campground is a primitive campground within Amistad National Recreation Area, located 9 miles northwest of Del Rio, Texas. The campground provides access to Lake Amistad, a reservoir formed at the confluence of the Rio Grande, Devils, and Pecos Rivers known for excellent bass fishing, swimming, boating, and scuba diving year-round.

The campground offers 41 total sites: 34 standard drive-in sites suitable for tents or RVs, 8 walk-in tent-only sites, and one group site that must be reserved through Recreation.gov. Each individual site includes a covered picnic table and BBQ grill. The group site features a large pavilion, campfire ring with benches, vault toilet, pedestal grill, and table. Vault toilets are available throughout but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own water supply.

Of Amistad's campgrounds, San Pedro is best suited for large RVs. The campground is accessed via a 1.25-mile graded gravel road off Spur 454. While there are no hookups at the campground, an RV dump station with potable water is available at Diablo East boat ramp for registered campers. Standard sites are first-come, first-served at $6 per night. The group site accommodates 1-75 people with tiered pricing from $35 to $155.

location.directions: From Amistad NRA Visitor Center, head east on Highway 90 for 3.2 miles. Turn left onto Spur 454 and travel 0.7 miles. Turn right and follow directional signs up the 1.25-mile graded gravel road to the campground.

photos.name: Fire Ring at San Pedro Group Campground
Yellow mesquite flowers frame a view of Lake Amistad National Recreation Area
San Pedro Group Campground  Picnic Shelter

alerts.title: County-wide Burn Ban in Effect until July 8
alerts.content: In keeping with the county-wide burn ban enacted on January 15 and extended on April 9, fires--including charcoal fires--are not permitted within Amistad National Recreation Area. To read the Val Verde County Commissioners Court Order, click "More".

alerts.title: Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and Walkway Access Are Closed
alerts.content: The Diablo East Marina Cove, Scuba Cove, and walkway access are closed because of the presence of excessive docking material, unsafe walkway and dock, and unstable, loose ground. The area will reopen once these hazards have been corrected.

alerts.title: Only Left Side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon Boat Ramps Are Open - Rest Are Closed
alerts.content: Due to low water levels, only the left side of Diablo East and Rough Canyon boat ramps are open. Please use caution with Spur 406 and Spur 454 launches, as the water may be too shallow to launch most boats. To see a list of open ramps, click on "more."

alerts.title: Help Prevent Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Infestation
alerts.content: A number of lakes are infested with an array of aquatic invasive species that damage natural ecosystems and waterways. Boaters are advised to Clean, Drain, and Dry all boats and equipment every time they leave the water.

alerts.title: Visitor Center Will Be Open But Cannot Process Transactions on 8/14
alerts.content: On August 14, Amistad Visitor Center will provide orientation and information but cannot sell passes or permits or exchange annual lake use pass receipts. Camping permits and lake use passes may be purchased at fee machines or at Pay.gov.

payload.name: South Fork Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground operates from Father's Day weekend through October. Reservations can be made through Recreation.gov 4 days to 12 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Large group campground in the Crystal Basin Recreation Area of Eldorado National Forest, accommodating up to 125 guests with vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings.
payload.medium_description: South Fork Group Campground is the largest group campground in the Crystal Basin Recreation Area, offering a single reservable group site that can host up to 125 people and 20 vehicles. Located at 5,200 feet elevation in Eldorado National Forest, it features vault toilets, picnic tables, fire rings, a group cooking area with double grills, and bear boxes. There is no potable water available.
payload.long_description:
South Fork Group Campground is the largest group campground in the Crystal Basin Recreation Area, nestled within the Eldorado National Forest at 5,200 feet elevation. The campground offers a single reservable group site that accommodates up to 125 guests and 20 vehicles, making it ideal for large gatherings, family reunions, or group outings. The site features a group cooking area with food preparation tables and double grills, bear boxes, and campfire rings.

The South Fork of the Rubicon River is within walking distance, providing excellent fishing and swimming opportunities. Gerle Creek Reservoir is 5 miles north for non-motorized boating. The campground is also a popular staging area for OHV users, though off-road vehicles are not permitted within the campground itself.

Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings at each site. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own supply or boil river water. Reservations are required through Recreation.gov. The campground has a gated entrance with a combination lock provided after booking.

location.directions: Travel 21 miles east from Placerville on Highway 50 and turn left on Ice House Road. Go 25 miles north and turn left on South Fork Road. The campground is a mile from the turn-off, on the right side of the road.

payload.name: Lower Bucks
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Expected to open May 22, 2026, conditions permitting. Operates first-come, first-served from approximately Memorial Day through Labor Day.
payload.short_description: Small, primitive lakeside campground with 7 shady sites on Bucks Lake in Plumas National Forest, adjacent to the Bucks Lake Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Lower Bucks is a rustic 7-site campground on the shores of Bucks Lake in the Mount Hough Ranger District of Plumas National Forest. The high mountain lake is bordered by the Bucks Lake Wilderness on one side and recreation residences and resorts on the other. Sites are first-come, first-served with bear boxes at each site. No water or restrooms are available. Supplies and boat rentals can be found at nearby resorts.
payload.long_description:
Lower Bucks Campground offers a primitive camping experience on the scenic shores of Bucks Lake, a high mountain lake in Plumas National Forest. The campground features 7 shady, lakeside sites that provide direct access to the water and proximity to the Bucks Lake Wilderness. Each site is equipped with a bear box for food storage, essential in this black bear habitat.

This is a minimalist campground with no restrooms and no potable water, so campers must be fully self-sufficient. The trade-off is a quieter, more secluded experience compared to the larger developed campgrounds in the Bucks Lake Recreation Area. The campground is popular with hunters in season.

Nearby resorts offer supplies, boat rentals, and other services. The area provides excellent opportunities for fishing, boating, hiking into the Bucks Lake Wilderness, and wildlife viewing.

location.directions: Located 32 miles northeast of Oroville on Oroville-Bucks Lake Road, or 17 miles west of Quincy on Oroville-Bucks Lake Road.

address.full: 1901 W End Rd, Meadow Valley, CA 95956

payload.name: Crystal Springs
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 1 through September 30. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Check-in at 6:00 PM (self-check-in with cards at entrance), check-out at 4:00 PM. Location is unstaffed.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on Lake Ouachita with 74 sites featuring electric/water hookups, flush toilets, hot showers, and access to one of Arkansas's clearest lakes for scuba diving and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Crystal Springs Campground sits on the shores of Lake Ouachita, approximately 10 miles west of Hot Springs National Park. The campground offers 63 sites with electric (50/30/20 amp) and water hookups plus 11 tent-only sites, all surrounded by Ouachita National Forest pines. Amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, dump station, fish cleaning station, two swim beaches, playground, and the largest boat ramp on Lake Ouachita. The lake's exceptional clarity makes it popular for scuba diving, with rare freshwater jellyfish and striped bass visible among the rocks.
payload.long_description:
Crystal Springs Campground occupies a prime position on Lake Ouachita, a 40,000-acre reservoir fed by the cool Ouachita River in the Ouachita Mountains of Arkansas. The campground serves as a gateway to one of the state's most popular lakes, drawing approximately 1.2 million visitors annually for its crystal-clear waters and exceptional underwater visibility. Sites are positioned along lake coves with pine tree shade throughout.

The campground features 74 total sites: 63 standard electric sites with water and electric hookups (50/30/20 amp service), and 11 tent-only sites. Each site includes a concrete picnic table and grills. Two handicap-accessible sites are available (#22 and #73). Facilities include flush restrooms, hot showers, a dump station, and a fish cleaning station. Two group picnic shelters with electricity can be reserved.

Recreation centers on the lake, with scuba diving being particularly notable due to the high underwater visibility. Anglers target striped bass and other species, while the Charlton trailhead at the campground entrance provides access to a four-mile hiking and mountain biking trail that connects to the 223-mile Ouachita National Recreation Trail. Winter months bring bald eagles for bird watching and photography.

location.directions: From Hot Springs, Arkansas, take US 270 west about 15.4 miles to North Crystal Springs Road. Turn right and follow access road three miles north to the park.

address.full: 1330 N Crystal Springs Rd, Royal, AR 71968

payload.name: Blue Rock Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with full amenities available during summer months. From November 1 through April 15, services are limited: hot showers are closed, the upper campground is closed, and only the lower camp (sites 51-102) with vault toilets remains accessible. Reservations required via reserveohio.com or by calling 866-OHIOPARKS.
payload.short_description: Blue Rock State Park offers rustic non-electric camping amid rugged hills and oak-hickory forests in southeastern Ohio, with a 15-acre lake, swimming beach, and family-oriented atmosphere.
payload.medium_description: Blue Rock State Park provides 97 non-electric campsites split between upper and lower campgrounds surrounding a scenic 15-acre lake. The lower campground offers proximity to the swimming beach and camp store, while the upper area accommodates tent campers and equestrians. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Amenities include flush toilets at the lower camp, vault toilets, seasonal hot showers at the beach bathhouse, and a dump station. This primitive campground has no hookups or potable water.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the rugged hills of Muskingum County, Blue Rock State Park encompasses 322 acres of land dominated by oak and hickory forests, plus a 15-acre lake stocked with bass, trout, catfish, and bluegill. The campground offers a quiet, family-oriented experience for those seeking a more rustic outdoor adventure without electrical hookups.

Camping is divided between two areas: the lower campground (sites 51-102) sits near the 250-foot swimming beach and seasonal camp store, while the upper campground provides tent-only sites and accommodates equestrian campers with access to 26 miles of bridle trails in the adjacent state forest. Each campsite comes equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Facilities include flush toilets at the lower camp, vault toilets throughout, seasonal hot showers at the beach bathhouse, and a dump station. Campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available on-site.

Recreational opportunities include five marked hiking trails totaling approximately 3 miles, fishing, swimming, and boating with electric motors, rowboats, or canoes. The park also features basketball and volleyball courts, horseshoe pits, an archery range, and a playground. Pets are welcome on leash but not permitted on the swimming beach.

location.directions: 7924 Cutler Lake Road, Blue Rock, Ohio 43720

address.full: 7911 Cutler Lake Rd, Blue Rock, OH 43720

payload.name: Douthat State Park Cabins And Lodges
payload.status_description: Open year-round with daily park hours 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Check-in is 4 p.m., check-out is 10 a.m. Memorial Day to Labor Day requires 6-night minimum stays. Off-season minimum is 2 nights. Reservations available via reservevaparks.com.
payload.short_description: Historic CCC-built cabins and lodges in Virginia's Allegheny Mountains, featuring 32 rustic cabins and 3 lodges with full kitchens, bathrooms, and mountain views at Douthat State Park.
payload.medium_description: Douthat State Park offers 32 cabins and 3 lodges nestled in the Allegheny Mountains. Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s, these accommodations feature rustic wood construction with modern amenities including heat, AC, full kitchens, and bathrooms. Each unit includes outdoor fire pits, charcoal grills, and picnic tables. The park surrounds a 50-acre lake with hiking trails, fishing, and swimming.
payload.long_description:
Douthat State Park Cabins and Lodges preserve the legacy of CCC craftsmanship while providing comfortable mountain retreats. The 32 cabins range from efficiency to three-bedroom units, each featuring heat and AC, full kitchens with refrigerators, stoves, microwaves, and all necessary cookware. Cabins 1-25, 33, and 35 have open porches with rocking chairs, while cabins 26-30 feature enclosed screened porches. Most cabins have wood-burning fireplaces with one complimentary bundle provided. Cabin 34 has a gas-log fireplace.

Three lodges accommodate larger groups: Douthat Lodge (12 guests, renovated in 2025) sits atop the mountain with five bedrooms and three bathrooms. Creasey Lodge (18 guests) is a universally accessible single-story structure near the park office with WiFi. Beards Mountain Lodge (16 guests) is fully universally accessible with six bedrooms and a gas-log fireplace. All lodges include dishwashers and washer/dryers, amenities not available in the cabins.

Guests must bring their own linens and towels. Pets are welcome for a nightly fee. The park offers hiking trails, lake swimming, fishing, and boat rentals. Cell service is limited, but WiFi is available at the Park Office and Camp Store.

location.directions: From I-64, take Exit 27 near Clifton Forge. Turn north onto State Route 629. Travel north two miles to the park entrance sign and another four miles to the park office at 14239 Douthat State Park Road, Millboro, VA 24460.

address.full: 12786 Douthat State Park Rd, Millboro, VA 24460

payload.name: Mitchell State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Some sites in the northern section of the campground experienced flooding from the April 2026 storms. Boat docks may not be fully installed and boat mooring along the canal may be limited. Reservations available via MIDNRReservations.com.
payload.short_description: Modern 221-site campground between Lake Mitchell and Lake Cadillac in northern Michigan, offering electric hookups, showers, boat launches, and beach access.
payload.medium_description: William Mitchell State Park sits on 660 acres between Lake Mitchell and Lake Cadillac, connected by the historic Clam Lake Canal. The modern campground features 221 sites with electrical hookups, mature tree shade, and select sites along the canal. Amenities include flush toilets and showers, dump station, swimming beach, two boat launches, paddlesport rentals, and the Carl T. Johnson Hunting and Fishing Center. Popular for fishing (walleye, perch, bass, panfish) and winter activities including ice fishing and snowmobiling.
payload.long_description:
William Mitchell State Park occupies 660 acres in Wexford County between Lake Mitchell and Lake Cadillac, with the historic Clam Lake Canal running through the property. Established in 1920 and named for local sawmill operator William W. Mitchell, the park has long been a popular camping, fishing, and boating destination in northern Michigan.

The modern campground offers 221 sites nestled between the Clam Lake Canal and Lake Cadillac. Most sites are shaded by mature trees, with select spots along the canal. All sites feature electrical hookups (some with 50-amp service), picnic tables, and fire rings. Facilities include a toilet and shower building, sanitation station, drinking water, pull-through sites, and ADA-accessible sites. The park has two boat launches, an accessible fishing pier, swimming beach with buoyed swim area, playground, paddlesport rentals, and a camp store.

Beyond camping, the 2.5-mile Heritage Nature Trail winds through woodlands and marshes. The Carl T. Johnson Hunting and Fishing Center offers exhibits on regional wildlife and educational programs. Winter brings ice fishing, snowmobiling, snowshoeing, and cross-country skiing.
