location.directions: Located at 6093 East M-115 in Cadillac, Michigan. The park is situated between Lake Mitchell and Lake Cadillac.

payload.name: Lake Loramie State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All sites require advance reservations through reserveohio.com; no walk-ins. Check-in is 3 PM for campsites and 4 PM for cabins. Park gates open 6 AM to 11 PM daily. The dog park is temporarily closed due to wind storm damage as of March 2026.
payload.short_description: Year-round Ohio state park campground on Lake Loramie featuring 177 sites with full hookups, electric, and non-electric options, plus ADA-compliant cedar cabins near hiking trails and a swimming beach.
payload.medium_description: Lake Loramie State Park Campground sits along the historic Miami-Erie Canal corridor in west-central Ohio. The campground offers 177 sites ranging from primitive to full-hookup, along with ADA-compliant cedar cabins. On-site amenities include a full-service camp store with bike rentals and equipment loans, modern shower facilities, and a dump station. The park provides access to over 8 miles of hiking trails, an 18-hole disc golf course, and Lake Loramie for boating, fishing, and swimming.
payload.long_description:
Lake Loramie State Park Campground is located on the shores of Lake Loramie, a reservoir originally constructed as a feeder lake for the Miami-Erie Canal in the 1840s. The campground offers a variety of site types including full-hookup sites with water, sewer, and electric; electric-only sites; and non-electric tent sites. ADA-compliant cedar cabins provide an alternative for those seeking a roofed accommodation.

The park offers extensive recreational opportunities throughout the year. Summer visitors enjoy the swimming beach, boating, and fishing on the 845-acre lake. Over 8 miles of hiking trails wind through the park, with portions following the historic canal towpath as part of both the Buckeye Trail and the North Country National Scenic Trail. An 18-hole disc golf course provides additional recreation.

Winter activities include ice fishing, sledding, and snowmobiling when conditions permit. The on-site camp store is open to the public and offers bike rentals along with loans of games, fishing equipment, and sporting gear. All reservations are made through reserveohio.com or by calling the state parks reservation line.

location.directions: From I-75, take Exit 102 for State Route 119 toward Anna/Botkins. Head west on SR-119 for about 5 miles, then turn north onto State Route 362. The park entrance is approximately 2 miles ahead on the left.

payload.name: Falcon State Park
payload.status_description: Open daily 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. year-round. The boat ramp is currently closed due to low lake levels; shore launching remains available. Electrical work is underway near the park entrance and headquarters with possible service interruptions.
payload.short_description: Falcon State Park offers lakeside camping on Falcon International Reservoir with full hookup RV sites, pull-through configurations, and year-round South Texas birding opportunities.
payload.medium_description: Falcon State Park sits on the shores of the 84,000-acre Falcon International Reservoir in the Rio Grande Valley. The park features 98 campsites across three loops: full hookup pull-through sites at Javelina Run, water/electric sites at Mesquite Bend, and water-only sites at Black Bass Loop. The subtropical climate makes it a popular winter destination for RVers and a premier birding location with species rarely seen elsewhere in the U.S.
payload.long_description:
Falcon State Park occupies 572 acres along the Texas-Mexico border at Falcon International Reservoir, one of South Texas's premier fishing and water recreation destinations. The park draws visitors year-round with its mild subtropical climate, though winter months see the heaviest RV traffic as snowbirds flock to the region.

The campground offers 98 sites divided among three distinct areas. Javelina Run provides 31 full-hookup pull-through sites with 30/50-amp electrical service, water, and sewer connections. Mesquite Bend has 31 water/electric pull-through sites with a wheelchair-accessible restroom. Black Bass Loop contains 36 primitive water-only sites available first-come, first-served. All sites include fire rings, picnic tables, and access to hot showers and restrooms.

Beyond camping, the park is renowned as a birding hotspot along the Central Flyway, with species like the green jay, Altamira oriole, and ringed kingfisher drawing birders from across the country. The reservoir offers excellent fishing for largemouth bass, channel catfish, and white bass, along with swimming, water skiing, and kayaking. A 2.8-mile trail system winds through the thornscrub habitat typical of this South Texas brush country.

location.directions: From US-83 in Falcon Heights, turn west onto Park Road 46 and continue 2.5 miles to the park entrance at 146 Park Road 46, Falcon Heights, TX 78545.

address.full: 139 St Park Rd, Falcon Heights, TX 78545

payload.name: East Chickenbone Campground
payload.status_description: Isle Royale National Park is open for the season (April 16 through October 31). Early season conditions apply through late May with potential snowbanks, downed trees, and limited services at Rock Harbor and Windigo. A 2-night stay limit applies June 1 through Labor Day. Free overnight permit required for parties of 6 or fewer.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry tent campground on the east end of Chickenbone Lake in Isle Royale National Park, accessible only by foot or portage.
payload.medium_description: East Chickenbone Campground is an inland backcountry campground situated on the east end of Chickenbone Lake within Isle Royale National Park. The campground has 4 tent sites (3 first-come, first-served and 1 reservable group site) and is accessible only by foot or by canoe/kayak via a 1.2-mile portage from McCargoe Cove or a 0.2-mile portage from Lake Livermore. No motorboat access. Self-contained stoves only; campfires are prohibited.
payload.long_description:
East Chickenbone Campground is a primitive backcountry campground located on the east end of Chickenbone Lake, accessed via the East Chickenbone Trail in Isle Royale National Park. This inland site offers solitude for backpackers and paddlers willing to make the trek. The campground features 4 tent sites: 3 individual sites available first-come, first-served and 1 group site requiring advance reservation. Note that the campground is not on the lakeshore itself.

Access is limited to foot travel or canoe/kayak with portaging. Paddlers can reach the campground via a 1.2-mile portage from McCargoe Cove or a shorter 0.2-mile portage from Lake Livermore. There is no direct boater access; West Chickenbone Campground is more suitable for watercraft access. A 2-night consecutive stay limit applies from June 1 through Labor Day.

Amenities are minimal: seasonal composting toilets and food storage lockers are provided. Water is available but non-potable and must be filtered and chemically treated. Campers must pack out all trash. Campfires are prohibited; only self-contained camp stoves are allowed. Pets are not permitted anywhere in Isle Royale National Park. A free overnight permit is required for parties of 6 or fewer, obtained upon arrival. Groups of 7 or more must reserve in advance.

location.directions: Located on the east end of Chickenbone Lake, off the East Chickenbone Trail. Accessible by foot via the trail system, or by canoe/kayak using a 1.2-mile portage from McCargoe Cove or a 0.2-mile portage from Lake Livermore. No direct motorboat access.

links.title: Isle Royale Operating Hours & Seasons - NPS

photos.name: Tent in East Chickenbone Campground during fall.
The East Lake Chickenbone Trail travels along Chickenbone Lake for part of the trail.

payload.name: Simpson Springs Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Potable water is available March through November. Sites 1-10 are reservable through Recreation.gov; sites 11-19 are first-come, first-served. Maximum two vehicles and eight persons per site.
payload.short_description: Historic BLM campground on the Pony Express National Historic Trail in Utah's West Desert, offering 20 sites with vault toilets, seasonal water, and access to OHV trails and geode beds.
payload.medium_description: Simpson Springs Campground sits at 5,100 feet elevation on the eastern edge of Utah's West Desert, near the historic Simpson Springs Pony Express station. The campground features 20 sites with accessible vault toilets, seasonal potable water, fire rings, and picnic tables. Sites 1-10 are reservable through Recreation.gov while sites 11-19 are first-come, first-served. Popular activities include OHV riding, mountain biking, horseback riding, and exploring the Pony Express Trail.
payload.long_description:
Simpson Springs Campground is a Bureau of Land Management facility located near the historic Simpson Springs station on the Pony Express National Historic Trail. At 5,100 feet elevation on the eastern edge of Utah's West Desert, the campground provides a launching point for exploring this remote and historically significant landscape. The site was home to a Civilian Conservation Corps camp in the late 1930s and early 1940s.

The campground offers 20 sites, many with pull-through parking on compacted gravel suitable for RVs up to 30 feet. Amenities include three accessible unisex vault restrooms, five water hydrants dispersed throughout the campground (operational March through November), fire rings at each site, and cement picnic tables. The campground is designed with accessibility in mind, featuring wheelchair-accessible water hydrants and restrooms.

Popular activities include OHV riding, mountain biking, horseback riding, wildlife viewing, and hunting for geodes at nearby geode beds. Wild horses roam the surrounding desert. Sites 1-10 can be reserved through Recreation.gov, while sites 11-19 remain first-come, first-served at $15 per night.

location.directions: From Interstate 80, take Exit 199 (Tooele) and travel south on Highway 36 for approximately 40 miles. Near Faust, turn west onto the Pony Express Road and drive 25 miles on maintained gravel road to the campground. Alternatively, from I-80 take Exit 77 (Dugway-Rowley), drive south on State Route 196 to Dugway, continue south 10 miles on maintained dirt road to Pony Express Road, then turn west for 10 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Upper Wind River Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance through reserve.wyoming.gov. The dump station at park headquarters operates April through October.
payload.short_description: Scenic riverside campground in Boysen State Park along the Wind River tailwaters, popular for fishing and offering shade trees and pull-through sites for RVs up to 105 feet.
payload.medium_description: Upper Wind River Campground sits along the Wind River below Boysen Reservoir in central Wyoming. The campground offers 36 sites with shade trees and interesting geological features. The tailwaters below the dam provide excellent fly fishing opportunities. Three rental cabins are also available on-site.
payload.long_description:
Upper Wind River Campground occupies a scenic stretch of the Wind River just below Boysen Dam in Boysen State Park. The campground features 36 sites including 2 tent-only sites and 34 RV/trailer sites that can accommodate rigs between 20 and 105 feet. Most sites are gravel pull-throughs with fire rings. The location offers more shade trees than other campgrounds in the park, along with a playground and nearby boat ramp.

The tailwaters below Boysen Reservoir provide quality fly fishing, making this campground particularly attractive to anglers. Three rental cabins are available at the campground, each with wood furniture, bunk beds, a futon, and an outdoor fire pit and picnic table. The park sits within the Wind River Indian Reservation and offers access to Boysen Reservoir for boating, swimming, and water sports.

Amenities include vault toilets, potable water from spigots, and a dump station located at park headquarters (operational April through October). The park grounds are open year-round, 24 hours daily.

location.directions: From Shoshoni, travel north on US-20 to Boysen State Park. The campground is located along the Wind River below the dam. Park headquarters address: 120 Boysen Drive, Shoshoni, WY 82649.

payload.name: Clear Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Stage 1 fire restrictions begin May 21, 2026. 7-day stay limit. Check-in 2 p.m., check-out 11 a.m. Quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
payload.short_description: Creekside campground in the Verde Valley with vault toilets, potable water, and cottonwood shade at 3,200 feet elevation in Coconino National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Clear Creek Campground sits along a cool desert creek in the Lower Sonoran zone of Coconino National Forest, seven miles southeast of Camp Verde. The flat, grassy sites are shaded by mature cottonwoods and offer easy creek access for wading and fishing. The campground has 18 family sites (13 reservable, 5 first-come-first-served) plus one group site accommodating up to 80 people.
payload.long_description:
Clear Creek Campground occupies a riparian oasis in the Verde Valley at 3,200 feet elevation. The creek runs year-round with cool water supporting smallmouth bass and green sunfish. Large cottonwoods provide welcome shade in summer, and the grassy terrain makes for comfortable tent camping. Birdwatching is excellent here, with raptors including hawks and bald eagles frequenting the area.

The campground offers 18 family sites with cement picnic tables and fire rings with grill surfaces. Thirteen sites are reservable through Recreation.gov while five remain first-come-first-served. A separate group site handles larger gatherings up to 80 people with parking for 20-30 vehicles. Vault toilets and potable water from hand pumps are available. There are no hookups or showers.

Montezuma Castle National Monument is a short drive away, featuring a remarkably preserved 1,000-year-old cliff dwelling. The nearby Montezuma Well is a natural spring producing over a million gallons daily.

location.directions: From Interstate 17, take the Camp Verde exit and drive through town. Continue east on State Route 260 approximately 5-6 miles to FS Road 626. The campground is at 4600 E. FS 626, Camp Verde, AZ 86322.

payload.name: Lefleur's Bluff State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. daily. Reservations accepted through the MDWFP reservation system.
payload.short_description: Urban state park campground in Jackson, Mississippi offering developed RV sites with water/electric hookups and primitive tent camping near Mayes Lake.
payload.medium_description: LeFleur's Bluff State Park provides a green oasis within Mississippi's capital city, featuring 28 developed campsites with water and electric hookups plus 30 primitive tent sites near Mayes Lake. The campground includes bathhouses with hot showers, a central dump station, and fire rings at each site. Located off I-55 on the Pearl River, the 305-acre park offers fishing, an 18-hole disc golf course, and proximity to the Mississippi Museum of Natural Science and Children's Museum.
payload.long_description:
LeFleur's Bluff State Park sits on 305 acres along the Pearl River within Jackson's city limits, offering a convenient escape for campers visiting Mississippi's capital. The developed campground features 28 sites equipped with water and 30-amp electric hookups, each with a picnic table, fire ring, and barbecue stand. A bathhouse provides hot showers and flush toilets, while a central dump station serves RV campers.

Thirty primitive tent sites are scattered in shaded areas near Mayes Lake, ideal for scout groups and tent campers seeking a more rustic experience while remaining within walking distance of water and shower facilities. The 50-acre Mayes Lake offers fishing for bass, bream, catfish, and crappie from accessible piers.

Beyond camping, the park features an 18-hole disc golf course, nature trails through the forested grounds, and a playground. The west entrance on Museum Drive provides access to the Mississippi Museum of Natural Science and Mississippi Children's Museum, making this an excellent base for families exploring the Jackson area.

location.directions: Located off Interstate 55 in Jackson, Mississippi. Take the Lakeland Drive exit and follow signs to 3315 Lakeland Terrace, Jackson, MS 39216.

payload.name: Sand Harbor State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Sand Harbor is a day-use only facility. Overnight camping is not permitted. The group use area (Ramada) is available for daytime group reservations through ReserveNevada.com.
payload.short_description: Sand Harbor is a day-use only facility within Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. Overnight camping is not permitted; the group use area (Ramada) is for daytime events only.
payload.medium_description: Sand Harbor State Park is a popular day-use beach destination on Lake Tahoe's east shore within Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. No overnight camping is allowed at this location. The group use area, called the Ramada, accommodates up to 120 people for daytime gatherings and includes picnic tables, a gas grill, electrical outlets, and potable water, but it is not a campground.
payload.long_description:
Sand Harbor State Park is a stunning day-use beach area located on the east shore of Lake Tahoe within Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park. The crystal-clear waters, granite boulders, and sandy beaches make it one of the most popular destinations in the Tahoe basin. However, overnight camping is explicitly prohibited at Sand Harbor.

The group use area, known as the Ramada, is available for reservation for day-use events only. It can accommodate up to 120 people and includes twelve cafeteria-style tables, a large gas grill with park-supplied propane, two 110V electrical outlets, and potable water (weather-dependent). The Ramada provides a lakeside location but does not guarantee beach space, which remains first-come, first-served.

Day-use reservations are required for vehicle entry from May 15 through September 30. Entry fees are $10 for Nevada-registered vehicles and $15 for out-of-state vehicles, plus a $5 reservation fee. For overnight camping near Lake Tahoe, visitors should look to other nearby campgrounds.

location.directions: From Incline Village, head south on Highway 28 for approximately 3 miles. Sand Harbor is located at 2005 Highway 28, Incline Village, NV 89450.

links.title: Lake Tahoe Nevada State Park - Sand Harbor

payload.name: Lassen Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally, typically mid-May through late October depending on weather and snow conditions. No fee, no reservations, first-come first-served. Currently under discussion for decommissioning.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground near historic obsidian mines in Modoc National Forest, featuring open area camping with vault toilets and fire rings amid high desert terrain.
payload.medium_description: Lassen Creek is a rustic, no-fee campground in the Warner Mountain Ranger District of Modoc National Forest. This open area camping site has no designated campsites, with rock fire rings scattered throughout. Located near the historic Glass Mountain obsidian mines, the campground offers vault toilets but no potable water or trash service. Currently under discussion for decommissioning.
payload.long_description:
Lassen Creek Campground is a primitive, free camping area nestled in the remote northeastern corner of California within the Modoc National Forest. Unlike traditional campgrounds, this is open area camping with no designated sites. Rock fire rings are positioned throughout the area for campfire use, and vault toilets are available.

The campground sits near the historically significant Glass Mountain obsidian mines, where Native Americans once collected volcanic glass for tool-making. The high desert landscape offers solitude and dark skies, though the remote location means campers must come fully prepared.

No potable water is available, so visitors must bring sufficient water for drinking, cooking, washing, and extinguishing campfires. All trash must be packed out. Dogs are allowed but must remain on leash. The 14-day camping limit applies. The campground is currently under discussion for decommissioning.

location.directions: From Alturas, go north on US Hwy 395 approximately 20 miles to Davis Creek. Turn east on County Road 11 and continue approximately 9 miles to County Road 30/Modoc Backcountry Discovery Trail, then turn left/north. Continue north approximately 15 miles to the campground on the right. Alternatively, continue past Davis Creek to County Road 47, turn right (east) and follow signs to the campground.

payload.name: Fort Stevenson State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open. Reservations available 95 days in advance via reservendparks.com or 800-807-4723. Check-in at 4:00 PM, check-out at 3:00 PM. Maximum stay is 14 nights per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Campground along Lake Sakakawea's northeastern shore with premium full-hookup, modern, and primitive sites, plus marinas, boat ramps, and a swim beach.
payload.medium_description: Fort Stevenson State Park sits in the wooded bluffs above Lake Sakakawea, three miles south of Garrison. The campground offers 48 premium sites with full hookups, 56 modern sites with electric and water, and 17 primitive sites. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, a dump station, two multilane boat ramps, two marinas with slip rentals, a swim beach, fish cleaning stations, and nearly 10 miles of trails.
payload.long_description:
Fort Stevenson State Park occupies a scenic stretch of the northeastern shore of Lake Sakakawea, North Dakota's largest body of water. The park is located three miles south of Garrison, known as the "Walleye Capital" of North Dakota, making it a prime destination for anglers. Two marinas at Garrison Bay and de Trobriand Bay offer electric slips, gas docks, and boat rentals ranging from motorboats to kayaks and paddleboards.

The campground provides 121 total sites across several loops. Premium sites feature full hookups with electric, water, and sewer connections, while modern sites have electric and water. Primitive sites offer a more rustic experience at a lower cost. Group camping is available for larger parties. Park facilities include flush toilets, showers, a sewage dump station, playgrounds, picnic shelters, and a swim beach. Nearly 10 miles of trails wind through the park for hiking, mountain biking, and winter activities like snowshoeing and cross-country skiing.

The park's Guardhouse Interpretive Center explores the area's military history, and seasonal events include Sky Fest and Frontier Military Days. Equipment rentals are available for boats, bikes, and paddlesports. Reservations can be made 95 days in advance through reservendparks.com.

location.directions: From Garrison, head south on ND Highway 37 for approximately 3 miles to the park entrance on the northeastern shore of Lake Sakakawea.

payload.name: New Brighton Sb Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for camping. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia up to six months in advance. Highway 1 construction may affect Park Avenue access; northbound travelers should exit at Bay Ave/Porter Street and follow detour signs.
payload.short_description: Popular beachfront campground on the bluffs above Monterey Bay in Capitola, offering over 100 developed campsites including 11 electric hookup sites.
payload.medium_description: New Brighton State Beach Campground sits atop coastal bluffs overlooking the Monterey Bay Marine Sanctuary in Capitola, just south of Santa Cruz. The campground features over 100 developed campsites including 11 sites with electric hookups, hot showers, flush restrooms, and an RV dump station. A visitor center, campfire center with summer programs, and beach access via trails make this one of the most sought-after coastal campgrounds in California.
payload.long_description:
New Brighton State Beach Campground occupies a scenic bluff top setting above the Monterey Bay Marine Sanctuary near Capitola. The campground offers over 100 developed campsites spread across multiple loops, with 11 sites (numbered 46-56) providing electric hookups. All sites accommodate tents, and most can handle RVs and trailers up to 36 feet. The campground includes hot showers, flush restrooms, potable water, and an RV dump station.

The park features a visitor center museum, a shaded ramada for group gatherings, and a campfire center that hosts free interpretive programs during summer months. Beach access is available via trails leading down from the bluffs. The surrounding forest of Monterey pine, coast live oak, and eucalyptus provides welcome shade in the campground. Dogs are permitted in campsites on leashes no longer than six feet but are not allowed on the beach.

Five standard campsites and one hookup site meet ADA accessibility requirements, with accessible restrooms and showers available throughout the camping loops. Beach wheelchairs can be reserved through Friends of Santa Cruz State Parks for those wanting beach access.

location.directions: From Highway 1, take the New Brighton/Park Avenue exit. Head toward the ocean on Park Avenue to the park entrance. Due to ongoing Highway 1 construction, alternate access may be required: northbound travelers exit at Bay Ave/Porter Street and follow detour to Soquel Drive then Park Avenue; southbound travelers exit at State Park Drive, turn left, take Soquel Drive to Park Avenue.

payload.name: Spring Hill Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally mid-May through mid-September, weather dependent. Nine sites are reservable through Recreation.gov; six sites are first-come, first-served. Food storage order in effect due to bear activity.
payload.short_description: A 15-site campground in the lodgepole pine forests of southwestern Montana, eight miles from Georgetown Lake with access to excellent fishing and hiking.
payload.medium_description: Spring Hill Campground sits in the Pintler Ranger District of Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, surrounded by lodgepole pines. The 15-site campground offers ADA-accessible vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables, and garbage services. It's eight miles from Georgetown Lake and near Warm Springs Creek, both popular for fishing rainbow, cutthroat, brook, and brown trout.
payload.long_description:
Spring Hill Campground is located in the lodgepole pine forests of southwestern Montana within the Pintler Ranger District of Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, the largest national forest in Montana. The campground offers 15 camping units, with 9 sites available for reservation through Recreation.gov and 6 sites on a first-come, first-served basis. Facilities include ADA-accessible vault toilets, potable water from faucets, picnic tables, garbage services, and bear-resistant food storage lockers.

The campground is eight miles from Georgetown Lake, a 3,000-acre mountain lake at over 6,000 feet elevation that draws anglers seeking kokanee salmon, rainbow trout, and brook trout. Warm Springs Creek flows near the campground and is well-known for rainbow, cutthroat, brook, and brown trout. Bull trout are catch-and-release only. Hikers, horseback riders, and mountain bikers will find numerous trails within a few miles of the campground.

The historic town of Anaconda is 11 miles east via Montana Highway 1. Bears are prevalent in the area; food storage regulations are enforced and bear-resistant lockers are provided at sites.

location.directions: Travel approximately 11 miles west of Anaconda along Montana Highway 1 to the campground.

payload.name: Trace State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 12 months in advance through ReserveAmerica or the MDWFP reservation system.
payload.short_description: Full hookup RV campground in northeast Mississippi with 76 sites surrounding 565-acre Trace Lake, offering bathhouses, dump station, and access to 35 miles of multi-use trails.
payload.medium_description: Trace State Park campground surrounds scenic Trace Lake in the rolling hills of northeast Mississippi. The developed campground offers 76 RV sites with full hookups and 16 primitive tent sites. Three bathhouses with hot showers, a coin-op laundry, and a central dump station serve campers. The park provides access to 35 miles of trails for mountain biking, horseback riding, and ATVs, plus fishing, boating, and two disc golf courses.
payload.long_description:
Trace State Park is a 2,500-acre recreation area centered on 565-acre Trace Lake, named for the nearby historic Natchez Trace trail. The campground sits in the Pontotoc Ridge region of northeast Mississippi, roughly equidistant between Tupelo and Pontotoc.

The developed campground features 76 RV sites with full hookups including 30/50-amp electric, water, and sewer connections. Each site includes a picnic table and grill, with most featuring fire rings. Three modern bathhouses provide hot showers and restrooms, and a coin-operated laundromat offers convenient amenities. A central dump station serves the campground. Primitive tent camping is also available at 16 sites.

Beyond camping, the park offers fishing and boating on Trace Lake, 35 miles of multi-use trails for mountain biking, horseback riding, and off-road vehicles, two 18-hole disc golf courses, and the Jason M. Stewart Nature Trail. Cabins and cottages are available for those preferring more amenities.

location.directions: From Tupelo, head west on MS Highway 6 for approximately 9 miles. From Pontotoc, head east on MS Highway 6 for approximately 8 miles. Watch for park signs on Highway 6 directing you to turn onto Faulkner Road; the park entrance is about 2 miles down Faulkner Road.

payload.name: Maumee Bay State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required and available six months in advance via reserveohio.com or by calling (866) 644-6727. Shower houses are heated May through October; off-season (November through April) has two heated family restrooms with shower facilities. Full-hookup sites do not have water during winter months.
payload.short_description: Year-round lakeside campground on Lake Erie with 256 electric sites, full hookups available, heated showers, and paved pads accommodating large RVs.
payload.medium_description: Maumee Bay State Park Campground sits on the shores of Lake Erie in Lucas County, Ohio, offering 256 spacious sites with electric hookups year-round. The campground features 20 full-hookup sites with water, sewer, and electric connections. All sites include paved parking pads, picnic tables, and fire rings, with privacy hedges between sites. Amenities include heated shower houses with flush toilets, a dump station, camp store, and WiFi throughout most of the park.
payload.long_description:
Maumee Bay State Park Campground is a modern, year-round camping facility located just five miles east of Toledo on Lake Erie's southwestern shore. The campground spans over 1,300 acres and offers 256 sites with 20-30-50 amp electric hookups. Twenty sites (1-11 and 21-29) feature full hookups including water and sewer connections, though water is only available at these sites during warmer months. Each site includes a paved parking pad, grassy area, picnic table, and fire ring, with foliage providing privacy between sites.

The campground is well-equipped with heated shower houses featuring flush toilets during peak season (May through October). During off-peak months (November through April), two family restrooms remain heated and include shower facilities. Additional amenities include a well-stocked camp store near the entrance, a dump station with potable water and hoses, WiFi coverage throughout most of the park, and ADA-accessible sites (9 and 21). Pets are welcome on designated sites.

Campground ponds are open exclusively to registered campers for fishing, and five miles of paved bicycle and pedestrian trails connect to most day-use areas. Bike rentals, a basketball court, and horseshoe pits are available. The park features a nature center and access to Lake Erie swimming beaches.

location.directions: Maumee Bay State Park Campground is located at 1400 State Park Road, Oregon, OH 43616. From Toledo, take Route 24 West to Exit 41 in Napoleon, Ohio. Head south on Industrial Drive, then turn right onto 424/E Riverview Ave. The campground is approximately 1.5 miles on the left.

payload.name: Allequash Lake Boat In Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from April 30 through November 1. Reservations are required before occupying any site and can be made same-day through 11 months in advance via wisconsin.goingtocamp.com. Maximum stay is 14 nights per visit with up to 6 people per site.
payload.short_description: Primitive boat-in campsites on undeveloped Allequash Lake in Wisconsin's Northern Highland American Legion State Forest, accessible only by water.
payload.medium_description: Four remote, reservable boat-in campsites on Allequash Lake between Minocqua and Boulder Junction. Each waterfront site includes a picnic table and fire ring with an open-air toilet nearby. The lake has no development except the boat landing, offering solitude and excellent paddling.
payload.long_description:
Allequash Lake Boat In Campground offers four primitive campsites scattered along the shores of this undeveloped lake in Vilas County. Located between Minocqua and Boulder Junction east of Highway M, the lake's only development is the public boat landing. Sites are spaced far apart for privacy and each accommodates up to two small tents.

These water-access-only sites provide the essentials: a picnic table and fire ring at each location with an open-air toilet nearby. The surrounding Northern Highland American Legion State Forest is part of Wisconsin's extensive Northwoods lake country, with excellent opportunities for fishing, paddling, and wildlife observation. Campers may gather dead and downed wood from the forest floor for campfires.

location.directions: From the intersection of County K and M (Cut-off Road) in Boulder Junction, head south on County K for 1.9 miles. Continue south on County M for 3.2 miles, then turn east on the access road to reach the Allequash Lake boat landing and parking area. Launch and paddle to your reserved site.

address.full: 10200 Allequash Lake Rd, Boulder Junction, WI 54512

payload.name: Little Therriault Lake Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is managed from late June through Labor Day but remains accessible year-round, weather permitting. Sites are first-come, first-served with no reservations. Access roads may be impassable due to snow outside summer months.
payload.short_description: Small, rustic 6-site campground on a high-elevation lake in the Ten Lakes Scenic Area, offering fishing and pack boat access in a remote setting.
payload.medium_description: Little Therriault Lake Campground is a secluded 6-site campground in the Ten Lakes Scenic Area of Kootenai National Forest. The campground sits along a small alpine lake at high elevation, offering fishing, undeveloped boat access for pack boats, and a peaceful setting. Each site has a table and fire ring, with vault toilets and food storage boxes available. The campground accommodates RVs up to 32 feet.
payload.long_description:
Little Therriault Lake Campground is a small, primitive campground tucked into the Ten Lakes Scenic Area of northwest Montana's Kootenai National Forest. Located 12.5 air miles from Fortine, the campground sits along a subalpine lake in the Whitefish Range, providing a quiet retreat for anglers and those seeking solitude. The lake supports fishing and allows pack boats for water access.

The campground has six individual sites, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets and food storage boxes are provided. A hand pump provides drinking water during the managed season, though availability may vary. The area is popular with hikers exploring the surrounding Ten Lakes Scenic Area trails.

Access requires a drive on forest roads, with the final approach via Bluebird Creek Road. The route is generally passable for vehicles up to 32 feet, though road conditions are weather-dependent. Snow typically limits access outside the summer season.

location.directions: From Fortine, follow Highway 93 northeast approximately 3 miles to mile marker 169.34 and turn right onto Grave Creek Road (FS Road 114). Follow Road 114 for 14 miles to the junction with Therriault Lakes Road (FS Road 319). Continue north on Road 319 for 14 miles to the Y intersection. Turn right onto Bluebird Creek Road (FS Road 7085) and follow for approximately 0.7 miles to the campground entrance.

address.full: 2546 Grave County Rd Rd, Eureka, MT 59917

payload.name: Paradise Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open late May through late September. Currently operating first-come, first-served with reservations available via Recreation.gov starting late May. A campground host is present during the season.
payload.short_description: Old-growth forest campground at the confluence of Paradise Creek and Wind River in Gifford Pinchot National Forest, offering 42 sites with fishing access and proximity to Falls Creek Falls.
payload.medium_description: Paradise Creek Campground sits beneath towering old-growth cedars, firs, alders, and maples at the confluence of Paradise Creek and the Wind River. The 42-site campground offers a quiet, remote setting with access to steelhead and Chinook salmon fishing in the Wind River and hiking on the Lava Butte Trail. Located about 5 miles from the Falls Creek Falls Trailhead, it serves as an excellent base for exploring Mount St. Helens and Mount Adams.
payload.long_description:
Paradise Creek Campground occupies a scenic location in the Wind River drainage of Gifford Pinchot National Forest, where Paradise Creek meets the Wind River beneath a canopy of old-growth forest. Sites near the river enjoy privacy from lush undergrowth, while interior sites offer a more open, spacious feel. The campground's remote location provides a quiet atmosphere for those seeking to escape crowds.

All 42 back-in sites feature paved parking spurs ranging from 20 to 40 feet in length, with each site equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Potable water is available from a hand pump, and vault toilets serve the campground. A campground host is present during the operating season. A short, easy trail winds through the campground for casual walks.

The Wind River offers excellent fishing for steelhead and Chinook salmon below Wind River Dam (check Washington regulations for seasons and boundaries). Wading is permitted in Paradise Creek, though fishing is not allowed within the campground itself. The nearby Falls Creek Falls Trailhead is about 5 miles away, and the Lava Butte Trail #200 is accessible from the campground.

location.directions: From Vancouver, WA, travel east on Highway 14 to Carson, WA. Then travel 14 miles northwest on Wind River Highway to the forest boundary. At the forest boundary, continue north on Forest Road 30 for 6 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Salt Point Sp Gerstle Cove Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. Walk-In Environmental Campsites and the visitor center are closed indefinitely. Reservations through ReserveCalifornia.com; some first-come, first-served sites may be available.
payload.short_description: Coastal blufftop campground at Salt Point State Park with 30 family sites featuring fire rings, picnic tables, and food lockers. Adjacent to Gerstle Cove State Marine Reserve with excellent tide pooling.
payload.medium_description: Gerstle Cove Campground sits atop scenic coastal bluffs on the ocean side of Highway 1, about 90 miles north of San Francisco. Each of the 30 family campsites includes a fire ring, picnic table, and food locker. Water spigots are distributed throughout the campground loops. The campground has restrooms but no showers, hookups, or dump station. The adjacent Gerstle Cove is a State Marine Reserve with a healthy kelp forest and exceptional tide pooling.
payload.long_description:
Gerstle Cove Campground occupies a prime location atop the coastal bluffs at Salt Point State Park in Sonoma County. The 30 developed family campsites are mostly level and paved, each equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and bear-resistant food locker. Water spigots are distributed throughout the campground loops. The park lies about 90 miles north of San Francisco along the rugged Sonoma Coast.

The campground is adjacent to Gerstle Cove, a designated State Marine Reserve protecting a thriving underwater kelp forest ecosystem. Tide pooling here is exceptional, though as a reserve, collecting anything is prohibited. The surrounding park offers hiking through pygmy forests, sandstone formations, and over 6 miles of coastline. Sea lions, harbor seals, and gray whales are common sights.

Facilities include restrooms but no showers, hookups, or dump station. Campers needing to fill water tanks or dump waste can use Bodega Dunes Campground at no charge. Dogs are permitted on-leash in the campground and paved areas but prohibited on trails and beaches.

location.directions: From San Francisco, take US-101 north to Petaluma. Exit onto Bodega Avenue/D Street west, which becomes Valley Ford Road then Highway 1. Continue north on Highway 1 for approximately 35 miles past Bodega Bay and Jenner. The park entrance is on the left.

links.title: Salt Point State Park - CA State Parks

payload.name: Dillon State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From November 1 through April 1, only shower house A and the dump station are available with no rinse water. Area A (sites 1-104 and 184-195) remains open during winter.
payload.short_description: Family-friendly state park campground on Dillon Lake in eastern Ohio with 195 sites, electric and full hookups, showers, and year-round access for RV and tent camping.
payload.medium_description: Dillon State Park Campground offers 195 campsites along the shores of Dillon Lake, approximately six miles northwest of Zanesville, Ohio. The three-loop campground includes 183 electric sites, 14 full hookup sites, and walk-in primitive sites. Facilities include three shower houses with flush toilets, a dump station, and each site has a fire ring and picnic table. The campground operates year-round, though winter months have limited water services.
payload.long_description:
Dillon State Park Campground sits on the shores of 1,560-acre Dillon Lake in Muskingum County, offering one of eastern Ohio's most popular camping destinations. The campground features 195 sites spread across three loops (Area A, B, and C) with varying levels of shade and privacy. Most sites have electric hookups (183 sites), while 14 premium sites offer full water, electric, and sewer connections. Walk-in primitive sites provide a more secluded tent camping experience.

The park provides excellent amenities including three shower houses with flush toilets, a dump station, and each campsite comes equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Activities abound with access to the lake for fishing, boating, and swimming at the 1,360-foot beach. The park also features hiking trails, an equestrian campground, and rental cabins.

The campground operates year-round, making it a destination for all seasons. During winter months (November 1 through April 1), services are reduced with only shower house A and the dump station available, and no rinse water provided. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance through ReserveOhio.

location.directions: Dillon Lake is approximately six miles northwest of Zanesville, Ohio and twenty miles east of Newark, Ohio. Access to the lake is provided by State Route 146 via State Routes 16 and 586 from the north, and US 40 and Interstate 70 from the south.

links.title: Ohio DNR Dillon State Park Campground

payload.name: Grayson Highlands State Park Chestnut Hollow Horse Campground
payload.status_description: Open for full-service camping through October. Bathhouse, showers, and water hookups are operational. Primitive camping only operates March, April, and November with porta-johns and no water. Closed first Monday in December through first Friday in March. Reservations by phone only at 1-800-933-PARK.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground at Grayson Highlands State Park offering 24 campsites with electric and water hookups, horse stalls, and access to Virginia's highest mountain trails.
payload.medium_description: Chestnut Hollow Horse Campground is the equestrian hub of Grayson Highlands State Park, situated near Virginia's highest peaks including Mount Rogers and Whitetop Mountain. The campground offers 24 campsites with electric and water hookups, along with 44 horse stalls in covered and open configurations. A bathhouse with showers, dump station, fire rings, picnic tables, and grills are available during full-service season from May through October.
payload.long_description:
Chestnut Hollow Horse Campground serves as the dedicated equestrian camping area at Grayson Highlands State Park, Virginia's gateway to the state's highest elevations. The campground provides 24 campsites equipped with 20, 30, and 50-amp electric service along with water hookups to accommodate horse trailers. Horse stalls are available in three configurations: 20 wide covered stalls (approximately 8x10 feet with park-provided sawdust), 5 wide open stalls (8x10 feet), and 19 smaller open stalls (5x8 feet).

During full-service season from May through October, campers have access to a bathhouse with showers, potable water, dump station, and a camp store for supplies. Each campsite includes a fire ring, picnic table, and grill. Primitive camping operates during March, April, and November with porta-johns only and no water service. The campground closes from the first Monday in December through the first Friday in March.

Reservations for Chestnut Hollow can only be made by calling 1-800-933-PARK. Equestrian campers receive booking priority, while non-equestrian campers may reserve beginning 30 days prior to arrival. Virginia state law requires all visitors to carry a negative Coggins report for each horse brought to the park.

location.directions: From I-81 Exit 45 in Marion: south on Route 16 for 24 miles to US 58, then right 8 miles to park entrance. From I-77 Exit 14: west on US 58 for 40 miles to Volney, then left 8 miles to park.

address.full: 3546 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

payload.name: Dockery Lake Recreation Area
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 peak season through October 31. Potable water is available. Off-peak season runs November 1 through January 1 at reduced rates with no water service. The campground closes January 2 through March 31.
payload.short_description: Small lakeside campground with 11 sites on a 6-acre trout-stocked lake in the Blue Ridge Mountains, 12 miles north of Dahlonega, Georgia.
payload.medium_description: Dockery Lake Recreation Area offers 11 standard campsites nestled along the banks of a 6-acre trout-stocked lake in the Chattahoochee National Forest. The campground sits under a dense canopy of deciduous and evergreen trees, providing excellent shade during summer months. Accessible trails include the 0.5-mile Lakeshore Trail loop and the 3.5-mile Dockery Lake Trail connecting to the Appalachian Trail at Miller Gap.
payload.long_description:
Dockery Lake Recreation Area is a U.S. Forest Service campground located in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia, approximately 12 miles north of Dahlonega. The campground features 11 standard nonelectric sites arranged along the banks of Dockery Lake, a 6-acre man-made lake stocked with trout. The area sits beneath a dense forest of mixed deciduous and evergreen trees, offering substantial shade throughout the camping season.

The lake allows fishing with a Georgia Trout Stamp and permits electric trolling motors only. Swimming is prohibited. Two hiking trails depart from the recreation area: the easy 0.5-mile Lakeshore Trail circling the lake, and the moderate 3.5-mile Dockery Lake Trail ascending to the Appalachian Trail at Miller Gap. The Appalachian Trail crosses Highway 60 at Woody Gap, and the Benton MacKaye Trail crosses Highway 60 in two locations about 12 miles north.

The campground operates as a self-service facility with reservations made through Recreation.gov. Sites include picnic tables and fire grills. A flush toilet is available in the campground, with a vault toilet at the day-use area. Potable water is available during peak season only. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 PM to 6 AM, and the area follows bear-aware protocols for food storage.

location.directions: From Dahlonega, GA take GA Highway 60 north approximately 13 miles to Forest Service Road 654 on the right. Turn right and go 1 mile to campground.

payload.name: Lightfoot Landing
payload.status_description: Open for camping with sites available through Recreation.gov. Off-season rates of $10 per night apply March 15 through April 15 and October 1 through November 30 with electricity only. Regular season rates are $14 to $30 per night. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive days.
payload.short_description: Quiet Corps of Engineers campground on Pomme de Terre Lake with 35 electric/water sites, boat ramp, and excellent muskie fishing in Missouri's Ozark hills.
payload.medium_description: Lightfoot Landing is a smaller, peaceful Army Corps of Engineers campground on Pomme de Terre Lake, known as the Gem of the Ozarks. All 35 sites have electric and water hookups, with amenities including a shower house, dump station, boat ramp with courtesy dock, playground, and picnic shelter. The lake offers exceptional fishing for muskie, bass, walleye, crappie, and catfish.
payload.long_description:
Lightfoot Landing sits on the shores of Pomme de Terre Lake, a 7,790-acre reservoir fed by the Pomme de Terre River and Lindley Creek in Missouri's Ozark hills. The campground's smaller size compared to neighboring facilities makes it a quieter option for anglers and boaters seeking access to the lake.

All 35 sites feature electric (including 50-amp) and water hookups on gravel pads, with a mix of pull-through and back-in configurations accommodating RVs up to 45 feet. The facility includes a shower house, dump station, boat ramp with courtesy dock, playground, horseshoe pits, and a reservable picnic shelter. One site is ADA accessible.

Pomme de Terre Lake is renowned for fishing, boasting one of the highest catch ratios in the country. The lake is stocked with muskie each fall and holds healthy populations of bass, walleye, crappie, and catfish. Power boating, water skiing, and canoeing are popular on the expansive waters.

location.directions: From Springfield, MO, go north on Highway 13 to Bolivar, MO. Take Highway 83 northeast to RB Highway. Follow RB Highway east to the Lightfoot Park entrance.

payload.name: Mill Valley Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Water is currently off for the season. Trash service operates only during summer months; pack out all garbage at other times. Access to the Letts Lake basin may be affected by the M10 Road construction project.
payload.short_description: A 15-site first-come, first-served campground in Mendocino National Forest, popular with OHV enthusiasts, located one mile north of Letts Lake near Stonyford.
payload.medium_description: Mill Valley Campground offers 15 primitive campsites in the Grindstone District of Mendocino National Forest, 17 miles west of Stonyford. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. The campground serves as a staging area for OHV recreation, with trails leading directly in and out. Vault toilets are available, and potable water is seasonal.
payload.long_description:
Mill Valley Campground is a rustic 15-site campground nestled in the mixed coniferous forest of the Stonyford Recreation Area within Mendocino National Forest. Located one mile north of Letts Lake and 17 miles west of Stonyford, the campground sits at roughly 4,600 feet elevation and caters primarily to off-highway vehicle enthusiasts, with OHV trails leading directly from the campground into the surrounding network.

Each campsite is equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are on-site. Potable water is available seasonally but is typically turned off during winter months. Trash service operates only during summer; campers must pack out garbage at other times. The campground accommodates trailers up to 24 feet.

Mill Valley operates on a first-come, first-served basis year-round. Payment is made on-site via QR code using the Recreation.gov mobile app. Peak season rates (May through September) are $10 per night; off-season rates are $5 per night.

location.directions: Located 17 miles west of Stonyford and one mile north of Letts Lake off of Forest Road 17N02.

payload.name: Chippokes State Park Cabins
payload.status_description: Cabins 1-4 and Walnut Valley House are open and available for rent year-round. Peak season runs Memorial Day through Labor Day with a six-night minimum stay requirement, reduced to four nights three months out and two nights within the final month. Off-season requires a two-night minimum.
payload.short_description: Historic colonial-style cabins on one of America's oldest continuously farmed plantations, just across the James River from Jamestown in Surry County, Virginia.
payload.medium_description: Chippokes State Park offers four restored tenant house cabins and the historic Walnut Valley House lodge on a working plantation dating to 1619. Each cabin features heat and air conditioning, a fully equipped kitchen, and bathroom with shower. The colonial-style structures range from a cozy one-bedroom to a three-bedroom, with one ADA-accessible cabin. Guests must bring their own linens. The park provides scenic views of farmland and access to hiking trails, a visitor center, and the James River waterfront.
payload.long_description:
Chippokes State Park preserves one of the oldest continuously farmed plantations in America, with agricultural operations dating back to 1619. The four rental cabins are restored tenant houses from the plantation's working days, offering a unique lodging experience steeped in colonial Virginia history. Cabin styles range from the one-bedroom Osborne House to the three-bedroom Brown House built around 1850, each with its own character and layout.

All cabins include heat and air conditioning, a kitchen with refrigerator, stove, microwave, toaster, and coffee maker, plus cooking utensils and dishware. Bathrooms have showers, though Cabin 2 features a vintage claw-foot tub. No linens are provided, so guests must bring sheets, towels, and blankets. WiFi is not available, and TV reception is spotty with no cable service. Pets are welcome with a nightly fee.

The Walnut Valley House, built around 1770, is the oldest structure on the property and serves as a four-bedroom historic lodge sleeping up to eight guests. It features a screened porch, full kitchen, and ADA-accessible first floor with a wheelchair lift. The park surrounds guests with working farmland, the Farm and Forestry Museum, hiking and biking trails, and swimming pool access in season.

location.directions: 695 Chippokes Park Rd., Surry, VA 23883. The park is located just across the James River from historic Jamestown.

payload.name: Hurricane Lake South Campground Blackwater River State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations available up to 11 months in advance via Reserve America. Subject to county burn bans which may restrict campfires.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent campground on the south shore of 318-acre Hurricane Lake in Florida's largest state forest, offering fishing, boating, and wildlife viewing about an hour northeast of Pensacola.
payload.medium_description: Hurricane Lake South Campground offers 18 primitive tent sites along the southern shore of Hurricane Lake within the 210,000-acre Blackwater River State Forest. Each site features fire rings and grills, with potable water faucets, a bathhouse, dump station, and boat ramp nearby. The 318-acre lake provides excellent fishing opportunities, though swimming is prohibited due to alligator presence.
payload.long_description:
Hurricane Lake South Campground sits on the southern shore of Hurricane Lake, a 318-acre fishing lake in the heart of Blackwater River State Forest. This primitive campground provides 18 tent-only sites in a natural longleaf pine and wiregrass ecosystem characteristic of Florida's panhandle. Each site accommodates up to 8 people with equipment lengths varying from 25 to 50 feet depending on the specific site.

The campground features fire rings and grills at each site, with potable water faucets conveniently located throughout. A bathhouse provides restroom facilities, and a dump station serves the recreation area. A boat ramp offers direct access to Hurricane Lake for fishing and non-motorized boating, with a fish cleaning station available for anglers.

Blackwater River State Forest is Florida's largest state forest, encompassing over 210,000 acres of woodlands, lakes, and streams. Visitors should note that swimming is prohibited in Hurricane Lake due to resident alligators. During hunting season, wearing fluorescent orange is recommended even in non-hunting zones. The campground operates year-round and hosts a campground host on-site.

location.directions: From Milton, FL, head north on State Road 87. Turn east on Munson Highway (State Road 4). The Hurricane Lake Recreation Area entrance is approximately 20 miles from Milton. Follow signs to the South Campground.

address.full: 7760 Hurricane Lake Entrance Rd S, Baker, FL 32531

links.title: Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica - Campground Details
FDACS - Blackwater River State Forest Recreation Areas

payload.name: D.h. Day Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Reservations via Recreation.gov are required May 1 through October 15. Early season (April 27 to May 14) and late season (October 16 through the last Sunday of November) are first-come, first-served at $10/night with no water available. Reservation season sites are $20/night. A $25 park entrance pass is required per vehicle.
payload.short_description: Rustic wooded campground at Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore with 81 sites within walking distance of Lake Michigan beaches and the Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail.
payload.medium_description: D.H. Day Campground is a rustic 81-site campground in the northern district of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore. The beautifully wooded sites sit within a 5-minute walk of Lake Michigan shoreline and offer easy access to the Dune Climb, Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive, and the 20-mile Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail that passes directly through the campground.
payload.long_description:
D.H. Day Campground occupies a prime location in the northern district of Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore on Michigan's lower peninsula. The 81 wooded campsites are spread across Generator, Upper, and Lower loops, with sites ranging from standard and tent-only to walk-to options. Each site includes a fire ring, large picnic table, and tent pad. The campground sits just minutes from Lake Michigan's pebble beaches, making it ideal for swimming, kayaking, and fishing.

The multi-use Sleeping Bear Heritage Trail runs through the campground, connecting campers to over 20 miles of paved biking and hiking. The historic village of Glen Haven is a 15-minute walk away, while the Dune Climb and Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive are a short drive south. Nearby Glen Arbor offers restaurants, shops, and canoe and bicycle rentals.

This is bear country; all food and scented items must be stored in sealed vehicles. The campground has vault toilets year-round, seasonal potable water from shared spigots, and a dump station at the entrance. Generator use is restricted to sites 1-31 between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. Quiet hours are 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., and camping is limited to 14 total days between Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends.

location.directions: From Empire: Drive north on M-22 for 2 miles to M-109, turn left onto M-109, continue 5.3 miles past the Scenic Drive and Dune Climb. The entrance is on the left. From Glen Arbor: Drive west on M-109 for 1.4 miles; entrance is on the right. Physical address: 8000 W. Harbor Hwy, Glen Arbor, MI 49636.

address.full: 8012 W Harbor Hwy, Glen Arbor, MI 49636

alerts.title: North Manitou Island village and dock are closed for the 2025 season
alerts.content: The North Manitou Island village and dock are closed for the 2025 season due to construction of a new dock. The island remains open for camping via access by private boat and CUA holders.

alerts.title: Ironman Triathlon: Sunday, September 14, 2025
alerts.content: Road closures on SUNDAY, SEPTEMBER 14. The race takes place on M-22 and will have a significant impact on local traffic. M-22 will be closed between Esch Road and Frankfort until 2 pm. Lake Michigan Road will not be accessible during the race.

payload.name: Pacific Beach State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 8 a.m. to dusk daily. Reservations available through washington.goingtocamp.com. Level 1 burn ban in effect allowing fires only in designated pits/grills and propane/gas grills.
payload.short_description: Oceanfront campground on Washington's Pacific coast featuring 59 campsites with electric hookups, yurts, and direct beach access for razor clamming and saltwater fishing.
payload.medium_description: Pacific Beach State Park offers 59 campsites just steps from the Pacific Ocean, including 16 standard sites, 41 partial-hookup sites with electricity, and two furnished yurts. The park provides modern restrooms with showers, a dump station, potable water, and Wi-Fi. This small but popular campground draws visitors for razor clam harvesting during open season and year-round beachcombing.
payload.long_description:
Pacific Beach State Park is a compact oceanfront campground on Washington's central coast, located northwest of Aberdeen in Grays Harbor County. The park offers 59 campsites arranged close to the roaring Pacific surf: 16 standard tent sites, 41 partial-hookup sites with electricity only, and two 16-foot yurts that sleep up to five guests each. The one-way park road requires all RVs to back in to their sites.

Amenities include ADA-accessible restrooms with flush toilets and showers, a dump station with fresh water, potable drinking water, trash service, and Wi-Fi. Wood-burning campfires are prohibited throughout the park, though portable gas or propane fire pits and grills are permitted. Beach fires are allowed only when positioned at least 100 feet from dunes and vegetation.

The park is a prime destination for razor clam harvesting during designated seasons and offers easy access to saltwater fishing, beachcombing, and wildlife watching. Reservations can be made through washington.goingtocamp.com up to nine months in advance.

location.directions: From Hoquiam, follow Highway 101 to Ocean Beach Road. Continue on Ocean Beach Road to Pacific Beach. The park is located at 49 Second Street, Pacific Beach, WA 98571.

links.title: Pacific Beach State Park - WA Parks

payload.name: Burlingame State Park Picnic Area
payload.status_description: The picnic area is closed for the season through May 22, 2026 and reopens May 23, 2026. The season runs through September 7, 2026. Shelter reservations are required from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day; outside these dates the shelter is first-come-first-served. No alcohol permitted.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic area on Watchaug Pond featuring a sandy beach, swimming area, picnic tables, fireplaces, and a reservable covered shelter pavilion for up to 50 guests.
payload.medium_description: Burlingame State Park Picnic Area is a 31-acre day-use recreation area on Watchaug Pond in Charlestown, Rhode Island. The area offers a sandy beach with a designated swimming area, approximately 20 first-come-first-served picnic tables, fireplaces, and a large covered log cabin-style shelter pavilion that can accommodate up to 50 people. The picnic area also provides access to a boat launch for fishing and boating, and the adjacent 8-mile John Vincent Gormley Trail for hiking.
payload.long_description:
Burlingame State Park Picnic Area is a scenic 31-acre day-use recreation area situated on the shores of Watchaug Pond, one of the largest freshwater ponds in Rhode Island. Located in Charlestown within South County, the area provides a peaceful setting for picnicking, swimming, and enjoying the natural beauty of the region.

The picnic area features a wooded grove with approximately 20 first-come-first-served picnic tables and fireplaces scattered throughout. A sandy shoreline offers a small designated swimming area, though no lifeguards are on duty. The highlight of the facility is a large covered log cabin-style shelter pavilion that can accommodate up to 50 people and is available for rental. There are four self-composting toilets on site, including one that is ADA accessible.

This is strictly a day-use facility with no overnight camping permitted. The adjacent boat launch provides access to Watchaug Pond for fishing and boating, though personal watercraft are prohibited. The nearby Kimball Sanctuary and the 8-mile John Vincent Gormley Trail offer additional opportunities for hiking and nature exploration. For overnight camping, visitors should look to the separate Burlingame State Campground located a short drive away.

location.directions: The entrance to Burlingame State Park Picnic Area is on the right approximately 0.6 miles off Prosser Trail, which you access from an exit off US Route 1 South in Charlestown, RI.

links.title: RI State Parks ReserveAmerica - Picnic Area

payload.name: Dan Moller Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via Recreation.gov with a two-night maximum consecutive stay. The cabin is open to the public as a warming shelter from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily. High avalanche danger exists in winter and early spring. Trail planks are slippery when wet or frosty.
payload.short_description: Remote alpine cabin on Douglas Island accessible via a 3-mile hike with 1,800 ft elevation gain. Sleeps 7 with propane heat, wood stove, and outhouse. Reservable year-round through Recreation.gov.
payload.medium_description: Dan Moller Cabin is a rustic two-level Forest Service cabin situated at 1,800 feet elevation in the scenic alpine landscape of central Douglas Island, near the headwaters of Kowee Creek. The 16x20 cedar structure sleeps seven with bunk beds on two floors, a propane wall furnace, wood stove, table and benches, and an outside pit toilet. Guests must hike, ski, snowshoe, or snowmobile the 3-mile Dan Moller Trail from West Juneau. No potable water, electricity, or cooking facilities are provided.
payload.long_description:
Dan Moller Cabin offers a backcountry experience on Douglas Island, just 3.5 miles southwest of Juneau in the Tongass National Forest. The two-level cedar cabin sits at 1,800 feet elevation surrounded by snow-capped peaks and alpine meadows near Kowee Creek. Views from the front deck reveal the dramatic mountain scenery of central Douglas Island. Wildlife in the area includes black bear, deer, grouse, and wolves.

The cabin accommodates up to seven people with a double bunk and single bunk downstairs and four single bunks in the sleeping loft. Amenities include a propane wall furnace (propane provided), wood stove, table with benches, covered decks, and an outside pit toilet. Visitors must bring their own sleeping bags, pads, cook stove, cookware, food, water, lantern, toilet paper, garbage bags, and fire extinguisher.

Access requires a 3-mile hike along the Dan Moller Trail with an 1,800-foot elevation gain. The partially planked trail passes through muskeg and can be slippery when wet or frosty. In winter, the cabin is popular with skiers and snowshoers, though high avalanche danger exists in winter and early spring. Snowmobile access is permitted only when snow depth exceeds one foot.

location.directions: Located 3.5 miles southwest of Juneau on Douglas Island. Access via the 3-mile Dan Moller Trail. From West Juneau, turn left onto Pioneer Avenue; the trailhead is past the eleventh house on the right with a small parking area. Alternate access at the end of Jackson Street above the Blueberry Hills subdivision. The cabin is also accessible by helicopter.

links.title: USFS Tongass NF - Dan Moller Cabin

photos.name: Fire place to supplement the propane heater
Snow machine access in the winter

payload.name: Meadow Creek Loop Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 18. Full summer services including flush toilets, hot showers, and running water are operational. Camping loops close September 2. Reservations must be made at least 4 days in advance through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Meadow Creek Loop is a scenic campground within Lake Sherwood Recreation Area in Monongahela National Forest, featuring sites along the largest lake in the forest with swimming, boating, and hiking access.
payload.medium_description: Meadow Creek Loop Campground sits within Lake Sherwood Recreation Area, part of Monongahela National Forest in Greenbrier County, West Virginia. The loop offers standard campsites with picnic tables, fire rings, and tent pads overlooking Lake Sherwood, the largest lake on the forest. Summer amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, and running water, while spring and fall seasons provide vault toilets and a hand pump well. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Meadow Creek Loop is one of several camping loops at Lake Sherwood Recreation Area, perched along the shores of the 164-acre Lake Sherwood, the largest lake in Monongahela National Forest. The campground provides a base for exploring swimming beaches, a boat ramp, and multiple hiking trails including the 7-mile Lake Sherwood Trail that circles the lake.

Each campsite includes a parking spur, tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. During summer operations, the campground offers full services including restrooms with running water, flush toilets, hot showers, and electricity. During the shoulder seasons of spring and fall, services transition to vault toilets and a hand pump well for water. The recreation area also has a dump station available for RVs.

The campground operates seasonally with reservations available through Recreation.gov. An alcohol prohibition order is in effect throughout the Lake Sherwood Recreation Area.

location.directions: From White Sulphur Springs, head northeast on E Main Street toward Mill Hill Avenue. Turn left onto WV-92 N/Pocahontas Trail and drive 15.4 miles. Turn right onto Lake Sherwood Road and continue 3.8 miles, then continue straight to stay on Lake Sherwood Road for 6.4 miles. Turn right to reach Lake Sherwood Recreation Area.

payload.name: Laurel Ridge Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Camping runs from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December. Reservations available online at Virginia State Parks or by phone.
payload.short_description: Small RV-focused campground at Holliday Lake State Park with 6 electric/water hookup sites accommodating RVs up to 40 feet, nestled in Appomattox-Buckingham State Forest near Appomattox Court House National Historical Park.
payload.medium_description: Laurel Ridge Campground is the smaller of two camping areas at Holliday Lake State Park, specifically designed for larger recreational vehicles. With just 6 sites offering electric (20, 30, and 50 amp) and water hookups, each site includes a fire ring with adjustable cooking grate, lantern post, and picnic table. A modern bathhouse provides hot showers and flush toilets with ADA-accessible facilities.
payload.long_description:
Laurel Ridge Campground sits within Holliday Lake State Park, a 250-acre retreat tucked deep in the 19,000-acre Appomattox-Buckingham State Forest. The campground caters to RV campers with 6 sites equipped with electric (20, 30, and 50 amp service) and water hookups, accommodating rigs up to 40 feet in length. Each site features a fire ring with adjustable grate, lantern post, and picnic table, with parking for two vehicles included.

The Laurel Ridge Bathhouse serves the campground with hot showers and flush toilets, including an ADA-accessible toilet and shower. Paved roadways and sidewalks lead to restroom facilities, and staff can arrange placement near restrooms for guests with disabilities upon request.

Beyond camping, Holliday Lake offers a 150-acre lake with swimming beach, fishing for largemouth bass, crappie, and bluegill, and seasonal boat rentals including canoes, kayaks, Jon boats, and paddleboards. The 6.5-mile Lakeshore Trail circles the lake, connecting to the extensive trail network of the surrounding state forest. Appomattox Court House National Historical Park lies just minutes away.

location.directions: Located within Holliday Lake State Park in Appomattox County, Virginia. The park entrance is accessible via Route 626 (State Park Road) off Route 24.

links.title: Holliday Lake State Park - Virginia DCR

payload.name: Sleepy Grass
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens May 15, 2026. Reservations available through Recreation.gov. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect forest-wide; campfires permitted in designated fire rings at developed campgrounds.
payload.short_description: Sleepy Grass Campground offers 15 forested sites near Cloudcroft in Lincoln National Forest with vault toilets, potable water, and picnic tables at 8,600 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Sleepy Grass Campground is a seasonal Forest Service campground located 1.4 miles south of Cloudcroft in the Sacramento Mountains of Lincoln National Forest. The campground features 15 units including single, double, and triple sites nestled among ponderosa pine and mixed conifer forest. Amenities include vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables, and trash service. Maximum RV length is 30 feet. The campground operates from mid-May through October.
payload.long_description:
Sleepy Grass Campground sits in the cool Sacramento Mountains of Lincoln National Forest, just 1.4 miles south of the village of Cloudcroft. At roughly 8,600 feet elevation, the campground provides relief from desert heat and offers access to hiking, mountain biking, and scenic drives through ponderosa pine and mixed conifer forest.

The campground has 15 units consisting of 10 single sites, 2 double sites, and 3 triple sites. All sites are non-electric and suitable for tents, campers, and RVs up to 30 feet. Each site has a picnic table and access to vault toilets and potable water. Trash service is provided. Showers and an RV dump station are available at the nearby Silver Overflow recreation area for an additional fee.

Sleepy Grass operates seasonally from mid-May through October, weather dependent. Reservations are available through Recreation.gov. The 14-day stay limit applies, and pets are welcome on a 6-foot leash. Stage 1 fire restrictions may be in effect during high fire danger periods, though campfires in designated fire structures at developed campgrounds remain permitted.

location.directions: From Cloudcroft, head south on NM 130 for 1.4 miles. Turn left onto Forest Road 24B, directly across from Deerhead Campground.

payload.name: Hog Pen Landing Primitive Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours a day. Sites are first-come, first-served. No potable water available; bring your own.
payload.short_description: Primitive waterfront camping on Ocean Pond in Osceola National Forest with vault toilets, boat ramp access, and first-come, first-served sites.
payload.medium_description: Hog Pen Landing Primitive Camp offers waterfront camping along the northwest shore of Ocean Pond in Florida's Osceola National Forest. The primitive campground features about a dozen sites scattered among cypress and pine trees, with half directly facing the water. A boat ramp provides access to Ocean Pond for fishing and boating. Sites are first-come, first-served at $10 per night.
payload.long_description:
Hog Pen Landing Primitive Camp sits on the northwest shore of Ocean Pond within Osceola National Forest in Baker County, Florida. The campground offers roughly a dozen primitive sites scattered along the shoreline, with about half providing direct waterfront views and the remainder nestled back in the shade of cypress and pine trees draped with Spanish moss.

The facility is popular with anglers, boaters, and hunters, featuring a public boat ramp for easy access to Ocean Pond. During hunting season, the area serves as a hunt camp. Amenities are minimal: vault toilets and picnic tables are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply.

Sites are available first-come, first-served at $10 per night, with an additional $5 fee for extra vehicles. The campground is open year-round and operates 24 hours a day.

location.directions: Located on Forest Road 241 approximately 2 miles north of US 90.

payload.name: Ahtus Melder Horse Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Free primitive camping with no reservations required. Trail use fee of $5 per horse for the Claiborne Multi-Use Trail.
payload.short_description: Primitive free equestrian campground in Kisatchie National Forest with direct access to over 70 miles of Claiborne Multi-Use Trails.
payload.medium_description: Ahtus Melder Horse Camp is a very primitive, free equestrian camping area in the Calcasieu Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest. The open grassy area beneath large pines allows campers flexibility in their setup. The camp provides direct access to the Claiborne Multi-Use Trail system, which offers more than 70 miles of trails for horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Ahtus Melder Horse Camp is a designated equestrian camping facility in the Calcasieu Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest in Rapides Parish, Louisiana. The site is intentionally minimalist, described as "very primitive" and "set up very openly, leaving campers to use their imagination on how best to camp." The open grassy area beneath large pine trees provides space for horse trailers and camping rigs.

The camp serves as a staging area for the Claiborne Multi-Use Trail system, offering more than 70 miles of trails open to horseback riding. There is a $5 fee per horse for trail use, but camping itself is free. Visitors may also ride horses anywhere on the forest that is safe, not limited to designated trails.
