This is a pack-it-in, pack-it-out facility with no water, no restrooms, and no developed amenities. Campers must be fully self-sufficient with their own water supply and waste management.

location.directions: From LA Highway 112 West, travel approximately one mile past the Forest Road 258 turnoff to Loran/Claiborne Trailhead Camp. Turn south on Forest Road 267 and take an immediate left onto Forest Road 269. The camping area is on the right in the grassy area under the large pines.

payload.name: Tidewater Campground Goethe State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through FloridaStateForests.ReserveAmerica.com up to 11 months in advance. Drought conditions may result in fire restrictions affecting campfire use.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground in Goethe State Forest offering RV, tent, and group sites with fire rings and picnic tables amid 53,000 acres of Florida forest.
payload.medium_description: Tidewater Campground is a primitive camping area in Goethe State Forest, Levy County, approximately 15 minutes northeast of Inglis. The campground offers 5 RV/tent sites with pull-through options, 4 tent-only backpacking sites, and a group tent site for up to 20 people. Sites include fire rings, grills, and picnic tables but no electric hookups. Restrooms are available but campers must bring their own drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Tidewater Campground sits adjacent to the Tidewater Trailhead within the 53,000+ acre Goethe State Forest in Levy County, Florida. This primitive camping area caters to tent campers and RV users seeking a rustic experience without hookups. The campground provides 11 reservable sites: 5 RV or tent sites accommodating up to 8 people each, 4 tent-only primitive backpacking sites, one group tent site for up to 20 people, and a day-use pavilion.

Each campsite features a fire ring, grill, and picnic table. Restrooms are located at the trailhead but provide only non-potable water, so campers must bring their own drinking water. No showers, electric hookups, or dump stations are available. Recreational activities include hiking, horseback riding, mountain biking, hunting, fishing, bird watching, and wildlife photography.

Campers should be aware of snakes and alligators in the area and must bear and raccoon-proof all food and garbage. During hunting seasons, wearing day-glo orange is recommended. Prescribed burns and logging operations occur regularly throughout the forest.

location.directions: Located at 9110 SE CR 337, Dunnellon, FL 34431, approximately 15 minutes northeast of Inglis, Florida.

payload.name: Stewart Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Reservations required through ReserveOhio up to 6 months in advance. Water is seasonal.
payload.short_description: Primitive walk-in tent campground at Scioto Trail State Park featuring 18 rustic sites near Stewart Lake in Ohio's Appalachian foothills.
payload.medium_description: Stewart Lake Campground is a primitive walk-in family camp area at Scioto Trail State Park in Ross County, Ohio. The 18 non-electric tent sites offer a secluded, rustic experience near Stewart Lake Dam within the 9,000-acre Scioto Trail State Forest. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings, with pit toilets and seasonal potable water available.
payload.long_description:
Stewart Lake Campground provides a primitive camping experience at Scioto Trail State Park, located south of Chillicothe in Ohio's Appalachian foothills. This walk-in tent camping area features 18 non-electric sites situated near Stewart Lake Dam, accessible via an unblazed bridle trail west of the picnic area. The campground offers a quieter, more secluded alternative to the developed Caldwell Lake Campground located 0.7 miles away.

The park encompasses 218 acres within the larger 9,000-acre Scioto Trail State Forest, offering ridgetop vistas of the Scioto River Valley. Campers can enjoy hiking, fishing at Stewart Lake (9 acres), and exploring the surrounding forest trails. The Buckeye Trail passes through the area, making it a convenient stop for long-distance hikers.

Amenities are minimal but adequate for primitive camping: pit toilets, seasonal potable water, picnic tables at each site, and fire rings. Reservations are required through ReserveOhio. The main Caldwell Lake campground nearby provides additional services including a dump station and camp store at the check-in station.

location.directions: From Chillicothe, take US Route 23 south approximately 10 miles. The park entrance is on the east side of the highway. Follow signs to the Stewart Lake area and park at the day use area, then walk in to the primitive campground via the bridle trail west of the picnic area below Stewart Lake Dam.

links.title: Scioto Trail State Park Campground Map

payload.name: Lakeside
payload.status_description: Current operating status could not be confirmed from official sources. The USFS recreation page for this campground redirects to a general listing, and the facility does not appear on Recreation.gov's current Apache-Sitgreaves campground inventory. Contact the Lakeside Ranger District at (928) 368-2100 for current availability.
payload.short_description: Historic National Forest campground near the dam at Rainbow Lake in Pinetop-Lakeside, one of the oldest Forest Service campgrounds in Arizona.
payload.medium_description: Lakeside Campground is a small, historic campground located near the dam at Rainbow Lake in the Pinetop-Lakeside area of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests. Situated at approximately 6,000 feet elevation among Ponderosa pines, it is one of the oldest National Forest campgrounds in Arizona. The campground offers basic amenities for tent and RV camping with access to Rainbow Lake.
payload.long_description:
Lakeside Campground sits near the dam at Rainbow Lake in the Pinetop-Lakeside area of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests. Established as one of the oldest National Forest campgrounds in Arizona, the site offers a scenic setting among Ponderosa pines at approximately 6,000 feet elevation, the lowest in the White Mountains.

The campground provides basic camping facilities for tents, trailers, and motorhomes up to 32 feet. Its location near Rainbow Lake offers convenient access for fishing and water recreation. Much of the land surrounding Rainbow Lake is privately owned, with the campground occupying a small parcel of public land near the dam.

Due to its relatively low elevation compared to other White Mountains campgrounds, the area experiences milder conditions, though winters can still be cold. The Lakeside Ranger District manages recreation in this area.

location.directions: The campground is located near the dam at Rainbow Lake in Pinetop-Lakeside. Rainbow Lake is within the town limits of Pinetop-Lakeside, Arizona.

address.full: 2106 W White Mountain Blvd, Lakeside, AZ 85929

payload.name: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Reservations are available through the Louisiana State Parks reservation system online or by calling 1-833-609-0686.
payload.short_description: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park is the ticket for when you need to get away for a couple of days.
payload.medium_description: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park features 54 campsites along a scenic 2,700-acre man-made lake in northeastern Louisiana. Premium sites include full hookups (water, electric, sewer) while improved sites offer water and electric. The campground provides bathhouses with showers, laundry facilities, a water playground, swimming beach, boat launch, marina, and fishing pier. Deluxe cabins and lodges are also available for those seeking more comfort.
payload.long_description: Poverty Point Reservoir State Park is the ticket for when you need to get away for a couple of days. Located in Delhi, Louisiana, this state park is considered a fisherman's paradise. Bring your rod and reel and you might catch any number of fish in the reservoir that is home to a variety of fish. Birdwatchers can delight in the many different species of feathered friends that can be spotted in the area. Our waterfront cabins that sleep 6 are an absolute treasure. They include everything you will need for a relaxing getaway. Just bring some food and a good book and you are all set! The views of the lake from the back deck are mesmerizing. Or consider staying in one of the deluxe rustic lodges that have an upstairs loft. For more relaxation one can enjoy the beach located a few miles up the road at the Marina. Black Bear Conference Center The Conference Center at Black Bear Golf Club in Delhi, La. is one of Northeast Louisiana’s premier venues of the area. Situated just off the 18th hole, the Conference Center is the perfect place to hold your next golf tournament, cooperate event, family reunion or wedding. The building’s design is inspired by Craftsman Lodge-style architecture. A handsome lobby greets guests then flows into the main event space which features sweeping panoramic views of the golf course appointed with Craftsman Lodge design elements. Moving to the exterior spaces, the venue boosts expansive front and rear covered plazas to entertain guests. Additionally, the rear plaza features a 38-foot-high tower, a focal point from various locations on the golf course. There is also an integrated PA system designed for golf tournaments, special events and general safety announcements. A central multi-purpose breezeway connects the conference center building to the restaurant and pro shop building. The area features seating nooks, cart parking, television displays providing the latest tournament standings and other information.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks - Poverty Point Reservoir
Louisiana State Parks - Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Judith Guard Station
payload.status_description: The cabin opens for the 2026 season on May 21. Reservations required through Recreation.gov. Water from the hand-pump well is available May through September; bring your own water outside this window. Road may require 4WD or snowmobile access in winter conditions.
payload.short_description: Historic 1900s ranger station cabin rental near the Middle Fork of the Judith River, accommodating 8 guests with propane heat and cookstove in the Helena-Lewis and Clark National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Judith Guard Station is a National Historic Site dating from the early 1900s, offering rustic cabin accommodations for up to 8 guests. The two-story frame building features propane heating and cookstove, with a vault toilet outside. A hand-pump well provides drinking water from May through September. Located 30 miles south of Stanford, Montana, the cabin sits near the Middle Fork of the Judith River with hiking, OHV, hunting, and mountain biking opportunities nearby.
payload.long_description:
Judith Guard Station is a historic ranger station from the early 1900s, designated as a National Historic Site and decorated with historically accurate furnishings and wallpaper. This two-story frame building accommodates up to 8 guests and features propane heating, a propane cookstove, beds, kitchen table with chairs, and cooking utensils. A modern vault toilet is located outside, along with a porch with chairs.

The cabin sits at approximately 5,000 feet elevation on the northern banks of the Middle Fork of the Judith River, surrounded by wooded hills of Ponderosa Pine, lodgepole pine, and Douglas fir. Wildlife in the area includes deer, elk, bear, bobcats, and mountain lions. Mandatory bear food storage requirements apply.

Guests must bring bedding, food, an ice chest, and garbage bags as there is no electricity or garbage service. A hand-pump well provides drinking water from May through September; winter visitors must bring their own water. The cabin is accessible by highway vehicle except when roads are snow-covered. Parking is limited to 2 vehicles.

location.directions: From Great Falls, travel east on US Highway 87 approximately 63 miles to Windham. Turn south off MT Highway 200/US 87 and continue about 10 miles to Utica. At the Oxen Yoke Inn, turn south onto the gravel county road. Continue 13 miles, turn right at the Y junction. Continue southwest about one mile, at the second Y junction stay left and continue one mile to the Judith Guard Station.

payload.name: Cedar Creek State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally spring through fall. Reservations accepted online, by phone, or at the campground office. Two-night minimum on Friday-Saturday; one-night stays permitted Sunday through Thursday. 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Set on 2,588 wooded acres near Glenville in West Virginia’s central region, Cedar Creek State Park’s rolling hills and wide valleys provide and ideal backdrop for a variety of recreational activities from hiking to fishing. Park highlights include a furnished one-room schoolhouse and a fully restored log cabin, which serves as the campground check-in station.
payload.medium_description: Cedar Creek State Park Campground sits on 2,588 wooded acres near Glenville in West Virginia's central hill country. The 76-site campground offers water and 30-amp electric hookups, fire rings, grills, and picnic tables at each site. Three bathhouses with showers and laundry facilities serve campers, while a restored log cabin serves as the check-in station. The park features a heated outdoor pool, miniature golf, three fishing ponds stocked with trout and bass, and 14 miles of multi-use trails.
payload.long_description:
Cedar Creek State Park Campground occupies a forested valley in Gilmer County, about 4 miles south of Glenville. The campground includes 66 regular sites and 10 group sites, all with water hookups and 30-amp electric service. Each site has a fire ring, grill, and picnic table. Three bathhouses with showers and a laundry facility are spread throughout the campground. A restored 1800s log cabin serves as the check-in station, adding historical character to the camping experience.

Beyond camping, the park offers a heated outdoor swimming pool open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day, a miniature golf course, and courts for tennis, basketball, and volleyball. Three small ponds stocked with trout, catfish, bass, and bluegill provide fishing opportunities, and Cedar Creek itself offers additional angling. Fourteen miles of trails wind through the wooded terrain for hiking and biking. A park store sells groceries, ice, and firewood.

The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, with reservations available online, by phone, or at the campground office. A two-night minimum applies to weekend stays. The park recommends using Route 5 through Glenville rather than Cedarville and Copen Road when hauling trailers.

location.directions: From Glenville, take Route 5 south approximately 4 miles. Those hauling campers should use Route 5 through Glenville rather than the Cedarville and Copen Road route.

address.full: 423 Cedar Creek Park Rt 803, Glenville, WV 26351

links.title: Cedar Creek State Park Main Page

payload.name: Buck Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the 2026 season due to extensive flood damage to Suiattle River Road. The facility is currently inaccessible. Normal operating season is May through September, with hosting from Memorial Day through Labor Day weekends.
payload.short_description: Primitive old-growth forest campground along Buck Creek in Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, offering secluded creekside sites near Darrington, WA.
payload.medium_description: Buck Creek Campground offers 14 primitive sites scattered beneath towering old-growth forest along Buck Creek. Every site can hear the rushing water, with some creekfront sites available. Popular as a quiet getaway and base camp for area trails. No potable water; campers must bring their own supplies. Vault toilets available.
payload.long_description:
Situated on the banks of Buck Creek in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest, Buck Creek Campground provides a rustic, secluded camping experience in the Northern Cascade Range. The 14 standard nonelectric sites are scattered beneath a towering canopy of old-growth forest, with every campsite within earshot of the rushing creek. Creekfront sites offer the most direct access to the water.

This primitive campground is popular with those seeking a quiet getaway and serves as an ideal base camp for accessing many area trails. Activities include fishing, hiking, wildlife viewing, swimming, and picnicking. The forest is hemmed in by several designated wilderness areas and showcases rugged peaks and sparkling alpine lakes.

Facilities are minimal: vault toilets and picnic tables at each site, with fire rings for campfires (subject to seasonal restrictions). No drinking water is available, so campers must bring adequate supplies. Dogs are allowed but must remain on leash. Check-in is at 2:00 p.m., check-out at noon, with quiet hours from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. and a 14-day stay limit.

location.directions: From Darrington, travel north on SR 530 approximately 7 miles to Suiattle River Road (Forest Road 26). Drive approximately 16 miles to the campground, located on the left/north side of the road. The last 5 miles are gravel.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Due to extensive flood damage to the Suiattle River Road, this facility is currently inaccessible and will be closed for the 2026 season. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. **

payload.name: Harris Springs Office
payload.status_description: Harris Springs Office is a historic guard station that is not available for overnight stays or rental. It is not part of the USFS cabin rental program. For camping in this area, use the adjacent Harris Spring Campground.
payload.short_description: Historic Forest Service guard station in Shasta-Trinity National Forest that has been restored but is not available for rental or overnight stays.
payload.medium_description: Harris Springs Office is a historic Forest Service guard station located in the remote McCloud area of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The building has been restored but is no longer part of the USFS Lookouts and Cabins Rental Program and is not available for overnight accommodation. An adjacent primitive camping area, Harris Spring Campground, offers free dispersed camping for those seeking overnight stays in this area.
payload.long_description:
Harris Springs Office is a historic Forest Service guard station situated in the remote backcountry of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest, approximately 17 miles up Forest Road 15 from Highway 89 near McCloud, California. The building has been restored by the Forest Service but is no longer available through the cabin rental program.

Visitors looking for overnight camping in this area should instead use the adjacent Harris Spring Campground, a separate primitive camping area with approximately 15 user-created sites, a vault toilet, and no fees. The campground has no potable water, and campers must be self-sufficient.

The area is accessed via Harris Springs Road (Forest Road 15), a remote route that also provides access to other destinations like Little Mt. Hoffman Lookout. The forested terrain features pine and fir trees at approximately 4,800 feet elevation.

location.directions: From McCloud Ranger Station on Highway 89, turn left onto Forest Road 15 (Harris Springs Road) and travel approximately 17 miles to the site on the right.

payload.name: Portola Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. The seasonal creek bridges have been removed. Campground may close temporarily during severe winter weather; affected reservations can be refunded or relocated to another Santa Cruz District park.
payload.short_description: Tent and small RV campground nestled among towering old-growth redwoods in the Santa Cruz Mountains, featuring 55 shaded sites with flush toilets and pay showers.
payload.medium_description: Portola Campground sits beneath old-growth coast redwoods in the Santa Cruz Mountains about 45 minutes from Silicon Valley. The 55-site campground offers flush toilets, pay showers, and drinking water, with each site equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and food locker. Six designated sites accommodate RVs and trailers up to 24 feet, though no hookups are available. Group camps, hike-and-bike sites, and a backcountry trail camp at Slate Creek provide additional options.
payload.long_description:
Portola Redwoods State Park protects one of the finest remaining stands of old-growth coast redwoods in the Santa Cruz Mountains, including the Shaw Flat Trail's ancient specimens. The campground occupies a shaded canyon along Peters and Pescadero Creeks, surrounded by towering redwoods, Douglas fir, and a lush understory of ferns and sorrel. Despite being less than an hour from San Jose, the park feels remote and sees lighter crowds than many Bay Area parks.

The main campground has 55 family sites suitable for tents and small RVs (max 24 ft motorhomes, 21 ft trailers). Sites 1, 4, 7, 8, 9, and 19 can accommodate RVs, though none offer hookups. Four walk-in sites require a short carry from parking. Amenities include flush restrooms, pay showers (25 cents for 2 minutes, may close during droughts), drinking water, a campfire center, firewood sales, and a visitor center staffed on weekends. Each site has a picnic table, fire ring with grate, and bear-proof food locker.

Beyond car camping, the park offers four group camps (25-50 person capacity), first-come-first-served hike-and-bike sites at Huckleberry Campground, and the Slate Creek Trail Camp about 2.5 miles in for backpackers. Over 18 miles of trails wind through the forest, connecting to adjacent Big Basin Redwoods and Pescadero Creek Park for extended hiking.

location.directions: From Highway 35 (Skyline Boulevard), take Alpine Road west for 3 miles to Portola State Park Road. Turn left and continue 3 miles to the park entrance. Alternatively, from Highway 84 in La Honda, take Pescadero Creek Road south for 1 mile, then turn left onto Portola State Park Road and continue 4 miles to the park.

address.full: 9000 Portola State Park Rd, La Honda, CA 94020

payload.name: Iron Phone Junction Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served, no fee. Road access may be blocked by snow during winter months. No potable water or trash service; campers must pack out all garbage.
payload.short_description: Primitive 4-site horse campground in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests with vault toilets, fire rings, and hitching rails. No water, no fee, pack-it-out.
payload.medium_description: Iron Phone Junction is a small, free, primitive horse campground with four sites nestled in the rugged backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. Each site features a fire ring and hitching rails for stock. A vault toilet is available, but there is no potable water, trash service, or cell phone coverage. Access is via Forest Road 241, about 11 miles west of Riggins.
payload.long_description:
Iron Phone Junction Campground is a rustic, no-fee horse camping destination located in the remote backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Idaho County. The campground offers four primitive campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and hitching rails for horses and pack stock. A vault toilet is on site, but campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash.

This is true backcountry territory with no cell phone service and rugged conditions. The campground serves as a staging area for horseback riding and exploring the surrounding wilderness. While officially open year-round, winter snow often makes the access road impassable. The 11-mile drive on Forest Road 241 from Riggins requires a vehicle suited for unpaved mountain roads.

location.directions: North of Riggins, Idaho, turn west on Forest Road 241. Follow Road 241 approximately 11 miles to Iron Phone Junction.

payload.name: Pocahontas Banquet Halls
payload.status_description: This is an event venue for weddings and meetings, not a campground. The banquet halls are available for rental year-round. For overnight camping at Pocahontas State Park, look for the park's designated campground facilities.
payload.short_description: Indoor banquet halls for weddings and events at Pocahontas State Park, not a campground. Two halls accommodate up to 150 guests with commercial kitchens and climate control.
payload.medium_description: Pocahontas Banquet Halls are indoor event venues at Pocahontas State Park, not camping facilities. The Algonquian (Powhatan) Hall seats 125 guests and Swift Creek Hall seats 150 guests. Both feature commercial kitchens, heating/AC, restrooms, and tables/chairs. The venues are popular for weddings and include access to outdoor ceremony spaces and a bride cabin.
payload.long_description:
Pocahontas Banquet Halls at Pocahontas State Park are indoor event facilities designed for weddings, meetings, and receptions. This is NOT a campground or overnight camping area. The park offers two banquet halls: Algonquian (Powhatan) Hall accommodates up to 125 guests and features hardwood floors, wood ceiling beams, and windows overlooking wooded areas. Swift Creek Hall has a larger capacity of 150 guests and includes a gas fireplace.

Both halls are equipped with commercial-grade kitchens featuring stoves, ovens, refrigerators, freezers, and microwaves. The venues are heated and air-conditioned for year-round use. Tables and chairs are included in the rental. Reservations for the banquet halls include access to the newly renovated Bride Cabin for wedding party preparation, plus complimentary use of outdoor ceremony spaces throughout the park.

For actual camping at Pocahontas State Park, visitors should look for the park's designated campgrounds, which are separate facilities from these banquet halls.

location.directions: Located within Pocahontas State Park at 10301 State Park Road, Chesterfield, VA 23832. From I-95 south of Richmond, take exit 61 onto Route 10 west, then left onto Route 655 (Beach Road). Go about four miles to State Park Road on the right.

address.full: 10397 E State Park Rd, Chesterfield, VA 23832

payload.name: Clackamas Lake Historic Cabin
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The cabin typically operates from late May through early October. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Firewood and garbage service are provided. Guests must bring their own bedding, towels, and food.
payload.short_description: Historic 1933 CCC-built ranger cabin in Mount Hood National Forest near Clackamas Lake, offering rustic lodging with modern amenities for up to 8 guests.
payload.medium_description: The Clackamas Lake Historic Cabin is a beautifully preserved two-story ranger cabin built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933. Located in a 4-acre compound listed on the National Register of Historic Places, the 1,380 square foot cabin features a massive rock chimney, knotty pine interior, flush toilet with shower, full kitchen with propane appliances, and a fireplace insert for heating. Situated a quarter-mile from Clackamas Lake and 3 miles from Timothy Lake at 3,400 feet elevation.
payload.long_description:
The Clackamas Lake Historic Cabin offers a unique overnight experience in a well-preserved Depression Era Forest Service building. Built in 1933 by the Civilian Conservation Corps, this two-story cabin features classic rustic architecture with a massive rock chimney, knot-free interior paneling, and hand-wrought ironwork. The cabin is part of a historic ranger station compound that includes the old District Ranger's office, now serving as a visitor center and museum staffed by on-site volunteer caretakers.

The 1,380 square foot cabin accommodates up to 8 guests across three bedrooms: a downstairs room with a queen bed, an east upstairs room with a full and twin bed, and a west upstairs room with bunk beds and two twins. Amenities include a fully equipped kitchen with propane range and refrigerator, bathroom with flush toilet and hot water shower, living room with fireplace insert, dining area, and sun porch. Electricity is provided by a generator operating 6-10am and 5-10pm, with propane lanterns available for other hours.

Clackamas Lake offers fishing for cutthroat, brook, rainbow, and German brown trout, plus swimming and non-motorized boating. The 2.2-mile Miller Trail connects to the Pacific Crest Trail, and nearby 1,400-acre Timothy Lake provides additional recreation including power boating. Mt. Hood is less than 40 miles away for hiking and year-round skiing.

location.directions: From Portland, take Highway 26 east to Sandy. Continue on Highway 26 for approximately 39 miles and turn right (south) on Skyline Road/Forest Road 42. Travel 10 miles on Road 42. Just past the Forest Road 57 junction is the Clackamas Lake Historic Ranger Station on the left.

links.title: Mt. Hood NF - Clackamas Lake Historic House

payload.name: Red Cloud Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours. First-come, first-served with no reservations. Stage 1 Fire Restrictions are in effect on the Mountainair Ranger District through August 31, 2026; campfires are permitted in agency-built fire rings at developed campsites. Services may be reduced; prepare for limited or no trash service.
payload.short_description: Small, quiet primitive campground with 5 sites nestled in a Ponderosa pine forest at 7,600 feet elevation near an old mining district in Cibola National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Red Cloud Campground offers a quiet, primitive camping experience in a secluded Ponderosa pine forest at 7,600 feet elevation. With only 5 sites, this campground provides solitude and easy access to hiking. Located near a historic mining district, it sees heavier use during fall hunting seasons but remains peaceful most of the year.
payload.long_description:
Red Cloud Campground is a small, primitive facility tucked into a Ponderosa pine forest within Cibola National Forest's Mountainair Ranger District. At 7,600 feet elevation, the campground offers cool mountain conditions and serves as a base for exploring the surrounding landscape, which includes remnants of an old mining district.

The campground has just 5 sites, each with a picnic table and fire ring. A vault toilet is available, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. Services may be reduced, including trash collection, so pack-out preparation is recommended. No hookups are available, making this strictly a primitive camping destination.

Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations, Red Cloud sees increased use during fall hunting seasons but remains quiet during other times. The remote location and small size make it ideal for campers seeking solitude.

location.directions: Located approximately 12 miles west of Corona, New Mexico in the Gallinas Mountains.

payload.name: Hocking Hills Family Hike In Camp
payload.status_description: Open and accepting reservations. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance through ReserveOhio.com or by calling (866) 644-6727.
payload.short_description: Primitive hike-in campground at Hocking Hills State Park offering a rustic backcountry experience with sites accessible only by foot, featuring fire rings, picnic tables, and pit latrines.
payload.medium_description: Hocking Hills Family Hike-In Campground provides a primitive, backcountry-style camping experience within one of Ohio's most scenic state parks. There is no road access to these sites; campers must hike their gear up to half a mile from the parking area located across State Route 374. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with pit latrines throughout and a water spigot at the parking area. Hike-in campers may use the showers and laundry facilities at the main Old Man's Cave Campground.
payload.long_description:
Hocking Hills Family Hike-In Campground offers a more secluded and rustic alternative to the main campground at Hocking Hills State Park. Situated in Ohio's dramatic sandstone gorge region, these primitive sites appeal to campers seeking a quieter experience away from RVs and drive-up sites. The parking area is located across State Route 374, approximately one mile from the main camp check-in, and campers must carry their gear up to half a mile on foot to reach their assigned site.

Each hike-in site is equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Pit latrines are distributed throughout the campground for restroom access, and potable water is available from a spigot at the parking area. Although the sites themselves are primitive, registered hike-in campers have access to the hot showers and laundry facilities at the main Old Man's Cave Campground.

Hocking Hills State Park is renowned for its sandstone cliffs, recess caves, and waterfalls, including the iconic Old Man's Cave, Ash Cave, and Cedar Falls. The hike-in campground puts backpackers within easy reach of the park's extensive trail system, making it an ideal base for exploring the Hocking Hills region.

location.directions: From Logan, take State Route 664 south. The hike-in campground parking area is located across State Route 374, approximately one mile from the main Old Man's Cave Campground check-in station.

links.title: Hocking Hills Family Hike-In Campground Map (PDF)

payload.name: Big Basin Redwoods Sp Sky Meadow Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely. The campground was destroyed in the 2020 CZU Lightning Complex Fire and has not been rebuilt. The Reimagining Big Basin project plans to reconstruct Sky Meadow with group sites, cabins, and walk-in camping, but no reopening date has been announced. Day-use parking at Big Basin is available by reservation only.
payload.short_description: Large group campground surrounded by towering redwoods at Big Basin Redwoods State Park, featuring two sites for up to 40 campers each with pit toilets and water but no showers.
payload.medium_description: Sky Meadow Group Campground consists of two large group sites in Big Basin Redwoods State Park, each accommodating up to 40 campers. Located in a flat, spacious clearing amid old-growth redwoods, it provides access to the park's extensive trail system including the Sempervirens Falls. Unlike other Big Basin facilities, Sky Meadow has pit toilets rather than flush and no showers on site.
payload.long_description:
Sky Meadow Group Campground sits within California's oldest state park, Big Basin Redwoods, surrounded by ancient coast redwoods and dense forest. The campground offers two large group sites, each capable of hosting up to 40 people, which can be reserved individually or together for larger gatherings. The flat, spacious sites are nestled directly in the redwood forest, providing an immersive wilderness experience.

The facility serves as a launching point for exploring Big Basin's trail network, with the Sempervirens River and falls nearby. Unlike the main campground areas at Big Basin, Sky Meadow has more rustic amenities with pit toilets and no shower facilities, though potable water is available. Campers seeking showers can use facilities at other campgrounds within the park.

The campground and all Big Basin camping facilities were destroyed in the August 2020 CZU Lightning Complex Fire, which burned through 97% of the park. The Reimagining Big Basin project is planning to rebuild Sky Meadow with a mix of cabins, car-camping, group sites, walk-in sites, a campfire center, and shuttle access. Most of the ancient redwood trees survived the fire and new growth is regenerating throughout the park.

location.directions: From Highway 9 in Boulder Creek, turn north onto Highway 236 and continue 9 miles to the Big Basin park entrance. The park is approximately 25 miles northwest of Santa Cruz.

links.title: Big Basin Fire Rebuilding Plan News Release

payload.name: Catalina Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The restroom and shower building in Campground A is closed through mid-June 2026 for renovation; portable restrooms are available and showers in Campground B remain operational. Park gates open 5:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. Limited to 14 consecutive nights per stay.
payload.short_description: Catalina State Park offers 120 electric and water hookup campsites at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains north of Tucson, with flush restrooms, hot showers, and dump stations.
payload.medium_description: Catalina State Park campground features 120 sites with electric (20/30/50A) and water hookups across Campgrounds A and B. Modern facilities include flush restrooms with hot showers and two RV dump stations. The park sits at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains, providing access to trails through Sonoran Desert landscape. A seasonal primitive campground (Ringtail) operates January through March.
payload.long_description:
Catalina State Park campground is located at the base of the Santa Catalina Mountains, approximately 9 miles north of Tucson along Oracle Road. The park encompasses nearly 5,500 acres of Sonoran Desert foothills, offering camping amid saguaro cacti, mesquite, and palo verde trees with mountain views.

Campgrounds A and B contain 120 paved sites, each equipped with electric hookups (20/30/50A), water connections, a picnic table, and BBQ grill. Modern restroom buildings provide flush toilets and hot showers. Two dump stations serve RV campers. There is no RV length limit, making the campground suitable for large rigs. The seasonal Ringtail Campground offers primitive camping without hookups from January through March.

The park provides access to multiple hiking and equestrian trails, including connections to Coronado National Forest. An equestrian center with 16 horse stalls is available for camping with horses. A small visitor center gift shop sells maps, snacks, and basic supplies, though no full camp store exists on site.

location.directions: From Tucson, take Oracle Road (State Route 77) north approximately 9 miles. The park entrance is on the right at 11570 N. Oracle Road. From Phoenix, take I-10 south to Tucson, exit onto Oracle Road and head north.

links.title: Catalina State Park RV and Tent Camping

payload.name: Harrys Hollow
payload.status_description: Open seasonally May 1 through September 30. First-come, first-served only, no reservations. No fee.
payload.short_description: Small, free primitive campground with 3 sites in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest near Bear Lake, featuring forested creekside camping at 6,670 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Harrys Hollow is a small, free primitive campground with just 3 sites, located in the Montpelier Ranger District of the Caribou-Targhee National Forest near Paris, Idaho. The campground sits at 6,670 feet elevation in a forested canyon setting with creekside spots. Open seasonally from May through September 30, it operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations.
payload.long_description:
Harrys Hollow is a small, rustic campground tucked into a forested canyon in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest, managed by the Montpelier Ranger District. With only 3 campsites at 6,670 feet elevation, it offers a quiet, secluded experience for those seeking primitive camping near Bear Lake. The campground features creekside spots nestled among trees.

The campground operates seasonally from May through September 30 and is entirely first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted. There is no fee to camp. Basic facilities include vault toilets, but campers should be prepared to bring their own water. The nearby town of Paris is a few miles away, and Bear Lake's recreational opportunities are within easy driving distance.

location.directions: From Paris, Idaho, head east on Harrys Hollow Road into the National Forest. The campground is approximately 3-4 miles from town.

links.title: Caribou-Targhee NF Montpelier Ranger District Office

payload.name: Valentine Ridge Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round as a dispersed camping area. No fees required. 14-day stay limit. Four-wheel drive or chains may be advisable after heavy snows. Winter temperatures drop into the teens.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed camping area in Tonto National Forest near Canyon Creek, featuring a 9-mile mountain bike loop and rainbow trout fishing.
payload.medium_description: Valentine Ridge is a primitive dispersed camping area in Tonto National Forest's high country near Canyon Creek. The area offers free camping with a 14-day stay limit, access to a 9-mile all-terrain bicycle loop trail, and proximity to rainbow trout fishing. Wildlife in the area includes elk, black bear, mountain lion, turkey, and Abert squirrel.
payload.long_description:
Valentine Ridge Dispersed Camping Area sits in the high country of Tonto National Forest near Canyon Creek, a stream known for its rainbow trout fishing. This is primitive dispersed camping with no developed amenities. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. A 9-mile all-terrain bicycle loop trail begins at the camping area.

The area is home to diverse wildlife including Abert squirrel, black bear, mountain lion, elk, turkey, and deer. Winter temperatures can drop into the teens, and four-wheel drive or chains may be needed after heavy snowfall. Bear-proofing of camps is mandatory. Trailers are limited to under 16 feet due to road conditions.

Canyon Creek offers regulated fishing opportunities. Upstream of OW Bridge, a 4-trout limit applies with artificial fly or lure only using single barbless hooks. From OW Bridge to the Fort Apache Reservation boundary, catch-and-release only regulations are in effect.

location.directions: From Payson, travel 33 miles east on State Hwy. 260. Turn right on unpaved Young Road/FR 512 and continue for approximately 5 miles to FR 188. Turn left on FR 188 and travel 2 miles to the site. Alternatively, from Young, take State Hwy. 288/FR 512 north for 20 miles to FR 188, turn right and follow for 2 miles.

links.title: USFS Valentine Ridge Dispersed Camping Area

payload.name: Summit Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently decommissioned. All facilities have been removed and vehicular access is no longer available. This site is not open for camping.
payload.short_description: Summit Creek Campground in Gifford Pinchot National Forest has been permanently decommissioned. All facilities have been removed and the site is no longer accessible for camping.
payload.medium_description: Summit Creek Campground was a small, rustic Forest Service campground located along Forest Road 4510 in Gifford Pinchot National Forest, Washington. The site has been permanently decommissioned, with all facilities removed and vehicular access no longer available. Campers seeking developed camping in this area should consider nearby alternatives such as La Wis Wis Campground or Soda Spring Campground.
payload.long_description:
Summit Creek Campground was once a small, primitive campground situated on a flat area between Summit Creek and Forest Road 4510 in Gifford Pinchot National Forest. The site sat at approximately 2,350 feet elevation in a mid-elevation forest of Douglas fir, western hemlock, and red cedar. Before its closure, the campground offered six tent-only or small camper sites.

The campground has been permanently decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service. All facilities have been removed and vehicular access to the former campground is no longer available. The site is no longer maintained or operated as a camping area.

Campers looking for developed camping in this area of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest have alternatives nearby. La Wis Wis Campground on US Highway 12, approximately 7 miles east of Packwood, and Soda Spring Campground on Forest Road 4510 are options in the local area.

location.directions: From Packwood, WA, proceed northeast on US Highway 12 for approximately 9 miles to Forest Road 45. Turn left on Forest Road 45 and proceed 0.35 miles to Forest Road 4510. Continue straight on Forest Road 4510 for 1.8 miles to the former Summit Creek Campground location. Note: vehicular access to the site is no longer available.

payload.name: Sam Houston Jones State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. Park gates are open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Reservations are available through GoOutdoorsLouisiana.com.
payload.short_description: A 1,047-acre Louisiana State Park north of Lake Charles featuring 30 premium RV campsites with full hookups, cabins, and a lodge along the Calcasieu River and scenic lagoons.
payload.medium_description: Sam Houston Jones State Park sits on 1,047 acres of cypress-tupelo swamp and mixed pine-hardwood forest along the west fork of the Calcasieu River. The campground features 30 premium pull-through sites with water, sewer, and 50-amp electric hookups positioned along picturesque lagoons. Facilities include flush restrooms, hot showers, and a dump station. Ten deluxe cabins and a 14-person lodge are also available for overnight stays.
payload.long_description:
Sam Houston Jones State Park encompasses 1,047 acres of diverse Louisiana landscape, including cypress-tupelo swamp, mixed pine-hardwood forest, and scenic lagoons fed by the west fork of the Calcasieu River. Established in 1944, the park underwent extensive reconstruction following devastating damage from Hurricanes Laura and Delta in 2020, reopening in 2022 with modernized facilities. Over 5,000 longleaf pine trees were planted as part of the restoration effort.

The campground features 30 premium pull-through RV sites arranged along the lagoons, each equipped with water, sewer, and 50-amp electrical connections, plus a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. Hot showers, flush restrooms, and an RV dump station serve campers. Ten deluxe cabins sleeping up to 8 guests and a lodge accommodating 14 are available for those seeking more amenities.

Recreational opportunities include hiking and biking on multi-use trails, paddling the lagoons and river, fishing for bass and catfish, and wildlife observation along a 500-foot accessible boardwalk. The park serves as an excellent base for exploring the greater Lake Charles area while enjoying a quiet natural retreat.

location.directions: From Lake Charles, head north on LA-171 for approximately 10 miles. Turn right onto Sutherland Road and follow it to the park entrance at 107 Sutherland Road, Lake Charles, LA 70611.

links.title: Sam Houston Jones State Park Official Page

payload.name: Bessey Recreation Complex
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Approximately half the sites are reservable mid-May through mid-October via Recreation.gov; remaining sites are first-come, first-served year-round. Showers and flush toilets operate mid-May to mid-October, weather permitting. Vault toilets and potable water at the recreation building are available year-round.
payload.short_description: Forest Service campground in central Nebraska's Sandhills adjacent to Middle Loup River, offering fishing, tubing, and access to the world's largest hand-planted forest.
payload.medium_description: Bessey Recreation Complex sits within the Nebraska National Forest near Halsey, adjacent to Middle Loup River. The campground features electric and non-electric sites across three loops (Hardwood, Cedar, and River), plus a group site. A seven-acre pond stocked with bass, bluegill, trout, and catfish offers fishing with an accessible pier. The shallow, steady-flowing river provides tubing and canoeing opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Bessey Recreation Complex is located in the heart of the Nebraska Sandhills, home to the world's largest hand-planted forest established in the early 1900s at the Charles E. Bessey Nursery. The campground offers sites across three loops adjacent to Middle Loup River, with options for tents and RVs. Roughly half the sites have electric hookups with 20, 30, or 50 amp service.

The complex features a seven-acre fishing pond stocked with largemouth bass, bluegill, trout, and catfish, plus an accessible fishing pier. Middle Loup River runs shallow and steady, making it ideal for tubing and canoeing. Wildlife viewing is excellent, with prairie chickens, sharp-tailed grouse, mule deer, whitetail deer, pronghorn, turkeys, and raptors in the surrounding Sandhills ecosystem.

Nearby attractions include the Scott Lookout Tower for panoramic views of the sand hills and prairies, and the Bessey OHV Trail System for off-highway vehicle recreation.

location.directions: From Thedford, Nebraska, take Highway 2 about 17 miles east, then turn south onto State Spur 86B. After crossing the river, continue straight into the complex.

photos.name: Bessey Picnic area located within the Bessey Recreation Complex near Halsey, NE.
Looking out the Entrance to the Bessey Recreation Complex
The Bessey Picnic Shelter, available for reservations year around.
Bessey Ranger District and Nursery Office

payload.name: South Toledo Bend State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. The ATV/OHV trail is temporarily closed. Reservations are available through gooutdoorslouisiana.com. A $4.50 non-refundable fee applies to each reservation transaction.
payload.short_description: There are overnight accommodations for those that want to get close to nature and those that enjoy a few creature comforts with their outdoor experience.
payload.medium_description: South Toledo Bend State Park sits on the shores of Toledo Bend Reservoir, one of the largest man-made lakes in the South. The campground offers 55 improved campsites with water and electric hookups on concrete pads, many with lake views. Five primitive tent sites perch on bluffs above the water. The park includes a comfort station with restrooms, showers, and coin-operated laundry. A 12-mile OHV trail system with 9 loops attracts off-road enthusiasts, though it is temporarily closed. Fishing and boating access to Toledo Bend's renowned bass fishing are primary draws.
payload.long_description: There are overnight accommodations for those that want to get close to nature and those that enjoy a few creature comforts with their outdoor experience. The 19-two bedroom cabins sleep up to eight guests each, and include a full kitchen and bathroom facilities. Each cabin has an enclosed back porch with a picnic table and chairs, and a deck. There is a picnic table and a primitive style grill behind each of the cabins. Many of the 55 improved campsites feature a lake view, and all have water and electrical hookups. 5 primitive sites are located on one of the bluffs overlooking the lake, and offer a spectacular view for that early morning wakeup. There is a comfort station in the campground area that has restrooms, showers, and laundry facilities. There are two playgrounds in the park, one behind the comfort station, the other between cabins 5 and 6.

location.directions: From Leesville, take LA-8 West approximately 20 miles. Turn south on LA-191 and follow signs to the park.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks - South Toledo Bend

payload.name: Gold Rush Campground And Trailhead
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 5. The vault toilet closes October 31. No reservations; first-come, first-served only.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive campground in a shady forest canyon along a stream in Lolo National Forest. First-come, first-served with vault toilets, no water.
payload.medium_description: Gold Rush Campground is a small, no-fee campground tucked into a narrow canyon bottom along a stream in the Lolo National Forest. The site is forested and shady, offering a quiet retreat. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. A hiking trail to the CC Divide starts near campsite #4. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Gold Rush Campground sits in a forested, shady canyon bottom along a stream in the Plains/Thompson Falls area of Lolo National Forest. The primitive campground offers a peaceful setting for tent camping and provides access to the Gold Rush Trail, which begins near campsite #4 and climbs steeply to the CC Divide.

This is a no-fee, first-come, first-served campground with no reservations. Each campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring. A vault toilet is available on site but closes October 31. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available. Pets are allowed but must be kept on leash; horses and pack animals are prohibited.

location.directions: From Thompson Falls, travel west on Prospect Creek Road for 2 miles. Turn left (east) on Cherry Creek Road. Turn right (south) on Dry Creek Road #352 for 6 miles. Campground is on the right (west) side near the 6-mile marker.

address.full: 706 Dry Creek Rd, Thompson Falls, MT 59873

payload.name: Moncove Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open spring through fall, weather permitting. The campground typically operates April 1 through the end of October, with limited availability in November for hunters by calling ahead. Reservations require a minimum of two consecutive nights on weekends or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Moncove Lake State Park offers a peaceful setting for families to enjoy the outdoors. The park is a popular destination for outdoor social gatherings, quiet strolls, camping and water recreation. This 250-acre park contains a larger, 500-acre wildlife management area. Located in the hills of the southeastern edge of the state, near Union in Monroe County, the park offers many opportunities for fishing, hunting, boating, swimming, birdwatching and hiking.
payload.medium_description: Moncove Lake State Park Campground is a 48-site campground located in the hills of southeastern West Virginia near Gap Mills. The campground features 34 sites with electric hookups, a central bathhouse with showers, drinking water, a dump station, and firewood for purchase. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill. The park surrounds a peaceful lake ideal for fishing, boating, and swimming, with hiking trails and abundant wildlife in the adjacent 500-acre wildlife management area.
payload.long_description:
Moncove Lake State Park Campground sits on the southeastern edge of West Virginia in Monroe County, offering a peaceful retreat centered around a scenic lake. The 48-site campground provides 34 sites with electric hookups for RVs and trailers, while the remaining sites accommodate tent campers seeking a more primitive experience. Every site is equipped with a picnic table and fire ring with grill surface, and the campground features a central bathhouse with showers, drinking water, and a dump station.

The surrounding park covers 250 acres and connects to a 500-acre wildlife management area, creating ample opportunities for fishing, boating, swimming, hiking, and birdwatching. The lake is stocked and popular with anglers, while the mixed hardwood forests attract diverse wildlife. Three picnic shelters are available for day use by reservation, and playground areas make this a family-friendly destination.

location.directions: The campground is located at 695 Moncove Lake Access Rd, Gap Mills, WV 24941, in Monroe County near Union.

address.full: 1047 Moncove Lake Access Rd, Gap Mills, WV 24941

payload.name: Temperance River State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Upper Campground has seasonal flush toilets and hot showers (May through October). Lower Campground vault toilets available year-round. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance at reservemn.usedirect.com or by calling 866-857-2757.
payload.short_description: Scenic North Shore campground along the Temperance River with two camping areas offering electric and rustic sites, flush toilets, seasonal showers, and Lake Superior views.
payload.medium_description: Temperance River State Park Campground sits along Minnesota's North Shore near Schroeder, featuring two distinct camping areas. The Upper Campground offers 18 electric sites with flush toilets and seasonal hot showers, while the Lower Campground provides 34 rustic sites with vault toilets and views of Lake Superior. The park is known for its dramatic river gorge and waterfalls, accessible via 22 miles of hiking trails.
payload.long_description:
Located along Highway 61 on Minnesota's North Shore, Temperance River State Park Campground offers camping within walking distance of the dramatic Temperance River gorge, where the river cascades through ancient volcanic rock formations on its way to Lake Superior. The park takes its name from the river's unusually calm mouth, which lacks the traditional sand bar found at other North Shore rivers.

The campground is divided into two areas. The Upper Campground contains 18 electric sites, including two pull-through sites and one wheelchair-accessible site, with modern amenities including flush toilets and seasonal hot showers. The Lower Campground offers 34 rustic non-electric sites in a more secluded setting, some with partial Lake Superior views, served by vault toilets available year-round. Six additional cart-in sites provide a backcountry experience with bear-proof food storage.

Beyond camping, the park features 22 miles of hiking trails that wind through boreal forest and along the river gorge, providing access to multiple waterfalls including the popular Lower Falls. Winter visitors can access groomed snowmobile trails. The campground operates year-round, though showers and flush toilets are typically available only from May through October.

location.directions: From Duluth, take Highway 61 northeast approximately 80 miles along Lake Superior. The park entrance is located just off Highway 61 near Schroeder, Minnesota at mile marker 80.

payload.name: Station Creek Camp
payload.status_description: This is a primitive dispersed camping area. Road access via FR-250 is seasonal and depends on snow conditions. Contact the North Fork Ranger District at 208-476-4541 for current road and site conditions.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground along Forest Service Road 250 in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, offering basic dispersed camping near the North Fork Clearwater River corridor.
payload.medium_description: Station Creek Camp is a primitive dispersed camping area located along Forest Service Road 250 in Clearwater County, Idaho. Situated at approximately 2,329 feet elevation within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, this small site offers about 5 undeveloped campsites for those seeking a rustic backcountry experience in the North Fork Clearwater River corridor.
payload.long_description:
Station Creek Camp is a primitive dispersed camping area in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, accessible via Forest Service Road 250 south of Pierce, Idaho. At roughly 2,329 feet elevation, the site sits within the scenic North Fork Clearwater River corridor, an area known for its remote wilderness character, fishing opportunities, and old-growth forest.

This is not a developed campground with maintained facilities. As a dispersed camping area on National Forest land, campers should expect primitive conditions and come fully self-sufficient. The site is typically accessible when the road is clear of snow, generally late spring through fall depending on conditions.

The surrounding area offers access to backcountry recreation including hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing. The North Fork Clearwater corridor is remote and visitors should be prepared for limited cell service and services.

location.directions: From Pierce, Idaho, head south on Forest Service Road 250. The campground is located along this road approximately 7-8 miles from Pierce. FR-250 is paved for several miles from its junction with State Highway 11 south of Pierce, then becomes a well-maintained gravel road.

payload.name: Spruce Grove Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served with no fees or reservations required. Fire danger is currently at Moderate, meaning campfires and stoves are allowed in the Klamath stoves provided, but a valid California Campfire Permit is required. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own.
payload.short_description: A free, primitive hike-in trail camp with 7 sites nestled in the San Gabriel Mountains, accessible via a 4-mile hike from Chantry Flat.
payload.medium_description: Spruce Grove Trail Camp is a backcountry destination in the Angeles National Forest within the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument. This hike-in campground offers 7 primitive sites with picnic tables and Klamath stoves for cooking. The 4-mile approach from Chantry Flat follows portions of the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail. Pack all water and supplies as no potable water or trash service is available.
payload.long_description:
Spruce Grove Trail Camp is a rustic backcountry campground located in the heart of the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument within Angeles National Forest. The camp features seven primitive walk-in sites, each equipped with a picnic table, and Klamath stoves are available for cooking when fire conditions permit. The setting along the upper reaches of the canyon provides a quiet retreat for hikers seeking solitude away from the more accessible frontcountry campgrounds.

Reaching Spruce Grove requires a roughly 4-mile hike from the Chantry Flat trailhead. The route follows portions of the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail and connects to the Upper Winter Creek Trail, making it a solid basecamp for further exploration. There is no potable water on site; seasonal stream water may be present but requires treatment and cannot be relied upon due to variable rainfall. Campers must pack in all supplies and pack out all trash.

No fees or reservations are required. Dogs are permitted but must remain leashed at all times. Fire restrictions vary with current conditions, so campers should verify the fire danger level before visiting. A valid California Campfire Permit is required for any stove or campfire use.

location.directions: Exit I-210 in Arcadia at Santa Anita Avenue and head north approximately 6 miles to Chantry Flat. Park at the Chantry Flat Picnic Area (Adventure Pass required for parking). Hike approximately 4 miles on the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail to reach the campground.

payload.name: Whitehorse Falls Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. First-come, first-served only via Scan & Pay at the site or fee envelopes. No potable water; campers must bring their own or treat water from nearby sources. Pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: A quiet, primitive five-site campground beneath old-growth Douglas-fir along the Clearwater River, featuring Whitehorse Falls and located on the Rogue-Umpqua National Scenic Byway.
payload.medium_description: Whitehorse Falls Campground offers five peaceful campsites nestled under a canopy of old-growth Douglas-fir in the Umpqua National Forest. The Clearwater River flows nearby, cascading into a tranquil pool at the scenic Whitehorse Falls. Located along the Rogue-Umpqua National Scenic Byway, this primitive campground provides vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings at each site but no potable water or trash services.
payload.long_description:
Whitehorse Falls Campground is a small, serene retreat set beneath towering old-growth Douglas-fir trees in Oregon's Umpqua National Forest. The five campsites offer a peaceful escape with easy access to Whitehorse Falls, where the Clearwater River tumbles into a clear pool. A day-use area with a viewing platform provides excellent views of the waterfall.

Situated along the Rogue-Umpqua National Scenic Byway, the campground is approximately 10 miles from Lemolo Lake and 15 miles from Diamond Lake Recreation Area. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Campers should be prepared for a primitive experience: there is no potable water on-site (filter or treat water from nearby sources), no trash services (pack it out), and no cell coverage.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with payment via the Recreation.gov Scan & Pay mobile app or fee envelopes on-site. Check-in is 1 p.m. and check-out is 11 a.m. Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 8 a.m.

location.directions: From Roseburg, OR, travel east on OR-138 / Diamond Lake Boulevard for 66 miles. Turn left at the Whitehorse Falls Campground sign.

payload.name: Landon Cabin
payload.status_description: Landon Cabin does not appear in the USFS public cabin rental program on recreation.gov. It may be an administrative facility not available for public reservation.
payload.short_description: Landon Cabin is a Forest Service cabin on the West Fork Madison River in the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, southwestern Montana.
payload.medium_description: Landon Cabin is a historic Forest Service cabin located in the Gravelly Range area of the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest near the West Fork Madison River. The cabin does not currently appear in the USFS public cabin rental program through recreation.gov.
payload.long_description:
Landon Cabin is a Forest Service structure situated in the remote Gravelly Range of the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest in Madison County, Montana, near the headwaters of the West Fork Madison River. The area offers access to high-elevation terrain and the surrounding wilderness.

The cabin is classified in Forest Service records as a Lookout/Cabin type facility; however, it does not appear in the current USFS public cabin rental inventory available through recreation.gov. This may indicate it serves as an administrative facility, is undergoing restoration, or is otherwise not open to the public for overnight stays.

location.directions: Landon Cabin is located near Lima, Montana in the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest. The cabin sits along a scenic meadow at the forest's edge. Access routes are typical of forest service cabins, best reached by local roads leading out from Lima.

payload.name: North Bend State Park Cokeley Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting. Reservations available online at wvstateparks.com, by phone, or at the campground office. Two-night minimum on weekends, 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Found among the Mid-Ohio Valley’s rolling hills, lakes and streams, North Bend State Park offers a multitude of recreational facilities in a beautiful pastoral setting. Named for the horseshoe curve of the North Fork of the Hughes River, this year-round park is lush with fishing streams, hiking trails and abundant wildlife. Located near Cairo and Harrisville, North Bend State Park is best known for the 72-mile North Bend Rail Trail, which follows an abandoned B&O Railroad corridor with several tunnels along the way.
payload.medium_description: Cokeley Campground is designed for RVs and campers, featuring 28 sites with electrical systems supporting A/C units and water hookups. The campground includes WiFi access, a coin-operated laundry facility, and ADA-compliant sites. Located within North Bend State Park, campers have access to the 72-mile North Bend Rail Trail, swimming pool, nature center, and lake activities.
payload.long_description:
Cokeley Campground sits within North Bend State Park in the rolling hills of Ritchie County, West Virginia. The campground was specifically designed for RVs and campers, with 28 sites equipped with electrical systems capable of supporting air conditioning units along with water hookups. WiFi coverage extends throughout the campground, and a coin-operated laundry facility is available on-site for extended stays.

The park offers extensive recreational opportunities beyond the campground. The 72-mile North Bend Rail Trail passes through the park, ideal for hiking and biking. The park's lake provides fishing, paddle boats, canoes, kayaks, and motorized boat rentals. A swimming pool, nature center, and playground are located nearby at the River Run Campground area.

Reservations require a minimum of two consecutive nights on weekends (Friday-Saturday) or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a maximum stay of 14 nights. The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting.

location.directions: Located at 202 North Bend State Park Road, Cairo, WV 26337. The park is in Ritchie County, accessible from US Route 50.

address.full: 626 N Bend Cokeley Boat Ramp, Cairo, WV 26337

payload.name: St. Bernard State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gate hours are 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station hours are 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday, and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday, Saturday, and holidays.
payload.short_description: St.
payload.medium_description: St. Bernard State Park offers 51 improved campsites with water and electrical hookups nestled among mature oak trees and man-made lagoons. Located only 20 minutes from New Orleans, the park provides a peaceful retreat with flush restrooms, hot showers, laundry facilities, and a dump station. A popular water playground operates seasonally, and nature trails wind through the grounds.
payload.long_description: St. Bernard is located along the Mississippi River, just 18 miles from the New Orleans French Quarter, providing a peaceful, natural setting for recreation and relaxation among wetlands & woodlands.

links.title: St. Bernard State Park - Louisiana State Parks
Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Beans Camp
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May through October. First-come, first-served, no reservations. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water supply.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 6 tent sites in Six Rivers National Forest at 4,000 feet elevation near Orleans, California.
payload.medium_description: Beans Camp is a small, free primitive campground located in the Ukonom Ranger District of Six Rivers National Forest, approximately 17 miles south of Orleans via Eyesee Road. The campground sits at 4,000 feet elevation and offers 6 tent sites with basic vault toilet facilities. The remote, backcountry setting provides access to the surrounding national forest lands.
payload.long_description:
Beans Camp is a rustic backcountry campground nestled in the mountains of the Ukonom Ranger District, which is geographically within the Klamath National Forest boundary but administered by Six Rivers National Forest. The campground offers 6 primitive tent camping sites at an elevation of approximately 4,000 feet, providing a quiet retreat for campers seeking solitude.

The campground operates seasonally from May through October, depending on road and weather conditions. Access is via Eyesee Road (Forest Road 15N01) heading south from Highway 96 in Orleans for about 17 miles, then turning onto Forest Road 12N22. The remote forest roads may require high-clearance vehicles, particularly early or late in the season.

As a primitive facility, Beans Camp provides basic vault toilet facilities but minimal other amenities. Campers should come prepared with their own water supply and all necessary camping gear. The campground is free to use and operates on a first-come, first-served basis.

location.directions: From Highway 96 in Orleans, head south on Eyesee Road (Forest Road 15N01) for approximately 17 miles, then turn onto Forest Road 12N22 to reach the campground.

links.title: Six Rivers NF Ukonom Ranger District

payload.name: Barlett Lane Day Use Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round for day use. The boat docks are removed before the reservoir ices over in winter. This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping. The group picnic shelter is reservable via reserve.wyoming.gov.
payload.short_description: Day-use area at Buffalo Bill State Park featuring a reservable group picnic shelter and boat ramp on Buffalo Bill Reservoir near Cody, Wyoming.
payload.medium_description: Bartlett Lane is a day-use facility at Buffalo Bill State Park, located on the shores of Buffalo Bill Reservoir near Cody, Wyoming. The area features a reservable group picnic shelter and a boat dock with ramp for water access. This is strictly a day-use site with no overnight camping available.
payload.long_description:
Bartlett Lane Day Use Area is part of Buffalo Bill State Park, situated along Buffalo Bill Reservoir in the scenic Absaroka Mountains near Cody, Wyoming. The facility offers a group picnic shelter that can be reserved up to four months in advance for $66 per day, making it suitable for family gatherings, group outings, and special events.

The area also features a boat dock and ramp providing access to Buffalo Bill Reservoir for boating, fishing, and water recreation. The reservoir is fed by the Shoshone River and offers excellent fishing opportunities. Note that this is a day-use only facility; no overnight camping is permitted at Bartlett Lane. Visitors seeking overnight accommodations should check the North Shore Bay or North Fork campgrounds within Buffalo Bill State Park.

location.directions: From Cody, Wyoming, head west on US-14/16/20 toward Yellowstone. The Bartlett Lane Day Use Area is located along the north shore of Buffalo Bill Reservoir within Buffalo Bill State Park.

links.title: Buffalo Bill State Park Activities & Amenities

payload.name: South Maxwell Snow Shelter
payload.status_description: The shelter is closed for overnight use until November 15. Overnight stays are permitted from November 15 through April 30 only, with a maximum capacity of 4 persons and 3-night stay limit. The shelter cannot be reserved and must be shared with other visitors.
payload.short_description: A backcountry snow shelter in Willamette National Forest accessible by skiing or snowshoeing from Maxwell Sno-Park, offering primitive overnight stays for up to 4 people during winter months.
payload.medium_description: South Maxwell Snow Shelter is a primitive backcountry warming shelter located in the Santiam winter recreation area of Willamette National Forest. Accessible only by skiing or snowshoeing from Maxwell Sno-Park via trail intersections #1 or #7, this rustic shelter features a wood stove, gravel floor, and no door. Overnight stays are permitted from November 15 through April 30 for up to 4 people with a maximum 3-night limit.
payload.long_description:
South Maxwell Snow Shelter is a primitive backcountry warming shelter situated in the Santiam winter recreation area of Willamette National Forest near Santiam Junction, Oregon. The shelter serves as a destination for cross-country skiers and snowshoers exploring the 25 miles of trails accessible from Maxwell Sno-Park, which sits at 3,800 feet elevation.

The shelter is accessed by skiing or snowshoeing from Maxwell Sno-Park through trail intersections #1 or #7. There is no vehicle access to the shelter itself. The structure features a wood stove for heating, a gravel floor, and notably has no door. Overnight capacity is limited to 4 persons maximum.

This is a true backcountry experience with no amenities. No drinking water or restrooms are available. Visitors must pack out all garbage and human waste following Leave No Trace principles. The shelter cannot be reserved and must be shared with other users. Candles are prohibited; visitors should bring their own lighting. Firewood may be used only in the wood stove. An Oregon Sno-Park permit is required for parking at Maxwell Sno-Park from November 1 through April 30.

location.directions: From Detroit, Oregon, travel east on Highway 22 for 29 miles to Maxwell Sno-Park on the left (3.5 miles west of Santiam Junction). From the parking lot, ski or snowshoe through trail intersections #1 or #7 to reach the shelter.

payload.name: Pickett State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is closed for renovations to the bathhouse and campground facilities. Closure began May 26, 2025 with reopening expected mid-2026. Boat dock and swimming area are also closed for accessibility improvements; personal canoes, kayaks, and paddle boards are permitted during closures.
payload.short_description: A 26-site campground in Tennessee's first certified Dark Sky Park, offering electric and water hookups amid sandstone formations on the Cumberland Plateau.
payload.medium_description: Pickett CCC Memorial State Park Campground features 26 sites nestled in a 922-acre park on the Cumberland Plateau. All sites have water hookups and picnic tables, with 16 offering electric. The park holds Dark Sky designation, making it exceptional for stargazing. Adjacent to Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area.
payload.long_description:
Pickett CCC Memorial State Park Campground sits within one of the most pristine natural areas in Tennessee. The 922-acre park on the Cumberland Plateau showcases unique sandstone formations including natural bridges, rock shelters, and dramatic bluffs. As the first certified Dark Sky Park in the Southeast, the campground offers exceptional stargazing opportunities with minimal light pollution.

The campground provides 26 sites, all equipped with water hookups and picnic tables with charcoal grills. Sixteen sites offer 30-amp electric service. A modern bathhouse includes flush toilets, hot water showers, and coin laundry. A dump station serves RV campers. The park is adjacent to the 20,887-acre Pickett State Forest and Big South Fork National River and Recreation Area, providing access to extensive hiking trails, swimming at Arch Lake, boating, and fishing.

location.directions: From I-40, take Exit 317 and travel north on Highway 127 for 46 miles. Turn right on Highway 154 and continue 12 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Pipestem Resort State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, weather permitting. Reservations are available online at wvstateparks.com, by phone at 1-833-WV-PARKS, or at the campground office. Weekend stays require a two-night minimum; maximum stay is 14 nights.
payload.short_description: Pipestem Resort State Park sits on the east rim of the Bluestone River Gorge, which carves through the plateau to the scenic Bluestone River 1,200 feet below. The 4,050-acre park is located on the border of Summers and Mercer counties and features two hotels, one of which lies at the bottom of the gorge and can only be accessed by an aerial tramway. In addition to canyon floor sites, Pipestem offers elevated views from the Bolar Lookout Tower overlook.
payload.medium_description: Situated atop the east rim of the Bluestone River Gorge in Summers County, Pipestem Resort State Park Campground provides 82 campsites ranging from full-hookup RV sites to primitive tent camping. The campground features heated bathhouses, coin laundry, a camp store, and playground. Open year-round weather permitting, the park spans 4,050 acres and offers access to ziplines, horseback riding, hiking trails, and an aerial tramway descending into the gorge.
payload.long_description:
Pipestem Resort State Park Campground occupies a scenic plateau along the eastern rim of the Bluestone River Gorge, where the 4,050-acre park straddles the Summers and Mercer county line.
