The campground accommodates everything from small pop-up tents to large RVs across its 82 sites: 31 with full hookups (electric, water, sewer), 19 with electric only, and the remainder primitive. Heated bathhouses provide year-round comfort, while coin-operated laundry facilities and a well-stocked camp store handle the essentials.

The park earned its name from the pipestem bush (Spiraea alba), whose hollow stems Native Americans once fashioned into pipe stems. Today the property serves as a full-service resort destination, featuring McKeever Lodge perched on the canyon rim, an aerial tramway descending 3,600 feet to Mountain Creek Lodge at the gorge floor, championship golf, horseback riding, zip line tours, and over 20 miles of trails. The Bluestone and New Rivers provide fishing and paddling opportunities nearby.

Quiet hours run 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., check-in is 1 p.m., and checkout is noon. A maximum stay of 14 consecutive nights applies. Weekend reservations require a two-night minimum (Friday-Saturday), while weeknight stays have a one-night minimum. Reservations can be made online at wvstateparks.com, by phone, or at the campground office.

location.directions: From I-64, take Exit 139 south onto Route 20. Follow Route 20 approximately 14 miles south through Hinton to Pipestem. The park entrance is on Route 20.

payload.name: Summersville Lake State Park Deer Run Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. The campground opened in May 2025. Reservations available through the WV State Parks online booking system. Check-in at 1 p.m., check-out at noon. Quiet hours from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
payload.short_description: Summersville Lake State Park in Nicholas County is West Virginia's newest state park. Encompassing 177 acres, it overlooks the north shore of the beautiful Summersville Lake, the largest in WV. The lake offers over 60 miles of shoreline, making it a boating and water sports paradise.  The park features hiking and biking trails, and day use picnic areas, with many more recreational activities to come.
payload.medium_description: Deer Run Campground is one of three campgrounds at Summersville Lake State Park, West Virginia's first new state park in over 30 years. The campground features nine premium RV sites nestled in lush woods, providing privacy and seclusion. Sites offer a mix of pull-through and back-in configurations with full hookups, ideal for campers seeking a quieter, more intimate experience while still having easy access to the 2,790-acre lake.
payload.long_description:
Deer Run Campground is a premium RV camping area within Summersville Lake State Park, located on the northern shore of West Virginia's largest lake in Nicholas County. The campground opened in May 2025 as part of a groundbreaking public-private partnership that created the state's first new state park in more than 30 years.

The campground offers nine wooded sites designed for RV campers looking for more privacy and seclusion than the larger Overlook Campground. A mix of pull-through and back-in sites accommodates different RV configurations, and all sites feature full hookups. The natural setting among the trees provides ample room to relax and enjoy the outdoors.

Summersville Lake itself spans 2,790 acres with 60 miles of shoreline, known for its exceptionally clear blue-green water and towering sandstone cliffs. Campers can enjoy swimming, boating, scuba diving, rock climbing, and hiking on trails including the Mountaineer Mile. The park operates 24/7, with reservations available through the West Virginia State Parks booking system.

location.directions: The park is located at 36 Park Rd., Summersville, WV 26651, on the northern shore of Summersville Lake in Nicholas County.

links.title: Camping at Summersville Lake State Park
Summersville Lake State Park Main Page

payload.name: Tickfaw State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Gates open 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Entrance station staffed 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Reservations required at least 48 hours in advance through the Louisiana State Parks reservation system. Maximum consecutive stay is 15 days.
payload.short_description: The park features a spacious Nature Center and a network of boardwalk trails into the wetlands adjacent to the Tickfaw River.
payload.medium_description: Tickfaw State Park Campground in Springfield, Louisiana provides overnight camping options ranging from full-hookup RV sites to primitive tent camping. The 1,199-acre park features extensive boardwalk trails through cypress swamps, a water playground, nature center with an 800-gallon aquarium, and canoe rentals. Premium sites include water, electric, and sewer hookups, while unimproved sites offer water only.
payload.long_description: The park features a spacious Nature Center and a network of boardwalk trails into the wetlands adjacent to the Tickfaw River. Visitors can canoe the river or utilize the trail system for nature photography and birdwatching opportunities. Overnight facilities include 14 cabins, a group camp, 30 improved campsites and 20 tent campsites. Picnic pavilions can be rented for day use. All visitors in the Park's Campground are required by LA Office of State Parks Rules & Regulation to inhabit all camping sites using a Conversion Van (recreational vehicle), Pickup Truck with a Camper top or tent conversion, Pop – up Camper or a Camper Trailer/RV, an enclosed tent or any combination of the stated equipment. "Car Camping" is allowed in combination with any of the the above unit descriptions. When planning an event such as family gatherings, employee picnic, school field trips, youth activities, weddings, birthday parties or your group has any special request please contact the park directly to obtain a "Facility Use Agreement" which is required for all events. A minimum of two weeks in advance is needed to process the Agreement and to allow the Park Staff ample time to have your area ready for your group. PLEASE NOTE: SUN - THUR THE ENTRANCE STATION IS OPEN FROM 8 AM UNTIL 5 PM. FRI - SAT THE ENTRANCE STATION IS OPEN FROM 8 AM UNTIL 8 PM.

location.directions: Located at 27225 Patterson Road, Springfield, Louisiana 70462. The park is in Livingston Parish approximately 45 miles east of Baton Rouge.

links.title: Louisiana State Parks Fees and Facilities

payload.name: Governor Dodge State Park Horse Campground
payload.status_description: The equestrian campground operates seasonally from May through November 15. Currently closed for the early season, with sites becoming available starting May 14, 2026. Reservations can be made through wisconsin.goingtocamp.com up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Equestrian campground at Governor Dodge State Park with 20 sites, 18 electric hookups, vault toilets, horse washing station, and direct access to 22 miles of equestrian trails including the Driftless Horse Trail.
payload.medium_description: Governor Dodge State Park's equestrian campground offers 20 campsites in the Hickory Ridge area, with 18 featuring electric hookups. Each site includes a high-line hitching post with cable, picnic table, and fire ring. Amenities include drinking water, vault toilets, a horse washing station, manure bunkers, and access to showers at the nearby Hickory Ridge group camp. The campground provides direct access to 22 miles of equestrian trails, including the interior horse trail system and the 15-mile Driftless Horse Trail.
payload.long_description:
Located in the scenic Driftless Area of southwestern Wisconsin, Governor Dodge State Park's equestrian campground sits within the Hickory Ridge area and caters specifically to horse campers. The 20-site campground features 18 sites with electric hookups, each equipped with a high-line hitching post and cable for safely securing horses overnight.

Facilities include vault toilets, potable drinking water, a horse washing station for cleaning up after rides, and manure bunkers for proper waste disposal. Campers can access shower facilities at the adjacent Hickory Ridge group camp area. Site 765E is designated accessible for persons with disabilities.

The campground serves as a base for exploring 22 miles of equestrian trails within the park, including the interior horse trail network and the 15-mile Driftless Horse Trail. The surrounding landscape features rugged terrain with sandstone bluffs, deep valleys, and two lakes within the 5,270-acre park.

location.directions: The park is located off Highway 23, approximately 3 miles north of Dodgeville, Wisconsin. The equestrian campground is in the Hickory Ridge area of the park.

links.title: Governor Dodge State Park - Wisconsin DNR

payload.name: East Fork State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with full services available seasonally. Two campground loops remain operational during winter months with limited services. Reservations available up to six months in advance through ReserveOhio. Over 30 sites are first-come, first-served only.
payload.short_description: Large 416-site campground in one of Ohio's biggest state parks, offering electric and full hookup sites with modern amenities on Harsha Lake, 25 miles from Cincinnati.
payload.medium_description: East Fork State Park Campground is one of Ohio's largest camping areas with 416 sites on the north shore of Harsha Lake. The campground offers a mix of electric-only and full hookup sites with modern facilities including flush toilets, hot showers, drinking water, and a dump station. Each site features a paved pad, picnic table, and fire ring. A camper's beach, multiple boat ramps, and access to 82 miles of hiking trails make this a prime destination for outdoor enthusiasts.
payload.long_description:
East Fork State Park Campground sits within one of Ohio's largest state parks, encompassing 4,870 acres of land surrounding the 2,160-acre Harsha Lake just 25 miles from Cincinnati. The campground features 416 sites spread across multiple loops, primarily offering electric hookups with 20, 30, and 50 amp service, while select sites provide full hookups including water and sewer connections. Loop A accommodates equestrian campers with horse-friendly electric sites. Modern amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, drinking water throughout, and a dump station.

Each campsite has a paved pad, picnic table, and fire ring. A camper's beach provides direct lake access for swimming, and six boat ramps serve boaters on the unlimited-horsepower lake. The park offers exceptional recreational opportunities including 82 miles of hiking trails (including the 37-mile Steven Newman Worldwalker Perimeter Trail), 55 miles of bridle trails, fishing for largemouth bass, bluegill, crappie, catfish, and hybrid striped bass, plus mini golf, tennis, and volleyball courts.

Rent-A-Camp units and Rent-A-RV units are available seasonally for those without their own equipment. Over 30 sites remain first-come, first-served for spontaneous trips. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance through ReserveOhio.

location.directions: From Cincinnati, take I-275 to State Route 125 East. Continue approximately 8 miles to the park entrance on the right. The campground is located at 3294 Elklick Road, Bethel, OH 45106.

payload.name: Angostura Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From October 1 through April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Check-in and check-out time is 4 p.m. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Angostura Reservoir in the Angostura Recreation Area is a water-lover's haven with breathtaking scenic views.
payload.medium_description: Angostura Recreation Area sits on a 4,400-acre reservoir 10 miles southeast of Hot Springs. The park features four campgrounds with 171 sites and 14 camping cabins, many with electric hookups. Facilities include flush toilets and showers (seasonal), vault toilets year-round, a dump station, fish cleaning stations, playground, marina, and visitor center. The reservoir is popular for swimming, boating, and fishing.
payload.long_description: Angostura Reservoir in the Angostura Recreation Area is a water-lover's haven with breathtaking scenic views. Offering crystal clear waters, 36 miles of shoreline, and some of the finest sandy beaches in the state, the area boasts many water sports and summer fun activities - camping, boating, fishing, and swimming. Each campsite at Angostura Recreation Area has a gravel or paved camping pad, a fire grate and picnic table, and flush toilets and showers are installed. Electric hookups are available at the majority of the campsites. One-room, log-style cabins are found in all four Angostura campgrounds and overlook the reservoir. Each cabin has heating, air conditioning, electricity and a porch. Furnishings include a bunk bed, a double bed, table and benches. Look for walleye, smallmouth bass, crappie, northern pike, largemouth bass, perch and bluegill in Angostura, one of the few large reservoirs in western South Dakota. To help you manage your catch, there is a fishing dock, boat ramp, fish cleaning station and fishing pole checkout. Rent a canoe or kayak to glide along the lake and take in the sights. Among the other amenities at Angostura Recreations Area are a marina, picnic shelter, playground and visitor center. Angostura Recreation Area hosts an array of interpretive and educational activities during the summer season. Each program is geared for families with young children and will expose participants to the various natural and cultural features of the Southern Black Hills. A geocache scavenger hunt takes place every year. The hunt begins on April 1 and ends on October 31. Participants who successfully answer the treasure hunt questions are entered into a drawing for a variety of prizes.

location.directions: From Hot Springs, South Dakota, travel 10 miles southeast on US Highways 385/18. Turn south onto North Angostura Road and follow signs to the recreation area.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Spinning Wheel Campground
payload.status_description: The campground generally operates from late spring through early fall, weather permitting. Similar campgrounds in the Highway 120 corridor typically open in May and close in September. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own water supply. Payment is cash or check only.
payload.short_description: A primitive USFS campground in Stanislaus National Forest near Cherry Lake and Yosemite National Park, offering vault toilets but no drinking water.
payload.medium_description: Spinning Wheel Campground is a small, primitive camping area in the Stanislaus National Forest along the Highway 120 corridor near Cherry Lake. The campground offers basic amenities including vault toilets and established campsites, but campers must bring their own drinking water. Located in close proximity to Yosemite National Park, it provides a quieter alternative to more developed campgrounds in the area.
payload.long_description:
Spinning Wheel Campground is a primitive camping area situated in the Stanislaus National Forest, managed by the Groveland Ranger District. The campground is located near Cherry Lake, the largest lake in the forest, and provides convenient access to Yosemite National Park's Big Oak Flat entrance along Highway 120.

The campground offers basic facilities typical of national forest camping areas, including vault toilets. However, there is no potable water available on site, so campers must bring an adequate supply of drinking water. Sites are available for $25 per night and payment is by cash or check only.

The surrounding area offers opportunities for fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing. Cherry Lake is approximately 1.5 miles northeast and provides fishing for brook trout, brown trout, kokanee salmon, and rainbow trout. The mixed conifer forest setting at approximately 3,000 feet elevation offers relief from summer valley heat while maintaining reasonable accessibility.

location.directions: From Highway 120, head east towards Sweetwater Campground via Forest Road 1S15Y.

payload.name: URDAHL CAMPGROUND
payload.status_description: The campground is closed for the winter season. USFS campgrounds in this area typically open in late spring or early summer depending on snow conditions and road access.
payload.short_description: A small, developed Forest Service campground in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest near Wells in northeastern Nevada.
payload.medium_description: Urdahl Campground is a Forest Service campground located in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest in Elko County, northeastern Nevada. The campground sits in the mountainous terrain near Wells.
payload.long_description:
Urdahl Campground is a developed Forest Service campground located within the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest in Elko County, northeastern Nevada. The campground is situated in the mountainous regions near the town of Wells, providing access to the surrounding national forest lands. As a USFS campground in this region, it typically serves as a base for outdoor recreation including hiking, wildlife viewing, and exploring the remote areas of northeastern Nevada. The campground is part of the vast Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, the largest national forest in the lower 48 states.

Like many Forest Service campgrounds in this elevation range of northeastern Nevada, the site likely offers basic amenities typical of established USFS facilities. The campground provides access to the natural beauty and solitude of the East Humboldt region, making it suitable for campers seeking a quieter, more rustic experience in the national forest.

location.directions: Approximately 4 miles south of the town of Jarbidge, Nevada.

payload.name: Buryanek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Buryanek Recreation Area is popular with boaters and anglers, as well those looking for scenic beauty along the Missouri River.
payload.medium_description: Buryanek Recreation Area is a scenic campground along the Missouri River and Lake Francis Case in Gregory County, South Dakota. Popular with boaters and anglers, it offers 44 campsites including electrical options, 3 camping cabins, modern amenities like flush toilets and showers (seasonal), and year-round vault toilet access. The park features boat ramps, a fish cleaning station, and playground facilities.
payload.long_description: Buryanek Recreation Area is popular with boaters and anglers, as well those looking for scenic beauty along the Missouri River. History buffs will enjoy knowing that the Lewis and Clark expedition traveled through the area, where they were told to watch for "burning bluffs" along the river. Modern-day travelers can book campsites and cabins online using the handy online system. The system is fast, easy-to-use and available 24 hours a day. Both the park and the cabins are open year-round to take advantage of the changing seasons. The three cozy cabins have contemporary touches, like heating, air conditioning and electricity. A family can sleep comfortably with 2 twin beds and 1 full size bed, then dine outdoors using the fire grate and picnic table. Make sure to pack cooking utensils, sleeping bags and linens and a container for water. Amenities of Buryanek Recreation Area include a boat ramp, beach, dump station, fish cleaning station, playground and picnic shelter. Bring your fishing gear to lure walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, sauger, pan fish and channel catfish. The Lewis and Clark expedition has forever left its mark on this area with the story of Private George Shannon. Shannon, the youngest member of the expedition at 19 years old, became lost when he was sent to fetch strayed horses. Thinking the crew had moved up river, Shannon raced to meet the boats. When he was found exhausted and starving two weeks later, he quickly learned that the expedition had been downstream from him the entire time.

location.directions: Located at 27450 Buryanek Road, Burke, SD 57523. The recreation area is situated along the Missouri River in Gregory County.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Big Sioux State Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are typically closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Big Sioux Recreation Area lies on the banks of South Dakota's Big Sioux River.
payload.medium_description: Big Sioux Recreation Area sits on the banks of South Dakota's Big Sioux River near Brandon and Sioux Falls. The park offers 49 campsites ranging from electrical to non-electrical tent sites, plus three camping cabins. Amenities include showers, flush toilets, a dump station, potable water, and paved accessible trails. Popular activities include canoeing, hiking, disc golf, and archery.
payload.long_description: Big Sioux Recreation Area lies on the banks of South Dakota's Big Sioux River. Close to the cities of Brandon and Sioux Falls, and is popular among campers, canoers, bicyclists, hikers, disc golfers, history buffs and archers. When the snow flies, groups of snowmobilers gather at the enclosed warming house. Campsites are open from May to October and log cabins can be booked year-round. Big Sioux Recreation Area features an archery range and course, an 18-hole disc golf course, a paved bike trail and a dog training area. Among the events at the park are the annual Big Sioux Bustle GPS/Geocaching Race, where teams race to find hidden caches, Spooktacular Trails at Halloween time and the Dutch Oven Gathering potluck. Comfy cabins come with a set of bunk beds, a double bed, table and benches. Outside, you'll find a fire grate, picnic table and delightful scenery. Be sure to bring utensils for outdoor cooking, sleeping bags and bed linens, a cooler for food storage and container for water. RV sites are back-in and there are also tent-only sites. Amenities to make your stay more enjoyable include a playground, picnic shelter, flush toilets and showers. Fishing poles, games and snowshoes can be checked out for use at the park. Comfy cabins come with a set of bunk beds, a double bed, table and benches. Outside, you'll find a fire grate, picnic table and delightful scenery. Be sure to bring utensils for outdoor cooking, sleeping bags and bed linens, a cooler for food storage and container for water. RV sites are back-in and there are also tent-only sites. Amenities to make your stay more enjoyable include a playground, picnic shelter, flush toilets and showers. Fishing poles, games and snowshoes can be checked out for use at the park.

location.directions: Located at 410 West Park Street in Brandon, SD, approximately 10 miles east of Sioux Falls via I-90 and SD-11.

payload.name: Chief White Crane Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Vehicle traffic is prohibited from November 15 through the last Friday in March during bald eagle nesting season. Water systems may close between October 1 and April 30. Reservations can be made online or by phone up to 90 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Chief White Crane Recreation Area is near the Missouri River and Gavins Point Dam and is a great place to take advantage of a wide variety of recreation opportunities.
payload.medium_description: Chief White Crane Recreation Area is a popular South Dakota state park situated along Lewis & Clark Lake near Yankton. The campground offers 146 campsites including 144 electric sites with 50 amp service and 2 non-electric tent sites, plus 10 heated and air-conditioned camping cabins. Full amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. The park is renowned for winter bald eagle viewing, with vehicle access restricted from November 15 through March to protect nesting eagles.
payload.long_description: Chief White Crane Recreation Area is near the Missouri River and Gavins Point Dam and is a great place to take advantage of a wide variety of recreation opportunities. The area is popular for fishing, kayaking, and canoeing on Lake Yankton and the Missouri River. The park was named after Chief White Crane who met with Lewis and Clark in this area in 1804. Campers may choose from 146 50-amp electric campsites, 2 tent campsites or 10 one-room log-style cabins. Cabins have accommodation for four people, including air conditioning/heat and electricity. Park amenities include picnic shelter, playground, hiking and biking trails, and a fishing dock with easy access to Lake Yankton. Many eagles spend their winters below Gavins Point Dam along the Missouri River where they can catch fish and prey on waterfowl in the open water. The campground is closed during the winter months when the majestic bald eagle is known to roost in the large cottonwood trees throughout the park.

location.directions: Located 4 miles west of Yankton off SD Highway 52, then 2 miles south on Toe Road. Address: 31323 Toe Road, Yankton, SD 57078.

South Dakota State Parks Camping Regulations

payload.name: Cow Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets typically remain available.
payload.short_description: Water-lovers enjoy fishing, boating, or just watching the waves at Cow Creek Recreation Area.
payload.medium_description: Cow Creek Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Oahe, a massive Missouri River reservoir 15 miles northwest of Pierre, South Dakota. The campground offers 46 developed sites (both electric and non-electric), four ADA-accessible camping cabins, and primitive shoreline camping with outstanding reservoir views. Facilities include drinking water, flush toilets, showers, vault toilets, a dump station, boat ramps, and fish cleaning stations.
payload.long_description: Water-lovers enjoy fishing, boating, or just watching the waves at Cow Creek Recreation Area. Both primitive shoreline camping and campground camping are available. The shoreline sites offer outstanding views of Oahe Reservoir while providing a great deal of privacy. Campsites in the campground have easy access to drinking water and restrooms/showers and can be booked in advance. Four camping cabins are also available. Camping cabins at Cow Creek Recreation Area accommodate four people in the one-room space with a set of bunk beds, double bed, table and benches. Heating, air conditioning and electricity provide for year-round comfort. Cabins do not have restrooms, running water or kitchens. A porch, picnic table and fire grate allow for pleasant outdoor dining while enjoying the scenic surroundings. Park amenities include a boat ramp and picnic shelter. Anglers landing walleye, sauger, northern pike, channel catfish, trout and bass can prepare their catch in the fish-cleaning station. Lake Oahe Reservoir, located on the Missouri River, provides hours of outdoor fun. The lake has more than 2,000 miles of shoreline and its clear waters are ideal for boating, sailing, fishing, water skiing and diving. Campers, history buffs, mountain bikers and hikers will find new adventures in this rugged land first explored by Lewis and Clark.

location.directions: 15 miles northwest of Pierre off SD Highway 1804.

links.title: SD Game, Fish & Parks - Cow Creek

payload.name: Clay County Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally. Potable water is available May through September. Reservations can be made via campsd.com.
payload.short_description: Quiet, secluded campground with tall trees along the Missouri River, 4 miles southwest of Vermillion, South Dakota, offering electric sites, showers, and river access.
payload.medium_description: Clay County Park is a peaceful riverside campground tucked among tall trees along one of the last natural stretches of the Missouri River. The park offers 32 electrical campsites with modern amenities including restrooms with showers, a dump station, and playground. A boat ramp provides access to the Missouri National Recreational River, and three miles of paved nature trails wind through the grounds.
payload.long_description:
Clay County Park sits 4 miles southwest of Vermillion, South Dakota, on a quiet, wooded stretch of the Missouri River. Managed by the Clay County Park Board in cooperation with South Dakota Game, Fish, and Parks, the campground offers a secluded retreat with tall shade trees and direct access to one of the last free-flowing sections of the Missouri.

The park features 32 electrical campsites plus designated tent sites, with facilities including flush restrooms and showers, a dump station, playground, and volleyball and horseshoe courts. Three miles of paved nature trails loop through the property, connecting campers to the river and surrounding forest. The boat ramp at Clay County River Access provides paddlers and anglers a launch point at River Mile 781.

This campground serves as a comfortable base for exploring the Missouri National Recreational River. The natural setting appeals to campers seeking a quiet experience with modern conveniences, while the river access draws boaters and kayakers heading onto the water.

location.directions: From Vermillion: Take SD Highway 50 west, turn south onto Highway 19, then right onto Timber Road for 1.7 miles, then left onto 460th Ave for 1.4 miles to reach the park.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Custer State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The park is open year-round. Most campgrounds operate from Open House Weekend in late April through September or October, with Game Lodge offering limited winter camping. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems close at most campgrounds, though vault toilets remain available. Reservations are accepted one year in advance online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: The clear mountain waters are inviting, and the open ranges are waiting to be discovered at Custer State Park in the Black Hills.
payload.medium_description: Custer State Park in South Dakota's Black Hills provides nine distinct campgrounds totaling over 300 campsites plus camping cabins. Options range from primitive tent-only sites at Center Lake to full-hookup RV sites at Blue Bell and Game Lodge. The park is renowned for its wildlife loop road where bison, pronghorn, and burros roam freely. Campgrounds feature flush toilets, showers, dump stations, and drinking water during the primary season, with vault toilets available year-round at most locations.
payload.long_description: The clear mountain waters are inviting, and the open ranges are waiting to be discovered at Custer State Park in the Black Hills. The park encompasses 71,000 acres of spectacular terrain and an abundance of wildlife. A herd of 1,300 bison roam freely throughout the park, one of the largest publically owned herds in the world. Custer State Park campgrounds offer a variety of scenic sites. Set up camp along a flowing stream, in the midst of pine forest, or near a mountain lake. Each campsite at Custer State Park has a gravel or paved camping pad, a fire grate and picnic table. Electric hookups are available in most campgrounds. One-room, log-style cabins are equipped with heating, air conditioning, electricity and a porch. Furnishings include a bunk bed, a double bed, table and benches. During the summer season, trout fishing is perhaps one of the most popular recreational activities in Custer State Park. The park offers four mountainous lakes worth exploring in this regard. Center Lake, Legion Lake, Stockade Lake and Sylvan Lake comprise about 182 acres of crystal blue water and offer habitat for several species of fish. Whether hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, or rock climbing, find your adventure along the roads and trails. Custer State Park's early pioneers, ranchers and loggers have left behind miles of trails and backcountry roads to explore. In addition to the magnificent buffalo, other animals like pronghorn, prairie dogs, elk, deer, bighorn sheep, mountain goats, mountain lions and burros are found in the park. Feeding and disturbing park wildlife is against park regulations. While the animals within the park are used to visitors and vehicles, they are still wild animals. Please remain in your vehicle or stay at least 100 yards from bison, elk, and other animals.

location.directions: Located in the southern Black Hills of South Dakota. From Rapid City, take US-16 south approximately 35 miles to the park. From Custer, head east on US-16A. GPS can be unreliable in the Black Hills; consult a map or call the park office at 605-394-2693 for directions. Large RVs should avoid Needles Highway due to narrow tunnels.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Fisher Grove State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: The first crossing for the Watertown-to-Pierre stage line crossed the river here on American Indians' traditional rock river crossing.
payload.medium_description: Fisher Grove State Park Campground offers 22 electrical campsites nestled among cottonwood trees along the James River in Spink County. The campground provides modern amenities including flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station during the main season. Vault toilets remain accessible year-round. The park features shore fishing access, picnic shelters, playgrounds, and opportunities for canoeing and kayaking on the James River.
payload.long_description: The first crossing for the Watertown-to-Pierre stage line crossed the river here on American Indians' traditional rock river crossing. Belchers Ford, as the site was called, had a hotel for tourists. The park is named after Frank I. Fisher, the first permanent European settler in Spink County who lived at this site. Fisher Grove is managed and maintained by the Fisher Grove Country Club. The country club also manages the ten-hole golf course adjacent to the park. For information, please call 605.472.1336.

location.directions: Located at 17290 Fishers Lane, Frankfort, SD 57440.

links.title: Fisher Grove State Park - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Red Hills Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed and decommissioned. This campground is no longer operational and has been removed from the Bridger-Teton National Forest campground inventory.
payload.short_description: Red Hills Campground in Bridger-Teton National Forest near Kelly, Wyoming has been permanently closed and decommissioned.
payload.medium_description: Red Hills Campground was a small, quiet campground located along the Gros Ventre River in Bridger-Teton National Forest, approximately 12 miles from Kelly, Wyoming. The campground has been permanently closed and decommissioned by the Forest Service and is no longer available for camping.
payload.long_description:
Red Hills Campground was situated in the scenic Gros Ventre River corridor of Bridger-Teton National Forest, near Kelly, Wyoming. The area is characterized by its distinctive reddish-colored hills and proximity to Grand Teton National Park and the National Elk Refuge.

The campground has been permanently closed and decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service. It is no longer listed in the forest's campground inventory and is not available for overnight camping. Visitors seeking camping in the Gros Ventre area should consider Crystal Creek Campground or other developed sites along the Gros Ventre River corridor that remain open and operational.

location.directions: Red Hills Campground is located within Glendo State Park, Wyoming. From I-25, take exit 111 (Glendo), then follow Glendo Park Road and park signage to the Red Hills Campground. It is situated on hilly terrain sloping toward the reservoir, approximately 1 hour 20 minutes east of Casper.

payload.name: Grandview Playground Shelter
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter only. No overnight camping is permitted. Reservations for the shelter are available through Recreation.gov. Weddings and receptions require a Special Use Permit by calling 304-465-6517.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter at Grandview in New River Gorge National Park, accommodating up to 200 guests with covered seating, grills, and electrical outlets.
payload.medium_description: The Grandview Playground Shelter is a large day-use picnic pavilion in New River Gorge National Park, located near the main playground and ball fields. It can host up to 200 people and features a covered eating area with picnic tables, three charcoal grills, and six electrical outlets. Nearby restrooms and a drinking fountain are available. This is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping permitted.
payload.long_description:
The Grandview Playground Shelter is the main picnic pavilion at Grandview, one of the most popular day-use areas in New River Gorge National Park. Located just past the amphitheater and closest to the main playground and ball fields, this covered shelter can accommodate up to 200 people, making it ideal for large family reunions, company picnics, and group events.

The shelter provides a covered eating area with picnic tables, three charcoal grills for cooking, and six electrical outlets. Restrooms and a drinking fountain are located nearby. The surrounding Grandview area offers five hiking trails, scenic overlooks at 1,400 feet above the New River, a seasonal visitor center (open June through August), playgrounds, a volleyball court, baseball field, and basketball court. Theatre West Virginia presents summer outdoor dramas in the area.

This is strictly a day-use facility. No overnight camping is permitted at the shelter. Weddings and wedding receptions require a Special Use Permit. Prohibited items include glitter, confetti, silly string, helium and water balloons, fireworks, loud audio devices, and mechanical rides.

location.directions: From Beckley, follow I-64 East five miles to Exit 129B. From Lewisburg, follow I-64 West forty miles to Exit 129. From either exit, turn right and follow Route 9 North six miles to Grandview.

payload.name: Equestrian Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No potable water or trash services. Campers must pack out all trash and bring their own water.
payload.short_description: A small equestrian-focused campground with six sites featuring individual corrals and a central holding pen, located along the San Rafael River in Utah's Buckhorn Draw.
payload.medium_description: Built by equestrians for equestrians, this six-site campground sits along the San Rafael River at the southern end of Buckhorn Draw. Each site includes pullouts for vehicles and horse trailers, individual corrals, tent pads, picnic tables, fire rings, and vault toilets. A central holding pen with three separate stalls serves all campers. No potable water or trash services are available.
payload.long_description:
The Equestrian Campground offers a purpose-built facility for horse campers in the heart of Utah's San Rafael Swell Recreation Area. Situated just downstream from the San Rafael Swinging Bridge Campground along the scenic San Rafael River, the campground provides six sites specifically designed to accommodate equestrians with their trailers and horses.

Each campsite features a pullout large enough for a vehicle and horse trailer, an individual corral, tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and access to vault toilets. A central holding pen with three separate stalls offers additional horse containment options. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis at $15 per night.

Campers should come prepared as there is no potable water and no trash service. All trash must be packed out. Cell phone reception is limited depending on carrier. Nearby recreation includes hiking, horseback riding along the river corridor, and exploring the dramatic canyon country of Buckhorn Draw and the Little Grand Canyon overlook.

location.directions: Located along the San Rafael River at the southern end of Buckhorn Draw, approximately 15 miles from the nearest paved road. Contact the BLM Price Field Office for detailed driving directions.

address.street1: N Lawrence / Tan Seeps (cottonwood Wash Rd
address.full: 3395 N Lawrence / Tan Seeps (cottonwood Wash Rd, Castle Dale, UT 84513

BLM San Rafael Swell Recreation Area

payload.name: Spillway Campground
payload.status_description: Open first-come, first-served. The primary season runs Memorial Day through Labor Day with water and trash services available. Off-season camping is permitted at a reduced rate, but campers must bring water and pack out trash. Access to the Letts Lake basin may be impacted by M10 Road construction.
payload.short_description: Quiet 9-site loop at Letts Lake in Mendocino National Forest offering lakeside camping with fishing, swimming, and a mile-long accessible trail around the 35-acre lake.
payload.medium_description: Spillway Campground is one of four loops at Letts Lake, featuring sites 34-42 nestled among conifers near a 35-acre mountain lake. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table. The lake offers trout fishing, swimming, and non-motorized boating, with an accessible fishing pier and a one-mile lakeside trail. Vault toilets and potable water are available during the summer season.
payload.long_description:
Spillway Campground sits at the southern end of Letts Lake within Mendocino National Forest, about 19 miles west of Stonyford. This intimate 9-site loop (sites 34-42) is part of the larger Letts Lake recreation area, which encompasses 42 total sites across four distinct loops. The campground occupies a forested setting near the shores of a scenic 35-acre mountain lake.

The lake is the primary attraction, supporting non-motorized boating, swimming, and trout fishing. A fully accessible fishing pier makes angling easy for visitors of all abilities. A one-mile trail circles the lakeshore, offering gentle hiking with lake views. Each campsite is equipped with a fire ring and picnic table, and the area is served by accessible vault toilets.

Potable water and trash service are available only during the primary season from Memorial Day through Labor Day. During shoulder seasons the campground remains accessible at a reduced fee, but campers must bring their own water and pack out trash. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no advance reservations. Payment is made on-site via QR code through the Recreation.gov app.

location.directions: Located 19 miles west of Stonyford via M10 Road. Access roads are suitable for vehicles with camping trailers up to 30 feet.

payload.name: Canyonlands National Park Needles District Group Campsites
payload.status_description: Open for the peak season March 15 through November 15. Reservations available up to six months in advance via Recreation.gov. Sites are best suited for tents and small RVs under 25 feet. There are no hookups or dump stations in the Needles District.
payload.short_description: Remote group campsites in Canyonlands Needles District offering tent camping amid red rock desert and pinyon-juniper forest for groups of 11-50 people.
payload.medium_description: The Needles District Group Campsites offer three reservable sites for groups of 11 or more in the remote southeast corner of Canyonlands National Park. Dutch Oven sits within the main campground with flush toilets, while Wooden Shoe and Split Top are isolated sites with vault toilets. All sites have potable water, fire rings, and access to the Needles' extensive trail system through colorful Cedar Mesa Sandstone formations.
payload.long_description:
Located in the Needles District of Canyonlands National Park at approximately 4,900 feet elevation, these group campsites provide a base for exploring one of Utah's most spectacular desert landscapes. The area is named for the colorful spires of Cedar Mesa Sandstone that dominate the region, with stands of Utah juniper and pinyon pine providing shade among the slickrock and sand.

Three group sites are available: Dutch Oven accommodates 11-50 people and is located within Loop A of the main campground with flush toilets, potable water, fire rings, picnic tables, and a paved pull-through driveway. Wooden Shoe handles 11-25 campers and Split Top accommodates 11-15; both are isolated from the main campground and feature vault toilets, water spigots, and fire rings.

The Needles District's extensive trail system provides day hikes and backpacking opportunities to Confluence Overlook, Druid Arch, the Joint Trail, and Chesler Park. Four-wheel-drive roads and mountain biking routes add to the recreation options. The area is 1.5 hours from Moab and 1.25 hours from Monticello via Highway 211.

location.directions: From US Highway 191, drive 40 miles south of Moab or 14 miles north of Monticello, then take Utah Highway 211 west approximately 35 miles to the Needles entrance. Dutch Oven is in Loop A of the main campground. Wooden Shoe is 1.8 miles from the entrance station on the second left. Split Top is 1 mile from the entrance on the first left toward Salt Creek/Cave Springs, then left on the dirt access road.

payload.name: Amsden Dam Lakeside Use Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Vault toilets remain open all year. No potable water is available. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Amsden Lake Lakeside Use Area is a 150 area that is located 14 miles to the southwest of Groton, South Dakota.
payload.medium_description: Amsden Lakeside Use Area is a small, primitive-style park managed by South Dakota Game, Fish, and Parks. Located on 235-acre Amsden Lake, the area offers 12 non-electrical campsites with vault toilets, a boat ramp, swim beach, and shore fishing access. The lake reaches depths of 27 feet due to an old gravel pit below the surface, making it a popular muskie fishing destination where the state record 40-pound Muskellunge was caught in 1991.
payload.long_description: Amsden Lake Lakeside Use Area is a 150 area that is located 14 miles to the southwest of Groton, South Dakota. The area is nestled beside Amsden Lake. The area has a campground that has 11 primitive campsites, a boat dock, beach two vault toilets and areas to shore fish.

location.directions: From Groton, go 6 miles East on US-12, then South on 412th Ave for 5 miles. Turn East on 423rd Ave for 1 mile, then North on 413th Ave.

payload.name: Isabella Point Camp
payload.status_description: Seasonal access depending on snow and road conditions on FS Road 700. No fee and no reservations required. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Primitive two-site trailhead camp providing access to the Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area via Trail 95 in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests.
payload.medium_description: Isabella Point Camp is a small, no-fee primitive campground with two units located at the Isabella Point Trailhead. The site serves as the gateway to Trail 95, which connects to Trail 399 and leads hikers and stock users into the spectacular Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area. No potable water is available; campers must pack in all water and supplies.
payload.long_description:
Isabella Point Camp sits at the Isabella Point Trailhead along Forest Service Road 700 in the North Fork of the Clearwater Corridor. This primitive, no-fee campground offers two dispersed camping units and provides direct access to Trail 95, which connects to Trail 399 leading into the Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area.

The Mallard Larkins Pioneer Area features numerous high mountain lakes, streams, and steep-walled valleys, with elevations ranging from 2,400 feet to 6,870 feet at Mallard Peak. The area offers excellent opportunities for day hiking, backpacking, and horseback riding. Campers should come fully prepared as no potable water or confirmed restroom facilities are available at this trailhead camp.

location.directions: Access via Forest Service Road 700 in the North Fork of the Clearwater Corridor. Road 247 from Headquarters or Road 250 from its junction with State Highway 11 south of Pierce provide the main access routes to reach the FS Road 700 area.

payload.name: Farm Island Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Full services including showers and flush toilets available May through September. Limited services from October 1 through April 30, with vault toilets remaining open.
payload.short_description: Located east of Pierre, Farm Island Recreation Area attracts all types of visitors - campers, swimmers, hikers, anglers, bird watchers and bicyclists.
payload.medium_description: Farm Island Recreation Area is a popular destination near Pierre, situated on Lake Sharpe along the Missouri River. The park offers 90 electrical campsites across two campgrounds plus four camping cabins. Visitors enjoy swimming beaches, hiking and biking trails, fishing access, and excellent bird watching opportunities. The park operates year-round with full services from May through September and limited services during winter months.
payload.long_description: Located east of Pierre, Farm Island Recreation Area attracts all types of visitors - campers, swimmers, hikers, anglers, bird watchers and bicyclists. With easy access to Lake Sharpe and popular beaches and trails, this park stays busy throughout the year. Additionally, the park has ties to the Lewis and Clark expedition, which is detailed in the Lewis and Clark Family Center. Two campgrounds contain a total of 90 sites and feature showers and electric hookups. Camping cabins, outfitted with beds, heating, air conditioning and electricity, are open year-round. Farm Island features an island nature area, which provides an outdoor classroom for visitors. Eight miles of hiking trails wind through the island and give hikers, walkers, cross-country skiers and bicyclists a chance for peace, quiet and nature observation. Deer and a variety of birds are very common to see on the island. Trail users may also notice traces of beaver activity near the water. Visitors also have access to a nature observation blind. The Farm Island Visitor Center stands in the center of the original Fort Sully and provides exhibits that help visitors learn more about the fort. No buildings remain, since it was abandoned and dismantled to use as steamboat fuel.

location.directions: From Pierre, head east on SD Highway 34 for 4 miles. The park entrance is on the left at 1301 Farm Island Road.

links.title: Farm Island Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: SIXTEENER
payload.status_description: No official USFS or Recreation.gov information exists for a campground named Sixteener in Pike National Forest. The site may be an informal dispersed camping area, a locally-named site, or may no longer exist. Current status cannot be verified.
payload.short_description: A campground in Pike National Forest located in Park County, Colorado.
payload.medium_description: Sixteener Campground is situated in Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado. The campground is located in a mountainous area of the central Colorado Rockies.
payload.long_description:
Sixteener Campground is located within Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado. Pike National Forest encompasses parts of the Front Range and contains numerous fourteeners, alpine lakes, and wilderness areas. The forest provides diverse recreation opportunities including camping, hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing.

The campground's location in Park County places it in a mountainous region of central Colorado. Pike National Forest campgrounds typically operate seasonally due to snow and cold temperatures at elevation, with most facilities closing in fall and reopening in late spring or early summer.

location.directions: Sixteener Road is accessible from Lake George, Colorado. From Lake George, head north on County Road 77 (Tarryall Road) for approximately 10 miles. Turn right onto Forest Service Road 211 (also known as Sixteener Road) and continue for about 2 miles to reach the campground area.

payload.name: Fort Sisseton State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations accepted online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com.
payload.short_description: Named after the nearby Sisseton Indian Tribe, this historic fort is now a picturesque state park that unfolds the area's past.
payload.medium_description: Fort Sisseton Historic State Park preserves one of the best-maintained frontier military posts in the United States, offering camping adjacent to restored 1864-era buildings. The campground features 14 sites with electrical and non-electrical options, plus three rustic cabins. Facilities include drinking water, flush toilets, showers, and picnic tables. The park hosts an annual Historical Festival each June and offers hiking trails through prairie landscapes.
payload.long_description: Named after the nearby Sisseton Indian Tribe, this historic fort is now a picturesque state park that unfolds the area's past. Walk the grounds where the officers' quarters, stone barracks, powder magazine, guard house, and other buildings that remain from the time of the western frontier. This 1864 fort, atop the Coteau des Prairies (or hills of the prairies), was originally a frontier army outpost called Fort Wadsworth. The site was chosen because it provided a strong natural defense, an ample supply of lime and clay for making bricks, an abundance of lake water for drinking and a thick stand of trees for timber and fuel. Visitor Center with interpretive displays and gift shop is open daily from Open House Weekend through September. Guided tours are available, please call ahead. Join the festivities for entertainment, culture and history during the annual Fort Sisseton Historical Festival. The festival features period entertainment and activities and attracts thousands of visitors each year.

location.directions: Located at 11907 434th Avenue, Lake City, SD 57247, in Marshall County in northeastern South Dakota.

links.title: Fort Sisseton Historic State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Llewellyn Johns Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems close October 1 through April 30; vault toilets remain available. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: A small, get-away park, Llewellyn Johns' 10 campsites offer a quiet camping experience.
payload.medium_description: Llewellyn Johns Recreation Area offers ten campsites with electrical hookups in a peaceful, off-the-beaten-path setting. Located 12 miles south of Lemmon off SD Highway 73, this small campground provides vault toilets, drinking water, picnic tables, and a group shelter. The area holds historical significance as the site of Hugh Glass's 1823 grizzly bear attack.
payload.long_description: A small, get-away park, Llewellyn Johns' 10 campsites offer a quiet camping experience. Nearby Shadehill Recreation Area offers recreational opportunities as well as points of historical interest to keep you busy all day. Or, if you prefer peace and quiet, this is a great campground to just sit back and relax. Many historic figures have crossed through the area, including Hugh Glass and Custer's 1874 Expedition. In 1823, Glass was attacked by a grizzly bear in this area, which is documented in the novel "Lord Grizzly." For more historical information, tour the Petrified Wood Park and Museum and the Grand River Museum, which displays artifacts and photos of life on the ranch, Native American history and more. At Shadehill Recreation Area, a beach and boat ramp gives you access to one of western South Dakota's largest lakes, Campgrounds and camping cabins let you spend extra time to appreciate the outdoors. A mile from Llewellyn Johns Recreation Area is the Grand River National Grassland, part of the vast Dakota Prairie Grasslands. Visitors can fish, hike, ride horses and backpack.

location.directions: Located 12 miles south of Lemmon off South Dakota Highway 73. Address: 19150 Summerville Road, Shadehill, SD 57653.

links.title: SD GFP Llewellyn Johns Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Same-day reservations available by phone starting at 7 a.m. CT.
payload.short_description: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area, 5 miles west of Yankton, is one of the state park system’s most popular resort parks.
payload.medium_description: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lewis and Clark Lake, 5 miles west of Yankton. This resort-style state park offers four campgrounds with 418 sites ranging from full-hookup electrical sites to primitive tent camping. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, dump station, boat ramps, swim beaches, and hiking trails. The park operates year-round, though water systems shut down October through April.
payload.long_description: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area, 5 miles west of Yankton, is one of the state park system’s most popular resort parks. Campgrounds along the shore of Lewis and Clark Lake draw visitors from throughout the Midwest. Campsites provide 50-amp service and cozy one-room, log-style cabins have accommodation for four people, including air conditioning/ heat and electricity. Swim beaches, boat ramps, paved bike trails and a disc golf course provide a variety of outdoor activities. Two privately operated concessions are located on park grounds - Lewis and Clark Marina, South Dakota’s largest marina, features 486 boat slips, convenience store and restaurant; Lewis and Clark Resort offers a modern lodge, cabins, cottages, motel rooms and an outdoor pool for resort guests. Nearby attractions include Gavins Point National Fish Hatchery and Aquarium and Gavins Point Dam.

location.directions: 5 miles west of Yankton off SD Highway 52

links.title: Lewis and Clark Recreation Area - SD GFP

payload.name: Boswell Creek Campground
payload.status_description: This campground does not appear in current USFS developed recreation site listings. It may be a dispersed camping area or may no longer be operational. Contact the Laramie Ranger District at (307) 745-2300 for current status.
payload.short_description: Primitive campground in Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, located southwest of Laramie in Albany County, Wyoming.
payload.medium_description: Boswell Creek Campground is a primitive camping area in the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest in southeastern Wyoming. The campground is accessed via Highway 230 southwest of Laramie, then east on Forest Service Road 526. Limited official information is available about this site.
payload.long_description:
Boswell Creek Campground is located in the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest in Albany County, Wyoming. The site sits at approximately 9,000 feet elevation in the mountains southwest of Laramie.

This appears to be a primitive or dispersed camping area that is not currently listed in the USFS developed campground database or on Recreation.gov. Access is via Highway 230 southwest of Laramie, then east on National Forest System Road 526. Campers should be prepared for rustic conditions with minimal to no developed facilities.

The Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest offers numerous camping opportunities ranging from developed campgrounds to dispersed camping throughout its nearly 3 million acres. For current conditions and accessibility, contact the Laramie Ranger District.

location.directions: From Laramie, travel 38 miles southwest on Highway 230, then 3 miles east on National Forest System Road 526.

payload.name: South Fork State Recreation Area East Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via reservenevada.com from 3 days to 11 months in advance. Maximum stay of 14 consecutive days in any 30-day period. Check-in at 2 p.m., check-out at 11 a.m.
payload.short_description: Year-round campground at South Fork Reservoir with 25 electric sites, flush restrooms with showers, and views of Nevada's Ruby Mountains.
payload.medium_description: East Campground at South Fork State Recreation Area sits along the shores of South Fork Reservoir, offering 25 gravel campsites with electric hookups. The campground features flush restrooms with showers, grills and tables at each site, and an RV dump station. Six pull-through sites accommodate larger rigs up to 40 feet. The reservoir provides excellent fishing for bass, catfish, and trophy trout.
payload.long_description:
South Fork State Recreation Area's East Campground occupies a scenic location on the shores of South Fork Reservoir, approximately five miles south of Elko in northeastern Nevada. The campground offers 25 developed sites on gravel pads, each equipped with a picnic table and grill. Electric hookups are available at all sites for an additional fee. Six pull-through sites (5, 9, 11, 19, 20, and 25) accommodate larger RVs up to 40 feet in length.

The facility includes a flush restroom with shower facilities and an RV dump station accessible year-round from the main north park entrance road. Sites 1 and 25 feature expanded amenities with three picnic tables and a large grill, suitable for group camping. One ADA-accessible site is available.

The 1,650-acre reservoir provides fishing opportunities for largemouth bass, channel catfish, and trophy-sized rainbow and brown trout. Boating, swimming, and hunting are popular activities in the surrounding 4,000-acre recreation area, which features rolling hills and meadows characteristic of the Ruby Mountains foothills.

location.directions: 353 Lower South Fork #8, Spring Creek, NV 89815. Located approximately 5 miles south of Elko via the north park access road.

links.title: South Fork State Recreation Area - Nevada State Parks

payload.name: Bailey's Lakeside Use Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for day use. No park entrance license required. This is primarily a fishing and boat launch access site with minimal developed facilities.
payload.short_description: A small lakeside use area near Hot Springs, South Dakota, primarily offering fishing access and a boat ramp on Bailey Lake, managed by South Dakota Game, Fish, and Parks.
payload.medium_description: Bailey's Lakeside Use Area is a minimal-development fishing and boating access site located 2 miles north of Hot Springs off SD Highway 71 in Fall River County. The area provides a boat ramp on the west shore of Bailey Lake and shore fishing access. As a lakeside use area rather than a full recreation area, facilities are limited and no park entrance license is required.
payload.long_description:
Bailey's Lakeside Use Area is a small, primitive-style recreation site managed by South Dakota Game, Fish, and Parks in Fall River County. Located approximately 2 miles north of Hot Springs off SD Highway 71, the area provides public access to Bailey Lake for fishing and boating.

The primary facilities include a boat ramp on the west shore maintained by SDGFP and shore fishing access near the boat ramp and along the eastern shore. As a lakeside use area rather than a developed state park or recreation area, Bailey's offers minimal amenities and is geared toward day-use activities like fishing and boat launching rather than overnight camping.

The lake and surrounding property are primarily under State of South Dakota and private ownership. No park entrance license is required to access Bailey's Lakeside Use Area.

location.directions: From Hot Springs, travel north on SD Highway 71 for approximately 2 miles.

address.full: 28612 W South Shore Rd, Hot Springs, SD 57747

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Nelson Creek Campground
payload.status_description: This free primitive campground is typically accessible during snow-free months, generally late spring through fall depending on conditions. No reservations are required.
payload.short_description: Free primitive USFS campground along Nelson Creek in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Nelson Creek Campground is a small, free primitive campground located in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Idaho County. Situated near the South Fork Clearwater River drainage, this undeveloped site offers a rustic camping experience in the mountainous terrain of central Idaho.
payload.long_description:
Nelson Creek Campground is a primitive, no-fee campground managed by the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Idaho County, Idaho. Located in the remote backcountry near the South Fork Clearwater River drainage, this site provides a rustic camping option for those seeking solitude in the Rocky Mountains.

As a primitive USFS campground, facilities are minimal. Campers should come prepared to be self-sufficient, bringing their own water and packing out all trash. The surrounding area offers access to national forest lands for hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing.

location.directions: From Grangeville, Idaho, head south on the Grangeville-Salmon Road. Turn left at the drive-in theater toward Mt. Idaho. Continue on the Mt. Idaho Grade toward Elk City on Highway 14. Nelson Creek Campground is located along the South Fork of the Clearwater River at milepost 14 on Highway 14.

payload.name: Mille Lacs Kathio Petaga Campground
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. The campground operates seasonally from late spring through mid-autumn. Reservations can be made online up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota DNR reservation system.
payload.short_description: Developed campground in Mille Lacs Kathio State Park featuring 22 electric and 19 non-electric shaded sites along the Rum River, each with a picnic table and fire ring.
payload.medium_description: Petaga Campground offers 41 wooded sites bordered by tall shade trees in Mille Lacs Kathio State Park. The campground includes 22 electric sites and 19 non-electric sites, all with picnic tables and fire rings. A shower building serves the campground, and five year-round camper cabins are nearby. The Rum River access area offers canoe and kayak rentals for family paddling trips on the slow-moving river.
payload.long_description:
Petaga Campground is the more developed of two campgrounds at Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, located on the southwest corner of Mille Lacs Lake. The campground features 22 electric sites and 19 non-electric sites set among tall shade trees, providing a comfortable woodland camping experience. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill for cooking. A shower building serves campers, and an RV sanitation station is available in the park.

The park sits at the headwaters of the Rum River, which flows 145 miles south to the Mississippi. The slow current makes it ideal for family canoe outings, with rental canoes and kayaks available at the Rum River access area. Mille Lacs Kathio preserves over 10,000 years of human history, including ancient copper artifacts and wild rice harvesting traditions of the Ojibwe people.

Beyond camping, the park offers over 35 miles of trails for hiking, biking, and horseback riding. The 100-foot observation tower near Ogechie Lake provides panoramic views of the surrounding forests and wetlands. Winter activities include cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and snowmobiling on designated trails.

location.directions: From US-169, exit at Onamia and follow signs to Mille Lacs Kathio State Park at 15066 Kathio State Park Road, Onamia, MN 56359. The park is located on the southwest corner of Mille Lacs Lake.

address.full: 17501 Kathio State Park Rd, Onamia, MN 56359

links.title: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park Virtual Tour

payload.name: Arrastre Trail Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round as a free, first-come first-served hike-in trail camp. No reservations required. Campers must pack out all trash and bring their own drinking water.
payload.short_description: Primitive hike-in Pacific Crest Trail camp at 7,700 feet in San Bernardino National Forest with minimal facilities and no fees.
payload.medium_description: Arrastre Trail Camp is a free, first-come first-served PCT trail camp located approximately one mile north of Forest Service Road 2N01 along the Pacific Crest Trail. At 7,700 feet elevation, this primitive backcountry site offers two picnic tables, one fire ring, and a seasonal equestrian trough with non-potable water. No restrooms or drinking water are available; campers must pack out all waste.
payload.long_description:
Arrastre Trail Camp is a primitive backcountry camping area designed primarily for Pacific Crest Trail through-hikers and equestrians. Located at 7,700 feet elevation in the Mountaintop Ranger District of San Bernardino National Forest, the camp sits approximately one mile north of Forest Service Road 2N01 along the PCT.

The site offers minimal amenities befitting its backcountry nature: two picnic tables, one fire ring, and a seasonal equestrian trough with non-potable water. There are no restrooms, no potable water, and no trash services. Campers must practice Leave No Trace principles and pack out all waste.

Dogs are permitted but must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet. Bicycles are prohibited on the Pacific Crest Trail. Horse and pack animals are welcome. The camp is free and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required.

location.directions: Located approximately one mile north of Forest Service Road 2N01 along the Pacific Crest Trail at 7,700 feet elevation. Hike-in access only via the PCT.

links.title: USFS Arrastre-Deer Springs PCT Trail Camp

payload.name: Mole Harbor Shelter Lookout/cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations required and no fee to use the shelter.
payload.short_description: Remote 3-sided CCC Adirondack-style shelter on Admiralty Island in the Kootznoowoo Wilderness. Free first-come, first-served backcountry camping on the cross-Admiralty canoe route.
payload.medium_description: A historic CCC-era 3-sided Adirondack-style shelter with gravel floor at the west end of Mole Harbor on Admiralty Island National Monument. Access is by float plane (40 minutes from Juneau), boat, kayak, canoe, or the Mole Harbor to Alexander Trail from Lake Alexander. Extreme tides combine with Mole River to create exceptional tidepooling and summer salmon fishing opportunities. No restrooms or potable water; treat stream water before drinking.
payload.long_description:
The Mole Harbor Shelter is a historic Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) Adirondack-style structure situated at the west end of Mole Harbor on Admiralty Island National Monument within the Kootznoowoo Wilderness. This 12' x 10' three-sided shelter features a gravel floor and provides a basecamp for exploring one of Southeast Alaska's most remote and pristine wilderness areas.

Access to the shelter is exclusively by water or air: float plane from Juneau takes approximately 40 minutes, or visitors can arrive by boat, kayak, or canoe. An overland route via the Mole Harbor to Alexander Trail connects to Lake Alexander. The shelter sits on the popular cross-Admiralty canoe route, which traverses the island through a series of lakes and portages.

Extreme tidal fluctuations at Mole Harbor create extensive tidal flats ideal for tidepooling, while the Mole River offers excellent fishing during summer salmon runs. Admiralty Island supports one of the highest concentrations of brown bears in North America, so proper food storage and bear awareness are essential. Day hiking opportunities abound along miles of shoreline and the enormous tidal flat.

location.directions: Located on the west end of Mole Harbor, one mile north of Mole River. Access by boat, kayak, canoe, or float plane. Also accessible via the Mole Harbor to Alexander Trail from Lake Alexander. One-way flight time from Juneau is approximately 40 minutes. Suggested USGS topo map: Sitka C-1.

links.title: Tongass NF - Admiralty Island National Monument

payload.name: Savoy Mountain State Forest
payload.status_description: Open for camping through July 30, 2026. The campground will close on July 31, 2026 to accommodate a bathhouse construction project. Reservations required via ReserveAmerica; no walk-in camping.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground in the northwestern Berkshires with 45 tent/RV sites and 4 rustic log cabins, featuring flush toilets, showers, and a dump station.
payload.medium_description: Savoy Mountain State Forest offers 45 spacious campsites nestled in a former apple orchard in the northwestern Berkshires of Massachusetts. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and food storage locker. The campground features flush toilets, showers, and a dump station at the park entrance. Four rustic log cabins with wood-burning stoves are also available for rent.
payload.long_description:
Savoy Mountain State Forest campground is set within a historic apple orchard in the rugged northwestern Berkshires of Massachusetts. The 45 wooded campsites offer good spacing and privacy, each equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and bear-proof food storage locker. Four log cabins provide a more sheltered option, featuring bunk beds, a table and chairs, and a wood-burning stove for heat and cooking.

The campground provides flush toilets and hot showers during the main camping season, with a dump station and potable water fill station located at the park entrance. There are no hookups at any sites. The surrounding forest offers over 50 miles of trails for hiking and mountain biking, plus Tannery Falls and North Pond for swimming and fishing.

Reservations are required and can be made up to four months in advance through ReserveAmerica. Each site is limited to two tents or one tent plus one RV/trailer, with a maximum of two vehicles. Pets are permitted at campsites with proof of rabies vaccination but are not allowed in cabins.

location.directions: From the east: Follow Route 2 West to the Town of Florida. Turn left onto Central Shaft Road and follow signs to the campground on the right past the day use parking lot. From the west: Follow Route 2 East to Florida, turn right onto Central Shaft Road. GPS may be unreliable; follow written directions.

payload.name: Hartford Beach State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Reservations available via campsd.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267. Flush toilets, showers, and water systems operate from approximately May 1 through September 30; vault toilets remain available year-round.
payload.short_description: Big Stone Lake provides the setting for Hartford Beach State Park, a popular camping and picnic area nestled in the shade of a native wooded forest.
payload.medium_description: Hartford Beach State Park campground sits along the shores of Big Stone Lake in northeastern South Dakota. The park features 89 campsites split between east and west camping areas, plus four year-round camping cabins. Electrical hookups are available at select sites. Amenities include flush toilets and showers during summer months, with vault toilets available year-round. The park also offers a boat ramp, swimming beach, fish cleaning station, and playground.
payload.long_description: Big Stone Lake provides the setting for Hartford Beach State Park, a popular camping and picnic area nestled in the shade of a native wooded forest. Runoff from melting glaciers 10,000 years ago created the River Warren, a section of which is known today as Big Stone Lake. Rugged rock-strewn bluffs and scenic timbered shorelines surround Hartford Beach. When you stay at the campground, take advantage of the park amenities that include a boat ramp, beach, fish cleaning station, fishing pole checkout, playground, games and picnic shelter. A nine-hole disc golf course has also been set up at Hartford Beach State Park. Camping cabins are open year-round to enjoy the seasons and the views. The one-room cabins come with heating, air conditioning, electricity and sleeping accommodations for four people. No cooking is allowed inside, but you will find a fire grate, picnic table and porch outside. Five hiking trails at Hartford Beach State Park take visitors past historic sites and scenic overlooks, including burial mounds and a prehistoric village site. The American Indian mounds found in Hartford Beach State Park are typical of numerous such mounds in eastern South Dakota. They cover a time span from approximately 300 A.D. to possibly 1600 A.D. At the eastern end of the Robar Trail is the log cabin trading post, which operated from 1863-73.

location.directions: Located near Corona, South Dakota on the western shore of Big Stone Lake in Roberts County.

links.title: Hartford Beach State Park - SD GFP
