payload.name: Indian Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: The rolling hills and beautiful river views make Indian Creek Recreation Area an excellent place to camp, picnic and explore.
payload.medium_description: Indian Creek Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Oahe near Mobridge, South Dakota, offering 123 campsites across east and west campgrounds plus two camping cabins. The area features electrical and non-electrical sites, flush toilets and showers (seasonal), vault toilets year-round, drinking water, a dump station, fish cleaning station, boat ramps, and hiking/biking trails. Bridge City Marina provides boat rentals, fuel, and a convenience store.
payload.long_description: The rolling hills and beautiful river views make Indian Creek Recreation Area an excellent place to camp, picnic and explore. Park visitors will find new adventure in this rugged land explored by Lewis and Clark in 1804. During the late 1800s and early 1900s, cowboys used the area to fatten thousands of cattle for shipment south. Plan ahead and make reservations for one of the two campgrounds or a camping cabin, open year-round. It's quick and easy with the online system. All of the campsites have electric hookups, with access to comfort stations with flush toilets and showers. The cozy one-bedroom cabins sleep four in a set of bunk beds and a double bed. Heating and air conditioning allow you to stay comfortable whatever the weather. Outdoors, a picnic table and fire grate make outdoor cooking and dining a pleasure. Within the park, anglers will find the facilities they need: boat ramp, fish-cleaning station and fishing pole checkout. Ice fishing in the colder months is popular. The whole family can come together for some fun by checking out a game, and children can romp on the playground. Indian Creek Recreation Area offers over 2.5 miles of hiking and biking trails. Along any of the three trails, a person can spot a variety of wildlife, from deer, raccoons, beavers, and bull snakes to turkeys, pheasants and orchard orioles. Onsite is the Bridge City Marina and Resort, which offers boat slip rentals, a floating fuel dock, Beef's Restaurant, bait, guide service, convenience store and several modern cabins. Close to Indian Creek is the Revheim Bay Recreation Area, a day-use park with four picnic shelters, a playground, an off-highway vehicle area, Archery Range and two sets of horseshoe pits, and a sand volleyball court.

location.directions: Located at 12905 288th Avenue, Mobridge, SD 57601. GPS coordinates: 45.52214°N, -100.3868°W.

links.title: SD Game, Fish & Parks - Indian Creek Recreation Area

payload.name: Grizzly Creek Redwoods Sp River Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the summer season. The campground operates from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia; some sites available first-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Intimate 28-site campground nestled among old-growth redwoods along the Van Duzen River, offering a quieter alternative to the more crowded North Coast redwood parks.
payload.medium_description: Grizzly Creek Redwoods State Park's River Campground sits between Highway 36 and the Van Duzen River, surrounded by towering old-growth redwoods. The 28 tent-focused sites provide a more secluded redwood camping experience than the busier coastal parks. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with flush toilets, hot pay showers, and drinking water nearby. The campground serves as a base for exploring the park's trails, including the accessible Cheatham Grove loop through ancient redwoods, and for swimming in the river where Grizzly Creek meets the Van Duzen.
payload.long_description:
Grizzly Creek Redwoods State Park is a hidden gem among California's redwood parks, offering old-growth groves without the crowds found at more famous coastal locations. The River Campground's 28 sites are arranged along the scenic Van Duzen River, 17 miles inland from Highway 101. The forested setting provides natural shade and privacy, with massive redwoods creating a cathedral-like atmosphere throughout the camping area.

The park centers around the confluence of Grizzly Creek and the Van Duzen River, creating a popular swimming hole near the visitor center and campground. Summer weekends feature ranger-led campfire programs, nature walks, and Junior Ranger activities from Memorial Day through Labor Day. The Cheatham Grove Trail offers a 0.6-mile accessible loop through pristine old-growth forest with a compacted native soil surface.

Campsites are best suited for tent camping and smaller RVs, with a maximum length of 24 feet for trailers and motorhomes. The campground lacks hookups and dump stations, maintaining a more primitive character consistent with the natural setting. Two sites are designated accessible with paved surfaces, though the terrain has some slopes. Dogs are allowed in the campground but prohibited on trails except for service animals.

location.directions: From Eureka, drive 20 miles southeast on Highway 101, then 17 miles east on Highway 36 to the park entrance at 16949 Highway 36 in Carlotta.

payload.name: TIMBER CREEK RESERVOIR LOWER CAMPGROUND
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates seasonally from late spring through fall, weather and road conditions permitting. First-come, first-served; no reservations. Check with the Leadore Ranger District for current road and campground conditions before traveling.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground with 4 sites at Timber Creek Reservoir in the Salmon-Challis National Forest, offering fishing access and a remote backcountry setting near Leadore, Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Timber Creek Reservoir Lower Campground is a small, primitive campground with 4 sites located in the Leadore Ranger District of the Salmon-Challis National Forest. The campground sits near Timber Creek Reservoir and provides fishing opportunities in both the reservoir and nearby Hawley Creek. This is a remote, first-come, first-served facility accessed via forest roads west of Leadore.
payload.long_description:
Timber Creek Reservoir Lower Campground is a small, primitive facility with 4 campsites located in the Beaverhead Mountains of the Salmon-Challis National Forest. The campground provides access to Timber Creek Reservoir for fishing and offers a quiet, remote setting for those seeking solitude in the Idaho backcountry.

The campground features basic amenities including potable water. Fishing is available in Timber Creek Reservoir and nearby Hawley Creek. The area is popular with anglers and those seeking to escape more crowded developed campgrounds. The Upper campground, located nearby, offers an additional 6 sites with vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings.

Access is via forest roads west of Leadore. From Leadore, travel west on Lee Creek Road for approximately 0.9 miles, then turn left onto Forest Service Road 105 toward Big Timber Creek. After about 7.5 miles, take the right fork onto Forest Service Road 172, then follow for one mile to a fork where the right branch leads to the Lower campground.

location.directions: From Leadore, go west on Lee Creek Road for 0.9 miles. Turn left onto Forest Service Road 105 toward Big Timber Creek. Continue approximately 7.5 miles to a road junction and take the right fork onto Forest Service Road 172. Follow for one mile to a fork; the right branch leads to Timber Creek Reservoir Lower Campground.

payload.name: Lake Herman State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From October 1 through April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Melting glacial ice formed this 1,350-acre lake thousands of years ago.
payload.medium_description: Lake Herman State Park Campground offers 72 campsites along the shores of Lake Herman near Madison, South Dakota. The campground provides both electrical ($30/night) and non-electrical ($16/night) sites, plus four camping cabins. Modern amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station during the warmer months, with vault toilets available year-round. The park features hiking trails through native oak woodlands and prairie grasses, disc golf, fishing piers, and boat access.
payload.long_description: Melting glacial ice formed this 1,350-acre lake thousands of years ago. Lake Herman State Park is located on a peninsula and offers visitors spectacular views of Lake Herman. Camping, boating, fishing, and cross country skiing are favorite activities at the park. Observe wildlife in the native oak woodlands and prairie grasses that serve as a habitat for a variety of birds and animals. Making a reservation for a campsite or camping cabin at Lake Herman State Park is easy. A few minutes on the computer and your vacation plans are set. Campsites are either basic or come with electricity. Cabins have air conditioning and heating, ensuring year-round comfort no matter the outside temperature. A party of four can be accommodated with bunk beds and a double bed. Bring food suitable for outdoor cooking on the fire grate, as well as sleeping bags, linens and utensils. Once settled in, explore the many features of the park, like the beach, boat ramp, disc golf, playground, ski beach and fishing dock. Canoes and kayaks may be rented, and fishing poles and games can be checked out. Lake Herman has been a popular campsite for hundreds of years. Before white settlers entered the region, it was popular among Indians traveling to nearby Pipestone quarries. The first settlers at Lake Herman were Herman Luce and his son, William. They settled the timberland on the east side of the lake and assumed squatters' rights on June 17, 1870.The log cabin in the park was built for Herman Luce in the summer of 1871. The cabin is made of sturdy oak logs hand hewn to fit snugly and chinked to keep out the cold. Luce's cabin briefly served as a U. S. Land Office, with Herman Luce in charge. In 1977, the Herman Luce Cabin was placed on the National Register of Historic Places.

location.directions: Located at 23409 State Park Drive, Madison, SD 57042. The park is situated on the north shore of Lake Herman, approximately 2 miles west of Madison off SD Highway 34.

payload.name: Lake Thompson Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by phone at 1-800-710-2267. Minimum two-night stay required; reservations must be made at least two days prior to arrival.
payload.short_description: So distinct is Lake Thompson that it is designated a National Natural Landmark.
payload.medium_description: Lake Thompson Recreation Area offers 103 campsites (electric and non-electric), five camping cabins, and a group lodge on the shores of South Dakota's largest natural lake. The park features modern amenities including flush toilets, showers, and a dump station during the primary season. Recreational opportunities include boating, fishing, swimming at the beach, and exploring hiking and biking trails. The area holds historical significance as one of Laura Ingalls Wilder's Twin Lakes featured in her books.
payload.long_description: So distinct is Lake Thompson that it is designated a National Natural Landmark. Originally called Dry Woods Lake by American Indians, the lake was renamed for Jacob Thompson, Secretary of the Interior under President James Buchanan. In the 1930s, the lake was completely dry and used for pasture. In the 1980s, the area was a 9,000-acre marsh. Heavy rains and snowmelt in the mid-80s filled the lake to over 20 feet deep. A variety of options are open for staying at Lake Thompson Recreation Area: campsites, cabins and a lodge. Sites in the campground have electricity, dump station and comfort stations with flush toilets and showers. One-room cabins sleep four and have heating, air conditioning and electricity. The lodge at Lake Thompson Recreation Area was once a farm house. Now, the five-bedroom facility houses up to 12 guests in one of the state's most popular recreation areas. Author Laura Ingalls Wilder mentions Lake Thompson as one of the Twin Lakes in her books, including "By the Shores of Silver Lake" and "The Long Winter." Modern-day visitors will also have plenty to write home about, as they enjoy the beach, boat ramp, ski beach and playground in the lovely area. Those fishing for walleye, northern pike, crappie, perch and bass have access to a fish-cleaning station and fishing-pole checkout. Hikers, bikers and walkers can take the park tour trail to see all parts of Lake Thompson Recreation Area.

location.directions: Located 6 miles southwest of Lake Preston off US Highway 14. Address: 21176 Flood Club Road, Lake Preston, SD 57249.

address.full: 21176 Flood Club Rd, Lake Preston, SD 57249

payload.name: Lake Poinsett Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From October 1 through April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Summer season is fully operational with all amenities.
payload.short_description: One of the largest lakes in the state, Lake Poinsett was named after Joel Poinsett who served as U.
payload.medium_description: Lake Poinsett Recreation Area is a popular destination on one of the largest natural lakes in eastern South Dakota. The park features two campgrounds with 112 campsites and 4 camping cabins, along with a swim beach, boat ramp, fish cleaning station, and a visitor center museum housing the Harlan Olson collection. Electrical and non-electrical sites are available, with showers and flush toilets in season.
payload.long_description: One of the largest lakes in the state, Lake Poinsett was named after Joel Poinsett who served as U.S. Secretary of War. He was instrumental in promoting the expedition of Joseph Nicollet and John Fremont who first explored the region in 1838. The party camped on the north side of Lake Poinsett. Today, the lakeshore still provides excellent camping opportunities, as well as many other recreational activities. Stake out your territory at Lake Poinsett Recreation Area by booking a campsite or camping cabin. Two campgrounds at the park offer both electric and non-electric sites. Showers and flush toilets are found in the comfort stations. You can stay any time of year in the camping cabins, furnished with beds and heating/air conditioning. The one-room, log-style cabins sleep four. Cooking is not permitted indoors, so bring utensils for use on the outdoor fire grate. The large expanse of water at Lake Poinsett Recreation Area invites you to swim, water ski, boat and fish for walleye, bass, perch, northern pike and bullhead. The Lake Poinsett Visitor Center and Museum is a fascinating place to learn about the history of the area. The Museum is home to a variety of artifacts that came from the collection of Harlan Olson and were donated to South Dakota Game, Fish & Parks by his family. The exhibits will take you back in time from prehistoric days to the late 1990s.Hike or bike along the Vista, Woodland, or Lakeshore Trail where you will see wooded, grass, and wetland areas.

location.directions: Located 14 miles northeast of Arlington, South Dakota off US Highway 81.

payload.name: Bothe-napa Valley Sp Cabins And Yurts
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia. Yurts and cabins sell out quickly when released. Wood fires periodically banned during fire season.
payload.short_description: Five historic cabins and ten yurts in Napa Valley's redwood forest, offering semi-rustic lodging with access to showers, restrooms, and hiking trails near wine country.
payload.medium_description: Bothe-Napa Valley State Park offers five restored historic cabins and ten yurts nestled among coastal redwoods and mixed forest. Cabins feature private bathrooms, kitchens, heaters, and electricity, sleeping two to four guests. Yurts include beds and cots, outdoor fire pits, and picnic tables, with nearby restrooms and pay showers. Pet-friendly and ADA-accessible options are available. Reservations through ReserveCalifornia.
payload.long_description:
Bothe-Napa Valley State Park provides unique overnight accommodations in five restored historic cabins and ten yurts within a 1,900-acre preserve of coastal redwoods, Douglas fir, and oak woodlands. The park sits four miles north of St. Helena, offering easy access to Napa Valley wineries while providing a secluded forest retreat.

The five cabins range from standard two-person units with kitchenettes to premium four-person cabins with full kitchens. All cabins include private bathrooms with showers, electricity, heaters, and furnished porches. Oak and Redwood cabins are ADA accessible. The ten yurts come in large (sleeps 6) and small (sleeps 4) sizes, each equipped with a queen bed and cots, outdoor fire pit, and picnic table. Yurts have no interior heat but provide access to nearby restrooms and pay showers. Select yurts are pet-friendly and ADA accessible.

The park features over 10 miles of hiking and equestrian trails, a seasonal swimming pool, and connects to Bale Grist Mill State Historic Park via the History Trail. Wood fires may be banned during fire season; charcoal and propane alternatives are recommended.

location.directions: Located at 3801 St. Helena Highway North (Highway 29), four miles north of St. Helena and five miles south of Calistoga.

payload.name: Glendalough State Park Remote Yurt And Canoe-in Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Yurts available Thursday through Sunday only during winter months. Reservations available through Minnesota DNR up to 120 days in advance.
payload.short_description: Remote yurts and canoe-in tent sites on Annie Battle Lake's southeast shore, accessible only by paddle, hike, or bike in this Heritage Fishery where motors are prohibited.
payload.medium_description: Glendalough State Park's Remote Yurt and Canoe-in Camp offers a secluded backcountry experience on the southeast shore of Annie Battle Lake, a 335-acre Heritage Fishery where motors and electronics are banned. Two wood-heated yurts (sleeping 3 and 7) and three primitive tent sites are accessible via a 1.25-mile hike/bike on the Annie Battle Lake Trail or by paddling across the lake. Vault toilets and firewood are provided, but campers must bring their own drinking water or filter from the lake.
payload.long_description:
The Remote Yurt and Canoe-in Camp at Glendalough State Park provides one of Minnesota's most secluded camping experiences. Situated on the southeast shore of Annie Battle Lake, the area is accessible only by canoe, kayak, hiking, or biking along the Annie Battle Lake Trail (approximately 1.25 miles from parking). The 335-acre lake is designated a Heritage Fishery with special regulations that sustain excellent populations of sunfish, crappie, bass, and occasional walleye.

Two yurts are available: a 16-foot diameter unit sleeping three people and a 20-foot unit sleeping seven. Both feature wood stoves for heating with free firewood provided by the park. The yurts include sleeping platforms with bunk configurations, tables, and chairs, but have no electricity or indoor plumbing. Cooking must be done outdoors at the fire ring. One yurt is ADA accessible. Three primitive tent sites with fire rings round out the camping options.

Facilities include vault toilets near the sites and a food storage locker to protect provisions from wildlife. There is no potable water; campers must pack in their own supply or filter from the lake. The remote location and motor-free waters create an exceptionally quiet setting for fishing, paddling, and wildlife observation. Glendalough is one of only three Minnesota state parks offering yurt accommodations.

location.directions: From Battle Lake, Minnesota, take County Road 16 west for approximately 2 miles. Turn right onto Glendalough State Park Road and follow to the park entrance. The Trail Center provides access to the Annie Battle Lake Trail leading to the remote camp area, or launch canoes/kayaks from the designated access point on Annie Battle Lake.

payload.name: Spruce Campground
payload.status_description: This campground has been permanently decommissioned and is closed to overnight camping. Fishing access to Libby Creek remains available at the site.
payload.short_description: Decommissioned campground in the Libby Creek Recreation Area along the Snowy Range Scenic Byway. Fishing access to Libby Creek remains available.
payload.medium_description: Spruce Campground, located off the Snowy Range Scenic Byway in the Libby Creek Recreation Area, has been decommissioned and is no longer operational for overnight camping. The site still provides fishing access to Libby Creek and is managed by the Laramie Ranger District of Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests.
payload.long_description:
Spruce Campground was once a developed camping area in the Libby Creek Recreation Area, situated along Wyoming's scenic Highway 130 (Snowy Range Scenic Byway) west of Centennial. The campground has been decommissioned by the Forest Service and is no longer open for overnight camping.

While camping is no longer permitted at this location, the area still offers recreational value. Fishing access to Libby Creek remains available for anglers. The site is located approximately one mile west of the Forest boundary near Centennial, on the south side of the Snowy Range Highway, beyond Forest Road 351 (Barber Lake Road).

Campers seeking overnight accommodations in this area should consider nearby alternatives in the Libby Creek Recreation Area or other campgrounds along the Snowy Range Scenic Byway managed by Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests.

location.directions: From Laramie, take WY 130 west to the Forest Boundary near Centennial, then travel 1 mile west to the Libby Creek Recreation Area on the south side of Snowy Range Highway. Spruce Campground is on the left, beyond Forest Road 351 (Barber Lake Road).

payload.name: Lake Griffin State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is temporarily closed as of May 15, 2025. No reopening date has been announced. The day-use areas of the park remain open from 8 a.m. to sunset daily.
payload.short_description: A 40-site campground nestled in a mature live oak hammock near Lake Griffin, offering full hookups, showers, and boat access in central Florida.
payload.medium_description: Lake Griffin State Park Campground offers 40 shaded campsites in a mature live oak hammock on the shores of Lake Griffin. All sites have water and electric hookups, with select sites offering full sewer hookups. The campground includes modern amenities such as hot showers, flush restrooms, laundry facilities, and a dump station. A boat ramp provides direct lake access for fishing and paddling.
payload.long_description:
Lake Griffin State Park Campground sits within a 620-acre park on the shores of Lake Griffin in central Florida, approximately three miles north of Leesburg. The 40 well-shaded campsites are tucked into a mature live oak hammock, providing natural shade and a peaceful atmosphere. Each site features water and electric hookups, a picnic table, and a fire ring with grate.

Seven sites are pull-through configurations suitable for larger rigs up to 40 feet, while the remaining sites are back-in. Five to seven sites offer full hookups including sewer connections. Central facilities include hot showers, flush restrooms, laundry machines, and a dump station. Three sites are ADA accessible.

The park offers excellent fishing and boating access to Lake Griffin, part of the Harris Chain of Lakes. Kayak and canoe rentals are available. A nature trail loops through the oak hammock and along the lake shore, and an observation platform provides wildlife viewing opportunities.

location.directions: Located at 3089 US Highway 441/27 in Fruitland Park, three miles north of Leesburg and 30 miles south of Ocala.

links.title: Lake Griffin State Park Official Page

payload.name: Alafia River State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 365 days. Park hours 8 a.m. until sundown. Gravitron bike trails closed as of March 27, 2026; all other areas including campground open. Reservations available through Reserve America.
payload.short_description: Family-friendly campground at a reclaimed phosphate mine featuring 30 electric/water sites, solar-heated showers, and 20+ miles of mountain biking trails in Hillsborough County, Florida.
payload.medium_description: Alafia River State Park Campground offers 30 RV and tent sites with water and electric hookups on a unique landscape of reclaimed phosphate mining pits. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. Solar-heated showers, flush restrooms, dump station, and two picnic pavilions serve campers. The park is renowned for its challenging mountain bike trails and also features equestrian camping with 12 designated sites near stables and paddocks.
payload.long_description:
Alafia River State Park Campground sits on 6,500 acres of reclaimed phosphate mining land in Hillsborough County, creating an unusual Florida landscape of rolling hills, ridges, and lakes. The family campground contains 30 sites suitable for both RVs and tent campers, each equipped with water and electric hookups, a paved parking spur, picnic table, and fire ring with grill. Clean restrooms with solar-heated showers serve the campground, along with two large picnic pavilions and a community fire pit.

The park is best known for its extensive mountain biking trail system, offering over 20 miles of challenging single-track across varied terrain that draws riders from throughout the region. A full-service bike shop on-site provides rentals, repairs, and lessons. Beyond biking, visitors can enjoy paddling the South Prong of the Alafia River, hiking, fishing, and wildlife observation.

Equestrian camping is available with 12 sites featuring horse tie-outs, plus twelve stables and six paddocks on a first-come, first-served basis. Glamping options through Comfy Camping offer furnished luxury bell tents for those seeking an upscale outdoor experience.

location.directions: From Interstate 75 exit 240 south of Riverview, follow SR 674 east to CR 39, then continue north to the park entrance at 14326 South County Road 39, Lithia. Note: Some GPS navigation leads to incorrect entrances. The main entrance to the ranger station and campground is on County Road 39, not Jameson Road.

payload.name: Cave Lake State Park Lake View Campground
payload.status_description: Lake View Campground is open year-round, currently operating in the lower loop only. Flush toilets and showers are available, though facilities may close during extremely cold winter conditions. Elk Flat Campground remains closed until May 1.
payload.short_description: Year-round lakeside camping at Cave Lake State Park with flush toilets, showers, and scenic mountain views at 7,300 feet elevation in the Schell Creek Range.
payload.medium_description: Lake View Campground offers year-round camping near the shore of a 32-acre reservoir in eastern Nevada's Schell Creek Range. The lower loop features level sites with fire pits, grills, and tables, along with flush toilets and showers. The primitive campground has no hookups but provides a dump station near the entrance. Excellent trout fishing, boating, swimming, and hiking are accessible from camp.
payload.long_description:
Lake View Campground sits adjacent to Cave Lake, a 32-acre stocked trout reservoir at approximately 7,300 feet elevation in the Schell Creek Range near Ely. The campground operates year-round, though only the lower loop is currently open. Each site is level with a fire pit, grill, picnic table, and parking space. Access roads within the campground are unpaved but maintained.

The campground features flush toilets and hot showers, a notable upgrade from typical primitive camping. A sanitary dump station is located near the campground entrance, though it may close seasonally in winter. No electric, water, or sewer hookups are available at individual sites. In extremely cold conditions, facilities may be temporarily closed, so winter campers should contact the park before arriving.

Cave Lake provides excellent year-round fishing for rainbow and brown trout, with ice fishing popular during winter months. Boating is permitted with a combined camping and boat launch fee available. Hiking trails include the Overlook Trail offering panoramic views of the lake and surrounding mountains. The park enforces a seven-day camping limit within any 30-day period.

location.directions: From Ely, Nevada, travel south on US-93 for approximately 7 miles. Turn right onto Success Summit Road (also signed for Cave Lake State Park). Continue approximately 7 miles to the park entrance. Lake View Campground is located past the fee station near the lake.

links.title: Cave Lake State Park - Nevada State Parks
Cave Lake State Park - Park Rules

payload.name: Medano Pass Primitive Road Campsites
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season as of May 15. The road typically opens mid-to-late May and closes late November depending on snow and conditions. All 21 sites fill on summer holiday weekends. No reservations; first-come, first-served only.
payload.short_description: Free primitive roadside campsites along Medano Pass Road in Great Sand Dunes National Preserve, accessible only by high-clearance 4WD vehicles with nine creek crossings.
payload.medium_description: Twenty-one free, first-come, first-served primitive campsites line Medano Pass Road in Great Sand Dunes National Preserve, starting 5.2 miles from Pinon Flats Campground. The road requires a full-size 4WD vehicle with low-range transfer case and crosses Medano Creek nine times. Each site has a fire ring and most have bear boxes, but there are no toilets or trash service. Sites fill quickly on summer weekends.
payload.long_description:
Medano Pass Primitive Road Campsites offer backcountry vehicle camping in Great Sand Dunes National Preserve along a rugged 22-mile 4WD route connecting the park to the Wet Mountain Valley. The 21 numbered sites are free and first-come, first-served with no reservations. Each site features a fire ring and most include bear-proof food storage boxes. This is true primitive camping with no toilets, no trash service, and seasonal potable water availability only.

Accessing the campsites requires a high-clearance 4WD vehicle with low-range transfer case. All-wheel drive crossovers, mini-SUVs, and ATVs are prohibited. The road traverses deep sand sections, rocky terrain, and nine crossings of Medano Creek, taking 2.5-3 hours to drive. Heavy-duty off-road tires with 10-ply sidewall rating are strongly recommended. There is no cell signal along the entire route.

The road typically opens in mid-to-late May and closes in late November depending on snow and conditions. Sites fill on summer holiday weekends and often on regular summer weekends. Campers must pack out all trash and bury human waste 6 inches deep. The area passes through excellent bighorn sheep habitat and the 2010 Medano Fire burn area.

location.directions: The south entrance to Medano Pass Road begins just below Pinon Flats Campground, one mile north of the visitor center. The road's north access is in the Wet Mountain Valley on Highway 69 south of Westcliffe.

links.title: Medano Pass Primitive Road Campsites Official Website

photos.name: A full-size SUV, Jeep or truck with 4WD is required to access Medano Pass Primitive Road campsites
Campsites along the road generally have tall trees for shade.

payload.name: Burgdorf Guard Station
payload.status_description: The cabin is currently closed for the winter season. Reservations are made through Recreation.gov. Contact the McCall Ranger District at (208) 634-0400 to obtain the lock combination 24-48 hours before arrival.
payload.short_description: Renovated cabin rental at 6,250 feet elevation in Payette National Forest with two bedrooms, full bathroom with accessible shower, kitchen, and wood stove heating.
payload.medium_description: The Burgdorf Guard Station Rental Cabin is a freshly renovated Forest Service cabin situated in a small meadow near McCall, Idaho. The cabin features two bedrooms with queen beds, a full bathroom with wheelchair-accessible shower, kitchen with refrigerator and gas range, and a wood burning stove for heat. Solar-powered lighting provides illumination, though no electrical outlets are available.
payload.long_description:
The Burgdorf Guard Station Rental Cabin sits at 6,250 feet elevation in a scenic meadow within the Payette National Forest. Fully renovated in 2024, this former Forest Service facility now offers comfortable overnight accommodations for up to four guests. The cabin includes two bedrooms each with a queen bed, a living room, full kitchen with refrigerator, gas range/oven, and sink, plus a full bathroom with flush toilet and wheelchair-accessible shower.

The cabin is heated by a wood burning stove and illuminated by solar-powered lights. Note that no electrical outlets are available. A fire pit is located at the rear of the cabin. Limited kitchen utensils are provided, but guests should bring their own supplies. There is no trash collection, so pack out all garbage.

The location provides excellent access to recreation including several trailheads departing from the nearby Burgdorf Campground: Nethker Creek Trail #143, Jeanette Creek Trail #140, and Burgdorf Trails #175 and #176. The area is within driving distance of Burgdorf Hot Springs, Warren Guard Station, and the historic towns of Secesh and Warren.

location.directions: Travel approximately 30 miles north of McCall on the paved Warren Wagon Road (21). Turn left on gravel Forest Road #246 and in two miles the campground will be on your left. The Guard Station is just beyond the campground.

payload.name: Byers Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed and slated for decommissioning. The campground no longer appears on official USFS recreation listings.
payload.short_description: Byers Creek Campground is a former USFS campground in Arapaho National Forest near Fraser, Colorado, now permanently closed and slated for decommissioning.
payload.medium_description: Byers Creek Campground was a small primitive campground located in the Arapaho National Forest southwest of Fraser, Colorado, near the Byers Peak Wilderness. The campground is permanently closed and slated for decommissioning by the USFS. Nearby St. Louis Creek Campground remains an active option for camping in this area.
payload.long_description:
Byers Creek Campground was a small, primitive campground located in the Arapaho National Forest in Grand County, Colorado, approximately 7 miles southwest of Fraser along County Road 73 (St. Louis Creek Road). The campground was situated in a forested setting near Byers Creek and provided access to the Byers Peak Wilderness.

The campground is permanently closed and has been slated for decommissioning by the U.S. Forest Service. It no longer appears on official USFS recreation listings or Recreation.gov. Campers seeking overnight accommodations in this area should consider nearby St. Louis Creek Campground, which remains active and offers 16 sites with access to the same Byers Peak and Vasquez Wilderness areas.

location.directions: From Fraser, head southwest on County Road 73 (St. Louis Creek Road) for approximately 7 miles.

payload.name: Grand Island Thumb Area Facilities
payload.status_description: The Thumb area is a day-use viewing destination for the historic East Channel Lighthouse, which sits on private property and cannot be accessed by land. The lighthouse can be viewed from the water year-round, weather permitting. Ferry service to Grand Island operates from the Friday before Memorial Day through mid-October. No overnight camping facilities exist at this specific location, though backcountry camping is available elsewhere on the island during the reservation season.
payload.short_description: Day-use viewing area on the Thumb section of Grand Island, featuring views of the historic 1868 East Channel Lighthouse on private property surrounded by Lake Superior.
payload.medium_description: The Thumb Area Facilities are located on the eastern lobe of Grand Island in Lake Superior, near Munising, Michigan. This area features the historic Grand Island East Channel Lighthouse (1868), which operated until 1913 and remains on private property, inaccessible by land. Visitors can view the lighthouse via commercial boat tours, private watercraft, or kayak. The broader Grand Island National Recreation Area offers backcountry camping at designated sites with primitive facilities.
payload.long_description:
The Thumb is the distinctive eastern peninsula of Grand Island, a 13,500-acre National Recreation Area situated half a mile from Munising, Michigan in Lake Superior. The area's primary feature is the historic Grand Island East Channel Lighthouse, a wooden structure built between 1868-1870 by the Lighthouse Board to guide vessels through the eastern channel into Munising Harbor. The lighthouse was decommissioned by 1913 and remains on private property, inaccessible by land.

Visitors can view the lighthouse from the water via Pictured Rocks cruises, Alger underwater preserve tours departing from Munising Harbor, or by private boat and kayak. Grand Island itself offers dramatic 300-foot sandstone cliffs, pristine beaches, inland lakes, and dense hardwood forests. Access to the island is by passenger ferry from Grand Island Landing on M-28 (approximately 2.5 miles west of Munising) or by private watercraft.

While the Thumb Area Facilities itself is primarily a viewing destination with no developed camping infrastructure, the broader Grand Island NRA offers 19 individual backcountry campsites and two group sites with primitive facilities including vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and bear lockers. Camping reservations are required via Recreation.gov from Memorial Day through Columbus Day.

location.directions: Access Grand Island via passenger ferry or private watercraft. The ferry departs from Grand Island Landing on M-28, approximately 2.5 miles west of downtown Munising, Michigan. The Thumb is located on the southeastern shore of the island. The lighthouse cannot be reached by land as it sits on private property; it must be viewed from the water via boat tour or kayak.

links.title: Grand Island East Channel Lighthouse - USFS

payload.name: Hugh Glass Lakeside Use Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations accepted. Primitive facilities with water and vault toilets available.
payload.short_description: Hugh Glass Lakeside Use Area
payload.medium_description: Hugh Glass Lakeside Use Area is a primitive camping destination on Shadehill Reservoir, located 14 miles south of Lemmon off SD Highway 73. Named for the legendary mountain man who was mauled by a grizzly bear in this area in 1823, the site serves both general campers and equestrians. The area provides first-come, first-served camping with water access and vault toilets, plus over 6,000 acres of open state park land and National Grassland to explore on horseback or foot.
payload.long_description: Hugh Glass Lakeside Use Area

location.directions: From Lemmon, travel 14 miles south on SD Highway 73 to Hugh Glass Road.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Rolling M. Ranch Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservations available via ReserveCalifornia.com. Park closes for at least 48 hours following rain exceeding one quarter inch and during Red Flag fire warnings. Gates lock at 5pm (winter) or 7pm (summer); after-hours arrivals must call ahead. Check-in 2pm, check-out noon.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent campground with 20 sites nestled in Chino Hills State Park, offering access to over 90 miles of trails through oak woodlands and rolling grasslands of Southern California.
payload.medium_description: Rolling M. Ranch Campground is a primitive 20-site campground in Chino Hills State Park, located in the oak-studded hills between Orange, Riverside, and San Bernardino counties. The campground features flush toilets, hot showers, and potable water. Sites accommodate tents and small trailers up to 28 feet. The historic Rolling M Ranch barn sits nearby, and campers have direct access to over 90 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Rolling M. Ranch Campground sits within Chino Hills State Park, one of the last remaining large open spaces in the rapidly urbanizing Puente-Chino Hills corridor. The 20 primitive campsites are set among native California landscapes featuring coast live oaks, elderberry, and toyon, with wildlife including mule deer, coyotes, and over 100 bird species. The campground offers basic amenities including flush toilets, hot showers, and potable water, though no hookups are available.

The historic Rolling M Ranch, once a working cattle operation, provides a glimpse into Southern California's ranching heritage. An accessible horse-mounting platform and the Native Plant Trail are located nearby. Over 90 miles of multi-use trails radiate from the area, suitable for hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian use. Trails are limited to daylight hours only.

The park operates on seasonal hours, with gates closing at 5pm in winter and 7pm in summer. Notably, campfires, ground fires, and charcoal BBQs are prohibited throughout the park due to fire danger. The park may close for 48 hours following significant rainfall or during Red Flag fire warnings.

location.directions: From the 91-Freeway, take Highway 71-North, turn left at Soquel Canyon, proceed to Elinvar, then turn left. The park entrance is at 4721 Sapphire Road, Chino Hills, CA 91709.

address.full: 18155 Upper Aliso Trl, Chino Hills, CA 91709

payload.name: Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. The campground operates from late April through October 31. Reservations required through mndnr.gov/reservations. A state park vehicle permit is required in addition to campsite fees.
payload.short_description: Cuyuna Country's group camp accommodates up to 25 people in a wooded setting near Portsmouth Mine Lake, with access to restrooms, showers, a swimming beach, and renowned mountain bike trails.
payload.medium_description: The group campground at Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area is situated within the Portsmouth Campground on the northwest shore of Portsmouth Mine Lake. It accommodates up to 25 people in a wooded setting within walking distance of restrooms, showers, a swimming beach, and one of Minnesota's premier mountain biking trail systems. Reservations are required through the Minnesota DNR.
payload.long_description:
Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area's group campground offers a dedicated camping area for groups of up to 25 people within the Portsmouth Campground. Set on the northwest shore of Portsmouth Mine Lake, the wooded site provides convenient access to shared restrooms and showers, a swimming beach, and the recreation area's extensive mountain biking trail network.

The recreation area spans 5,000 acres of former iron mining land, now featuring clear, deep lakes formed in abandoned mine pits. Portsmouth Mine Lake reaches depths of 395-450 feet, making it one of Minnesota's deepest inland lakes. Anglers will find trout, northern pike, bass, crappie, and sunfish in these waters. The area is particularly popular with mountain bikers, offering miles of single-track trails ranging from beginner to advanced difficulty.

Group camping reservations can be made up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota DNR reservation system. Campers should note that single-track trails may close after rain until conditions improve, and all trails close during the November firearms deer season.

location.directions: From Crosby, head north on MN-6 and follow signs to Cuyuna Country State Recreation Area. The park office is located at 307 3rd Street in Ironton.

payload.name: Starr Spring Campground
payload.status_description: Open and operating on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations accepted. Individual sites are $10 per night; the group site is $20 per night, payable on-site.
payload.short_description: Remote BLM campground at 6,300 feet on the southeast slope of Mount Hillers in Utah's Henry Mountains, popular with geology enthusiasts, rock hounds, and late-season hunters.
payload.medium_description: Starr Springs Campground offers 12 individual sites and one group site on the southeast end of Mount Hillers in the remote Henry Mountains. The campground features pit toilets, potable water, picnic tables, fire rings, grills, and a nature trail. At 6,300 feet elevation, it provides access to Mount Hillers (10,723 feet) and the surrounding mesas, with a resident bison herd in the area.
payload.long_description:
Starr Springs Campground sits at 6,300 feet on the southeast slope of Mount Hillers, offering a secluded basecamp in Utah's Henry Mountains. The campground provides 12 individual sites and one large group site, each equipped with picnic tables, fire rings, and grills. Pit toilets and potable water are available on-site, along with a nature trail for exploring the surrounding terrain.

The Henry Mountains are among the most isolated ranges in the Lower 48, with Mount Hillers towering at 10,723 feet above the campground. The area draws geology enthusiasts and rock hounds eager to explore the igneous intrusions and mineralized formations, while late-season hunters come for the free-roaming bison herd that inhabits these highlands. Access is via a dirt road 7 miles west of State Route 276 at milepost 17.

location.directions: From State Route 276 at milepost 17, travel 7 miles west on a dirt road to the campground. From Hanksville, drive 25 miles south on Highway 95, then 17 miles southwest on Highway 276 to milepost 17.

payload.name: Bonita Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with all 23 sites available by reservation only through Recreation.gov. Elevated fire risk March through June may trigger additional fire restrictions without notice. Ground fires and wood collection are prohibited at all times; only purchased firewood or charcoal in provided grills.
payload.short_description: A small, shaded campground in Chiricahua National Monument's 'Wonderland of Rocks' offering 23 reservation-only sites amid pine and oak forest with excellent hiking and birding.
payload.medium_description: Bonita Canyon Campground sits at 5,400 feet in Chiricahua National Monument, surrounded by the dramatic rock spires and hoodoos that define this southeastern Arizona sky island. The 23 sites are nestled in a shaded pine and oak forest along typically-dry Bonita Creek. All sites have picnic tables, raised grills, and access to food storage lockers. The campground serves as a base for 17 miles of day-use trails and world-class birding opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Bonita Canyon Campground occupies a historic, tree-covered setting within Chiricahua National Monument, known as the 'Wonderland of Rocks' for its towering rhyolite columns and balanced rock formations. At approximately 5,400 feet elevation, the campground offers cooler temperatures than the surrounding desert valleys, with summer highs in the 80s and 90s and winter lows often near or below freezing.

The 23 sites include 22 standard non-electric sites ($25/night) and one group tent-only site accommodating 9-24 people ($50/night). Each site features a picnic table, raised charcoal/wood grill, and shared food storage lockers. Flush toilets and potable water are available year-round. No hookups, showers, or dump station exist on site.

The campground provides access to 17 miles of day-use hiking trails through the monument's volcanic rock formations. The 8-mile Bonita Canyon Scenic Drive ends at Massai Point with sweeping views of the Sulphur Springs and San Simon valleys. Birders frequent the area for the exceptional diversity of species in this Madrean sky island ecosystem. Ground fires and firewood collection are permanently prohibited; only purchased firewood or charcoal may be used in the provided grills.

location.directions: From I-10, take exit 336 toward Willcox for 4 miles. Turn left onto AZ-186 E for 31 miles. Turn left onto AZ-181 E for 4 miles. Veer left onto E Bonita Canyon Road into the monument. The campground is 2.5 miles ahead on the left, about 3.5 miles past the entrance station.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: **Elevated Fire Risk:** Fire danger is especially high in southeastern Arizona March through June. Red Flag Warnings and fire restrictions may be implemented without notice. Be prepared to go without a campfire and to cook using an enclosed propane device. **Note: **Ground fires and wood collection are prohibited at all times.

payload.name: Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The park is open year-round. Turkey Oak campground loop is closed for renovations as of March 2026; Sandhill and Lakeview loops remain open and accepting reservations. Reservations via reserve.floridastateparks.org up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Florida state park campground with three loops nestled in a unique ravine ecosystem, featuring water and electric hookups, flush restrooms, hot showers, and lakefront cabins near Keystone Heights.
payload.medium_description: Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park offers camping in one of Florida's most distinctive landscapes, where a deep ravine carved by spring water flows through sandhills. The campground has three loops (Sandhill, Turkey Oak, and Lakeview) with 73 sites total, though Turkey Oak is currently closed for renovations. Sites feature water and electric hookups, concrete pads, picnic tables, and ground grills, with flush restrooms, hot showers, and a dump station nearby. Swimming and paddling are available at Little Lake Johnson.
payload.long_description:
Located in Clay County's sandhills region, Mike Roess Gold Head Branch State Park protects a rare ravine ecosystem formed by Gold Head Branch spring. The 2,099-acre park features dramatic terrain unusual for Florida, with steep slopes dropping into a lush ravine filled with ferns, magnolias, and towering hardwoods. The spring-fed stream flows into Little Lake Johnson, where campers can swim from the beach or paddle along the shoreline.

The campground consists of three loops: Sandhill, Turkey Oak, and Lakeview, collectively offering 73 sites. Each campsite includes a concrete pad, picnic table, and ground grill, with water and 20/30-amp electric hookups at most sites. Select sites (16-18, 58, 59) offer 50-amp service. The Lakeview bathhouse is fully ADA accessible, with paved sidewalks connecting sites 58 and 59. Flush restrooms with hot showers and a centralized dump station serve all camping areas.

Beyond camping, the park offers miles of hiking trails through longleaf pine sandhills and down into the ravine, plus 16 fully equipped lakefront vacation cabins. The park's Civilian Conservation Corps history is evident in the distinctive 1930s-era architecture of the cabins and other structures. Fishing is available at Big and Little Lake Johnson, and the park is known for excellent birding and wildlife viewing.

location.directions: From downtown Keystone Heights at the intersection with SR 100, drive SR 21 north 6 miles to the state park entrance. The park is located at 6239 State Road 21, Keystone Heights, FL 32656.

links.title: Florida State Parks - Gold Head Branch

payload.name: Oak Grove Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The campground was decommissioned in 2024 with restroom buildings removed. The site is no longer available for camping.
payload.short_description: Oak Grove Campground in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest is permanently closed and has been decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service.
payload.medium_description: Oak Grove Campground, located within the Whiskeytown-Shasta-Trinity National Recreation Area near Shasta Lake, is permanently closed. The site was shuttered many years ago and the U.S. Forest Service completed decommissioning in 2024, removing the restroom buildings while leaving concrete foundations and septic systems in place.
payload.long_description:
Oak Grove Campground was a recreation site in the Shasta Lake Ranger District of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County, California. The campground has been closed for many years and is no longer available for public use.

In 2024, the U.S. Forest Service formally decommissioned the site, demolishing the two remaining restroom buildings. The concrete foundations and septic systems were left in place. The decommissioning project was approved in April 2024 and implemented in May 2024.

Campers seeking alternatives should explore other developed campgrounds in the Shasta Lake area or the broader Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

location.directions: From Interstate 15, take Highway 79 East. The campground is on the north side of the highway, across from the fire station. From Temecula, take State Route 79 south for 24.1 miles and turn left at the campground sign.

links.title: USFS Oak Grove Recreation Site Decommissioning Project

payload.name: Shenango Lake Mahaney Spruce Cove Trails End Rolling Meadows Skyline Picnic Shelters
payload.status_description: Day-use facility open for the 2026 season. Shelters are available free first-come, first-served without electric, or can be reserved through Recreation.gov for $51 with electric service. Restrooms and water are seasonal. No overnight camping is permitted at this location.
payload.short_description: Four reservable group picnic shelters at Shenango Lake's Mahaney Recreation Area with electric, flush toilets, drinking water, playground, and disc golf course. Day-use only; no overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: The Mahaney Recreation Area Day Use facility at Shenango Lake offers four covered group picnic shelters: Trails End, Spruce Cove, Skyline, and Rolling Meadows. Each shelter accommodates 42-56 people with tables, grills, and electric service (20-amp max with paid reservation). Flush restrooms and drinking water are available seasonally. The area features an 18-hole disc golf course, children's playground, swing sets, and soccer field. The Seth Myers interpretive hiking trail begins near the Trails End shelter. This is a day-use facility only; overnight camping is not permitted.
payload.long_description:
Located adjacent to the Shenango Dam in Hermitage, Pennsylvania, the Mahaney Recreation Area provides four covered group picnic shelters managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. The Trails End and Spruce Cove shelters are situated in the lower area near the lake access, while the Skyline and Rolling Meadows shelters are in the upper Mahaney Recreation Area. Each shelter can accommodate 42-56 guests depending on table configuration.

Shelters include picnic tables, grills, and electric service (20-amp maximum) available only with a paid reservation. If not reserved, shelters are available free on a first-come, first-served basis without electric. Flush restrooms and drinking water are provided seasonally at adjacent facilities. A children's playground is located next to Spruce Cove, and swing sets and a large soccer field are near Skyline and Rolling Meadows.

The area features an 18-hole disc golf course and the Seth Myers interpretive hiking trail near Trails End. Visitors have access to the lake for boating and fishing. This is strictly a day-use facility; overnight camping is not allowed at these shelters. For overnight accommodations, the separate Shenango Rec Area Campground offers 330 campsites.

location.directions: Take Exit 4B off I-80 and follow Route 18 north approximately 5 miles. Turn left at the stoplight onto Lamor Road (at Dollar General and D'Onofrio's Food Center). Continue 2 miles as Lamor Road becomes South Walnut Street. Turn right onto East High Street and cross the one-lane steel bridge. At the Y intersection, stay straight to enter Mahaney Recreation Area. Veer left; Trails End and Spruce Cove shelters are about a mile down on the right. At the stop sign, turn left for Skyline and Rolling Meadows shelters in the upper area, or continue straight for the boat launch.

payload.name: Aspen Cabin
payload.status_description: This cabin does not appear to be available for public rental. The Santa Fe National Forest officially states they do not currently have cabins for rent, and this listing's web pages redirect to general recreation information.
payload.short_description: Aspen Cabin is a historic cabin listing in Santa Fe National Forest that does not appear to be currently available for public rental.
payload.medium_description: Aspen Cabin is listed in USFS records as a lookout/cabin in Santa Fe National Forest near Santa Fe, New Mexico. However, the official Santa Fe National Forest website states that the forest does not currently have cabins for rent, and specific pages for this listing redirect to general recreation information. The cabin does not appear on Recreation.gov for reservations.
payload.long_description:
Aspen Cabin appears in USFS administrative records as a lookout/cabin facility within Santa Fe National Forest in northern New Mexico. Located at approximately 10,000 feet elevation in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains near Santa Fe, the area is known for aspen groves and access to alpine terrain.

Despite its presence in the USFS database, the official Santa Fe National Forest camping and cabins page explicitly states that the forest does not currently have cabins for rent. The specific USFS web pages for Aspen Cabin redirect to the general recreation portal rather than displaying cabin details, suggesting the facility is not currently operational for public rentals.

Campers seeking overnight accommodations in this area should consider Aspen Basin Campground, a free primitive campground with 10 sites located at the Santa Fe Ski Basin. It offers picnic tables, fire rings, and a vault toilet, though no potable water.

location.directions: Located in Santa Fe National Forest near Santa Fe Ski Basin. Access via Highway 475 (Hyde Park Road) from Santa Fe. Take Bishop's Lodge Road to Artist Road, which becomes Highway 475.

payload.name: Lake Cochrane Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available.
payload.short_description: Nestled between Lake Cochrane and Lake Oliver is an 88-acre playground for campers, anglers, boaters and those who simply enjoy the outdoors.
payload.medium_description: Lake Cochrane Recreation Area sits between Lake Cochrane and Lake Oliver in northeastern South Dakota near the Minnesota border. The campground provides 30 electric campsites and a cabin, with flush toilets, showers (seasonal), potable water, and a dump station. Both lakes offer excellent fishing for walleye, largemouth bass, bluegill, and northern pike, with boat ramps and fishing piers for easy access.
payload.long_description: Nestled between Lake Cochrane and Lake Oliver is an 88-acre playground for campers, anglers, boaters and those who simply enjoy the outdoors. Both the quality of the park and the clear, spring-fed lake bring people to this area. Lake Cochrane Recreation Area was named for the area's first homesteader, Byron J. Cochrane, who settled on the south side of the lake in 1872. The area's rich farmlands and beautiful setting soon attracted other homesteaders You can make it your home too--at least for a fun-filled vacation. Reservations may be made for one of the campsites with electricity or the one-room log-style cabin. Simply book your site online. Bring family or friends to enjoy the scenery of Lake Cochrane Recreation Area while settling into the cabin. Four can sleep comfortably in the set of bunk beds and double bed. Inside is a table and benches; outside, a porch, picnic table and fire grate. Put sleeping bags and linens, cooking utensils for outside cooking and a cooler on your packing list.

location.directions: 10 miles east of Clear Lake off SD Highway 22

links.title: Lake Cochrane Recreation Area - SD GFP
