payload.name: Lake Carthage Lakeside Use Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water hydrants are shut off October 1 through April 30; vault toilets remain accessible. Reservations available through campsd.com.
payload.short_description: Tucked along the shore of Lake Carthage, this small but complete park with a boat ramp, boat beach, 13 electrical campsites and multiple primitive tent sites.
payload.medium_description: Lake Carthage Lakeside Use Area sits on the shores of a 1,300-acre lake in Miner County, offering 13 electrical campsites and several primitive tent sites. The campground provides vault toilets, a boat ramp, and a swimming beach. Water hydrants operate May through September; the nearby town of Carthage has a dump station and shower house.
payload.long_description: Tucked along the shore of Lake Carthage, this small but complete park with a boat ramp, boat beach, 13 electrical campsites and multiple primitive tent sites. In the town of Carthage just a short distance away, campers can use the dump station, and shower house. The Lakeside Use Area provides Campsites that offer picturesque views of the 1,300-acre lake, while anglers enjoy both on- and off-shore fishing.

location.directions: From SD Highway 25, travel 8 miles west on 222nd Street, then turn north on 425th Avenue to the campground entrance.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Roberts Creek East Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opened for the 2026 season on April 10. Operating season runs April through October. Reservations available through mycountyparks.com.
payload.short_description: Full hook-up campground on 300-acre Roberts Creek Lake in central Iowa, offering 55 sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups, modern showers, and access to the no-wake lake.
payload.medium_description: Roberts Creek East Campground sits on the east side of 300-acre Roberts Creek Lake near Pella, Iowa. The campground offers 55 full hook-up sites with 20/30/50 amp electric, water, and sewer connections. Facilities include a modern shower building, flush restrooms, dump station, and playground. The no-wake lake provides excellent crappie fishing and kayaking without motorboat interference.
payload.long_description:
Roberts Creek East Campground is operated by Marion County Conservation and sits along the eastern shore of 300-acre Roberts Creek Lake in central Iowa. The campground features 55 full-service campsites with 20/30/50 amp electric service, water, and sewer hookups. A modern shower building, flush restrooms, dump station, and playground serve campers, with an on-site campground host available for assistance.

The campground is situated on the no-wake side of Roberts Creek Lake, making it ideal for kayakers, canoeists, and anglers seeking a quieter experience. Crappie fishing draws regular visitors to the lake. A paved trail system connects to the area for biking and walking. The park is just 6 miles west of the Dutch heritage town of Pella and offers convenient access to nearby Lake Red Rock recreation opportunities.

location.directions: Located 6 miles west of Pella on County Highway G28, then one half mile north to 1617 Fillmore Drive, Otley, IA 50214.

links.title: Marion County Conservation - Roberts Creek Park

payload.name: Taylor Burn Campground
payload.status_description: This campground has been permanently decommissioned. No camping facilities are available. The site now serves only as a trailhead for access to the Waldo Lake wilderness area.
payload.short_description: Taylor Burn Campground is a decommissioned historic campground in Willamette National Forest, now serving only as a trailhead for the Waldo Lake wilderness area.
payload.medium_description: Taylor Burn Campground was originally constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1939 but has been decommissioned. The site now functions as a trailhead providing access to trails in the Waldo Lake area, including the Erma Bell Lakes Trail and Williams Lake Trail. No camping facilities remain.
payload.long_description:
Taylor Burn Campground was one of the original forest camps in the Willamette National Forest, constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC) in 1939 at a cost of $2,804. The campground served visitors to the Waldo Lake area for decades before being decommissioned.

Today, the Taylor Burn site functions solely as a trailhead area providing access to hiking trails in the surrounding wilderness, including the Erma Bell Lakes Trail and Williams Lake Trail. No camping facilities, restrooms, or water sources remain at this location.

The area is accessed via Forest Road 5898-514 (Taylor Burn Road) off Waldo Lake Road (Forest Road 5897). Visitors seeking developed camping in this region should consider nearby alternatives such as North Waldo Campground.

location.directions: From Oakridge, travel east on Highway 58 for 23 miles to Forest Road 5897 (Waldo Lake Road). Turn left and follow Forest Road 5897 for 11 miles to Forest Road 5898. Continue left on Forest Road 5898 toward North Waldo Campground, then turn right onto Forest Road 5898-514 (Taylor Burn Road). Follow Forest Road 514 for 7 miles to the trailhead.

links.title: Willamette NF Taylor Burn Trail Area

payload.name: Buck Spring
payload.status_description: Currently closed due to the Gifford Fire. A closure order (05-07-53-26-04) was issued April 7, 2026. When open, the campground operates year-round on a first-come-first-served basis with no fees.
payload.short_description: A small, primitive 2-site OHV campground in Los Padres National Forest at 1,640 feet elevation, shaded by oak trees and popular as a fall hunting camp.
payload.medium_description: Buck Spring is a small, primitive campground with just two sites nestled among oak trees and chaparral in the Santa Lucia Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. This free, first-come-first-served campground is popular with OHV users and fall hunters. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring, with vault toilets available but no potable water. High-clearance 4x4 vehicles are recommended due to the dirt access road.
payload.long_description:
Buck Spring is a remote, primitive 2-site campground located at 1,640 feet elevation in the Santa Lucia Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. Shaded by oak trees and surrounded by chaparral vegetation, this campground offers a quiet escape for those seeking backcountry solitude. The campground serves as a popular base camp for fall hunters and OHV enthusiasts.

Each of the two campsites includes a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available on site; however, there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The campground is free with no reservations required, operating on a first-come-first-served basis with a 14-day stay limit.

Access requires a high-clearance 4x4 vehicle via 2 miles of dirt road off Highway 166. OHV users must comply with California law requiring red or green stickers, current registration, and an operating spark arrestor. The McPherson Peak Trail and Aliso Trail both originate from this campground, providing hiking opportunities for those looking to explore beyond camp.

location.directions: Take Highway 166, turn onto Forest Road 30S06, and travel 2 miles on a dirt road. High-clearance 4x4 vehicle recommended.

links.title: Los Padres NF Buck Spring Campground

payload.name: Hungry Mother State Park Shelter And Amphitheater
payload.status_description: This is a day-use rental facility, not an overnight campground. Shelters are available for reservation April 1 through October 31; outside this period they are first-come, first-served. Rental hours are 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. for shelters and noon to 10 p.m. for the amphitheater.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelters and amphitheater at Hungry Mother State Park in Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains, available for group rentals and events.
payload.medium_description: Hungry Mother State Park's Shelter and Amphitheater facilities are day-use rental areas, not overnight campgrounds. The park offers three picnic shelters accommodating 40-75 people each, with charcoal grills, picnic tables, electrical outlets, and fireplaces. The amphitheater seats 60 on wooden benches with additional standing room, located on a scenic island accessible via footbridge.
payload.long_description:
Hungry Mother State Park's Shelter and Amphitheater facilities are day-use group rental areas located within this scenic 2,180-acre park in Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. These facilities are designed for picnics, family reunions, and special events rather than overnight camping.

Three shelters are available for full-day rental from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Shelter 1 accommodates 75 people and is universally accessible near the beach area. Shelter 2 holds 75 people in a more secluded setting near boat rentals. Shelter 3 is the largest and can be rented as two separate sections, each holding 40 people. All shelters include charcoal grills, picnic tables, electrical outlets (April 1 through October 31), fireplaces, and restroom access.

The amphitheater is situated on an island accessible by footbridge and is available noon to 10 p.m. It features wooden bench seating for 60 with room for 40 additional standing. The facility includes one electrical outlet and is suitable for ceremonies, performances, and gatherings.

location.directions: From Interstate 81, take Exit 47. Travel approximately one mile on Route 11 toward Marion. Turn right on Route 16 north and travel four miles to the park. The amphitheater is located on an island accessed by a footbridge near parking lot 5. Shelters are located throughout the day-use area near the lake.

address.full: 213 E Hungry Mother Dr, Marion, VA 24354

links.title: Virginia DCR - Hungry Mother State Park

payload.name: Turkey Run Trailhead
payload.status_description: Open year-round for primitive camping. No reservations, no fees. During general gun deer hunting season, camping is restricted to designated sites only. 14-day per month stay limit applies.
payload.short_description: Primitive FNST trailhead with camp shelter in Osceola National Forest. No water, no restrooms, no fees. Free dispersed camping for backpackers.
payload.medium_description: Turkey Run Trailhead provides access to the Florida National Scenic Trail in Osceola National Forest. The site features a camp shelter with an information kiosk for backpackers. This is a primitive facility with no drinking water or restrooms. Free dispersed camping is permitted along the trail.
payload.long_description:
Turkey Run Trailhead is a primitive access point for the Florida National Scenic Trail in the northwest corner of Osceola National Forest in Columbia County, Florida. The site features an open-sided camp shelter and information kiosk, serving backpackers hiking the FNST. The 11.4-mile trail segment from Turkey Run to Deep Creek offers contrasts between pine flatwoods and bogs, with possible wading after heavy rains.

This is strictly a primitive backcountry facility with no developed amenities. There is no drinking water, no restrooms, and no fee to camp. Dispersed camping is permitted anywhere in Osceola National Forest except Olustee Beach. During general gun deer season, camping is restricted to designated sites only.

Backpackers must pack out all trash and bury human waste at least 6 inches deep and 100 feet from any water source. A 14-day per month stay limit applies throughout the National Forests in Florida.

location.directions: Located on CR 250 approximately 500 feet north of the intersection with SR 250-A in Columbia County, Florida.

address.full: 11454 Gum Swamp Rd NE, Lake City, FL 32055

links.title: National Forests in Florida - Osceola Recreation

payload.name: Cloud Cap Saddle Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season due to snow. Cloud Cap Road (FR 3512) typically opens in early July when enough snow has melted. The campground is first-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground on the north side of Mount Hood at the Cloud Cap Trailhead, offering access to Timberline Trail and Tilly Jane Trail. No potable water; high-clearance vehicle recommended.
payload.medium_description: Cloud Cap Saddle Campground is a small, primitive first-come, first-served campground located at the Cloud Cap Trailhead on Mount Hood's north side. The site provides access to Timberline National Historic Trail #600 and Tilly Jane Trail #600A. Due to its high elevation and the condition of Cloud Cap Road (FR 3512), the campground is subject to seasonal snow closures and typically opens in early July. There is no potable water, and a high-clearance or 4WD vehicle is recommended for the narrow, winding access road.
payload.long_description:
Cloud Cap Saddle Campground is a small, primitive campground situated at the trailhead for some of Mount Hood's most scenic north-side trails. The site serves as the starting point for the Timberline National Historic Trail #600 and Tilly Jane Trail #600A, making it popular with hikers and climbers seeking access to the mountain's northern approaches.

The campground is operated by Lost Lake Resort and is first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted. Amenities are minimal: vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The Historic Cloud Cap Inn, now used by the Hood River Crag Rats search and rescue team, is located just up the road.

Access to the campground requires navigating Cloud Cap Road (Forest Road 3512), a narrow, winding route that may require a high-clearance or four-wheel drive vehicle. The road is subject to seasonal closure due to snow, typically opening in early July and closing in fall depending on conditions. Mount Hood Wilderness restrictions apply to the surrounding area.

location.directions: From Hood River, travel approximately 13.1 miles south on Oregon Hwy 35 and turn right (west) onto Cooper Spur Road, approximately 0.3 miles south of milepost 74. Follow Cooper Spur Road 2.4 miles to Cloud Cap Road (Forest Road 3512) and turn left (southeast). Follow Cloud Cap Road approximately 9.8 miles to the campground. Note: Forest Road 3512 is narrow and winding and may require a high-clearance or 4WD vehicle.

address.full: 12025 Forest Service Road 4400.630, Mount Hood-Parkdale, OR 97041

payload.name: Bromley Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees or reservations. Hikers must treat water from nearby sources and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Backcountry overnight shelter on the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, accessible via a 2-mile hike from Route 11/30.
payload.medium_description: Bromley Shelter is a three-sided backcountry lean-to on the Appalachian Trail/Long Trail, located roughly 2 miles north of the Route 11/30 trailhead near Peru, Vermont. The shelter accommodates 6-10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations. A composting privy is on site and water is available from a nearby stream that must be filtered or treated.
payload.long_description:
Bromley Shelter is a backcountry overnight shelter situated on the coincident Appalachian Trail and Long Trail within Green Mountain National Forest. The shelter lies approximately 2 miles north of the Route 11/30 AT trailhead, along the gradual ascent toward Bromley Mountain summit. Originally constructed as a replacement for the former Mad Tom Notch Shelter, it features a three-sided lean-to design with a covered cooking and seating area.

The shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservation system. Capacity is typically 6-10 hikers. A composting privy is provided on site. Water must be obtained from a nearby stream or spring and should be filtered or treated before drinking, as water purity cannot be guaranteed. Hikers should carry backup shelter as the site frequently fills during peak season.

As with all Long Trail overnight sites, the Green Mountain Club requests stays be limited to two consecutive nights. Dogs are permitted but must be leashed at overnight sites. Hikers must pack out all trash. The shelter is accessible only by foot; there is no vehicle access.

location.directions: Hike the Appalachian Trail/Long Trail north from the Route 11/30 AT trailhead for approximately 2 miles. The trailhead is located between Manchester and Peru, Vermont.

payload.name: Lake Hiddenwood Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for camping. Between October 1 and April 30, the dump station and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. The lake and dam have not been restored following the 2018 flood.
payload.short_description: Melting glaciers carved the valley of Hiddenwood Creek.
payload.medium_description: Lake Hiddenwood Recreation Area is a small campground located 5 miles northeast of Selby, South Dakota. The park offers 13 campsites with both basic and electrical hookup options. Amenities include vault toilets, drinking water, a dump station, playground, and picnic shelters. Note that the lake and dam were destroyed in a 2018 flood and have not been restored, so there is no lake for fishing or swimming.
payload.long_description: Melting glaciers carved the valley of Hiddenwood Creek. Traditionally, this area was home for several American Indian tribes. Early explorers crossed this area on their way between Big Stone Lake and the Rocky Mountains. The first European settlers named the area because no trees were visible on the vast prairie until they reached the crest of the hills overlooking the valley. In 1927, the Department of Game and Fish used a new technique called an earthen dam to make Lake Hiddenwood, one of the first artificial lakes in South Dakota. Unfortunately in 2018 a flood event caused the dam to collapse and drained most of the lake. The park was closed for 4 years and reopened in 2022 when a new access road was built into the park. All 13 campsites have available electrical hookups and the park offers 3 wooded hiking trails totaling 5 miles that surround the lake bed that take you thru a forest of undergrowth with several scenic overlooks.

location.directions: Located 5 miles northeast of Selby, South Dakota, off Highway 12/83.

links.title: Lake Hiddenwood Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Lake Vermillion Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain operational. Reservations can be made up to 90 days in advance. A state park entrance license is required for all motorized vehicles and is not included in reservation costs.
payload.short_description: Known for its clear waters and abundant fish, Lake Vermillion Recreation Area is a popular place among fishermen, boaters and swimmers.
payload.medium_description: Lake Vermillion Recreation Area offers 130 campsites across four campgrounds plus nine camping cabins at a scenic 512-acre reservoir 27 miles west of Sioux Falls. The park features electrical and non-electrical sites, modern facilities including flush toilets, showers, and a dump station, along with excellent opportunities for fishing, swimming, boating, and hiking.
payload.long_description: Known for its clear waters and abundant fish, Lake Vermillion Recreation Area is a popular place among fishermen, boaters and swimmers. During the fall, sportsmen can find waterfowl and upland game within minutes from the park. This 512-acre reservoir is located 27 miles west of Sioux Falls. Three campgrounds with both electrical and non-electrical sites and camping cabins provide plenty of space for overnight visitors. You can hit the beach, rent a canoe or kayak or unpack your fishing gear to haul in a catch of walleye, northern pike, crappie or blue gill. If you choose to stay in a cabin at Lake Vermillion Recreation Area, they are available year-round. Each sleeps four people and is furnished with a set of bunk beds, double bed, table, benches and heating/air conditioning. Lake Vermillion was created by impounding waters from the east fork of the Vermillion River in 1958. The river itself was first noted on an 1801 map by a French trapper who called it Otter Stream. The word vermillion means vivid red color. Some say the stream got its name from the outcropping of red quartzite along its bank. Along with red, you'll find three other R's at Lake Vermillion Recreation Area: rest, relaxation and recreation.

location.directions: Located 5 miles south of I-90 at Montrose Exit 374, approximately 27 miles west of Sioux Falls. Address: 26140 451st Ave, Canistota, SD 57012.

links.title: Lake Vermillion Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: North Point Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by phone.
payload.short_description: Located on the shores of the Missouri River just above Fort Randall Dam, North Point Recreation Area provides a spectacular river view.
payload.medium_description: North Point Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Francis Case just above Fort Randall Dam, about 1 mile northwest of Pickstown off US Highway 281. The park offers 115 electric campsites at $30/night and 7 camping cabins at $60/night. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, vault toilets, drinking water, a dump station, playground, fish cleaning station, and ADA-accessible facilities. The area holds historical significance as Lewis and Clark passed through in 1804, documenting their first prairie dog sightings.
payload.long_description: Located on the shores of the Missouri River just above Fort Randall Dam, North Point Recreation Area provides a spectacular river view. Lewis and Clark came up the river in late-August, early-September in 1804. In this area, they saw their first prairie dogs, which they called "barking squirrels." They were also told to watch for an infrequent phenomenon called "burning bluffs," where the shale ignites and smokes. From the beach, cool off in the water, or see if the fish--walleye, northern pike, bass, crappie and catfish--are biting. Bike or hike on the North Point trail. It's rated easy, with a few moderate grades. Checkout a game for fun and bring a picnic. You'll find a floating fuel dock and convenience store at The Fort Randall Marina onsite at North Point Recreation Area. Modern-day visitors can follow in the footsteps of Lewis and Clark and explore the area. All campsites have electric hookups, with access to a dump station and restrooms equipped with flush toilets and showers. Cabins, open year-round, have a set of bunk beds and a double bed to accommodate four people. Sleep comfortably with air-conditioning and heating. Although cooking is not allowed indoors, a picnic table and fire grate give you outdoor options.

location.directions: Located 1 mile northwest of Pickstown off US Highway 281. Address: 38180 297th Avenue, Lake Andes, SD 57356.

address.full: 801 Lighthouse Island Ave, Lake Andes, SD 57356

links.title: North Point Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: LEGGETT CREEK
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Access may be limited during winter due to snow. No reservations required.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 5 sites along Leggett Creek, offering fishing access to the South Fork Clearwater River in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests.
payload.medium_description: Leggett Creek Campground is a small, free primitive campground with 5 sites located 14 miles west of Elk City along Highway 14. The campground provides public fishing access to Leggett Creek and the South Fork of the Clearwater River, with easy access for larger RVs and trailers. Amenities are minimal with a single vault toilet and fire rings at each site, but no potable water or trash services.
payload.long_description:
Leggett Creek Campground is a rustic, no-fee campground in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, situated along Leggett Creek approximately 14 miles west of Elk City, Idaho. The campground features 5 sites with fire rings and easy access suitable for larger RVs and trailers. A single vault toilet serves the campground.

The primary draw for campers is the excellent fishing access to both Leggett Creek and the nearby South Fork of the Clearwater River. Road access to lower Leggett Creek and the Reed Mountain area is available via Leggett Creek Road #649. The campground operates on a pack-it-in, pack-it-out basis with no trash receptacles or garbage services provided.

The campground is open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis, though winter access may be limited by snow conditions. Campers should bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available on site.

location.directions: Travel east on State Highway 14 toward Elk City. Turn north at the junction with Leggett Creek Road #649, approximately 14 miles west of Elk City. The campground is just west of Road #649.

payload.name: Cyper Creek
payload.status_description: Current operating status cannot be confirmed from official online sources. Contact the Long Cane Ranger District at (803) 624-9471 for availability and reservation information.
payload.short_description: A group campground in the Long Cane Ranger District of the Sumter National Forest in Edgefield County, South Carolina.
payload.medium_description: Cyper Creek is a group campground located in the Sumter National Forest, managed by the Long Cane Ranger District. The campground is situated in Edgefield County, South Carolina, in the western portion of the state near the Georgia border.
payload.long_description:
Cyper Creek is a group campground in the Sumter National Forest, part of the Francis Marion and Sumter National Forests system in South Carolina. The campground is managed by the Long Cane Ranger District, which oversees approximately 120,000 acres across Abbeville, Edgefield, Greenwood, McCormick, and Saluda counties in the western piedmont region of the state.

The Long Cane Ranger District offers a variety of recreational opportunities including hiking, horseback riding, hunting, and fishing in the surrounding forest lands. The district is known for its diverse wildlife habitat and scenic landscapes along the fall line between the piedmont and coastal plain.

location.directions: Cyper Creek Campground is located at 212-256 Wade Morgan Road, McCormick, SC 29835.

address.full: 174 State Hwy S-19-295, Plum Branch, SC 29845

links.title: Francis Marion and Sumter NF Camping

payload.name: Pioneer Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates May through September on a first-come, first-served basis. Potable water becomes available Memorial Day Weekend. No reservations accepted for individual sites; group reservations available for the entire campground.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 5 sites near Soldier Mountain Ski Area in Sawtooth National Forest. Features vault toilets, potable water, fire rings, and access to Soldier Creek trails.
payload.medium_description: Pioneer Campground is a small, free developed campground located next to Soldier Mountain Ski Area in the Sawtooth National Forest. The campground offers 5 sites along Soldier Creek with vault toilets, seasonal potable water, picnic tables, and fire rings. It can also be reserved in its entirety for groups of up to 50 people. The South Fork and North Fork of Soldier Creek trails begin nearby and connect to a major trail network in the Soldier Mountains.
payload.long_description:
Pioneer Campground sits at the base of Soldier Mountain Ski Area in Idaho's Sawtooth National Forest, offering a quiet camping experience along Soldier Creek. This small, developed campground features just 5 sites, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available, and potable water is provided from Memorial Day Weekend through the end of the season.

The campground is free to use and operates on a first-come, first-served basis for individual campers. Groups of up to 50 people can reserve the entire campground for events, utilizing the on-site amphitheater and adjacent picnic area. The setting provides convenient access to the South Fork and North Fork Soldier Creek trailheads along Forest Road 093, which connect to an extensive trail network throughout the Soldier Mountains.

location.directions: From Fairfield, travel north 11 miles on Forest Road 094, bear left at the fork onto Forest Road 093, continue past Soldier Mountain Ski Area. The campground is on the right.

address.full: 1031-1043 N Soldier Creek Rd, Fairfield, ID 83327

payload.name: Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The Ranger Station is closed for renovations as of February 5, 2026; visitors should use the alternate entrance at 10405 Foster Barnes Drive. The campground closes annually for the Florida Folk Festival over Memorial Day weekend, from 9 a.m. Monday before the holiday through 2 p.m. the following Tuesday. Park gates close at sunset.
payload.short_description: Florida state park campground with 45 oak-shaded sites along the Suwannee River, featuring water and electric hookups, fire rings, and access to the Stephen Foster museum and carillon tower.
payload.medium_description: Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park Campground offers 45 spacious, oak-shaded sites near the Suwannee River in White Springs, Florida. Each site includes water and electric hookups, a picnic table, and an in-ground fire ring. Two ADA-accessible restrooms with hot showers and a dump station serve the campground. The park honors American songwriter Stephen Foster and features a museum, the world's largest tubular bell carillon, craft demonstrations, and miles of trails for hiking and biking.
payload.long_description:
Located along the banks of the legendary Suwannee River in White Springs, Stephen Foster Folk Culture Center State Park preserves the cultural heritage of Florida's folk traditions while honoring the songwriter who made the river famous. The 45-site campground sits beneath a canopy of mature oaks, providing welcome shade in Florida's warm climate. Each site offers water and electric hookups, a picnic table, and an in-ground fire ring for evening campfires.

The campground facilities include two ADA-accessible restrooms with hot showers and a dump station for RV waste disposal. All campsites are designated ADA accessible, accommodating visitors with mobility needs. The campground can handle large RVs up to 100 feet in length. Pets are welcome but must remain on a 6-foot leash and be confined to camping units during quiet hours from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.

Beyond camping, visitors can explore the Stephen Foster Museum, climb the 200-foot carillon tower for panoramic views, walk the Craft Square featuring demonstrations of traditional Florida crafts, and enjoy miles of paved and natural trails. The Suwannee River offers excellent paddling opportunities, and fishing is popular along the riverbank. The park hosts the annual Florida Folk Festival over Memorial Day weekend, during which the campground is closed to regular camping.

location.directions: From Interstate 75, follow SR 136 east for 3 miles into downtown White Springs. Turn left at the blinker onto US 41. Make the left along the curve to enter the park. Due to ranger station renovations, currently use the alternate entrance at 10405 Foster Barnes Drive, White Springs, FL 32096.

links.title: Stephen Foster CSO - About the Park

payload.name: RUBY GUARD STATION RENTAL
payload.status_description: Could not verify current status. No official Recreation.gov or USFS listing found for this facility as of May 2026. The facility may no longer be available for reservation.
payload.short_description: Historic guard station rental in the Ruby Mountains of Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, Elko County, Nevada.
payload.medium_description: Ruby Guard Station Rental is listed as a Forest Service facility in the Ruby Mountains of northeastern Nevada's Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. However, no official listing could be found on Recreation.gov or the USFS website, suggesting this facility may no longer be available for reservation or may have been renamed.
payload.long_description:
Ruby Guard Station Rental is reportedly located in the Ruby Mountains of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest in Elko County, Nevada. The Ruby Mountains, sometimes called the "Swiss Alps of Nevada," feature glacially carved peaks, alpine lakes, and elevations exceeding 11,000 feet at Ruby Dome.

Despite extensive research, no official Recreation.gov listing or USFS webpage could be found for this specific facility. The Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest's camping and cabins page lists 59 camping facilities but does not include any guard station rentals. This facility may no longer be available for public reservation, may operate under a different name, or the listing data may be outdated.

Campers interested in this area should contact the Mountain City-Ruby Mountains-Jarbidge Ranger District office in Elko for current information about available facilities in the Ruby Mountains.

location.directions: Not available from the provided data.

payload.name: North Wheeler Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, water systems are shut down and vault toilets remain available. Sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: This small, quiet park is a great get-away for those seeking to relax.
payload.medium_description: North Wheeler Recreation Area is a small, quiet campground on Lake Francis Case between Pease Creek and Platte Creek. The 25-site campground offers both electrical and non-electrical sites, vault toilets, a boat ramp, fish cleaning station, and shore fishing access. It serves as a relaxed base for anglers and boaters exploring this section of the Missouri River reservoir.
payload.long_description: This small, quiet park is a great get-away for those seeking to relax. And, if your idea of relaxation involves a fishing pole, North Wheeler aims to please. With lake access between Pease Creek and Platte Creek, visitors can spend their days on the water and their night relaxing in the campground.

location.directions: 16 miles south of Platte off SD Highway 1804. Nearest town is Geddes.

links.title: North Wheeler Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Campground 3 and the day-use area are open year-round. Campgrounds 1 and 2 are closed November 15 through the last Friday of March for bald eagle winter roosting. Water systems may be shut off October 1 through April 30.
payload.short_description: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area's three campgrounds give visitors a variety of recreational opportunities, from boating to hiking to disc golf.
payload.medium_description: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area sits on the Missouri River just south of Oahe Dam, 5 miles north of Fort Pierre. The park offers 205 campsites across three campgrounds, plus camping cabins, modern cabins, and a group lodge. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, a dump station, and electrical hookups at select sites. Activities include boating, fishing, hiking, and disc golf.
payload.long_description: Oahe Downstream Recreation Area's three campgrounds give visitors a variety of recreational opportunities, from boating to hiking to disc golf. The Corps of Engineers began building the dam in 1948 and in 1962 started generating electricity. It's one of the largest constructed reservoirs in the United States, measuring 231 miles connecting the capital cities of South Dakota and North Dakota. Three camping options are offered at Oahe Downstream Recreation Area: campsites with electricity, camping cabins and a picturesque lodge. Each of the one-room cabins sleep four in a set of bunk beds and a double bed. The Oahe Downstream group lodge was constructed within the recreation area in 2006. With shoreline access, guests are now treated to a beautiful view and private shoreline for swimming, canoeing, or other types of water recreation. The lodge is equipped with a full kitchen with cookware, serving utensils, and appliances and is separated from the "great" room" by a 16 foot serving bar. The 25 x 30 foot "Great" room provides comfortable seating for up to 65 guests. Tables and folding chairs are available on-site. Large grassy areas are also maintained around the lodge and provide ample room for those wishing to tent. A large campfire ring is situated near the river for evening cooking or socializing.

location.directions: Located 5 miles north of Fort Pierre on Highway 1806, on the south side of Oahe Dam. Address: 20439 Marina Loop Road, Fort Pierre, SD 57532.

links.title: SD GFP Oahe Downstream Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Big Bog State Recreation Area Camper Cabins
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Cabins are heated and available in all seasons. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance via reservemn.usedirect.com or by calling 866-857-2757.
payload.short_description: Remote camper cabins in Minnesota's largest peatland, offering year-round rustic lodging with electricity, propane heat, and access to the longest boardwalk in the lower 48 states.
payload.medium_description: Big Bog State Recreation Area's camper cabins provide year-round lodging on the edge of Minnesota's largest peat bog. Five heated cabins with electricity and propane fireplaces sit near the Tamarac River, with access to shower facilities and a 24/7 restroom at the visitor center. Each cabin features a screened porch, deck, outdoor picnic table, and fire ring.
payload.long_description:
Big Bog State Recreation Area offers five winterized camper cabins in the Southern Unit, located along the Tamarac River in remote northern Minnesota. The area encompasses a 500-square-mile peatland, the largest in the lower 48 states, and features the longest boardwalk in the United States stretching one mile into the bog.

The camper cabins are compact 12x16-foot wooden structures equipped with bunk beds, a table, benches, ceiling fan, and propane fireplace for heat. Cabins 2 through 5 each accommodate six guests with two bunk beds (double on bottom, single on top), while Cabin 1 is ADA-accessible and sleeps five. All cabins include electricity, a screened porch, deck, outdoor picnic table, and fire ring. Guests must bring their own linens. Indoor cooking is limited to crockpots and coffeepots only.

The nearby campground provides access to a shower/restroom facility, with a family-style shower/restroom at the visitor center available 24/7 year-round. The Southern Unit also features a boat launch, fishing docks along the river, fish cleaning house, and sandy beach. Reservations can be made up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota DNR reservation system.

location.directions: Located on Highway 72, just north of the town of Waskish, Minnesota.

payload.name: Jacks River Fields Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. January through March, access is only possible from Blue Ridge, GA as Forest Service Road 64 is closed west of the campground. Payment via Recreation.gov mobile app QR code or cash/check in the fee deposit box. 14-day stay limit per 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Secluded 7-site primitive campground on the south fork of the Jacks River in north Georgia's Blue Ridge Mountains, popular with equestrians and hikers seeking a remote forest experience.
payload.medium_description: Jacks River Fields Campground is a remote, first-come, first-served primitive campground with 7 sites situated along the south fork of the Jacks River at 2,700 feet elevation. The campground accommodates horses and mules with corrals and hitching posts available. Each site includes a tent pad, parking spur, picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. The adjacent South Fork Trail provides multi-use access for hiking, biking, and horseback riding into the surrounding Cohutta Wilderness area.
payload.long_description:
Jacks River Fields Campground sits in a small hollow in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia, surrounded by mixed hardwood forests of yellow poplar, oak, hickory, and white pine, interspersed with hemlock and rhododendron. The seven primitive campsites rest along the banks of the south fork of the Jacks River, which eventually flows into the biologically diverse Conasauga River watershed. This remote location served as a thriving mountain community in the late 1800s and early 1900s before becoming part of the national forest.

The campground is particularly well-suited for equestrians, with horse trailer day-use parking, corrals, and hitching posts available. The South Fork Trail begins just an eighth of a mile from the campground, offering a multi-use route for horses, hikers, and mountain bikers along the river. The nearby 45,000-acre Cohutta Wilderness, the largest congressionally designated wilderness east of the Mississippi, provides extensive backcountry opportunities.

Reaching the campground requires navigating over 15 miles of steep, narrow, winding gravel roads. Cell service is extremely limited or nonexistent. Visitors must bring their own drinking water and prepare for a self-sufficient camping experience. Bear-resistant trash receptacles are provided, and vault toilets are available on site.

location.directions: From Ellijay, take Boardtown Road 12 miles to Bearden Road. Turn left onto Bearden Road and follow to Chestnut Gap Road. Turn left onto Chestnut Gap Road and travel 2.8 miles to Old Hwy 2. Turn left onto Old 2 and continue 8.1 miles to the junction with Forest Service Road 64. Turn left and follow FSR 64 for 4 miles. Campground will be on your left.

payload.name: Lake Louise Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets typically remain open through winter.
payload.short_description: Enjoy swimming from the lakeside beach and fishing from the dock.
payload.medium_description: Lake Louise Recreation Area is a South Dakota state recreation area featuring 41 campsites split between a developed section with 32 electric sites and a comfort station, and a primitive area with 8 non-electric sites and vault toilets. The 163-acre prairie lake offers fishing, boating, and swimming at a sandy beach. The 3.2-mile Pheasant Run Trail winds through thick wooded areas offering easy hiking suitable for all ages.
payload.long_description: Enjoy swimming from the lakeside beach and fishing from the dock. The Pheasant Run Trail at Lake Louise Recreation Area is a pleasant, easy hike, suitable for all ages. Bird-watchers and nature observers will be rewarded with glimpses of wildlife and native trees. The whole family can participate in Frisbee golf, horseshoes and other outdoor sports at this "peaceful prairie oasis." Lake Louise was created in 1932, when the south fork of Wolf Creek was dammed. Water depth in this 164-acre impoundment averages nine feet, with a maximum depth of 25 feet. Anglers and hunters come to this area for its abundant game. Lake Louise Recreation Area is located in the heart of pheasant and duck country. If that sounds like the perfect spot for you to spend some time, reservations can be made for campsites, either with or without electricity, during the camping season, and for cabins, open year-round. Furnishings in the cozy cabins at Lake Louise Recreation Area consist of a set of bunk beds, double bed, table and benches. Outside accommodations are a fire grate, picnic table and porch. Air conditioning and heating keep the temperature inside comfortable throughout the year.

location.directions: Located northwest of Miller, South Dakota, off US Highway 14.

links.title: SD GFP Lake Louise Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Nook Bar Camping and Day Use Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Winter camping on the gravel bar is discouraged due to frequent high-water events. Garbage service is only available from Memorial Day through Labor Day; pack out trash outside this period.
payload.short_description: Dispersed riverside camping on a gravel bar along the Wild and Scenic Chetco River in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest. First-come, first-served with basic amenities.
payload.medium_description: Nook Bar offers dispersed tent and small trailer camping on a large gravel bar beside the crystal-clear Wild and Scenic Chetco River. The site provides a vault toilet and seasonal garbage service, with a few shaded spots along the tree line. Campers enjoy direct river access for swimming, fishing, and non-motorized boating in one of Oregon's most scenic river corridors.
payload.long_description:
Nook Bar Camping and Day Use Area provides dispersed camping on a large gravel river bar along the Wild and Scenic Chetco River in southwestern Oregon. The site accommodates tents and small trailers, with a few shaded spots available along the tree line. Campers have direct access to the pristine Chetco River, known for its crystal-clear waters, salmon and steelhead fishing, swimming, and kayaking opportunities.

The area offers basic facilities including a vault toilet and garbage disposal from Memorial Day through Labor Day. Campers must bring their own drinking water as no potable water is available. Campfires are permitted only in developed fire pits. Nearby trails include the Redwood Nature Trail through old-growth redwoods and the Chetco Gorge Trail along the river.

Winter camping on the gravel bar is discouraged due to frequent high-water events that can flood the river bar. The maximum length of stay is 14 days, and quiet hours are enforced between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

location.directions: From Brookings, turn off US Highway 101 onto North Bank Chetco River Road (County Road 784). This becomes Forest Service Road 1376. Nook Bar is approximately 3 miles from the forest boundary on Forest Service Road 1376.

payload.name: Kentucky Dam Village State Resort Park
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from April 1 through October 31. Reservations available up to 12 months in advance. Minimum 2-night stay required on weekends and holidays. Firewood must be sourced from within Marshall County to prevent spread of Emerald Ash Borer.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground at Kentucky Dam Village State Resort Park offering electric and water hookups, modern facilities, and access to Kentucky Lake for fishing, boating, and swimming.
payload.medium_description: Kentucky Dam Village campground sits on the shores of Kentucky Lake near Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area. The campground offers 221 paved campsites with electric and water hookups, including 50-amp service. Four central service buildings provide showers and restrooms, with laundry facilities, a dump station, and grocery store on site. Activities include marina access with boat rentals, an 18-hole golf course, riding stables, and walking trails throughout the park.
payload.long_description:
Kentucky Dam Village State Resort Park is one of three resort parks on the waters surrounding Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area, a 170,000-acre wooded peninsula bound by Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley. The campground provides direct access to one of the finest fishing and boating lakes in the Southeast, with a full-service marina offering boat rentals, fuel, and 36 slip spaces.

The campground features 221 paved campsites with electric (30 and 50 amp) and water hookups. Four central service buildings provide modern restrooms and showers, with laundry facilities available on site. A grocery store and gift shop serve camper needs, and firewood is available for purchase. Note that hookups on most sites are several feet from the pads, so bring a long heavy-duty extension cord and hose.

Beyond camping, the park offers an 18-hole golf course, guided horseback trail rides, tennis courts, a beach swimming area, and extensive walking trails. The on-site restaurant provides dining options, and the convention center hosts events. The campground operates from April 1 through October 31, with reservations available up to 12 months in advance through Kentucky State Parks.

location.directions: From the junction of I-24 and US-62/US-641 (exit 27), travel south 2.2 miles on US-62/US-641 to SR-282, then north 0.5 miles.

payload.name: Malabar Farm State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open with sites available. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance through ReserveOhio. Winter camping rates are $18 per night; spring, summer, and fall rates are $22 per night.
payload.short_description: Primitive 15-site horseman's camp in Ohio's historic Malabar Farm State Park, offering fire rings, picnic tables, vault toilets, and potable water with direct bridle trail access.
payload.medium_description: Malabar Farm State Park Campground is an intimate 15-site primitive camp primarily designed for equestrian visitors, though family campers are welcome. Each site features a fire ring, picnic table, hitching post, and gravel parking pad. Facilities include vault toilets and potable water, but no hookups, showers, or dump station. The campground provides direct access to 12 miles of bridle trails winding through the historic 914-acre farm once owned by Pulitzer Prize-winning author Louis Bromfield.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the Pleasant Valley of Richland County, Malabar Farm State Park Campground offers a rustic camping experience on the grounds of Ohio's only working farm within the state park system. The 15 primitive sites cater primarily to horseback riders but welcome all campers seeking a quiet retreat. Each site includes a gravel parking pad, fire ring, picnic table, and hitching post, with shared vault toilets and potable water available.

The campground serves as a base for exploring 12 miles of bridle and hiking trails that traverse the 914-acre property. The park preserves the legacy of Louis Bromfield, the Pulitzer Prize-winning author who developed the farm using sustainable agricultural practices in the 1940s. Visitors can tour the Big House, explore the working farm with its seasonal livestock, and visit nearby geological features including Rock City Cave's sandstone formations.

The experience here is distinctly primitive with no hookups, showers, dump station, or reliable cell service. Campers should come prepared to be self-sufficient while enjoying the pastoral setting of rolling farmland, mature hardwood forests, and spring-fed streams.

location.directions: From I-71, take exit 165 for US-30 West toward Mansfield. Continue on US-30 for approximately 12 miles, then turn south on SR-603. Follow SR-603 for about 4 miles to Pleasant Valley Road and turn right. The park entrance is at 4050 Bromfield Road, Lucas, Ohio 44843.

payload.name: Mille Lacs Kathio Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-May through October. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance through reservemn.usedirect.com or by calling 866-857-2757.
payload.short_description: Rustic group camping near the Rum River in Mille Lacs Kathio State Park, offering two tent-only sites for groups of 15 to 45 people with basic amenities.
payload.medium_description: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park offers two group campsites located near the Rum River access area. GC1 accommodates up to 15 people at $50 per night, while GC2 handles up to 45 people at $75 per night. Both sites feature multiple tent pads, fire rings with grills, and picnic tables, with access to drinking water and primitive pit toilets. Modern restrooms and showers are not available at the group camp area.
payload.long_description:
Mille Lacs Kathio State Park's group campground provides a rustic camping experience along the Rum River on the southwest shore of Mille Lacs Lake. The two group sites are designed for family reunions, Scout troops, and organized groups seeking a natural setting within the park's 10,500 acres of forests and wetlands. Each site includes multiple tent pads, fire rings with grills, and picnic tables.

The group camp is located near the Rum River access, providing convenient opportunities for canoeing and kayaking. The park offers 35 miles of hiking trails, a 100-foot observation tower with panoramic views, and access to Ogechie Lake. The area holds significant archaeological importance as a National Historic Landmark.

Amenities at the group camp are basic: drinking water and primitive vault toilets are provided, but modern restrooms and showers are not available. Campers should bring their own firewood purchased locally or certified, as moving firewood is restricted to prevent the spread of invasive species.

location.directions: From US-169 N, the park is located on the southwest corner of Mille Lacs Lake, north of Onamia and south of Vineland. The park office is at 15066 Kathio State Park Road, Onamia, MN 56359.

payload.name: North Fork Catherine Creek Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-June through the end of October. Reservations available via Recreation.gov. Forest Road 7785 is not maintained during winter, and snow may block access from October through May. No potable water available; campers must bring their own. Pack-it-in, pack-it-out trash policy.
payload.short_description: Secluded group campground along North Fork Catherine Creek near Eagle Cap Wilderness, ideal for groups seeking a rustic forest setting in the Wallowa Mountains.
payload.medium_description: North Fork Catherine Creek Group Campground is a small, secluded group site nestled along the North Fork of Catherine Creek in a mixed pine and fir forest. With 4 large campsites around a central parking area, it accommodates up to 30 people and serves as an excellent base camp for accessing the nearby Eagle Cap Wilderness trailhead, just one mile upstream.
payload.long_description:
North Fork Catherine Creek Group Campground sits in the southeast Wallowa Mountains within Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, offering a peaceful retreat along the perennial North Fork Catherine Creek. The campground features four large campsites arranged around a central parking area, with picnic tables and fire rings distributed throughout the site. A single vault toilet serves the facility, though campers must bring their own water as none is available on-site.

The campground's prime appeal is its proximity to the Eagle Cap Wilderness. The North Fork Catherine Creek Trailhead lies just one mile upstream, providing hikers and horseback riders direct access to the wilderness area. The trail is closed to motorized vehicles and bicycles. The surrounding mixed conifer forest supports abundant wildlife, making this a popular destination for both summer recreation and fall hunting seasons.

Forest Road 7785 provides access but is not maintained during winter months. Snow can block access anytime from October through May, so campers should check conditions before traveling. The pack-it-in, pack-it-out policy means campers must bring garbage bags and remove all trash.

location.directions: From La Grande, travel south on Highway 203 for 14 miles toward Union. In Union, turn left on East Beakman Street and continue on Highway 203 for 11 miles to Catherine Creek Road (Forest Road 7785). Turn left and proceed 5.5 miles to the campground entrance on the right. From Baker City, travel north on I-84 for 5 miles to exit 282 (Highway 203), turn right and go 27 miles to Catherine Creek Road, then turn right and go 5.5 miles to the entrance.

payload.name: Lake Holland Beach Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for reservations. Park hours are 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. daily. No alcohol is permitted in the park.
payload.short_description: Modern paved campground located just over the dune from Lake Michigan at Holland State Park, featuring 98 campsites with electrical service and easy beach access.
payload.medium_description: Holland Modern Beach Campground sits just over the dune from Lake Michigan at Holland State Park. The modern campground features 98 paved sites, with most offering 30-amp electrical service and 31 sites offering full hookups with 50-amp service, water, and sewer. All camping equipment must remain on the pavement. The campground provides convenient access to the park's sandy beach, iconic Big Red lighthouse views, and various recreational activities.
payload.long_description:
Holland Modern Beach Campground is located at Holland State Park, positioned just over the dune from Lake Michigan's sandy shoreline. The campground features 98 fully paved sites designed to accommodate RVs and campers of all sizes. Most sites provide 30-amp electrical service, while 31 premium sites offer full hookups including 50-amp electric, water, and sewer connections. All camping equipment, including commercial fire pits, must stay on the pavement.

The park is best known for its sugar sand beaches, spectacular sunsets, and views of the iconic Big Red lighthouse across the channel. Campers enjoy easy access to a quarter-mile of Lake Michigan beach, modern restroom facilities with showers, and an accessible playground. The beach house includes concessions, changing areas, and food service during peak season.

Recreational opportunities abound with swimming in buoyed areas, fishing along the channel walkway, paddling on Lake Michigan and Lake Macatawa, and connections to the 20-mile paved Lakeshore Trail. The park offers seasonal nature programs, paddlesport rentals at the nearby Macatawa Boat House, and a sanitation station for RV waste disposal. Registration for the campground is handled at the Lake Macatawa Campground office at 2175 Ottawa Beach Road.

location.directions: From downtown Holland, take Ottawa Beach Road west for approximately 6 miles to reach Holland State Park. The Beach Campground is located near the Lake Michigan shoreline within the park.

payload.name: Big Reservoir Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens around late May for the summer season through early September. Reservations through Recreation.gov must be made at least 3 weeks in advance.
payload.short_description: Forested campground in Tahoe National Forest adjacent to Big Reservoir and Morning Star Campground, offering lakeside access in the Sierra foothills near Foresthill.
payload.medium_description: Big Reservoir Campground sits at the edge of Big Reservoir in Tahoe National Forest, approximately 13 miles northeast of Foresthill. The campground features 19 reservable sites through Recreation.gov, with additional sites available through the adjacent privately-operated Morning Star Campground. Access to the lake and Morning Star facilities requires a separate $25 fee. Nearby Sugar Pine OHV staging area provides miles of off-highway vehicle trails, and Sugar Pine Reservoir offers fishing, boating, and swimming 9 miles away.
payload.long_description:
Big Reservoir Campground is a seasonal Forest Service campground located in the Sierra foothills of Tahoe National Forest, adjacent to the privately-operated Big Reservoir (also known as Morning Star Lake). Sites 1-19 are managed by the Forest Service and reservable through Recreation.gov, while sites 20 and above are operated by Morning Star Campground and require separate booking through their office.

The campground provides vault toilets and drinking water from faucets. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with cooking grille. Firewood is available for purchase at the Morning Star Campground office. Note that use of the lake and Morning Star facilities requires a separate $25 fee not included in your campsite reservation.

The area offers easy access to outdoor recreation including OHV trails at the nearby Sugar Pine staging area and fishing, boating, and swimming at Sugar Pine Reservoir, located 9 miles away. Restrictions prohibit gasoline-powered boats on Big Reservoir, as well as firearms, slingshots, fireworks, and chainsaws.

location.directions: From I-80, take the Foresthill Road exit and continue 17 miles to Foresthill. Continue 9 miles to Sugar Pine Road, turn left and drive 3 miles to Forest Road 24, then continue 3 miles to the campground.

links.title: USFS Tahoe NF - Big Reservoir Campground

payload.name: Spring Valley State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 7 days a week. Check-in starts at 2 p.m., check-out by 11 a.m. Camping limited to 7 days within any 30-day period. Group reservations must be made in advance through Reserve Nevada.
payload.short_description: Group camping area at Spring Valley State Park on the south end of Eagle Valley Reservoir, offering a scenic setting for overnight group gatherings with advance reservations through Reserve Nevada.
payload.medium_description: Spring Valley State Park Group Campground is located at the south end of the 65-acre Eagle Valley Reservoir in Lincoln County, Nevada. The group area accommodates both day and overnight groups and requires advance reservations. The park features primitive restrooms and water access, with camping limited to designated areas only.
payload.long_description:
Spring Valley State Park Group Campground sits at the south end of Eagle Valley Reservoir, a 65-acre impoundment in Lincoln County, Nevada. Named for the abundance of natural springs that irrigate the surrounding lush pastures, the park is dotted with turn-of-the-century stone ranch buildings that provide historic character. The group camping area is designed to accommodate larger parties for both day use and overnight stays, with reservations required in advance through the Reserve Nevada system.

The park offers a primitive camping experience with water and vault restrooms available. Fires are permitted only in provided fire rings and grills; collection of firewood within the park is prohibited. Pets are welcome but must remain on a leash no longer than six feet. Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. The reservoir is stocked with trout and offers a boat launch with ramp, dock, and temporary docking slips for anglers and boaters.

location.directions: From Pioche, Nevada, travel east on State Route 322 approximately 18 miles to the park entrance.

links.title: Spring Valley State Park Official Page
Nevada State Parks Group Use Fees

payload.name: Pines Point Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Operating dates are early May through mid-October. Some sites are first-come, first-served; others are reservable through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Secluded national forest campground on the White River featuring flush toilets, potable water, and excellent fishing and tubing access amid towering white pines.
payload.medium_description: Pines Point Campground sits on the banks of the White River in Michigan's Huron-Manistee National Forests. The 27 family campsites and 5 group sites are surrounded by towering white pines and rolling hills. Float the river's signature "point" by canoe, kayak, or tube in about an hour, or fish for trout, salmon, and sucker. Each site has a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern post with flush toilets and potable water available.
payload.long_description:
Pines Point Campground occupies a scenic stretch of the White River in the Huron-Manistee National Forests of western Michigan. The campground earned its name from the majestic white pines standing watch over the river's bend. With 27 family campsites and 5 group sites capable of hosting 20 guests each, the facility blends solitude with group camping flexibility.

The White River defines the experience here. Paddlers can float the "point" in roughly an hour by canoe, kayak, or tube, with a walk-in canoe landing providing river access. Anglers target trout, salmon, and sucker in these waters. Several campsites overlook the river directly.

Facilities include flush toilets, vault toilets, and potable water from faucets. Each site comes equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern post. The campground operates from early May through mid-October. Some sites are first-come, first-served while others can be reserved through Recreation.gov.

location.directions: From Hesperia, travel south on M-20 for 1 mile. Turn right and travel west on Garfield Road for 5 miles. Turn left and travel south on 168th Avenue for 1.5 miles. 168th Avenue turns into Forest Road 5637; continue on FR 5637 to the campground.

payload.name: Lincoln Rock State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available May 15 through October 15; first-come, first-served October 16-31 and March 1-May 14. Level 1 burn ban currently in effect with fires allowed in designated fire pits only.
payload.short_description: Shaded lakeside campground on Lake Entiat with full and partial hookup sites, boat launch, hiking trails, and views of Rocky Reach Dam.
payload.medium_description: Lincoln Rock State Park offers 67 campsites along the Columbia River just above Rocky Reach Dam. Sites in Loop 3 feature full hookups (water, sewer, electric) while Loop 2 sites have partial hookups (water, electric). The park provides calm waters ideal for paddleboarding and kayaking, two miles of hiking trails, and excellent fishing opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Lincoln Rock State Park sits on the shores of Lake Entiat, a reservoir created by Rocky Reach Dam on the Columbia River. The campground features 67 sites split between two loops: Loop 3 (sites 28-58) offers full hookup sites with water, sewer, and electric connections, while Loop 2 (sites 60-94) provides partial hookups with water and electric. Maximum site length is 65 feet with limited availability for longer rigs.

The park's calm waters make it popular for paddleboarding, kayaking, swimming, and fishing. A boat launch with ADA accessibility provides easy water access. On land, visitors can explore two miles of hiking trails and two miles of biking trails. The day-use area includes picnic shelters, a playground, and sports fields.

Beyond traditional camping, Lincoln Rock offers both standard and deluxe cabins. Deluxe cabins include kitchenettes and private bathrooms with showers, while standard cabins share bathroom facilities in Loop 2. A group camp accommodates up to 50 people for larger gatherings.

location.directions: From East Wenatchee, head north on State Route 97 approximately 7 miles. The park entrance is on the left at 91 Lincoln Rock Park Road.

address.full: 101 Lincoln Rock Park Rd, East Wenatchee, WA 98802

payload.name: Mina Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Flush toilets, showers, and water systems are closed October 1 through April 30; vault toilets remain available during winter months. Reservations available through CampSD.com.
payload.short_description: Nestled along the wooded shores of Mina Lake, Mina Lake Recreation Area is a water-lover's haven with plenty of room for boating, fishing, and swimming.
payload.medium_description: Mina Lake Recreation Area sits on a 737-acre prairie lake in northeastern South Dakota, 12 miles west of Aberdeen. The campground offers 38 electrical campsites with seasonal flush toilets and showers, a swimming beach, fishing pier, boat ramp, and hiking trails. A dump station, playground, and group picnic shelters round out the amenities.
payload.long_description: Nestled along the wooded shores of Mina Lake, Mina Lake Recreation Area is a water-lover's haven with plenty of room for boating, fishing, and swimming. When you leave the water, a spacious campground, hiking trail, and several picnic areas provide hours of family fun. The cozy three-bedroom modern cabin sleeps up to eight people and includes a kitchen, lake access, dock and a dog house with a kennel. Guests at the modern cabin can relax on the deck that over looks beautiful Mina Lake. Reservations for the modern cabin can be made a year in advance. Campground sites are available with electricity, and the one-room cabin is furnished with beds, heating/air-conditioning and electricity. Among the amenities at Mina Lake Recreation Area are a fishing dock, modern comfort station, playground and games ready to check out. Mina was one of the first man-made lakes in northeast South Dakota. Its beginning dates back to the 1930s, when area residents sought relief from years of drought. In 1934, the Mina Dam was completed and the lake was named Shake Maza, a Lakota word for "shaped like a horseshoe." The name never quite caught on and it was later renamed (Mina) in honor of a railroad president's daughter.

location.directions: From Aberdeen, drive 12 miles west on US Highway 12 to the park entrance near the town of Mina.

links.title: Mina Lake Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Bucktail Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round with no fee. First-come, first-served only. The site is only maintained during hunting season; expect very primitive conditions outside hunting season.
payload.short_description: A free, primitive hunter's camp in Kisatchie National Forest open year-round but only maintained during hunting season. Expect very rustic conditions with minimal amenities.
payload.medium_description: Bucktail Hunter Camp is a designated primitive hunter's camp in the Middle Fork area of Kisatchie National Forest, managed by the Caney Ranger District. The site is open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no fee required. Visitors should expect very primitive camping conditions, as the facility is only actively maintained during hunting season.
payload.long_description:
Bucktail Hunter Camp is a designated primitive hunter's camp located in the Middle Fork Unit of the Caney Ranger District within Kisatchie National Forest. Situated in Claiborne Parish near Homer, Louisiana, this rustic site caters primarily to hunters seeking a no-frills camping experience in the piney woods of northwest Louisiana.

The camp is open year-round and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no camping fee. However, visitors should note that the site is only maintained during hunting season, so those visiting at other times will find an even more primitive experience. Potable water is available on-site, but other amenities are extremely limited.

This location is ideal for hunters and outdoor enthusiasts seeking solitude and a back-to-basics experience. The surrounding Kisatchie National Forest offers opportunities for hunting and wildlife observation in a dense forest setting with flat terrain.

location.directions: Travel north on Louisiana Highway 520 and turn east onto Forest Road 913. Bucktail Camp will be on the south side of the road.

payload.name: Carpinteria Sb Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia.com up to six months in advance. Stay limits: 7 consecutive nights March 1 through November 30, 15 consecutive nights December 1 through February 28. Maximum 30 nights per calendar year with a 48-hour vacancy required between stays.
payload.short_description: Beachfront campground 12 miles south of Santa Barbara featuring four camping loops with ocean views, full-hookup RV sites, and direct beach access along the Southern California coast.
payload.medium_description: Carpinteria State Beach offers year-round camping along one of the safest swimming beaches in Southern California. The campground features four loops with 200+ sites ranging from tent camping to full-hookup RV sites in the Santa Rosa Loop. Premium beachside sites in Santa Cruz and Santa Rosa loops put campers steps from the sand. The park features restrooms with hot showers, drinking water, an RV dump station, and accessible facilities throughout.
payload.long_description:
Carpinteria State Beach Campground sits on the coastline 12 miles south of Santa Barbara, offering campers direct access to a wide sandy beach known for its gentle waves and tidepools. The campground is divided into four loops: Anacapa, Santa Cruz, Santa Rosa, and San Miguel. Santa Cruz and Santa Rosa loops feature premium beachside campsites with ocean views, while Santa Rosa Loop is the only area with full hookups (water, 30-amp electric, and sewer).

Each campsite includes a fire ring (except San Miguel beach row) and a picnic table. The park provides restrooms with flush toilets and hot showers in each loop, drinking water, and an RV dump station. Multiple ADA-accessible campsites are available in all four loops, along with accessible restroom facilities. A beach wheelchair is available upon request.

The park enforces seasonal stay limits: 7 consecutive days from March through November, and 15 consecutive days December through February, with a maximum of 30 days per calendar year. Dogs are allowed in the campground on a 6-foot leash but are not permitted on the beach. The nearby town of Carpinteria offers restaurants, shops, and the famous Carpinteria Salt Marsh Nature Park.

location.directions: From U.S. 101, take the Casitas Pass Road exit in Carpinteria. Turn toward the ocean onto Palm Avenue (Highway 224) and follow signs to Carpinteria State Beach.

links.title: CA State Parks - Carpinteria Main Page

payload.name: Dayton State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The RV dump station is closed until further notice for repairs with no estimated reopening date. Check-in starts at 2 p.m., check-out by 11 a.m. Camping limited to 7 consecutive days within a 30-day period.
payload.short_description: Small 10-site campground along the Carson River in historic Dayton, Nevada, offering flush toilets, picnic tables, and barbecues at each site with a 34-foot RV limit.
payload.medium_description: Dayton State Park Campground is a compact 10-site facility nestled along the Carson River, 12 miles east of Carson City. The park offers flush restrooms, drinking water, and trash service. Each site includes a picnic table and barbecue. The campground accommodates RVs up to 34 feet but has no hookups. Fishing access to the Carson River and short hikes to historic Rock Mill Site are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Dayton State Park Campground sits along the banks of the Carson River in one of Nevada's oldest settlements. The small campground offers just 10 sites, providing a quieter camping experience compared to larger state park facilities. Each site is equipped with a picnic table and barbecue, with flush restrooms and drinking water available on-site.

The park's location makes it ideal for anglers targeting walleye, white bass, hybrid wiper, catfish, and trout in the Carson River. Two short trails lead from the campground to the river and to the historic Rock Mill Site, remnants of the area's mining past. The shaded group-use area with picnic facilities is available for day visitors.

The campground can accommodate RVs up to 34 feet but operates as a dry camping facility with no hookups. Reservations can be made through reservenevada.com from 3 days to 11 months in advance. Camping is limited to 7 days within any 30-day period. Pets are welcome but must remain on a leash no longer than 6 feet.

location.directions: Located at 825 US Hwy 50 East, Dayton, NV 89403. From Carson City, drive 12 miles east on US Highway 50.

payload.name: Fish Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground typically opens in June and operates through October. First-come, first-served only; no reservations.
payload.short_description: Remote, primitive tent-only campground with 5 walk-in sites at 3,350 feet elevation near a small lake and the Cle Elum River in Washington's Cascade Range.
payload.medium_description: Fish Lake Campground is a free, primitive campground offering 5 walk-in tent sites at a high elevation location near a small alpine lake and the Cle Elum River. The campground provides vault toilets but no potable water or trash service. Campers should be prepared to pack out all trash and bring their own water supply.
payload.long_description:
Fish Lake Campground offers a backcountry camping experience at 3,350 feet elevation in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The campground features 5 walk-in tent-only sites situated near a small lake that provides fishing opportunities and the scenic Cle Elum River. This is a true primitive camping destination with no fees required.

Facilities are minimal, limited to vault toilets. There is no potable water available, and campers must pack out all trash. The remote location requires driving approximately 11 miles on Forest Service Road 4330 after turning off Highway 903. The road conditions may require high-clearance vehicles.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservation system. It is best suited for self-sufficient tent campers seeking solitude and access to lake fishing and the surrounding forest wilderness.

location.directions: From Cle Elum, WA travel 19 miles northwest on Highway 903/Salmon La Sac Highway. Turn right on Forest Service Road 4330 and travel about 11 miles. Campground is on the right.

payload.name: Hidden Valley Campground
payload.status_description: Open mid-March through mid-December. All sites are first-come, first-served only; no reservations accepted. Bear safety food storage requirements are in effect.
payload.short_description: First-come, first-served campground in the George Washington & Jefferson National Forest, featuring wildflower meadows, trout fishing on the Jackson River, and a secluded mountain valley setting.
payload.medium_description: Hidden Valley Campground offers a peaceful retreat in Virginia's Bath County within the George Washington & Jefferson National Forest. The Jackson River, stocked with trout, flows through the valley surrounded by vast wildflower meadows that attract butterflies and wildlife. All sites are first-come, first-served with vault toilets and potable water available.
payload.long_description:
Hidden Valley Campground sits in a secluded mountain valley within the George Washington & Jefferson National Forest in Bath County, Virginia. The area earned its name from its hidden, tucked-away character amid the Allegheny Mountains. Vast fields of wildflowers blanket the valley, attracting countless butterflies, birds, and other wildlife throughout the warmer months.

The Jackson River winds through the recreation area and is regularly stocked with trout, making this a popular destination for anglers.
