Movie buffs may recognize the landscape as the filming location for the 1993 film Somersby. A historic antebellum-era mansion, now operated as a bed and breakfast, adds to the area's character.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. Sites include picnic tables, and the campground provides vault toilets and potable drinking water from faucets. Campers can pay on-site via the Recreation.gov Scan and Pay mobile app. Dogs are permitted but must remain on a leash no longer than 6 feet. Bear safety food storage requirements are in effect.

location.directions: From the intersection of State Route 39 and US Route 220, follow SR 39 west for about 3.25 miles to State Route 621. Turn right on SR 621 and follow it about 1 mile to Forest Service Road 241 (Hidden Valley Road). Turn left on FSR 241 and follow it about 1.5 miles to Hidden Valley Campground on the left.

address.full: 1531 Hidden Valley Rd, Warm Springs, VA 24484

payload.name: Newton Hills State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain open. Reservations available 90 days in advance through gooutdoorssouthdakota.com.
payload.short_description: Newton Hills State Park's unique dark forest, amidst a vast open prairie, has prompted many legends, including buried gold, robbers' hideouts and horse thieves.
payload.medium_description: Newton Hills State Park Campground sits within one of the largest and oldest woodlands in southeastern South Dakota, a rare forested oasis in the prairie landscape. The campground features 126 campsites with both electric and non-electric options, 11 camping cabins, a modern cabin, and two group lodges. Facilities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. The surrounding park offers a swim beach, fishing piers, extensive trail system, and horse camping facilities.
payload.long_description: Newton Hills State Park's unique dark forest, amidst a vast open prairie, has prompted many legends, including buried gold, robbers' hideouts and horse thieves. But visitors today recognize it as a great place to camp, swim, hike and fish. The park also plays host to folk music concerts and the popular FestiFall in October. The Newton Hills Lodge, built in 1915, served as the historic caretaker's home in Canton, SD, and played an important role in serving the healthcare needs of a variety of patients before being opened to guests. It can sleep up to 12 people and has four bedrooms and two baths. Like the lodge, camping cabins are open year-round. Each cabin accommodates 4 people with a set of bunk beds and a double bed. Both RV and tent sites are available, as well as horse camp sites. A boat ramp, beach and fishing dock let you enjoy water activities at Newton Hills State Park. More than 200 species of birds visit the area each year, and white-tailed deer, wild turkeys, marmots, rabbits, red and gray fox and squirrels are also found within the park. Newton Hills hosts numerous folk music concerts in conjunction with the Friends of Traditional Music. One of the most popular concerts, the Sioux River Folk Festival, is a 3-day event held annually on the first full weekend in August. The popular FestiFall event is held each year on the first Saturday in October. It features many family activities including arts and crafts, kids' games, hay rides and bluegrass music. The pumpkin takes center stage with pumpkin catapulting, pumpkin carving demonstrations and decorated pumpkin contests. Following the FestiFall event, the Candlelight Walk will lead visitors along 2.2 miles of candle-lit trail through the deep woods of Newton Hills. The trail will be solely lit by candles and carved pumpkins.

location.directions: From I-29, take Exit 56 and travel 12 miles east on County Road 140. Alternatively, the park is located 6 miles south of Canton off County Road 135.

links.title: Newton Hills State Park - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Headquarters Hookup
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. Gates open at 8am and close at 10pm with no entry permitted after 10pm. Mountain lions have been spotted in the park; hikers should avoid going alone, especially during dawn and dusk hours.
payload.short_description: Beachside campground in Point Mugu State Park offering flush toilets, coin-operated showers, fire rings, and picnic tables at each site along the scenic Malibu coastline.
payload.medium_description: Headquarters Hookup is a campground within Point Mugu State Park's 13,300-acre expanse along the Pacific Coast Highway. The campground accommodates tents, trailers, and RVs up to 35 feet and features flush toilets, coin-operated showers, potable water, and fire rings with picnic tables at each site. Beach access, over 70 miles of hiking trails, and five miles of rocky bluffs and sandy beaches are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Headquarters Hookup sits within Point Mugu State Park, one of the largest stretches of protected coastline in Southern California. The park spans over 13,300 acres at the western end of the Santa Monica Mountains, where Big Sycamore Canyon meets the Pacific Ocean. Campers have direct access to five miles of rocky bluffs, sandy beaches, and sand dunes, along with over 70 miles of hiking and equestrian trails that wind through native grasslands, coastal sage scrub, and sycamore-shaded canyons.

The campground offers developed amenities including flush toilets, coin-operated showers (bring dollar bills), and potable water from spigots throughout the grounds. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill. The campground can accommodate tents, trailers up to 31 feet, and RVs up to 35 feet with a height limit of 13 feet 6 inches. Pull-through sites are available. An RV dump station is located at nearby Sycamore Canyon Campground, approximately 1.5 miles away.

The park is home to diverse wildlife including deer, bobcats, and mountain lions. Visitors should be aware that mountain lion sightings have occurred in the area; avoid hiking alone, especially between dusk and dawn. Cell service is limited to Verizon coverage only.

location.directions: From Oxnard, head south on Highway 1 (Pacific Coast Highway) for approximately 15 miles. The campground entrance is at 9000 W. Pacific Coast Highway, Malibu, CA 90265.

links.title: Point Mugu State Park - CA State Parks
Santa Monica Mountains NRA Camping - NPS

payload.name: Staunton River Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Camping runs from the first Friday in March through the first Monday in December. A burn ban is currently in effect for Halifax County; no open-air outdoor fires are allowed until further notice. Fire ring use is restricted March 1 through April 30 to 4 p.m. to midnight only.
payload.short_description: Staunton River State Park campground offers 48 sites with electric/water hookups and tent-only options along John H. Kerr Reservoir at the confluence of the Dan and Staunton rivers.
payload.medium_description: Located on 1,597 acres along John H. Kerr Reservoir (Buggs Island Lake), Staunton River State Park's campground features 48 sites ranging from full electric/water hookups accommodating RVs up to 45 feet to primitive tent sites. The park sits at the convergence of the Dan and Staunton rivers, offering access to 17 miles of multi-use trails, fishing, and boating. A heated bathhouse with hot showers, dump station, and laundry facilities serve campers.
payload.long_description:
Staunton River State Park encompasses 1,597 acres along the scenic shoreline of John H. Kerr Reservoir, locally known as Buggs Island Lake, at the confluence of the Dan and Staunton rivers in southern Virginia. The campground provides 48 sites across several categories: four electric/water sites accommodating RVs up to 45 feet, ten electric/water sites for rigs up to 30 feet, twenty electric/water sites for pop-ups and tents up to 20 feet, and thirteen standard tent-only sites without hookups.

Amenities include a heated bathhouse with hot showers, a dump station, laundry facilities, and water spigots throughout. Each campsite features a fire ring, charcoal grill, and picnic table. The park also offers an equestrian campground with pull-through sites accommodating trailers up to 55 feet and covered stalls.

Beyond camping, the park features seven historic CCC-built cabins from the 1930s, 17 miles of multi-use trails for hiking, biking, and horseback riding, and excellent fishing and boating access on the reservoir. The Captain Staunton pool operates during summer months.

location.directions: From South Boston, take U.S. 360 east approximately 8 miles to Route 344. Turn right onto Route 344 and travel 10 miles to the park entrance, located southeast of Scottsburg, Virginia.

payload.name: Rolston Rest Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fee or reservation required. Maximum stay is two consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Primitive three-sided backcountry shelter on the Long Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, offering free first-come, first-served overnight stays for hikers.
payload.medium_description: Rolston Rest Shelter is a rustic Adirondack-style backcountry shelter along the Long Trail near Brandon Gap. The shelter accommodates 6-10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations. Water must be treated or filtered from nearby sources, and a privy is available. This is a hike-in only site suited for Long Trail thru-hikers and backpackers.
payload.long_description:
Rolston Rest Shelter sits at approximately 2,160 feet elevation on the Long Trail within the Green Mountain National Forest. The property spans 2,744 acres of dense forest, headwater streams, and scenic peaks, containing 3 miles of the Long Trail as well as sections of the Catamount Trail and Velomont Trail. Brandon Gap marks the transition between easier southern terrain and more challenging northern sections of the Long Trail.

The shelter is a traditional three-sided Adirondack-style structure that can accommodate 6-10 hikers. A privy is located nearby, and water sources are available but require treatment or filtering before consumption. The site is managed by the US Forest Service in partnership with the Green Mountain Club, which provides caretakers at high-use shelters along the trail system.

Use of the shelter is limited to two consecutive nights. During peak hiking season, shelters frequently fill, so carrying a tent or tarp is strongly recommended. The shelter is accessible only by hiking from Brandon Gap trailhead parking.

location.directions: From Brandon, take Route 73 east for 7.5 miles. Trailhead parking is on the right just before the top of Brandon Gap. The trail starts on the opposite side of Route 73. Note: trailhead parking lot experiences vandalism, so secure valuables.

payload.name: Hurricane Lake North Youth Group Camp Blackwater River State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica up to 11 months in advance. Facility is restricted to organized youth groups with adult chaperones.
payload.short_description: Primitive youth group camp on the north shore of Hurricane Lake in Blackwater River State Forest. Designed for organized youth groups with adult chaperones.
payload.medium_description: Hurricane Lake North Youth Group Camp is a primitive group camping area reserved exclusively for organized youth groups with adult supervision. Located on the north side of 318-acre Hurricane Lake in Blackwater River State Forest, the site offers potable water but no electricity. Campers have access to restrooms, showers, and a boat ramp at the adjacent Hurricane Lake North Campground. Activities include fishing, boating, hiking, and wildlife viewing.
payload.long_description:
Hurricane Lake North Youth Group Camp is situated on the north shore of Hurricane Lake, a 318-acre lake within Florida's largest state forest. The camp provides a dedicated primitive camping experience for organized youth groups accompanied by adult chaperones. The site includes potable water but no electric hookups, fitting its primitive character.

Campers share facilities with the adjacent Hurricane Lake North Campground, which provides restrooms, hot showers, and a dump station. A boat ramp on the north side of the lake offers direct water access for fishing and paddling. Hurricane Lake supports a warm-water fishery managed by FWC.

The surrounding longleaf pine and wiregrass ecosystem supports diverse wildlife. During hunting season from Thanksgiving through mid-February, campers hiking away from the camping area should wear fluorescent orange. Alligators inhabit the lake; swimming is prohibited.

location.directions: Located in northwest Okaloosa County within Blackwater River State Forest, approximately 12 miles northwest of Baker, FL. Access Hurricane Lake North Campground Road off Beaver Creek Road, north of Kennedy Bridge Road.

address.full: 482 Hurricane Lake Entrance Rd N, Baker, FL 32531

links.title: FDACS Recreation Areas - Blackwater River State Forest

payload.name: Cottonwood Spring Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for overnight camping. Day use only. Potable water is available but there are no restroom facilities.
payload.short_description: Day-use only site in Colville National Forest near Conconully with potable water but no restrooms. Overnight camping is not permitted.
payload.medium_description: Cottonwood Spring is a day-use site located in Colville National Forest, approximately 1 mile north of Conconully via Forest Service Road 38. The site offers potable water from faucets but has no restroom facilities. Overnight camping is not allowed.
payload.long_description:
Cottonwood Spring is a small day-use site in Colville National Forest, situated just north of the town of Conconully in Okanogan County, Washington. Despite its listing as a "campground," the site is closed to overnight camping and operates strictly as a day-use facility.

The site provides potable drinking water from faucets, making it a useful stop for visitors exploring the area. However, there are no restroom facilities available. No fees are required to use this site.

To reach Cottonwood Spring, drive through Conconully heading north on County Road 2361, which becomes Forest Service Road 38 at the forest boundary. Continue on FS Road 38 for approximately 1 mile; the site is on the right.

location.directions: From Conconully, drive through town to the north on County Road 2361, which turns into Forest Service Road 38 at the forest boundary. Continue on Forest Service Road 38 for 1 mile to Cottonwood Spring on the right.

address.full: 494 N Fork Salmon Creek Rd, Conconully, WA 98819

payload.name: Rattlesnake Group Campground
payload.status_description: This campground has been permanently decommissioned. The site now operates as Rattlesnake Cove Picnic Site, a day-use only area. No overnight camping is permitted.
payload.short_description: Rattlesnake Group Campground has been decommissioned. The site now operates as Rattlesnake Cove Picnic Site, a day-use only facility on Bartlett Lake in Tonto National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Rattlesnake Group Campground in Tonto National Forest has been permanently decommissioned and no longer offers overnight camping. The location now functions as Rattlesnake Cove Picnic Site, a day-use area on the shores of Bartlett Lake featuring 41 ramadas with picnic tables and grills, vault toilets, and shoreline access. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
Rattlesnake Group Campground was a group camping facility located on Bartlett Lake within Arizona's Tonto National Forest. The campground has been permanently decommissioned and no longer accepts overnight camping.

The site now operates as Rattlesnake Cove Picnic Site, a day-use only facility open from 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. The picnic area offers 41 ramadas equipped with picnic tables and grills, vault toilets, and staircase access to the Bartlett Lake shoreline. No potable water is available on-site.

Campers seeking group camping options in the Tonto National Forest should explore other facilities in the Cave Creek Ranger District or nearby areas around Bartlett Lake.

location.directions: From Carefree, take Cave Creek Road 7 miles, turn right on Bartlett Dam Road and continue for 13 miles, then turn left on FR 459. Travel half a mile on FR 459 and turn right into the site.

address.full: 30806 E Bartlett Dam Rd, Carefree, AZ 85377

links.title: Rattlesnake Cove Picnic Site - Tonto NF

payload.name: Oakwood Lakes State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems including showers and flush toilets may close between October 1 and April 30; vault toilets remain accessible. Reservations available online or by phone 90 days in advance. Maximum consecutive stay is 14 nights.
payload.short_description: Nestled among eight connecting lakes, this park provides a never-ending variety of activities throughout the year, from hiking and swimming, to ice fishing and cross-country skiing.
payload.medium_description: Oakwood Lakes State Park features 139 campsites across two campground loops plus 7 camping cabins and 6 horse campsites, all nestled among eight connecting glacial lakes. The shaded campgrounds offer a mix of electrical ($30/night) and non-electrical ($16/night) sites, with amenities including flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. Activities include hiking, biking, swimming at the beach, fishing, and boating.
payload.long_description: Nestled among eight connecting lakes, this park provides a never-ending variety of activities throughout the year, from hiking and swimming, to ice fishing and cross-country skiing. Shaded campgrounds and picnic areas complement the park's excellent swimming and boating facilities. The park was once used as a summer camp and an annual gathering spot for American Indians. Later, Samuel Mortimer arrived in 1869 and built the log cabin that still stands at the park.

location.directions: From I-29, take Exit 140 and head west. The park is located 7 miles north and 3 miles west of Volga off US Highway 14. Address: 20247 Oakwood Drive, Bruce, SD 57220.

links.title: Oakwood Lakes State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Lake Superior Cart-in Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available via reservemn.usedirect.com up to 120 days in advance. Reservation fees apply ($8 online, $10 phone).
payload.short_description: Secluded cart-in campground with 13 sites along Lake Superior's shoreline at Tettegouche State Park, offering primitive camping with fire rings, picnic tables, and vault toilets.
payload.medium_description: Tettegouche State Park's Lake Superior Cart-in Campground features 13 primitive sites positioned along the Lake Superior shoreline. Sites are located a half mile or less from parking, with large carts provided to transport gear. Each site includes a fire ring, picnic table, and tent pad, with access to vault toilets and water. The campground operates year-round and offers a more secluded experience than the park's drive-in options.
payload.long_description:
The Lake Superior Cart-in Campground at Tettegouche State Park provides a semi-backcountry camping experience along Minnesota's North Shore. The 13 sites are situated near the Lake Superior shoreline, offering dramatic views and a more secluded atmosphere than traditional drive-in camping. Sites are not accessible by motor vehicle but are located within a half mile of parking, and large carts are available at the trailhead to help transport gear.

Each site is equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and tent pad. Campers have access to vault toilets and water. This primitive setup appeals to those seeking a quieter, more immersive experience without a full backcountry commitment. Pets are welcome but must be kept leashed and attended at all times.

Tettegouche State Park is located 58 miles northeast of Duluth along Highway 61 and is known for High Falls (Minnesota's second-tallest waterfall), Shovel Point, and Palisade Head. The Superior Hiking Trail passes through the park, connecting the campground to miles of North Shore hiking.

location.directions: Located at 5702 Highway 61, Silver Bay, MN 55614. The park is 58 miles northeast of Duluth along scenic Highway 61 on Minnesota's North Shore.

payload.name: Province Pond Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served. No reservations. No potable water available; filter or purify water from the pond. Fire danger is currently low in the White Mountain National Forest.
payload.short_description: Backcountry lean-to shelter on the edge of Province Pond in the White Mountain National Forest, accessed via a 1.6-mile hike from the trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Province Pond Shelter is a rustic Appalachian Trail-style lean-to sleeping 6-8 people on the shore of Province Pond. The shelter requires a 1.6-mile hike from the parking area at the end of Peaked Hill Road. Tent camping is available in the open woods behind the shelter. Water must be filtered from the pond and campers should practice Leave No Trace principles.
payload.long_description:
Province Pond Shelter is a backcountry lean-to located on the scenic edge of Province Pond within the White Mountain National Forest. The open-sided shelter sleeps 6-8 campers and provides a classic backcountry camping experience in the forests of eastern New Hampshire near Chatham.

Access requires a 1.6-mile hike from the parking area at the end of Peaked Hill Road (Forest Service Road 450). Beyond the shelter, ample space exists in the surrounding woods for tent camping. An open-air toilet with privacy screen is available, but no potable water exists on site. Campers must filter or purify water from the pond.

The shelter operates first-come, first-served with no reservations or fees. Standard White Mountain National Forest backcountry regulations apply, including restrictions on fires within 1/4 mile of shelters. A bear-proof canister is recommended for food storage.

location.directions: From South Chatham Road, take Peaked Hill Road (Forest Service Road 450) north for 2.6 miles to the parking area at the end of the road. The trailhead is located north of the eastern terminus of Hurricane Mountain Road. Hike 1.6 miles to reach the shelter.

payload.name: Crystal Creek Primitive Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates May through October. Reservations required via Recreation.gov. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights from May 15 through September 15, or 30 days total per calendar year.
payload.short_description: Secluded tent-only primitive campground with two creekside sites in Whiskeytown National Recreation Area, offering shade, bear lockers, and access to nearby waterfalls.
payload.medium_description: Crystal Creek Primitive Campground offers two intimate tent-only sites nestled along Crystal Creek in the northwest corner of Whiskeytown National Recreation Area. Both sites feature heavy tree canopy from fir, maple, and pine providing significant shade and privacy. Each site includes a bear-proof storage locker, picnic table, fire pit with swing-arm BBQ grill, and lamp pole, with a shared ADA-accessible vault toilet. No potable water is available. The campground provides convenient access to Crystal Creek Falls and the James K. Carr Trail to Whiskeytown Falls.
payload.long_description:
Crystal Creek Primitive Campground sits in a forested setting along its namesake creek, 19 miles west of Redding, California, within Whiskeytown National Recreation Area. The two tent-only sites stay relatively cool even during hot summer months thanks to the flowing creek and dense canopy of fir, maple, and pine trees. The burbling year-round creek and heavy shade make this an ideal location for a peaceful retreat.

Each campsite accommodates up to six people and two vehicles, featuring a bear-resistant storage locker, picnic table, metal fire pit with swing-arm barbecue grill, and lamp pole. A single ADA-accessible vault toilet serves both sites. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on-site. The steep unpaved entrance road prohibits RVs, trailers, and any towed vehicles.

Three nearby trails lead to scenic waterfalls, including Crystal Creek Falls and Whiskeytown Falls via the James K. Carr Trail. The Tower House Historic District, located less than five miles away, offers California Gold Rush history including historic buildings, water ditches, and gold panning opportunities. Oak Bottom, eight miles from the campground, provides beaches, lakeside picnicking, and a full-service marina with boat rentals on the 3,200-acre Whiskeytown Lake.

location.directions: From Redding, CA, drive 19 miles west on Highway 299. Turn left on Crystal Creek Road and follow it for 3.5 miles to the campground. The campground will be on the left-hand side of the road down an unpaved driveway. The road beyond the James K. Carr Trailhead becomes dirt and gravel requiring high clearance.

payload.name: HUNT CAMP 80B
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required at least 48 hours in advance via Recreation.gov. Receipt must be on-site. No services at individual sites; potable water available at Delta Work Center on FSR 703.
payload.short_description: Primitive hunt camp in Delta National Forest, Mississippi's only bottomland hardwood forest. Features a graveled pad, fire ring, lantern post, and picnic table amid bald cypress and hardwood terrain.
payload.medium_description: Hunt Camp 80B is one of 57 designated primitive campsites scattered throughout Delta National Forest in Sharkey County, Mississippi. Each site offers a graveled parking pad, fire ring, lantern post, and picnic table. No water or restrooms are available at individual sites; potable water is located at the Delta Work Center on FSR 703, and restroom facilities are along FS Roads 715, 717, 720, and 707.
payload.long_description:
Hunt Camp 80B is a primitive campsite within Delta National Forest, the only bottomland hardwood forest in the national forest system. Located in Sharkey County approximately 10 miles east of Rolling Fork, Mississippi, this site is part of a network of 57 dispersed campsites designed primarily for hunters and outdoor enthusiasts exploring the 60,898-acre forest.

The campsite features a graveled parking pad, fire ring, lantern post, and picnic table. No potable water, restrooms, or other services are available at the site itself. Campers should obtain drinking water at the Delta Work Center on Forest Service Road 703. Restroom facilities are located along FS Roads 715, 717, 720, and 707.

The surrounding landscape features majestic bald cypress trees, bottomland hardwoods, and terrain crisscrossed by bayous, rivers, and lakes. Hunting is cooperatively managed through the Sunflower Wildlife Management Area. ATVs are prohibited at campsites but permitted on designated trails with proper permits. Alcohol is not allowed per Mississippi WMA regulations.

location.directions: Located approximately 10 miles east of Rolling Fork, Mississippi in Delta National Forest. For specific directions, contact the Delta Ranger District Office at 68 Frontage Road, Rolling Fork, MS 39159.

payload.name: Fawn Creek Camp
payload.status_description: No current status information available from official sources. Access roads in this remote area are typically impassable due to snow from late fall through early summer.
payload.short_description: Primitive dispersed campsite in the remote backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests near Dixie, Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Fawn Creek Camp is a primitive dispersed camping area located deep in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. Situated in the remote backcountry near Dixie, this undeveloped site offers a secluded wilderness experience for campers seeking solitude in Idaho's rugged terrain.
payload.long_description:
Fawn Creek Camp is a primitive dispersed camping area located in the backcountry of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in north-central Idaho. The site sits in the remote reaches of Clearwater County near the historic mining town of Dixie, accessible via forest roads that wind through dense conifer forests and rugged mountain terrain.

This undeveloped campsite offers a true backcountry experience with minimal amenities, making it suitable for self-sufficient campers comfortable with primitive conditions. The surrounding Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests encompass over 4 million acres of diverse landscapes including deep canyons, pristine rivers, and dense old-growth cedar forests, providing ample opportunities for hiking, fishing, hunting, and wildlife viewing.

Access to this remote area is limited by seasonal road conditions, with forest roads typically closed by snow from late fall through early summer. Visitors should come fully prepared with supplies as services are extremely limited in this isolated region.

location.directions: From Reedsport, Oregon, take Highway 101 north for 0.25 miles. Turn right onto Smith River Road and travel approximately 25 miles to the site. There is no sign at the site, only an old road that parallels the main road between the road and the river.

payload.name: Beulah Vista Yurt
payload.status_description: Open for summer season reservations. Year-round availability with winter season (December 1 through April 30) reservations opening on the last Monday of October at 8 AM and summer reservations opening in late April. Demand is high; book early.
payload.short_description: Backcountry yurt accommodating 12 guests at 8,860 feet elevation on Utah's north Uinta slope, featuring views of Mount Beulah and accessed via a 2.75-mile non-motorized trail.
payload.medium_description: Beulah Vista Yurt is the largest yurt in the BRORA system, a 24-foot structure sleeping up to 12 people. Located about 2.75 miles from the trailhead at 8,860 feet elevation on the East Fork Bench trail system, it offers views of Mount Beulah on clear days. The yurt is equipped with a wood-burning stove for heat, propane cooking stove, kitchen utensils, bunk beds, and a gas lantern. Guests must bring their own water, food, and sleeping bags.
payload.long_description:
Beulah Vista Yurt is the newest and largest yurt in the Bear River Outdoor Recreation Alliance (BRORA) system, located on the north slope of the Uinta Mountains in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The 24-foot diameter yurt accommodates up to 12 guests and sits at approximately 8,860 feet elevation, accessible via a 2.75-mile non-motorized trail with 474 feet of elevation gain from the East Fork trailhead. On clear days, the yurt offers stunning views of Mount Beulah from the front door.

The yurt is equipped for backcountry comfort with bunk beds (no bedding provided), a wood-burning stove for heat with a stocked woodshed and axes, a propane cooking stove with fuel included, kitchen utensils and cookware, a dining table and chairs, and a hard-wired gas lantern. An outhouse is available nearby. There is no electricity or potable water; guests must pack in their own drinking water or filter from nearby sources.

Access varies by season: cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and fat biking in winter; hiking, biking, or ATV in summer. Snowmobiles are not permitted on the trail. The yurt operates year-round with winter reservations (December through April) opening on the last Monday of October and summer reservations opening in late April. BRORA membership ($20) is required in addition to the nightly rental fee.

location.directions: From Evanston, Wyoming, head south approximately 30 miles to the north slope of the Uinta Mountains. Access is via the East Fork trailhead on the non-motorized East Fork Bench trail system. The yurt is located about 2.75 miles from the trailhead, approximately one mile past the East Fork Yurt on the Lower East Fork Trail.

payload.name: Camp Howe Group Campground
payload.status_description: This facility is not open to the public. It is not a public campground and does not accept reservations or visitors.
payload.short_description: Camp Howe is a restricted facility within Gifford Pinchot National Forest that is not open to the public for camping.
payload.medium_description: Camp Howe is located within Gifford Pinchot National Forest in Skamania County, Washington. Despite its name suggesting a group campground, this facility is not available for public camping and is restricted from public access.
payload.long_description:
Camp Howe is a facility within Gifford Pinchot National Forest in Skamania County, Washington. Although it may be listed in some databases as a group campground, it is not open to the public for recreational camping.

The site does not appear on official U.S. Forest Service campground listings for Gifford Pinchot National Forest and is not available for reservation through Recreation.gov. Campers seeking group camping options in the area should look to nearby public facilities such as Atkisson Group Camp or other developed campgrounds in the forest.

location.directions: Camp Howe is located northwest of Northampton, Massachusetts, within a 52-acre wooded area surrounded by DAR State Forest. Access is primarily for rental groups or youth programs, and the site includes parking for up to 50 vehicles. Follow local signage in Goshen to the Camp Howe entrance.

payload.name: Palisades State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed October 1 through April 30; vault toilets remain available. The park is using a new entrance at 48422 256th Street. Reservations available up to 90 days in advance via CampSD.com.
payload.short_description: Palisades State Park is one of the most unique areas in South Dakota.
payload.medium_description: Palisades State Park offers 111 campsites across two campgrounds along the striking pink Sioux Quartzite cliffs of Split Rock Creek. The park provides both electric (20/30/50 amp) and non-electric tent sites, flush toilets, showers, a dump station, and 10 camping cabins. Rock climbing, hiking, and fishing draw visitors to this unique geological feature in eastern South Dakota.
payload.long_description: Palisades State Park is one of the most unique areas in South Dakota. Split Rock Creek, which flows through the park, is lined with Sioux quartzite formations varying from shelves several feet above the water to 50-foot vertical cliffs. Scenic overlooks and rushing water make Palisades an appealing getaway. The park is popular among campers, photographers, sightseers, picnickers, rock climbers and hikers. A perfect site for weddings, reunions and meeting is the lodge at Palisades State Park, open year-round. It has four bedrooms that sleep up to 12 people and also offers a full kitchen, dining area and relaxation room. The back deck has a great view of the creek and Sioux quartzite rock formations. You can reserve the lodge, a campsite or camping cabin by using the online system. Camp sites come with or without electricity, and the one-room cabins sleep four. Furnishings include a set of bunk beds, a double bed, table and benches, with a picnic table, porch and fire grate outside. For millions of years, Split Rock Creek cut deep gorges through Palisades State Park. Geologists estimate the Sioux quartzite spires are 1.2 billion years old. Five hiking trails twist and turn through these beautiful Sioux quartzite formations and prairie areas. The cliffs and formations at Palisades are used by rock climbers to practice their scaling and rappelling techniques.

location.directions: The park entrance is located at 48422 256th Street near Garretson, South Dakota, approximately 20 miles northeast of Sioux Falls.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Summersville Lake State Park Joe Branch Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season. Reservations are available through the West Virginia State Parks reservation system. Check-in is at 1 p.m. and check-out is at noon.
payload.short_description:
Joe Branch Primitive Campground at Summersville Lake SP is just that, no water, no electricity, just nature at its finest. Snuggled in among the laurels along Joe Branch creek, you’ll find yourself submerged in nature and the forest. There is a bathhouse with two bathrooms, an outdoor sink for washing dishes and utensils, and an outdoor shower. Tent sites do not have parking on-site but there is a parking lot nearby.
West Virginia's newest state park encompasses 177 acres, overlooking the north shore of the beautiful Summersville Lake, the largest lake in West Virginia. At summer pool water level, it covers 2,790 acres, with over 60 miles of shoreline making it a boating and water sports paradise.
payload.medium_description: Joe Branch Campground offers rustic camping at Summersville Lake State Park, West Virginia's first new state park in over 30 years. The 15 primitive sites plus five camper van spots sit among mountain laurels along Joe Branch Creek, providing an immersive nature experience near the state's largest lake.
payload.long_description:
Joe Branch Campground is the most rustic of three campgrounds at Summersville Lake State Park, nestled among mountain laurels along scenic Joe Branch Creek. The campground features 15 primitive tent sites and five designated camper van spots, making it ideal for campers seeking a close-to-nature experience rather than modern amenities. A shared bathhouse with four restrooms, an outdoor dishwashing sink, and an outdoor shower serve the campground.

Summersville Lake State Park opened in May 2025 as West Virginia's first new state park addition in more than 30 years. The 177-acre park sits on the northern shore of Summersville Lake, the state's largest body of water. The lake offers excellent fishing for largemouth and smallmouth bass, walleye, panfish, and catfish, with trout stocked below the dam in spring and fall.

Beyond camping, visitors can explore the Mountaineer Mile trail unveiled at the park's opening, and the historic Carnifex Ferry Battlefield State Park is just a 10-minute drive away. Whitewater rafting on the world-class Gauley River is available year-round for adventure seekers.

links.title: WV State Parks - Camping at Summersville Lake

payload.name: Whitetail Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. Limited services outside Memorial Day through Labor Day. No potable water is available. Access road crosses a low water crossing that may be impassable during high runoff.
payload.short_description: Free, primitive 10-site walk-in campground in the Little Missouri National Grassland with vault toilet, fire grates, and no water or fees.
payload.medium_description: Whitetail Campground is the only free campground on the Little Missouri National Grassland. This rustic 10-site walk-in facility is set in the wooded Whitetail Creek drainage and offers fire grates, a vault toilet, and a large parking area accommodating trailers of all sizes. No potable water or electricity is available. All sites are first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit.
payload.long_description:
Whitetail Campground offers a quiet, primitive camping experience in the wooded Whitetail Creek drainage within the Little Missouri National Grassland. The 10 walk-in sites are free and operate on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Each site has a fire grate, and there is one vault toilet serving the campground. A large parking area accommodates trailers and RVs of all sizes.

This is a pack-it-in, pack-it-out facility with no potable water, electricity, or trash service. Campers must bring all necessary supplies including drinking water. The 14-day stay limit applies. The access road crosses Whitetail Creek via a low water crossing that may become impassable during periods of high runoff, so check conditions before traveling in spring or after heavy rain.

The campground is open year-round, though services are limited outside the Memorial Day to Labor Day season. Pets are allowed but must remain leashed. Campfires are permitted in the fire grates when conditions allow, though fire bans are common during dry periods.

location.directions: From Fairfield, ND, head north on I-85 to just north of town. Turn west on 15th Street. The campground is on the left side of the road approximately 4 miles west of I-85.

payload.name: San Elijo Sb Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations required through ReserveCalifornia. The camp store and laundry facility are currently closed. Check-in at 2:00 PM with no early check-in available.
payload.short_description: Oceanside group campsite at San Elijo State Beach accommodating up to 40 people with full hookups, fire pit, and direct beach access near Cardiff-by-the-Sea.
payload.medium_description: The Grunion Run Group Campsite at San Elijo State Beach is a dedicated group camping area on the scenic San Diego coast. The site accommodates up to 40 people with 10 vehicles and features 6 picnic tables, a fire pit, barbecue grill, and a 50-amp hookup with water and sewer connections. Located along Coast Highway 101 near Cardiff-by-the-Sea, campers have easy access to swimming, surfing, and the San Elijo Lagoon Ecological Reserve.
payload.long_description:
San Elijo State Beach Group Campground, known as the Grunion Run site, offers a unique group camping experience on a narrow stretch of coastal bluff overlooking the Pacific Ocean. The fenced group area can host up to 40 campers with parking for 10 vehicles, though only 2 vehicles may park inside the campsite itself. The site is equipped with 6 picnic tables, a fire pit, a barbecue grill, and a single 50-amp hookup providing water and sewer connections.

The campground sits along Historic Coast Highway 101, approximately three-quarters of a mile north of San Elijo Lagoon's entrance channel. The nearby reef is part of the San Elijo State Marine Conservation Area, making it popular for surfing and tide pooling. The main campground offers restrooms with flush toilets and showers, drinking water, and an RV dump station. Dogs are permitted in the campground but not on the beach.

Reservations are required through ReserveCalifornia. The group site is a pull-through configuration accessed via the northern gate. An extra-long sewage hose is recommended to reach the dump connection. The adjacent beach provides excellent opportunities for swimming, surfing, and enjoying Southern California's mild coastal climate year-round.

location.directions: Exit I-5 at Encinitas Boulevard and head west. Turn left (south) on South Coast Highway 101 and continue approximately 2 miles to the campground entrance.

address.full: 33 S Coast Highway 101, Cardiff By The Sea, CA 92007

links.title: San Elijo State Beach - CA State Parks

payload.name: Christmas Creek Ranch
payload.status_description: Access and availability information for this remote site is limited. The facility is not listed on Recreation.gov and does not appear to operate as a formal rental cabin. No fees are required. Winter access is essentially impossible due to snow and the site's extreme remoteness. Contact the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest for current conditions.
payload.short_description: A remote historic ranch site in the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area along the Snake River corridor in northeastern Oregon, offering primitive backcountry access in one of North America's deepest canyons.
payload.medium_description: Christmas Creek Ranch is a historic homestead site located in the rugged Snake River corridor of Hells Canyon National Recreation Area within the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest. Originally homesteaded by Homer Hayes prior to 1913, this extremely remote location requires self-sufficiency and careful planning. The site is not listed on Recreation.gov and no fees are required.
payload.long_description:
Christmas Creek Ranch is a remote historic ranch site situated in the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area, managed by the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest. The property was originally homesteaded by Homer Hayes sometime prior to 1913, with ranch buildings likely constructed by the Johnson family in the 1930s. Located along the Snake River corridor on the Oregon side just upstream from Dug Bar, this is one of the most isolated sites in the recreation area.

The ranch is classified by the USFS as a "Lookout/Cabin" facility, though it is not currently available through Recreation.gov's reservation system and no fees are required. Visitors should expect primitive conditions and must be entirely self-sufficient. Access is extremely difficult, typically requiring boat travel on the Snake River or lengthy backcountry travel. Winter access is essentially impossible due to snow and terrain.

The surrounding Hells Canyon landscape offers dramatic views of North America's deepest river gorge, with opportunities for wildlife viewing, hiking historic trails, and experiencing the remote character of this protected wilderness area. The Hells Canyon Recreation Collaborative performs ongoing maintenance on the site's facilities.

payload.name: Joy Creek Camp
payload.status_description: No official information is available for this campground. Joy Creek Camp does not appear in current USFS or Recreation.gov databases for the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. The site may be unmaintained, closed, or an informal dispersed camping area.
payload.short_description: Joy Creek Camp is a primitive undeveloped site in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Joy Creek Camp is a primitive camping area located in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in north-central Idaho. The campground is situated in heavily forested terrain typical of the region.
payload.long_description:
Joy Creek Camp is a primitive camping area within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. Located in the rugged and heavily forested landscapes of north-central Idaho, this campground offers a remote camping experience in the national forest. The Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests are known for their vast wilderness areas, pristine water quality, and diverse recreational opportunities.

As a primitive USFS campground, Joy Creek Camp provides basic facilities in a natural setting. The area is typical of national forest campgrounds in this region, offering access to the surrounding forest for hiking, wildlife viewing, and solitude. The campground's remote location makes it ideal for campers seeking a backcountry experience away from developed areas.

Access and availability are seasonal, with winter conditions typically limiting or preventing access from late fall through spring. Campers should be prepared for primitive conditions and practice Leave No Trace principles when visiting this area.

location.directions: From Pierce, Idaho, head west on Main Street, then turn left onto Joy Creek Road. Follow Joy Creek Road for approximately 5 miles to reach the campground entrance.

payload.name: Droz Creek Cabin
payload.status_description: The cabin is available on a first-come, first-served basis and is maintained by the Heart of the Rockies Snowmobile Club. No advance reservations are available. Access is typically best during winter months for snowmobile and backcountry skiing access.
payload.short_description: A backcountry cabin located along Droz Creek near Marshall Pass in the San Isabel National Forest, primarily used for winter recreation access.
payload.medium_description: Droz Creek Cabin, also known as Wood's Cabin, is a backcountry facility maintained by the Heart of the Rockies Snowmobile Club. Located approximately 2 miles from the Marshall Pass road intersection near O'Haver, this cabin serves winter recreationists accessing the Marshall Pass area.
payload.long_description:
Droz Creek Cabin, locally referred to as Wood's Cabin, is a backcountry cabin situated in the San Isabel National Forest near Marshall Pass in Chaffee County, Colorado. The cabin is maintained by the Heart of the Rockies Snowmobile Club and serves as a warming hut and shelter for winter recreationists exploring the Marshall Pass area. Located approximately 2 miles from the main Marshall Pass road intersection below O'Haver, the cabin provides a rustic refuge for snowmobilers, cross-country skiers, and winter adventurers in this high-elevation terrain.

The area around Droz Creek offers access to extensive winter recreation opportunities in the San Isabel National Forest. The cabin's location makes it a popular stopping point for those exploring the historic Marshall Pass route and surrounding backcountry. The remote setting provides a genuine wilderness experience in one of Colorado's scenic mountain ranges.

location.directions: From the intersection below O'Haver on the main Marshall Pass road, travel approximately 2 miles to reach the cabin at Droz Creek.

payload.name: Beegum Gorge Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees. No potable water available; bring your own water supply.
payload.short_description: A tiny, free, tent-only campground near Beegum Creek in Shasta-Trinity National Forest with vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Beegum Gorge Campground is a small, primitive tent-only site nestled near Beegum Creek in the South Fork Trinity River area of Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The partially shaded campground offers a quiet base for exploring the surrounding wilderness. Vault toilets are provided, but campers must bring their own water.
payload.long_description:
Beegum Gorge Campground is a tiny, primitive campground designed for tent campers seeking solitude in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. Located near Beegum Creek in the Hayfork Ranger District, this partially shaded site provides a peaceful retreat and staging area for backcountry adventures, including OHV recreation in the surrounding area.

The campground offers minimal amenities typical of dispersed-style Forest Service sites. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water on-site, so campers must bring an adequate water supply. There is no fee to camp here, making it an economical option for self-sufficient campers comfortable with primitive conditions.

location.directions: From Platina, head east on Highway 36 to Beegum Gorge Road, then proceed south to the campground.

payload.name: Occoneechee State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: The shelters are open for reservations from the first weekend in March through the first weekend in December. Available 8 a.m. until dusk for day-use only. Reservations recommended for weekends.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelters at Occoneechee State Park on Buggs Island Lake. Shelter 1 accommodates up to 35 guests; Shelter 2 holds up to 100 and is ADA-accessible.
payload.medium_description: Occoneechee State Park offers two rentable picnic shelters overlooking John H. Kerr Reservoir (Buggs Island Lake) in southern Virginia. Shelter 1 is a small shelter near the playground accommodating up to 35 people. Shelter 2 is a large, universally accessible shelter that can host up to 100 guests. Both include electricity, lights, and nearby restroom access. These are day-use facilities only, available from 8 a.m. until dusk.
payload.long_description:
Occoneechee State Park's picnic shelters provide group gathering spaces on Virginia's largest lake, John H. Kerr Reservoir (locally known as Buggs Island Lake). The park sits in Mecklenburg County near Clarksville and offers scenic lake views along with access to the park's trails and amenities.

Two shelters are available for reservation. Shelter 1 is a smaller facility near the playground that comfortably accommodates up to 35 people, with a trail leading to lakefront views. Shelter 2 is the larger option, holding up to 100 guests and meeting universal accessibility standards. Both shelters feature electrical outlets, lights, and access to nearby modern restroom facilities.

These are day-use facilities operating from 8 a.m. until dusk. They are not available for overnight use. Guests seeking overnight accommodations at Occoneechee should consider the park's campsites, cabins, yurts, or lodges instead.

location.directions: From Clarksville, VA, take US-58 Business east. Turn right onto VA-364 (Occoneechee Park Road) and continue to the park entrance at 1192 Occoneechee Park Road, Clarksville, VA 23927.

payload.name: Chapparal Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground operates from mid-May through October and is first-come first-served only. No potable water on-site; nearest water is 9 miles east near Baumgartner Campground.
payload.short_description: Primitive riverside campground with 10 sites on the South Fork of the Boise River in Sawtooth National Forest, offering fishing, hiking, and tubing.
payload.medium_description: Chaparral Campground is a small, first-come first-served campground located along the South Fork of the Boise River in the Fairfield Ranger District of Sawtooth National Forest. The campground features 7 single sites and 3 double sites, each with a picnic table and fire ring. Three vault toilets serve the campground. No potable water is available on-site; the nearest water source is 9 miles east near Baumgartner Campground. Popular activities include fishing, tubing, day hiking, and backpacking.
payload.long_description:
Chaparral Campground sits at approximately 5,200 feet elevation along the scenic South Fork of the Boise River, about 3 miles east of the historic mining town of Featherville. This small, no-reservation campground offers 7 single sites and 3 double sites spread among mature forest along the river corridor. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, and three vault toilet restrooms serve the campground.

The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through October, weather permitting. Fees are $6 per night for single sites and $12 per night for double sites. Campers must bring their own drinking water, as no potable water is available on-site. The nearest water fill station is located 9 miles east, just outside Baumgartner Campground along Forest Road 071, and is typically available until late September or early October.

Popular activities include fishing in the South Fork of the Boise River, tubing on the river, day hiking, and backpacking into the surrounding Sawtooth National Forest. Pets are allowed but must remain leashed or contained. OHVs are permitted only for campground access. Horses and pack animals are not allowed in the campground.

location.directions: From Highway 20, travel north on Forest Highway 61 (Pine-Featherville Road) approximately 30 miles to the town of Featherville. From there, travel east on Forest Road 227 approximately 3 miles to Chaparral Campground.

payload.name: Jonathan Dickinson State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 365 days. Park hours are 8 a.m. until sundown daily. The swim area is closed. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through the Florida State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Large Florida state park campground along the Loxahatchee River offering 142 sites across two campgrounds with full hookups, restrooms with hot showers, and diverse outdoor recreation.
payload.medium_description: Jonathan Dickinson State Park features two distinct campgrounds: Pine Grove (90 sites) near the entrance with full hookups including sewer, and River Campground (52 sites) near the Loxahatchee River. Both have modern restrooms with hot showers, laundry facilities, picnic tables, and fire rings. The 10,500-acre park offers hiking, biking, paddling, and boat tours.
payload.long_description:
Jonathan Dickinson State Park spans over 10,500 acres of Florida scrub habitat along the Loxahatchee River in Martin County. The park offers two family campgrounds: Pine Grove Campground with 90 sites located near the ranger station, and River Campground with 52 sites situated 4 miles from the entrance near the river. Pine Grove features full hookups with 50-amp electric, water, and sewer at each site, while River Campground offers electric and water hookups.

Both campgrounds include large tiled restrooms with hot showers and washer/dryer facilities. Each campsite has a picnic table and either a standing grill or fire ring with cooking grate. A dump station is available at Pine Grove Campground. The park's concession offers boat rentals, kayaks, canoes, bikes, firewood, and guided pontoon boat tours on the river.

Recreational opportunities include over 44 miles of multi-use trails for hiking and mountain biking, paddling the designated Florida Paddling Trail, freshwater fishing, and wildlife viewing. The historic Trapper Nelson homestead is accessible by boat or hiking trail.

location.directions: From I-95 southbound, take Exit 87A and go east on Indiantown Road to US 1. Turn left (north) on US 1. The park entrance is 5 miles ahead on the left at 16450 SE Federal Hwy, Hobe Sound.

payload.name: Mcclendon Spring Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations accepted. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Semi-developed BLM campground near Malta, Idaho, offering primitive camping in the Cotterel Mountains at a historic California Trail emigrant resting spot.
payload.medium_description: McClendon Spring Campground is a free, semi-developed BLM site located approximately 5 miles northwest of Malta in Idaho's Cotterel Mountains. This historic location served as a resting place for emigrants traveling the California Trail. The primitive campground provides basic amenities and access to hiking, hunting, fishing, horseback riding, and OHV trails in the surrounding public lands.
payload.long_description:
McClendon Spring Campground sits in the Cotterel Mountains of south-central Idaho, managed by the BLM Burley Field Office. The site holds historical significance as a favored resting spot for emigrants traveling the California Trail during westward expansion. Today it serves as a base for exploring the surrounding public lands.

The semi-developed campground offers primitive camping with minimal facilities. Activities include hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, fishing, and hunting for upland birds and deer. OHV use is permitted in designated areas. The remote location provides mountain views overlooking the Malta valley.

This is a first-come, first-served campground with no reservations accepted. Campers should come prepared with their own water supply and plan to pack out all trash. The site is accessible via Highway 77 west of Malta, following posted signs.

location.directions: Located approximately 5 miles northwest of Malta, Idaho. Follow signs from Highway 77 west of Malta.

payload.name: Illahee Camping Area
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed and unusable. No facilities are operational. There is no indication of a planned reopening date.
payload.short_description: Closed USFS campground on the Lower Rogue River near Foster Bar in the Wild Rogue Wilderness area of southwestern Oregon.
payload.medium_description: Illahee Camping Area is a primitive Forest Service campground situated along the Lower Rogue Wild and Scenic River, approximately 34 miles downstream from Grave Creek and one mile upriver from Foster Bar. The campground is currently closed and unusable, with no operational facilities.
payload.long_description:
Illahee Camping Area lies within the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest in Curry County, Oregon, along the Lower Rogue Wild and Scenic River. The remote location is accessed via a winding 33-mile drive from Gold Beach on County Road 375 (Agness-Illahe Road). Historically, the campground served as a base for hikers on the Rogue River National Recreation Trail and anglers targeting Chinook salmon, coho salmon, steelhead, and cutthroat trout.

The campground is currently closed and in a state of disrepair. When operational, it featured vault toilets and seasonal drinking water available from May through September, with camp hosts staffing the facility during that period. The site is surrounded by forested terrain within the Wild Rogue Wilderness corridor.

Nearby Foster Bar remains accessible and provides an alternative trailhead with parking for those looking to hike the Rogue River Trail. The area sees significant variation in weather, with temperatures ranging from around 30°F in winter to 85°F in summer.

location.directions: From Gold Beach, OR, take the road on the south side of the Rogue River just before the bridge (Forest Route 33/County Road 375) east approximately 33 miles through Agness to Illahe. The campground is located about 2.5 miles past Foster Bar.

payload.name: Pelican Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by phone.
payload.short_description: Naturalists enjoy the migrating birds and vast numbers of prairie grasses and wildflowers at Pelican Lake Recreation Area.
payload.medium_description: Pelican Lake Recreation Area is a South Dakota state recreation area located 9 miles southwest of Watertown in Codington County. The campground features 76 spacious sites with 50-amp electric service, two camping cabins, and 7 horse camp sites. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. The park offers an ADA-accessible fishing pier, swim beach, boat ramp, kayak rentals, a 14-target archery range, and over 5 miles of hiking and horseback riding trails through prairie and woodland.
payload.long_description: Naturalists enjoy the migrating birds and vast numbers of prairie grasses and wildflowers at Pelican Lake Recreation Area. Winter enthusiasts appreciate the park's cross-country ski trails, snowshoeing and ice fishing. Pelican Lake is a popular stopping point for migrating waterfowl. Each fall, geese and ducks use the lake's open waters as a resting area. A variety of shore birds spend their entire summer in or near the park. Most noticeable are the large white pelicans that frequent the lake. Pelicans were so numerous when the region was first settled that the lake was named in their honor. An observation tower on one of the hiking trails gives visitors a bird's-eye view of the area. The park also has an archery range and course including practice target ranging 10 to 70 yards with an elevated shooting platform. The course is an NFAA approved 14-station course winding through native prairie.

location.directions: 9 miles southwest of Watertown off US Highway 212

links.title: SD GFP Pelican Lake Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Pease Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed October 1 through April 30; vault toilets remain available during winter months.
payload.short_description: With almost 600 acres to explore and easy access to the Missouri River's Lake Francis Case for great fishing, Pease Creek Recreation Area is a popular day use and camping park.
payload.medium_description: Pease Creek Recreation Area sits on nearly 600 wooded acres above Lake Francis Case on the Missouri River. The campground offers 23 electric campsites and 5 horse campsites with flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. Boat ramps provide direct access to excellent walleye and bass fishing, while hiking and horse trails wind through the bluffs above the lake.
payload.long_description: With almost 600 acres to explore and easy access to the Missouri River's Lake Francis Case for great fishing, Pease Creek Recreation Area is a popular day use and camping park. The wooded terrain provides shaded campsites and hiking opportunities on the bluffs above Lake Francis Case, a reservoir behind Fort Randall Dam. It offers a secure and time-saving way to plan your vacation at Pease Creek Recreation Area. Select an electrical site or a non-electrical horse camp site. Campers will find comfort stations with showers and flush toilets, drinking water and picnic shelter. Fisherman should pack their gear to reel in walleye, northern pike, bass, crappie and catfish. A boat ramp, fish-cleaning station and fishing dock are there to help anglers find and prepare their catch. The Pease Creek Multi-Use Trail is open for hikers, equestrians, bikers, cross-country skiers and those on snowshoes. The three-mile route is moderate to difficult, consisting of gentle rolling hills and several steep grades. To discover more of the terrain of South Dakota, visit the North Point Recreation Area, North Wheeler Recreation Area and Randall Creek Recreation Area.

location.directions: Located 9 miles south of Geddes, SD. From Lake Andes, travel 11 miles west on SD Highway 1804.

links.title: SD GFP - Pease Creek Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Pickerel Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From October 1 through April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations accepted online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by phone.
payload.short_description: Noted for its cool, spring-fed waters, Pickerel Lake is one of the deepest natural lakes in the state.
payload.medium_description: Pickerel Lake Recreation Area sits on the shores of one of South Dakota's deepest natural lakes, a 955-acre spring-fed body of water with exceptionally clear, cool waters. The park offers 65 electric campsites across two campgrounds (East and West), plus camping cabins and a modern cabin. Full amenities include flush toilets, showers, potable water, a dump station, boat ramps, fishing piers, and ADA-accessible facilities throughout.
payload.long_description: Noted for its cool, spring-fed waters, Pickerel Lake is one of the deepest natural lakes in the state. The 955-acre lake bears an American Indian name meaning "where you spear long fish." Visitors to the Pickerel Lake Recreation Area can try their hand at reeling in a catch, as well as swimming, hiking and other outdoor activities. Choose from among the options of an electrical or basic campsite, or a snug one-room cabin. The log-style cabins are open year-round, with air conditioning and heating to keep the indoor temperature comfortable. Each is furnished with beds for four people (a set of bunk beds and a double bed), table and benches. You'll be able to use the fire grate and picnic table for dining outdoors. If you're at Pickerel Lake Recreation Area fishing for walleye, northern pike, crappie, perch and bass, the fishing dock, fish-cleaning station and fishing pole checkout will come in handy. Canoes and kayaks can be rented, and games are available for use at the park. A hike on the Glacial Mounds Trail shows several examples of how glaciers formed the landscape of the area, and the Ponderosa trail provides visitors with the chance to surround themselves with the delightful sight and smell of pine trees.

location.directions: Located 10 miles north of Waubay off US Highway 12. Nearest town is Grenville, SD.

links.title: SD GFP Pickerel Lake Recreation Area

payload.name: Pierson Ranch Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Pierson Ranch Recreation Area, 4.
payload.medium_description: Pierson Ranch Recreation Area is a 60-acre South Dakota state park situated below Gavins Point Dam, just 4 miles west of Yankton. The campground features 67 campsites with 50-amp electric hookups and two one-room log-style cabins. Amenities include flush toilets and showers (seasonal), vault toilets year-round, drinking water, a dump station, playground, basketball court, 18-hole disc golf course, and hiking/biking trails. The area provides shore fishing access and proximity to Lewis and Clark Lake.
payload.long_description: Pierson Ranch Recreation Area, 4.5 miles west of Yankton, opened in 1959 and is the oldest campground in the area. It was the first campground to be constructed after Gavins Point Dam was completed. The area offers 67 50-amp electric campsites and 2 one-room log-style cabins. Cabins have accommodation for four people, including air conditioning/heat and electricity. Park amenities include a large day-use area with tennis/pickle ball courts, 18-hole disc golf course, soccer goals, non-profit youth group tent area and 2 large picnic shelters that are popular for family reunions and large group picnics.

location.directions: 4 miles west of Yankton off SD Highway 52. Address: 31144 Toe Road, Yankton, SD 57078.
