payload.name: Yakima River Canyon Campgrounds
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available May 1 through September 30 via Recreation.gov. First-come, first-served October 1 through April 30. Construction at Big Pines and Roza during summer 2026 may result in temporary closures of up to two weeks; exact dates will be posted when schedules are finalized.
payload.short_description: Four BLM campgrounds along the scenic Yakima River Canyon offering riverside camping, Blue Ribbon trout fishing, and wildlife viewing amidst dramatic basalt cliffs.
payload.medium_description: The Yakima River Canyon Campgrounds consist of four BLM-managed sites—Umtanum, Lmuma Creek, Big Pines, and Roza—spread along 27 miles of the Yakima River between Ellensburg and Yakima. All sites feature vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and trash service but no potable water or hookups. The canyon is renowned for its bighorn sheep viewing, Blue Ribbon catch-and-release trout fishing, and Class 1 family-friendly floating.
payload.long_description:
The Yakima River Canyon Campgrounds encompass four developed Bureau of Land Management recreation sites along Washington State's Scenic Highway 821. Big Pines is the largest with 42 campsites and a non-motorized boat launch. Roza offers 6 shaded sites near Roza Dam. Umtanum has 18 sites and a historic footbridge providing the only pedestrian crossing to the west side of the river. Lmuma Creek is the smallest with 7 campsites and a scenic overlook.

The gentle Yakima River winds through massive basalt cliffs rising over 2,000 feet and rolling desert hills, creating excellent habitat for bighorn sheep, birds of prey, and mule deer. The river is classified as a Blue Ribbon trout stream with catch-and-release fishing only. Summer floating from Umtanum to Roza is popular, as the Class 1 water has no rapids.

All sites are primitive with vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, and dumpsters, but no potable water or hookups. Campers are limited to 7-day stays, 10 people, and 2 vehicles per site. Dogs must be leashed.

location.directions: Located along Washington State Scenic Highway 821 (Canyon Road) between Ellensburg and Yakima. Umtanum is near milepost 16, Lmuma Creek near milepost 12, Big Pines near milepost 8, and Roza near milepost 7.

photos.name: The beautiful Yakima River winds its way through the scenic Yakima River Canyon in Washington State.
The Yakima River flows through the stunning Yakima River Canyon in central Washington.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Our facility will be undergoing construction that could impact the availability of some campsites for a few weeks in the summer of 2026. Your reservation maybe cancelled if it conflicts with the construction period.

payload.name: Sullivan Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Minnesota state forest campgrounds operate from the first Saturday in May through the second Sunday in September. No advance reservations; first-come, first-served with payment required before occupying a site via Yodel portal. Maximum stay is 14 days during the primary season.
payload.short_description: A rustic 11-site state forest campground on Sullivan Lake in Minnesota's Finland State Forest, offering lakeside sites with vault toilets, drinking water, and first-come first-served camping.
payload.medium_description: Sullivan Lake Campground is a small, primitive campground nestled in Minnesota's Finland State Forest, about 26 miles north of Two Harbors. The 11 drive-in campsites are spread along the forested shoreline of Sullivan Lake, providing scenic water views and a quiet retreat. Sites include picnic tables and fire rings, with vault toilets and a hand-pumped well available. The campground offers carry-in boat access to Sullivan Lake.
payload.long_description:
Sullivan Lake Campground is a peaceful 11-site state forest campground located in the Finland State Forest of Lake County, Minnesota. Situated about 26 miles north of Two Harbors and roughly seven miles from Lake Superior's North Shore, the campground offers a rustic camping experience on the shores of Sullivan Lake.

The naturally-surfaced campsites are spread along the forested shoreline, providing scenic views of the lake from a wooded setting. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground features vault toilets and a hand-pumped well for drinking water. A carry-in boat launch provides access to Sullivan Lake for fishing and paddling. There are no hookups or showers.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis at $17 per night. The road serving the campsites has a tight turnaround circle at the end, making shorter vehicles more practical. One ADA-accessible campsite, toilet, and well are available.

location.directions: From Two Harbors, take County Road 2 north for 26 miles to County Road 15. Turn left (west) and continue 0.5 miles, then turn left (south) at the Sullivan Lake Road entrance.

payload.name: Ore Hill Tent Site
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours a day. No reservations or fees required. First-come, first-served. No potable water on site.
payload.short_description: Primitive backcountry tent site in White Mountain National Forest with two tent pads, a central fire ring, and a privy at the former Ore Hill Shelter location.
payload.medium_description: Ore Hill Tentsite is a free, primitive backcountry camping area in the Pemigewasset Ranger District of White Mountain National Forest. The original Ore Hill Shelter burned down in 2011 and was converted to a tent site with two primitive tent pads, a central fire ring where the shelter once stood, and a privy. A water source is located 250 feet south via a side trail, though it is not potable and must be treated before drinking.
payload.long_description:
Ore Hill Tentsite occupies the former location of Ore Hill Shelter, which burned down in 2011. Located in the Pemigewasset Ranger District near Warren, New Hampshire, this backcountry site offers a rustic camping experience in White Mountain National Forest.

The site features two primitive tent pads and a central fire ring situated where the shelter once stood. A privy provides basic sanitation facilities. Water can be found 250 feet south of the site via a side trail, but this is a backcountry water source and must be treated before drinking.

As a dispersed backcountry site, Ore Hill Tentsite requires no reservations or fees. Campers should arrive prepared with their own drinking water or water treatment capability, and follow Leave No Trace principles including packing out all trash.

location.directions: Access the Ore Hill Tent Site via the Appalachian Trail. From NH Route 25C, head southbound on the white-blazed trail, passing the summit of Ore Hill. The tent site is located along this route.

payload.name: Key Bridge
payload.status_description: Access to Key Bridge from the south is currently affected by the Key Road highway bridge replacement project. Contact the Long Cane Ranger District at (803) 637-5396 for current access conditions and permit requirements.
payload.short_description: Primitive hunt camp in Sumter National Forest's Long Cane Ranger District, serving as an access point for Turkey Creek paddling and offering basic camping facilities.
payload.medium_description: Key Bridge is a primitive hunt camp located at the border of Edgefield and McCormick counties in the Long Cane Ranger District of Sumter National Forest. The camp serves as a key access point for the Turkey-Stevens Creek Canoe Trail and offers basic facilities for hunters and paddlers exploring the diverse habitats along Turkey and Stevens Creeks.
payload.long_description:
Key Bridge Hunt Camp is a primitive camping area in the Long Cane Ranger District of Sumter National Forest in South Carolina, situated at the county line between Edgefield and McCormick counties. The camp serves as the midpoint access for the Turkey-Stevens Creek Canoe Trail, which features steep hardwood bluffs, floodplain forests, and small marshy areas along the southeastern portion of the ranger district.

Primitive camping is allowed at Key Bridge with a permit from the Long Cane Ranger District. The area is popular with hunters during big game and turkey seasons, as well as paddlers using the Turkey-Stevens Canoe Trail segments between SC Highway 283 and Modoc Bridge. Contact the Long Cane Ranger District at (803) 637-5396 for current conditions and permit information.

location.directions: From McCormick, take SC 28/US 221 South to Plum Branch. Turn left onto SC 283, go approximately 3.5 miles, then turn right onto Key Road (SC 138). The site is approximately 4 miles on the right before the bridge.

payload.name: Platte Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. From October 1 through April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; only vault toilets remain operational. Reservations available online at campsd.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Fishing and water recreation draws a quieter crowd to Platte Creek Recreation Area to enjoy Lake Francis Case on the Missouri River.
payload.medium_description: Platte Creek Recreation Area sits on Lake Francis Case along the Missouri River in Charles Mix County, South Dakota. This quieter alternative to nearby Snake Creek offers 36 campsites with electric hookups available, plus boat ramps, a swim beach, fish cleaning stations, and playground. The campground operates year-round, though water systems and flush toilets close October through April.
payload.long_description: Fishing and water recreation draws a quieter crowd to Platte Creek Recreation Area to enjoy Lake Francis Case on the Missouri River. Visitors to Platte Creek enjoy natural features similar to those at Snake Creek, but from a quieter campground with similar amenities. The earliest maps refer to this stream as Fish Creek. After the 1880s, the creek was renamed to honor Bernard Pratte, who operated a fur post near the mouth of the creek. A spelling error forever changed the name to Platte Creek. It was in this area, also, that Lewis and Clark were told to watch for the "burning bluffs."

location.directions: From Platte, SD: Drive 8 miles west and 10 miles south via SD Highway 44. Alternatively, take Highway 50 south 6 miles then west 8 miles.

links.title: SD Game, Fish & Parks - Platte Creek Recreation Area

payload.name: Joe T. Fallini Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Sites are first-come-first-served with payment via Recreation.gov scan-and-pay app or cash/check fee envelopes. 14-day stay limit.
payload.short_description: BLM campground on Mackay Reservoir with full RV hookups, vault toilets, dump station, and boat ramp. Views of the Lost River Range with fishing, boating, and ice fishing.
payload.medium_description: Joe T. Fallini Recreation Site sits on the banks of Mackay Reservoir in central Idaho, offering the only full RV hookups in the Challis Field Office. The campground features 26 sites across two loops (Grouse and Chukar) with electric and water hookups, fire rings, picnic tables, and shade shelters. A boat ramp provides reservoir access for fishing, water skiing, and jet skiing, while ice fishing draws visitors in late winter.
payload.long_description:
Named for BLM Idaho State Director Joseph T. Fallini (1959-1970), this campground occupies a scenic location on Mackay Reservoir with striking views of the Lost River Range and Mt. McCaleb. The site underwent major reconstruction in 2004/05 to accommodate modern RVs and improve universal accessibility.

The Grouse Loop contains 14 single RV sites with electric and water hookups, plus 4 tent-only sites with central water access. The Chukar Loop adds 4 double RV sites and 4 single RV sites, all with hookups. Eight RV sites and all tent sites have shade shelters. Five sets of vault toilets serve the campground, along with an RV dump station. A group shelter and four day-use shelters are available for picnicking.

Mackay Reservoir supports boating, jet skiing, water skiing, sailing, and fishing. A county-operated boat ramp and docks provide reservoir access. An interpretive trail offers wildlife viewing and nature walks. Ice fishing is popular during late winter when the reservoir freezes.

location.directions: From Mackay, Idaho, travel north on Highway 93 for approximately 6 miles. The campground is on the west side of the highway.

links.title: BLM Joe T. Fallini Recreation Site

photos.name: Overview of campground with Lost River Range in background.
Ice fishing huts on the reservoir.

payload.name: WEST END DISPERSED CAMPING
payload.status_description: Open for dispersed camping. No restrooms or potable water available. Campers must be self-contained and pack out all trash. 14-day stay limit within any 28-day period.
payload.short_description: Primitive dispersed camping on the western shore of Island Park Reservoir with boat ramp access and fishing opportunities in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest.
payload.medium_description: West End Dispersed Camping is a primitive camping area on the edge of Island Park Reservoir, a large 8,400-acre impoundment of the Henry's Fork of the Snake River. The area offers a boat ramp and fishing access but no developed amenities. Campers must be fully self-sufficient with their own water, waste disposal, and fire equipment.
payload.long_description:
West End Dispersed Camping sits along the western shore of Island Park Reservoir, approximately 60 miles north of Rexburg in the Caribou-Targhee National Forest. The reservoir covers 8,400 acres and supports fishing, motorized boating, and water skiing. A boat ramp is available at West End, making it a convenient staging point for reservoir recreation.

As a dispersed camping area, West End provides no developed facilities. There are no restrooms, potable water, trash service, or established campsites with amenities. Campers must bring all supplies and pack out all waste following Leave No Trace principles. Campsites should be located at least 100 feet from water sources and human waste must be disposed of at least 200 feet from water, trails, and camps.

The standard 14-day stay limit applies within a 28-day period, after which campers must relocate at least 5 road miles away. Campfires are permitted using only dead and down wood from the ground, and fires must be fully extinguished before leaving.

location.directions: From Harriman State Park, turn west on Green Canyon Road and go 9.5 miles.

payload.name: Grayson Highlands State Park Shelters Campground
payload.status_description: The shelters are listed as day-use facilities available 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. according to Virginia State Parks. Reservations are made through the Virginia State Parks reservation system. Hickory Ridge Campground reopened May 15, 2026 after extended renovation closures.
payload.short_description: Covered picnic shelters at Grayson Highlands State Park with grills, picnic tables, and restroom access in Virginia's high-country wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Two reservable shelters at Grayson Highlands State Park offer covered group gathering spaces in Virginia's highest state park. Shelter One accommodates 100 people with grills, picnic tables, water fountain, and electric hookup. Shelter Two (The Barn) also holds 100 under cover with additional outdoor capacity. Both provide access to park restrooms.
payload.long_description:
Grayson Highlands State Park sits at elevations above 4,500 feet in the Mount Rogers highlands of southwest Virginia, offering two rentable picnic shelters for group gatherings. The park is known for its wild ponies, alpine-like meadows, and access to the Appalachian Trail.

Shelter One accommodates up to 100 guests and includes grills, picnic tables, a water fountain, and an electric hookup. Shelter Two, known as The Barn, can hold 100 people under cover with space for an additional 100 around the shelter when a special permit is obtained. Both shelters provide access to park restroom facilities.

The park features a visitor center with a gift shop offering camping supplies, snacks, and local goods. The surrounding area includes access to over 9,000 hiking trail miles connecting to the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area and Appalachian Trail.

location.directions: From I-81, take Exit 45 at Marion. Follow US-16 South for approximately 25 miles to Volney. Turn right onto US-58 West and continue about 8 miles. Turn right onto Grayson Highland Lane and follow to the park entrance.

address.full: 2324 Mill Creek Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

payload.name: Seedhouse Group Site
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. The campground operates mid-June through mid-October, weather dependent. Reservations are required and can be made through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Group campsite near the Elk River accommodating up to 100 guests with primitive tent sites, a picnic pavilion, and access to Mt. Zirkel Wilderness hiking.
payload.medium_description: Seedhouse Group Site is a reservation-only group campground in the Routt National Forest, about 25 miles north of Steamboat Springs. The site accommodates up to 100 guests across 8 primitive tent sites, each with fire rings and picnic tables. A 20-person picnic pavilion, group fire ring, bear-proof food storage, and vault toilets are provided. RV trailers up to 30 feet can be accommodated, though no hookups are available. The Elk River offers trout fishing nearby, and the Continental Divide Trail is accessible via a short connector trail.
payload.long_description:
Seedhouse Group Site provides a private mountain setting for large gatherings at 8,000 feet elevation in the Routt National Forest. Located near the Elk River and just miles from Steamboat Springs, the campground serves as a basecamp for fishing, hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding in the Park Range. The nearby Mt. Zirkel Wilderness offers excellent backcountry opportunities.

The facility features 8 primitive tent sites with campfire rings and picnic tables, plus a sheltered pavilion that seats 20 guests. A group fire ring provides a central gathering spot. Bear-proof food storage lockers and trash receptacles are provided for visitor safety. Vault toilets are available on site. Note that potable water is not available; campers should bring their own drinking water.

The group site can accommodate RV trailers up to 30 feet, though no hookups are provided. Visitors may also enjoy nearby Steamboat Lake State Park or explore the extensive trail systems throughout the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests.

location.directions: Take US Highway 40 to County Road 129 north on the west side of Steamboat Springs. Continue for 16 miles, through the town of Clark and across the Elk River, and turn right on County Road 64/Seedhouse Road. Proceed approximately 7.5 miles and look for Seedhouse Campground on the right. Continue past the campground and turn right to access Seedhouse Group Site.

photos.name: Seedhouse Group Site, one of several picnic tables & fire rings in meadow
Seedhouse Group Campsite picnic pavilion, hand pump, & bear box
Seedhouse Group Site fire rign, picnic tables, bear box
View of Mount Zirkel Wilderness Area early winter on drive to Seedhouse Group Site

payload.name: Roy Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Full services including flush toilets and showers typically operate May through September. Between October 1 and April 30, water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available through reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Roy Lake State Park is known for its excellent fishing, but you don't have to be an angler to enjoy all this park has to offer.
payload.medium_description: Roy Lake State Park in Marshall County features 101 campsites split between two campgrounds on the shores of a 460-acre glacial lake. Amenities include electrical sites, flush toilets, showers, a dump station, drinking water, and boat ramps. The park operates year-round, though water systems may close between October 1 and April 30.
payload.long_description: Roy Lake State Park is known for its excellent fishing, but you don't have to be an angler to enjoy all this park has to offer. Visitors will find sandy beaches, campgrounds, picnic areas, boat ramps and a variety of trails to keep them busy. Plan to enjoy all the park offers by camping overnight. Two campgrounds at Roy Lake State Park provide electrical and basic sites, modern comfort stations with showers and flush toilets and dump station. Snuggle into a charming camping cabin that sleeps four in a set of bunk beds and double bed. Savor a meal outdoors cooked on the grill and served at the picnic table. Fishermen will find the facilities they need: boat ramp, fishing dock, fishing pole checkout and fish-cleaning station. The earliest known inhabitants of Roy Lake were members of the Woodland Culture, who built large burial mounds. Artifacts dating between 900 and 1300 A.D. have been found near the park. The Roy (or Roi) family is credited with building the area's first white settlement. Local American Indians called the crops planted along the lakeshore the "Roy Planting" and the name persisted.

location.directions: From Lake City, travel west on SD Highway 10. The park entrance is located on the north side of Roy Lake. Address: 11545 Northside Drive, Lake City, SD 57247.

links.title: Roy Lake State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Shadehill Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems and some facilities may be closed from November 30 through April 30; contact the park at 605-374-5114 for current conditions during winter months.
payload.short_description: Nestled on the shores of Shadehill Reservoir, Shadehill Recreation Area offers opportunities to enjoy land- and water-based activities.
payload.medium_description: Shadehill Recreation Area sits on the shores of Shadehill Reservoir, 12 miles south of Lemmon off SD Highway 73. The campground offers 85 campsites with electrical options, seven camping cabins, and a group lodge sleeping 12. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, a dump station, boat ramps, swim beach, and fish cleaning stations.
payload.long_description: Nestled on the shores of Shadehill Reservoir, Shadehill Recreation Area offers opportunities to enjoy land- and water-based activities. The reservoir is one of western South Dakota's few large lakes. The dam, built in 1951 by the Bureau of Reclamation, creates more than 5,000 surface acres of water to enjoy. Give yourself plenty of time to explore the area by reserving a campsite, cabin or the three-bedroom lodge. The three-bedroom lodge at Shadehill Recreation Area is a favorite for family retreats and hunting groups. The furnished lodge sleeps up to 12 people and is air-conditioned and heated. It can be reserved a year in advance. The cabins, which accommodate four people, also have heating, air conditioning, electricity and a fire grate and picnic table outside. Campsites all come with electricity and access to comfort stations with showers and flush toilets. To take advantage of the large inviting lake at Shadehill Recreation Area, guests may hit the beach, use the boat ramp and fish for walleye, smallmouth bass and crappie. The town of Lemmon, 12 miles away, is home to the Petrified Wood Park and Museum and the annual Boss Cowman Rodeo Celebration.

location.directions: Located 12 miles south of Lemmon on South Dakota Highway 73.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Sheps Canyon Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems and showers close seasonally between October 1 and April 30; vault toilets remain available year-round. Reservations available through CampSD.com up to one year in advance.
payload.short_description: Nestled along Sheps Canyon Bay, Sheps Canyon Campground is the newest campground on Angostura Reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Sheps Canyon Recreation Area is the newest campground on Angostura Reservoir, located southeast of Hot Springs in the Black Hills region. The campground offers 22 electrical sites with 50-amp hookups, 40 non-electrical sites, and 11 horse campsites. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, drinking water, dump station, WiFi, and boat ramp access. The recreation area also features a three-bedroom group lodge and camping cabins.
payload.long_description: Nestled along Sheps Canyon Bay, Sheps Canyon Campground is the newest campground on Angostura Reservoir. It offers great access to the boat ramp and excellent shore fishing opportunities. Sheps Canyon Lodge: This lodge was originally located at the US Army Ordnance Depot at Provo, SD, (active from 1942 to 1968), and served as a commander's quarters. The home was purchased at auction and moved to its present location in 1996 by Sam and Diane Hill. This property was sold to the State of South Dakota in October of 2012. Situated near the lodge is a full log bunkhouse, which was originally used as a schoolhouse in the northern Black Hills near Engelwood. It is now a camping cabin. The lodge affords great views of Angostura Reservoir to the east, along with surrounding areas of the southern Black Hills.

location.directions: From Hot Springs, travel 6 miles south on SD Highway 71, then 5 miles east on Sheps Canyon Road.

address.full: 13031 Shep's Canyon Rd, Hot Springs, SD 57747

links.title: Sheps Canyon Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: HUGHES MILL
payload.status_description: Open and operating first-come, first-served with no reservations. Stage 1 Fire Restrictions are in effect on the Magdalena Ranger District from May 8, 2026 through August 31, 2026, which may prohibit or limit campfires.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground at 8,100 feet elevation in the Magdalena Mountains with just 2 designated sites and dispersed camping, serving as the trailhead for the challenging 7-mile hike to Mt. Withington Lookout.
payload.medium_description: Hughes Mill is a remote, primitive campground in Cibola National Forest's Magdalena Ranger District at 8,100 feet elevation. The site offers 2 designated campsites plus dispersed camping opportunities for those seeking solitude in the Magdalena Mountains. It serves as the trailhead for the strenuous 7-mile hike to Mt. Withington Lookout, the highest point in the forest.
payload.long_description:
Hughes Mill Campground sits at 8,100 feet in the Magdalena Mountains of Cibola National Forest, offering a primitive camping experience for those willing to venture off the beaten path. With only 2 designated campsites and additional dispersed camping available, this small facility provides solitude that larger campgrounds cannot match.

The campground serves as the primary trailhead for the challenging 7-mile hike to Mt. Withington Lookout, making it popular with hikers seeking to summit the highest point in the Cibola National Forest. The Hughes Mill Trail also connects to Forest Road 138, providing a 5.1-mile route open to horseback riding.

Facilities are minimal: a vault toilet is available but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The site operates first-come, first-served with no reservations accepted. Access is via US 60 and Forest Road 549, located 26 miles southwest of Magdalena.

location.directions: From Magdalena, travel 26 miles southwest via US 60 and Forest Road 549.

payload.name: Crooked River Campground #4
payload.status_description: Open year-round with no fee, though winter access may be restricted by snow. First-come, first-served with no reservations. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with four tree-screened sites near a fishing pond and the Crooked River in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests.
payload.medium_description: Crooked River Campground #4 is a small, free primitive campground offering four tree-screened camping pads at 3,960 feet elevation. The site features a small fishing and swimming pond and easy access to Crooked River for trout fishing and gold panning. Good for large visitor parties and serves as a base camp for big game hunting in the area.
payload.long_description:
Crooked River Campground #4 is a primitive, no-fee campground located in the Highway 14 Corridor of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Idaho County. Situated at 3,960 feet elevation, the campground offers four camping pads that are screened by trees for privacy, making it suitable for larger visitor parties seeking a secluded wilderness experience.

The campground features a small on-site pond ideal for fishing and swimming, with easy access to Crooked River nearby. Anglers can pursue trout in the river, and gold panning opportunities exist in the area. The location also serves as a solid base camp for big game hunting during season.

This is a true primitive camping experience with no developed amenities. Campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash. The campground is technically open year-round but may be inaccessible during winter months due to snow on the access road.

location.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south on Crooked River Road #233 and travel approximately 2.5 miles.

payload.name: Eastern Lake Campground 1 Point Washington State Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through ReserveAmerica. Maximum stay is 14 nights within a 30-day period. Active bear area; store food properly. Wear blaze orange during hunting seasons.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent-only campground in Point Washington State Forest with 4 sites along the Eastern Lake Trail system. No RVs, no water hookups, pack-out trash required.
payload.medium_description: Eastern Lake Campground 1 is a small primitive tent-only campground within Point Washington State Forest, located about 9 miles south of Freeport in Walton County. With just 4 sites, the campground offers a quiet forest experience along the Eastern Lake Trail system. Amenities are minimal: vault toilets, fire rings, and picnic tables are available, but there is no potable water, electricity, or showers. All trash must be packed out.
payload.long_description:
Eastern Lake Campground 1 sits in the heart of Point Washington State Forest, a 15,000-acre preserve known for its longleaf pine sandhills, scrub habitats, and coastal dune lakes. The campground provides direct access to the Eastern Lake Trail system, which offers 3.5-, 5-, and 10-mile loop options for hiking and mountain biking. Eastern Lake itself is a rare coastal dune lake and a popular spot for paddling.

This is a primitive tent-only campground with 4 designated sites. RVs and trailers are not permitted. Each site has an 8-person occupancy limit, with a maximum 14-night stay within any 30-day period. The forest has an active black bear population, so campers must store food in approved containers or inside vehicles. During hunting season, wearing blaze orange is advised.

The campground operates year-round on a reservation system through ReserveAmerica, with bookings available up to 11 months in advance. At under $10 per night, it's one of the more affordable camping options along Florida's Emerald Coast, though the trade-off is minimal infrastructure and pack-it-out policies.

location.directions: From the intersection of US 98 and US 79: head west on US 98 for 15.1 miles to Forest Road 2. Follow signs 2.7 miles to Forest Road 7. The campground is 1 mile down FR 7 on the left.

address.full: 3957 Forest Road 11, Santa Rosa Beach, FL 32459

links.title: Florida State Forests ReserveAmerica - Eastern Lake Campground 1

payload.name: Frisco Camp
payload.status_description: This site is officially listed as a day-use picnic area by the Forest Service. Whether overnight camping is permitted is unclear from official sources. Contact the Clifton Ranger District at (928) 687-8600 for current use policies.
payload.short_description: A primitive day-use picnic area along the San Francisco River in the Clifton Ranger District of Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests, Greenlee County, Arizona.
payload.medium_description: Frisco Camp Picnic Site is a small, primitive recreation area located along the San Francisco River in the Clifton Ranger District of Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests. The site offers a scenic spot for day-use activities including picnicking, fishing, and wildlife viewing at approximately 6,300 feet elevation.
payload.long_description:
Frisco Camp Picnic Site is a primitive recreation area situated along the San Francisco River in the remote Clifton Ranger District of the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests in Greenlee County, Arizona. At approximately 6,300 feet elevation, the site provides a forested setting with a mix of trees and open spaces.

The site is officially designated as a picnic area by the U.S. Forest Service, though some sources suggest limited primitive camping may be available. Visitors should contact the Clifton Ranger District directly to confirm current use policies. The area is free to use, with no reservations accepted.

Facilities are minimal at this remote location. Visitors should come prepared to pack out all trash and bring their own water supply. The San Francisco River provides opportunities for fishing and wildlife viewing in this relatively undeveloped corner of the national forest.

location.directions: Frisco Camp Picnic Site is located in the Apache-Sitgreaves National Forests near Morenci, Arizona. From Morenci, take US Route 191 north for approximately 13 miles; the campground will be on the right.

payload.name: Ferris Ford
payload.status_description: Illahe Campground is currently closed. Recent reports indicate the absence of signage, an abandoned pay station, and overgrown facilities. The campground's reopening date is unknown.
payload.short_description: Historic Cedar Bark House in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest, approximately 15 miles south of Powers, Oregon.
payload.medium_description: Ferris Ford is the site of a historic Cedar Bark House in Coos County, located within the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest. The structure is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and was formerly part of the Ferris Ford Work Center.
payload.long_description:
Ferris Ford is home to a historic Cedar Bark House, a unique structure located approximately 15 miles south of Powers, Oregon, in the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest. The site was once the location of the Ferris Ford Work Center, an expansion of a former experimental forest headquarters in the 1960s. The Cedar Bark House is the only remaining structure from the original site and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The Forest Service undertook restoration efforts on this historic structure, with plans to make it available to the public as a recreational rental. The cabin represents a significant piece of regional history and offers a distinctive overnight experience in a remote forest setting.

The area is situated in the coastal mountains of southwestern Oregon, providing access to the natural beauty and recreational opportunities of the Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest.

location.directions: From Gold Beach, Oregon, take Forest Route 33 east for 31.1 miles to Foster Bar/Rogue River trail signs. Bear right onto Curry County Route 375 and continue 2.5 miles to the campground sign. Bear right into the campground.

payload.name: Greer Crossing Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations. Potable water and trash collection available April 1 through November 1; outside this window, bring your own water and pack out trash. Quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Combined vehicle and trailer length cannot exceed 60 feet.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground on the Eleven Point National Wild and Scenic River in the Missouri Ozarks, offering 19 sites with vault toilets and seasonal water. Popular launch point for floating the river.
payload.medium_description: Greer Crossing Campground sits along the Eleven Point National Wild and Scenic River in Mark Twain National Forest. The 19-site campground (16 single, 3 double) provides a secluded, wooded setting with vault toilets and seasonal potable water. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. The adjacent boat launch is one of the most popular put-ins for floating the Eleven Point, and a 4-mile hiking trail connects to McCormack Lake.
payload.long_description:
Greer Crossing Campground occupies a flat, level area adjacent to Highway 19, set back from the Eleven Point National Wild and Scenic River in Mark Twain National Forest. The campground offers 16 single sites and 3 double sites, each with a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern post. Sites are well-spaced and provide good privacy among the Ozark hardwoods. A campground host is present during summer months.

The boat launch here is one of the most popular access points for floating the Eleven Point, making the campground a natural base for paddlers. A 4-mile out-and-back hiking trail follows the river before climbing through typical Ozark hills to McCormack Lake. Fishing opportunities include rainbow trout, smallmouth bass, and sunfish.

Nearby attractions include Greer Spring (one of the largest springs in the Ozarks), Greer Mill historic site, and several other historic mills and springs within a short drive. The campground operates first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.

location.directions: From Winona, MO take Highway 19 south 17 miles to Forest Road 3188. Turn left at the junction of Highway 19 and Forest Road 3188. The campground is on the left; the boat launch and day use area are straight ahead. The site is just north of the Eleven Point Bridge.

payload.name: Randall Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Camping and vehicle access close November 15, 2026 through the third Friday of March 2027 to protect roosting bald eagles. Water systems may be shut off October 1 through April 30.
payload.short_description: Randall Creek Recreation Area is located on the banks of the Missouri River, downstream from Fort Randall Dam.
payload.medium_description: Randall Creek Recreation Area sits on the Missouri River downstream from Fort Randall Dam, offering both primitive and electric campsites along with camping cabins. Facilities include flush toilets, vault toilets, showers, drinking water, a dump station, boat ramps, fishing piers, and a fish cleaning station. The area provides access to the Missouri National Recreational River and is adjacent to Karl E. Mundt National Wildlife Refuge.
payload.long_description: Randall Creek Recreation Area is located on the banks of the Missouri River, downstream from Fort Randall Dam. Spend hours peacefully watching the water flow, observing the animals and birds that frequent the area, and enjoying he breathtaking beauty of the surrounding shoreline. The US Army Corps of Engineers began building the dam in 1946 and started generating electricity in 1954. Randall Creek is one of the South Dakota state parks that offers the opportunity for visitors to see the majestic bald eagle. The eagle roost area in the park is a designated National Natural Landmark. In South Dakota, many bald eagles spend their winters below the Missouri River dams where they are able to catch fish and prey on waterfowl attracted to the open water. They typically perch within 50 feet of the riverbank in tall cottonwood trees. The birds usually feed in the morning and rest in their roosting trees in the afternoon.

location.directions: 1 mile west of Pickstown off US Highway 281, below Fort Randall Dam on the west side. Address: 136 Randall Creek Road, Pickstown, SD 57367.

links.title: SD GFP Randall Creek Recreation Area
NPS Missouri National Recreational River Campgrounds

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Richmond Lake Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations accepted online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Three separate areas in Richmond Lake Recreation cater to the needs of campers, swimmers, naturalists, boaters and anglers.
payload.medium_description: Richmond Lake Recreation Area offers 24 electrical campsites, 2 tent sites, and a camping cabin on the shores of a 1,000-acre lake in northeastern South Dakota. The park features a swim beach, boat ramp, fishing pier, and extensive multi-use trail system with hiking, biking, and an 18-hole disc golf course. Seasonal flush toilets and showers are available; vault toilets remain open year-round.
payload.long_description: Three separate areas in Richmond Lake Recreation cater to the needs of campers, swimmers, naturalists, boaters and anglers. Campers stay in the South Unit, while the 200-acre Forest Drive Unit is a great place for wildlife viewing. The Boat Ramp Unit provides access to the more than 1,000-acre lake. Campsites with electricity are available, and the one-room camping cabin is equipped with heating and air conditioning and sleeping space for four people. Campers can avail themselves of the comfort station's showers and flush toilets and dump station. On the grounds of Richmond Lake Recreation Area is a fun disc golf course, fishing dock, picnic shelter, playground, boat ramp and beach. Plenty of walleye, northern pike, bass, perch, crappie, bluegill, catfish and bullheads fill the lake. Around the area, short trips can take your to the Dacotah Prairie Museum, Sand Lake National Wildlife Refuge and Mina Lake Recreation Area.

location.directions: 11 miles northwest of Aberdeen off US Highway 281. Campground address: 12800 379th Avenue, Aberdeen, SD 57401.

links.title: SD GFP Richmond Lake Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Kiser Lake State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Reservations required, available up to six months in advance via ReserveOhio or by calling (866) 644-6727. Off-peak rates apply November 1 through April 1.
payload.short_description: Primitive group camping on the south shore of Kiser Lake, with three sites accommodating up to 100 people total, fire rings, picnic tables, and latrine facilities.
payload.medium_description: Kiser Lake State Park Group Campground provides primitive group camping for youth and adult organizations on the south side of Kiser Lake in Champaign County, Ohio. Three partially shaded group sites are equipped with fire rings, picnic tables, and latrine facilities, with a dump station nearby. The sites are located near a fishing pier, picnic shelter, and playground.
payload.long_description:
Kiser Lake State Park Group Campground offers primitive group camping facilities designed for organized youth and adult groups on the scenic south shore of Kiser Lake. The campground features three partially shaded sites that can collectively accommodate up to 100 people, making it suitable for scout troops, church groups, and other organizations seeking an affordable outdoor experience.

Each group site is equipped with fire rings and picnic tables, with pit latrines located nearby. While the group camp area is primitive without hookups or showers, a dump station is available for groups with trailers. The location provides convenient access to recreational amenities including a fishing pier, picnic shelter, and playground.

The 396-acre park offers additional activities such as swimming at the beach, boating, fishing for largemouth bass and channel catfish, and hiking trails through rolling wooded terrain. Reservations are required for group camping and can be made up to six months in advance through the Ohio State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: From I-70, take State Route 235 north approximately 15 miles to the park entrance. The park is located at 4889 N State Route 235, Conover, Ohio 45317.

address.full: 3725 Kiser Lake Rd, Saint Paris, OH 43072

links.title: Kiser Lake State Park Campground - ODNR

payload.name: Rocky Point Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Rocky Point Recreation Area is located on the 8,000-acre Belle Fourche Reservoir.
payload.medium_description: Rocky Point Recreation Area sits on the 8,000-acre Belle Fourche Reservoir, created in 1911 by Orman Dam, once the largest earthen dam in the world. The campground offers 62 electrical sites and camping cabins with seasonal flush toilets, showers, and drinking water. Year-round vault toilets and a dump station serve campers during the off-season when water systems close.
payload.long_description: Rocky Point Recreation Area is located on the 8,000-acre Belle Fourche Reservoir. The reservoir was created in 1911, when Orman Dam was constructed to store water for agricultural use. At the time of its completion, Orman Dam was the largest earthen dam in the world. In 1989, Orman Dam was designated a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark. Glide along the water in a kayak or canoe, fish and take a boat out on the water when you camp overnight. Rocky Point Recreation Area offers sites with or without electricity and cozy one-bedroom cabins in scenic locations. Book your reservation quickly and easily using the online system. Cabins are built for four people and furnished with a double bed, set of bunk beds, heating, air conditioning and electricity. Cooking is not permitted inside, but an outdoor fire grate and picnic table are provided. Fishing is a popular activity at Rocky Point Recreation Area, and a boat ramp, fish-cleaning station and fishing pole checkout are provided. Species found in the reservoir are walleye, yellow perch, channel catfish, black crappie, smallmouth bass, white bass and tigermuskie. If you're in the mood for a good hike, visit the George S. Mickelson Trail, in the heart of the beautiful Black Hills. Its gentle slopes and easy access allow people of all ages and abilities to enjoy the beauty of the area.

location.directions: 8 miles east of Belle Fourche off SD Highway 212. Address: 18513 Fisherman's Road, Belle Fourche, SD 57717.

links.title: Rocky Point Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Sandy Shore Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers and flush toilets close; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at campsd.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267, opening 90 days before arrival.
payload.short_description: On the banks of Lake Kampeska, Sandy Shore Recreation Area offers just that.
payload.medium_description: Sandy Shore Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Kampeska, about 5 miles west of Watertown, South Dakota. The campground offers 15 modern electric campsites and 2 shorefront camping cabins with access to the lake's largest boat ramp, swim beaches, and excellent fishing for walleye, northern pike, and smallmouth bass.
payload.long_description: On the banks of Lake Kampeska, Sandy Shore Recreation Area offers just that ... a long, sandy beach. The beach is a great place to enjoy Lake Kampeska, which is a glacial lake named for its clear water. Early homesteaders settled along the shores of the lake. Both RVers and tent campers will find spaces that meet their needs. Back-in sites at the campground come with electricity and partial shade. The facilities at Sandy Shore Recreation Area are designed to make the outdoor experience more pleasant: boat ramp, flush toilets and showers, picnic shelter, playground and game checkout. Fishermen seeking the catch-of-the-day will find walleye, northern pike, perch and bass in the waters of Lake Kampeska. You can check out a pole, if you didn't have room to pack your own or decided at the last minute that the fishing was just too good to pass up. Sandy Shore Recreation Area is five miles west of Watertown. In the town, interesting places to visit include the Terry Redlin Art Center, the Bramble Park Zoo, the Mellette House, home of South Dakota's first governor, and the Codington County Historical Museum.

location.directions: 5 miles west of Watertown off US Highway 212.

links.title: Sandy Shore Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Snake Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain accessible. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Sparking Lake Francis Case draws visitors to Snake Creek Recreation Area.
payload.medium_description: Snake Creek Recreation Area is a 735-acre South Dakota state park on Lake Francis Case featuring two campgrounds with 115 campsites and 10 camping cabins. The park offers electric and non-electric sites, modern amenities including flush toilets, showers, and a dump station, plus boat ramps, a swim beach, fish cleaning stations, and hiking trails connecting both campgrounds.
payload.long_description: Sparking Lake Francis Case draws visitors to Snake Creek Recreation Area. The park is popular with boaters and anglers, as well those looking for scenic beauty along the Missouri River. History buffs will enjoy knowing that the Lewis and Clark expedition traveled through the area, where they were told to watch for "burning bluffs" along the river. Stay in one of the two campgrounds with either a basic site or one with electricity. One-room cabins have sleeping accommodations for four people (2 twin beds and 1 full bed) and are furnished with a table, benches, outside fire grate and picnic table. Cabins are open year-round, so heating and air conditioning is provided. The beach and boat ramp beckon you to the beautiful water at Snake Creek Recreation Area, while anglers can make good use of the fish-cleaning station. Children will have fun going for a catch in their own fishing pond. Dock 44 Marina, privately operated at the park, not only has a marina, but cabins, a restaurant, convenience store and floating fuel dock. One of the unique local attractions is Red Rock, an upstream rock several hundred feet high once used as a landmark for steamboat captains.

location.directions: 14 miles west of Platte off SD Highway 44, Platte, SD 57369.

links.title: SD Game, Fish & Parks - Snake Creek Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Sica Hollow State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The campground has 14 non-electrical sites. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267. Vault toilets are operational year-round.
payload.short_description: Sioux legends of Sica Hollow (pronounced SHE-cha) recall mysterious happenings, and you can still feel the eerie spell today.
payload.medium_description: Sica Hollow State Park Campground offers 14 non-electrical campsites in a secluded wooded ravine in the Coteau des Prairies of northeastern South Dakota. The campground serves as a base camp for exploring the park's signature Trail of the Spirits and 15 miles of trails winding through oak, aspen, and maple forest. A separate horse camp with corrals is available for equestrian visitors.
payload.long_description: Sioux legends of Sica Hollow (pronounced SHE-cha) recall mysterious happenings, and you can still feel the eerie spell today. Along the Trail of the Spirits, you’ll see gurgling reddish bogs, which Indians saw as the blood and flesh of their ancestors. Indian lore gives new meaning to Sica’s streams, rustic bridges, waterfalls, and wildflowers as you hike along over 8 miles of trails. Sica Hollow State Park has also earned attention nation-wide. The Old River Warren and Coteau des Prairies are designated National Natural Landmarks. The Trail of the Spirits, a self-guided interpretive foot trail, was designated as a National Recreation Trail in 1971. There are 8 miles of marked trails to guide horseback riders through the 900 acres of woodland in the park.

location.directions: From Sisseton, travel west on SD Highway 10, then north on BIA Route 25 approximately 12 miles to the park entrance at 44950 Park Road, Sisseton, SD 57262.

links.title: Sica Hollow State Park - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: FAHEY CABIN
payload.status_description: Fahey Cabin is a historic structure preserved by the Forest Service. It is not available for camping or overnight rental. The cabin was restored in 2023 and serves as a historical landmark only.
payload.short_description: Historic 1870s pioneer cabin in Stanislaus National Forest near Long Barn. Not available for overnight camping or rental; preserved as a historical site.
payload.medium_description: Fahey Cabin is a historic structure built in the 1870s by early pioneer rancher Michael Fahey, who used it as an outpost for summer cattle grazing operations. Located approximately 3 miles southeast of Long Barn at Wright's Creek crossing, the cabin came under Forest Service administration in 1938 through a land exchange and remained in use until the 1970s. Restored by Forest Service volunteers in 2023, it is preserved as a historical site and is not available for public camping or overnight rental.
payload.long_description:
Fahey Cabin is a historic pioneer cabin in the Stanislaus National Forest, located approximately 3 miles southeast of Long Barn, California, at Wright's Creek crossing. Built in the 1870s by Michael Fahey, an Irish immigrant who came to Tuolumne County during the Gold Rush era, the cabin served as a summer outpost for cattle grazing operations. In 1877, Fahey purchased 160 acres from John Whelan for $50, establishing what became known as the "Fahey Cow Camp."

The cabin came under U.S. Forest Service administration in 1938 through a land exchange and continued to serve as a residential facility until the 1970s. For over a century, this landmark was a summer residence for the Fahey family during their cattle operations. The surrounding area once formed a greater mountain community where families spent seasonal months managing livestock.

In 2023, approximately 20 Forest Service volunteers from several states, including New Jersey, Maryland, and Arizona, spent two weeks restoring the aging cabin. The structure is preserved as a historical site and is not available for public camping, rental, or overnight stays. Visitors may view the cabin as part of the area's pioneer heritage.

location.directions: Located approximately 3 miles southeast of Long Barn, California, at Wright's Creek crossing in Stanislaus National Forest.

links.title: DVIDS - Stanislaus NF Fahey Cabin Photo

payload.name: Camden State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for reservations. The park operates year-round with some seasonal facilities. A Minnesota state park vehicle permit is required for entry.
payload.short_description: Riverside group campground for up to 50 people in a wooded setting along the Redwood River at Camden State Park in southwestern Minnesota.
payload.medium_description: Camden State Park Group Campground sits in a wooded area along the banks of the Redwood River in Lyon County, Minnesota. The tent-only group camp accommodates up to 50 people and includes an enclosed shelter, a toilet building with running water, picnic tables, and fire rings with grills. Reservations are made through Minnesota's state park reservation system.
payload.long_description:
Camden State Park Group Campground offers a shaded, riverside setting for organized groups seeking a primitive camping experience in southwestern Minnesota. Located along the Redwood River within the 1,745-acre park, the group camp accommodates up to 50 people in tents and features an enclosed shelter that provides protection from weather and space for group meals and activities.

The campground includes a toilet building with running water, multiple picnic tables, and fire rings equipped with grills. The wooded setting along the river provides natural scenery and access to the park's trail system. The main park offers additional amenities including a spring-fed swimming pool and beach, fishing on Brawner Lake, and over 15 miles of hiking trails through the Redwood River valley.

Camden State Park operates year-round, though some facilities are seasonal. The group camp requires advance reservations through the Minnesota state parks reservation system. A vehicle permit is required for entry.

location.directions: Located 10 miles southwest of Marshall, Minnesota on State Highway 23. The park address is 1897 Camden Park Rd, Lynd, MN 56157.

payload.name: Delaware Day Use
payload.status_description: This is a day-use only facility. No overnight camping is permitted. Shelter houses are available for reservation through ReserveOhio.
payload.short_description: Day-use area at Delaware State Park featuring picnic facilities and scenic lake views. No overnight camping; shelter houses available for reservation.
payload.medium_description: Delaware Day Use is a day-use facility at Delaware State Park in Ohio, offering picnic areas and shelter houses overlooking the 1,330-acre Delaware Lake. This is not a campground; overnight camping is not permitted at day-use areas. Shelter houses can be reserved through ReserveOhio for group gatherings and events.
payload.long_description:
Delaware Day Use refers to the day-use facilities at Delaware State Park, a 1,686-acre park surrounding Delaware Lake in central Ohio. These areas include picnic tables in scenic spots overlooking the lake and a reservable shelter house for group gatherings.

This is not an overnight camping area. Day-use facilities are separate from the park's campground, which has 214 sites located elsewhere in the park. Visitors to the day-use area can enjoy lake views, access to hiking trails, and proximity to the park's 800-foot swimming beach with bathhouse and snack bar.

Ohio State Parks do not charge entrance fees, so day visitors can access picnic areas without a fee. Shelter house reservations can be made through ReserveOhio up to one year in advance, with a 3-day minimum advance booking requirement.

location.directions: From Columbus, take US-23 North to Delaware. Turn east on US-36/SR-37 and continue approximately 5 miles to the park entrance on the south side of the road.

payload.name: Rock Creek Camground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from mid-June through late October. As of May 12, 2026, the area is closed for the season and expected to reopen in mid-June. No reservations required; first-come, first-served dispersed camping only.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed camping along Rock Creek in the Gore Range, managed by the Yampa Ranger District. Vault toilet provided but no potable water, fire rings, or tables.
payload.medium_description: Rock Creek Recreation Area offers several dispersed campsites along Rock Creek in the Gore Range of the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest. Popular with hunters and families, this free camping area provides a vault toilet but no potable water, fire rings, or picnic tables. Mountain biking opportunities are available nearby at the Rock Creek Trailhead.
payload.long_description:
Rock Creek Recreation Area is a dispersed camping destination in the Gore Range of the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest, managed by the Yampa Ranger District. The area provides several primitive campsites scattered along Rock Creek, offering a rustic backcountry experience without designated sites or amenities typical of developed campgrounds.

This area is a favorite among hunters and families seeking a quiet, undeveloped camping experience. A single vault toilet serves the area, but campers must bring their own drinking water as potable water is not available. Fire rings and picnic tables are not provided at individual sites. Mountain biking opportunities can be found nearby at the Rock Creek Trailhead, and the area offers fishing access along Rock Creek.

The recreation area is accessed via Rock Creek Road #250 off State Highway 134, east of Toponas. Usage is typically light, making it an appealing option for those seeking solitude in the Colorado high country.

location.directions: From Yampa, travel south on State Highway 131 for 10 miles to State Highway 134 at Toponas. Follow State Highway 134 east to Rock Creek Road #250.

payload.name: Spring Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for cabin and suite lodging. No tent or RV campsites are available at this location. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain open.
payload.short_description: Sitting on the shores of beautiful Lake Oahe, Spring Creek is a water-lover's paradise.
payload.medium_description: Spring Creek Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Oahe, 15 miles northwest of Pierre. The facility offers 10 modern cabins and 12 suites with heating, air conditioning, electricity, and bathroom facilities. There are no tent or RV campsites at Spring Creek; visitors seeking traditional camping must reserve sites at the adjacent Cow Creek Recreation Area. The marina, convenience store, and on-site restaurant provide services for boating, fishing, and water recreation on Lake Oahe.
payload.long_description: Sitting on the shores of beautiful Lake Oahe, Spring Creek is a water-lover's paradise. The lake has more than 2,000 miles of shoreline and its clear waters are ideal for boating, sailing, fishing, water skiing and diving. Campers, history buffs, mountain bikers and hikers will find new adventures in this rugged land first explored by Lewis and Clark. The recreation area offers a marina and convenience store, as well as an on-site restaurant run by the park's concessionaire. Whether you are looking to enjoy one of the top fishing destinations in the region, a relaxing family vacation, ride the waves or just enjoy time with your family and friends for a day trip there is no better place to live your legacy than at Spring Creek on Lake Oahe.

location.directions: 15 miles northwest of Pierre off SD Highway 1804

address.full: 28229 E Spring Creek Pl, Pierre, SD 57501

links.title: SD GFP - Spring Creek Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Red Fir Flat Group Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Opens June 15, weather permitting. Snowpack at this elevation may extend into late June in heavy snow years. Season typically runs through mid to late October until the first significant snowfall.
payload.short_description: Group campground at 6,400 ft on Mt. Shasta's southern slope, set in old-growth red fir forest. Popular with meditation and retreat groups. Reservable via Recreation.gov.
payload.medium_description: Red Fir Flat Group Campground sits at 6,400 feet elevation on the southern slope of Mt. Shasta within Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The site is nestled in an old-growth Shasta red fir forest offering shade and solitude, and is a popular destination for meditation and retreat groups. Reservations are required with a minimum of 12 and maximum of 30 people per group.
payload.long_description:
Red Fir Flat Group Campground is a reservable group site located at 6,400 feet on the southern slope of Mt. Shasta in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The campground is set in an impressive stand of old-growth Shasta red fir, providing ample shade with some open sunny areas. While there are no views of the upper mountain from this location, the site offers views to the west and south including the Trinity Alps, Mount Eddy, and Castle Crags.

The campground is particularly popular with meditation and retreat groups seeking peace and solitude in the forest setting. Several hiking trails are located nearby, including the trail to the historic Sierra Club stone cabin at timberline. Upper and Lower Panther Meadows, the South Gate Meadows access trail, and the Gray Butte trail are all within a few miles.

Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, an established fire ring, and bear-proof trash receptacles. There is no potable water on site; campers must bring their own. The town of Mt. Shasta is 10 miles away and offers full services including grocery stores and restaurants.

location.directions: From Interstate 5, take exit 738. Head east through the town of Mt. Shasta on Lake Street. Lake Street becomes Everitt Memorial Highway as it ascends the mountain. At approximately milepost 9, look for the campground entrance sign on the left.

links.title: USFS Red Fir Flat Group Campground

payload.name: Schwartz Cabin
payload.status_description: Open May through November. Closed December through April. Advanced reservations through Recreation.gov are always required; walk-ups are not available. Entry is by combination lock provided in the confirmation letter.
payload.short_description: Historic 1880s one-room rustic cabin at the base of Boreas Pass in Pike National Forest, featuring a wood stove and sleeping up to 3 guests.
payload.medium_description: Schwartz Cabin is a small single-room historic cabin dating to the 1880s mining and railroad era, located at the base of Boreas Pass near Como, Colorado. The cabin features a full bed and twin bed, plus a full-size wood stove for heating. A shared vault toilet is located approximately 200 yards away near Roberts Cabin. Guests must bring their own water, bedding, cooking equipment, and firewood.
payload.long_description:
Schwartz Cabin is one of two historic 1880s cabins available for rental in the South Park Ranger District of Pike National Forest, nestled at the base of Boreas Pass in Park County, Colorado. This rustic single-room structure is eligible for placement on the National Register of Historic Places and offers a glimpse into Colorado's mining and railroad heritage.

The cabin accommodates up to 3 guests with one full bed and one twin bed, heated by a full-size wood stove. No water, electricity, cooking utensils, or bedding are provided. Guests must bring an ample water supply, sleeping bags or blankets, flashlights, matches, and firewood. A vault toilet is shared with nearby Roberts Cabin, located about 200 yards to the south.

The location provides convenient access to Como, Breckenridge, Fairplay, and the Colorado Trail. Winter activities like cross-country skiing and sledding are available when conditions permit.

location.directions: From Como, CO, drive west on County Road 33 for approximately 4 miles until the road turns sharply right towards Boreas Pass. Schwartz Cabin is located behind Roberts Cabin. Parking is along the east side of the road.

payload.name: Union Grove State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Contact the park for current facility status.
payload.short_description: Rich glacial soils support a lush growth of native woods in this hidden treasure, Union Grove State Park.
payload.medium_description: Union Grove State Park offers 25 shaded campsites in the rolling hills of southeast South Dakota, including 4 horse campsites for equestrian visitors. The park features electric and non-electric sites, modern restrooms with showers, a dump station, and 4.3 miles of multi-use trails ideal for horseback riding and mountain biking.
payload.long_description: Rich glacial soils support a lush growth of native woods in this hidden treasure, Union Grove State Park. Horseback riders, hikers, bikers and cross-country skiers enjoy several miles of trail through the forest along Brule Creek. The trees and plants attract a variety of birds sure to keep botanists and birdwatchers entertained for hours. Campers enjoy the quiet well-shaded campsites, and the horse camp is the perfect base for a weekend of riding. Union Grove State Park began as a county park around 1936. The land was leased to the State of South Dakota in 1946 and since then the park has been host to residents and vacationers alike. Visitors enjoy the abundant wildlife and beautiful scenery, along with modern conveniences like showers, flush toilets, dump station and picnic shelter. Deer, wild turkeys, beaver and many small animals abound in the park as well as a variety of trees and plant life. Birdwatchers will enjoy the opportunities to see many species of birds including cardinals, orioles, grosbeak, warblers, red-winged blackbirds, blue jays, pheasants and wild turkeys. All types of hunting is allowed within the park from October 1 until April 30th during designated hunting seasons. Uncased firearms and bows are not allowed with the campground and picnic areas. Please refer to Hunting Handbook for more info. The multi-use trails are ideal for horses and mountain bikes and spand up to 4.3 miles. The hiking trail is foot traffic only and is 1.2 miles

location.directions: 11 miles south of Beresford off I-29, Exit 38. Located at 30828 471st Avenue, Beresford, SD 57004.

links.title: Union Grove State Park - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Dillard Mill State Historic Site Shelters
payload.status_description: Open for day use only. Grounds hours are 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily May through October, and 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily November through April. The picnic shelter can be reserved for day-use gatherings. No overnight camping is available at this site.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter at a preserved 1908 gristmill on Huzzah Creek in the Missouri Ozarks. No overnight camping available.
payload.medium_description: Dillard Mill State Historic Site features a reservable picnic shelter at one of Missouri's best-preserved water-powered gristmills, built in 1908 on Huzzah Creek. The day-use area includes a shelter with picnic tables and grills, two accessible restrooms, a playground, and a 1.5-mile hiking trail through oak-hickory forest. Fishing is available in Huzzah Creek. This is a day-use facility only with no overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Dillard Mill State Historic Site preserves one of Missouri's finest examples of a water-powered gristmill, completed in 1908 on Huzzah Creek in Crawford County. The site offers a limited day-use area with a small picnic shelter available for reservation, featuring picnic tables and barbecue grills. Two accessible restrooms serve the area.

Visitors can enjoy a 1.5-mile hiking trail that winds through oak-hickory forest and pine uplands east of the mill, as well as fishing access along Huzzah Creek. Guided mill tours are offered year-round, with schedules varying by season. The grounds are open daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. May through October, and 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. November through April.

This is strictly a day-use facility. There is no overnight camping, RV sites, or lodging available at Dillard Mill State Historic Site. The picnic shelter can be reserved for day-use gatherings only.

location.directions: Located at 142 Dillard Mill Road, Davisville, MO 65456, in Crawford County.

payload.name: West Pollock Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and drinking water systems are closed. Vault toilets remain available during the off-season.
payload.short_description: The town of Pollock and the recreation area are both named after a pioneer lay minister and respected citizen of the area, R.
payload.medium_description: West Pollock Recreation Area sits on the shores of Lake Oahe along the Missouri River, offering 29 campsites with both electric and non-electric options. The recreation area serves as a base camp for anglers targeting walleye and other Lake Oahe species, as well as hunters pursuing pheasant, grouse, and waterfowl in the fall. Facilities include a boat ramp, fish cleaning station, flush toilets, showers, and dump station.
payload.long_description: The town of Pollock and the recreation area are both named after a pioneer lay minister and respected citizen of the area, R.Y. Pollock. Anglers enjoy this recreation area as a prime location to stay when fishing for walleyes and an abundance of other Lake Oahe fish. The boat ramp provides easy access to the water. In the fall, pheasant, grouse and waterfowl hunters come to camp. West Pollock Recreation Area is one of the South Dakota state parks along the Lewis and Clark Trail.

location.directions: 3 miles southwest of Pollock off SD Highway 1804

links.title: West Pollock Recreation Area - SD GFP
