payload.name: Kersey Lake Cabin
payload.status_description: The cabin is typically available for rental year-round, though winter access may require snowmobiles or cross-country skis depending on snow conditions. Reservations are made through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Historic Forest Service cabin in the Beartooth Mountains of Custer Gallatin National Forest near Cooke City, Montana, adjacent to the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Kersey Lake Cabin is a historic Forest Service cabin located in the remote Beartooth Mountains within the Custer Gallatin National Forest in Park County, Montana. Situated near Kersey Lake and the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness boundary, the cabin provides access to alpine scenery and backcountry recreation near Cooke City.
payload.long_description:
Kersey Lake Cabin is a historic Forest Service rental cabin situated in the dramatic Beartooth Mountains of the Custer Gallatin National Forest in Park County, Montana. The cabin sits at high elevation near Kersey Lake, a scenic alpine lake accessible via the Clarks Fork Trailhead off US Highway 212 between Cooke City and Red Lodge.

The surrounding area offers outstanding opportunities for hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing in pristine mountain terrain adjacent to the Absaroka-Beartooth Wilderness. The Beartooth Mountains are known for rugged alpine scenery, abundant wildlife including grizzly bears, moose, and eagles, and relatively short hiking access to alpine lakes. Visitors should be prepared for a rustic backcountry experience and practice proper food storage in bear country.

Access to the cabin area is typically via US Highway 212, which is subject to seasonal closures due to snow. The highway generally opens in late May and closes in early to mid-October depending on weather conditions.

location.directions: From Cooke City, Montana, travel approximately 3.4 miles east on US Highway 212 toward the Clarks Fork Trailhead area. From Red Lodge, Montana, travel approximately 58 miles west on US Highway 212. Access is dependent on seasonal road conditions; US Highway 212 over Beartooth Pass typically opens late May and closes in October.

payload.name: Oxbow Campsite
payload.status_description: Open year-round with no reservations required. Access may be limited during winter due to snow on Newsome Creek Road. Fire danger is currently low.
payload.short_description: A free, solitary campsite on Newsome Creek in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, ideal for anglers seeking a quiet fishing retreat in remote Idaho backcountry.
payload.medium_description: Oxbow Campsite offers a single primitive campsite on the banks of Newsome Creek at 3,830 feet elevation. This free, first-come, first-served site features two camp pads and a toilet. There is no potable water, and campers must pack out all trash. The area to the east is closed to motor vehicles year-round, making the existing roads ideal for mountain biking.
payload.long_description:
Oxbow Campsite is a remote, solitary camping spot nestled along Newsome Creek in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests near Elk City, Idaho. At 3,830 feet elevation, this free primitive site caters to anglers looking to fish the creek in complete solitude. The single campsite includes two camp pads and a toilet.

This is a true backcountry experience with minimal amenities. There is no potable water, no picnic tables, and garbage services are not available, so visitors must pack out everything they bring in. The area east of the campsite is closed to motor vehicles year-round, though the existing road network provides excellent mountain biking opportunities.

Access is via Newsome Creek Road from State Highway 14. The site is open year-round but may become inaccessible during winter months due to snow. No reservations are accepted; camping is first-come, first-served.

location.directions: From State Highway 14, turn north on Newsome Creek Road No. 1858 and travel approximately 2.2 miles to the campsite.

payload.name: Buckhead Shelter
payload.status_description: This site is designated as day-use only by the U.S. Forest Service. No overnight camping is permitted. The area is open sunrise to sunset with no fees required.
payload.short_description: Buckhead Shelter is located in the Willamette National Forest near Oakridge, Oregon, in an area designated for day-use only with no established overnight camping facilities.
payload.medium_description: Buckhead Shelter is situated in the Middle Fork Willamette River area of Willamette National Forest. Official Forest Service sources indicate the Buckhead area is designated as a day-use site only, open sunrise to sunset, with access to the interpretive Buckhead Trail. There are no restrooms, no potable water, and no established camping infrastructure at this location.
payload.long_description:
Buckhead Shelter is located in the Willamette National Forest near Oakridge in Lane County, Oregon. The site is part of the Buckhead area that provides access to the Buckhead Trail #3474, a short 0.5-mile paved interpretive loop through riparian forest habitat along the Middle Fork Willamette River.

Official U.S. Forest Service documentation indicates the Buckhead Nature Trailhead area is designated for day-use only, with operating hours from sunrise to sunset. There are no restroom facilities, no potable water, and no fee required for access. The area is managed by the Middle Fork Ranger District.

Visitors should note that Forest Service roads in this area are not maintained for snow and ice during winter months, which may limit accessibility seasonally. The site is primarily used as a trailhead for day hikers interested in the interpretive nature trail rather than as an overnight camping destination.

location.directions: From Oakridge, travel 4 miles west on Highway 58. Turn right onto Westfir Road at Mile Post 31.5. After crossing the green bridge over the Middle Fork Willamette River, continue 1 mile toward Westfir, turn left at Hemlock junction, cross another bridge, and proceed 2.2 miles on Forest Road 5821 to the parking lot.

payload.name: Gavan Hill Hut
payload.status_description: The shelter is available year-round on a first-come, first-served basis for emergency use. No reservations are accepted.
payload.short_description: Four-sided emergency backcountry shelter on the Harbor Mountain-Gavan Hill Trail, approximately 3 miles northeast of Sitka in the Tongass National Forest.
payload.medium_description: The Gavan Hill Hut is a primitive four-sided emergency shelter located along the 6.2-mile Harbor Mountain-Gavan Hill Trail in the Tongass National Forest. Situated about 3 miles from Sitka, this shelter provides basic emergency protection for hikers but has no amenities. It operates on a first-come, first-served basis and is intended for emergency use only.
payload.long_description:
The Gavan Hill Hut is an emergency backcountry shelter positioned on the Harbor Mountain-Gavan Hill Trail in the Tongass National Forest near Sitka, Alaska. This four-sided shelter provides basic protection from the elements for hikers traveling the rugged 6.2-mile trail that connects Harbor Mountain Road to Baranof Street in Sitka.

The shelter is minimally equipped with no stove, no restrooms, and no potable water. Hikers must be fully self-sufficient, bringing their own water, food, and supplies. The shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis and is intended primarily for emergency use rather than planned overnight camping.

Access from the Gavan endpoint begins at the end of Baranof Street in Sitka, where the trail starts with an 800-foot ADA-accessible boardwalk section before climbing steeply through hemlock-spruce forest via switchbacks to approximately 2,000 feet elevation. The trail and surrounding area offer opportunities for hiking, backpacking, and scenery viewing in this remote Alaskan wilderness.

location.directions: From downtown Sitka, the Gavan Hill Trailhead is located at the end of Baranof Street. The shelter is approximately 3 miles up the trail. Alternatively, access from Harbor Mountain Road: travel approximately 4 miles on Halibut Point Road from downtown Sitka, then turn onto Harbor Mountain Road for 5.5 miles.

payload.name: Springfield Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and other water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online at reservations.gooutdoorssouthdakota.com or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: Springfield Recreation Area is nestled along the shore with breathtaking views of the Missouri River.
payload.medium_description: Springfield Recreation Area sits along the Missouri River shore in Bon Homme County, offering 20 campsites with electrical and non-electrical options plus two camping cabins. The park features flush toilets, showers, drinking water, a dump station, and accessible facilities. A bike trail connects to the nearby town of Springfield, and an adjacent nine-hole golf course overlooks the river.
payload.long_description: Springfield Recreation Area is nestled along the shore with breathtaking views of the Missouri River. Adjacent to the park overlooking the river is a beautiful nine-hole golf course, and a bike trail connects the park to the town of Springfield. Camping at the park gives you time to relax and appreciate the scenery. Springfield Recreation Area's campsites come with or without electricity. Guests will find modern comfort stations with showers and flush toilets, dump station, playground and picnic shelter. The comfortable cabins fit four family members or friends. Inside the one-room log-style buildings are a set of bunk beds, double bed, table and benches. Meals outdoors can be prepared on the fire grate and served at the picnic table. Heating, air-conditioning and electricity are all included. Tee off at the Springfield Golf Course, although it might be hard to keep your eye on the ball when the views from the bluffs are so mesmerizing. Drop a line in the water to catch walleye, smallmouth bass and largemouth bass. Springfield Recreation Area has a boat ramp, fishing dock and fish-cleaning station.

location.directions: Located in Springfield, South Dakota at 1412 Boat Basin Drive, Springfield, SD 57062.

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Guillard Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Listed by USFS as a day-use fishing area with no developed overnight camping facilities. Dispersed camping in Francis Marion National Forest requires a free permit obtained 5+ business days in advance from the Francis Marion Ranger District.
payload.short_description: A primitive fishing area on a 10-acre oxbow of the Santee River within Francis Marion National Forest, featuring old-growth bald cypress and access via rough dirt road.
payload.medium_description: Guilliard Lake is a 10-acre oxbow lake off the Santee River in Francis Marion National Forest's coastal plain. The USFS lists it as a day-use fishing destination rather than a developed campground. The area contains rare old-growth timber with massive bald cypress and water tupelo, including cypress knees up to nine feet tall. Access is via a rutted dirt road with significant potholes.
payload.long_description:
Guilliard Lake is a scenic 10-acre oxbow lake formed from the Santee River, located in the coastal plain of Francis Marion National Forest in Berkeley County, South Carolina. The USFS officially designates this as a day-use fishing area rather than a developed campground with overnight facilities. The lake supports fishing for various species, with creel limits established under Supervisor's Order FM-14-01.

An 18-acre portion of the site was established as a Research Natural Area in 1963, protecting a remnant of old-growth bottomland timber along the Santee River. The stand features towering bald cypress and water tupelo, with some cypress knees reaching nine feet tall and three feet in diameter at the base. Wildlife includes white-tailed deer, bears, bobcats, wood ducks, herons, and bald eagles.

Access is via a rough dirt road with large potholes requiring careful navigation. While dispersed camping in Francis Marion National Forest requires a free permit obtained at least 5 business days in advance, the official USFS page for Guilliard Lake lists it as day-use only with no restroom facilities. Campers seeking overnight stays should contact the Francis Marion Ranger District for current regulations.

location.directions: Guilliard Lake Campground is located near Jamestown in the Francis Marion National Forest. Access is via a dirt road with large potholes; caution is advised, especially at night. Standard passenger vehicles can manage with care, but large RVs and trailers are not recommended.

links.title: USFS Guilliard Lake Research Natural Area

payload.name: Swan Creek Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available.
payload.short_description: Situated on the rolling prairie bluffs, the east and west campgrounds at Swan Creek Recreation Area provide anglers the opportunity to stay overnight.
payload.medium_description: Swan Creek Recreation Area features two campgrounds (east and west) perched on rolling prairie bluffs overlooking Lake Oahe. The 26-site facility offers both electrical ($30/night) and non-electrical ($16/night) camping with flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. Two boat ramps provide direct lake access for anglers and boaters exploring the Lewis and Clark Trail region.
payload.long_description: Situated on the rolling prairie bluffs, the east and west campgrounds at Swan Creek Recreation Area provide anglers the opportunity to stay overnight. Two ramps offer access to Lake Oahe for boating and fishing fun. Swan Creek, nine miles west of the town of Akaska, is one of the South Dakota state parks along the Lewis and Clark Trail. Before you bait your hook, get on the computer to book a site using the convenient online reservation system. Select either a basic site or one with electricity, then let your getaway to Swan Creek begin. Lake Oahe is packed with walleye, smallmouth bass, white bass, northern pike and perch. After bringing in your catch, use the fish-cleaning station to prepare for some fine dining.

location.directions: Located 9 miles west of Akaska off US Highway 83.

links.title: SD GFP Swan Creek Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Walkers Point Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water systems, flush toilets, and showers close seasonally from October 1 through April 30. Vault toilets remain available during the off-season.
payload.short_description: Tucked along the shore of Lake Madison, this small but complete park meets the many needs of campers, anglers and boaters.
payload.medium_description: Walker's Point Recreation Area sits on the scenic shores of Lake Madison, a 2,800-acre lake popular for fishing, boating, and swimming. The campground features 42 electric campsites and 2 camping cabins, with amenities including flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station during the warmer months. Year-round vault toilets are available. A boat ramp, fishing pier, fish cleaning station, and ski beach provide ample water recreation opportunities.
payload.long_description: Tucked along the shore of Lake Madison, this small but complete park meets the many needs of campers, anglers and boaters. Campsites at Walker's Point Recreation Area offer picturesque views of the 2,800-acre lake, while anglers enjoy both on- and off-shore fishing. Select a basic site or one with electricity in the campground at Walker's Point Recreation Area. To make your stay more comfortable, showers and flush toilets are provided in the comfort station. One room, log-style cabins sleep four and are furnished with a set of bunk beds, double bed, table and benches. Air-conditioning keeps you cool in the summer and you can turn on the heat in the winter months. Cook outdoors on the fire grate provided and gather around the picnic table to dine. One of those meals might be fresh-caught fish pulled right from the lake. Varieties found here are walleye, perch, northern pike, crappie and bullhead. A fish-cleaning station helps get your catch ready for dinner. There's also a beach, boat ramp, playground and ski beach for guests at Walker's Point Recreation Area to use and enjoy. For a step back in time, visit Prairie Village near Madison. The living museum has exhibits reflecting life at the turn of the century. While there, you can ride a rare steam-powered carousel.

location.directions: From Madison, SD: Head southeast on SD Highway 19 for approximately 9 miles. Turn east onto Walker's Point Drive and continue to the recreation area entrance.

links.title: Walker's Point Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: West Bend Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems may be closed; vault toilets remain available. A zebra mussel alert is in effect for Lake Sharpe requiring all watercraft to be cleaned, drained, and dried before moving.
payload.short_description: Excellent walleye and small mouth bass fishing is supported by a relatively stable lake level and cool water temperatures at West Bend Recreation Area.
payload.medium_description: West Bend Recreation Area is a South Dakota state recreation area situated on the shores of Lake Sharpe, a Missouri River reservoir. The campground features 120 sites across three campground loops plus four camping cabins, with amenities including electrical hookups, flush toilets, showers, drinking water, and a dump station. The area is known for walleye and smallmouth bass fishing, with boat ramps, a fish cleaning station, and a sandy beach.
payload.long_description: Excellent walleye and small mouth bass fishing is supported by a relatively stable lake level and cool water temperatures at West Bend Recreation Area. With most fishing done from boats, the protected marina offers convenient boat launching, regardless of the wind direction. In the autumn, hunters use this as a base camp to hunt pheasant and Canadian geese. No matter the weather, camping cabins provide comfortable accommodations year-round at West Bend Recreation Area. The one-room cabins can be reserved online, with the convenient system in place. Four people can sleep in the cabin with the two bunk beds and double bed provided. Heating, air conditioning and electricity are included, as well as an outdoor fire grate and picnic table. Campsites on the grounds can also be reserved online. Electric sites are available, and the restrooms come with showers and flush toilets. West Bend Recreation Area is one of the South Dakota parks along the Lewis and Clark Trail. Other nearby parks are the Farm Island Recreation Area and the Oahe Downstream Recreation Area. West Bend Recreation Area counts among its amenities a boat ramp, beach, fish-cleaning station, playground, ski beach and Wi-Fi. Boat and camper storage is available at West Bend Recreation Area between April 30 and September 30.

location.directions: From Pierre, head east on SD Highway 34 for approximately 35 miles, then turn north following signs to West Bend Recreation Area at 22154 West Bend Road, Harrold, SD 57536.

links.title: SD Game, Fish & Parks - West Bend Recreation Area

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: West Whitlock Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Between October 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets, and water systems are closed; vault toilets remain available. Reservations available online through South Dakota GFP or by calling 1-800-710-2267.
payload.short_description: A popular campsite for the Arikara and Mandan people in the past, West Whitlock now draws modern-day campers and fishermen to its shores.
payload.medium_description: West Whitlock Recreation Area sits on the western shores of Lake Oahe, a Missouri River reservoir in central South Dakota. The campground offers 105 campsites including electrical options, two camping cabins, modern restrooms with showers, a dump station, swim beach, boat ramps, fish cleaning stations, playground, and hiking trails. Open year-round, though water-dependent facilities close from October through April.
payload.long_description: A popular campsite for the Arikara and Mandan people in the past, West Whitlock now draws modern-day campers and fishermen to its shores. When the area became a park, it was named for Mrs. J.F. Whitlock, whose pioneering family once owned the land. Whitlock Crossing was the name given to a small settlement that operated a ferry across the river near the area.

location.directions: From Gettysburg, SD, head west on US-212 for approximately 15 miles, then turn north to the recreation area entrance.

links.title: West Whitlock Recreation Area - SD GFP

management.agency_name: South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks

payload.name: Whetstone Bay Lakeside Use Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for camping. Vault toilets typically remain open all year. No potable water available on site. A park entrance license is required for vehicle access.
payload.short_description: Whetstone Bay Lakeside Use Area
payload.medium_description: Whetstone Bay Lakeside Use Area is a primitive camping destination on Lake Francis Case, part of the Missouri River reservoir system in south-central South Dakota. The area features boat ramps, shore fishing access, vault toilets, a dump station, and picnic facilities. Camping is first-come, first-served with a park entrance license required.
payload.long_description: Whetstone Bay Lakeside Use Area

location.directions: From Bonesteel, head north on US Highway 1806 for approximately 10 miles. The lakeside use area is located on the east side of the highway along Lake Francis Case.

links.title: SD GFP Parks and Recreation Fees

payload.name: Saltwater State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Campground closed as of March 24, 2026 due to flooding and erosion impacts. No reopening date announced. The park is reevaluating camping operations while day-use areas remain open 8 a.m. to dusk.
payload.short_description: A 137-acre urban beach park on Puget Sound in Des Moines with forested campsites along McSorley Creek, tide pools, and Washington's only state park underwater artificial reef.
payload.medium_description: Saltwater State Park offers a sandy beach getaway just two miles from I-5 in Des Moines. The 137-acre park features 1,445 feet of Puget Sound shoreline, tide pools, a bubbling creek with forested trails, and Washington's only state park artificial reef popular with scuba divers.
payload.long_description:
Saltwater State Park sits on the shores of Puget Sound between Seattle and Tacoma, providing an accessible urban escape with 1,445 feet of saltwater beach. The 137-acre park features tide pools, driftwood-strewn shores, and McSorley Creek winding through a forested ravine with trails crossing rustic bridges. The underwater artificial reef makes this the only Washington state park offering scuba diving opportunities.

When operational, the campground offers 15 standard sites nestled in the forest along the creek, with restrooms, showers, and a dump station. Sites accommodate vehicles up to 50 feet with limited availability. Wood fires are prohibited in the campground. A seasonal snack shack operates from Memorial Day through Labor Day, with weekend service in spring and fall.

location.directions: From I-5, take exit 149 (Kent-Des Moines Road) and head west. Turn south on Marine View Drive, then west on South 252nd Street to the park entrance.

payload.name: Dosewallips State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations available. Water is turned off at most sites from November 15 through March 31, except sites 21-29 which retain water service during winter. Fires are currently allowed in all designated fire pits and grills.
payload.short_description: Dosewallips State Park offers 97 campsites with hookup options along the scenic Dosewallips River and Hood Canal, featuring cabins, standard and utility sites, with elk herds that often wander through camp.
payload.medium_description: Located where the Dosewallips River meets Hood Canal on Washington's Olympic Peninsula, this 425-acre park provides both saltwater beach and freshwater river access. The campground offers standard sites, partial hookups (water/electric), and full hookups (water/electric/sewer), plus rustic cabins. Resident elk herds frequently pass through the campground. Activities include clamming, fishing, hiking on over 5 miles of trails, and wildlife watching.
payload.long_description:
Dosewallips State Park occupies 425 acres at the confluence of the Dosewallips River and Hood Canal, providing a rare combination of saltwater tidelands, freshwater river access, and forested uplands on Washington's Olympic Peninsula. The campground features 97 sites accommodating tents and RVs up to 40 feet, with options ranging from standard tent sites to partial hookups (water and electric) and full hookups including sewer. Platform tents and cabins are also available for those seeking a roof overhead.

Wildlife is a defining feature of this park. A resident elk herd regularly wanders through the campground, and campers should maintain 100 feet of distance and never feed them. The park offers over 5 miles of hiking trails through diverse ecosystems, access to Hood Canal for clamming and saltwater fishing, and the Dosewallips River for steelhead and salmon fishing. Facilities include flush restrooms with showers, a dump station, firewood sales, kitchen shelter, and an amphitheater for ranger programs.

The campground operates year-round with reservations available through washington.goingtocamp.com. During winter months (November 15 through March 31), water is turned off at most sites except sites 21-29, which remain winterized with water access. A winter water supply is also available near the dump station.

location.directions: From US Highway 101, the park entrance is located at milepost 306 approximately 1 mile south of Brinnon, Washington. The park is on the east side of Highway 101 at the mouth of the Dosewallips River where it meets Hood Canal.

links.title: Dosewallips State Park - WA State Parks

payload.name: LETNEY
payload.status_description: Letney does not appear in current USFS recreation listings for Angelina National Forest or on Recreation.gov, suggesting the campground may be closed, decommissioned, or converted to a different use. Contact the Angelina National Forest ranger district at (936) 897-1068 for current status.
payload.short_description: Historic USFS recreation site on Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Angelina National Forest, Jasper County, Texas.
payload.medium_description: Letney is a historic recreation site located on the shores of Sam Rayburn Reservoir within Angelina National Forest in East Texas. Documented as a USFS camping unit in 1967, the site is situated near popular recreation areas like Ebenezer Park and Sandy Creek along the 114,000-acre reservoir.
payload.long_description:
Letney Recreation Area is a historic US Forest Service site on Sam Rayburn Reservoir in Angelina National Forest, Jasper County, Texas. The site was established as a camping unit and documented in USFS records dating back to 1967.

Sam Rayburn Reservoir is the largest lake entirely within Texas at 114,000 surface acres, offering extensive fishing, boating, and water recreation opportunities. The Angelina National Forest surrounds portions of the reservoir, providing access to both developed and primitive camping experiences.

The Letney site is located in a region with several other USFS and Army Corps of Engineers recreation areas, including nearby facilities like Ebenezer Park, Sandy Creek, Caney Creek, and Boykin Springs.

location.directions: From Jasper, Texas, head north on US-96 for approximately 10 miles. Turn left onto FM 255 and continue for about 5 miles. The entrance to Letney Recreation Site will be on your right.

payload.name: Cat Highway 472 Camp
payload.status_description: Open year-round. No fee required. First-come, first-served with no reservations. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Free primitive hunter's camp in Kisatchie National Forest, open year-round with vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Highway 472 Camp is a free, primitive camping area in the Kisatchie National Forest's Catahoula district, primarily used by hunters but open to all visitors year-round. The camp is split into two locations directly across Highway 472 from each other, with basic facilities including vault toilets and information boards. Campers must be self-contained, bringing their own water and packing out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Highway 472 Camp provides a rugged, no-fee camping experience within Louisiana's Kisatchie National Forest, situated near the National Catahoula Wildlife Management Preserve. The camp is split into two distinct areas on opposite sides of Highway 472 near Packton, with the northern section in the Winn Ranger District and the southern section in the Catahoula Ranger District.

This primitive camping area caters primarily to hunters taking advantage of the surrounding wildlife management preserve, though it remains open to the general public year-round. Both camping areas offer vault toilets and information boards, but campers must come fully prepared with their own water supply and follow pack-in, pack-out principles for all waste.

The location offers direct access to the forest's backcountry and hunting opportunities. Sites are available first-come, first-served with no reservations required or accepted.

location.directions: Located on Highway 472, just off Highway 167 near Packton, Louisiana. The camp is split into two locations directly across Highway 472 from each other.

payload.name: SOUTH FOURCHE
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No restrooms or potable water available on site. Campers must be fully self-sufficient.
payload.short_description: Primitive roadside campground on Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway providing floating access to the South Fourche River in the Ouachita National Forest.
payload.medium_description: South Fourche Recreation Area is a primitive campground located one mile south of Hollis, AR on the Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway. The peaceful setting offers non-motorized boating access to the South Fourche River and sits within three miles of several trail systems including Horsethief and Billy Creek Trails. Sites are $5 per night with no water or restroom facilities available.
payload.long_description:
South Fourche Recreation Area is a primitive roadside campground nestled along the scenic Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway in Yell County. Located just one mile south of Hollis, this Ouachita National Forest site provides direct access to the South Fourche River for non-motorized floating and paddling.

The campground offers a peaceful, minimalist camping experience for those seeking solitude in the Ouachita Mountains. While amenities are limited with no restrooms or potable water available, the low $5 per night fee and year-round access make it an appealing option for self-sufficient campers. A picnic area is available for day use at no charge.

Outdoor enthusiasts will appreciate the proximity to several trail systems, with the Horsethief and Billy Creek Trails located within three miles. The area is managed by the Jessieville-Winona-Fourche Ranger District.

location.directions: One mile south of Hollis, AR on Arkansas Scenic 7 Byway (Highway 7).

payload.name: Summersville Lake State Park Overlook Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. Reservations available through the West Virginia State Parks website. Check-in at 1 p.m., checkout by noon. Quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.
payload.short_description: Summersville Lake State Park in Nicholas County is West Virginia's newest state park. Encompassing 177 acres, it overlooks the north shore of the beautiful Summersville Lake, the largest in WV. The lake offers over 60 miles of shoreline, making it a boating and water sports paradise.  The park features hiking and biking trails, and day use picnic areas, with many more recreational activities to come.
payload.medium_description: Overlook Campground is part of West Virginia's newest state park, which opened in May 2025. The campground features 38 RV sites with full hookups (electric, water, sewer) positioned behind the welcome center with panoramic mountain views. Amenities include a centrally located bathhouse with showers and restrooms, two coin-operated laundry rooms, a playground, and outdoor sink.
payload.long_description:
Overlook Campground is the largest of three campgrounds at Summersville Lake State Park, West Virginia's first new state park in over 30 years. The park occupies 177 acres on the northern shore of Summersville Lake, the state's largest body of water known for its remarkably clear blue waters and 60-mile shoreline.

The campground features 38 RV sites offering full hookups including electric, water, and sewer connections. Sites are positioned behind the welcome center and provide sweeping mountain views. A centrally located bathhouse offers showers and restrooms, while additional amenities include two coin-operated laundry rooms, a playground, and outdoor sink.

Summersville Lake is renowned for water recreation including boating, swimming, scuba diving, and fishing. The park also features the Mountaineer Mile trail unveiled during the campground's opening ceremony in May 2025.

location.directions: The park is located at 36 Park Rd., Summersville, WV 26651 on the northern shore of Summersville Lake in Nicholas County.

links.title: Summersville Lake State Park Main Page

payload.name: Fairy Stone State Park Electric / Water Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping from March 6 through December 7, 2026. Reservations available through reservevaparks.com or by phone at 1-800-933-PARK.
payload.short_description: RV-focused campground at Fairy Stone State Park with electric and water hookups on pull-through sites near scenic Fairy Stone Lake.
payload.medium_description: Fairy Stone State Park's Electric/Water Campground offers graveled pull-through sites designed for RVs and camping units up to 50 feet. All sites include 20, 30, and 50-amp electric hookups and water connections. The campground provides a common fire area with picnic tables at each end, pit toilets, and access to a dump station. No tent camping is permitted in this area.
payload.long_description:
The Electric/Water Campground at Fairy Stone State Park provides dedicated RV camping with full hookup amenities in Virginia's Blue Ridge foothills. Each graveled pull-through site accommodates units up to 50 feet long and features 20, 30, and 50-amp electric service alongside water connections. The sites are open and unshaded, designed specifically for self-contained camping units rather than tent camping.

While individual sites lack fire rings and picnic tables, the campground provides common fire areas with picnic seating at each end for socializing. Pit toilets serve the campground, and a dump station is available on-site. The campground is ADA accessible.

Fairy Stone State Park spans 4,741 acres and is famous for its unique fairy stones, cross-shaped staurolite crystals found in the area. Campers can enjoy Fairy Stone Lake's sandy beach, boat rentals, hiking trails, and the park's camp store. The park operates from early March through early December.

location.directions: From Stuart, VA, take Route 8 north approximately 7 miles to Route 57. Turn left and follow signs to Fairy Stone State Park at 967 Fairystone Lake Drive, Stuart, VA 24171.

links.title: Fairy Stone State Park Official Page

payload.name: MARTIN CREEK GS RENTAL
payload.status_description: This facility could not be located in current Recreation.gov or USFS active rental listings. Historical references exist to a Martin Creek Ranger Station in this district. The facility may be inactive, closed, or available only through direct contact with the Santa Rosa Ranger District.
payload.short_description: Historic guard station rental in the remote Santa Rosa Range of northern Nevada's Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Martin Creek Guard Station Rental is located in the Santa Rosa Range of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest in Humboldt County, Nevada. The guard station sits near Martin Creek, which originates on the east side of Buckskin Mountain at 8,000 feet elevation. This remote area offers access to the Santa Rosa-Paradise Peak Wilderness and primitive backcountry recreation.
payload.long_description:
Martin Creek Guard Station is a historic Forest Service rental facility located in the Santa Rosa Range of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest in Humboldt County, Nevada. This remote guard station sits in a mountainous area near Martin Creek, which originates on the east side of Buckskin Mountain at elevations around 8,000 feet. The surrounding landscape features rugged mountain terrain and alpine streams characteristic of this part of northwestern Nevada.

As a guard station rental, this facility offers a unique opportunity to stay in a rustic Forest Service building that was historically used by forest rangers and staff. Guard stations typically provide basic shelter and are more suited for visitors seeking a remote, self-sufficient experience rather than traditional campground amenities. The location provides access to the backcountry of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest.

Visitors should come prepared for primitive conditions and bring all necessary supplies including water, food, and bedding. The remote setting offers solitude and opportunities for outdoor recreation in the surrounding national forest lands. This rental is best suited for those comfortable with rustic accommodations and self-reliant camping.

location.directions: From U.S. Route 95, take State Route 290 northeast for approximately 22 miles to reach Paradise Valley. Martin Creek GS Rental is located near Martin Creek, a stream in Humboldt County, Nevada.

links.title: Nevada Dept of Wildlife - Martin Creek

payload.name: Denver Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed due to fire damage from the East Troublesome Fire. The campground was expected to reopen as soon as 2026, but remains closed as of the latest update.
payload.short_description: A 22-site first-come, first-served campground in the Willow Creek Valley along Highway 125, 16 miles northwest of Granby. Features two loops with vault toilets, drinking water, and fire grates.
payload.medium_description: Denver Creek Campground sits at 8,800 feet elevation in the Willow Creek Valley along US Highway 125. The campground is divided into two loops on each side of the highway, with Willow Creek flowing by the west loop. All 22 non-electric sites include tent pads, fire grates, and picnic tables. Popular activities include fishing in Willow Creek, scenic driving, hiking, and wildlife viewing.
payload.long_description:
Denver Creek Campground is located in the Arapaho National Forest's Sulphur Ranger District, 16 miles northwest of Granby along Colorado Highway 125. The campground occupies a scenic spot in the Willow Creek Valley at 8,800 feet elevation. It is divided into two loops, one on each side of the highway, with Willow Creek running alongside the west loop.

The campground offers 22 non-electric sites that accommodate tents, trailers, and RVs. Each site includes a tent pad, fire grate, and picnic table. Parking spurs range from 25 to 45 feet. Amenities include vault toilets and drinking water from a hand pump. Most sites lack shade. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations.

Popular activities include fishing in Willow Creek, scenic driving, hiking, and wildlife viewing. The area sees moderate usage. Dogs must be kept on a hand-held leash, and a single site may hold up to eight people.

location.directions: 16 miles northwest of Granby on Colorado Highway 125

payload.name: Hazard Mill Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The Forest Service no longer operates this site as a campground.
payload.short_description: Hazard Mill Campground is a permanently closed Forest Service campground in the George Washington National Forest in Warren County, Virginia.
payload.medium_description: Hazard Mill Campground was a primitive camping area located in the George Washington National Forest in Warren County, Virginia near the South Fork of the Shenandoah River. The site has been permanently closed by the U.S. Forest Service and is no longer available for overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Hazard Mill Campground was a primitive recreation site located in the George Washington National Forest in Warren County, Virginia, near the South Fork of the Shenandoah River. The campground provided a basic backcountry camping experience for visitors exploring this section of the Shenandoah Valley.

The U.S. Forest Service has permanently closed this campground. The site offered no developed amenities such as potable water, restrooms, or other facilities. The closure means the area is no longer maintained or operated as an official camping destination.

Campers seeking overnight accommodations in the George Washington National Forest should consider other active campgrounds in the area, such as Elizabeth Furnace or other developed sites managed by the Lee Ranger District.

location.directions: From McCall, Idaho, travel five miles west on Highway 55. Turn right on Goose Lake Road/Forest Road #257. Follow the paved road past Brundage Mountain Resort, where the road turns to gravel. Continue approximately 18 miles to the campground.

links.title: Virginia DWR - Hazard Mill Landing Withdrawn

payload.name: Hades
payload.status_description: The campground is closed for the season. Hades typically opens late May through mid-September, depending on snow conditions. Potable water is currently unavailable due to a sanitation system failure.
payload.short_description: Scenic 14-site campground in the North Fork Drainage of Ashley National Forest, offering trout fishing on the North Fork Duchesne River and access to the High Uintas Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Hades Campground sits at 7,400 feet in a mixed forest of aspen, subalpine fir, lodgepole pine, and spruce along the North Fork Duchesne River. The 14 single and double-family sites feature picnic tables and fire rings with grills, with some sites overlooking the river. Popular activities include fly-fishing for brook, brown, and rainbow trout, as well as hiking, mountain biking, OHV riding, and horseback riding. The Grandview Trail provides access to the Granddaddy Lake region of the High Uintas Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Hades Campground is nestled in the scenic North Fork Drainage off Highway 35, about 17 miles from Tabiona, Utah. The North Fork Drainage lies on the southern slope of the Uinta Mountains in northeastern Utah, where visitors enjoy fly-fishing and exploring numerous local trails. The campground sits at an elevation of 7,400 feet in a forest of aspen, subalpine fir, lodgepole pine, and spruce just above the North Fork Duchesne River.

The campground offers 14 sites including both single and double-family configurations. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring with grill, and some sites overlook the river. Vault toilets and trash collection are provided. Single sites accommodate up to 8 people with 1 vehicle, 1 RV/trailer, and 1 tent. Double sites accommodate up to 16 people with 2 vehicles, 2 RV/trailers, and 2 tents.

Fishing for brook, brown, and rainbow trout is the primary draw on the North Fork Duchesne. The area also offers excellent opportunities for hiking, mountain biking, OHV riding, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing. The North Fork Drainage provides access to the Granddaddy Lake region of the High Uintas Wilderness via the Grandview Trail, where numerous sparkling alpine lakes offer backcountry fishing.

location.directions: From Duchesne, Utah: Take Highway 27 north to the junction with Highway 35. Turn west on Highway 35 towards Tabiona. Travel about 28 miles to the campground in the North Fork Drainage. From Highway 40, turn north on Highway 208 to Tabiona, then proceed northwest through Hanna to the North Fork Drainage.

payload.name: BIG EDDY CAMPGROUND
payload.status_description: Open mid-May through end of September. First-come, first-served with no reservations. Fee campground with self-registration at entrance. No potable water available.
payload.short_description: Small 4-site first-come, first-served campground along the North Fork Payette River in Boise National Forest, popular with whitewater enthusiasts.
payload.medium_description: Big Eddy Campground is a compact 4-site campground situated in a scenic canyon along Highway 55, about 15 miles north of Banks, Idaho. The forested setting features Ponderosa and lodgepole pines at 4,000 feet elevation along the North Fork Payette River, a premier destination for whitewater rafting and kayaking. The site has historical significance as a former water stop for old steam engines.
payload.long_description:
Big Eddy Campground occupies a scenic canyon position just above Highway 55 in the Boise National Forest, approximately 15 miles north of Banks and 38 miles north of Boise. At 4,000 feet elevation, the small campground offers four shaded sites nestled among Ponderosa and lodgepole pines along the North Fork Payette River.

The river corridor is renowned for whitewater rafting and kayaking, making this an ideal base camp for paddlers. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Vault restrooms are provided, but there is no potable water so campers must bring their own supply.

The area holds historical interest as a former water stop for steam locomotives. Across the river, the foundation of the old water tower remains visible. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with fee collection via self-registration envelopes at the entrance.

location.directions: From Boise, travel north on State Highway 55 approximately 38 miles to Banks. Continue north on Highway 55 approximately 15 miles to the campground sign. The campground is located just off the highway at 4,000 feet elevation.

payload.name: Jarbidge Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens in June when snow clears from access roads, operating through October. Road conditions in May are variable; access may still be restricted by snow. First-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.short_description: Small, primitive free campground in the remote Jarbidge Wilderness area of northeastern Nevada, offering vault toilets and access to Nevada's first designated wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Jarbidge Campground is a small, free primitive campground located approximately 1 mile south of the historic mining town of Jarbidge in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. This remote campground provides vault toilets but no potable water. The area offers access to the Jarbidge Wilderness, Nevada's first designated wilderness, with opportunities for hiking, fishing in the Jarbidge Wild and Scenic River, hunting, and wildlife viewing.
payload.long_description:
Jarbidge Campground sits in one of Nevada's most isolated mountain ranges, approximately 1 mile south of the historic gold mining town of Jarbidge. The campground is part of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest and provides a gateway to the Jarbidge Wilderness, Nevada's first designated wilderness area. The rugged landscape features rocky peaks, cirque basins, and narrow canyons carved into the surrounding mountains.

This free, primitive campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Facilities are minimal: vault toilets are available but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The remote setting attracts hikers, anglers targeting trout in the Jarbidge Wild and Scenic River, hunters, and those seeking solitude far from developed areas.

Access to Jarbidge requires navigating remote gravel roads from Elko via State Route 225 north, then County Roads 746 and 748. The road is typically impassable due to snow from late October through June, making this a summer and early fall destination only.

location.directions: From Elko, take Nevada State Route 225 north for approximately 65 miles. Turn east onto Elko County Road 746, then north onto Elko County Road 748. Follow signs to Jarbidge. The campground is approximately 1 mile south of town. Roads are unpaved and may be impassable during winter and early spring due to snow.

payload.name: Twin Falls Resort State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Check-in is 1 p.m. and check-out is noon. Two-night minimum required on weekends, with a 14-consecutive-night maximum stay. One bathhouse is heated for winter camping.
payload.short_description: Set on a high, wooded ridge in the rugged mountains of Wyoming County in southern West Virginia, Twin Falls Resort State Park is the ideal site for nature lovers. With multiple lodging options, more than 25 miles of hiking trails, a championship golf course and its restored Pioneer Farm, Twin Falls offers an abundance of recreation and relaxation for guests of all ages.
payload.medium_description: Twin Falls Resort State Park Campground is nestled on a high, wooded ridge in the rugged mountains of southern West Virginia. The campground offers 50 paved campsites divided between two loops: Foxhunters Point, a more shaded and wooded area, and Dogwood Flats, which has a sunnier atmosphere. Twenty-five sites have electric hookups (30/20/15 amp), and all sites include grills and picnic tables. Two bathhouses with restrooms and showers serve the campground, one heated for winter camping. A dump station and seasonal contact station with laundry and small store are on-site.
payload.long_description:
Twin Falls Resort State Park Campground occupies 3,776 acres of forested mountain terrain in Wyoming County, West Virginia. The campground features 50 paved campsites arranged in two distinct loops. Foxhunters Point offers heavily wooded, shaded sites for a more tranquil camping experience, while Dogwood Flats provides sunnier sites that showcase the surrounding scenic beauty. Of the 50 sites, 25 offer electric hookups with 30, 20, and 15 amp service. All sites are equipped with grills and picnic tables.

The campground operates year-round, making it one of the few options in the region for winter camping. Two bathhouses serve campers, with one heated for cold-weather use. Additional amenities include a dump station, and a seasonal contact station that houses a laundromat, small convenience store, and registration area. Reservations can be made online at wvstateparks.com, by phone, or at the campground office, with a two-night minimum on weekends and 14-night maximum stay.

Beyond camping, the park offers over 25 miles of hiking and biking trails, including routes to Twin Falls and Black Fork Falls. The 18-hole golf course, splash pad, game room, tennis court, and playgrounds provide additional recreation. The park also features a lodge and cabins for those seeking more comfortable accommodations.

location.directions: Located off Route 97 in Mullens, West Virginia. From Beckley, take US-19 south to WV-54 west, then follow signs to Twin Falls Resort State Park.

links.title: Twin Falls Resort State Park Official Page
Camping at Twin Falls Resort State Park

payload.name: Watoga State Park Riverside Campground
payload.status_description: Open spring through fall, weather permitting. Reservations accepted starting February 15 via mail, with call-in reservations beginning March 15 and walk-in reservations starting April 1. Minimum two-night stay on weekends, one-night minimum Sunday through Thursday. Maximum 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Located in the mountains of Pocahontas County, just 14 miles south of Marlinton, Watoga State Park is West Virginia’s largest state park. With 10,100 acres of land, Watoga is filled with many recreational activities. There’s hiking, fishing, boating and vacation cabins, open year-round. Watoga Lake is known for excellent fishing opportunities and is part of the Division of Natural Resources' stocking program. A multipurpose building, museum and observation tower are a few of the unique attractions at Watoga State Park.
payload.medium_description: Riverside Campground is the larger of two campgrounds at Watoga State Park, featuring 50 campsites with 50-amp electric hookups. Situated along the Greenbrier River, each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The campground offers a central bathhouse with showers, coin-operated laundry, dish-washing stations, and free WiFi at the bathhouse. Open spring through fall, weather permitting.
payload.long_description:
Riverside Campground is located within Watoga State Park, West Virginia's largest state park spanning 10,100 acres in the mountains of Pocahontas County. The campground provides 50 sites, all equipped with 50-amp electric service, making it suitable for RVs, travel trailers, truck campers, and tents. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring for campfires.

Amenities include a central bathhouse with showers, coin-operated laundry facilities, and dish-washing stations. Free WiFi is available at the bathhouse. The campground sits along the Greenbrier River, providing easy access to fishing and kayaking. Watoga State Park offers extensive recreational opportunities including over 40 miles of hiking trails, swimming at the Watoga Lake, and wildlife viewing.

Reservations can be made online at wvstateparks.com or by phone. Weekend stays require a minimum of two consecutive nights (Friday-Saturday), while weeknight stays have a one-night minimum. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. The campground accepts tents, folding campers, travel trailers, truck campers, motor homes, and van conversions.

location.directions: From Marlinton, WV, take US-219 south approximately 10 miles, then turn left onto Seebert Road/County Route 27. Follow signs to Watoga State Park. The park address is 4800 Watoga Park Road, Marlinton, WV 24954-9550.

payload.name: QUIST
payload.status_description: Closed for the season. Campgrounds on the South Park Ranger District typically close in mid-October and reopen in late spring, though specific opening dates vary by year and conditions.
payload.short_description: A campground in Pike National Forest's South Park Ranger District in Park County, Colorado, operating seasonally.
payload.medium_description: Quist Campground is located in the South Park Ranger District of Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado. As with other campgrounds in this district, it operates seasonally and is closed during winter months.
payload.long_description: Quist Campground sits within the South Park Ranger District of Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado. The South Park Ranger District encompasses over 456,000 acres of diverse terrain in the South Park basin, one of Colorado's high mountain parks. The area offers access to National Forest recreation opportunities including hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing. Like other developed campgrounds in the South Park Ranger District, Quist operates on a seasonal schedule, typically closing in mid-October and remaining closed through the winter months due to snow and weather conditions. The Pike National Forest provides a variety of camping experiences across its districts, from developed campgrounds to dispersed camping opportunities on National Forest land.

payload.name: Nathan And Olive Boone Homestead Shs Shelters
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic shelter only. No overnight camping is available at this historic site. The site is open April through October (Wednesday through Sunday) and November through March (Friday through Sunday). Closed on major holidays.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelter at Nathan and Olive Boone Homestead State Historic Site. This is NOT an overnight campground; the shelters are for picnicking only.
payload.medium_description: The shelter at Nathan and Olive Boone Homestead State Historic Site is a day-use picnic facility, not an overnight campground. The 22' x 36' shelter accommodates up to 50 people and includes six picnic tables, electricity, and two grills. Accessible restrooms with running water and a water fountain are nearby. The shelter can be reserved in advance or used on a first-come, first-served basis if not reserved.
payload.long_description:
Nathan and Olive Boone Homestead State Historic Site preserves the 1837 home of Nathan Boone, youngest son of legendary frontiersman Daniel Boone. The site features hiking trails, interpretive programs, and a picnic area with a reservable shelter.

The shelter is strictly a day-use facility. No overnight camping is available at this historic site. The shelter measures 22' x 36' and accommodates up to 50 people. It includes six picnic tables, electricity, and two grills. Accessible restrooms with running water are located nearby, along with a drinking fountain. The shelter is located approximately one-quarter mile from the historic Boone home.

Reservations can be made 30 days to 12 months in advance online, or by contacting the site directly for shorter-notice reservations. If not reserved, the shelter is available first-come, first-served during operating hours.

location.directions: Located at 7850 N. State Highway V, Ash Grove, Missouri, approximately 2 miles north of Ash Grove in Greene County.

address.full: 7850 N State Highway V, Ash Grove, MO 65604

payload.name: North Boulder Lake Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates first-come, first-served with no reservations. Access depends on road conditions and snow levels on Burnt Lake Road. No potable water is available; bring your own supply.
payload.short_description: Free primitive BLM campground with 5 first-come, first-served sites on the northwest shore of Boulder Lake near Pinedale, Wyoming.
payload.medium_description: North Boulder Lake Campground is a small, free BLM campground located on the northwest end of Boulder Lake at 7,300 feet elevation. The campground offers 5 first-come, first-served sites, each with a fire ring and picnic table, plus a shared double vault toilet. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
North Boulder Lake Campground is a primitive Bureau of Land Management campground situated on the northwest shore of Boulder Lake in Sublette County, Wyoming. The campground sits at approximately 7,300 feet elevation and provides access to a scenic high-country lake with about 3 miles of shoreline.

The campground has five basic campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. A single double vault toilet serves all campers. There is no potable water, so visitors must bring their own supply. Sites are free and available first-come, first-served with a 14-day stay limit.

Boulder Lake offers opportunities for fishing, boating (motorized and non-motorized), swimming, wildlife viewing, and photography. The area is also popular for hiking, horseback riding, and hunting in season. The nearby Boulder Lake Trailhead provides access to backcountry trails.

location.directions: Approximately 11 miles south of Pinedale on US 191, then 7 miles north on Burnt Lake Road.

payload.name: DISTILLERY BAY
payload.status_description: No official documentation found for this campground through USFS, Recreation.gov, or Idaho state park resources. The site may be an informal dispersed camping area, known locally by a different name, or no longer operational.
payload.short_description: Distillery Bay is a remote location along Priest Lake in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests, accessible via the Lakeshore Trail.
payload.medium_description: Distillery Bay is situated along the shores of Priest Lake in Bonner County, Idaho, within the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. This remote location is accessed via the Priest Lake Lakeshore Trail and offers a secluded experience in the forested mountains of the Selkirk Range.
payload.long_description:
Distillery Bay is a remote location on Priest Lake, surrounded by the rugged Selkirk Mountains in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. Often called Idaho's crown jewel, Priest Lake offers stunning natural beauty with clear waters and dense forests of hemlock and cedar. The bay is accessed via the Priest Lake Lakeshore Trail, making it ideal for those seeking a more primitive and secluded camping experience away from developed facilities.

The area sits at approximately 2,500 feet elevation and provides opportunities for fishing, hiking, and water activities on the 25,000-acre Priest Lake. The surrounding forests are home to diverse wildlife, and the Selkirk Mountains provide a dramatic backdrop to the pristine lake waters.

location.directions: From Clark Fork, drive south on Road 278 (Johnson Creek Road) for approximately 30 miles to reach the campground. Alternatively, by boat, the site is located on the west shore of Lake Pend Oreille, about 10 miles south of Garfield Bay.

payload.name: Haskins Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally, typically opening in mid-June after snowmelt and closing in October. At nearly 9,000 feet elevation, opening and closing dates depend on snow conditions. All sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Remote Forest Service campground along Haskins Creek in the Sierra Madre Range of Medicine Bow National Forest, offering primitive camping at nearly 9,000 feet elevation west of Encampment, Wyoming.
payload.medium_description: Haskins Creek Campground is a small, developed Forest Service campground located approximately 15 miles west of Encampment, Wyoming along Highway 70. Situated at roughly 8,950 feet elevation in the Sierra Madre Range, this 13-site campground provides a rustic mountain camping experience with access to fishing in Haskins Creek and nearby hiking trails to Baby Lakes and Huston Park Wilderness. Wildlife including deer, moose, and elk frequent the area.
payload.long_description:
Haskins Creek Campground occupies a scenic forested setting along its namesake creek in the Sierra Madre Range of the Medicine Bow National Forest. The campground sits at approximately 8,950 feet elevation, providing cool mountain temperatures and a remote atmosphere about 15 miles west of Encampment via Wyoming Highway 70.

The 13 campsites offer basic amenities including picnic tables, fire rings, vault toilets, and trash service. A camp host is typically on site during the operating season. The campground serves as a base for anglers fishing Haskins Creek and nearby streams, as well as hikers accessing trails to Baby Lakes and the Huston Park Wilderness. Wildlife viewing opportunities abound, with deer, moose, and elk commonly seen in the surrounding forest.

location.directions: From Encampment, Wyoming, travel west on Wyoming Highway 70 for approximately 15 miles. The campground is located along the highway near Haskins Creek.

payload.name: John F Kennedy
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The campground was shut down years ago due to vandalism and is now gated off. The site serves only as a trailhead parking area with no camping permitted.
payload.short_description: Former Forest Service campground in the Manzano Mountains, permanently closed due to vandalism. Now serves only as a trailhead parking area for Trigo Canyon Trail and other hiking routes.
payload.medium_description: John F Kennedy Campground was once an established Forest Service campground with 12 sites at the western base of the Manzano Mountains near Belen. The facility was permanently closed years ago due to persistent vandalism issues. The campground area is now gated off and only ruins remain. The site continues to serve as a trailhead parking area for Trigo Canyon Trail, Salas Trail, and Comanche Canyon Trail.
payload.long_description:
John F Kennedy Campground was a developed Forest Service campground located in Cibola National Forest at the western base of the Manzano Mountains in Valencia County, New Mexico. The campground sat at approximately 6,148 feet elevation and once offered 12 camping units in a setting of pinyon, juniper, and Gambel oak.

The facility has been permanently closed for many years due to persistent vandalism issues. The camping area is now gated off and only ruins remain of the former campground infrastructure. The Forest Service no longer lists it among active campgrounds in Cibola National Forest.

Today, the site serves only as a trailhead parking area providing access to Trigo Canyon Trail (185), Salas Trail (184), and Comanche Canyon Trail (182). Access requires navigating rough dirt roads best suited for high-clearance 4WD vehicles, particularly after rain when large mud puddles can form. No facilities remain at the site. The Mountainair Ranger District manages the area.

location.directions: Located approximately 10 miles northeast of Belen via rough dirt roads from the Tome Hill area. High-clearance 4WD vehicle recommended, especially after rain. Contact Mountainair Ranger District at +1 (505) 847-2990 for current road conditions.

payload.name: Beaver Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season with full services. Water and dump station are operational. Reservations available 95 days in advance through reservendparks.com. Limited services begin in fall, typically with water shut-off around October 1-4 and dump station closure.
payload.short_description: Beaver Lake State Park offers modern and primitive campsites on a quiet prairie lake in southeastern North Dakota, featuring flush toilets, showers, and a dump station.
payload.medium_description: Beaver Lake State Park provides a peaceful escape on the rolling North Dakota prairie. The campground offers 25 modern campsites with electric and water hookups, 3 modern group sites, and 5 primitive sites along the lakeshore. Amenities include flush toilets, showers, and a dump station. Three seasonal camping cabins are also available near the primitive loop.
payload.long_description:
Beaver Lake State Park sits along a quiet lake in Logan County, offering campers a secluded retreat amid gently rolling prairie. The campground features 25 modern sites with electric and water hookups priced at $25-30 per night, along with 5 primitive sites at $15 per night for those seeking a simpler experience. Three modern group campsites accommodate multiple units for larger gatherings.

The park provides solid amenities including flush toilets, showers, and a sewage dump station. Three seasonal camping cabins (Hoberg, Homestead, and Pioneer) sit along the lake's edge near the primitive loop, sleeping five guests each with climate control, refrigerator, and microwave. The park's 5.4-mile non-motorized trail system offers hiking and biking through the scenic prairie landscape.

Reservations are available through reservendparks.com or by calling 800-807-4723, opening 95 days in advance. Check-in is at 4 pm with checkout at 3 pm for campsites. The park operates year-round but transitions to limited services from fall through spring, with campground water and dump station typically shut down in early October.

location.directions: Located in Logan County, southeastern North Dakota, near the town of Wishek.

links.title: Beaver Lake State Park - ND Parks

payload.name: BERYLLIUM
payload.status_description: Open for dispersed camping. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through August 1, 2026, prohibiting campfires except in permanent fire pits at developed Forest Service campgrounds. Badger Flats occupancy restrictions require camping only at designated dispersed campsites or more than ¼ mile from National Forest roads.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed camping area in Pike National Forest along Forest Service Road 225 (Beryllium Road), part of the Badger Flats Trail Network near Lake George, Colorado.
payload.medium_description: Beryllium is a dispersed camping area in the Badger Flats Management Area of Pike National Forest's South Park Ranger District. Located on Forest Service Road 225 (Beryllium Road), the area features a mix of ponderosa pine forest and open meadows. As dispersed camping, there are no developed facilities, fees, or reservations. Popular with OHV enthusiasts due to extensive trail access in the Badger Flats network.
payload.long_description:
Beryllium is a dispersed camping area along Forest Service Road 225 (Beryllium Road) in Pike National Forest, approximately 5 miles south of Lake George via County Road 96. The 4-mile unpaved road winds through coniferous forest and open meadows at elevations around 9,000 feet in the South Park Ranger District.

As part of the Badger Flats Management Area, camping is restricted to designated dispersed campsites (marked with campsite markers) or locations more than one-quarter mile from National Forest System roads. The area is popular with off-road vehicle enthusiasts due to the extensive OHV-friendly trail network. Nearby fishing destinations include Spinney Reservoir, the Dream Stream, and Eleven Mile Reservoir.

This is primitive dispersed camping with no developed facilities. Campers must be fully self-sufficient, pack out all trash, and practice Leave No Trace principles. Cell coverage is available from AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile.

location.directions: From Lake George, Colorado, head south on County Road 96 for approximately 5 miles. Turn onto Forest Service Road 225 (Beryllium Road), an unpaved road within the Badger Flats Trail Network. Look for designated dispersed campsites marked with campsite markers.

payload.name: Aroostook State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for primitive camping and day-use. Drinking water, flush toilets, and showers are not available due to infrastructure improvements. Vault toilets are available. Campers must bring their own drinking water. Reservations available through campwithme.com through September 12, 2026; first-come, first-served after September 14.
payload.short_description: Aroostook offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Aroostook State Park, established in 1939 as Maine's first state park, encompasses nearly 800 acres on Echo Lake south of Presque Isle. The campground features approximately 30 wooded sites with picnic tables and fire rings, some offering water and electric hookups. Popular activities include hiking Quaggy Jo Mountain for panoramic views, fishing for brook trout, boating, and cross-country skiing in winter.
payload.long_description:
Aroostook State Park holds the distinction of being Maine's first state park. In 1938, citizens of Presque Isle donated 100 acres of land to the State of Maine, and the park opened in 1939. Today it encompasses nearly 800 acres including Quaggy Jo Mountain and frontage on Echo Lake, offering hiking trails with outstanding views, brook trout fishing, and winter cross-country skiing.

The campground features approximately 30 wooded sites that accommodate both tents and camping trailers. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, and some sites offer water and electric hookups. The park provides a boat launch and dock for accessing Echo Lake, where canoes and paddleboats are available for rent. A kitchen pavilion with lights and running water serves campers.

The park is open daily from 9:00 a.m. to sunset year-round. Reservations can be made through campwithme.com, with sites transitioning to first-come, first-served after mid-September. The 14-night maximum stay limit applies during peak summer season.

location.directions: Off U.S. Route 1 south of Presque Isle. The park entrance is at 87 State Park Road, Presque Isle, on Echo Lake.

address.full: 87 Old State Park Rd, Presque Isle, ME 04769

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Camden Hills State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season. The campground opened May 15. As of June 1, 2026, a Do Not Drink the Water Order is in effect; campers should bring their own drinking water. Reservations available at campwithme.com.
payload.short_description: Camden Hills offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Camden Hills State Park Campground offers 107 wooded sites nestled in the hills above Penobscot Bay. The campground provides a mix of tent sites and RV sites with electric and water hookups. Comfort stations with hot showers, a dump station, and Wi-Fi are available. The park features over 30 miles of hiking trails and scenic views from Mount Battie, accessible by vehicle or foot.
payload.long_description:
Camden Hills State Park Campground sits in the forested hills of mid-coast Maine, about two miles north of the town of Camden on Route 1. The 107-site campground accommodates tents, pop-ups, and RVs with sites ranging from small (up to 20 feet) to extra-large (35+ feet). Select sites offer electric and water hookups. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Comfort stations provide hot showers and flush toilets, and a dump station serves RV campers.

The park encompasses over 5,700 acres with more than 30 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, cross-country skiing, and horseback riding. Mount Battie, the park's signature summit, offers panoramic views of Penobscot Bay and the surrounding islands. A paved auto road provides vehicle access to the summit for those who prefer to drive. The campground serves as an excellent base for exploring the Camden area, with the harbor town's shops and restaurants just a short drive away.

Winter camping is available by reservation with rustic shelter accommodations. The park maintains year-round day-use access with seasonal hours for camping operations.

location.directions: From Camden, drive 2 miles north on US Route 1 (Belfast Road). The park entrance is on the left at 280 Belfast Road.

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Cobscook Bay State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. The new shower and toilet building is operational with flush toilets, showers, and drinking water. Electrical power on campsites 1-27 is not available due to a mechanical issue; those sites remain open with water access. Winter camping available by contacting the park.
payload.short_description: Cobscook Bay offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Cobscook Bay State Park offers 106 campsites spread across 888 acres on three sides of Cobscook Bay, where tides fluctuate up to 24 feet. Many waterfront sites border Whiting Bay. The campground features a new bathhouse with flush toilets and showers, a dump station, and boat launch access to the bay's challenging tidal waters.
payload.long_description:
Cobscook Bay State Park sits on an 888-acre peninsula surrounded on three sides by the waters of Cobscook Bay, home to some of the most extreme tidal fluctuations on the Atlantic coast. The bay's name derives from the Maliseet-Passamaquoddy word meaning "boiling tides," and the 24-foot tidal range creates a dynamic ecosystem that attracts seals, bald eagles, ospreys, and migratory shorebirds.

The campground offers 106 sites for tents and RVs, with many premier waterfront locations along Whiting Bay. A newly constructed bathhouse provides flush toilets, hot showers, and drinking water. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with firewood available for purchase in the park. Two group camping areas accommodate parties of 12 and 30 campers respectively.

The park serves as an excellent base for exploring Washington County's remote Downeast coast. Two easy hiking trails wind through the property, and the boat launch provides access to Cobscook Bay for experienced paddlers and boaters comfortable with strong tidal currents.

location.directions: Located on U.S. Route 1, four miles south of Dennysville in Edmunds Township.

address.full: 41 S Edmunds Rd, Edmunds Twp, ME 04628

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: WRENS NEST
payload.status_description: Unable to verify this campground exists through official USFS or Recreation.gov sources. The site may be an unofficial dispersed camping area, may be known by a different name, or may no longer be operational.
payload.short_description: A National Forest campground in Pike National Forest, located in Park County, Colorado at approximately 10,000 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Wrens Nest Campground is situated in Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado. The campground is located in a high-elevation mountain setting typical of Pike National Forest campgrounds in this region.
payload.long_description: Wrens Nest Campground is located in Pike National Forest within Park County, Colorado. Situated at high elevation in the Rocky Mountains, the campground offers access to the recreational opportunities of Pike National Forest. The Pike National Forest encompasses diverse terrain from the Front Range west of Colorado Springs, providing opportunities for hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing. Like many Forest Service campgrounds in this area, Wrens Nest likely provides a rustic camping experience surrounded by mountain scenery and coniferous forest.

location.directions: The information provided does not contain any directions to a physical campground, and only includes details about a historic home museum and a bakery.

payload.name: MARBLE CREEK
payload.status_description: The campground typically operates from June through September, depending on road conditions and snowmelt. Forest Road 321 is not maintained in winter. First-come, first-served.
payload.short_description: Small primitive USFS campground with 2 sites in the Marble Creek drainage of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests, offering access to historic logging sites and creek-side recreation.
payload.medium_description: Marble Creek Campground is a small, rustic Forest Service campground with just 2 sites along Marble Creek in the St. Joe River area of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The primitive campground sits at approximately 3,500 feet elevation and provides a quiet, intimate camping experience for those seeking solitude near historic logging areas and excellent fishing.
payload.long_description:
Marble Creek Campground is a primitive Forest Service campground tucked along Marble Creek Road (FR 321) in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. With only 2 campsites, this rustic facility offers a quiet, secluded camping experience away from more developed recreation areas.
