The campground provides basic amenities including a vault toilet but no potable water, so campers must bring their own supplies.

The Marble Creek area is rich in early 20th-century logging history, with remnants of historic logging camps, splash dams, and an old incline railroad visible along the trail system. The creek itself offers good fishing opportunities, and the surrounding forest produces excellent huckleberry picking when in season. The nearby Marble Creek Trail system provides access to multiple trails including Trail #261, #251, and #273 for hiking, horseback riding, and wildlife viewing.

Access to the campground requires driving 35 miles east of St. Maries on Forest Highway 50 to the Marble Creek Historical Site, then continuing approximately 6 miles south on Forest Road 321. The road is not maintained in winter and access depends on seasonal snowmelt conditions.

location.directions: From St. Maries, Idaho, travel 35 miles east on Forest Highway 50 (St. Joe River Road) to the Marble Creek Historical Site. Turn south onto Forest Road 321 (Marble Creek Road) and continue approximately 6 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Lewis And Clark State Park Equipment Rental
payload.status_description: This is a day-use equipment rental service, not an overnight campground. Equipment including bikes, kayaks, canoes, paddle boards, and snowshoes is available for rent during park hours. Reserve through reservendparks.com or contact the park.
payload.short_description: Day-use equipment rental service at Lewis & Clark State Park offering bikes, kayaks, canoes, stand-up paddle boards, and snowshoes on the shores of Lake Sakakawea.
payload.medium_description: Lewis & Clark State Park Equipment Rental is a day-use service offering recreational gear for exploring the park and Lake Sakakawea. Available equipment includes fat tire bikes, kayaks, canoes, stand-up paddle boards, and snowshoes. This is not an overnight camping facility.
payload.long_description:
Lewis & Clark State Park Equipment Rental provides day-use recreational equipment for visitors to explore the park and Lake Sakakawea. The rental program includes fat tire bikes at $8/hour or $50/day with helmets included, snowshoes at $15/day, and watercraft including kayaks, canoes, and stand-up paddle boards for summer use.

This is a day-use service only and does not include overnight accommodations. Visitors seeking camping should look at the main Lewis & Clark State Park campground, which offers 96 campsites with various hookup options. Equipment can be reserved through the online reservation system at reservendparks.com or by contacting the park directly. Groups should call ahead to ensure equipment availability.

location.directions: Located at Lewis & Clark State Park, 4904 119th Road NW, Epping, ND 58843, on the north shore of Lake Sakakawea.

payload.name: Bradbury Mountain State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round from 9:00 a.m. to sunset daily. Campground facilities are closed during off-season; water is not available during winter camping. Reservations open February 1st at 9:00 AM EST and must be made by phone. Quiet hours 10:00 PM to 7:00 AM.
payload.short_description: Bradbury Mountain offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Bradbury Mountain State Park offers group camping on 800 acres of forested land in Pownal, Maine. The campground features two secluded group sites, each accommodating up to 50 campers in a tent-only setting. Each site includes a large Adirondack shelter that sleeps 6-8, a fire ring, and a picnic table. Hot showers are available during the regular season. The park is open year-round and sits conveniently between Portland and Lewiston-Auburn, a short drive west of Freeport.
payload.long_description:
Bradbury Mountain State Park Campground provides a group camping experience on 800 acres of forested land in Pownal, Maine. Located on Route 9 between Portland and Lewiston-Auburn and just west of Freeport, the park attracts visitors who enjoy hiking, picnicking, and camping in a natural setting. The summit of Bradbury Mountain offers views of Casco Bay and the White Mountains.

The campground consists of two secluded group campsites designed for tent camping only. Each site accommodates up to 50 campers and features a large Adirondack shelter that can sleep 6-8 people, along with a fire ring and picnic table. Hot showers are available during the regular operating season. Potable water is available seasonally but not during winter camping periods.

Reservations open February 1st at 9:00 AM EST each year and must be made by phone. The park is open year-round from 9:00 AM to sunset daily, though campground facilities are closed during the off-season. Winter camping is available with prior arrangement by calling the park directly.

location.directions: Located at 528 Hallowell Road, Pownal, ME. The park is on Route 9 about halfway between Portland and Lewiston-Auburn, a short drive west of Freeport.

links.title: Bradbury Mountain State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Enduro Ohv
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to hurricane damage. The Enduro Trail system was heavily destroyed and requires complete reconstruction. Reopening date is undetermined.
payload.short_description: Primitive OHV trailhead camp in Kisatchie National Forest offering vault toilets and access to multi-use trails. No water or trash services.
payload.medium_description: Enduro Camp is a primitive camping area at the Enduro Multiple-Use Trailhead in the Calcasieu Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest. The camp provides vault restrooms but no potable water or trash services. It serves as a base for OHV riders accessing approximately 30 miles of designated trails through the Vernon Unit.
payload.long_description:
Enduro Camp is a primitive overnight camping area located at the Enduro Multiple-Use Trailhead in Vernon Parish within the Calcasieu Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest. The campground serves primarily as a staging area for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts accessing the Enduro Trail system, which features roughly 30 miles of designated routes including the South Loop, Fullerton Loop, and Mogul Loop.

Facilities are minimal, consisting only of vault restrooms. There is no potable water available, so campers must bring an adequate supply. No trash receptacles are provided, making this a pack-it-out facility. The camp operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations accepted through Recreation.gov.

The site is located in a remote forested area accessed via Forest Roads 440 and 442 off Highway 399. Group picnicking is also available at the site.

location.directions: From Leesville, take US Highway 171 south 7 miles to LA Highway 10. Turn left and proceed east 18 miles to Highway 399. Turn left on Highway 399 and proceed 2 miles to Forest Road 440. Turn left and proceed 1 mile to Forest Road 442 and the Enduro Trailhead Camp.

payload.name: Chinquapin Hollow
payload.status_description: The campground is currently closed until further notice due to infrastructure damage. Trails and the boat launch remain open for day use only.
payload.short_description: A group tent-only campsite at Lake Wedington in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest, offering a secluded setting for groups of 7 to 50 people near a scenic 102-acre lake.
payload.medium_description: Chinquapin Hollow is a reservable group tent campground within the Lake Wedington Recreation Area, located 13 miles west of Fayetteville in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest. The site accommodates groups of 7 to 50 people with a fire ring, water hookup, and shade. Lake Wedington offers fishing, swimming, and boating on its 102-acre lake, plus hiking and mountain biking trails including the 16-mile North Twin Trail.
payload.long_description:
Chinquapin Hollow is a designated group tent camping area at Lake Wedington Recreation Area in the Boston Mountain Ranger District of the Ozark-St. Francis National Forest. Situated in the scenic Ozark Plateau of northwest Arkansas, the campground provides a peaceful retreat for organized groups of 7 to 50 people. The site features a fire ring with seating logs, water hookup, and natural shade, though no electrical hookups are available.

Lake Wedington's 102-acre lake offers excellent recreational opportunities including fishing, non-motorized boating and kayaking, and swimming at the designated beach. Motors are limited to 10 horsepower or less. The surrounding forest provides hiking and mountain biking on trails including the Lakeshore Hiking Trail that circles much of the lake and the 16-mile North Twin Trail.

The group campsite requires advance reservations and has specific rules including no pets (except qualified service animals) and a locked gate policy after posted closing times. Groups receive the lock combination at check-in.

location.directions: From Fayetteville, travel west on State Highway 16 for approximately 13 miles to reach Lake Wedington Recreation Area.

payload.name: Lake St. George State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for summer camping. Winter camping is currently unavailable due to ongoing construction. Reservations are handled through CampWithME.com.
payload.short_description: Lake St. George offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Lake St. George State Park campground occupies the northwest shore of its namesake lake in Liberty, Maine. Some sites sit directly on the water, offering sunrise views over the crystal-clear lake. The day-use area with beach, playground, and boat launch is a short walk from camp. Canoe, kayak, and paddleboat rentals are available on-site.
payload.long_description:
Lake St. George State Park campground is set on the undeveloped northwest shore of Lake St. George, a clear-water lake known for landlocked salmon and brook trout. Many campsites are positioned directly on the shoreline, and each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. The adjacent day-use area features a swimming beach staffed by lifeguards from mid-June through mid-August, along with picnic tables, grills, a playground, and courts for volleyball and basketball.

Boaters have access to a trailered boat launch and can rent canoes, paddle boats, or kayaks to explore the lake's quiet coves. The 1.5-mile Old Jeep Trail provides a moderate-to-difficult hiking option through the surrounding forest. In winter the park connects to 17 miles of groomed snowmobile trails leading to Frye Mountain, and anglers can ice fish the lake.

The park is located 16 miles west of Belfast and 25 miles east of Augusta on Maine Route 3, making it an accessible base for exploring Waldo County.

location.directions: From Belfast, drive 16 miles west on Maine Route 3. From Augusta, drive 25 miles east on Route 3. The park entrance is at 278 Belfast Augusta Rd. in Liberty.

links.title: Maine DACF Lake St. George Trail Conditions
Maine State Parks RVs and Campers

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: STANSHAW
payload.status_description: Open for camping on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations available. Forest-wide stay limit of 14 consecutive days and 30 days per calendar year applies.
payload.short_description: Remote equestrian campground at 4,900 feet serving as a base camp for horseback riders accessing the Stanshaw trail into Marble Mountains Wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Stanshaw Equestrian Camp is a dispersed camping area designed for horseback riders venturing into the Marble Mountains Wilderness via the Stanshaw trail. The camp features five large sites with tables and fire rings, a vault restroom, and corrals with running water for stock animals. At 4,900 feet elevation, the site offers comfortable summer temperatures but no potable water for humans.
payload.long_description:
Stanshaw Equestrian Camp is a remote dispersed camping area in Six Rivers National Forest, situated at 4,900 feet elevation near the boundary of the Marble Mountains Wilderness. The camp serves as a staging area for equestrian recreationists heading out on the Stanshaw trail, which provides access to the wilderness area's craggy peaks, deep conifer-cloaked canyons, abundant meadows, and numerous alpine lakes.

The campground offers five large campsites, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Several corrals with running water are available for stock animals. A single vault restroom serves the camp. Potable water is not available, so visitors must bring their own drinking water supply.

Access is via a 14-mile drive on Forest Road 15N17 from Highway 96 near the Salmon River Road junction. The road is suitable for horse trailers. Travel time from the highway is approximately 1¼ hours. The camp operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations.

location.directions: From Highway 96, take Salmon River Road (Forest Highway 93) for ¼ mile, then turn left onto Forest Road 15N17. Continue approximately 14 miles to Stanshaw Campground/Trailhead. Travel time is approximately 1¼ hours. Road is suitable for horse trailers.

links.title: Six Rivers NF - Stanshaw Equestrian Camp

payload.name: Lamoine State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open May 15 through October 15. Park hours are 9:00 a.m. to sunset daily. Reservations available online at CampWithME.com. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights June through August.
payload.short_description: Lamoine offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Lamoine State Park is a 55-acre oceanfront park on the shores of Frenchman Bay, offering 61 campsites spread across wooded loops from grassy hilltops to shaded waterfront. The campground features flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and an RV dump station. A trailered boat launch provides direct bay access for paddling and fishing. Located just 8 miles southeast of Ellsworth, the park serves as an excellent base camp for exploring Acadia National Park and the Downeast Maine coast.
payload.long_description:
Lamoine State Park sits on 55 acres along the rocky shores of Frenchman Bay in Downeast Maine. The campground offers 61 single-family sites arranged in loops descending from higher ground to the waterfront. Sites at the top of the campground tend to be grassier with more sun exposure, while those closer to the water provide more shade and tree cover. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grate.

Facilities include a bathhouse with flush toilets and hot showers, additional vault toilets throughout the campground, potable water from spigots, and a dump station near the entrance. There is one ADA-accessible site. The park accommodates RVs and trailers up to 35 feet, though some sources indicate the park can handle units up to 45 feet depending on the specific site.

Beyond camping, Lamoine offers a trailered boat launch for exploring Frenchman Bay by kayak, canoe, or motorboat. The park also features a picnic area, playground, and day-use beach access. Its location 8 miles southeast of Ellsworth makes it a quieter, more affordable alternative to staying directly in Acadia National Park while still providing convenient access to Bar Harbor, Mount Desert Island, and the surrounding Downeast coast.

location.directions: From Ellsworth, take Route 184 southeast for 8 miles to the park entrance at 23 State Park Road, Lamoine.

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Tomlinson Run State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the season, operating spring through fall, weather permitting. Reservations require a minimum two-night stay on weekends (Friday-Saturday) or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Located near the foremost tip of the Northern Panhandle along the Ohio River, Tomlinson Run can claim the title of West Virginia’s “top park.” This park’s wide range of recreational opportunities attract local and out-of-state visitors and include camping, picnicking, boating, miniature golf, swimming, basketball and volleyball. The park's 1,398 acres are roughly divided into two sections: a wilderness area with heavily forested hills, overhanging cliffs of sandstone and shale, and many wildflowers and fauna, and a developed area with traditional park offerings.
payload.medium_description: Tomlinson Run State Park's campground offers 48 traditional campsites in a 1,398-acre park along the Ohio River at the top of West Virginia's Northern Panhandle. The campground features both electric and non-electric sites, two bathhouses with showers and laundry facilities, a dump station, and a convenience store. Sites accommodate tents and trailers, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring.
payload.long_description:
Tomlinson Run State Park sits along the Ohio River at the top of West Virginia's Northern Panhandle, encompassing 1,398 acres divided between a wilderness area with forests and cliffs and a developed section with traditional park amenities. The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting, with park hours from 6 AM to 10 PM.

The campground features 48 traditional campsites available in both electric and non-electric configurations. All sites accommodate tents and trailers, with each site including a picnic table and fire ring. Two bathhouses provide hot showers and laundry facilities. A contact station and convenience store serve campers, and a dump station is available for RVs. Five camper cabins are also available for rent from April through October.

Recreational opportunities include boating, swimming, miniature golf, basketball, and volleyball. The wilderness section offers hiking through forested terrain and along dramatic cliffs. Reservations require a minimum two-night stay on weekends or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a 14-night maximum stay limit.

location.directions: Located at 84 Osage Road, New Manchester, WV 26056. The park is in Hancock County at the northern tip of West Virginia's Northern Panhandle, along the Ohio River.

payload.name: Tygart Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting. Reservations require a two-night minimum on weekends (Friday-Saturday) or one night Sunday through Thursday. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. Check-in is 1 p.m., checkout is noon.
payload.short_description: Located in the foothills of the Allegheny Mountains in scenic north central West Virginia, Tygart Lake provides guests with some of the most breathtaking views across the state. This park is a cozy, quiet destination for couples and families. It’s also a perfect destination for group conferences and retreats. Located four miles south of Grafton, Tygart Lake State Park is known for its 10-mile long, 1,750-acre lake, which offers watersports like boating, water skiing, scuba diving, swimming, kayaking, canoeing and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Tygart Lake State Park Campground sits at the end of the park road, about three miles from the east entrance, offering 36 campsites with views of the 1,750-acre lake. Ten sites feature 50-amp electric and water hookups while 26 are standard non-hookup sites. The campground provides showers, flush toilets, a dump station near the beach, and Wi-Fi coverage at most sites. The lake supports boating, swimming, fishing, kayaking, and scuba diving.
payload.long_description:
Tygart Lake State Park Campground occupies a prime location in the foothills of the Allegheny Mountains in north-central West Virginia, approximately three miles from the park's east entrance. The 36-site campground overlooks the 10-mile-long, 1,750-acre Tygart Lake, created by the Tygart Dam on the Tygart Valley River. Ten sites offer 50-amp electric and water hookups suitable for RVs, while the remaining 26 standard sites accommodate tent campers and smaller rigs.

The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting, and offers modern amenities including shower facilities, flush restrooms, and a dump station located near the beach area. Wi-Fi is available throughout most of the campground, though signal strength weakens at sites 28-40. Reservations can be made online, by phone, or at the campground office, with a two-night minimum required for weekend stays.

The park provides excellent water recreation opportunities including boating, water skiing, swimming, fishing, kayaking, canoeing, and scuba diving. Pets are welcome on leash throughout the campground. The maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights, with check-in at 1 p.m. and checkout at noon.

location.directions: From Grafton, head south on County Road 9 for approximately 3 miles to the park's east entrance. The campground is located at the end of the park road, about 3 miles from the entrance.

address.full: 1240 Paul E Malone Rd, Grafton, WV 26354

payload.name: Watoga State Park Beaver Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting. Reservations require a two-night minimum on weekends or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a 14-night maximum stay. Check-in is 1 p.m. and check-out is noon.
payload.short_description: Located in the mountains of Pocahontas County, just 14 miles south of Marlinton, Watoga State Park is West Virginia’s largest state park. With 10,100 acres of land, Watoga is filled with many recreational activities. There’s hiking, fishing, boating and vacation cabins, open year-round. Watoga Lake is known for excellent fishing opportunities and is part of the Division of Natural Resources' stocking program. A multipurpose building, museum and observation tower are a few of the unique attractions at Watoga State Park.
payload.medium_description: Beaver Creek Campground at Watoga State Park provides 38 campsites with 50-amp electric service in the heart of West Virginia's largest state park. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring, with access to a central bathhouse featuring coin-operated laundry and dishwashing stations. Free wifi is available at check-in, and firewood and ice are sold on-site.
payload.long_description:
Beaver Creek Campground sits within Watoga State Park, a sprawling 10,100-acre mountain wilderness in Pocahontas County. The 38-site campground caters to RVs and tent campers alike, with each site equipped with 50-amp electric service (including 50, 30, and household outlets), a picnic table, and fire ring.

Campers have access to a central bathhouse with flush toilets, coin-operated laundry facilities, and dishwashing stations. Free guest wifi is provided at check-in, and firewood and ice are available for purchase. The campground operates seasonally from spring through fall, weather permitting.

Watoga offers 40 miles of hiking trails, an 11-acre lake for fishing and boating, and abundant wildlife viewing opportunities. The park's remote Pocahontas County location provides dark skies and a true backcountry feel while maintaining modern campground conveniences.

location.directions: The campground is located at 4800 Watoga Park Rd., Marlinton, WV 24954 in Pocahontas County.

address.full: 2656 Steven Hole Run Rd, Buckeye, WV 24924

payload.name: Philpot Picnic Area
payload.status_description: This is a day-use picnic area only; overnight camping is not permitted. Open seasonally from May 1st through mid-October. No fees required.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic area in Shasta-Trinity National Forest with six picnic spots, vault toilets, and access to the Philpot Interpretive Trail. No overnight camping permitted.
payload.medium_description: Philpot Picnic Area is a day-use site located in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest near Hayfork, California. The facility offers six picnic spots with tables, vault toilets, and trailhead access to the Philpot Interpretive Trail. No potable water is available and the access road is unpaved. Overnight camping is not permitted.
payload.long_description:
Philpot Picnic Area is a small day-use recreation site in the South Fork Trinity River area of the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. Previously designated as a campground, the site now operates exclusively for day use with no overnight camping allowed.

The facility features six picnic spots with tables and vault toilets. No potable water is available, so visitors should bring their own. Access is via an unpaved forest road. The picnic area serves as a trailhead for the Philpot Interpretive Trail, offering a pleasant hiking opportunity through the surrounding forest.

There are no fees to use this site. The area is open seasonally from May 1st through mid-October, weather permitting.

location.directions: From Hayfork, travel south on CA State Route 3, turn west on Rattlesnake Road, then turn right on Forest Road 30N31. The picnic area is on the left.

payload.name: Big Branch Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Forest Road 10 is closed to vehicles in winter but the shelter remains accessible by foot. Two-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Primitive three-sided backcountry shelter on the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail in Vermont's Big Branch Wilderness, offering overnight accommodations for hikers.
payload.medium_description: Big Branch Shelter is a backcountry overnight shelter located on the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and coincident Long Trail within the Big Branch Wilderness of Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest. The primitive three-sided structure accommodates 6-10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations. A composting privy is available, and water can be obtained from nearby sources but must be treated or filtered.
payload.long_description:
Big Branch Shelter is a rustic overnight shelter situated along the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail as they pass through the Big Branch Wilderness in southern Vermont. Named after Big Branch Stream, the surrounding wilderness provides habitat for moose, black bears, white-tailed deer, wild turkeys, and beavers. The landscape is dominated by northern hardwoods including maple, beech, and birch, with red spruce, balsam fir, and hemlock at higher elevations.

The shelter is a traditional three-sided wooden structure typical of Long Trail accommodations, sleeping 6-10 hikers. Facilities are primitive: a composting privy is available, but there is no potable water on site. Hikers must treat or filter water from nearby streams. Small campfires are permitted in fire rings following Leave No Trace principles.

Access is via a one-mile hike south on the Appalachian Trail from the Long Trail parking area on Forest Road 10 in Mount Tabor. The access road is closed to vehicles in winter but the shelter remains accessible to hikers year-round. Stays are limited to two consecutive nights.

location.directions: From US-7 in Mount Tabor, turn onto Brooklyn Road just past the Mount Tabor Country Store. Follow Brooklyn Road uphill as it becomes Forest Road 10 upon entering Green Mountain National Forest. Park at the Long Trail parking lot. The trailhead is across the road, about 200 feet west of the parking entrance. Hike south on the Appalachian Trail for approximately one mile to reach the shelter.

links.title: USFS Green Mountain NF Camping & Cabins

payload.name: Upper Basin Camp
payload.status_description: Seasonal campground typically closed late fall through spring due to snow. Access roads in the North Fork Clearwater district have experienced significant slide damage. Forest Road 250 (Black Canyon) is currently impassable and may remain closed for an extended period. Contact the North Fork Ranger Station for current road and campground conditions.
payload.short_description: Remote primitive USFS campground in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of north-central Idaho, typically accessible seasonally when forest roads are clear of snow.
payload.medium_description: Upper Basin Camp is a primitive Forest Service campground located in Clearwater County within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. This remote site is situated in rugged backcountry terrain accessible via forest roads that are typically snow-covered from late fall through spring. The campground offers a rustic, undeveloped camping experience in Idaho's mountainous interior.
payload.long_description:
Upper Basin Camp is a primitive campground managed by the U.S. Forest Service within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. Located in the remote backcountry of north-central Idaho, this site provides a rustic camping experience far from developed amenities.

The Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests encompass approximately 4 million acres of diverse terrain including steep river canyons, high mountain meadows, and dense conifer forests. High-elevation campgrounds in this region typically operate seasonally, with access limited by snow and road conditions from late fall through spring. Forest roads in the North Fork Clearwater area, including Forest Road 250, have experienced significant slide damage that may affect access.

Campers should come prepared for primitive conditions with limited or no developed facilities. The area offers opportunities for dispersed recreation including fishing for westslope cutthroat trout and bull trout in nearby streams.

location.directions: From Moscow, Idaho, travel northeast on State Road 8 to Elk River. Turn north onto Forest Road 382 and then east onto Forest Road 1705. The campground is about 45 minutes from Moscow.

payload.name: Warland Flat
payload.status_description: This is a primitive dispersed camping area with no formal season or reservation system. Access may be limited by snow and road conditions in winter and spring months.
payload.short_description: Primitive dispersed camping area in northwestern Montana's Kootenai National Forest, near the historical site of Warland.
payload.medium_description: Warland Flat is an undeveloped dispersed camping area in the Kootenai National Forest in Lincoln County, Montana. Located near the historical community of Warland, this remote site offers primitive camping opportunities typical of national forest dispersed areas.
payload.long_description:
Warland Flat is a dispersed camping area in the Kootenai National Forest of northwestern Montana, situated near the historical community of Warland in Lincoln County. As an undeveloped camping area rather than a formal campground, it offers a primitive backcountry experience for self-sufficient campers.

The Kootenai National Forest covers over 2.2 million acres of rugged terrain in northwestern Montana, featuring remote valleys, high peaks, and pristine waterways. Dispersed camping throughout the forest typically follows standard Forest Service regulations including a 14-day maximum stay and pack-in/pack-out policies.

Campers should come prepared for primitive conditions and contact the Libby Ranger District for current access conditions and any restrictions that may be in effect.

location.directions: Warland Flat Camping Area is located within U.S. Forest Service land. Access is typically via forest roads; look for signage indicating Warland Flat. Forest roads in this region can be unpaved and may require careful navigation, especially after inclement weather. Use a detailed forest map and local directions to find the site.

payload.name: Raddue Forest Camp
payload.status_description: This is not an active campground. USFS records indicate Raddue Forest Camp is designated for future use only and is not currently a developed recreation site.
payload.short_description: Raddue Forest Camp is an undeveloped site in Malheur National Forest designated for potential future use. It is not currently an active campground.
payload.medium_description: Raddue Forest Camp is located in Grant County within Malheur National Forest but is not currently a developed recreation site. According to USFS records, this area is designated for future use only and does not offer camping facilities, restrooms, or potable water at this time.
payload.long_description:
Raddue Forest Camp is a site within Malheur National Forest in eastern Oregon's Grant County. However, according to official USFS records, this location is designated as a "future use not existing recreation site," meaning it is not currently developed or operational as a campground.

The site has no facilities including no restrooms and no potable water. There are no fees associated with the area since it is not an active recreation site. Visitors looking for camping in Malheur National Forest should consider established campgrounds such as Big Creek, Strawberry, Wickiup, or one of the other 30+ developed campgrounds in the forest.

location.directions: From John Day, OR, travel approximately 18 miles west on US Highway 26 to the junction of Forest Service Road 21. Travel south on Forest Service Road 21 for approximately 6 miles; Billy Fields Forest Camp will be on the right.

payload.name: Lily Bay State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round from 9 a.m. to sunset daily. Summer camping reservations for 2026 opened February 2. Online reservations continue through September 13 at 4 p.m., after which sites become first-come, first-served. Winter camping available December 15 through March 15.
payload.short_description: Lily Bay offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Located nine miles north of Greenville on the east shore of Moosehead Lake, Lily Bay State Park spans 925 acres with two campgrounds containing 90 well-spaced wooded and waterfront campsites. The park features a swim beach, playground, two trailerable boat ramps with boat slips, and a two-mile shoreline walking trail. Amenities include hot showers, vault toilets, water spigots, and a dump station.
payload.long_description:
Lily Bay State Park sits along the scenic east shore of Moosehead Lake, Maine's largest lake, approximately nine miles north of Greenville in the state's remote Highlands region. The 925-acre park offers 90 well-spaced campsites divided between two campgrounds, with options ranging from wooded interior sites to coveted waterfront locations directly on the lake. Each site includes a fireplace and picnic table, while water spigots are distributed throughout both camping areas.

The park provides year-round recreational opportunities centered on Moosehead Lake. Summer visitors enjoy swimming at the designated beach, boating from two trailerable ramps with boat slips, and fishing for landlocked salmon and lake trout. A two-mile shoreline trail offers easy hiking with lake views. Winter brings cross-country skiing on five miles of groomed trails, snowshoeing, and snowmobiling access. Winter camping is available from December 15 through March 15.

Facilities include hot showers, vault toilets, and an RV dump station, though no hookups are available. The park accommodates both tent campers and RVs, making it a versatile base for exploring the Moosehead Lake region. Small watercraft users should note that Moosehead Lake can experience rapid wind changes, so staying close to shorelines is recommended.

location.directions: From Greenville, travel north on Lily Bay Road for nine miles along Moosehead Lake's east shore to the park entrance.

address.full: 1 State Park Rd, Beaver Cove, ME 04441

links.title: Lily Bay State Park Trail Conditions

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Mount Blue State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping May 15 through October 15. Reservations available through campwithme.com starting February 5, 2026. Two-night minimum on weekends before July 1; one-night minimum after. Winter camping is suspended until further notice due to construction.
payload.short_description: Mount Blue offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Mount Blue State Park Campground offers 136 wooded sites a short walk from Webb Lake's sandy beach. Select sites have water and electric hookups. Amenities include showers, an RV dump station, boat launch, playground, and nature center. The park encompasses over 8,000 acres with hiking trails, including a climb to the summit of Mount Blue.
payload.long_description:
Mount Blue State Park Campground sits in the western Maine mountains near the village of Weld. The 136 wooded sites are positioned a short walk from Webb Lake's sandy beach and picnic area. This is one of six Maine state parks offering water and electric hookups, making it suitable for both tent campers and RVs. Amenities include hot showers, an RV dump station, playground, boat launch for trailered boats, and a nature center with exhibits.

The park spans over 8,000 acres and connects to Tumbledown Public Lands, offering extensive hiking opportunities including the climb to Mount Blue's summit. In winter, the park maintains Nordic ski trails, a snowshoe trail system, and an ice-skating rink, though winter camping is currently suspended due to construction.

Pets are allowed but must be kept on a leash less than 4 feet at all times and never left unattended. The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through mid-October. Reservations are recommended and can be made through campwithme.com.

location.directions: From Farmington, take Route 4 north to Route 142, then follow signs to Weld and Mount Blue State Park. The campground entrance is at 187 Webb Beach Road, Weld, ME.

links.title: Mount Blue State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Peaks-Kenny State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open from May 15 through October 1. Reservations for May 22 to September 10 open the first workday in February via campwithme.com. Minimum 2-night stay required for reservations. Maximum stay of 14 nights during July and August.
payload.short_description: Peaks-Kenny offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Peaks-Kenny State Park Campground sits on the shores of Sebec Lake, offering 56 wooded campsites set among stately trees and large glacial boulders. The park features a sandy beach, 10 miles of hiking trails, a boat launch, and swimming area. Six sites have water and electric hookups, while all sites include a picnic table and fire ring. Modern amenities include hot showers, flush toilets, drinking water, and a dump station.
payload.long_description:
Peaks-Kenny State Park Campground occupies a peaceful, wooded setting along the shores of Sebec Lake in Dover-Foxcroft, Maine. The 56 campsites are nestled among stately trees and large glacial boulders near the lake, providing a classic Maine camping experience. Six sites (22, 24, 25, 26, 55, and 56) offer water and electric hookups, while all sites include a picnic table and fire ring.

The park features a sandy beach with swimming area, a trailered boat launch, and over 10 miles of interconnected hiking trails. A centrally located bathhouse provides flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers, and drinking water is available from spigots throughout the campground. Additional amenities include a dishwashing station, dump station, trash collection, playground, and picnic areas.

The campground operates from May 15 through October 1. Reservations can be made online at campwithme.com starting the first workday in February for dates between May 22 and September 10, with a minimum 2-night stay required. Pets are welcome but must be kept on a leash no longer than 4 feet and cannot be left unattended.

location.directions: From Dover-Foxcroft, head north on State Park Road. The park entrance is approximately 6 miles north of town on the shores of Sebec Lake.

address.full: 401 State Park Rd, Dover Foxcroft, ME 04426

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Rangeley Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open May 1 through October 15. Park hours are 9 a.m. to sunset daily. Reservations available through CampWithME.com or by calling 800-332-1501 (in Maine) or 207-624-9950. As of June 2026, all bathrooms and water service are fully operational.
payload.short_description: Rangeley Lake offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Rangeley Lake State Park encompasses 869 acres in the heart of Maine's Western Mountains. The campground features 50 well-spaced sites near the lakeshore, where a sandy beach offers commanding views of Saddleback Mountain. Facilities include hot showers, flush toilets, a dump station, and some sites with water and electric hookups. A trailerable boat launch with finger docks provides lake access.
payload.long_description:
Rangeley Lake State Park encompasses 869 acres along the southern shore of Rangeley Lake in Maine's Western Mountains. The campground features 50 well-spaced sites positioned close to the lakeshore, ranging from small tent-only spots to large sites accommodating RVs up to 35+ feet. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Facilities include hot showers, flush toilets, and an RV dump station. Select sites offer water and electric hookups.

The park's sandy beach provides swimming and stunning views of Saddleback Mountain across the lake. A trailerable boat launch with finger docks serves both campers and day visitors. The area is renowned for fishing, particularly brook trout and landlocked salmon. Hiking trails wind through the property's mixed forest. Wildlife watching, photography, and winter sports round out the recreational opportunities.

Forty sites accept advance reservations through CampWithME.com, while ten sites remain first-come, first-served. The minimum reservation stay is two nights, with a maximum stay of 14 consecutive days.

location.directions: From Rangeley village, head south on Route 17/4. The park entrance is approximately 3 miles south of town on the left.

links.title: Maine State Parks - RVs and Campers

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Sebago Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. Reservations available through CampWithME.com until September 12, 2026. After September 14, sites become first-come, first-served through mid-October. Winter camping available by contacting the park directly.
payload.short_description: Sebago Lake offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Sebago Lake State Park Campground is Maine's most popular camping destination, featuring 250 sites spread across wooded areas near Sebago Lake's sandy beaches. The campground offers a mix of standard tent sites and RV sites with water and electric hookups. Facilities include modern bathhouses with flush toilets and hot showers, an RV dump station, playground, and boat launch. Note that pets are not permitted in the campground.
payload.long_description:
Sebago Lake State Park Campground sits on the northern shore of Maine's second largest lake, a premier destination for swimming, fishing, and boating. The 250-site campground spreads through mature forests, with many sites offering shade and privacy. Sites range from tent pads to large RV-compatible spots, with select sites featuring water and electric hookups.

Facilities are well-maintained and include multiple bathhouses with flush toilets and hot showers, an RV dump station, and potable water throughout. Each site comes equipped with a picnic table and fire ring, with firewood available for purchase in the park. The Songo Lock connects Sebago Lake to neighboring waterways, operating from May through mid-October.

The park offers excellent swimming at sandy beaches on both the Casco and Naples sides, plus a trailered boat launch and miles of hiking trails along the lake and Songo River. The nature center provides educational programming during summer months. Reservations are highly recommended and open in early February, as this is one of Maine's most sought-after campgrounds.

location.directions: From Portland, take Route 302 northwest through Windham and Raymond to Casco. The park entrance is on Route 302, approximately 35 miles from Portland. The campground is on the Casco side of the park at 3 Campground Lane, Naples, ME 04055.

links.title: Sebago Lake State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Warren Island State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open 9:00 a.m. to sunset daily from Memorial Day through September 15. Reservations are made through CampWithME.com. Visitors must provide their own boat as there is no public ferry service to the island.
payload.short_description: Warren Island offers reservable camping through Maine State Park Campground Reservations.
payload.medium_description: Warren Island State Park is a 70-acre island campground in Penobscot Bay near Islesboro, Maine. Accessible only by private boat, the park offers 12 campsites and 3 Adirondack shelters. Amenities include drinking water at the pier and island center, privy toilets, fire pits, grills, and picnic areas. Courtesy carts are available to transport gear. A limited number of moorings are available first-come, first-served for $20.
payload.long_description:
Warren Island State Park is a secluded 70-acre island campground located in Penobscot Bay near Islesboro, Maine. The park is accessible only by private boat, making it a unique destination for campers seeking a true island camping experience. A limited number of moorings are available on a first-come, first-served basis for $20.

The campground offers 12 tent campsites and 3 Adirondack shelters spread across the forested island. Each site includes a fire pit and grill, with firewood gathering permitted on-site. Drinking water is available at the pier and island center, and privy toilets are located throughout the park. Courtesy carts are provided to help transport gear from the dock to campsites.

This primitive island setting has no showers, dump stations, electricity, or landline phones, though cellphone service is generally reliable. The park is patrolled regularly by rangers during the operating season. Campers should be aware of browntail moth activity and check park alerts before visiting.

location.directions: Warren Island is located in Penobscot Bay near Islesboro and is accessible only by private boat. The island has a dock and limited moorings available on a first-come, first-served basis.

links.title: Warren Island State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands

payload.name: Taylor Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally and is closed during winter months. Spring opening depends on snowmelt and road conditions. All 6 sites are free and first-come, first-served with no reservations available.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 6 dispersed sites near Mono Lake at 7,354 ft elevation, offering rustic camping amid geologically interesting Glass Mountain terrain.
payload.medium_description: Taylor Canyon Campground is a primitive, first-come first-served camping area located off Highway 120 East near Lee Vining. The 6 dispersed sites sit at 7,354 feet elevation in the geologically distinctive Glass Mountain and Mono Lake environs. Amenities are minimal with only vault toilets and picnic tables. Campers must bring their own water and pack out trash.
payload.long_description:
Taylor Canyon Campground provides rustic, backcountry-style camping on Bureau of Land Management and Inyo National Forest land northeast of Mono Lake. The 6 dispersed sites are accessed via Adobe Ranch Road, an unpaved route off Highway 120 East. At 7,354 feet elevation, the area offers striking views of the Glass Mountain volcanic field and the Mono Basin.

This is primitive camping with minimal development. Each site has a picnic table, and the campground has vault toilets. There is no potable water, so campers must bring adequate supplies. No trash service is provided, and campers are expected to pack out all garbage. The terrain is open and exposed with little shade, so sun protection is advisable.

The campground operates seasonally, typically opening after snowmelt in late spring and closing with the first significant winter weather. All sites are free and available on a first-come, first-served basis with no advance reservations. The nearest services are in Lee Vining, approximately 15 miles away.

location.directions: From Lee Vining, head east on Highway 120 (Benton Crossing Road). Turn north onto Adobe Ranch Road (unpaved) and follow it to Taylor Canyon Road. The campground is located along Taylor Canyon Road in an undeveloped area.

links.title: Mono County Tourism - Taylor Canyon Campground

payload.name: Corral Park
payload.status_description: Corral Park was proposed for inclusion in the Roosevelt National Forest cabin rental program in 2022. As of May 2026, it does not appear available for public reservation on Recreation.gov. Contact the Canyon Lakes Ranger District at 970-295-6700 for current status.
payload.short_description: Historic rustic cabin in Roosevelt National Forest's Long Draw area, offering views of the Mummy Range. Sleeps four with wood stove and propane amenities.
payload.medium_description: Corral Park is a small historic log cabin in Roosevelt National Forest, situated in the scenic Long Draw area with views of the Mummy Range. The cabin sleeps four and features a wood stove for heating, propane generator, propane refrigerator, and propane lights. A vault toilet is available on site. This rustic backcountry cabin was restored by the Forest Service and Historicorps and was proposed for inclusion in the cabin rental program in 2022.
payload.long_description:
Corral Park is a historic log cabin located in the Long Draw area of Roosevelt National Forest in Larimer County, Colorado. The original cabin at this site was constructed in 1916 by range permittees, with the current structure built in 1951. Over the years, the Forest Service rehabilitated the cabin with help from Historicorps volunteers, USFS staff, and contractors as part of the Poudre Headwaters Project.

The cabin sleeps four guests and offers rustic accommodations including a wood stove for heating, propane generator for electricity, propane refrigerator, and propane lights. A vault toilet is located on site. The setting provides scenic views of the Mummy Range and access to the surrounding national forest lands, which are important habitat for greenback cutthroat trout conservation efforts.

Access is via Long Draw Road (Forest Service Road 156), which departs from Colorado Highway 14 approximately 5 miles east of Cameron Pass. The unpaved road runs about 10 miles to Long Draw Reservoir and provides access to numerous trailheads including Corral Creek and Peterson Lake.

location.directions: From Fort Collins, take US-287 north to Colorado Highway 14 west. Continue on Highway 14 toward Cameron Pass. Approximately 5 miles east of Cameron Pass, turn onto Long Draw Road (Forest Service Road 156). The cabin is located off Long Draw Road.

payload.name: Farles Prairie  Campground
payload.status_description: Day-use only; no overnight camping is permitted. The site operates dawn to dusk. The associated Farles Lake Hunt Camp is closed.
payload.short_description: Day-use only recreation area on the shores of Farles Lake in Ocala National Forest. No overnight camping is permitted. Farles Lake Hunt Camp is closed.
payload.medium_description: Farles Prairie Recreation Area is a day-use site set along the shores of Farles Lake in Ocala National Forest. The area provides access for boating, fishing, birding, and OHV riding on the Ocala Centennial Trail. There is no overnight camping; the site operates dawn to dusk only. The associated Farles Lake Hunt Camp is currently closed.
payload.long_description:
Farles Prairie Recreation Area sits along the shores of Farles Lake in the Ocala National Forest, framed by tall longleaf pines and surrounded by sand pine scrub habitat. The area serves as a launch point for boating, fishing, and wildlife viewing. A boat ramp provides access to the long north-south lake, and anglers can fish from boats or wade into the grassy shallows.

The site is particularly notable for birding, especially during winter months when sandhill cranes arrive in large numbers. A walk along the prairie rim and lakeshore yields high counts of songbird and wading bird species. The Florida Trail passes through the area, offering hiking opportunities, and an OHV corral serves riders on the Ocala Centennial Trail.

This is strictly a day-use area with no overnight camping permitted. The associated Farles Lake Hunt Camp is currently closed. Facilities include vault toilets, picnic tables, and a boat ramp, but no potable water is available on site.

location.directions: From SR 40, turn south onto SR 19 and drive approximately 6 miles. Turn right onto Forest Road 595 and follow the dirt road for about 2.5 miles to the recreation area.

links.title: National Forests in Florida Camping & Cabins

payload.name: Sunset Campground
payload.status_description: Administratively closed. The campground is not accepting visitors and is not available through the recreation.gov reservation system. Contact the Salt Lake Ranger District at (801) 733-2660 for current information.
payload.short_description: A small Forest Service campground in Farmington Canyon, Davis County, Utah, currently administratively closed.
payload.medium_description: Sunset Campground is a small USFS campground located in Farmington Canyon in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The campground is currently administratively closed. Before closure, it offered approximately 10 first-come, first-served campsites along Farmington Canyon Road, accessible via Skyline Drive from Farmington.
payload.long_description:
Sunset Campground sits in Farmington Canyon within the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest in Davis County, Utah. The campground is accessed by traveling north on 100 East in Farmington, which becomes Skyline Drive and winds up the gravelly canyon road.

The campground is currently administratively closed by the Forest Service. Before its closure, Sunset Campground offered approximately 10 first-come, first-served sites, with most sites being small and suitable for one or two tents. The campground previously provided vault toilets, picnic tables, fire rings, and water spigots.

Historically, the campground served as a boundary marker for winter camping restrictions in upper Farmington Canyon, with camping prohibited within 1/2 mile of the road above the campground from November 1 to April 1 to maintain access to Francis Peak for FAA personnel.

location.directions: From Salt Lake City, head north on I-15 and take the Farmington exit. Turn right (east) at the stop sign to 100 East Street, then turn left (north). 100 East becomes Skyline Drive and winds up Farmington Canyon. The campground is located approximately 5 miles up the canyon.

payload.name: Frank Jackson State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 6 AM to 7 PM daily. Reservations available up to one year in advance through reserve.alapark.com. Check-in 2 PM, check-out 11 AM.
payload.short_description: 32-site RV campground on 1,000-acre Lake Jackson in south Alabama with full hookups, modern bathhouse, fishing, swimming beach, and lakeside trails.
payload.medium_description: Frank Jackson State Park campground sits on the shores of 1,000-acre Lake Jackson near Opp in south Alabama. The 32 RV sites feature full hookups including water, electric, sewer, and cable TV. A modern handicap-accessible bathhouse serves campers, and the park offers excellent bass and crappie fishing, a swimming beach, over three miles of trails, and a boardwalk to a small island.
payload.long_description:
Frank Jackson State Park encompasses 2,050 acres around the scenic 1,000-acre Lake Jackson in Covington County, Alabama. The campground features 32 RV sites, all equipped with water, electric, sewer, and cable TV hookups. Three sites are designated ADA-accessible. A modern handicap-accessible bathhouse with showers serves the campground, and tent camping is permitted in RV sites at the regular rate. Eight primitive sites are also available near the bathhouse for those seeking a simpler experience.

Lake Jackson provides excellent fishing for largemouth bass, bream, crappie, and catfish, with an ADA-accessible fishing platform and boat launch ramps. The park features a grassy swimming beach, over three miles of walking trails, and a boardwalk leading to an island in the lake. A playground, picnic pavilions, and a gazebo with garden area round out the amenities.

Reservations can be made up to one year in advance through the Alabama State Parks online system at reserve.alapark.com. Check-in is at 2 PM and check-out at 11 AM. The park operates daily from 6 AM to 7 PM.

location.directions: Located at 100 Jerry Adams Drive, Opp, AL 36467 in Covington County. From US-331 in Opp, head east toward the park.

links.title: Frank Jackson State Park - Main Page
Frank Jackson State Park - Primitive Camping
Alabama State Parks - Dog Friendly Policies
Frank Jackson State Park - Entrance Fees

payload.name: Gulf State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Office hours are 7:00 AM to 5:30 PM daily. Check-in is at 2:00 PM, check-out at 11:00 AM. Reservations available online at reserve.alapark.com/gulf. Late arrivals receive an email with gate code for after-hours entry.
payload.short_description: Gulf State Park Campground offers over 600 full-hookup and primitive sites near Alabama's Gulf Coast beaches, featuring modern bathhouses, a pool, camp store, and 28 miles of trails.
payload.medium_description: Gulf State Park Campground in Gulf Shores, Alabama sits 1.5 miles from the white-sand beaches of the Gulf Coast. The campground offers 496 full-hookup improved sites with paved pads, 8 primitive tent sites, and a separate 104-site RV Resort with premium amenities. Facilities include 11 air-conditioned bathhouses, laundry, a swimming pool with splash pad, camp store, tennis and pickleball courts, and access to 28 miles of connector trails.
payload.long_description:
Gulf State Park Campground is located along the shore of Middle Lake in Gulf Shores, Alabama, just 1.5 miles from the white-sand beaches of the Gulf Coast. The main campground features 496 full-hookup improved campsites with paved pads ranging from 45 to 65 feet in length, accommodating both back-in and pull-through configurations. Eight primitive tent-only sites are also available for those seeking a simpler experience. Tents are welcome on all sites throughout the campground.

The park's newer RV Resort offers 104 premium full-hookup sites with concrete patios, up to 50-amp electric service, fire pits, and pedestal grills at each site. Resort guests enjoy exclusive amenities including a saltwater swimming pool with splash pad, clubhouse with kitchen facilities, pickleball courts, putting green, and playground. Modern bathhouses with private shower suites serve the resort area.

The main campground features 11 air-conditioned bathhouses with handicap-accessible showers distributed throughout, along with laundry facilities. A camp store adjacent to the Nature Center stocks food, beverages, camping supplies, firewood, and Gulf State Park souvenirs. Additional amenities include a swimming pool, tennis and pickleball courts, horseshoe and volleyball courts, and direct access to 28 miles of paved trails connecting the park's natural areas. Wildlife is abundant, including alligators and snakes, so visitors should remain alert.

location.directions: The campground is located at 20115 State Park Road, Gulf Shores, AL 36542.

payload.name: Roland Cooper State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 7 AM to sunset daily. Reservations available up to one year in advance through reserve.alapark.com. Check-in is 2 PM, check-out is 11 AM. A non-refundable $5.25 reservation fee applies per campsite.
payload.short_description: Quiet Alabama State Park on the Alabama River offering 41 improved RV sites with full hookups and 14 primitive tent sites, plus access to fishing piers, boat launch, and cabins.
payload.medium_description: Roland Cooper State Park sits along the peaceful Alabama River in Wilcox County. The campground features 41 improved sites with water, electric (30/50 amp), and sewer hookups, plus 14 primitive tent sites with fire rings and picnic tables. Campers have access to bathhouses with showers, a free boat launch with overnight stays, fish cleaning stations, and nearby restrooms throughout the park.
payload.long_description:
Roland Cooper State Park is a tranquil retreat on the Alabama River near Camden in Wilcox County. The park caters to both RV campers and tent enthusiasts, with 41 improved campsites featuring full hookups including water, 30-amp and 50-amp electric, and sewer connections. Each improved site includes a picnic table and fire pit, with dump stations, trash containers, and a bathhouse with showers conveniently nearby.

For those seeking a more rustic experience, 14 primitive camping sites offer picnic tables and fire rings with access to a nearby restroom, though these sites have no utility connections. The park's location on the Alabama River makes it popular with anglers, offering a free boat launch for overnight guests, fishing piers, and fish cleaning stations. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 PM to 6 AM.

The park also features furnished cabins ranging from studio primitives to two-bedroom options, including one ADA-compliant tiny cabin. Pets are welcome throughout the park with leash requirements and applicable fees. Reservations can be made online through reserve.alapark.com up to one year in advance.

location.directions: Located at 285 Deer Run Drive, Camden, AL 36726. The park is situated on the Alabama River in Wilcox County.

links.title: Roland Cooper State Park Official Page

payload.name: George H. Crosby Manitou State Park Backpack Campsites
payload.status_description: Open year-round including winter camping. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance through the Minnesota State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Remote backpack-only wilderness camping in a volcanic canyon with waterfalls and old-growth forest on Minnesota's North Shore.
payload.medium_description: George H. Crosby Manitou State Park offers 21 secluded backpack-in campsites ranging from 0.5 to 4.5 miles from the trailhead. This 3,320-acre wilderness park features rugged terrain, the Manitou River gorge with cascading waterfalls, and stands of old-growth yellow birch. Sites are primitive with vault toilets and fire rings; campers must pack out trash and carry in water.
payload.long_description:
George H. Crosby Manitou State Park is Minnesota's only designated backpack camping state park, offering a Boundary Waters-like wilderness experience on the North Shore. The 21 primitive campsites are scattered throughout the park, with several positioned along the Manitou River gorge and four near Benson Lake. Hikes to sites range from half a mile to 4.5 miles over steep, challenging terrain that rewards with spectacular views of volcanic rock formations and cascading waterfalls.

The park's 3,320 acres protect stands of old-growth yellow birch and provide habitat for moose, black bear, deer, and wolves. Trails offer peek-a-boo views of Lake Superior through the forest canopy. Each campsite has a vault toilet and fire pit with a moveable grate, but there is no running water at the sites. The only potable water source is a hand pump near the park entrance, so campers should fill up before hiking in. This is true pack-it-in, pack-it-out wilderness camping.

location.directions: Located at 7616 County Highway 7, Finland, Minnesota. The park is on Lake Superior's North Shore, northeast of Finland.

payload.name: Roaring River State Park Campground 3
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from February 25 through October 31. Reservations available up to 12 months in advance through Missouri State Parks reservation system or by calling 877-422-6766. Camping limited to 15 days within any 30-consecutive-day period.
payload.short_description: Seasonal campground in Missouri's Ozark hills offering basic, electric, and full-hookup sites near premier rainbow trout fishing at Roaring River State Park.
payload.medium_description: Campground 3 at Roaring River State Park provides a range of camping options from basic sites to full sewer/electric/water hookups, recently upgraded in 2025. The campground features accessible showers, restrooms, laundry facilities, and a dump station. Located in the scenic southwest Missouri Ozarks, it offers direct access to one of Missouri's premier trout fishing destinations.
payload.long_description:
Campground 3 at Roaring River State Park sits in the Ozark hills of southwest Missouri, offering easy access to the park's renowned rainbow trout fishing and spring-fed waters. The campground underwent significant improvements completed in February 2025, converting many sites to full sewer/electric/water hookups while retaining basic and electric-only options.

Facilities include modern accessible showerhouses, restrooms, laundry, and a dump station. Each campsite comes standard with a parking pad, picnic table, grill, and lantern post. The park's nature center is nearby, and seven hiking trails wind through the surrounding hills. A park store provides basic supplies and fishing gear.

Note that park staff use pyrotechnic devices between 8-10 a.m. daily near Campground 3 to deter black vultures. Pets are permitted with a maximum of two dogs per site on leashes no longer than 10 feet.

location.directions: Located approximately 7 miles south of Cassville on Highway 112 in Barry County. Park address is 12716 Farm Road 2239, Cassville, MO 65625.

payload.name: Snowberry Bowl Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Opens May 22, 2026. First-come, first-served with no advance reservations.
payload.short_description: Secluded forest campground in the 25 Mile Creek drainage near Lake Chelan with nine sites, vault toilets, and a group shelter accessible via barrier-free trails.
payload.medium_description: Snowberry Bowl Campground offers a quiet forested retreat tucked into the 25 Mile Creek drainage, away from the bustle of Chelan while remaining close to Lake Chelan's recreational opportunities. The campground features seven single tent sites and two double sites that can accommodate small RVs up to 25 feet. All sites have fire rings and picnic tables. A group shelter with four picnic tables is accessible via barrier-free trails and available to all campers on a first-come basis.
payload.long_description:
Snowberry Bowl Campground sits at 1,950 feet elevation in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, nestled in the forested 25 Mile Creek drainage. The campground provides a peaceful alternative to the busier lakeside areas while maintaining easy access to Lake Chelan and its recreational activities.

The campground offers nine sites total: seven single tent sites and two double sites suitable for small groups or RVs up to 25 feet in length. Every site includes a fire ring and picnic table. A covered group shelter containing four picnic tables can be reached via barrier-free trails from both double campsites and is available to all campers on a first-come, first-served basis.

This is a primitive campground with vault toilets but no potable water, hookups, or garbage service. Campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash. Fees are $15 per night for single sites and $30 for double sites, with an additional $5 charge for extra vehicles.

location.directions: From Chelan, travel south on Highway 97A for 3 miles. Turn right onto Southshore Road and go approximately 20 miles to Shady Pass Road #5900. Turn left up Shady Pass Road #5900 and go 3 miles to Slide Ridge Road #8410. Take a left onto Slide Ridge Road #8410 and travel 3/4 mile to Snowberry Bowl Campground.

address.full: 701 Slide Ridge Fs 8410th Rd, Chelan, WA 98816

payload.name: Grayson Highlands State Park Backpack Parking Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with reservations required. Check-in is 1 p.m. and check-out is noon. Sleeping in vehicles is prohibited. When the lot is full, alternate parking is available at the VA-600 Elk Garden or VA-603 Fox Creek parking areas in Mount Rogers NRA.
payload.short_description: Designated overnight parking lot for backpackers accessing the Appalachian Trail and Mount Rogers National Recreation Area from Grayson Highlands State Park.
payload.medium_description: The Backpack Parking Campground provides reserved overnight parking for hikers accessing the Appalachian Trail and Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. This is a parking space only; actual camping occurs outside park boundaries on adjacent federal land. Reservations are required year-round, and campers must hike approximately 1.5 to 2.5 miles to reach legal camping areas.
payload.long_description:
Grayson Highlands State Park's Backpack Parking Campground is a designated overnight parking facility for backpackers accessing the adjacent Mount Rogers National Recreation Area and Appalachian Trail. Located at Virginia's highest state park with elevations ranging from 3,698 to 5,089 feet, this lot separates overnight hikers from day-use visitors and eliminates dangerous roadside parking.

The reservation includes parking only. Camping is not permitted within the park or in your vehicle. Hikers must travel approximately 1.5 miles south or 2.5+ miles north on the Appalachian Trail to reach legal camping areas on federal land. Bear boxes are available near Thomas Knob Shelter, Rhododendron Gap, Wise Shelter, and Scales. Campfires are prohibited; bring a camp stove.

Weather at this elevation can change rapidly with snow possible May through September and winds regularly exceeding 50 mph. Cell service is unreliable, so download offline maps via the Avenza app or bring National Geographic Trails Illustrated Map #318. The park's famous wild ponies roam the area but should not be approached, fed, or petted.

location.directions: From I-81, take exit 45 (Marion/Chilhowie). Follow US-16 South for approximately 25 miles to Volney. Turn right onto US-58 West and continue about 8 miles to the park entrance at 829 Grayson Highland Lane, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363.

address.full: 4997 Grayson Highland Ln, Mouth of Wilson, VA 24363

payload.name: Clackamas Lake
payload.status_description: The campground opens for the 2026 season on May 22. Operating season typically runs through early September. Some sites are first-come, first-served while others are reservable through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Peaceful campground near a shallow 3-acre lake in Mt. Hood National Forest, offering 49 sites including 11 equestrian sites with corrals, access to the Pacific Crest Trail, and excellent trout fishing.
payload.medium_description: Clackamas Lake Campground sits at 3,400 feet elevation in a heavily wooded pine forest within the Clackamas Lake Historic District. The 49-site campground includes 11 equestrian sites with horse corrals and offers access to fishing, swimming, and non-motorized boating on the small 3-acre lake. The 2.2-mile Miller Trail connects directly to the Pacific Crest Trail, and the historic Clackamas Lake Ranger Station is less than a mile away.
payload.long_description:
Clackamas Lake Campground provides a quieter alternative when nearby Timothy Lake fills up. Nestled in a forest of pines with a lush green understory providing privacy between sites, the campground sits near the shores of the shallow 3-acre Clackamas Lake. Anglers can pursue cutthroat, brook, rainbow, and German brown trout, while the lake also supports swimming and non-motorized boating.

The campground features 49 sites spread across two loops, including 11 equestrian sites with 2, 3, or 4 horse corrals reserved exclusively for those camping with horses. The 2.2-mile Miller Trail begins within the campground and connects to the Pacific Crest Trail. The Clackamas Lake Ranger Station Historic District, featuring early 1900s Forest Service structures built in rustic architecture, is less than a mile away and draws thousands of visitors annually. Additional trails lead to Little Crater Lake and the Mt. Jefferson Wilderness.

location.directions: From Sandy, OR, travel east on Highway 26 for approximately 40 miles to Skyline Road (Forest Road 42). Turn right onto Skyline Road and travel south for 10 miles to the Clackamas Lake entrance sign. Turn left and drive 0.25 mile to the campground entrance.

payload.name: Lahontan State Recreation Area Silver Springs Group Use Area
payload.status_description: Open year-round for reservations through Reserve Nevada. Flush toilets and showers are closed during the off-season from October through May. A 14-day camping limit within any 30-day period applies.
payload.short_description: Group camping area at Lahontan Reservoir near Silver Springs, Nevada, offering developed facilities with restrooms, tables, and grills along 69 miles of shoreline.
payload.medium_description: Silver Springs Group Use Area is a reservable group camping facility within Lahontan State Recreation Area on the Carson River reservoir. The developed site features restrooms, picnic tables, and grills, with access to the reservoir's 69 miles of shoreline for fishing, boating, and water skiing.
payload.long_description:
The Silver Springs Group Use Area is a designated group camping facility at Lahontan State Recreation Area, located along the Lahontan Reservoir in western Nevada. This developed group site offers amenities including restrooms, picnic tables, and grills, making it suitable for organized group outings and gatherings.

Lahontan Reservoir spans 17 miles with 69 miles of shoreline, providing excellent opportunities for water-based recreation. The reservoir is popular for fishing walleye, white bass, hybrid wiper, catfish, and trout. Boating and water skiing are permitted, though boat ramp availability may vary with water levels.

The recreation area is located off U.S. Highway 50 near the town of Silver Springs, approximately 18 miles west of Fallon and 45 miles east of Carson City. A sanitary dump station is available near the park entrance. Reservations are required through Reserve Nevada, with a 14-day camping limit within any 30-day period enforced.

location.directions: From Carson City, travel east on U.S. Highway 50 for approximately 45 miles to Silver Springs. From Fallon, travel west on U.S. Highway 50 for approximately 18 miles. The park entrance is accessible from multiple points off Highway 50.

payload.name: Bass River State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round for camping. Reservations available at camping.nj.gov. Trailer sanitary station operates March 1 through November 30. Shelters and cabins operate April 1 through October 31.
payload.short_description: Bass River State Forest was the first forest acquired by the state of New Jersey in 1905 for public recreation, water conservation, and wildlife and timber management. Lake Absegami, a 67-acre lake created in the 1930's, is the center of the forest's recreational activities and provides an area for swimming and a serene setting for boating and canoeing. A trail through the Absegami Natural Area wanders through a pine/oak woods and a small Atlantic white cedar bog. With the Carry-In/Carry-Out Program you can help us keep your parks clean and beautiful by carrying out the trash you carry in. Bags are provided throughout the site. Thank you for your cooperation and remember to recycle.
payload.medium_description: Bass River State Forest offers 176 wooded campsites surrounding Lake Absegami in New Jersey's Pine Barrens. Sites include fire rings and picnic tables, with flush toilets and showers within walking distance. Additional accommodations include lean-tos, shelters, and cabins. Pets are allowed at sites 1-85 on the south shore for an additional fee.
payload.long_description:
Bass River State Forest, established in 1905 as New Jersey's first state forest, encompasses over 29,000 acres within the Pinelands National Reserve. The campground surrounds Lake Absegami, a 67-acre lake created by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s. The 176 standard campsites accommodate tents and trailers, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Flush toilets and shower facilities are within walking distance of all sites.

Beyond standard campsites, the forest offers diverse overnight options including six group campsites for parties up to 25 people, nine lean-tos on the south shore with hardwood floors and wood-burning stoves, six enclosed shelters, and six cabins with kitchens and bathrooms. The trailer sanitary station operates from March 1 through November 30. Standard campsites remain open year-round, while shelters and cabins operate April 1 through October 31.

The surrounding forest provides extensive recreational opportunities including hiking the Batona Trail, swimming at Lake Absegami beach, fishing, and canoeing. The Pine Barrens landscape features unique ecology with pitch pine and Atlantic white cedar forests, cranberry bogs, and diverse wildlife.

location.directions: From the Garden State Parkway, take Exit 50 and follow signs to Bass River State Forest. The park entrance is located on Stage Road (County Route 679).

links.title: Bass River State Forest Official Page

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Voorhees State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally April 1 through October 31. Reservations through camping.nj.gov. The campground is currently closed for the off-season.
payload.short_description: Located in the wooded hills of Northern Hunterdon County, two miles north of the town of High Bridge, Voorhees State Park is a popular hiking and camping destination. This 1,040-acre park can be reached from Interstate 78, taking Route 31 North to Route 513 North or from Route 206 to Route 513 South. Family campsites, shelters and group campsites are available from April 1 – October 31. Each campsite is equipped with a picnic table, fire ring and parking for two vehicles.
payload.medium_description: Voorhees State Park Campground offers 30 tent and trailer sites plus 3 shelters nestled in New Jersey's Highlands region. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring with grill. The campground has modern restrooms with showers and potable water. A highlight is the on-site Paul Robinson Observatory, open for public viewing on select evenings. Nine miles of hiking trails wind through hardwood forest.
payload.long_description:
Voorhees State Park Campground sits in Lebanon Township within New Jersey's Highlands, roughly an hour west of New York City.
