The campground provides 30 tent and trailer sites, 3 lean-to shelters with wood-burning stoves and bunk beds, and 2 group sites for larger parties. Each family site includes a picnic table, fire ring with attached grill, and parking for two vehicles.

Facilities include a centrally located modern restroom building with flush toilets and hot showers, potable water spigots, and a dishwashing station. An RV dump station is available at nearby Spruce Run Recreation Area. The park is known for the Paul Robinson Observatory, operated by amateur astronomers who host public viewing nights.

Nine miles of trails traverse the 1,400-acre park through mixed hardwood forest. The Highlands Trail passes through, connecting to a larger regional trail network. Black bears are present; campers must store food properly in vehicle trunks. No pets are allowed in the campground.

location.directions: From Route 78, take exit 17 for Route 31 North. Follow Route 31 to High Bridge, then turn right onto County Route 513 East. The park entrance is approximately 2 miles on the left.

links.title: NJ State Parks - Voorhees State Park

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Washington Crossing State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campgrounds are closed until further notice. No reservations are currently being accepted. Check camping.nj.gov for updates on when the campground may reopen.
payload.short_description: Washington Crossing State Park is located along the Delaware River, just eight miles north of Trenton. The Continental Army, commanded by General George Washington, landed here after its historic crossing of the Delaware River on Christmas night in 1776. The cultural, historic, natural and recreational features of this park provide a unique blend of activities for visitors.
payload.medium_description: Washington Crossing State Park offers primitive group camping at four designated sites in the Phillips Farm area. Each site includes fire rings, picnic tables, and composting toilets. These are true backcountry-style group sites with no water, electric, or dump facilities. The total capacity across all four sites is 115 people. Reservations are made through camping.nj.gov.
payload.long_description:
Washington Crossing State Park preserves the site where George Washington and the Continental Army crossed the Delaware River on December 25, 1776. The park spans over 3,500 acres along the Delaware River, approximately eight miles north of Trenton in Mercer County.

Camping is limited to four primitive group campsites located in the Phillips Farm area. These sites are designed for organized groups such as scouts, clubs, or other gatherings. Each site features fire rings, picnic tables, and composting toilets. There are no water or electric hookups, no dump station, and campers must pack out all trash. The combined capacity of all four sites is 115 people.

Beyond camping, the park offers extensive hiking and biking trails, the historic Johnson Ferry House, a nature center, and open-air theater. The terrain is mostly flat with deciduous forest and meadows along the river corridor.

location.directions: From Trenton, take Route 29 north approximately 8 miles. The park entrance is on Washington Crossing-Pennington Road (Route 546) in Titusville.

links.title: Washington Crossing State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Chewacla State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open year-round. Reservations are available online through reserve.alapark.com up to 12 months in advance for out-of-state residents and 13 months for Alabama residents. Two-night minimum on weekends; three-night minimum on Memorial Day, Fourth of July, and Labor Day weekends. Football game weekends are non-refundable and non-transferable.
payload.short_description: Chewacla State Park offers 31 full-hookup RV sites and 9 primitive tent sites near Auburn, Alabama, with bathhouses, a dump station, a 26-acre lake, and extensive hiking and mountain biking trails.
payload.medium_description: Chewacla State Park Campground sits on 696 scenic acres just minutes from Auburn-Opelika. The campground features 31 modern RV sites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer) accommodating rigs up to 60 feet, plus 9 primitive tent sites with fire rings. Two temperature-controlled bathhouses serve the campground, and amenities include a dump station, small camp store, and a 26-acre lake with swimming area.
payload.long_description:
Chewacla State Park Campground occupies a forested setting within the park's 696 acres, located a short drive from Auburn and Opelika. The campground is arranged in two separate loops featuring 31 modern RV sites with full hookups including water, electric (30A and 50A), sewer, and satellite TV connections. Sites have gravel pads and can accommodate motorhomes, travel trailers, and fifth wheels up to 60 feet in length. Both pull-through and back-in sites are available.

Nine primitive tent-only sites are situated between the full-hookup loops, each with a fire ring and access to the bathhouses. The primitive sites accommodate one vehicle, one tent, and up to four adults. Two temperature-controlled bathhouses provide showers, changing areas, sinks, and restrooms for all campers. A dump station is available on-site, and a small camp store sells firewood ($10/bag), ice ($3/bag), snacks, drinks, and souvenirs.

Beyond the campground, the park offers a 26-acre lake with a swimming area, playground, picnic areas with shelters, and an extensive trail system for hiking and mountain biking. Six renovated CCC-era stone cabins and glamping safari tents provide alternative accommodations.

location.directions: From Interstate 85, take Exit 51 (Wire Road/US-29) and head south. Turn right onto Shell Toomer Parkway and continue approximately 4 miles to the park entrance on the left.

address.full: 124 Shell Toomer Pkwy, # FOOTBRIDGE, Auburn, AL 36830

payload.name: Cheaha State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to one year in advance via reserve.alapark.com with a $5.25 non-refundable fee per site. Check-in at noon, check-out at 11 AM. The group campground is winterized November 1 through March with no water or restroom access.
payload.short_description: Alabama's highest campground at 2,407 feet elevation in Cheaha State Park, offering 77 full-hookup sites and 54 primitive tent sites surrounded by Talladega National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Cheaha State Park Campground sits atop Alabama's highest point at 2,407 feet, offering improved campsites with full hookups (water, electric, sewer) and primitive tent camping near the summit. The park encompasses 2,799 acres surrounded by 392,567 acres of Talladega National Forest, with access to hiking and mountain biking trails. Facilities include bathhouses, a camp store, and a dog park.
payload.long_description:
Cheaha State Park Campground occupies the summit of Alabama's highest point at 2,407 feet elevation, providing sweeping views of the Talladega National Forest. The Upper and Lower Improved Campgrounds offer 77 sites with full hookups including 20/30/50 amp electric, water, and sewer connections, plus bathhouse access. Four sites are ADA accessible. The primitive camping areas include the 26-site Upper Primitive Campground near Tower Road (Alabama's highest point) and the 28-site CCC Primitive Campground near the lake, both with fire rings and shared water spigots.

Primitive campers should note that bathhouse and shower access is not included; shower passes are available at the Mountain Store for $5 per person. A group campground accommodates parties of 9-25 people per site but is winterized from November through March with no water or restroom access. Safari glamping tents are also available for those seeking a unique experience.

The 2,799-acre park is surrounded by 392,567 acres of Talladega National Forest, offering extensive hiking and mountain biking trails. Amenities include the Mountain Store for supplies and snacks, a dog park, interpretive center, museums, and playground. Quiet hours are enforced from 10 PM to 6 AM.

location.directions: Located at 19644 Hwy 281, Delta, AL 36258. The park is situated in Cleburne County, approximately 30 minutes from Anniston and Oxford.

payload.name: Pine Creek Camp
payload.status_description: This appears to be a primitive, undeveloped campground. No official seasonal closure information or reservation system was found. Campers should contact the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests office at +1 (208) 935-2513 for current conditions.
payload.short_description: A primitive campground in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho, offering a secluded forest camping experience.
payload.medium_description: Pine Creek Camp is a small, primitive campground located within the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in north-central Idaho. The camp provides basic backcountry camping opportunities in a forested setting typical of the Clearwater region, which features a mix of cedar forests and mountain terrain.
payload.long_description:
Pine Creek Camp is situated in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests in Clearwater County, Idaho. This primitive campground offers a quiet, undeveloped camping experience in the rugged forests of north-central Idaho.

The Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests encompass over 4 million acres of diverse landscapes, ranging from dry canyons to moist cedar forests. Pine Creek Camp provides access to backcountry recreation including hiking, fishing, and wildlife viewing opportunities common throughout this remote region.

As a primitive site, campers should come prepared to be self-sufficient. The area is best suited for those seeking a more rustic camping experience away from developed campgrounds.

location.directions: From Victor, ID, head west on Idaho State Highway 31 for 4 miles; the campground is on the left side of the highway.

payload.name: Bear Valley Work Center
payload.status_description: Bear Valley Work Center is not an active recreation site. USFS records indicate it is designated for future use only. No camping facilities are available.
payload.short_description: A USFS administrative work center not currently operating as a public campground. No camping facilities are available at this location.
payload.medium_description: Bear Valley Work Center is a Forest Service administrative facility in Malheur National Forest, not a developed campground. The site is designated for future use and does not currently offer recreation facilities or camping opportunities.
payload.long_description:
Bear Valley Work Center is a United States Forest Service administrative facility located in the Malheur National Forest near Seneca, Oregon. This site is not a functional campground and is noted in USFS records as being for future use rather than existing recreation. No camping infrastructure exists at this location.

The site is located in a remote area of Grant County, accessed via US 395 north from Seneca, then County Road 63 and Forest Road 6300-982. However, visitors seeking camping opportunities should look elsewhere in Malheur National Forest, where most campgrounds operate on a first-come, first-served basis during the summer season.

As this is an administrative work center rather than a public recreation site, campers should not plan to use this location. The Malheur National Forest offers numerous other established campgrounds throughout the forest for public camping use.

location.directions: From Seneca, OR take US 395 North for 7.5 miles, turn left on County Rd 63 for 8 miles, turn right onto FS RD 6300-982.

payload.name: Reservoir
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May through September. First-come, first-served; no reservations. No potable water available on site.
payload.short_description: Remote primitive campground at 7,900 feet near Yellowstone Reservoir with access to the High Uintas Wilderness via Swift Creek Trailhead.
payload.medium_description: Reservoir Campground sits at 7,900 feet in the Uinta Mountains near Yellowstone Reservoir and the Yellowstone River. This primitive, low-cost campground offers vault toilets but no potable water. The nearby Swift Creek Trailhead at the end of Forest Road #124 provides access to the High Uintas Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Reservoir Campground is a primitive camping area at 7,900 feet elevation in the Uinta Mountains of Ashley National Forest. Located near Yellowstone Reservoir and the Yellowstone River, it serves as a base for anglers, hikers, and OHV enthusiasts exploring this remote corner of northeastern Utah.

The campground provides vault restrooms but no potable water, so campers must pack in their own supply. At $5 per night, it offers an affordable option for those seeking solitude and wilderness access. The Swift Creek Trailhead at the end of Forest Road #124 provides direct entry to the High Uintas Wilderness.

Quiet hours are enforced from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Dogs are permitted but must remain leashed. Firewood cannot be transported into the area due to pest prevention regulations.

location.directions: From Duchesne, Utah on Highway 40, head north on Highway 87 for 15.5 miles to the Mountain Home turnoff. Continue north approximately 6 miles on county roads, then follow Yellowstone Road (Forest Road #119) north for 9 miles to the campground.

payload.name: Hewinta Guard Station
payload.status_description: This is an administrative USFS guard station not available for public rental or camping. For cabin accommodations in the Evanston-Mountain View Ranger District, contact the Evanston Recreation Center at 307-789-1770 for yurt reservations.
payload.short_description: Historic administrative Forest Service guard station in the High Uintas area at 9,505 ft elevation. Not available for public rental or overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Hewinta Guard Station is an administrative Forest Service facility located in the remote High Uintas backcountry of the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. At approximately 9,505 feet elevation near the Bear River-Smiths Fork drainage, the station serves as a base camp for USFS field crews conducting projects in the area. This is not a public rental cabin and is not available for overnight stays.
payload.long_description:
Hewinta Guard Station is an administrative facility of the USFS Evanston-Mountain View Ranger District, situated at approximately 9,505 feet elevation in Summit County, Utah, within the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. The station is located near the Bear River-Smiths Fork Trail corridor in the remote High Uintas backcountry.

Historically, the main telephone line from Whitney Guard Station to Hewinta Guard Station followed the Bear River-Smiths Fork Trail route. Today the facility is used periodically by Forest Service field crews as a base camp for projects in the surrounding wilderness area, including fish population management work in the West Fork Smiths Fork drainage.

This is an administrative guard station, not a public rental cabin. The property is not listed on Recreation.gov and is not available for overnight camping or cabin rental by the public. Visitors seeking cabin accommodations in the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest should consider the Mirror Lake Guard Station, Payson Lakes Guard Station, or the district's yurt rentals at Bear Claw, East Fork, Lily Lake, Ridge, or Boundary Creek.

location.directions: From Robertson, Wyoming, head south on State Highway 150 for approximately 20 miles. Turn left onto Forest Service Road 058 and continue for about 5 miles to reach the Hewinta Guard Station.

payload.name: Willow Oak Group Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is closed. It does not appear on current USFS recreation listings or Recreation.gov, suggesting it may be indefinitely closed or decommissioned.
payload.short_description: Closed group campground in the Enoree Ranger District of Sumter National Forest in Newberry County, South Carolina.
payload.medium_description: Willow Oak Group Campground is a group camping facility located in the Enoree Ranger District of the Sumter National Forest in Newberry County, South Carolina. The campground is currently closed and does not appear to be accepting reservations or visitors.
payload.long_description:
Willow Oak Group Campground is situated within the Sumter National Forest on the Enoree Ranger District in Newberry County, South Carolina. As a group campground, it was designed to accommodate larger parties seeking a rustic camping experience in the Piedmont region of South Carolina.

The campground is currently closed and does not appear on active Forest Service recreation listings or reservation systems. No fees were associated with this site when it was operational. Campers seeking group camping in this area should consider other options within the Francis Marion and Sumter National Forests.

location.directions: Willow Tree RV Resort & Campground is located at 520 Southern Sights Drive, Longs, SC 29568. For GPS, use the alternate address at 2000 Old Buck Creek Road, Longs SC 29568, which is near the park entrance. The entrance is a private paved road off Old Buck Creek Road, with a barrier gate that requires a code for re-entry after hours.

links.title: Francis Marion and Sumter NF Recreation

payload.name: Cheesequake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the 2026 season, operating April 1 through October 31. Reservations are available through camping.nj.gov. There is an 11-foot vehicle height restriction for entering the camping area.
payload.short_description: CHEESEQUAKE STATE PARK offers reservable camping through New Jersey Outdoors.
payload.medium_description: Cheesequake State Park Campground offers 50 tent and trailer sites in a distinctive setting where five different ecosystems meet, including pine barrens, salt marsh, and hardwood forest. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with flush toilets and showers within walking distance. The campground operates seasonally from April through October and accepts reservations through camping.nj.gov. An 11-foot vehicle height restriction applies to the camping area.
payload.long_description:
Cheesequake State Park Campground sits at a rare ecological crossroads in central New Jersey, where the coastal pine barrens, freshwater and saltwater marshes, and hardwood forest all converge. This 50-site campground accommodates both tents and trailers, with each site equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Flush toilet and shower facilities are located within walking distance of the campsites, and a trailer sanitary (dump) station is available for RV campers.

The park's location in Old Bridge Township provides easy access from the Garden State Parkway, making it one of the most accessible state park campgrounds for campers coming from the New York City metropolitan area. The campground operates seasonally from April 1 through October 31. Reservations can be made online at camping.nj.gov or by calling the park office. An 11-foot vehicle height restriction applies when entering the camping area.

Pet-friendly campsites are available with an additional $5 per pet per night fee, and proof of rabies vaccination is required. The Gordon Field Group Area offers four separate sites that can each accommodate up to 25 campers, with fire rings, upright grills, picnic tables, flush toilets, and potable water. Note that RVs and trailers are not permitted at the group campsites.

location.directions: From the Garden State Parkway, take Exit 120. Follow signs to Cheesequake State Park. The park entrance is located on Gordon Road in Old Bridge Township.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Belleplain State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. North Shore campground closes November 1 through March 31; Meisle and CCC campgrounds remain open during winter. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through NJ Outdoors. Minimum 2-night stay required except for same-day walk-ins. Maximum 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Belleplain State Forest consists of almost 23,000 acres of Pine, Oak, and Atlantic White Cedar Forest spanning over Cape May and Cumberland Counties in Southern New Jersey. The State Forest was established in 1928 for public recreation. During the Depression, The Civilian Conservation Corps, or C.C.C dug out the existing cranberry bog into a 26 acre recreational lake for the community. Lake Nummy is now the center of activities for the Forest, where one can canoe, swim, or hike along the lake. Picnic tables with charcoal grills are located lake side, along with horseshoe pits, canoe rental and a concession stand. All State Parks and Forests in New Jersey participate in the Carry in/Carry out Program, you can keep our Parks clean by carrying out the trash you carry in with you. The State Park Service does not provide bags. The Belleplain State Forest recreational facilities are partially accessible for persons with disabilities. Please contact the park office for further information regarding disability access needs. Text telephone (TT) users, call the New Jersey Relay Service at (800) 852-7899.
payload.medium_description: Belleplain State Forest Campground offers 169 tent and trailer sites spread across three camping areas: North Shore, Meisle, and CCC. The CCC campground is the only area with water and electric hookups. All sites include fire rings and picnic tables, with flush toilets, showers, and laundry facilities within walking distance. Fourteen heated lean-tos provide winter camping comfort from November through March. Lake Nummy offers swimming and boating, and miles of trails wind through the surrounding pine-oak forest.
payload.long_description:
Belleplain State Forest Campground sits within 21,000 acres of pine-oak forest in southern New Jersey's Cape May County, part of the Pinelands National Reserve. The campground offers 169 tent and trailer sites distributed across three distinct areas: North Shore (seasonal, closes November 1 through March 31), Meisle (open year-round with winter shower/restroom access), and CCC (the only area with water and electric hookups, sites numbered in the 100s). Each site accommodates up to six people, two vehicles, and three tents, with fire rings and picnic tables standard throughout.

Fourteen lean-tos with propane heaters provide a comfortable option for cold-weather camping. Flush toilets, hot showers, and laundry facilities serve all campsites. A trailer sanitary station operates year-round, though the hose is unavailable from November through March. Pet-friendly camping is available at Meisle Field and CCC campgrounds for dogs and cats with proof of rabies vaccination.

Lake Nummy anchors the recreation opportunities with lifeguard-supervised swimming from Memorial Day through Labor Day and boat rentals. The forest's extensive trail system supports hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian use. Hunting is permitted in designated areas during appropriate seasons.

location.directions: From Route 550, head south on Route 347 (Belleplain Road) to the forest entrance at 1 Henkinsifkin Road, Woodbine, NJ 08270. The park office is located near Lake Nummy.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Round Valley Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open April 1 through October 31. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance via camping.nj.gov. Same-day reservations available in-person if space exists. No vehicle access to campsites; access by hiking 3-6 miles or by boat only.
payload.short_description: Welcome to Round Valley Recreation Area, the only NJ State Park that offers wilderness camping, each campsite is in a secluded clearing in the woods along the south-eastern shoreline of Round Valley Reservoir at the base of the Cushetunk Mountain. Wilderness camping is a challenging experience that is recommended for experienced campers, backpackers and boaters, these campsites are not recommended for young children or for the elderly due to the difficulty and distance (3-6 miles hiking mountainous terrain or 1-4 miles paddling by boat). There is no vehicle access to the Round Valley campground.
payload.medium_description: Round Valley Recreation Area offers the only wilderness camping experience in New Jersey's state park system. The 60 primitive campsites are located on the southeastern shore of the 2,350-acre reservoir and are accessible only by hiking 3-6 miles along the rugged Cushetunk Trail or by boat. Sites are waterfront or near-waterfront, offering a remote backcountry experience within an hour of New York City.
payload.long_description:
Round Valley Recreation Area is New Jersey's premier wilderness camping destination, featuring 60 primitive campsites along the southeastern shore of a deep, 2,350-acre reservoir. Unlike typical campgrounds, there is no vehicle access to the camping area. Campers must either hike 3-6 miles on the steep and rugged Cushetunk Trail or arrive by boat, making this a true backcountry experience recommended for experienced backpackers and boaters.

The campground offers 52 family sites accommodating up to 6 people and 8 group sites for up to 25 people. Forty-two of the sites are waterfront and require boat access. Primitive pit toilets are available, and water spigots are located near sites 7 and 50, though campers in the middle section face up to a 3-mile round-trip walk for water. As wilderness sites, fire pits and picnic tables may not be included at every site. Pets are welcome at all sites for an additional fee.

The reservoir is known for excellent fishing, including trophy lake trout, and offers swimming at the lifeguarded beach from mid-June through Labor Day. The park provides a rare opportunity for remote camping within an hour's drive of major metropolitan areas.

location.directions: From I-78, take Exit 17 (Route 31 South) toward Clinton. Continue on Route 31 South for approximately 3 miles, then turn left onto Route 629 (Stanton Station Road). Continue to the park entrance at 1220 Stanton-Lebanon Road, Lebanon, NJ 08833.

links.title: NJ DEP Round Valley Recreation Area

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Spruce Run Recreation Area Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping April 1 through October 31, 2026. Reservations through camping.nj.gov. The swim area is closed for the 2026 season. Harmful algal blooms have been confirmed in the reservoir; boating is restricted when winds exceed 25 mph.
payload.short_description: Surrounded by the rolling hills of Hunterdon County, Spruce Run Recreation Area is popular with picnickers, anglers, boaters and campers. The reservoir was one of the first water supply facilities to be constructed and operated by the state and covers 1,290 acres with 15 miles of shoreline for recreation. Spruce Run is the third largest reservoir in the state after Round Valley and Wanaque reservoirs. April 1 through October 31 we offer campers 67 tent and trailer sites and three shelters with fire rings and picnic tables. Modern restrooms, showers and a trailer sanitary dump station are within walking distance. Hunting is permitted in designated areas within the park and is subject to Division of Fish and Wildlife regulations. Please contact park office for more details.
payload.medium_description: Spruce Run Recreation Area Campground sits along the 1,290-acre Spruce Run Reservoir in Clinton, New Jersey. The campground offers 67 tent and trailer sites plus three shelters, with seven sites featuring water and electric hookups. Modern restrooms with showers, a dump station, fire rings, and picnic tables are provided. Reservations are made through camping.nj.gov.
payload.long_description:
Spruce Run Recreation Area Campground is located on the shores of Spruce Run Reservoir, one of New Jersey's largest bodies of water at 1,290 acres. The campground operates seasonally from April 1 through October 31 and offers 67 tent and trailer sites along with three shelters equipped with bunk beds. Seven trailer-only sites (1-4 and 55-57) provide water and electric hookups with 30/50 amp service.

Facilities include modern restrooms with showers on both sides of the campground, a sanitary dump station, and potable water. Each campsite comes equipped with a picnic table, fire ring with attached grill, and parking for two vehicles. The maximum occupancy is six persons per campsite. Pets are not permitted in the campground area.

The surrounding recreation area offers boating (electric motors and sailboats only), fishing for bass and trout, swimming (when the beach is open), and picnicking. The reservoir is subject to harmful algal bloom advisories and boating restrictions during high winds.

location.directions: From I-78, take Exit 17 to NJ Route 31 North. Continue approximately 3 miles to Van Syckles Road. Turn left and follow signs to the park entrance.

links.title: Spruce Run Recreation Area - NJ State Parks

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Buck's Pocket State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open and accepting reservations. Check-in begins at 2:00 PM at the park office; check-out is 11:00 AM. Maximum occupancy is 8 persons and 2 vehicles per site. Cancellations require 72 hours notice for refund eligibility.
payload.short_description: Scenic campground atop Sand Mountain in northeast Alabama with 23 RV sites featuring hookups and Wi-Fi, plus 11 primitive tent sites in a wooded interior setting.
payload.medium_description: Buck's Pocket State Park Campground sits atop Sand Mountain in the Appalachian foothills of northeast Alabama. The renovated campground offers 23 developed RV sites with concrete pads, including 13 full-hookup sites and 4 pull-through options, plus 11 primitive tent sites tucked into the quiet campground interior. High-speed Wi-Fi covers the main camping area, and modern bathhouses with an ADA-compliant facility serve all guests.
payload.long_description:
Buck's Pocket State Park Campground occupies a dramatic setting atop Sand Mountain, where the Appalachian foothills meet the Cumberland Plateau across DeKalb, Jackson, and Marshall counties in northeast Alabama. The park takes its name from the deep canyon carved by South Sauty Creek, creating a natural pocket in the mountain that has drawn visitors since the park's establishment. The renovated campground provides modern amenities while preserving access to the rugged terrain that defines this corner of the state.

The campground features 23 developed RV sites, each with a 16-by-60-foot concrete pad, picnic table, fire pit, and charcoal grill. Thirteen sites offer full hookups including water, power, and sewer, with four of these configured as pull-through sites for easier maneuvering. The remaining ten developed sites provide water and electric connections. For tent campers seeking a more rustic experience, 11 primitive sites are nestled in the wooded interior of the campground away from RV traffic.

Amenities include high-speed Wi-Fi throughout the main campground area, a dump station, and bathhouses with both standard and ADA-compliant facilities. One developed campsite is designated ADA-accessible. The campground also serves as a base for the park's OHV trail system, with registered guests able to access the trails for an additional fee. A pavilion is available for group gatherings. Buck's Pocket is operated as a facility of Lake Guntersville State Park, with reservations available online or by phone up to one year in advance.

location.directions: From Geraldine, turn onto AL-227 North toward Grove Oak and continue approximately 7.5 miles, then follow county road signs to the park entrance. Note that County Road 173 leading into the campground features a steep grade with switchbacks when accessed from DeKalb County.

links.title: Buck's Pocket State Park Official Page

payload.name: Alamo Lake Ramada Camping
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park gates open 24 hours for campers. Day use hours are 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Reservations available through azstateparks.com or by calling 1-877-697-2757.
payload.short_description: Electric campsites with shade ramadas at Alamo Lake State Park, a remote desert reservoir in western Arizona known for bass fishing and stargazing.
payload.medium_description: Alamo Lake State Park's ramada camping area offers 12 electric sites with shade structures at $40 per night. Located 37 miles north of Wenden in the Sonoran Desert, the park surrounds a 3,000-acre reservoir known for excellent largemouth bass fishing. Amenities include restrooms, showers in nearby campgrounds, dump stations, and a camp store. The park is open year-round.
payload.long_description:
Alamo Lake State Park's ramada camping area provides electric campsites with individual shade ramadas, ideal for beating the intense summer heat of western Arizona's Sonoran Desert. These sites offer a middle ground between primitive dry camping and full-hookup RV sites, with electric connections and covered shade structures at each site.

The park sits at the edge of Alamo Lake, a 3,000-acre reservoir created by damming the Bill Williams River. The lake is regionally famous for largemouth bass, channel catfish, and crappie. Beyond fishing, the remote location and minimal light pollution make this one of Arizona's better stargazing destinations. Wildlife including javelina, mule deer, and coyotes are common.

Restrooms are located throughout the campgrounds and are ADA accessible. Showers are available in Campgrounds A, C, and the main campground area. Two dump stations serve the park. A camp store at the visitor center sells basic supplies, though the nearest fuel and propane is in Salome. The park operates year-round with 24-hour access for campers.

location.directions: From Phoenix, take US-60 west to Wenden. Turn north on Alamo Road and continue 37 miles to the park entrance.

links.title: Alamo Lake State Park - RV and Tent Camping
Alamo Lake State Park - Facility Information
Alamo Lake State Park - Group Sites
Alamo Lake State Park - Main Page

payload.name: Spruce Peak Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Two-night consecutive stay limit. During mud season through Memorial Day, hikers should expect wet trail conditions on the approach from Route 11/30.
payload.short_description: A rare fully-enclosed log shelter on the Appalachian and Long Trails in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, featuring a woodstove and sleeping space for 16 hikers.
payload.medium_description: Spruce Peak Shelter is one of only two shelters on Vermont's Long Trail system equipped with a woodstove. This four-sided enclosed log cabin sits 0.4 miles south of Spruce Peak summit, accessible via a 2.9-mile hike from the Route 11/30 trailhead in Winhall. The shelter accommodates up to 16 people on wooden bunks and includes an interior table. A composting privy and spring water source (requiring treatment) are located nearby.
payload.long_description:
Spruce Peak Shelter stands as one of the few fully-enclosed cabin-style shelters on the Appalachian Trail and coincident Long Trail in Vermont. Unlike typical three-sided Adirondack lean-tos, this rustic log structure features a sliding door, four large sleeping bunks for up to 16 hikers, an interior table, and a woodstove for heating. It's one of only two Long Trail shelters with a woodstove, making it a popular winter camping destination.

The shelter is located 0.4 miles south of Spruce Peak summit at approximately 2,200 feet elevation, reached via a 2.9-mile hike from the Route 11/30 trailhead in Winhall. A composting privy is located near the shelter, and a spring approximately 100 feet south provides water that must be filtered or treated before drinking.

The site operates on a first-come, first-served basis with a two-night consecutive stay limit. No fees are required. Leave No Trace principles apply, meaning all trash must be packed out. The shelter sits on Green Mountain National Forest land within the Manchester Ranger District.

location.directions: From Route 11/30 in Winhall, locate the Appalachian Trail/Long Trail trailhead parking area. Hike south on the AT/LT for 2.9 miles to reach the shelter, which is 0.4 miles south of Spruce Peak summit.

payload.name: Kakul Narrows Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round. First-come, first-served with no reservations. This is a primitive emergency/overnight shelter with no fees, no potable water, and no restroom facilities. Visitors must be fully self-sufficient and access is by boat or floatplane only.
payload.short_description: A primitive three-sided Adirondack shelter on Baranof Island accessible only by boat, offering basic overnight accommodations with wood stove and bunks in the remote wilderness of Tongass National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Kakul Narrows Shelter is a rustic three-sided Adirondack-style shelter located on Baranof Island on the east side of Kakul Narrows, between Salisbury Sound and Fish Bay, approximately 25 miles north of Sitka. The shelter provides basic overnight accommodations including a wood stove, plywood bunks, and a small table. Access is by boat only, and the site receives light use.
payload.long_description:
Kakul Narrows Shelter is a remote three-sided Adirondack-style structure managed by the USFS Sitka Ranger District in Tongass National Forest. Situated on Baranof Island along the east side of Kakul Narrows between Salisbury Sound and Fish Bay, the shelter sits approximately 25 miles north of Sitka in Southeast Alaska's island wilderness.

The shelter provides minimal but functional overnight accommodations including a wood stove for heating, plywood bunks for sleeping, and a small table. This type of shelter is designed primarily for emergency use and overnight stays by boaters, kayakers, and hunters exploring the surrounding waters and coastline.

There are no developed facilities at this site. Visitors must bring all potable water, pack out all trash, and be fully self-sufficient. Access is exclusively by boat or floatplane, with no trail connections. The area offers opportunities for wildlife viewing, fishing, and exploring the protected waters of Kakul Narrows.

location.directions: Located on Baranof Island on the east side of Kakul Narrows between Salisbury Sound and Fish Bay, approximately 25 miles north of Sitka. Access is by boat or floatplane only. Coordinates: 57.371°N, -135.682°W.

payload.name: High Point State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open April 1 through October 31. Reservations available at camping.nj.gov with a $5 service fee. Two-night minimum stay required. Alcohol is prohibited in the campground.
payload.short_description: Cancellation Policy - If you are unable to make your scheduled dates, you can make a change to your reservation for a $5.00 fee. Changes must be made prior to your check in date and time.
payload.medium_description: High Point State Park Campground sits along Sawmill Lake on the Kittatinny Ridge at New Jersey's highest point. The 50 tent sites each have a fire ring and picnic table, with pit toilets nearby. The campground operates April through October and accepts reservations via camping.nj.gov. Alcohol and pets are prohibited at family campsites.
payload.long_description:
High Point State Park Campground occupies the eastern shore of Sawmill Lake within New Jersey's highest-elevation state park. The Kittatinny Ridge setting provides access to over 50 miles of trails, including a section of the Appalachian Trail, plus swimming at the park beach and fishing opportunities. The campground is a tent-focused facility with minimal infrastructure for RVs.

The 50 family campsites accommodate up to two tents each, and some can fit small trailers. Every site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Pit toilets are within walking distance of the camping area. There are no hookups, dump station, or showers in the campground. Drinking water is available at the group camping area and park facilities, though campers should plan to carry water to their sites. Trash must be packed out.

location.directions: From I-84 in New York, take Exit 1 onto Route 23 South. Follow Route 23 for approximately 7 miles into New Jersey to the park entrance on the right. The campground is located along Sawmill Lake Road within the park.

links.title: High Point State Park Official Page

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Cathedral Caverns State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Check-in is 2:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. with campers required to occupy sites by 8:00 p.m. Check-out is noon. Two-night minimum on weekends, three-night minimum on major holidays.
payload.short_description: Cathedral Caverns State Park offers 36 improved campsites with full hookups or basic electric/water near one of Alabama's most spectacular caves, featuring a massive 126-foot-wide entrance.
payload.medium_description: Cathedral Caverns State Park campground provides 36 developed sites ranging from full-service RV spots with 50/30 amp power, water, and sewer to basic sites with electric and water hookups. The campground features a bathhouse, dump station, and convenient access to guided cave tours showcasing dramatic formations including a frozen waterfall and one of the world's largest stalagmites.
payload.long_description:
Cathedral Caverns State Park campground sits in the rolling hills of Marshall County, Alabama, offering direct access to one of the state's most impressive underground attractions. The campground features 25 full-service sites with 50/30 amp power, water, and sewer connections accommodating RVs with large slide-outs, plus 11 basic sites with 30 amp power and water. All improved sites include a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. A centrally located bathhouse and complimentary dump station serve the campground.

Primitive camping options include five tent sites with basic amenities and two backcountry sites accessible via a 3/4-mile hike, each offering a lean-to shelter, picnic table, and fire ring. Overnight guests receive discounted rates on cave tours, which wind through a cavern system featuring a 126-foot-wide entrance, frozen waterfall formations, and one of the world's largest stalagmites. The park maintains a consistent 60-degree temperature inside the cave year-round.

The campground sits near Lake Guntersville and within easy reach of Monte Sano, DeSoto, and Buck's Pocket State Parks. Reservations can be made up to one year in advance through the Alabama State Parks system, with a two-night minimum on weekends and three-night minimum on major holidays.

location.directions: 637 Cave Road, Woodville, AL 35776. Located in Marshall County near Lake Guntersville.

payload.name: Mill Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May 1 through September 30. Reservations available through ReserveCalifornia from May through September; first-come, first-served the rest of the year when accessible. Reservations are recommended for Memorial Day through Labor Day weekends.
payload.short_description: Sleep beneath towering maples and young redwoods at this 145-site campground in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park, with access to Mill Creek and miles of coastal hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Mill Creek Campground offers 145 campsites nestled among towering maples and young redwoods in Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park. Each site features a picnic table, food storage locker, and fire ring. The campground provides flush toilets, hot coin-operated showers, potable water, and a dump station during its operating season. Located 7 miles south of Crescent City, it serves as an ideal basecamp for exploring the 8-mile coastline and the greater Redwood National and State Parks.
payload.long_description:
Mill Creek Campground is set within Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park, one of four parks comprising Redwood National and State Parks. The 145-site campground is tucked into a second-growth forest of maples and young redwoods along Mill Creek, providing a shaded, tranquil atmosphere. Each campsite includes a picnic table, bear-proof food storage locker, and fire ring. Site dimensions vary from 15x15 feet to 28x28 feet, with several tent-only sites requiring short walks from parking areas.

Seasonal amenities include flush toilets, hot coin-operated showers, potable water, and an RV dump station. A camp host is present during the operating season, and firewood is available for purchase. The campground features an amphitheater for ranger programs during summer months.

The park encompasses 31,000 acres of old-growth coast redwoods, second-growth forest, and 8 miles of wild coastline. Popular activities include hiking trails of varying difficulty, exploring tidepools at Wilson Beach, and wildlife viewing. Note that dogs are allowed in the campground but prohibited on park trails.

location.directions: From Crescent City, drive 7 miles south on Highway 101. Turn east on the campground road (signed) and continue 2 miles to the campground entrance.

links.title: CA State Parks - Del Norte Coast Redwoods

payload.name: Dr. Julian G. Bruce St. George Island State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open and accepting reservations via ReserveAmerica. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance. Gap Point primitive camping is also available by arrangement with the park office.
payload.short_description: Barrier island campground with 60 electric/water sites nestled in pine flatwoods, a quarter-mile from miles of undeveloped Gulf beaches on St. George Island.
payload.medium_description: Dr. Julian G. Bruce St. George Island State Park Campground offers 60 campsites with electric and water hookups in a pine flatwoods setting behind historic dunes. Located on a 1,962-acre barrier island, campers enjoy proximity to pristine beaches, excellent fishing, kayaking, and some of Florida's best stargazing. Each site includes a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern hook, with two bathhouses providing hot showers and flush toilets.
payload.long_description:
Dr. Julian G. Bruce St. George Island State Park sits on a barrier island fronting Apalachicola Bay, featuring miles of undeveloped white sand beaches along the Gulf of Mexico. The 60-site campground is tucked behind the dunes in a pine flatwoods forest, providing shade and wind protection while remaining just a quarter-mile walk from the beach. All sites include water and electric hookups, a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern post, accommodating RVs up to 43 feet.

Two modern bathhouses with hot showers and flush toilets serve the campground, along with a dump station and playground. Six ADA-accessible concrete pads connect directly to restroom facilities. Hammock camping is permitted at all sites. The park also offers Gap Point primitive camping accessible only by foot via the 2.5-mile Gap Point Trail or by paddle craft.

The island is renowned for fishing, birdwatching, and stargazing due to minimal light pollution. Beach facilities include six large shelters with grills and picnic tables. Three beach wheelchairs and two electric mobility devices are available. Access to St. George Island is via a 4-mile bridge from Eastpoint, approximately 75 miles southwest of Tallahassee.

location.directions: From Eastpoint, Florida, cross the 4-mile St. George Island Causeway Bridge. Turn left onto Gulf Beach Drive and continue approximately 4 miles to the park entrance. The campground is located behind the dunes within the park.

address.full: 1925 E Gulf Beach Dr, Eastpoint, FL 32328

links.title: Florida State Parks - St. George Island

payload.name: Lake Carlos State Park Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. Most Minnesota group camps operate mid-May through October. Reservations available 120 days in advance through reservemn.usedirect.com.
payload.short_description: Group campground at Lake Carlos State Park offering rustic tent camping with fire rings, picnic tables, and primitive toilets near scenic Lake Carlos in west-central Minnesota.
payload.medium_description: Lake Carlos State Park Group Campground provides rustic group camping facilities in the rolling hills and hardwood forests of west-central Minnesota. The group camps feature open-sided shelters, fire rings with grills, picnic tables, and access to primitive toilets. Located just five miles north of Alexandria, the campground offers easy access to Lake Carlos for swimming, boating, and fishing.
payload.long_description:
Lake Carlos State Park Group Campground sits within 1,238 acres of glacially carved terrain featuring rolling hills, hardwood forests, and three lakes. The park includes both Pioneer Group Camp in the northeast corner with an open-sided shelter plus electricity and water, and Lakeview Group Camp on the west side of Lake Carlos accommodating up to 50 people in a tent-only setting surrounded by woods.

Group camps provide basic amenities including picnic tables and fire rings with grills at each site, water access, and primitive vault toilets. Modern restroom and shower facilities are not available at the group camps. The park offers excellent recreational opportunities including a swimming beach, boat ramp suitable for large boats and pontoons, nine miles of horseback riding trails, and multiple hiking trails through maple-basswood forests.

Reservations are available 120 days in advance through the Minnesota DNR reservation system. Pets are permitted when leashed and attended at all times. Only approved firewood may be burned to prevent the spread of invasive species.

location.directions: From Alexandria, drive 5 miles north on County Road 38 to the park entrance.

links.title: Lake Carlos State Park - MN DNR

payload.name: Warnica Springs Group Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently decommissioned as of August 18, 2023. This site is no longer available for camping.
payload.short_description: Former group campground in Tonto National Forest that was permanently decommissioned in August 2023.
payload.medium_description: Warnica Springs Group Campground was a group camping area in the Tonto National Forest in Gila County, Arizona. The site was permanently decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service on August 18, 2023, and is no longer available for camping.
payload.long_description:
Warnica Springs Group Campground was located in the Tonto National Forest in Gila County, Arizona. The site served as a group camping facility before it was permanently decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service on August 18, 2023.

The campground is no longer operational and has been removed from active USFS recreation facility listings. Campers seeking group camping in the Tonto National Forest should consider alternative sites such as Timber Camp Recreation Area or other active group campgrounds managed by the forest.

location.directions: Wekiwa Springs State Park is located at 1800 Wekiwa Circle, Apopka, FL 32712. From downtown Orlando, take FL-434 or I-4 west to exit 94, then continue north on Wekiwa Springs Road until you reach the park entrance. Follow signs within the park to reach the main springs area and designated campground loops.

payload.name: Jenny Jump State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season. Standard campsites operate April 1 through October 31. Shelters are available year-round. Reservations are made through camping.nj.gov.
payload.short_description: Jenny Jump State Forest is located in Warren County along the magnificent rolling terrain of Jenny Jump Mountain. Panoramic vistas of the Highlands, Kittatinny Mountain Range and Valley to the west, and scenic views of the Great Meadows in the east, dramatically greet the visitors who climb the narrow path leading to the top of Jenny Jump Mountain. Rocky outcroppings and boulders line the trail as evidence of the great glaciers that once covered the area now known as Jenny Jump State Forest.
payload.medium_description: Jenny Jump State Forest Campground sits in the Highlands of northwestern New Jersey, offering 22 standard tent and trailer sites open April through October. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with showers and flush toilets within walking distance. Eight year-round shelters near the mountain summit and two group sites expand overnight options for larger parties.
payload.long_description:
Jenny Jump State Forest Campground occupies a wooded setting in Warren County's Highlands region. The 22 standard campsites accommodate tents and trailers, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. Showers and flush toilets are located within walking distance of the camping loop. The season runs from April 1 through October 31, with reservations available through camping.nj.gov.

Beyond the standard sites, the forest offers two group campsites (accommodating 25 and 40 campers respectively) that include fire rings, picnic tables, and pit toilets. Eight rustic shelters near the Jenny Jump Mountain summit are available year-round; each sleeps six people with double-deck bunks, a woodburning stove, furnished living area, outdoor grill, and access to showers and flush toilets. Pets are not permitted at shelter sites.

Fourteen miles of hiking trails wind through the forest, and Ghost Lake provides fishing for largemouth bass, sunfish, and catfish. The park's location offers dark skies valued by astronomers visiting the United Astronomy Clubs of New Jersey observatory on the summit.

location.directions: From I-80, take Exit 12 for Hope/Blairstown. Head north on County Route 521 toward Hope. Turn left onto Great Meadows Road, then right onto Shiloh Road. Follow Shiloh Road to State Park Road and turn left to the park entrance.

links.title: Jenny Jump State Forest Official Page

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: East Fork Baker Creek Campground
payload.status_description: The campground typically opens in early June and closes in November, depending on snow conditions. As of late May, the campground may still be closed due to seasonal access restrictions. First-come, first-served only; no reservations or fees.
payload.short_description: Free primitive 7-site campground along the East Fork of Baker Creek in Sawtooth National Forest. Vault toilet and fire rings provided; bring your own water.
payload.medium_description: East Fork Baker Creek Campground is a primitive, no-fee campground with 7 sites nestled along the East Fork of Baker Creek in the Sawtooth National Forest. Open seasonally from June through November, it offers a quiet backcountry experience with basic amenities including a vault toilet and fire rings at each site. Fishing opportunities are available in Baker Creek.
payload.long_description:
East Fork Baker Creek Campground is a rustic, no-fee campground located along the East Fork of Baker Creek within the Sawtooth National Forest near Ketchum, Idaho. The campground features 7 primitive campsites, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table, offering a quiet backcountry camping experience in the central Idaho mountains.

This first-come, first-served campground operates seasonally from June through November, with access limited by snow during winter months. Amenities are minimal: a vault toilet is provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply. The campground does not accept reservations and has no fees.

The surrounding area offers excellent recreation opportunities including fishing in Baker Creek, hiking, backpacking, and mountain biking on nearby trails. The scenic drive along Forest Road 162 provides access to additional backcountry exploration in the Sawtooth National Forest.

location.directions: From Ketchum, head north 15 miles on ID-75, then west 3 miles on Forest Road #162.

links.title: USFS East Fork Baker Creek Campground

payload.name: TRAPPER CREEK CG
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fee required. Access may be limited during winter due to snow.
payload.short_description: Primitive single-site campground in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests along the South Fork Red River, offering free camping and winter snowmobile access.
payload.medium_description: Trapper Creek Camp Area is a no-fee, single-site primitive campground set in tall timber beside the South Fork Red River in Idaho's Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. The site features a vault toilet and serves as a winter snow park for accessing groomed snowmobile trails. Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Trapper Creek Camp Area offers a quiet, primitive camping experience in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of central Idaho. The single camp pad sits among tall timber along the South Fork Red River, providing a rustic setting for those seeking solitude. The site is free to use and operates on a first-come, first-served basis year-round, though winter snow can make access difficult.

Facilities are minimal, consisting only of a vault toilet and information board. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply, and all trash must be packed out. The area is popular for stream fishing in warmer months and doubles as a snow park in winter, serving as a staging area for snowmobilers accessing the groomed trail system.

location.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south onto Red River-Dixie Road #222. Follow Road #222 past the closed Red River Ranger Station and continue approximately 4 miles to the camp area on the right.

payload.name: West Branch State Park Shelters
payload.status_description: These are day-use picnic shelters only, not overnight camping facilities. Shelters are available for reservation year-round. No overnight camping is permitted at the shelter sites.
payload.short_description: Day-use picnic shelters at West Branch State Park in northeastern Ohio, available for reservations for parties and gatherings near the lake.
payload.medium_description: West Branch State Park Shelters are day-use picnic pavilions located within the 5,379-acre park in Portage County, Ohio. The park offers six picnic shelters, with four available for reservation. These approximately 30' x 20' structures feature eight picnic tables each with charcoal grills nearby, positioned within 100 yards of restroom facilities and offering scenic lake views with fishing access.
payload.long_description:
West Branch State Park Shelters are day-use picnic facilities, not overnight camping accommodations. The park features six picnic shelters scattered around Michael J. Kirwan Lake, with four available for advance reservation. Each main pavilion measures approximately 30' x 20' and accommodates eight picnic tables, with charcoal grills located nearby for cookouts and gatherings.

The shelters are positioned within 100 yards of restroom facilities and provide scenic lake views with direct fishing access. These day-use facilities are ideal for family reunions, birthday parties, company picnics, and other group gatherings. Reservations can be made up to one year in advance through Reserve Ohio or by calling the reservation center.

For those seeking overnight accommodations, the adjacent West Branch State Park Campground offers over 200 campsites with various amenities including electric and full hookup sites, showers, and a dump station. The shelters themselves are strictly day-use facilities with no overnight camping permitted.

location.directions: From Ravenna, Ohio, take State Route 5 east for approximately 5 miles. Turn left onto Esworthy Road and continue for about 1 mile to reach the park entrance.

payload.name: Parvin State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping. The sanitary dump station at Jaggers Point is closed until further notice. Swimming at Parvin Lake is closed for the 2026 season. Reservations through camping.nj.gov.
payload.short_description: Hidden in the southwestern part of the state is Parvin State Park, a park whose history is as varied as its wildlife. Situated on the edge of the Pine Barrens, the park not only has pine forests typical to the area but also a swamp hardwood forest. Spring bursts out in bright colors and rich fragrances with blossoming dogwood, laurel, holly, magnolia, wild azalea and over 200 kinds of flowering plants. Thundergust Lake, Parvin Lake and Muddy Run are popular for fishing and boating. Swimming is allowed in Parvin Lake only. This park served as home for the Civilian Conservation Corps from 1933 to 1941, a summer camp for the children of displaced Japanese Americans in 1943, a POW camp for German prisoners in 1944 and temporary housing for the Kalmycks who fled their homelands in Eastern Europe in 1952.
payload.medium_description: Parvin State Park Campground offers 56 tent and trailer sites along the scenic south shore of Parvin Lake in southern New Jersey. Each site features a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern hook. Flush toilets and showers are within walking distance. The park also has 18 furnished cabins on Thundergust Lake and 4 group campsites accommodating up to 100 people total.
payload.long_description:
Parvin State Park Campground sits along the south shore of Parvin Lake in Salem County, about five miles west of Vineland and 40 miles south of Philadelphia. The 56-site campground accommodates both tents and trailers, with each site equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern hook. Flush toilets and showers are conveniently located within walking distance, and a playground is nearby for families.

Beyond the main campground, the park offers 4 group campsites that can each hold up to 25 people, plus 18 furnished cabins on the north shore of Thundergust Lake. The cabins include a living room with wood-burning fireplace, two bedrooms, a full kitchen with electric stove and refrigerator, and a private bathroom with shower. Two ADA-accessible cabins accommodate up to 6 people.

The park encompasses over 2,000 acres of forests, wetlands, and streams, with trails for hiking and opportunities for fishing and boating on the lakes. Designated pet-friendly campsites (sites 35-56) allow up to two dogs or cats per permit with proof of current rabies vaccination.

location.directions: From Vineland, take NJ Route 540 west approximately 5 miles. The park entrance is at 701 Almond Road, Pittsgrove, NJ 08318.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Stokes State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Campsite reservations available via camping.nj.gov. Sunrise Mountain Road, Crigger Road, Grau Road, and Struble Road close seasonally from December 15 through April 15 or during hazardous weather conditions.
payload.short_description: Tent sites at Lake Ocquittunk T001-T024 and Shotwell sites T101-T112 are open year round. Lake Ocquittunk sites T025-T026 are open March 15 to December 15, and Shotwell sites T121-T137 are open April 15 to December 15. Steam Mill tent sites are open April 15 to November 15. Group sites at Haskins and Lake Ashroe are open from April 15 to October 31.
payload.medium_description: Stokes State Forest offers diverse camping across several areas: the main campground with 90 tent/trailer sites, Steam Mill (27 sites), Lake Ocquittunk (26 sites plus 10 cabins), and Shotwell (27 sites plus 9 lean-tos). Shotwell and sites 101-137 at the main campground are pet-friendly. Haskins provides group camping for 10-65 people. All sites include fire rings and picnic tables. Flush toilets and showers are available at some areas; others have pit toilets.
payload.long_description:
Stokes State Forest Campground sits within one of New Jersey's largest state forests, spanning over 16,000 acres of forested ridges in the Kittatinny Mountains. The campground system includes multiple distinct areas: the main family campground with 90 tent and trailer sites, Steam Mill Camping Area with 27 sites, Lake Ocquittunk with 26 sites and 10 cabins, and Shotwell with 27 sites plus 9 lean-tos. The 10 group sites at Haskins accommodate parties from 10 to 65 people.

Every site comes with a fire ring and picnic table. Flush toilets and hot showers are available at certain locations while others have pit toilets. The cabins near Lake Ocquittunk include cold and hot running water, refrigerators, electric stoves, and wood stoves. Lean-tos at Shotwell also have wood stoves. Shotwell and family campsites 101-137 welcome pets on leashes no longer than six feet.

The forest offers excellent trout fishing in Big Flat Brook, extensive hiking on 45+ miles of trails including a section of the Appalachian Trail, and panoramic views from Sunrise Mountain. Mountain biking, hunting in season, cross-country skiing, and snowmobiling round out the recreational opportunities.

location.directions: From Interstate 80, take Route 206 North. The park entrance is approximately 3 miles north of Branchville on Route 206. Turn onto Coursen Road to reach the park office at 1 Coursen Road, Branchville, NJ 07826.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Swartswood State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping April 1 through October 31. Shelters remain open through December 15. Check-in is 3 p.m., check-out is noon. Reservations available through camping.nj.gov.
payload.short_description: Come visit New Jersey’s first state park and historic landmark destination for outdoor recreation and leisure activities. Swartswood Lake is the park’s main attraction, welcoming visitors from all around to its calm waters for canoeing, kayaking, sailing, fishing, swimming or simply relaxing along the shores.
payload.medium_description: Swartswood State Park Campground sits within walking distance of Swartswood Lake in Sussex County, offering wooded and grassy tent sites, three group camping areas, and six cabin-like shelters with wood stoves. Each campsite includes a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern holder. The park provides flush toilets, showers, and drinking water, with a boat launch for lake access.
payload.long_description:
Swartswood State Park Campground occupies a scenic setting in the rolling hills of northwestern New Jersey, providing convenient access to Swartswood Lake and the park's trail network. The campground offers a mix of wooded and grassy tent sites, each equipped with a fire ring, picnic table, and lantern holder. Three group campsites across from the park office accommodate parties of 7 to 20 people in a secluded area near Duck Pond.

For those seeking more shelter, six cabin-like structures with wood stoves sleep up to four people each and remain open through mid-December, extending beyond the main camping season. Amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, and drinking water. The park prohibits pets in all overnight facilities and does not permit alcoholic beverages. No electrical hookups are available.

Swartswood Lake offers fishing, swimming, and boating opportunities, with a boat launch located within the park. The surrounding trails provide hiking through mixed hardwood forests and wetlands. Reservations are made through the New Jersey camping reservation system at camping.nj.gov.

location.directions: From Interstate 80, take Exit 25 and head north on Route 206. Continue approximately 10 miles through Newton, then turn left onto Route 519 North. Follow Route 519 for about 5 miles, then turn right onto Route 619 (Swartswood Road). The park entrance is on the left.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Wawayanda State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for group camping April 1 through October 31. Reservations available online at camping.nj.gov. Water must be carried from the main office; no showers on site.
payload.short_description: Wawayanda State Park was purchased with Green Acres funds beginning with the 1961 bond act. The park opened to the public in 1963. Wawayanda State Park is rich in history. The remains of the iron-smelting town of Double Pond lie along the northern shore of Wawayanda Lake. Operated during the 19th century, the charcoal blast furnace is the only remnant of a once-thriving village. Visitors are invited to observe the raceways and foundations that were once part of this industrial town. The focal point of Wawayanda State Park is the pristine 255-acre Wawayanda Lake and the numerous water related recreational activities. Almost one-third of the park has been preserved as designated natural areas.
payload.medium_description: Wawayanda State Park Campground provides group camping in Sussex County's Highlands region. Four primitive campsites accommodate groups of 7 to 35 people, each equipped with picnic tables and fire rings. A composting restroom serves the camping area, though water must be carried from the main office and no showers are available. The park encompasses over 34,000 acres including Wawayanda Lake, offering swimming, boating, fishing, and extensive hiking trails.
payload.long_description:
Situated in the rugged New Jersey Highlands near Vernon Township, Wawayanda State Park Campground offers group camping experiences in a forested wilderness setting. The park spans more than 34,000 acres of mixed hardwood forest, hemlock ravines, and swamps, with Wawayanda Lake serving as a centerpiece for recreation. Four group campsites provide tent camping for parties ranging from 7 to 35 people, making this an ideal destination for scout troops, family reunions, or outdoor clubs.

The camping facilities are intentionally rustic. Each site includes picnic tables and fire rings, with a composting restroom serving the campground area. Potable water is not piped to the sites and must be carried from the main park office. There are no showers, hookups, or dump stations. Firewood can be purchased at the park office. This primitive setup appeals to groups seeking a back-to-basics outdoor experience rather than developed amenities.

Beyond camping, the park offers over 60 miles of trails for hiking and mountain biking, including a section of the Appalachian Trail. Wawayanda Lake provides a swimming beach, boat launch, and fishing opportunities. The surrounding terrain features geological wonders including rhyolite outcrops and evidence of past iron mining operations.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Wharton State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: All campgrounds are open year-round. Reservations are made through camping.nj.gov. Cabins on Atsion Lake are seasonal, typically May through October.
payload.short_description: Nestled in the heart of the Pinelands National Reserve, Wharton State Forest offers a chance to experience the unique Pine Barrens ecosystem with a variety of natural and historic activities. Visitors may enjoy scenic hiking trails, canoeing or kayaking, exploring historic Batsto Village, swimming and picnicking at Atsion Recreation Area during the summer, fishing, bicycling, bird watching, camping, and more.
payload.medium_description: Wharton State Forest spans over 124,000 acres in the heart of New Jersey's Pine Barrens and is the largest single tract in the state park system. Camping options range from the developed Atsion Family Campground with flush toilets and showers to primitive wilderness sites accessible only on foot or by canoe. Multiple campgrounds serve different needs: Atsion for families and RVs up to 22 feet, Godfrey Bridge for a more rustic experience with pit toilets, and backcountry sites like Lower Forge and Mullica River for wilderness camping.
payload.long_description:
Wharton State Forest encompasses over 124,000 acres of New Jersey's Pine Barrens, making it the largest single tract within the state park system. The forest protects a landscape of pitch pine and oak forests, cedar swamps, and the slow-moving tea-colored rivers characteristic of the Pinelands. Historic sites like Batsto Village, a former bog iron and glassmaking community, offer a window into the region's industrial past.

Camping options span the spectrum from developed to primitive. Atsion Family Campground provides 50 tent and trailer sites with flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, fire rings, picnic tables, and a dump station. Trailers are limited to 22 feet. Godfrey Bridge offers 34 more rustic sites with pit toilets and potable water but no showers. For wilderness seekers, primitive campgrounds at Batona, Bodine Field, Goshen Pond, Hawkins Bridge, Buttonwood Hill, Lower Forge, and Mullica River provide fire rings and varying levels of amenities. Lower Forge and Mullica River are walk-in or paddle-in only with no motor vehicle access.

The forest offers outstanding paddling on the Mullica, Batsto, and Wading rivers, plus over 500 miles of unpaved roads popular with mountain bikers, equestrians, and off-highway vehicles. The Batona Trail passes through, connecting to trails spanning the Pinelands from Lebanon State Forest to Bass River State Forest.

location.directions: From the New Jersey Turnpike, take Exit 4 to Route 73 South. Follow Route 73 to Route 206 South. Continue on Route 206 through Hammonton to Atsion. The Atsion Recreation Area entrance is on the left. For Godfrey Bridge, continue south on Route 206 and turn right onto Quaker Bridge Road.

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Worthington State Forest Campground
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the off-season. Reservations are made through camping.nj.gov when the campground reopens for the camping season.
payload.short_description: Worthington State Forest was established in 1954 after the State of New Jersey purchased land from the Charles Campbell Worthington family. Located in Warren County in northwest New Jersey, Worthington State Forest is comprised of more than 6,400 acres and offers various recreational activities. While camping along the scenic Delaware River is one of the most popular attractions, there are also several hikes within the park worth noting. There are more than 26 miles of hiking trails including the hike to Sunfish Pond, one of New Jersey's 7 natural wonders. Millions of years in the making, the pond was carved out by glacial forces during the last ice age and is one of fourteen rock-basin lakes between the Delaware Water Gap and the end of the Kittatinny Ridge. Visitors may also hike to the top of Mt. Tammany to experience a 360 degree view of the Delaware Water Gap.
payload.medium_description: Worthington State Forest Campground sits along two miles of scenic Delaware River frontage within the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area. The 78-site campground splits between tent-only sites (1-23) and combined tent/trailer sites (29-82), with each site equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern holder. Flush toilets, bathhouses with showers, and potable water are available throughout. Three group sites accommodate up to 35 people each. A single backpacker site offers first-come, first-served overnight stays with bear boxes.
payload.long_description:
Worthington State Forest Campground occupies a prime stretch of Delaware River shoreline in northwestern New Jersey, providing direct access to the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area. The campground spans two miles of river frontage, offering excellent kayaking, canoeing, and fishing opportunities along one of the East's most scenic waterways. The Appalachian Trail passes through the forest, making this a popular basecamp for day hikes and thru-hikers.

The 78 established sites are divided into 23 tent-only sites and 52 combined tent/trailer sites suitable for motorhomes and travel trailers. Each site includes a picnic table, fire ring, and lantern holder. Campers have access to flush toilets throughout the campground, bathhouses with showers, and potable water. Bear-proof dumpsters and recycling bins handle waste management, and firewood is sold at the main office during business hours. The forest also maintains three group sites (capacity 35 each) with bear-proof food lockers and modern restrooms.

The campground enforces strict rules to preserve the wilderness character. Pets are prohibited in the camping area (service dogs excepted). Alcohol and swimming are not permitted. Black bears are active in the area, so all food must be stored in vehicles or provided bear-proof containers. Quiet hours run from 10 PM to 6 AM, with a 14-night maximum stay and two-night minimum reservation requirement.

location.directions: From I-80, take Exit 1 (last exit before the Delaware Water Gap toll bridge). Follow Old Mine Road north approximately 3 miles to the campground entrance on the left.

links.title: NJ State Parks - Worthington State Forest

management.agency_name: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection

payload.name: Bear Head Lake Camper Cabins
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available up to 120 days in advance through Reserve MN. Seasonal restrooms and showers operate May through September; vault toilets available year-round.
payload.short_description: Rustic heated camper cabins at Bear Head Lake State Park near Tower, MN, featuring bunk beds, screened porches, electricity, and fire pits along the north bay shoreline.
payload.medium_description: Bear Head Lake State Park offers five rustic 12x16-foot camper cabins along the north bay, each equipped with bunk beds, a table, screened porch, electric outlets, and heat. Every cabin has its own picnic table and fire ring. No indoor plumbing; seasonal flush toilets and hot showers are available May through September, with vault toilets accessible year-round. Pets are not permitted in camper cabins.
payload.long_description:
Bear Head Lake State Park's five camper cabins provide a comfortable year-round lodging option in Minnesota's Northwoods. Each 12x16-foot wooden cabin includes bunk beds with mattresses accommodating up to six people, a table with benches, screened porch, electric outlets, and heat for cooler months. The cabins are situated near docks in the north bay of Bear Head Lake, offering convenient access to fishing for walleye, northern pike, and bass.

The park features two designated trout lakes (Norberg and Cub), a sandy swimming beach, boat launch, fish cleaning shack, and over 17 miles of hiking trails including the scenic Blueberry Lake route. Winter visitors can enjoy 5.5 miles of groomed cross-country ski trails, snowshoeing, and ice fishing with free equipment rentals from the park office.

Camper cabins do not have indoor plumbing. Comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers operate from May through September. Vault toilets remain available year-round. Cooking inside cabins is limited to crockpots and coffeepots; outdoor cooking is done over the fire ring. Only approved firewood is permitted.

location.directions: From Tower, go east on MN Highway 169 for 9 miles to County Highway 128, then south 7 miles to the park entrance.
