address.full: 9311 Bear Head State Park Rd, Ely, MN 55731

links.title: Bear Head Lake State Park Things to Do

payload.name: Hocking Hills Youth Group Area
payload.status_description: Open and accepting reservations. All sites are reservation-only with no walk-ins permitted. Reserve online through ReserveOhio.com or by calling (866) 644-6727.
payload.short_description: Primitive tent-only youth group camping with 13 sites at Hocking Hills State Park, offering rustic camping near Ohio's iconic rock formations and waterfalls.
payload.medium_description: The Hocking Hills Youth Group Area provides primitive tent camping with 13 reservable sites for groups seeking a rustic experience within Hocking Hills State Park. Sites 1-10 accommodate up to 10 people at $20/night, while sites 11-13 handle groups up to 60 at $50/night. The area features pit latrines but no running water on-site. Campers have access to the main campground amenities including heated showers, flush toilets, camp store, and swimming pool.
payload.long_description:
The Hocking Hills Youth Group Area is a primitive tent camping facility within Hocking Hills State Park in southeastern Ohio. Originally designated exclusively for youth organizations, the campground now welcomes any tent campers seeking a more rustic experience while still having vehicle access to their site. The 13 sites are divided into small group sites (Y1-Y10) accommodating up to 10 people and large group sites (Y11-Y13) for groups up to 60.

The campground offers a back-to-basics experience with pit latrines provided on-site. Running water is not available at the youth group area; the nearest water access is at the Hike-In Campground. However, registered campers can utilize the main campground amenities including heated showers, flush toilets, laundry facility, dump station, camp store, and seasonal swimming pool.

Hocking Hills State Park is renowned for its dramatic rock formations, caves, waterfalls, and forested gorges. Popular hiking destinations like Old Man's Cave, Ash Cave, Cedar Falls, and Rock House are nearby. The park operates year-round, though specific campground seasons may vary.

location.directions: From the Hocking Hills State Park Camp Store/Check-In Office, turn right onto OH-664 N and drive 0.4 miles. Turn right onto OH-374 W and drive 3.1 miles. Turn left onto Fairview Road; the Organized Youth Group Campground will be on the right.

payload.name: Eagle Creek Campground - Custer Gallatin National Forest
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. Site 6 is currently closed due to beaver damage. Peak season reservations available through Recreation.gov. Food storage order in effect March 1 through December 1.
payload.short_description: Rustic 20-site campground near Yellowstone's north entrance with vault toilets, fire rings, horse corrals, and spectacular views of the Gallatin Mountains at 6,100 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Eagle Creek Campground sits at 6,100 feet elevation just 2 miles northeast of Gardiner, Montana, offering 20 sites with views overlooking Yellowstone National Park's peaks. The campground features vault toilets, fire rings, picnic tables, bear boxes at each site, and horse corrals for equestrian users. The Yellowstone River Trailhead is located within the campground. No potable water, hookups, or trash service available. Sites 19-20 are reserved for stock users until 4 pm daily.
payload.long_description:
Eagle Creek Campground is a scenic Forest Service campground located 2 miles northeast of Gardiner on Jardine Road, serving as an excellent basecamp for exploring Yellowstone National Park's north entrance, just a 10-minute drive away. At 6,100 feet elevation, the campground overlooks the majestic peaks of the Gallatin Mountains, with a small creek lined with aspens running along its western edge. Elk frequently roam through the area and bed down in the grass.

The campground offers 18 single sites and 2 double sites on gravel roads with unpaved parking spurs. Each site includes a fire ring, picnic table, and bear box. Horse corrals are available adjacent to the campground, and sites 19-20 are held for stock users until 4 pm daily. The Yellowstone River Trailhead provides direct access to hiking from within the campground.

Campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash. A food storage order is in effect from March 1 through December 1 due to bear activity. Dispersed camping is prohibited on Jardine Road downhill from the campground, 1.5 miles past the campground, and the first 3 miles of Eagle Creek Road.

location.directions: From Livingston, MT: Head south toward Gardiner on Highway 89 for 54 miles. Turn left onto Jardine Road. Go 0.9 miles, stay right at the split. Continue another 1.2 miles; campground will be on your left.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Due to beaver damage, site 6 is currently closed.

payload.name: Nemo Campsites Entry & Info Site
payload.status_description: Open for camping when not occupied by island host volunteers. The site is primarily used for volunteer housing and summer evening programs. First-come, first-served with no reservations.
payload.short_description: Remote entry and information site for Nemo Campsites on Wrangell Island, serving as host volunteer quarters with camping available when not occupied.
payload.medium_description: The Nemo Campsites Entry & Info Site serves as the gateway to the Nemo Campsites area in Tongass National Forest on Wrangell Island. Primarily occupied by Wrangell Island Host Volunteers during summer months, the site hosts evening campground programs and features information boards for visitors. Camping is available when not occupied by island hosts.
payload.long_description:
The Nemo Campsites Entry & Info Site is a unique facility in the Tongass National Forest that serves dual purposes. Located at the beginning of the Nemo-Skip Loop Road on Wrangell Island, this site functions as the primary information station for the broader Nemo Campsites recreation area. Information boards provide posted updates and guidance for visitors exploring the area.

During summer months, the site is typically occupied by Wrangell Island Host Volunteers who lead evening campground programs for visitors. When not in use by hosts, the site becomes available for overnight camping on a first-come, first-served basis. Usage is light, making this a quiet option for those seeking solitude in Southeast Alaska's temperate rainforest.

Facilities are minimal: an outhouse is available but there is no potable water on site. Campers should come fully prepared with their own water supply. The site provides easy access to the Nemo-Skip Loop Road and surrounding recreational opportunities on Wrangell Island.

location.directions: From Wrangell, drive 14 miles south on Zimovia Highway. Turn right onto Forest Road 6267 (Nemo-Skip Loop Road). The site is located at mile marker 0.5.

links.title: USFS Nemo Campsites Entry & Info Site

payload.name: Little Fan Creek Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for safety reasons. No reopening date has been announced.
payload.short_description: Primitive walk-in site on the Collawash River in Mount Hood National Forest, currently closed for safety reasons.
payload.medium_description: Little Fan Creek is a primitive walk-in area along the Collawash River in Mount Hood National Forest's Clackamas River Ranger District. Located at approximately 1,500 feet elevation and accessed via Forest Road 63, the site offers a quiet forest setting near the river. The area is currently closed for safety reasons with no announced reopening date.
payload.long_description:
Little Fan Creek sits along the Collawash River within Mount Hood National Forest, offering a primitive forest experience in the Clackamas River Ranger District. The site is accessed via Forest Road 63 at roughly 1,500 feet elevation, placing visitors in a quiet old-growth forest environment where the river provides a scenic backdrop.

The area historically functioned as a walk-in campground with a small number of sites, though it has been closed for safety reasons. No services are available at this location. Visitors must pack in and pack out all supplies and waste. There is no potable water, no restrooms, and no developed facilities.

The Collawash River corridor offers fishing opportunities and access to the surrounding forest. When operational, the area operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservation system.

location.directions: Access via Forest Road 63 from Highway 224 in the Clackamas River Ranger District.

links.title: Mt. Hood NF - Little Fan Creek Day Use

payload.name: Boiling Springs State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance through okstateparks.reserveamerica.com. Peak season runs May 22 through September 7, 2026.
payload.short_description: Boiling Springs State Park offers 63 camping sites including RV hookups, tent sites, and cabins in an 820-acre oasis near Woodward, Oklahoma, featuring a spring-fed lake, swimming pool, and hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Boiling Springs State Park is an 820-acre oasis in northwest Oklahoma near Woodward. The campground offers 10 modern RV sites with full hookups (electric, water, sewer), 30 semi-modern RV sites with electric and water, 12 tent sites, and 4 cabins. Amenities include a swimming pool, restrooms with showers, picnic areas with tables and grills, playgrounds, and fishing on the 7-acre spring-fed Lake Shaul. Five hiking trails wind through the park's unique landscape of natural springs and blackjack oak forest.
payload.long_description:
Boiling Springs State Park is an 820-acre natural oasis located 6 miles northeast of Woodward in the rolling gypsum hills of northwestern Oklahoma. The park's namesake comes from the natural artesian springs that bubble up through the sandy soil, creating a unique ecosystem of blackjack oak forest surrounded by otherwise arid High Plains landscape. The spring-fed 7-acre Lake Shaul provides fishing opportunities while the park's interpretive center showcases the natural spring phenomenon.

The campground features 63 total sites across multiple accommodation types. Ten modern RV sites offer full hookups with 20/30/50-amp electric, water, and sewer connections, with six of these being pull-through sites up to 50 feet. Thirty semi-modern RV sites provide 20/30-amp electric and water hookups in back-in configurations accommodating rigs up to 50-60 feet. Twelve primitive tent sites are available for those seeking a more rustic experience. Four cabins offer climate-controlled comfort with kitchenettes, fireplaces, and linens provided.

Park amenities include a swimming pool with concession stand, restrooms with showers, over 150 picnic tables and grills, three reservable pavilions, playgrounds, and five hiking trails of varying lengths. Two group camps can accommodate large gatherings with bunkhouse sleeping for up to 168 and 144 guests respectively, each with kitchen and dining hall facilities. An adjacent 18-hole golf course is privately operated.

location.directions: Located 6 miles northeast of Woodward, Oklahoma on State Highway 34C. The park address is 207745 Boiling Springs Road, Woodward, OK 73801.

payload.name: Foss State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 22 through October 31. Reservations accepted up to 11 months in advance through okstateparks.reserveamerica.com. Same-day reservations available for RV and tent sites; cabins, shelters, and palapas require at least one day advance notice.
payload.short_description: Western Oklahoma state park on Foss Lake offering 212 campsites from primitive tent sites to full-hookup RV spots, plus cabins, showers, and lake recreation.
payload.medium_description: Foss State Park sits on the shores of Foss Lake in western Oklahoma, offering over 200 campsites ranging from primitive tent spots to RV sites with water and 30/50-amp electric hookups. Ten sites feature full hookups including sewer. The park provides comfort stations with showers, a dump station, playgrounds, fire rings, and grills. Lake activities include swimming, fishing, boating, waterskiing, and kayak rentals. Two furnished cabins are available, one ADA-accessible.
payload.long_description:
Foss State Park occupies the western Oklahoma shoreline of Foss Lake, a 1,749-acre reservoir about 11 miles west of Clinton. The campground includes 212 sites spread across several areas: 93 tent sites, 54 semi-modern RV sites, 45 premium RV sites, and 10 modern RV sites with full hookups. Premium and semi-modern RV sites provide water and 30/50-amp electric service with sites accommodating rigs up to 50 feet. Both pull-through and back-in configurations are available.

Facilities include comfort stations with coin-operated showers, a dump station, picnic areas with grills and fire rings, playgrounds, and a gift shop. The park also offers two fully furnished tiny cabins at $110/night, one of which is ADA compliant, plus five palapas at Sunset Beach and group shelters with air conditioning.

Recreation centers on Foss Lake with swimming beaches, lighted boat ramps, a seasonal marina, and kayak rentals. On land, visitors can explore hiking and biking trails, a disc golf course, and equestrian trails (bring your own horse). The park sits on historic Cheyenne and Arapaho tribal lands in Custer County.

location.directions: From Clinton, Oklahoma, drive 11 miles west on Highway 44, then 2 miles north.

payload.name: Grand Cherokee State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All campsites must be reserved online through OklahomaParks.com. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Grand Lake O' The Cherokees in northeast Oklahoma featuring RV sites with full hookups, tent camping, swimming beach, boat ramp, and proximity to Pensacola Dam.
payload.medium_description: Grand Cherokee State Park is part of the Cherokee Area at Grand Lake State Park, situated on the shore of Grand Lake O' The Cherokees. The park offers four campground areas: Grand Cherokee Campground with full-hookup RV sites and showers, Lakeside Campground with a swimming beach, Riverside Campground below Pensacola Dam with river access, and Grand View Campground with tent sites. Amenities include comfort stations, playgrounds, a lighted boat ramp, and a 9-hole golf course.
payload.long_description:
Grand Cherokee State Park is part of the Cherokee Area at Grand Lake State Park, located on the shores of Grand Lake O' The Cherokees in northeastern Oklahoma. Grand Lake is one of Oklahoma's largest lakes with 46,500 surface acres and 1,300 miles of shoreline, making it a popular destination for fishing, boating, and water sports.

The Cherokee Area is divided into four campground areas near Pensacola Dam. Grand Cherokee Campground offers RV sites with full hookups including 50-amp electric service and a comfort station with showers. Lakeside Campground features 12 RV sites and 15 tent sites along with a swimming beach, playground, and group shelter. Riverside Campground sits below the dam with tent sites, a boat ramp providing river access, and pit toilets. Grand View Campground has four RV sites with electric-only service and 45 tent sites with a group shelter and comfort station.

The park provides excellent access to Grand Lake's renowned crappie, bass, and catfish fishing. Additional amenities include picnic sites, playgrounds, comfort stations, and a 9-hole golf course at Grand Cherokee. All campsites must be reserved online through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: From intersection of Hwys 82/28, go south approximately 1 mile to Hwy 28. Turn east, go approximately 1/2 mile, turn south on Hwy 82A. Take first left to stop sign. Turn east onto river road. Follow road until you cross over the river. Next right will be Grand Cherokee Golf Course where the park office is located.

links.title: Cherokee Area at Grand Lake State Park - TravelOK

payload.name: Lake Guntersville State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available online or by phone. Check-in is 2:00 PM to 9:00 PM; check-out is 11:00 AM. Two-night minimum on weekends, three-night minimum on major holiday weekends.
payload.short_description: Lake Guntersville State Park offers 282 campsites on Alabama's largest lake, featuring full hookup RV sites, water/electric tent sites, and primitive camping with seven bathhouses and modern amenities.
payload.medium_description: Lake Guntersville State Park Campground sits along the shores of Lake Guntersville, Alabama's largest lake at over 69,000 acres. The campground provides 282 improved sites ranging from full hookup RV sites with 50/30 amp service to primitive tent camping at Town Creek. Facilities include seven bathhouses (two with laundry), a splash pad, playground, basketball and tennis courts, and a campground store selling firewood, ice, and camping supplies.
payload.long_description:
Lake Guntersville State Park Campground is situated on the banks of Lake Guntersville, a 69,000-acre reservoir on the Tennessee River in northeast Alabama. The park encompasses over 6,000 acres of forested terrain and offers some of the best camping in the Tennessee Valley region. The campground features 282 improved campsites spread across multiple loops, accommodating everything from large RVs to tent campers.

Site options include full hookup sites with 50/30 amp and 30 amp electrical service plus water and sewer connections, as well as water and electric tent sites. Primitive tent camping is available at the Town Creek area for those seeking a more rustic experience without hookups. Seven bathhouses serve the campground, with two offering laundry facilities. Additional amenities include a playground, splash pad, basketball and tennis courts, and an outdoor classroom.

The campground store operates daily and stocks firewood, ice, snacks, beer and wine, fishing tackle with live bait, RV accessories, and camping supplies. The park offers excellent fishing opportunities on Lake Guntersville, known for its largemouth bass, as well as hiking trails including the accessible Bobo Trail. Eagle Awareness programs run on weekends from January through February when bald eagles winter on the lake.

location.directions: From Guntersville, take AL-227 north approximately 6 miles to the park entrance at 1155 Lodge Drive.

links.title: Lake Guntersville State Park Main Page

payload.name: Lakepoint State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Beach access is currently unavailable due to alligator presence in the area. Check-in and check-out are both at 12:00 PM; check-in is processed at the Marina Store. Two-night minimum on weekends, three-night minimum on holidays. Reservations available up to one year in advance via reserve.alapark.com or by calling 334-687-6710.
payload.short_description: Lakepoint State Park offers 192 improved campsites on the shores of Lake Eufaula in eastern Alabama, featuring full hookup and water/electric sites, bathhouses, a marina, swimming pool, and resort-style amenities.
payload.medium_description: Lakepoint State Park sits on 1,220 acres along Lake Eufaula, one of the best bass fishing lakes in the South. The campground offers 192 improved sites across three areas: Deer Court with pull-through full-hookup sites, and Barbour and Clark Loops with water and electric. All sites now feature 50-amp electric service. The park includes a full-service marina, swimming pool complex, restaurant and lounge, tennis courts, archery park, ORV course, and playgrounds.
payload.long_description:
Lakepoint State Park occupies 1,220 acres along the western shore of Lake Eufaula, a 45,000-acre reservoir on the Chattahoochee River known as the "Bass Capital of the World." The park combines resort-style amenities with traditional campground facilities, making it a destination for both anglers and families seeking a full-featured outdoor experience.

The campground features 192 improved sites divided among three loops. Deer Court offers pull-through sites with water, electric, and sewer hookups, while Barbour Loop and Clark Loop provide water and electric connections. All sites have been upgraded to 50-amp electric service. Each camping area has its own bathhouse, and a sanitary dump station serves the campground. Tent camping is welcome throughout.

Beyond camping, the park offers a 101-room lodge, lakeside cabins and cottages, a full-service marina with boat rentals and slip rentals, a swimming pool complex, two restaurants and a lounge, tennis courts, hiking trails, an archery park, an ORV course, and multiple picnic pavilions. The marina serves as the check-in point for campground arrivals.

location.directions: From Montgomery, take Highway 110 to Highway 82 East toward Eufaula. At Highway 431, turn left heading north for about 7 miles until Highway 285 appears on the right as the park entrance. From Atlanta, take I-85 South to I-185 toward Columbus, exit to US 80 West, turn left on US 280 toward Highway 431 South, then turn left on Highway 285. From the Florida Panhandle/Mobile area, take I-10 to Highway 231 North to Dothan, then Highway 431 North through Eufaula approximately 50 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Rickwood Caverns State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park office hours are 9 AM to 5 PM. Swimming pool opens mid-May; showers closed November through February. Reservations available through reserve.alapark.com.
payload.short_description: State park campground in north-central Alabama offering 13 improved RV sites with water and electric hookups, 5 primitive tent sites, access to a unique limestone cavern, and an Olympic-size swimming pool.
payload.medium_description: Rickwood Caverns State Park Campground sits atop 260-million-year-old limestone formations in Blount County. The small, well-maintained campground offers 13 improved sites with 30/50-amp electric and water hookups for RVs up to 40 feet, plus 5 primitive tent sites with fire pits and picnic tables. Campers enjoy free pool access, discounted cave tours, a bathhouse with showers, and 24-hour patrol.
payload.long_description:
Rickwood Caverns State Park Campground provides a unique camping experience above one of Alabama's most remarkable geological features. The park protects a 260-million-year-old limestone cavern system filled with formations, a blind cavefish pool, and fossils from an ancient sea floor. The campground sits in a wooded setting with 13 improved sites offering water and 30/50-amp electric hookups that can accommodate RVs up to 40 feet, plus 5 primitive tent sites equipped with fire pits and picnic tables.

Overnight guests receive free access to the Olympic-size swimming pool (open mid-May through Labor Day) and discounted cave tour rates. The bathhouse provides modern restrooms and showers, though shower facilities close November through February. A dump station is available on-site. The park also features gemstone mining, a gift shop, playground, and picnic pavilions. Guided cave tours descend 175 feet below the surface where temperatures remain a constant 58-62°F year-round.

Reservations are accepted up to one year in advance through the Alabama State Parks reservation system. A 2-night minimum stay is required on weekends, with a 3-night minimum on major holidays. Check-in is 2 PM and check-out is 11 AM. Pets are allowed in the campground but are not permitted inside the cave or park buildings.

location.directions: Located at 370 Rickwood Park Road, Warrior, AL 35180. From I-65, take Exit 284 onto AL-160 West toward Hayden. Follow signs approximately 5 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Crystal Springs Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The campground is no longer operational and no camping is available at this site.
payload.short_description: Crystal Springs Campground in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest is permanently closed and no longer available for camping.
payload.medium_description: Crystal Springs Campground was a Forest Service campground located in the Cle Elum Ranger District of the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest in Kittitas County, Washington. The site has been permanently closed by the U.S. Forest Service and is no longer operational for overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
Crystal Springs Campground was once a developed campground managed by the U.S. Forest Service within the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, located near Snoqualmie Pass in Kittitas County, Washington. The campground sat at approximately 3,000 feet elevation in the Cascade Range along the I-90 corridor.

The site has been permanently closed by the Forest Service and is no longer available for camping. No reservations or first-come, first-served camping is offered. Campers seeking alternatives in the area should consider other Cle Elum Ranger District campgrounds such as Cle Elum River Campground, Kachess Campground, or Salmon La Sac Campground.

The nearby Crystal Springs Sno-Park remains operational as a winter recreation area for cross-country skiing, snowshoeing, and snowmobiling, but does not offer camping facilities.

location.directions: From I-90, take Exit 62 and proceed south on USFS Road 54 for approximately 1 mile to reach the Crystal Springs area.

payload.name: Weitas Butte Lookout
payload.status_description: Currently not available for rental. The lookout is closed and no reservations are being accepted. When operational, reservations are handled through Recreation.gov.
payload.short_description: Historic 1953 fire lookout tower on the Lolo Motorway at 5,967 feet, offering sweeping views of the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness along the Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail.
payload.medium_description: Weitas Butte Lookout is a historic fire lookout tower originally built in 1931, with the current timbered structure dating to 1953. Perched at 5,967 feet along the famous Lolo Motorway, approximately 3 miles north of Rocky Ridge Lake, this remote cabin sleeps up to four guests and is equipped with a woodstove and propane heater. The location along the Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail provides stunning panoramic views of the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Weitas Butte Lookout is a historic fire lookout tower situated along the iconic Lolo Motorway in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests of north-central Idaho. Originally constructed in 1931 as part of the Forest Service's fire detection network, the current timbered structure visitors see today was rebuilt in 1953. The lookout stands at 5,967 feet elevation, approximately 3 miles north of Rocky Ridge Lake.

The cabin sleeps up to four guests and features a woodstove and propane heater for warmth during cool mountain nights. No potable water is available on site, so visitors must bring their own water supply. A vault toilet is provided nearby. The remote location offers exceptional solitude and sweeping vistas of the surrounding wilderness.

Positioned along the Nez Perce and Lewis and Clark National Historic Trail, the lookout provides a unique opportunity to experience the same landscapes that Lewis and Clark traversed over 200 years ago. Recreation opportunities in the area include day hiking, OHV riding on forest roads, lake fishing, horseback riding, and scenic driving along the historic Lolo Motorway.

location.directions: 38 miles east of Pierce, Idaho via Forest Service Road 500/557 along the Lolo Motorway.

payload.name: Alevin Campground
payload.status_description: No current status information available. This campground does not appear in official USFS or Recreation.gov listings. Contact the Cle Elum Ranger District at (509) 852-1100 for current conditions.
payload.short_description: A small primitive campground in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest in Kittitas County, Washington. Free, no fees required.
payload.medium_description: Alevin Campground is a small primitive camping area located in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest in Kittitas County, Washington. The site is free with no fees required. Limited official information is available about this campground.
payload.long_description:
Alevin Campground is a primitive camping area situated in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest in Kittitas County, Washington, in the eastern slopes of the Cascade Range. The campground is free to use with no fees required.

This appears to be a small, undeveloped site with minimal amenities typical of primitive forest camping areas. Very limited official documentation exists for this campground, and it does not appear in standard USFS campground listings or reservation systems.

location.directions: No specific directions are provided for Alevin Campground. The location details and access information are not available in the provided sources.

payload.name: Upper Payette Lake Campground
payload.status_description: Closed for the winter season. Opening date is snow-dependent. Reservations for reservable sites are available through Recreation.gov up to six months in advance. The lake is drawn down starting September 1st, making boat launching increasingly difficult after that date.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground on Upper Payette Lake in Payette National Forest, 16 miles north of McCall, Idaho, offering tent and RV camping with vault toilets, potable water, and access to fishing, kayaking, and hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Upper Payette Lake Campground sits at 5,586 feet elevation on the shores of Upper Payette Lake, a no-wake lake ideal for fishing, canoeing, and kayaking. The campground offers 20 single and double-family sites with picnic tables and fire rings, plus two group sites. Amenities include vault toilets and potable water from a hand pump. The paved Shoreline Trail begins in the campground, and additional hiking and biking trails are accessible across the road.
payload.long_description:
Upper Payette Lake Campground is located 16 miles north of McCall, Idaho, on the shores of Upper Payette Lake within the Payette National Forest. At 5,586 feet elevation, the campground is nestled in an Engelmann spruce and lodgepole pine forest at the foot of the Salmon River Mountains. The lake is a designated no-wake zone, making it excellent for fishing, canoeing, and kayaking.

The campground has 20 single and double-family sites, with 12 available first-come, first-served and 8 reservable up to six months in advance through Recreation.gov. Two group sites accommodate 20 and 30 guests respectively. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets and potable water from a hand pump are provided. Campers must pack out all trash.

A boat ramp provides lake access, though launching becomes difficult after the annual lake drawdown beginning September 1st. The paved, mile-long Shoreline Trail begins within the campground, and an accessible half-mile interpretive trail lies just to the north. Additional hiking and biking trails start across the road from the campground entrance.

location.directions: From McCall, Idaho, take Highway 55 north to Warren Wagon Road/Forest Highway 21. Turn right and continue for 16 miles to gravel Forest Road 495. Turn left (west) and follow for about one mile into the campground.

photos.name: Campsite at Upper Payette Lake Campground.
Campsite in Upper Payette Lake Campground.
A calm morning on Upper Payette Lake.
Upper Payette Lake from the Campground Site 7 with lake in the background.

payload.name: Arrowhead State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 22 through September 7. Reservations available through ReserveAmerica up to 11 months in advance. Campfires allowed unless a county-wide burn ban is in effect.
payload.short_description: Arrowhead State Park offers over 170 campsites on Lake Eufaula in southeastern Oklahoma, with full hookup RV sites, modern comfort stations, and access to hiking, equestrian trails, and a marina.
payload.medium_description: Arrowhead State Park sits on 2,200 scenic acres along Lake Eufaula, Oklahoma's largest man-made lake. The campground features 91 RV and tent sites with options ranging from primitive tent camping to full hookup RV sites with 30/50-amp electric, water, and sewer. Modern comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers are located throughout the park, along with a dump station. Each campsite includes a picnic table, charcoal grill, fire pit, and lantern holder.
payload.long_description:
Arrowhead State Park encompasses 2,200 acres in southeastern Oklahoma on the shores of Lake Eufaula, the largest man-made lake in the state. The park offers diverse camping options including 100 tent sites and 91 RV sites, with 20 sites providing full hookups (water, electric, and sewer) and six pull-through sites available. RV sites accommodate rigs up to 60 feet depending on the site. Modern comfort stations with air-conditioned restrooms, flush toilets, and hot showers are conveniently located throughout the campground.

Beyond camping, the park features extensive recreational opportunities including 25 miles of equestrian trails with a dedicated equestrian campground, hiking trails ranging from easy nature walks to challenging terrain, a swim beach, and boat ramp access to Lake Eufaula. The on-site Area 51 Marina provides boat rentals and a restaurant. An 18-hole golf course with driving range and putting green rounds out the amenities.

The park also offers group camping facilities with kitchen and bunkhouse accommodations for up to 144 people, making it suitable for large gatherings. A unique feature is the park's airstrip for fly-in visitors. Reservations are available through the Oklahoma State Parks ReserveAmerica system up to 11 months in advance.

location.directions: 18 miles north of McAlester on Highway 69, then 4 miles east on State Park Road.

links.title: Oklahoma State Parks ReserveAmerica - Campground Details
Oklahoma State Parks ReserveAmerica - Facility Details

payload.name: Cherokee Landing State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 22 through September 7, 2026. Off-peak season runs September 8, 2026 through May 27, 2027. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system. The south end of the park may be closed during high water events.
payload.short_description: Cherokee Landing State Park campground occupies a scenic peninsula on Lake Tenkiller in the Cookson Hills of northeast Oklahoma, offering 111 campsites with electric and water hookups, a swimming beach, boat ramp, and access to excellent bass and crappie fishing.
payload.medium_description: Cherokee Landing State Park sits on a 146-acre peninsula at the north end of Lake Tenkiller in Cherokee County, Oklahoma. The campground features 111 sites including RV sites with 15/20/30/50-amp electric and water hookups, tent premium sites, and group camping areas. Amenities include restrooms with hot showers, a dump station, swimming beach, lighted boat ramp, handicapped fishing dock, disc golf course, playground, and hiking along the Red Fox trail.
payload.long_description:
Cherokee Landing State Park is a 146-acre Oklahoma state park located on a peninsula jutting into Lake Tenkiller in the Cookson Hills, about 14 miles south of Tahlequah. The park offers exceptional access to one of Oklahoma's clearest lakes, known for excellent bass, crappie, and catfish fishing. The campground features a mix of RV and tent sites spread across the peninsula, with the Creek RV area providing concrete pads, water, electric hookups, fire rings, picnic tables, and BBQ grills.

The park accommodates RVs up to 40 feet and offers multiple amperage options including 50-amp service. Facilities include modern restrooms with hot showers, a dump station, swimming beach, lighted boat ramp, and a handicapped-accessible fishing dock. Recreation options extend beyond the water with a 9-hole disc golf course, outdoor volleyball court, playground, softball field, and the Red Fox hiking trail featuring spring wildflowers and birding opportunities including migratory cranes.

The south end of the park can be subject to flooding during high water events, so RV camping is restricted to the north end during such conditions. The park is situated within Cherokee Nation territory and provides a quieter alternative to the busier recreation areas further south on Lake Tenkiller.

location.directions: Located 14 miles south of Tahlequah on Highway 82. Address: 28610 Park 20, Park Hill, OK 74451.

payload.name: Greenwood Point Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No advance reservations. No potable water is available; campers must bring their own. Bear-proof food storage required.
payload.short_description: Remote, boat-in or hike-in primitive campground on Lake Moomaw in George Washington National Forest offering solitude and lakeside wooded campsites with no road access.
payload.medium_description: Greenwood Point Campground sits on an isolated peninsula of Lake Moomaw, accessible only by boat or a 1.5-mile hike from Bolar Mountain Campground. Five primitive wooded sites encircle an open grassy common area with lakeside views. No potable water is available; vault toilets are provided. The remote setting and lack of road access make this a quiet destination for paddlers and backpackers seeking solitude.
payload.long_description:
Greenwood Point Campground at Lake Moomaw offers the solitude of an isolated and remote location within the George Washington National Forest. With no road access, reaching the campground is part of the adventure. Visitors can strap on a pack and hike the Greenwood Point Trail from Bolar Mountain Campground, or paddle or canoe directly to the shores from Fortney Branch Boat Launch or Coles Point Day Use Area.

The campground features five primitive wooded campsites arranged around an open, grassy common area. Lakeside views and the absence of vehicle traffic make this a popular destination for those seeking privacy and quiet. Vault toilets are provided, but there is no potable water, so campers must pack in all drinking water.

This is bear country, and proper food storage is required. Pets are welcome but must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet. Quiet hours are observed from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

location.directions: Access by boat from Fortney Branch Boat Launch or Coles Point Day Use Area on Lake Moomaw. Alternatively, hike in via the Greenwood Point Trail from Bolar Mountain Campground (trailhead at campsite #63 in the cul-de-sac of campground 3). From Covington, take US 220 north to Hwy 39, turn left on Hwy 39, then left on Hwy 600 (Bolars Draft Road) to Bolar Mountain Recreation Area.

payload.name: Mallard Bay Overflow Recreation Site
payload.status_description: Operating season runs May through October. This overflow area opens only when all other Fish Lake campgrounds reach full capacity. No potable water available; campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Overflow campground at Fish Lake that opens only when other campgrounds in the basin reach capacity, offering flush toilets but no potable water at 9,000 feet elevation.
payload.medium_description: Mallard Bay Overflow is a primitive camping area on Fish Lake in central Utah's Fishlake National Forest. This site serves as overflow capacity when the six developed campgrounds in the Fish Lake Basin fill up. Located at 9,000 feet elevation, it provides access to Utah's largest natural mountain lake, known for trophy Mackinaw trout fishing. Flush toilets are available, but campers must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Mallard Bay Overflow Recreation Site sits along the shores of Fish Lake in the Fishlake National Forest of central Utah. At 9,000 feet elevation, the site offers expansive views of Fish Lake, Utah's largest natural mountain lake covering 2,500 acres. The campground operates as overflow capacity for the Fish Lake Basin, opening only when Doctor Creek, Bowery Creek, Mackinaw, Frying Pan, Paiute, and Tasha Equestrian campgrounds reach full occupancy.

Fish Lake is renowned for its trophy fishing, particularly Mackinaw lake trout that can reach 20-40 pounds. Rainbow trout and splake also draw anglers. Beyond fishing, the lake supports boating, canoeing, swimming, and scuba diving. The nearby five-mile Pelican Canyon Trail starts at Bowery Creek Campground and climbs through meadows and dense spruce, pine, and aspen forests to the 11,633-foot Fish Lake Hightop.

As a primitive overflow area, the site has flush toilets but no potable water. Campers must bring adequate drinking water and pack out all trash. The campground is managed by High Country Recreation under a Forest Service concession permit.

location.directions: From Richfield, Utah, head east on UT-118 N/E 300 N toward N 100 E for 0.8 miles. Continue straight onto UT-119 E for 8.8 miles. Turn right onto UT-24 E for 23.1 miles, then turn left onto UT-25 N for 7 miles. Turn right on Doctor Creek Campground road and travel 0.3 miles.

payload.name: Savanna Portage Group Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-May through October. Reservations required up to 120 days in advance via reservemn.usedirect.com or 866-857-2757.
payload.short_description: Secluded group campground on Savanna Lake within Minnesota's third largest state park, featuring primitive camping with fire rings, picnic tables, and a private beach.
payload.medium_description: Savanna Portage Group Campground (Site GC1) is a primitive group camping area nestled in a mixed pine and oak forest overlooking Savanna Lake. The secluded setting offers terraced camping areas for up to 30 people, with a boat landing, swimming beach, and dock. Electric trolling motors only are allowed on the lake, where anglers can pursue northern pike, bass, and panfish.
payload.long_description:
Located within Savanna Portage State Park, Minnesota's third largest state park at over 15,000 acres, the group campground sits on the shores of Savanna Lake in a secluded mixed pine and oak forest. The terraced camping areas accommodate groups of up to 30 people and are drive-in accessible for small trailers and campers.

The campground features primitive amenities including vault toilets, a hand pump for water, fire rings with grills, and picnic tables at each site. A boat landing provides direct lake access restricted to electric trolling motors, while the private beach and dock offer swimming and fishing opportunities for northern pike, bass, and panfish.

The park preserves the historic Savanna Portage, a grueling six-mile trail once used by Dakota, Ojibwe, and European traders to connect the Mississippi River watershed to Lake Superior. Today visitors can hike the Continental Divide Trail and explore the park's rolling hills, lakes, and bogs.

location.directions: Located 17 miles northeast of McGregor, Minnesota. From McGregor, take Highway 65 north, then follow County Road 14 east to the park entrance.

links.title: MN DNR Savanna Portage Virtual Tour

payload.name: Bernice State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All campsites require online reservations through TravelOK.com. Nature center open Wednesday through Sunday, 9 AM to 4 PM.
payload.short_description: Lakeside state park campground on Grand Lake featuring 33 RV sites with 50 amp electric and water hookups, primitive tent camping, swimming beach, nature center, and ADA-accessible trails. Known as the Crappie Capital of the World.
payload.medium_description: Bernice Area at Grand Lake State Park sits on 88 acres along the northwestern shore of Grand Lake in Delaware County. The campground offers 33 semi-improved RV sites with 50 amp electric and water hookups on concrete pads, plus primitive tent sites. Amenities include two comfort stations with hot showers, a centrally located dump station, swimming beach, nature center, two playgrounds, and a mile-long paved ADA-accessible walking path with wildlife viewing towers.
payload.long_description:
Bernice Area at Grand Lake State Park occupies 88 acres on the northwestern corner of Grand Lake in northeastern Oklahoma, near the town of Bernice. The campground provides 33 semi-improved RV sites featuring 50 amp electric and water hookups on level concrete pads, each equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and BBQ grill with lighting on the power pedestals. Primitive tent camping is also available throughout the park.

The park is renowned as the Crappie Capital of the World, offering excellent fishing for crappie, largemouth bass, white bass, channel catfish, and bluegill. Two boat ramps provide lake access. Beyond fishing, visitors enjoy a swimming beach, nature center (open Wednesday through Sunday, 9 AM to 4 PM), two playgrounds, and a mile-long paved walking and jogging path that is handicap accessible. The path winds along the shoreline past a wildlife feeding area to two wildlife viewing towers.

Two comfort stations with hot showers are located on either side of the park, and a centrally located dump station serves RV campers. Online reservations are required for all campsites through TravelOK.com.

location.directions: Located half a mile east of Bernice on Highway 85A, on the northwestern corner of Grand Lake. Address: 54101 E Hwy 85A, Bernice, OK 74331.

payload.name: Lake Lurleen State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Check-in is 2:00-7:00 p.m. and check-out is 11:00 a.m. A $5.25 non-refundable reservation fee applies per stay, plus a 4% nightly resort fee. Maximum stay is limited to 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Lake Lurleen State Park offers 67 full-hookup RV sites and 7 improved tent sites on a scenic 250-acre lake just nine miles northwest of Tuscaloosa, Alabama.
payload.medium_description: Lake Lurleen State Park features 67 renovated full-hookup campsites with 20/30/50-amp electrical, water, and sewer connections, plus 7 improved tent sites. The campground sits on the banks of 250-acre Lake Lurleen and offers modern bathhouses, laundry facilities, Wi-Fi, and waterfront sites with private deck patios.
payload.long_description:
Lake Lurleen State Park encompasses 1,625 acres surrounding its namesake 250-acre lake, located nine miles northwest of Tuscaloosa near Coker, Alabama. The park is named for Lurleen Burns Wallace, Alabama's only female governor. The campground underwent recent renovations, resulting in 67 full-hookup RV sites featuring smooth paved pads, 20/30/50-amp electrical service, water, and sewer connections. Seven improved tent sites offer a more traditional camping experience. Waterfront campsites include private deck patios with direct water access.

The campground is divided into multiple loops, with Loops C and D featuring 46 combined sites, a dump station, children's playground, pavilion, and trail access. Modern amenities include brand-new bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, on-site laundry facilities, and upgraded Wi-Fi throughout the campground. The park offers fishing, boating with a boat launch, hiking trails, swimming beaches, and picnic areas. Reservations are handled through the Alabama State Parks reservation system at reserve.alapark.com.

location.directions: Located at 13226 Lake Lurleen Road, Coker, AL 35452. The park is approximately nine miles northwest of Tuscaloosa and Northport.

payload.name: Oak Mountain State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Check-in at 2 p.m., check-out at 11 a.m. Maximum stay is 14 nights (extended to 31 nights from November 1 through March 31). Minimum two-night stay on weekends; three nights on holidays. North gate closes at sunset; use South gate for late arrivals.
payload.short_description: Alabama's largest state park offers diverse camping options including full-hookup RV sites, primitive tent camping, and equestrian sites across 11,861 acres of forested terrain near Birmingham.
payload.medium_description: Oak Mountain State Park Campground provides a full-service camping experience within Alabama's largest state park. Sites range from full-hookup RV spots with 30/50 amp service to primitive tent sites, plus dedicated equestrian camping. All sites include picnic tables, fire rings, grills, and tent pads. Amenities include two bathhouses with coin laundry, a country store, dump station, playground, and off-leash dog park. Over 100 miles of hiking trails accessible from camp.
payload.long_description:
Oak Mountain State Park Campground sits within Alabama's largest state park, spanning 11,861 acres of oak-covered ridges and valleys just south of Birmingham. The campground offers multiple site types to accommodate different camping styles: full-hookup RV sites with water, electric (30/50 amp), and sewer connections; partial hookup sites with water and electric only; primitive tent sites; and 12 equestrian sites with covered horse stalls. Most sites are back-in configurations, though nine pull-through options exist for larger rigs.

Every campsite includes a picnic table, tent pad, grill, lantern hook, and fire ring. The campground features two bathhouses with hot showers and restrooms, plus an additional restroom near the playground and dog park. Two coin laundry facilities serve each side of the campground. A dump station is available for $3 to non-registered campers. The country store stocks camping supplies, firewood, snacks, and gifts.

The park's trail network provides direct access from camp to over 100 miles of hiking, biking, and equestrian paths. Additional park amenities include two fishing lakes, a beach and swim area, marina rentals, an 18-hole golf course, and the Alabama Wildlife Center. Reservations can be made up to one year in advance through reserve.alapark.com or by calling 205-620-2527.

location.directions: From I-65, take Exit 246 and head east on State Route 119. Follow signs to Oak Mountain State Park. The park entrance is at 200 Terrace Drive, Pelham, AL 35124.

links.title: Oak Mountain State Park Main Page

payload.name: Shangri-la Trailhead And Campground Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with campground hosts on-site 365 days. Gates open 8 a.m. until sundown. Reservations available through the Florida State Parks system up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Primitive equestrian-friendly campground with 24 pull-through sites on the Cross Florida Greenway, offering trail access to Santos mountain bike network and Florida National Scenic Trail.
payload.medium_description: Shangri-La Trailhead and Campground sits in the rolling sandhills along the southern boundary of the Cross Florida Greenway, 5 miles west of I-75 off County Road 484. The 24 pull-through primitive sites on compacted shell are popular with equestrians but accommodate RVs, trailers, and tents. Amenities include a bathhouse with showers, communal potable water, dump station, horse wash racks, and covered picnic pavilions. The trailhead connects to the greenway's 63.4-mile mountain bike network including Santos, plus a 3.5-mile segment of the Florida National Scenic Trail.
payload.long_description:
Shangri-La Trailhead and Campground occupies a scenic stretch of rolling sandhills along the southern boundary of the Marjorie Harris Carr Cross Florida Greenway in Marion County. The campground's 24 pull-through sites sit on compacted shell and are designed with equestrians in mind, though they accommodate RVs, trailers, and tent campers equally well. Sites are primitive with no individual hookups, but communal water is available and generators are permitted outside quiet hours.

The facility includes a full bathhouse with showers and accessible restrooms, a dump station, two horse wash racks, and two covered picnic pavilions. Day-use visitors can access the equestrian and bike trailhead without a fee. A single-track trail from Shangri-La connects to the greenway's internationally-recognized 63.4-mile mountain bike network, which includes the famous Santos trails. Hikers can pick up a 3.5-mile moderate-difficulty segment of the Florida National Scenic Trail, marked with orange blazes.

The campground operates year-round with hosts on-site 365 days. Reservations are available through the Florida State Parks reservation system up to 11 months in advance. Pets are welcome but must be leashed when outside the camping unit and confined during quiet hours from 11 p.m. to 7 a.m.

location.directions: From I-75: Go west on Hwy 484 for approximately two miles, then turn right on Marion Oaks Course. After the curve to the left, Marion Oaks Course becomes Marion Oaks Trail. Continue approximately six miles, then turn right onto S.W. 69th Court. Continue straight into the Shangri-La Campground entrance.

links.title: Florida State Parks - Shangri-La Trailhead & Campground
Florida State Parks - Hours and Fees

payload.name: Nellie Martin River Cabin
payload.status_description: Open year-round, 24 hours a day. Reservations available via Recreation.gov up to 180 days in advance. Check-in and check-out at 12:00 p.m. Maximum seven consecutive nights per group. During August, limited to one reservation per person.
payload.short_description: Remote fly-in cabin on Montague Island in Prince William Sound, accessible only by wheel plane at low tide. Excellent coho salmon fishing and wildlife viewing.
payload.medium_description: Nellie Martin River Cabin is a rustic 12x14 Forest Service cabin on Montague Island in Chugach National Forest, accessible only by wheel plane landing on the beach at low tide. The cabin sleeps up to six on wooden bunks and includes wood and oil stoves, a rainwater catchment barrel, and basic tools. The Nellie Martin River hosts one of the largest coho salmon runs in Prince William Sound, making this a prime fishing destination from August through September.
payload.long_description:
Located on remote Montague Island at the entrance to Prince William Sound, Nellie Martin River Cabin offers a wilderness lodging experience for those seeking solitude and exceptional fishing. The cabin sits on the Nellie Martin River at the edge of a dense spruce forest, less than a mile from the beach landing area. Access is by wheel plane only, landing on the beach at low tide, typically a 45-minute flight from Seward or Cordova.

The rustic 12x14-foot cabin accommodates up to six people on wooden bunks without mattresses. Amenities include a table, wood stove, oil stove, axe, saw, splitting maul, and a rainwater catchment barrel. There is no running water, electricity, cut firewood, or cooking utensils. Visitors must bring all water for drinking, cooking, and cleaning, or boil surface water for at least five minutes. An outdoor pit toilet is provided.

The Nellie Martin River features one of the largest coho salmon runs in the Prince William Sound area, drawing heavy use from August through September. Pink salmon arrive earlier in the season, along with sea-run Dolly Varden and cutthroat trout. Hunters can pursue Sitka black-tail deer and brown bear during their respective seasons. The nearby beach offers beachcombing for glass floats and other sea-borne treasures. Wildlife includes migratory waterfowl and brown bears.

location.directions: Access is by wheel plane only, landing on the beach at low tide. The flight is typically 45 minutes from either Seward or Cordova. The cabin is located less than a mile from the beach landing area. Coordinate with a local air charter service and check tide tables before planning your arrival.

alerts.title: From Rec.gov
alerts.content: Fee changes in effect. This facility will now charge the same fee year-round.

payload.name: Big Woods Hiker-biker Overnight Campsite
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served, no fee or reservation required. Overnight stays limited to one night. Non-potable well water available mid-April through mid-November only; bring water treatment capability.
payload.short_description: Free first-come, first-served hiker-biker campsite at mile 82.7 on the C&O Canal towpath with chemical toilet, picnic table, firepit, and seasonal non-potable well water.
payload.medium_description: Big Woods Hiker-Biker Campsite is a primitive walk-in campground at mile 82.7 along the Chesapeake and Ohio Canal towpath near Mercersville, Maryland. This free, first-come, first-served site accommodates tents only with no reservations required. Amenities include a chemical toilet, picnic table, firepit, and non-potable well water available mid-April through mid-November. Overnight stays are limited to one night per trip.
payload.long_description:
Big Woods Hiker-Biker Campsite sits at mile 82.7 along the historic Chesapeake and Ohio Canal towpath in Washington County, Maryland. Part of a network of hiker-biker campsites spaced every 5-7 miles along the 184.5-mile towpath, Big Woods provides a convenient overnight stop for long-distance cyclists and hikers traveling the trail.

This primitive, tent-only campsite is free and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations accepted. Each site includes a chemical toilet, picnic table, and firepit. Non-potable well water is available from mid-April through mid-November; campers must filter, chemically treat, or boil all water before use. Well handles are removed during winter months to prevent freeze damage.

Fires are restricted to provided firepits and grills or portable grills positioned off the ground. All coals must be fully extinguished and packed out. This is a trash-free park requiring campers to pack out all waste. Quiet hours are 10 PM to 6 AM. The site accommodates 5-10 tents depending on conditions, with overnight stays limited to one night per trip.

location.directions: Located at mile 82.7 on the C&O Canal towpath near Mercersville. Accessible only by foot or bicycle. A sign marks the path from the towpath to the campsite, which is set back from the main trail for privacy.

links.title: Big Woods Hiker-Biker Overnight (HBO) Campsite Official Website

payload.name: Rocky Point
payload.status_description: Rocky Point Picnic Site is currently closed until further notice. This is a day-use picnic area only with no overnight camping permitted.
payload.short_description: Rocky Point is a day-use picnic site in Angeles National Forest within the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument. No overnight camping is permitted.
payload.medium_description: Rocky Point Picnic Site is a day-use recreation area in the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument portion of Angeles National Forest. This is a picnic-only facility with no overnight camping allowed. When operational, the site charges $5 per vehicle per day or $30 annually.
payload.long_description:
Rocky Point Picnic Site is a day-use area located in the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument within Angeles National Forest. This site is designated for picnicking only and does not permit overnight camping.

When open, the site offers basic amenities including restroom facilities. There is no potable water available, so visitors must bring their own. The day-use fee is $5 per vehicle per day or $30 per vehicle annually.

location.directions: Rocky Point Picnic Site is located at 32930 Cheseboro Rd, Palmdale, California 93552.

payload.name: Table Rock State Park Campground 1
payload.status_description: Open year-round. On-season runs March through November; off-season December through February. Water at individual sewer/electric/water campsites is weather-dependent during March and November, and unavailable at individual sites December through February. Potable water remains available year-round at the dump station. One shower house stays open during off-season. Two-night minimum required on weekends.
payload.short_description: Modern lakeside campground in Table Rock State Park offering electric and full-hookup sites along Table Rock Lake near Branson, Missouri.
payload.medium_description: Campground 1 at Table Rock State Park offers electric and sewer/electric/water campsites along the Table Rock Lake shoreline. The campground features modern amenities including shower houses with laundry facilities, a dump station, and playground. Sites include a parking pad, picnic table, grill, and lantern post. Water at individual hookup sites operates March through November, with potable water available year-round at the dump station.
payload.long_description:
Campground 1 at Table Rock State Park sits along the scenic shoreline of Table Rock Lake in the Ozarks near Branson, Missouri. The campground provides electric sites with 30-amp and 50-amp service as well as full-hookup sewer/electric/water sites for RVs and trailers. Each campsite includes a parking pad, picnic table, grill, and lantern post. The campground operates year-round, though water service at individual sites runs from March 1 through November 30.

Facilities include a shower house with restrooms and laundry, a dump station with year-round potable water access, playground, and amphitheater. During the off-season (December through February), one shower house remains operational. ADA-accessible sites are available, including three electric sites and one sewer/electric/water site. Showerhouse 1 and its laundry facility are accessible.

The park provides access to Table Rock Lake activities including fishing for bass, crappie, catfish, and trout, as well as a marina with boat rentals. Hiking and mountain biking trails are nearby. Reservations can be made up to 12 months in advance through the Missouri State Parks reservation system. A two-night minimum stay applies on weekends.

location.directions: From Branson, take State Highway 165 south. The park entrance is at 5272 State Highway 165, Branson, MO 65616.

links.title: Table Rock State Park Main Page
Missouri State Parks Guide to Campsites

payload.name: Beavers Bend State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 22 through November 30, 2026. Reservations available online through OKStateParks.ReserveAmerica.com. Cancellations require 5 days advance notice for full refund.
payload.short_description: Sprawling 3,482-acre Oklahoma state park offering 393 RV campsites and 50+ tent sites across multiple campgrounds along Broken Bow Lake and the Mountain Fork River, with options from primitive tent camping to modern full-hookup RV sites.
payload.medium_description: Beavers Bend State Park features eight distinct camping areas spread between the River Area and Lake Area near Broken Bow Lake. RV campers can choose from semi-modern sites with water and 30 or 50-amp electric, or the modern Turkey Campground with full hookups including sewer. Primitive tent camping is available at Dogwood, Elm, Grapevine, Hickory, Bluejay, Coyote, Deer, and Eagle campgrounds. The park also offers two riverside yurts and comfort stations throughout.
payload.long_description:
Beavers Bend State Park occupies 3,482 acres in the mountainous region of southeast Oklahoma along the shores of Broken Bow Lake and the Mountain Fork River. The park offers one of the most diverse camping experiences in the Oklahoma state park system, with 393 RV campsites and over 50 tent sites distributed across eight camping areas.

The River Area campgrounds include Acorn and Cypress with water and electric hookups (50-amp and 30-amp respectively), Fern with 30-amp electric near the miniature train and stables, and primitive tent-only areas at Dogwood, Elm, Grapevine, and Hickory. The Lake Area campgrounds feature Armadillo (50-amp), Quail (30-amp), and Turkey, the only modern campground with water, 30-amp electric, and sewer hookups. Tent camping in the Lake Area is available at Bluejay, Coyote, Deer, and Eagle.

Beyond camping, the park offers extensive recreation including hiking, biking, boating, fishing, water skiing, canoeing, horseback riding, and nature center programs. The Mountain Fork River below Broken Bow Dam is stocked year-round with rainbow and brown trout, with two catch-and-release trophy areas.

location.directions: Located 8 miles north of Broken Bow, Oklahoma on Highway 259A. The park address is 4350 S Hwy 259A, Broken Bow, OK 74728.

address.full: A97 Beavers Bnd, Broken Bow, OK 74728

links.title: Beavers Bend State Park Official Site

payload.name: Sequoyah State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All campsite reservations must be made online through ReserveAmerica. Check-in is 5pm, check-out is 2pm. Quiet hours are 11pm to 6am.
payload.short_description: Large Oklahoma state park on Fort Gibson Lake with over 400 campsites ranging from full-hookup RV sites to primitive tent camping, featuring showers, dump stations, and lake access.
payload.medium_description: Sequoyah State Park sits on a 2,200-acre peninsula on the eastern shore of Fort Gibson Lake in Cherokee County. The park offers over 400 campsites across multiple areas: Choctaw and Seminole campgrounds provide full hookups (water, electric, sewer), Cherokee has water and electric only, and The Creek and Paradise Cove offer tent camping. Each camping area has comfort stations with restrooms and hot showers. The park features lighted boat ramps, a nature center, hiking trails, and the Sequoyah Lodge with restaurant.
payload.long_description:
Sequoyah State Park occupies a scenic 2,200-acre peninsula on the eastern shore of Fort Gibson Lake, making it one of Oklahoma's premier lakeside camping destinations. The park provides extensive camping options with over 400 sites distributed across several distinct areas. RV campers can choose between full-hookup sites at Choctaw and Seminole campgrounds (water, electric, sewer with 30/50 amp service) or water and electric only at Cherokee. Tent campers have dedicated areas at The Creek, Choctaw, and Paradise Cove.

Each camping area includes comfort stations with flush restrooms and hot showers, and both campgrounds have dump stations. Sites feature picnic tables, charcoal grills, and fire rings. The park accommodates big rigs with pull-through sites available and a maximum RV length of 60 feet. ADA-accessible sites and shower facilities are available in each campground area.

Beyond camping, the park offers lighted boat ramps, the Three Forks Nature Center, hiking trails, a recreation room, tennis and basketball courts, horseshoe pits, and playgrounds. The Sequoyah Lodge provides lodging and dining at the Lookout Kitchen restaurant. The Sequoyah Group Camp features a dining hall with full kitchen and 10 A-frame cabins for larger gatherings.

location.directions: Located 8 miles east of Wagoner, Oklahoma and 18 miles west of Tahlequah on State Highway 51. Address: 17131 Park 10, Hulbert, OK 74441.

payload.name: Meaher State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. daily, with the gate closing to day-use visitors at 5 p.m. Office hours are 7 a.m. to 3 p.m. Two-night minimum on weekends, three-night minimum on holidays.
payload.short_description: Meaher State Park offers 108 RV sites with full hookups and 10 tent sites in the Mobile Bay wetlands, featuring a 300-foot fishing pier, boat ramp, and boardwalk access to Ducker Bay.
payload.medium_description: Located in the wetlands of north Mobile Bay near Spanish Fort, Meaher State Park provides 108 paved RV campsites with 50-amp electric, water, and sewer hookups, plus 10 improved tent sites with 20-amp electric and water. The 1,327-acre park features two modern bathhouses, laundry facilities, a 300-foot fishing pier with a 200-foot T-section, boat ramp with Blakeley River access, boardwalk, and kayak/canoe rentals.
payload.long_description:
Meaher State Park sits on 1,327 acres in the wetlands along north Mobile Bay, offering campers direct access to coastal Alabama's unique ecosystems. The campground features 108 paved RV sites equipped with 50-amp electrical service, water, and sewer hookups, each with its own picnic table and grill. Generous spacing between sites ensures privacy. Ten improved tent sites provide 20-amp electrical outlets, water spigots, circular ground grills, picnic tables, and food/trash hanging poles on gravel pads.

Two modern bathhouses with laundry facilities serve the campground. A 300-foot fishing pier extends into the bay with a 200-foot T-section, and a boat ramp provides access to the Blakeley River. The park's boardwalk winds through the wetlands, and canoe and kayak rentals are available for paddling the bay and surrounding waterways.

The park is located just off Battleship Parkway (US-90/98) in Spanish Fort, offering easy access while maintaining a natural setting along Ducker Bay. Reservations can be made up to one year in advance through the Alabama State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: From I-10, take Exit 30 toward Spanish Fort/Battleship Parkway. Head south on US-90/98 (Battleship Parkway) for approximately 2.5 miles. The park entrance is at 5200 Battleship Parkway East, Spanish Fort, AL 36527.

payload.name: Davis Farm Primitive Trail Campsite
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees or reservations. Stays limited to 3 days within a 30-day period. Bring all water as none is available on site.
payload.short_description: Primitive Appalachian Trail campsite near Burkes Garden, Virginia with westward-facing valley views and room for a few tents on a flattened slope.
payload.medium_description: Davis Farm Campsite is a primitive backcountry site along the Appalachian Trail in Virginia's Jefferson National Forest. Located 0.5 miles off the main trail down a steep switchback, the site sits on a flattened slope accommodating a few tents. It offers panoramic westward views of the valley below, making it a scenic spot for sunset watching. Pack in all water and supplies as there are no facilities.
payload.long_description:
Davis Farm Campsite is a primitive overnight site along the Appalachian Trail in Tazewell County, Virginia, within the Jefferson National Forest. The campsite lies approximately half a mile off the main AT corridor, accessed via a steep switchback descent. The site itself occupies a flattened area on a hillside slope that can accommodate two to three tents.

The campsite faces west, providing excellent views of the pastoral valley below and memorable sunset vistas. The surrounding area borders agricultural land, so hikers may hear cattle in the valley. This is a true backcountry experience with no amenities: no drinking water, no restrooms, and no trash service. All water must be packed in or sourced and purified from natural sources along the trail.

As with other AT overnight sites in the Southern Region, stays are limited to three consecutive days within any 30-day period. There is no fee and no reservation system; the site operates on a first-come, first-served basis year-round.

location.directions: From the Appalachian Trail, follow the blue-blazed side trail 0.5 miles downhill via steep switchbacks to reach the campsite.

payload.name: Black Mesa State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through Oklahoma State Parks ReserveAmerica up to 11 months in advance. The Nature Preserve is accessible dawn to dusk only.
payload.short_description: Remote state park in Oklahoma's far northwest panhandle adjacent to Lake Carl Etling, offering RV and tent camping with dark sky designation near the state's highest point at Black Mesa.
payload.medium_description: Black Mesa State Park sits in the remote Oklahoma panhandle near the Colorado and New Mexico borders, adjacent to Lake Carl Etling. The park offers 52 campsites including RV sites with water and electric hookups and primitive tent sites. Each site includes a picnic table, fire pit, and grill. The park's dark sky designation makes it exceptional for stargazing, and the nearby Black Mesa Nature Preserve features Oklahoma's highest point at 4,973 feet.
payload.long_description:
Black Mesa State Park occupies a remote corner of Oklahoma's panhandle, about 30 miles northwest of Boise City near the tiny community of Kenton. The park sits adjacent to Lake Carl Etling and serves as a base camp for exploring the nearby Black Mesa Nature Preserve, home to Oklahoma's highest point at 4,973 feet elevation. The landscape here feels more like the desert Southwest than the Great Plains, with juniper-dotted mesas and dramatic rock formations.

The campground offers 52 sites split between RV and tent camping. The 25 RV sites feature water and 30/50 amp electric hookups on cement or gravel pads ranging from 30 to 62 feet in length. A dump station is located near the comfort station. The 25 tent sites and 2 primitive tent sites are spread across three areas: Creek, West Canyon, and Lake View, with varying levels of shade and water access.

The park holds official dark sky designation, making it one of the premier stargazing destinations in the region. Quiet hours from 11 PM to 7 AM include requests to minimize exterior lighting and use red flashlights when possible. The August Perseid meteor shower draws visitors specifically for the pristine night sky viewing conditions.

location.directions: From Boise City, take OK-325 west/northwest approximately 28 miles. From Kenton, take OK-325 east for about 5 miles, then turn right on North Lake Road to the park entrance. The park address is 11546 North Lake Road, Kenton, OK 73946.

payload.name: Wagon Flat
payload.status_description: Road access destroyed by 2011 floods and has not been repaired. Accessible only by foot, bike, or horseback. No developed facilities currently maintained.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry trail camp along La Brea Creek in Los Padres National Forest, accessible only by foot, bike, or horseback after 2011 flood damage destroyed road access.
payload.medium_description: Wagon Flat is a primitive trail camp set among grassy hills and oaks at 1,411 feet elevation along the seldom-flowing La Brea Creek. Once a developed car-camping destination, the campground was severely impacted by the 2009 La Brea Fire and subsequent 2011 winter floods that destroyed road access. The Forest Service has not repaired the road, making this a walk-in, bike-in, or horse-in destination only.
payload.long_description:
Wagon Flat Camp sits in a canyon bottom surrounded by oak trees along La Brea Creek in the Santa Barbara Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. At 1,411 feet elevation, the area features the characteristic grassy hills and oak woodlands of this section of the backcountry. The creek flows intermittently, so reliable water is not guaranteed.

This site has a complex recent history. The 2009 La Brea Fire burned through the area, followed by severe flooding during the 2011 winter storms that washed out the access road. The Forest Service has not undertaken repairs, effectively converting what was once a drive-in campground into a remote backcountry destination. Visitors now reach the camp only by hiking, mountain biking, or horseback.

The area offers proximity to hunting opportunities, mountain biking trails, and OHV routes. Wildlife including bears and mountain lions have been reported in the vicinity. Due to fire restrictions in the Santa Barbara Front Country, campfires may be prohibited depending on current conditions.

location.directions: From Santa Barbara, take Highway 154 north. Access requires traveling toward the La Brea Creek area southeast of Buckhorn Ridge in the Santa Barbara Ranger District. The vehicle access road is closed due to flood damage, so the campground must be reached by foot, bicycle, or horseback from the nearest accessible road or trailhead.

payload.name: Lake Wister State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All RV and tent sites require online reservations made at least 1 day in advance, up to 11 months ahead. Peak season runs May 22 through September 7.
payload.short_description: Lake Wister State Park offers 145 campsites across five scenic camping areas along the 115-mile shoreline of Lake Wister in southeast Oklahoma's Ouachita Mountain foothills.
payload.medium_description: Lake Wister State Park features five distinct camping areas spread along the lake's scenic shoreline. The park offers modern sites with full hookups including 30-amp electric, water, and sewer at Victor Area, semi-modern sites with partial hookups, and primitive tent camping. Comfort stations with showers, dump stations, and a water spray park are available on-site.
payload.long_description:
Lake Wister State Park sits nestled in a ring of pine and oak-covered mountains, serving as a gateway to the Ouachita National Forest. The park encompasses five camping areas around the 7,300-acre lake: Below Dam (16 sites), Quarry Island (31 sites), Victor Landing (62 sites), Wards (25 sites), and Wister Ridge (15 sites). Victor Area offers 57 modern campsites with 30-amp electric, water, and sewer hookups, while Quarry Island and Wards Landing provide water and 30-amp electric connections.

Beyond camping, the park features 15 cabins with stone-framed fireplaces, a water spray park, miniature golf course, swimming beach, and a group camp facility accommodating up to 100 visitors. An ADA-compliant paved trail in Wards Campground provides wheelchair-accessible scenic views along a 1/3-mile route. The lake supports boating, water skiing, and fishing, with the nearby Wister Wildlife Management Area offering additional outdoor recreation.

The park roads can be tight for larger RVs, and while some sites list capacities up to 50 feet, campers with rigs over 35 feet may find maneuvering challenging. A dump station is available on-site, though low-hanging tree branches may affect access for tall vehicles.

location.directions: From Wister, 2 miles east on US 270

payload.name: Robbers Cave State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations through Oklahoma State Parks system required at least 1 day in advance; can book up to 11-12 months ahead. Park hours 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM daily.
payload.short_description: Historic state park campground in Oklahoma's Sans Bois Mountains offering 230 sites from primitive tent camping to full-hookup RV sites, plus unique accommodations like yurts and a covered wagon.
payload.medium_description: Robbers Cave State Park, tucked into the rugged Sans Bois Mountains of southeast Oklahoma, offers camping options for every style. Choose from 97 tent sites, modern RV sites with full hookups, equestrian camping areas, or unique stays like yurts and a covered wagon. The park features comfort stations with showers, a dump station, swimming pool, swim beach, hiking trails, rock climbing, and a nature center.
payload.long_description:
Robbers Cave State Park lies in the scenic, hilly woodlands of the Sans Bois Mountains in southeast Oklahoma, 5 miles north of Wilburton. The park takes its name from a cave once used as a hideout by outlaws including Belle Starr and Jesse James. Today it draws campers with 230 sites spread across multiple loops, ranging from primitive tent camping along secluded trails to modern RV sites with full hookups.
