The campground offers 97 tent sites, 47 semi-modern RV sites with water and electric, 20 modern RV sites with full hookups, 3 premium RV sites, and 50 equestrian sites for those bringing horses. Unique accommodations include 2 yurts, a lake hut, and a covered wagon. Amenities include comfort stations with showers, a dump station, grills, an outdoor pool, swim beach, playground, and WiFi. The park also has a restaurant (The Lookout Kitchen), nature center, gift shop, and offers activities like fishing, hiking, rock climbing, rappelling, disc golf, and ATV trails.

Reservations are made through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system and can be booked up to 11-12 months in advance with a minimum 1-day advance notice required.

location.directions: 5 miles north of Wilburton on Highway 2

payload.name: Monte Sano State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available through reserve.alapark.com up to one year in advance. Check-in at 2 PM, check-out at 11 AM. Two-night minimum on weekends, three-night minimum on holidays. Improved sites have a 14-day stay limit from March 1 through November 1; primitive sites limited to 5 consecutive nights year-round.
payload.short_description: Monte Sano State Park Campground offers 113 campsites including primitive, water/electric, and full-hookup options atop Monte Sano mountain near Huntsville, Alabama.
payload.medium_description: Monte Sano State Park Campground sits atop Monte Sano mountain overlooking Huntsville, Alabama. The campground features 113 sites across three tiers: 23 primitive tent-only sites, 69 water and electric sites with 30/50 amp service, and 21 full-hookup premium sites with sewer connections. Two bathhouses with showers and coin-operated laundry, two dump stations, and a camp store selling firewood serve the campground. Every site includes a fire pit and picnic table.
payload.long_description:
Monte Sano State Park Campground occupies a scenic plateau on Monte Sano mountain, just minutes from downtown Huntsville. The campground divides into three site categories: primitive tent-only sites tucked into wooded areas, standard water and electric sites with gravel pads and 30/50 amp service, and premium full-hookup sites offering water, electric, and sewer connections along the bluff with views. Two modern bathhouses provide hot showers and coin-operated laundry facilities.

The park surrounds campers with over 20 miles of hiking and mountain biking trails through hardwood forests. A Japanese garden, disc golf course, playground, and the Von Braun Planetarium provide diversions beyond the trails. The camp store stocks firewood and essentials, staying open year-round from 8am to 5pm. Two dump stations serve RV campers.

Reservations are strongly recommended, especially for weekends when a two-night minimum applies. Holiday weekends require three-night stays. The improved campground enforces a 14-day stay limit from March 1 through November 1, while primitive sites cap at five consecutive nights year-round. RVers should avoid GPS-directed routes via Bankhead Parkway and follow official directions from Governors Drive instead.

location.directions: From Huntsville: Stay left to South Memorial Parkway. Take the right-hand exit to Governors Drive. Turn left onto Governors Drive. Follow Governors Drive up the mountain to Monte Sano Blvd. Turn left onto Monte Sano Blvd. Continue 2.5 miles and then turn right onto Nolen Ave. Follow Nolen Ave one mile until you arrive at the Park Entrance Gate. Do NOT use GPS or Bankhead Parkway if pulling a camper or RV.

links.title: Monte Sano State Park Main Page

payload.name: Wind Creek State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Park hours are 7 a.m. to dark daily. Reservation office open Monday through Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Check-in is 2:00 p.m. Reservations available up to one year in advance through reserve.alapark.com.
payload.short_description: One of the largest state-owned campgrounds in the United States, with 586 campsites on Lake Martin featuring water and electrical hookups, waterfront sites, and extensive recreational amenities.
payload.medium_description: Wind Creek State Park sits on 1,444 acres along Lake Martin's shoreline near Alexander City, Alabama. The campground offers 586 sites with water and electrical hookups, including 157 waterfront sites and 268 sites with sewer connections. Premium sites feature 60-foot concrete pads with 50-amp service, sewer, and TV hookups. Bathhouses with laundry facilities are located throughout the campground. The park provides extensive recreation including a marina, boat rentals, zipline tours, archery range, putt-putt golf, swimming beach, and horseback riding.
payload.long_description:
Wind Creek State Park operates one of the largest state-owned campgrounds in the United States, spanning 1,444 acres along the scenic shoreline of Lake Martin. The park serves as the primary public access point to the 44,000-acre lake and offers exceptional fishing for crappie, bluegill, and striped bass. All 586 campsites include water and electrical hookups, with 157 sites offering waterfront access and 268 sites featuring full sewer connections.

The campground features 39 recently renovated premium sites with 16-foot-wide, 60-foot-long concrete pads, 50 or 30-amp electrical service, water, sewer, waterfront access, and TV service. Bathhouses are distributed throughout the campground, and two laundry facilities are available at the marina and B-1 bathhouse. The park also offers seven air-conditioned camping cabins, glamping safari tents, lakeside cottages, and 20 first-come, first-served equestrian camping sites.

Beyond camping, Wind Creek provides diverse recreation including a full-service marina with boat rentals, zipline canopy tours, an archery range, putt-putt golf course, guided horseback rides through Rockin' K, swimming beach, hiking and biking trails, and picnic pavilions. The on-site Creem@The Creek restaurant offers dining without leaving the park. Senior citizens 62+, veterans, active military, and guests with disabilities receive a 15% discount on overnight accommodations.

location.directions: Located south of Alexander City on Alabama Highway 128. The park address is 4325 Alabama Highway 128, Alexander City, AL 35010.

links.title: Wind Creek State Park - Main Page

payload.name: Sublett Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open. Operating season is typically June through November depending on weather. No reservations; first-come, first-served. 14-day camping limit within any 28-day period.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with 9 sites near Sublett Reservoir in Idaho's Sawtooth National Forest, offering vault toilets, tables, grills, and access to fishing and boating.
payload.medium_description: Sublett Campground is a free, first-come first-served campground located two miles from Sublett Reservoir in the Sublett Division of Sawtooth National Forest. The campground features 9 sites with tables and grills, vault toilets, and nearby boat ramp access. This is a pack-in/pack-out area with no potable water, making it well-suited for self-sufficient tent and RV campers seeking a quiet fishing and camping destination.
payload.long_description:
Sublett Campground offers a remote camping experience in the Sublett Division of Sawtooth National Forest, situated just two miles from Sublett Reservoir. The campground provides 9 individual sites that can collectively accommodate up to 40 visitors. Each site includes a table and grill, with vault toilets available on-site. A nearby boat ramp provides access to the reservoir for fishing and boating.

This is a primitive, no-fee campground operating on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservation system. Campers must bring their own drinking water as none is available on-site, and all trash must be packed out. The campground is accessible for RVs and trailers, though specific size limitations are not published. Livestock facilities are available nearby, but horses are prohibited within the campground itself.

The typical operating season runs from June through November, depending on weather and road conditions. A 14-day camping limit applies within any 28-day period, after which campers must leave National Forest lands for at least 14 days before returning. Vehicle parking is limited to two vehicles per site on designated gravel spurs.

location.directions: From I-84, take exit 245 and go east 13 miles on Sublett Road around the north end of Sublett Reservoir.

payload.name: Herbert Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is closed. No reopening date or additional details are available from official sources.
payload.short_description: A primitive campground in Union County within the Enoree Ranger District of Sumter National Forest, currently closed.
payload.medium_description: Herbert Campground is located in Union County within the Enoree Ranger District of Sumter National Forest in South Carolina. The campground is currently closed and does not appear on official USFS recreation listings.
payload.long_description:
Herbert Campground is situated in Union County, South Carolina, within the Enoree Ranger District of Sumter National Forest. The site is located in the Piedmont region of the forest, which encompasses over 170,000 acres across Newberry, Union, Chester, Laurens, and Fairfield counties.

The campground is currently closed and does not appear on official USFS recreation pages or Recreation.gov. It may be a primitive site, hunt camp, or a campground that has been decommissioned. The Enoree Ranger District requires free primitive camping permits for dispersed camping in the area.

For current information about this site, contact the Enoree District Office at 803-276-4810.

location.directions: From the intersection of Hwy. 72 and Hwy. 215 in Carlisle, drive north 0.3 miles on Hwy. 72. Turn right onto Fishdam Rd. and proceed 0.1 miles. Turn right onto Pickney Street and continue 0.5 miles to the railroad crossing. After crossing the tracks, drive another 0.4 miles. Turn right onto FS Road 404 and drive 0.2 miles to the campground entrance on the right.

payload.name: Lake Thunderbird State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Peak season runs May 22 through October 31. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance through Oklahoma State Parks. Cancellations require 5 days advance notice for a full refund.
payload.short_description: Lake Thunderbird State Park offers over 350 campsites ranging from primitive tent sites to full-hookup RV sites, with two marinas, nine boat ramps, and swim beaches near Norman, Oklahoma.
payload.medium_description: Lake Thunderbird State Park features 352 campsites across multiple campground areas including RV sites with electric, water, and sewer hookups, as well as primitive tent camping. The park offers modern restroom facilities with showers, dump stations, and playgrounds. Located just 13 miles east of Norman, the park surrounds a 6,070-acre reservoir popular for fishing, boating, swimming, and water sports.
payload.long_description:
Lake Thunderbird State Park encompasses over 1,800 acres surrounding the 6,070-acre Lake Thunderbird reservoir, approximately 13 miles east of Norman, Oklahoma. The park offers 352 campsites spread across multiple camping areas, including RV sites with full hookups (electric up to 50-amp, water, and sewer), semi-modern RV sites with electric only, and primitive tent camping. Pull-through sites and waterfront locations are available. Each campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring.

Modern comfort stations with flush toilets and hot showers are distributed throughout the campground areas, along with dump stations for RV waste disposal. A gift shop serves campers, and two laundry facilities are on-site. The park features two storm shelters for severe weather protection.

Recreational opportunities abound with two marinas (Calypso Cove and Little River), nine boat ramps, and two swim beaches. The lake supports year-round fishing for largemouth bass, catfish, crappie, and white bass. Extensive hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian trails wind through the park, and an archery range is available. A nature center offers educational programming.

location.directions: From Norman, travel approximately 13 miles east on State Highway 9 to reach the park. The main park address is 13101 Alameda Dr, Norman, OK 73026.

payload.name: McGee Creek State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round with online reservations required. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. Quiet hours are 11:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. with no generators allowed during this time.
payload.short_description: Lakeside state park campground on McGee Creek Reservoir featuring paved RV sites with electric and water hookups, comfort stations with showers, and primitive camping areas in southeastern Oklahoma.
payload.medium_description: McGee Creek State Park offers year-round camping on the shores of McGee Creek Reservoir, 17 miles east of Atoka. The park features two developed camping areas with paved RV sites that include electric and water hookups, comfort stations with hot showers, a dump station, swim beach, and fishing piers. Primitive tent sites are also available throughout the park.
payload.long_description:
McGee Creek State Park sits along McGee Creek Reservoir in the Ouachita Mountains of southeastern Oklahoma. The park provides a scenic escape with over 8,900 acres of lake and surrounding wilderness. Two main developed campgrounds serve overnight visitors: Buster Hight Area features paved sites with water and electric hookups, a four-lane boat ramp, comfort stations with showers, a dump station, fishing pier, playground, and swim beach. Potapo Area offers paved RV sites with water and electric service, a comfort station with showers, and a two-lane boat ramp.

Primitive camping sites are scattered throughout both areas for tent campers seeking a more rustic experience. The park also features eight lake huts near Potapo Campground, which include back porches overlooking the lake, bunk beds, fireplaces, air conditioning, water service, and outdoor barbecue grills. Linens are not provided in the huts.

The reservoir supports excellent fishing for bass, catfish, and crappie, while the surrounding McGee Creek Natural Scenic Recreation Area offers hiking trails through undeveloped wilderness. All campsite reservations are made online through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: From Atoka, take Highway 3 east for 17 miles, then turn north on McGee Creek Lake Road and continue 3 miles to the park.

payload.name: Melville Nauheim Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees or reservations required. Stays limited to two consecutive nights. Bear-resistant food storage required.
payload.short_description: Backcountry three-sided shelter on the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, accessible via a 1.5-mile hike from Route 9.
payload.medium_description: Melville Nauheim Shelter is a primitive three-sided lean-to located where the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail coincide in southern Vermont. The shelter accommodates approximately 8 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations required. Amenities include a composting privy and a nearby water source that must be filtered or treated before drinking. Additional tent platforms are available near the shelter for overflow camping.
payload.long_description:
Melville Nauheim Shelter sits in the Green Mountain National Forest along the shared corridor of the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and Vermont's Long Trail. Reached via a short spur trail approximately 1.5 miles north of Route 9 near Woodford, this classic three-sided Adirondack-style shelter offers a rustic overnight option for through-hikers and section hikers alike.

The shelter can accommodate around 8 people inside, with additional tent platforms available nearby for overflow during peak season. A composting privy is located near the shelter, and water can be obtained from a stream where the spur trail meets the main trail. All water must be filtered or chemically treated before drinking. As with all Long Trail shelters, stays are limited to two consecutive nights.

Maintained by the Green Mountain Club, the shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis year-round with no fees required. Hikers should bring a tent as backup during busy periods when shelters often fill. Bear-resistant food storage is required on Green Mountain National Forest land using bear boxes, bear canisters, or proper hanging techniques.

location.directions: From Route 9 near Woodford, Vermont, hike north on the Appalachian Trail/Long Trail for approximately 1.5 miles. The shelter is accessed via a short spur trail off the main trail.

links.title: USFS Green Mountain NF Camping & Cabins

payload.name: Natural Falls State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Campers have 24-hour access. Online reservations required for all RV and tent sites via Oklahoma State Parks. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Natural Falls State Park Campground offers RV and tent camping in the scenic Ozark Highlands of northeast Oklahoma, near a stunning 77-foot waterfall accessible via paved trails and overlook.
payload.medium_description: Located near the Oklahoma/Arkansas border in the Ozark Highlands, Natural Falls State Park features a dramatic 77-foot waterfall cascading through rock formations. The campground offers 44 RV sites (7 with full hookups, others with partial hookups) and 17 tent sites, plus five yurts. Amenities include modern comfort stations with showers, dump station, fire rings, and picnic tables. The park provides 4.5 miles of hiking trails, an 18-hole disc golf course, playgrounds, and catch-and-release fishing.
payload.long_description:
Natural Falls State Park sits in the scenic Ozark Highlands of northeast Oklahoma, showcasing a 77-foot waterfall that plunges through ancient rock formations into a forested canyon. The falls can be viewed from an ADA-accessible paved observation deck at the canyon rim, with additional trails descending into the canyon for closer views. The park pumps water from the pool below back to the top of the falls, ensuring the waterfall runs year-round regardless of seasonal rainfall.

The campground offers 44 RV sites and 17 tent sites spread through a wooded setting. Seven RV sites feature full hookups (electric, water, sewer), while the remaining sites offer partial hookups with electric and water. All sites include picnic tables, charcoal grills, and fire rings, with modern comfort stations providing restrooms and showers. A dump station is available for RV waste disposal. Five yurts are also available for those seeking a more comfortable overnight option, each equipped with climate control, refrigerator, microwave, and outdoor fire ring.

Beyond camping, the park provides 4.5 miles of hiking and nature trails, an 18-hole disc golf course, volleyball and basketball courts, horseshoe pits, playgrounds, and a catch-and-release fishing pond. The park is located just minutes from the Arkansas border, making it an accessible destination for campers from both states.

location.directions: Located at 58035 S. 682 Rd., Colcord, OK 74338, near the Oklahoma/Arkansas border in Delaware County.

payload.name: Tenkiller State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations must be made at least 1 day in advance and can be booked up to 11 months ahead. Park entrance fee required ($10/day out-of-state, $8/day Oklahoma plates; annual passes available). Vehicle entrance fee waived for honorably discharged veterans and Oklahoma residents 62 and older.
payload.short_description: Tenkiller State Park campground sits along the shores of Lake Tenkiller in Oklahoma's Ozark foothills, offering tent and RV camping across 10 campgrounds with full hookup options, comfort stations, and lake access.
payload.medium_description: Tenkiller State Park offers camping along the 130 miles of shoreline at Lake Tenkiller, known as Oklahoma's clear-water gem. The park features 10 campgrounds ranging from primitive tent sites to full-hookup RV pads with 30 and 50-amp electric service. Seven comfort stations with restrooms and showers are scattered throughout, along with two dump stations, a seasonal swimming pool with splash pad, and direct lake access for boating and fishing.
payload.long_description:
Tenkiller State Park occupies the shores of Lake Tenkiller, a 13,000-acre reservoir in the Ozark foothills of eastern Oklahoma renowned for its unusually clear blue-green water. The park spreads across 10 campgrounds offering a range of camping styles. Primitive tent campgrounds include Bluff View, Eagle Point, and Fisherman's Point, each with basic facilities. RV campers can choose from Blue Jay Knob and Flying Squirrel (30-amp electric and water) or upgrade to Fox Squirrel and Shady Grove for full hookups with 50-amp service.

The Fox Squirrel Campground is the most developed, with 52 sites featuring electric, water, and sewer connections. Both pull-through and back-in sites are available throughout the park. Seven comfort stations provide restrooms and hot showers, and two dump stations serve RV campers. Additional amenities include 172 picnic tables, group pavilions, a volleyball court, basketball court, playground, and a seasonal swimming pool with water slide and splash pad.

The park also offers 38 cabins and direct access to Lake Tenkiller for swimming, scuba diving, fishing, and boating. The 1.5-mile Tenkiller Multi-Use Trail is paved and ADA accessible. Reservations are required for all RV and tent sites through the Oklahoma State Parks system.

location.directions: From Tahlequah, take Highway 82 south approximately 12 miles to Highway 100. Turn west and follow signs to Tenkiller State Park. The park entrance is on Tenkiller Drive off Highway 100.

payload.name: Tunnel Rock Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. This campground is no longer available for camping and all facilities have been decommissioned.
payload.short_description: Tunnel Rock Campground is a former Forest Service campground on Lewiston Lake that has been permanently closed.
payload.medium_description: Tunnel Rock Campground was a small primitive campground located on the shores of Lewiston Lake in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest. The campground has been permanently closed and is no longer available for camping. No facilities are currently operational at this site.
payload.long_description:
Tunnel Rock Campground was once a small, primitive camping area situated along Lewiston Lake within the Trinity Unit of the Whiskeytown-Shasta-Trinity National Recreation Area. The campground was managed by the Shasta-Trinity National Forest and offered a rustic camping experience near the cold, clear waters of Lewiston Lake.

The campground has been permanently closed by the U.S. Forest Service. All facilities have been decommissioned, including water systems and restrooms. The site is no longer available for overnight camping.

Campers seeking alternatives in the Lewiston Lake area can consider nearby campgrounds such as Mary Smith Campground, Ackerman Campground, or Cooper Gulch Campground, which remain operational within the Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

location.directions: From Weaverville, take Highway 3 north for 7 miles. Turn right on Rush Creek Road and continue for 9 miles. Then, turn left on Trinity Dam Boulevard for 6.25 miles; the campground is located on the left side of the road.

payload.name: J R Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The access road is being decommissioned.
payload.short_description: J R Campground in Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest is permanently closed. The access road is being decommissioned.
payload.medium_description: J R Campground was a small primitive campground with 8 sites along the Chiwawa River in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest. The site has been permanently closed and the access road is being decommissioned.
payload.long_description:
J R Campground was a small, primitive Forest Service campground located along the scenic Chiwawa River in the Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, approximately 21 miles from Fish Lake. The campground featured 8 first-come, first-served campsites set in a valley floor surrounded by the forested terrain of the Cascade Mountains.

The campground has been permanently closed by the U.S. Forest Service. The access road leading to the site is being decommissioned, meaning this closure is not seasonal or temporary. Campers should seek alternative campgrounds in the Wenatchee River Ranger District.

location.directions: J R Campground is located off SR Hwy 20 near Twisp, WA. However, the site is permanently closed, and the access road is scheduled for decommissioning.

payload.name: Bungalow Camp
payload.status_description: This appears to be a historic site rather than an active developed campground. The area may offer dispersed camping under standard National Forest regulations. Forest Road 250 access is seasonal and may be blocked by snow. Check current road conditions with the North Fork Ranger District before traveling.
payload.short_description: Historic site near the Bungalow Ranger Station on the North Fork Clearwater River in remote Clearwater County, Idaho. Dispersed camping may be available in the area.
payload.medium_description: Bungalow Camp is located near the historic Bungalow Ranger Station site along Forest Service Road 250, approximately 45 miles northeast of Pierce, Idaho. The area sits along the North Fork Clearwater River in a remote section of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. This was originally a Civilian Conservation Corps camp (F-193) established in 1936. While not a developed campground with designated sites, the area offers dispersed camping opportunities typical of National Forest lands.
payload.long_description:
Bungalow Camp refers to the area surrounding the historic Bungalow Ranger Station site on the North Fork Clearwater River in Clearwater County, Idaho. Originally established as a Civilian Conservation Corps camp (designated F-193, Company 603) in 1936, this remote location served as an important administrative and work site during the CCC era. The historic ranger station is now used primarily as a landmark for navigation along Forest Service Road 250.

The area sits within the North Fork Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests, surrounded by rugged mountain terrain and dense forests. The North Fork Clearwater River offers excellent fishing and class III-IV whitewater opportunities. Access is via FSR 250, a gravel road that continues northeast from Pierce toward Superior, Montana. Road conditions are highly seasonal, with snow blocking access from late fall through late spring.

This is not a developed campground with designated sites or maintained facilities. Dispersed camping may be available in the general area under standard National Forest regulations, including a 14-day stay limit. Campers should be fully self-sufficient and prepared for primitive backcountry conditions.

location.directions: From Pierce, Idaho, take Forest Service Road 250 northeast approximately 45 miles. The historic Bungalow Ranger Station site is located after crossing the North Fork of the Clearwater River. The road is gravel and conditions vary seasonally.

payload.name: Roman Nose State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Boecher Lake Dam has a sink hole causing the dam to erode, resulting in no water activities on Boecher Lake or Lake Watonga until further notice. The dam and trailhead at Two Lakes Campground are closed. Trails accessible only from the lodge. All campgrounds remain operational.
payload.short_description: Oklahoma state park campground featuring multiple camping areas with full hookups, pull-through sites for large RVs, equestrian facilities, comfort stations with showers, and easy access to canyon trails and natural springs.
payload.medium_description: Roman Nose State Park offers 47 RV campsites across three distinct camping areas: Two Lakes (8 RV sites accommodating up to 55 feet), Canyon Vista (23 RV sites with full hookups and ADA accessible options), and Bitter Creek (5 pull-through sites popular with equestrians). Comfort stations provide modern restrooms and hot showers. The park is named after Cheyenne Chief Henry Roman Nose and sits in scenic gypsum canyons with natural springs.
payload.long_description:
Roman Nose State Park campground in northwest Oklahoma provides 47 designated RV sites and tent camping across three distinct areas. Two Lakes RV/Tent Area offers 8 modern RV sites with 50-amp electric service and pull-through parking, accommodating rigs up to 55 feet. Canyon Vista RV/Tent Area is the largest section with 23 RV sites, five of which feature full hookups (electric, water, sewer) and are ADA accessible. Bitter Creek RV/Tent Area caters to equestrians with pull-through sites for horse trailers, horse pen rentals, and 5 semi-modern RV sites with 50-amp service.

Comfort stations throughout the campgrounds provide modern restrooms, hot showers (token-operated), and drinking water. The dump station is located in Canyon Vista Campground near the boat ramp. Each site includes a stone picnic table, and fire pits are available. The park also offers 11 cabins and seasonal teepee rentals from April through October.

The park is currently affected by Boecher Lake Dam deterioration, which has closed water activities on both lakes until further notice. The dam and trailhead at Two Lakes Campground are closed, though trails remain accessible via the lodge. Despite lake closures, all campgrounds remain operational. Reservations are made through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system.

location.directions: Located 7 miles north of Watonga, Oklahoma on State Highway 8A. Address: 3236 St Hwy 8A, Watonga, OK 73772.

payload.name: TRIPOD POINT
payload.status_description: Closed for the winter season. Most Idaho Panhandle National Forest campgrounds operate seasonally from late spring through fall, typically closing when snow arrives.
payload.short_description: Remote campground in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests in Bonner County, Idaho.
payload.medium_description: Tripod Point is a campground located within the Idaho Panhandle National Forests in Bonner County. This area of northern Idaho offers access to the forests and mountains of the Idaho Panhandle region.
payload.long_description:
Tripod Point campground is situated in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests in Bonner County, Idaho. The Idaho Panhandle National Forests span across northern Idaho, offering visitors access to rugged mountain terrain, dense forests, and numerous recreational opportunities. The region is known for its natural beauty and remote wilderness character.

The campground's location in this area provides a base for exploring the surrounding national forest lands. Typical activities in the Idaho Panhandle National Forests include hiking, fishing, wildlife viewing, and berry picking during the summer and fall months. The forests are home to diverse wildlife and vegetation native to the northern Rocky Mountains.

location.directions: Tripod Point is accessible by boat or hiking. From Beaver Creek Campground, travel approximately 5 miles east along the northwest shoreline of Priest Lake. The site is located near the shoreline and is marked accordingly.

payload.name: New River Campground
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely. The campground was temporarily closed approximately 20 years ago and has never reopened. No facilities are maintained.
payload.short_description: Former USFS campground in Mount Rogers National Recreation Area that has been closed for approximately two decades and remains non-operational.
payload.medium_description: New River Campground is a former Forest Service campground in the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area of Jefferson National Forest. The site was temporarily closed around 2005 and has never reopened. It is no longer maintained and has been withdrawn from the Virginia Bird & Wildlife Trail. No facilities are available.
payload.long_description:
New River Campground was once an established campground within the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area, part of the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests in Carroll County, Virginia. The campground was temporarily closed approximately 20 years ago and has never been restored to operational status.

The site currently has no maintained facilities. There is no potable water, no restrooms, and no active camping infrastructure. The Forest Service does not list New River Campground among its active recreation sites in the Mount Rogers area. The Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources has also withdrawn the site from the Virginia Bird & Wildlife Trail program.

Campers seeking overnight options in the Mount Rogers area should consider nearby active campgrounds such as Grindstone Recreation Area, Hurricane Campground, Beartree Recreation Area, or Comers Rock Recreation Area.

location.directions: From Jefferson, take US 221/Hwy 16 N for 4.7 miles to Tom Fowler Rd. Turn right on Tom Fowler Rd and go 1.3 miles to Old US 221, turn left for 2.6 miles to the park entrance on the right at 358 New River State Park Road, Laurel Springs, NC. The park also has access points at Wagoner Access Road and Kings Creek Road.

links.title: Virginia DWR - New River Campground Area

payload.name: Devore Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come-first-served. No reservations. Campfire permit required. Adventure Pass or Interagency Pass required for trailhead parking at Red Box Saddle.
payload.short_description: Remote backcountry trail camp with six shaded sites along the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail, accessible only via a 5.5-mile hike from Red Box Saddle in the San Gabriel Mountains.
payload.medium_description: Devore Trail Camp is a primitive hike-in campground nestled at 3,000 feet elevation along the Gabrielino National Recreation Trail in the San Gabriel Mountains. The camp offers six spacious, tree-shaded sites near a seasonal creek, each equipped with a picnic table and fire ring. Accessible only by a moderately strenuous 5.5-mile hike from Red Box Saddle, this free, first-come-first-served facility requires complete self-sufficiency as there are no toilets, potable water, or trash services.
payload.long_description:
Devore Trail Camp is a secluded backcountry destination for hikers seeking solitude in the San Gabriel Mountains National Monument. Situated at approximately 3,000 feet along the historic Gabrielino National Recreation Trail, the camp provides six well-spaced sites beneath a canopy of oaks and conifers near a small seasonal stream. Each site features a picnic table and fire ring, making it suitable for overnight backpacking trips.

Access requires parking at Red Box Saddle (approximately 14 miles up Angeles Crest Highway from Interstate 210 in La Cañada Flintridge) and hiking 5.5 miles on the Gabrielino Trail. The trail descends through mixed chaparral and riparian corridors, losing roughly 1,500 feet of elevation on the way in. The camp is also accessible via longer routes from JPL/Arroyo Seco to the south.

This is a true primitive backcountry camp with no toilets, no potable water, and no trash collection. Campers must pack out all waste and bring adequate water supplies. A California Campfire Permit is required for any stove or campfire use, and an Adventure Pass or Interagency Pass is required for vehicles parked at Red Box trailhead.

location.directions: From Interstate 210 in La Cañada Flintridge, take Angeles Crest Highway (Highway 2) approximately 14 miles to Red Box Saddle. Park at the Red Box parking area (Adventure Pass required) and follow the Gabrielino Trail 5.5 miles downhill to the campground.

payload.name: Elk Flat Spring Campground
payload.status_description: Closed indefinitely due to wildfire damage. No reopening date announced.
payload.short_description: Small primitive campground in Malheur National Forest, currently closed indefinitely due to wildfire damage.
payload.medium_description: Elk Flat Spring Campground is a primitive, no-fee campground in Malheur National Forest in Baker County, Oregon. The site was burned over by wildfire and remains closed indefinitely. No official reopening date has been announced.
payload.long_description:
Elk Flat Spring Campground is a primitive dispersed camping area located in Malheur National Forest in eastern Oregon's Baker County. The campground was damaged by wildfire and has been closed to camping.

As a result of the fire damage, the campground is not currently operational. There is no official information available regarding restoration or reopening plans. Campers seeking alternatives should consider other developed campgrounds in the Malheur National Forest such as Elk Creek Campground, Billy Fields Campground, or Dixie Campground.

location.directions: From Highway 22 at Detroit, Oregon, turn onto Breitenbush Road (FSR 46). Proceed 4.4 miles, turn left onto FS Road 4696. Proceed 0.8 miles, turn left on FS Road 4697. Follow FS Road 4697 for 4.5 miles and turn left at an unmarked junction (still FS Road 4697), continue 2.1 miles to a small spur road located at west end of Elk Lake (FS Road 390). The camping area is about 0.3 miles ahead. CAUTION: FS Road 4697 is not maintained for the last 4 miles into Elk Lake. Access by low-clearance vehicles and trailers not recommended as the road is rough and rocky.

payload.name: Wiggins Day Use Area
payload.status_description: This is a day-use only area with no overnight camping. No restrooms or drinking water are available. Visitors must bring their own water and pack out all trash.
payload.short_description: Small day-use fishing pond in Osceola National Forest offering primitive shoreline fishing and picnicking with no facilities.
payload.medium_description: Wiggins Day Use Area is a 2-acre fishing pond in the Osceola National Forest near Lake City, Florida. This primitive day-use site offers shoreline fishing and picnicking opportunities but has no restrooms or potable water. Visitors should bring all supplies including drinking water.
payload.long_description:
Wiggins Day Use Area is a small recreation site in the Osceola National Forest featuring a 2-acre constructed pond for fishing. Like other borrow pit ponds throughout the forest, water levels can vary with seasonal conditions, and access may be limited by unimproved roads that become muddy after rain.

This is a day-use only facility with no overnight camping permitted. The site offers basic picnicking opportunities along with shoreline fishing. A Florida fishing license is required. There are no restrooms or potable water available, so visitors must be self-sufficient and pack out all trash.

location.directions: Located on CR 250 approximately 1/2 mile west of the intersection with FR 215 in Osceola National Forest.

payload.name: Alabaster Caverns State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. The campground remains operational even when the cave is closed during winter months. Reservations can be made 1 day to 11 months in advance through Oklahoma State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Oklahoma state park campground at the world's largest natural gypsum cave open to the public, featuring RV sites with hookups and primitive tent camping.
payload.medium_description: Alabaster Caverns State Park campground offers 11 semi-modern RV sites with electric and water hookups on level concrete pads, plus two remote primitive tent sites. The Mesa Campground sits near a comfort station with hot-water pay showers and modern restrooms. Open year-round, the park provides access to guided tours of the rare alabaster cavern and miles of hiking trails through rugged gypsum formations.
payload.long_description:
Alabaster Caverns State Park is home to the largest natural gypsum cave in the world that is open to the public and the only gypsum show cave in the United States. The 200-acre park in northwestern Oklahoma offers camping that serves as an excellent base for exploring this geological wonder. The cavern features massive alabaster formations and is home to five species of bats.

The Mesa Campground contains 11 semi-modern sites with 30-amp electric and water hookups. Sites 1 through 9 occupy a tree-lined loop with level concrete pads and asphalt approaches. Site 10 is completely surrounded by trees for added privacy. One ADA-accessible pull-through site with 50-amp service is available. Each site includes a picnic table and outdoor grill. Two remote primitive tent sites offer a more secluded experience for tent campers seeking solitude.

The comfort station near the campground provides modern restrooms and hot-water pay showers. An RV dump station is located a short distance down the road. Additional park amenities include a children's playground with rock climbing wall, group picnic area, amphitheater, horseshoe pit, and volleyball court. Guided cavern tours run hourly from 9am to 4pm daily, and unique cave camping experiences in Water Cave are available by reservation.

location.directions: From Freedom, Oklahoma: 6 miles south on Highway 50, then 1/2 mile east on Highway 50A. From Mooreland, Oklahoma: 20 miles north on Highway 50.

payload.name: Fishers Landing
payload.status_description: The site is currently closed due to damage from Hurricane Florence. This is a day-use only area; overnight camping is not permitted. No reopening date has been announced.
payload.short_description: Day-use recreation area on the Neuse River in Croatan National Forest offering fishing and picnicking. Not an overnight camping facility.
payload.medium_description: Fishers Landing is a day-use recreation area located on the Neuse River approximately 8 miles south of New Bern in the Croatan National Forest. The site offers river and stream fishing along with picnicking opportunities. This is not an overnight camping facility.
payload.long_description:
Fishers Landing is a day-use recreation area situated on the Neuse River within the Croatan National Forest, approximately 8 miles south of New Bern, North Carolina. The site provides access for river and stream fishing as well as picnicking.

This is a day-use only facility and does not permit overnight camping. The site has historically been a free-access area managed by the Croatan Ranger District.

The site suffered damage from Hurricane Florence and has remained closed for repairs. Visitors seeking overnight camping in the Croatan National Forest should consider nearby options such as Flanners Beach Recreation Area.

location.directions: From New Bern, take US 70 East for approximately 8-10 miles to reach Fishers Landing on the Neuse River.

payload.name: Pine Springs Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground operates May 1 through October 31 on a first-come-first-served basis. No reservations accepted. An Adventure Pass or $5 overnight fee is required per vehicle.
payload.short_description: Remote 12-site campground in Los Padres National Forest at 5,800 ft elevation, shaded by pinyon pines with vault toilets but no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Pine Springs Campground is a primitive, first-come-first-served campground in the Mt. Pinos Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. The 12-site loop sits at 5,800 feet elevation amid pinyon pine woodland. Each site has a picnic table and fire ring. Vault toilets are available but there is no potable water, so campers must be fully self-sufficient.
payload.long_description:
Pine Springs Campground offers a quiet, primitive camping experience in the Mt. Pinos Ranger District of Los Padres National Forest. Located at 5,800 feet elevation, the campground features 12 sites arranged in a loop beneath shady pinyon pine trees. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring for campfires when permitted.

This is a pack-it-in, pack-it-out style campground with no potable water available. A vault toilet provides the only facility. Campers should arrive fully self-sufficient with all water and supplies needed for their stay. The campground operates on a first-come-first-served basis with no reservations. An Adventure Pass, America the Beautiful Pass, or $5 overnight fee is required.

Access is via Grade Valley Road (FS 7N03), approximately three miles south of the Lockwood Valley/Grade Valley Road junction. The campground is seasonally closed from November 1 through April 30 due to winter road conditions. Quiet hours are observed from 10 PM to 6 AM.

location.directions: Take Grade Valley Road (FS 7N03) approximately three miles south of the Lockwood Valley/Grade Valley Road junction.

payload.name: Mountain View Group Campground
payload.status_description: This site is closed and does not appear in current Forest Service campground listings. The USFS indicates it is not operating as a group campground.
payload.short_description: A closed site in Gifford Pinchot National Forest near Mt. Adams; no longer operating as a campground.
payload.medium_description: Mountain View Group Campground is listed as a closed site within Gifford Pinchot National Forest. According to USFS records, this location is not currently operating as a group campground and the site is closed to public use.
payload.long_description: Mountain View Group Campground is located in the Gifford Pinchot National Forest in Skamania County, Washington. However, official USFS records indicate that this site is currently closed and is not functioning as a group campground. The site does not appear in the active reservation system and no fees are associated with it, suggesting it has been decommissioned or is indefinitely closed. Gifford Pinchot National Forest offers numerous other established campgrounds throughout its 1.3 million acres, many of which provide both reservable and first-come, first-served camping options during their operating seasons.

location.directions: From Kettle Falls, WA: Head west on US-395 N for approximately 3.7 miles. Turn left onto WA-20 W for 5.2 miles. Turn right onto Trout Lake Rd (Forest Road 020) and continue for 5.1 miles to Trout Lake.

payload.name: Whiterocks
payload.status_description: Open for the season. The campground typically operates from mid-May through late November, weather and conditions permitting. First-come, first-served only; no reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Primitive forest campground at 7,500 feet elevation in scenic Whiterocks Canyon, offering fishing access along the Whiterocks River in Ashley National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Whiterocks Campground is a first-come, first-served campground located in the scenic Whiterocks Canyon of Ashley National Forest. At approximately 7,500 feet elevation, the 21-site campground offers vault toilets but no potable water. The campground provides access to fishing on the Whiterocks River and dramatic canyon cliff formations. Maximum RV length is 30 feet.
payload.long_description:
Whiterocks Campground sits at approximately 7,500 feet elevation within the striking Whiterocks Canyon in northeastern Utah's Ashley National Forest. The campground features 21 sites surrounded by the dramatic cliff formations that give the canyon its name. Vault toilets are available, but there is no potable water on site, so campers must bring their own supply.

The Whiterocks River runs through the area, providing fishing opportunities for anglers. OHV use is restricted to designated trails only. The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis at $8 per night for a single unit.

Access is via Forest Road 492 from the town of Whiterocks. The seasonal opening typically occurs around mid-May, with closure in late November depending on snow conditions. The campground accommodates RVs up to 30 feet in length.

location.directions: From Whiterocks, Utah, travel 7 miles north on County Road, turn east at the sign for 2.5 miles, then north on Forest Road 492 for 5.25 miles.

payload.name: Fort Cobb State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system and must be made at least 1 day ahead of arrival.
payload.short_description: Lakeside state park campground on Fort Cobb Lake offering nearly 400 campsites with water/electric hookups, primitive tent sites, comfort stations with showers, and easy access to boating and fishing.
payload.medium_description: Fort Cobb State Park sprawls across 1,872 acres along the shores of 4,100-acre Fort Cobb Lake in southwest Oklahoma. The park offers nearly 400 campsites ranging from full-hookup RV sites to primitive tent camping, spread across multiple coves including Sunset Cove, Eagle's Nest Cove, and Deer Run Cove. Amenities include comfort stations with showers, a dump station, marina, swimming beach, and an 18-hole golf course.
payload.long_description:
Fort Cobb State Park sits on the western shores of Fort Cobb Lake, a 4,100-acre reservoir in Caddo County that draws anglers targeting bass, catfish, and crappie. The 1,872-acre park offers camping spread across multiple coves, with sites ranging from full-hookup RV pads to primitive tent spots near the water.

The park's five camping areas include Sunset Cove, Eagle's Nest Cove, White Catfish Cove, Blackjack Cove, and Deer Run Cove. Modern RV sites feature water and electric hookups, while 34 sites offer full hookups including sewer. Eagle's Nest Cove has pull-through sites for larger rigs. Each area has comfort stations with flush toilets, and showers are available (coin-operated, approximately $1.50 for seven minutes). A dump station is located near the park office.

Beyond camping, the park offers a marina with boat rentals, a swimming beach, picnic pavilions, playgrounds, a nature center, and an 18-hole golf course. The enclosed Eagle's Nest shelter accommodates group gatherings with a full kitchen and fire ring. Kodiak Pines Cabins provide an alternative for those seeking a roof overhead.

location.directions: From Anadarko, take State Highway 9 west, then turn north on State Highway 146 to the park entrance.

payload.name: Osage Hills State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Water to RV sites is shut off from November 1 through April 1. Reservations required for all tent and RV sites via the Oklahoma State Parks online system.
payload.short_description: Historic Oklahoma state park campground offering RV and tent sites amid 1,100 acres of oak-covered hills, native stone CCC cabins, and Lookout Lake fishing in the heart of the Osage Nation.
payload.medium_description: Osage Hills State Park features a mix of RV sites with water and electric hookups, designated tent camping areas on elevated terrain, and eight 1930s CCC-built stone cabins. The campground includes modern bathhouses with showers, a dump station, playground, swimming pool, and fishing access at Lookout Lake. Located 11 miles west of Bartlesville, the park spans 1,100 acres of wooded bluffs and prairie.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the rolling oak hills of Osage County, Osage Hills State Park preserves 1,100 acres of northeastern Oklahoma terrain that includes rocky bluffs, lush forests, and Sand Creek winding through its southern reaches. The Civilian Conservation Corps constructed the park's distinctive native stone cabins and structures in the 1930s, giving the property historic character alongside its natural appeal.

The campground offers 20 RV sites equipped with water and 30/50-amp electric hookups, plus over 20 designated tent sites positioned on higher ground with fire rings and lantern poles. Eight stone cabins feature central heat and air, fireplaces, and full kitchen facilities. Modern bathhouses with showers serve the camping areas, and a dump station is available for RV waste disposal.

Lookout Lake provides fishing for bass, crappie, catfish, and perch, while hiking and mountain biking trails wind through the property. Other facilities include a swimming pool, tennis courts, basketball and volleyball courts, and a playground. The group camp accommodates up to 118 guests across nine bunkhouses.

location.directions: 11 miles west of Bartlesville on Highway 60 from Highway 123

payload.name: Deep Creek Campground -f
payload.status_description: Permanently closed. The USFS has decommissioned this site and it is no longer an active campground. Vehicle access has been destroyed by storm damage.
payload.short_description: Deep Creek Campground in Shasta-Trinity National Forest is permanently closed and no longer operates as a camping facility.
payload.medium_description: Deep Creek Campground, a former primitive campground in Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County, California, is permanently closed. The site had no water or restroom facilities even when operational, and vehicle access has been destroyed by storm damage.
payload.long_description:
Deep Creek Campground was a primitive camping area located in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest in Shasta County, California. The campground has been permanently closed by the USFS and is no longer an active recreation site.

Even when the campground was operational, it offered only basic primitive camping with no water, no restrooms, and no fees. The area's high elevation meant it typically only operated during a short summer season, generally from around July 4 through late October.

The access road to the campground has been destroyed by storm damage, and the Forest Service has marked it as permanently closed. The campground is no longer listed among active camping facilities in the Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

location.directions: Big Bend Campground is located 3 miles up Poole Power Plant Road off Highway 120 in Lee Vining Canyon. The final section of the access road is well-graded dirt. Follow signs for Lee Vining Creek to reach the campground, nestled among a mature conifer forest.

payload.name: Honey Creek State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. All campsites require online reservations through the Oklahoma State Parks reservation system. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance. Generator use prohibited between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Lakeside Oklahoma state park campground on Grand Lake featuring 206 campsites, full hookups, boat ramp, swimming pool, and fishing access.
payload.medium_description: Honey Creek State Park occupies 38 acres on the shore of Grand Lake near Grove, Oklahoma. The campground offers 52 semi-modern RV sites with 30/50 amp electric hookups and 150 primitive tent sites. Amenities include comfort stations with showers, two dump stations, a lighted boat ramp, courtesy fishing dock, fish cleaning station, playground, and a seasonal swimming pool open Memorial Day through late August.
payload.long_description:
Honey Creek State Park sits on the western shore of Grand Lake O' the Cherokees in northeastern Oklahoma. The 38-acre park provides direct access to 46,300-acre Grand Lake, one of Oklahoma's premier fishing and boating destinations known for largemouth bass, catfish, crappie, and sunfish. The campground is divided into two areas: Raccoon Ridge offers electric hookups with picnic tables and fire pits, while Squirrel Hollow is situated closer to the boat launch and fishing dock.

The park features 52 semi-modern RV sites with 30 and 50 amp electric service, plus 150 primitive tent camping sites. Paved interior roads and RV pads make navigation easy. Four comfort stations with showers are distributed throughout the campground, and two RV dump stations are available. Recreation options include a seasonal outdoor swimming pool, basketball court, playground, two covered group shelters with outdoor grills, and a lighted boat ramp with courtesy dock for loading and unloading.

location.directions: South of Grove, off of Highway 59. Address: 901 State Park Rd, Grove, OK 74344.

links.title: Honey Creek Area at Grand Lake State Park - TravelOK

payload.name: Dutch Creek Guard Sta
payload.status_description: This site has been permanently decommissioned due to wildfire damage and is no longer available for public use.
payload.short_description: Former Forest Service guard station cabin in Boise National Forest that has been permanently decommissioned following wildfire damage.
payload.medium_description: Dutch Creek Guard Station was a historic Forest Service rental cabin located along the Middle Fork of the Boise River in a remote section of Boise National Forest. The cabin was decommissioned after sustaining wildfire damage and is no longer available for public use.
payload.long_description:
Dutch Creek Guard Station was a historic Forest Service guard station situated in an open meadow overlooking the Middle Fork Boise River near its confluence with Dutch Creek. The remote cabin was accessible via Forest Road 268, approximately 49 miles from Highway 21.

The guard station previously offered rustic accommodations including vault toilet facilities but no potable drinking water. The site provided access to fishing opportunities in the Middle Fork of the Boise River and hiking on Trail 047 toward the Hot Creek and Lake areas. A natural hot springs was located about 3 miles west of the cabin along FR 268.

The facility has been permanently decommissioned following wildfire damage and is no longer available for overnight stays or recreational use.

location.directions: From Boise, travel north on Highway 21, then turn right on Forest Road 268 and continue approximately 49 miles.

payload.name: Shoemaker Bay Overlook Shelter Site
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. No reservations required and no fee. Campers must bring their own potable water.
payload.short_description: Free-use backcountry shelter on Wrangell Island offering scenic views of Zimovia Strait and Shoemaker Bay, accessible via 3.5 to 5.2 mile hikes.
payload.medium_description: The Shoemaker Bay Overlook Shelter is a free-use backcountry shelter located at the end of the Institute Creek Trail in the North Wrangell trail system on Wrangell Island. The shelter provides excellent views of Zimovia Strait, Shoemaker Bay, and surrounding islands. Access requires hiking 3.5 miles from the Rainbow Falls Trailhead or 5.2 miles from the North Wrangell Trailhead.
payload.long_description:
The Shoemaker Bay Overlook Shelter is a primitive free-use shelter located in the Tongass National Forest on Wrangell Island, Alaska. Situated at the terminus of the Institute Creek Trail, the shelter offers stunning panoramic views of Zimovia Strait, Shoemaker Bay, and the surrounding islands. This backcountry destination provides opportunities for overnight or multi-night trips in a remote alpine setting.

Access to the shelter requires a moderate to strenuous hike. The shorter route covers 3.5 miles from the Rainbow Falls Trailhead via the Rainbow Falls Trail connecting to the Institute Creek Trail. The longer option spans 5.2 miles from the North Wrangell Trailhead on the Spur Road Extension via the North Wrangell Trail system. The area offers cross-country skiing and snowshoeing opportunities during winter months.

Facilities are minimal, consisting of a basic shelter structure and an outhouse. Campers must bring all potable water and be prepared for backcountry conditions. No reservations are required and there is no fee to use the shelter.

location.directions: Option 1: 3.5 miles from the Rainbow Falls Trailhead via Rainbow Falls Trail to Institute Creek Trail. Option 2: 5.2 miles from the North Wrangell Trailhead on the Spur Road Extension via the North Wrangell Trail to Institute Creek Trail. The shelter is at the end of the Institute Creek Trail.

payload.name: Devils Canyon Campground
payload.status_description: This campground has been permanently decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service and is no longer available for camping.
payload.short_description: Devils Canyon Campground in Tonto National Forest near Superior, Arizona has been decommissioned and is no longer available for overnight camping.
payload.medium_description: Devils Canyon Campground was a developed campground located in the Tonto National Forest near Superior, Arizona. The site has been decommissioned by the U.S. Forest Service and is no longer available for camping. The nearby Oak Flat Campground remains an alternative for visitors seeking camping in this area of the Pinal Mountains.
payload.long_description:
Devils Canyon Campground was once a developed camping facility in the Tonto National Forest, situated in the scenic terrain near Superior, Arizona in Pinal County. The campground provided access to the Devils Canyon area, known for its rugged desert landscape and proximity to hiking opportunities.

The U.S. Forest Service has permanently decommissioned this campground, and it is no longer maintained or available for overnight use. The site does not appear on current USFS recreation listings or Recreation.gov. Visitors looking for camping in this region should consider nearby alternatives such as Oak Flat Campground in the Tonto National Forest.

location.directions: The former campground was located near Devils Canyon, approximately 4 miles east of Superior, Arizona, in the Tonto National Forest. The area is accessed via Highway 60 and Forest Road 469.

payload.name: PINE STRIKE
payload.status_description: The campground is currently open for reservations and offers 28 campsites accommodating tents, trailers, and RVs up to 40 feet.
payload.short_description: Pine Strike is a campground located in Pike National Forest in Park County, Colorado.
payload.medium_description: Pine Point Campground, located next to Vallecito Reservoir in southwestern Colorado, offers 28 campsites with scenic mountain views and access to various recreational activities.
payload.long_description: Pine Point Campground is situated next to Vallecito Reservoir in southwestern Colorado, offering 28 campsites with picturesque views of the surrounding mountains. The campground accommodates tents, trailers, and RVs up to 40 feet. Each site is equipped with a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. Amenities include drinking water, vault toilets, and trash collection. Firewood is available for purchase from the camp host. The nearest boat ramp is on the west side of the lake. Generators are permitted from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Cell service is fair in the area. Vallecito Reservoir provides opportunities for fishing, boating, canoeing, and kayaking. Nearby activities include hiking, mountain biking, horseback riding, picnicking, and wildlife viewing.

location.directions: From Bayfield, Colorado, turn north on County Road 501 for about 13 miles to the Vallecito area. Turn right on County Road 501A and travel almost 4 miles to the campground, which is located on the left side of the road.

payload.name: Detroit State Park
payload.status_description: Open year-round for camping. Reservations available up to six months in advance through Oregon State Parks. Note: The park is within Marion County's emerald ash borer quarantine zone; ash, olive, and white fringe tree firewood must remain within the county.
payload.short_description: Large state park campground on Detroit Lake in Oregon's Cascade Mountains with nearly 300 sites including full-hookup RV sites, electrical sites, and tent camping.
payload.medium_description: Detroit Lake State Recreation Area offers nearly 300 campsites along the shores of a scenic nine-mile reservoir in the Cascade Mountains. The campground features full-hookup sites, electrical sites with water, and tent sites, plus flush toilets, hot showers, and a visitor center with firewood and supplies. Popular activities include fishing, boating, swimming, and water skiing on the forest-ringed lake.
payload.long_description:
Detroit Lake State Recreation Area sits on the shore of a nine-mile-long reservoir nestled in a forested canyon of the Cascade Mountains in Marion County, Oregon. The campground offers nearly 300 sites spread across various configurations: 107 full-hookup sites for RVs, 68 electrical sites with water, 96 tent sites with water nearby, and 6 mini cabins that sleep up to three guests each.

The park provides excellent facilities including flush toilets, hot showers, and a visitor center that sells firewood, ice, soft drinks, and souvenirs. Recreational amenities include horseshoe pits, a basketball court, volleyball area, playground, two courtesy boat ramps, two reservable boat moorages, and a fishing dock. Eight campsites are ADA-accessible.

Detroit Lake is a premier destination for water recreation including fishing, boating, swimming, and water skiing. The surrounding Willamette National Forest offers additional hiking and outdoor opportunities. Reservations can be made up to six months in advance through Oregon State Parks.

location.directions: From Detroit, Oregon, travel east on State Highway 22 for 2.7 miles to Blowout Road/Forest Service Road 10. Proceed on Blowout Road for 4.7 miles to the campground on the right.

links.title: Detroit Lake State Recreation Area - Oregon State Parks

payload.name: Crystal Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend. The cottage requires a one-week minimum stay from June 15 through Labor Day, with a 3-night minimum before and after that period. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: A 16-acre day-use state park on Crystal Lake in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom, featuring a historic CCC-era granite bathhouse, nearly a mile of sandy beach, swimming, and one lakefront cottage rental.
payload.medium_description: Crystal Lake State Park is a scenic day-use park in Barton, Vermont, established in 1942 and listed on the National Register of Historic Places. The park features nearly a mile of sandy shoreline with a marked swimming area, a historic granite bathhouse built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, approximately 80 picnic tables, 40 charcoal grills, play areas, and boat rentals. One lakefront cottage sleeping up to six is available for weekly rental during the operating season.
payload.long_description:
Crystal Lake State Park sits at the northwestern end of Crystal Lake in Barton, Vermont, within the scenic Northeast Kingdom region. This 16-acre day-use park was developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in the 1930s and completed in 1942, earning a place on the National Register of Historic Places in 2005. The centerpiece is a striking granite bathhouse featuring partly Modern design with rusticated stone, housing restrooms, changing areas, and a concession stand.

The park offers nearly a mile of sandy shoreline with a marked swimming area, making it a popular summer destination. Facilities include approximately 80 picnic tables scattered throughout the grounds, around 40 free-standing charcoal grills, play areas for children, and boat rentals including canoes. While there is no boat launch, personal boats are welcome on the lake.

Overnight accommodations consist of a single lakefront cottage that sleeps up to six guests. The cottage includes one bedroom with a double bed and bunk bed set, a sleeper sofa, a complete kitchen with toaster, microwave, coffee maker, cookware and dishes, a bathroom with shower, electric heat, a front porch, and a canoe for guest use. The cottage is located within the village of Barton rather than a remote setting. A one-week minimum stay applies from June 15 through Labor Day, with a 3-night minimum before and after that period.

location.directions: From I-91, take Exit 25 toward Barton. Follow US-5 north to Barton, then turn east onto Vermont Route 16 (Willoughby Lake Road). The park entrance is on Bellwater Avenue at 96 Bellwater Ave, Barton, VT 05822.

payload.name: Lava Butte Campground
payload.status_description: This campground does not currently exist. USFS records indicate it is a proposed campground that has not yet been developed. No facilities or camping is available at this location.
payload.short_description: A proposed campground along Tenmile Road in Giant Sequoia National Monument within Sequoia National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Lava Butte Campground is listed as a proposed Forest Service campground along Tenmile Road in the Giant Sequoia National Monument. No operational information, amenities, or reservation system currently exists for this site.
payload.long_description: Lava Butte Campground appears in Forest Service records as a proposed campground along Tenmile Road in Fresno County, within the Giant Sequoia National Monument boundaries of Sequoia National Forest. The campground does not appear to be operational or developed at this time. Tenmile Road provides access to the nearby Ten Mile Campground and connects to areas near Hume Lake, a popular recreation destination in the forest. The region features sequoia groves, mountain biking trails, and opportunities for hiking at elevations around 5,800 feet.

location.directions: The campground will be located along Tenmile Road.

payload.name: AMERICAN HOUSE OHV CAMP
payload.status_description: This campground is not listed in current USFS or Recreation.gov databases. Official status could not be confirmed. Contact the Feather River Ranger District at +1 (530) 534-6500 to verify whether this site is open and operational.
payload.short_description: Remote OHV staging camp in Plumas National Forest near the historic La Porte area, reportedly offering primitive camping for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts.
payload.medium_description: American House OHV Camp is a primitive camping area in Plumas National Forest designed for off-highway vehicle users. Located near La Porte in the western foothills of the northern Sierra Nevada, the site reportedly serves as a staging point for OHV trails in the region. The campground is not listed on Recreation.gov or current USFS campground directories, suggesting it may be an informal dispersed camping area or a site that operates outside the standard reservation system.
payload.long_description:
American House OHV Camp sits in Plumas National Forest near the historic gold mining settlement of La Porte in Yuba County, California. The area is characterized by mixed conifer forest typical of the western Sierra Nevada foothills at elevations around 4,000 feet.

The campground reportedly caters to off-highway vehicle enthusiasts seeking access to OHV trails in the Plumas and surrounding national forests. As with many primitive OHV staging areas in California national forests, facilities are expected to be minimal. The La Porte area has a network of forest roads and trails popular with OHV riders.

Important: This campground does not appear in official USFS or Recreation.gov listings as of May 2026. Campers should contact the Feather River Ranger District at the Plumas National Forest to confirm current status, access conditions, and any applicable restrictions before visiting.

location.directions: From Hwy 101, take the Santa Margarita exit, turning off at El Camino Real and across the railroad tracks at the east end of town on Estrada Avenue/Hwy 58. After 1.4 miles, Hwy 58 turns left, but continue straight on Pozo Road. Follow Pozo Road for almost 20 miles, through the town of Pozo, keeping right at the La Panza Road junction, until you reach the Avenales Ranch Road. Follow Avenales Ranch Road about 5 miles, through a gate (keep closed!) to the sign for American Canyon where you turn left and continue another 2 miles.

payload.name: Mount Philo State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Summit facilities are undergoing accessibility and sustainability improvements through August 2026; the summit shelter is not accepting new reservations during construction.
payload.short_description: Small campground at the base of Mount Philo offering 7 tent sites and 3 lean-tos with flush toilets, hot showers, and stunning views of Lake Champlain and the Adirondacks.
payload.medium_description: Mount Philo State Park Campground sits at the base of Vermont's oldest state park, providing intimate camping with breathtaking views of Lake Champlain Valley and New York's Adirondack Mountains. The 10-site campground features 7 tent sites and 3 rustic lean-tos, each with a fire ring and picnic table. Modern amenities include flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers. The summit is a short 10-minute hike from camp, making sunset viewing a popular activity.
payload.long_description:
Mount Philo State Park Campground offers a small, intimate camping experience at the base of Vermont's oldest state park in Charlotte, Vermont. The campground features 7 tent sites and 3 wooden lean-tos nestled in a wooded setting, each equipped with a fire ring and picnic table. From the campground, a short 10-minute hike leads to the 968-foot summit where panoramic views of the Lake Champlain Valley and New York's Adirondack Mountains await.

Facilities include restrooms with flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and coin-operated showers. Water spigots are available both in the campground and at the mountain summit. A rustic lodge that seats up to 60 people with electricity is available for group gatherings. The park welcomes leashed pets throughout.

Due to the steep grade and narrow width of the access road, recreational vehicles and trailers are not recommended for this campground. Most sites accommodate up to 8 people, though sites T02 and T04 are limited to 4 people. The campground operates seasonally from Memorial Day weekend through mid-October.

location.directions: From Burlington, take US-7 south approximately 12 miles to Charlotte. Turn right onto State Park Road and follow signs to Mount Philo State Park.

payload.name: Vernon Reservoir Campground
payload.status_description: Open. No potable water available; campers must bring their own. 16-day stay limit. Powerboats are prohibited on the reservoir.
payload.short_description: Primitive lakeside campground in the Stansbury Mountains offering fishing at Vernon Reservoir with vault toilets and no potable water.
payload.medium_description: Vernon Reservoir Campground is a primitive, open-setting camping area located in the Stansbury Mountains of the Uinta-Wasatch-Cache National Forest. Lake fishing is the primary draw, and the reservoir prohibits powerboats, keeping the area quiet. Campers must bring their own water as none is available on-site. Vault restrooms and picnic tables are provided.
payload.long_description:
Vernon Reservoir Campground sits at roughly 6,500 feet in the Stansbury Mountains, about 9 miles south of the town of Vernon via a dirt road off Highway 36. The reservoir is the centerpiece, providing fishing in a peaceful setting since powerboats are prohibited. The surrounding high desert terrain offers open views and solitude.

This is a primitive camping area with no modified facilities beyond vault restrooms and picnic tables. There is no potable water, hookups, or developed individual campsites. Campers should come prepared with their own water supply and be self-sufficient. A day use fee applies: $10 per vehicle for three days, $20 for seven days, or $60 for a season pass. Interagency Recreation Passes are honored. The area has a 16-day stay limit.

location.directions: From Highway 36, turn south at Vernon and travel 9 miles on a dirt road to the reservoir.

payload.name: SEGALE  CABIN
payload.status_description: Segale Cabin does not appear to be a public rental or campground. It may be a private recreation residence under the USFS Recreation Residence Program, which permits privately-owned cabins on National Forest land that are not available for public use.
payload.short_description: A Forest Service rental cabin located in Stanislaus National Forest in the Central Sierra Nevada, offering a rustic backcountry lodging experience in Tuolumne County.
payload.medium_description: Segale Cabin is a Forest Service rental cabin in Stanislaus National Forest, located in the Central Sierra Nevada mountains. The cabin provides rustic lodging in a remote forest setting at approximately 5,900 feet elevation, with access to hiking, fishing, and wilderness recreation.
payload.long_description:
Segale Cabin is a USFS rental cabin situated in Stanislaus National Forest at approximately 5,900 feet elevation. The cabin provides a remote lodging option for visitors exploring the nearly 900,000-acre Stanislaus National Forest, which features diverse terrain including alpine lakes, rivers, and extensive trail systems in California's Central Sierra Nevada. The cabin offers a backcountry experience while providing basic shelter in the forested mountain environment.

Stanislaus National Forest spans the western slope of the Sierra Nevada and contains 78 lakes, over 800 miles of streams and rivers, and more than 1,000 miles of trails. The forest provides year-round recreation opportunities including hiking, fishing, winter sports, and wildlife viewing. Access and conditions vary significantly by season, with winter snow potentially limiting accessibility.

payload.name: Cedar Camp Campground
payload.status_description: Permanently closed due to safety hazards from the 2018 Ranch Fire and 2020 August Complex. The access road (M5 Road) is blocked by slides. The campground will be decommissioned and is not expected to reopen.
payload.short_description: A primitive Forest Service campground in Mendocino National Forest, permanently closed due to fire damage from the 2018 Ranch Fire and 2020 August Complex and slated for decommissioning.
payload.medium_description: Cedar Camp Campground is a small, primitive campground located in a timber area of mature fir and pine at approximately 4,300 feet elevation in Mendocino National Forest. The campground is permanently closed due to safety hazards resulting from the 2018 Ranch Fire and 2020 August Complex fires, and the access road (M5 Road) is blocked by slides. The Forest Service has announced the campground will be decommissioned.
payload.long_description:
Cedar Camp Campground sits in a forested setting of mature fir and pine trees in the remote backcountry of Mendocino National Forest, approximately 19 miles southwest of Stonyford via Goat Mountain Road. At roughly 4,300 feet elevation, the campground historically offered a quiet, primitive camping experience for those seeking solitude in Northern California's Coast Range.

The campground is permanently closed and will not reopen. Fire damage from both the 2018 Ranch Fire and the massive 2020 August Complex has created safety hazards throughout the area, and mudslides have rendered the M5 Road impassable. The Forest Service has determined that the campground will be decommissioned rather than repaired.

When operational, the site offered vault toilets but no potable water, and access roads were not recommended for trailers. Campers seeking alternatives should contact the Mendocino National Forest Supervisor's Office for information about other campgrounds in the forest.
