location.directions: Located 19 miles southwest of Stonyford via Goat Mountain Road. Access up Trough Ridge or Little Stony Road is not recommended for trailers. Note: M5 Road is currently impassable due to slides.

payload.name: LONG LAKE SHELTER
payload.status_description: The shelter is available year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations are accepted. The 1.4-mile access trail is not routinely maintained and may be difficult to navigate.
payload.short_description: Remote three-sided USFS shelter at Long Lake near Behm Narrows, accessible by floatplane or boat and a 1.4-mile unmaintained trail from Cut Point.
payload.medium_description: Long Lake Shelter is a primitive three-sided Forest Service shelter located 45 air miles north of Ketchikan at Cut Point in Behm Narrows. Access requires floatplane or boat transportation to the trailhead, followed by a 1.4-mile hike. The trail is not routinely maintained and may be difficult to navigate. This is a backcountry shelter for self-sufficient visitors comfortable with remote wilderness conditions.
payload.long_description:
Long Lake Shelter is a remote three-sided Forest Service shelter situated at Long Lake in the Tongass National Forest, approximately 45 air miles north of Ketchikan. The shelter is accessed via floatplane or boat to Cut Point on the shore of Behm Narrows, then hiking the 1.4-mile Long Lake Trail to the shelter.

This is a primitive backcountry facility with no developed amenities. The trail is not routinely maintained by the Forest Service and may be challenging to navigate. Potable water is not available, and visitors must be fully self-sufficient, bringing all necessary supplies, drinking water, and safety equipment.

The area offers opportunities for day hiking, fishing, and experiencing the pristine wilderness of Southeast Alaska's temperate rainforest. Due to the remote location and lack of regular maintenance, this shelter is best suited for experienced backcountry travelers comfortable with navigation and wilderness self-reliance.

location.directions: Located 45 air miles north of Ketchikan at Cut Point in Behm Narrows. Access is by floatplane or boat to Cut Point, then hike the 1.4-mile Long Lake Trail to the shelter.

payload.name: Elmore State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance. Reservations made more than 7 days out require a two-night minimum; one-night stays are allowed within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Lakeside campground in Vermont's Green Mountains featuring 59 wooded sites and lean-tos along Lake Elmore, with a sandy swimming beach and trails to the summit of Elmore Mountain fire tower.
payload.medium_description: Elmore State Park offers 44 tent/RV campsites and 15 lean-tos set among hardwood forests along the shores of Lake Elmore in northern Vermont. The park features a large sandy beach for swimming, a historic CCC-built beach house with concessions, and hiking trails including a route to the Elmore Mountain fire tower with panoramic views of the Green Mountains. Boat rentals are available, and the campground provides flush toilets, hot showers, and potable water.
payload.long_description:
Nestled in the northern Green Mountains of Vermont, Elmore State Park surrounds the pristine waters of Lake Elmore in Lamoille County. The campground offers 44 tent/RV sites and 15 rustic lean-tos spread across wooded loops, with sites accommodating equipment up to 45 feet depending on location. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, and the campground provides flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, and potable water spigots throughout.

The centerpiece of the day-use area is a large sandy beach perfect for swimming, backed by a historic Civilian Conservation Corps-built beach house from the 1930s that houses bathrooms, changing rooms, and a concession stand. The park offers canoe, kayak, pedal boat, and paddleboard rentals for exploring the lake. Anglers can fish for bass, perch, and northern pike.

Hiking is a major draw, with trails leading to the summit of Elmore Mountain where a fire tower provides sweeping views of the surrounding peaks and valleys. The park also offers a playground, volleyball court, and horseshoe pit. An RV dump station is available, though no hookups are provided at individual sites.

location.directions: From the south: Take I-89 to exit 8, then follow VT Route 12 north to Lake Elmore. From the north: Take I-89 south to exit 10, follow VT Route 100 north, then continue on VT Route 12 south to the park.

payload.name: Mollys Falls Pond State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through September 6. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through Vermont State Parks. Day use hours are 10 AM to sunset.
payload.short_description: Remote paddle-in campground on a 411-acre reservoir in north-central Vermont with 8 boat-access-only sites featuring moldering toilets and fire rings.
payload.medium_description: Molly's Falls Pond State Park offers 8 remote campsites accessible only by boat on a scenic 411-acre reservoir near Cabot, Vermont. Each site includes a tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and moldering toilet. The park provides a paved boat launch on Vermont Route 2 and opportunities for fishing, paddling, and swimming from the shoreline.
payload.long_description:
Molly's Falls Pond State Park encompasses over 1,000 acres of forestland surrounding a 411-acre reservoir about 15 miles from Barre in north-central Vermont. The park's 8 remote campsites are accessible exclusively by boat, offering a true backcountry camping experience without the hike. Each site provides a tent pad, picnic table, fire ring, and nearby moldering toilet.

The reservoir supports excellent fishing for rainbow trout, brown trout, smallmouth bass, northern pike, pickerel, and yellow perch. A paved boat launch operated by Vermont Fish & Wildlife on Route 2 in Cabot provides lake access. Swimming is permitted from the shoreline but not at the boat launch. The park also features ten remote picnic sites and two fishing platforms.

Nearby Groton State Forest offers additional recreation, and the Groton Nature Center provides interpreter-led programs including night hikes, nature crafts, and campfire programs during the operating season.

location.directions: From Barre, head north on US-302 to Groton. Turn north onto Route 232, then west onto Vermont Route 2 toward Cabot. The paved boat launch is located on Route 2 in Cabot.

payload.name: Molly Stark State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from Friday, May 22 through Sunday, October 11. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Two-night minimum required for reservations made more than 7 days ahead; one-night stays permitted within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Wooded campground in southern Vermont with 23 tent/RV sites and 11 lean-tos, flush toilets, showers, dump station, and hiking access to Mt. Olga fire tower.
payload.medium_description: Molly Stark State Park Campground sits along the scenic Molly Stark Trail (Route 9) in Vermont's Green Mountains. The campground offers 35 sites across two loops: tent/RV sites accommodating up to 28 feet, tent-only sites, and classic three-sided lean-tos. Loop A has flush toilets with hot showers; Loop B has flush toilets with cold water. Firewood and ice are available on-site. The Mt. Olga fire tower trail provides panoramic views from the summit.
payload.long_description:
Molly Stark State Park Campground occupies a forested hillside along Vermont's Route 9, the historic Molly Stark Trail connecting Brattleboro to Bennington. The park is named for the wife of Revolutionary War General John Stark. Two camping loops offer a mix of 17 tent/RV sites, 6 tent-only sites, and 11 lean-tos spread through the hardwood and conifer forest. Most RV sites accommodate trailers up to 28 feet, though site dimensions vary.

Loop A features flush restrooms with hot and cold water plus token-operated showers. Loop B has flush restrooms with cold water only. An RV dump station is centrally located. Each campsite includes a fire ring and picnic table. Firewood and ice are sold on-site. The campground has no electric hookups.

The park's main attraction is the trail to the Mt. Olga fire tower, a moderate 1.6-mile round-trip hike to a restored tower with 360-degree views of the surrounding mountains. The day-use area includes a picnic pavilion, basketball and volleyball courts, and horseshoe pits. Pets are allowed on leash throughout the campground but not in the day-use area.

location.directions: Located on Route 9 (Molly Stark Trail) between Wilmington and Brattleboro in southern Vermont. The park entrance is approximately 3 miles east of Wilmington.

payload.name: Smugglers' Notch State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 15 through October 11. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through Vermont State Parks. Bears are active in the area; secure food and trash in vehicles or bear canisters.
payload.short_description: Historic Vermont campground at the base of Smugglers' Notch, featuring 34 wooded tent sites and lean-tos with flush toilets, hot showers, and access to dramatic 1,000-foot cliffs.
payload.medium_description: Smugglers' Notch State Park Campground sits at the base of the famous narrow pass through the Green Mountains, surrounded by 1,000-foot cliffs. The campground features 34 sites including tent-only, tent/RV, and lean-to options, most requiring short walks from parking. Historic CCC structures were relocated here in 2003. Facilities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, and drinking water throughout.
payload.long_description:
Smugglers' Notch State Park Campground occupies a stunning location at the base of one of Vermont's most dramatic mountain passes. The narrow, winding road through Smugglers' Notch is flanked by 1,000-foot cliffs and closes each winter due to snow. The campground itself was relocated in 2003, with historic Civilian Conservation Corps structures carefully moved and restored to preserve their Depression-era craftsmanship.

The 34-site campground includes 15 tent-only sites, 5 tent/RV sites, and 14 lean-tos spread through a forested setting that prioritizes privacy. Most sites are walk-in, requiring short carries from parking areas, though a handful accommodate RVs up to 28-34 feet depending on the site. Facilities include accessible flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, and drinking water spigots throughout the campground. Firewood and ice are available for purchase.

Bears are active in this park, so campers must secure all food and trash in vehicles or bear canisters. The location provides access to hiking and the dramatic scenery of the notch itself, making it a popular basecamp for exploring this corner of the Green Mountains.

location.directions: From Stowe, take Mountain Road (Route 108) north approximately 8 miles. The park entrance is on the left at 6443 Mountain Road, just before the road begins climbing into Smugglers' Notch.

links.title: VT Dept. of Forests, Parks and Recreation

payload.name: Townshend State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through September 6, 2026. The Bald Mountain Trail footbridge is temporarily closed due to flood damage. Reservations are available up to 11 months in advance through the Vermont State Parks reservation system with a two-night minimum for bookings made more than 7 days ahead.
payload.short_description: Vermont State Park campground nestled in the Townshend State Forest featuring 34 wooded tent and lean-to sites, including the only CCC-style tent platforms in the Vermont State Parks system.
payload.medium_description: Townshend State Park offers 34 campsites including 25 tent-only sites with distinctive CCC-era tent platforms, 5 tent/trailer sites, and 4 lean-tos. The campground features flush toilets, hot and cold running water, coin-operated showers, and the 1.7-mile Bald Mountain Trail leading to panoramic summit views. Swimming is available at the nearby Army Corps of Engineers Townshend Dam recreation area.
payload.long_description:
Townshend State Park is a historic Vermont campground set within the Townshend State Forest, distinguished by its Civilian Conservation Corps-era architecture including the only tent platforms of this style in the Vermont State Parks system. The 34-site campground offers a mix of tent-only sites, tent/trailer sites accommodating units up to 20 feet, and four rustic lean-tos scattered throughout the forested hillside.

The park centers on the 1.7-mile Bald Mountain Trail, a moderate hike ascending to the 1,680-foot summit with views of the West River valley and surrounding Green Mountains. Campers have access to flush toilets, hot and cold running water at spigots throughout the campground, and coin-operated showers. The day-use area includes a picnic shelter and basketball courts.

Swimming is not available within the state park itself but is accessible at the adjacent Townshend Lake Recreation Area operated by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, which also offers a boat ramp with a 10 HP motor limit. The campground operates seasonally from late May through early September.

location.directions: Located 19 miles north of Brattleboro on Route 30. Turn onto State Forest Road and continue 2.5 miles to the park entrance at 2755 State Forest Road, Townshend, VT 05353.

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Townshend Campground Details

payload.name: Story Spring Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served with no reservations. Stay limited to two consecutive nights. Hikers should avoid the trail during mud season from April through Memorial Day to protect trail conditions. Fire danger is currently low across the Manchester District.
payload.short_description: Backcountry three-sided shelter on the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, free and first-come, first-served.
payload.medium_description: Story Spring Shelter is a primitive Adirondack-style shelter located along the Appalachian Trail and coincident Long Trail in the Green Mountain National Forest. The shelter accommodates 6-10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations. A composting privy and water source requiring treatment are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Story Spring Shelter is a traditional three-sided Adirondack-style backcountry shelter situated on the Appalachian National Scenic Trail where it coincides with Vermont's Long Trail. Located in the Manchester Ranger District of the Green Mountain National Forest near Sunderland, the shelter provides overnight accommodations for long-distance hikers traveling through southern Vermont.

The shelter typically accommodates 6-10 people and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or advance reservations. Amenities are primitive: a composting privy is located nearby, and water is available from a spring source but must be filtered or treated before drinking. There is no potable water on site. Hikers should practice Leave No Trace principles and pack out all trash.

Access is by foot only via the Appalachian Trail south from Kelly Stand Road. The stay limit is two consecutive nights. Hikers are advised to avoid hiking during Vermont's mud season from April through Memorial Day weekend to protect fragile trail conditions.

location.directions: Hike the Appalachian Trail south from Kelly Stand Road.

address.full: 7916 Kelley Stand Rd, East Arlington, VT 05252

links.title: USFS Green Mountain NF Camping & Cabins
USFS Green Mountain NF Current Conditions

payload.name: O'BRIEN LOOP
payload.status_description: O'Brien Gulch is a day-use picnic area only. Overnight camping is not permitted at this location. For camping, use the established campgrounds in Eleven Mile Canyon (Cove, Riverside, Spillway, or Springer Gulch).
payload.short_description: O'Brien Gulch is a day-use picnic area in Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area in Pike National Forest, offering riverside recreation along the South Platte River.
payload.medium_description: O'Brien Gulch is one of four designated picnic areas within the Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area, managed by the U.S. Forest Service. Located along the South Platte River below Eleven Mile Reservoir dam, this day-use area provides scenic riverside recreation opportunities but does not offer overnight camping.
payload.long_description:
O'Brien Gulch is a day-use picnic area situated within the Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area in Pike National Forest, Park County, Colorado. The canyon lies below the dam of Eleven Mile Reservoir along the South Platte River, offering scenic views and family-friendly recreation.

As a picnic area, O'Brien Gulch is designated for day-use only. Overnight camping is not permitted at this location. Visitors seeking overnight accommodations should consider the four established campgrounds within the Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area: Cove, Riverside, Spillway, or Springer Gulch, all of which require reservations through Recreation.gov.

The Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area charges a one-time vehicle entry fee of $11 per stay, or visitors can purchase an annual pass for $100. Dispersed camping is prohibited within the canyon. The area is managed by the South Park Ranger District of Pike-San Isabel National Forests.

location.directions: From Lake George, Colorado, head west on County Road 96 into Eleven Mile Canyon. O'Brien Gulch is one of the designated picnic areas along the canyon road.

links.title: Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area - USFS

payload.name: Crosho Lake Camground
payload.status_description: Open for dispersed camping from approximately June through November, weather dependent. Winter access is by snowmobile only. The road to Crosho Lake requires high-clearance vehicles. No reservations or fees required.
payload.short_description: Free dispersed camping at a scenic high-altitude lake in the Little Flat Tops, popular for cutthroat trout and Arctic grayling fishing with non-motorized boating.
payload.medium_description: Crosho Lake offers 10 undeveloped dispersed camping spots overlooking the lake and Little Flat Tops in the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest. This free, lightly-used recreation area is popular for shore fishing, fly fishing, and non-motorized boating. Facilities are minimal with only a vault toilet available. High-clearance vehicles are required to access the rough road.
payload.long_description:
Crosho Lake Recreation Area provides primitive dispersed camping opportunities in a scenic mountain setting within the Medicine Bow-Routt National Forest. The area offers approximately 10 undeveloped campsites with views of the lake and the Little Flat Tops. This is a lightly-used destination that appeals to campers seeking solitude and a back-to-basics experience.

The lake is a popular destination for fishing, with Colorado River Cutthroat Trout and Arctic Grayling present in its waters. Anglers can fish from shore, wade, or use float tubes and small non-motorized boats such as canoes and kayaks. Motorized boats are prohibited.

Facilities are minimal at this dispersed camping area. There is one vault toilet, but no picnic tables, fire grates, or potable water. Campers should be fully self-sufficient and prepared to pack out all trash. Day-use parking is very limited. The access road requires a high-clearance vehicle due to rough conditions.

location.directions: From Yampa, proceed west/northwest on County Road 17 approximately 4 miles to County Road 15 (watch for sign pointing towards Crosho Lake). Turn left (west) on Road 15 and continue 6 miles to Crosho Lake. High-clearance vehicle required.

payload.name: Camp Plymouth State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open through October 11, 2026. Peak season runs May 22 through October 11. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through Vermont State Parks. Cottages require a one-week minimum stay from June 15 through Labor Day.
payload.short_description: Southern Vermont's most visited state park on Echo Lake, offering group camping with lean-tos, rental cottages, swimming, boating, and gold panning.
payload.medium_description: Camp Plymouth State Park sits on the eastern shore of Echo Lake in Plymouth, Vermont. The park specializes in group camping with six lean-tos and large tent sites, plus four rental cottages and pavilions. Visitors enjoy a sandy beach, swimming, boat rentals, paddleboarding, and the unique opportunity to pan for gold. The Vista Trail offers a moderate one-mile round-trip hike through white pine forest.
payload.long_description:
Camp Plymouth State Park occupies the eastern shore of Echo Lake in the historic town of Plymouth, Vermont. Originally a Boy Scout camp, the park has evolved into southern Vermont's most popular state park, drawing visitors with its combination of lakefront recreation and group camping facilities. The campground features six lean-tos in a dedicated group camping area, along with three group tenting sites that can accommodate up to 20 people each.

The park offers four fully furnished rental cottages with electricity, each accommodating up to six guests. For larger gatherings, indoor and outdoor pavilion spaces seat between 60 and 150 people and include electricity, stoves, refrigerators, sinks, and banquet furniture. A beachside concession stand serves visitors during the season.

Recreational opportunities extend beyond camping. Echo Lake provides swimming at a sandy beach, cartop boat launching, and rentals for boats and stand-up paddleboards. The park is one of the few places in Vermont where visitors can try gold panning. The Vista Trail winds one mile through white pine forest. Buffalo Brook runs through the property, adding to the natural setting.

location.directions: From Route 100, take Scout Camp Road (Town Highway 42) approximately one mile to the park entrance. The paved road bisects the property.

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Camp Plymouth Reservations
Vermont Dept of Forests, Parks and Recreation

payload.name: Coolidge State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 12. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance; bookings more than 7 days out require a two-night minimum.
payload.short_description: A rustic hillside campground in Vermont's Green Mountains featuring 35 lean-to sites with panoramic valley views, tent/RV sites, flush toilets, and hot showers.
payload.medium_description: Coolidge State Park offers 61 campsites nestled in the hills of Plymouth, Vermont within the Coolidge State Forest. The park is distinctive for having Vermont's largest collection of lean-to sites, many perched on hillsides with sweeping views of the Black River Valley and Green Mountains. Facilities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, potable water, a dump station, and a nature center.
payload.long_description:
Coolidge State Park sits at elevation in the hills above Plymouth, Vermont, within the 21,500-acre Coolidge State Forest. The campground is arranged across two loops containing 61 sites: 35 lean-tos, 17 tent/RV sites, 8 tent-only sites, and one walk-in lean-to. The park holds the distinction of having the most lean-to sites of any Vermont State Park, with several offering wide views across the Black River Valley to the peaks of the Green Mountains.

The steep, winding access road creates a secluded atmosphere but limits RV access to units 28 feet or shorter. Facilities include four restroom buildings with flush toilets and two with coin-operated hot showers. Potable water spigots are distributed throughout the campground, and an RV dump station is available though no hookups exist at individual sites. Each campsite has a fire ring and picnic table.

The park features hiking trails, a nature center, horseshoe pit, and a historic log picnic pavilion available for group rental. Cell service and Wi-Fi are available. The campground's elevation and forested setting provide cooler temperatures than valley campgrounds, making it popular during summer months.

location.directions: From Plymouth Union, travel north on Route 100A for approximately 3 miles. Turn right onto Coolidge State Park Road and continue 2.5 miles to the park entrance. The road is steep and narrow with sharp turns.

address.full: 855 Coolidge State Park Rd, Plymouth, VT 05056

payload.name: Knight Island State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from May 22 through September 6. Reservations required with a two-night minimum for bookings made more than 7 days in advance. Accessible by private boat only; there is no dock or ferry service.
payload.short_description: Remote island campground on Lake Champlain with seven rustic lean-to and tent sites accessible only by private boat, offering a true wilderness experience.
payload.medium_description: Knight Island State Park is a remote, boat-access-only campground in Lake Champlain's "inland sea" near North Hero, Vermont. The island features seven primitive campsites (six lean-tos and one tent site) spaced around a 2.5-mile shoreline connected by trails. Composting toilets are available but there is no potable water. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table, and campers must carry in and carry out all supplies and trash.
payload.long_description:
Knight Island State Park offers a true backcountry camping experience on a remote island in northern Lake Champlain, accessible only by private boat. The 185-acre island is one of three nearby island state parks (along with Burton Island and Woods Island) and provides a quiet, primitive escape from mainland crowds. Seven campsites are positioned around the island's 2.5-mile shoreline, each offering waterfront access and connected by hiking trails.

The campground features six lean-to shelters and one tent-only site, all requiring advance reservations with a two-night minimum for bookings made more than seven days ahead. Sites include fire rings and picnic tables. Composting toilets are available, but there is no potable water, showers, or trash service. Campers must bring all water and supplies and pack out all garbage. Pets are allowed but must be cleaned up after.

This is a destination for self-sufficient paddlers and boaters seeking solitude. There is no dock, so campers must beach their boats or anchor offshore. The island's trails, rocky shores, and forested interior provide opportunities for hiking and wildlife observation in a setting that feels genuinely remote despite being just a few miles from the mainland.

location.directions: Knight Island is located in northern Lake Champlain and can only be reached by private boat. The nearest mainland launch points are in North Hero and Grand Isle. GPS coordinates: 44.81033, -73.25742. There is no dock on the island.

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Knight Island Campground

payload.name: Woods Island State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground opens May 22, 2026 and operates through September 6, 2026. Reservations require a 2-night minimum if booked more than 7 days in advance; one-night stays are permitted within 7 days of arrival. Sites can be reserved up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis.
payload.short_description: Remote island campground on Lake Champlain accessible only by boat, featuring 5 primitive tent sites with composting toilets and fire rings amid peaceful island wilderness.
payload.medium_description: Woods Island State Park offers a secluded backcountry camping experience on a small island in Lake Champlain. The five remote tent sites are accessible only by private boat or water taxi, providing a quiet escape with hiking trails, swimming, and fishing. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table, with composting toilets nearby. Campers must bring all supplies including drinking water and pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Woods Island State Park sits in northern Lake Champlain near Burton Island, offering one of Vermont's most remote camping experiences. The 125-acre island features five primitive tent sites spread along the shoreline, each providing waterfront solitude accessible only by boat. A 2-mile interpretive loop trail circles the island through mixed forest, and the rocky shoreline offers excellent swimming and fishing opportunities.

This is true backcountry camping. There are no docks, so visitors must beach their boats or anchor offshore. The island has no potable water, electricity, or modern facilities. Each campsite includes a fire ring and picnic table, with composting outhouses serving the camping area. Campers must pack in all supplies and pack out all trash.

If you don't have your own boat, water taxi services operate from Grand Isle County. The remote setting rewards paddlers and boaters seeking a wilderness island experience within reach of Burlington.

location.directions: Woods Island is located in Lake Champlain approximately 2.5 miles from Burton Island. Access is by private boat or water taxi only. Water taxi services available from Grand Isle County include Capt. Mark Sperber at +1 (802) 234-1397 and St. Albans Bay Marina at +1 (802) 528-3111. There are no docks; beach your boat or anchor offshore.

links.title: Woods Island State Park - Vermont State Parks

payload.name: Wendover Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is scheduled to open June 6, 2026 after repairs from 2024 windstorm damage. Water systems have been turned on and tested. The typical operating season runs late May through early October.
payload.short_description: Riverside campground with 27 sites in a moss-covered pine forest along the Wild and Scenic Lochsa River on the Northwest Passage Scenic Byway at milepost 158.2.
payload.medium_description: Wendover Campground offers 27 campsites nestled in a mature, moss-covered pine forest along the Wild and Scenic Lochsa River. Each site features a paved driveway, picnic table, and fire ring. The campground accommodates RVs up to 40 feet and provides opportunities for fishing, hiking, wildlife viewing, and scenic driving on US Highway 12.
payload.long_description:
Wendover Campground is situated along the Wild and Scenic Lochsa River off the Northwest Passage Scenic Byway and All American Road (US Highway 12) at milepost 158.2. The 27 campsites are positioned within a mature, moss-covered pine forest centered around a small stream, offering a serene setting for camping, picnicking, fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing.

The campground features paved driveways at each site with picnic tables and fire rings. It can accommodate RVs up to 40 feet. Drinking water is available from a hand pump, and vault toilets are provided. Campground hosts are present when the facility is open. The location provides excellent access to the Lochsa River corridor's recreational opportunities including world-class whitewater and backcountry exploration in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests.

location.directions: From Lolo, MT drive west on Highway 12 for approximately 49 miles to the campground at milepost 158.2.

payload.name: Emerald Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open through October 12, 2026. Peak season runs May 22 through October 11, 2026. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance with a two-night minimum required for bookings made more than 7 days ahead.
payload.short_description: Wooded hillside campground in southern Vermont with 103 sites including tent sites, lean-tos, and RV sites overlooking scenic Emerald Lake, offering swimming, boat rentals, and hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Emerald Lake State Park Campground sits on a heavily wooded ridge above the 20-acre Emerald Lake between Manchester and Rutland. The campground offers 103 sites including 43 tent/RV sites, 22 tent-only sites, and 37 lean-tos. Facilities include flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and a dump station. The park features a sandy beach, boat rentals (canoes, kayaks, paddleboards), hiking trails through forests and along cliffs, volleyball courts, and a playground.
payload.long_description:
Emerald Lake State Park Campground occupies a scenic wooded hillside above the crystal-clear waters of Emerald Lake in southern Vermont's Green Mountains. Located conveniently between Manchester and Rutland along Route 7, the park provides an excellent base for exploring the region while enjoying quality camping facilities.

The campground offers 103 sites spread across several loops, including 43 tent/RV sites, 22 tent-only sites, and 37 rustic lean-tos. Each site features a fire ring and picnic table. Modern amenities include flush toilets, token-operated hot showers, potable water spigots, and an RV dump station. A concession stand sells firewood, ice, and snacks.

The 20-acre lake is the centerpiece of recreation here, with a sandy swimming beach, boat rentals including canoes, kayaks, pedal boats, and stand-up paddleboards. Miles of hiking trails wind through working forests, past wetlands, and along cliff faces offering panoramic views. Additional amenities include a playground, volleyball courts, horseshoe pits, and a nature center.

location.directions: From Rutland, take Route 7 South for 23.5 miles, turn right onto Sweeney Lane, then take an immediate left onto Emerald Lake Lane.

address.full: 235 Emerald Lake Ln, East Dorset, VT 05253

payload.name: Fort Dummer State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for camping from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis through the Vermont State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Rustic tent and lean-to camping on 217 forested acres in the Connecticut River Valley, just south of Brattleboro. Token-operated hot showers, dump station, and access to hiking trails.
payload.medium_description: Fort Dummer State Park offers 50 tent/trailer sites and 10 lean-tos spread across two adjacent camping loops in a 217-acre hardwood forest. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring. Amenities include flush toilets with token-operated hot showers, potable water spigots, RV dump station, and recycling. The park features three hiking trails ranging from easy to moderate difficulty, plus a recreation field, horseshoe pit, and volleyball court. Firewood and ice available for purchase.
payload.long_description:
Fort Dummer State Park sits on 217 acres of mixed hardwood forest in the Connecticut River Valley, a few miles south of Brattleboro near the site of the first permanent European settlement in Vermont. The campground divides into two adjacent loops containing 50 tent/trailer sites and 10 three-sided lean-tos, all set among mature trees that provide good shade and privacy.

Each site has a picnic table and fire ring with grate. Two restroom buildings serve the camping area, both equipped with flush toilets and token-operated hot showers. Potable water is available from spigots throughout the campground. An RV dump station and large recycling bin are on site, though no electric, water, or sewer hookups are available at individual sites.

The park offers three hiking trails of easy to moderate difficulty, including a path to a viewpoint overlooking the Connecticut River. A recreation field, horseshoe pit, volleyball court, and small picnic area round out the day-use facilities. Firewood and ice are sold at the campground.

location.directions: From I-91 Exit 1 in Brattleboro, go 0.1 mile north on US-5, then 0.5 mile east on Fairground Road, then 1 mile south on Main Street and Old Guilford Road to the park entrance at 517 Old Guilford Road.

address.full: 517 Ft Dummer Park Dr, Brattleboro, VT 05301

links.title: VT Dept of Forests, Parks & Recreation

payload.name: Green River Reservoir State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The park operates from the third weekend in May through the second Monday in October. For 2026, the season runs approximately May 15 through October 11. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis through the Vermont State Parks reservation system online, by calling the park at 802-888-1349 during season, or via the Reservation Call Center at 888-409-7579.
payload.short_description: Remote boat-in camping on a pristine 653-acre reservoir with 27 tent sites scattered along 19 miles of undeveloped shoreline in Vermont's Green Mountains.
payload.medium_description: Green River Reservoir State Park offers a true backcountry paddling and camping experience on a designated quiet lake where only electric motors (5 mph max) and human-powered boats are allowed. The 27 remote tent sites are accessible only by canoe or kayak, with paddles ranging from 1 to 2 miles from the launch. Each site has a fire ring and privy, but no potable water. The reservoir's undeveloped shoreline and lack of motor noise make it a favorite for those seeking solitude.
payload.long_description:
Green River Reservoir State Park surrounds a 653-acre reservoir that has long been a destination for paddlers and campers seeking a primitive, quiet experience. The park protects 19 miles of undeveloped shoreline and is designated a quiet lake under Vermont's Use of Public Waters Rules, meaning only electric motors at 5 mph or less and human-powered watercraft are permitted. There are no boat rentals at the park; visitors must bring their own canoe or kayak or rent from outfitters in nearby Morrisville or Stowe.

The 27 remote tent sites are spread along the shoreline and can only be reached by paddling, with some sites a mile or two from the launch area. Each site includes a fire ring and a privy, but there is no potable water anywhere in the park, so campers must bring their own supply. Site capacity varies based on each site's characteristics. Two group sites can accommodate up to 12 people each.

An ADA-accessible boardwalk leads from the parking area to the boat launch. Parking is extremely limited and first-come, first-served. Firewood is available for purchase at the park.

location.directions: From the junction of VT Route 100 and VT Route 12 in Morrisville, briefly follow Route 12 South to Route 15A. Follow Route 15A to Route 15 East and turn right. Take the first left onto Garfield Road and follow it 3.1 miles to the yield sign, then turn right (still Garfield Road). Take your next immediate left onto Green River Dam Road and follow it 1.3 miles to the park entrance.

address.full: 1394 Green River Dam Rd, Hyde Park, VT 05655

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Green River Reservoir
VT Dept of Forests, Parks & Recreation - Green River Reservoir
Green River Reservoir State Park Map (PDF)

payload.name: Half Moon Pond State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 camping season from Memorial Day weekend through the second Monday in October. Reservations are available through vtstateparks-visit.com up to 11 months in advance. Two-night minimum for reservations made more than 7 days ahead; one-night stays allowed within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Half Moon Pond State Park offers 52 tent/RV sites and 11 lean-tos nestled within the 3,500-acre Bomoseen State Park forest, featuring waterfront sites on a serene pond with boat rentals, flush toilets, and hot showers.
payload.medium_description: Half Moon Pond State Park sits in a sheltered basin surrounded by dense woods in Vermont's Taconic Mountains. The campground offers 52 tent/RV sites and 11 lean-tos, some with lakefront views on the quiet Half Moon Pond. Facilities include flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and an RV dump station. Rowboats, kayaks, canoes, and pedal boats are available for rent. Two small sandy beaches provide swimming and sunbathing, while an extensive trail network connects to the surrounding Bomoseen State Park.
payload.long_description:
Half Moon Pond State Park is tucked into the forests of the 3,500-acre Bomoseen State Park in Vermont's Taconic Mountains, sitting in a sheltered basin around the peaceful Half Moon Pond. The campground contains 52 tent/RV sites and 11 lean-tos, with options ranging from wooded sites to waterfront locations directly on the pond. Five furnished cabins and the Tall Timbers Cottage are also available for those seeking more comfortable accommodations.

The park features restrooms with flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and token-operated showers. An RV dump station is available, though no hookups exist at individual sites. Each campsite includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill. The camp store sells firewood, ice, groceries, and supplies.

Recreation centers on the pond, where rowboats, kayaks, canoes, pedal boats, and stand-up paddleboards are available for rent from the park office. Two small sandy beaches offer swimming and sunbathing. On land, a vast trail system provides hikes for all abilities, connecting to the larger Bomoseen State Park trail network. Additional amenities include a volleyball court, horseshoe pit, and playground.

location.directions: From West, East, and South: Take US-4 to exit 4 VT-30 N. Take VT-30 N for 7 miles, turn left on Hortonia Rd. In 1.7 miles turn left on Black Pond Rd. Park is on left in 2.1 miles. From North: Take US-7 South to VT-30 in Middlebury. Follow VT-30 S for 21.8 miles, turn right onto Hortonia Rd. In 1.7 miles turn left onto Black Pond Rd. Park is on left at 2.1 miles.

address.full: 1621 Black Pond Rd, Fair Haven, VT 05743

links.title: Half Moon Pond - Vermont State Parks
Halfmoon State Park - VT Dept of Forests, Parks and Recreation

payload.name: Lake St Catherine State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 12. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance through the Vermont State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Lakeside Vermont campground with 60 sites including tent, RV, lean-to, and cabin options on Lake St. Catherine, offering swimming, boating, and an 18-hole disc golf course.
payload.medium_description: Lake St. Catherine State Park offers 60 campsites including tent-only, tent/RV, lean-tos, and a cabin on a scenic Vermont lake. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated showers, dump station, beach access, boat rentals, a nature center, and an 18-hole disc golf course. No hookups available.
payload.long_description:
Lake St. Catherine State Park is located in Poultney, Vermont, on the shores of Lake St. Catherine. The campground features 60 sites: 36 tent/RV sites, 12 tent-only sites, 11 lean-tos, and one electric cabin. Sites range from grassy open areas to wooded locations, many with direct lake access. The park provides flush toilets (ADA accessible), coin-operated hot showers, water spigots throughout, and an RV dump station, though no hookups are available at individual sites.

Beyond camping, the park offers well-developed day-use facilities including a swimming beach, playground, nature center, and snack bar concession. Boat rentals are available including canoes, kayaks, rowboats, and pedal boats. An 18-hole disc golf course winds through the open fields and trees, providing 1-2 hours of play depending on skill level. Hiking trails explore the surrounding area.

Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Stays booked more than 7 days ahead require a 2-night minimum; one-night stays are permitted within 7 days of arrival.

location.directions: Located at 3034 VT Route 30 in Poultney, Vermont.

address.full: 70 Lake Saint Catherine Dr, Poultney, VT 05764

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Lake St. Catherine Reservations

payload.name: Lake Shaftsbury State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season through October 12. Day use hours are 10 AM to sunset. Group lean-to reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance.
payload.short_description: Group camping destination in southwestern Vermont featuring 15 lean-to shelters, a sandy swimming beach, and boat rentals on scenic Lake Shaftsbury.
payload.medium_description: Lake Shaftsbury State Park offers group camping on an 84-acre parcel surrounding a picturesque lake in Bennington County. The campground features 15 lean-to shelters divided into three bookable clusters, each accommodating up to 40 people. Amenities include flush toilets, drinking water, a sandy beach, boat rentals, concession stand, and the Healing Springs Nature Trail circling the lake.
payload.long_description:
Lake Shaftsbury State Park occupies 84 acres surrounding the small but scenic Lake Shaftsbury in southwestern Vermont. Originally a private campground and cabin resort, it became a state park in 1974. The park specializes in group camping, making it ideal for scout troops, family reunions, church groups, and other organizations seeking a rustic outdoor experience.

The camping area consists of 15 lean-to shelters organized into three reservable clusters: L01-L06, L07-L11, and L12-L15. Each cluster can accommodate up to 40 people, with the entire group area holding a maximum of 120 campers. Facilities include flush toilets with hot and cold running water, portable toilets near the camping area, and potable drinking water throughout the park.

Beyond camping, the park offers a sandy swimming beach, boat rentals including kayaks, canoes, and pedal boats, and a lakeside pavilion with group grills and seating for 100. The Healing Springs Nature Trail provides an easy hike around the lake. A fully furnished waterfront cottage sleeping six is also available for those seeking more comfortable accommodations.

location.directions: From Bennington, take VT Route 7A north. Turn east onto Shaftsbury State Park Road and follow signs to the park entrance at 262 Shaftsbury State Park Rd, Shaftsbury, VT 05262.

payload.name: Zealand
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from mid-May through mid-October. All 11 sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations accepted. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Small 11-site first-come, first-served campground along the Ammonoosuc River, serving as a base for Zealand Valley hiking and the Zealand Falls Hut.
payload.medium_description: Zealand Campground is an intimate 11-site campground nestled along the Ammonoosuc River near Twin Mountain, New Hampshire. Open mid-May through mid-October on a first-come, first-served basis, it offers a mix of open and partially wooded sites ideal for tent camping. The campground provides convenient access to the Zealand Trailhead, leading to the AMC's Zealand Falls Hut, the Appalachian Trail, and the Pemigewasset Wilderness.
payload.long_description:
Zealand Campground is a small, rustic campground tucked along the Ammonoosuc River in the White Mountain National Forest. With just 11 sites offering a mix of open meadow and partially wooded settings, it provides a quieter alternative to the larger developed campgrounds in the area. Sites are first-come, first-served with no advance reservations, making it a good option for spontaneous trips or as a backup when other campgrounds fill.

The campground is ideally situated for exploring the Zealand Valley. The Zealand Trailhead is nearby, providing access to a network of trails including the route to AMC's Zealand Falls Hut, the Appalachian Trail, and the Pemigewasset Wilderness. The hike to Zealand Falls is a moderate 2.8-mile trek that rewards with views of the cascading falls and the opportunity to continue deeper into the backcountry.

Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grilling grate. Vault toilets and potable water are available on-site, and trash dumpsters are provided. The campground operates seasonally from mid-May through mid-October, with a nightly fee of $24 per site. Pets are welcome but must remain leashed at all times.

location.directions: From the junction of NH Route 3 and NH Route 302 in Twin Mountain, travel east on Route 302 for 2 miles. Turn right onto Zealand Road at the Zealand Campground sign. The campground is 0.5 miles on your right.

payload.name: Lost Pond Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations. No fees. Overnight use limited to two consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: A primitive three-sided backcountry shelter on the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail in Vermont's Big Branch Wilderness, accessible via a 3-mile hike from Forest Road 10.
payload.medium_description: Lost Pond Shelter is a backcountry overnight shelter on the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and coincident Long Trail within the Big Branch Wilderness of Green Mountain National Forest. The shelter is a primitive hike-in structure with a composting toilet and nearby water sources that require treatment. No fees or reservations are required.
payload.long_description:
Lost Pond Shelter is a backcountry overnight shelter located along the Appalachian National Scenic Trail and the coincident Long Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest. Situated within the Big Branch Wilderness and the Robert T. Stafford White Rocks National Recreation Area near Mount Tabor, this primitive shelter offers through-hikers and backpackers a place to rest during their journey.

The shelter is typical of Long Trail shelters: a three-sided Adirondack-style structure that can accommodate approximately 6-10 hikers. Amenities are minimal by design. A composting toilet is available, and water can be obtained from nearby sources but must be treated or filtered before drinking. There is no potable water, trash service, or other developed facilities.

Access is via a roughly 3-mile hike south on the Appalachian Trail from Forest Road 10 in Mount Tabor. The shelter operates year-round on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations or fees. Use is limited to two consecutive nights to ensure availability for through-hikers.

location.directions: Hike the Appalachian Trail south from Forest Road 10 in Mount Tabor for approximately 3 miles.

payload.name: Camp Penacook Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations accepted. Campers must bring their own water and bear-proof food storage. Forest-wide fire danger is currently low.
payload.short_description: A rustic 3-sided backcountry shelter on the southeast side of Mt. Chocorua, accessed via the Piper Trail, offering scenic overlooks and tent camping for hikers.
payload.medium_description: Camp Penacook Shelter is a primitive 3-sided lean-to situated on the southeast side of Mt. Chocorua, approximately 1.5 miles from the summit. The shelter accommodates 6-8 people and includes a small earthen tent pad below. A pit toilet is nearby. Hikers can enjoy scenic granite slab overlooks to the east near the Piper Trail junction.
payload.long_description:
Camp Penacook Shelter is a backcountry 3-sided shelter located on the southeast slopes of Mt. Chocorua within the Mount Chocorua Scenic Area of the White Mountain National Forest. Positioned roughly 1.5 miles from the summit, the shelter provides a base for hikers exploring this popular peak via the Piper Trail.

The shelter accommodates 6-8 people and features a small earthen tent pad below that can fit one small tent. A pit toilet is located in the vicinity. There is no potable water at the site, so hikers must pack in all drinking water. Scenic granite slab overlooks to the east near the Piper Trail junction offer rewarding views.

As a primitive backcountry shelter, Camp Penacook operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations. Standard White Mountain National Forest backcountry regulations apply, including the requirement to carry a bear-proof canister for food storage.

location.directions: From NH Route 16 in Albany, take the Piper Trail to access Camp Penacook Shelter, located approximately 1.5 miles below the summit of Mt. Chocorua on the southeast side of the mountain.

payload.name: Jamaica State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open from the third weekend in May through the second Monday in October. Due to construction at Ball Mountain Dam, camping opened May 16, 2026 for the season. Reservations available through vtstateparks.com up to 11 months in advance; two-night minimum for reservations made more than 7 days ahead.
payload.short_description: A 772-acre Vermont state park along the West River offering 41 tent/RV sites and 18 lean-tos, known for whitewater paddling, hiking trails, and swimming at Salmon Hole.
payload.medium_description: Jamaica State Park sits along the West River in southern Vermont's Green Mountains. The 772-acre park offers 41 tent/RV sites and 18 lean-tos nestled among hemlock groves and mixed hardwoods. The campground features two restroom buildings with flush toilets and token-operated hot showers. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table. Popular activities include whitewater paddling during seasonal dam releases, swimming at Salmon Hole, and hiking trails including the West River Trail and Hamilton Falls.
payload.long_description:
Jamaica State Park encompasses 772 acres along the West River in Windham County, Vermont. Opened in 1969, the park occupies land once home to the village of Jamaica, which was flooded when Ball Mountain Dam was constructed upstream. The campground spreads across forested terrain featuring hemlock groves and mixed hardwoods, with 41 tent/RV sites and 18 lean-tos available.

The park is renowned for its whitewater paddling opportunities, particularly during scheduled dam releases from Ball Mountain Dam that create Class II-III rapids. Salmon Hole provides a popular swimming area with a sandy beach. The West River Trail offers hiking and biking along the old railroad grade, while Hamilton Falls Trail leads to one of Vermont's tallest waterfalls.

Facilities include two restroom buildings with flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and token-operated hot showers ($0.50 for 5 minutes). A dump station is available for RVs. Each campsite has a fire ring and picnic table on a gravel pad. The park also features a playground, volleyball court, horseshoe pit, and a picnic shelter for campers. Note that the Depot Street Bridge leading to the park has an 8-ton weight limit.

location.directions: From Route 30 in the village of Jamaica, turn north onto Depot Street. Continue 0.5 miles to the park entrance. Note: Depot Street Bridge has an 8-ton weight limit.

payload.name: Kingsland Bay State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. The remote paddle-in tent site on Hulbert Point is reservable through Vermont State Parks up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis.
payload.short_description: Day-use park on Lake Champlain with one remote paddle-in tent site on Hulbert Point accessible only by boat or kayak.
payload.medium_description: Kingsland Bay State Park is primarily a day-use area on Lake Champlain featuring picnicking, hiking, and kayaking. The park offers one remote tent site on Hulbert Point that is only accessible by boat or paddle. Group pavilions and historic buildings are available for rental, but there are no traditional drive-in campsites.
payload.long_description:
Kingsland Bay State Park occupies 264 acres on the eastern shore of Lake Champlain in Ferrisburgh, Vermont. The park is centered around the historic Hawley Farm and features a small beach, boat rentals, hiking trails, and several buildings available for group events. Much of the southern portion of the park, including McDonough Point and Hulbert Point, is a State Designated Natural Area.

The only overnight camping option is a single remote tent site located on the northern side of Hulbert Point, part of the Champlain Paddler's Trail. This site accommodates up to 8 people and requires paddling or boating in with all gear. The rest of the park functions as a day-use facility with picnic pavilions, a group shelter, and the Hawley House available for rentals. Pets are allowed at the remote tent site but are prohibited elsewhere in the park.

Composting toilets are available, and the park has water spigots, picnic tables, and grills at the day-use areas. There are no showers, hookups, or traditional campground amenities. The park operates seasonally from late May through mid-October.

address.full: 3056 Kingsland Bay State Park Rd, Ferrisburg, VT 05456

links.title: Vermont FPR - Kingsland Bay State Park

payload.name: Waterbury Reservoir Remote Sites Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 15 through October 17. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis, with a minimum 1-day advance booking required. Maximum stay is 7 consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Boat-in remote campsites on Waterbury Reservoir within Mount Mansfield State Forest. 27 waterfront tent sites accessible only by paddling or motorboat, each with a fire ring and composting toilet.
payload.medium_description: Waterbury Reservoir Remote Sites offers 27 primitive, boat-access-only campsites scattered along 5 miles of shoreline within Mount Mansfield State Forest. All sites are waterfront or have water views. Each campsite includes a fire ring and a nearby roofed composting toilet. No potable water is available. Access requires a one-to-two-mile paddle from boat launches at Waterbury Dam, Blush Hill, or Moscow/Cotton Brook.
payload.long_description:
Waterbury Reservoir Remote Sites provides a true backcountry camping experience on a scenic Vermont reservoir within Mount Mansfield State Forest. The 27 primitive campsites are spread over 5 miles of shoreline and are accessible only by canoe, kayak, or motorboat from three launch points: Waterbury Dam, Blush Hill, and Moscow/Cotton Brook.

Each site is waterfront or offers water views and includes a fire ring and a nearby roofed composting toilet (moldering privy). There is no potable water, so campers must pack in all drinking water. This is pack-in, pack-out camping with no trash service. Bears are active in the area, so proper food storage is essential.

The reservoir offers excellent opportunities for fishing, paddling, swimming, and hiking. Day-use boat rentals are available at nearby Waterbury Center State Park for those without their own watercraft. Maximum occupancy is 6 people per site, with two sites accommodating up to 12. Reservations are required and can be made up to 11 months in advance via vtstateparks.com or by calling the reservation center.

location.directions: Access the reservoir via boat launches at Waterbury Dam (off Waterbury Dam Road), Blush Hill (off Blush Hill Road), or Moscow/Cotton Brook. From Waterbury, take Route 100 north toward Stowe. Sites are boat-in only, typically a 1-2 mile paddle from launch points.

payload.name: Wilgus State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 8 through October 11. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis through the Vermont State Parks reservation system.
payload.short_description: Small riverside Vermont state park campground on the Connecticut River with tent sites, lean-tos, and cabins. Popular for paddling with canoe and kayak rentals available on-site.
payload.medium_description: Wilgus State Park is a compact riverside campground on the Connecticut River in southeastern Vermont. The park offers 15 tent/RV sites, 6 lean-to shelters, and 4 electric cabins, many with river views. Canoe and kayak rentals are available at the contact station, making it a popular base for paddling. The Pinnacle Trail climbs to ridge-top views of the Connecticut River and New Hampshire, while the Wilgus Nature Trail provides an easy half-mile walk.
payload.long_description:
Wilgus State Park sits along the western bank of the Connecticut River in Weathersfield, Vermont. This intimate campground offers 15 tent/RV sites, 6 lean-to shelters, and 4 electric cabins, many positioned to take advantage of river views. The park is particularly popular with paddlers since canoe and kayak rentals are available at the contact station, and a boat launch provides direct access to the Connecticut River for fishing and exploration.

Facilities include two restroom buildings with flush toilets and coin-operated hot showers, potable water spigots throughout the campground, and an RV dump station near the ranger's quarters. Wi-Fi is available at the contact station. Recreational options include horseshoe pits, a volleyball net, a swimming area with river access, and hiking trails. The Pinnacle Trail is approximately one mile and climbs to ridge-top views overlooking the river and New Hampshire, while the shorter Wilgus Nature Trail offers a level half-mile walk.

The park has multiple ADA-accessible campsites and facilities, including accessible restrooms and showers. Pets are allowed on leash throughout most of the park except the swimming area; one cabin (Otter) is pet-friendly while the other three do not permit pets. No hookups are available at individual sites, though the dump station serves RV needs.

location.directions: Located on Route 5 in Weathersfield, Vermont. The park address is 3985 RT 5, Weathersfield, VT 05156.

payload.name: Woodford State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Reservations made more than 7 days in advance require a two-night minimum stay.
payload.short_description: Vermont's highest-elevation campground at 2,400 feet, Woodford State Park offers 100 wooded sites including lean-tos and cabins surrounding Adams Reservoir in the Green Mountain National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Woodford State Park is a 398-acre property nestled at 2,400 feet elevation in the southern Green Mountains, making it Vermont's highest-elevation campground. The park features 100 campsites including tent/RV sites, tent-only sites, lean-tos, and four cabins surrounding the scenic Adams Reservoir. Flush toilets, hot showers, and a dump station are available. The 2.7-mile Woodford Trail circles the reservoir while the shorter Atwood Trail runs along the shoreline.
payload.long_description:
Woodford State Park sits at 2,400 feet in Vermont's southern Green Mountains, surrounded by the Green Mountain National Forest including the Aiken Wilderness. This 398-acre property centers around Adams Reservoir, offering a quieter, high-elevation camping experience with cooler temperatures than lower Vermont parks.

The campground provides 100 sites: 60 tent/RV sites, 16 tent-only sites, 20 lean-tos, and 4 cabins (two of which are pet-friendly). Each campsite includes a picnic table, fire ring, and grill. Facilities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, drinking water spigots throughout, and an RV dump station. There are no hookups at individual sites.

Recreation centers on Adams Reservoir with a swimming area and car-top boat launch. The 2.7-mile Woodford Trail loops the entire park and reservoir, while the 0.5-mile Atwood Trail follows a portion of the shoreline. Fishing is popular for rainbow and brown trout. The surrounding national forest lands provide additional hiking opportunities.

location.directions: Located at 142 State Park Road, Bennington, VT 05201. From Bennington, take Route 9 east approximately 10 miles. The park entrance is on the north side of the road.

payload.name: FRENCH GULCH
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fee required. Road access may be limited during winter due to snow conditions.
payload.short_description: Small, free 2-site primitive campground along French Gulch Creek offering fishing access to the Red River in Idaho's Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests.
payload.medium_description: French Gulch Campground is a compact 2-site primitive campground in the Red River Ranger District of the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. Situated at 4,210 feet elevation along French Gulch Creek, the campground provides easy fishing access to the nearby Red River. Facilities are minimal with only a vault toilet and parking area. There is no potable water, no picnic tables, and no trash service, so campers must pack out all garbage.
payload.long_description:
French Gulch Campground serves as a convenient base camp for exploring the Red River Ranger District in the Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests. This small, free campground features just two campsites at 4,210 feet elevation along the Highway 14 Corridor.

French Gulch Creek flows through the campground, and the Red River is nearby for fishing opportunities. The site offers ample parking space despite its small footprint. However, facilities are primitive: only a vault toilet is available. Campers must bring their own drinking water and pack out all trash.

The campground is located approximately 11 miles south of State Highway 14 on Red River-Dixie Road #222. While officially open year-round, winter snow may make access difficult or impossible during certain months.

location.directions: From State Highway 14, turn south on Red River-Dixie Road #222. Follow Road #222 approximately 11 miles to French Gulch Campground on the left (east).

address.full: 1500-1598 Red River Rd, Elk City, ID 83525

payload.name: ELLISON GUARD STATION RENTAL
payload.status_description: Unable to verify current rental availability or operating status through official sources. Contact the Ely Ranger District at +1 (775) 289-3031 for current information about this facility.
payload.short_description: Historic guard station near the Bald Mountain Wilderness in Nevada's White Pine Range, managed by the Ely Ranger District of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Ellison Guard Station is located in White Pine County, Nevada, within the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. The station provides access to the Bald Mountain Wilderness, a 22,366-acre wilderness area in the White Pine Range of west-central Nevada. The area offers remote backcountry experiences in one of Nevada's most isolated mountain ranges.
payload.long_description:
Ellison Guard Station sits at the edge of the Bald Mountain Wilderness in Nevada's White Pine Range, managed by the Ely Ranger District of the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest. This remote location in White Pine County provides access to one of Nevada's most pristine wilderness areas.

The Bald Mountain Wilderness encompasses 22,366 acres of rugged terrain in west-central Nevada. The White Pine Range features dramatic landscapes typical of the Great Basin, with subalpine forests and high desert ecosystems. The area is known for its solitude and backcountry opportunities.

Visitors to this region should be prepared for extremely remote conditions with limited services. The nearest town is Ely, Nevada, which serves as the gateway to several wilderness areas in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest.

location.directions: From Highway 6, take County Road 10 to Ellison Creek Guard Station. Alternatively, from Highway 50, travel south on Forest Service Road 400 for approximately 20 miles.

address.full: 13687 W Gardner Ranch Rd, Lund, NV 89317

payload.name: Little River State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open for the 2026 season from May 15 through October 17. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Reservations made more than 7 days in advance require a two-night minimum.
payload.short_description: Central Vermont's largest state park campground featuring 101 wooded sites along the Waterbury Reservoir, with flush restrooms, hot showers, swimming beaches, and boat rentals within Mount Mansfield State Forest.
payload.medium_description: Little River State Park hosts central Vermont's largest and most popular campground with 81 tent/RV sites, 20 lean-tos, and 5 cabins nestled in the forested hills of Mount Mansfield State Forest. Amenities include flush toilets with running water, token-operated hot showers, a dump station, swimming beaches, boat launch, and kayak/canoe rentals. An additional 27 remote boat-in sites line the Waterbury Reservoir shoreline for those seeking backcountry camping.
payload.long_description:
Little River State Park, located just 30 miles south of Burlington off I-89, is home to central Vermont's largest and most popular campground. The 101-site developed campground includes 81 tent and RV sites, 20 lean-tos, and 5 electric cabins spread throughout the wooded terrain of Mount Mansfield State Forest. Four restroom buildings provide flush toilets and hot/cold running water, with three offering token-operated hot showers.

The campground offers an RV dump station but no hookups. Each campsite includes a fire ring, picnic table, and grill. Within the campground, campers have access to swimming beaches, play areas, ball fields, a boat launch, and canoe/kayak rentals. Miles of hiking and mountain biking trails wind through the surrounding forest, and a nature center provides educational programming.

For those seeking more solitude, 27 remote campsites along the Waterbury Reservoir shoreline are accessible only by boat and available first-come, first-served. The park's location on the reservoir makes it a prime destination for paddling, fishing, and swimming throughout the summer season.

location.directions: From I-89, take Exit 10 toward Waterbury/Stowe. Head north on Route 100 for approximately 1.5 miles, then turn west onto Little River Road. Follow Little River Road for about 3.5 miles to the park entrance.

payload.name: Maidstone State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through September 6. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance. Reservations made more than 7 days in advance require a two-night minimum stay; one-night stays are available within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Vermont's most remote state park campground on pristine Maidstone Lake, offering 63 wooded sites including tent sites, tent/RV sites, and lean-tos with beach access, boat rentals, and flush restrooms.
payload.medium_description: Maidstone State Park Campground sits on the shore of Maidstone Lake in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom, making it the most remote of Vermont's state parks. The campground offers 63 sites across two loops, including 20 tent-only sites, 13 tent/RV sites, and 29 lean-tos, with several waterfront locations. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated showers, potable water, a dump station, a sandy beach, and canoe/kayak rentals for registered campers.
payload.long_description:
Maidstone State Park Campground occupies a forested peninsula on Maidstone Lake in Vermont's remote Northeast Kingdom. The 63-site campground spreads across two loops designated Camping Area A and Camping Area B, with prime waterfront sites and quieter interior locations. Site types include 20 tent-only sites, 13 tent/RV sites accommodating rigs up to 20-30 feet, and 29 lean-tos. Each site has a fire ring and picnic table.

The campground provides flush toilets with hot and cold running water, coin-operated showers, drinking water spigots throughout the park, and an RV dump station. A sandy beach provides swimming access, and registered campers can rent canoes, kayaks, and rowboats from the park office for use on Maidstone Lake. The lake holds trout, perch, bullhead, and panfish. Firewood and ice are available for purchase.

Bears are active in this park, and campers must securely store food and trash in vehicles or bear canisters. Pets are allowed on leash in the campground but are not permitted in the day use area or on beaches.

location.directions: From Bloomfield, go 5 miles south on VT Route 102, then 5 miles southwest on Maidstone Lake Road. The campground is located 1 mile past the day use area.

payload.name: Ricker Pond State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open through October 11, 2026. Season runs May 22 to October 11. Bears have been active in this park; secure all food and trash. Reservations made more than 7 days in advance require a two-night minimum.
payload.short_description: Quiet campground on Ricker Pond's western shore in Groton State Forest, offering tent sites, lean-tos, cabins, and cottages with swimming beach, boat rentals, and trail access.
payload.medium_description: Ricker Pond State Park sits on the western shore of Ricker Pond within Vermont's Groton State Forest. The campground offers 56 sites including tent/RV sites, lean-tos, cabins, and cottages. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, drinking water, an RV dump station, swimming beach, boat launch, and watercraft rentals. The park connects to the Montpelier-Wells Rail Trail and Cross Vermont Trail for hiking and biking.
payload.long_description:
Established in the 1930s, Ricker Pond State Park occupies a scenic setting on the western shore of Ricker Pond in Vermont's Groton State Forest. The 56-site campground features 14 tent-only sites, 12 tent/RV sites, 23 lean-tos, 5 cabins with electricity, and 2 cottages with electricity. Two of the three restroom buildings include coin-operated hot showers alongside flush toilets with hot and cold running water. Drinking water spigots are distributed throughout the campground.

The park offers a sandy swimming beach, cartop boat launch, and rentals for canoes, kayaks, and rowboats. Anglers can fish directly from the pond. A nature center provides interpretive programs during the camping season. The campground connects to miles of hiking and mountain biking trails, including direct access to the Montpelier-Wells Rail Trail, which forms part of the Cross Vermont Trail.

No hookups are available, but an RV dump station serves self-contained units. Firewood and ice are sold on-site. Bears are active in this park, so campers must securely store food and trash. Pets are allowed on leash throughout the park except at the swimming beach.

location.directions: Located at 18 Ricker Pond Campground Road, Groton, VT 05046. The park is situated within Groton State Forest on the western shore of Ricker Pond.

links.title: Vermont State Parks Reservation System - Ricker Pond

payload.name: Battell Shelter
payload.status_description: Open for the hiking season on a first-come, first-served basis. No reservations or fees; donations accepted. A GMC caretaker is stationed here during hiking season. Groups are prohibited from staying overnight. Maximum stay is two consecutive nights. Water must be filtered or treated from nearby stream sources.
payload.short_description: Backcountry three-sided lean-to shelter on the Long Trail at 3,300 feet, just under a mile from Mount Abraham's summit in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest.
payload.medium_description: Battell Shelter is a historic three-sided Adirondack-style lean-to on the Long Trail, built in 1967 at 3,300 feet elevation on the south side of Mount Abraham. The shelter sleeps eight and features tent platforms, a privy, and a water source 1/8 mile south on the trail. A GMC caretaker is stationed here during hiking season. The site is popular among Long Trail thru-hikers and day hikers seeking an overnight near one of Vermont's 4,000-foot summits.
payload.long_description:
Battell Shelter sits at 3,300 feet on the Long Trail, positioned on the south side of Mount Abraham in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest. Built in 1967 by work parties from Farm and Wilderness Camp in Plymouth, this three-sided Adirondack-style lean-to is one of the highest shelters on the Long Trail System. The shelter sleeps eight and is accompanied by tent platforms for overflow camping.

Access is via the blue-blazed Battell Trail, a 2-mile hike from the trailhead at the end of USFS Road 350 off Lincoln Gap Road. The route gains significant elevation through hardwood and spruce-fir forest before reaching the Long Trail junction, then continues a short distance to the shelter. Water is available from a stream 1/8 mile south on the trail but must be filtered or treated.

The Green Mountain Club maintains a backcountry caretaker at this site during hiking season to manage use and protect the surrounding high-elevation vegetation. Groups are prohibited from staying overnight due to the shelter's popularity and environmental sensitivity. The GMC has announced plans to build a new shelter adjacent to the existing structure to increase capacity while preserving the historic 1967 lean-to.

location.directions: From Lincoln, Vermont, take Quaker Street to Elder Hill Road (USFS Road 350). Bear right at Ball Diamond Road, then bear left to stay on FR 350. Continue to the Battell Trail trailhead parking at the road's end. Hike 2 miles on the blue-blazed Battell Trail to the Long Trail junction, then continue uphill to the shelter.

links.title: Green Mountain Club - Battell Shelter History
Green Mountain Club - Group Hiking Policies

payload.name: POWERLINE
payload.status_description: Status unknown. This appears to be a dispersed camping area in Pike National Forest. Dispersed camping on National Forest land is generally permitted unless posted otherwise. Check current fire restrictions before camping, as Stage I Fire Restrictions have been in effect for Pike-San Isabel National Forests in 2026.
payload.short_description: Primitive dispersed camping area in Pike National Forest's South Park Ranger District, located in Park County near Eleven Mile Canyon.
payload.medium_description: Powerline is a dispersed camping area in Pike National Forest within the South Park Ranger District of Park County, Colorado. Located near Eleven Mile Canyon at approximately 9,000 feet elevation, this primitive site offers a backcountry camping experience without developed amenities. As with most dispersed camping in the forest, campers should be self-sufficient and prepared to pack out all trash.
payload.long_description:
Powerline is a dispersed camping area within Pike National Forest, managed by the South Park Ranger District. Situated in Park County at coordinates near Eleven Mile Canyon and the Tarryall area, this primitive camping spot sits at roughly 9,000 feet elevation in the Colorado high country.

As a dispersed camping site rather than a developed campground, Powerline lacks the amenities found at established USFS campgrounds in the region such as Spillway, Riverside, or Happy Meadows. Campers should arrive fully self-sufficient with their own water supply and be prepared to pack out all trash. Standard National Forest dispersed camping regulations apply, including a 14-day stay limit within any 30-day period.

The surrounding South Park area offers access to Eleven Mile Canyon Recreation Area, the Tarryall Mountains, and numerous hiking and fishing opportunities. High clearance vehicles may be recommended depending on road conditions, particularly during or after wet weather.

location.directions: From Lake George, Colorado, head west on US-24 for approximately 1.5 miles. Turn left onto County Road 96 and continue for about 2 miles. The campground is located near the power lines; look for designated camping spots along the road.

address.full: 11747 Clear Creek Rd, Lake George, CO 80827

payload.name: Bankston Camp
