payload.status_description: Open year-round. No fee required. First-come, first-served with no reservations. Potable water is not available; campers must bring their own water supply.
payload.short_description: A free, primitive tent camping area in Kisatchie National Forest, located near the Catahoula National Wildlife Management Preserve in Grant Parish, Louisiana.
payload.medium_description: Bankston Camp offers a rustic, no-fee camping experience in the Catahoula Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest. This primitive site northeast of Williana provides a secluded forest setting near the Catahoula National Wildlife Management Preserve. Campers must be self-sufficient as no potable water or developed facilities are available.
payload.long_description:
Bankston Camp is a primitive camping area managed by the Catahoula Ranger District of Kisatchie National Forest. Located northeast of Williana, Louisiana, just outside the borders of the Catahoula National Wildlife Management Preserve, the camp offers a truly backcountry experience for those seeking solitude in the Louisiana pine forests.

This is a no-fee, undeveloped site with minimal amenities. Potable water is not available, so campers must bring their own water supply. The flat, densely forested terrain provides a quiet setting away from developed recreation areas. The nearby Kisatchie Bayou Recreation Area offers additional opportunities for exploration.

Due to its primitive nature, this camp is best suited for experienced campers comfortable with self-sufficient backcountry camping. The site operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required or accepted.

location.directions: From Alexandria, travel north on U.S. Highway 167 for 23 miles, then northeast on Louisiana Highway 472 for approximately 4 miles, then east on Forest Road 145 for 2 miles to reach the camp.

payload.name: Quechee State Park Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates from May 22 through October 11, 2026. Reservations open up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Day use hours are 10 am to sunset.
payload.short_description: Vermont state park campground near the scenic Quechee Gorge, offering 56 wooded sites including tent/RV, lean-tos, and cabins with modern amenities.
payload.medium_description: Quechee State Park Campground sits in a wooded area near the Ottauquechee River, just a short walk from Vermont's deepest gorge. The campground offers 56 sites including tent/RV sites, lean-tos, and electric cabins. Amenities include flush toilets, coin-operated hot showers, drinking water, a dump station, fire rings, picnic tables, trash service, and Wi-Fi. Popular activities include hiking the Quechee Gorge Trail, fishing, disc golf, and volleyball.
payload.long_description:
Quechee State Park Campground is located along US Route 4 in Hartford, Vermont, positioned near the dramatic 165-foot-deep Quechee Gorge, often called Vermont's Little Grand Canyon. The wooded campground offers a mix of 40 tent/RV sites, 3 tent-only sites, 7 lean-tos, and 6 electric cabins, making it suitable for a variety of camping styles.

Two modern restroom buildings serve the campground with flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and coin-operated hot showers. A sanitary dump station is available for RVs, though no hookups are provided at individual sites except for the cabins which have electric service. Every site includes a fire ring and picnic table, and campers have access to trash disposal, Wi-Fi, ice, and firewood for purchase.

The park's main attraction is the Quechee Gorge Trail, which offers stunning views and leads down to the gorge floor. Additional recreation includes fishing access, disc golf, horseshoe pits, and a volleyball court. The campground's proximity to Upper Valley attractions like Woodstock and the Simon Pearce glassblowing facility makes it a popular tourist destination.

location.directions: From I-89 Exit 1: Travel 3 miles west on U.S. Route 4.

links.title: Vermont State Parks Quechee Reservation Page

payload.name: Gecko Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served with a 14-day limit. Currently in off-season (April 16 through September 30) when no recreation permit is required. Extreme summer temperatures exceed 100°F. Permit season resumes October 1.
payload.short_description: The largest campground in Imperial Sand Dunes Recreation Area, featuring paved north and south loops with vault toilets, popular for OHV camping in California's desert dunes.
payload.medium_description: Gecko Campground is the largest developed campground in the Imperial Sand Dunes Recreation Area, located east of Brawley, California. The campground features two paved loops (north and south) with numerous vault toilets throughout. It serves as a base camp for off-highway vehicle enthusiasts exploring the expansive dune system. No reservations are accepted; all sites are first-come, first-served with a 14-day camping limit.
payload.long_description:
Gecko Campground anchors the Imperial Sand Dunes Recreation Area, the most visited BLM site in the nation with over 1.2 million annual visitors. The campground's paved north and south loops provide access to numerous dispersed camping spots along the edge of the dunes. Vault toilets are stationed throughout both loops. The area is a premier destination for OHV recreation, with direct access to open riding areas south of Highway 78.

The campground operates on a first-come, first-served basis year-round with a 14-day stay limit. Recreation permits are required from October 1 through April 15, costing $55/week in advance or $70/week purchased onsite. Season permits are available for $185. From mid-April through September, no permits are required, though extreme summer temperatures make camping challenging during this period.

Campers should come prepared for primitive desert camping. There is no potable water, hookups, or dump station at the campground. Trash collection is provided throughout the recreation area. Pets are allowed but must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet. Fires are permitted but burning hazardous materials and using wood pallets or lumber with nails is prohibited.

location.directions: From Brawley, California, take Highway 78 east toward the Imperial Sand Dunes. Turn left onto Gecko Road; the campground entrance is on the left side of the road.

links.title: Imperial Sand Dunes Rules and Regulations

payload.name: New Discovery State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Reservations made more than 7 days out require a two-night minimum; one-night stays are allowed within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Rustic campground in Groton State Forest with 69 sites including tent/RV sites, lean-tos, and remote backcountry sites near Osmore, Kettle, and Ricker Ponds.
payload.medium_description: New Discovery State Park sits within the 26,000-acre Groton State Forest in Vermont's Northeast Kingdom. The campground offers 69 sites ranging from tent/RV sites and lean-tos to remote hike-in or boat-in sites at Osmore Pond. Campers enjoy direct trail access to the forest's extensive hiking network and can rent boats or fish the nearby ponds. Flush toilets, hot showers, and drinking water are available throughout the campground.
payload.long_description:
New Discovery State Park is part of the expansive Groton State Forest, one of the largest contiguous landholdings managed by the State of Vermont. The campground provides a gateway to the forest's extensive trail system, with paths departing directly from camp to scenic overlooks and surrounding ponds including Osmore, Kettle, and Ricker.

The park offers diverse camping options across 69 total sites: 33 tent/RV sites, 12 tent-only sites, 15 lean-tos, and 7 remote sites accessible by hiking or paddling to Osmore Pond. Equestrian campers have access to 8 horse-camping sites with hitching racks, corrals, and watering stations. Facilities include flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and coin-operated showers. Each campsite has a fire ring and picnic table. Firewood is sold on-site.

A Nature Center offers interpretive programs throughout the season. While there are no hookups, an RV dump station is available. The campground can accommodate RVs up to 45 feet depending on the site. Pets are welcome on leash throughout the park.

location.directions: From Groton, travel 2 miles west on U.S. 302, then 9.5 miles northwest on VT 232.

payload.name: Silver Lake State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through September 6. Reservations can be made up to 11 months in advance on a rolling basis. Reservations made more than 7 days ahead require a two-night minimum; one-night stays are available within 7 days of arrival.
payload.short_description: Family-friendly Vermont campground on Silver Lake featuring a sandy beach, 47 campsites with flush toilets and hot showers, boat rentals, and nature programs near Woodstock.
payload.medium_description: Silver Lake State Park offers 47 campsites including tent/RV sites and lean-tos on the shores of Silver Lake in Barnard, Vermont. The park features a large sandy swimming beach, coin-operated hot showers, flush toilets, an RV dump station, and boat rentals. Located near Woodstock and central Vermont attractions, it serves as an excellent base for family vacations with nature programs, a playground, and court games.
payload.long_description:
Silver Lake State Park sits on the eastern shore of Silver Lake in the small town of Barnard, Vermont, offering one of the more popular camping experiences in the state park system. The 47-site campground includes 29 tent/RV sites, 10 tent-only sites, and 7 lean-to shelters, all equipped with picnic tables and fire rings. Two restroom buildings provide flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and coin-operated showers. An RV dump station is available, though no hookups are provided at individual sites.

The park's main draw is its expansive sandy beach with designated swimming area, making it ideal for families. Kayaks, canoes, pedal boats, and rowboats are available for rent at the park office. A car-top boat launch provides access for personal watercraft. The day-use area includes a concession stand, large playground, basketball court, horseshoe pits, and volleyball net. Ranger-led nature programs run throughout the summer season.

Silver Lake's proximity to Woodstock and other central Vermont destinations makes it a convenient base camp for exploring the region while enjoying lakeside camping amenities.

location.directions: From I-89 Exit 3: Travel west on VT 107 for 2.6 miles, turn left onto VT 107 West / VT 12 South for 0.4 miles, make a slight left onto North Rd and travel 6.7 miles. Park entrance is on the left. Address: 20 State Park Beach Rd, Barnard, VT 05031.

address.full: 20 State Park Beach Rd, Barnard, VT 05031

links.title: Vermont State Parks - Silver Lake Reservations

payload.name: Stillwater State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 15 through September 13. Reservations are available up to 11 months in advance through the Vermont State Parks online reservation system. Bears have been active in this park; campers should store food and trash in vehicles or bear canisters.
payload.short_description: Lakefront campground on Lake Groton in Vermont's Groton State Forest with 76 sites including tent, RV, and lean-to options, flush restrooms, hot showers, and a swimming beach.
payload.medium_description: Stillwater State Park offers 76 campsites on the shores of Lake Groton in Vermont's scenic Groton State Forest. The campground features a mix of tent-only sites, tent/RV sites, and rustic lean-tos. Amenities include flush toilets, hot showers, potable water, and an RV dump station. A swimming beach, boat launch, playground, and access to extensive hiking trails make this a popular destination for families and outdoor enthusiasts.
payload.long_description:
Stillwater State Park is one of seven state parks within the 26,000-acre Groton State Forest in northeastern Vermont. The campground sits on the western shore of Lake Groton, offering waterfront access and scenic views of the surrounding hardwood and conifer forests. With 76 sites ranging from tent-only to tent/RV to traditional lean-tos, the park accommodates a variety of camping styles.

Facilities include modern restrooms with flush toilets, hot and cold running water, and coin-operated hot showers. An RV sanitary dump station is available, though no hookups are offered at individual sites. Each campsite features a fire ring and picnic table. The park provides trash and recycling services. A swimming beach with a designated swimming area, boat launch and dock, boat rentals, playground, and horseshoe pit round out the recreation options.

The Groton Nature Center is within walking distance, and miles of hiking trails connect Stillwater to the other parks in Groton State Forest. Bears are active in the area, so campers should store food and trash securely in vehicles or bear canisters. Pets are allowed on leash throughout the park but are prohibited at the swimming beach.

payload.name: Deschutes Bridge Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is currently not operational. No facilities are available including water and restrooms.
payload.short_description: A non-operational campground in Deschutes National Forest, Oregon. The site is currently closed with no facilities available.
payload.medium_description: Deschutes Bridge Campground is a Forest Service site in Deschutes National Forest that is currently not operational. No amenities are available at this location, including water or restrooms. Campers seeking similar options in the area should consider Lower Bridge Campground on the Metolius River or Sheep Bridge Campground near Wickiup Reservoir.
payload.long_description:
Deschutes Bridge Campground is a Forest Service recreation site located in Deschutes National Forest in central Oregon. The campground is currently not operational and has no facilities or amenities available.

No water, restrooms, or other services are present at this site. No fees are required, but the campground is not accepting visitors in its current state. Those seeking camping in the Deschutes National Forest should look to nearby alternatives such as Lower Bridge Campground along the Metolius River or Sheep Bridge Campground at the confluence of the Deschutes River and Wickiup Reservoir.

The surrounding Deschutes National Forest offers numerous recreational opportunities including fishing, hiking, and wildlife viewing across its varied terrain of high desert, volcanic features, and forested river corridors.

location.directions: From Bend, travel 41.1 miles west and south on Cascade Lakes Highway (46).

payload.name: Underhill State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open for the 2026 season from May 22 through October 11. Reservations available up to 11 months in advance. Two-night minimum required for reservations made more than 7 days ahead; one-night stays permitted within 7 days of arrival. Due to limited parking capacity, carpooling is recommended.
payload.short_description: A primitive walk-in campground on the western slopes of Mount Mansfield in Vermont, offering tent sites and lean-tos with access to extensive hiking trails including routes to Vermont's highest peak.
payload.medium_description: Underhill State Park Campground sits on the western slopes of Mount Mansfield within Mount Mansfield State Forest. This walk-in campground features 18 sites including tent sites and lean-tos, all requiring a short walk from parking with wheelbarrows provided for gear transport. The park serves as a gateway to hiking trails leading to the summit of Vermont's highest peak.
payload.long_description:
Underhill State Park Campground is a primitive walk-in camping destination nestled on the western slopes of Mount Mansfield, Vermont's highest peak at 4,393 feet. Located within Mount Mansfield State Forest in Chittenden County, the campground offers a rustic experience with 18 total sites including tent sites, lean-tos, and a group camping area that accommodates up to 75 people.

The lower camp area features flush toilets with running cold water but no showers, while the upper group area has pit toilets and composting outhouses. All camping is walk-in only, with wheelbarrows provided at the parking area to help transport gear. The campground operates on a pack-it-out trash policy. Each site includes a fire ring and picnic table.

The park provides direct trail access to the summit of Mount Mansfield via scenic hiking routes. Due to limited parking capacity, carpooling is recommended. Day use hours are 10 am to sunset. The campground is not suitable for RVs or tent trailers.

location.directions: 352 Mountain Rd, Underhill, VT 05490. GPS coordinates: 44.52895, -72.84277

payload.name: Jeffers Brook Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fee required. No reservations accepted.
payload.short_description: Free Adirondack-style backcountry shelter on the Appalachian Trail in White Mountain National Forest, sleeping 10 with a moldering privy and brook water source.
payload.medium_description: Jeffers Brook Shelter is a classic three-sided Adirondack-style backcountry shelter managed by the US Forest Service within White Mountain National Forest. Located just off the Town Line Trail section of the Appalachian Trail, approximately 1.1 miles north of NH Route 25 in Glencliff, the shelter sleeps up to 10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fee required.
payload.long_description:
Jeffers Brook Shelter is a traditional Adirondack-style backcountry shelter situated at approximately 1,350 feet elevation on the western slopes of Mount Moosilauke in the White Mountain National Forest. The three-walled wooden shelter with an open front provides basic protection from the elements and sleeps up to 10 people. It serves as a popular stopping point for Appalachian Trail thru-hikers and those exploring the White Mountains.

The shelter is accessible via a short side trail from Town Line Trail, located 1.1 miles north of NH Route 25 in the village of Glencliff. An alternate approach follows Long Pond Road, reaching the shelter 0.2 miles south on Town Line Trail. Jeffers Brook flows directly in front of the shelter, providing a reliable water source that must be treated before drinking. A moldering privy is available for sanitation.

This is a primitive backcountry site with no potable water, no electricity, and no developed amenities beyond the shelter structure and privy. Visitors should be prepared with water treatment, appropriate gear, and Leave No Trace practices.

location.directions: From NH Route 25 in the village of Glencliff, take Town Line Trail (Appalachian Trail) north for approximately 1.1 miles to the shelter side trail. Alternatively, access via Long Pond Road, then hike 0.2 miles south on Town Line Trail.

payload.name: Bagley Flat Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Stage 1 fire restrictions are in effect through September 30, 2026, which may limit fire use outside of Forest Service-provided grills. No camping fees required; boat launch fees apply at Saguaro Del Norte.
payload.short_description: Boat-access-only campground on Saguaro Lake with 10 designated sites featuring grills, tables, and a courtesy dock for fishing, shaded by a mesquite grove.
payload.medium_description: Bagley Flat is a unique boat-access-only campground on Saguaro Lake in Tonto National Forest. The 10 designated sites come equipped with grills and picnic tables, nestled in a shady mesquite grove. A courtesy dock provides easy access for fishing, and a vault toilet serves as the only restroom facility on the upper portion of the lake. No camping fees are required, though boat launch fees apply at Saguaro Del Norte.
payload.long_description:
Bagley Flat Campground offers a distinctive camping experience on Saguaro Lake, accessible only by boat. Located 35 miles east of Mesa, campers must first drive to Saguaro Del Norte Recreation Site to launch their watercraft, then travel approximately 4 miles by boat to reach the campground. The effort is rewarded with a peaceful, semi-secluded setting shaded by a grove of mesquite trees.

The campground features 10 designated sites, each equipped with a grill and picnic table. A vault toilet serves the area and is notably the only restroom facility on the upper portion of the lake. A courtesy dock makes fishing access convenient. There is no potable water, so campers must bring their own supply.

Camping at Bagley Flat is free, though fees apply at the boat launch. Quiet hours run from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. with no generators permitted during that time. Glass containers are prohibited. The 14-day stay limit applies.

location.directions: 35 miles east of Mesa. Travel 27 miles north on State Hwy 87 to Bush Highway/Forest Road 204 and turn right. Follow FR 204 for 4 miles to Saguaro Del Norte boat launch (all paved). From there, travel approximately 4 miles by boat to Bagley Flat. Boat access only.

payload.name: LITTLE BEAR SPRING TRAIL CAMP
payload.status_description: Open for backcountry camping. No reservations required. Hike-in access only via the Pacific Crest Trail.
payload.short_description: Backcountry hike-in trail camp along the Pacific Crest Trail at 6,588 feet in San Bernardino National Forest, offering a fire ring, picnic table, vault toilet, and horse corrals.
payload.medium_description: Little Bear Springs PCT Trail Camp is a primitive hike-in campsite along the Pacific Crest Trail in the San Bernardino National Forest. Located at 6,588 feet elevation, the camp features one picnic table, a fire ring, and a vault restroom. Non-potable water is available, along with a water trough and pipe horse corrals for equestrian users. This backcountry camp serves PCT thru-hikers, day hikers, and horseback riders.
payload.long_description:
Little Bear Springs PCT Trail Camp is a primitive backcountry campsite situated along the Pacific Crest Trail in the Mountaintop Ranger District of San Bernardino National Forest. At 6,588 feet elevation, this hike-in-only camp offers a rustic stopping point for PCT thru-hikers and section hikers traversing the Onyx Peak to Holcomb Creek corridor.

The camp provides basic amenities including a single picnic table, fire ring, and vault restroom. A non-potable water source is available on site. Equestrian visitors will find a water trough and pipe horse corrals, making this a viable overnight option for horseback riders as well.

As a primitive trail camp, visitors should come prepared with their own potable water and supplies. Dogs are permitted but must be kept on a leash no longer than six feet.

location.directions: Access the campground via Coxey Road (Forest Road 3N14) from Fawnskin, California. The trailhead is located along the Pacific Crest Trail, south of Holcomb Creek Road.

links.title: USFS Little Bear Springs PCT Trail Camp

payload.name: Red Bridge
payload.status_description: Currently closed for the season. Specific reopening dates are not published; contact the Mt. Hough Ranger District for current status.
payload.short_description: A free, primitive 5-site campground along the Middle Fork Feather River in Plumas National Forest, featuring vault toilets and first-come, first-served camping.
payload.medium_description: Red Bridge Campground is a small, free primitive campground in Plumas National Forest with five sites located on both sides of the Middle Fork Feather River. The campground is managed by the Mt. Hough Ranger District and operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required. Basic facilities include two vault toilets, but campers must bring their own water as none is available on site.
payload.long_description:
Red Bridge Campground is one of two free campgrounds on the Mt. Hough Ranger District in Plumas National Forest. This small, rustic campground offers five campsites situated along both banks of the Middle Fork Feather River, providing a peaceful setting for those seeking a primitive camping experience in the Sierra Nevada foothills.

The campground is located approximately 7 miles south of Highway 70 via La Porte Road from Quincy. As a free, first-come, first-served facility, it tends to attract visitors looking for a quiet, no-frills camping experience. The river provides opportunities for fishing and wading during warmer months.

Facilities are minimal, consisting of two vault toilets. There is no potable water available at the site, so campers must bring an adequate supply. This is a primitive campground best suited for tent camping or small, self-contained units.

location.directions: From Quincy, travel east on Highway 70 and turn south onto La Porte Road. The campground is located approximately 7 miles south.

address.full: 5511 Quincy La Porte Rd, Quincy, CA 95971

payload.name: Babcock State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open from the third Friday in April through the fourth Monday in October, weather permitting. Currently within the 2026 operating season. Reservations available online, by phone, or at park headquarters. Minimum two consecutive nights on weekends, one night Sunday through Thursday, 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Babcock State Park’s 52-unit campground has 28 sites with electric hookups and 24 non-electric sites. The campground has a central bathhouse with coin-operated washers and dryers, a water fill-up station, and two sewage dump facilities. Wi-Fi is also available and cell phone service is available from most major cell phone companies. If you are looking to bring a group, Babcock offers a group tent camping area that can accommodate up to 20 tents and features a covered shelter with nine picnic tables, electric and a covered stone fireplace. The campground is open mid-April through late October, weather permitting.
payload.medium_description: Babcock State Park Campground features 52 sites in the wooded terrain of southern West Virginia, just 20 miles from the New River Gorge Bridge. The campground offers 28 electric sites and 24 non-electric sites suitable for tents or trailers. Amenities include a central bathhouse with coin-operated laundry, two water fill-up stations, two dump stations, and WiFi. The park's famous Glade Creek Grist Mill and over 20 miles of hiking trails are nearby.
payload.long_description:
Babcock State Park Campground sits in the forested hills of Fayette County, about 20 miles southeast of the New River Gorge Bridge. The campground offers 52 sites spread across a wooded setting: 28 sites have electric-only hookups (four of which are ADA accessible) and 24 are non-electric, all accommodating tents or trailers. A central bathhouse provides restrooms, showers, and coin-operated laundry facilities.

Campers have access to two water fill-up stations, two sewage dump facilities, WiFi, and cell service from most major carriers. Firewood and ice are available for purchase. The park is best known for the Glade Creek Grist Mill, a fully functional replica that draws visitors year-round. Over 20 miles of hiking and biking trails wind through the 4,127-acre park, and a stocked lake offers fishing and boating opportunities.

The campground operates from the third Friday in April through the fourth Monday in October, weather permitting. Reservations require a minimum two-night stay on weekends or one night Sunday through Thursday, with a 14-night maximum stay. Check-in is at 1 p.m. and check-out is at noon.

location.directions: 486 Babcock Road, Clifftop, WV 25831. Located 20 miles southeast of the New River Gorge Bridge in Fayette County.

payload.name: Beech Fork State Park Moxley Branch Campground
payload.status_description: The campground is open mid-April through mid-October. Reservations are available from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. Check-in is 1:00 p.m. and check-out is noon.
payload.short_description: Beech Fork State Park offers some of the best recreational opportunities in West Virginia’s southwestern region. Visitors to this 3,144-acre park can hike in the hills, watch birds, fish or take a boat out on Beech Fork Lake. The lake is a 720-acre reservoir, with 31 miles of shoreline. Located 12 miles south of Huntington and Barboursville, Beech Fork State Park is the perfect getaway for visitors from neighboring states and cities, like Cincinnati, Ohio and Lexington, Kentucky.
payload.medium_description: Moxley Branch Campground is one of four camping areas at Beech Fork State Park, offering both 30-amp electric and non-electric sites. The campground operates seasonally from mid-April through mid-October and features full-service bathhouse facilities. Reservations are available from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend via the West Virginia State Parks reservation system.
payload.long_description:
Moxley Branch Campground is located within Beech Fork State Park in Wayne County, West Virginia, near the 720-acre Beech Fork Lake. The campground offers a choice between 30-amp electric sites and non-electric primitive sites, making it suitable for both RV campers and tent campers seeking a more traditional experience.

The campground features full-service bathhouse and restroom facilities. A camp store called Camper's Corner Store is located at the park headquarters, offering basic groceries, camping supplies, fishing supplies, bait, ice, firewood, and hand-dipped ice cream. The store operates seasonally from April through October.

Beech Fork State Park encompasses 3,144 acres with opportunities for boating, fishing, swimming at the beach, and hiking on over 7 miles of trails. The park maintains 275 total campsites across four campgrounds, with 99 lakefront sites available throughout the park.

location.directions: From Huntington, take I-64 East to Exit 11 (Hal Greer Boulevard/US-10). Head south on US-10 to WV-10, then follow signs to Beech Fork State Park at 5601 Long Branch Road, Barboursville, WV 25504.

address.full: 88 Moxley Branch Camp Rd, Barboursville, WV 25504

links.title: WV State Parks - Beech Fork Camping

payload.name: White River Campground
payload.status_description: The campground operates seasonally from end of May through mid-October, weather permitting. As of mid-May, the campground may not yet be open for the season. No reservations required; all sites are first-come, first-served with no fee. Campers must bring their own water.
payload.short_description: Free primitive campground with five sites in Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest, featuring vault toilets, picnic tables, and fire rings along the White River near Ely, Nevada.
payload.medium_description: White River Campground is a small, free primitive campground located in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest west of Ely, Nevada. The campground offers five sites with picnic tables and campfire rings, vault toilets, and access to stream fishing and OHV trails. No potable water is available.
payload.long_description:
White River Campground is a rustic, no-fee campground nestled in the Humboldt-Toiyabe National Forest within White Pine County, Nevada. Located about 40 miles west of Ely via US-6 and Forest Road 405, this small campground offers five dispersed-style sites along the White River.

Each site includes a picnic table and campfire ring. The campground has vault toilets but no potable water, so campers must bring their own water supply. Popular activities include stream fishing in the White River and OHV riding on nearby trails.

Dogs are permitted but must be kept on a leash within the campground. Horses and pack animals are also allowed. The campground operates seasonally from late May through mid-October, weather and conditions permitting.

location.directions: From Ely, Nevada, travel west on US-6 for 30 miles, then turn right onto NFSR-405. The campground is 9.5 miles down this road.

payload.name: Baldface Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served. No reservations or fees required. Winter access requires appropriate gear and backcountry skills. Bear canisters are required for overnight stays.
payload.short_description: A free backcountry shelter below South Baldface Mountain in White Mountain National Forest, sleeping 6-8 with views of Evans Notch Valley. Reached via a 2.5-mile hike on the Baldface Circle Trail.
payload.medium_description: Baldface Shelter is a rustic USFS backcountry shelter located just below the smooth granite ledges of South Baldface Mountain. The shelter sleeps 6-8 people and features a fire ring, composting toilet, and nearby water source (non-potable). A small designated camping area sits a short distance from the shelter. Access requires a 2.5-mile hike from the Baldface Trailhead via the Baldface Circle Trail.
payload.long_description:
Baldface Shelter offers backcountry camping at the edge of treeline on the popular Baldface Circle Trail in New Hampshire's White Mountain National Forest. Situated below the granite ledges of South Baldface Mountain, the shelter provides sweeping views of the Evans Notch Valley. The wooden shelter sleeps 6-8 hikers and serves as a base for exploring the exposed alpine terrain above.

The site includes a fire ring for campfires, a composting toilet, and access to a natural water source (which must be treated before drinking). A small designated tent camping area near the shelter accommodates additional campers. This is a primitive backcountry site with no potable water, trash service, or other developed amenities. Campers must pack out all waste and practice Leave No Trace principles.

The shelter is managed by the Saco Ranger District and is free to use on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations required. Dogs are permitted but must remain under control. Bear-proof food storage canisters are required for overnight backcountry trips in the White Mountain National Forest.

location.directions: From the Baldface Trailhead on NH Route 113 in Chatham, hike 2.5 miles up the Baldface Circle Trail (south branch) to reach the shelter.

payload.name: Beech Fork State Park Lakeview Campground
payload.status_description: Open year-round. Reservations available online at wvstateparks.com, by phone, or at the campground office. Two-night minimum on weekends, one-night minimum Sunday through Thursday. 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Beech Fork State Park offers some of the best recreational opportunities in West Virginia’s southwestern region. Visitors to this 3,144-acre park can hike in the hills, watch birds, fish or take a boat out on Beech Fork Lake. The lake is a 720-acre reservoir, with 31 miles of shoreline. Located 12 miles south of Huntington and Barboursville, Beech Fork State Park is the perfect getaway for visitors from neighboring states and cities, like Cincinnati, Ohio and Lexington, Kentucky.
payload.medium_description: Lakeview Campground is one of four camping areas at Beech Fork State Park, offering year-round access to lakefront camping on the scenic 720-acre Beech Fork Lake. The campground provides 30-amp electric hookups and full-service bathhouses with restroom facilities. A camp store on-site sells camping supplies and firewood from April through October.
payload.long_description:
Lakeview Campground sits along the shores of Beech Fork Lake, a 720-acre reservoir on the western edge of West Virginia near Huntington. The campground operates year-round and features 30-amp electric hookups at each site, with full-service bathhouses providing restroom facilities.

Beech Fork State Park encompasses over 3,100 acres and offers four distinct camping areas with 275 total campsites, 99 of which are lakefront. Lakeview is among the two year-round campgrounds (along with Old Orchard), while Moxley Branch and Four Coves operate seasonally from mid-April through October. The park features Camper's Corner Store for supplies and firewood, though Wi-Fi is only available at the Old Orchard bathhouse.

Reservations can be made online through WV State Parks, by phone, or at the campground office. Weekend reservations require a minimum two-night stay (Friday and Saturday), while weeknight stays have a one-night minimum. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights. Checkout is at noon and check-in begins at 1 p.m.

location.directions: Located at 5601 Long Branch Road, Barboursville, WV 25504, in Cabell County approximately 12 miles south of Huntington.

address.full: 490 Beech Fork Cabins Rd, Huntington, WV 25701

links.title: Beech Fork State Park Official Site

payload.name: Audra State Park Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally from April through mid-October, weather permitting. Reservations accepted online or by phone. Two-night minimum on weekends; 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Audra State Park is a heavily wooded area bisected by the Middle Fork River located in southwestern Barbour County and a portion of Upshur County. Each year, visitors are drawn to the natural beauty of the Middle Fork and its surroundings, which offers opportunities for hiking, camping and family picnics. This park is an ideal destination for families who enjoy the outdoors. The clear, clean water of the Middle Fork River and the rock overhang of the Alum Cave offer picture-perfect backdrops.
payload.medium_description: Nestled in the heavily forested hills of Barbour County, Audra State Park Campground provides 65 scenic campsites along the Middle Fork River. Thirty-nine sites offer electric hookups while the remainder are primitive. Two modern bathhouses with flush toilets, coin-operated laundry, a dump station, and a camp store stocking firewood, ice, and supplies serve the campground.
payload.long_description:
Audra State Park Campground sits in a heavily wooded valley where the Middle Fork River carves through ancient rock formations in southwestern Barbour County, West Virginia. The park's 355 acres offer a rugged Appalachian setting with deep forests, sandstone cliffs, and clear river pools popular for swimming. Many campsites lie along the stream, providing easy access to the water.

The campground features 65 sites, with 39 offering 30-amp electric hookups and the rest remaining primitive tent sites. Facilities include two bathhouses with flush toilets and showers, coin-operated laundry machines, and an RV dump station. A camp store near the entrance sells camping supplies, snacks, firewood, and bagged ice. The park's trail system, including the Alum Cave Trail and Rock Cliff Trail, starts within walking distance of the campground.

Reservations are available online through the West Virginia State Parks booking system, by phone, or at the campground office. A two-night minimum applies on weekends (Friday-Saturday) while single-night stays are permitted Sunday through Thursday. Maximum stay is 14 consecutive nights.

location.directions: From Buckhannon, take US-119 north approximately 10 miles, then turn east onto Route 11 (Audra Park Road) and continue about 4 miles to the park entrance at 8397 Audra Park Rd, Buckhannon, WV 26201.

payload.name: Sunrise Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round on a first-come, first-served basis. No fees or reservations. Water must be treated from natural sources. Maximum stay is two consecutive nights.
payload.short_description: Primitive backcountry shelter on Vermont's Long Trail in the Green Mountain National Forest, offering free first-come, first-served overnight stays for hikers.
payload.medium_description: Sunrise Shelter is a three-sided Adirondack-style backcountry shelter located on the Long Trail/North Country Trail in the Green Mountain National Forest near Chittenden, Vermont. The shelter accommodates 6-10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees or reservations. A privy is located nearby, and water is available from natural sources but must be treated before drinking.
payload.long_description:
Sunrise Shelter is a primitive backcountry shelter situated along the Long Trail and North Country Trail in Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest, within the Middlebury/Rochester Ranger District. The shelter features classic three-sided Adirondack-style construction designed to provide basic protection from the elements for through-hikers and backpackers traversing the ridgeline of the Green Mountains.

The shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no fees and no reservations accepted. Overnight stays are limited to two consecutive nights. A privy is located nearby, and water is available from natural sources in the area but must be filtered or treated before consumption. Hikers should always carry a tent as backup, since shelters typically fill up during peak hiking season.

This is a backcountry hiking shelter intended for Long Trail travelers, not a drive-up campground. Access requires hiking in on the trail. The shelter provides minimal amenities and is best suited for experienced backpackers who are self-sufficient and practice Leave No Trace principles.

location.directions: Sunrise Shelter is located near Brandon Gap in the Green Mountain National Forest. Access is typically via hiking trails in the area.

payload.name: Beech Fork State Park Four Coves Campground
payload.status_description: Open seasonally mid-April through October. Two-night minimum stay required on weekends (Friday and Saturday). Checkout at noon. 14-night maximum stay.
payload.short_description: Beech Fork State Park offers some of the best recreational opportunities in West Virginia’s southwestern region. Visitors to this 3,144-acre park can hike in the hills, watch birds, fish or take a boat out on Beech Fork Lake. The lake is a 720-acre reservoir, with 31 miles of shoreline. Located 12 miles south of Huntington and Barboursville, Beech Fork State Park is the perfect getaway for visitors from neighboring states and cities, like Cincinnati, Ohio and Lexington, Kentucky.
payload.medium_description: Four Coves Campground is one of four camping areas at Beech Fork State Park, offering 88 sites with 30-amp electric hookups along the shores of Beech Fork Lake. The campground features a full-service bathhouse with showers, flush toilets, and coin-operated laundry. Each site includes a picnic table and fire ring with grill, and several waterfront sites provide direct lake access for kayaking and fishing.
payload.long_description:
Four Coves Campground sits within the 3,144-acre Beech Fork State Park in Wayne County, West Virginia, about 12 miles south of Huntington. The campground occupies a scenic peninsula along Beech Fork Lake, a 720-acre impoundment known for its bass, muskie, and catfish populations. All 88 sites have 30-amp electric hookups, picnic tables, and fire rings with grills.

The campground operates seasonally from mid-April through October and offers a full-service bathhouse with hot showers, flush toilets, and coin-operated laundry facilities. Waterfront sites like 183 and 184 provide direct lake access with mature trees for shade. The park headquarters houses a camp store open April through October selling groceries, camping supplies, fishing gear, bait, ice, and firewood.

Beech Fork State Park offers extensive recreational opportunities including hiking and biking trails, two disc golf courses, and exceptional bird watching. The lake supports non-motorized and limited motorized boating. Reservations can be made online, by phone, or at the campground office, with a two-night minimum on weekends and 14-night maximum stay.

payload.name: Douglas Trail Shelter
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come, first-served. No reservations or fees required. Maximum two consecutive nights requested. Hikers should carry backup shelter as the site may be full during peak season.
payload.short_description: Backcountry lean-to shelter in the Lye Brook Wilderness on a side trail from the Appalachian Trail and Long Trail, accommodating up to 10 hikers on a first-come, first-served basis.
payload.medium_description: William B. Douglas Shelter is a classic log lean-to located within the Lye Brook Wilderness of Vermont's Green Mountain National Forest. Built in 1956 and named after a dedicated GMC trail maintainer from Brattleboro, the shelter sits at approximately 2,210 feet elevation on a 0.5-mile side trail from the AT/Long Trail, about 3.2 miles south of the Route 11/30 trailhead. The shelter has bunks for 10, a fireplace with stovepipe, a composting privy, and a spring 50 feet to the south.
payload.long_description:
William B. Douglas Shelter is a traditional backcountry lean-to situated in Vermont's Lye Brook Wilderness within the Green Mountain National Forest. Originally called Swezey Camp when completed in 1956 by the Brattleboro Section of the Green Mountain Club, it was renamed in late 1973 to honor William B. Douglas for his significant contributions to the shelter's planning and construction. The shelter was extensively renovated in 2005.

The log structure accommodates up to 10 hikers with built-in bunks and features a fireplace with stovepipe. Worked-up stove firewood is typically left for hikers and hunters. A composting privy is located nearby, and a spring lies 50 feet to the south along the trail, though all water must be treated or filtered before drinking. A historic logging railroad passes nearby, and the Branch Pond Trail follows much of the old railroad grade.

As a wilderness shelter, this is a hike-in only destination with no vehicle access or developed amenities. All camping is first-come, first-served with no reservations or fees required. Hikers should practice Leave No Trace principles and pack out all trash.

location.directions: From the Route 11/30 trailhead parking area between Manchester and Peru, hike south on the Appalachian Trail/Long Trail for approximately 3.2 miles. The shelter is located 0.5 mile down a side trail to the west.

payload.name: GENTIAN POND SHELTER
payload.status_description: Open year-round, first-come first-served. No reservations or fees. Group size limited to 10 people. Camping prohibited within 1/4 mile of the shelter. Bear canisters required for food storage.
payload.short_description: Primitive three-sided backcountry shelter with tent platforms along the Appalachian Trail in the Mahoosuc Range, accessed via a 3.5-mile hike from North Road.
payload.medium_description: Gentian Pond Shelter is a rustic three-sided lean-to with adjacent tent platforms situated along the Appalachian Trail in the Mahoosuc Range of the White Mountain National Forest. The shelter sits near Gentian Pond and is accessed via a 3.5-mile hike from North Road, at the intersection of the Austin Brook and Mahoosuc Trails. This is a primitive backcountry site with no facilities, requiring hikers to be fully self-sufficient.
payload.long_description:
Gentian Pond Shelter offers backcountry camping in one of the more remote sections of the White Mountain National Forest. The three-sided wooden lean-to with adjacent tent platforms provides basic overnight accommodation for hikers traversing the Appalachian Trail through the rugged Mahoosuc Range. The shelter is located near scenic Gentian Pond, offering access to both day hiking and extended backpacking opportunities.

Reaching the shelter requires a 3.5-mile hike from North Road, starting near the intersection of the Austin Brook and Mahoosuc Trails. The terrain is typical of the Mahoosucs: challenging and rocky. This is a primitive site with no developed amenities. There is no potable water, no restrooms, and no established fire rings or picnic tables. Campers must bring all water, food (in a bear-proof canister as required by WMNF regulations), and pack out all trash.

The shelter operates on a first-come, first-served basis with no reservations or fees. Group size is limited to 10 people per WMNF backcountry regulations. Camping is prohibited within 1/4 mile of the shelter, so overflow campers must disperse farther into the backcountry.

location.directions: From North Road in Shelburne, NH, hike approximately 3.5 miles north via the Austin Brook Trail to its intersection with the Mahoosuc Trail. The shelter is located at this junction along the Appalachian Trail.
